definitionLines: art. 一（个）；每一（个）；（同类 事物中的）任何一个
entries.definition: art. 一（个）；每一（个）；（同类 事物中的）任何一个
entries.etymology:
indefinite article before words beginning with vowels, 12c., from Old English an (with a long vowel) "one; lone," also used as a prefix an- "single, lone;" see one for the divergence of that word from this. Also see a, of which this is the older, fuller form.

In other European languages, identity between indefinite article and the word for "one" remains explicit (as in French un, German ein, etc.) Old English got by without indefinite articles: He was a good man in Old English was he wæs god man. Circa 15c., a and an commonly were written as one word with the following noun, which contributed to the confusion over how such words as newt and umpire ought to be divided (see N).

In Shakespeare, etc., an sometimes is a contraction of as if (a usage first attested c. 1300), especially before it.
entries.etymologyZh: indefinite article before words beginning with vowels, 12 世纪, 源自 古英语 an (with a long vowel) "one; lone," also used 作为 prefix an- "single, lone;" 参见 one for the divergence of that word 源自 this. Also 参见 a, of which this is the older, fuller form. In other European languages, identity between indefinite article and the word for "one" remains explicit (as in 法语 un, 德语 ein, etc.) 古英语 got by without indefinite articles: He was a good man in 古英语 was he wæs god man. Circa 15 世纪, a and an commonly were written as one word with the following 名词, which contributed to the confusion over how such words as newt and umpire ought to be divided （参见 N). In Shakespeare, etc., an 有时 is a contraction of as if (a usage 最早见于 约 1300 年), 尤指 before it.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to give up, surrender (oneself or something), give over utterly; to yield (oneself) utterly (to religion, fornication, etc.)," from Old French abandoner (12c.), from adverbial phrase à bandon "at will, at discretion," from à "at, to" (see ad-) + bandon "power, jurisdiction," from Latin bannum, "proclamation," from a Frankish word related to ban (v.).

Etymologically, the word carries a sense of "put someone under someone else's control." Meaning "to give up absolutely" is from late 14c. Related: Abandoned; abandoning.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to give up, surrender (oneself or something), give over utterly; to yield (oneself) utterly (to religion, fornication, etc.)," 源自 古法语 abandoner (12 世纪), 源自 adverbial phrase à bandon "at will, at discretion," 源自 à "at, to" （参见 ad-) + bandon "power, jurisdiction," 源自 拉丁语 bannum, "proclamation," 源自 a Frankish word related to ban （动）. Etymologically, the word carries a 语义 "put someone under someone else's control." 义为 "to give up absolutely" 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Abandoned; abandoning.

example.en: He decided to abandon his plan after learning about the legal risks involved.
example.zh: 了解到相关法律风险之后，他决定放弃原计划。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French ableté "expert at handling (something)," from Latin habilitatem (nominative habilitas) "aptitude," noun of quality from habilis "easy to manage, handy" (see able). One case where a Latin silent -h- failed to make a return in English (despite efforts of 16c.-17c. scholars); see H.

example.en: Her natural ability for mathematics earned her a scholarship.

entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French (h)able (14c.), from Latin habilem, habilis "easily handled, apt," verbal adjective from habere "to hold" (see habit (n.)). "Easy to be held," hence "fit for a purpose." The silent h- was dropped in English and resisted academic attempts to restore it 16c.-17c. (see H), but some derivatives (such as habiliment, habilitate) acquired it via French.

entries.etymology: 1835, displaced older abnormous (1742) and rival anormal (1835) under influence of Latin abnormis "deviating from a rule," from ab- "off, away from" (see ab-) + norma "rule" (see norm). The older forms were via Old French anormal (13c.), from Medieval Latin anormalos, from Greek anomalos, from an- "not" + homalos, from homos "same." The older forms were 经由 古法语 anormal (13 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 anormalos, 源自 希腊语 anomalos, 源自 an- "not" + homalos, 源自 homos "same." The 希腊语 word was altered in 拉丁语 by association with norma. 同源词：Abnormally.

entries.definition: vt. 废除，废止；取消，革除
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French aboliss-, present participle stem of abolir "to abolish" (15c.), from Latin abolere "destroy, cause to die out, retard the growth of," perhaps from ab- "from" (see ab-) + adolere "to grow," from PIE *ol-eye-, causative of root *al- (3) "to grow, nourish" (see old), and perhaps formed as an antonym to adolere. But the Latin word rather could be from a root in common with Greek ollymi, apollymi "destroy." Tucker writes that there has been a confusion of forms in Latin, based on similar roots, one meaning "to grow," the other "to destroy." Application to persons and concrete objects has long been obsolete. Related: Abolished; abolishing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 aboliss-, present participle stem of abolir "to abolish" (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 abolere "destroy, cause to die out, retard the growth of," 或源自 ab- "from" （参见 ab-) + adolere "to grow," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ol-eye-, 为 … 的使役形式 root *al- (3) "to grow, nourish" （参见 old), and 或许 formed 作为 antonym to adolere. But the 拉丁语 word rather could be 源自 a root in common with 希腊语 ollymi, apollymi "destroy." Tucker writes that there has been a confusion of forms in 拉丁语, based on similar roots, one 意为 "to grow," the other "to destroy." Application to persons and concrete objects has long been 已废. 同源词：Abolished; abolishing.

entries.etymology:
1540s, originally of both deliberate and unintended miscarriages; from Latin abortionem (nominative abortio) "miscarriage; abortion," noun of action from past participle stem of aboriri "to miscarry" (see abortive).

Earlier noun in English was simple abort (early 15c.) "miscarriage." In 19c. some effort was made to distinguish abortion "expulsion of the fetus between 6 weeks and 6 months" from miscarriage (the same within 6 weeks of conception) and premature labor (delivery after 6 months but before due time). The deliberate miscarriage was criminal abortion. This broke down late 19c. as abortion came to be used principally for intentional miscarriages, probably via phrases such as procure an abortion.

Foeticide (n.) appears 1823 as a forensic medical term for deliberate premature fatal expulsion of the fetus; also compare prolicide. Another 19c. medical term for it was embryoctony, from Latinized form of Greek kteinein "to destroy." Abortion was a taboo word for much of early 20c., disguised in print as criminal operation (U.S.) or illegal operation (U.K.), and replaced by miscarriage in film versions of novels.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 原义为 of both deliberate and unintended miscarriages; 源自 拉丁语 abortionem (主格 abortio) "miscarriage; abortion," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of aboriri "to miscarry" （参见 abortive). Earlier 名词 in English was simple abort (15 世纪初) "miscarriage." In 19 世纪 some effort was made to distinguish abortion "expulsion of the fetus between 6 weeks and 6 months" 源自 miscarriage (the same within 6 weeks of conception) and premature labor (delivery after 6 months but before due time). The deliberate miscarriage was criminal abortion. This broke down 19 世纪晚期 as abortion came to be used principally for intentional miscarriages, 可能 经由 phrases such as procure an abortion. Foeticide （名） appears 1823 年 作为 forensic medical term for deliberate premature fatal expulsion of the fetus; also 对比 prolicide. Another 19 世纪 medical term for it was embryoctony, 源自 Latinized form of 希腊语 kteinein "to destroy." Abortion was a taboo word for much of 20 世纪初, disguised in print as criminal operation (U.S.) or illegal operation (U.K.), and replaced by miscarriage in film versions of novels.

entries.etymology: Old English abutan, earlier onbutan "on the outside of," from on (see on; also see a- (1)) + be "by" (see by) + utan "outside," from ut (see out (adv.)). By 13c. it had forced out Old English ymbe, ymbutan for meaning "in the neighborhood of." Abouts, with adverbial genitive, still found in hereabouts, etc., probably is a northern dialectal form. About face as a military command (short for right about face) is first attested 1861, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 abutan, earlier onbutan "on the outside of," 源自 on （参见 on; also 参见 a- (1)) + be "by" （参见 by) + utan "outside," 源自 ut （参见 out （副）). By 13 世纪 it had forced out 古英语 ymbe, ymbutan for 意为 "in the neighborhood of." Abouts, with adverbial 属格, still found in hereabouts, etc., 可能 is a northern 方言 form. About face 作为 military command (short for right about face) is 最早见于 1861 年, American English.

entries.etymology: Old English abufan, earlier onbufan, from on (see on; also see a- (1)) + bufan "over," compound of be "by" (see by) + ufan "over/high," from Proto-Germanic *ufan- (source also of Old Saxon, Old High German oban, German oben), from PIE root *upo (see up (adv.)). Meaning "in addition" first corded 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 abufan, earlier onbufan, 源自 on （参见 on; also 参见 a- (1)) + bufan "over," 由 … 复合而成 be "by" （参见 by) + ufan "over/high," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ufan- (source also of 古撒克逊语, 古高地德语 oban, 德语 oben), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *upo （参见 up （副）). 义为 "in addition" first corded 1590 年代.

entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 abruptus "broken off, precipitous, disconnected," 为 … 的过去分词 abrumpere "break off," 源自 ab- "off" （参见 ab-) + rumpere "break" （参见 rupture （名）). 同源词：Abruptly; abruptness.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French absence (14c.), from Latin absentia, noun of state from absentem (nominative absens), present participle of abesse "be away from, be absent," from ab- "away" (see ab-) + esse "to be" (see essence).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 absence (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 absentia, 名词 of state 源自 absentem (主格 absens), 为 … 的现在分词 abesse "be away from, be absent," 源自 ab- "away" （参见 ab-) + esse "to be" （参见 essence).

example.en: His long absence from work worried his colleagues greatly.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Middle French absent (Old French ausent), from Latin absentem (nominative absens), present participle of abesse "be away from, be absent" (see absence). Related: Absently; absentness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 中古法语 absent (古法语 ausent), 源自 拉丁语 absentem (主格 absens), 为 … 的现在分词 abesse "be away from, be absent" （参见 absence). 同源词：Absently; absentness.

example.en: Three students were absent from class without any explanation yesterday.
example.zh: 昨天有三名学生无故缺席课堂。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "unrestricted; complete, perfect;" also "not relative to something else" (mid-15c.), from Middle French absolut (14c., Old French asolu, Modern French absolu), from Latin absolutus, past participle of absolvere "to set free, make separate" (see absolve).

Most of the current senses also were in the Latin word. Sense evolution was "detached, disengaged," thus "perfect, pure." Meaning "despotic" (1610s) is from notion of "absolute in position." Absolute monarchy is recorded from 1735 (absolute king is recorded from 1610s); scientific absolute magnitude (1902), absolute value (1907) are from early 20c. In metaphysics, the absolute "that which is absolute" is from 1809.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "unrestricted; complete, perfect;" also "not relative to something else" (15 世纪中期), 源自 中古法语 absolut (14 世纪, 古法语 asolu, 现代法语 absolu), 源自 拉丁语 absolutus, 为 … 的过去分词 absolvere "to set free, make separate" （参见 absolve). Most of the current senses also were in the 拉丁语 word. Sense evolution was "detached, disengaged," thus "perfect, pure." 义为 "despotic" (1610 年代) 始于 概念 "absolute in position." Absolute monarchy 见于 1735 年 (absolute king 见于 1610 年代); scientific absolute magnitude (1902 年), absolute value (1907 年) 始于 20 世纪初 In metaphysics, the absolute "that which is absolute" 始于 1809 年.

example.en: The evidence provided absolute proof that the suspect was innocent.
example.zh: 这些证据提供了被告无罪的确凿证明。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French absorber (Old French assorbir, 13c.), from Latin absorbere "to swallow up," from ab- "from" (see ab-) + sorbere "suck in," from PIE root *srebh- "to suck, absorb" (source also of Armenian arbi "I drank," Greek rhopheo "to sup greedily up, gulp down," Lithuanian srebiu "to drink greedily"). Figurative meaning "to completely grip (one's) attention" is from 1763. Related: Absorbed; absorbing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 absorber (古法语 assorbir, 13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 absorbere "to swallow up," 源自 ab- "from" （参见 ab-) + sorbere "suck in," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *srebh- "to suck, absorb" (source also of Armenian arbi "I drank," 希腊语 rhopheo "to sup greedily up, gulp down," Lithuanian srebiu "to drink greedily"). Figurative 意为 "to completely grip (one's) attention" 始于 1763 年. 同源词：Absorbed; absorbing.

example.en: Students tend to absorb information more easily when it is presented visually.
example.zh: 当信息以视觉形式呈现时，学生往往更容易吸收。

entries.definition: n. 摘要，提要 a.抽象的，不具体的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., originally in grammar (of nouns), from Latin abstractus "drawn away," past participle of abstrahere "to drag away, detach, pull away, divert;" also figuratively, from ab(s)- "away" (see ab-) + trahere "draw" (see tract (n.1)).

Meaning "withdrawn or separated from material objects or practical matters" is from mid-15c. That of "difficult to understand, abstruse" is from c. 1400. Specifically in reference to modern art, it dates from 1914; abstract expressionism as an American-based uninhibited approach to art exemplified by Jackson Pollock is from 1952, but the term itself had been used in the 1920s of Kandinsky and others.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 原义为 in grammar (of nouns), 源自 拉丁语 abstractus "drawn away," 为 … 的过去分词 abstrahere "to drag away, detach, pull away, divert;" also figuratively, 源自 ab(s)- "away" （参见 ab-) + trahere "draw" （参见 tract (n.1)). 义为 "withdrawn or separated from material objects or practical matters" 始于 15 世纪中期 That of "difficult to understand, abstruse" 始于 约 1400 年. Specifically in reference to modern art, it dates 自 1914 年起; abstract expressionism 作为 American-based uninhibited approach to art exemplified by Jackson Pollock 始于 1952 年, but the term itself had been used in the 1920 年代 of Kandinsky and others.

example.en: The professor's lecture was too abstract for first-year students to follow.
example.zh: 教授的讲座对一年级学生来说太抽象了，难以理解。

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French absurde (16c.), from Latin absurdus "out of tune; foolish" (see absurdity). The main modern sense (also present in Latin) is a figurative one, "out of harmony with reason or propriety." Related: Absurdly; absurdness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 absurde (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 absurdus "out of tune; foolish" （参见 absurdity). The main modern sense (also present in 拉丁语) is a figurative one, "out of harmony with reason or propriety." 同源词：Absurdly; absurdness.

example.en: It is absurd to expect perfection from every single employee.
example.zh: 期望每一位员工都做到完美，这是荒谬的。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French abondance and directly from Latin abundantia "fullness, plenty," noun of state from abundantem (nominative abundans), present participle of abundare "to overflow" (see abound).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 abondance and 直接源自 拉丁语 abundantia "fullness, plenty," 名词 of state 源自 abundantem (主格 abundans), 为 … 的现在分词 abundare "to overflow" （参见 abound).

example.en: The region is blessed with an abundance of natural resources and fertile land.
example.zh: 该地区拥有得天独厚的丰富自然资源和肥沃土地。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French abundant and directly from Latin abundantem (nominative abundans) "overflowing," present participle of abundare "to overflow" (see abound). Related: Abundantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 abundant and 直接源自 拉丁语 abundantem (主格 abundans) "overflowing," 为 … 的现在分词 abundare "to overflow" （参见 abound). 同源词：Abundantly.

definitionLines: n. 滥用，虐待；辱骂；陋习，弊端
entries.definition: n. 滥用，虐待；辱骂；陋习，弊端 vt. 滥用，虐待；辱骂
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to misuse, misapply," from Middle French abuser, from Vulgar Latin *abusare, from Latin abusus "an abusing, using up," past participle of abuti "use up," also "misuse," from ab- "away" (see ab-) + uti "use" (see use). Of sexual situations from early 15c., but originally incest, homosexuality, prostitution, etc.; meaning "to misuse sexually, ravish" is from 1550s. Specifically of drugs, from 1968. Related: Abused; abusing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to misuse, misapply," 源自 中古法语 abuser, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *abusare, 源自 拉丁语 abusus "an abusing, using up," 为 … 的过去分词 abuti "use up," also "misuse," 源自 ab- "away" （参见 ab-) + uti "use" （参见 use). Of sexual situations 源自 15 世纪初, but 原义为 incest, homosexuality, prostitution, etc.; 意为 "to misuse sexually, ravish" 始于 1550 年代. Specifically of drugs, 自 1968 年起. 同源词：Abused; abusing.

example.en: The report exposed widespread abuse of power within the organization.
example.zh: 该报告揭露了组织内部普遍存在的权力滥用现象。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "relating to an academy," also "collegiate, scholarly," from Latin academicus "of the Academy," from academia (see academy). Meaning "theoretical, not practical, not leading to a decision" (such as university debates or classroom legal exercises) is from 1886. Academic freedom is attested from 1901. Related: Academically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "relating to an academy," also "collegiate, scholarly," 源自 拉丁语 academicus "of the Academy," 源自 academia （参见 academy). 义为 "theoretical, not practical, not leading to a decision" (such as university debates or classroom legal exercises) 始于 1886 年. Academic freedom 见于 1901 年. 同源词：Academically.

example.en: Publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals boosts a researcher's reputation.
example.zh: 在经过同行评审的学术期刊上发表文章能提升研究者的声誉。

definitionLines: n. 学院；学/协会；研究院
entries.definition: n. 学院；学/协会；研究院
entries.etymology:
late 15c., "the classical Academy," from French Académie, from Latin Academia, from Greek Akademeia "grove of Akademos," a legendary Athenian of the Trojan War tales (his name apparently means "of a silent district"), whose estate, six stadia from Athens, was the enclosure where Plato taught his school.

Sense broadened 16c. into "any school or training place." Academy awards (1941) so called for their distributor, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "the classical Academy," 源自 法语 Académie, 源自 拉丁语 Academia, 源自 希腊语 Akademeia "grove of Akademos," a legendary Athenian of the Trojan War tales (his name 似乎 means "of a silent district"), whose estate, six stadia 源自 Athens, was the enclosure where Plato taught his school. Sense broadened 16 世纪 into "any school or training place." Academy awards (1941 年) so called for their distributor, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

example.en: She was admitted to a prestigious academy for the performing arts in New York.
example.zh: 她被纽约一所著名的表演艺术学院录取了。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "particular mode of pronunciation," from Middle French accent, from Old French acent (13c.), from Latin accentus "song added to speech," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + cantus "a singing," past participle of canere "to sing" (see chant (v.)). Loan-translation of Greek prosoidia, from pros- "to" + oide "song," which apparently described the pitch scheme in Greek verse. The decorating sense of "something that emphasizes or highlights" is from 1972.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "particular mode of pronunciation," 源自 中古法语 accent, 源自 古法语 acent (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 accentus "song added to speech," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + cantus "a singing," 为 … 的过去分词 canere "to sing" （参见 chant （动）). Loan-translation of 希腊语 prosoidia, 源自 pros- "to" + oide "song," which 似乎 described the pitch scheme in 希腊语 verse. The decorating 语义 "something that emphasizes or highlights" 始于 1972 年.

example.en: She spoke English with a distinct French accent.
example.zh: 她说英语时带有明显的法语口音。

definitionLines: v. 同意，认可；接受，领受
entries.definition: v. 同意，认可；接受，领受
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to take what is offered," from Old French accepter (14c.) or directly from Latin acceptare "take or receive willingly," frequentative of accipere "receive," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + capere "to take" (see capable). Related: Accepted; accepting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to take what is offered," 源自 古法语 accepter (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 acceptare "take or receive willingly," 为 … 的反复体 accipere "receive," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + capere "to take" （参见 capable). 同源词：Accepted; accepting.

example.en: She was pleased to accept the invitation to speak at the conference.
example.zh: 她很高兴接受了在会议上发言的邀请。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French acceptable, from Latin acceptabilis "worthy of acceptance," from acceptare "take or receive willingly" (see accept). Related: Acceptably.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 acceptable, 源自 拉丁语 acceptabilis "worthy of acceptance," 源自 acceptare "take or receive willingly" （参见 accept). 同源词：Acceptably.

example.en: The committee found the proposal acceptable and voted to move forward.
example.zh: 委员会认为该提案可接受，并投票决定推进。

entries.etymology: 1570s, from Middle French acceptance, from accepter (see accept). Earlier in same sense was acceptation (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 源自 中古法语 acceptance, 源自 accepter （参见 accept). Earlier in same sense was acceptation (14 世纪晚期).

example.en: Her acceptance into the prestigious club came after years of dedication.
example.zh: 经过多年的努力，她终于被这个享有盛誉的俱乐部接纳。

entries.definition: n.通路；访问 vt. 访问，存取
entries.etymology: early 14c., "an attack of fever," from Old French acces "onslaught, attack; onset (of an illness)" (14c.), from Latin accessus "a coming to, an approach," noun use of past participle of accedere "to approach" (see accede). The later senses are directly from Latin. Meaning "an entrance" is from c. 1600. Meaning "habit or power of getting into the presence of (someone or something)" is from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "an attack of fever," 源自 古法语 acces "onslaught, attack; onset (of an illness)" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 accessus "a coming to, an approach," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 accedere "to approach" （参见 accede). The later senses are 直接源自 拉丁语. 义为 "an entrance" 始于 约 1600 年. 义为 "habit or power of getting into the presence of (someone or something)" 始于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: Students can gain access to the library's digital database with their ID cards.
example.zh: 学生可以凭借学生证访问图书馆的数字数据库。

definitionLines: n. 附件，配件；附加物件
entries.definition: n. 附件，配件；附加物件
entries.etymology: also accessary, early 15c. as a legal term in the criminal sense of "one aiding in a crime;" also "that which is subordinate to something else," from Late Latin accessorius, from accessor, agent noun from accedere "to approach" (see accede). Attested from 1896 as "woman's smaller articles of dress;" hence accessorize.
entries.etymologyZh: also accessary, 15 世纪初 作为 legal term in the criminal 语义 "one aiding in a crime;" also "that which is subordinate to something else," 源自 晚期拉丁语 accessorius, 源自 accessor, agent 名词 源自 accedere "to approach" （参见 accede). Attested 自 1896 年起 as "woman's smaller articles of dress;" hence accessorize.

example.en: The phone case comes with a accessory pack that includes a screen protector.
example.zh: 这款手机壳附带一个配件包，里面有一片屏幕保护膜。

definitionLines: n. 事故；意外的事，偶然的事
entries.definition: n. 事故；意外的事，偶然的事
entries.etymology: late 14c., "an occurrence, incident, event," from Old French accident (12c.), from Latin accidentem (nominative accidens), present participle of accidere "happen, fall out, fall upon," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + cadere "fall" (see case (n.1)). Meaning grew from "something that happens, an event," to "something that happens by chance," then "mishap." Philosophical sense "non-essential characteristic of a thing" is late 14c. Meaning "unplanned child" is attested by 1932.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "an occurrence, incident, event," 源自 古法语 accident (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 accidentem (主格 accidens), 为 … 的现在分词 accidere "happen, fall out, fall upon," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + cadere "fall" （参见 case (n.1)). 义为 grew 源自 "something that happens, an event," to "something that happens by chance," 之后 "mishap." Philosophical sense "non-essential characteristic of a thing" is 14 世纪晚期 义为 "unplanned child" is attested 截至 1932 年.

example.en: The accident blocked two lanes and caused a three-mile traffic jam on the highway.
example.zh: 这场事故堵塞了两条车道，造成高速公路上三英里长的交通拥堵。

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Latin accomodatus "suitable," past participle of accomodare "make fit, adapt, fit one thing to another," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + commodare "make fit," from commodus "fit" (see commode). Related: Accommodated; accommodating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 拉丁语 accomodatus "suitable," 为 … 的过去分词 accomodare "make fit, adapt, fit one thing to another," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + commodare "make fit," 源自 commodus "fit" （参见 commode). 同源词：Accommodated; accommodating.

example.en: The conference center can accommodate up to five hundred delegates at a time.
example.zh: 该会议中心一次最多可容纳五百名代表。

entries.etymology: "room and provisions, lodging," c. 1600, now usually plural (accommodations) and chiefly U.S.; from French accommodation, from Latin accommodationem (nominative accommodatio), noun of action from past participle stem of accommodare (see accommodate). Meaning "appliance, anything which affords aid" is from 1610s; that of "act of accommodating" is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: "room and provisions, lodging," 约 1600 年, 现在 通常 plural (accommodations) and chiefly U.S.; 源自 法语 accommodation, 源自 拉丁语 accommodationem (主格 accommodatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of accommodare （参见 accommodate). 义为 "appliance, anything which affords aid" 始于 1610 年代; that of "act of accommodating" 始于 1640 年代.

example.en: The conference provided free accommodation for all international participants.
example.zh: 会议为所有国际参与者提供了免费住宿。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to be in company with," from Middle French accompagner, from Old French acompaignier (12c.) "take as a companion," from à "to" (see ad-) + compaignier, from compaign (see companion). Related: Accompanied; accompanying.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to be in company with," 源自 中古法语 accompagner, 源自 古法语 acompaignier (12 世纪) "take as a companion," 源自 à "to" （参见 ad-) + compaignier, 源自 compaign （参见 companion). 同源词：Accompanied; accompanying.

example.en: A nurse will accompany the patient throughout the entire examination.
example.zh: 一名护士将全程陪伴患者完成检查。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French acompliss-, present participle stem of acomplir "to fulfill, fill up, complete" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *accomplere, from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + complere "fill up" (see complete (adj.)). Related: Accomplished; accomplishing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 acompliss-, present participle stem of acomplir "to fulfill, fill up, complete" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *accomplere, 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + complere "fill up" （参见 complete （形）). 同源词：Accomplished; accomplishing.

example.en: She trained every day to accomplish her dream of running a marathon.
example.zh: 她每天训练以实现跑马拉松的梦想。

entries.etymology: early 12c., from Old French acorder (12c.) "reconcile, agree, be in harmony," from Vulgar Latin *accordare "make agree," literally "be of one heart, bring heart to heart," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + cor (genitive cordis) "heart," from PIE root *kerd- (1) "heart" (see heart (n.)). Related: Accorded; according.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, 源自 古法语 acorder (12 世纪) "reconcile, agree, be in harmony," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *accordare "make agree," 字面义为 "be of one heart, bring heart to heart," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + cor (属格 cordis) "heart," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kerd- (1) "heart" （参见 heart （名）). 同源词：Accorded; according.

example.en: Both parties must accord with the terms of the agreement before it takes effect.
example.zh: 双方必须与协议条款保持一致，协议才能生效。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "in agreement with," from according + -ly (2). From mid-15c. as "properly; adequately;" meaning "in agreement with logic or expectation" is recorded 1680s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "in agreement with," 源自 according + -ly (2). From 15 世纪中期 as "properly; adequately;" 意为 "in agreement with logic or expectation" is recorded 1680 年代.

example.en: Sales dropped sharply in winter, and the company cut its budget accordingly.
example.zh: 冬季销售额大幅下滑，公司相应地削减了预算。

entries.definition: n. 账，账户；说明，叙述 vi. （for）解释
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "reckoning of money received and paid," from Old French acont "account, reckoning, terminal payment," from a "to" (see ad-) + cont "counting, reckoning of money to be paid," from Late Latin computus "a calculation," from Latin computare "calculate" (see compute).

Meaning "sum of (one's) money in a bank" is from 1833. Sense of "narration" is first attested 1610s. Plural accounts used as a collective or singular in phrases such as to give accounts (of something), is from mid-13c. Phrase by all accounts is attested from 1798.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "reckoning of money received and paid," 源自 古法语 acont "account, reckoning, terminal payment," 源自 a "to" （参见 ad-) + cont "counting, reckoning of money to be paid," 源自 晚期拉丁语 computus "a calculation," 源自 拉丁语 computare "calculate" （参见 compute). 义为 "sum of (one's) money in a bank" 始于 1833 年. 义为 "narration" is 最早见于 1610 年代. Plural accounts used 作为 collective or singular in phrases such as to give accounts (of something), 始于 13 世纪中期 Phrase by all accounts 见于 1798 年.

example.en: You need to open a bank account before your salary can be deposited.
example.zh: 在工资存入之前，你需要开设一个银行账户。

definitionLines: a. 有责任的；有解释义务的；可|acre
entries.definition: a. 有责任的；有解释义务的；可|acre
entries.etymology: "answerable," literally "liable to be called to account," c. 1400 (mid-14c. in Anglo-French); see account (v.) + -able. Related: Accountably.
entries.etymologyZh: "answerable," 字面义为 "liable to be called to account," 约 1400 年 (14 世纪中期 in 盎格鲁-法语); 参见 account （动） + -able. 同源词：Accountably.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "accounting officer, one who renders accounts," from Old French acuntant (Modern French accomptant), from present participle of accompter (see account (v.)). Sense of "professional maker of accounts" is recorded from 1530s. The word also was an adjective in Middle English, "accountable; liable to render accounts" (early 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "accounting officer, one who renders accounts," 源自 古法语 acuntant (现代法语 accomptant), 源自 为 … 的现在分词 accompter （参见 account （动）). 义为 "professional maker of accounts" 见于 1530 年代. The word also was an 形容词 in 中古英语, "accountable; liable to render accounts" (15 世纪初).

example.en: The company hired a senior accountant to manage its annual tax filings.
example.zh: 该公司聘请了一名资深会计来处理年度税务申报。

entries.etymology: "reckoning of numbers," late 14c., verbal noun from account (v.). Phrase no accounting for tastes (1823) translates Latin de gustibus non est disputandum.
entries.etymologyZh: "reckoning of numbers," 14 世纪晚期, verbal 名词 源自 account （动）. Phrase no accounting for tastes (1823 年) translates 拉丁语 de gustibus non est disputandum.

example.en: She studied accounting in college and now works at a major firm.
example.zh: 她大学时学的是会计，现在在一家大公司工作。

entries.definition: vi. 积累；积聚 vt. 堆积
entries.etymology: 1520s, from Latin accumulatus, past participle of accumulare "to heap up" (see accumulation). Related: Accumulated; accumulating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 拉丁语 accumulatus, 为 … 的过去分词 accumulare "to heap up" （参见 accumulation). 同源词：Accumulated; accumulating.

example.en: He spent decades trying to accumulate enough savings to retire comfortably.
example.zh: 他花了数十年时间，努力积攒足够的存款以便安心退休。

entries.etymology: 1660s, from accurate + -cy.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 accurate + -cy.

example.en: The surgeon performed the operation with remarkable accuracy and skill.
example.zh: 外科医生以惊人的精确度和技巧完成了手术。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "done with care," from Latin accuratus "prepared with care, exact, elaborate," past participle of accurare "take care of," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + curare "take care of" (see cure (n.1)). The notion of doing something carefully led to that of being exact (1650s). Related: Accurately; accurateness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "done with care," 源自 拉丁语 accuratus "prepared with care, exact, elaborate," 为 … 的过去分词 accurare "take care of," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + curare "take care of" （参见 cure (n.1)). The 概念 doing something carefully led to that of being exact (1650 年代). 同源词：Accurately; accurateness.

example.en: The lab requires all measurements to be accurate to three decimal places.
example.zh: 实验室要求所有测量结果精确到小数点后三位。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "charge (with an offense, etc.), impugn, blame," from Old French acuser "to accuse, indict, reproach, blame" (13c.), earlier "announce, report, disclose" (12c.), or directly from Latin accusare "to call to account, make complaint against, reproach, blame; bring to trial, prosecute, arraign indict," from ad causa (see ad- + cause (n.)). Related: Accused; accusing; accusingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "charge (with an offense, etc.), impugn, blame," 源自 古法语 acuser "to accuse, indict, reproach, blame" (13 世纪), earlier "announce, report, disclose" (12 世纪)，或直接源自 拉丁语 accusare "to call to account, make complaint against, reproach, blame; bring to trial, prosecute, arraign indict," 源自 ad causa （参见 ad- + cause （名）). 同源词：Accused; accusing; accusingly.

example.en: The journalist was accused of spreading false information.
example.zh: 这名记者被指控传播虚假信息。

entries.etymology: late 15c., "made customary, habitual," past participle adjective from accustom (v.).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "made customary, habitual," past participle 形容词 源自 accustom （动）.

entries.etymology: Old English acan "to ache, suffer pain," from Proto-Germanic *akanan, perhaps from a PIE root *ag-es- "fault, guilt," represented also in Sanskrit and Greek, perhaps imitative of groaning. The verb was pronounced "ake," the noun "ache" (as in speak/speech) but while the noun changed pronunciation to conform to the verb, the spelling of both was changed to ache c. 1700 on a false assumption of a Greek origin (specifically Greek akhos "pain, distress," which is rather a distant relation of awe (n.)). Related: Ached; aching.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 acan "to ache, suffer pain," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *akanan, 或源自 a 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ag-es- "fault, guilt," represented also in 梵语 and 希腊语, 或许 imitative of groaning. The 动词 was pronounced "ake," the 名词 "ache" (as in speak/speech) but while the 名词 changed pronunciation to conform to the 动词, the spelling of both was changed to ache 约 1700 年 on a false assumption of a 希腊语 origin (specifically 希腊语 akhos "pain, distress," which is rather a distant relation of awe （名）). 同源词：Ached; aching.

entries.etymology:
early 14c., from Old French achever (12c.) "to finish, accomplish, complete," from phrase à chef (venir) "at an end, finished," or Vulgar Latin *accapare, from Late Latin ad caput (venire); both the French and Late Latin phrases meaning literally "to come to a head," from stem of Latin caput "head" (see capitulum).

Related: Achieved; achieving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 achever (12 世纪) "to finish, accomplish, complete," 源自 phrase à chef (venir) "at an end, finished," or 通俗拉丁语 *accapare, 源自 晚期拉丁语 ad caput (venire); both the 法语 and 晚期拉丁语 phrases 意为 字面义为 "to come to a head," 源自 stem of 拉丁语 caput "head" （参见 capitulum). 同源词：Achieved; achieving.

example.en: Years of hard work helped her finally achieve her lifelong career goals.
example.zh: 多年的努力帮助她最终实现了毕生的职业目标。

definitionLines: n. 完成，达到；成就，成绩
entries.definition: n. 完成，达到；成就，成绩
entries.etymology: late 15c., "act of completing" (something), from Middle French achèvement "a finishing," noun of action from Old French achever "to finish, accomplish" (see achieve). Meaning "thing achieved" is recorded from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "act of completing" (something), 源自 中古法语 achèvement "a finishing," 名词 of action 源自 古法语 achever "to finish, accomplish" （参见 achieve). 义为 "thing achieved" 见于 1590 年代.

example.en: Being published in a top journal was his greatest achievement as a researcher.
example.zh: 在顶级期刊发表文章是他作为研究者最大的成就。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "of the taste of vinegar," from French acide (16c.) or directly from Latin acidus "sour, sharp," adjective of state from acere "to be sour," from PIE root *ak- "sharp, pointed" (see acrid). Figurative use from 1775; applied to intense colors from 1916. Acid test is American English, 1892, from the frontier days, when gold was distinguished from similar metals by application of nitric acid. Acid rain is first recorded 1859 in reference to England.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "of the taste of vinegar," 源自 法语 acide (16 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 acidus "sour, sharp," 形容词 of state 源自 acere "to be sour," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ak- "sharp, pointed" （参见 acrid). Figurative use 自 1775 年起; applied to intense colors 自 1916 年起. Acid test is American English, 1892 年, 源自 frontier days, when gold was distinguished 源自 similar metals by application of nitric acid. Acid rain is 首见于 1859 年 in reference to England.

example.en: The scientist tested whether the solution was acid or alkaline.
example.zh: 科学家测试了溶液是酸性的还是碱性的。

entries.etymology: 1550s, a blend of Middle English aknow (from Old English oncnawan "understand," from on + cnawan "recognize;" see know) and Middle English knowlechen "admit, acknowledge" (c. 1200; see knowledge). In the merger, a parasitic -c- slipped in, so that while the kn- became a simple "n" sound (as in know), the -c- stepped up to preserve, in this word, the ancient "kn-" sound. Related: Acknowledged; acknowledging.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, a blend of 中古英语 aknow (源自 古英语 oncnawan "understand," 源自 on + cnawan "recognize;" 参见 know) and 中古英语 knowlechen "admit, acknowledge" (约 1200 年; 参见 knowledge). In the merger, a parasitic -c- slipped in, so that while the kn- became a simple "n" sound (as in know), the -c- stepped up to preserve, in this word, the ancient "kn-" sound. 同源词：Acknowledged; acknowledging.

example.en: She refused to acknowledge any mistakes in her report.
example.zh: 她拒绝承认报告中的任何错误。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French acointier "make known, make acquaintance of," from Vulgar Latin accognitare "to make known," from Latin accognitus "acquainted with," past participle of accognoscere "know well," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + cognitus, past participle of cogniscere "come to know," from com- "with" (see com-) + gnoscere "know" (see notice (n.)). Originally reflexive, "to make oneself known;" sense of "to gain for oneself personal knowledge of" is from early 14c. Related: Acquainted; acquainting.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 acointier "make known, make acquaintance of," 源自 通俗拉丁语 accognitare "to make known," 源自 拉丁语 accognitus "acquainted with," 为 … 的过去分词 accognoscere "know well," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + cognitus, 为 … 的过去分词 cogniscere "come to know," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + gnoscere "know" （参见 notice （名）). Originally reflexive, "to make oneself known;" 语义 "to gain for oneself personal knowledge of" 始于 14 世纪初 同源词：Acquainted; acquainting.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "state of being acquainted;" late 14c., "person with whom one is acquainted;" also "personal knowledge;" from Old French acointance "acquaintance, friendship, familiarity," noun of action from acointer (see acquaint). Acquaintant (17c.), would have been better in the "person known" sense but is now obsolete.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "state of being acquainted;" 14 世纪晚期, "person with whom one is acquainted;" also "personal knowledge;" 源自 古法语 acointance "acquaintance, friendship, familiarity," 名词 of action 源自 acointer （参见 acquaint). Acquaintant (17 世纪), would have been better in the "person known" sense but is 今废.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., acqueren, from Old French aquerre "acquire, gain, earn, procure," from Vulgar Latin *acquaerere, corresponding to Latin acquirere "to seek in addition to" (see acquisition). Reborrowed in current form from Latin c. 1600. Related: Acquired; acquiring.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, acqueren, 源自 古法语 aquerre "acquire, gain, earn, procure," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *acquaerere, corresponding to 拉丁语 acquirere "to seek in addition to" （参见 acquisition). Reborrowed in current form 源自 拉丁语 约 1600 年. 同源词：Acquired; acquiring.

example.en: It takes years of practice to acquire fluency in a foreign language.
example.zh: 需要多年练习才能获得外语流利能力。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of obtaining," from Old French acquisicion (13c.) or directly from Latin acquisitionem (nominative acquisitio), noun of action from past participle stem of acquirere "get in addition, accumulate," from ad- "extra" (see ad-) + quaerere "to seek to obtain" (see query (v.)). Meaning "thing obtained" is from late 15c. The vowel change of -ae- to -i- in Latin is due to a Latin phonetic rule involving unaccented syllables in compounds.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of obtaining," 源自 古法语 acquisicion (13 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 acquisitionem (主格 acquisitio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of acquirere "get in addition, accumulate," 源自 ad- "extra" （参见 ad-) + quaerere "to seek to obtain" （参见 query （动）). 义为 "thing obtained" 始于 15 世纪晚期 The vowel change of -ae- to -i- in 拉丁语 is due to a 拉丁语 phonetic rule involving unaccented syllables in compounds.

example.en: The company completed its acquisition of the smaller rival last month.
example.zh: 该公司上个月完成了对这家小竞争对手的收购。

entries.definition: ad. /prep. 横越，横断 prep. 在……对面
entries.etymology: early 14c., acros, earlier a-croiz (c. 1300), from Anglo-French an cros "in a crossed position," literally "on cross" (see cross (n.)). Prepositional meaning "from one side to another" is first recorded 1590s; meaning "on the other side (as a result of crossing)" is from 1750. Phrase across the board originally is from horse-racing, in reference to a bet of the same amount of money on a horse to win, place, or show.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, acros, earlier a-croiz (约 1300 年), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 an cros "in a crossed position," 字面义为 "on cross" （参见 cross （名）). Prepositional 意为 "from one side to another" is 首见于 1590 年代; 意为 "on the other side (as a result of crossing)" 始于 1750 年. Phrase across the board 原义为 始于 horse-racing, in reference to a bet of the same amount of money on a horse to win, place，或show.

definitionLines: n. 行，动作；（一）幕；法令，条例
n. 行动，举动；起作用；表演
entries.definition: n. 行，动作；（一）幕；法令，条例 n. 行动，举动；起作用；表演
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "a thing done," from Old French acte "(official) document," and directly from Latin actus "a doing, a driving, impulse; a part in a play, act," and actum "a thing done," originally a legal term, both from agere "to do, set in motion, drive, urge, chase, stir up," from PIE root *ag- "to drive, draw out or forth, move" (source also of Greek agein "to lead, guide, drive, carry off," agon "assembly, contest in the games," agogos "leader;" Sanskrit ajati "drives," ajirah "moving, active;" Old Norse aka "to drive;" Middle Irish ag "battle").

Theatrical ("part of a play," 1510s) and legislative (early 15c.) senses of the word also were in Latin. Meaning "display of exaggerated behavior" is from 1928. In the act "in the process" is from 1590s, perhaps originally from the 16c. sense of the act as "sexual intercourse." Act of God "uncontrollable natural force" recorded by 1726.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a thing done," 源自 古法语 acte "(official) document," and 直接源自 拉丁语 actus "a doing, a driving, impulse; a part in a play, act," and actum "a thing done," 原义为 a legal term, both 源自 agere "to do, set in motion, drive, urge, chase, stir up," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ag- "to drive, draw out or forth, move" (source also of 希腊语 agein "to lead, guide, drive, carry off," agon "assembly, contest in the games," agogos "leader;" 梵语 ajati "drives," ajirah "moving, active;" 古北欧语 aka "to drive;" Middle 爱尔兰语 ag "battle"). Theatrical ("part of a play," 1510 年代) and legislative (15 世纪初) senses of the word also were in 拉丁语. 义为 "display of exaggerated behavior" 始于 1928 年. In the act "in the process" 始于 1590 年代, 或许 原义为 源自 16 世纪 语义 the act as "sexual intercourse." Act of God "uncontrollable natural force" recorded 截至 1726 年.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "cause or grounds for a lawsuit," from Anglo-French accioun, Old French accion (12c.) "action, lawsuit, case," from Latin actionem (nominative actio) "a putting in motion; a performing, doing," noun of action from past participle stem of agere "to do" (see act (n.)). Sense of "something done, an act, deed" is late 14c. Meaning "fighting" is from c. 1600. As a film director's command, it is attested from 1923. Meaning "excitement" is recorded from 1968. Phrase actions speak louder than words is attested from 1731.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "cause or grounds for a lawsuit," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 accioun, 古法语 accion (12 世纪) "action, lawsuit, case," 源自 拉丁语 actionem (主格 actio) "a putting in motion; a performing, doing," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of agere "to do" （参见 act （名）). 义为 "something done, an act, deed" is 14 世纪晚期 义为 "fighting" 始于 约 1600 年. 作为 film director's command, it 见于 1923 年. 义为 "excitement" 见于 1968 年. Phrase actions speak louder than words 见于 1731 年.

example.en: The government took immediate action to contain the spread of the virus.
example.zh: 政府立即采取行动遏制病毒蔓延。

entries.etymology: 1620s; see active + -ate (2). Related: Activated; activating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代; 参见 active + -ate (2). 同源词：Activated; activating.

example.en: Press the button to activate the alarm system before you leave the building.
example.zh: 离开大楼前请按下按钮启动警报系统。

definitionLines: a. 活动的，活跃的；积极的，主 动的
entries.definition: a. 活动的，活跃的；积极的，主 动的
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "given to worldly activity" (opposed to contemplative or monastic), from Old French actif (12c.) or directly from Latin activus, from actus (see act (n.)). As "capable of acting" (opposed to passive), from late 14c. Meaning "energetic, lively" is from 1590s; that of "working, effective, in operation" is from 1640s. Active voice is recorded from 1765 (grammatical use of active dates from mid-15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "given to worldly activity" (opposed to contemplative or monastic), 源自 古法语 actif (12 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 activus, 源自 actus （参见 act （名）). As "capable of acting" (opposed to passive), 源自 14 世纪晚期 义为 "energetic, lively" 始于 1590 年代; that of "working, effective, in operation" 始于 1640 年代. Active voice 见于 1765 年 (grammatical use of active dates 源自 15 世纪中期).

example.en: Students who are active in class tend to learn more effectively.
example.zh: 在课堂上积极主动的学生往往学得更有效。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "active or secular life," from Old French activité, from Medieval Latin activitatem (nominative activitas), a word in Scholastic philosophy, from Latin activus (see active). Meaning "state of being active, briskness, liveliness" recorded from 1520s; that of "capacity for acting on matter" is from 1540s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "active or secular life," 源自 古法语 activité, 源自 中古拉丁语 activitatem (主格 activitas), a word in Scholastic philosophy, 源自 拉丁语 activus （参见 active). 义为 "state of being active, briskness, liveliness" recorded 源自 1520 年代; that of "capacity for acting on matter" 始于 1540 年代.

example.en: The school offers a wide range of after-school activities for students.
example.zh: 学校为学生提供丰富的课外活动。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "an overseer, guardian, steward," from Latin actor "an agent or doer," also "theatrical player," from past participle stem of agere (see act (n.)). Mid-15c. as "a doer, maker," also "a plaintiff." Sense of "one who performs in plays" is 1580s, originally applied to both men and women.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "an overseer, guardian, steward," 源自 拉丁语 actor "an agent or doer," also "theatrical player," 源自 past participle stem of agere （参见 act （名）). Mid-15 世纪 as "a doer, maker," also "a plaintiff." 义为 "one who performs in plays" is 1580 年代, 原义为 applied to both men and women.

example.en: The actor rehearsed his lines for hours before the opening night performance.
example.zh: 这位男演员在首演之夜前花了几个小时排练台词。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "female who does something;" see actor + -ess; stage sense is from 1700. Sometimes French actrice was used.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "female who does something;" 参见 actor + -ess; stage sense 始于 1700 年. Sometimes 法语 actrice was used.

example.en: The actress won an award for her role in the drama series.
example.zh: 这位女演员凭借在电视剧中的角色获得了奖项。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "pertaining to an action," from Old French actuel "now existing, up to date" (13c.), from Late Latin actualis "active, pertaining to action," adjectival form of Latin actus (see act (n.)). The broader sense of "real, existing" (as opposed to potential, ideal, etc.) is from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "pertaining to an action," 源自 古法语 actuel "now existing, up to date" (13 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 actualis "active, pertaining to action," adjectival form of 拉丁语 actus （参见 act （名）). The broader 语义 "real, existing" (as opposed to potential, ideal, etc.) 始于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The actual cost of the project was twice the original estimate.
example.zh: 该项目的实际成本是最初预算的两倍。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "in fact, in reality" (as opposed to in possibility), from actual + -ly (2). Meaning "actively, vigorously" is from mid-15c.; that of "at this time, at present" is from 1660s. As an intensive added to a statement and suggesting "as a matter of fact, really, in truth" it is attested from 1762.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "in fact, in reality" (as opposed to in possibility), 源自 actual + -ly (2). 义为 "actively, vigorously" 始于 15 世纪中期; that of "at this time, at present" 始于 1660 年代. 作为 intensive added to a statement and suggesting "as a matter of fact, really, in truth" it 见于 1762 年.

example.en: The film looks lighthearted, but it actually deals with very serious issues.
example.zh: 这部电影看起来轻松愉快，但实际上处理的是非常严肃的议题。

entries.etymology: 1680s, "pricking with a needle" to ease pain, from Latin acus "needle" (see acuity) + puncture. The verb is first recorded 1972.
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, "pricking with a needle" to ease pain, 源自 拉丁语 acus "needle" （参见 acuity) + puncture. The 动词 is 首见于 1972 年.

entries.etymology: late 14c., originally of fevers and diseases, "coming and going quickly" (opposed to a chronic), from Latin acutus "sharp, pointed," figuratively "shrill, penetrating; intelligent, cunning," past participle of acuere "sharpen" (see acuity). Meaning "sharp, irritating" is from early 15c. Meaning "intense" is from 1727. Related: Acutely; acuteness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 原义为 of fevers and diseases, "coming and going quickly" (opposed to a chronic), 源自 拉丁语 acutus "sharp, pointed," figuratively "shrill, penetrating; intelligent, cunning," 为 … 的过去分词 acuere "sharpen" （参见 acuity). 义为 "sharp, irritating" 始于 15 世纪初 义为 "intense" 始于 1727 年. 同源词：Acutely; acuteness.

example.en: Dogs have an acute sense of smell that helps them detect drugs.
example.zh: 狗拥有敏锐的嗅觉，能帮助它们探测毒品。

entries.etymology: early 15c. (implied in adapted) "to fit (something, for some purpose)," from Middle French adapter (14c.), from Latin adaptare "adjust," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + aptare "to join," from aptus "fitted" (see apt). Meaning "to undergo modification so as to fit new circumstances" (intransitive) is from 1956. Related: Adapting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (implied in adapted) "to fit (something, for some purpose)," 源自 中古法语 adapter (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 adaptare "adjust," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + aptare "to join," 源自 aptus "fitted" （参见 apt). 义为 "to undergo modification so as to fit new circumstances" (intransitive) 始于 1956 年. 同源词：Adapting.

example.en: It took the explorers several weeks to adapt to the thin air at such a high altitude.
example.zh: 探险队员花了好几周才适应如此高海拔处稀薄的空气。

definitionLines: vt. 加，加上；增加，增进；进一 步说/写
entries.definition: vt. 加，加上；增加，增进；进一 步说/写 vi. （to）增添
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to join or unite (something to something else)," from Latin addere "add to, join, attach, place upon," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + -dere comb. form meaning "to put, place," from dare "to give" (see date (n.1)). Meaning "to do sums, do addition" also is from late 14c. Related: Added; adding. To add up "make sense" is from 1942.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to join or unite (something to something else)," 源自 拉丁语 addere "add to, join, attach, place upon," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + -dere comb. form 意为 "to put, place," 源自 dare "to give" （参见 date (n.1)). 义为 "to do sums, do addition" also 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Added; adding. To add up "make sense" 始于 1942 年.

example.en: The chef decided to add more garlic to enhance the flavor of the soup.
example.zh: 厨师决定多加一些大蒜来增强汤的风味。

definitionLines: a. 沉溺于某种（尤其是不良的） 嗜好的；入了迷的，上了瘾的
entries.definition: a. 沉溺于某种（尤其是不良的） 嗜好的；入了迷的，上了瘾的
entries.etymology: 1530s, "delivered over" by judicial sentence; past participle adjective from addict (v.). Modern sense of "dependent" is short for self-addicted "to give over or award (oneself) to someone or some practice" (1560s; exact phrase from c. 1600); specialization to narcotics dependency is from c. 1910.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "delivered over" by judicial sentence; past participle 形容词 源自 addict （动）. 现代 语义 "dependent" is short for self-addicted "to give over or award (oneself) to someone or some practice" (1560 年代; exact phrase 源自 约 1600 年); specialization to narcotics dependency 始于 约 1910 年.

definitionLines: n. 加，加法；附加部分，增加 （物）
entries.definition: n. 加，加法；附加部分，增加 （物）
entries.etymology: late 14c., "action of adding numbers;" c. 1400, "that which is added," from Old French adition "increase, augmentation" (13c.), from Latin additionem (nominative additio) "an adding to, addition," noun of action from past participle stem of addere (see add). Phrase in addition to "also" is from 1680s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "action of adding numbers;" 约 1400 年, "that which is added," 源自 古法语 adition "increase, augmentation" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 additionem (主格 additio) "an adding to, addition," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of addere （参见 add). Phrase in addition to "also" 始于 1680 年代.

example.en: The new wing is a welcome addition to the museum.
example.zh: 新侧翼是博物馆受欢迎的新增部分。

entries.definition: n. 地址，通讯处 vt./n.致词，讲话 vt.致函；写地址
entries.etymology: early 14c., "to guide or direct," from Old French adrecier "go straight toward; straighten, set right; point, direct" (13c.), from Vulgar Latin *addirectiare "make straight," from Latin ad "to" (see ad-) + *directiare, from Latin directus "straight, direct" (see direct (v.)). Late 14c. as "to set in order, repair, correct." Meaning "to write as a destination on a written message" is from mid-15c. Meaning "to direct spoken words (to someone)" is from late 15c. Related: Addressed; addressing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to guide or direct," 源自 古法语 adrecier "go straight toward; straighten, set right; point, direct" (13 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *addirectiare "make straight," 源自 拉丁语 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + *directiare, 源自 拉丁语 directus "straight, direct" （参见 direct （动）). Late 14 世纪 as "to set in order, repair, correct." 义为 "to write as a destination on a written message" 始于 15 世纪中期 义为 "to direct spoken words (to someone)" 始于 15 世纪晚期 同源词：Addressed; addressing.

example.en: The mayor delivered a formal address at the opening ceremony.
example.zh: 市长在开幕式上发表了一篇正式演讲。

entries.etymology: 1610s, from Latin adaequatus "equalized," past participle of adaequare "to make equal to," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + aequare "make level," from aequus (see equal (adj.)). The sense is of being "equal to what is required." Related: Adequateness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 拉丁语 adaequatus "equalized," 为 … 的过去分词 adaequare "to make equal to," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + aequare "make level," 源自 aequus （参见 equal （形）). The sense is of being "equal to what is required." 同源词：Adequateness.

example.en: The resources available were barely adequate for the project.
example.zh: 现有资源对这个项目来说勉强够用。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Middle French adhérer (15c.) or directly from Latin adhaerare "to stick to" (see adherent (adj.)). Originally often of persons, "to cleave to a leader, cause, party, etc." (compare adherent (n.), which still often retains this sense). Related: Adhered; adhering.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 adhérer (15 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 adhaerare "to stick to" （参见 adherent （形）). Originally 常 of persons, "to cleave to a leader, cause, party, etc." (对比 adherent （名）, which still 常 retains this sense). 同源词：Adhered; adhering.

example.en: Scientists must adhere to strict ethical guidelines in their research.
example.zh: 科学家在研究中必须严格遵守道德准则。

entries.etymology: late 14c., as an adjective, "adjectival," in noun adjective, from Old French adjectif (14c.), from Latin adjectivum "that is added to (the noun)," neuter of adjectivus "added," from past participle of adicere "to throw or place (a thing) near," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + comb. form of iacere "to throw" (see jet (v.)). Also as a noun from late 14c. In 19c. Britain, the word itself often was a euphemism for the taboo adjective bloody.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 作形容词时, "adjectival," in 名词 形容词, 源自 古法语 adjectif (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 adjectivum "that is added to (the noun)," neuter of adjectivus "added," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 adicere "to throw or place (a thing) near," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + comb. form of iacere "to throw" （参见 jet （动）). Also 作名词时 源自 14 世纪晚期 In 19 世纪 Britain, the word itself 常 was a euphemism for the taboo 形容词 bloody.

entries.definition: v 调整，调节；校准 vi. （to）适应于
entries.etymology:
late 14c., ajusten, "to correct, remedy;" reborrowed by c. 1600 in sense "arrange, settle, compose," from Middle French adjuster, Old French ajouter "to join" (12c.), from Late Latin adiuxtare "to bring near," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + iuxta "next," related to iungere "to join" (see jugular).

Influenced by folk etymology derivation from Latin iustus "just, equitable, fair." Meaning "to arrange (something) so as to conform with (a standard or another thing)" is from 1660s. Insurance sense is from 1755. Meaning "to get used to" first recorded 1924. Related: Adjusted; adjusting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, ajusten, "to correct, remedy;" reborrowed by 约 1600 年 in sense "arrange, settle, compose," 源自 中古法语 adjuster, 古法语 ajouter "to join" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 adiuxtare "to bring near," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + iuxta "next," related to iungere "to join" （参见 jugular). Influenced by folk etymology derivation 源自 拉丁语 iustus "just, equitable, fair." 义为 "to arrange (something) so as to conform with (a standard or another thing)" 始于 1660 年代. Insurance sense 始于 1755 年. 义为 "to get used to" 首见于 1924 年. 同源词：Adjusted; adjusting.

example.en: You can adjust the brightness of the screen by sliding this small bar.
example.zh: 你可以通过滑动这个小滑块来调节屏幕的亮度。

definitionLines: vi. 给予帮助；担当管理人
entries.definition: vt. 管理；执行；给予 vi. 给予帮助；担当管理人
entries.etymology: late 14c., administren, aministren "to manage as a steward," from Old French amenistrer "help, aid, be of service to" (12c., Modern French administrer, the -d- restored 16c.), and directly from Latin administrare "to help, assist; manage, control, guide, superintend; rule, direct," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + ministrare "serve" (see minister (v.)). Used of medicine, etc., "to give," from 1540s. Related: Administered; administering.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, administren, aministren "to manage as a steward," 源自 古法语 amenistrer "help, aid, be of service to" (12 世纪, 现代法语 administrer, the -d- restored 16 世纪), and 直接源自 拉丁语 administrare "to help, assist; manage, control, guide, superintend; rule, direct," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + ministrare "serve" （参见 minister （动）). Used of medicine, etc., "to give," 源自 1540 年代. 同源词：Administered; administering.

example.en: She was hired to administer the overseas branch of the company.
example.zh: 她被聘来管理公司的海外分部。

definitionLines: n. 管理；行政，行政机关，政府
entries.definition: n. 管理；行政，行政机关，政府
entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "act of giving or dispensing;" late 14c., "management, act of administering," from Latin administrationem (nominative administratio) "aid, help, cooperation; direction, management," noun of action from past participle stem of administrare (see administer).

Early 15c. as "management of a deceased person's estate." Meaning "the government" is attested from 1731 in British usage. Meaning "a U.S. president's period in office" is first recorded 1796 in writings of George Washington.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "act of giving or dispensing;" 14 世纪晚期, "management, act of administering," 源自 拉丁语 administrationem (主格 administratio) "aid, help, cooperation; direction, management," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of administrare （参见 administer). Early 15 世纪 as "management of a deceased person's estate." 义为 "the government" 见于 1731 年 in British usage. 义为 "a U.S. president's period in office" is 首见于 1796 年 in writings of George Washington.

example.en: The city's administration announced new measures to reduce air pollution.
example.zh: 市政府宣布了新的减少空气污染的措施。

entries.etymology: early 15c. (implied in admired), from Middle French admirer (Old French amirer, 14c.), or directly from Latin admirari "to wonder at" (see admiration). Related: Admiring; admiringly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (implied in admired), 源自 中古法语 admirer (古法语 amirer, 14 世纪)，或直接源自 拉丁语 admirari "to wonder at" （参见 admiration). 同源词：Admiring; admiringly.

example.en: Everyone at school seemed to admire her dedication to helping others.
example.zh: 学校里的每个人似乎都钦佩她助人为乐的精神。

definitionLines: n. 承认；进入许可；录用；入 场费
entries.definition: n. 承认；进入许可；录用；入 场费
entries.etymology: early 15c., "acceptance, reception, approval," from Latin admissionem (nominative admissio) "a letting in," noun of action from past participle stem of admittere (see admit). Meaning "an acknowledging" is from 1530s. Sense of "a literal act of letting in" is from 1620s. As short for admission price, by 1792.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "acceptance, reception, approval," 源自 拉丁语 admissionem (主格 admissio) "a letting in," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of admittere （参见 admit). 义为 "an acknowledging" 始于 1530 年代. 义为 "a literal act of letting in" 始于 1620 年代. As short for admission price, 截至 1792 年.

example.en: His admission to the university was confirmed in the acceptance letter.
example.zh: 大学寄来的录取通知书确认了他的入学资格。

definitionLines: vt. 允许进入；接纳；承认
entries.definition: vt. 允许进入；接纳；承认
entries.etymology: late 14c., "let in," from Latin admittere "to allow to enter, let in, let come, give access," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + mittere "let go, send" (see mission). Sense of "to concede as valid or true" is first recorded early 15c. Related: Admitted; Admitting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "let in," 源自 拉丁语 admittere "to allow to enter, let in, let come, give access," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + mittere "let go, send" （参见 mission). 义为 "to concede as valid or true" is 首见于 15 世纪初 同源词：Admitted; Admitting.

example.en: He finally admitted to stealing the money after hours of questioning.
example.zh: 经过数小时的审问，他终于承认偷了钱。

entries.etymology: "age following childhood" (especially the period from the 15th to the 21st year), early 15c., from Middle French adolescence (14c.), from Latin adolescentia "youth," noun of state from adolescentem (see adolescent (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: "age following childhood" (尤指 the period 源自 15th to the 21st year), 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 adolescence (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 adolescentia "youth," 名词 of state 源自 adolescentem （参见 adolescent （名）).

definitionLines: vt. 收养；采用，采纳；通过
entries.definition: vt. 收养；采用，采纳；通过
entries.etymology: c. 1500, a back-formation from adoption or else from Middle French adopter or directly from Latin adoptare "take by choice, choose for oneself, select, choose" (especially a child). Originally in English also of friends, fathers, citizens, etc. Sense of "to legally take as one's own child" and that of "to embrace, espouse" a practice, method, etc. are from c. 1600. Related: Adopted; adopting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, a back-formation 源自 adoption or else 源自 中古法语 adopter or 直接源自 拉丁语 adoptare "take by choice, choose for oneself, select, choose" (尤指 a child). Originally in English also of friends, fathers, citizens, etc. 义为 "to legally take as one's own child" and that of "to embrace, espouse" a practice, method, etc. 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Adopted; adopting.

example.en: After much debate, the committee voted to adopt the new policy and put it into effect next month.
example.zh: 经过多番讨论，委员会投票通过了这项新政策，并将于下月起实施。

definitionLines: vt. 爱慕；崇拜；喜爱；［口］极 喜欢
entries.definition: vt. 爱慕；崇拜；喜爱；［口］极 喜欢
entries.etymology: late 14c., aouren, "to worship, pay divine honors to, bow down before," from Old French aorer "to adore, worship, praise" (10c.), from Latin adorare "speak to formally, beseech, ask in prayer," in Late Latin "to worship," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + orare "speak formally, pray" (see orator). Meaning "to honor very highly" is attested from 1590s; weakened sense of "to be very fond of" emerged by 1880s. Related: Adored; adoring.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, aouren, "to worship, pay divine honors to, bow down before," 源自 古法语 aorer "to adore, worship, praise" (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 adorare "speak to formally, beseech, ask in prayer," in 晚期拉丁语 "to worship," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + orare "speak formally, pray" （参见 orator). 义为 "to honor very highly" 见于 1590 年代; weakened 语义 "to be very fond of" emerged by 1880 年代. 同源词：Adored; adoring.

entries.definition: n. 成人 a.成年的，成熟的
entries.etymology: 1530s (but not common until mid-17c.), from Latin adultus "grown up, mature, adult, ripe," past participle of adolescere "grow up, mature" (see adolescent). As a euphemism for "pornographic," it dates to 1958 and does no honor to the word.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代 (but not common until 17 世纪中期), 源自 拉丁语 adultus "grown up, mature, adult, ripe," 为 … 的过去分词 adolescere "grow up, mature" （参见 adolescent). 作为 euphemism for "pornographic," it dates to 1958 年 and does no honor to the word.

example.en: The evening course is open exclusively to adult learners over eighteen.
example.zh: 这门夜间课程仅面向十八岁以上的成年学员开放。

definitionLines: vt. 推进，促进；提升，提高
entries.definition: vt. 推进，促进；提升，提高 vi. 前进，进展 n. 前进，进展；预付
entries.etymology:
mid-13c., avauncen, transitive, "improve (something), further the development of," from Old French avancier "move forward" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *abanteare (source of Italian avanzare, Spanish avanzar), from Late Latin abante "from before," composed of ab- "from" (see ab-) + ante "before, in front of, against" (see ante).

The -d- was inserted 16c. on mistaken notion that initial a- was from Latin ad-. From c. 1300 as "to promote;" intransitive sense is mid-14c., "move forward." Meaning "to give money before it is legally due" is first attested 1670s. Related: Advanced; advancing. The adjective (in advance warning, etc.) is recorded from 1843.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, avauncen, transitive, "improve (something), further the development of," 源自 古法语 avancier "move forward" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *abanteare (source of 意大利语 avanzare, 西班牙语 avanzar), 源自 晚期拉丁语 abante "from before," composed of ab- "from" （参见 ab-) + ante "before, in front of, against" （参见 ante). The -d- was inserted 16 世纪 on mistaken notion that initial a- was 源自 拉丁语 ad-. From 约 1300 年 as "to promote;" intransitive sense is 14 世纪中期, "move forward." 义为 "to give money before it is legally due" is 最早见于 1670 年代. 同源词：Advanced; advancing. The 形容词 (in advance warning, etc.) 见于 1843 年.

example.en: New surgical robots continue to advance the field of minimally invasive medicine.
example.zh: 新型手术机器人持续推动微创医学领域的进步。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "far ahead in the course of actions or ideas," past participle adjective from advance (v.). Of studies, from 1790. Military use is from 1795. In late 19c. used especially in reference to views on women's equality.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "far ahead in the course of actions or ideas," past participle 形容词 源自 advance （动）. Of studies, 自 1790 年起. Military use 始于 1795 年. In 19 世纪晚期 used 尤指 in reference to views on women's equality.

example.en: This course is designed for advanced learners with prior experience.
example.zh: 这门课程是为有一定基础的进阶学习者设计的。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, avauncement, "a raising to a higher rank," from Old French avancement "advancement, profit, advance payment," from avancer (see advance (v.)). Of money, from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, avauncement, "a raising to a higher rank," 源自 古法语 avancement "advancement, profit, advance payment," 源自 avancer （参见 advance （动）). Of money, 源自 1640 年代.

definitionLines: n. 优点，有利条件；利益，好处
entries.definition: n. 优点，有利条件；利益，好处
entries.etymology:
early 14c., avantage, "position of being in advance of another," from Old French avantage "advantage, profit, superiority," from avant "before," probably via an unrecorded Late Latin *abantaticum, from Latin abante (see advance).

The -d- is a 16c. intrusion on the analogy of Latin ad- words. Meaning "a favoring circumstance" (the opposite of disadvantage) is from late 15c. Tennis score sense is from 1640s, first recorded in writings of John Milton, of all people. Phrase to take advantage of is first attested late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, avantage, "position of being in advance of another," 源自 古法语 avantage "advantage, profit, superiority," 源自 avant "before," 可能 经由 an unrecorded 晚期拉丁语 *abantaticum, 源自 拉丁语 abante （参见 advance). The -d- is a 16 世纪 intrusion on the analogy of 拉丁语 ad- words. 义为 "a favoring circumstance" (the opposite of disadvantage) 始于 15 世纪晚期 Tennis score sense 始于 1640 年代, 首见于 in writings of John Milton, of all people. Phrase to take advantage of is 最早见于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: Fluency in Mandarin gives job applicants a clear advantage over rivals in Asia.

definitionLines: n. 冒险，惊险活动；奇遇
entries.definition: n. 冒险，惊险活动；奇遇
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, auenture "that which happens by chance, fortune, luck," from Old French aventure (11c.) "chance, accident, occurrence, event, happening," from Latin adventura (res) "(a thing) about to happen," from adventurus, future participle of advenire "to come to, reach, arrive at," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + venire "to come" (see venue).

Meaning developed through "risk/danger" (a trial of one's chances), c. 1300, and "perilous undertaking" (late 14c.) and thence to "a novel or exciting incident" (1560s). Earlier it also meant "a wonder, a miracle; accounts of marvelous things" (13c.). The -d- was restored 15c.-16c. Venture is a 15c. variant.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, auenture "that which happens by chance, fortune, luck," 源自 古法语 aventure (11 世纪) "chance, accident, occurrence, event, happening," 源自 拉丁语 adventura (res) "(a thing) about to happen," 源自 adventurus, future participle of advenire "to come to, reach, arrive at," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + venire "to come" （参见 venue). 义为 developed through "risk/danger" (a trial of one's chances), 约 1300 年, and "perilous undertaking" (14 世纪晚期) and thence to "a novel or exciting incident" (1560 年代). Earlier it also meant "a wonder, a miracle; accounts of marvelous things" (13 世纪). The -d- was restored 15 世纪-16 世纪 Venture is a 15 世纪 variant.

example.en: The documentary followed their adventure across the Sahara Desert.
example.zh: 这部纪录片跟踪记录了他们穿越撒哈拉沙漠的冒险历程。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Late Latin adverbium "adverb," literally "that which is added to a verb," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + verbum "verb, word" (see verb). Coined by Flavius Sosipater Charisius as a translation of Greek epirrhema "adverb," from epi- "upon, on" + rhema "verb."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 晚期拉丁语 adverbium "adverb," 字面义为 "that which is added to a verb," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + verbum "verb, word" （参见 动词). Coined by Flavius Sosipater Charisius 作为 translation of 希腊语 epirrhema "adverb," 源自 epi- "upon, on" + rhema "verb."

definitionLines: a. 不利的；相反的；敌对的
entries.definition: a. 不利的；相反的；敌对的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "contrary, opposing," from Old French avers (13c., Modern French adverse) "antagonistic, unfriendly, contrary, foreign" (as in gent avers "infidel race"), from Latin adversus "turned against, turned toward, fronting, facing," figuratively "hostile, adverse, unfavorable," past participle of advertere, from ad- "to" (see ad-) + vertere "to turn" (see versus). For distinction of use, see see averse. Related: Adversely.

entries.etymology:
early 15c., "to take notice of," from Middle French advertiss-, present participle stem of a(d)vertir "to warn" (12c.), from Latin advertere "turn toward," from ad- "toward" (see ad-) + vertere "to turn" (see versus).

Sense shifted to "to give notice to others, warn" (late 15c.) by influence of advertisement; specific meaning "to call attention to goods for sale, rewards, etc." had emerged by late 18c. Original meaning remains in the verb advert "to give attention to." Related: Advertised; advertising.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to take notice of," 源自 中古法语 advertiss-, present participle stem of a(d)vertir "to warn" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 advertere "turn toward," 源自 ad- "toward" （参见 ad-) + vertere "to turn" （参见 versus). Sense shifted to "to give notice to others, warn" (15 世纪晚期) by influence of advertisement; specific 意为 "to call attention to goods for sale, rewards, etc." had emerged by 18 世纪晚期 Original 意为 remains in the 动词 advert "to give attention to." 同源词：Advertised; advertising.

example.en: The company spent millions to advertise its new product on social media.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "written statement calling attention to" something, "public notice" (of anything, but often of a sale); from Middle French avertissement, from stem of avertir (see advertise). Meaning "public notice" (usually paid), the main modern sense, emerged 1580s and was fully developed by 18c.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "written statement calling attention to" something, "public notice" (of anything, but 常 of a sale); 源自 中古法语 avertissement, 源自 stem of avertir （参见 advertise). 义为 "public notice" (通常 paid), the main modern sense, emerged 1580 年代 and was fully developed by 18 世纪

entries.etymology:
late 13c., auys "opinion," from Old French avis "opinion, view, judgment, idea" (13c.), from phrase ço m'est à vis "it seems to me," or from Vulgar Latin *mi est visum "in my view," ultimately from Latin visum, neuter past participle of videre "to see" (see vision).

The unhistorical -d- was introduced in English 15c., on model of Latin words in ad-. Substitution of -c- for -s- is 18c., to preserve the breath sound and to distinguish from advise. Meaning "opinion given as to action, counsel" is from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, auys "opinion," 源自 古法语 avis "opinion, view, judgment, idea" (13 世纪), 源自 phrase ço m'est à vis "it seems to me," or 源自 通俗拉丁语 *mi est visum "in my view," 最终源自 拉丁语 visum, neuter 为 … 的过去分词 videre "to see" （参见 vision). The unhistorical -d- was introduced in English 15 世纪, on model of 拉丁语 words in ad-. Substitution of -c- for -s- is 18 世纪, to preserve the breath sound and to distinguish 源自 advise. 义为 "opinion given as to action, counsel" 始于 14 世纪晚期

entries.etymology: late 13c., avisen "to view, consider," from Old French aviser "deliberate, reflect, consider" (13c.), from avis "opinion" (see advice). Meaning "to give counsel to" is late 14c. Related: Advised; advising.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, avisen "to view, consider," 源自 古法语 aviser "deliberate, reflect, consider" (13 世纪), 源自 avis "opinion" （参见 advice). 义为 "to give counsel to" is 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Advised; advising.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "one whose profession is to plead cases in a court of justice," a technical term from Roman law, from Old French avocat "barrister, advocate, spokesman," from Latin advocatus "one called to aid; a pleader, advocate," noun use of past participle of advocare "to call" (as witness or advisor) from ad- "to" (see ad-) + vocare "to call," related to vocem (see voice (n.)). definitionLines: a. 美的；美学的；审美的
entries.definition: a. 美的；美学的；审美的
entries.etymology:
1798, from German Ästhetisch or French esthétique, both from Greek aisthetikos "sensitive, perceptive," from aisthanesthai "to perceive (by the senses or by the mind), to feel," from PIE *awis-dh-yo-, from root *au- "to perceive" (see audience).
Popularized in English by translations of works of Immanuel Kant and used originally in the classically correct sense "the science which treats of the conditions of sensuous perception." Kant had tried to correct the term after Alexander Baumgarten had taken it in German to mean "criticism of taste" (1750s), but Baumgarten's sense attained popularity in English c. 1830s (despite scholarly resistance) and removed the word from any philosophical base. Walter Pater used it (1868) to describe the late 19c. movement that advocated "art for art's sake," which further blurred the sense. As an adjective by 1803. Related: Aesthetically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1798 年, 源自 德语 Ästhetisch or 法语 esthétique, both 源自 希腊语 aisthetikos "sensitive, perceptive," 源自 aisthanesthai "to perceive (by the senses or by the mind), to feel," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *awis-dh-yo-, 源自 root *au- "to perceive" （参见 audience). Popularized in English by translations of works of Immanuel Kant and used 原义为 in the classically correct sense "the science which treats of the conditions of sensuous perception." Kant had tried to correct the term after Alexander Baumgarten had taken it in 德语 to mean "criticism of taste" (1750 年代), but Baumgarten's sense attained popularity in English c. 1830s (despite scholarly resistance) and removed the word from any philosophical base. Walter Pater used it (1868) to describe the late 19c. movement that advocated "art for art's sake," which further blurred the sense. 作形容词时 截至 1803 年. 同源词：Aesthetically.

example.en: The museum's new gallery has a clean, minimalist aesthetic that visitors admire.
example.zh: 博物馆新画廊拥有简洁的极简主义美感，令参观者赞叹。

entries.etymology: 1803, from aesthetic (also see -ics).
entries.etymologyZh: 1803 年, 源自 aesthetic (also 参见 -ics).

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "what one has to do," from Anglo-French afere, Old French afaire  "business, event; rank, estate" (12c., Modern French affaire), from the infinitive phrase à faire "to do," from Latin ad "to" (see ad-) + facere "to do, make" (see factitious).

A Northern word originally, brought into general use and given a French spelling by Caxton (15c.). General sense of "vague proceedings" (in romance, war, etc.) first attested 1702. Meaning "an affair of the heart; a passionate episode" is from French affaire de coeur (itself attested in English from 1809); to have an affair with someone in this sense is by 1726, earlier have an affair of love:
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "what one has to do," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 afere, 古法语 afaire "business, event; rank, estate" (12 世纪, 现代法语 affaire), 源自 infinitive phrase à faire "to do," 源自 拉丁语 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + facere "to do, make" （参见 factitious). A Northern word 原义为, brought into general use and given a 法语 spelling by Caxton (15 世纪). General 语义 "vague proceedings" (in romance, war, etc.) 最早见于 1702 年. 义为 "an affair of the heart; a passionate episode" 始于 法语 affaire de coeur (itself 见于 English 自 1809 年起); to have an affair with someone in this sense is 截至 1726 年, earlier have an affair of love:

example.en: The minister refused to discuss his personal affair with the press.
example.zh: 这位部长拒绝与媒体讨论他的私事。

definitionLines: vt. 影响，作用；感动；（疾病） 侵袭
entries.definition: vt. 影响，作用；感动；（疾病） 侵袭
entries.etymology: late 14c., "mental state," from Latin noun use of affectus "furnished, supplied, endowed," figuratively "disposed, constituted, inclined," past participle of afficere "to do; treat, use, manage, handle; act on; have influence on, do something to," a verb of broad meaning, from ad- "to" (see ad-) + facere (past participle factus) "to make, do" (see factitious). Perhaps obsolete except in psychology. Related: Affects.
