entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "mental state," 源自 拉丁语 为 … 的名词用法 affectus "furnished, supplied, endowed," figuratively "disposed, constituted, inclined," 为 … 的过去分词 afficere "to do; treat, use, manage, handle; act on; have influence on, do something to," a 动词 of broad 意为, 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + facere (past participle factus) "to make, do" （参见 factitious). Perhaps 已废 except in psychology. 同源词：Affects.

example.en: Lack of sleep can severely affect your ability to concentrate on work.
example.zh: 睡眠不足会严重影响你集中注意力工作的能力。

entries.etymology: early 13c., "an emotion of the mind, passion, lust as opposed to reason," from Old French afection (12c.) "emotion, inclination, disposition; love, attraction, enthusiasm," from Latin affectionem (nominative affectio) "a relation, disposition; a temporary state; a frame, constitution," noun of state from past participle stem of afficere "to do something to, act on" (see affect (n.)). Sense developed from "disposition" to "good disposition toward" (late 14c.). Related: Affections.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "an emotion of the mind, passion, lust as opposed to reason," 源自 古法语 afection (12 世纪) "emotion, inclination, disposition; love, attraction, enthusiasm," 源自 拉丁语 affectionem (主格 affectio) "a relation, disposition; a temporary state; a frame, constitution," 名词 of state 源自 past participle stem of afficere "to do something to, act on" （参见 affect （名）). Sense developed 源自 "disposition" to "good disposition toward" (14 世纪晚期). 同源词：Affections.

example.en: The child grew up feeling her parents' deep affection and never doubted their love.
example.zh: 孩子在感受到父母深深的爱意中成长，从未怀疑过他们的爱。

entries.etymology: 1761, from Latin affiliatus, past participle of affiliare "to adopt" (see affiliation). Outside legal use, always figurative. Related: Affiliated; affiliating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1761 年, 源自 拉丁语 affiliatus, 为 … 的过去分词 affiliare "to adopt" （参见 affiliation). Outside legal use, always figurative. 同源词：Affiliated; affiliating.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French afermier (Modern French affirmer) "affirm, confirm; strengthen, consolidate," from Latin affirmare "to make steady, strengthen," figuratively "confirm, corroborate," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + firmare "strengthen, make firm," from firmus "strong" (see firm (adj.)). Spelling refashioned 16c. in French and English on Latin model. Related: Affirmed; affirming.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 afermier (现代法语 affirmer) "affirm, confirm; strengthen, consolidate," 源自 拉丁语 affirmare "to make steady, strengthen," figuratively "confirm, corroborate," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + firmare "strengthen, make firm," 源自 firmus "strong" （参见 firm （形）). Spelling refashioned 16 世纪 in 法语 and English on 拉丁语 model. 同源词：Affirmed; affirming.

entries.etymology:
1530s, from Medieval Latin affixare, frequentative of Latin affigere (past participle affixus) "fasten to, attach," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + figere "fasten" (see fix (v.)).

First used by Scottish writers and perhaps from Middle French affixer, a temporarily re-Latinized spelling of Old French afichier (Modern French afficher). Related: Affixed; affixing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 affixare, 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 affigere (past participle affixus) "fasten to, attach," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + figere "fasten" （参见 fix （动）). First used by 苏格兰语 writers and 或源自 中古法语 affixer, a temporarily re-Latinized spelling of 古法语 afichier (现代法语 afficher). 同源词：Affixed; affixing.

definitionLines: vt. 提供，给予；供应得起
entries.definition: vt. 提供，给予；供应得起
entries.etymology:
Middle English aforthen, from Old English geforðian "to put forth, contribute; further, advance; carry out, accomplish," from ge- completive prefix (see a- (1)) + forðian "to further," from forð "forward, onward" (see forth).

Change of -th- to -d- took place late 16c. (and also transformed burthen and murther into their modern forms). Prefix shift to af- took place 16c. under mistaken belief that it was a Latin word in ad-. Notion of "accomplish" (late Old English) gradually became "be able to bear the expense of, have enough money" to do something (late 14c.). Older sense is preserved in afford (one) an opportunity. Related: Afforded; affording.
entries.etymologyZh: 中古英语 aforthen, 源自 古英语 geforðian "to put forth, contribute; further, advance; carry out, accomplish," 源自 ge- completive prefix （参见 a- (1)) + forðian "to further," 源自 forð "forward, onward" （参见 forth). Change of -th- to -d- took place 16 世纪晚期 (and also transformed burthen and murther into their modern forms). Prefix shift to af- took place 16 世纪 under mistaken belief that it was a 拉丁语 word in ad-. Notion of "accomplish" (late 古英语) gradually became "be able to bear the expense of, have enough money" to do something (14 世纪晚期). Older sense is preserved in afford (one) an opportunity. 同源词：Afforded; affording.

example.en: Not everyone can afford to buy a house in the city center.
example.zh: 不是每个人都能负担得起在市中心买房。

entries.etymology: 1866, from afford + -able. Related: Affordably; affordability.
entries.etymologyZh: 1866 年, 源自 afford + -able. 同源词：Affordably; affordability.

example.en: The new housing project aims to provide affordable homes for young families.
example.zh: 这一新住房项目旨在为年轻家庭提供负担得起的住所。

definitionLines: a. 怕的，害怕的；惊恐的，担 心的
entries.definition: a. 怕的，害怕的；惊恐的，担 心的
entries.etymology: early 14c., originally past participle of verb afray "frighten," from Anglo-French afrayer, Old French esfreer "to worry, concern, trouble, disturb" (see affray (n.)). A rare case of an English adjective that never stands before a noun. Because it was used in A.V. Bible, it acquired independent standing and thrived while affray faded, and it chased off the once more common afeared. Sense in I'm afraid "I regret to say, I suspect" (without implication of fear) is first recorded 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 原义为 为 … 的过去分词 动词 afray "frighten," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 afrayer, 古法语 esfreer "to worry, concern, trouble, disturb" （参见 affray （名）). A rare case of an English 形容词 that never stands before a 名词. Because it was used in A.V. Bible, it acquired independent standing and thrived while affray faded, and it chased off the once more common afeared. Sense in I'm afraid "I regret to say, I suspect" (without implication of fear) is 首见于 1590 年代.

example.en: "I'm afraid we've sold out of tickets," the clerk said politely to the disappointed customer.
example.zh: "很抱歉，我们的票已经售完了，"售票员礼貌地对失望的顾客说。

entries.etymology: Latin Africa (terra) "African land, Libya, the Carthaginian territory," fem. of adjective Africus, from Afer "an African," a word of uncertain origin. The Latin word originally was used only in reference to the region around modern Tunisia; it gradually was extended to the whole continent. Derivation from Arabic afar "dust, earth" is tempting, but the early date seems to argue against it. The Middle English word was Affrike.
entries.etymologyZh: 拉丁语 Africa (terra) "African land, Libya, the Carthaginian territory," fem. of 形容词 Africus, 源自 Afer "an African," a word 来源存疑. The 拉丁语 word 原义为 was used only in reference to the region around modern Tunisia; it gradually was extended to the whole continent. Derivation 源自 阿拉伯语 afar "dust, earth" is tempting, but the early date seems to argue against it. The 中古英语 word was Affrike.

entries.etymology: Old English Africanas (plural), from Latin Africanus (adj.), from Africa (see Africa). Used of white residents of Africa from 1815. Used of black residents of the U.S. from late 18c., when it especially meant "one brought from Africa" and sometimes was contrasted to native-born Negro. As an adjective by 1560s, "pertaining to Africa or Africans" (Old English had Africanisc); from 1789 as "of or pertaining to black Americans."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 Africanas (plural), 源自 拉丁语 Africanus （形）, 源自 Africa （参见 Africa). Used of white residents of Africa 自 1815 年起. Used of black residents of the U.S. 源自 18 世纪晚期, when it 尤指 meant "one brought from Africa" and 有时 was contrasted to 本族-born Negro. 作形容词时 by 1560 年代, "pertaining to Africa or Africans" (古英语 had Africanisc); 自 1789 年起 as "of or pertaining to black Americans."

entries.definition: prep./conj. 在……之后 ad. 以后，后来
entries.etymology:
Old English æfter "after, next, throughout, following in time, later," from Old English of "off" (see of) + -ter, a comparative suffix; thus the original meaning was "more away, farther off." Compare Old Norse eptir "after," Old High German aftar, Gothic aftra "behind." Cognate with Greek apotero "farther off."

After hours "after regular working hours" is from 1861. Afterwit "wisdom that comes too late" is attested from c. 1500 but seems to have fallen from use, despite being more needed now than ever. After you as an expression in yielding precedence is recorded by 1650.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 æfter "after, next, throughout, following in time, later," 源自 古英语 of "off" （参见 of) + -ter, a comparative suffix; thus the original 意为 was "more away, farther off." 对比 古北欧语 eptir "after," 古高地德语 aftar, Gothic aftra "behind." Cognate with 希腊语 apotero "farther off." After hours "after regular working hours" 始于 1861 年. Afterwit "wisdom that comes too late" 见于 约 1500 年 but seems to have fallen 源自 use, despite being more needed 现在 than ever. After you 作为 expression in yielding precedence is recorded 截至 1650 年.

entries.definition: n. 下午，午后 afterward（s） ad. 以后，后来
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from after + noon. In 15c.-16c., the form was at afternoon; from c. 1600 it has been in the afternoon. Middle English also had aftermete "afternoon, part of the day following the noon meal," mid-14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 after + noon. In 15 世纪-16 世纪, the form was at afternoon; 源自 约 1600 年 it has been in the afternoon. 中古英语 also had aftermete "afternoon, part of the day following the noon meal," 14 世纪中期

entries.etymology:
late Old English agan, from earlier ongean "toward, opposite, against, in exchange for," from on "on" (see on) + -gegn "against, toward," compounded for a sense of "lined up facing, opposite," and "in the opposite direction, returning." For -gegn, compare Old Norse gegn "straight, direct;" Danish igen "against;" Old Frisian jen, Old High German gegin, German gegen "against, toward," entgegen "against, in opposition to."

In Old English, eft was the main word for "again" (see eftsoons), but this often was strengthened by ongean, which became the principal word by 13c. Norse influence is responsible for the hard -g-. Differentiated from against 16c. in southern writers, again becoming an adverb only, and against taking over as preposition and conjunction, but again clung to all senses in northern and Scottish dialect (where against was not adopted).
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 agan, 源自 earlier ongean "toward, opposite, against, in exchange for," 源自 on "on" （参见 on) + -gegn "against, toward," compounded for a 语义 "lined up facing, opposite," and "in the opposite direction, returning." For -gegn, 对比 古北欧语 gegn "straight, direct;" Danish igen "against;" 古弗里西语 jen, 古高地德语 gegin, 德语 gegen "against, toward," entgegen "against, in opposition to." In 古英语, eft was the main word for "again" （参见 eftsoons), but this 常 was strengthened by ongean, which became the principal word by 13 世纪 Norse influence is responsible for the hard -g-. Differentiated 源自 against 16 世纪 in southern writers, again becoming an 副词 only, and against taking over as preposition and conjunction, but again clung to all senses in northern and 苏格兰语 dialect (where against was not adopted).

example.en: She missed the bus and had to call her friend again.
example.zh: 她错过了公交车，不得不再次给朋友打电话。

definitionLines: prep. 对（着），逆；反对，违反； 靠，靠近；和……对比
entries.definition: prep. 对（着），逆；反对，违反； 靠，靠近；和……对比
entries.etymology: early 12c., agenes "in opposition to," a southern variant of agen "again" (see again), with adverbial genitive. The parasitic -t turned up mid-14c. and was standard by early 16c., perhaps from influence of superlatives.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, agenes "in opposition to," a southern 为 … 的变体 agen "again" （参见 again), with adverbial 属格. The parasitic -t turned up 14 世纪中期 and was standard by 16 世纪初, 或源自 influence of superlatives.

entries.definition: n. 年龄；时代 vi. 变老
entries.etymology: late 13c., "long but indefinite period in human history," from Old French aage (11c., Modern French âge) "age; life, lifetime, lifespan; maturity," earlier edage, from Vulgar Latin *aetaticum (source of Spanish edad, Italian eta, Portuguese idade "age"), from Latin aetatem (nominative aetas), "period of life, age, lifetime, years," from aevum "lifetime, eternity, age," from PIE root *aiw- "vital force, life, long life, eternity" (see eon). Meaning "time something has lived, particular length or stage of life" is from early 14c. Used especially for "old age" since early 14c. Expelled native eld.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "long but indefinite period in human history," 源自 古法语 aage (11 世纪, 现代法语 âge) "age; life, lifetime, lifespan; maturity," earlier edage, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *aetaticum (source of 西班牙语 edad, 意大利语 eta, 葡萄牙语 idade "age"), 源自 拉丁语 aetatem (主格 aetas), "period of life, age, lifetime, years," 源自 aevum "lifetime, eternity, age," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *aiw- "vital force, life, long life, eternity" （参见 eon). 义为 "time something has lived, particular length or stage of life" 始于 14 世纪初 Used 尤指 for "old age" 自 14 世纪初 Expelled 本族 eld.

example.en: Children under the age of twelve get in for free at this museum.
example.zh: 在这家博物馆，十二岁以下的儿童免费入场。

entries.etymology: 1650s, "active operation," from Medieval Latin agentia, noun of state from Latin agentem (nominative agens) "effective, powerful," present participle of agere "to drive, conduct" (see act (n.)). Meaning "establishment where business is done for another" first recorded 1861.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "active operation," 源自 中古拉丁语 agentia, 名词 of state 源自 拉丁语 agentem (主格 agens) "effective, powerful," 为 … 的现在分词 agere "to drive, conduct" （参见 act （名）). 义为 "establishment where business is done for another" 首见于 1861 年.

example.en: They hired a travel agency to book all flights and hotels for the trip.
example.zh: 他们聘请了一家旅行社来预订旅途中所有的机票和酒店。

entries.etymology: 1650s, from Latin agenda, literally "things to be done," neuter plural of agendus, gerundive of agere "to do" (see act (n.)). Originally theological (opposed to matters of belief), sense of "items of business to be done at a meeting" first attested 1882. "If a singular is required (=one item of the agenda) it is now agendum, the former singular agend being obsolete" [Fowler].
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, 源自 拉丁语 agenda, 字面义为 "things to be done," neuter 为 … 的复数 agendus, gerundive of agere "to do" （参见 act （名）). Originally theological (opposed to matters of belief), 语义 "items of business to be done at a meeting" 最早见于 1882 年. "If a singular is required (=one item of the agenda) it is now agendum, the former singular agend being obsolete" [Fowler].

example.en: The first item on the meeting agenda was the budget report.
example.zh: 会议议程上的第一项是预算报告。

entries.etymology: late 15c., "one who acts," from Latin agentem (nominative agens) "effective, powerful," present participle of agere "to set in motion, drive, lead, conduct" (see act (n.)). Meaning "any natural force or substance which produces a phenomenon" is from 1550s. Meaning "deputy, representative" is from 1590s. Sense of "spy, secret agent" is attested by 1916.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "one who acts," 源自 拉丁语 agentem (主格 agens) "effective, powerful," 为 … 的现在分词 agere "to set in motion, drive, lead, conduct" （参见 act （名）). 义为 "any natural force or substance which produces a phenomenon" 始于 1550 年代. 义为 "deputy, representative" 始于 1590 年代. 义为 "spy, secret agent" is attested 截至 1916 年.

example.en: The company hired a local agent to handle all sales negotiations.
example.zh: 公司聘请了一位当地代理人处理所有销售谈判。

entries.etymology:
1520s, "make heavy, burden down," from past participle adjective aggravate "burdened; threatened" (late 15c.), from Latin aggravatus, past participle of aggravare "to render more troublesome," literally "to make heavy" (see aggravation). Earlier in this sense was aggrege (late 14c.). Meaning "to make a bad thing worse" is from 1590s; that of "exasperate, annoy" is from 1610s.

Related: Aggravated; aggravating. Phrase aggravating circumstances is recorded from 1790.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "make heavy, burden down," 源自 past participle 形容词 aggravate "burdened; threatened" (15 世纪晚期), 源自 拉丁语 aggravatus, 为 … 的过去分词 aggravare "to render more troublesome," 字面义为 "to make heavy" （参见 aggravation). Earlier in this sense was aggrege (14 世纪晚期). 义为 "to make a bad thing worse" 始于 1590 年代; that of "exasperate, annoy" 始于 1610 年代. 同源词：Aggravated; aggravating. Phrase aggravating circumstances 见于 1790 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1400, from Latin aggregatus "associated," literally "united in a flock," past participle of aggregare "add to (a flock), lead to a flock, bring together (in a flock)," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + gregare "herd" (see gregarious).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 拉丁语 aggregatus "associated," 字面义为 "united in a flock," 为 … 的过去分词 aggregare "add to (a flock), lead to a flock, bring together (in a flock)," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + gregare "herd" （参见 gregarious).

definitionLines: a. 进攻的；有进取心的
entries.definition: a. 进攻的；有进取心的
entries.etymology: 1791, from Latin aggress-, past participle stem of aggredi "to approach, attack" (see aggression) + -ive. In psychological use from 1913, first in translations of Freud. Related: Aggressively; aggressiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1791 年, 源自 拉丁语 aggress-, past participle stem of aggredi "to approach, attack" （参见 aggression) + -ive. In psychological use 自 1913 年起, first in translations of Freud. 同源词：Aggressively; aggressiveness.

example.en: The prosecutor launched an aggressive cross-examination of the key witness.
example.zh: 检察官对关键证人发起了咄咄逼人的交叉盘问。

entries.etymology: early 14c., shortened form of Old English agan, agone "departed, passed away," past participle of an obsolete verb ago "to go forth," formed from a- "away" (perhaps here used as an intensive prefix) + gan "go" (see go (v.)). Agone remains a dialectal variant.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, shortened form of 古英语 agan, agone "departed, passed away," 为 … 的过去分词 an 已废 动词 ago "to go forth," formed 源自 a- "away" (或许 here used 作为 intensive prefix) + gan "go" （参见 go （动）). Agone remains a 方言 variant.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "mental suffering" (especially that of Christ in the Garden of Gethsemane), from Old French agonie, agoine "anguish, terror, death agony" (14c.), and directly from Late Latin agonia, from Greek agonia "a (mental) struggle for victory," originally "a struggle for victory in the games," from agon "assembly for a contest," from agein "to lead" (see act (n.)). Sense of "extreme bodily suffering" first recorded c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "mental suffering" (尤指 that of Christ in the Garden of Gethsemane), 源自 古法语 agonie, agoine "anguish, terror, death agony" (14 世纪), and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 agonia, 源自 希腊语 agonia "a (mental) struggle for victory," 原义为 "a struggle for victory in the games," 源自 agon "assembly for a contest," 源自 agein "to lead" （参见 act （名）). 义为 "extreme bodily suffering" 首见于 约 1600 年.

definitionLines: vi.（with...on...）同意，赞 同；（to）一致，适合；商定， 约定
entries.definition: vi.（with...on...）同意，赞 同；（to）一致，适合；商定， 约定
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to be to one's liking;" also "to give consent," from Old French agreer "to receive with favor, take pleasure in" (12c.), from phrase a gré "favorably, of good will," literally "to (one's) liking," from Latin ad "to" (see ad-) + gratum "pleasing," neuter of gratus (see grace (n.)); the original sense survives best in agreeable. Meaning "to be in harmony in opinions" is from late 15c. Related: Agreed; agreeing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to be to one's liking;" also "to give consent," 源自 古法语 agreer "to receive with favor, take pleasure in" (12 世纪), 源自 phrase a gré "favorably, of good will," 字面义为 "to (one's) liking," 源自 拉丁语 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + gratum "pleasing," neuter of gratus （参见 grace （名）); the original sense survives best in agreeable. 义为 "to be in harmony in opinions" 始于 15 世纪晚期 同源词：Agreed; agreeing.

example.en: Both sides finally agree to sign the peace agreement.
example.zh: 双方最终同意签署和平协议。

definitionLines: a. 使人愉快的；欣然同意的；适 合的
entries.definition: a. 使人愉快的；欣然同意的；适 合的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to one's liking," from Old French agreable (12c., Modern French agréable) "pleasing, in agreement, consenting, thankful," from agreer "to please" (see agree). Related: Agreeably. To do the agreeable (1825) was to "act in a courteous manner."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to one's liking," 源自 古法语 agreable (12 世纪, 现代法语 agréable) "pleasing, in agreement, consenting, thankful," 源自 agreer "to please" （参见 agree). 同源词：Agreeably. To do the agreeable (1825 年) was to "act in a courteous manner."

definitionLines: n. 同意，一致；协议，协定，契约
entries.definition: n. 同意，一致；协议，协定，契约
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "mutual understanding" (among persons), also (of things) "mutual conformity," from Old French agrement, noun of action from agreer "to please" (see agree).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "mutual understanding" (among persons), also (of things) "mutual conformity," 源自 古法语 agrement, 名词 of action 源自 agreer "to please" （参见 agree).

example.en: Both sides finally reached an agreement after weeks of negotiations.
example.zh: 经过数周谈判，双方终于达成了协议。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Late Latin agricultura "cultivation of the land," compound of agri cultura "cultivation of land," from agri, genitive of ager "a field" (see acre) + cultura "cultivation" (see culture (n.)). In Old English, the idea could be expressed by eorðtilþ.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 晚期拉丁语 agricultura "cultivation of the land," 由 … 复合而成 agri cultura "cultivation of land," 源自 agri, 属格 of ager "a field" （参见 acre) + cultura "cultivation" （参见 culture （名）). In 古英语, the idea could be expressed by eorðtilþ.

example.en: The government invested heavily in agriculture to improve food security in rural areas.
example.zh: 政府大力投资农业，以改善农村地区的粮食安全。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "at the head, in front," from a- "on" (see a- (1)) + head (n.). Originally nautical. To be ahead of (one's) time attested by 1837.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "at the head, in front," 源自 a- "on" （参见 a- (1)) + head （名）. Originally nautical. To be ahead of (one's) time attested 截至 1837 年.

example.en: We need to push ahead with the project despite the budget cuts.
example.zh: 尽管预算削减，我们需要继续推进这个项目。

definitionLines: n. 援助，救护；助手，辅助物
entries.definition: vi. 援助，救援 n. 援助，救护；助手，辅助物
entries.etymology: early 15c., "war-time tax," also "help, support, assistance," from Old French aide, earlier aiudha "aid, help, assistance" (9c.), from Late Latin adjuta, from fem. past participle of Latin adiuvare (past participle adiutus) "to give help to," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + iuvare "to help" (see adjutant). Meaning "thing by which assistance is given" is recorded from c. 1600. Meaning "material help given by one country to another" is from 1940.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "war-time tax," also "help, support, assistance," 源自 古法语 aide, earlier aiudha "aid, help, assistance" (9 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 adjuta, 源自 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 adiuvare (past participle adiutus) "to give help to," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + iuvare "to help" （参见 adjutant). 义为 "thing by which assistance is given" 见于 约 1600 年. 义为 "material help given by one country to another" 始于 1940 年.

example.en: International organizations rushed to aid the earthquake victims with food and shelter.
example.zh: 国际组织迅速向地震受害者提供食物和住所方面的援助。

definitionLines: vi. （at） 志在，旨在；瞄准，针对
entries.definition: vt. 瞄准，把……对准 vi. （at） 志在，旨在；瞄准，针对 n. 目标，目的
entries.etymology: early 14c., "to estimate, calculate," also "to intend," from Old French aesmer "value, rate; count, estimate," from Latin aestimare "appraise" (see estimation); current meaning apparently developed from "esteem," to "calculate," to "calculate with a view to action" (c. 1400), then to "direct a missile, a blow, etc." (1570s). Related: Aimed; aiming.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to estimate, calculate," also "to intend," 源自 古法语 aesmer "value, rate; count, estimate," 源自 拉丁语 aestimare "appraise" （参见 estimation); current 意为 似乎 developed 源自 "esteem," to "calculate," to "calculate with a view to action" (约 1400 年), 之后 to "direct a missile, a blow, etc." (1570 年代). 同源词：Aimed; aiming.

example.en: The company aim to cut carbon emissions by fifty percent within five years.
example.zh: 该公司的目标是在五年内将碳排放量减少50%。

entries.definition: n. 空气，大气；天空 v.晾干；使通气
entries.etymology: "to expose to open air," 1520s, from air (n.1). Figurative sense of "to expose, make public" is from 1610s of objects, 1862 of opinions, grievances, etc. Meaning "to broadcast" (originally on radio) is from 1933. Related: Aired; airing.
entries.etymologyZh: "to expose to open air," 1520 年代, 源自 air (n.1). Figurative 语义 "to expose, make public" 始于 1610 年代 of objects, 1862 年 of opinions, grievances, etc. 义为 "to broadcast" (原义为 on radio) 始于 1933 年. 同源词：Aired; airing.

example.en: After the storm, the air smelled fresh and clean.
example.zh: 暴风雨过后，空气闻起来清新洁净。

entries.etymology: "to expose to open air," 1520s, from air (n.1). Figurative sense of "to expose, make public" is from 1610s of objects, 1862 of opinions, grievances, etc. Meaning "to broadcast" (originally on radio) is from 1933. Related: Aired; airing.
entries.etymologyZh: "to expose to open air," 1520 年代, 源自 air (n.1). Figurative 语义 "to expose, make public" 始于 1610 年代 of objects, 1862 年 of opinions, grievances, etc. 义为 "to broadcast" (原义为 on radio) 始于 1933 年. 同源词：Aired; airing.

entries.etymology: 1851, originally in reference to airships and balloons, from air (n.1) + craft (n.); a term from boating, as were many early aviation words. Of airplanes from 1907 and since 1930s exclusively of them. Aircraft carrier is attested from 1919 (H.M.S. Hermes, launched September 1919, was the first ship to be built from the hull up as an aircraft carrier).
entries.etymologyZh: 1851 年, 原义为 in reference to airships and balloons, 源自 air (n.1) + craft （名）; a term 源自 boating, as were many early aviation words. Of airplanes 自 1907 年起 and 自 1930 年代 exclusively of them. Aircraft carrier 见于 1919 年 (H.M.S. Hermes, launched September 1919 年, was the first ship to be built 源自 hull up 作为 aircraft carrier).

example.en: The military aircraft was spotted flying low over the city.
example.zh: 那架军用飞机被发现在城市上空低飞。

definitionLines: n. 航空公司；（飞机的）航线
entries.definition: n. 航空公司；（飞机的）航线
entries.etymology: also air-line, 1813, "beeline, straight line between two points on the earth's surface" (as through the air, rather than over terrain; from 1853 and in later 19c. especially in reference to railways that ran directly between big cities in the U.S. instead of meandering from town to town in search of stock subscriptions as early railways typically did), from air (n.1) + line (n.). Meaning "public aircraft transportation company" is from 1914.
entries.etymologyZh: also air-line, 1813 年, "beeline, straight line between two points on the earth's surface" (as through the air, rather than over terrain; 自 1853 年起 and in later 19 世纪 尤指 in reference to railways that ran directly between big cities in the U.S. instead of meandering 源自 town to town in search of stock subscriptions as early railways typically did), 源自 air (n.1) + line （名）. 义为 "public aircraft transportation company" 始于 1914 年.

example.en: The airline cancelled dozens of flights due to the storm.
example.zh: 由于暴风雨，这家航空公司取消了数十个航班。

entries.etymology: 1907, from air (n.1) + plane (n.1); though the original references are British, the word caught on in American English, where it largely superseded earlier aeroplane (1873 in this sense and still common in British English). Aircraft "airplane" also is from 1907. Lord Byron, speculatively, used air-vessel (1822).
entries.etymologyZh: 1907 年, 源自 air (n.1) + plane (n.1); though the original references are British, the word caught on in American English, where it largely superseded earlier aeroplane (1873 年 in this sense and still common in British English). Aircraft "airplane" also 始于 1907 年. Lord Byron, speculatively, used air-vessel (1822 年).

entries.etymology: 1919, from air (n.1) + port (n.1). First reference is to Bader Field, outside Atlantic City, New Jersey, U.S., which opened in 1910.
entries.etymologyZh: 1919 年, 源自 air (n.1) + port (n.1). First reference is to Bader Field, outside Atlantic City, New Jersey, U.S., which opened 于 1910 年.

example.en: Passengers must check in at the airport counter at least two hours before departure.
example.zh: 旅客必须在出发前至少两小时在机场柜台办理值机手续。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., ele, "lateral division of a church (usually separated by a row of pillars), from Old French ele "wing (of a bird or an army), side of a ship" (12c., Modern French aile), from Latin ala, related to axilla "wing, upper arm, armpit; wing of an army," from PIE *aks- "axis" (see axis), via a suffixed form *aks-la-. The root meaning in "turning" connects it with axle and axis.

Confused from 15c. with unrelated ile "island" (perhaps from notion of a "detached" part of a church), and so it took an -s- when isle did, c. 1700; by 1750 it had acquired an a-, on the model of French cognate aile. The word also was confused with alley, which gave it the sense of "passage between rows of pews or seats" (1731), which was thence extended to railway cars, theaters, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, ele, "lateral division of a church (usually separated by a row of pillars), from Old French ele "wing (of a bird or an army), side of a ship" (12c., Modern French aile), from Latin ala, related to axilla "wing, upper arm, armpit; wing of an army," from PIE *aks- "axis" (see axis), via a suffixed form *aks-la-. The root meaning in "turning" connects it with axle and axis. Confused from 15c. with unrelated ile "island" (perhaps from notion of a "detached" part of a church), and so it took an -s- when isle did, c. 1700; by 1750 it had acquired an a-, on the model of French cognate aile. The word also was confused with alley, which gave it the sense of "passage between rows of pews or seats" (1731 年), which was thence extended to railway cars, theaters, etc.

example.en: The flight attendant walked down the aisle to collect meal trays.
example.zh: 空乘走过过道收集餐盘。

entries.definition: n. 惊恐；警报；警报器 vt. 惊动，惊吓；向……报警
entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French alarme (14c.), from Italian all'arme "to arms!" (literally "to the arms"). An interjection that came to be used as the word for the call or warning (compare alert). Extended 16c. to "any sound to warn of danger or to arouse." Weakened sense of "apprehension, unease" is from 1833. Variant alarum is due to the rolling -r- in the vocalized form. Sometimes in early years Englished as all-arm. Alarm clock is attested from 1690s (as A Larum clock).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 alarme (14 世纪), 源自 意大利语 all'arme "to arms!" (字面义为 "to the arms"). An interjection that came to be used as the word for the call or warning (对比 alert). Extended 16 世纪 to "any sound to warn of danger or to arouse." Weakened 语义 "apprehension, unease" 始于 1833 年. Variant alarum is due to the rolling -r- in the vocalized form. Sometimes in early years Englished as all-arm. Alarm clock 见于 1690 年代 (as A Larum clock).

example.en: A loud alarm woke the entire neighborhood when the fire broke out.
example.zh: 火灾发生时，响亮的警报声惊醒了整个社区。

entries.etymology: 1650s, from Latin album "white color, whiteness," neuter of albus "white" (see alb). In classical times "a blank tablet on which the Pontifex Maximus registered the principal events of the year; a list of names." Revived 16c. by German scholars whose custom was to keep an album amicorum of colleagues' signatures; meaning then expanded into "book to collect souvenirs." According to Johnson, "a book in which foreigners have long been accustomed to insert autographs of celebrated people." Photographic albums first recorded 1859. Meaning "long-playing gramophone record" is by 1951, because the sleeves they came in resembled large albums.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, 源自 拉丁语 album "white color, whiteness," neuter of albus "white" （参见 alb). In classical times "a blank tablet on which the Pontifex Maximus registered the principal events of the year; a list of names." Revived 16 世纪 by 德语 scholars whose custom was to keep an album amicorum of colleagues' signatures; 意为 之后 expanded into "book to collect souvenirs." According to Johnson, "a book in which foreigners have long been accustomed to insert autographs of celebrated people." Photographic albums 首见于 1859 年. 义为 "long-playing gramophone record" is 截至 1951 年, because the sleeves they came in resembled large albums.

example.en: She kept all her childhood photos in a worn leather album.
example.zh: 她把所有童年照片保存在一本破旧的皮革相册里。

entries.etymology:
1540s (early 15c. as alcofol), "fine powder produced by sublimation," from Medieval Latin alcohol "powdered ore of antimony," from Arabic al-kuhul "kohl," the fine metallic powder used to darken the eyelids, from kahala "to stain, paint." The al- is the Arabic definite article, "the."

"Powdered cosmetic" was the earliest sense in English; definition broadened 1670s to "any sublimated substance, the pure spirit of anything," including liquids. Modern sense of "intoxicating ingredient in strong liquor" is first recorded 1753, short for alcohol of wine, which was extended to "the intoxicating element in fermented liquors." In organic chemistry, the word was extended 1850 to the class of compounds of the same type as this.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代 (15 世纪初 as alcofol), "fine powder produced by sublimation," 源自 中古拉丁语 alcohol "powdered ore of antimony," 源自 阿拉伯语 al-kuhul "kohl," the fine metallic powder used to darken the eyelids, 源自 kahala "to stain, paint." The al- is the 阿拉伯语 definite article, "the." "Powdered cosmetic" was the earliest sense in English; definition broadened 1670 年代 to "any sublimated substance, the pure spirit of anything," including liquids. 现代 语义 "intoxicating ingredient in strong liquor" is 首见于 1753 年, short for alcohol of wine, which was extended to "the intoxicating element in fermented liquors." In organic chemistry, the word was extended 1850 年 to the class of compounds of the same type as this.

example.en: Doctors warn that excessive alcohol consumption can damage the liver.
example.zh: 医生警告说，过量饮酒会损害肝脏。

entries.definition: a. 警觉的，提防的 vt.（to）使警觉 n.警惕，警报
entries.etymology: "on the watch," 1590s, from French alerte "vigilant" (17c.), from phrase à l'erte "on the watch," from Italian all'erta "to the height," from erta "lookout, high tower," noun use of fem. of erto, past participle of ergere "raise up," from Latin erigere "raise" (see erect). The adjective is attested from 1610s, the noun from 1803, and the verb from 1868. Related: Alerted; alerting.
entries.etymologyZh: "on the watch," 1590 年代, 源自 法语 alerte "vigilant" (17 世纪), 源自 phrase à l'erte "on the watch," from Italian all'erta "to the height," 源自 erta "lookout, high tower," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. of erto, 为 … 的过去分词 ergere "raise up," 源自 拉丁语 erigere "raise" （参见 erect). The 形容词 见于 1610 年代, the 名词 自 1803 年起, and the 动词 自 1868 年起. 同源词：Alerted; alerting.

example.en: Travelers should stay alert to the risk of pickpockets in crowded areas.
example.zh: 旅行者应对拥挤地区扒手的风险保持警觉。

definitionLines: a. 外国的；相异的，不相容的
entries.definition: a. 外国的；相异的，不相容的 n. 外星人；外国人
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "strange, foreign," from Old French alien "alien, strange, foreign; an alien, stranger, foreigner," from Latin alienus "of or belonging to another, foreign, alien, strange," also, as a noun, "a stranger, foreigner," adjectival form of alius "(an)other" (see alias (adv.)). Meaning "not of the Earth" first recorded 1920. An alien priory (c. 1500) is one owing obedience to a mother abbey in a foreign country.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "strange, foreign," 源自 古法语 alien "alien, strange, foreign; an alien, stranger, foreigner," 源自 拉丁语 alienus "of or belonging to another, foreign, alien, strange," also, 作名词时, "a stranger, foreigner," adjectival form of alius "(an)other" （参见 alias （副）). 义为 "not of the Earth" 首见于 1920 年. An alien priory (约 1500 年) is one owing obedience to a mother abbey in a foreign country.

example.en: The concept of private ownership felt alien to him after years in a commune.
example.zh: 在公社生活了多年之后，私有制的概念对他来说感觉很陌生。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, aliche, from Old English gelic and/or onlice "similar," from Proto-Germanic *galikam "associated form" (source also of Old Frisian gelik, German gleich, Gothic galeiks, Old Norse glikr; see like (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, aliche, 源自 古英语 gelic and/or onlice "similar," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *galikam "associated form" (source also of 古弗里西语 gelik, 德语 gleich, Gothic galeiks, 古北欧语 glikr; 参见 like （形）).

example.en: Twins are not always alike in personality, even if they look similar.
example.zh: 即使外貌相似，双胞胎在性格上也不一定相同。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, from Old English on life "in living." The fuller form on live was still current 17c. Used emphatically, especially with man; as in:

Thus abstracted as an expletive, man alive! (1845). Alive and kicking "alert, vigorous," attested from 1823; Farmer says "The allusion is to a child in the womb after quickening," but kicking in the sense "lively and active" is recorded from 1550s (e.g. "the wanton or kicking flesh of yong maydes," "Lives of Women Saints," c. 1610).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古英语 on life "in living." The fuller form on live was still current 17 世纪 Used emphatically, 尤指 with man; as in: Thus abstracted 作为 expletive, man alive! (1845 年). Alive and kicking "alert, vigorous," attested 自 1823 年起; Farmer says "The allusion is to a child in the womb after quickening," but kicking in the sense "lively and active" 见于 1550 年代 (e.g. "the wanton or kicking flesh of yong maydes," "Lives of Women Saints," 约 1610 年).

example.en: Rescuers found the hiker alive after three days in the wilderness.
example.zh: 救援人员在荒野中找到了那名徒步旅行者，他在那里待了三天，依然活着。

definitionLines: a.全部的，所有的；非常的，极 度的
entries.definition: a.全部的，所有的；非常的，极 度的 pron. 全部，一切 ad.完全地，很
entries.etymology:
Old English eall "all, every, entire," from Proto-Germanic *alnaz (source also of Old Frisian, Old High German al, Old Norse allr, Gothic alls), with no certain connection outside Germanic.

Combinations with all meaning "wholly, without limit" were common in Old English (such as eall-halig "all-holy," eall-mihtig "all-mighty") and the method continued to form new compound words throughout the history of English. First record of all out "to one's full powers" is 1880. All-terrain vehicle first recorded 1968. All clear as a signal of "no danger" is recorded from 1902. All right, indicative of approval, is attested from 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 eall "all, every, entire," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *alnaz (source also of 古弗里西语, 古高地德语 al, 古北欧语 allr, Gothic alls), with no certain connection outside 日耳曼语. Combinations with all 意为 "wholly, without limit" were common in 古英语 (such as eall-halig "all-holy," eall-mihtig "all-mighty") and the method continued to form new 复合词 words throughout the history of English. First record of all out "to one's full powers" is 1880 年. All-terrain vehicle 首见于 1968 年. All clear 作为 signal of "no danger" 见于 1902 年. All right, indicative of approval, 见于 1953 年.

example.en: Scientists from all over the world gathered to discuss climate change.
example.zh: 来自全世界各地的科学家聚集在一起讨论气候变化。

entries.etymology: c. 1300. It has the form of one French verb and the meaning of another. The form is Anglo-French aleger, Old French eslegier "to clear at law," from Latin ex- "out of" (see ex-) and litigare "bring suit" (see litigate); however eslegier meant "acquit, clear of charges in a lawsuit." It somehow acquired the meaning of French alléguer, from Latin allegare "send for, bring forth, name, produce in evidence," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + legare "to depute, send" (see legate). Related: Alleged; alleging.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年. It has the form of one 法语 动词 and the 意为 of another. The form is 盎格鲁-法语 aleger, 古法语 eslegier "to clear at law," 源自 拉丁语 ex- "out of" （参见 ex-) and litigare "bring suit" （参见 litigate); however eslegier meant "acquit, clear of charges in a lawsuit." It somehow acquired the 意为 of 法语 alléguer, 源自 拉丁语 allegare "send for, bring forth, name, produce in evidence," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + legare "to depute, send" （参见 legate). 同源词：Alleged; alleging.

example.en: The company alleges that its new product can double battery life.
example.zh: 该公司声称其新产品能够将电池寿命延长一倍。

definitionLines: a.所谓的；声称的；被断言的
entries.definition: a.所谓的；声称的；被断言的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "quoted," past participle adjective from allege. Attested from 1610s in sense of "brought forth in court;" 1670s as "asserted but not proved."
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "quoted," past participle 形容词 源自 allege. Attested 源自 1610 年代 in 语义 "brought forth in court;" 1670 年代 as "asserted but not proved."

example.en: The alleged thief was caught on camera near the store.
example.zh: 这名所谓的小偷在商店附近被摄像头拍到。

entries.etymology: 1911, from allergy + -ic; perhaps modeled on French allergique (1906). Figurative use, "antipathetic, repulsed" is from 1936.
entries.etymologyZh: 1911 年, 源自 allergy + -ic; 或许 modeled on 法语 allergique (1906 年). Figurative use, "antipathetic, repulsed" 始于 1936 年.

entries.etymology: late 15c., from Middle French allevier or directly from Late Latin alleviatus, past participle of alleviare "to lighten," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + levis "light" in weight (see lever). Related: Alleviated; alleviating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 中古法语 allevier or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 alleviatus, 为 … 的过去分词 alleviare "to lighten," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + levis "light" in weight （参见 lever). 同源词：Alleviated; alleviating.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "bond of marriage" (between ruling houses or noble families), from Old French aliance (12c., Modern French alliance) "alliance, bond; marriage, union," from aliier (Modern French allier) "combine, unite" (see ally (v.)). As a bond or treaty between rulers, late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "bond of marriage" (between ruling houses or noble families), 源自 古法语 aliance (12 世纪, 现代法语 alliance) "alliance, bond; marriage, union," 源自 aliier (现代法语 allier) "combine, unite" （参见 ally （动）). 作为 bond or treaty between rulers, 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The two countries formed a military alliance to defend against common threats.
example.zh: 两国结成军事联盟，共同抵御共同威胁。

entries.etymology: 1630s, from verbal used of adjective allocate (mid-15c. in legal use), from Medieval Latin allocate (the common first word of writs authorizing payment), imperative plural of allocare "allocate," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + locare "to place" (see locate). Related: Allocated; allocating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, 源自 verbal used of 形容词 allocate (15 世纪中期 in legal use), 源自 中古拉丁语 allocate (the common first word of writs authorizing payment), imperative 为 … 的复数 allocare "allocate," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + locare "to place" （参见 locate). 同源词：Allocated; allocating.

entries.definition: vt. 允许，准许；给予 vi.（for）考虑到
entries.etymology:
early 14c., allouen, "to commend, praise; approve of, be pleased with; appreciate the value of;" also, "take into account or give credit for," also, in law and philosophy, "recognize, admit as valid" (a privilege, an excuse, a statement, etc.). From late 14c. as "sanction or permit; condone;" in business use from early 15c.

The Middle English word is from Anglo-French alouer, Old French aloer, alloiier (13c.) "allot, apportion, bestow, assign," from Latin allocare (see allocate). This word in Old French was confused and ultimately merged with aloer; alloer "to praise, commend," from Latin allaudare, adlaudare, compound of ad- "to" (see ad-) + laudare "to praise" (see laud). From the first word came the sense preserved in allowance as "money granted;" from the second came its meaning "permission based on approval."

Related: Allowed; allowing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, allouen, "to commend, praise; approve of, be pleased with; appreciate the value of;" also, "take into account or give credit for," also, in law and philosophy, "recognize, admit as valid" (a privilege, an excuse, a statement, etc.). From 14 世纪晚期 as "sanction or permit; condone;" in business use 源自 15 世纪初 The 中古英语 word 始于 盎格鲁-法语 alouer, 古法语 aloer, alloiier (13 世纪) "allot, apportion, bestow, assign," 源自 拉丁语 allocare （参见 allocate). This word in 古法语 was confused and ultimately merged with aloer; alloer "to praise, commend," 源自 拉丁语 allaudare, adlaudare, 由 … 复合而成 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + laudare "to praise" （参见 laud). From the first word came the sense preserved in allowance as "money granted;" 源自 second came its 意为 "permission based on approval." 同源词：Allowed; allowing.

example.en: School rules do not allow students to use phones during examinations.
example.zh: 校规不允许学生在考试期间使用手机。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "praise" (a sense now obsolete), from Old French aloance "allowance, granting, allocation," from alouer (see allow). Sense of "a sum alloted to meet expenses" is from c. 1400. In accounts, meaning "a sum placed to one's credit" is attested from 1520s. To make allowances is literally to add or deduct a sum from someone's account for some special circumstance. Figurative use of the phrase is attested from 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "praise" (a sense 今废), 源自 古法语 aloance "allowance, granting, allocation," 源自 alouer （参见 allow). 义为 "a sum alloted to meet expenses" 始于 约 1400 年. In accounts, 意为 "a sum placed to one's credit" 见于 1520 年代. To make allowances is 字面义为 to add or deduct a sum 源自 someone's account for some special circumstance. Figurative use of the phrase 见于 1670 年代.

entries.etymology: Old English eallmæst "nearly all, for the most part," literally "mostly all;" see all + most. Modern form from 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 eallmæst "nearly all, for the most part," 字面义为 "mostly all;" 参见 all + most. 现代 form 源自 15 世纪

example.en: The project is almost finished; only the final report remains.
example.zh: 项目几乎完成了，只剩最后的报告还没写。

definitionLines: ad. 在高处；在上面；在空中
a.在上面的；在空中的；在高 处的
entries.definition: ad. 在高处；在上面；在空中 a.在上面的；在空中的；在高 处的
entries.etymology: c. 1200, from a Scandinavian source such as Old Norse a lopti "up above," literally "up in the air," from a "in, on" + lopt "sky, air, atmosphere; loft, upper room" (cognates: Gothic luftus, Old High German luft, Old English lyft "air;" see loft).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 a Scandinavian source such as 古北欧语 a lopti "up above," 字面义为 "up in the air," 源自 a "in, on" + lopt "sky, air, atmosphere; loft, upper room" (cognates: Gothic luftus, 古高地德语 luft, 古英语 lyft "air;" 参见 loft).

entries.definition: a./ad. 独自，单独 ad. 仅仅，只

example.en: She chose to live alone in a small apartment after retiring.
example.zh: 退休后，她选择独自一人住在一套小公寓里。

entries.definition: prep. 沿着 ad. 向前
entries.etymology: Old English andlang "entire, continuous; extended; all day long; alongside of," from and- "opposite, against" (from Proto-Germanic *andi-, *anda-, from PIE *anti "against," locative singular of *ant- "front, forehead;" see ante) + lang "long" (see long (adj.)). Sense extended to "through the whole length of."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 andlang "entire, continuous; extended; all day long; alongside of," 源自 and- "opposite, against" (源自 原始日耳曼语 *andi-, *anda-, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *anti "against," locative singular of *ant- "front, forehead;" 参见 ante) + lang "long" （参见 long （形）). Sense extended to "through the whole length of."

entries.etymology: late 14c., from a- (1) + loud.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 a- (1) + loud.

entries.etymology: 1570s, from Late Latin alphabetum (Tertullian), from Greek alphabetos, from alpha + beta. Alphabet soup first attested 1907. Words for it in Old English included stæfræw, literally "row of letters," stæfrof "array of letters."
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 alphabetum (Tertullian), 源自 希腊语 alphabetos, 源自 alpha + beta. Alphabet soup 最早见于 1907 年. Words for it in 古英语 included stæfræw, 字面义为 "row of letters," stæfrof "array of letters."

entries.etymology: c. 1300, compound of all + ready (adj.); literally "fully ready." Compare Norwegian, Danish allerede "already." Colloquial use in U.S. as a terminal emphatic (as in enough, already!) is attested from 1903, translating Yiddish shoyn, which is used in same sense. The pattern also is attested in Pennsylvania German and in South African.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 由 … 复合而成 all + ready （形）; 字面义为 "fully ready." 对比 Norwegian, Danish allerede "already." Colloquial use in U.S. 作为 terminal emphatic (as in enough, already!) 见于 1903 年, translating Yiddish shoyn, which is used in same sense. The pattern also is 见于 Pennsylvania 德语 and in South African.

entries.etymology: Old English eallswa "just as, even as, as if, so as, likewise," compound of all + so. The demonstrative sense of "similarly" weakened to "in addition to" in 12c., replacing eke. The compound has parallel forms in German also, Dutch alzoo.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 eallswa "just as, even as, as if, so as, likewise," 由 … 复合而成 all + so. The demonstrative 语义 "similarly" weakened to "in addition to" in 12 世纪, replacing eke. The 复合词 has parallel forms in 德语 also, 荷兰语 alzoo.

example.en: She speaks French fluently and also knows some Italian.
example.zh: 她法语说得很流利，而且还懂一些意大利语。

entries.etymology: Old English alter, altar, from Latin altare (plural altaria) "high altar, altar for sacrifice to the great gods," perhaps originally meaning "burnt offerings" (compare Latin adolere "to worship, to offer sacrifice, to honor by burning sacrifices to"), but influenced by Latin altus "high." In Middle English, often auter, from Old French auter. Reintroduced from Latin 1500s. As a symbol of marriage, by 1820.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 alter, altar, 源自 拉丁语 altare (plural altaria) "high altar, altar for sacrifice to the great gods," 或许 原义为 意为 "burnt offerings" (对比 拉丁语 adolere "to worship, to offer sacrifice, to honor by burning sacrifices to"), but influenced by 拉丁语 altus "high." In 中古英语, 常 auter, 源自 古法语 auter. Reintroduced 源自 拉丁语 1500 年代. 作为 symbol of marriage, 截至 1820 年.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to change (something)," from Old French alterer "change, alter," from Medieval Latin alterare "to change," from Latin alter "the other (of the two)," from PIE *al- "beyond" (see alias (adv.)) + comparative suffix -ter (as in other). Intransitive sense "to become otherwise" first recorded 1580s. Related: Altered; altering.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to change (something)," 源自 古法语 alterer "change, alter," 源自 中古拉丁语 alterare "to change," 源自 拉丁语 alter "the other (of the two)," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *al- "beyond" （参见 alias （副）) + comparative suffix -ter (as in other). Intransitive sense "to become otherwise" 首见于 1580 年代. 同源词：Altered; altering.

example.en: The tailor will need to alter the jacket because it's too tight.
example.zh: 裁缝需要修改这件夹克，因为它太紧了。

entries.definition: vi.交替；轮流 vt.使交替；使轮流 a. 交替的；轮流的
entries.etymology: 1510s, from Latin alternatus "one after the other," past participle of alternare "to do first one thing then the other; exchange parts," from alternus "one after the other, alternate, in turns, reciprocal," from alter "the other" (see alter). Alternate means "by turns;" alternative means "offering a choice." Both imply two kinds or things.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, 源自 拉丁语 alternatus "one after the other," 为 … 的过去分词 alternare "to do first one thing then the other; exchange parts," 源自 alternus "one after the other, alternate, in turns, reciprocal," 源自 alter "the other" （参见 alter). Alternate means "by turns;" alternative means "offering a choice." Both imply two kinds or things.

definitionLines: a.两者选一的，可供选择的
entries.definition: a.两者选一的，可供选择的 n. 选择，替换物
entries.etymology: 1580s, "offering one or the other of two," from Medieval Latin alternativus, from Latin alternatus, past participle of alternare (see alternate (v.)). Meaning "purporting to be a superior choice to what is in general use" was current by 1970 (earliest reference is to the media). Alternative energy is from 1975. Related: Alternatively.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "offering one or the other of two," 源自 中古拉丁语 alternativus, 源自 拉丁语 alternatus, 为 … 的过去分词 alternare （参见 alternate （动）). 义为 "purporting to be a superior choice to what is in general use" was current 截至 1970 年 (earliest reference is to the media). Alternative energy 始于 1975 年. 同源词：Alternatively.

example.en: If you cannot attend in person, video call is a good alternative.
example.zh: 如果你不能亲自出席，视频通话是一个很好的替代选择。

entries.etymology: early 14c., althagh, compound of all + though, showing once-common emphatic use of all. "All though was originally more emphatic than though, but by 1400 it was practically only a variant of it, and all having thus lost its independent force, the phrase was written as one word" [OED].
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, althagh, 由 … 复合而成 all + though, showing once-common emphatic use of all. "All though was originally more emphatic than though, but by 1400 it was practically only a variant of it, and all having thus lost its independent force, the phrase was written as one word" [OED].

entries.definition: ad. 完全，总之，全部 alumin（i） um n. 铝
entries.etymology: early 13c., altogedere, a strengthened form of all (also see together); used in the sense of "a whole" from 1660s. The altogether "nude" is from 1894.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, altogedere, a strengthened form of all (also 参见 together); used in the 语义 "a whole" 源自 1660 年代. The altogether "nude" 始于 1894 年.

example.en: There were fifty guests altogether at the wedding ceremony.
example.zh: 婚礼上总共有五十位宾客。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., compound of Old English phrase ealne weg "always, quite, perpetually," literally "all the way," with accusative of space or distance, though the oldest recorded usages refer to time; see all + way (n.). The adverbial genitive -s appeared early 13c. and is now the standard, though the variant alway survived into 1800s. OED speculates allway was originally of space or distance, "but already in the oldest Eng. transferred to an extent of time."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 由 … 复合而成 古英语 phrase ealne weg "always, quite, perpetually," 字面义为 "all the way," with 宾格 of space or distance, though the oldest recorded usages refer to time; 参见 all + way （名）. The adverbial 属格 -s appeared 13 世纪初 and is 现在 the standard, though the variant alway survived into 1800 年代. OED speculates allway was 原义为 of space or distance, "but already in the oldest Eng. transferred to an extent of time."

entries.etymology: late 15c., "to heap up for oneself," from Old French amasser, from à "to" (see ad-) + masser (see mass (n.1)). Related: Amassed; amassing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "to heap up for oneself," 源自 古法语 amasser, 源自 à "to" （参见 ad-) + masser （参见 mass (n.1)). 同源词：Amassed; amassing.

entries.etymology: 1784, "one who has a taste for (something)," from French amateur "lover of," from Latin amatorem (nominative amator) "lover," agent noun from amatus, past participle of amare "to love" (see Amy). Meaning "dabbler" (as opposed to professional) is from 1786. As an adjective, by 1838.
entries.etymologyZh: 1784 年, "one who has a taste for (something)," 源自 法语 amateur "lover of," 源自 拉丁语 amatorem (主格 amator) "lover," agent 名词 源自 amatus, 为 … 的过去分词 amare "to love" （参见 Amy). 义为 "dabbler" (as opposed to professional) 始于 1786 年. 作形容词时, 截至 1838 年.

example.en: As an amateur, he plays chess purely for fun rather than competition.
example.zh: 作为一名业余爱好者，他下棋纯粹是为了乐趣而非竞赛。

entries.etymology: early 13c., amasian "stupefy, make crazy," from a-, probably used here as an intensive prefix, + -masian, related to maze (q.v.). Sense of "overwhelm with wonder" is from 1580s. Related: Amazed; amazing.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, amasian "stupefy, make crazy," 源自 a-, 可能 used here 作为 intensive prefix, + -masian, related to maze (q.v.). 义为 "overwhelm with wonder" 始于 1580 年代. 同源词：Amazed; amazing.

definitionLines: a.令人惊讶的，令人吃惊的
entries.definition: a.令人惊讶的，令人吃惊的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "stupefactive;" 1590s, "dreadful;" present participle adjective from amaze. Sense of "wonderful" is recorded from 1704. Related: Amazingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "stupefactive;" 1590 年代, "dreadful;" present participle 形容词 源自 amaze. 义为 "wonderful" 见于 1704 年. 同源词：Amazingly.

example.en: The view from the cliff edge was so amazing that every hiker stopped to take photos.
example.zh: 悬崖边的景色如此令人惊叹，每位徒步者都停下来拍照。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Greek Amazon (mostly in plural Amazones) "one of a race of female warriors in Scythia," probably from an unknown non-Indo-European word, possibly from an Iranian compound *ha-maz-an- "(one) fighting together" [Watkins], but in folk etymology long derived from a- "without" + mazos "breasts," hence the story that the Amazons cut or burned off one breast so they could draw bowstrings more efficiently.

The river in South America (originally called by the Spanish Rio Santa Maria de la Mar Dulce) rechristened by Francisco de Orellana, 1541, after an encounter with female warriors of the Tapuyas (or, as some say, beardless, long-haired male tribesmen; still others hold that the name is a corruption of a native word in Tupi or Guarani meaning "wave").
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 希腊语 Amazon (mostly in plural Amazones) "one of a race of female warriors in Scythia," 可能 源自 an unknown non-Indo-European word, possibly 源自 an Iranian 复合词 *ha-maz-an- "(one) fighting together" [Watkins], but in folk etymology long derived 源自 a- "without" + mazos "breasts," hence the story that the Amazons cut or burned off one breast so they could draw bowstrings more efficiently. The river in South America (原义为 called by the 西班牙语 Rio Santa Maria de la Mar Dulce) rechristened by Francisco de Orellana, 1541 年, after an encounter with female warriors of the Tapuyas (or, as some say, beardless, long-haired male tribesmen; still others hold that the name is a corruption of a 本族 word in Tupi or Guarani 意为 "wave").

entries.etymology: late 14c., also embassador, from Middle French ambassadeur, from Old French embassator, via Provençal or Old Spanish from Latin ambactus "a servant, vassal," from Celtic amb(i)actos "a messenger, servant," from PIE *ambhi- "about" (see ambi-) + *ag- "drive, lead" (see act (v.)). Compare embassy. Forms in am- and em- were used indiscriminately 17c.-18c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, also embassador, 源自 中古法语 ambassadeur, 源自 古法语 embassator, 经由 Provençal or Old 西班牙语 源自 拉丁语 ambactus "a servant, vassal," 源自 Celtic amb(i)actos "a messenger, servant," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ambhi- "about" （参见 ambi-) + *ag- "drive, lead" （参见 act （动）). 对比 embassy. Forms in am- and em- were used indiscriminately 17 世纪-18 世纪

example.en: The ambassador delivered her country's formal protest to the foreign ministry.
example.zh: 大使向外交部递交了她国家的正式抗议书。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "uncertainty, doubt, indecision, hesitation," also from Medieval Latin ambiguitatem (nominative ambiguitas) "double meaning, equivocalness, double sense," noun of state from ambiguus (see ambiguous).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "uncertainty, doubt, indecision, hesitation," 亦源自 中古拉丁语 ambiguitatem (主格 ambiguitas) "double meaning, equivocalness, double sense," 名词 of state 源自 ambiguus （参见 ambiguous).

entries.etymology: 1520s, from Latin ambiguus "having double meaning, shifting, changeable, doubtful," adjective derived from ambigere "to dispute about," literally "to wander," from ambi- "about" (see ambi-) + agere "drive, lead, act" (see act (n.)). Sir Thomas More (1528) seems to have first used it in English, but ambiguity dates back to c. 1400. Related: Ambiguously; ambiguousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 拉丁语 ambiguus "having double meaning, shifting, changeable, doubtful," 形容词 derived 源自 ambigere "to dispute about," 字面义为 "to wander," 源自 ambi- "about" （参见 ambi-) + agere "drive, lead, act" （参见 act （名）). Sir Thomas More (1528 年) seems to have first used it in English, but ambiguity dates back to 约 1400 年. 同源词：Ambiguously; ambiguousness.

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., from Middle French ambition or directly from Latin ambitionem (nominative ambitio) "a going around," especially to solicit votes, hence "a striving for favor, courting, flattery; a desire for honor, thirst for popularity," noun of action from past participle stem of ambire "to go around" (see ambient).

Rarely used in the literal sense in English, where it carries the secondary Latin sense of "eager or inordinate desire of honor or preferment." In early use always pejorative, of inordinate or overreaching desire; ambition was grouped with pride and vainglory.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 ambition or 直接源自 拉丁语 ambitionem (主格 ambitio) "a going around," 尤指 to solicit votes, hence "a striving for favor, courting, flattery; a desire for honor, thirst for popularity," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of ambire "to go around" （参见 ambient). Rarely used in the literal sense in English, where it carries the secondary 拉丁语 语义 "eager or inordinate desire of honor or preferment." In early use always pejorative, of inordinate or overreaching desire; ambition was grouped with pride and vainglory.

example.en: Her ambition to become a doctor motivated her to study harder every day.
example.zh: 她成为医生的雄心激励她每天更加努力学习。

definitionLines: n. 有雄心的，有抱负的
entries.definition: n. 有雄心的，有抱负的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin ambitiosus "going around to canvass for office," from ambitio (see ambition). Related: Ambitiously.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 ambitiosus "going around to canvass for office," 源自 ambitio （参见 ambition). 同源词：Ambitiously.

example.en: She is ambitious enough to apply for the most competitive program in the country.
example.zh: 她足够有抱负，敢于申请全国最具竞争性的项目。

entries.etymology:
1798, "mobile or field hospital," from French (hôpital) ambulant, literally "walking (hospital)," from Latin ambulantem (nominative ambulans), present participle of ambulare "to walk" (see amble).

The word was not common in English until the meaning transferred from "field hospital" to "vehicle for conveying wounded from field" (1854) during the Crimean War. In late 19c. U.S. the word was used dialectally to mean "prairie wagon." Ambulance-chaser as a contemptuous term for a type of lawyer dates from 1897.
entries.etymologyZh: 1798 年, "mobile or field hospital," 源自 法语 (hôpital) ambulant, 字面义为 "walking (hospital)," 源自 拉丁语 ambulantem (主格 ambulans), 为 … 的现在分词 ambulare "to walk" （参见 amble). The word was not common in English until the 意为 transferred 源自 "field hospital" to "vehicle for conveying wounded from field" (1854 年) during the Crimean War. In 19 世纪晚期 U.S. the word was used dialectally to mean "prairie wagon." Ambulance-chaser 作为 contemptuous term for a type of lawyer dates 自 1897 年起.

example.en: Someone called an ambulance immediately after the accident on the road.
example.zh: 事故发生后，有人立即叫了救护车。

definitionLines: vi. 改正，改善；改过自新
entries.definition: vt. 改善，改进；修改 vi. 改正，改善；改过自新
entries.etymology:
early 13c., "to free from faults, rectify," from Old French amender (12c.), from Latin emendare "to correct, free from fault," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + menda "fault, blemish," from PIE *mend- "physical defect, fault" (source also of Sanskrit minda "physical blemish," Old Irish mennar "stain, blemish," Welsh mann "sign, mark").

Supplanted in senses of "repair, cure" by its shortened offspring mend (v.). Meaning "to add to legislation" (ostensibly to correct or improve it) is recorded from 1777. Related: Amended; amending.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "to free from faults, rectify," 源自 古法语 amender (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 emendare "to correct, free from fault," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + menda "fault, blemish," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mend- "physical defect, fault" (source also of 梵语 minda "physical blemish," Old 爱尔兰语 mennar "stain, blemish," Welsh mann "sign, mark"). Supplanted in senses of "repair, cure" by its shortened offspring mend （动）. 义为 "to add to legislation" (ostensibly to correct or improve it) 见于 1777 年. 同源词：Amended; amending.

entries.etymology:
1507, in Cartographer Martin Waldseemüller's treatise "Cosmographiae Introductio," from Modern Latin Americanus, after Amerigo Vespucci (1454-1512) who made two trips to the New World as a navigator and claimed to have discovered it. His published works put forward the idea that it was a new continent, and he was first to call it Novus Mundus "New World." Amerigo is more easily Latinized than Vespucci.

The name Amerigo is Germanic, said to derive from Gothic Amalrich, literally "work-ruler." The Old English form of the name has come down as surnames Emmerich, Emery, etc. The Italian fem. form merged into Amelia.

Colloquial pronunciation "Ameri-kay," not uncommon 19c., goes back to at least 1643 and a poem that rhymed the word with away. Amerika "U.S. society viewed as racist, fascist, oppressive, etc." first attested 1969; the spelling is German, but may also suggest the KKK.
entries.etymologyZh: 1507 年, in Cartographer Martin Waldseemüller's treatise "Cosmographiae Introductio," 源自 现代 拉丁语 Americanus, after Amerigo Vespucci (1454 年-1512 年) who made two trips to the New World 作为 navigator and claimed to have discovered it. His published works put forward the idea that it was a new continent, and he was first to call it Novus Mundus "New World." Amerigo is more easily Latinized than Vespucci. The name Amerigo is 日耳曼语, said to derive 源自 Gothic Amalrich, 字面义为 "work-ruler." The 古英语 form of the name has come down as surnames Emmerich, Emery, etc. The 意大利语 fem. form merged into Amelia. Colloquial pronunciation "Ameri-kay," not uncommon 19 世纪, goes back to at least 1643 年 and a poem that rhymed the word with away. Amerika "U.S. society viewed as racist, fascist, oppressive, etc." 最早见于 1969 年; the spelling is 德语, but may also suggest the KKK.

entries.etymology: 1570s (n.); 1590s (adj.), from Modern Latin Americanus, from America (q.v.); originally in reference to what now are called Native Americans; the sense of "resident of North America of European (originally British) descent" is first recorded 1640s (adj.); 1765 (n.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代 （名）; 1590 年代 （形）, 源自 现代 拉丁语 Americanus, 源自 America (q.v.); 原义为 in reference to what 现在 are called Native Americans; the 语义 "resident of North America of European (originally British) descent" is 首见于 1640 年代 （形）; 1765 年 （名）.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from amidde (c. 1200), from Old English on middan "in the middle," from dative singular of midde "mid, middle" (see middle); the phrase evidently was felt as "in (the) middle" and thus followed by a genitive case, and if this had endured we would follow it today with of. (See amidst for further evolution along this line).

The same applies to equivalents in Latin (in medio) and Greek (en meso), both originally adjective phrases which evolved to take the genitive case. But in later Old English on middan also was treated as a preposition and followed by dative. Used in compounds from early 13c. (such as amidships, attested from 1690s and retaining the genitive, as the compounds usually did in early Middle English, suggesting this one is considerably older than the written record of it.)
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 amidde (约 1200 年), 源自 古英语 on middan "in the middle," 源自 dative singular of midde "mid, middle" （参见 middle); the phrase 显然 was felt as "in (the) middle" and thus followed by a 属格 case, and if this had endured we would follow it today with of. (See amidst for further evolution along this line). The same applies to equivalents in 拉丁语 (in medio) and 希腊语 (en meso), both 原义为 形容词 phrases which evolved to take the 属格 case. But in later 古英语 on middan also was treated 作为 preposition and followed by dative. Used in compounds 源自 13 世纪初 (such as amidships, attested 源自 1690 年代 and retaining the 属格, as the compounds 通常 did in early 中古英语, suggesting this one is considerably older than the written record of it.)

entries.definition: n. 弹药；军火 among（st） prep.在……之中，在…之间
entries.etymology: 1620s, from French soldiers' faulty separation of Middle French la munition into l'ammunition; from Latin munitionem (nominative munitio) "a fortifying" (see munition), and at first meaning all military supplies in general. The mistake in the word perhaps was by influence of French a(d)monition "warning." The error was corrected in French (Modern French munition), but retained in English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 法语 soldiers' faulty separation of Middle French la munition into l'ammunition; 源自 拉丁语 munitionem (主格 munitio) "a fortifying" （参见 munition), and at first 意为 all military supplies in general. The mistake in the word 或许 was by influence of 法语 a(d)monition "warning." The error was corrected in 法语 (现代法语 munition), but retained in English.

entries.definition: n. 数量，数额，总数 vt.（to）合计，相当于，等同
entries.etymology: late 13c., "to go up, rise, mount (a horse)," from Old French amonter, from a mont "upward," literally "to the mountain," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + montem (nominative mons) "mountain" (see mount (n.1)). Meaning "to rise in number or quality (so as to reach)" is from c. 1300. Related: Amounted; amounting.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "to go up, rise, mount (a horse)," 源自 古法语 amonter, 源自 a mont "upward," 字面义为 "to the mountain," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + montem (主格 mons) "mountain" （参见 mount (n.1)). 义为 "to rise in number or quality (so as to reach)" 始于 约 1300 年. 同源词：Amounted; amounting.

example.en: A large amount of work was needed to clear the debris after the storm.
example.zh: 暴风雨过后，需要做大量的工作来清理废墟。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French ample, from Latin amplus "large, spacious," related to ampla "handle, grip."
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 ample, 源自 拉丁语 amplus "large, spacious," related to ampla "handle, grip."

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to enlarge or expand," from Middle French amplifier, from Latin amplificare "to enlarge," from amplificus "splendid," from amplus "large" (see ample) + the root of facere "to make, do" (see factitious). Meaning "augment in volume or amount" is from 1570s. Restriction of use to sound seems to have emerged in the electronic age, c. 1915, in reference to radio technology.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to enlarge or expand," 源自 中古法语 amplifier, 源自 拉丁语 amplificare "to enlarge," 源自 amplificus "splendid," 源自 amplus "large" （参见 ample) + the root of facere "to make, do" （参见 factitious). 义为 "augment in volume or amount" 始于 1570 年代. Restriction of use to sound seems to have emerged in the electronic age, 约 1915 年, in reference to radio technology.

definitionLines: vt. 逗乐，使开心；给……提供 娱乐
entries.definition: vt. 逗乐，使开心；给……提供 娱乐
entries.etymology: late 15c., "to divert the attention, beguile, delude," from Middle French amuser "divert, cause to muse," from a "at, to" (but here probably a causal prefix) + muser "ponder, stare fixedly" (see muse (v.)). Sense of "divert from serious business, tickle the fancy of" is recorded from 1630s, but through 18c. the primary meaning was "deceive, cheat" by first occupying the attention. Bemuse retains more of the original meaning. Related: Amused; amusing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "to divert the attention, beguile, delude," 源自 中古法语 amuser "divert, cause to muse," 源自 a "at, to" (but here 可能 a causal prefix) + muser "ponder, stare fixedly" （参见 muse （动）). 义为 "divert from serious business, tickle the fancy of" 见于 1630 年代, but through 18 世纪 the primary 意为 was "deceive, cheat" by first occupying the attention. Bemuse retains more of the original 意为. 同源词：Amused; amusing.

entries.etymology: 1540s (perhaps early 15c.), from Old French analogie or directly from Latin analogia, from Greek analogia "proportion," from ana- "upon, according to" (see ana-) + logos "ratio," also "word, speech, reckoning" (see logos). A mathematical term used in a wider sense by Plato.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代 (或许 15 世纪初), 源自 古法语 analogie or 直接源自 拉丁语 analogia, 源自 希腊语 analogia "proportion," 源自 ana- "upon, according to" （参见 ana-) + logos "ratio," also "word, speech, reckoning" （参见 logos). A mathematical term used in a wider sense by Plato.

example.en: The teacher used an analogy to help students understand the concept.
example.zh: 老师用了一个类比来帮助学生理解这个概念。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "resolution of anything complex into simple elements" (opposite of synthesis), from Medieval Latin analysis (15c.), from Greek analysis "a breaking up, a loosening, releasing," noun of action from analyein "unloose, release, set free; to loose a ship from its moorings," in Aristotle, "to analyze," from ana "up, throughout" (see ana-) + lysis "a loosening," from lyein "to unfasten" (see lose). Psychological sense is from 1890. Phrase in the final (or last) analysis (1844), translates French en dernière analyse.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "resolution of anything complex into simple elements" (opposite of synthesis), 源自 中古拉丁语 analysis (15 世纪), 源自 希腊语 analysis "a breaking up, a loosening, releasing," 名词 of action 源自 analyein "unloose, release, set free; to loose a ship from its moorings," in Aristotle, "to analyze," 源自 ana "up, throughout" （参见 ana-) + lysis "a loosening," 源自 lyein "to unfasten" （参见 lose). Psychological sense 始于 1890 年. Phrase in the final (or last) analysis (1844 年), translates 法语 en dernière analyse.

example.en: A detailed analysis of the survey results revealed several trends.
example.zh: 对调查结果的详细分析揭示了几个趋势。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "to dissect," from French analyser, from analyse (see analysis). Literature sense is attested from 1610s; meaning in chemistry dates from 1660s. General sense of "to examine closely" dates from 1809; psychological sense is from 1909. Related: Analyzed; analyzing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "to dissect," 源自 法语 analyser, 源自 analyse （参见 analysis). Literature sense 见于 1610 年代; 意为 in chemistry dates 源自 1660 年代. General 语义 "to examine closely" dates 自 1809 年起; psychological sense 始于 1909 年. 同源词：Analyzed; analyzing.

example.en: Researchers must carefully analyze the survey data before drawing any conclusions about consumer behavior.
example.zh: 研究人员在得出有关消费者行为的任何结论之前，必须仔细分析调查数据。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, ancestre, antecessour, from Old French ancestre (12c., Modern French ancêtre), from Late Latin antecessor "predecessor," literally "foregoer," agent noun from past participle stem of Latin antecedere "to precede," from ante- "before" (see ante) + cedere "to go" (see cede). Current form from early 15c. Feminine form ancestress recorded from 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, ancestre, antecessour, 源自 古法语 ancestre (12 世纪, 现代法语 ancêtre), 源自 晚期拉丁语 antecessor "predecessor," 字面义为 "foregoer," agent 名词 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 antecedere "to precede," 源自 ante- "before" （参见 ante) + cedere "to go" （参见 cede). Current form 源自 15 世纪初 Feminine form ancestress recorded 源自 1570 年代.

example.en: She traced her ancestors back to a small village in Ireland.
example.zh: 她追溯到她的祖先来自爱尔兰一个小村庄。

entries.etymology: Old English ancor, borrowed 9c. from Latin ancora "anchor," from or cognate with Greek ankyra "anchor, hook" (see ankle). A very early borrowing and said to be the only Latin nautical term used in the Germanic languages. The -ch- form emerged late 16c., a pedantic imitation of a corrupt spelling of the Latin word. The figurative sense of "that which gives stability or security" is from late 14c. Meaning "host or presenter of a TV or radio program" is from 1965, short for anchorman.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ancor, borrowed 9 世纪 源自 拉丁语 ancora "anchor," 源自 or 与 … 同源 希腊语 ankyra "anchor, hook" （参见 ankle). A very early borrowing and said to be the only 拉丁语 nautical term used in the 日耳曼语 languages. The -ch- form emerged 16 世纪晚期, a pedantic imitation of a corrupt spelling of the 拉丁语 word. The figurative 语义 "that which gives stability or security" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "host or presenter of a TV or radio program" 始于 1965 年, short for anchorman.

example.en: They dropped the anchor to keep the boat in place.
example.zh: 他们抛下锚，使船保持在原位。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., auncyen, from Old French ancien "old, long-standing, ancient," from Vulgar Latin *anteanus, literally "from before," adjectivization of Latin ante "before, in front of, against" (from PIE *anti "against," locative singular of *ant- "front, forehead;" see ante). The parasitic -t dates from 15c. by influence of words in -ent.

Specifically, in history, "belonging to the period before the fall of the Western Roman Empire" (and contrasted with medieval and modern). In English law, "from before the Norman Conquest." Ancient of Days is from Dan. vii:9. Related: Anciently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, auncyen, 源自 古法语 ancien "old, long-standing, ancient," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *anteanus, 字面义为 "from before," adjectivization of 拉丁语 ante "before, in front of, against" (源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *anti "against," locative singular of *ant- "front, forehead;" 参见 ante). The parasitic -t dates 源自 15 世纪 by influence of words in -ent. Specifically, in history, "belonging to the period before the fall of the Western Roman Empire" (and contrasted with medieval and modern). In English law, "from before the Norman Conquest." Ancient of Days 始于 Dan. vii:9. 同源词：Anciently.

example.en: Archaeologists discovered ancient pottery dating back over three thousand years.
example.zh: 考古学家发现了距今三千多年的古代陶器。

entries.etymology: Old English and, ond, originally meaning "thereupon, next," from Proto-Germanic *unda (source also of Old Saxon endi, Old Frisian anda, Middle Dutch ende, Old High German enti, German und, Old Norse enn), from PIE *en; cognate with Latin ante, Greek anti (see ante). Phrase and how as an exclamation of emphatic agreement dates from early 1900s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 and, ond, 原义为 意为 "thereupon, next," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *unda (source also of 古撒克逊语 endi, 古弗里西语 anda, Middle 荷兰语 ende, 古高地德语 enti, 德语 und, 古北欧语 enn), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *en; 与 … 同源 拉丁语 ante, 希腊语 anti （参见 ante). Phrase and how 作为 exclamation of emphatic agreement dates 源自 early 1900 年代.

entries.etymology: alternative (chiefly U.S.) spelling of anaemia (q.v.). See ae. As a genus of plants, Modern Latin, from Greek aneimon "unclad," from privative prefix an- (see an- (1)) + eima "a dress, garment" (see wear (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: alternative (chiefly U.S.) spelling of anaemia (q.v.). See ae. 作为 genus of plants, 现代 拉丁语, 源自 希腊语 aneimon "unclad," 源自 privative prefix an- （参见 an- (1)) + eima "a dress, garment" （参见 wear （动）).

entries.etymology:
14c. fusion of Old English engel (with hard -g-) and Old French angele, both from Latin angelus, from Greek angelos "messenger, envoy, one that announces," possibly related to angaros "mounted courier," both from an unknown Oriental word (Watkins compares Sanskrit ajira- "swift;" Klein suggests Semitic sources). Used in Scriptural translations for Hebrew mal'akh (yehowah) "messenger (of Jehovah)," from base l-'-k "to send." An Old English word for it was aerendgast, literally "errand-spirit."

Of persons, "loving; lovely," by 1590s. The medieval gold coin (a new issue of the noble, first struck 1465 by Edward VI) was so called for the image of archangel Michael slaying the dragon, which was stamped on it. It was the coin given to patients who had been "touched" for the King's Evil. Angel food cake is from 1881; angel dust "phencyclidine" is from 1968.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪 fusion of 古英语 engel (with hard -g-) and 古法语 angele, both 源自 拉丁语 angelus, 源自 希腊语 angelos "messenger, envoy, one that announces," possibly related to angaros "mounted courier," both 源自 an unknown Oriental word (Watkins compares 梵语 ajira- "swift;" Klein suggests Semitic sources). Used in Scriptural translations for 希伯来语 mal'akh (yehowah) "messenger (of Jehovah)," from base l-'-k "to send." An 古英语 word for it was aerendgast, 字面义为 "errand-spirit." Of persons, "loving; lovely," by 1590 年代. The medieval gold coin (a new issue of the noble, first struck 1465 年 by Edward VI) was so called for the image of archangel Michael slaying the dragon, which was stamped on it.
