It was the coin given to patients who had been "touched" for the King's Evil. Angel food cake 始于 1881 年; angel dust "phencyclidine" 始于 1968 年.

entries.definition: n. 气愤，愤怒 vt. 使发怒，激怒
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "to irritate, annoy, provoke," from Old Norse angra "to grieve, vex, distress; to be vexed at, take offense with," from Proto-Germanic *angus (source also of Old English enge "narrow, painful," Middle Dutch enghe, Gothic aggwus "narrow"), from PIE root *angh- "tight, painfully constricted, painful" (source also of Sanskrit amhu- "narrow," amhah "anguish;" Armenian anjuk "narrow;" Lithuanian ankstas "narrow;" Greek ankhein "to squeeze," ankhone "a strangling;" Latin angere "to throttle, torment;" Old Irish cum-ang "straitness, want"). In Middle English, also of physical pain. Meaning "excite to wrath, make angry" is from late 14c. Related: Angered; angering.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "to irritate, annoy, provoke," 源自 古北欧语 angra "to grieve, vex, distress; to be vexed at, take offense with," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *angus (source also of 古英语 enge "narrow, painful," Middle 荷兰语 enghe, Gothic aggwus "narrow"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *angh- "tight, painfully constricted, painful" (source also of 梵语 amhu- "narrow," amhah "anguish;" Armenian anjuk "narrow;" Lithuanian ankstas "narrow;" 希腊语 ankhein "to squeeze," ankhone "a strangling;" 拉丁语 angere "to throttle, torment;" Old 爱尔兰语 cum-ang "straitness, want"). In 中古英语, also of physical pain. 义为 "excite to wrath, make angry" 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Angered; angering.

example.en: She was filled with anger when she discovered she had been cheated.
example.zh: 当她发现自己被欺骗时，她充满了愤怒。

entries.etymology: member of a Teutonic tribe, Old English, from Latin Angli "the Angles," literally "people of Angul" (Old Norse Öngull), a region in what is now Holstein, said to be so-called for its hook-like shape (see angle (n.)). People from the tribe there founded the kingdoms of Mercia, Northumbia, and East Anglia in 5c. Britain. Their name, rather than that of the Saxons or Jutes, may have become the common one for the whole group of Germanic tribes because their dialect was the first committed to writing.
entries.etymologyZh: member of a Teutonic tribe, 古英语, 源自 拉丁语 Angli "the Angles," 字面义为 "people of Angul" (古北欧语 Öngull), a region in what is 现在 Holstein, said to be so-called for its hook-like shape （参见 angle （名）). People 源自 tribe there founded the kingdoms of Mercia, Northumbia, and East Anglia in 5 世纪 Britain. Their name, rather than that of the Saxons or Jutes, may have become the common one for the whole group of 日耳曼语 tribes because their dialect was the first committed to writing.

example.en: He always approaches problems from a technical angle, not a social one.
example.zh: 他总是从技术角度而非社会角度来思考问题。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from anger (n.) + -y (2). Originally "full of trouble, vexatious;" sense of "enraged, irate" also is from late 14c. The Old Norse adjective was ongrfullr "sorrowful," and Middle English had angerful "anxious, eager" (mid-13c.). The phrase angry young man dates to 1941 but was popularized in reference to the play "Look Back in Anger" (produced 1956) though it does not occur in that work.

"There are three words in the English language that end in -gry. Two of them are angry and hungry. What is the third?" There is no third (except some extremely obscure ones). Richard Lederer calls this "one of the most outrageous and time-wasting linguistic hoaxes in our nation's history" and traces it to a New York TV quiz show from early 1975.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 anger （名） + -y (2). Originally "full of trouble, vexatious;" 语义 "enraged, irate" also 始于 14 世纪晚期 The 古北欧语 形容词 was ongrfullr "sorrowful," and 中古英语 had angerful "anxious, eager" (13 世纪中期). The phrase angry young man dates to 1941 年 but was popularized in reference to the play "Look Back in Anger" (produced 1956 年) though it does not occur in that work. "There are three words in the English language that end in -gry. Two of them are angry and hungry. What is the third?" There is no third (except some extremely obscure ones). Richard Lederer calls this "one of the most outrageous and time-wasting linguistic hoaxes in our nation's history" and traces it to a New York TV quiz show 源自 early 1975 年.

example.en: She was angry at being kept waiting for over an hour.
example.zh: 被晾了一个多小时，她非常生气。

entries.definition: n. 动物，野兽，牲畜 c.动物的，野兽的
entries.etymology: early 14c. (but rare before c. 1600, and not in KJV, 1611), "any living creature" (including humans), from Latin animale "living being, being which breathes," neuter of animalis "animate, living; of the air," from anima "breath, soul; a current of air" (see animus, and compare deer). Drove out the older beast in common usage. Used of brutish humans from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初 (but rare before 约 1600 年, and not in KJV, 1611 年), "any living creature" (including humans), 源自 拉丁语 animale "living being, being which breathes," neuter of animalis "animate, living; of the air," 源自 anima "breath, soul; a current of air" （参见 animus, and 对比 deer). Drove out the older beast in common usage. Used of brutish humans 源自 1580 年代.

example.en: A wild animal suddenly appeared on the hiking trail ahead of us.
example.zh: 一只野生动物突然出现在我们前方的登山小道上。

entries.definition: vt. 使有生气；使活泼 a. 有生命的
entries.etymology: 1530s, "to fill with boldness or courage," from Latin animatus past participle of animare "give breath to," also "to endow with a particular spirit, to give courage to," from anima "life, breath" (see animus). Sense of "give life to" in English attested from 1742. Related: Animated; animating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "to fill with boldness or courage," 源自 拉丁语 animatus 为 … 的过去分词 animare "give breath to," also "to endow with a particular spirit, to give courage to," 源自 anima "life, breath" （参见 animus). 义为 "give life to" in English attested 自 1742 年起. 同源词：Animated; animating.

entries.etymology: Old English ancleow "ankle," from PIE root *ang-/*ank- "to bend" (see angle (n.)). The modern form seems to have been influenced by Old Norse ökkla or Old Frisian ankel, which are immediately from the Proto-Germanic form of the root (source also of Middle High German anke "joint," German Enke "ankle"); the second element in the Old English, Old Norse and Old Frisian forms perhaps suggests claw (compare Dutch anklaauw), or it may be from influence of cneow "knee," or it may be diminutive suffix -el. Middle English writers distinguished inner ankle projection (hel of the ancle) from the outer (utter or utward).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ancleow "ankle," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ang-/*ank- "to bend" （参见 angle （名）). The modern form seems to have been influenced by 古北欧语 ökkla or 古弗里西语 ankel, which are immediately 源自 原始日耳曼语 form of the root (source also of Middle High 德语 anke "joint," 德语 Enke "ankle"); the second element in the 古英语, 古北欧语 and 古弗里西语 forms 或许 suggests claw (对比 荷兰语 anklaauw)，或it may be 源自 influence of cneow "knee," or it may be diminutive suffix -el. 中古英语 writers distinguished inner ankle projection (hel of the ancle) 源自 outer (utter or utward).

example.en: She twisted her ankle while running and had to stop the race.
example.zh: 她在跑步时扭了脚踝，不得不停止比赛。

entries.etymology: early 13c., originally especially of the day of a person's death, from Medieval Latin anniversarium, from Latin anniversarius (adj.) "returning annually," from annus (genitive anni) "year" (see annual (adj.)) + versus, past participle of vertere "to turn" (see versus). The adjective came to be used as a noun in Church Latin as anniversaria (dies) in reference to saints' days. An Old English word for "anniversary" (n.) was mynddæg, literally "mind-day."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 原义为 尤指 of the day of a person's death, from Medieval Latin anniversarium, from Latin anniversarius (adj.) "returning annually," from annus (genitive anni) "year" (see annual (adj.)) + versus, past participle of vertere "to turn" (see versus). The adjective came to be used as a noun in Church Latin as anniversaria (dies) in reference to saints' days. An 古英语 word for "anniversary" （名） was mynddæg, 字面义为 "mind-day."

example.en: They held a dinner party to celebrate their twentieth wedding anniversary.
example.zh: 他们举办了一场晚宴，庆祝结婚二十周年纪念日。

entries.definition: vt.宣布；述说；预示；播报 vi. 宣布参加竞选
entries.etymology: c. 1500, "proclaim, make known," from Old French anoncier "announce, proclaim" (12c., Modern French annoncer), from Latin annuntiare, adnuntiare "to announce, relate," literally "to bring news," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + nuntiare "relate, report," from nuntius "messenger" (see nuncio). Related: Announced; announcing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "proclaim, make known," 源自 古法语 anoncier "announce, proclaim" (12 世纪, 现代法语 annoncer), 源自 拉丁语 annuntiare, adnuntiare "to announce, relate," 字面义为 "to bring news," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + nuntiare "relate, report," 源自 nuntius "messenger" （参见 nuncio). 同源词：Announced; announcing.

example.en: The school will announce the winners of the essay competition at tomorrow's assembly.
example.zh: 学校将于明天的集会上宣布征文比赛的获奖者。

definitionLines: vt. 使烦恼，使生气，打搅
entries.definition: vt. 使烦恼，使生气，打搅
entries.etymology: late 13c., from Anglo-French anuier, Old French enoiier, anuier "to weary, vex, anger; be troublesome or irksome to," from Late Latin inodiare "make loathsome," from Latin (esse) in odio "(it is to me) hateful," ablative of odium "hatred" (see odium). Earliest form of the word in English was as a noun, c. 1200, "feeling of irritation, displeasure, distaste." Related: Annoyed; annoying; annoyingly. Middle English also had annoyful and annoyous (both late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 anuier, 古法语 enoiier, anuier "to weary, vex, anger; be troublesome or irksome to," 源自 晚期拉丁语 inodiare "make loathsome," 源自 拉丁语 (esse) in odio "(it is to me) hateful," ablative of odium "hatred" （参见 odium). Earliest form of the word in English was 作名词时, 约 1200 年, "feeling of irritation, displeasure, distaste." 同源词：Annoyed; annoying; annoyingly. 中古英语 also had annoyful and annoyous (both 14 世纪晚期).

entries.definition: a.每年的，年度的 n. 年刊，年鉴
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French annuel (12c.) or directly from Late Latin annualem (nominative annualis), corresponding to Latin annalis as adjective form of annus "year," from PIE *at-no-, from root *at- "to go," on notion of "period gone through" (source also of Sanskrit atati "goes, wanders," Gothic aþnam (dative plural) "year," Oscan akno- "year, holiday, time of offering"). Used of plants since 1710.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 annuel (12 世纪) or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 annualem (主格 annualis), corresponding to 拉丁语 annalis as 形容词 form of annus "year," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *at-no-, 源自 root *at- "to go," on 概念 "period gone through" (source also of 梵语 atati "goes, wanders," Gothic aþnam (dative plural) "year," Oscan akno- "year, holiday, time of offering"). Used of plants 自 1710 年.

example.en: The company publishes an annual report summarizing its financial performance.
example.zh: 该公司发布年度报告，总结其财务表现。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from Late Latin anonymus, from Greek anonymos "without a name," from an- "without" (see an- (1)) + onyma, Æolic dialectal form of onoma "name" (see name (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 晚期拉丁语 anonymus, 源自 希腊语 anonymos "without a name," 源自 an- "without" （参见 an- (1)) + onyma, Æolic 方言 form of onoma "name" （参见 name （名）).

example.en: The donor wished to remain anonymous and asked that their name not be published.
example.zh: 这位捐赠者希望保持匿名，要求不公开姓名。

entries.definition: a. 另一，再一；别的 pron. 另一个
entries.etymology: early 13c., merger of an other. Old English used simply oþer. Originally "a second of two." Compound reciprocal pronoun one another is recorded from 1520s.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, merger of an other. 古英语 used simply oþer. Originally "a second of two." Compound reciprocal pronoun one another 见于 1520 年代.

entries.definition: n. 回答，答复；答案 v.回答，答复
entries.etymology: Old English andswaru "an answer, a reply," from and- "against" (see ante) + -swaru "affirmation," from swerian "to swear" (see swear), suggesting an original sense of "make a sworn statement rebutting a charge." A common Germanic compound (cognates: Old Saxon antswor, Old Norse andsvar, Old Frisian ondser, Danish and Swedish ansvar), implying a Proto-Germanic *andswara-. Meaning "a reply to a question," the main modern sense, was present in Old English. Meaning "solution of a problem" is from c. 1300.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 andswaru "an answer, a reply," 源自 and- "against" （参见 ante) + -swaru "affirmation," 源自 swerian "to swear" （参见 swear), suggesting an original 语义 "make a sworn statement rebutting a charge." A common 日耳曼语 复合词 (cognates: 古撒克逊语 antswor, 古北欧语 andsvar, 古弗里西语 ondser, Danish and Swedish ansvar), implying a 原始日耳曼语 *andswara-. 义为 "a reply to a question," the main modern sense, was present in 古英语. 义为 "solution of a problem" 始于 约 1300 年.

entries.etymology:
c. 1500, from Middle English ampte (late 14c.), from Old English æmette "ant," from West Germanic *amaitjo (source also of Old High German ameiza, German Ameise) from a compound of bases *ai- "off, away" + *mai- "cut," from PIE *mai- "to cut" (source also of maim). Thus the insect's name is, etymologically, "the biter off."

Emmet survived into 20c. as an alternative form. White ant "termite" is from 1729. To have ants in one's pants "be nervous and fidgety" is from 1934, made current by a popular song; antsy embodies the same notion.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, 源自 中古英语 ampte (14 世纪晚期), 源自 古英语 æmette "ant," 源自 West 日耳曼语 *amaitjo (source also of 古高地德语 ameiza, 德语 Ameise) 源自 a 由 … 复合而成 bases *ai- "off, away" + *mai- "cut," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mai- "to cut" (source also of maim). Thus the insect's name is, etymologically, "the biter off." Emmet survived into 20c. as an alternative form. White ant "termite" is from 1729. To have ants in one's pants "be nervous and fidgety" 始于 1934 年, made current by a popular song; antsy embodies the same notion.

definitionLines: vt. 预期，预料；指望，期待
entries.definition: vt. 预期，预料；指望，期待
entries.etymology:
1530s, "to cause to happen sooner," a back-formation from anticipation, or else from Latin anticipatus, past participle of anticipare "take (care of) ahead of time," literally "taking into possession beforehand," from ante "before" (see ante) + capere "to take" (see capable).

Later "to be aware of (something) coming at a future time" (1640s). Used in the sense of "expect, look forward to" since 1749, but anticipate has an element of "prepare for, forestall" that should prevent its being used as a synonym for expect. Related: Anticipated; anticipating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "to cause to happen sooner," a back-formation 源自 anticipation，或else 源自 拉丁语 anticipatus, 为 … 的过去分词 anticipare "take (care of) ahead of time," 字面义为 "taking into possession beforehand," 源自 ante "before" （参见 ante) + capere "to take" （参见 capable). Later "to be aware of (something) coming at a future time" (1640 年代). Used in the 语义 "expect, look forward to" 自 1749 年, but anticipate has an element of "prepare for, forestall" that should prevent its being used 作为 synonym for expect. 同源词：Anticipated; anticipating.

example.en: We did not anticipate such a large turnout at the event.
example.zh: 我们没有预料到活动会有这么多人参加。

entries.definition: a. 古时的，古老的 n. 古物，古董
entries.etymology: 1530s, "aged, venerable," from Middle French antique "old" (14c.), from Latin antiquus (later anticus) "ancient, former, of olden times; old, long in existence, aged; venerable; old-fashioned," from PIE *anti in sense of "before" (see ante) + *okw- "appearance" (see eye (n.)). Originally pronounced in English like its parallel antic, but French pronunciation and spelling were adopted from c. 1700.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "aged, venerable," 源自 中古法语 antique "old" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 antiquus (later anticus) "ancient, former, of olden times; old, long in existence, aged; venerable; old-fashioned," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *anti in 语义 "before" （参见 ante) + *okw- "appearance" （参见 eye （名）). Originally pronounced in English like its parallel antic, but 法语 pronunciation and spelling were adopted 源自 约 1700 年.

example.en: She paid a fortune for that antique vase at the auction.
example.zh: 她在拍卖会上花了一大笔钱买下那件古董花瓶。

definitionLines: n. 挂念，焦虑，担心；渴望，热望
entries.definition: n. 挂念，焦虑，担心；渴望，热望
entries.etymology: 1520s, from Latin anxietatem (nominative anxietas) "anguish, anxiety, solicitude," noun of quality from anxius (see anxious). Psychiatric use dates to 1904. Age of Anxiety is from Auden's poem (1947). For "anxiety, distress," Old English had angsumnes, Middle English anxumnesse.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 拉丁语 anxietatem (主格 anxietas) "anguish, anxiety, solicitude," 名词 of quality 源自 anxius （参见 anxious). Psychiatric use dates to 1904 年. Age of Anxiety 始于 Auden's poem (1947 年). For "anxiety, distress," 古英语 had angsumnes, 中古英语 anxumnesse.

example.en: Public speaking often triggers a feeling of anxiety in students.
example.zh: 公开演讲常常会在学生中引发一种焦虑感。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin anxius "solicitous, uneasy, troubled in mind" (also "causing anxiety, troublesome"), from angere, anguere "choke, squeeze," figuratively "torment, cause distress" (see anger (v.)). The same image is in Serbo-Croatian tjeskoba "anxiety," literally "tightness, narrowness." Related: Anxiously; anxiousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 anxius "solicitous, uneasy, troubled in mind" (also "causing anxiety, troublesome"), 源自 angere, anguere "choke, squeeze," figuratively "torment, cause distress" （参见 anger （动）). The same image is in Serbo-Croatian tjeskoba "anxiety," 字面义为 "tightness, narrowness." 同源词：Anxiously; anxiousness.

example.en: She felt anxious about the results of her medical test.
example.zh: 她对医学检测结果感到焦虑不安。

definitionLines: a.任何的，任一的；［否定、疑 问、条件句中］什么，一些
pron. 无论哪个，无论哪些，任一
entries.definition: a.任何的，任一的；［否定、疑 问、条件句中］什么，一些 pron. 无论哪个，无论哪些，任一
entries.etymology:
Old English ænig "any, anyone," literally "one-y," from Proto-Germanic *ainagas (source also of Old Saxon enig, Old Norse einigr, Old Frisian enich, Dutch enig, German einig), from PIE *oi-no- "one, unique" (see one). The -y may have diminutive force here.

Emphatic form any old ______ (British variant: any bloody ______) is recorded from 1896. At any rate is recorded from 1847. Among the large family of compounds beginning with any-, anykyn "any kind" (c. 1300) did not survive, and Anywhen (1831) is rarely used, but OED calls it "common in Southern [British] dialects."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ænig "any, anyone," 字面义为 "one-y," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ainagas (source also of 古撒克逊语 enig, 古北欧语 einigr, 古弗里西语 enich, 荷兰语 enig, 德语 einig), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *oi-no- "one, unique" （参见 one). The -y may have diminutive force here. Emphatic form any old ______ (British variant: any bloody ______) 见于 1896 年. At any rate 见于 1847 年. Among the large family of compounds beginning with any-, anykyn "any kind" (约 1300 年) did not survive, and Anywhen (1831 年) is rarely used, but OED calls it "common in Southern [British] dialects."

definitionLines: pron.［否定、疑问、条件句中］ 任何人；［肯定句中］随便 哪一个人
entries.definition: pron.［否定、疑问、条件句中］ 任何人；［肯定句中］随便 哪一个人
entries.etymology: c. 1300, ani-bodi, from any + body. One-word form is attested by 1826. Phrase anybody's game (or race, etc.) is from 1840.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, ani-bodi, 源自 any + body. One-word form is attested 截至 1826 年. Phrase anybody's game (or race, etc.) 始于 1840 年.

definitionLines: ad.无论如何，不管怎样；不管 以什么方法；总之
entries.definition: ad.无论如何，不管怎样；不管 以什么方法；总之 anyone=anybody
entries.etymology: 1740, from any + how (adv.). Unlike the cases of most other any + (interrogative) compounds, there is no record of it in Old or Middle English. Emphatic form any old how is recorded from 1900, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1740 年, 源自 any + how （副）. Unlike the cases of most other any + (interrogative) compounds, there is no record of it in Old or 中古英语. Emphatic form any old how 见于 1900 年, American English.

definitionLines: pron. ［否定、疑问、条件句中］ 任何事（物）；无论什么事 （物）
entries.definition: pron. ［否定、疑问、条件句中］ 任何事（物）；无论什么事 （物） anyway=anyhow
entries.etymology: late Old English aniþing, from any + thing. But Old English ænig þinga apparently also meant "somehow, anyhow" (glossing Latin quoquo modo).
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 aniþing, 源自 any + thing. But 古英语 ænig þinga 似乎 also meant "somehow, anyhow" (glossing 拉丁语 quoquo modo).

definitionLines: ad.无论哪里；［否定、疑问、条 件句中］任何地方
entries.definition: ad.无论哪里；［否定、疑问、条 件句中］任何地方
entries.etymology: late 14c., from any + where. Earlier words in this sense were owhere, oughwhere, aywhere, literally "aught where" (see aught (1)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 any + where. Earlier words in this sense were owhere, oughwhere, aywhere, 字面义为 "aught where" （参见 aught (1)).

example.en: I could not find my keys anywhere in the apartment.
example.zh: 我在公寓里任何地方都找不到我的钥匙。

definitionLines: ad. 分离，隔开；相距，相隔
entries.definition: ad. 分离，隔开；相距，相隔
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French à part "to the side," from Latin ad "to" (see ad-) + partem, accusative of pars "a side" (see part (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 à part "to the side," 源自 拉丁语 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + partem, 宾格 of pars "a side" （参见 part （名）).

entries.etymology: 1640s, "private rooms for the use of one person within a house," from French appartement (16c.), from Italian appartimento, literally "a separated place," from appartere "to separate," from a "to" (see ad-) + parte "side, place," from Latin partem (see part (n.)). Sense of "set of private rooms in a building entirely of these" (the U.S. equivalent of British flat) is first attested 1874.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "private rooms for the use of one person within a house," 源自 法语 appartement (16 世纪), 源自 意大利语 appartimento, 字面义为 "a separated place," 源自 appartere "to separate," 源自 a "to" （参见 ad-) + parte "side, place," 源自 拉丁语 partem （参见 part （名）). 义为 "set of private rooms in a building entirely of these" (the U.S. equivalent of British flat) is 最早见于 1874 年.

example.en: They rented a small apartment in the city center after moving for work.
example.zh: 为了工作搬家后，他们在市中心租了一套小公寓。

entries.etymology:
early 15c., "defense, justification," from Late Latin apologia, from Greek apologia "a speech in defense," from apologeisthai "to speak in one's defense," from apologos "an account, story," from apo- "from, off" (see apo-) + logos "speech" (see lecture (n.)).

The original English sense of "self-justification" yielded a meaning "frank expression of regret for wrong done," first recorded 1590s, but this was not the main sense until 18c. The old sense tends to emerge in Latin form apologia (first attested in English 1784), especially since J.H. Newman's "Apologia pro Vita Sua" (1864).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "defense, justification," 源自 晚期拉丁语 apologia, 源自 希腊语 apologia "a speech in defense," 源自 apologeisthai "to speak in one's defense," 源自 apologos "an account, story," 源自 apo- "from, off" （参见 apo-) + logos "speech" （参见 lecture （名）). The original English 语义 "self-justification" yielded a 意为 "frank expression of regret for wrong done," 首见于 1590 年代, but this was not the main sense until 18 世纪 The old sense tends to emerge in 拉丁语 form apologia (最早见于 in English 1784 年), 尤指 自 J.H. Newman's "Apologia pro Vita Sua" (1864 年).

example.en: He offered a sincere apology for his rude behavior.
example.zh: 他为自己粗鲁的行为诚挚地道了歉。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French aparant "evident, obvious, visible," from Latin apparentem (nominative apparens) "visible, manifest," present participle of apparere (see appear). First attested in phrase heir apparent (see heir). Meaning "superficial" is c. 1400. Apparent magnitude in astronomy (how bright a heavenly body looks from earth, as opposed to absolute magnitude, which is how bright it really is) is attested from 1875.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 aparant "evident, obvious, visible," 源自 拉丁语 apparentem (主格 apparens) "visible, manifest," 为 … 的现在分词 apparere （参见 appear). First 见于 phrase heir apparent （参见 heir). 义为 "superficial" is 约 1400 年. Apparent magnitude in astronomy (how bright a heavenly body looks 源自 earth, as opposed to absolute magnitude, which is how bright it really is) 见于 1875 年.

example.en: It was apparent from his furrowed brow and tight lips that he disagreed.
example.zh: 从他皱起的眉头和紧绷的嘴唇，可以明显看出他表示不同意。

definitionLines: vi.（to）请求，呼吁；吸引；上 诉；求助
entries.definition: vi.（to）请求，呼吁；吸引；上 诉；求助 n. 呼吁；吸引力；上诉
entries.etymology:
early 14c., originally in legal sense of "to call" to a higher judge or court, from Anglo-French apeler "to call upon, accuse," Old French apeler "make an appeal" (11c., Modern French appeler), from Latin appellare "to accost, address, appeal to, summon, name," iterative of appellere "to prepare," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + pellere "to beat, drive" (see pulse (n.1)). Related: Appealed; appealing.

Probably a Roman metaphoric extension of a nautical term for "driving a ship toward a particular landing." Popular modern meaning "to be attractive or pleasing" is quite recent, attested from 1907 (appealing in this sense is from 1891), from the notion of "to address oneself in expectation of a sympathetic response."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 原义为 in legal 语义 "to call" to a higher judge or court, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 apeler "to call upon, accuse," 古法语 apeler "make an appeal" (11 世纪, 现代法语 appeler), 源自 拉丁语 appellare "to accost, address, appeal to, summon, name," 为 … 的反复体 appellere "to prepare," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + pellere "to beat, drive" （参见 pulse (n.1)). 同源词：Appealed; appealing. Probably a Roman metaphoric extension of a nautical term for "driving a ship toward a particular landing." Popular modern 意为 "to be attractive or pleasing" is quite recent, attested 自 1907 年起 (appealing in this sense 始于 1891 年), 源自 概念 "to address oneself in expectation of a sympathetic response."

example.en: The charity appealed to the public for donations after the devastating flood.
example.zh: 毁灭性洪灾过后，该慈善机构向公众呼吁捐款。

definitionLines: vi. 出现，出场，问世；好像是
entries.definition: vi. 出现，出场，问世；好像是
entries.etymology: late 13c., "to come into view," from stem of Old French aparoir (12c., Modern French apparoir) "appear, come to light, come forth," from Latin apparere "to appear, come in sight, make an appearance," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + parere "to come forth, be visible." Of persons, "present oneself," late 14c. Meaning "seem, have a certain appearance" is late 14c. Related: Appeared; appearing.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "to come into view," 源自 stem of 古法语 aparoir (12 世纪, 现代法语 apparoir) "appear, come to light, come forth," 源自 拉丁语 apparere "to appear, come in sight, make an appearance," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + parere "to come forth, be visible." Of persons, "present oneself," 14 世纪晚期 义为 "seem, have a certain appearance" is 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Appeared; appearing.

example.en: Dark clouds began to appear on the horizon just before the storm hit.
example.zh: 暴风雨来临前，乌云开始在地平线上出现。

definitionLines: n. 出现，出场，露面；外表，外观
entries.definition: n. 出现，出场，露面；外表，外观
entries.etymology: late 14c., "visible state or form, figure; mere show," from Anglo-French apparaunce, Old French aparance "appearance, display, pomp" (13c.), from Latin apparentia, abstract noun from aparentem, past participle of apparere (see appear). Meaning "semblance" is recorded from early 15c.; that of "action of coming into view" is mid-15c. Phrase keep up appearances attested from 1760 (save appearances in same sense is 1711).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "visible state or form, figure; mere show," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 apparaunce, 古法语 aparance "appearance, display, pomp" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 apparentia, abstract 名词 源自 aparentem, 为 … 的过去分词 apparere （参见 appear). 义为 "semblance" 见于 15 世纪初; that of "action of coming into view" is 15 世纪中期 Phrase keep up appearances attested 自 1760 年起 (save appearances in same sense is 1711 年).

example.en: His sudden appearance at the party surprised everyone.
example.zh: 他在派对上的突然出现让所有人都感到惊讶。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "craving for food," from Anglo-French appetit, Old French apetit (13c.) "appetite, desire, eagerness," from Latin appetitus "appetite," literally "desire toward," from appetitus, past participle of appetere "to long for, desire; strive for, grasp at," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + petere "go to, seek out" (see petition (n.)).

Of other desires or cravings, from late 14c. As an adjective form, OED lists appetitious (1650s) and appetitual (1610s) as "obsolete," but appetitive (1570s) continues.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "craving for food," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 appetit, 古法语 apetit (13 世纪) "appetite, desire, eagerness," 源自 拉丁语 appetitus "appetite," 字面义为 "desire toward," 源自 appetitus, 为 … 的过去分词 appetere "to long for, desire; strive for, grasp at," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + petere "go to, seek out" （参见 petition （名）). Of other desires or cravings, 源自 14 世纪晚期 作形容词时 form, OED lists appetitious (1650 年代) and appetitual (1610 年代) as "obsolete," but appetitive (1570 年代) continues.

example.en: The smell of fresh bread immediately triggered his appetite.
example.zh: 新鲜面包的香味立刻激起了他的食欲。

entries.definition: vt. 向……喝彩；赞同；称赞 vi. 喝彩；鼓掌欢迎
entries.etymology: late 15c. (implied in applauding), "to express agreement or approval; to praise," from Latin applaudere "to clap the hands in approbation, to approve by clapping hands; to strike upon, beat," from ad "to" (see ad-) + plaudere "to clap" (see plaudit). Sense of "express approval of" is from 1590s; that of "to clap the hands" is from 1590s. Figurative sense arrived in English before literal. Related: Applauded; applauding.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期 (implied in applauding), "to express agreement or approval; to praise," 源自 拉丁语 applaudere "to clap the hands in approbation, to approve by clapping hands; to strike upon, beat," 源自 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + plaudere "to clap" （参见 plaudit). 义为 "express approval of" 始于 1590 年代; that of "to clap the hands" 始于 1590 年代. Figurative sense arrived in English before literal. 同源词：Applauded; applauding.

entries.etymology:
Old English æppel "apple; any kind of fruit; fruit in general," from Proto-Germanic *ap(a)laz (source also of Old Saxon, Old Frisian, Dutch appel, Old Norse eple, Old High German apful, German Apfel), from PIE *ab(e)l "apple" (source also of Gaulish avallo "fruit;" Old Irish ubull, Lithuanian obuolys, Old Church Slavonic jabloko "apple"), but the exact relation and original sense of these is uncertain (compare melon).

In Middle English and as late as 17c., it was a generic term for all fruit other than berries but including nuts (such as Old English fingeræppla "dates," literally "finger-apples;" Middle English appel of paradis "banana," c. 1400). Hence its grafting onto the unnamed "fruit of the forbidden tree" in Genesis. Cucumbers, in one Old English work, are eorþæppla, literally "earth-apples" (compare French pomme de terre "potato," literally "earth-apple;" see also melon). French pomme is from Latin pomum "apple; fruit" (see Pomona).

Apple of Discord (c. 1400) was thrown into the wedding of Thetis and Peleus by Eris (goddess of chaos and discord), who had not been invited, and inscribed kallisti "To the Prettiest One." Paris, elected to choose which goddess should have it, gave it to Aphrodite, offending Hera and Athene, with consequences of the Trojan War, etc.

Apple of one's eye (Old English), symbol of what is most cherished, was the pupil, supposed to be a globular solid body. Apple-polisher "one who curries favor" first attested 1928 in student slang. The image of something that upsets the apple cart is attested from 1788. Road apple "horse dropping" is from 1942.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 æppel "apple; any kind of fruit; fruit in general," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ap(a)laz (source also of 古撒克逊语, 古弗里西语, 荷兰语 appel, 古北欧语 eple, 古高地德语 apful, 德语 Apfel), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ab(e)l "apple" (source also of Gaulish avallo "fruit;" Old 爱尔兰语 ubull, Lithuanian obuolys, Old Church Slavonic jabloko "apple"), but the exact relation and original 语义 these is uncertain (对比 melon). In 中古英语 and as late as 17 世纪, it was a generic term for all fruit other than berries but including nuts (such as 古英语 fingeræppla "dates," 字面义为 "finger-apples;" 中古英语 appel of paradis "banana," 约 1400 年). Hence its grafting onto the unnamed "fruit of the forbidden tree" in Genesis. Cucumbers, in one 古英语 work, are eorþæppla, 字面义为 "earth-apples" (对比 法语 pomme de terre "potato," 字面义为 "earth-apple;" 亦参见 melon). 法语 pomme 始于 拉丁语 pomum "apple; fruit" （参见 Pomona). Apple of Discord (约 1400 年) was thrown into the wedding of Thetis and Peleus by Eris (goddess of chaos and discord), who had not been invited, and inscribed kallisti "To the Prettiest One." Paris, elected to choose which goddess should have it, gave it to Aphrodite, offending Hera and Athene, with consequences of the Trojan War, etc. Apple of one's eye (古英语), symbol of what is most cherished, was the pupil, supposed to be a globular solid body. Apple-polisher "one who curries favor" 最早见于 1928 年 in student 俚语. The image of something that upsets the apple cart 见于 1788 年. Road apple "horse dropping" 始于 1942 年.

definitionLines: n. 用具，设备；器械；装置
entries.definition: n. 用具，设备；器械；装置
entries.etymology: 1560s, "action of putting into use," from apply + -ance. Meaning "instrument, thing applied for a purpose" is from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "action of putting into use," 源自 apply + -ance. 义为 "instrument, thing applied for a purpose" 始于 1590 年代.

example.en: The kitchen is equipped with every modern appliance you could need.
example.zh: 厨房里配备了你可能需要的所有现代家用设备。

entries.etymology: "one who applies," late 15c., from Latin applicantem (nominative applicans), present participle of applicare (see apply).
entries.etymologyZh: "one who applies," 15 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 applicantem (主格 applicans), 为 … 的现在分词 applicare （参见 apply).

example.en: Every applicant must submit a resume and a cover letter by Friday.
example.zh: 每位申请者必须在周五之前提交简历和求职信。

definitionLines: n. 申请，申请书；运用，应用
entries.definition: n. 申请，申请书；运用，应用
entries.etymology: early 15c., "the bringing of something to bear on something else," from Old French aplicacion (14c.), from Latin applicationem (nominative applicatio) "a joining to, an attaching oneself to," noun of action from past participle stem of applicare (see apply). Meaning "sincere hard effort" is from c. 1600. Meaning "a formal request to be hired for a job or paid position" is by 1851.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "the bringing of something to bear on something else," 源自 古法语 aplicacion (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 applicationem (主格 applicatio) "a joining to, an attaching oneself to," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of applicare （参见 apply). 义为 "sincere hard effort" 始于 约 1600 年. 义为 "a formal request to be hired for a job or paid position" is 截至 1851 年.

example.en: He submitted his application for the graduate program by the deadline.
example.zh: 他在截止日期前提交了研究生项目的申请书。

entries.etymology: "put to practical use," (as opposed to abstract or theoretical), 1650s, from past participle of apply. Earlier it was used in a sense of "folded" (c. 1500).
entries.etymologyZh: "put to practical use," (as opposed to abstract or theoretical), 1650 年代, 源自 为 … 的过去分词 apply. Earlier it was used in a 语义 "folded" (约 1500 年).

example.en: She studied applied linguistics to improve language teaching methods.
example.zh: 她学习应用语言学，以改善语言教学方法。

entries.definition: vi. （for） 申请 vt. （to）运用，应用
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to put (one's faculties, etc.) to some task or career," late 14c., from Old French aploiier "apply, use, attach" (12c., Modern French appliquer), from Latin applicare "attach to, join, connect;" figuratively, "devote (oneself) to, give attention," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + plicare "fold" (see ply (v.1)). The etymological sense is "bring things in contact with one another." Of lotions, from early 15c. Meaning "seek a job by submitting an application for one" is from 1851. A by-form applicate is recorded from 1530s. Related: Applied; applying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to put (one's faculties, etc.) to some task or career," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 aploiier "apply, use, attach" (12 世纪, 现代法语 appliquer), 源自 拉丁语 applicare "attach to, join, connect;" figuratively, "devote (oneself) to, give attention," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + plicare "fold" （参见 ply (v.1)). The etymological sense is "bring things in contact with one another." Of lotions, 源自 15 世纪初 义为 "seek a job by submitting an application for one" 始于 1851 年. A by-form applicate 见于 1530 年代. 同源词：Applied; applying.

example.en: Students must apply for financial aid before the semester begins.
example.zh: 学生必须在学期开始前申请财务援助。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to decide, resolve; to arrange the time of (a meeting, etc.)," from Anglo-French appointer, Old French apointier "make ready, arrange, settle, place" (12c.), from apointer "duly, fitly," from phrase à point "to the point," from a- "to" (see ad-) + point "point," from Latin punctum (see point (n.)). The ground sense is "to come to a point (about some matter)," therefore "agree, settle." Meaning "put (someone) in charge" is early 15c. Related: Appointed; appointing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to decide, resolve; to arrange the time of (a meeting, etc.)," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 appointer, 古法语 apointier "make ready, arrange, settle, place" (12 世纪), 源自 apointer "duly, fitly," 源自 phrase à point "to the point," 源自 a- "to" （参见 ad-) + point "point," 源自 拉丁语 punctum （参见 point （名）). The ground sense is "to come to a point (about some matter)," therefore "agree, settle." 义为 "put (someone) in charge" is 15 世纪初 同源词：Appointed; appointing.

example.en: The board voted to appoint a new CEO to lead the company.
example.zh: 董事会投票任命一位新的首席执行官来领导公司。

definitionLines: n. 约会，约见；任命，委派
entries.definition: n. 约会，约见；任命，委派
entries.etymology: early 15c., "an agreement," also "a fixing of a date for official business," from Middle French apointement, from apointer (see appoint). Meaning "act of placing in office" is attested from 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "an agreement," also "a fixing of a date for official business," 源自 中古法语 apointement, 源自 apointer （参见 appoint). 义为 "act of placing in office" 见于 1650 年代.

example.en: I have a doctor's appointment at three o'clock this afternoon.
example.zh: 我今天下午三点有一个看诊预约。

definitionLines: vt. 感激，感谢；评价，欣赏， 赏识
entries.definition: vt. 感激，感谢；评价，欣赏， 赏识
entries.etymology: 1650s, "to esteem or value highly," from Late Latin appretiatus, past participle of appretiare "to set a price to" (see appraise). Meaning "to rise in value" (intransitive) first recorded 1789. Related: Appreciated; appreciating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "to esteem or value highly," 源自 晚期拉丁语 appretiatus, 为 … 的过去分词 appretiare "to set a price to" （参见 appraise). 义为 "to rise in value" (intransitive) 首见于 1789 年. 同源词：Appreciated; appreciating.

example.en: I truly appreciate all the effort you put into organizing this event.
example.zh: 我真心感激你为组织这次活动所付出的所有努力。

definitionLines: n. 走进；方法，探讨；观点
entries.definition: v. 接近，走进 vt. 处理，对待 n. 走进；方法，探讨；观点
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Anglo-French approcher, Old French aprochier "approach, come closer" (12c., Modern French approcher), from Late Latin appropiare "go nearer to," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + Late Latin propiare "come nearer," comparative of Latin prope "near" (see propinquity). Replaced Old English neahlæcan.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 approcher, 古法语 aprochier "approach, come closer" (12 世纪, 现代法语 approcher), 源自 晚期拉丁语 appropiare "go nearer to," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + 晚期拉丁语 propiare "come nearer," comparative of 拉丁语 prope "near" （参见 propinquity). Replaced 古英语 neahlæcan.

example.en: Scientists need a new approach to tackle this complex problem.
example.zh: 科学家需要一种新方法来解决这个复杂问题。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "take possession of," from Late Latin appropriatus, past participle of appropriare, adpropriare (c.450) "to make one's own," from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + propriare "take as one's own," from proprius "one's own" (see proper). Related: Appropriated; appropriating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "take possession of," 源自 晚期拉丁语 appropriatus, 为 … 的过去分词 appropriare, adpropriare (约 450 年) "to make one's own," 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + propriare "take as one's own," 源自 proprius "one's own" （参见 proper). 同源词：Appropriated; appropriating.

example.en: Please wear appropriate clothing to the formal ceremony on Saturday evening.
example.zh: 请在周六晚上的正式典礼上穿着得体的服装。

entries.etymology: 1680s, from approve + -al (2). According to OED, "Rare bef. 1800; now generally used instead of" approvance (1590s, from French aprovance).
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, 源自 approve + -al (2). According to OED, "Rare bef. 1800; now generally used instead of" approvance (1590 年代, 源自 法语 aprovance).

example.en: The construction project finally received official approval from the planning committee.
example.zh: 该建设项目终于获得了规划委员会的正式批准。

definitionLines: v.（of）赞成，赞许，同意；批准， 审议，通过
entries.definition: v.（of）赞成，赞许，同意；批准， 审议，通过
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to demonstrate, prove;" mid-14c., "to attest (something) with authority," from Old French aprover (Modern French approuver) "approve, agree to," from Latin approbare "to assent to as good, regard as good," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + probare "to try, test something (to find if it is good)," from probus "honest, genuine" (see prove).

The meaning extended late 14c. to "to sanction, endorse, confirm formally" then to "assent to (something) as good" (early 15c.), especially in reference to the actions of authorities, parliaments, etc. Related: Approved; approving.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to demonstrate, prove;" 14 世纪中期, "to attest (something) with authority," 源自 古法语 aprover (现代法语 approuver) "approve, agree to," 源自 拉丁语 approbare "to assent to as good, regard as good," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + probare "to try, test something (to find if it is good)," 源自 probus "honest, genuine" （参见 prove). The 意为 extended 14 世纪晚期 to "to sanction, endorse, confirm formally" 之后 to "assent to (something) as good" (15 世纪初), 尤指 in reference to the actions of authorities, parliaments, etc. 同源词：Approved; approving.

example.en: The board voted to approve the merger after months of negotiation.
example.zh: 经过数月谈判，董事会投票批准了这次合并。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin approximatus, past participle of approximare "to come near to," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + proximare "come near," from proximus "nearest," superlative of prope "near" (see propinquity).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 approximatus, 为 … 的过去分词 approximare "to come near to," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + proximare "come near," 源自 proximus "nearest," superlative of prope "near" （参见 propinquity).

entries.etymology: fourth month, c. 1300, aueril, from Old French avril (11c.), from Latin (mensis) Aprilis, second month of the ancient Roman calendar, of uncertain origin, perhaps based on Apru, an Etruscan borrowing of Greek Aphrodite. Or perhaps *ap(e)rilis "the following, the next," from its place as the second month of the old Roman calendar, from Proto-Italic *ap(e)ro-, from PIE *apo- "away, off" (see apo-; compare Sanskrit aparah "second," Gothic afar "after"). With month-name suffix -ilis as in Quintilis, Sextilis (the old names of July and August). In English in Latin form from mid-12c. Replaced Old English Eastermonað, which was named for a fertility goddess (see Easter). Re-spelled in Middle English on Latin model (apprile first attested late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: fourth month, 约 1300 年, aueril, 源自 古法语 avril (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 (mensis) Aprilis, second month of the ancient Roman calendar, 来源存疑, 或许 based on Apru, an Etruscan borrowing of 希腊语 Aphrodite. Or 或许 *ap(e)rilis "the following, the next," 源自 its place as the second month of the old Roman calendar, 源自 Proto-Italic *ap(e)ro-, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *apo- "away, off" （参见 apo-; 对比 梵语 aparah "second," Gothic afar "after"). With month-name suffix -ilis as in Quintilis, Sextilis (the old names of July and August). In English in 拉丁语 form 源自 12 世纪中期 Replaced 古英语 Eastermonað, which was named for a fertility goddess （参见 Easter). Re-spelled in 中古英语 on 拉丁语 model (apprile 最早见于 14 世纪晚期).

definitionLines: a. 有……倾向的；恰当的；灵 敏的
entries.definition: a. 有……倾向的；恰当的；灵 敏的
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "inclined, disposed;" late 14c., "suited, fitted, adapted," from Old French ate (13c., Modern French apte), or directly from Latin aptus "fit, suited," adjectival use of past participle of *apere "to attach, join, tie to," from PIE root *ap- (1) "to grasp, take, reach" (source also of Sanskrit apnoti "he reaches," Latin apisci "to reach after, attain," Hittite epmi "I seize"). Elliptical sense of "becoming, appropriate" is from 1560s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "inclined, disposed;" 14 世纪晚期, "suited, fitted, adapted," 源自 古法语 ate (13 世纪, 现代法语 apte)，或直接源自 拉丁语 aptus "fit, suited," adjectival use of 为 … 的过去分词 *apere "to attach, join, tie to," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ap- (1) "to grasp, take, reach" (source also of 梵语 apnoti "he reaches," 拉丁语 apisci "to reach after, attain," Hittite epmi "I seize"). Elliptical 语义 "becoming, appropriate" 始于 1560 年代.

entries.definition: n. 阿拉伯人 a. 阿拉伯的
entries.etymology: late 14c. (Arabes, a plural form), from Old French Arabi, from Latin Arabs (accusative Arabem), from Greek Araps (genitive Arabos), from Arabic 'arab, indigenous name of the people, perhaps literally "inhabitant of the desert" and related to Hebrew arabha "desert." Meaning "homeless little wanderer, child of the street" is from 1848 (originally Arab of the city), in reference to nomadic ways. Arab League formed in Cairo, March 22, 1945.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 (Arabes, a plural form), 源自 古法语 Arabi, 源自 拉丁语 Arabs (宾格 Arabem), 源自 希腊语 Araps (属格 Arabos), 源自 阿拉伯语 'arab, indigenous name of the people, 或许 字面义为 "inhabitant of the desert" and related to 希伯来语 arabha "desert." 义为 "homeless little wanderer, child of the street" 始于 1848 年 (原义为 Arab of the city), in reference to nomadic ways. Arab League formed in Cairo, March 22, 1945 年.

definitionLines: a. 阿拉伯人的，阿拉伯的
entries.definition: a. 阿拉伯人的，阿拉伯的
entries.etymology: c. 1300, adjective and noun; see Arab + -ian. As a prized type of horse, it is attested from 1660s. The Arabian bird was the phoenix.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 形容词 and 名词; 参见 Arab + -ian. 作为 prized type of horse, it 见于 1660 年代. The Arabian bird was the phoenix.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "deciding by one's own discretion," from Old French arbitraire (14c.) or directly from Latin arbitrarius "depending on the will, uncertain," from arbiter (see arbiter). The original meaning gradually descended to "capricious" and "despotic" (1640s). Related: Arbitrarily; arbitrariness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "deciding by one's own discretion," 源自 古法语 arbitraire (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 arbitrarius "depending on the will, uncertain," 源自 arbiter （参见 arbiter). The original 意为 gradually descended to "capricious" and "despotic" (1640 年代). 同源词：Arbitrarily; arbitrariness.

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "ancient history," from French archéologie (16c.) or directly from Greek arkhaiologia "the study of ancient things;" see archaeo- + -ology. Meaning "scientific study of ancient peoples" recorded by 1825. Related: Archaeological; archaeologically.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "ancient history," 源自 法语 archéologie (16 世纪) or 直接源自 希腊语 arkhaiologia "the study of ancient things;" 参见 archaeo- + -ology. 义为 "scientific study of ancient peoples" recorded 截至 1825 年. 同源词：Archaeological; archaeologically.

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French architecte, from Latin architectus, from Greek arkhitekton "master builder, director of works," from arkhi- "chief" (see archon) + tekton "builder, carpenter" (see texture). An Old English word for it was heahcræftiga "high-crafter."
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 architecte, 源自 拉丁语 architectus, 源自 希腊语 arkhitekton "master builder, director of works," 源自 arkhi- "chief" （参见 archon) + tekton "builder, carpenter" （参见 texture). An 古英语 word for it was heahcræftiga "high-crafter."

example.en: The architect presented the blueprint for the new city library.
example.zh: 建筑师展示了新城市图书馆的设计蓝图。

entries.etymology: 1560s, from Middle French architecture, from Latin architectura, from architectus "architect" (see architect).
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 中古法语 architecture, 源自 拉丁语 architectura, 源自 architectus "architect" （参见 architect).

example.en: The city is famous for its stunning Renaissance architecture that draws millions of tourists.
example.zh: 这座城市以其令人叹为观止的文艺复兴时期建筑而闻名，吸引了数百万游客。

definitionLines: a. 热烈的，激动的；热心的，热 切的；燃烧的，炽热的
entries.definition: a. 热烈的，激动的；热心的，热 切的；燃烧的，炽热的
entries.etymology:
early 14c., of alcoholic distillates, brandy (ardent spirits), etc., from Old French ardant (13c.) "burning, hot; zealous," from Latin ardentem (nominative ardens) "glowing, fiery, hot, ablaze," also used figuratively of passions, present participle of ardere "to burn," from PIE root *as- "to burn, glow" (source also of Old English æsce "ashes;" see ash (n.1)).

Ardent spirits (late 15c.) so called because they are inflammable, but the term now, if used at all, probably is felt in the figurative sense. The figurative sense (of "burning with" passions, desire, etc.) is from late 14c.; literal sense of "burning, parching" (c. 1400) remains rare. Related: Ardently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, of alcoholic distillates, brandy (ardent spirits), etc., 源自 古法语 ardant (13 世纪) "burning, hot; zealous," 源自 拉丁语 ardentem (主格 ardens) "glowing, fiery, hot, ablaze," also used figuratively of passions, 为 … 的现在分词 ardere "to burn," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *as- "to burn, glow" (source also of 古英语 æsce "ashes;" 参见 ash (n.1)). Ardent spirits (15 世纪晚期) so called because they are inflammable, but the term 现在, if used at all, 可能 is felt in the figurative sense. The figurative sense (of "burning with" passions, desire, etc.) 始于 14 世纪晚期; literal 语义 "burning, parching" (约 1400 年) remains rare. 同源词：Ardently.

definitionLines: n. 面积；地区；范围，领域
entries.definition: n. 面积；地区；范围，领域
entries.etymology: 1530s, "vacant piece of ground," from Latin area "level ground, open space," used of building sites, playgrounds, threshing floors, etc.; which is of uncertain origin. Perhaps related to arere "to become dry," on notion of a burned clearing or dry, bare space. The generic sense of "amount of surface (whether open or not) contained within any set of limits" is from 1845. Area code in North American telephone systems is attested from 1959.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "vacant piece of ground," 源自 拉丁语 area "level ground, open space," used of building sites, playgrounds, threshing floors, etc.; which is 来源存疑. Perhaps related to arere "to become dry," on 概念 a burned clearing or dry, bare space. The generic 语义 "amount of surface (whether open or not) contained within any set of limits" 始于 1845 年. Area code in North American telephone systems 见于 1959 年.

example.en: The new highway will connect rural areas to the city center.
example.zh: 新高速公路将把农村地区与市中心连接起来。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "place of combat," from Latin harena "place of combat," originally "sand, sandy place," perhaps from Etruscan. The central stages of Roman amphitheaters were strewn with sand to soak up the blood.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "place of combat," 源自 拉丁语 harena "place of combat," 原义为 "sand, sandy place," 或源自 Etruscan. The central stages of Roman amphitheaters were strewn with sand to soak up the blood.

example.en: Social media has become a new arena for political debate.
example.zh: 社交媒体已成为政治辩论的新竞技场。

entries.definition: vi. 辩论，争论 vt.辩论，论证；说服
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to make reasoned statements to prove or refute a proposition," from Old French arguer "maintain an opinion or view; harry, reproach, accuse, blame" (12c.), from Latin argutare "to prattle, prate," frequentative of arguere "make clear, make known, prove, declare, demonstrate," from PIE *argu-yo-, from root *arg- "to shine, be white, bright, clear" (see argent). Meaning "to oppose, dispute" is from late 14c. Related: Argued; arguing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to make reasoned statements to prove or refute a proposition," 源自 古法语 arguer "maintain an opinion or view; harry, reproach, accuse, blame" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 argutare "to prattle, prate," 为 … 的反复体 arguere "make clear, make known, prove, declare, demonstrate," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *argu-yo-, 源自 root *arg- "to shine, be white, bright, clear" （参见 argent). 义为 "to oppose, dispute" 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Argued; arguing.

example.en: The lawyer argued that the evidence was unreliable in court.
example.zh: 律师在法庭上论证说该证据不可靠。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "statements and reasoning in support of a proposition," from Old French arguement "reasoning, opinion; accusation, charge" (13c.), from Latin argumentum "evidence, ground, support, proof; a logical argument," from arguere "to argue" (see argue). Sense passed through "subject of contention" to "a quarrel," a sense formerly attached to argumentation.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "statements and reasoning in support of a proposition," 源自 古法语 arguement "reasoning, opinion; accusation, charge" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 argumentum "evidence, ground, support, proof; a logical argument," 源自 arguere "to argue" （参见 argue). Sense passed through "subject of contention" to "a quarrel," a sense formerly attached to argumentation.

example.en: His argument in favor of stricter regulations was well supported by data.
example.zh: 他支持更严格法规的论点有充分的数据支撑。

definitionLines: vi. 出现，发生；（from） 由…• 引起，由……产生
entries.definition: vi. 出现，发生；（from） 由…• 引起，由……产生
entries.etymology: Old English arisan "to get up, rise; spring from, originate; spring up, ascend" (cognate with Old Saxon arisan, Gothic urreisan), from a- (1) "of" + rise (v.). Mostly replaced by rise except in reference to circumstances. Related: Arising; arose; arisen.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 arisan "to get up, rise; spring from, originate; spring up, ascend" (与 … 同源 古撒克逊语 arisan, Gothic urreisan), 源自 a- (1) "of" + rise （动）. Mostly replaced by rise except in reference to circumstances. 同源词：Arising; arose; arisen.

example.en: Disputes often arise when partners fail to put agreements in writing.
example.zh: 当合作伙伴未能将协议书面化时，纠纷往往由此产生。

entries.etymology:
mid-13c., arsmetike, from Old French arsmetique (12c.), from Latin arithmetica, from Greek arithmetike (tekhne) "(the) counting (art)," fem. of arithmetikos "of or for reckoning, arithmetical," from arithmos "number, counting, amount," from PIE root *re(i)- "to reason, count" (source also of Old English, Old High German rim "number;" Old Irish rim "number," dorimu "I count;" Latin ritus "religious custom;" see read).

Originally in English also arsmetrik, on folk etymology from Medieval Latin ars metrica; spelling corrected early 16c. Replaced native tælcræft, literally "tell-craft."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, arsmetike, 源自 古法语 arsmetique (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 arithmetica, 源自 希腊语 arithmetike (tekhne) "(the) counting (art)," fem. of arithmetikos "of or for reckoning, arithmetical," 源自 arithmos "number, counting, amount," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *re(i)- "to reason, count" (source also of 古英语, 古高地德语 rim "number;" Old 爱尔兰语 rim "number," dorimu "I count;" 拉丁语 ritus "religious custom;" 参见 read). Originally in English also arsmetrik, on folk etymology 源自 中古拉丁语 ars metrica; spelling corrected 16 世纪初 Replaced 本族 tælcræft, 字面义为 "tell-craft."

entries.definition: n. 手臂，臂状物；（pl.）武器 vt. 武装，装备 armo（u）r n.装甲；盔甲
entries.etymology: "to furnish with weapons," c. 1200, from Old French armer or directly from Latin armare, from arma (see arm (n.2)). Related: Armed; arming.
entries.etymologyZh: "to furnish with weapons," 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 armer or 直接源自 拉丁语 armare, 源自 arma （参见 arm (n.2)). 同源词：Armed; arming.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "armed expedition," from Old French armée (14c.) "armed troop, armed expedition," from Medieval Latin armata "armed force," from Latin armata, fem. of armatus "armed, equipped, in arms," past participle of armare "to arm," literally "act of arming," related to arma "tools, arms" (see arm (n.2)). Originally used of expeditions on sea or land; the specific meaning "land force" first recorded 1786. Transferred meaning "host, multitude" is c. 1500.

The Old English words were here (still preserved in derivatives like harrier), from PIE *kor- "people, crowd;" and fierd, with an original sense of "expedition," from faran "travel." In spite of etymology, in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, here generally meant "invading Vikings" and fierd was used for the local militias raised to fight them.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "armed expedition," 源自 古法语 armée (14 世纪) "armed troop, armed expedition," 源自 中古拉丁语 armata "armed force," 源自 拉丁语 armata, fem. of armatus "armed, equipped, in arms," 为 … 的过去分词 armare "to arm," 字面义为 "act of arming," related to arma "tools, arms" （参见 arm (n.2)). Originally used of expeditions on sea or land; the specific 意为 "land force" 首见于 1786 年. Transferred 意为 "host, multitude" is 约 1500 年. The 古英语 words were here (still preserved in derivatives like harrier), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kor- "people, crowd;" and fierd, with an original 语义 "expedition," 源自 faran "travel." In spite of etymology, in the 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 Chronicle, here generally meant "invading Vikings" and fierd was used for the local militias raised to fight them.

example.en: The general commanded his army to advance at dawn.
example.zh: 将军命令他的军队在黎明时前进。

definitionLines: ad. 周围，在附近；到处；大约
prep. 在……周围，围着；在…… 各地
entries.definition: ad. 周围，在附近；到处；大约 prep. 在……周围，围着；在…… 各地
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "in circumference," from phrase on round. Rare before 1600. In sense of "here and there with no fixed direction" it is 1776, American English (properly about). Of time, from 1888. To have been around "gained worldly experience" is from 1927, U.S. colloquial.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "in circumference," 源自 phrase on round. Rare 1600 年之前. In 语义 "here and there with no fixed direction" it is 1776 年, American English (properly about). Of time, 自 1888 年起. To have been around "gained worldly experience" 始于 1927 年, U.S. 口语.

example.en: Several coffee shops are scattered around the university campus for students to study in.
example.zh: 校园里散布着几家供学生学习的咖啡店。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "awaken" (transitive), from a- (1) "on" + rouse. Related: Aroused; arousing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "awaken" (transitive), 源自 a- (1) "on" + rouse. 同源词：Aroused; arousing.

definitionLines: vt. 整理，布置；安排，筹备
entries.definition: vt. 整理，布置；安排，筹备
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "draw up a line of battle," from Old French arengier (12c.), from a- "to" (see ad-) + rangier "set in a row" (Modern French ranger), from rang "rank," from Frankish *hring (see rank (n.)).

A rare word until the meaning generalized to "to place things in order" c. 1780-1800. Musical sense of "adapt for other instruments or voices" is from 1808. Related: Arranged; arranging. Arranged marriage attested from 1854.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "draw up a line of battle," 源自 古法语 arengier (12 世纪), 源自 a- "to" （参见 ad-) + rangier "set in a row" (现代法语 ranger), 源自 rang "rank," 源自 Frankish *hring （参见 rank （名）). A rare word until the 意为 generalized to "to place things in order" 约 1780 年-1800 年. Musical 语义 "adapt for other instruments or voices" 始于 1808 年. 同源词：Arranged; arranging. Arranged marriage attested 自 1854 年起.

example.en: The team manager will arrange travel and accommodation for all participants.
example.zh: 团队经理将为所有参与者安排交通和住宿。

definitionLines: n. 安排，准备工作；整理，布置
entries.definition: n. 安排，准备工作；整理，布置
entries.etymology: 1727, from French arrangement, from arranger "arrange" (see arrange).
entries.etymologyZh: 1727 年, 源自 法语 arrangement, 源自 arranger "arrange" （参见 arrange).

example.en: The logistics team made careful arrangements for shipping the fragile goods overseas.
example.zh: 物流团队为将易碎货物运往海外做了周密的安排。

entries.definition: n. 排列，列阵；衣服 vt. 排列，部署；打扮
entries.etymology: early 14c., from stem of Old French areer "to put in order," from Vulgar Latin *ar-redare (source of Italian arredare), from Latin ad- "to" (see ad-) + Frankish *ræd- "ready" or some cognate Germanic source, from Proto-Germanic *raidjan "to place in order" (source also of Gothic garadis, Old English geræde "ready;" see ready (adj.)). Related: Arrayed; arraying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 stem of 古法语 areer "to put in order," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *ar-redare (source of 意大利语 arredare), 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + Frankish *ræd- "ready" or some 同源 日耳曼语 source, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *raidjan "to place in order" (source also of Gothic garadis, 古英语 geræde "ready;" 参见 ready （形）). 同源词：Arrayed; arraying.

example.en: The store displayed an impressive array of locally produced cheeses and wines.
example.zh: 这家店展示了一系列令人印象深刻的本地产奶酪和葡萄酒。

entries.etymology: "to cause to stop," also "to detain legally," late 14c., from Old French arester "to stay, stop" (Modern French arrêter), from Vulgar Latin *arrestare (source also of Italian arrestare, Spanish and Portuguese arrestar), from ad- "to" (see ad-) + Latin restare "to stop, remain behind, stay back" (see rest (n.2)). Figurative sense of "to catch and hold" (the attention, etc.) is from 1814.
entries.etymologyZh: "to cause to stop," also "to detain legally," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 arester "to stay, stop" (现代法语 arrêter), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *arrestare (source also of 意大利语 arrestare, 西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 arrestar), 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + 拉丁语 restare "to stop, remain behind, stay back" （参见 rest (n.2)). Figurative 语义 "to catch and hold" (the attention, etc.) 始于 1814 年.

example.en: The police made several arrest following the robbery.
example.zh: 警方在抢劫案发生后进行了数次逮捕。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of coming to land at the end of a voyage by sea, disembarkation," from Anglo-French arrivaille, from Old French arriver "to come to land" (see arrive). Arrivage (late 14c.) also was used.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of coming to land at the end of a voyage by sea, disembarkation," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 arrivaille, 源自 古法语 arriver "to come to land" （参见 arrive). Arrivage (14 世纪晚期) also was used.

example.en: The arrival of spring brings warmer temperatures and longer days.
example.zh: 春天的到来带来了更温暖的气温和更长的白昼。

definitionLines: vi. 到来，到达；（at）达成，得出
entries.definition: vi. 到来，到达；（at）达成，得出
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "reach land, reach the end of a journey by sea," from Anglo-French ariver, Old French ariver "to come to land" (11c.), from Vulgar Latin *arripare "to touch the shore," from Latin ad ripam "to the shore," from ad "to" (see ad-) + ripa "shore" (see riparian). The original notion is of coming ashore after a long voyage. Of journeys other than by sea, from late 14c. Sense of "to come to a position or state of mind" is from late 14c. Related: Arrived; arriving.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "reach land, reach the end of a journey by sea," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 ariver, 古法语 ariver "to come to land" (11 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *arripare "to touch the shore," 源自 拉丁语 ad ripam "to the shore," 源自 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + ripa "shore" （参见 riparian). The original notion is of coming ashore after a long voyage. Of journeys other than by sea, 源自 14 世纪晚期 义为 "to come to a position or state of mind" 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Arrived; arriving.

example.en: After a twelve-hour delay, the exhausted passengers finally arrived at the airport.
example.zh: 经过十二个小时的延误，疲惫不堪的乘客终于抵达了机场。

entries.etymology:
early 14c., from Old English arwan, earlier earh "arrow," possibly borrowed from Old Norse ör (genitive örvar), from Proto-Germanic *arkhwo (source also of Gothic arhwanza), from PIE root *arku- "bow and/or arrow," source of Latin arcus (see arc (n.)). The ground sense would be "the thing belonging to the bow," perhaps a superstitious avoidance of the actual name. Meaning "a mark like an arrow in cartography, etc." is from 1834.

A rare word in Old English, where more common words for "arrow" were stræl (cognate with the word still common in Slavic, once prevalent in Germanic, too; meaning related to "flash, streak") and fla, flan, from Old Norse (the -n perhaps mistaken for a plural inflection), a North Germanic word, perhaps originally with the sense of "splinter." Stræl disappeared by 1200; fla became flo in early Middle English and lingered in Scottish until after 1500.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古英语 arwan, earlier earh "arrow," possibly 借自 古北欧语 ör (属格 örvar), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *arkhwo (source also of Gothic arhwanza), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *arku- "bow and/or arrow," source of 拉丁语 arcus （参见 arc （名）). The ground sense would be "the thing belonging to the bow," 或许 a superstitious avoidance of the actual name. 义为 "a mark like an arrow in cartography, etc." 始于 1834 年. A rare word in 古英语, where more common words for "arrow" were stræl (与 … 同源 the word still common in Slavic, once prevalent in 日耳曼语, too; 意为 related to "flash, streak") and fla, flan, 源自 古北欧语 (the -n 或许 mistaken for a plural inflection), a North 日耳曼语 word, 或许 原义为 with the 语义 "splinter." Stræl disappeared 截至 1200 年; fla became flo in early 中古英语 and lingered in 苏格兰语 until after 1500 年.

example.en: Follow the arrow on the sign to find the nearest emergency exit.
example.zh: 按照标志上的箭头指示找到最近的紧急出口。

definitionLines: n. 艺术，美术；技术，技艺； （pl.）文科
entries.definition: n. 艺术，美术；技术，技艺； （pl.）文科
entries.etymology:
early 13c., "skill as a result of learning or practice," from Old French art (10c.), from Latin artem (nominative ars) "work of art; practical skill; a business, craft," from PIE *ar-ti- (source also of Sanskrit rtih "manner, mode;" Greek arti "just," artios "complete, suitable," artizein "to prepare;" Latin artus "joint;" Armenian arnam "make;" German art "manner, mode"), from root *ar- "fit together, join" (see arm (n.1)).

In Middle English usually with a sense of "skill in scholarship and learning" (c. 1300), especially in the seven sciences, or liberal arts. This sense remains in Bachelor of Arts, etc. Meaning "human workmanship" (as opposed to nature) is from late 14c. Sense of "cunning and trickery" first attested c. 1600. Meaning "skill in creative arts" is first recorded 1610s; especially of painting, sculpture, etc., from 1660s. Broader sense of the word remains in artless.

Fine arts, "those which appeal to the mind and the imagination" first recorded 1767. Expression art for art's sake (1824) translates French l'art pour l'art. First record of art critic is from 1847. Arts and crafts "decorative design and handcraft" first attested in the Arts and Crafts Exhibition Society, founded in London, 1888.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "skill as a result of learning or practice," 源自 古法语 art (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 artem (主格 ars) "work of art; practical skill; a business, craft," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ar-ti- (source also of 梵语 rtih "manner, mode;" 希腊语 arti "just," artios "complete, suitable," artizein "to prepare;" 拉丁语 artus "joint;" Armenian arnam "make;" 德语 art "manner, mode"), 源自 root *ar- "fit together, join" （参见 arm (n.1)). In 中古英语 通常 with a 语义 "skill in scholarship and learning" (约 1300 年), 尤指 in the seven sciences，或liberal arts. This sense remains in Bachelor of Arts, etc. 义为 "human workmanship" (as opposed to nature) 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "cunning and trickery" 最早见于 约 1600 年. 义为 "skill in creative arts" is 首见于 1610 年代; 尤指 of painting, sculpture, etc., 源自 1660 年代. Broader 语义 the word remains in artless. Fine arts, "those which appeal to the mind and the imagination" 首见于 1767 年. Expression art for art's sake (1824) translates French l'art pour l'art. First record of art critic 始于 1847 年. Arts and crafts "decorative design and handcraft" 最早见于 in the Arts and Crafts Exhibition Society, founded in London, 1888 年.

example.en: The museum's collection of modern art attracts thousands of visitors each year.
example.zh: 这座博物馆的现代艺术藏品每年吸引数千名游客。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "separate parts of anything written" (such as the statements in the Apostles' Creed, the clauses of a statute or contract), from Old French article (13c.), from Latin articulus, diminutive of artus "a joint" (from PIE *ar-tu-, from *ar- "to fit together;" (see arm (n.1)).

Meaning extended to "a small division," then generalized to "item, thing." Older sense preserved in Articles of War "military regulations" (1716) and Articles of Confederation (U.S. history). Meaning "literary composition in a journal, etc." (independent, but part of a larger work) first recorded 1712. Meaning "piece of property" (clothing, etc.) first attested 1796, originally in rogue's cant.

Meaning extended to "a small division," then generalized to "item, thing." Older sense preserved in Articles of War "military regulations" (1716) and Articles of Confederation (U.S. history). definitionLines: a. 人工的，人造的；人的，做 作的
entries.definition: a. 人工的，人造的；人的，做 作的
entries.etymology: late 14c., in the phrase artificial day "part of the day from sunrise to sunset," from Old French artificial, from Latin artificialis "of or belonging to art," from artificium (see artifice). Meaning "made by man" (opposite of natural) is from early 15c. Applied to things that are not natural, whether real (artificial light) or not (artificial flowers). Artificial insemination dates from 1897. Artificial intelligence "the science and engineering of making intelligent machines" was coined in 1956.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in the phrase artificial day "part of the day from sunrise to sunset," 源自 古法语 artificial, 源自 拉丁语 artificialis "of or belonging to art," 源自 artificium （参见 artifice). 义为 "made by man" (opposite of natural) 始于 15 世纪初 Applied to things that are not natural, whether real (artificial light) or not (artificial flowers). Artificial insemination dates 自 1897 年起. Artificial intelligence "the science and engineering of making intelligent machines" was coined 于 1956 年.

example.en: The park installed artificial flowers that glow at night.

definitionLines: a. 艺术（家）的，美术（家）的
entries.definition: n. 艺术家，美术家 artistic（al） a. 艺术（家）的，美术（家）的
entries.etymology:
1580s, "one who cultivates one of the fine arts," from Middle French artiste (14c.), from Italian artista, from Medieval Latin artista, from Latin ars (see art (n.)).

Originally used especially of the arts presided over by the Muses (history, poetry, comedy, tragedy, music, dancing, astronomy), but also used 17c. for "one skilled in any art or craft" (including professors, surgeons, craftsmen, cooks). Now especially of "one who practices the arts of design or visual arts" (a sense first attested 1747).
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "one who cultivates one of the fine arts," 源自 中古法语 artiste (14 世纪), 源自 意大利语 artista, 源自 中古拉丁语 artista, 源自 拉丁语 ars （参见 art （名）). Originally used 尤指 of the arts presided over by the Muses (history, poetry, comedy, tragedy, music, dancing, astronomy), but also used 17 世纪 for "one skilled in any art or craft" (including professors, surgeons, craftsmen, cooks). Now 尤指 of "one who practices the arts of design or visual arts" (a sense 最早见于 1747 年).

example.en: The artist spent three years painting the mural on the city wall.
example.zh: 这位艺术家花了三年时间在城墙上绘制这幅壁画。

definitionLines: conj. 当/在……时候；如…… 一样；由于，因沩

entries.etymology: c. 1200, worn-down form of Old English alswa "quite so" (see also), fully established by c. 1400. Equivalent to so; any distinction in use is purely idiomatic. Related to German als "as, than," from Middle High German also. Phrase as well "just as much" is recorded from late 15c.; the phrase also can imply "as well as not," "as well as anything else." Interjection of incredulity as if! (i.e. "as if that really could happen") is attested from 1995, an exact duplication of Latin quasi.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, worn-down form of 古英语 alswa "quite so" （亦参见), fully established by 约 1400 年. Equivalent to so; any distinction in use is purely idiomatic. Interjection of incredulity as if! (i.e. "as if that really could happen") 见于 1995 年, an exact duplication of 拉丁语 quasi.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin ascendere "to climb up, mount, ascend," figuratively "to rise, reach," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + scandere "to climb" (see scan (v.)). Also in 15c. used with a sense "to mount (a female) for copulation." Related: Ascended; ascending. An Old English word for it was stigan.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 ascendere "to climb up, mount, ascend," figuratively "to rise, reach," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + scandere "to climb" （参见 scan （动）). Also in 15 世纪 used with a sense "to mount (a female) for copulation." 同源词：Ascended; ascending. An 古英语 word for it was stigan.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to inform, to give assurance," from Anglo-French acerteiner, Old French acertener "to assure, certify" (13c.), from a "to" (see ad-) + certain "sure, assured" (see certain). Modern meaning of "find out for sure by experiment or investigation" is first attested 1794. Related: Ascertained; ascertaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to inform, to give assurance," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 acerteiner, 古法语 acertener "to assure, certify" (13 世纪), 源自 a "to" （参见 ad-) + certain "sure, assured" （参见 certain). 现代 意为 of "find out for sure by experiment or investigation" is 最早见于 1794 年. 同源词：Ascertained; ascertaining.

entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, ascrive, 源自 古法语 ascrivre "to inscribe; attribute, impute," 源自 拉丁语 ascribere "to write in, to add to in a writing," 源自 ad- "to" （参见 ad-) + scribere "to write" （参见 script （名）). Spelling restored by 16 世纪 同源词：Ascribed; ascribing.

late 14c., "inhabitant of Asia (Minor)," from Latin Asianus (adjective and noun, "belonging to the province of Asia;" "an inhabitant of Asia"), from Greek Asianos, from Asia (see Asia). Ousted Asiatic as the preferred term in Britain c. 1950.

definitionLines: v. 问，询问；要求，请求；邀请， 约请
entries.definition: v. 问，询问；要求，请求；邀请， 约请
entries.etymology:
Old English ascian "ask, call for an answer; make a request," from earlier ahsian, from Proto-Germanic *aiskon (source also of Old Saxon escon, Old Frisian askia "request, demand, ask," Middle Dutch eiscen, Dutch eisen "to ask, demand," Old High German eiscon "to ask (a question)," German heischen "to ask, demand"), from PIE *ais- "to wish, desire" (source also of Sanskrit icchati "seeks, desires," Armenian aic "investigation," Old Church Slavonic iskati "to seek," Lithuanian ieškau "to seek").

Form in English influenced by a Scandinavian cognate (such as Danish æske; the Old English would have evolved by normal sound changes into ash, esh, which was a Midlands and southwestern England dialect form). Modern dialectal ax is as old as Old English acsian and was an accepted literary variant until c. 1600. Related: Asked; asking. Old English also had fregnan/frignan which carried more directly the sense of "question, inquire," and is from PIE root *prek-, the common source of words for "ask" in most Indo-European languages (see pray). If you ask me "in my opinion" is attested from 1910. Asking price is attested from 1755.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ascian "ask, call for an answer; make a request," 源自 earlier ahsian, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aiskon (source also of 古撒克逊语 escon, 古弗里西语 askia "request, demand, ask," Middle 荷兰语 eiscen, 荷兰语 eisen "to ask, demand," 古高地德语 eiscon "to ask (a question)," 德语 heischen "to ask, demand"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ais- "to wish, desire" (source also of 梵语 icchati "seeks, desires," Armenian aic "investigation," Old Church Slavonic iskati "to seek," Lithuanian ieškau "to seek"). Form in English influenced by a Scandinavian 同源 (such as Danish æske; the 古英语 would have evolved by normal sound changes into ash, esh, which was a Midlands and southwestern England dialect form). 现代 方言 ax is as old as 古英语 acsian and was an accepted literary variant until 约 1600 年. 同源词：Asked; asking. 古英语 also had fregnan/frignan which carried more directly the 语义 "question, inquire," and 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *prek-, the common source of words for "ask" in most Indo-European languages （参见 pray). If you ask me "in my opinion" 见于 1910 年. Asking price 见于 1755 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, aslepe, o slæpe, from Old English on slæpe (see sleep). The parallel form on sleep continued until c. 1550. Of limbs, "numb through stoppage of circulation," from late 14c. Meaning "inattentive, off guard" is from mid-14c.

entries.etymology: late 14c., an astrological term, "relative position of the planets as they appear from earth" (i.e., how they "look at" one another); later also "way of viewing things," from Latin aspectus "a seeing, looking at, sight, view, countenance, appearance," from past participle of aspicere "to look at," from ad- "to" (see ad-) + specere "to look" (see scope (n.1)). Meaning "the look one wears, the appearance of things" attested by early 15c.

entries.etymology: 1610s, from past participle stem of Medieval Latin assassinare (see assassin). "Assassinate means to kill wrongfully by surprise, suddenly, or by secret assault" [Century Dictionary]. Of reputations, characters, etc., from 1620s. Related: Assassinated; assassinating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 past participle stem of 中古拉丁语 assassinare （参见 assassin). "Assassinate means to kill wrongfully by surprise, suddenly, or by secret assault" [Century Dictionary]. Of reputations, characters, etc., 源自 1620 年代. 同源词：Assassinated; assassinating.

entries.definition: n. 袭击；攻击 vt. 袭击；攻击 vi. 袭击；动武
entries.etymology: late 14c., earlier asaut (c. 1200), from Old French asaut, assaut "an attack, an assault, attacking forces" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *adsaltus "attack, assault," from ad "to" (see ad-) + Latin saltus "a leap," from salire "to leap, spring" (see assail). In law by 1580s; historically, assault includes menacing words or actions; battery is an actual blow.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, earlier asaut (约 1200 年), 源自 古法语 asaut, assaut "an attack, an assault, attacking forces" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *adsaltus "attack, assault," 源自 ad "to" （参见 ad-) + 拉丁语 saltus "a leap," 源自 salire "to leap, spring" （参见 assail). In law by 1580 年代; historically, assault includes menacing words or actions; battery is an actual blow.

example.en: He was charged with assault for attacking the officer.
