example.en: Burning fossil fuels releases large amounts of carbon dioxide into the air.
example.zh: 燃烧化石燃料会向空气中释放大量二氧化碳。

entries.etymology:
c. 1600, from French cardiaque (14c.) or directly from Latin cardiacus, from Greek kardiakos "pertaining to the heart," from kardia "heart," from PIE root *kerd- (1) "heart" (see heart (n.)). Cardiac arrest is attested from 1950.

Greek kardia also could mean "stomach" and Latin cardiacus "pertaining to the stomach." This terminology continues somewhat in modern medicine. Confusion of heart and nearby digestive organs also is reflected in Breton kalon "heart," from Old French cauldun "bowels," and English heartburn for "indigestion."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 cardiaque (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 cardiacus, 源自 希腊语 kardiakos "pertaining to the heart," 源自 kardia "heart," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kerd- (1) "heart" （参见 heart （名）). Cardiac arrest 见于 1950 年. 希腊语 kardia also could mean "stomach" and 拉丁语 cardiacus "pertaining to the stomach." This terminology continues somewhat in modern medicine. Confusion of heart and nearby digestive organs also is reflected in Breton kalon "heart," 源自 古法语 cauldun "bowels," and English heartburn for "indigestion."

definitionLines: n. 注意，小心；挂念；照顾，照料
vi. 关心，计较；喜欢，愿意
entries.definition: n. 注意，小心；挂念；照顾，照料 vi. 关心，计较；喜欢，愿意
entries.etymology: Old English caru, cearu "sorrow, anxiety, grief," also "burdens of mind; serious mental attention," from Proto-Germanic *karo "lament; grief, care" (see care (v.)). Different sense evolution in related Dutch karig "scanty, frugal," German karg "stingy, scanty." The sense development in English is from "cry" to "lamentation" to "grief." Meaning "charge, oversight, protection" is attested c. 1400, the sense in care of in addressing. To take care of "take in hand, do" is from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 caru, cearu "sorrow, anxiety, grief," also "burdens of mind; serious mental attention," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *karo "lament; grief, care" （参见 care （动）). Different sense evolution in related 荷兰语 karig "scanty, frugal," 德语 karg "stingy, scanty." The sense development in English 始于 "cry" to "lamentation" to "grief." 义为 "charge, oversight, protection" is attested 约 1400 年, the sense in care of in addressing. To take care of "take in hand, do" 始于 1580 年代.

example.en: Every parent should care deeply about the physical safety of their children.
example.zh: 每位家长都应该深切关心孩子的人身安全。

entries.etymology: Old English cearful "mournful, sad," also "full of care or woe; anxious; full of concern" (for someone or something), thus "applying attention, painstaking, circumspect;" from care (n.) + -ful.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cearful "mournful, sad," also "full of care or woe; anxious; full of concern" (for someone or something), thus "applying attention, painstaking, circumspect;" 源自 care （名） + -ful.

example.en: Be careful not to spill the paint on the carpet.
example.zh: 小心别把油漆洒在地毯上。

entries.etymology: Old English carleas "free from anxiety; unconcerned," from care (n.) + -less; a compound probably from Proto-Germanic. Original senses extinct by mid-17c.; main modern meaning "not paying attention, inattentive, not taking due care" is first recorded 1560s (in carelessly).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 carleas "free from anxiety; unconcerned," 源自 care （名） + -less; a 复合词 可能 源自 原始日耳曼语. Original senses extinct by 17 世纪中期; main modern 意为 "not paying attention, inattentive, not taking due care" is 首见于 1560 年代 (in carelessly).

entries.etymology: 1650s, "freight loaded on a ship," from Spanish cargo "burden," from cargar "to load, impose taxes," from Late Latin carricare "to load on a cart" (see charge (v.)). South Pacific cargo cult is from 1949. Cargo pants attested from 1977.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "freight loaded on a ship," 源自 西班牙语 cargo "burden," 源自 cargar "to load, impose taxes," 源自 晚期拉丁语 carricare "to load on a cart" （参见 charge （动）). South Pacific cargo cult 始于 1949 年. Cargo pants attested 自 1977 年起.

example.en: The ship's cargo included machinery and food supplies.
example.zh: 这艘船的货物包括机械和食品物资。

definitionLines: a. 有同情心的；表示或感到关 怀或关心的
entries.definition: a. 有同情心的；表示或感到关 怀或关心的
entries.etymology: "compassionate," 1966, present participle adjective from care (v.). Related: Caringly; caringness.
entries.etymologyZh: "compassionate," 1966 年, present participle 形容词 源自 care （动）. 同源词：Caringly; caringness.

entries.etymology:
"wood-worker," c. 1300 (attested from early 12c. as a surname), from Anglo-French carpenter, Old North French carpentier (Old French and Modern French charpentier), from Late Latin (artifex) carpentarius "wagon (maker)," from Latin carpentum "wagon, two-wheeled carriage, cart," from Gaulish, from Old Celtic *carpentom (compare Old Irish carpat, Gaelic carbad "carriage"), probably related to Gaulish karros (see car).

Also from the Late Latin word are Spanish carpintero, Italian carpentiero. Replaced Old English treowwyrhta, literally "tree-wright." German Zimmermann "carpenter" is from Old High German zimbarman, from zimbar "wood for building, timber," cognate with Old Norse timbr (see timber). First record of carpenter bee is from 1844. A carpenter's rule (1690s) is foldable, suitable for carrying in the pocket.
entries.etymologyZh: "wood-worker," 约 1300 年 (attested 源自 12 世纪初 作为 surname), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 carpenter, Old North 法语 carpentier (古法语 and 现代法语 charpentier), 源自 晚期拉丁语 (artifex) carpentarius "wagon (maker)," 源自 拉丁语 carpentum "wagon, two-wheeled carriage, cart," 源自 Gaulish, 源自 Old Celtic *carpentom (对比 Old 爱尔兰语 carpat, Gaelic carbad "carriage"), 可能 related to Gaulish karros （参见 car). Also 源自 晚期拉丁语 word are 西班牙语 carpintero, 意大利语 carpentiero. Replaced 古英语 treowwyrhta, 字面义为 "tree-wright." 德语 Zimmermann "carpenter" 始于 古高地德语 zimbarman, 源自 zimbar "wood for building, timber," 与 … 同源 古北欧语 timbr （参见 timber). First record of carpenter bee 始于 1844 年. A carpenter's rule (1690 年代) is foldable, suitable for carrying in the pocket.

entries.etymology:
late 13c., "coarse cloth;" mid-14c., "tablecloth, bedspread;" from Old French carpite "heavy decorated cloth, carpet," from Medieval Latin or Old Italian carpita "thick woolen cloth," probably from Latin carpere "to card, pluck," probably so called because it was made from unraveled, shreded, "plucked" fabric; from PIE *kerp- "to gather, pluck, harvest" (see harvest (n.)). Meaning shifted 15c. to floor coverings.

From 16c.-19c. as an adjective often with a tinge of contempt, when used of men (as in carpet-knight, 1570s) by association with luxury, ladies' boudoirs, and drawing rooms. On the carpet "summoned for reprimand" is 1900, U.S. colloquial (but compare carpet (v.) "call (someone) to be reprimanded," 1823, British servants' slang). To sweep or push something under the carpet in the figurative sense is first recorded 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "coarse cloth;" 14 世纪中期, "tablecloth, bedspread;" 源自 古法语 carpite "heavy decorated cloth, carpet," 源自 中古拉丁语 or Old 意大利语 carpita "thick woolen cloth," 可能 源自 拉丁语 carpere "to card, pluck," 可能 so called because it was made 源自 unraveled, shreded, "plucked" fabric; 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kerp- "to gather, pluck, harvest" （参见 harvest （名）). 义为 shifted 15 世纪 to floor coverings. From 16 世纪-19 世纪 作形容词时 常 with a tinge of contempt, when used of men (as in carpet-knight, 1570 年代) by association with luxury, ladies' boudoirs, and drawing rooms. On the carpet "summoned for reprimand" is 1900, U.S. colloquial (but compare carpet (v.) "call (someone) to be reprimanded," 1823, British servants' 俚语). To sweep or push something under the carpet in the figurative sense is 首见于 1953 年.

example.en: The living room had a thick red carpet covering the floor.
example.zh: 客厅地板上铺着一块厚厚的红色地毯。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of carrying, means of conveyance; wheeled vehicles collectively," from Anglo-French and Old North French cariage "cart, carriage, action of transporting in a vehicle" (Old French charriage, Modern French charriage), from carier "to carry" (see carry (v.)). Meaning "individual wheeled vehicle" is c. 1400; specific sense of "horse-drawn, wheeled vehicle for hauling people" first attested 1706; extended to railway cars by 1830. Meaning "way of carrying one's body" is 1590s. Carriage-house attested from 1761.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of carrying, means of conveyance; wheeled vehicles collectively," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 and Old North 法语 cariage "cart, carriage, action of transporting in a vehicle" (古法语 charriage, 现代法语 charriage), 源自 carier "to carry" （参见 carry （动）). 义为 "individual wheeled vehicle" is 约 1400 年; specific 语义 "horse-drawn, wheeled vehicle for hauling people" 最早见于 1706 年; extended to railway cars 截至 1830 年. 义为 "way of carrying one's body" is 1590 年代. Carriage-house attested 自 1761 年起.

example.en: The royal family arrived at the ceremony in an elegant horse-drawn carriage.
example.zh: 王室成员乘坐优雅的马车抵达了典礼现场。

definitionLines: n. 搬运人；携带者；运载工具
entries.definition: n. 搬运人；携带者；运载工具
entries.etymology: late 14c., agent noun from carry (v.). Meaning "person or animal that carries and disseminates infection without suffering obvious disease" is from 1899; genetic sense is 1933. As a short form of aircraft carrier it dates from 1917. Carrier pigeon is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, agent 名词 源自 carry （动）. 义为 "person or animal that carries and disseminates infection without suffering obvious disease" 始于 1899 年; genetic sense is 1933 年. 作为 short form of aircraft carrier it dates 自 1917 年起. Carrier pigeon 始于 1640 年代.

example.en: The airline is now the largest carrier of international passengers in Asia.
example.zh: 这家航空公司现在是亚洲最大的国际旅客运输商。

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French carrotte, from Latin carota, from Greek karoton "carrot," probably from PIE *kre-, from root *ker- (1) "horn, head" (see horn (n.)); so called for its horn-like shape. Originally white-rooted and a medicinal plant to the ancients, who used it as an aphrodisiac and to prevent poisoning. Not entirely distinguished from parsnips in ancient times. Reintroduced in Europe by Arabs c. 1100. The orange carrot, which existed perhaps as early as 6c., probably began as a mutation of the Asian purple carrot and was cultivated into the modern edible plant 16c.-17c. in the Netherlands. Thus the word is used as a color name but not before 1670s in English, originally of red hair.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 carrotte, 源自 拉丁语 carota, 源自 希腊语 karoton "carrot," 可能 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kre-, 源自 root *ker- (1) "horn, head" （参见 horn （名）); so called for its horn-like shape. Originally white-rooted and a medicinal plant to the ancients, who used it 作为 aphrodisiac and to prevent poisoning. Not entirely distinguished 源自 parsnips in ancient times. Reintroduced in Europe by Arabs 约 1100 年. The orange carrot, which existed 或许 as early as 6 世纪, 可能 began 作为 mutation of the Asian purple carrot and was cultivated into the modern edible plant 16 世纪-17 世纪 in the Netherlands. Thus the word is used 作为 color name but not before 1670 年代 in English, 原义为 of red hair.

definitionLines: vt. 搬运，运送，携带；传送， 传播
entries.definition: vt. 搬运，运送，携带；传送， 传播
entries.etymology:
early 14c., from Anglo-French carier "to transport in a vehicle" or Old North French carrier "to cart, carry" (Modern French charrier), from Gallo-Roman *carrizare, from Late Latin carricare, from Latin carrum (see car).

Meaning "take by force" is from 1580s. Sense of "gain victory in an election" is from 1610s. Of sound, "to be heard at a distance" by 1896. Carrying capacity is attested from 1836. Carry on "continue to advance" is from 1640s; carryings-on "questionable doings" is from 1660s. Carry-castle (1590s) was an old descriptive term for an elephant.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 carier "to transport in a vehicle" or Old North 法语 carrier "to cart, carry" (现代法语 charrier), 源自 Gallo-Roman *carrizare, 源自 晚期拉丁语 carricare, 源自 拉丁语 carrum （参见 car). 义为 "take by force" 始于 1580 年代. 义为 "gain victory in an election" 始于 1610 年代. Of sound, "to be heard at a distance" 截至 1896 年. Carrying capacity 见于 1836 年. Carry on "continue to advance" 始于 1640 年代; carryings-on "questionable doings" 始于 1660 年代. Carry-castle (1590 年代) was an old descriptive term for an elephant.

example.en: The pipeline was built to carry natural gas across the region.
example.zh: 这条管道建成的目的是在整个地区输送天然气。

definitionLines: n. 手推车；两轮运货马车
entries.definition: n. 手推车；两轮运货马车
entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old Norse kartr or a similar Scandinavian source, akin to and replacing Old English cræt "cart, wagon, chariot," perhaps originally "body of a cart made of wickerwork, hamper" and related to Middle Dutch cratte "woven mat, hamper," Dutch krat "basket," Old English cradol (see cradle (n.)). To put the cart before the horse in a figurative sense is from 1510s in those words; the image in other words dates to mid-14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古北欧语 kartr or a similar Scandinavian source, akin to and replacing 古英语 cræt "cart, wagon, chariot," 或许 原义为 "body of a cart made of wickerwork, hamper" and related to Middle 荷兰语 cratte "woven mat, hamper," 荷兰语 krat "basket," 古英语 cradol （参见 cradle （名）). To put the cart before the horse in a figurative sense 始于 1510 年代 in those words; the image in other words dates to 14 世纪中期

example.en: She loaded the groceries into the cart before heading to the checkout.
example.zh: 她在去结账之前把食品杂货装进了推车。

definitionLines: n. 卡通画，漫画；卡通片，动 画片
entries.definition: n. 卡通画，漫画；卡通片，动 画片
entries.etymology:
1670s, "a drawing on strong paper (used as a model for another work)," from French carton, from Italian cartone "strong, heavy paper, pasteboard," thus "preliminary sketches made by artists on such paper" (see carton). Extension to comical drawings in newspapers and magazines is 1843.

Also see -oon.
entries.etymologyZh: 1670 年代, "a drawing on strong paper (used as a model for another work)," 源自 法语 carton, 源自 意大利语 cartone "strong, heavy paper, pasteboard," thus "preliminary sketches made by artists on such paper" （参见 carton). Extension to comical drawings in newspapers and magazines is 1843 年. Also 参见 -oon.

example.en: As a child, he spent every Saturday morning watching his favorite cartoon on TV.
example.zh: 小时候，他每个周六早上都看他最喜欢的卡通片。

entries.definition: vt. 雕刻；切开；开创 vi. 切开；做雕刻工作
entries.etymology:
Old English ceorfan (class III strong verb; past tense cearf, past participle corfen) "to cut, cut down, slay; to carve, cut out, engrave," from West Germanic *kerfan (source also of Old Frisian kerva, Middle Dutch and Dutch kerven, German kerben "to cut, notch"), from PIE root *gerbh- "to scratch," making carve the English cognate of Greek graphein "to write," originally "to scratch" on clay tablets with a stylus.

Once extensively used, most senses now usurped by cut (v.). Meaning specialized to sculpture, meat, etc., by 16c. Related: Carved; carving. Original strong conjugation has been abandoned, but archaic carven lingers.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ceorfan (class III strong 动词; past tense cearf, past participle corfen) "to cut, cut down, slay; to carve, cut out, engrave," 源自 West 日耳曼语 *kerfan (source also of 古弗里西语 kerva, Middle 荷兰语 and 荷兰语 kerven, 德语 kerben "to cut, notch"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gerbh- "to scratch," making carve the English 同源 of 希腊语 graphein "to write," 原义为 "to scratch" on clay tablets with a stylus. Once extensively used, most senses 现在 usurped by cut （动）. 义为 specialized to sculpture, meat, etc., by 16 世纪 同源词：Carved; carving. Original strong conjugation has been abandoned, but 古旧 carven lingers.

example.en: The artist carve a beautiful dragon out of a single block of wood.
example.zh: 艺术家从一整块木头中雕刻出了一条美丽的龙。

definitionLines: n. 事实，情况；案件；病例；箱 子，盒子
entries.definition: n. 事实，情况；案件；病例；箱 子，盒子
entries.etymology: "enclose in a case," 1570s, from case (n.2). Related: Cased; casing. Meaning "examine, inspect" (usually prior to robbing) is from 1915, American English slang, perhaps from the notion of giving a place a look on all sides (compare technical case (v.) "cover the outside of a building with a different material," 1707).
entries.etymologyZh: "enclose in a case," 1570 年代, 源自 case (n.2). 同源词：Cased; casing. 义为 "examine, inspect" (通常 prior to robbing) 始于 1915 年, American English 俚语, 或源自 the 概念 giving a place a look on all sides (对比 technical case （动） "cover the outside of a building with a different material," 1707 年).

example.en: The judge reviewed every detail of the murder case carefully.
example.zh: 法官仔细审查了这起谋杀案的每一个细节。

entries.etymology:
1590s, "money box;" also "money in hand, coin," from Middle French caisse "money box" (16c.), from Provençal caissa or Italian cassa, from Latin capsa "box" (see case (n.2)); originally the money box, but the secondary sense of the money in it became sole meaning 18c. Cash crop is attested from 1831; cash flow from 1954; the mechanical cash register from 1878.

Like many financial terms in English (bankrupt, etc.), ultimately from Italian. Not related to (but influencing the form of) the colonial British cash "Indian monetary system, Chinese coin, etc.," which is from Tamil kasu, Sanskrit karsha, Sinhalese kasi.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "money box;" also "money in hand, coin," 源自 中古法语 caisse "money box" (16 世纪), 源自 Provençal caissa or 意大利语 cassa, 源自 拉丁语 capsa "box" （参见 case (n.2)); 原义为 the money box, but the secondary 语义 the money in it became sole 意为 18 世纪 Cash crop 见于 1831 年; cash flow 自 1954 年起; the mechanical cash register 自 1878 年起. Like many financial terms in English (bankrupt, etc.), 最终源自 意大利语. Not related to (but influencing the form of) the colonial British cash "Indian monetary system, Chinese coin, etc.," which 始于 Tamil kasu, 梵语 karsha, Sinhalese kasi.

example.en: The street vendor only accepted cash and refused credit cards.
example.zh: 这位街头小贩只收现金，拒绝信用卡。

entries.etymology: "person in charge of money," 1590s, from Middle French caissier "treasurer," from caisse "money box" (see cash (n.)). The immediate source of the English word might be Middle Dutch kassier.
entries.etymologyZh: "person in charge of money," 1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 caissier "treasurer," 源自 caisse "money box" （参见 cash （名）). The immediate source of the English word might be Middle 荷兰语 kassier.

entries.etymology: 1793, "little box," from French cassette, from Middle French casset, diminutive of Old North French casse "box" (see case (n.2)). Meaning "magnetic tape recorder cartridge" is from 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: 1793 年, "little box," 源自 法语 cassette, 源自 中古法语 casset, 为 … 的指小形式 Old North 法语 casse "box" （参见 case (n.2)). 义为 "magnetic tape recorder cartridge" 始于 1960 年.

entries.definition: vt. 投，掷，抛；铸造 n. 演员表
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "to throw, fling, hurl," from a Scandinavian source akin to Old Norse kasta "to throw" (cognate with Swedish kasta, Danish kaste, North Frisian kastin), of uncertain origin. Meaning "to form in a mold" is late 15c. In the sense of "warp, turn" it replaced Old English weorpan (see warp (v.)), and itself largely has been superseded now by throw, though cast still is used of fishing lines and glances. Meaning "calculate, find by reckoning; chart (a course)" is from c. 1300.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "to throw, fling, hurl," 源自 a Scandinavian source akin to 古北欧语 kasta "to throw" (与 … 同源 Swedish kasta, Danish kaste, North Frisian kastin), 来源存疑. 义为 "to form in a mold" is 15 世纪晚期 In the 语义 "warp, turn" it replaced 古英语 weorpan （参见 warp （动）), and itself largely has been superseded 现在 by throw, though cast still is used of fishing lines and glances. 义为 "calculate, find by reckoning; chart (a course)" 始于 约 1300 年.

entries.etymology:
late Old English castel "village" (this sense from a biblical usage in Vulgar Latin); later "large fortified building, stronghold," in this sense from Old North French castel (Old French chastel, 12c.; Modern French château), from Latin castellum "a castle, fort, citadel, stronghold; fortified village," diminutive of castrum "fort," from Proto-Italic *kastro- "part, share;" cognate with Old Irish cather, Welsh caer "town" (and perhaps related to castrare via notion of "cut off;" see caste). In early bibles, castle was used to translate Greek kome "village."

This word also had come to Old English as ceaster and formed the -caster and -chester in place names. Spanish alcazar "castle" is from Arabic al-qasr, from Latin castrum. Castles in Spain translates 14c. French chastel en Espaigne (the imaginary castles sometimes stood in Brie, Asia, or Albania) and probably reflects the hopes of landless knights to establish themselves abroad. The statement that an (English) man's home is his castle is from 16c.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 castel "village" (this sense 源自 a biblical usage in 通俗拉丁语); later "large fortified building, stronghold," in this sense 源自 Old North 法语 castel (古法语 chastel, 12 世纪; 现代法语 château), 源自 拉丁语 castellum "a castle, fort, citadel, stronghold; fortified village," 为 … 的指小形式 castrum "fort," 源自 Proto-Italic *kastro- "part, share;" 与 … 同源 Old 爱尔兰语 cather, Welsh caer "town" (and 或许 related to castrare 经由 概念 "cut off;" 参见 caste). In early bibles, castle was used to translate 希腊语 kome "village." This word also had come to 古英语 as ceaster and formed the -caster and -chester in place names. 西班牙语 alcazar "castle" 始于 阿拉伯语 al-qasr, 源自 拉丁语 castrum. Castles in Spain translates 14 世纪 法语 chastel en Espaigne (the imaginary castles 有时 stood in Brie, Asia，或Albania) and 可能 reflects the hopes of landless knights to establish themselves abroad. The statement that an (English) man's home is his castle 始于 16 世纪

example.en: Tourists came from afar to see the ancient castle on the hill.
example.zh: 游客们从远方赶来参观山丘上那座古老的城堡。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "subject to or produced by chance," from Middle French casuel (15c.), from Late Latin casualis "by chance," from Latin casus "chance, occasion, opportunity; accident, event" (see case (n.1)).

Of persons, in the sense of "not to be depended on, unmethodical," it is attested from 1883; meaning "showing lack of interest" is from 1916. Of clothes, "informal," from 1939. Related: Casually.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "subject to or produced by chance," 源自 中古法语 casuel (15 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 casualis "by chance," 源自 拉丁语 casus "chance, occasion, opportunity; accident, event" （参见 case (n.1)). Of persons, in the 语义 "not to be depended on, unmethodical," it 见于 1883 年; 意为 "showing lack of interest" 始于 1916 年. Of clothes, "informal," 自 1939 年起. 同源词：Casually.

example.en: They struck up a casual conversation while waiting for the bus.
example.zh: 他们在等公交车时随意地聊了起来。

definitionLines: n. 意外事故；（pl.）伤亡人员
entries.definition: n. 意外事故；（pl.）伤亡人员
entries.etymology: early 15c., "chance, accident; incidental charge," from casual (adj.) on model of royalty, penalty, etc. Casuality had some currency 16c.-17c. but is now obsolete. Meaning "losses in numbers from a military or other troop" is from late 15c. Meaning "an individual killed,  wounded, or lost in battle" is from 1844.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "chance, accident; incidental charge," 源自 casual （形） on model of royalty, penalty, etc. Casuality had some currency 16 世纪-17 世纪 but is 今废. 义为 "losses in numbers from a military or other troop" 始于 15 世纪晚期 义为 "an individual killed, wounded, or lost in battle" 始于 1844 年.

entries.definition: n. 猫 catalog（ue） n. 目录 vt.将……编人目录
entries.etymology: 1975, medical acronym for computerized axial tomography or something like it. Related: CAT scan.
entries.etymologyZh: 1975 年, medical acronym for computerized axial tomography or something like it. 同源词：CAT scan.

entries.etymology: 1530s, "reversal of what is expected" (especially a fatal turning point in a drama), from Latin catastropha, from Greek katastrophe "an overturning; a sudden end," from katastrephein "to overturn, turn down, trample on; to come to an end," from kata "down" (see cata-) + strephein "turn" (see strophe). Extension to "sudden disaster" is first recorded 1748.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "reversal of what is expected" (尤指 a fatal turning point in a drama), 源自 拉丁语 catastropha, 源自 希腊语 katastrophe "an overturning; a sudden end," 源自 katastrephein "to overturn, turn down, trample on; to come to an end," 源自 kata "down" （参见 cata-) + strephein "turn" （参见 strophe). Extension to "sudden disaster" is 首见于 1748 年.

definitionLines: vt. 捕，捉；赶上；感染，染上病； 听清楚
entries.definition: vt. 捕，捉；赶上；感染，染上病； 听清楚
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "to take, capture," from Anglo-French or Old North French cachier "catch, capture" (animals) (Old French chacier "hunt, pursue, drive (animals)," Modern French chasser "to hunt;" making it a doublet of chase (v.)), from Vulgar Latin *captiare "try to seize, chase" (also source of Spanish cazar, Italian cacciare), from Latin captare "to take, hold," frequentative of Latin capere "to take, hold" (see capable).

Senses in early Middle English also included "chase, hunt," which later went with chase (v.). Of sleep, etc., from early 14c.; of infections from 1540s; of fire from 1734 (compare Greek apto "fasten, grasp, touch," also "light, kindle, set on fire, catch on fire"). Related: Catched (obsolete); catching; caught.

Meaning "act as a catcher in baseball" recorded from 1865. To catch on "apprehend" is 1884, American English colloquial. To catch (someone's) eye is first attested 1813, in Jane Austen. Catch as catch can first attested late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "to take, capture," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 or Old North 法语 cachier "catch, capture" (animals) (古法语 chacier "hunt, pursue, drive (animals)," 现代法语 chasser "to hunt;" making it a doublet of chase （动）), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *captiare "try to seize, chase" (also source of 西班牙语 cazar, 意大利语 cacciare), 源自 拉丁语 captare "to take, hold," 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 capere "to take, hold" （参见 capable). Senses in early 中古英语 also included "chase, hunt," which later went with chase （动）. Of sleep, etc., 源自 14 世纪初; of infections 源自 1540 年代; of fire 自 1734 年起 (对比 希腊语 apto "fasten, grasp, touch," also "light, kindle, set on fire, catch on fire"). 同源词：Catched (已废); catching; caught. 义为 "act as a catcher in baseball" recorded 自 1865 年起. To catch on "apprehend" is 1884 年, American English 口语. To catch (someone's) eye is 最早见于 1813 年, in Jane Austen. Catch as catch can 最早见于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: She forgot to cover her mouth and caught a bad cold.
example.zh: 她忘记捂住嘴，结果感冒了。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Middle French catégorie, from Late Latin categoria, from Greek kategoria "accusation, prediction, category," verbal noun from kategorein "to speak against; to accuse, assert, predicate," from kata "down to" (or perhaps "against;" see cata-) + agoreuein "to harangue, to declaim (in the assembly)," from agora "public assembly" (see agora). Original sense of "accuse" weakened to "assert, name" by the time Aristotle applied kategoria to his 10 classes of things that can be named.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 中古法语 catégorie, 源自 晚期拉丁语 categoria, 源自 希腊语 kategoria "accusation, prediction, category," verbal 名词 源自 kategorein "to speak against; to accuse, assert, predicate," 源自 kata "down to" (or 或许 "against;" 参见 cata-) + agoreuein "to harangue, to declaim (in the assembly)," 源自 agora "public assembly" （参见 agora). Original 语义 "accuse" weakened to "assert, name" by the time Aristotle applied kategoria to his 10 classes of things that can be named.

example.en: These books fall into the category of science fiction.
example.zh: 这些书属于科幻小说这一类别。

definitionLines: vi. （for）满足需要；投合，迎 合；提供饮食及服务
entries.definition: vi. （for）满足需要；投合，迎 合；提供饮食及服务
entries.etymology:
"provide food for," c. 1600, from Middle English catour (n.) "buyer of provisions" (c. 1400; late 13c. as a surname), a shortening of Anglo-French achatour "buyer" (Old North French acatour, Old French achatour, 13c., Modern French acheteur), from Old French achater "to buy," originally "to buy provisions," perhaps from Vulgar Latin *accaptare, from Latin ad- "to" + captare "to take, hold," frequentative of capere "to take" (see capable).

Or else from Vulgar Latin *accapitare "to add to one's capital," with second element from verbal stem of Latin caput (genitive capitis); see capital (adj.). Figuratively from 1650s. Related: Catered; catering.
entries.etymologyZh: "provide food for," 约 1600 年, 源自 中古英语 catour （名） "buyer of provisions" (约 1400 年; 13 世纪晚期 作为 surname), a shortening of 盎格鲁-法语 achatour "buyer" (Old North 法语 acatour, 古法语 achatour, 13 世纪, 现代法语 acheteur), 源自 古法语 achater "to buy," 原义为 "to buy provisions," 或源自 通俗拉丁语 *accaptare, 源自 拉丁语 ad- "to" + captare "to take, hold," 为 … 的反复体 capere "to take" （参见 capable). Or else 源自 通俗拉丁语 *accapitare "to add to one's capital," with second element 源自 verbal stem of 拉丁语 caput (属格 capitis); 参见 capital （形）. Figuratively 源自 1650 年代. 同源词：Catered; catering.

entries.etymology:
1580s, "church of a bishop," from phrase cathedral church (c. 1300), partially translating Late Latin ecclesia cathedralis "church of a bishop's seat," from Latin cathedra "an easy chair (principally used by ladies)," also metonymically, as in cathedrae molles "luxurious women;" also "a professor's chair;" from Greek kathedra "seat, bench," from kata "down" (see cata-) + hedra "seat, base, chair, face of a geometric solid," from PIE root *sed- (1) "to sit" (see sedentary).

It was born an adjective, and attempts to cobble further adjectivization onto it in 17c. yielded cathedraical (1670s), cathedratic (1660s), cathedratical (1660s), after which the effort seems to have been given up.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "church of a bishop," 源自 phrase cathedral church (约 1300 年), partially translating 晚期拉丁语 ecclesia cathedralis "church of a bishop's seat," 源自 拉丁语 cathedra "an easy chair (principally used by ladies)," also metonymically, as in cathedrae molles "luxurious women;" also "a professor's chair;" 源自 希腊语 kathedra "seat, bench," 源自 kata "down" （参见 cata-) + hedra "seat, base, chair, face of a geometric solid," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *sed- (1) "to sit" （参见 sedentary). It was born an 形容词, and attempts to cobble further adjectivization onto it in 17 世纪 yielded cathedraical (1670 年代), cathedratic (1660 年代), cathedratical (1660 年代), after which the effort seems to have been given up.

definitionLines: n. 原因，理由，缘故；事业，奋斗 目标
entries.definition: n. 原因，理由，缘故；事业，奋斗 目标 vt. 引起
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "reason for action, grounds for action; motive," from Old French cause "cause, reason; lawsuit, case in law" (12c.), and directly from Latin causa "a cause; a reason; interest; judicial process, lawsuit," which is of unknown origin. In English, sense of "matter of concern; side taken in controversy" is from c. 1300; that of "the source of an effect" is early 14c.; meaning "reason for something taking place" is late 14c. Cause célèbre "celebrated legal case" is 1763, from French. Cause why? "for what reason?" is in Chaucer.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "reason for action, grounds for action; motive," 源自 古法语 cause "cause, reason; lawsuit, case in law" (12 世纪), and 直接源自 拉丁语 causa "a cause; a reason; interest; judicial process, lawsuit," which is 来源不详. In English, 语义 "matter of concern; side taken in controversy" 始于 约 1300 年; that of "the source of an effect" is 14 世纪初; 意为 "reason for something taking place" is 14 世纪晚期 Cause célèbre "celebrated legal case" is 1763 年, 源自 法语. Cause why? "for what reason?" is in Chaucer.

example.en: Years of heavy smoking can eventually cause serious damage to the lungs.
example.zh: 多年的大量吸烟最终会对肺部造成严重损害。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "bail, guarantee, pledge," from Old French caution "security, surety" (13c.), from Latin cautionem (nominative cautio) "caution, care, foresight, precaution," noun of action from past participle stem of cavere "to be on one's guard" (see caveat). The Latin sense re-emerged in English 16c.-17c. Meaning "word of warning" is from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "bail, guarantee, pledge," 源自 古法语 caution "security, surety" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 cautionem (主格 cautio) "caution, care, foresight, precaution," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of cavere "to be on one's guard" （参见 caveat). The 拉丁语 sense re-emerged in English 16 世纪-17 世纪 义为 "word of warning" 始于 约 1600 年.

example.en: The doctor cautioned her to avoid strenuous exercise for two weeks.
example.zh: 医生告诫她两周内避免剧烈运动。

entries.definition: a. 谨慎的；十分小心的
entries.etymology: 1640s, from caution + -ous. The Latin word for this was cautus "careful, heedful." Related: Cautiously; cautiousness.

example.en: Be cautious when crossing the road on a foggy morning.
example.zh: 在雾天早晨过马路时要小心谨慎。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French cave "a cave, vault, cellar" (12c.), from Latin cavea "hollow" (place), noun use of neuter plural of adjective cavus "hollow," from PIE root *keue- "a swelling, arch, cavity" (see cumulus). Replaced Old English eorðscrafu. First record of cave man is 1865.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 cave "a cave, vault, cellar" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 cavea "hollow" (place), 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的复数 形容词 cavus "hollow," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *keue- "a swelling, arch, cavity" （参见 cumulus). Replaced 古英语 eorðscrafu. First record of cave man is 1865 年.

example.en: The hikers discovered ancient paintings inside a limestone cave.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, cesen, from Old French cesser "to come to an end, stop, cease; give up, desist," from Latin cessare "to cease, go slow, give over, leave off, be idle," frequentative of cedere (past participle cessus) "go away, withdraw, yield" (see cede). Related: Ceased; ceasing. Old English in this sense had geswican, blinnan.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, cesen, 源自 古法语 cesser "to come to an end, stop, cease; give up, desist," 源自 拉丁语 cessare "to cease, go slow, give over, leave off, be idle," 为 … 的反复体 cedere (past participle cessus) "go away, withdraw, yield" （参见 cede). 同源词：Ceased; ceasing. 古英语 in this sense had geswican, blinnan.

example.en: The factory was ordered to cease all production immediately.
example.zh: 工厂被命令立即停止全部生产。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., celynge, "act of paneling a room," noun formed (with -ing) from Middle English verb ceil "put a cover or ceiling over," later "cover (walls) with wainscoting, panels, etc." (early 15c.); probably from Middle French celer "to conceal," also "cover with paneling" (12c.), from Latin celare (see cell). Probably influenced by Latin caelum "heaven, sky" (see celestial).

Extended to the paneling itself from late 14c. The meaning "top surface of a room" is attested by 1530s. Figurative sense "upper limit" is from 1934. Colloquial figurative phrase hit the ceiling "lose one's temper, get explosively angry" attested by 1908; earlier it meant "to fail" (by 1900, originally U.S. college slang). Glass ceiling in the figurative sense of "invisible barrier that prevents women from advancing" in management, etc., is attested from 1988.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, celynge, "act of paneling a room," 名词 formed (with -ing) 源自 中古英语 动词 ceil "put a cover or ceiling over," later "cover (walls) with wainscoting, panels, etc." (15 世纪初); 可能 源自 中古法语 celer "to conceal," also "cover with paneling" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 celare （参见 cell). Probably influenced by 拉丁语 caelum "heaven, sky" （参见 celestial). Extended to the paneling itself 源自 14 世纪晚期 The 意为 "top surface of a room" is attested by 1530 年代. Figurative sense "upper limit" 始于 1934 年. Colloquial figurative phrase hit the ceiling "lose one's temper, get explosively angry" attested 截至 1908 年; earlier it meant "to fail" (截至 1900 年, 原义为 U.S. college 俚语). Glass ceiling in the figurative 语义 "invisible barrier that prevents women from advancing" in management, etc., 见于 1988 年.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., originally of the Mass, from Latin celebratus "much-frequented; kept solemn; famous," past participle of celebrare "assemble to honor," also "to publish; sing praises of; practice often," originally "to frequent in great numbers," from celeber "frequented, populous, crowded;" with transferred senses of "well-attended; famous; often-repeated." Related: Celebrated; celebrating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 原义为 of the Mass, 源自 拉丁语 celebratus "much-frequented; kept solemn; famous," 为 … 的过去分词 celebrare "assemble to honor," also "to publish; sing praises of; practice often," 原义为 "to frequent in great numbers," 源自 celeber "frequented, populous, crowded;" with transferred senses of "well-attended; famous; often-repeated." 同源词：Celebrated; celebrating.

example.en: The whole town came together to celebrate the school's centenary.
example.zh: 全镇人聚在一起庆祝学校百年校庆。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "solemn rite or ceremony," from Old French celebrité "celebration" or directly from Latin celibritatem (nominative celebritas) "multitude, fame," from celeber "frequented, populous" (see celebrate). Meaning "condition of being famous" is from c. 1600; that of "famous person" is from 1849.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "solemn rite or ceremony," 源自 古法语 celebrité "celebration" or 直接源自 拉丁语 celibritatem (主格 celebritas) "multitude, fame," 源自 celeber "frequented, populous" （参见 celebrate). 义为 "condition of being famous" 始于 约 1600 年; that of "famous person" 始于 1849 年.

example.en: The celebrity was surrounded by fans the moment she stepped outside.
example.zh: 这位名人一走出门就被粉丝围住了。

entries.etymology:
early 12c., "small monastery, subordinate monastery" (from Medieval Latin in this sense), later "small room for a monk or a nun in a monastic establishment; a hermit's dwelling" (c. 1300), from Latin cella "small room, store room, hut," related to Latin celare "to hide, conceal."

The Latin word represents PIE root *kel- (2) "to cover, conceal" (source also of Sanskrit cala "hut, house, hall;" Greek kalia "hut, nest," kalyptein "to cover," koleon "sheath," kelyphos "shell, husk;" Latin clam "secret;" Old Irish cuile "cellar," celim "hide," Middle Irish cul "defense, shelter;" Gothic hulistr "covering," Old English heolstor "lurking-hole, cave, covering," Gothic huljan "cover over," hulundi "hole," hilms "helmet," halja "hell," Old English hol "cave," holu "husk, pod").

Sense of monastic rooms extended to prison rooms (1722). Used in 14c., figuratively, of brain "compartments;" used in biology by 17c. of various cavities (wood structure, segments of fruit, bee combs), gradually focusing to the modern sense of "basic structure of living organisms" (which OED dates to 1845).

Electric battery sense is from 1828, based on original form. Meaning "small group of people working within a larger organization" is from 1925. Cell body is from 1851; cell division from 1846; cell membrane from 1837 (but cellular membrane is 1732); cell wall from 1842.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, "small monastery, subordinate monastery" (源自 中古拉丁语 in this sense), later "small room for a monk or a nun in a monastic establishment; a hermit's dwelling" (约 1300 年), 源自 拉丁语 cella "small room, store room, hut," related to 拉丁语 celare "to hide, conceal." Used in 14 世纪, figuratively, of brain "compartments;" used in biology by 17 世纪 of various cavities (wood structure, segments of fruit, bee combs), gradually focusing to the modern 语义 "basic structure of living organisms" (which OED dates to 1845 年). Electric battery sense 始于 1828 年, based on original form. 义为 "small group of people working within a larger organization" 始于 1925 年. Cell body 始于 1851 年; cell division 自 1846 年起; cell membrane 自 1837 年起 (but cellular membrane is 1732 年); cell wall 自 1842 年起.

example.en: Scientists examined the cancer cell under a high-powered microscope.
example.zh: 科学家们在高倍显微镜下检查了癌细胞。

entries.etymology: early 13c., "store room," from Anglo-French celer, Old French celier "cellar, underground passage" (12c., Modern French cellier), from Latin cellarium "pantry, storeroom," literally "group of cells;" which is either directly from cella (see cell), or from noun use of neuter of adjective cellarius "pertaining to a storeroom," from cella. The sense in late Middle English gradually shifted to "underground room." Cellar door attested by 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "store room," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 celer, 古法语 celier "cellar, underground passage" (12 世纪, 现代法语 cellier), 源自 拉丁语 cellarium "pantry, storeroom," 字面义为 "group of cells;" which is either 直接源自 cella （参见 cell)，或源自 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of 形容词 cellarius "pertaining to a storeroom," 源自 cella. The sense in late 中古英语 gradually shifted to "underground room." Cellar door attested by 1640 年代.

entries.etymology: 1850, for Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius (1701-1744) inventor of the centigrade scale in 1742.
entries.etymologyZh: 1850 年, for Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius (1701 年-1744 年) inventor of the centigrade scale 于 1742 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French ciment "cement, mortar, pitch," from Latin cæmenta "stone chips used for making mortar" (singular caementum), from caedere "to cut down, chop, beat, hew, fell, slay" (see -cide). The sense evolution from "small broken stones" to "powdered stones used in construction" took place before the word reached English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 ciment "cement, mortar, pitch," 源自 拉丁语 cæmenta "stone chips used for making mortar" (singular caementum), 源自 caedere "to cut down, chop, beat, hew, fell, slay" （参见 -cide). The sense evolution 源自 "small broken stones" to "powdered stones used in construction" took place before the word reached English.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French cimetiere "graveyard" (12c.), from Late Latin coemeterium, from Greek koimeterion "sleeping place, dormitory," from koiman "to put to sleep," keimai "I lie down," from PIE root *kei- "to lie, rest," also "bed, couch," hence secondary sense of "beloved, dear" (source also of Greek keisthai "to lie, lie asleep," Old Church Slavonic semija "family, domestic servants," Lithuanian šeima "domestic servants," Lettish sieva "wife," Old English hiwan "members of a household," higid "measure of land," Latin cunae "a cradle,"  Sanskrit Sivah "propitious, gracious"). Early Christian writers were the first to use it for "burial ground," though the Greek word also had been anciently used in reference to the sleep of death. An Old English word for "cemetery" was licburg.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 cimetiere "graveyard" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 coemeterium, 源自 希腊语 koimeterion "sleeping place, dormitory," 源自 koiman "to put to sleep," keimai "I lie down," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kei- "to lie, rest," also "bed, couch," hence secondary 语义 "beloved, dear" (source also of 希腊语 keisthai "to lie, lie asleep," Old Church Slavonic semija "family, domestic servants," Lithuanian šeima "domestic servants," Lettish sieva "wife," 古英语 hiwan "members of a household," higid "measure of land," 拉丁语 cunae "a cradle," 梵语 Sivah "propitious, gracious"). example.en: The family gathered at the cemetery to place flowers on the grave.
example.zh: 家人聚集在墓地，在坟墓上摆放鲜花。

entries.definition: n. 审查机构；审查制度

entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "office of a censor," 源自 censor （名） + -ship. 义为 "action of censoring" 始于 1824 年.

definitionLines: n. 人口普查，人口调查
entries.definition: n. 人口普查，人口调查
entries.etymology: 1610s, from Latin census "the enrollment of the names and property assessments of all Roman citizens," originally past participle of censere "to assess" (see censor (n.)). The modern census begins in the U.S., 1790., and Revolutionary France. Property for taxation was the primary purpose in Rome, hence Latin census also was used for "one's wealth, one's worth, wealthiness."
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 拉丁语 census "the enrollment of the names and property assessments of all Roman citizens," 原义为 为 … 的过去分词 censere "to assess" （参见 censor （名）). The modern census begins in the U.S., 1790 年., and Revolutionary France. Property for taxation was the primary purpose in Rome, hence 拉丁语 census also was used for "one's wealth, one's worth, wealthiness."

example.en: The national census revealed that the population had grown by five percent.
example.zh: 全国人口普查显示，人口增长了5%。

definitionLines: n. 分，分币；［作单位的］百
entries.definition: n. 分，分币；［作单位的］百
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin centum "hundred" (see hundred). Middle English meaning was "one hundred," but it shifted 17c. to "hundredth part" under influence of percent. Chosen in this sense in 1786 as a name for a U.S. currency unit by Continental Congress. The word first was suggested by Robert Morris in 1782 under a different currency plan. Before the cent, Revolutionary and colonial dollars were reckoned in ninetieths, based on the exchange rate of Pennsylvania money and Spanish coin.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 centum "hundred" （参见 hundred). 中古英语 意为 was "one hundred," but it shifted 17 世纪 to "hundredth part" under influence of percent. Chosen in this sense 于 1786 年 作为 name for a U.S. currency unit by Continental Congress. The word first was suggested by Robert Morris 于 1782 年 under a different currency plan. Before the cent, Revolutionary and colonial dollars were reckoned in ninetieths, based on the exchange rate of Pennsylvania money and 西班牙语 coin.

entries.etymology: 1799, from French; see centi- "hundred" + Latin gradus "degree" (see grade (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1799 年, 源自 法语; 参见 centi- "hundred" + 拉丁语 gradus "degree" （参见 grade （名）).

entries.etymology: also centimetre, 1801, from French centimètre (18c.), coined from Latin centum "hundred" (see hundred) + French mètre (see meter (n.2)).
entries.etymologyZh: also centimetre, 1801 年, 源自 法语 centimètre (18 世纪), coined 源自 拉丁语 centum "hundred" （参见 hundred) + 法语 mètre （参见 meter (n.2)).

definitionLines: a. 中心的，中央的，中枢的；主 要的
entries.definition: a. 中心的，中央的，中枢的；主 要的
entries.etymology:
1640s, from French central  or directly from Latin centralis "pertaining to a center," from centrum (see center (n.)). Centrally is attested perhaps as early as early 15c., which might imply a usage of central earlier than the attested date.

Slightly older is centric (1580s). As a U.S. colloquial noun for "central telephone exchange," first recorded 1889 (hence, "Hello, Central?"). Central processing unit attested from 1961. Central America is attested from 1826.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 法语 central or 直接源自 拉丁语 centralis "pertaining to a center," 源自 centrum （参见 center （名）). Centrally is attested 或许 as early as 15 世纪初, which might imply a usage of central earlier than the attested date. Slightly older is centric (1580 年代). 作为 U.S. 口语 名词 for "central telephone exchange," 首见于 1889 年 (hence, "Hello, Central?"). Central processing unit attested 自 1961 年起. Central America 见于 1826 年.

example.en: The new train station will be built in the central part of the city, near City Hall.
example.zh: 新火车站将建在城市的中心地带，靠近市政厅。

entries.etymology:
1530s, "one hundred (of anything)," from Latin centuria "group of one hundred" of things of one kind (including a measure of land and a division of the Roman army, one-sixteenth of a legion, headed by a centurion), from centum "hundred" (see hundred) on analogy of decuria "a company of ten."

Used in Middle English from late 14c. as a division of land, from Roman use. The Modern English meaning is attested from 1650s, short for century of years (1620s). The older, general sense is preserved in the meaning "score of 100 points" in cricket and some other sports. Related: Centurial.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "one hundred (of anything)," 源自 拉丁语 centuria "group of one hundred" of things of one kind (including a measure of land and a division of the Roman army, one-sixteenth of a legion, headed by a centurion), 源自 centum "hundred" （参见 hundred) on analogy of decuria "a company of ten." Used in 中古英语 源自 14 世纪晚期 作为 division of land, 源自 Roman use. The 现代英语 意为 见于 1650 年代, short for century of years (1620 年代). The older, general sense is preserved in the 意为 "score of 100 points" in cricket and some other sports. 同源词：Centurial.

example.en: The printing press was invented in the fifteenth century.
example.zh: 印刷机发明于十五世纪。

entries.etymology: 1832, "grass yielding edible grain," originally an adjective (1818) "having to do with edible grain," from French céréale (16c., "of Ceres;" 18c. in grain sense), from Latin Cerealis "of grain," originally "of Ceres," from Ceres, Italic goddess of agriculture, from PIE *ker-es-, from root *ker- (3) "to grow" (see crescent). The application to breakfast food cereal made from grain is American English, 1899.
entries.etymologyZh: 1832 年, "grass yielding edible grain," 原义为 an 形容词 (1818 年) "having to do with edible grain," 源自 法语 céréale (16 世纪, "of Ceres;" 18 世纪 in grain sense), 源自 拉丁语 Cerealis "of grain," 原义为 "of Ceres," 源自 Ceres, Italic goddess of agriculture, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ker-es-, 源自 root *ker- (3) "to grow" （参见 crescent). The application to breakfast food cereal made 源自 grain is American English, 1899 年.

example.en: She poured milk over her bowl of cereal and ate it before heading to work.
example.zh: 她在麦片上倒了牛奶，在上班前吃了一碗。

entries.etymology: late 14c., cerymonye, from Old French ceremonie and directly from Medieval Latin ceremonia, from Latin caerimonia "holiness, sacredness; awe; reverent rite, sacred ceremony," an obscure word, possibly of Etruscan origin, or a reference to the ancient rites performed by the Etruscan pontiffs at Caere, near Rome. Introduced in English by Wyclif.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, cerymonye, 源自 古法语 ceremonie and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 ceremonia, 源自 拉丁语 caerimonia "holiness, sacredness; awe; reverent rite, sacred ceremony," an obscure word, possibly of Etruscan origin，或a reference to the ancient rites performed by the Etruscan pontiffs at Caere, near Rome. Introduced in English by Wyclif.

example.en: The graduation ceremony was held in the university auditorium.
example.zh: 毕业典礼在大学礼堂举行。

definitionLines: a. 确实的，可靠的；某一，某些； 一定的，必然的
entries.definition: a. 确实的，可靠的；某一，某些； 一定的，必然的
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "determined, fixed," from Old French certain "reliable, sure, assured" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *certanus, from Latin certus "sure, fixed, settled, determined" (also source of Italian certo, Spanish cierto), originally a variant past participle of cernere "to distinguish, decide," literally "to sift, separate" (see crisis).

Of persons, "full of confidence in one's knowledge or judgment," from mid-14c. Euphemistic use (of a certain age, etc.) attested from mid-18c. Certainer, certainest were common to c. 1750, but have fallen from proper use for some reason. Expression for certain "assuredly" is attested by early 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "determined, fixed," 源自 古法语 certain "reliable, sure, assured" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *certanus, 源自 拉丁语 certus "sure, fixed, settled, determined" (also source of 意大利语 certo, 西班牙语 cierto), 原义为 a variant 为 … 的过去分词 cernere "to distinguish, decide," 字面义为 "to sift, separate" （参见 crisis). Of persons, "full of confidence in one's knowledge or judgment," 源自 14 世纪中期 Euphemistic use (of a certain age, etc.) attested 源自 18 世纪中期 Certainer, certainest were common to 约 1750 年, but have fallen 源自 proper use for some reason. Expression for certain "assuredly" is attested by 14 世纪初

example.en: I am certain that she will pass the exam with flying colors.
example.zh: 我确信她会以优异成绩通过考试。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, in all main modern senses, from certain + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, in all main modern senses, 源自 certain + -ly (2).

example.en: This is certainly the finest violin performance I have ever witnessed.
example.zh: 这毫无疑问是我见过的最精彩的小提琴演出。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "action of certifying," from French certificat, from Medieval Latin certificatum "thing certified," noun use of neuter past participle of certificare (see certify). Of documents, from mid-15c., especially a document which attests to someone's authorization to practice or do something (1540s).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "action of certifying," 源自 法语 certificat, 源自 中古拉丁语 certificatum "thing certified," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的过去分词 certificare （参见 certify). Of documents, 源自 15 世纪中期, 尤指 a document which attests to someone's authorization to practice or do something (1540 年代).

example.en: She received a teaching certificate after completing the training program.
example.zh: 她完成培训项目后获得了一张教学资格证书。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "to declare the truth of," also "to vouch for or confirm" (an official record, etc.), from Old French certefiier "make certain, witness the truth of" (12c.), from Late Latin certificare "to certify, to make certain," from Latin certus (see certain) + root of facere "to make, do" (see factitious). Also used in Middle English in broader senses of "inform, give notice; instruct, to direct; to designate." Related: Certified; certifying. Certified public accountant attested from 1896.

definitionLines: n. 链，链条；一连串，连锁
entries.definition: n. 链，链条；一连串，连锁
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French chaeine "chain" (12c., Modern French chaîne), from Latin catena "chain" (source also of Spanish cadena, Italian catena), which is of unknown origin, perhaps from PIE root *kat- "to twist, twine" (source also of Latin cassis "hunting net, snare").

Figurative use from c. 1600. As a type of ornament worn about the neck, from late 14c. Chain of stores is American English, 1846. Chain gang is from 1834; chain reaction is from 1916 in physics, specific nuclear physics sense is from 1938; chain mail first recorded 1822, in Scott, from mail (n.2). Before that, mail alone sufficed. Chain letter recorded from 1892; usually to raise money at first; decried from the start as a nuisance.
Chain smoker is attested from 1886, originally of Bismarck (who smoked cigars), thus probably a loan-translation of German Kettenraucher. Chain-smoking is from 1930.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 chaeine "chain" (12 世纪, 现代法语 chaîne), 源自 拉丁语 catena "chain" (source also of 西班牙语 cadena, 意大利语 catena), which is 来源不详, 或源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kat- "to twist, twine" (source also of 拉丁语 cassis "hunting net, snare"). Figurative use 源自 约 1600 年. 作为 type of ornament worn about the neck, 源自 14 世纪晚期 Chain of stores is American English, 1846 年. Chain gang 始于 1834 年; chain reaction 始于 1916 年 in physics, specific nuclear physics sense 始于 1938 年; chain mail 首见于 1822 年, in Scott, 源自 mail (n.2). Before that, mail alone sufficed. Chain letter recorded 自 1892 年起; 通常 to raise money at first; decried 源自 start 作为 nuisance. Chain smoker 见于 1886 年, 原义为 of Bismarck (who smoked cigars), thus 可能 a loan-translation of 德语 Kettenraucher. Chain-smoking 始于 1930 年.

example.en: The supermarket chain has over three hundred stores across the country.
example.zh: 这家连锁超市在全国拥有三百多家门店。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., chaere, from Old French chaiere "chair, seat, throne" (12c.; Modern French chaire "pulpit, throne;" the more modest sense having gone since 16c. with variant form chaise), from Latin cathedra "seat" (see cathedral).

Figurative sense of "authority" was in Middle English, of bishops and professors. Meaning "office of a professor" (1816) is extended from the seat from which a professor lectures (mid-15c.). Meaning "seat of a person presiding at  meeting" is from 1640s. As short for electric chair from 1900.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, chaere, 源自 古法语 chaiere "chair, seat, throne" (12 世纪; 现代法语 chaire "pulpit, throne;" the more modest sense having gone 自 16 世纪 with variant form chaise), 源自 拉丁语 cathedra "seat" （参见 cathedral). Figurative 语义 "authority" was in 中古英语, of bishops and professors. 义为 "office of a professor" (1816 年) is extended 源自 seat 源自 which a professor lectures (15 世纪中期). 义为 "seat of a person presiding at meeting" 始于 1640 年代. As short for electric chair 自 1900 年起.

entries.etymology: 1650s, "occupier of a chair of authority," from chair (n.) + man (n.). Meaning "member of a corporate body chosen to preside at meetings" is from c. 1730. Chairwoman in this sense first attested 1752; chairperson 1971.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "occupier of a chair of authority," 源自 chair （名） + man （名）. 义为 "member of a corporate body chosen to preside at meetings" 始于 约 1730 年. Chairwoman in this sense 最早见于 1752 年; chairperson 1971 年.

example.en: The chairman opened the meeting and asked everyone to take their seats.

entries.etymology: Old English cealc "chalk, lime, plaster; pebble," a West Germanic borrowing from Latin calx (2) "limestone, lime (crushed limestone), small stone," from Greek khalix "small pebble," which many trace to a PIE root for "split, break up." In most Germanic languages still with the "limestone" sense, but in English transferred to the opaque, white, soft limestone found abundantly in the south of the island. Modern spelling is from early 14c. The Latin word for "chalk" was creta, which also is of unknown origin.

definitionLines: n. 挑战，挑战书；艰巨任务， 难题
entries.definition: n. 挑战，挑战书；艰巨任务， 难题 vt. 向……挑战
entries.etymology: early 14c., "something one can be accused of, a fault, blemish;" mid-14c., "false accusation, malicious charge; accusation of wrong-doing," also "act of laying claim" (to something), from Anglo-French chalenge, Old French chalonge "calumny, slander; demand, opposition," in legal use, "accusation, claim, dispute," from Anglo-French chalengier, Old French chalongier "to accuse, to dispute" (see challenge (v.)). Accusatory connotations died out 17c. Meanings "an objection" in law, etc.; "a calling to fight" are from mid-15c. Meaning "difficult task" is from 1954.

In anatomy from late 14c.; of machinery from 1769. Gunnery sense is from 1620s. Meaning "legislative body" is from c. 1400. Chamber music (1789) was that meant to be performed in private rooms instead of public halls.

definitionLines: n. 机会，机遇；可能性，偶然性， 运气
entries.definition: n. 机会，机遇；可能性，偶然性， 运气
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "something that takes place, what happens, an occurrence" (good or bad, but more often bad), from Old French cheance "accident, chance, fortune, luck, situation, the falling of dice" (12c., Modern French chance), from Vulgar Latin *cadentia "that which falls out," a term used in dice, from neuter plural of Latin cadens, present participle of cadere "to fall" (see case (n.1)).

In English frequently in plural, chances. The word's notions of "opportunity" and "randomness" are as old as the record of it in English and now all but crowd out the word's original notion of "mere occurrence." Main chance "thing of most importance" is from 1570s, bearing the older sense. The mathematical (and hence odds-making) sense is attested from 1778. To stand a chance (or not) is from 1796.

To take (one's) chances "accept what happens" (early 14c.) is from the old, neutral sense; to take a chance/take chances is originally (by 1814) "participate in a raffle or lottery or game;" extended sense of "take a risk" is by 1826.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "something that takes place, what happens, an occurrence" (good or bad, but more 常 bad), 源自 古法语 cheance "accident, chance, fortune, luck, situation, the falling of dice" (12 世纪, 现代法语 chance), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *cadentia "that which falls out," a term used in dice, 源自 neuter 为 … 的复数 拉丁语 cadens, 为 … 的现在分词 cadere "to fall" （参见 case (n.1)). In English frequently in plural, chances. The word's notions of "opportunity" and "randomness" are as old as the record of it in English and now all but crowd out the word's original 概念 "mere occurrence." Main chance "thing of most importance" 始于 1570 年代, bearing the older sense. The mathematical (and hence odds-making) sense 见于 1778 年. To stand a chance (or not) 始于 1796 年. To take (one's) chances "accept what happens" (14 世纪初) 始于 the old, neutral sense; to take a chance/take chances is 原义为 (截至 1814 年) "participate in a raffle or lottery or game;" extended 语义 "take a risk" is 截至 1826 年.

example.en: You should take this chance to improve your public speaking skills.
example.zh: 你应该抓住这个机会提高你的公众演讲技能。

entries.definition: v./n. 改变，变化 vt.换，兑换 n. 找头，零头
entries.etymology: early 13c., "to substitute one for another; to make (something) other than what it was" (transitive); from late 13c. as "to become different" (intransitive), from Old French changier "to change, alter; exchange, switch," from Late Latin cambiare "to barter, exchange," from Latin cambire "to exchange, barter," of Celtic origin, from PIE root *kemb- "to bend, crook" (with a sense evolution perhaps from "to turn" to "to change," to "to barter"); cognate with Old Irish camm "crooked, curved;" Middle Irish cimb "tribute," cimbid "prisoner;" see cant (n.2). Meaning "to take off clothes and put on other ones" is from late 15c. Related: Changed; changing. To change (one's) mind is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "to substitute one for another; to make (something) other than what it was" (transitive); 源自 13 世纪晚期 as "to become different" (intransitive), 源自 古法语 changier "to change, alter; exchange, switch," 源自 晚期拉丁语 cambiare "to barter, exchange," 源自 拉丁语 cambire "to exchange, barter," of Celtic origin, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kemb- "to bend, crook" (with a sense evolution 或源自 "to turn" to "to change," to "to barter"); 与 … 同源 Old 爱尔兰语 camm "crooked, curved;" Middle 爱尔兰语 cimb "tribute," cimbid "prisoner;" 参见 cant (n.2). 义为 "to take off clothes and put on other ones" 始于 15 世纪晚期 同源词：Changed; changing. To change (one's) mind 始于 1610 年代.

example.en: Listening to music can significantly change your mood after a stressful day.
example.zh: 在压力较大的一天后，听音乐可以显著改变你的情绪。

definitionLines: n. 海峡，水道，沟渠，渠道；频道
entries.definition: n. 海峡，水道，沟渠，渠道；频道
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "bed of running water," from Old French chanel "bed of a waterway; tube, pipe, gutter," from Latin canalis "groove, channel, waterpipe" (see canal). Given a broader, figurative sense 1530s (of information, commerce, etc.); meaning "circuit for telegraph communication" (1848) probably led to that of "band of frequency for radio or TV signals" (1928).

English Channel is from 1825; the older name was British Channel (by 1730). John of Trevisa's Middle English translation of the encyclopedia De Proprietatibus Rerum (c. 1398) has frensshe see for "English Channel." The Channel Islands are the French Îles Anglo-Normandes.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "bed of running water," 源自 古法语 chanel "bed of a waterway; tube, pipe, gutter," 源自 拉丁语 canalis "groove, channel, waterpipe" （参见 canal). Given a broader, figurative sense 1530 年代 (of information, commerce, etc.); 意为 "circuit for telegraph communication" (1848 年) 可能 led to that of "band of frequency for radio or TV signals" (1928 年). example.en: Social media has become the most powerful channel for spreading news.
example.zh: 社交媒体已成为传播新闻最强大的渠道。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "gaping void," from Old French chaos (14c.) or directly from Latin chaos, from Greek khaos "abyss, that which gapes wide open, is vast and empty," from *khnwos, from PIE root *gheu- "to gape, yawn" (source also of Greek khaino "I yawn," Old English ginian, Old Norse ginnunga-gap; see yawn (v.)).

Meaning "utter confusion" (c. 1600) is extended from theological use of chaos for "the void at the beginning of creation" in Vulgate version of Genesis (1530s in English). The Greek for "disorder" was tarakhe, however the use of chaos here was rooted in Hesiod ("Theogony"), who describes khaos as the primeval emptiness of the Universe, begetter of Erebus and Nyx ("Night"), and in Ovid ("Metamorphoses"), who opposes Khaos to Kosmos, "the ordered Universe." Meaning "orderless confusion" in human affairs is from c. 1600. Chaos theory in the modern mathematical sense is attested from c. 1977.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "gaping void," 源自 古法语 chaos (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 chaos, 源自 希腊语 khaos "abyss, that which gapes wide open, is vast and empty," 源自 *khnwos, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gheu- "to gape, yawn" (source also of 希腊语 khaino "I yawn," 古英语 ginian, 古北欧语 ginnunga-gap; 参见 yawn （动）). 义为 "utter confusion" (约 1600 年) is extended 源自 theological use of chaos for "the void at the beginning of creation" in Vulgate version of Genesis (1530 年代 in English). The 希腊语 for "disorder" was tarakhe, however the use of chaos here was rooted in Hesiod ("Theogony"), who describes khaos as the primeval emptiness of the Universe, begetter of Erebus and Nyx ("Night"), and in Ovid ("Metamorphoses"), who opposes Khaos to Kosmos, "the ordered Universe." 义为 "orderless confusion" in human affairs 始于 约 1600 年. Chaos theory in the modern mathematical sense 见于 约 1977 年.

example.en: The sudden power outage threw the entire city into chaos.
example.zh: 突然的停电使整座城市陷入混乱。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "customer," short for obsolete chapman "purchaser, trader" (see cheap). Colloquial sense of "lad, fellow" is first attested 1716 (compare slang tough customer).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "customer," short for 已废 chapman "purchaser, trader" （参见 cheap). Colloquial 语义 "lad, fellow" is 最早见于 1716 年 (对比 俚语 tough customer).

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "main division of a book," from Old French chapitre (12c.) "chapter (of a book), article (of a treaty), chapter (of a cathedral)," alteration of chapitle, from Late Latin capitulum, diminutive of caput (genitive capitis) "head" (see capitulum). Sense of "local branch" (1815) is from cathedral sense (late 15c.), which seems to trace to convocations of canons at cathedral churches, during which the rules of the order by chapter, or a chapter (capitulum) of Scripture, were read aloud to the assembled. Chapter and verse "in full and thoroughly" (1620s) is a reference to Scripture.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "main division of a book," 源自 古法语 chapitre (12 世纪) "chapter (of a book), article (of a treaty), chapter (of a cathedral)," alteration of chapitle, 源自 晚期拉丁语 capitulum, 为 … 的指小形式 caput (属格 capitis) "head" （参见 capitulum). 义为 "local branch" (1815 年) 始于 cathedral sense (15 世纪晚期), which seems to trace to convocations of canons at cathedral churches, during which the rules of the order by chapter，或a chapter (capitulum) of Scripture, were read aloud to the assembled. Chapter and verse "in full and thoroughly" (1620 年代) is a reference to Scripture.

example.en: The last chapter of the novel reveals the true identity of the killer.

definitionLines: n. 性格，品质；特性，特征；人 物，角色；（书写或印刷）符 号，（汉）字
entries.definition: n. 性格，品质；特性，特征；人 物，角色；（书写或印刷）符 号，（汉）字
entries.etymology: mid-14c., carecter, "symbol marked or branded on the body;" mid-15c., "symbol or drawing used in sorcery," from Old French caratere "feature, character" (13c., Modern French caractère), from Latin character, from Greek kharakter "engraved mark," also "symbol or imprint on the soul," also "instrument for marking," from kharassein "to engrave," from kharax "pointed stake," from PIE root *gher- (4) "to scrape, scratch." Meaning extended in ancient times by metaphor to "a defining quality."Meaning "sum of qualities that define a person" is from 1640s. Sense of "person in a play or novel" is first attested 1660s, in reference to the "defining qualities" he or she is given by the author. Meaning "a person" in the abstract is from 1749; especially "eccentric person" (1773). Colloquial sense of "chap, fellow" is from 1931. The Latin ch- spelling was restored from 1500s. Character actor attested from 1861; character assassination from 1888; character-building (n.) from 1886.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, carecter, "symbol marked or branded on the body;" 15 世纪中期, "symbol or drawing used in sorcery," 源自 古法语 caratere "feature, character" (13 世纪, 现代法语 caractère), 源自 拉丁语 character, 源自 希腊语 kharakter "engraved mark," also "symbol or imprint on the soul," also "instrument for marking," 源自 kharassein "to engrave," 源自 kharax "pointed stake," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gher- (4) "to scrape, scratch." 义为 extended in ancient times by metaphor to "a defining quality."义为 "sum of qualities that define a person" 始于 1640 年代. 义为 "person in a play or novel" is 最早见于 1660 年代, in reference to the "defining qualities" he or she is given by the author. 义为 "a person" in the abstract 始于 1749 年; 尤指 "eccentric person" (1773 年). Colloquial 语义 "chap, fellow" 始于 1931 年. The 拉丁语 ch- spelling was restored 源自 1500 年代. Character actor attested 自 1861 年起; character assassination 自 1888 年起; character-building （名） 自 1886 年起.

example.en: His honest character made him the most trusted member of the group.
example.zh: 他诚实的品格使他成为团队中最受信任的成员。

entries.definition: a. 特有的，独特的 n. 特征，特性
entries.etymology: adjective and noun both first attested 1660s, from character + -istic on model of Greek kharakteristikos. Earlier in the adjectival sense was characteristical (1620s). Related: Characteristically (1640s). Characteristics "distinctive traits" also attested from 1660s.
entries.etymologyZh: 形容词 and 名词 both 最早见于 1660 年代, 源自 character + -istic on model of 希腊语 kharakteristikos. Earlier in the adjectival sense was characteristical (1620 年代). 同源词：Characteristically (1640 年代). Characteristics "distinctive traits" also attested 源自 1660 年代.

example.en: Stubbornness is the most prominent characteristic of his personality.
example.zh: 固执是他个性中最突出的特征。

entries.etymology: early 13c., "to load, fill," from Old French chargier "to load, burden, weigh down," from Late Latin carricare "to load a wagon or cart," from Latin carrus "wagon" (see car). Senses of "entrust," "command," "accuse" all emerged in Middle English and were found in Old French. Sense of "rush in to attack" is 1560s, perhaps through earlier meaning "load a weapon" (1540s). Meaning "impose a burden of expense" is from mid-14c. Meaning "fill with electricity" is from 1748. Related: Charged; charging. Chargé d'affaires was borrowed from French, 1767, literally "(one) charged with affairs."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "to load, fill," 源自 古法语 chargier "to load, burden, weigh down," 源自 晚期拉丁语 carricare "to load a wagon or cart," 源自 拉丁语 carrus "wagon" （参见 car). Senses of "entrust," "command," "accuse" all emerged in 中古英语 and were found in 古法语. 义为 "rush in to attack" is 1560 年代, 或许 through earlier 意为 "load a weapon" (1540 年代). 义为 "impose a burden of expense" 始于 14 世纪中期 义为 "fill with electricity" 始于 1748 年. 同源词：Charged; charging. Chargé d'affaires was 借自 法语, 1767 年, 字面义为 "(one) charged with affairs."

example.en: The hotel will charge an extra fee for late check-out requests.
example.zh: 酒店会对晚退房的请求收取额外费用。

definitionLines: n. 慈善事业（行为）；施舍；慈 悲；博爱
entries.definition: n. 慈善事业（行为）；施舍；慈 悲；博爱
entries.etymology:
mid-12c., "benevolence for the poor," from Old French charité "(Christian) charity, mercy, compassion; alms; charitable foundation" (12c., Old North French carité), from Latin caritatem (nominative caritas) "costliness, esteem, affection" (in Vulgate often used as translation of Greek agape "love" -- especially Christian love of fellow man -- perhaps to avoid the sexual suggestion of Latin amor), from carus "dear, valued," from PIE *karo-, from root *ka- "to like, desire" (see whore (n.)).

Vulgate also sometimes translated agape by Latin dilectio, noun of action from diligere "to esteem highly, to love" (see diligence).

Sense of "charitable foundation or institution" in English attested by 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, "benevolence for the poor," 源自 古法语 charité "(Christian) charity, mercy, compassion; alms; charitable foundation" (12 世纪, Old North 法语 carité), 源自 拉丁语 caritatem (主格 caritas) "costliness, esteem, affection" (in Vulgate 常 used as translation of 希腊语 agape "love" -- 尤指 Christian love of fellow man -- 或许 to avoid the sexual suggestion of 拉丁语 amor), 源自 carus "dear, valued," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *karo-, 源自 root *ka- "to like, desire" （参见 whore （名）). Vulgate also 有时 translated agape by 拉丁语 dilectio, 名词 of action 源自 diligere "to esteem highly, to love" （参见 diligence). 义为 "charitable foundation or institution" in English attested by 1690 年代.

example.en: She donated a large sum to charity every year.
example.zh: 她每年都向慈善事业捐赠一大笔钱。

definitionLines: n. 魅力，魔力；咒文；护咒
entries.definition: n. 魅力，魔力；咒文；护咒 vt.迷住；使陶醉
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "incantation, magic charm," from Old French charme (12c.) "magic charm, magic, spell; incantation, song, lamentation," from Latin carmen "song, verse, enchantment, religious formula," from canere "to sing" (see chant (v.)), with dissimilation of -n- to -r- before -m- in intermediate form *canmen (for a similar evolution, see Latin germen "germ," from *genmen). The notion is of chanting or reciting verses of magical power.

Sense of "pleasing quality" evolved 17c. Meaning "small trinket fastened to a watch-chain, etc." first recorded 1865. Quantum physics sense is from 1964. To work like a charm (figuratively) is recorded by 1824.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "incantation, magic charm," 源自 古法语 charme (12 世纪) "magic charm, magic, spell; incantation, song, lamentation," 源自 拉丁语 carmen "song, verse, enchantment, religious formula," 源自 canere "to sing" （参见 chant （动）), with dissimilation of -n- to -r- before -m- in intermediate form *canmen (for a similar evolution, 参见 拉丁语 germen "germ," 源自 *genmen). The notion is of chanting or reciting verses of magical power. 义为 "pleasing quality" evolved 17 世纪 义为 "small trinket fastened to a watch-chain, etc." 首见于 1865 年. Quantum physics sense 始于 1964 年. To work like a charm (figuratively) is recorded 截至 1824 年.

example.en: She won the audience over with her natural charm and wit.
example.zh: 她凭借天生的魅力和机智赢得了观众的喜爱。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "map for the use of navigators," from Middle French charte "card, map," from Late Latin charta "paper, card, map" (see card (n.1)). Charte is the original form of the French word in all senses, but after 14c. (perhaps by influence of Italian cognate carta), carte began to supplant it. English used both carte and card 15c.-17c. for "chart, map," and in 17c. chart could mean "playing card," but the words have gone their separate ways and chart has predominated since in the "map" sense. In the music score sense from 1957.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "map for the use of navigators," 源自 中古法语 charte "card, map," 源自 晚期拉丁语 charta "paper, card, map" （参见 card (n.1)). Charte is the original form of the 法语 word in all senses, but after 14 世纪 (或许 by influence of 意大利语 同源 carta), carte began to supplant it. English used both carte and card 15 世纪-17 世纪 for "chart, map," and in 17 世纪 chart could mean "playing card," but the words have gone their separate ways and chart has predominated 自 in the "map" sense. In the music score sense 自 1957 年起.

example.en: The sales team presented a chart showing monthly revenue growth.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old French chartre (12c.) "charter, letter, document, covenant," from Latin chartula/cartula, literally "little paper," diminutive of charta/carta "paper, document" (see chart (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 chartre (12 世纪) "charter, letter, document, covenant," 源自 拉丁语 chartula/cartula, 字面义为 "little paper," 为 … 的指小形式 charta/carta "paper, document" （参见 chart （名）).

example.en: The organization was established under a charter that guaranteed equal rights for all members.
example.zh: 该组织依据一份保障所有成员平等权利的宪章而成立。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, chacen "to hunt; to cause to go away; put to flight," from Old French chacier "to hunt, ride swiftly, strive for" (12c., Modern French chasser), from Vulgar Latin *captiare (source of Italian cacciare, Catalan casar, Spanish cazar, Portuguese caçar "to chase, hunt;" see catch (v.)).

Meaning "run after" developed mid-14c. Related: Chased; chasing. Older European words for "pursue" often also cover "persecute" (Greek dioko, Old English ehtan); modern ones often derive from words used primarily for the hunting of animals.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, chacen "to hunt; to cause to go away; put to flight," 源自 古法语 chacier "to hunt, ride swiftly, strive for" (12 世纪, 现代法语 chasser), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *captiare (source of 意大利语 cacciare, Catalan casar, 西班牙语 cazar, 葡萄牙语 caçar "to chase, hunt;" 参见 catch （动）). 义为 "run after" developed 14 世纪中期 同源词：Chased; chasing. example.en: The dog began to chase the squirrel across the yard.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "talk idly, babble," short for chatter (v.). Meaning "to converse familiarly" is from 1550s. Sense of "flirt with, ingratiate oneself with" (in later use often with up (adv.)) is from 1898. Related: Chatted; chatting.

example.en: They often chat about their weekend plans during lunch.

definitionLines: a. 便宜，贱；低劣，劣质的
entries.definition: a. 便宜，贱；低劣，劣质的
entries.etymology:
"low in price, that may be bought at small cost," c. 1500, ultimately from Old English noun ceap "traffic, a purchase," from ceapian (v.) "trade," probably from an early Germanic borrowing from Latin caupo "petty tradesman, huckster" (see chapman).

The sense evolution is from the noun meaning "a barter, a purchase" to "a purchase as rated by the buyer," hence adjectival meaning "inexpensive," the main modern sense, via Middle English phrases such as god chep "favorable bargain" (12c., a translation of French a bon marché).

Sense of "lightly esteemed, common" is from 1590s (compare similar evolution of Latin vilis). The meaning "low in price" was represented in Old English by undeor, literally "un-dear" (but deop ceap, literally "deep cheap," meant "high price").

The word also was used in Old English for "market" (as in ceapdæg "market day"), a sense surviving in place names Cheapside, East Cheap, etc. Related: Cheaply. Expression on the cheap is first attested 1888. Cheap shot originally was U.S. football jargon for a head-on tackle; extended sense "unfair hit" in politics, etc. is by 1970. German billig "cheap" is from Middle Low German billik, originally "fair, just," with a sense evolution via billiger preis "fair price," etc.
entries.etymologyZh: "low in price, that may be bought at small cost," 约 1500 年, 最终源自 古英语 名词 ceap "traffic, a purchase," 源自 ceapian （动） "trade," 可能 源自 an early 日耳曼语 borrowing 源自 拉丁语 caupo "petty tradesman, huckster" （参见 chapman). The sense evolution 始于 the 名词 意为 "a barter, a purchase" to "a purchase as rated by the buyer," hence adjectival 意为 "inexpensive," the main modern sense, 经由 中古英语 phrases such as god chep "favorable bargain" (12 世纪, a translation of 法语 a bon marché). 义为 "lightly esteemed, common" 始于 1590 年代 (对比 similar evolution of 拉丁语 vilis). The 意为 "low in price" was represented in 古英语 by undeor, 字面义为 "un-dear" (but deop ceap, 字面义为 "deep cheap," meant "high price"). The word also was used in 古英语 for "market" (as in ceapdæg "market day"), a sense surviving in place names Cheapside, East Cheap, etc. 同源词：Cheaply. Expression on the cheap is 最早见于 1888 年. Cheap shot 原义为 was U.S. football jargon for a head-on tackle; extended sense "unfair hit" in politics, etc. is 截至 1970 年. 德语 billig "cheap" 始于 Middle Low 德语 billik, 原义为 "fair, just," with a sense evolution 经由 billiger preis "fair price," etc.

example.en: The market sells fresh fruit at very cheap prices.
example.zh: 这个市场以非常低廉的价格出售新鲜水果。

entries.definition: vt.欺骗，骗取 vi.作弊，欺诈 n. 欺骗；骗子
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "to escheat," a shortening of Old French escheat, legal term for revision of property to the state when the owner dies without heirs, literally "that which falls to one," past participle of escheoir "happen, befall, occur, take place; fall due; lapse (legally)," from Late Latin *excadere "fall away, fall out," from Latin ex- "out" (see ex-) + cadere "to fall" (see case (n.1)). Also compare escheat. The royal officers evidently had a low reputation. Meaning evolved through "confiscate" (mid-15c.) to "deprive unfairly" (1580s). To cheat on (someone) "be sexually unfaithful" first recorded 1934. Related: Cheated; cheating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "to escheat," a shortening of 古法语 escheat, legal term for revision of property to the state when the owner dies without heirs, 字面义为 "that which falls to one," 为 … 的过去分词 escheoir "happen, befall, occur, take place; fall due; lapse (legally)," 源自 晚期拉丁语 *excadere "fall away, fall out," 源自 拉丁语 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + cadere "to fall" （参见 case (n.1)). Also 对比 escheat. The royal officers 显然 had a low reputation. 义为 evolved through "confiscate" (15 世纪中期) to "deprive unfairly" (1580 年代). To cheat on (someone) "be sexually unfaithful" 首见于 1934 年. 同源词：Cheated; cheating.

example.en: The student was caught trying to cheat on the final exam.
example.zh: 该学生在期末考试中企图作弊时被抓住。
