The cloth "the clerical profession" 始于 17 世纪 in reference to characteristic dress.

example.en: She wiped the lens clean with a soft cloth.
example.zh: 她用一块软布把镜头擦干净。

entries.etymology: Old English claðas "cloths, clothes," originally plural of clað "cloth" (see cloth), which, in 19c., after the sense of "article of clothing" had mostly faded from it, acquired a new plural form, cloths, to distinguish it from this word.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 claðas "cloths, clothes," 原义为 为 … 的复数 clað "cloth" （参见 cloth), which, in 19 世纪, after the 语义 "article of clothing" had mostly faded 源自 it, acquired a new plural form, cloths, to distinguish it 源自 this word.

example.en: She packed warm clothes for the camping trip in the mountains.
example.zh: 她为山区露营之旅打包了保暖衣物。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "action of dressing in clothes," verbal noun from clothe. From late 13c. as "clothes collectively;" 1590s as an adjective.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "action of dressing in clothes," verbal 名词 源自 clothe. From 13 世纪晚期 as "clothes collectively;" 1590 年代 作形容词时.

example.en: She donated several bags of winter clothing to the homeless shelter.
example.zh: 她向无家可归者收容所捐赠了几袋冬季衣物。

entries.etymology:
Old English clud "mass of rock, hill," related to clod. Metaphoric extension to "raincloud, mass of evaporated water in the sky" is attested by c. 1200 based on similarity of cumulus clouds and rock masses. The usual Old English word for "cloud" was weolcan. In Middle English, skie also originally meant "cloud."

The four fundamental types of cloud classification (cirrus, cumulus, stratus, nimbus) were proposed by British amateur meteorologist Luke Howard (1772-1864) in 1802. Figuratively, as something that casts a shadow, from early 15c.; hence under a cloud (c. 1500). In the clouds "removed from earthly things; obscure, fanciful, unreal" is from 1640s. Cloud-compeller translates (poetically) Greek nephelegereta, a Homeric epithet of Zeus.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 clud "mass of rock, hill," related to clod. Metaphoric extension to "raincloud, mass of evaporated water in the sky" is attested by 约 1200 年 based on similarity of cumulus clouds and rock masses. The usual 古英语 word for "cloud" was weolcan. In 中古英语, skie also 原义为 meant "cloud." example.en: Dark cloud began to gather in the sky before the storm.
example.zh: 暴风雨前，乌云开始在天空聚集。

definitionLines: a. 多云，阴；似云的；模糊不清 的
entries.definition: a. 多云，阴；似云的；模糊不清 的
entries.etymology: Old English cludig "rocky, hilly, full of cliffs;" see cloud (n.). Meaning "of the nature of clouds" is recorded from c. 1300; meaning "full of clouds" is late 14c.; that of "not clear" is from 1580s. Figurative sense of "gloomy" is late 14c. Related: Cloudiness; cloudily.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cludig "rocky, hilly, full of cliffs;" 参见 cloud （名）. 义为 "of the nature of clouds" 见于 约 1300 年; 意为 "full of clouds" is 14 世纪晚期; that of "not clear" 始于 1580 年代. Figurative 语义 "gloomy" is 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Cloudiness; cloudily.

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "thick stick used as a weapon," from Old Norse klubba "cudgel" or a similar Scandinavian source (compare Swedish klubba, Danish klubbe), assimilated from Proto-Germanic *klumbon, related to clump (n.). Old English words for this were sagol, cycgel. Specific sense of "bat used in games" is from mid-15c.

The club suit in the deck of cards (1560s) bears the correct name (Spanish basto, Italian bastone), but the pattern adopted on English cards is the French trefoil. Compare Danish klőver, Dutch klaver "a club at cards," literally "a clover."

The social club (1660s) apparently evolved from this word from the verbal sense "gather in a club-like mass" (1620s), then, as a noun, "association of people" (1640s).

Club soda is by 1881, originally a proprietary name (Cantrell & Cochrane, Dublin). Club sandwich recorded by 1899, apparently as a type of sandwich served in clubs. Club car is from 1890, American English, originally one well-appointed and reserved for members of a club run by the railway company; later of any railway car fitted with chairs instead of benches, and other amenities (1917). Hence club for "class of fares between first-class and transit" (1978).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "thick stick used as a weapon," 源自 古北欧语 klubba "cudgel" or a similar Scandinavian source (对比 Swedish klubba, Danish klubbe), assimilated 源自 原始日耳曼语 *klumbon, related to clump （名）. 古英语 words for this were sagol, cycgel. Specific 语义 "bat used in games" 始于 15 世纪中期 The club suit in the deck of cards (1560 年代) bears the correct name (西班牙语 basto, 意大利语 bastone), but the pattern adopted on English cards is the 法语 trefoil. 对比 Danish klőver, 荷兰语 klaver "a club at cards," 字面义为 "a clover." The social club (1660 年代) 似乎 evolved 源自 this word 源自 verbal sense "gather in a club-like mass" (1620 年代), 之后, 作名词时, "association of people" (1640 年代). Club soda is 截至 1881 年, 原义为 a proprietary name (Cantrell & Cochrane, Dublin). Club sandwich recorded 截至 1899 年, 似乎 作为 type of sandwich served in clubs. Hence club for "class of fares between first-class and transit" (1978 年).

example.en: She joined a photography club to improve her skills and meet new people.
example.zh: 她加入了一个摄影俱乐部，以提高技能并结交新朋友。

entries.etymology: 1590s, spelling variant of clew "a ball of thread or yarn," in this sense with reference to the one Theseus used as a guide out of the Labyrinth. The purely figurative sense of "that which points the way" is from 1620s. As something which a bewildered person does not have, by 1948.

example.en: The detective found the first clue hidden beneath the floorboard.
example.zh: 侦探在地板下发现了第一条线索。

entries.etymology:
1590s, "acting as if benumbed," alteration of Middle English clumsid "numb with cold" (14c.), past participle of clumsen "to benumb, stiffen or paralyze with cold or fear," from a Scandinavian source akin to Old Norse klumsa "make speechless, palsy; prevent from speaking," intensive of kluma "to make motionless." For insertion of -s-, see flimsy.

Not in general use until 18c., with senses "manifesting awkwardness; so made as to be unwieldy." Related: Clumsily; clumsiness. Compare Swedish dialectal klummsen "benumbed with cold," Norwegian klumsad (past participle) "speechless, palsied by a spasm or by fear or witchery;" German verklammen "grow stiff or numb with cold." Also compare clumse (n.) "a stupid fellow."
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "acting as if benumbed," alteration of 中古英语 clumsid "numb with cold" (14 世纪), 为 … 的过去分词 clumsen "to benumb, stiffen or paralyze with cold or fear," 源自 a Scandinavian source akin to 古北欧语 klumsa "make speechless, palsy; prevent from speaking," intensive of kluma "to make motionless." For insertion of -s-, 参见 flimsy. Not in general use until 18 世纪, with senses "manifesting awkwardness; so made as to be unwieldy." 同源词：Clumsily; clumsiness. 对比 Swedish 方言 klummsen "benumbed with cold," Norwegian klumsad (past participle) "speechless, palsied by a spasm or by fear or witchery;" 德语 verklammen "grow stiff or numb with cold." Also 对比 clumse （名） "a stupid fellow."

definitionLines: n.客车，长途汽车；私人教练， 教练
entries.definition: n.客车，长途汽车；私人教练， 教练 v.训练，辅导，指导
entries.etymology: 1550s, "large kind of carriage," from Middle French coche (16c.), from German kotsche, from Hungarian kocsi (szekér) "(carriage) of Kocs," village where it was first made. In Hungary, the thing and the name for it date from 15c., and forms are found in most European languages (Spanish and Portuguese coche, Italian cocchino, Dutch koets). Applied to railway cars 1866, American English. Sense of "economy or tourist class" is from 1949. Meaning "instructor/trainer" is c. 1830 Oxford University slang for a tutor who "carries" a student through an exam; athletic sense is 1861.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "large kind of carriage," 源自 中古法语 coche (16 世纪), 源自 德语 kotsche, 源自 Hungarian kocsi (szekér) "(carriage) of Kocs," village where it was first made. In Hungary, the thing and the name for it date 源自 15 世纪, and forms are found in most European languages (西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 coche, 意大利语 cocchino, 荷兰语 koets). example.en: The team hired a new coach to improve their defensive skills.
example.zh: 球队聘请了一位新教练来提升防守技术。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "the growing together of parts," from French coalition (1540s), from Late Latin coalitus "fellowship," originally past participle of Latin coalescere "unite, grow together, become one in growth" (see coalesce). First used in a political sense 1715.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "the growing together of parts," 源自 法语 coalition (1540 年代), 源自 晚期拉丁语 coalitus "fellowship," 原义为 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 coalescere "unite, grow together, become one in growth" （参见 coalesce). First used in a political sense 1715 年.

example.en: Several opposition parties formed a coalition to challenge the ruling government.
example.zh: 几个反对党联合组建了一个联盟来挑战执政政府。

definitionLines: a. 粗，粗糙，粗劣；粗鲁，粗俗
entries.definition: a. 粗，粗糙，粗劣；粗鲁，粗俗
entries.etymology: early 15c., cors "ordinary" (modern spelling is from late 16c.), probably adjectival use of noun cours (see course (n.)), originally referring to rough cloth for ordinary wear. Developed a sense of "rude" c. 1500 and "obscene" by 1711. Perhaps related, via metathesis, to French gros, which had a similar sense development. Related: Coarsely; coarseness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, cors "ordinary" (modern spelling 始于 16 世纪晚期), 可能 adjectival use of 名词 cours （参见 course （名）), 原义为 referring to rough cloth for ordinary wear. Developed a 语义 "rude" 约 1500 年 and "obscene" 截至 1711 年. Perhaps related, 经由 metathesis, to 法语 gros, which had a similar sense development. 同源词：Coarsely; coarseness.

entries.etymology:
"margin of the land," early 14c.; earlier "rib as a part of the body" (early 12c.), from Old French coste "rib, side, flank; slope, incline;" later "coast, shore" (12c., Modern French côte), from Latin costa "a rib," perhaps related to a root word for "bone" (compare Old Church Slavonic kosti "bone," also see osseous).

Latin costa developed a secondary sense in Medieval Latin of "the shore," via notion of the "side" of the land, as well as "side of a hill," and this passed into Romanic (Italian costa "coast, side," Spanish cuesta "slope," costa "coast"), but only in the Germanic languages that borrowed it is it fully specialized in this sense (Dutch kust, Swedish kust, German Küste, Danish kyst). French also used this word for "hillside, slope," which led to verb meaning "sled downhill," first attested 1775 in American English. Expression the coast is clear (16c.) is an image of landing on a shore unguarded by enemies.
entries.etymologyZh: "margin of the land," 14 世纪初; earlier "rib as a part of the body" (12 世纪初), 源自 古法语 coste "rib, side, flank; slope, incline;" later "coast, shore" (12 世纪, 现代法语 côte), 源自 拉丁语 costa "a rib," 或许 related to a root word for "bone" (对比 Old Church Slavonic kosti "bone," also 参见 osseous). 拉丁语 costa developed a secondary sense in 中古拉丁语 of "the shore," 经由 概念 the "side" of the land, as well as "side of a hill," and this passed into Romanic (意大利语 costa "coast, side," 西班牙语 cuesta "slope," costa "coast"), but only in the 日耳曼语 languages that borrowed it is it fully specialized in this sense (荷兰语 kust, Swedish kust, 德语 Küste, Danish kyst). 法语 also used this word for "hillside, slope," which led to 动词 意为 "sled downhill," 最早见于 1775 年 in American English. Expression the coast is clear (16 世纪) is an image of landing on a shore unguarded by enemies.

example.en: They built a small cottage on the rocky coast facing the open sea.
example.zh: 他们在面朝大海的岩石海岸边建了一座小屋。

entries.definition: n. 外套，上衣；涂层 v.涂上，包上
entries.etymology: early 14c., "outer garment," from Old French cote "coat, robe, tunic, overgarment," from Frankish *kotta "coarse cloth" or some other Germanic source (compare Old Saxon kot "woolen mantle," Old High German chozza "cloak of coarse wool," German Kotze "a coarse coat"), of unknown origin. Transferred to animal's natural covering late 14c. Extended 1660s to a layer of any substance covering any surface. Spanish, Portuguese cota, Italian cotta are Germanic loan-words.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "outer garment," 源自 古法语 cote "coat, robe, tunic, overgarment," 源自 Frankish *kotta "coarse cloth" or some other 日耳曼语 source (对比 古撒克逊语 kot "woolen mantle," 古高地德语 chozza "cloak of coarse wool," 德语 Kotze "a coarse coat"), 来源不详. example.en: Workers applied a protective coat of paint to the metal surface.
example.zh: 工人在金属表面涂抹了一层保护漆。

definitionLines: n. 可口可乐（美国饮料公司）
entries.definition: n. 可口可乐（美国饮料公司）
entries.etymology:
invented 1886 in Atlanta, Georgia, U.S., by druggist Dr. John S. Pemberton. So called because original ingredients were derived from coca leaves and cola nuts. It contained minute amounts of cocaine until 1909.

Coca-colanization, also Coca-colonization coined 1950 during an attempt to ban the beverage in France, led by the communist party and the wine-growers.

Coca-colonialism attested by 1956.
entries.etymologyZh: invented 1886 年 in Atlanta, Georgia, U.S., by druggist Dr. John S. Pemberton. So called because original ingredients were derived 源自 coca leaves and cola nuts. It contained minute amounts of cocaine until 1909 年. Coca-colanization, also Coca-colonization coined 1950 年 during an attempt to ban the beverage in France, led by the communist party and the wine-growers. Coca-colonialism attested 截至 1956 年.

entries.etymology: 1874, from Modern Latin cocaine (1856), coined by Albert Niemann of Gottingen University from coca (from Quechua cuca) + chemical suffix -ine (2). A medical coinage, the drug was used 1870s as a local anaesthetic for eye surgery, etc. "It is interesting to note that although cocaine is pronounced as a disyllabic word it is trisyllabic in its formation." [Flood]

definitionLines: n. 公鸡，雄鸟；旋塞，开关

entries.etymology: mid-12c., cocken, "to fight;" 1570s, "to swagger;" seeming contradictory modern senses of "to stand up" (as in cock one's ear), c. 1600, and "to bend" (1898) are from the two cock nouns. The first is probably in reference to the posture of the bird's head or tail, the second to the firearm position. To cock ones hat carries the notion of "defiant boastfulness."
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, cocken, "to fight;" 1570 年代, "to swagger;" seeming contradictory modern senses of "to stand up" (as in cock one's ear), c. 1600, and "to bend" (1898) are from the two cock nouns. The first is probably in reference to the posture of the bird's head or tail, the second to the firearm position. To cock ones hat carries the 概念 "defiant boastfulness."

entries.definition: n. 鸡尾酒；开胃食品 a. 鸡尾酒的
entries.etymology: first attested 1806; H.L. Mencken lists seven versions of its origin, perhaps the most durable traces it to French coquetier "egg-cup" (15c.; in English cocktay). In New Orleans, c. 1795, Antoine Amédée Peychaud, an apothecary (and inventor of Peychaud bitters) held Masonic social gatherings at his pharmacy, where he mixed brandy toddies with his own bitters and served them in an egg-cup. On this theory, the drink took the name of the cup. Used from 1920s of any mix of substances (fruit, Molotov). Cocktail party first attested 1928.
entries.etymologyZh: 最早见于 1806 年; H.L. Mencken lists seven versions of its origin, 或许 the most durable traces it to 法语 coquetier "egg-cup" (15 世纪; in English cocktay). In New Orleans, 约 1795 年, Antoine Amédée Peychaud, an apothecary (and inventor of Peychaud bitters) held Masonic social gatherings at his pharmacy, where he mixed brandy toddies with his own bitters and served them in an egg-cup. On this theory, the drink took the name of the cup. Used 源自 1920 年代 of any mix of substances (fruit, Molotov). Cocktail party 最早见于 1928 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "systematic compilation of laws," from Old French code "system of laws, law-book" (13c.), from Latin codex, earlier caudex "book, book of laws," literally "tree trunk," hence, book made up of wooden tablets covered with wax for writing. Meaning "cipher" (the sense in secret code) is from 1808.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "systematic compilation of laws," 源自 古法语 code "system of laws, law-book" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 codex, earlier caudex "book, book of laws," 字面义为 "tree trunk," hence, book made up of wooden tablets covered with wax for writing. 义为 "cipher" (the sense in secret code) 始于 1808 年.

example.en: The spy sent a message hidden in code.
example.zh: 这名间谍用密码发送了一条隐藏信息。

entries.etymology:
c. 1600, from Italian caffe, from Turkish kahveh, from Arabic qahwah "coffee," said originally to have meant "wine," but perhaps rather from Kaffa region of Ethiopia, a home of the plant (coffee in Kaffa is called buno, which was borrowed into Arabic as bunn "raw coffee"). Much initial diversity of spelling, including chaoua.

Yemen was the first great coffee exporter and to protect its trade decreed that no living plant could leave the country. In 16c., a Muslim pilgrim brought some coffee beans from Yemen and raised them in India. Appeared in Europe (from Arabia) c. 1515-1519. Introduced to England by 1650, and by 1675 the country had more than 3,000 coffee houses. Coffee plantations established in Brazil 1727. Meaning "a light meal at which coffee is served" is from 1774. Coffee break attested from 1952, at first often in glossy magazine advertisements by the Pan-American Coffee Bureau. Coffee pot from 1705.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 意大利语 caffe, 源自 Turkish kahveh, 源自 阿拉伯语 qahwah "coffee," said 原义为 to have meant "wine," but 或许 rather 源自 Kaffa region of Ethiopia, a home of the plant (coffee in Kaffa is called buno, which was borrowed into 阿拉伯语 as bunn "raw coffee"). Much initial diversity of spelling, including chaoua. Yemen was the first great coffee exporter and to protect its trade decreed that no living plant could leave the country. In 16 世纪, a Muslim pilgrim brought some coffee beans 源自 Yemen and raised them in India. Appeared in Europe (源自 Arabia) 约 1515 年-1519 年. Introduced to England 截至 1650 年, and 截至 1675 年 the country had more than 3,000 coffee houses. Coffee plantations established in Brazil 1727 年. 义为 "a light meal at which coffee is served" 始于 1774 年. Coffee break attested 自 1952 年起, at first 常 in glossy magazine advertisements by the Pan-American Coffee Bureau. Coffee pot 自 1705 年起.

example.en: She ordered a large coffee and a muffin at the café counter.
example.zh: 她在咖啡馆柜台点了一大杯咖啡和一个松饼。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Latin cognit-, past participle stem of cognoscere "to get to know, recognize" (see cognizance) + -ive. Taken over by psychologists and sociologists after c. 1940. Related: Cognitively.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 cognit-, past participle stem of cognoscere "to get to know, recognize" （参见 cognizance) + -ive. Taken over by psychologists and sociologists after 约 1940 年. 同源词：Cognitively.

example.en: The study examined cognitive development in children under five years old.
example.zh: 该研究考察了五岁以下儿童的认知发展。

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French cohérent (16c.), from Latin cohaerentem (nominative cohaerens), present participle of cohaerere "cohere," from com- "together" (see co-)  + haerere "to stick" (see hesitation).
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 cohérent (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 cohaerentem (主格 cohaerens), 为 … 的现在分词 cohaerere "cohere," 源自 com- "together" （参见 co-) + haerere "to stick" （参见 hesitation).

entries.etymology: 1670s, from French cohésion, from Latin cohaesionem (nominative cohaesio) "a sticking together," noun of action from past participle stem of cohaerere "to stick together" (see cohere).

entries.definition: n. 卷，盘绕 n. （一）卷/圈；圈，圈线
entries.etymology: "to wind," 1610s, from Middle French coillir "to gather, pick," from Latin colligere "to gather together" (see collect). Meaning specialized perhaps in nautical usage. Related: Coiled; coiling.
entries.etymologyZh: "to wind," 1610 年代, 源自 中古法语 coillir "to gather, pick," 源自 拉丁语 colligere "to gather together" （参见 collect). 义为 specialized 或许 in nautical usage. 同源词：Coiled; coiling.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "a wedge," from Old French coing (12c.) "a wedge; stamp; piece of money; corner, angle," from Latin cuneus "a wedge." The die for stamping metal was wedge-shaped, and the English word came to mean "thing stamped, a piece of money" by late 14c. (a sense that already had developed in French). Compare quoin, which split off from this word 16c. Modern French coin is "corner, angle, nook." Coins were first struck in western Asia Minor in 7c. B.C.E.; Greek tradition and Herodotus credit the Lydians with being first to make and use coins of silver and gold.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "a wedge," 源自 古法语 coing (12 世纪) "a wedge; stamp; piece of money; corner, angle," 源自 拉丁语 cuneus "a wedge." The die for stamping metal was wedge-shaped, and the English word came to mean "thing stamped, a piece of money" by 14 世纪晚期 (a sense that already had developed in 法语). 对比 quoin, which split off 源自 this word 16 世纪 现代法语 coin is "corner, angle, nook." Coins were first struck in western Asia Minor in 7 世纪 B.C.E.; 希腊语 tradition and Herodotus credit the Lydians with being first to make and use coins of silver and gold.

definitionLines: vi.（with） 一致，符合；同时发生
entries.definition: vi.（with） 一致，符合；同时发生
entries.etymology: 1705, "be identical in substance or nature," but from 1640s as a verb in English in Latin form, "occupy the same space, agree in position," from Medieval Latin coincidere (used in astrology), literally "to fall upon together," from Latin com- "together" (see co-) + incidere "to fall upon" (in- "upon" + cadere "to fall;" see case (n.1)). From 1809 as "occur at the same time." Related: Coincided; coinciding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1705 年, "be identical in substance or nature," but 源自 1640 年代 作动词时 in English in 拉丁语 form, "occupy the same space, agree in position," 源自 中古拉丁语 coincidere (used in astrology), 字面义为 "to fall upon together," 源自 拉丁语 com- "together" （参见 co-) + incidere "to fall upon" (in- "upon" + cadere "to fall;" 参见 case (n.1)). From 1809 年 as "occur at the same time." 同源词：Coincided; coinciding.

definitionLines: a. 冷的，寒冷的；冷淡的
entries.definition: a. 冷的，寒冷的；冷淡的 n. 寒冷；感冒
entries.etymology:
Old English cald (Anglian), ceald (West Saxon) "cold, cool" (adj.), "coldness," from Proto-Germanic *kaldaz (source also of Old Frisian and Old Saxon kald, Old High German and German kalt, Old Norse kaldr, Gothic kalds "cold"), possibly a past participle adjective of *kal-/*kol-, from PIE root *gel-/*gol- "cold" (source also of Latin gelare "to freeze," gelu "frost," glacies "ice").

Meaning "not strong" (in reference to scent) is 1590s, from hunting. Cold front in weather is from 1921. Cold-call in the sales pitch sense first recorded 1972. Japanese has two words for "cold:" samui for coldness in the atmosphere or environment; tsumetai for things which are cold to touch, and also in the figurative sense, with reference to personalities, behaviors, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cald (Anglian), ceald (West Saxon) "cold, cool" （形）, "coldness," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kaldaz (source also of 古弗里西语 and 古撒克逊语 kald, 古高地德语 and 德语 kalt, 古北欧语 kaldr, Gothic kalds "cold"), possibly a past participle 形容词 of *kal-/*kol-, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gel-/*gol- "cold" (source also of 拉丁语 gelare "to freeze," gelu "frost," glacies "ice"). 义为 "not strong" (in reference to scent) is 1590 年代, 源自 hunting. Cold front in weather 始于 1921 年. Cold-call in the sales pitch sense 首见于 1972 年. 日语 has two words for "cold:" samui for coldness in the atmosphere or environment; tsumetai for things which are cold to touch, and also in the figurative sense, with reference to personalities, behaviors, etc.

entries.etymology: 1871, back-formation from collaborator. Given a bad sense in World War II. Related: Collaborated; collaborating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1871 年, back-formation 源自 collaborator. Given a bad sense in World War II. 同源词：Collaborated; collaborating.

example.en: The two universities agreed to collaborate on a joint research project.
example.zh: 两所大学同意合作开展一个联合研究项目。

entries.etymology: 1732, from Latin collapsus, past participle of collabi "fall together," from com- "together" (see com-) + labi "to fall, slip" (see lapse (n.)). The adjective collapsed is attested from c. 1600, from Latin collapsus, and perhaps this suggested a verb. Related: Collapsing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1732 年, 源自 拉丁语 collapsus, 为 … 的过去分词 collabi "fall together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + labi "to fall, slip" （参见 lapse （名）). The 形容词 collapsed 见于 约 1600 年, 源自 拉丁语 collapsus, and 或许 this suggested a 动词. 同源词：Collapsing.

example.en: The old bridge finally collapsed under the weight of the heavy truck.
example.zh: 这座老桥终于在重型卡车的重压下倒塌了。

definitionLines: n. 衣袖，领子；（狗的）项圈
entries.definition: n. 衣袖，领子；（狗的）项圈
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "neck armor, gorget," from Old French coler "neck, collar" (12c., Modern French collier), from Latin collare "necklace, band or chain for the neck," from collum "the neck," from PIE *kwol-o- "neck" (source also of Old Norse and Middle Dutch hals "neck"), literally "that on which the head turns," from root *kwel- (1) "move round, turn about" (see cycle (n.)). Late 14c. as "border at the neck of a garment."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "neck armor, gorget," 源自 古法语 coler "neck, collar" (12 世纪, 现代法语 collier), 源自 拉丁语 collare "necklace, band or chain for the neck," 源自 collum "the neck," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kwol-o- "neck" (source also of 古北欧语 and Middle 荷兰语 hals "neck"), 字面义为 "that on which the head turns," 源自 root *kwel- (1) "move round, turn about" （参见 cycle （名）). Late 14 世纪 as "border at the neck of a garment."

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French collègue (16c.), from Latin collega "partner in office," from com- "with" (see com-) + leg-, stem of legare "to choose" (see legate). So, "one chosen to work with another," or "one chosen at the same time as another."
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 collègue (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 collega "partner in office," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + leg-, stem of legare "to choose" （参见 legate). So, "one chosen to work with another," or "one chosen at the same time as another."

example.en: She discussed the budget report with her colleague before presenting it to management.
example.zh: 她在向管理层汇报之前与同事讨论了预算报告。

entries.definition: vt. 收集，收（税等） vi. 聚集，堆积
entries.etymology: early 15c. (transitive), from Old French collecter "to collect" (late 14c.), from Latin collectus, past participle of colligere "gather together," from com- "together" (see com-) + legere "to gather" (see lecture (n.)). The intransitive sense is attested from 1794. Related: Collected; collecting. As an adjective meaning "paid by the recipient" it is attested from 1893, originally with reference to telegrams.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (transitive), 源自 古法语 collecter "to collect" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 拉丁语 collectus, 为 … 的过去分词 colligere "gather together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + legere "to gather" （参见 lecture （名）). The intransitive sense 见于 1794 年. 同源词：Collected; collecting. 作形容词时 意为 "paid by the recipient" it 见于 1893 年, 原义为 with reference to telegrams.

example.en: The museum collects artifacts from more than 50 different countries.
example.zh: 这家博物馆收藏了来自50多个国家的文物。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "action of collecting," from Old French collection (14c.), from Latin collectionem (nominative collectio) "a gathering together," noun of action from colligere (see collect). Especially of money gathered for religious or charitable purposes from 1530s. Meaning "a group of objects viewed as a whole" is from c. 1400.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "action of collecting," 源自 古法语 collection (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 collectionem (主格 collectio) "a gathering together," 名词 of action 源自 colligere （参见 collect). Especially of money gathered for religious or charitable purposes 源自 1530 年代. 义为 "a group of objects viewed as a whole" 始于 约 1400 年.

example.en: The museum displayed its entire collection of ancient Greek pottery.
example.zh: 博物馆展出了其全部古希腊陶器收藏品。

entries.definition: a. 集体的，共同的 n. 集体
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French collectif, from Latin collectivus, from collectus (see collect). As a noun, short for collective farm (in the USSR) it dates from 1925. collective farm first attested 1919 in translations of Lenin. Collective bargaining coined 1891 by Beatrice Webb; defined in U.S. 1935 by the Wagner Act. Collective noun is recorded from 1510s; collective security first attested 1934 in speech by Winston Churchill.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 collectif, 源自 拉丁语 collectivus, 源自 collectus （参见 collect). 作名词时, short for collective farm (in the USSR) it dates 自 1925 年起. collective farm 最早见于 1919 年 in translations of Lenin. Collective bargaining coined 1891 年 by Beatrice Webb; defined in U.S. 1935 年 by the Wagner Act. Collective 名词 见于 1510 年代; collective security 最早见于 1934 年 in speech by Winston Churchill.

example.en: The project was a collective effort by all departments in the company.
example.zh: 这个项目是公司所有部门共同努力的成果。

entries.etymology: "body of scholars and students within a university," late 14c., from Old French college "collegiate body" (14c.), from Latin collegium "community, society, guild," literally "association of collegae" (see colleague). At first meaning any corporate group, the sense of "academic institution" attested from 1560s became the principal sense in 19c. via use at Oxford and Cambridge.
entries.etymologyZh: "body of scholars and students within a university," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 college "collegiate body" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 collegium "community, society, guild," 字面义为 "association of collegae" （参见 colleague). At first 意为 any corporate group, the 语义 "academic institution" attested 源自 1560 年代 became the principal sense in 19 世纪 经由 use at Oxford and Cambridge.

example.en: She was the first in her family to attend college and earn a degree.
example.zh: 她是家里第一个上大学并获得学位的人。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin collidere "strike together," from com- "together" (see com-) + laedere "to strike, injure by striking," which is of unknown origin. For Latin vowel change, see acquisition. Related: Collided; colliding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 collidere "strike together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + laedere "to strike, injure by striking," which is 来源不详. For 拉丁语 vowel change, 参见 acquisition. 同源词：Collided; colliding.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French collision (15c.), from Latin collisionem (nominative collisio) "a dashing together," noun of action from collidere (see collide).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 collision (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 collisionem (主格 collisio) "a dashing together," 名词 of action 源自 collidere （参见 collide).

example.en: The collision between the two vehicles caused significant damage to both cars.
example.zh: 两辆车之间的碰撞对双方车辆都造成了严重损毁。

definitionLines: n. 颜色，色彩；颜料；肤色
entries.definition: n. 殖民地；聚居地 colo（u）r n. 颜色，色彩；颜料；肤色 vi.给……染色
entries.etymology: late 14c., "ancient Roman settlement outside Italy," from Latin colonia "settled land, farm, landed estate," from colonus "husbandman, tenant farmer, settler in new land," from colere "to inhabit, cultivate, frequent, practice, tend, guard, respect," from PIE root *kwel- (1) "move around" (source of Latin -cola "inhabitant;" see cycle (n.)). Also used by the Romans to translate Greek apoikia "people from home." Modern application dates from 1540s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "ancient Roman settlement outside Italy," 源自 拉丁语 colonia "settled land, farm, landed estate," 源自 colonus "husbandman, tenant farmer, settler in new land," 源自 colere "to inhabit, cultivate, frequent, practice, tend, guard, respect," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kwel- (1) "move around" (source of 拉丁语 -cola "inhabitant;" 参见 cycle （名）). Also used by the Romans to translate 希腊语 apoikia "people from home." 现代 application dates 源自 1540 年代.

example.en: The island served as a British colony for over two centuries.
example.zh: 这座岛屿作为英国殖民地已有两个多世纪。

entries.etymology: 1889, in figurative sense of "interesting," from color (n.) + -ful. Related: Colorfully.
entries.etymologyZh: 1889 年, in figurative 语义 "interesting," 源自 color （名） + -ful. 同源词：Colorfully.

definitionLines: n. 柱，柱状物；栏，专栏（文章）
entries.definition: n. 柱，柱状物；栏，专栏（文章）
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "vertical division of a page," also "a pillar, post," from Old French colombe (12c., Modern French colonne "column, pillar"), from Latin columna "pillar," collateral form of columen "top, summit," from PIE root *kel- (4) "to project, be prominent" (see hill). Sense of "matter written for a newspaper" dates from 1785.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "vertical division of a page," also "a pillar, post," 源自 古法语 colombe (12 世纪, 现代法语 colonne "column, pillar"), 源自 拉丁语 columna "pillar," collateral form of columen "top, summit," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kel- (4) "to project, be prominent" （参见 hill). 义为 "matter written for a newspaper" dates 自 1785 年起.

example.en: She writes a weekly column on travel for a national newspaper.
example.zh: 她为一家全国性报纸撰写每周旅行专栏。

entries.etymology: Old English camb "comb, crest, honeycomb" (later Anglian comb), from Proto-Germanic *kambaz (source also of Old Saxon and Old High German camb, German Kamm, Middle Dutch cam, Dutch kam, Old Norse kambr), literally "toothed object," from PIE *gombhos, from root *gembh- "to bite, tooth" (source also of Greek gomphos "a molar tooth," Sanskrit gambha-s "tooth").
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 camb "comb, crest, honeycomb" (later Anglian comb), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kambaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 and 古高地德语 camb, 德语 Kamm, Middle 荷兰语 cam, 荷兰语 kam, 古北欧语 kambr), 字面义为 "toothed object," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *gombhos, 源自 root *gembh- "to bite, tooth" (source also of 希腊语 gomphos "a molar tooth," 梵语 gambha-s "tooth").

entries.definition: vt. 与……战斗；反对 vi. 战斗；搏斗 n. 战斗；争论
entries.etymology: 1560s, from Middle French combat (16c.), from Old French combattre (12c.), from Late Latin combattere, from Latin com- "with" (each other) (see com-) + battuere "to beat, fight" (see batter (v.)). Related: Combated; combating; combatted; combatting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 中古法语 combat (16 世纪), 源自 古法语 combattre (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 combattere, 源自 拉丁语 com- "with" (each other) （参见 com-) + battuere "to beat, fight" （参见 batter （动）). 同源词：Combated; combating; combatted; combatting.

example.en: The government launched a major campaign to combat the spread of corruption.
example.zh: 政府发起了一场重大行动，以打击腐败蔓延。

entries.etymology: late 14c., combinacyoun, from Old French combination (14c., Modern French combinaison), from Late Latin combinationem (nominative combinatio) "a joining two by two," noun of action from past participle stem of combinare (see combine (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, combinacyoun, 源自 古法语 combination (14 世纪, 现代法语 combinaison), 源自 晚期拉丁语 combinationem (主格 combinatio) "a joining two by two," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of combinare （参见 combine （动）).

example.en: The dish is made from a combination of fresh herbs and rare local spices.
example.zh: 这道菜由新鲜香草和稀有本地香料的精心组合制成。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French combiner (14c.), from Late Latin combinare "to unite, yoke together," from Latin com- "together" (see com-) + bini "two by two," adverb from bi- "twice" (see binary). Related: Combinative; combined; combining.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 combiner (14 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 combinare "to unite, yoke together," 源自 拉丁语 com- "together" （参见 com-) + bini "two by two," 副词 源自 bi- "twice" （参见 binary). 同源词：Combinative; combined; 结合.

example.en: The recipe asks you to combine flour and butter until smooth.
example.zh: 食谱要求你将面粉和黄油混合至顺滑。

entries.etymology:
Old English cuman "come, approach, land; come to oneself, recover; arrive; assemble" (class IV strong verb; past tense cuom, com, past participle cumen), from Proto-Germanic *kwem- (source also of Old Saxon cuman, Old Frisian kuma, Middle Dutch comen, Dutch komen, Old High German queman, German kommen, Old Norse koma, Gothic qiman), from PIE root *gwa-, *gwem- "to go, come" (source also of Sanskrit gamati "he goes," Avestan jamaiti "goes," Tocharian kakmu "come," Lithuanian gemu "to be born," Greek bainein "to go, walk, step," Latin venire "to come").

The substitution of Middle English -o- for Old English -u- before -m-, -n-, or -r- was a scribal habit before minims to avoid misreading the letters in the old style handwriting, which jammed letters. The practice similarly transformed some, monk, tongue, worm. Modern past tense form came is Middle English, probably from Old Norse kvam, replacing Old English cuom.

Remarkably productive with prepositions (NTC's "Dictionary of Phrasal Verbs" lists 198 combinations); consider the varied senses in come to "regain consciousness," come over "possess" (as an emotion), come at "attack," come on (interj.) "be serious," and come off "occur." For sexual senses, see cum.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cuman "come, approach, land; come to oneself, recover; arrive; assemble" (class IV strong 动词; past tense cuom, com, past participle cumen), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kwem- (source also of 古撒克逊语 cuman, 古弗里西语 kuma, Middle 荷兰语 comen, 荷兰语 komen, 古高地德语 queman, 德语 kommen, 古北欧语 koma, Gothic qiman), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gwa-, *gwem- "to go, come" (source also of 梵语 gamati "he goes," Avestan jamaiti "goes," Tocharian kakmu "come," Lithuanian gemu "to be born," 希腊语 bainein "to go, walk, step," 拉丁语 venire "to come"). The substitution of 中古英语 -o- for 古英语 -u- before -m-, -n-，或-r- was a scribal habit before minims to avoid misreading the letters in the old style handwriting, which jammed letters. The practice similarly transformed some, monk, tongue, worm. 现代 past tense form came is 中古英语, 可能 源自 古北欧语 kvam, replacing 古英语 cuom. Remarkably productive with prepositions (NTC's "Dictionary of Phrasal Verbs" lists 198 combinations); consider the varied senses in come to "regain consciousness," come over "possess" (作为 emotion), come at "attack," come on （叹） "be serious," and come off "occur." For sexual senses, 参见 cum.

example.en: The results came as a complete surprise to the skeptical research team.
example.zh: 结果对持怀疑态度的研究团队来说完全出乎意料。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French comedie (14c., "a poem," not in the theatrical sense), from Latin comoedia, from Greek komoidia "a comedy, amusing spectacle," probably from komodios "actor or singer in the revels," from komos "revel, carousal, merry-making, festival," + aoidos "singer, poet," from aeidein "to sing," related to oide (see ode).

The classical sense of the word, then, was "amusing play or performance," which is similar to the modern one, but in the Middle Ages the word came to mean poems and stories generally (albeit ones with happy endings), and the earliest English sense is "narrative poem" (such as Dante's "Commedia").  Generalized sense of "quality of being amusing" dates from 1877.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 comedie (14 世纪, "a poem," not in the theatrical sense), 源自 拉丁语 comoedia, 源自 希腊语 komoidia "a comedy, amusing spectacle," 可能 源自 komodios "actor or singer in the revels," 源自 komos "revel, carousal, merry-making, festival," + aoidos "singer, poet," 源自 aeidein "to sing," related to oide （参见 ode). The classical 语义 the word, 之后, was "amusing play or performance," which is similar to the modern one, but in the Middle Ages the word came to mean poems and stories generally (albeit ones with happy endings), and the earliest English sense is "narrative poem" (such as Dante's "Commedia"). Generalized 语义 "quality of being amusing" dates 自 1877 年起.

example.en: The film was a lighthearted comedy that made the whole audience laugh.
example.zh: 这部电影是一部轻松愉快的喜剧，让全场观众捧腹大笑。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old French comete (12c., Modern French comète), from Latin cometa, from Greek (aster) kometes, literally "long-haired (star)," from kome "hair of the head" (compare koman "let the hair grow long"), which is of unknown origin. So called from resemblance of a comet's tail to streaming hair.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 comete (12 世纪, 现代法语 comète), 源自 拉丁语 cometa, 源自 希腊语 (aster) kometes, 字面义为 "long-haired (star)," 源自 kome "hair of the head" (对比 koman "let the hair grow long"), which is 来源不详. So called 源自 resemblance of a comet's tail to streaming hair.

example.en: Halley's comet passes near Earth approximately every 75 years.
example.zh: 哈雷彗星大约每75年接近地球一次。

entries.definition: vt./n.慰问，安慰 n. 安逸，舒适
entries.etymology: late 13c., conforten "to cheer up, console," from Old French conforter "to comfort, to solace; to help, strengthen," from Late Latin confortare "to strengthen much" (used in Vulgate), from Latin com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + fortis "strong" (see fort). Change of -n- to -m- began in English 14c. Related: Comforted; comforting.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, conforten "to cheer up, console," 源自 古法语 conforter "to comfort, to solace; to help, strengthen," 源自 晚期拉丁语 confortare "to strengthen much" (used in Vulgate), 源自 拉丁语 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + fortis "strong" （参见 fort). Change of -n- to -m- began in English 14 世纪 同源词：Comforted; comforting.

example.en: His kind words brought great comfort to the grieving family.
example.zh: 他温暖的话语给悲痛的家人带来了极大的安慰。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "affording mental comfort," from Anglo-French confortable, from conforter "to comfort" (see comfort (v.)); also see -able. Meaning "offering physical comfort" is attested from 1769; that of "in a state of tranquil enjoyment" is from 1770.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "affording mental comfort," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 confortable, 源自 conforter "to comfort" （参见 comfort （动）); also 参见 -able. 义为 "offering physical comfort" 见于 1769 年; that of "in a state of tranquil enjoyment" 始于 1770 年.

example.en: The new sofa makes the living room feel more comfortable.
example.zh: 新沙发让客厅感觉更舒适了。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "of comedy in the dramatic sense," from Latin comicus "of comedy, represented in comedy, in comic style," from Greek komikos "of or pertaining to comedy," from komos (see comedy). Meaning "intentionally funny" first recorded 1791, and comedic (1630s) has since picked up the older sense of the word.
Something that is comic has comedy as its aim or origin; something is comical if the effect is comedy, whether intended or not.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "of comedy in the dramatic sense," 源自 拉丁语 comicus "of comedy, represented in comedy, in comic style," 源自 希腊语 komikos "of or pertaining to comedy," 源自 komos （参见 comedy). 义为 "intentionally funny" 首见于 1791 年, and comedic (1630 年代) has 自 picked up the older 语义 the word. Something that is comic has comedy as its aim or origin; something is comical if the effect is comedy, whether intended or not.

example.en: The actor was best known for his comic roles in popular films.
example.zh: 这位演员最为人熟知的是他在热门电影中扮演的喜剧角色。

entries.definition: vt./n.命令，指挥 n. 掌握，运用能力
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French comander "to order, enjoin, entrust" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *commandare, from Latin commendare "to recommend, entrust to" (see commend), altered by influence of Latin mandare "to commit, entrust" (see mandate (n.)). In this sense Old English had bebeodan. Related: Commanded; commanding.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 comander "to order, enjoin, entrust" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *commandare, 源自 拉丁语 commendare "to recommend, entrust to" （参见 commend), altered by influence of 拉丁语 mandare "to commit, entrust" （参见 mandate （名）). In this sense 古英语 had bebeodan. 同源词：Commanded; commanding.

example.en: Only the general has the authority to command troops to advance.
example.zh: 只有将军才有权命令部队推进。

entries.etymology: early 14c., comandur, from Old French comandeor, from comander (see command (v.)). Commander in chief attested from 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, comandur, 源自 古法语 comandeor, 源自 comander （参见 command （动）). Commander in chief attested 源自 1650 年代.

definitionLines: vt. 庆祝，纪念；成……的 纪念
entries.definition: vt. 庆祝，纪念；成……的 纪念
entries.etymology: 1590s, from Latin commemoratus, past participle of commemorare "bring to remembrance" (see commemoration). Related: Commemorated; commemorates; commemorating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 拉丁语 commemoratus, 为 … 的过去分词 commemorare "bring to remembrance" （参见 commemoration). 同源词：Commemorated; commemorates; commemorating.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French coment "commentary" or directly from Late Latin commentum "comment, interpretation," in classical Latin "invention, fabrication, fiction," neuter past participle of comminisci "to contrive, devise," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + base of meminisse "to remember," related to mens (genitive mentis) "mind" (see mind (n.)). The Latin word meaning "something invented" was taken by Isidore and other Christian theologians for "interpretation, annotation." No comment as a stock refusal to answer a journalist's question is first recorded 1950, from Truman's White House press secretary, Charles Ross.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 coment "commentary" or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 commentum "comment, interpretation," in classical 拉丁语 "invention, fabrication, fiction," neuter 为 … 的过去分词 comminisci "to contrive, devise," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + base of meminisse "to remember," related to mens (属格 mentis) "mind" （参见 mind （名）). The 拉丁语 word 意为 "something invented" was taken by Isidore and other Christian theologians for "interpretation, annotation." No comment 作为 stock refusal to answer a journalist's question is first recorded 1950, from Truman's White House press secretary, Charles Ross.

example.en: The editor asked readers to leave a comment on the article below.
example.zh: 编辑请读者在文章下方留下评论。

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French commentaire, or directly from Latin commentarius "notebook, annotation; diary, memoir," noun use of adjective, "relating to comments," from commentum (see comment (n.)). Perhaps the Latin noun is short for volumen commentarium. Originally in English as an adjective (early 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 commentaire，或直接源自 拉丁语 commentarius "notebook, annotation; diary, memoir," 为 … 的名词用法 形容词, "relating to comments," 源自 commentum （参见 comment （名）). Perhaps the 拉丁语 名词 is short for volumen commentarium. Originally in English 作形容词时 (15 世纪初).

example.en: The documentary offers a sharp commentary on modern consumerism.
example.zh: 这部纪录片对现代消费主义提出了犀利的评论。

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French commerce (14c.), from Latin commercium "trade, trafficking," from com- "together" (see com-) + merx (genitive mercis) "merchandise" (see market (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 commerce (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 commercium "trade, trafficking," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + merx (属格 mercis) "merchandise" （参见 market （名）).

example.en: The new trade agreement was expected to boost commerce between the two nations.
example.zh: 新的贸易协定预计将促进两国之间的商业往来。

entries.definition: a.商业的，商务的 n. 商业广告
entries.etymology: 1680s, "pertaining to trade," from commerce + -al (1). Meaning "paid for by advertisements" (in reference to radio, TV, etc.) is from 1932; meaning "done for the sake of financial profit" (of art, etc.) is from 1871. Related: Commercially.
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, "pertaining to trade," 源自 commerce + -al (1). 义为 "paid for by advertisements" (in reference to radio, TV, etc.) 始于 1932 年; 意为 "done for the sake of financial profit" (of art, etc.) 始于 1871 年. 同源词：Commercially.

example.en: The network aired a commercial during halftime that became instantly viral.
example.zh: 该电视网在中场休息时播出了一则商业广告，迅速走红。

definitionLines: n. 委员会，调查团；佣金，酬 劳金；（权限、任务等的）委 任，委托
entries.definition: n. 委员会，调查团；佣金，酬 劳金；（权限、任务等的）委 任，委托
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "authority entrusted to someone," from Latin commissionem (nominative commissio) "delegation of business," noun of action from past participle stem of committere (see commit). Meaning "body of persons charged with authority" is from late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "authority entrusted to someone," 源自 拉丁语 commissionem (主格 commissio) "delegation of business," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of committere （参见 commit). 义为 "body of persons charged with authority" 始于 15 世纪晚期

example.en: A royal commission was established to investigate the causes of the disaster.
example.zh: 成立了一个皇家调查委员会来调查这场灾难的原因。

definitionLines: vt. 犯（罪），干（错事）；（to） 把……交托给，使……承担 义务
entries.definition: vt. 犯（罪），干（错事）；（to） 把……交托给，使……承担 义务
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to give in charge, entrust," from Latin committere "to unite, connect, combine; to bring together," from com- "together" (see com-) + mittere "to put, send" (see mission). Evolution into modern range of meanings is not entirely clear. Sense of "perpetrating" was ancient in Latin; in English from mid-15c. The intransitive use (in place of commit oneself) first recorded 1982, probably influenced by existentialism use (1948) of commitment to translate Sartre's engagement "emotional and moral engagement."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to give in charge, entrust," 源自 拉丁语 committere "to unite, connect, combine; to bring together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + mittere "to put, send" （参见 mission). Evolution into modern range of meanings is not entirely clear. 义为 "perpetrating" was ancient in 拉丁语; in English 源自 15 世纪中期 The intransitive use (in place of commit oneself) 首见于 1982 年, 可能 influenced by existentialism use (1948 年) of commitment to translate Sartre's engagement "emotional and moral engagement."

example.en: He was arrested for attempting to commit fraud against elderly victims.
example.zh: 他因企图对老年受害者实施欺诈而被捕。

definitionLines: n. 承诺；信奉，献身；承担的责 任/义务
entries.definition: n. 承诺；信奉，献身；承担的责 任/义务
entries.etymology: 1610s, "action of officially consigning to the custody of the state," from commit + -ment. (Anglo-French had commettement.) Meaning "the committing of oneself, pledge, promise" is attested from 1793; hence, "an obligation, an engagement" (1864).
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "action of officially consigning to the custody of the state," 源自 commit + -ment. (盎格鲁-法语 had commettement.) 义为 "the committing of oneself, pledge, promise" 见于 1793 年; hence, "an obligation, an engagement" (1864 年).

example.en: Her commitment to the project was evident from the extra hours she put in every weekend.
example.zh: 她每个周末都额外付出时间，对项目的投入由此可见一斑。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from commit + -ee, or else a revival of Anglo-French commite, past participle of commettre "to commit," from Latin committere "to unite, connect" (see commit). Originally "person to whom something is committed" (late 15c.); from 17c. in reference to a body of such people.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 commit + -ee，或else a revival of 盎格鲁-法语 commite, 为 … 的过去分词 commettre "to commit," 源自 拉丁语 committere "to unite, connect" （参见 commit). Originally "person to whom something is committed" (15 世纪晚期); 源自 17 世纪 in reference to a body of such people.

example.en: The finance committee voted to approve the new budget proposal.
example.zh: 财务委员会投票通过了新的预算提案。

definitionLines: n. （pl.）日用品；商品；农/矿 产品；有用的东西
entries.definition: n. （pl.）日用品；商品；农/矿 产品；有用的东西
entries.etymology: early 15c., "benefit, profit, welfare;" later "a convenient or useful product," from Middle French commodité "benefit, profit," from Latin commoditatem (nominative commoditas) "fitness, adaptation, convenience, advantage," from commodus "suitable, convenient" (see commode). General sense "property possession" is from c. 1500.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "benefit, profit, welfare;" later "a convenient or useful product," 源自 中古法语 commodité "benefit, profit," 源自 拉丁语 commoditatem (主格 commoditas) "fitness, adaptation, convenience, advantage," 源自 commodus "suitable, convenient" （参见 commode). General sense "property possession" 始于 约 1500 年.

example.en: Gold has been used as a commodity for trade throughout history.
example.zh: 黄金在历史上一直被用作贸易商品。

definitionLines: a.普通的，平常的；公共的，共 同的
entries.definition: a.普通的，平常的；公共的，共 同的
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "belonging to all, general," from Old French comun "common, general, free, open, public" (9c., Modern French commun), from Latin communis "in common, public, shared by all or many; general, not specific; familiar, not pretentious," from PIE *ko-moin-i- "held in common," compound adjective formed from *ko- "together" + *moi-n-, suffixed form of root *mei- (1) "change, exchange" (see mutable), hence literally "shared by all."

Second element of the compound also is the source of Latin munia "duties, public duties, functions," those related to munia "office." Perhaps reinforced in Old French by the Germanic form of PIE *ko-moin-i- (compare Old English gemæne "common, public, general, universal;" see mean (adj.)), which came to French via Frankish.

Used disparagingly of women and criminals since c. 1300. Common pleas is 13c., from Anglo-French communs plets, hearing civil actions by one subject against another as opposed to pleas of the crown. Common prayer is contrasted with private prayer. Common stock is attested from 1888.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "belonging to all, general," 源自 古法语 comun "common, general, free, open, public" (9 世纪, 现代法语 commun), 源自 拉丁语 communis "in common, public, shared by all or many; general, not specific; familiar, not pretentious," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ko-moin-i- "held in common," 复合词 形容词 formed 源自 *ko- "together" + *moi-n-, suffixed form of root *mei- (1) "change, exchange" （参见 mutable), hence 字面义为 "shared by all." Second element of the 复合词 also is the source of 拉丁语 munia "duties, public duties, functions," those related to munia "office." Perhaps reinforced in 古法语 by the 日耳曼语 form of 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ko-moin-i- (对比 古英语 gemæne "common, public, general, universal;" 参见 mean （形）), which came to 法语 经由 Frankish. Used disparagingly of women and criminals 自 约 1300 年. Common pleas is 13 世纪, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 communs plets, hearing civil actions by one subject against another as opposed to pleas of the crown. Common prayer is contrasted with private prayer. Common stock 见于 1888 年.

example.en: It is common for young children to be afraid of the dark at bedtime.
example.zh: 幼儿在睡觉时害怕黑暗是很普遍的现象。

definitionLines: n. 老生常谈；司空见惯的事；普 通的东西
entries.definition: n. 老生常谈；司空见惯的事；普 通的东西 a. 平凡的；陈腐的
entries.etymology: 1540s, "a statement generally accepted," literal translation of Latin locus communis, from Greek koinos topos "general topic." See common (adj.) + place (n.). The adjectival sense of "having nothing original" dates from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "a statement generally accepted," literal translation of 拉丁语 locus communis, 源自 希腊语 koinos topos "general topic." See common （形） + place （名）. The adjectival 语义 "having nothing original" dates 源自 约 1600 年.

entries.etymology: late 15c., "public welfare, general good," from common (adj.) + wealth (n.); meaning "the state" is attested from 1510s; applied specifically to the government of England in the period 1649-1660.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "public welfare, general good," 源自 common （形） + wealth （名）; 意为 "the state" 见于 1510 年代; applied specifically to the government of England in the period 1649 年-1660 年.

entries.definition: vt. 传达，交流，通讯 vi. 传达，传播
entries.etymology: 1520s, "to impart" (information, etc.), from Latin communicatus, past participle of communicare "impart, inform" (see communication). Meaning "to share, transmit" (diseases, etc.) is from 1530s. Related: Communicated; communicating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "to impart" (information, etc.), 源自 拉丁语 communicatus, 为 … 的过去分词 communicare "impart, inform" （参见 communication). 义为 "to share, transmit" (diseases, etc.) 始于 1530 年代. 同源词：Communicated; communicating.

example.en: Pilots must communicate clearly with air traffic control at all times during flight.
example.zh: 飞行员在飞行全程必须与空中交通管制清晰沟通。

definitionLines: n. 通讯，通信；交际，交流；传 达，传送
entries.definition: n. 通讯，通信；交际，交流；传 达，传送
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French comunicacion (14c., Modern French communication), from Latin communicationem (nominative communicatio), noun of action from past participle stem of communicare "to share, divide out; communicate, impart, inform; join, unite, participate in," literally "to make common," from communis (see common (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 comunicacion (14 世纪, 现代法语 communication), 源自 拉丁语 communicationem (主格 communicatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of communicare "to share, divide out; communicate, impart, inform; join, unite, participate in," 字面义为 "to make common," 源自 communis （参见 common （形）).

example.en: Clear communication between team members is essential for a project's success.
example.zh: 团队成员之间清晰的沟通对项目的成功至关重要。

entries.etymology: "social system based on collective ownership," 1843, from French communisme (c. 1840) from commun (Old French comun; see common (adj.)) + -isme (see -ism). Originally a theory of society; as name of a political system, 1850, a translation of German Kommunismus (itself from French), in Marx and Engels' "Manifesto of the Communist Party." Compare communist. In some cases in early and mid-20c., a term of abuse implying anti-social criminality without regard to political theory.
entries.etymologyZh: "social system based on collective ownership," 1843 年, 源自 法语 communisme (约 1840 年) 源自 commun (古法语 comun; 参见 common （形）) + -isme （参见 -ism). Originally a theory of society; as name of a political system, 1850 年, a translation of 德语 Kommunismus (itself 源自 法语), in Marx and Engels' "Manifesto of the Communist Party." 对比 communist. In some cases in early and 20 世纪中期, a term of abuse implying anti-social criminality without regard to political theory.

definitionLines: a. 共产主义的，共产党的
entries.definition: n. 共产党员 a. 共产主义的，共产党的
entries.etymology: 1841, as both a noun and adjective, from French communiste (see communism). First attested in writing by John Goodwin Barmby (1820-1881), British Owenite and utopian socialist who founded the London Communist Propaganda Society in 1841. Main modern sense emerged after publication of Communist Manifesto ("Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei") in 1848. Shortened form Commie attested from 1940. Related: Communistic.
entries.etymologyZh: 1841 年, as both a 名词 and 形容词, 源自 法语 communiste （参见 communism). First 见于 writing by John Goodwin Barmby (1820 年-1881 年), British Owenite and utopian socialist who founded the London Communist Propaganda Society 于 1841 年. Main modern sense emerged after publication of Communist Manifesto ("Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei") 于 1848 年. Shortened form Commie attested 自 1940 年起. 同源词：Communistic.

example.en: The party was founded on communist ideals of collective ownership.
example.zh: 这个政党建立在集体所有制的共产主义理想之上。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French comunité "community, commonness, everybody" (Modern French communauté), from Latin communitatem (nominative communitas) "community, society, fellowship, friendly intercourse; courtesy, condescension, affability," from communis "common, public, general, shared by all or many," (see common (adj.)). Latin communitatem "was merely a noun of quality ... meaning 'fellowship, community of relations or feelings,' but in med.L. it was, like universitas, used concretely in the sense of 'a body of fellows or fellow-townsmen' " [OED].

An Old English word for "community" was gemænscipe "community, fellowship, union, common ownership," from mæne "common, public, general," probably composed from the same PIE roots as communis. Community service as a criminal sentence is recorded from 1972, American English. Community college is recorded from 1959.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 comunité "community, commonness, everybody" (现代法语 communauté), 源自 拉丁语 communitatem (主格 communitas) "community, society, fellowship, friendly intercourse; courtesy, condescension, affability," 源自 communis "common, public, general, shared by all or many," （参见 common （形）). 拉丁语 communitatem "was merely a noun of quality ... meaning 'fellowship, community of relations or feelings,' but in med.L. it was, like universitas, used concretely in the sense of 'a body of fellows or fellow-townsmen' " [OED]. An 古英语 word for "community" was gemænscipe "community, fellowship, union, common ownership," 源自 mæne "common, public, general," 可能 composed 源自 same 原始印欧语 (PIE) roots as communis. Community service 作为 criminal sentence 见于 1972 年, American English. Community college 见于 1959 年.

example.en: Volunteers planted trees along every street in their tight-knit community.
example.zh: 志愿者在这个紧密团结的社区的每条街道上都种了树。

entries.definition: vi. 乘公交车上下班 n. 上下班交通
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "to change, transform," from Latin commutare "to often change, to change altogether," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + mutare "to change" (see mutable). Sense of "make less severe" is 1630s. Sense of "go back and forth to work" is 1889, from commutation ticket "season pass" (on a railroad, streetcar line, etc.), from commute in its sense of "to change one kind of payment into another" (1795), especially "to combine a number of payments into a single one." Related: Commuted; commuting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "to change, transform," 源自 拉丁语 commutare "to often change, to change altogether," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + mutare "to change" （参见 mutable). 义为 "make less severe" is 1630 年代. 义为 "go back and forth to work" is 1889 年, 源自 commutation ticket "season pass" (on a railroad, streetcar line, etc.), 源自 commute in its 语义 "to change one kind of payment into another" (1795 年), 尤指 "to combine a number of payments into a single one." 同源词：Commuted; commuting.

definitionLines: a. 紧凑的，紧密的；简洁的
entries.definition: a. 紧凑的，紧密的；简洁的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Middle French compact (14c.) or directly from Latin compactus "concentrated," past participle of compingere "to fasten together, construct," from com- "with, together" (see com-) + pangere "to fix, fasten" (see pact). Compact car is 1960. Compact disc is from 1979.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 中古法语 compact (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 compactus "concentrated," 为 … 的过去分词 compingere "to fasten together, construct," 源自 com- "with, together" （参见 com-) + pangere "to fix, fasten" （参见 pact). Compact car is 1960 年. Compact disc 始于 1979 年.

example.en: The compact design of the laptop makes it easy to carry in a backpack.
example.zh: 笔记本电脑紧凑的设计使其便于放入背包携带。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French compagnon "fellow, mate, friend, partner" (12c.), from Late Latin companionem (nominative companio), literally "bread fellow, messmate," from Latin com- "with" (see com-) + panis "bread," from PIE root *pa- "to feed" (see food).

Found first in 6c. Frankish Lex Salica, and probably a translation of a Germanic word (compare Gothic gahlaiba "messmate," from hlaib "loaf of bread"). Replaced Old English gefera "traveling companion," from faran "go, fare."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 compagnon "fellow, mate, friend, partner" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 companionem (主格 companio), 字面义为 "bread fellow, messmate," 源自 拉丁语 com- "with" （参见 com-) + panis "bread," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *pa- "to feed" （参见 food). Found first in 6 世纪 Frankish Lex Salica, and 可能 a translation of a 日耳曼语 word (对比 Gothic gahlaiba "messmate," 源自 hlaib "loaf of bread"). Replaced 古英语 gefera "traveling companion," 源自 faran "go, fare."

example.en: Her dog had been her loyal companion throughout the long journey.
example.zh: 在漫长的旅途中，她的狗一直是她忠实的伴侣。

definitionLines: n. 公司，商号；陪伴，同伴
entries.definition: n. 公司，商号；陪伴，同伴
entries.etymology: mid-12c., "large group of people," from Old French compagnie "society, friendship, intimacy; body of soldiers" (12c.), from Late Latin companio (see companion). Meaning "companionship" is from late 13c. Sense of "business association" first recorded 1550s, having earlier been used in reference to trade guilds (c. 1300). Meaning "subdivision of an infantry regiment" is from 1580s. Abbreviation co. dates from 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, "large group of people," 源自 古法语 compagnie "society, friendship, intimacy; body of soldiers" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 companio （参见 companion). 义为 "companionship" 始于 13 世纪晚期 义为 "business association" 首见于 1550 年代, having earlier been used in reference to trade guilds (约 1300 年). 义为 "subdivision of an infantry regiment" 始于 1580 年代. Abbreviation co. dates 源自 1670 年代.

example.en: She joined the tech company as a junior engineer right after college.
example.zh: 她大学毕业后立刻以初级工程师身份加入了这家科技公司。

definitionLines: a. 可比较的，比得上的
entries.definition: a. 可比较的，比得上的
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French comparable, from Latin comparabilis "capable of comparison," from comparare (see comparison). Related: Comparably; comparability.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 comparable, 源自 拉丁语 comparabilis "capable of comparison," 源自 comparare （参见 comparison). 同源词：Comparably; comparability.

example.en: The new product's performance is comparable to that of leading competitors.
example.zh: 该新产品的性能与市场领先竞争对手不相上下。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French comparatif, from Latin comparativus "pertaining to comparison," from comparat-, past participle stem of comparare (see comparison). Originally grammatical; general sense is from c. 1600; meaning "involving different branches of a subject" is from 1670s. Related: Comparatively.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 comparatif, 源自 拉丁语 comparativus "pertaining to comparison," 源自 comparat-, past participle stem of comparare （参见 comparison). Originally grammatical; general sense 始于 约 1600 年; 意为 "involving different branches of a subject" 始于 1670 年代. 同源词：Comparatively.

definitionLines: vt.（with） 比较，相比，对照； （to）把……比作
entries.definition: vt.（with） 比较，相比，对照； （to）把……比作
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French comparer (12c., Modern French comparer), from Late Latin comparare "to liken, to compare" (see comparison). Related: Compared; comparing. To compare notes is from 1708. Phrase without compare (attested from 1620s, but similar phrasing dates to 1530s) seems to be altered by folk etymology from compeer "rival."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 comparer (12 世纪, 现代法语 comparer), 源自 晚期拉丁语 comparare "to liken, to compare" （参见 comparison). 同源词：Compared; comparing. To 对比 notes 始于 1708 年. Phrase without 对比 (attested 源自 1620 年代, but similar phrasing dates to 1530 年代) seems to be altered by folk etymology 源自 compeer "rival."

definitionLines: n. 比较，对照，比喻，比较关系
entries.definition: n. 比较，对照，比喻，比较关系
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French comparaison (12c.), from Latin comparationem (nominative comparatio), noun of action from past participle stem of comparare "make equal with, liken, bring together for a contest," literally "to couple together, to form in pairs," from com- "with" (see com-) + parare "prepare" (see pare).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 comparaison (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 comparationem (主格 comparatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of comparare "make equal with, liken, bring together for a contest," 字面义为 "to couple together, to form in pairs," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + parare "prepare" （参见 pare).

example.en: By comparison, the new model is much faster than its predecessor.
example.zh: 相比之下，新款式比前代快得多。

definitionLines: n. 隔间；卧车上的隔间
entries.definition: n. 隔间；卧车上的隔间
entries.etymology: 1560s, from Middle French compartiment "part partitioned off" (16c.), through Italian compartimento, from Late Latin compartiri "to divide," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + partis, genitive of pars "part" (see part (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 中古法语 compartiment "part partitioned off" (16 世纪), through 意大利语 compartimento, 源自 晚期拉丁语 compartiri "to divide," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + partis, 属格 of pars "part" （参见 part （名）).

example.en: Each passenger was assigned to a private compartment on the overnight train.
example.zh: 每位乘客在夜行列车上都被分配到一个私人隔间。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "space, area, extent, circumference," from Old French compas "circle, radius, pair of compasses" (12c.), from compasser "to go around, measure, divide equally," from Vulgar Latin *compassare "to pace out" (source of Italian compassare, Spanish compasar), from Latin com- "together" (see com-) + passus "a step" (see pace (n.)).

The mathematical instrument so called from mid-14c. The mariners' directional tool (so called since early 15c.) took the name, perhaps, because it's round and has a point like the mathematical instrument. The word is in most European languages, with a mathematical sense in Romance, a nautical sense in Germanic, and both in English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "space, area, extent, circumference," 源自 古法语 compas "circle, radius, pair of compasses" (12 世纪), 源自 compasser "to go around, measure, divide equally," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *compassare "to pace out" (source of 意大利语 compassare, 西班牙语 compasar), 源自 拉丁语 com- "together" （参见 com-) + passus "a step" （参见 pace （名）). The mathematical instrument so called 源自 14 世纪中期 The mariners' directional tool (so called since early 15c.) took the name, perhaps, because it's round and has a point like the mathematical instrument. The word is in most European languages, with a mathematical sense in Romance, a nautical sense in 日耳曼语, and both in English.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French compellir, from Latin compellere "to drive together, drive to one place" (of cattle), "to force or compel" (of persons), from com- "together" (see com-) + pellere "to drive" (see pulse (n.1)). Related: Compelled; compelling.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 compellir, 源自 拉丁语 compellere "to drive together, drive to one place" (of cattle), "to force or compel" (of persons), 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + pellere "to drive" （参见 pulse (n.1)). 同源词：Compelled; compelling.

example.en: Poverty compels many families to make difficult sacrifices.
example.zh: 贫困迫使许多家庭做出艰难的牺牲。

definitionLines: vt. （for） 给……补偿，酬报； 给…•…付工钱；赔偿
entries.definition: vt. （for） 给……补偿，酬报； 给…•…付工钱；赔偿
entries.etymology: 1640s, "to be equivalent;" 1650s, "to counterbalance, make up for," from Latin compensatus, past participle of compensare "to weigh one thing (against another)," thus, "to counterbalance," from com- "with" (see com-) + pensare, frequentative of pendere "to weigh" (see pendant). Meaning "to recompense, remunerate" is from 1814. Related: Compensated; compensating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "to be equivalent;" 1650 年代, "to counterbalance, make up for," 源自 拉丁语 compensatus, 为 … 的过去分词 compensare "to weigh one thing (against another)," thus, "to counterbalance," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + pensare, 为 … 的反复体 pendere "to weigh" （参见 pendant). 义为 "to recompense, remunerate" 始于 1814 年. 同源词：Compensated; compensating.

example.en: The company agreed to compensate workers for their overtime hours.
example.zh: 公司同意补偿员工的加班时间。

entries.etymology:
1610s, " to enter or be put in rivalry with," from Middle French compéter "be in rivalry with" (14c.), or directly from Late Latin competere "strive in common," in classical Latin "to come together, agree, to be qualified," later, "strive together," from com- "together" (see com-) + petere "to strive, seek, fall upon, rush at, attack" (see petition (n.)).

Rare 17c., revived from late 18c. in sense "to strive (alongside another) for the attainment of something" and regarded early 19c. in Britain as a Scottish or American word. Market sense is from 1840s (perhaps a back-formation from competition); athletics sense attested by 1857. Related: Competed; competing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, " to enter or be put in rivalry with," 源自 中古法语 compéter "be in rivalry with" (14 世纪)，或直接源自 晚期拉丁语 competere "strive in common," in classical 拉丁语 "to come together, agree, to be qualified," later, "strive together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + petere "to strive, seek, fall upon, rush at, attack" （参见 petition （名）). Rare 17 世纪, revived 源自 18 世纪晚期 in sense "to strive (alongside another) for the attainment of something" and regarded 19 世纪初 in Britain 作为 苏格兰语 or American word. Market sense 始于 1840 年代 (或许 a back-formation 源自 competition); athletics sense attested 截至 1857 年. 同源词：Competed; competing.

example.en: Athletes from over fifty countries will compete in the tournament.
example.zh: 来自五十多个国家的运动员将参加这场锦标赛竞争。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "rivalry" (based on compete); c. 1600 "adequate supply;" 1630s, "sufficiency of means for living at ease," from French compétence, from Latin competentia "meeting together, agreement, symmetry," from competens, present participle of competere, especially in its earlier sense of "fall together, come together, be convenient or fitting" (see compete). Meaning "sufficiency to deal with what is at hand" is from 1790.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "rivalry" (based on compete); 约 1600 年 "adequate supply;" 1630 年代, "sufficiency of means for living at ease," 源自 法语 compétence, 源自 拉丁语 competentia "meeting together, agreement, symmetry," 源自 competens, 为 … 的现在分词 competere, 尤指 in its earlier 语义 "fall together, come together, be convenient or fitting" （参见 compete). 义为 "sufficiency to deal with what is at hand" 始于 1790 年.

example.en: Employers value both technical skills and communication competence.
example.zh: 雇主同时看重技术技能和沟通能力。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "suitable," from Old French competent "sufficient, appropriate, suitable," from Latin competentem (nominative competens), present participle of competere "coincide, agree" (see compete). Meaning "able, fit" is from 1640s. Legal sense is late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "suitable," 源自 古法语 competent "sufficient, appropriate, suitable," 源自 拉丁语 competentem (主格 competens), 为 … 的现在分词 competere "coincide, agree" （参见 compete). 义为 "able, fit" 始于 1640 年代. Legal sense is 15 世纪晚期

example.en: We need someone competent to handle the financial accounts of this project.
example.zh: 我们需要一个有能力的人来处理这个项目的财务账目。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "action of competing," from Latin competitionem (nominative competitio) "agreement, rivalry," noun of action from past participle stem of competere (see compete). Meaning "a contest for something" is from 1610s. Sense of "rivalry in the marketplace" attested from 1793; that of "entity or entities with which one competes" is from 1961, especially in business.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "action of competing," 源自 拉丁语 competitionem (主格 competitio) "agreement, rivalry," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of competere （参见 compete). 义为 "a contest for something" 始于 1610 年代. 义为 "rivalry in the marketplace" attested 自 1793 年起; that of "entity or entities with which one competes" 始于 1961 年, 尤指 in business.

example.en: The competition for the gold medal was fierce between the top two athletes.
example.zh: 两位顶尖运动员之间争夺金牌的竞争非常激烈。

entries.etymology: 1826, from Latin competit-, past participle stem of competere (see compete) + -ive. Related: Competitively; competitiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1826 年, 源自 拉丁语 competit-, past participle stem of competere （参见 compete) + -ive. 同源词：Competitively; competitiveness.

example.en: The tech industry is highly competitive, with companies constantly racing to launch the next innovation.
example.zh: 科技行业竞争非常激烈，各公司不断竞相推出下一项创新。

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French compétiteur (16c.), or directly from Latin competitor "rival," agent noun from competere (see compete).
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 compétiteur (16 世纪)，或直接源自 拉丁语 competitor "rival," agent 名词 源自 competere （参见 compete).

example.en: The company lost market share to a stronger competitor.
example.zh: 该公司将市场份额输给了一个更强大的竞争对手。

entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French compiler "compile, collect" (13c.), from Latin compilare "to plunder, rob," probably originally "bundle together, heap up;" hence "to pack up and carry off," from com- "together" (see com-) + pilare "to compress, ram down." Related: Compiled; compiling.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 compiler "compile, collect" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 compilare "to plunder, rob," 可能 原义为 "bundle together, heap up;" hence "to pack up and carry off," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + pilare "to compress, ram down." 同源词：Compiled; compiling.

example.en: The research team spent months working to compile the data into a report.
example.zh: 研究团队花了数月时间将数据汇编成报告。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "find fault, lament," from stem of Old French complaindre "to lament" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *complangere, originally "to beat the breast," from Latin com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + plangere "to strike, beat the breast" (see plague (n.)). Older sense of "lament" died out 17c. Related: Complained; complaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "find fault, lament," 源自 stem of 古法语 complaindre "to lament" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *complangere, 原义为 "to beat the breast," 源自 拉丁语 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + plangere "to strike, beat the breast" （参见 plague （名）). Older 语义 "lament" died out 17 世纪 同源词：Complained; complaining.

example.en: Residents began to complain about the excessive noise from the construction site.
example.zh: 居民开始抱怨建筑工地过度的噪音。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "lamentation, grief," from Old French complainte (12c.) "complaint, lament," noun use of fem. past participle of complaindre (see complain). Meaning "bodily ailment" is from 1705 (often in U.S. colloquial use generalized as complaints).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "lamentation, grief," 源自 古法语 complainte (12 世纪) "complaint, lament," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 complaindre （参见 complain). 义为 "bodily ailment" 始于 1705 年 (常 in U.S. 口语 use generalized as complaints).

example.en: The hotel received dozens of complaints about the noise from the nearby construction site.
example.zh: 酒店收到了数十起关于附近建筑工地噪音的投诉。

entries.definition: n. 补语；补足物 vt. 补足，补助
entries.etymology: late 14c., "that which completes," from Old French compliement "accomplishment, fulfillment" (14c., Modern French complément), from Latin complementum "that which fills up or completes," from complere "fill up" (see complete (adj.)). Originally also having senses which were taken up c. 1650-1725 by compliment.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "that which completes," 源自 古法语 compliement "accomplishment, fulfillment" (14 世纪, 现代法语 complément), 源自 拉丁语 complementum "that which fills up or completes," 源自 complere "fill up" （参见 complete （形）). Originally also having senses which were taken up 约 1650 年-1725 年 by compliment.

entries.etymology: 1620s, "ceremonious," from complement + -ary. Sense "forming a complement" attested from 1829, earliest in complementary colors.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "ceremonious," 源自 complement + -ary. Sense "forming a complement" attested 自 1829 年起, earliest in complementary colors.

definitionLines: a. 全，完全；已完成的，彻底的
entries.definition: a. 全，完全；已完成的，彻底的 vt. 完成，结束
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French complet "full," or directly from Latin completus, past participle of complere "to fill up, complete the number of (a legion, etc.)," transferred to "to fill, to fulfill, to finish (a task)," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + plere "to fill" (see pleio-).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 complet "full," or 直接源自 拉丁语 completus, 为 … 的过去分词 complere "to fill up, complete the number of (a legion, etc.)," transferred to "to fill, to fulfill, to finish (a task)," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + plere "to fill" （参见 pleio-).

example.en: Please complete the form and submit it by Friday.
example.zh: 请填写完表格并在周五之前提交。

entries.etymology: 1650s, "composed of parts," from French complexe "complicated, complex, intricate" (17c.), from Latin complexus "surrounding, encompassing," past participle of complecti "to encircle, embrace," in transferred use, "to hold fast, master, comprehend," from com- "with" (see com-) + plectere "to weave, braid, twine, entwine," from PIE *plek-to-, from root *plek- "to plait" (see ply (v.1)). The meaning "not easily analyzed" is first recorded 1715. Complex sentence is attested from 1881.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "composed of parts," 源自 法语 complexe "complicated, complex, intricate" (17 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 complexus "surrounding, encompassing," 为 … 的过去分词 complecti "to encircle, embrace," in transferred use, "to hold fast, master, comprehend," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + plectere "to weave, braid, twine, entwine," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *plek-to-, 源自 root *plek- "to plait" （参见 ply (v.1)). The 意为 "not easily analyzed" is 首见于 1715 年. Complex sentence 见于 1881 年.
