example.en: The link between childhood trauma and adult behavior is far more complex than simple cause-and-effect.
example.zh: 童年创伤与成年行为之间的关联远比简单的因果关系复杂得多。

entries.etymology: 1721, "composite nature," from complex (adj.) + -ity. Meaning "intricacy" is from 1790. Meaning "a complex condition" is from 1794.
entries.etymologyZh: 1721 年, "composite nature," 源自 complex （形） + -ity. 义为 "intricacy" 始于 1790 年. 义为 "a complex condition" 始于 1794 年.

definitionLines: a. 错综复杂的，难懂的
entries.definition: a. 错综复杂的，难懂的
entries.etymology: 1640s, "tangled," from past participle adjective from complicate. Figurative meaning "not easy to solve, intricate, confused, difficult to unravel" is from 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "tangled," 源自 past participle 形容词 源自 complicate. Figurative 意为 "not easy to solve, intricate, confused, difficult to unravel" 始于 1650 年代.

example.en: The assembly instructions were so complicated that most users gave up halfway through.
example.zh: 组装说明太复杂，大多数用户中途就放弃了。

definitionLines: n. 组成部分，成分；部件，元件
entries.definition: n. 组成部分，成分；部件，元件
entries.etymology: 1640s, "constitutional element" (earlier "one of a group of persons," 1560s), from Latin componentem (nominative componens), present participle of componere "to put together" (see composite). As an adjective, from 1660s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "constitutional element" (earlier "one of a group of persons," 1560 年代), 源自 拉丁语 componentem (主格 componens), 为 … 的现在分词 componere "to put together" （参见 composite). 作形容词时, 源自 1660 年代.

example.en: Vitamins and minerals are essential component of a balanced diet.
example.zh: 维生素和矿物质是均衡饮食的必要组成部分。

definitionLines: vt. 写作，作曲；（of）由…… 组成
entries.definition: vt. 写作，作曲；（of）由…… 组成
entries.etymology: c. 1400, compousen, from Old French composer "put together, arrange, write" a work (12c.), from com- "with" (see com-) + poser "to place," from Late Latin pausare "to cease, lay down" (see pause (n.)). Meaning influenced in Old French by componere (see composite; also see pose (v.)). Musical sense is from 1590s. Related: Composed; composing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, compousen, 源自 古法语 composer "put together, arrange, write" a work (12 世纪), 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + poser "to place," 源自 晚期拉丁语 pausare "to cease, lay down" （参见 pause （名）). 义为 influenced in 古法语 by componere （参见 composite; also 参见 pose （动）). Musical sense 始于 1590 年代. 同源词：Composed; composing.

example.en: She was asked to compose a theme song for the opening ceremony.
example.zh: 她被要求为开幕式创作一首主题曲。

definitionLines: n. 写作，作文，习作；成分，合成 物；乐曲
entries.definition: n. 写作，作文，习作；成分，合成 物；乐曲
entries.etymology: late 14c., "action of combining," also "manner in which a thing is composed," from Old French composicion (13c., Modern French composition) "composition, make-up, literary work, agreement, settlement," from Latin compositionem (nominative compositio) "a putting together, connecting, arranging," noun of action from past participle stem of componere (see composite). Meaning "art of constructing sentences" is from 1550s; that of "literary production" (often also "writing exercise for students") is from c. 1600. Printing sense is 1832; meaning "arrangement of parts in a picture" is from 1706.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "action of combining," also "manner in which a thing is composed," 源自 古法语 composicion (13 世纪, 现代法语 composition) "composition, make-up, literary work, agreement, settlement," 源自 拉丁语 compositionem (主格 compositio) "a putting together, connecting, arranging," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of componere （参见 composite). 义为 "art of constructing sentences" 始于 1550 年代; that of "literary production" (常 also "writing exercise for students") 始于 约 1600 年. Printing sense is 1832 年; 意为 "arrangement of parts in a picture" 始于 1706 年.

example.en: The young pianist performed her own composition at the concert hall.
example.zh: 这位年轻钢琴家在音乐厅演奏了自己的原创作品。

entries.definition: a. 复合的 n. 复合物，化合物
entries.etymology: "to put together," late 14c., compounen "to mix, combine," from Old French compondre, componre "arrange, direct," from Latin componere "to put together" (see composite). The -d appeared 1500s in English on model of expound, etc. Related: Compounded; compounding.
entries.etymologyZh: "to put together," 14 世纪晚期, compounen "to mix, combine," 源自 古法语 compondre, componre "arrange, direct," 源自 拉丁语 componere "to put together" （参见 composite). The -d appeared 1500 年代 in English on model of expound, etc. 同源词：Compounded; compounding.

example.en: Water is a compound made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
example.zh: 水是由两个氢原子和一个氧原子构成的化合物。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French comprehénsion (15c.), from Latin comprehensionem (nominative comprehensio) "a seizing, laying hold of, arrest," figuratively "perception, comprehension," noun of action from past participle stem of comprehendere (see comprehend). In reading education, from 1921.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 comprehénsion (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 comprehensionem (主格 comprehensio) "a seizing, laying hold of, arrest," figuratively "perception, comprehension," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of comprehendere （参见 comprehend). In reading education, 自 1921 年起.

entries.etymology: "containing much," 1610s, from French comprehénsif, from Late Latin comprehensivus, from comprehens-, past participle stem of Latin comprehendere (see comprehend). Related: Comprehensively (mid-15c.); comprehensiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: "containing much," 1610 年代, 源自 法语 comprehénsif, 源自 晚期拉丁语 comprehensivus, 源自 comprehens-, past participle stem of 拉丁语 comprehendere （参见 comprehend). 同源词：Comprehensively (15 世纪中期); comprehensiveness.

example.en: The textbook provides a comprehensive guide to European history from 1800 to 1945.
example.zh: 这本教科书提供了一份涵盖1800年至1945年欧洲历史的全面指南。

entries.definition: vi. 受压缩小 vt. 压缩，压紧
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to press (something) together," from Old French compresser "compress, put under pressure," from Latin compressare "to press together," frequentative of comprimere "to squeeze," from com- "together" (see com-) + premere "to press" (see press (v.1)). Related: Compressed; compressing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to press (something) together," 源自 古法语 compresser "compress, put under pressure," 源自 拉丁语 compressare "to press together," 为 … 的反复体 comprimere "to squeeze," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + premere "to press" （参见 press (v.1)). 同源词：Compressed; compressing.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to include," from Old French compris, past participle of comprendre "to contain, comprise" (12c.), from Latin comprehendere (see comprehend). Related: Comprised; comprising.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to include," 源自 古法语 compris, 为 … 的过去分词 comprendre "to contain, comprise" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 comprehendere （参见 comprehend). 同源词：Comprised; comprising.

example.en: The committee comprises members from five different departments.
example.zh: 该委员会由来自五个不同部门的成员组成。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "a joint promise to abide by an arbiter's decision," from Middle French compromis (13c.), from Latin compromissus, past participle of compromittere "to make a mutual promise" (to abide by the arbiter's decision), from com- "together" (see com-) + promittere (see promise). The main modern sense of "a coming to terms" is from extension to the settlement itself (late 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "a joint promise to abide by an arbiter's decision," 源自 中古法语 compromis (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 compromissus, 为 … 的过去分词 compromittere "to make a mutual promise" (to abide by the arbiter's decision), 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + promittere （参见 promise). The main modern 语义 "a coming to terms" 始于 extension to the settlement itself (15 世纪晚期).

example.en: Both sides agreed to reach a compromise that satisfied their core demands.
example.zh: 双方同意达成一项满足各自核心诉求的妥协方案。

entries.etymology: 1640s, "one who calculates," agent noun from compute (v.). Meaning "calculating machine" (of any type) is from 1897; in modern use, "programmable digital electronic computer" (1945 under this name; theoretical from 1937, as Turing machine). ENIAC (1946) usually is considered the first. Computer literacy is recorded from 1970; an attempt to establish computerate (adjective, on model of literate) in this sense in the early 1980s didn't catch on. Computerese "the jargon of programmers" is from 1960, as are computerize and computerization.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "one who calculates," agent 名词 源自 compute （动）. 义为 "calculating machine" (of any type) 始于 1897 年; in modern use, "programmable digital electronic computer" (1945 年 under this name; theoretical 自 1937 年起, as Turing machine). ENIAC (1946 年) 通常 is considered the first. Computer literacy 见于 1970 年; an attempt to establish computerate (形容词, on model of literate) in this sense in the early 1980 年代 didn't catch on. Computerese "the jargon of programmers" 始于 1960 年, as are computerize and computerization.

example.en: She used her computer to look up the recipe while cooking.
example.zh: 她做饭时用电脑查找了菜谱。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "one who shares the same room," from Middle French camarade (16c.), from Spanish camarada "chamber mate," originally "chamberful," from Latin camera (see camera). In Spanish, a collective noun referring to one's company. In 17c., sometimes jocularly misspelled comrogue. Related: Comradely; comradeship.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "one who shares the same room," 源自 中古法语 camarade (16 世纪), 源自 西班牙语 camarada "chamber mate," 原义为 "chamberful," 源自 拉丁语 camera （参见 camera). In 西班牙语, a collective 名词 referring to one's company. In 17 世纪, 有时 jocularly misspelled comrogue. 同源词：Comradely; comradeship.

entries.etymology: early 14c., concelen, from Old French conceler "to hide, conceal, dissimulate," from Latin concelare "to hide," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + celare "to hide," from PIE root *kel- (2) "to cover, conceal" (see cell). Replaced Old English deagan. Related: Concealed; concealing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, concelen, 源自 古法语 conceler "to hide, conceal, dissimulate," 源自 拉丁语 concelare "to hide," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + celare "to hide," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kel- (2) "to cover, conceal" （参见 cell). Replaced 古英语 deagan. 同源词：Concealed; concealing.

example.en: He tried to conceal his disappointment with a forced smile.
example.zh: 他试图用勉强的微笑掩藏自己的失望。

definitionLines: vt. 承认；退让；给予，容许
entries.definition: vt. 承认；退让；给予，容许 vi.让步
entries.etymology: 1630s, from Middle French concéder or directly from Latin concedere "give way, yield, go away, depart, retire," figuratively "agree, consent, give precedence," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + cedere "to go, grant, give way" (see cede). Related: Conceded; conceding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, 源自 中古法语 concéder or 直接源自 拉丁语 concedere "give way, yield, go away, depart, retire," figuratively "agree, consent, give precedence," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + cedere "to go, grant, give way" （参见 cede). 同源词：Conceded; conceding.

example.en: After hours of debate, the negotiator finally conceded that the original plan had flaws.
example.zh: 经过数小时辩论，谈判代表终于承认原计划存在缺陷。

entries.definition: vt. 构思；持有；以；怀孕 vi. 怀孕；（of）设想，考虑
entries.etymology: late 13c., conceiven, "take (seed) into the womb, become pregnant," from stem of Old French conceveir (Modern French concevoir), from Latin concipere (past participle conceptus) "to take in and hold; become pregnant," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + comb. form of capere "to take," from PIE *kap- "to grasp" (see capable). Meaning "take into the mind" is from mid-14c., a figurative sense also found in the Old French and Latin words. Related: Conceived; conceiving.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, conceiven, "take (seed) into the womb, become pregnant," 源自 stem of 古法语 conceveir (现代法语 concevoir), 源自 拉丁语 concipere (past participle conceptus) "to take in and hold; become pregnant," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + comb. form of capere "to take," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kap- "to grasp" （参见 capable). 义为 "take into the mind" 始于 14 世纪中期, a figurative sense also found in the 古法语 and 拉丁语 words. 同源词：Conceived; conceiving.

example.en: She struggled to conceive a plot that would keep readers engaged throughout the novel.
example.zh: 她努力构思一个能让读者在整本小说中保持投入的情节。

entries.definition: vt. （on/upon）集中；聚集；浓缩 vi. （on/upon）集中，专心
entries.etymology: 1630s, "to bring or come to a common center," from concenter (1590s), from Italian concentrare, from Latin com- "together" (see com-) + centrum "center" (see center (n.)). Meaning "condense" is from 1680s. Sense of "mentally focus" is c. 1860. Related: Concentrated; concentrating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "to bring or come to a common center," 源自 concenter (1590 年代), 源自 意大利语 concentrare, 源自 拉丁语 com- "together" （参见 com-) + centrum "center" （参见 center （名）). 义为 "condense" 始于 1680 年代. 义为 "mentally focus" is 约 1860 年. 同源词：Concentrated; concentrating.

example.en: You need to concentrate on your studies if you want to pass the exam.
example.zh: 如果你想通过考试，就需要专心学习。

definitionLines: n. 专注，专心；集中；浓度
entries.definition: n. 专注，专心；集中；浓度
entries.etymology: 1630s, "action of bringing to a center," noun of action from verb concentrate (v.). Meaning "a mass so collected" is from 1670s; "continuous focus of mental activity" is from 1846.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "action of bringing to a center," 名词 of action 源自 动词 concentrate （动）. 义为 "a mass so collected" 始于 1670 年代; "continuous focus of mental activity" 始于 1846 年.

example.en: She needs complete silence to maintain her concentration while studying.
example.zh: 她学习时需要完全安静来保持专注。

entries.definition: vt. 涉及，关系到 n./v. 关心，挂念
entries.etymology: early 15c., "perceive, distinguish," also "refer to, relate to," from Middle French concerner, from Medieval Latin concernere "concern, touch, belong to," figurative use of Late Latin concernere "to sift, mix, as in a sieve," from Latin com- "with" (see com-) + cernere "to sift," hence "perceive, comprehend" (see crisis). Apparently the sense of the prefix shifted to intensive in Medieval Latin. Meaning "worry" is 17c. Related: Concerned; concerning. Letter opening to whom it may concern attested by 1740.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "perceive, distinguish," also "refer to, relate to," 源自 中古法语 concerner, 源自 中古拉丁语 concernere "concern, touch, belong to," figurative use of 晚期拉丁语 concernere "to sift, mix, as in a sieve," 源自 拉丁语 com- "with" （参见 com-) + cernere "to sift," hence "perceive, comprehend" （参见 crisis). Apparently the 语义 the prefix shifted to intensive in 中古拉丁语. 义为 "worry" is 17 世纪 同源词：Concerned; concerning. Letter opening to whom it may concern attested 截至 1740 年.

example.en: The new tax reform concerns every household with an income above the threshold.
example.zh: 新的税制改革涉及所有收入超过门槛的家庭。

entries.etymology:
1660s, "agreement, accord, harmony," from French concert (16c.), from Italian concerto "concert, harmony," from concertare "bring into agreement," in Latin "to contend, contest, dispute," from com- "with" (see com-) + certare "to contend, strive," frequentative of certus, variant past participle of cernere "separate, decide" (see crisis).

Before the word entered English, meaning shifted from "to strive against" to "to strive alongside." Sense of "public musical performance" is 1680s. But Klein considers this too much of a stretch and suggests Latin concentare "to sing together" (from con- + cantare "to sing") as the source of the Italian word in the musical sense.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, "agreement, accord, harmony," 源自 法语 concert (16 世纪), 源自 意大利语 concerto "concert, harmony," 源自 concertare "bring into agreement," in 拉丁语 "to contend, contest, dispute," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + certare "to contend, strive," 为 … 的反复体 certus, variant 为 … 的过去分词 cernere "separate, decide" （参见 crisis). Before the word entered English, 意为 shifted 源自 "to strive against" to "to strive alongside." 义为 "public musical performance" is 1680 年代. But Klein considers this too much of a stretch and suggests 拉丁语 concentare "to sing together" (源自 con- + cantare "to sing") as the source of the 意大利语 word in the musical sense.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Old French concession (14c.) or directly from Latin concessionem (nominative concessio) "an allowing, conceding," noun of action from past participle stem of concedere (see concede). Meaning "right or privilege granted by government" is from 1650s. "Refreshment stand" sense is from 1910.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 concession (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 concessionem (主格 concessio) "an allowing, conceding," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of concedere （参见 concede). 义为 "right or privilege granted by government" 始于 1650 年代. "Refreshment stand" sense 始于 1910 年.

example.en: The union made a major concession during the wage negotiations.
example.zh: 工会在薪资谈判中做出了重大让步。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Latin concisus "cut off, brief," past participle of concidere "to cut off, cut up, cut through, cut to pieces," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + caedere "to cut" (see -cide). Related: Concisely.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 concisus "cut off, brief," 为 … 的过去分词 concidere "to cut off, cut up, cut through, cut to pieces," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + caedere "to cut" （参见 -cide). 同源词：Concisely.

definitionLines: vt. 结束，完结；下结论，断定
entries.definition: vt. 结束，完结；下结论，断定
entries.etymology: early 14c., "end an argument," from Latin concludere "to shut up, enclose," from com- "together" (see com-) + -cludere, comb. form of claudere "to shut" (see close (v.)). Meaning "reach a mental conclusion, deduce" is from late 14c., a sense also in Latin. Related: Concluded; concluding.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "end an argument," 源自 拉丁语 concludere "to shut up, enclose," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + -cludere, comb. form of claudere "to shut" （参见 close （动）). 义为 "reach a mental conclusion, deduce" 始于 14 世纪晚期, a sense also in 拉丁语. 同源词：Concluded; concluding.

example.en: After months of research, the report concludes that action is needed.
example.zh: 经过数月研究，报告得出结论：需要采取行动。

definitionLines: n. 结束，终结，结论；推断，推论
entries.definition: n. 结束，终结，结论；推断，推论
entries.etymology: late 14c., "deduction or conclusion reached by reasoning," from Old French conclusion "conclusion, result, outcome," from Latin conclusionem (nominative conclusio), noun of action from past participle stem of concludere (see conclude). Also, from late 14c. "the end" (usually of speech or writing), "closing passages of a speech or writing."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "deduction or conclusion reached by reasoning," 源自 古法语 conclusion "conclusion, result, outcome," 源自 拉丁语 conclusionem (主格 conclusio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of concludere （参见 conclude). Also, 源自 14 世纪晚期 "the end" (通常 of speech or writing), "closing passages of a speech or writing."

example.en: The detective drew a clear conclusion from the evidence.
example.zh: 侦探从证据中得出了清晰的结论。

entries.definition: n. 混凝土 a. 具体的，实质性的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "actual, solid," from Latin concretus "condensed, hardened, thick, hard, stiff, curdled, congealed, clotted," figuratively "thick; dim," literally "grown together;" past participle of concrescere "to grow together," from com- "together" (see com-) + crescere "to grow" (see crescent). A logicians' term until meaning began to expand 1600s. Noun sense of "building material made from cement, etc." is first recorded 1834.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "actual, solid," 源自 拉丁语 concretus "condensed, hardened, thick, hard, stiff, curdled, congealed, clotted," figuratively "thick; dim," 字面义为 "grown together;" 为 … 的过去分词 concrescere "to grow together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + crescere "to grow" （参见 crescent). A logicians' term until 意为 began to expand 1600 年代. Noun 语义 "building material made from cement, etc." is 首见于 1834 年.

example.en: Can you give me a concrete example to illustrate your point?
example.zh: 你能给我举一个具体的例子来阐明你的观点吗？

entries.etymology: early 14c., condempner "to blame, censure," from Old French condamner "to condemn" (11c.), from Latin condemnare "to sentence, doom, blame, disapprove," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + damnare "to harm, damage" (see damn). Replaced Old English fordeman. Related: Condemned; condemning.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, condempner "to blame, censure," 源自 古法语 condamner "to condemn" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 condemnare "to sentence, doom, blame, disapprove," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + damnare "to harm, damage" （参见 damn). Replaced 古英语 fordeman. 同源词：Condemned; condemning.

example.en: Human rights groups condemn the use of force against civilians.
example.zh: 人权组织谴责对平民使用武力的行为。

entries.definition: vi. 浓缩；凝结 vt.使浓缩；使压缩
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French condenser (14c.) or directly from Latin condensare "to make dense," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + densare "make thick," from densus "dense, thick, crowded," a word used of crowds, darkness, clouds, etc. (see dense).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 condenser (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 condensare "to make dense," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + densare "make thick," 源自 densus "dense, thick, crowded," a word used of crowds, darkness, clouds, etc. （参见 dense).

definitionLines: n. 状况，状态；（pl.）环境，情 形；条件
entries.definition: n. 状况，状态；（pl.）环境，情 形；条件
entries.etymology: early 14c., condicioun, from Old French condicion "stipulation, state, behavior, social status" (12c., Modern French condition), from Latin condicionem (nominative condicio) "agreement, situation," from condicere "to speak with, talk together," from com- "together" (see com-) + dicere "to speak" (see diction). Evolution of meaning through "stipulation, condition," to "situation, mode of being."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, condicioun, 源自 古法语 condicion "stipulation, state, behavior, social status" (12 世纪, 现代法语 condition), 源自 拉丁语 condicionem (主格 condicio) "agreement, situation," 源自 condicere "to speak with, talk together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + dicere "to speak" （参见 diction). Evolution of 意为 through "stipulation, condition," to "situation, mode of being."

example.en: Cacti thrive in dry conditions and need very little water to survive.
example.zh: 仙人掌在干旱的条件下茁壮生长，存活只需极少的水。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "a bargainer," agent noun from condition (v.). Meaning "an agent that brings something into good condition" is from 1888; since c. 1960 usually in reference to hair care products. For about 20 years before that, it often was short for air conditioner.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "a bargainer," agent 名词 源自 condition （动）. 义为 "an agent that brings something into good condition" 始于 1888 年; 自 约 1960 年 通常 in reference to hair care products. For about 20 years before that, it 常 was short for air conditioner.

definitionLines: vt. 引导，指挥；传电，传热
entries.definition: vt. 引导，指挥；传电，传热 n. 行为，品行
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to guide," from Latin conductus, past participle of conducere "to lead or bring together" (see conduce). Sense of "convey" is from early 15c.; that of "to direct, manage" is from 1630s; "to behave in a certain way" from c. 1710; "to convey" from 1740. Related: Conducted; conducting. Earlier verb in the same sense was condyten (c. 1400), related to conduit. The noun is from mid-15c., "guide" (in sauf conducte); sense of "behavior" is first recorded 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to guide," 源自 拉丁语 conductus, 为 … 的过去分词 conducere "to lead or bring together" （参见 conduce). 义为 "convey" 始于 15 世纪初; that of "to direct, manage" 始于 1630 年代; "to behave in a certain way" 源自 约 1710 年; "to convey" 自 1740 年起. 同源词：Conducted; conducting. Earlier 动词 in the same sense was condyten (约 1400 年), related to conduit. The 名词 始于 15 世纪中期, "guide" (in sauf conducte); 语义 "behavior" is 首见于 1670 年代.

example.en: The professor was asked to conduct the survey on student mental health.
example.zh: 这位教授被要求主持一项关于学生心理健康的调查。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "hiring;" 1540s, "leading, guidance," from Old French conduction "hire, renting," from Latin conductionem (nominative conductio), noun of action from past participle stem of conducere (see conduce). Sense of "conducting of a liquid through a channel" is from 1610s; in physics, of heat, etc., from 1814.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "hiring;" 1540 年代, "leading, guidance," 源自 古法语 conduction "hire, renting," 源自 拉丁语 conductionem (主格 conductio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of conducere （参见 conduce). 义为 "conducting of a liquid through a channel" 始于 1610 年代; in physics, of heat, etc., 自 1814 年起.

definitionLines: n. 领队，乐队指挥；售票员，列|congratulate
entries.definition: n. 领队，乐队指挥；售票员，列|congratulate
entries.etymology:
1520s, "one who leads or guides," from Middle French conductour (14c., Old French conduitor), from Latin conductor "one who hires, contractor," in Late Latin "a carrier," from conductus, past participle of conducere (see conduce).

Earlier in same sense was conduitour (early 15c., from Old French conduitor). Meaning "leader of an orchestra or chorus" is from 1784; meaning "one who has charge of passengers and collects fares on a railroad" is 1832, American English. Physics sense of "object or device that passes heat" is from 1745; of electricity from 1737.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "one who leads or guides," 源自 中古法语 conductour (14 世纪, 古法语 conduitor), 源自 拉丁语 conductor "one who hires, contractor," in 晚期拉丁语 "a carrier," 源自 conductus, 为 … 的过去分词 conducere （参见 conduce). Earlier in same sense was conduitour (15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 conduitor). 义为 "leader of an orchestra or chorus" 始于 1784 年; 意为 "one who has charge of passengers and collects fares on a railroad" is 1832 年, American English. Physics 语义 "object or device that passes heat" 始于 1745 年; of electricity 自 1737 年起.

example.en: The conductor raised his baton to begin the symphony.
example.zh: 指挥举起了指挥棒，开始了交响乐演奏。

entries.etymology: 1550s, "act of conferring," from Middle French conférence (15c.), from Medieval Latin conferentia, from Latin conferens, present participle of conferre (see confer). Meaning "formal meeting for consultation" is from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "act of conferring," 源自 中古法语 conférence (15 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 conferentia, 源自 拉丁语 conferens, 为 … 的现在分词 conferre （参见 confer). 义为 "formal meeting for consultation" 始于 1580 年代.

example.en: The international conference on climate change drew over two thousand delegates.
example.zh: 这场国际气候变化会议吸引了逾两千名代表与会。

entries.definition: vt. 承认；坦白；供认 vi. 承认；坦白；供认
entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French confesser (transitive and intransitive), from Vulgar Latin *confessare, from Latin confess-, past participle stem of confiteri "to acknowledge," from com- "together" (see com-) + fateri "to admit," akin to fari "speak," from PIE root *bha- (2) "to speak, tell, say" (see fame (n.)).

Its original religious sense was of one who avows his religion in spite of persecution or danger but does not suffer martyrdom. Old French confesser thus had a figurative sense of "to harm, hurt, make suffer." Related: Confessed; confessing. An Old English word for it was andettan.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 confesser (transitive and intransitive), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *confessare, 源自 拉丁语 confess-, past participle stem of confiteri "to acknowledge," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + fateri "to admit," akin to fari "speak," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *bha- (2) "to speak, tell, say" （参见 fame （名）). Its original religious sense was of one who avows his religion in spite of persecution or danger but does not suffer martyrdom. 古法语 confesser thus had a figurative 语义 "to harm, hurt, make suffer." 同源词：Confessed; confessing. An 古英语 word for it was andettan.

example.en: He finally confessed that he had never actually read the report.
example.zh: 他终于承认自己其实从未读过那份报告。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French confidence or directly from Latin confidentia, from confidentem (nominative confidens) "firmly trusting, bold," present participle of confidere "to have full trust or reliance," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + fidere "to trust" (see faith). For sense of "swindle" see con (adj.).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 confidence or 直接源自 拉丁语 confidentia, 源自 confidentem (主格 confidens) "firmly trusting, bold," 为 … 的现在分词 confidere "to have full trust or reliance," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + fidere "to trust" （参见 faith). For 语义 "swindle" 参见 con （形）.

example.en: Winning the award gave her the confidence to pursue a career in music.
example.zh: 获奖让她有了追求音乐事业的信心。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "self-reliant, sure of oneself," from Middle French confident, from Latin confidentem (nominative confidens) "firmly trusting, reliant, self-confident, bold, daring," present participle of confidere (see confidence). Related: Confidently.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "self-reliant, sure of oneself," 源自 中古法语 confident, 源自 拉丁语 confidentem (主格 confidens) "firmly trusting, reliant, self-confident, bold, daring," 为 … 的现在分词 confidere （参见 confidence). 同源词：Confidently.

example.en: She spoke in a confident tone that impressed the interviewers.
example.zh: 她用自信的语气发言，给面试官留下了深刻印象。

definitionLines: a.机密的；表示信任的；获信 任的
entries.definition: a.机密的；表示信任的；获信 任的
entries.etymology: 1759, from Latin confidentia (see confidence) + -al (1). Related: Confidentiality; confidentially.
entries.etymologyZh: 1759 年, 源自 拉丁语 confidentia （参见 confidence) + -al (1). 同源词：Confidentiality; confidentially.

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Latin configurationem (nominative configuratio), noun of action from past participle stem of configurare (see configure).
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 拉丁语 configurationem (主格 configuratio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of configurare （参见 configure).

example.en: The technician changed the network configuration to improve connection speed.
example.zh: 技术员更改了网络配置以提升连接速度。

entries.definition: n. 界限，边界 vt. 限制；禁闭
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "boundary, limit" (usually as confines), from Old French confins "boundaries," from Medieval Latin confines, from Latin confinium (plural confinia) "boundary, limit," from confine, neuter of confinis "bordering on, having the same boundaries," from com- "with" (see com-) + finis "an end" (see finish (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "boundary, limit" (通常 as confines), 源自 古法语 confins "boundaries," 源自 中古拉丁语 confines, 源自 拉丁语 confinium (plural confinia) "boundary, limit," 源自 confine, neuter of confinis "bordering on, having the same boundaries," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + finis "an end" （参见 finish （动）).

example.en: The patient must confine himself to light exercise during recovery.
example.zh: 患者在康复期间必须将自己限制在轻度运动范围内。

definitionLines: vt. 证实；进一步确定；确认， 批准
entries.definition: vt. 证实；进一步确定；确认， 批准
entries.etymology: mid-13c., confirmyn "to ratify," from Old French confermer (13c., Modern French confirmer) "strengthen, establish, consolidate; affirm by proof or evidence; anoint (a king)," from Latin confirmare "make firm, strengthen, establish," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + firmare "to strengthen," from firmus "strong, steadfast" (see firm (adj.)). Related: Confirmative; confirmatory.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, confirmyn "to ratify," 源自 古法语 confermer (13 世纪, 现代法语 confirmer) "strengthen, establish, consolidate; affirm by proof or evidence; anoint (a king)," 源自 拉丁语 confirmare "make firm, strengthen, establish," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + firmare "to strengthen," 源自 firmus "strong, steadfast" （参见 firm （形）). 同源词：Confirmative; confirmatory.

example.en: Please confirm your attendance by replying to this email before Friday.
example.zh: 请在周五之前回复此邮件以确认您的出席。

entries.definition: n.（with）争论，抵触，冲突 vi.（with）抵触，冲突
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin conflictus, past participle of confligere "to strike together, be in conflict," from com- "together" (see com-) + fligere "to strike" (see afflict). Related: Conflicted; conflicting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 conflictus, 为 … 的过去分词 confligere "to strike together, be in conflict," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + fligere "to strike" （参见 afflict). 同源词：Conflicted; conflicting.

example.en: The new policy came into conflict with the existing workplace regulations.
example.zh: 新政策与现有的工作场所法规产生了冲突。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., confourmen, from Old French conformer "conform (to), agree (to), make or be similar, be agreeable" (13c.), from Latin conformare "to fashion, to form, to shape; educate; modify," from com- "together" (see com-) + formare "to form" (see form (v.)).

Sense of "to comply with the usages of the Church of England" is from 1610s; hence conformist (1630s), opposed to non-conformist or dissenter. Related: Conformance; conformed; conforming.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, confourmen, 源自 古法语 conformer "conform (to), agree (to), make or be similar, be agreeable" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 conformare "to fashion, to form, to shape; educate; modify," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + formare "to form" （参见 form （动）). 义为 "to comply with the usages of the Church of England" 始于 1610 年代; hence conformist (1630 年代), opposed to non-conformist or dissenter. 同源词：Conformance; conformed; conforming.

entries.etymology: 1560s, "to stand in front of," from Middle French confronter (15c.), from Medieval Latin confrontare "assign limits, adjoin," from Latin com- "together" (see com-) + frontem (nominative frons) "forehead" (see front (n.)). Sense of "to face in defiance or hostility" is late 16c. Related: Confronted; confronting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "to stand in front of," 源自 中古法语 confronter (15 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 confrontare "assign limits, adjoin," 源自 拉丁语 com- "together" （参见 com-) + frontem (主格 frons) "forehead" （参见 front （名）). 义为 "to face in defiance or hostility" is 16 世纪晚期 同源词：Confronted; confronting.

example.en: We must confront the problem rather than avoid it.
example.zh: 我们必须正视这个问题，而不是逃避它。

definitionLines: a. 孔子的，儒家的；儒家学说的
entries.definition: a. 孔子的，儒家的；儒家学说的 n. 儒家，儒家学者

entries.etymology: 1550s, in literal sense "mix or mingle things so as to render the elements indistinguishable;" attested from mid-18c. in active, figurative sense of "discomfit in mind or feeling;" not in general use until 19c., taking over senses formerly belonging to confound, dumbfound, flabbergast etc. The past participle confused (q.v.) is attested much earlier (serving as an alternative past tense to confound), and the verb here might be a back-formation from it. Related: Confusing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, in literal sense "mix or mingle things so as to render the elements indistinguishable;" attested 源自 18 世纪中期 in active, figurative 语义 "discomfit in mind or feeling;" not in general use until 19 世纪, taking over senses formerly belonging to confound, dumbfound, flabbergast etc. The past participle confused (q.v.) is attested much earlier (serving 作为 alternative past tense to confound), and the 动词 here might be a back-formation 源自 it. 同源词：Confusing.

example.en: Students often confuse the two terms because they sound so similar.
example.zh: 学生们常常混淆这两个术语，因为它们听起来非常相似。

entries.etymology: late 13c., "overthrow, ruin," from Old French confusion (11c.) "disorder, confusion, shame," from Latin confusionem (nominative confusio) "a mingling, mixing, blending; confusion, disorder," noun of action from confundere "to pour together," also "to confuse" (see confound). Sense of "a putting to shame" (a sort of mental "overthrow") is late 14c. in English, while that of "mental perplexity" is from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "overthrow, ruin," 源自 古法语 confusion (11 世纪) "disorder, confusion, shame," 源自 拉丁语 confusionem (主格 confusio) "a mingling, mixing, blending; confusion, disorder," 名词 of action 源自 confundere "to pour together," also "to confuse" （参见 confound). 义为 "a putting to shame" (a sort of mental "overthrow") is 14 世纪晚期 in English, while that of "mental perplexity" 始于 1590 年代.

example.en: The sudden change in plans caused great confusion among the team members.
example.zh: 计划的突然变化在团队成员中引起了极大的困惑。

definitionLines: n. 代表大会；国会，议会
entries.definition: n. 代表大会；国会，议会
entries.etymology:
c. 1400, "body of attendants; also "meeting of armed forces" (mid-15c.); main modern sense of "coming together of people, a meeting" is from 1520s; from Latin congressus "a friendly meeting; a hostile encounter," past participle of congredi "meet with, fight with," from com- "together" (see com-) + gradi "to walk," from gradus "a step" (see grade (n.)).

Sense of "meeting of delegates" is first recorded 1670s. Meaning "sexual union" is from 1580s. Used in reference to the national legislative body of the American states since 1775 (though since 1765 in America as a name for proposed bodies). Congress of Vienna met Nov. 1, 1814, to June 8, 1815, and redrew the map of Europe with an eye to creating a balance of powers after the disruptions of Napoleon.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "body of attendants; also "meeting of armed forces" (mid-15c.); main modern sense of "coming together of people, a meeting" is from 1520s; from Latin congressus "a friendly meeting; a hostile encounter," past participle of congredi "meet with, fight with," from com- "together" (see com-) + gradi "to walk," from gradus "a step" (see grade (n.)). Sense of "meeting of delegates" is first recorded 1670s. Meaning "sexual union" 始于 1580 年代. Used in reference to the national legislative body of the American states 自 1775 年 (though 自 1765 年 in America 作为 name for proposed bodies). Congress of Vienna met Nov. 1, 1814 年, to June 8, 1815 年, and redrew the map of Europe with an eye to creating a balance of powers after the disruptions of Napoleon.

example.en: The bill was passed by congress after weeks of debate.
example.zh: 经过数周辩论，该法案由国会通过。

definitionLines: n. 连接；接合；联合；连（接）词
entries.definition: n. 连接；接合；联合；连（接）词
entries.etymology: late 14c., originally of planets, from Old French conjonction "union, joining, sexual intercourse" (12c.), from Latin coniunctionem (nominative coniunctio), from past participle stem of coniugare "join together" (see conjugal). Compare Italian congiunzione, Spanish conjunción. Grammatical sense (late 14c.) was in Latin, a loan-translation of Greek syndesmos. The word also had the meaning "sexual union" 17c.-18c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 原义为 of planets, 源自 古法语 conjonction "union, joining, sexual intercourse" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 coniunctionem (主格 coniunctio), 源自 past participle stem of coniugare "join together" （参见 conjugal). 对比 意大利语 congiunzione, 西班牙语 conjunción. Grammatical sense (14 世纪晚期) was in 拉丁语, a loan-translation of 希腊语 syndesmos. The word also had the 意为 "sexual union" 17 世纪-18 世纪

entries.definition: vt. 连接，联系 vi. 连接，相通
entries.etymology:
mid-15c., from Latin conectere "join together" (see connection). Displaced 16c. by connex (1540s), from Middle French connexer, from Latin *connexare, a supposed frequentative of conectere (past participle stem connex-). Connect was re-established 1670s.

A similar change took place in French, where connexer was superseded by connecter. Meaning "to establish a relationship" (with) is from 1881. Slang meaning "get in touch with" is attested by 1926, from telephone connections. Meaning "awaken meaningful emotions, establish rapport" is from 1942. Of a hit or blow, "to reach the target," from c. 1920. Related: Connected; connecting; connectedness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 conectere "join together" （参见 connection). Displaced 16 世纪 by connex (1540 年代), 源自 中古法语 connexer, 源自 拉丁语 *connexare, a supposed 为 … 的反复体 conectere (past participle stem connex-). Connect was re-established 1670 年代. A similar change took place in 法语, where connexer was superseded by connecter. 义为 "to establish a relationship" (with) 始于 1881 年. Slang 意为 "get in touch with" is attested 截至 1926 年, 源自 telephone connections. 义为 "awaken meaningful emotions, establish rapport" 始于 1942 年. Of a hit or blow, "to reach the target," 源自 约 1920 年. 同源词：Connected; connecting; connectedness.

example.en: The new bridge will connect the two previously isolated communities by road.
example.zh: 这座新桥将通过公路把两个此前孤立的社区连接起来。

entries.etymology:
Middle English conneccion (late 14c.), also connexioun (mid-15c.), from Old French connexion, from Latin connexionem (nominative connexio) "a binding or joining together," from *connexare, frequentative of conectere "to fasten together, to tie, join together," from com- "together" (see com-) + nectere "to bind, tie" (see nexus).

Spelling shifted from connexion to connection (especially in American English) mid-18c. under influence of connect, abetted by affection, direction, etc. See -xion.
entries.etymologyZh: 中古英语 conneccion (14 世纪晚期), also connexioun (15 世纪中期), 源自 古法语 connexion, 源自 拉丁语 connexionem (主格 connexio) "a binding or joining together," 源自 *connexare, 为 … 的反复体 conectere "to fasten together, to tie, join together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + nectere "to bind, tie" （参见 nexus). Spelling shifted 源自 connexion to connection (尤指 in American English) 18 世纪中期 under influence of connect, abetted by affection, direction, etc. See -xion.

example.en: Scientists found a clear connection between sleep and memory.
example.zh: 科学家发现睡眠与记忆之间有明显的联系。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, cunquearen, from Old French conquerre "conquer, defeat, vanquish," from Vulgar Latin *conquaerere (for Latin conquirere) "to search for, procure by effort, win," from Latin com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + quaerere "to seek, gain" (see query (v.)). Related: Conquered; conquering.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, cunquearen, 源自 古法语 conquerre "conquer, defeat, vanquish," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *conquaerere (for 拉丁语 conquirere) "to search for, procure by effort, win," 源自 拉丁语 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + quaerere "to seek, gain" （参见 query （动）). 同源词：Conquered; conquering.

entries.etymology: early 14c., a merged word from Old French conquest "acquisition" (Modern French conquêt), and Old French conqueste "conquest, acquisition" (Modern French conquête), both from past participle of conquerre, from Vulgar Latin *conquaerere (see conquer).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, a merged word 源自 古法语 conquest "acquisition" (现代法语 conquêt), and 古法语 conqueste "conquest, acquisition" (现代法语 conquête), both 源自 为 … 的过去分词 conquerre, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *conquaerere （参见 conquer).

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Old French conscience "conscience, innermost thoughts, desires, intentions; feelings" (12c.), from Latin conscientia "knowledge within oneself, sense of right, a moral sense," from conscientem (nominative consciens), present participle of conscire "be (mutually) aware," from com- "with," or "thoroughly" (see com-) + scire "to know" (see science).

Probably a loan-translation of Greek syneidesis, literally "with-knowledge." Sometimes nativized in Old English/Middle English as inwit. Russian also uses a loan-translation, so-vest, "conscience," literally "with-knowledge."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 conscience "conscience, innermost thoughts, desires, intentions; feelings" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 conscientia "knowledge within oneself, sense of right, a moral sense," 源自 conscientem (主格 consciens), 为 … 的现在分词 conscire "be (mutually) aware," 源自 com- "with," or "thoroughly" （参见 com-) + scire "to know" （参见 science). Probably a loan-translation of 希腊语 syneidesis, 字面义为 "with-knowledge." Sometimes nativized in 古英语/中古英语 as inwit. 俄语 also uses a loan-translation, so-vest, "conscience," 字面义为 "with-knowledge."

example.en: His conscience would not allow him to accept the bribe.
example.zh: 他的良心不允许他接受贿赂。

definitionLines: a.意识到的；有知觉的；有觉悟 的，自觉的
entries.definition: a.意识到的；有知觉的；有觉悟 的，自觉的
entries.etymology: c. 1600, "knowing, privy to," from Latin conscius "knowing, aware," from conscire (see conscience); probably a loan-translation of Greek syneidos. A word adopted from the Latin poets and much mocked at first. Sense of "active and awake" is from 1837.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "knowing, privy to," 源自 拉丁语 conscius "knowing, aware," 源自 conscire （参见 conscience); 可能 a loan-translation of 希腊语 syneidos. A word adopted 源自 拉丁语 poets and much mocked at first. 义为 "active and awake" 始于 1837 年.

example.en: She became conscious of her surroundings the moment she woke up.
example.zh: 她一醒来就对周围的环境有了意识。

entries.etymology: 1854 as a term in physiology; 1861 of persons; from Latin consensus "agreement, accord," past participle of consentire (see consent (v.)). There is an isolated instance of the word from 1633.
entries.etymologyZh: 1854 年 作为 term in physiology; 1861 年 of persons; 源自 拉丁语 consensus "agreement, accord," 为 … 的过去分词 consentire （参见 consent （动）). There is an isolated instance of the word 自 1633 年起.

example.en: Scientists finally reached a consensus on the cause of the disease.
example.zh: 科学家们最终就该疾病的病因达成了共识。

definitionLines: n. 同意；赞成；（意见等的）一致
entries.definition: vi. 同意；答应；赞成 n. 同意；赞成；（意见等的）一致
entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French consentir (12c.) "agree, comply," from Latin consentire "feel together," from com- "with" (see com-) + sentire "to feel" (see sense (n.)). "Feeling together," hence, "agreeing, giving permission," apparently a sense evolution that took place in French before the word reached English. Related: Consented; consenting.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 consentir (12 世纪) "agree, comply," 源自 拉丁语 consentire "feel together," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + sentire "to feel" （参见 sense （名）). "Feeling together," hence, "agreeing, giving permission," 似乎 a sense evolution that took place in 法语 before the word reached English. 同源词：Consented; consenting.

example.en: The patient must consent to the operation before it can proceed.
example.zh: 手术进行前，患者必须同意该手术。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "inference, conclusion," from Old French consequence "result" (13c., Modern French conséquence), from Latin consequentia, from consequentem (nominative consequens), present participle of consequi "to follow after," from com- "with" (see com-) + sequi "to follow" (see sequel). Sense of "importance" (c. 1600) is from notion of being "pregnant with consequences."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "inference, conclusion," 源自 古法语 consequence "result" (13 世纪, 现代法语 conséquence), 源自 拉丁语 consequentia, 源自 consequentem (主格 consequens), 为 … 的现在分词 consequi "to follow after," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + sequi "to follow" （参见 sequel). 义为 "importance" (约 1600 年) 始于 概念 being "pregnant with consequences."

example.en: Failing to back up your files can have serious consequences if your hard drive fails suddenly.
example.zh: 如果你的硬盘突然损坏，未能备份文件可能会产生严重的后果。

definitionLines: a. 作为结果的，随之发生的
entries.definition: a. 作为结果的，随之发生的
entries.etymology: late 14c., in various senses now restricted to consequence, from Middle French conséquent "following, resulting," from Latin consequentem (nominative consequens); see consequence. Meaning "an event which follows another" is from 1610s. Mathematical sense is from 1560s. Related: Consequently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in various senses 现在 restricted to consequence, 源自 中古法语 conséquent "following, resulting," 源自 拉丁语 consequentem (主格 consequens); 参见 consequence. 义为 "an event which follows another" 始于 1610 年代. Mathematical sense 始于 1560 年代. 同源词：Consequently.

example.en: The project was poorly planned; consequently, it ran over budget and schedule.
example.zh: 该项目计划不当；因此，它超出了预算和时间表。

definitionLines: n.（对自然资源的）保护；保 存；节省
entries.definition: n.（对自然资源的）保护；保 存；节省
entries.etymology: late 14c., conservacioun, "preservation of one's health and soundness," from Latin conservationem (nominative conservatio) "a keeping, preserving, conserving," noun of action from past participle stem of conservare (see conserve). Meaning "preservation of existing conditions" in any sense is from mid-15c. Since late 15c., in reference to English municipal authorities who had charge of rivers, sewers, forests, fisheries, etc. Specifically of the environment from 1922.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, conservacioun, "preservation of one's health and soundness," 源自 拉丁语 conservationem (主格 conservatio) "a keeping, preserving, conserving," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of conservare （参见 conserve). 义为 "preservation of existing conditions" in any sense 始于 15 世纪中期 自 15 世纪晚期, in reference to English municipal authorities who had charge of rivers, sewers, forests, fisheries, etc. Specifically of the environment 自 1922 年起.

example.en: Wildlife conservation efforts have helped increase the population of endangered species.
example.zh: 野生动物保护工作已帮助增加了濒危物种的数量。

definitionLines: vt. 考虑，细想；认，以；关 心，顾及
entries.definition: vt. 考虑，细想；认，以；关 心，顾及
entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French considerer (13c.) "reflect on, consider, study," from Latin considerare "to look at closely, observe," perhaps literally "to observe the stars," from com- "with" (see com-) + sidus (genitive sideris) "constellation" (see sidereal).

Perhaps a metaphor from navigation, but more likely reflecting Roman obsession with divination by astrology. Tucker doubts the connection with sidus, however, because it is "quite inapplicable to desiderare," and suggests derivation instead from the PIE root of English side meaning "stretch, extend," and a sense for the full word of "survey on all sides" or "dwell long upon." Related: Considered; considering.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 considerer (13 世纪) "reflect on, consider, study," 源自 拉丁语 considerare "to look at closely, observe," 或许 字面义为 "to observe the stars," 源自 com- "with" （参见 com-) + sidus (属格 sideris) "constellation" （参见 sidereal). Perhaps a metaphor 源自 navigation, but more likely reflecting Roman obsession with divination by astrology. Tucker doubts the connection with sidus, however, because it is "quite inapplicable to desiderare," and suggests derivation instead 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root of English side 意为 "stretch, extend," and a sense for the full word of "survey on all sides" or "dwell long upon." 同源词：Considered; considering.

example.en: You should consider all your options carefully before making a final decision.
example.zh: 在做最终决定之前，你应该仔细考虑所有选项。

definitionLines: a. 值得考虑的；相当的，可观的
entries.definition: a. 值得考虑的；相当的，可观的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "capable of being considered," from Medieval Latin considerabilis "worthy to be considered," from Latin considerare (see consider). Meaning "pretty large" is from 1640s (implied in considerably).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "capable of being considered," 源自 中古拉丁语 considerabilis "worthy to be considered," 源自 拉丁语 considerare （参见 consider). 义为 "pretty large" 始于 1640 年代 (implied in considerably).

example.en: The charity raised a considerable sum for disaster relief.
example.zh: 慈善机构为救灾筹集了相当可观的款项。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "marked by deliberation," from Latin consideratus, past participle of considerare (see consider). Of persons, "deliberate, prudent," 1580s; meaning "showing consideration for others" is from c. 1700. Related: Considerately; considerateness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "marked by deliberation," 源自 拉丁语 consideratus, 为 … 的过去分词 considerare （参见 consider). Of persons, "deliberate, prudent," 1580 年代; 意为 "showing consideration for others" 始于 约 1700 年. 同源词：Considerately; considerateness.

definitionLines: n. 考虑；要考虑的事；体贴， 关心
entries.definition: n. 考虑；要考虑的事；体贴， 关心
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "a beholding, looking at," also "keeping in mind," from Old French consideracion (12c., Modern French considération), from Latin considerationem (nominative consideratio) "consideration, contemplation, reflection," noun of action from past participle stem of considerare (see consider). Meaning "a taking into account" is from mid-15c.; that of "something given in payment" is from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "a beholding, looking at," also "keeping in mind," 源自 古法语 consideracion (12 世纪, 现代法语 considération), 源自 拉丁语 considerationem (主格 consideratio) "consideration, contemplation, reflection," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of considerare （参见 consider). 义为 "a taking into account" 始于 15 世纪中期; that of "something given in payment" 始于 约 1600 年.

example.en: Cost is an important consideration when choosing between the two plans.
example.zh: 在两个方案之间做选择时，成本是一个重要的考量因素。

definitionLines: vi.（of）由…•…构成，由……组 成；（in）在于
entries.definition: vi.（of）由…•…构成，由……组 成；（in）在于
entries.etymology: 1520s, from Middle French consister (14c.) or directly from Latin consistere "to stand firm, take a standing position, stop, halt," from com- "together" (see com-) + sistere "to place," causative of stare "to stand, be standing" (see stay (v.)). Related: Consisted; consisting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 中古法语 consister (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 consistere "to stand firm, take a standing position, stop, halt," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + sistere "to place," 为 … 的使役形式 stare "to stand, be standing" （参见 stay （动）). 同源词：Consisted; consisting.

example.en: The United Kingdom consists of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
example.zh: 英国由英格兰、苏格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰构成。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "firmness of matter," from Medieval Latin consistentia or directly from Latin consistentem, from consistere (see consist). Meaning "state of being in agreement or harmony" (with something) is from 1650s; meaning "self-consistent" is from 1716.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "firmness of matter," 源自 中古拉丁语 consistentia or 直接源自 拉丁语 consistentem, 源自 consistere （参见 consist). 义为 "state of being in agreement or harmony" (with something) 始于 1650 年代; 意为 "self-consistent" 始于 1716 年.

example.en: The brand's success comes from the consistency of its product quality.
example.zh: 这个品牌的成功源于其产品质量的一致性。

definitionLines: a. 始终如一的，一致的
entries.definition: a. 始终如一的，一致的
entries.etymology: 1570s, "standing firm, standing still," from Latin consistentem (nominative consistens), present participle of consistere (see consist). Modern sense of "agreeing" (with with) is first attested 1640s. Older sense survives in consistency. Related: Consistently.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "standing firm, standing still," 源自 拉丁语 consistentem (主格 consistens), 为 … 的现在分词 consistere （参见 consist). 现代 语义 "agreeing" (with with) is 最早见于 1640 年代. Older sense survives in consistency. 同源词：Consistently.

example.en: Her consistent performance throughout the season earned her a spot on the national team.
example.zh: 她整个赛季始终如一的表现为她赢得了国家队的一席之地。

entries.etymology: 1690s, from French consoler "to comfort, console," from Latin consolari "offer solace, encourage, comfort, cheer," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + solari "to comfort" (see solace). Or perhaps a back-formation from consolation. The Latin word is glossed in Old English by frefran. Related: Consoled; consoling.
entries.etymologyZh: 1690 年代, 源自 法语 consoler "to comfort, console," 源自 拉丁语 consolari "offer solace, encourage, comfort, cheer," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + solari "to comfort" （参见 solace). Or 或许 a back-formation 源自 consolation. The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by frefran. 同源词：Consoled; consoling.

entries.definition: vt. 巩固，使固定；联合 vi. 巩固，加强
entries.etymology: 1510s, "to compact into one body," from Latin consolidatus, past participle of consolidare "to make solid," from com- "together" (see com-) + solidare "to make solid" (see solid). Meaning "to make firm or strong" is from mid-16c. Related: Consolidated; consolidating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "to compact into one body," 源自 拉丁语 consolidatus, 为 … 的过去分词 consolidare "to make solid," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + solidare "to make solid" （参见 solid). 义为 "to make firm or strong" 始于 16 世纪中期 同源词：Consolidated; consolidating.

definitionLines: a. 显著的；显而易见的
entries.definition: a. 显著的；显而易见的
entries.etymology: 1540s, from Latin conspicuus "visible, open to view, striking," from conspicere "to look at, observe, see, notice," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + specere (see scope (n.1)). Phrase conspicuous by its absence (1859) is said to be from Tacitus ("Annals" iii.76), in a passage about certain images: "sed præfulgebant ... eo ipso quod effigies eorum non visebantur."
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 源自 拉丁语 conspicuus "visible, open to view, striking," 源自 conspicere "to look at, observe, see, notice," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + specere （参见 scope (n.1)). Phrase conspicuous by its absence (1859 年) is said to be 源自 Tacitus ("Annals" iii.76), in a passage about certain images: "sed præfulgebant ... eo ipso quod effigies eorum non visebantur."

definitionLines: a.不断的，持续的；始终如一 的；坚定的，忠实的；恒定的， 经常的
entries.definition: a.不断的，持续的；始终如一 的；坚定的，忠实的；恒定的， 经常的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "steadfast, resolute," from Old French constant (14c.) or directly from Latin constantem (nominative constans) "standing firm, stable, steadfast, faithful," present participle of constare, from com- "together" (see com-) + stare "to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand" (see stet). Of actions and conditions from 1650s. Related: Constantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "steadfast, resolute," 源自 古法语 constant (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 constantem (主格 constans) "standing firm, stable, steadfast, faithful," 为 … 的现在分词 constare, 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + stare "to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand" （参见 stet). Of actions and conditions 源自 1650 年代. 同源词：Constantly.

example.en: The city is under constant pressure to improve its public transport system.
example.zh: 该市持续承受着改善公共交通系统的压力。

definitionLines: n2. 选举区；选举区全体选民
entries.definition: n2. 选举区；选举区全体选民
entries.etymology: "body of constituents," 1806, from constituent + -cy.
entries.etymologyZh: "body of constituents," 1806 年, 源自 constituent + -cy.

example.en: The senator returned to her constituency to meet local voters.
example.zh: 这位参议员回到她的选区与当地选民会面。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., verb use of adjective constitute, "made up, formed" (late 14c.), from Latin constitutus "arranged, settled," past participle adjective from constituere "to cause to stand, set up, fix, place, establish, set in order; form something new; resolve," of persons, "to appoint to an office," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + statuere "to set," from PIE root *stā- "to stand," with derivatives meaning "place or thing that is standing" (see stet). Related: Constituted; constituting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 为 … 的动词用法 形容词 constitute, "made up, formed" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 拉丁语 constitutus "arranged, settled," past participle 形容词 源自 constituere "to cause to stand, set up, fix, place, establish, set in order; form something new; resolve," of persons, "to appoint to an office," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + statuere "to set," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand," with derivatives 意为 "place or thing that is standing" （参见 stet). 同源词：Constituted; constituting.

example.en: Seven departments constitute the entire research institute.
example.zh: 七个部门构成了整个研究所。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "law, regulation, edict," from Old French constitucion (12c.) "constitution, establishment," and directly from Latin constitutionem (nominative constitutio) "act of settling, settled condition, anything arranged or settled upon, regulation, order, ordinance," from constitut-, past participle stem of constituere (see constitute).

Meaning "action of establishing" is from 1580s; that of "way in which a thing is constituted" is from c. 1600; that of "physical health, strength and vigor of the body" is from 1550s; of the mind, "temperament, character" from 1580s. Sense of "mode of organization of a state" is from c. 1600; that of "system of principles by which a community is governed" dates from 1730s; especially of a document of written laws since the U.S. and French constitutions, late 18c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "law, regulation, edict," 源自 古法语 constitucion (12 世纪) "constitution, establishment," and 直接源自 拉丁语 constitutionem (主格 constitutio) "act of settling, settled condition, anything arranged or settled upon, regulation, order, ordinance," 源自 constitut-, past participle stem of constituere （参见 constitute). 义为 "action of establishing" 始于 1580 年代; that of "way in which a thing is constituted" 始于 约 1600 年; that of "physical health, strength and vigor of the body" 始于 1550 年代; of the mind, "temperament, character" 源自 1580 年代. 义为 "mode of organization of a state" 始于 约 1600 年; that of "system of principles by which a community is governed" dates 源自 1730 年代; 尤指 of a document of written laws 自 the U.S. and 法语 constitutions, 18 世纪晚期

example.en: Any new law must be consistent with the country's constitution.
example.zh: 任何新法律都必须与该国宪法保持一致。

entries.etymology: early 14c., constreyen, from stem of Old French constreindre (Modern French contraindre) "restrain, control," from Latin constringere "to bind together, tie tightly, fetter, shackle, chain," from com- "together" (see com-) + stringere "to draw tight" (see strain (v.)). Related: Constrained; constraining.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, constreyen, 源自 stem of 古法语 constreindre (现代法语 contraindre) "restrain, control," 源自 拉丁语 constringere "to bind together, tie tightly, fetter, shackle, chain," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + stringere "to draw tight" （参见 strain （动）). 同源词：Constrained; constraining.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin constrictus, past participle of constringere "compress" (see constrain). A direct borrowing from Latin of the same word which, via French, became constrain. Related: Constricted; constricting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 constrictus, 为 … 的过去分词 constringere "compress" （参见 constrain). A direct borrowing 源自 拉丁语 of the same word which, 经由 法语, became constrain. 同源词：Constricted; constricting.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin constructus, past participle of construere "to heap up" (see construction). Related: Constructed; constructing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 constructus, 为 … 的过去分词 construere "to heap up" （参见 construction). 同源词：Constructed; constructing.

example.en: Engineers were hired to construct a suspension bridge over the canyon.
example.zh: 工程师们受雇在峡谷上建造一座悬索桥。

entries.definition: vt.（on）请教，咨询；查阅；就诊 vi. 商量，会诊
entries.etymology: 1520s, from Middle French consulter (16c.), from Latin consultare "consult, take the advice of," frequentative of consulere "to take counsel, meet and consider" (see consultation). Related: Consulted; consulting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 中古法语 consulter (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 consultare "consult, take the advice of," 为 … 的反复体 consulere "to take counsel, meet and consider" （参见 consultation). 同源词：Consulted; consulting.

example.en: Patients are advised to consult a doctor before taking any new medication.
example.zh: 建议患者在服用任何新药之前先咨询医生。

entries.etymology: 1690s, of persons going to oracles, from consult + -ant. Of physicians, from 1878; meaning "one qualified to give professional advice" is first attested 1893 in a Sherlock Holmes story. Related: Consultancy (1955).
entries.etymologyZh: 1690 年代, of persons going to oracles, 源自 consult + -ant. Of physicians, 自 1878 年起; 意为 "one qualified to give professional advice" is 最早见于 1893 年 in a Sherlock Holmes story. 同源词：Consultancy (1955 年).

example.en: The startup hired an outside consultant to restructure its financial operations.
example.zh: 这家初创企业聘请了一位外部顾问来重组其财务运营。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French consumer "to consume" (12c.) and directly from Latin consumere "to use up, eat, waste," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + sumere "to take," from sub- "under" + emere "to buy, take" (see exempt (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 consumer "to consume" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 consumere "to use up, eat, waste," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + sumere "to take," 源自 sub- "under" + emere "to buy, take" （参见 exempt （形）).

example.en: Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity to keep servers running.
example.zh: 数据中心消耗大量电力来维持服务器运转。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "one who squanders or wastes," agent noun from consume. In economic sense, "one who uses up goods or articles" (opposite of producer) from 1745. Consumer goods is attested from 1890. In U.S., consumer price index calculated since 1919, tracking "changes in the prices paid by urban consumers for a representative basket of goods and services" [Bureau of Labor Statistics]; abbreviation CPI is attested by 1971.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "one who squanders or wastes," agent 名词 源自 consume. In economic sense, "one who uses up goods or articles" (opposite of producer) 自 1745 年起. Consumer goods 见于 1890 年. In U.S., consumer price index calculated 自 1919 年, tracking "changes in the prices paid by urban consumers for a representative basket of goods and services" [Bureau of Labor Statistics]; abbreviation CPI is attested 截至 1971 年.

example.en: Rising prices are forcing consumers to cut back on spending.
example.zh: 价格上涨迫使消费者削减开支。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "wasting of the body by disease; wasting disease" (replacing Old English yfeladl "the evil disease"), from Old French consumpcion, from Latin consumptionem (nominative consumptio) "a using up, wasting," noun of state from past participle stem of consumere (see consume). Meaning "the using up of material" is 1530s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "wasting of the body by disease; wasting disease" (replacing 古英语 yfeladl "the evil disease"), 源自 古法语 consumpcion, 源自 拉丁语 consumptionem (主格 consumptio) "a using up, wasting," 名词 of state 源自 past participle stem of consumere （参见 consume). 义为 "the using up of material" is 1530 年代.

example.en: Rising energy consumption has put pressure on global fuel supplies.
example.zh: 能源消耗的增加给全球燃料供应带来了压力。

entries.etymology:
1620s, "action of touching," from Latin contactus "a touching," from past participle of contingere "to touch, seize," from com- "together" (see com-) + tangere "to touch" (see tangent (adj.)).

Figurative sense of "connection, communication" is from 1818. As a signal to the person about to spin an aircraft propeller that the ignition is switched on, the word was in use by 1913. Contact lens is first recorded 1888; short form contact is from 1961.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "action of touching," 源自 拉丁语 contactus "a touching," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 contingere "to touch, seize," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + tangere "to touch" （参见 tangent （形）). Figurative 语义 "connection, communication" 始于 1818 年. 作为 signal to the person about to spin an aircraft propeller that the ignition is switched on, the word was in use 截至 1913 年. Contact lens is 首见于 1888 年; short form contact 始于 1961 年.

example.en: For urgent matters, you can contact the helpdesk directly by phone.
example.zh: 如有紧急事项，您可以直接通过电话联系服务台。

definitionLines: vt. 容纳，含有，装有；克制，抑 制
entries.definition: vt. 容纳，含有，装有；克制，抑 制
entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French contein-, stem of contenir, from Latin continere (transitive) "to hold together, enclose," from com- "together" (see com-) + tenere "to hold" (see tenet). Related: Containable.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 contein-, stem of contenir, 源自 拉丁语 continere (transitive) "to hold together, enclose," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + tenere "to hold" （参见 tenet). 同源词：Containable.

example.en: This tank can contain up to five hundred liters of rainwater.
example.zh: 这个水箱最多能容纳五百升雨水。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., agent noun from contain.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, agent 名词 源自 contain.

example.en: Place the leftover food in a sealed container before putting it in the fridge.
example.zh: 把剩余食物放入密封容器后再放进冰箱。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French contaminer, from Latin contaminatus, past participle of contaminare "to defile," from contamen "contact, pollution," from com- "together" (see com-) + *tag-, base of tangere "to touch" (see tangent (adj.)). Related: Contaminant (1934); contaminable.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 contaminer, 源自 拉丁语 contaminatus, 为 … 的过去分词 contaminare "to defile," 源自 contamen "contact, pollution," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + *tag-, base of tangere "to touch" （参见 tangent （形）). 同源词：Contaminant (1934 年); contaminable.

definitionLines: vt. 沉思；注视；思忖；预期
vi. 冥思苦想；深思熟虑
entries.definition: vt. 沉思；注视；思忖；预期 vi. 冥思苦想；深思熟虑
entries.etymology: 1590s, from Latin contemplatus, past participle of contemplari "survey, observe" (see contemplation). Related: Contemplated; contemplating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 拉丁语 contemplatus, 为 … 的过去分词 contemplari "survey, observe" （参见 contemplation). 同源词：Contemplated; contemplating.

example.en: She sat quietly, beginning to contemplate the consequences of her decision.
example.zh: 她静静地坐着，开始深思自己决定的后果。

definitionLines: a.当代的；同时代的；属于同一 时期的
n. 同时代的人；同时期的东西
entries.definition: a.当代的；同时代的；属于同一 时期的 n. 同时代的人；同时期的东西
entries.etymology: 1630s, from Medieval Latin contemporarius, from Latin com- "with" (see com-) + temporarius "of time," from tempus "time, season, portion of time" (see temporal (adj.)). Meaning "modern, characteristic of the present" is from 1866.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 contemporarius, 源自 拉丁语 com- "with" （参见 com-) + temporarius "of time," 源自 tempus "time, season, portion of time" （参见 temporal （形）). 义为 "modern, characteristic of the present" 始于 1866 年.

example.en: The museum features works by both classical and contemporary artists.
example.zh: 该博物馆展出古典艺术家和当代艺术家的作品。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin contemptus "scorn," from past participle of contemnere "to scorn, despise," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + *temnere "to slight, scorn," which is of uncertain origin. Phrase contempt of court is attested from 19c., though the idea is several centuries older.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 contemptus "scorn," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 contemnere "to scorn, despise," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + *temnere "to slight, scorn," which is 来源存疑. Phrase contempt of court 见于 19 世纪, though the idea is several centuries older.

entries.definition: n. （pl.）内容，目录 a. 满足的，满意的
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French contenter, from content (adj.) "satisfied," from Latin contentus "contained, satisfied," past participle of continere (see contain). Sense evolved through "contained," "restrained," to "satisfied," as the contented person's desires are bound by what he or she already has. Related: Contented; contentedly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 contenter, 源自 content （形） "satisfied," 源自 拉丁语 contentus "contained, satisfied," 为 … 的过去分词 continere （参见 contain). Sense evolved through "contained," "restrained," to "satisfied," as the contented person's desires are bound by what he or she already has. 同源词：Contented; contentedly.

example.en: She felt perfectly content with her simple but fulfilling life in the countryside.
example.zh: 她对自己在乡下简单却充实的生活感到非常满足。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from French contester "dispute, oppose," from Middle French, from Latin contestari (litem) "to call to witness, bring action," from com- "together" (see com-) + testari "to bear witness," from testis "a witness," (see testament). Calling witnesses as the first step in a legal combat. Related: Contestable; contested; contesting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 contester "dispute, oppose," 源自 中古法语, 源自 拉丁语 contestari (litem) "to call to witness, bring action," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + testari "to bear witness," 源自 testis "a witness," （参见 testament). Calling witnesses as the first step in a legal combat. 同源词：Contestable; contested; contesting.

entries.etymology: 1660s, from French contestant, present participle of contester (see contest (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 法语 contestant, 为 … 的现在分词 contester （参见 contest （动）).

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin contextus "a joining together," originally past participle of contexere "to weave together," from com- "together" (see com-) + texere "to weave, to make" (see texture (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 contextus "a joining together," 原义为 为 … 的过去分词 contexere "to weave together," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + texere "to weave, to make" （参见 texture （名）).

example.en: Read the word in its context to figure out what it means.
example.zh: 在语境中读这个词，才能弄清它的含义。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "self-restraining," from Old French continent and directly from Latin continentem (nominative continens) "holding together, continuous," present participle of continere "hold together" (see contain). Meaning moved from "exercising self-restraint" to "chaste" 14c., and to bowel and bladder control 19c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "self-restraining," 源自 古法语 continent and 直接源自 拉丁语 continentem (主格 continens) "holding together, continuous," 为 … 的现在分词 continere "hold together" （参见 contain). 义为 moved 源自 "exercising self-restraint" to "chaste" 14 世纪, and to bowel and bladder control 19 世纪

example.en: Africa is the second largest continent in the world.
example.zh: 非洲是世界第二大洲。

entries.etymology: early 14c., continuell, from Old French continuel (12c.), from Latin continuus (see continue). That which is continual is that which is either always going on or recurs at short intervals and never comes to an end; that which is continuous is that in which there is no break between the beginning and the end. Related: Continually (c. 1300, contynuelliche).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, continuell, 源自 古法语 continuel (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 continuus （参见 continue). That which is continual is that which is either always going on or recurs at short intervals and never comes to an end; that which is continuous is that in which there is no break between the beginning and the end. 同源词：Continually (约 1300 年, contynuelliche).

entries.etymology: mid-14c., contynuen, from Old French continuer (13c.), from Latin continuare "join together, connect, make or be continuous," from continuus "uninterrupted," from continere (intransitive) "to be uninterrupted," literally "to hang together" (see contain). Related: Continued; continuing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, contynuen, 源自 古法语 continuer (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 continuare "join together, connect, make or be continuous," 源自 continuus "uninterrupted," 源自 continere (intransitive) "to be uninterrupted," 字面义为 "to hang together" （参见 contain). 同源词：Continued; continuing.

example.en: Despite the setback, the team chose to continue with the original plan.
example.zh: 尽管遭遇挫折，团队还是选择继续执行原计划。

entries.etymology: 1640s, from French continueus or directly from Latin continuus "uninterrupted, hanging together" (see continue). Related: Continuously.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 法语 continueus or 直接源自 拉丁语 continuus "uninterrupted, hanging together" （参见 continue). 同源词：Continuously.

example.en: The factory has been under continuous pressure to cut costs throughout the year.
example.zh: 整年来，工厂一直处于持续削减成本的压力下。

entries.definition: n. 契约，合同，包工 v.收缩；感染；定约
entries.etymology: late 14c., "make narrow, draw together;" early 15c. "make an agreement;" from Middle French contracter, from Latin contractus, past participle of contrahere "to draw together, combine, make an agreement" (see contract (n.)). Related: Contracted; contracting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "make narrow, draw together;" 15 世纪初 "make an agreement;" 源自 中古法语 contracter, 源自 拉丁语 contractus, 为 … 的过去分词 contrahere "to draw together, combine, make an agreement" （参见 contract （名）). 同源词：Contracted; contracting.

example.en: Both companies signed a binding contract agreeing on the terms of the partnership.
example.zh: 两家公司签署了一份具有约束力的合同，就合作条款达成了一致。

definitionLines: vt. 反驳；否定；与……矛盾； 与……抵触
vi. 反驳；否认；发生矛盾
entries.definition: vt. 反驳；否定；与……矛盾； 与……抵触 vi. 反驳；否认；发生矛盾
entries.etymology: 1570s, "speak against," also "assert the contrary" (1580s), from Latin contradictus, past participle of contradicere (see contradiction). Related: Contradicted; contradicting; contradictive.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "speak against," also "assert the contrary" (1580 年代), 源自 拉丁语 contradictus, 为 … 的过去分词 contradicere （参见 contradiction). 同源词：Contradicted; contradicting; contradictive.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French contradiction or directly from Latin contradictionem (nominative contradictio) "a reply, objection, counterargument," noun of action from past participle stem of contradicere, in classical Latin contra dicere "to speak against," from contra "against" (see contra) + dicere "to say, speak" (see diction).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 contradiction or 直接源自 拉丁语 contradictionem (主格 contradictio) "a reply, objection, counterargument," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of contradicere, in classical 拉丁语 contra dicere "to speak against," 源自 contra "against" （参见 contra) + dicere "to say, speak" （参见 diction).

example.en: There is a clear contradiction between what he says and what he does.
example.zh: 他说的和他做的之间存在明显的矛盾。

entries.definition: a.（to）相反的，矛盾的 n. 相反，反面
entries.etymology:
mid-14c., from Anglo-French contrarie, from Latin contrarius "opposite, opposed," from contra "against" (see contra).

As a noun from late 13c. Related: Contrarily; contrariwise.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 contrarie, 源自 拉丁语 contrarius "opposite, opposed," 源自 contra "against" （参见 contra). 作名词时 源自 13 世纪晚期 同源词：Contrarily; contrariwise.

example.en: Contrary to popular belief, drinking coffee does not necessarily cause insomnia.
example.zh: 与普遍看法相反，喝咖啡并不一定会导致失眠。

entries.etymology:
1690s, from French contraster (Old French contrester), modified by or from Italian contrastare "stand out against, strive, contend," from Vulgar Latin *contrastare "to withstand," from Latin contra "against" (see contra) + stare "to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand" (see stet).

Middle English had contrest "to fight against, to withstand," which became extinct. Modern word re-introduced as an art term. Related: Contrasted; contrasting; contrastive.
entries.etymologyZh: 1690 年代, 源自 法语 contraster (古法语 contrester), modified by or 源自 意大利语 contrastare "stand out against, strive, contend," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *contrastare "to withstand," 源自 拉丁语 contra "against" （参见 contra) + stare "to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand" （参见 stet). 中古英语 had contrest "to fight against, to withstand," which became extinct. 现代 word re-introduced 作为 art term. 同源词：Contrasted; contrasting; contrastive.

example.en: The report highlighted a sharp contrast between urban and rural income levels.
example.zh: 报告着重指出了城乡收入水平之间的巨大差异。

entries.etymology: 1520s, from Latin contributus, past participle of contribuere "to bring together, add, unite, collect, contribute" (see contribution). Figurative sense is from 1630s. Related: Contributed; contributing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 拉丁语 contributus, 为 … 的过去分词 contribuere "to bring together, add, unite, collect, contribute" （参见 contribution). Figurative sense 始于 1630 年代. 同源词：Contributed; contributing.

example.en: Volunteers contributed greatly to the success of the community event.
example.zh: 志愿者们对社区活动的成功作出了很大的贡献。

entries.etymology:
early 14c., "to check, verify, regulate," from Anglo-French contreroller "exert authority," from Medieval Latin contrarotulus "a counter, register," from Latin contra- "against" (see contra) + rotulus, diminutive of rota "wheel" (see roll (n.)). From a medieval method of checking accounts by a duplicate register. Sense of "dominate, direct" is mid-15c. Related: Controlled; controlling.

Control group in scientific experiments is attested from 1952 (from a sense of control attested since 1875).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to check, verify, regulate," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 contreroller "exert authority," 源自 中古拉丁语 contrarotulus "a counter, register," 源自 拉丁语 contra- "against" （参见 contra) + rotulus, 为 … 的指小形式 rota "wheel" （参见 roll （名）). From a medieval method of checking accounts by a duplicate register. 义为 "dominate, direct" is 15 世纪中期 同源词：Controlled; controlling. Control group in scientific experiments 见于 1952 年 (源自 a 语义 control attested 自 1875 年).

example.en: She found it hard to control her temper when her work was unfairly criticized.
example.zh: 当她的工作受到不公正批评时，她发现很难控制自己的脾气。

definitionLines: a. 争论的；引起争论的；被议论 的；可疑的
entries.definition: a. 争论的；引起争论的；被议论 的；可疑的
entries.etymology: 1580s, from Late Latin controversialis "pertaining to controversy," from Latin controversia (see controversy).
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 controversialis "pertaining to controversy," 源自 拉丁语 controversia （参见 controversy).

example.en: The proposed pipeline project remains controversial due to environmental concerns.
example.zh: 由于环保方面的担忧，这一拟议中的管道项目仍存在争议。

entries.definition: vt. 召集，集合；传唤 vi. 聚集，集合
