entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French convenir "to suit, agree," from Latin convenire "unite, be suitable, agree, assemble," from com- "together" (see com-) + venire "to come" (see venue). Related: Convened; convener; convening.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 convenir "to suit, agree," 源自 拉丁语 convenire "unite, be suitable, agree, assemble," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + venire "to come" （参见 venue). 同源词：Convened; convener; convening.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "agreement, conformity," from Latin convenientia "meeting together, agreement, harmony," from conveniens, present participle of convenire (see convene). Meaning "suitable, adapted to existing conditions" is from c. 1600; that of "personally not difficult" is from 1703.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "agreement, conformity," 源自 拉丁语 convenientia "meeting together, agreement, harmony," 源自 conveniens, 为 … 的现在分词 convenire （参见 convene). 义为 "suitable, adapted to existing conditions" 始于 约 1600 年; that of "personally not difficult" 始于 1703 年.

example.en: The new app was designed with the user's convenience in mind.
example.zh: 这款新应用在设计时充分考虑了用户的便利性。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin convenientem (nominative conveniens), present participle of convenire (see convene).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 convenientem (主格 conveniens), 为 … 的现在分词 convenire （参见 convene).

example.en: Living near a subway station makes commuting much more convenient.
example.zh: 住在地铁站附近让通勤方便多了。

definitionLines: n. 习俗，惯例；大会，会议；公约
entries.definition: n. 习俗，惯例；大会，会议；公约
entries.etymology: early 15c., "a formal agreement," also "a formal meeting or convention" (of rulers, etc.), also "a secret agreement," from Middle French convention and directly from Latin conventionem (nominative conventio) "meeting, assembly, covenant," noun of action from past participle stem of convenire (see convene).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "a formal agreement," also "a formal meeting or convention" (of rulers, etc.), also "a secret agreement," 源自 中古法语 convention and 直接源自 拉丁语 conventionem (主格 conventio) "meeting, assembly, covenant," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of convenire （参见 convene).

example.en: Breaking social convention can sometimes lead to creative breakthroughs.
example.zh: 打破社会惯例有时能带来创造性的突破。

definitionLines: a. 普通的，常见的；习惯的，常 规的
entries.definition: a. 普通的，常见的；习惯的，常 规的
entries.etymology: late 15c., "of the nature of an agreement," from Late Latin conventionalis "pertaining to convention or agreement," from Latin conventionem (see convention). Meaning "of the nature of a convention" is from 1812, now rare; "established by social convention" is from 1761; that of "following tradition" is from 1831; that of "non-nuclear" is from 1955. Realted: Conventionality; conventionally.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "of the nature of an agreement," 源自 晚期拉丁语 conventionalis "pertaining to convention or agreement," 源自 拉丁语 conventionem （参见 convention). 义为 "of the nature of a convention" 始于 1812 年, 今罕用; "established by social convention" 始于 1761 年; that of "following tradition" 始于 1831 年; that of "non-nuclear" 始于 1955 年. Realted: Conventionality; conventionally.

example.en: The method he used was conventional and lacked any creative approach.
example.zh: 他使用的方法很传统，缺乏任何创意。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "living together, having dealings with others," also "manner of conducting oneself in the world;" from Old French conversation, from Latin conversationem (nominative conversatio) "act of living with," noun of action from past participle stem of conversari "to live with, keep company with," literally "turn about with," from Latin com- "with" (see com-) + vertare, frequentative of vertere (see versus).

Specific sense of "talk" is 1570s. Used as a synonym for "sexual intercourse" from at least 1511, hence criminal conversation, legal term for adultery from late 18c. Related: Conversationalist; conversationist.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "living together, having dealings with others," also "manner of conducting oneself in the world;" 源自 古法语 conversation, 源自 拉丁语 conversationem (主格 conversatio) "act of living with," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of conversari "to live with, keep company with," 字面义为 "turn about with," 源自 拉丁语 com- "with" （参见 com-) + vertare, 为 … 的反复体 vertere （参见 versus). Specific 语义 "talk" is 1570 年代. Used 作为 synonym for "sexual intercourse" 源自 at least 1511 年, hence criminal conversation, legal term for adultery 源自 18 世纪晚期 同源词：Conversationalist; conversationist.

example.en: We had a long conversation about our travel plans over dinner last night.
example.zh: 我们昨晚吃饭时就旅行计划进行了长时间的交谈。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French convertir, from Vulgar Latin *convertire, from Latin convertere "turn around, transform," from com- "together" (see com-) + vertere "to turn" (see versus). Originally in the religious sense. The Latin word is glossed in Old English by gecyrren, from cierran "to turn, return." Related: Converted; converting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 convertir, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *convertire, 源自 拉丁语 convertere "turn around, transform," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + vertere "to turn" （参见 versus). Originally in the religious sense. The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by gecyrren, 源自 cierran "to turn, return." 同源词：Converted; converting.

example.en: After the renovation, the old factory was converted into a modern art museum.
example.zh: 翻修之后，这座旧工厂被改造成了一座现代艺术博物馆。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to go along with;" late 14c., "to carry, transport;" from Anglo-French conveier, from Old French convoier "to escort" (Modern French convoyer), from Vulgar Latin *conviare "to accompany on the way," from Latin com- "together" (see com-) + via "way, road" (see via). It was a euphemism for "steal" 15c.-17c., which helped broaden its meaning. Related: Conveyed; conveying.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to go along with;" 14 世纪晚期, "to carry, transport;" 源自 盎格鲁-法语 conveier, 源自 古法语 convoier "to escort" (现代法语 convoyer), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *conviare "to accompany on the way," 源自 拉丁语 com- "together" （参见 com-) + 经由 "way, road" （参见 经由). It was a euphemism for "steal" 15 世纪-17 世纪, which helped broaden its 意为. 同源词：Conveyed; conveying.

example.en: A firm handshake can convey confidence to the person you meet.
example.zh: 一个有力的握手能向对方传递自信。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "the proving of guilt," from Late Latin convictionem (nominative convictio) "proof, refutation," noun of action from past participle stem of convincere (see convince). Meaning "mental state of being convinced" is from 1690s; that of "firm belief, a belief held as proven" is from 1841.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "the proving of guilt," 源自 晚期拉丁语 convictionem (主格 convictio) "proof, refutation," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of convincere （参见 convince). 义为 "mental state of being convinced" 始于 1690 年代; that of "firm belief, a belief held as proven" 始于 1841 年.

entries.etymology: 1520s, "to overcome in argument," from Latin convincere "to overcome decisively," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + vincere "to conquer" (see victor). Meaning "to firmly persuade" is from c. 1600. Related: Convinced; convincing; convincingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "to overcome in argument," 源自 拉丁语 convincere "to overcome decisively," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + vincere "to conquer" （参见 victor). 义为 "to firmly persuade" 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Convinced; convincing; convincingly.

example.en: The lawyer used evidence to convince the jury of his client's innocence.
example.zh: 律师用证据使陪审团相信其当事人是清白的。

entries.definition: v. 烹调，煮，烧 n. 炊事员，厨师
entries.etymology: Old English coc, from Vulgar Latin cocus "cook," from Latin coquus, from coquere "to cook, prepare food, ripen, digest, turn over in the mind" from PIE root *pekw- "to cook" (source also of Oscan popina "kitchen," Sanskrit pakvah "cooked," Greek peptein, Lithuanian kepti "to bake, roast," Old Church Slavonic pecenu "roasted," Welsh poeth "cooked, baked, hot"). Germanic languages had no one native term for all types of cooking, and borrowed the Latin word (Old Saxon kok, Old High German choh, German Koch, Swedish kock).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 coc, 源自 通俗拉丁语 cocus "cook," 源自 拉丁语 coquus, 源自 coquere "to cook, prepare food, ripen, digest, turn over in the mind" 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *pekw- "to cook" (source also of Oscan popina "kitchen," 梵语 pakvah "cooked," 希腊语 peptein, Lithuanian kepti "to bake, roast," Old Church Slavonic pecenu "roasted," Welsh poeth "cooked, baked, hot"). 日耳曼语 languages had no one 本族 term for all types of cooking, and borrowed the 拉丁语 word (古撒克逊语 kok, 古高地德语 choh, 德语 Koch, Swedish kock).

example.en: She learned to cook traditional dishes over an open fire.
example.zh: 她学会了在明火上烹制传统菜肴。

definitionLines: a. 凉，凉爽；冷静，沉着，冷淡
entries.definition: a. 凉，凉爽；冷静，沉着，冷淡 v.（使）冷却，（使）镇静
entries.etymology:
Old English col "not warm" (but usually not as severe as cold), also, of persons, "unperturbed, undemonstrative," from Proto-Germanic *koluz (source also of Middle Dutch coel, Dutch koel, Old High German kuoli, German kühl "cool," Old Norse kala "be cold"), from PIE root *gel- "cold, to freeze" (see cold (adj.)).

Applied since 1728 to large sums of money to give emphasis to amount. Meaning "calmly audacious" is from 1825. Slang use for "fashionable" is 1933, originally African-American vernacular; modern use as a general term of approval is from late 1940s, probably from bop talk and originally in reference to a style of jazz; said to have been popularized in jazz circles by tenor saxophonist Lester Young. Related: Coolly.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 col "not warm" (but 通常 not as severe as cold), also, of persons, "unperturbed, undemonstrative," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *koluz (source also of Middle 荷兰语 coel, 荷兰语 koel, 古高地德语 kuoli, 德语 kühl "cool," 古北欧语 kala "be cold"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gel- "cold, to freeze" （参见 cold （形）). Applied 自 1728 年 to large sums of money to give emphasis to amount. 义为 "calmly audacious" 始于 1825 年. Slang use for "fashionable" is 1933 年, 原义为 African-American vernacular; modern use 作为 general term of approval 始于 late 1940 年代, 可能 源自 bop talk and 原义为 in reference to a style of jazz; said to have been popularized in jazz circles by tenor saxophonist Lester Young. 同源词：Coolly.

example.en: A glass of cool lemonade is refreshing on a hot day.
example.zh: 在炎热的天气里，一杯清凉的柠檬水令人神清气爽。

definitionLines: v.（使）协调，调整；（使）互相 配合
entries.definition: v.（使）协调，调整；（使）互相 配合
entries.etymology: 1640s, "of the same order," from Medieval Latin coordinatus, past participle of coordinare "to set in order, arrange" (see coordination). Meaning "involving coordination" is from 1769. Related: Coordinance.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "of the same order," 源自 中古拉丁语 coordinatus, 为 … 的过去分词 coordinare "to set in order, arrange" （参见 coordination). 义为 "involving coordination" 始于 1769 年. 同源词：Coordinance.

example.en: All departments must coordinate their efforts to meet the project deadline.
example.zh: 所有部门必须协调各自的努力以赶上项目截止日期。

entries.etymology: 1704, northern British dialect, "to seize, to catch," perhaps ultimately from Middle French caper "seize, to take," from Latin capere "to take" (see capable); or from Dutch kapen "to take," from Old Frisian capia "to buy," which is related to Old English ceapian (see cheap). Related: Copped; copping.
entries.etymologyZh: 1704 年, northern British dialect, "to seize, to catch," 或许 最终源自 中古法语 caper "seize, to take," 源自 拉丁语 capere "to take" （参见 capable); or 源自 荷兰语 kapen "to take," 源自 古弗里西语 capia "to buy," which is related to 古英语 ceapian （参见 cheap). 同源词：Copped; copping.

example.en: The cop arrived at the scene within minutes of the emergency call.
example.zh: 警察在紧急电话打来后几分钟内赶到了现场。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "come to blows with," from Old French couper, earlier colper "hit, punch," from colp "a blow" (see coup). Meaning evolved 17c. into "handle successfully," perhaps influenced by obsolete cope "to traffic" (15c.-17c.), a word in North Sea trade, from the Flemish version of the Germanic source of English cheap. Related: Coped; coping.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "come to blows with," 源自 古法语 couper, earlier colper "hit, punch," 源自 colp "a blow" （参见 coup). 义为 evolved 17 世纪 into "handle successfully," 或许 influenced by 已废 cope "to traffic" (15 世纪-17 世纪), a word in North Sea trade, 源自 Flemish version of the 日耳曼语 source of English cheap. 同源词：Coped; coping.

example.en: She found it hard to cope with the pressure of the new job.
example.zh: 她发现很难应对新工作带来的压力。

example.en: The old pipes were made of copper, which caused the water to taste metallic.
example.zh: 旧管道由铜制成，导致水有金属味。

entries.definition: n. 抄件，副本；本，册 v. 抄写，复印，临摹
entries.etymology: early 14c., "written account or record," from Old French copie (13c.), from Medieval Latin copia "reproduction, transcript," from Latin copia "plenty, means" (see copious). Sense extended 15c. to any specimen of writing (especially MS for a printer) and any reproduction or imitation. Related: Copyist.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "written account or record," 源自 古法语 copie (13 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 copia "reproduction, transcript," 源自 拉丁语 copia "plenty, means" （参见 copious). Sense extended 15 世纪 to any specimen of writing (尤指 MS for a printer) and any reproduction or imitation. 同源词：Copyist.

example.en: Please make a copy of the document before sending it out.
example.zh: 请在发送文件之前先复印一份。

entries.etymology: "the right to make or sell copies," 1729, from copy (v.) + right (n.). As a verb, from 1806 (implied in past participle adjective copyrighted).
entries.etymologyZh: "the right to make or sell copies," 1729 年, 源自 copy （动） + right （名）. 作动词时, 自 1806 年起 (implied in past participle 形容词 copyrighted).

example.en: The author retained full copyright over her work and refused to sell the rights.
example.zh: 这位作者保留了她作品的完整版权，拒绝出售版权。

entries.etymology: late 14c., probably from Old French coeur "core of fruit, heart of lettuce," literally "heart," from Latin cor "heart," from PIE root *kerd- (1) "heart" (see heart (n.)). Nuclear reactor sense is from 1949.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 可能 源自 古法语 coeur "core of fruit, heart of lettuce," 字面义为 "heart," 源自 拉丁语 cor "heart," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kerd- (1) "heart" （参见 heart （名）). Nuclear reactor sense 始于 1949 年.

example.en: Trust is the core of any healthy relationship.
example.zh: 信任是任何健康关系的核心。

definitionLines: n. 谷物；［美］玉米；［英］小麦
entries.definition: n. 谷物；［美］玉米；［英］小麦

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Anglo-French cornere (Old French corniere), from Old French corne "horn, corner," from Vulgar Latin *corna, from Latin cornua, plural of cornu "projecting point, end, horn," from PIE *ker- (1) "horn; head, uppermost part of the body" (see horn (n.)). Replaced Old English hyrne. As an adjective, from 1530s. To be just around the corner in the extended sense of "about to happen" is by 1905.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 cornere (古法语 corniere), 源自 古法语 corne "horn, corner," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *corna, 源自 拉丁语 cornua, 为 … 的复数 cornu "projecting point, end, horn," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ker- (1) "horn; head, uppermost part of the body" （参见 horn （名）). Replaced 古英语 hyrne. 作形容词时, 源自 1530 年代. To be just around the corner in the extended 语义 "about to happen" is 截至 1905 年.

entries.etymology: late 13c., from corner (n.) + stone (n.). The figurative use is from early 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 corner （名） + stone （名）. The figurative use 始于 14 世纪初

definitionLines: a.公司的；法人组织的；社团 的；共同的；自治的
entries.definition: a.公司的；法人组织的；社团 的；共同的；自治的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "united in one body," from Latin corporatus, past participle of corporare "form into a body," from corpus (genitive corporis) "body" (see corporeal).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "united in one body," 源自 拉丁语 corporatus, 为 … 的过去分词 corporare "form into a body," 源自 corpus (属格 corporis) "body" （参见 corporeal).

example.en: The new policy affects all corporate clients, not just individual customers.
example.zh: 新政策影响所有企业客户，而不仅仅是个人客户。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "persons united in a body for some purpose," from such use in Anglo-Latin, from Late Latin corporationem (nominative corporatio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin corporare "to embody" (see corporate). Meaning "legally authorized entity" (including municipal governments and modern business companies) is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "persons united in a body for some purpose," 源自 such use in Anglo-拉丁语, 源自 晚期拉丁语 corporationem (主格 corporatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 corporare "to embody" （参见 corporate). 义为 "legally authorized entity" (including municipal governments and modern business companies) 始于 1610 年代.

example.en: The corporation announced record profits for the third consecutive year.
example.zh: 该公司宣布连续第三年创下创纪录的利润。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., cors "body," from Old French cors "body, person, corpse, life" (9c.), from Latin corpus "body" (see corporeal). Sense in English evolved from "dead body" (13c.) to "live body" (14c.) to "body of citizens" (15c.) to "band of knights" (mid-15c.). The modern military sense (1704) is from French corps d'armée (16c.), picked up in English during Marlborough's campaigns.

French restored the Latin -p- in 14c., and English followed 15c., but the pronunciation remained "corse" at first and corse persisted as a parallel formation. After the -p- began to be sounded (16c. in English), corse became archaic or poetic only.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, cors "body," 源自 古法语 cors "body, person, corpse, life" (9 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 corpus "body" （参见 corporeal). Sense in English evolved 源自 "dead body" (13 世纪) to "live body" (14 世纪) to "body of citizens" (15 世纪) to "band of knights" (15 世纪中期). The modern military sense (1704 年) 始于 法语 corps d'armée (16c.), picked up in English during Marlborough's campaigns. 法语 restored the 拉丁语 -p- in 14 世纪, and English followed 15 世纪, but the pronunciation remained "corse" at first and corse persisted 作为 parallel formation. After the -p- began to be sounded (16 世纪 in English), corse became 古旧 or poetic only.

example.en: The peace corps was deployed to the region to monitor the ceasefire.
example.zh: 维和军团被部署到该地区以监督停火协议。

entries.etymology: 1540s, variant spelling of corps (q.v.). The -p- originally was silent, as in French, and with some speakers still is. The terminal -e was rare before 19c. Corpse-candle is attested from 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, variant spelling of corps (q.v.). The -p- 原义为 was silent, as in 法语, and with some speakers still is. The terminal -e was rare before 19 世纪 Corpse-candle 见于 1690 年代.

example.en: Police discovered a corpse hidden beneath the floorboards of the old house.
example.zh: 警察在那栋旧房子的地板下发现了一具尸体。

definitionLines: a. 正确的；恰当的，合适的
entries.definition: a. 正确的；恰当的，合适的 vt. 改正，修改，矫正
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "to set right, rectify" (a fault or error), from Latin correctus, past participle of corrigere "to put straight, reduce to order, set right;" in transferred use, "to reform, amend," especially of speech or writing, from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + regere "to lead straight, rule" (see regal). Originally of persons; with reference to writing, etc., attested from late 14c. Related: Corrected; correcting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to set right, rectify" (a fault or error), 源自 拉丁语 correctus, 为 … 的过去分词 corrigere "to put straight, reduce to order, set right;" in transferred use, "to reform, amend," 尤指 of speech or writing, 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + regere "to lead straight, rule" （参见 regal). Originally of persons; with reference to writing, etc., attested 源自 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Corrected; correcting.

example.en: The teacher used a red pen to correct every grammatical error in the essay.
example.zh: 老师用红笔批改了作文中的每一处语法错误。

definitionLines: vi. （to）相当，对应；（with）符 合；通讯
entries.definition: vi. （to）相当，对应；（with）符 合；通讯
entries.etymology:
1520s, "to be in agreement, to be in harmony with," from Middle French correspondre (14c.) or directly from Medieval Latin correspondere, from cor- (see com-) "together, with each other" + respondere "to answer" (see respond).

Originally in Medieval Latin of two things in mutual action, but by later Medieval Latin it could be used of one thing only. In English, sense of "to be similar" (to) is from 1640s; that of "to hold communication with" is from c. 1600; specifically "to communicate by means of letters" from 1640s (in mid-18c. it also could mean "have sex"). Related: Corresponded; corresponding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "to be in agreement, to be in harmony with," 源自 中古法语 correspondre (14 世纪) or 直接源自 中古拉丁语 correspondere, 源自 cor- （参见 com-) "together, with each other" + respondere "to answer" （参见 respond). Originally in 中古拉丁语 of two things in mutual action, but by later 中古拉丁语 it could be used of one thing only. In English, 语义 "to be similar" (to) 始于 1640 年代; that of "to hold communication with" 始于 约 1600 年; specifically "to communicate by means of letters" 源自 1640 年代 (in 18 世纪中期 it also could mean "have sex"). 同源词：Corresponded; corresponding.

example.en: The results of the study correspond closely with earlier findings from similar research.
example.zh: 研究结果与同类研究早期发现高度吻合。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "having an analogous relationship" (to), a sense taken up since 19c. by corresponding; from Medieval Latin correspondentem, present participle of correspondere (see correspond).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "having an analogous relationship" (to), a sense taken up 自 19 世纪 by corresponding; 源自 中古拉丁语 correspondentem, 为 … 的现在分词 correspondere （参见 correspond).

example.en: The newspaper's foreign correspondent filed a report from the conflict zone.
example.zh: 这家报纸的驻外记者从冲突地区发回了一篇报道。

definitionLines: a. 相应的，相当的；符合的，一 致的
entries.definition: a. 相应的，相当的；符合的，一 致的
entries.etymology: 1570s, past participle adjective from correspond. Not common until 19c., when it took on the adjectival function of correspondent. Related: Correspondingly (1836).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, past participle 形容词 源自 correspond. Not common until 19 世纪, when it took on the adjectival function of correspondent. 同源词：Correspondingly (1836 年).

entries.etymology: 1590s, from French corridor (16c.), from Italian corridore "a gallery," literally "a runner," from correre "to run," from Latin currere (see current (adj.)). Originally of fortifications, meaning "long hallway" is first recorded 1814.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 法语 corridor (16 世纪), 源自 意大利语 corridore "a gallery," 字面义为 "a runner," 源自 correre "to run," 源自 拉丁语 currere （参见 current （形）). Originally of fortifications, 意为 "long hallway" is 首见于 1814 年.

example.en: The fire drill required all students to exit through the designated corridor in an orderly fashion.
example.zh: 消防演习要求所有学生有序地通过指定走廊疏散。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French corropt "unhealthy, corrupt; uncouth" (of language), and directly from Latin corruptus, past participle of corrumpere "to destroy; spoil," figuratively "corrupt, seduce, bribe," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + rup-, past participle stem of rumpere "to break" (see rupture (n.)). Related: Corruptly; corruptness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 corropt "unhealthy, corrupt; uncouth" (of language), and 直接源自 拉丁语 corruptus, 为 … 的过去分词 corrumpere "to destroy; spoil," figuratively "corrupt, seduce, bribe," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + rup-, past participle stem of rumpere "to break" （参见 rupture （名）). 同源词：Corruptly; corruptness.

example.en: The corrupt official was caught accepting bribes from contractors.
example.zh: 这名腐败的官员被发现接受承包商的贿赂。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., of material things, especially dead bodies, also of the soul, morals, etc., from Latin corruptionem (nominative corruptio), noun of action from past participle stem of corrumpere (see corrupt). Of public offices from early 15c.; of language from late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, of material things, 尤指 dead bodies, also of the soul, morals, etc., 源自 拉丁语 corruptionem (主格 corruptio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of corrumpere （参见 corrupt). Of public offices 源自 15 世纪初; of language 源自 15 世纪晚期

example.en: The investigation revealed widespread corruption within the city's police department.
example.zh: 调查揭露了该市警察局内部普遍存在的腐败现象。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "art of beautifying," from Latinized form of Greek kosmetike (tekhne) "the art of dress and ornament," from fem. of kosmetikos (see cosmetic (adj.)). Meaning "a preparation for beautifying" attested from 1640s (now often cosmetics).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "art of beautifying," 源自 Latinized form of 希腊语 kosmetike (tekhne) "the art of dress and ornament," 源自 fem. of kosmetikos （参见 cosmetic （形）). 义为 "a preparation for beautifying" attested 源自 1640 年代 (现在 常 cosmetics).

entries.definition: n..成本，费用，代价 v.值，花费
entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old French cost (12c., Modern French coût) "cost, outlay, expenditure; hardship, trouble," from Vulgar Latin *costare, from Latin constare, literally "to stand at" (or with), with a wide range of figurative senses including "to cost." The idiom is the same one used in Modern English when someone says something "stands at X dollars" to mean it sells for X dollars. The Latin word is from com- "with" (see com-) + stare "to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand" (see stet).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 cost (12 世纪, 现代法语 coût) "cost, outlay, expenditure; hardship, trouble," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *costare, 源自 拉丁语 constare, 字面义为 "to stand at" (or with), with a wide range of figurative senses including "to cost." The idiom is the same one used in 现代英语 when someone says something "stands at X dollars" to mean it sells for X dollars. The 拉丁语 word 始于 com- "with" （参见 com-) + stare "to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand" （参见 stet).

example.en: It will cost you at least three hundred dollars to repair the engine.
example.zh: 修理这台发动机至少要花你三百美元。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from cost + -ly (1). Earlier formation with the same sense were costful (mid-13c.), costious (mid-14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 cost + -ly (1). Earlier formation with the same sense were costful (13 世纪中期), costious (14 世纪中期).

example.en: Repairing the historic building turned out to be far more costly than expected.
example.zh: 修缮这座历史建筑的费用远比预期的要高昂得多。

entries.etymology: 1715, "style of dress," an art term, from French costume (17c.), from Italian costume "fashion, habit," from Latin consuetudinem (nominative consuetudo) "custom, habit, usage." Essentially the same word as custom but arriving by a different etymology. From "customary clothes of the particular period in which the scene is laid," meaning broadened by 1818 to "any defined mode of dress." Costume jewelry is first attested 1933.
entries.etymologyZh: 1715 年, "style of dress," an art term, 源自 法语 costume (17 世纪), 源自 意大利语 costume "fashion, habit," 源自 拉丁语 consuetudinem (主格 consuetudo) "custom, habit, usage." Essentially the same word as custom but arriving by a different etymology. From "customary clothes of the particular period in which the scene is laid," 意为 broadened 截至 1818 年 to "any defined mode of dress." Costume jewelry is 最早见于 1933 年.

example.en: The actors wore elaborate period costume to recreate life in ancient Rome.
example.zh: 演员们穿着精心制作的历史服装，重现古罗马生活。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., from Old French cote "hut, cottage" + Anglo-French suffix -age (probably denoting "the entire property attached to a cote"). Old French cot is probably from Old Norse kot "hut," cognate of Old English cot, cote "cottage, hut," from Proto-Germanic *kutan (source also of Middle Dutch cot, Dutch kot).

Meaning "small country residence" (without suggestion of poverty or tenancy) is from 1765. Modern French cottage is a 19c. reborrowing from English. Cottage industry is attested from 1921. Cottage cheese is attested from 1831, American English, earliest in reference to Philadelphia:
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 cote "hut, cottage" + 盎格鲁-法语 suffix -age (可能 denoting "the entire property attached to a cote"). 古法语 cot is 可能 源自 古北欧语 kot "hut," 同源 of 古英语 cot, cote "cottage, hut," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kutan (source also of Middle 荷兰语 cot, 荷兰语 kot). 义为 "small country residence" (without suggestion of poverty or tenancy) 始于 1765 年. 现代法语 cottage is a 19 世纪 reborrowing 源自 English. Cottage industry 见于 1921 年. Cottage cheese 见于 1831 年, American English, earliest in reference to Philadelphia:

example.en: They rented a cozy cottage in the countryside for the weekend.
example.zh: 他们在乡下租了一间舒适的小屋过周末。

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French coton (12c.), ultimately (via Provençal, Italian, or Old Spanish) from Arabic qutn, a word perhaps of Egyptian origin. Philip Miller of the Chelsea Physic Garden sent the first cotton seeds to American colony of Georgia in 1732. Also ultimately from the Arabic word, Dutch katoen, German Kattun, Provençal coton, Italian cotone, Spanish algodon, Portuguese algodão. Cotton gin is recorded from 1794 (see gin (n.2)).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 coton (12 世纪), ultimately (经由 Provençal, 意大利语，或Old 西班牙语) 源自 阿拉伯语 qutn, a word 或许 of Egyptian origin. Philip Miller of the Chelsea Physic Garden sent the first cotton seeds to American colony of Georgia 于 1732 年. Also 最终源自 the 阿拉伯语 word, 荷兰语 katoen, 德语 Kattun, Provençal coton, 意大利语 cotone, 西班牙语 algodon, 葡萄牙语 algodão. Cotton gin 见于 1794 年 （参见 gin (n.2)).

example.en: The shirt is made of pure cotton and feels very comfortable.
example.zh: 这件衬衫由纯棉制成，穿起来非常舒适。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to overlay with gold, inlay," from Old French couchier "to lay down, place; go to bed, put to bed," from Latin collocare "to lay, place, station, arrange," from com- "together" (see com-) + locare "to place" (see locate). Meaning "to put into words" is from 1520s. Related: Couched; couching. Heraldic couchant ("lying down with the head up") is late 15c., from the French present participle.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to overlay with gold, inlay," 源自 古法语 couchier "to lay down, place; go to bed, put to bed," 源自 拉丁语 collocare "to lay, place, station, arrange," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + locare "to place" （参见 locate). 义为 "to put into words" 始于 1520 年代. 同源词：Couched; couching. Heraldic couchant ("lying down with the head up") is 15 世纪晚期, 源自 法语 present participle.

example.en: He sat on the couch and flipped through the television channels.
example.zh: 他坐在沙发上翻阅电视频道。

entries.etymology: early 14c., coughen, probably in Old English, but not recorded, from Proto-Germanic *kokh-, with the rough "kh" of German or of Scottish loch (source also of Middle Dutch kochen, Middle High German kuchen). Onomatopoeic. Related: Coughed; coughing. As a noun from c. 1300.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, coughen, 可能 in 古英语, but not recorded, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kokh-, with the rough "kh" of 德语 or of 苏格兰语 loch (source also of Middle 荷兰语 kochen, Middle High 德语 kuchen). Onomatopoeic. 同源词：Coughed; coughing. 作名词时 源自 约 1300 年.

example.en: She began to cough uncontrollably during the cold winter night.
example.zh: 在寒冷的冬夜，她开始不受控制地咳嗽。

entries.etymology: Old English cuðe, past tense of cunnan "to be able" (see can (v.1)); ending changed 14c. to standard English -d(e). The excrescent -l- was added 15c.-16c. on model of would, should, where it is historical.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cuðe, 为 … 的过去时 cunnan "to be able" （参见 can (v.1)); ending changed 14 世纪 to standard English -d(e). The excrescent -l- was added 15 世纪-16 世纪 on model of would, should, where it is historical.

definitionLines: n. 理事会，委员会；议事机构
entries.definition: n. 理事会，委员会；议事机构
entries.etymology: early 12c., from Anglo-French cuncile, from Old North French concilie (Old French concile, 12c.) "assembly; council meeting; body of counsellors," from Latin concilium "a meeting, a gathering of people," from PIE *kal-yo-, from root *kele- (2) "to shout" (see claim (v.)). The notion is of a calling together. Tendency to confuse it in form and meaning with counsel has been consistent since 16c.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 cuncile, 源自 Old North 法语 concilie (古法语 concile, 12 世纪) "assembly; council meeting; body of counsellors," 源自 拉丁语 concilium "a meeting, a gathering of people," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kal-yo-, 源自 root *kele- (2) "to shout" （参见 claim （动）). example.en: The city council voted to approve the new public transport plan.
example.zh: 市议会投票通过了新的公共交通方案。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French counseil (10c.) "advice, counsel; deliberation, thought," from Latin consilium "plan, opinion" (see consultation). As a synonym for "lawyer," first attested late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 counseil (10 世纪) "advice, counsel; deliberation, thought," 源自 拉丁语 consilium "plan, opinion" （参见 consultation). 作为 synonym for "lawyer," 最早见于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The therapist was asked to counsel the family on how to handle the situation.
example.zh: 治疗师被请求就如何处理这种情况向这家人提供建议。

entries.definition: vt. 数，计算；看做，认 vi. 计数；指望
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French conter "add up," but also "tell a story," from Latin computare (see compute). Related: Counted; counting. Modern French differentiates compter "to count" and conter "to tell," but they are cognates.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 conter "add up," but also "tell a story," 源自 拉丁语 computare （参见 compute). 同源词：Counted; counting. 现代法语 differentiates compter "to count" and conter "to tell," but they are cognates.

example.en: Your opinion counts just as much as anyone else's in this discussion.
example.zh: 在这场讨论中，你的意见和其他任何人的一样重要。

entries.etymology: 1953, American English, in early use especially of launches of rockets or missiles, from count (v.) + down.
entries.etymologyZh: 1953 年, American English, in early use 尤指 of launches of rockets or missiles, 源自 count （动） + down.

definitionLines: a. /ad. 相反的（地），反对 的（地）
entries.definition: n. 柜台；计数器 a. /ad. 相反的（地），反对 的（地） v. 反对，对抗
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "table where a money lender does business," from Old French contouer, comptoir (14c.) "counting room, table of a bank," from Medieval Latin computatorium "place of accounts," from Latin computatus, past participle of computare (see compute). Generalized 19c. from banks to shops, then extended to display cases for goods. Phrase under the counter is from 1926.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "table where a money lender does business," 源自 古法语 contouer, comptoir (14 世纪) "counting room, table of a bank," 源自 中古拉丁语 computatorium "place of accounts," 源自 拉丁语 computatus, 为 … 的过去分词 computare （参见 compute). entries.etymology: mid-15c., originally countre part "duplicate of a legal document," from Middle French contrepartie, from contre "facing, opposite" (see contra-) + partie "copy of a person or thing," originally fem. past participle of partir "to divide" (see party (n.)).

example.en: The CEO met with her Chinese counterpart to discuss trade cooperation.
example.zh: 首席执行官与她的中国对等人物会面，讨论贸易合作。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., "district, native land," from Old French contree, from Vulgar Latin *(terra) contrata "(land) lying opposite," or "(land) spread before one," from Latin contra "opposite, against" (see contra-). Sense narrowed 1520s to rural areas, as opposed to cities. Replaced Old English land. As an adjective from late 14c. First record of country-and-western music style is from 1942. Country club first recorded 1886. Country mile "a long way" is from 1915, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "district, native land," 源自 古法语 contree, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *(terra) contrata "(land) lying opposite," or "(land) spread before one," 源自 拉丁语 contra "opposite, against" （参见 contra-). Country mile "a long way" 始于 1915 年, American English.

example.en: This product is manufactured in one country but sold in dozens of others.
example.zh: 这款产品在一个国家生产，却在数十个其他国家销售。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., literally "one side of a country" (a valley, a mountain range, etc.), from country + side (n.); hence, "any tract of land having a natural unity" (1727).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 字面义为 "one side of a country" (a valley, a mountain range, etc.), 源自 country + side （名）; hence, "any tract of land having a natural unity" (1727 年).

example.en: They moved to the countryside to escape the noise of city life.
example.zh: 他们搬到了农村，以逃离城市生活的喧嚣。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Anglo-French counte, from Late Latin comitatus "jurisdiction of a count," from Latin comes (see count (n.)); replaced Old English scir "shire."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 counte, 源自 晚期拉丁语 comitatus "jurisdiction of a count," 源自 拉丁语 comes （参见 count （名）); replaced 古英语 scir "shire."

example.en: Each county in the state sends two representatives to the senate.
example.zh: 该州的每个县向参议院派遣两名代表。

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French cople "married couple, lovers" (12c., Modern French couple), from Latin copula "tie, connection," from PIE *ko-ap-, from *ko(m)- "together" + *ap- "to take, reach." Meaning broadened mid-14c. to "any two things."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 cople "married couple, lovers" (12 世纪, 现代法语 couple), 源自 拉丁语 copula "tie, connection," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ko-ap-, 源自 *ko(m)- "together" + *ap- "to take, reach." 义为 broadened 14 世纪中期 to "any two things."

example.en: The young couple moved into the neighborhood last weekend.
example.zh: 这对年轻夫妇上周末搬进了这个小区。

entries.etymology: 1822, "certificate of interest due on a bond" (which could be cut from the bond and presented for payment), from French coupon, literally "piece cut off," from couper "to cut," from coup "a blow" (see coup). Meaning widened to "discount ticket" 1860s by British travel agent Thomas Cook. The specific advertising sense is from 1906.
entries.etymologyZh: 1822 年, "certificate of interest due on a bond" (which could be cut 源自 bond and presented for payment), 源自 法语 coupon, 字面义为 "piece cut off," 源自 couper "to cut," 源自 coup "a blow" （参见 coup). 义为 widened to "discount ticket" 1860 年代 by British travel agent Thomas Cook. The specific advertising sense 始于 1906 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French corage (12c., Modern French courage) "heart, innermost feelings; temper," from Vulgar Latin *coraticum (source of Italian coraggio, Spanish coraje), from Latin cor "heart," from PIE root *kerd- (1) "heart" (see heart (n.)) which remains a common metaphor for inner strength. In Middle English, used broadly for "what is in one's mind or thoughts," hence "bravery," but also "wrath, pride, confidence, lustiness," or any sort of inclination. Replaced Old English ellen, which also meant "zeal, strength."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 corage (12 世纪, 现代法语 courage) "heart, innermost feelings; temper," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *coraticum (source of 意大利语 coraggio, 西班牙语 coraje), 源自 拉丁语 cor "heart," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kerd- (1) "heart" （参见 heart （名）) which remains a common metaphor for inner strength. In 中古英语, used broadly for "what is in one's mind or thoughts," hence "bravery," but also "wrath, pride, confidence, lustiness," or any sort of inclination. Replaced 古英语 ellen, which also meant "zeal, strength."

example.en: It took a lot of courage to stand up and speak in front of the large crowd.
example.zh: 在大批人群面前站起来发言需要很大的勇气。

definitionLines: n. 进程，过程；课程；（一） 道（菜）
entries.definition: n. 进程，过程；课程；（一） 道（菜）
entries.etymology:
late 13c., "onward movement," from Old French cors (12c.) "course; run, running; flow of a river," from Latin cursus "a running race or course," from curs- past participle stem of currere "to run" (see current (adj.)).

Most extended senses (meals, etc.) are present in 14c. Academic meaning "planned series of study" is c. 1600 (in French from 14c.). Phrase of course is attested from 1540s; literally "of the ordinary course;" earlier in same sense was bi cours (c. 1300).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "onward movement," 源自 古法语 cors (12 世纪) "course; run, running; flow of a river," 源自 拉丁语 cursus "a running race or course," 源自 curs- past participle stem of currere "to run" （参见 current （形）). Most extended senses (meals, etc.) are present in 14 世纪 Academic 意为 "planned series of study" is 约 1600 年 (in 法语 源自 14 世纪). Phrase of course 见于 1540 年代; 字面义为 "of the ordinary course;" earlier in same sense was bi cours (约 1300 年).

example.en: She completed three advanced course before earning her graduate certificate.
example.zh: 她在获得研究生证书之前修完了三门高级课程。

definitionLines: n. 法院，法庭；宫殿，朝延；院
entries.definition: n. 法院，法庭；宫殿，朝延；院
entries.etymology: late 12c., from Old French cort (11c., Modern French cour) "king's court, princely residence," from Latin cortem, accusative of cors (earlier cohors) "enclosed yard," and by extension (and perhaps by association with curia "sovereign's assembly"), "those assembled in the yard; company, cohort," from com- "together" (see com-) + stem hort- related to hortus "garden, plot of ground" (see yard (n.1)). Sporting sense is from 1510s, originally of tennis. Legal meaning is from late 13c. (early assemblies for justice were overseen by the sovereign personally).
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 cort (11 世纪, 现代法语 cour) "king's court, princely residence," 源自 拉丁语 cortem, 宾格 of cors (earlier cohors) "enclosed yard," and by extension (and 或许 by association with curia "sovereign's assembly"), "those assembled in the yard; company, cohort," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + stem hort- related to hortus "garden, plot of ground" （参见 yard (n.1)). Sporting sense 始于 1510 年代, 原义为 of tennis. Legal 意为 始于 13 世纪晚期 (early assemblies for justice were overseen by the sovereign personally).

example.en: The judge ordered both parties to appear in court on Monday morning.
example.zh: 法官命令双方于周一上午出庭。

entries.etymology: early 13c., curteisie, from Old French curteisie (Modern French courtoisie), from curteis "courteous" (see courteous). A specialized sense of curteisie is the source of English curtsy.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, curteisie, 源自 古法语 curteisie (现代法语 courtoisie), 源自 curteis "courteous" （参见 courteous). A specialized 语义 curteisie is the source of English curtsy.

example.en: She held the door open as a matter of courtesy, even for strangers.
example.zh: 她出于礼貌为他人开门，哪怕是陌生人也不例外。

entries.etymology: 1550s, from court (n.) + yard (n.1).
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 court （名） + yard (n.1).

example.en: The old mansion had a beautiful courtyard filled with fountains and flowers.
example.zh: 这座老宅有一个美丽的庭院，里面有喷泉和鲜花。

definitionLines: n. 堂/表兄弟，堂/表姐妹
entries.definition: n. 堂/表兄弟，堂/表姐妹
entries.etymology:
mid-12c., from Old French cosin (12c., Modern French cousin) "nephew, kinsman, cousin," from Latin consobrinus "cousin," originally "mother's sister's son," from com- "together" (see com-) + sobrinus (earlier *sosrinos) "cousin on mother's side," from soror (genitive sororis) "sister."

Italian cugino, Danish kusine, Polish kuzyn also are from French. German vetter is from Old High German fetiro "uncle," perhaps on the notion of "child of uncle." Words for cousin tend to drift to "nephew" on the notion of "father's nephew."

Many IE languages (including Irish, Sanskrit, Slavic, and some of the Germanic tongues) have or had separate words for some or all of the eight possible "cousin" relationships, such as Latin, which along with consobrinus had consobrina "mother's sister's daughter," patruelis "father's brother's son," atruelis "mother's brother's son," amitinus "father's sister's son," etc. Old English distinguished fæderan sunu "father's brother's son," modrigan sunu "mother's sister's son," etc.

Used familiarly as a term of address since early 15c., especially in Cornwall. Phrase kissing cousin is Southern U.S. expression, 1940s, apparently denoting "those close enough to be kissed in salutation;" Kentish cousin (1796) is an old British term for "distant relative."
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 cosin (12 世纪, 现代法语 cousin) "nephew, kinsman, cousin," 源自 拉丁语 consobrinus "cousin," 原义为 "mother's sister's son," 源自 com- "together" （参见 com-) + sobrinus (earlier *sosrinos) "cousin on mother's side," 源自 soror (属格 sororis) "sister." 意大利语 cugino, Danish kusine, Polish kuzyn also 始于 法语. 德语 vetter 始于 古高地德语 fetiro "uncle," 或许 on the 概念 "child of uncle." Words for cousin tend to drift to "nephew" on the 概念 "father's nephew." Many IE languages (including 爱尔兰语, 梵语, Slavic, and some of the 日耳曼语 tongues) have or had separate words for some or all of the eight possible "cousin" relationships, such as 拉丁语, which along with consobrinus had consobrina "mother's sister's daughter," patruelis "father's brother's son," atruelis "mother's brother's son," amitinus "father's sister's son," etc. 古英语 distinguished fæderan sunu "father's brother's son," modrigan sunu "mother's sister's son," etc. Used familiarly 作为 term of address 自 15 世纪初, 尤指 in Cornwall. Phrase kissing cousin is Southern U.S. expression, 1940 年代, 似乎 denoting "those close enough to be kissed in salutation;" Kentish cousin (1796 年) is an old British term for "distant relative."

example.en: My cousin from my uncle's side is visiting us this weekend.
example.zh: 我叔叔那边的堂兄弟这个周末来看我们。

entries.definition: vt.（with）盖，覆；包括，涉及 n. 覆盖物，套，封面
entries.etymology: mid-12c., from Old French covrir (12c., Modern French couvrir) "to cover, protect, conceal, dissemble," from Late Latin coperire, from Latin cooperire "to cover over, overwhelm, bury," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + operire "to close, cover" (see weir). Related: Covered; covering. Military sense is from 1680s; newspaper sense first recorded 1893; use in football dates from 1907. Betting sense is 1857. Of horses, as a euphemism for "copulate" it dates from 1530s. Covered wagon attested from 1745.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 covrir (12 世纪, 现代法语 couvrir) "to cover, protect, conceal, dissemble," 源自 晚期拉丁语 coperire, 源自 拉丁语 cooperire "to cover over, overwhelm, bury," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + operire "to close, cover" （参见 weir). 同源词：Covered; covering. Military sense 始于 1680 年代; newspaper sense 首见于 1893 年; use in football dates 自 1907 年起. Betting sense is 1857 年. Of horses, 作为 euphemism for "copulate" it dates 源自 1530 年代. Covered wagon attested 自 1745 年起.

example.en: The documentary aims to cover the major events of the past century.
example.zh: 这部纪录片旨在涵盖过去一个世纪的重大事件。

entries.etymology: Old English cu "cow," from Proto-Germanic *kwon (source also of Old Frisian ku, Middle Dutch coe, Dutch koe, Old High German kuo, German Kuh, Old Norse kyr, Danish, Swedish ko), earlier *kwom, from PIE *gwou- "cow, ox, bull" (cognates Sanskrit gaus, Greek bous, Latin bov-, Old Irish bo, Latvian guovs, Armenian gaus "cow," Slovak hovado "ox"), perhaps ultimately imitative of lowing (compare Sumerian gu, Chinese ngu, ngo "ox"). In Germanic and Celtic, of females only; in most other languages, of either gender. Other "cow" words sometimes are from roots meaning "horn, horned," such as Lithuanian karve, Old Church Slavonic krava. Compare kine.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cu "cow," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kwon (source also of 古弗里西语 ku, Middle 荷兰语 coe, 荷兰语 koe, 古高地德语 kuo, 德语 Kuh, 古北欧语 kyr, Danish, Swedish ko), earlier *kwom, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *gwou- "cow, ox, bull" (cognates 梵语 gaus, 希腊语 bous, 拉丁语 bov-, Old 爱尔兰语 bo, Latvian guovs, Armenian gaus "cow," Slovak hovado "ox"), 或许 ultimately imitative of lowing (对比 Sumerian gu, 汉语 ngu, ngo "ox"). In 日耳曼语 and Celtic, of females only; in most other languages, of either gender. Other "cow" words 有时 始于 roots 意为 "horn, horned," such as Lithuanian karve, Old Church Slavonic krava. 对比 kine.

entries.definition: n.懦夫，懦弱的人 a. 胆小的，怯懦的
entries.etymology:
mid-13c., from Old French coart "coward" (no longer the usual word in French, which has now in this sense poltron, from Italian, and lâche), from coe "tail," from Latin coda, popular dialect variant of cauda "tail," which is of uncertain origin + -ard, an agent noun suffix denoting one that carries on some action or possesses some quality, with derogatory connotation (see -ard).

The word probably reflects an animal metaphoric sense still found in expressions like turning tail and tail between legs. Coart was the name of the hare in Old French versions of "Reynard the Fox." Italian codardo, Spanish cobarde are from French.

As a surname (attested from 1255) it represents Old English cuhyrde "cow-herd." Farmer has coward's castle "a pulpit," "Because a clergyman may deliver himself therefrom without fear of contradiction or argument."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 coart "coward" (no longer the usual word in 法语, which has 现在 in this sense poltron, 源自 意大利语, and lâche), 源自 coe "tail," 源自 拉丁语 coda, popular dialect 为 … 的变体 cauda "tail," which is 来源存疑 + -ard, an agent 名词 suffix denoting one that carries on some action or possesses some quality, with derogatory connotation （参见 -ard). The word 可能 reflects an animal metaphoric sense still found in expressions like turning tail and tail between legs. Coart was the name of the hare in 古法语 versions of "Reynard the Fox." 意大利语 codardo, 西班牙语 cobarde 始于 法语. 作为 surname (attested 自 1255 年起) it represents 古英语 cuhyrde "cow-herd." entries.etymology: 1725, "boy who tends to cows," from cow (n.) + boy. Sense in Western U.S. is from 1849; in figurative use by 1942 for "brash and reckless young man" (as an adjective meaning "reckless," from 1920s). Cowhand is first attested 1852 in American English (see hand (n.)). Cowpoke (said to be 1881, not in popular use until 1940s) was said to be originally restricted to the cowboys who prodded cattle onto railroad cars with long poles.
entries.etymologyZh: 1725 年, "boy who tends to cows," 源自 cow （名） + boy.
