Cowpoke (said to be 1881 年, not in popular use until 1940 年代) was said to be 原义为 restricted to the cowboys who prodded cattle onto railroad cars with long poles.

entries.etymology: 1709, colsie, Scottish dialect, perhaps of Scandinavian origin (compare Norwegian kose seg "be cozy"). In Britain, usually cosy. Related: Cozily; coziness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1709 年, colsie, 苏格兰语 dialect, 或许 of Scandinavian origin (对比 Norwegian kose seg "be cozy"). In Britain, 通常 cosy. 同源词：Cozily; coziness.

definitionLines: vi. 使破裂，砸开；发爆裂声
entries.definition: vi. 使破裂，砸开；发爆裂声 n.裂纹，龟裂；爆裂声
entries.etymology: Old English cracian "make a sharp noise," from Proto-Germanic *krakojan (source also of Middle Dutch craken, Dutch kraken, German krachen), probably imitative. Related: Cracked; cracking. From early 14c. as "to utter, say, speak, talk," especially "speak loudly or boastingly" (late 14c.). To crack a smile is from 1835, American English; to crack the whip in the figurative sense is from 1886.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cracian "make a sharp noise," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *krakojan (source also of Middle 荷兰语 craken, 荷兰语 kraken, 德语 krachen), 可能 imitative. 同源词：Cracked; cracking. From 14 世纪初 as "to utter, say, speak, talk," 尤指 "speak loudly or boastingly" (14 世纪晚期). To crack a smile 始于 1835 年, American English; to crack the whip in the figurative sense 始于 1886 年.

example.en: The windshield began to crack after a stone hit it at high speed.
example.zh: 挡风玻璃被高速飞来的石块击中后开始出现裂纹。

entries.etymology: also crack down; 1935, from the verbal phrase (1915), from crack (v.) + down (adv.); probably from the sense of "to shoot at" (1913).
entries.etymologyZh: also crack down; 1935 年, 源自 verbal phrase (1915 年), 源自 crack （动） + down （副）; 可能 源自 语义 "to shoot at" (1913 年).

definitionLines: n. 技巧，手艺；飞机，飞船
entries.definition: n. 技巧，手艺；飞机，飞船
entries.etymology:
Old English cræft (West Saxon, Northumbrian), -creft (Kentish), originally "power, physical strength, might," from Proto-Germanic *krab-/*kraf- (source also of Old Frisian kreft, Old High German chraft, German Kraft "strength, skill;" Old Norse kraptr "strength, virtue"). Sense expanded in Old English to include "skill, dexterity; art, science, talent" (via a notion of "mental power"), which led by late Old English to the meaning "trade, handicraft, calling," also "something built or made." The word still was used for "might, power" in Middle English.

Use for "small boat" is first recorded 1670s, probably from a phrase similar to vessels of small craft and referring either to the trade they did or the seamanship they required, or perhaps it preserves the word in its original sense of "power."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cræft (West Saxon, Northumbrian), -creft (Kentish), 原义为 "power, physical strength, might," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *krab-/*kraf- (source also of 古弗里西语 kreft, 古高地德语 chraft, 德语 Kraft "strength, skill;" 古北欧语 kraptr "strength, virtue"). Sense expanded in 古英语 to include "skill, dexterity; art, science, talent" (经由 a 概念 "mental power"), which led by late 古英语 to the 意为 "trade, handicraft, calling," also "something built or made." The word still was used for "might, power" in 中古英语. Use for "small boat" is 首见于 1670 年代, 可能 源自 a phrase similar to vessels of small craft and referring either to the trade they did or the seamanship they required，或或许 it preserves the word in its original 语义 "power."

example.en: She learned the craft of pottery from her grandmother.
example.zh: 她从祖母那里学会了制陶手艺。

entries.etymology: Old English cran "large wading bird," common Germanic (cognates: Old Saxon krano, Old High German krano, German Kranich, and, with unexplained change of consonant, Old Norse trani), from PIE *gere-no-, suffixed form of root *gere- (2) "to cry hoarsely," also the name of the crane (cognates: Greek geranos, Latin grus, Welsh garan, Lithuanian garnys "heron, stork"). Thus the name is perhaps an echo of its cry in ancient ears. Metaphoric use for "machine with a long arm" is first attested late 13c. (a sense also in equivalent words in German and Greek).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cran "large wading bird," common 日耳曼语 (cognates: 古撒克逊语 krano, 古高地德语 krano, 德语 Kranich, and, with unexplained change of consonant, 古北欧语 trani), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *gere-no-, suffixed form of root *gere- (2) "to cry hoarsely," also the name of the crane (cognates: 希腊语 geranos, 拉丁语 grus, Welsh garan, Lithuanian garnys "heron, stork"). Thus the name is 或许 an echo of its cry in ancient ears. Metaphoric use for "machine with a long arm" is 最早见于 13 世纪晚期 (a sense also in equivalent words in 德语 and 希腊语).

entries.etymology: late 14c., crasschen "break in pieces;" probably imitative. Meaning "break into a party, etc." is 1922. Slang meaning "to sleep" dates from 1943; especially from 1965. Computing sense is from 1973. Related: Crashed; crashing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, crasschen "break in pieces;" 可能 imitative. 义为 "break into a party, etc." is 1922 年. Slang 意为 "to sleep" dates 自 1943 年起; 尤指 自 1965 年起. Computing sense 始于 1973 年. 同源词：Crashed; crashing.

example.en: The car lost control and crashed into the barrier on the highway.
example.zh: 汽车失控后撞上了高速公路的护栏。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, creulen, from a Scandinavian source, perhaps Old Norse krafla "to claw (one's way)," Danish kravle, from the same root as crab (n.1). If there was an Old English *craflian, it has not been recorded. Related: Crawled; crawling.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, creulen, 源自 a Scandinavian source, 或许 古北欧语 krafla "to claw (one's way)," Danish kravle, 源自 same root as crab (n.1). If there was an 古英语 *craflian, it has not been recorded. 同源词：Crawled; crawling.

example.en: The baby began to crawl across the kitchen floor.
example.zh: 婴儿开始在厨房地板上爬行。

definitionLines: a.疯狂的，蠢的；（about）狂热 爱好，着迷的
entries.definition: a.疯狂的，蠢的；（about）狂热 爱好，着迷的
entries.etymology: 1570s, "diseased, sickly," from craze + -y (2). Meaning "full of cracks or flaws" is from 1580s; that of "of unsound mind, or behaving as so" is from 1610s. Jazz slang sense "cool, exciting" attested by 1927. To drive (someone) crazy is attested by 1873. Phrase crazy like a fox recorded from 1935. Crazy Horse, Teton Lakhota (Siouan) war leader (d.1877) translates thašuka witko, literally "his horse is crazy."
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "diseased, sickly," 源自 craze + -y (2). 义为 "full of cracks or flaws" 始于 1580 年代; that of "of unsound mind, or behaving as so" 始于 1610 年代. Jazz 俚语 sense "cool, exciting" attested 截至 1927 年. To drive (someone) crazy is attested 截至 1873 年. Phrase crazy like a fox recorded 自 1935 年起. Crazy Horse, Teton Lakhota (Siouan) war leader (d.1877 年) translates thašuka witko, 字面义为 "his horse is crazy."

example.en: She is absolutely crazy about collecting vintage postcards from around the world.
example.zh: 她对收集来自世界各地的复古明信片绝对痴迷。

definitionLines: vt. 创造，创作；产生；制造， 建立
entries.definition: vt. 创造，创作；产生；制造， 建立
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin creatus, past participle of creare "to make, bring forth, produce, beget," related to crescere "arise, grow" (see crescent). Related: Created; creating.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 creatus, 为 … 的过去分词 creare "to make, bring forth, produce, beget," related to crescere "arise, grow" （参见 crescent). 同源词：Created; creating.

example.en: The nonprofit aims to create new job opportunities in rural areas.
example.zh: 该非营利组织旨在农村地区创造新的就业机会。

definitionLines: a. 有创造力的，创造性的
entries.definition: a. 有创造力的，创造性的
entries.etymology: 1670s, "having the quality of creating," from create + -ive. Of literature, "imaginative," from 1816, first attested in Wordsworth. Creative writing is attested from 1907. Related: Creatively.
entries.etymologyZh: 1670 年代, "having the quality of creating," 源自 create + -ive. Of literature, "imaginative," 自 1816 年起, 最早见于 in Wordsworth. Creative writing 见于 1907 年. 同源词：Creatively.

example.en: The design team is looking for creative individuals to develop new concepts.
example.zh: 设计团队正在寻找有创造力的人才来开发新概念。

entries.etymology: late 13c., "anything created," also "living being," from Old French creature (Modern French créature), from Late Latin creatura "thing created," from creatus, past participle of Latin creare "create" (see create). Meaning "anything that ministers to man's comforts" (1610s), after I Tim. iv:4, led to jocular use for "whiskey" (1630s).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "anything created," also "living being," 源自 古法语 creature (现代法语 créature), 源自 晚期拉丁语 creatura "thing created," 源自 creatus, 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 creare "create" （参见 create). 义为 "anything that ministers to man's comforts" (1610 年代), after I Tim. iv:4, led to jocular use for "whiskey" (1630 年代).

example.en: The deep ocean is home to many strange and exotic creatures.
example.zh: 深海是许多奇异生物的家园。

entries.etymology: "believable," late 14c., from Latin credibilis "worthy to be believed," from credere (see credo). Related: Credibly.
entries.etymologyZh: "believable," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 credibilis "worthy to be believed," 源自 credere （参见 credo). 同源词：Credibly.

example.en: Her account of the accident was credible because it matched all the evidence.
example.zh: 她对事故的陈述是可信的，因为与所有证据吻合。

definitionLines: n. 信贷，赊欠；信用，信誉；名 誉，名望；光荣，功劳；学分
entries.definition: n. 信贷，赊欠；信用，信誉；名 誉，名望；光荣，功劳；学分 vt. 记入贷方
entries.etymology: 1520s, from Middle French crédit (15c.) "belief, trust," from Italian credito, from Latin creditum "a loan, thing entrusted to another," from past participle of credere "to trust, entrust, believe" (see credo). The commercial sense was the original one in English (creditor is mid-15c.). Meaning "honor, acknowledgment of merit," is from c. 1600. Academic sense of "point for completing a course of study" is 1904. Movie/broadcasting sense is 1914. Credit rating is from 1958; credit union is 1881, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 中古法语 crédit (15 世纪) "belief, trust," 源自 意大利语 credito, 源自 拉丁语 creditum "a loan, thing entrusted to another," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 credere "to trust, entrust, believe" （参见 credo). The commercial sense was the original one in English (creditor is 15 世纪中期). 义为 "honor, acknowledgment of merit," 始于 约 1600 年. Academic 语义 "point for completing a course of study" is 1904 年. Movie/broadcasting sense is 1914 年. Credit rating 始于 1958 年; credit union is 1881 年, American English.

example.en: She bought the laptop on credit and paid it off in six months.
example.zh: 她用信用贷款买了这台笔记本电脑，并在六个月内还清了。

entries.definition: n. 爬，徐行，蠕动 vi.爬，蔓延，潜行
entries.etymology: Old English creopan "to creep" (class II strong verb; past tense creap, past participle cropen), from Proto-Germanic *kreupan (source also of Old Frisian kriapa, Middle Dutch crupen, Old Norse krjupa "to creep"), perhaps from a PIE root *g(e)r- "crooked" [Watkins]. Related: Crept; creeping.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 creopan "to creep" (class II strong 动词; past tense creap, past participle cropen), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *kreupan (source also of 古弗里西语 kriapa, Middle 荷兰语 crupen, 古北欧语 krjupa "to creep"), 或源自 a 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *g(e)r- "crooked" [Watkins]. 同源词：Crept; creeping.

example.en: A vine began to creep up the wall of the abandoned house.
example.zh: 一根藤蔓开始沿着废弃房屋的墙壁爬上去。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "group of soldiers," from Middle French crue (Old French creue) "an increase, recruit, military reinforcement," from fem. past participle of creistre "grow," from Latin crescere "arise, grow" (see crescent). Meaning "people acting or working together" is first attested 1560s. "Gang of men on a warship" is from 1690s. Crew-cut first attested 1938, so called because the style  originally was adopted by boat crews at Harvard and Yale.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "group of soldiers," 源自 中古法语 crue (古法语 creue) "an increase, recruit, military reinforcement," 源自 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 creistre "grow," 源自 拉丁语 crescere "arise, grow" （参见 crescent). 义为 "people acting or working together" is 最早见于 1560 年代. "Gang of men on a warship" 始于 1690 年代. Crew-cut 最早见于 1938 年, so called because the style 原义为 was adopted by boat crews at Harvard and Yale.

example.en: The pilot briefed the crew on emergency procedures before takeoff.
example.zh: 飞行员在起飞前向机组人员讲解了紧急程序。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., "sinfulness," from Old French crimne (12c., Modern French crime), from Latin crimen (genitive criminis) "charge, indictment, accusation; crime, fault, offense," perhaps from cernere "to decide, to sift" (see crisis). But Klein (citing Brugmann) rejects this and suggests *cri-men, which originally would have been "cry of distress" (Tucker also suggests a root in "cry" words and refers to English plaint, plaintiff, etc.). Meaning "offense punishable by law" is from late 14c. The Latin word is glossed in Old English by facen, also "deceit, fraud, treachery." Crime wave first attested 1893, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "sinfulness," 源自 古法语 crimne (12 世纪, 现代法语 crime), 源自 拉丁语 crimen (属格 criminis) "charge, indictment, accusation; crime, fault, offense," 或源自 cernere "to decide, to sift" （参见 crisis). But Klein (citing Brugmann) rejects this and suggests *cri-men, which 原义为 would have been "cry of distress" (Tucker also suggests a root in "cry" words and refers to English plaint, plaintiff, etc.). 义为 "offense punishable by law" 始于 14 世纪晚期 The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by facen, also "deceit, fraud, treachery." Crime wave 最早见于 1893 年, American English.

example.en: Authorities are working hard to reduce violent crime in the city.
example.zh: 当局正在努力减少城市中的暴力犯罪。

entries.definition: a.犯罪的，刑事的 n. 罪犯，刑事犯
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French criminel (11c.), from Latin criminalis "pertaining to crime," from crimen (genitive criminis); see crime. Preserves the Latin -n-. Criminal law (or criminal justice) distinguished from civil in English at least since late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 criminel (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 criminalis "pertaining to crime," 源自 crimen (属格 criminis); 参见 crime. Preserves the 拉丁语 -n-. Criminal law (or criminal justice) distinguished 源自 civil in English at least 自 15 世纪晚期

example.en: The police launched an investigation into the criminal activity in the neighborhood.
example.zh: 警方对该社区的犯罪活动展开调查。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latinized form of Greek krisis "turning point in a disease" (used as such by Hippocrates and Galen), literally "judgment, result of a trial, selection," from krinein "to separate, decide, judge," from PIE root *krei- "to sieve, discriminate, distinguish" (source also of Greek krinesthai "to explain;" Old English hriddel "sieve;" Latin cribrum "sieve," crimen "judgment, crime," cernere (past participle cretus) "to sift, separate;" Old Irish criathar, Old Welsh cruitr "sieve;" Middle Irish crich "border, boundary"). Transferred non-medical sense is 1620s in English. A German term for "mid-life crisis" is Torschlusspanik, literally "shut-door-panic," fear of being on the wrong side of a closing gate.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 Latinized form of 希腊语 krisis "turning point in a disease" (used as such by Hippocrates and Galen), 字面义为 "judgment, result of a trial, selection," 源自 krinein "to separate, decide, judge," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *krei- "to sieve, discriminate, distinguish" (source also of 希腊语 krinesthai "to explain;" 古英语 hriddel "sieve;" 拉丁语 cribrum "sieve," crimen "judgment, crime," cernere (past participle cretus) "to sift, separate;" Old 爱尔兰语 criathar, Old Welsh cruitr "sieve;" Middle 爱尔兰语 crich "border, boundary"). Transferred non-medical sense is 1620 年代 in English. A 德语 term for "mid-life crisis" is Torschlusspanik, 字面义为 "shut-door-panic," fear of being on the wrong side of a closing gate.

example.en: The government acted quickly to resolve the economic crisis.
example.zh: 政府迅速采取行动以解决经济危机。

entries.etymology: Old English crisp "curly," from Latin crispus "curled, wrinkled, having curly hair," from PIE root *(s)ker- (3) "to turn, bend" (see ring (n.)). It began to mean "brittle" 1520s, for obscure reasons, perhaps based on what happens to flat things when they are cooked. Figurative sense of "neat, brisk" is from 1814; perhaps a separate word. As a noun, from late 14c. Potato crisps (the British version of U.S. potato chips) is from 1929.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 crisp "curly," 源自 拉丁语 crispus "curled, wrinkled, having curly hair," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *(s)ker- (3) "to turn, bend" （参见 ring （名）). It began to mean "brittle" 1520 年代, for obscure reasons, 或许 based on what happens to flat things when they are cooked. Figurative 语义 "neat, brisk" 始于 1814 年; 或许 a separate word. 作名词时, 源自 14 世纪晚期 Potato crisps (the British version of U.S. potato chips) 始于 1929 年.

example.en: The biscuits came out of the oven golden and crisp, just the way she liked them.
example.zh: 饼干从烤箱里出来时金黄酥脆，正合她的口味。

entries.etymology: 1660s, from Latinized form of Greek kriterion "means for judging, standard," from krites "judge," from PIE root *krei- (see crisis). Used in English as a Greek word from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 Latinized form of 希腊语 kriterion "means for judging, standard," 源自 krites "judge," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *krei- （参见 crisis). Used in English 作为 希腊语 word 源自 1610 年代.

entries.etymology: 1580s, "one who passes judgment," from Middle French critique (14c.), from Latin criticus "a judge, literary critic," from Greek kritikos "able to make judgments," from krinein "to separate, decide" (see crisis). Meaning "one who judges merits of books, plays, etc." is from c. 1600. The English word always had overtones of "censurer, faultfinder."
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "one who passes judgment," 源自 中古法语 critique (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 criticus "a judge, literary critic," 源自 希腊语 kritikos "able to make judgments," 源自 krinein "to separate, decide" （参见 crisis). 义为 "one who judges merits of books, plays, etc." 始于 约 1600 年. The English word always had overtones of "censurer, faultfinder."

example.en: The film received harsh reviews from every critic who attended the premiere.
example.zh: 每位出席首映式的评论家都对这部电影给出了严苛的评价。

definitionLines: a.批评的，批判的；危急的，紧 要的
entries.definition: a.批评的，批判的；危急的，紧 要的
entries.etymology: 1580s, "censorious," from critic + -al (1). Meaning "pertaining to criticism" is from 1741; medical sense is from c. 1600; meaning "of the nature of a crisis" is from 1640s; that of "crucial" is from 1841, from the "decisive" sense in Latin criticus. Related: Criticality (1756; in the nuclear sense, 1950); critically (1650s, "accurately;" 1815, "in a critical situation"). In nuclear science, critical mass is attested from 1940.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "censorious," 源自 critic + -al (1). 义为 "pertaining to criticism" 始于 1741 年; medical sense 始于 约 1600 年; 意为 "of the nature of a crisis" 始于 1640 年代; that of "crucial" 始于 1841 年, 源自 "decisive" sense in 拉丁语 criticus. 同源词：Criticality (1756 年; in the nuclear sense, 1950 年); critically (1650 年代, "accurately;" 1815 年, "in a critical situation"). In nuclear science, critical mass 见于 1940 年.

example.en: The patient was in a critical condition and needed immediate surgery.
example.zh: 患者处于危急状态，需要立即手术。

entries.etymology: 1640s, "to pass judgment on something" (usually unfavorable), from critic + -ize. Meaning "to discuss critically" is from 1660s; that of "to censure" is from 1704. Related: Criticized; criticizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "to pass judgment on something" (通常 unfavorable), 源自 critic + -ize. 义为 "to discuss critically" 始于 1660 年代; that of "to censure" 始于 1704 年. 同源词：Criticized; criticizing.

example.en: The journalist was quick to criticize the government for its slow response.
example.zh: 这位记者迅速批评政府应对迟缓。

entries.etymology: Old English cropp "bird's craw," also "head or top of a sprout or herb." The common notion is "protuberance." Cognate with Old High German kropf, Old Norse kroppr. Meaning "harvest product" is c. 1300, probably through the verbal meaning "cut off the top of a plant" (c. 1200).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cropp "bird's craw," also "head or top of a sprout or herb." The common notion is "protuberance." Cognate with 古高地德语 kropf, 古北欧语 kroppr. 义为 "harvest product" is 约 1300 年, 可能 through the verbal 意为 "cut off the top of a plant" (约 1200 年).

example.en: A late frost destroyed nearly half of the wheat crop last year.
example.zh: 去年的一场晚霜摧毁了近一半的小麦收成。

definitionLines: v. 越过，穿过；使交叉，使相交
entries.definition: v. 越过，穿过；使交叉，使相交 n. 十字形，十字架 a. 交叉的，横穿的
entries.etymology:
Old English cros "instrument of Christ's crucifixion; symbol of Christianity" (mid-10c.), from Old Irish cros, probably via Scandinavian, from Latin crux (accusative crucem, genitive crucis) "stake, cross" on which criminals were impaled or hanged (originally a tall, round pole); hence, figuratively, "torture, trouble, misery." The word is possibly of Phoenician origin. Replaced Old English rood.

Also from Latin crux are Italian croce, French croix, Spanish and Portuguese cruz, Dutch kruis, German Kreuz.

By c. 1200 as "ornamental likeness of the cross, something resembling or in the form of a cross; sign of the cross made with the right hand or with fingers." From mid-14c. as "small cross with a human figure attached; a crucifix;" late 14c. as "outdoor structure or monument in the form of a cross." Also late 14c. as "a cross formed by two lines drawn or cut on a surface; two lines intersecting at right angles; the shape of a cross without regard to religious signification." From late 12c. as a surname.

From c. 1200 in the figurative sense "the burden of a Christian; suffering; a trial or affliction; penance in Christ's name," from Matt. x.38, xvi.24, etc. Theological sense "crucifixion and death of Christ as a necessary part of his mission" is from late 14c.

As "a mixing of breeds in the production of animals" from 1760, hence broadly "a mixture of the characteristics of two different things." In pugilism, 1906, from the motion of the blow (1880s as a verb; cross-counter (n.) is from 1883).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cros "instrument of Christ's crucifixion; symbol of Christianity" (10 世纪中期), 源自 Old 爱尔兰语 cros, 可能 经由 Scandinavian, 源自 拉丁语 crux (宾格 crucem, 属格 crucis) "stake, cross" on which criminals were impaled or hanged (原义为 a tall, round pole); hence, figuratively, "torture, trouble, misery." The word is possibly of Phoenician origin. Replaced 古英语 rood. Also 源自 拉丁语 crux are 意大利语 croce, 法语 croix, 西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 cruz, 荷兰语 kruis, 德语 Kreuz. By 约 1200 年 as "ornamental likeness of the cross, something resembling or in the form of a cross; sign of the cross made with the right hand or with fingers." From 14 世纪中期 as "small cross with a human figure attached; a crucifix;" 14 世纪晚期 as "outdoor structure or monument in the form of a cross." Also 14 世纪晚期 as "a cross formed by two lines drawn or cut on a surface; two lines intersecting at right angles; the shape of a cross without regard to religious signification." From 12 世纪晚期 作为 surname. From 约 1200 年 in the figurative sense "the burden of a Christian; suffering; a trial or affliction; penance in Christ's name," 源自 Matt. x.38, xvi.24, etc. Theological sense "crucifixion and death of Christ as a necessary part of his mission" 始于 14 世纪晚期 As "a mixing of breeds in the production of animals" 自 1760 年起, hence broadly "a mixture of the characteristics of two different things." In pugilism, 1906 年, 源自 motion of the blow (1880 年代 作动词时; cross-counter （名） 始于 1883 年).

example.en: It takes about twenty minutes to cross the tunnel by car.
example.zh: 开车穿过这条隧道大约需要二十分钟。

definitionLines: n. 横越，横渡；交叉点，渡口
entries.definition: n. 横越，横渡；交叉点，渡口
entries.etymology: 1530s, "a marking with a cross," verbal noun from cross (v.). From 1570s as "action of passing across;" 1630s as "place where (a river, a road, etc.) is crossed;" from 1690s as "intersection" (originally of streets). Meaning "action of crossing out by drawing crossed lines through" is from 1650s. Crossing-gate is from 1876.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "a marking with a cross," verbal 名词 源自 cross （动）. From 1570 年代 as "action of passing across;" 1630 年代 as "place where (a river, a road, etc.) is crossed;" 源自 1690 年代 as "intersection" (原义为 of streets). 义为 "action of crossing out by drawing crossed lines through" 始于 1650 年代. Crossing-gate 始于 1876 年.

definitionLines: n. 十字路口；交叉路；岔道；重 大的抉择关头
entries.definition: n. 十字路口；交叉路；岔道；重 大的抉择关头
entries.etymology: also cross-road, 1680s, from cross- + road. Figurative use from 1733.
entries.etymologyZh: also cross-road, 1680 年代, 源自 cross- + road. Figurative use 自 1733 年起.

entries.definition: n. 人群，群众 v.挤满，拥挤
entries.etymology: Old English crudan "to press, crush." Cognate with Middle Dutch cruden "to press, push," Middle High German kroten "to press, oppress," Norwegian kryda "to crowd." Related: Crowded; crowding.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 crudan "to press, crush." Cognate with Middle 荷兰语 cruden "to press, push," Middle High 德语 kroten "to press, oppress," Norwegian kryda "to crowd." 同源词：Crowded; crowding.

example.en: A large crowd had gathered outside the stadium before the match began.
example.zh: 一大群人在比赛开始前聚集在体育场外。

example.en: The subway car was so crowded that she could barely breathe.
example.zh: 地铁车厢太拥挤了，她几乎无法呼吸。

entries.definition: n. 王冠；花冠 vt. 加冠于
entries.etymology:
early 12c., "royal crown," from Anglo-French coroune, Old French corone (13c., Modern French couronne), from Latin corona "crown," originally "wreath, garland," related to Greek korone "anything curved, kind of crown." Old English used corona, directly from Latin.

Extended to coins bearing the imprint of a crown (early 15c.), especially the British silver 5-shilling piece. Also monetary units in Iceland, Sweden (krona), Norway, Denmark (krone), and formerly in German Empire and Austria-Hungary (krone). Meaning "top of the skull" is from c. 1300. Crown-prince is 1791, a translation of German kronprinz.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, "royal crown," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 coroune, 古法语 corone (13 世纪, 现代法语 couronne), 源自 拉丁语 corona "crown," 原义为 "wreath, garland," related to 希腊语 korone "anything curved, kind of crown." 古英语 used corona, 直接源自 拉丁语. Extended to coins bearing the imprint of a crown (15 世纪初), 尤指 the British silver 5-shilling piece. Also monetary units in Iceland, Sweden (krona), Norway, Denmark (krone), and formerly in 德语 Empire and Austria-Hungary (krone). 义为 "top of the skull" 始于 约 1300 年. Crown-prince is 1791 年, a translation of 德语 kronprinz.

definitionLines: a. 决定性的；重要的；定局的； 决断的
entries.definition: a. 决定性的；重要的；定局的； 决断的
entries.etymology: 1706, "cross-shaped," from French crucial, a medical term for ligaments of the knee (which cross each other), from Latin crux (genitive crucis) "cross" (see cross (n.)). The meaning "decisive, critical" (1830) is extended from a logical term, Instantias Crucis, adopted by Francis Bacon (1620); the notion is of cross fingerboard signposts at forking roads, thus a requirement to choose.
entries.etymologyZh: 1706 年, "cross-shaped," 源自 法语 crucial, a medical term for ligaments of the knee (which cross each other), 源自 拉丁语 crux (属格 crucis) "cross" （参见 cross （名）). The 意为 "decisive, critical" (1830 年) is extended 源自 a logical term, Instantias Crucis, adopted by Francis Bacon (1620 年); the notion is of cross fingerboard signposts at forking roads, thus a requirement to choose.

example.en: The judge's ruling was crucial in determining the outcome of the case.
example.zh: 法官的裁决在决定案件结果方面至关重要。

definitionLines: a. 天然，未加工的；简陋的；粗 鲁的
entries.definition: a. 天然，未加工的；简陋的；粗 鲁的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "in a raw state," from Latin crudus "rough; not cooked, raw, bloody," from PIE *krue-do-, from PIE *kreue- (1) "raw flesh" (see raw). Meaning "lacking grace" is first attested 1640s. Related: Crudely; crudeness. Crude oil is from 1865.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "in a raw state," 源自 拉丁语 crudus "rough; not cooked, raw, bloody," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *krue-do-, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kreue- (1) "raw flesh" （参见 raw). 义为 "lacking grace" is 最早见于 1640 年代. 同源词：Crudely; crudeness. Crude oil 始于 1865 年.

example.en: The sculpture was carved from crude stone found near the river.
example.zh: 这座雕塑是用河边发现的天然原石雕刻而成的。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French cruel (12c.), earlier crudel, from Latin crudelis "rude, unfeeling; cruel, hard-hearted," related to crudus "rough, raw, bloody" (see crude). Related: Cruelly. Latin medial -d- began to disappear 10c. in French: compare chance/cadentia, cheoir/cadere, joyeux/gaudiosus, juif/judaeus, moyen/medianus, obéir/obedire, séance/sedentia.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 cruel (12 世纪), earlier crudel, 源自 拉丁语 crudelis "rude, unfeeling; cruel, hard-hearted," related to crudus "rough, raw, bloody" （参见 crude). 同源词：Cruelly. 拉丁语 medial -d- began to disappear 10 世纪 in 法语: 对比 chance/cadentia, cheoir/cadere, joyeux/gaudiosus, juif/judaeus, moyen/medianus, obéir/obedire, séance/sedentia.

example.en: It was cruel to leave the injured animal in the cold.
example.zh: 把受伤的动物留在寒冷中是很残忍的行为。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French crualté (12c., Modern French cruauté), from Latin crudelitatem (nominative crudelitas) "cruelty," from crudelis (see cruel).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 crualté (12 世纪, 现代法语 cruauté), 源自 拉丁语 crudelitatem (主格 crudelitas) "cruelty," 源自 crudelis （参见 cruel).

entries.etymology: 1650s, from Dutch kruisen "to cross, sail to and fro," from kruis "cross," from Latin crux. Compare the sense evolution in cognate cross (v.). Related: Cruised; cruising. As a noun from 1706.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, 源自 荷兰语 kruisen "to cross, sail to and fro," 源自 kruis "cross," 源自 拉丁语 crux. 对比 the sense evolution in 同源 cross （动）. 同源词：Cruised; cruising. 作名词时 自 1706 年起.

example.en: They decided to cruise along the coast and enjoy the scenic views.
example.zh: 他们决定沿着海岸巡游，欣赏沿途风景。

entries.etymology: late 15c., kremelen, from Old English *crymelan, presumed frequentative of gecrymman "to break into crumbs," from cruma (see crumb). The -b- is 16c., probably on analogy of French-derived words like humble, where it belongs, or by influence of crumb. Related: Crumbled; crumbling.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, kremelen, 源自 古英语 *crymelan, presumed 为 … 的反复体 gecrymman "to break into crumbs," 源自 cruma （参见 crumb). The -b- is 16 世纪, 可能 on analogy of 法语-derived words like humble, where it belongs，或by influence of crumb. 同源词：Crumbled; crumbling.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French cruissir (Modern French écraser), variant of croissir "to gnash (teeth), crash, break," perhaps from Frankish *krostjan "to gnash" (cognates: Gothic kriustan, Old Swedish krysta "to gnash"). Figurative sense of "to humiliate, demoralize" is c. 1600. Related: Crushed; crushing. Italian crosciare, Catalan cruxir, Spanish crujirare "to crack" are Germanic loan-words.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 cruissir (现代法语 écraser), 为 … 的变体 croissir "to gnash (teeth), crash, break," 或源自 Frankish *krostjan "to gnash" (cognates: Gothic kriustan, Old Swedish krysta "to gnash"). Figurative 语义 "to humiliate, demoralize" is 约 1600 年. 同源词：Crushed; crushing. 意大利语 crosciare, Catalan cruxir, 西班牙语 crujirare "to crack" are 日耳曼语 loan-words.

example.en: The earthquake was strong enough to crush buildings and trap people inside.
example.zh: 这场地震足以压垮建筑物，将人困在里面。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "hard outer part of bread," from Old French crouste (13c., Modern French croûte) and directly from Latin crusta "rind, crust, shell, bark," from PIE *krus-to- "that which has been hardened," from root *kreus- "to begin to freeze, form a crust" (source also of Sanskrit krud- "make hard, thicken;" Avestan xruzdra- "hard;" Greek krystallos "ice, crystal," kryos "icy cold, frost;" Lettish kruwesis "frozen mud;" Old High German hrosa "ice, crust;" Old English hruse "earth;" Old Norse hroðr "scurf"). Meaning "outer shell of the earth" is from 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "hard outer part of bread," 源自 古法语 crouste (13 世纪, 现代法语 croûte) and 直接源自 拉丁语 crusta "rind, crust, shell, bark," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *krus-to- "that which has been hardened," 源自 root *kreus- "to begin to freeze, form a crust" (source also of 梵语 krud- "make hard, thicken;" Avestan xruzdra- "hard;" 希腊语 krystallos "ice, crystal," kryos "icy cold, frost;" Lettish kruwesis "frozen mud;" 古高地德语 hrosa "ice, crust;" 古英语 hruse "earth;" 古北欧语 hroðr "scurf"). 义为 "outer shell of the earth" 始于 1550 年代.

entries.etymology:
early 13c., "beg, implore," from Old French crier, from Vulgar Latin *critare, from Latin quiritare "to wail, shriek" (source of Italian gridare, Old Spanish cridar, Spanish and Portuguese gritar), which is of uncertain origin; perhaps a variant of quirritare "to squeal like a pig," from *quis, echoic of squealing, despite ancient folk etymology that traces it to "call for the help of the Quirites," the Roman constabulary. The meaning was extended 13c. to weep, which it largely replaced by 16c. Related: Cried; crying.

Most languages, in common with English, use the general word for "cry out, shout, wail" to also mean "weep, shed tears to express pain or grief." Romance and Slavic, however, use words for this whose ultimate meaning is "beat (the breast)," compare French pleurer, Spanish llorar, both from Latin plorare "cry aloud," but probably originally plodere "beat, clap the hands." Also Italian piangere (cognate with French plaindre "lament, pity") from Latin plangere, originally "beat," but especially of the breast, as a sign of grief. U.S. colloquial for crying out loud is 1924, probably another euphemism for for Christ's sake.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "beg, implore," 源自 古法语 crier, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *critare, 源自 拉丁语 quiritare "to wail, shriek" (source of 意大利语 gridare, Old 西班牙语 cridar, 西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 gritar), which is 来源存疑; 或许 a 为 … 的变体 quirritare "to squeal like a pig," 源自 *quis, echoic of squealing, despite ancient folk etymology that traces it to "call for the help of the Quirites," the Roman constabulary. The 意为 was extended 13 世纪 to weep, which it largely replaced by 16 世纪 同源词：Cried; crying. Most languages, in common with English, use the general word for "cry out, shout, wail" to also mean "weep, shed tears to express pain or grief." Romance and Slavic, however, use words for this whose ultimate 意为 is "beat (the breast)," 对比 法语 pleurer, 西班牙语 llorar, both 源自 拉丁语 plorare "cry aloud," but 可能 原义为 plodere "beat, clap the hands." Also 意大利语 piangere (与 … 同源 法语 plaindre "lament, pity") 源自 拉丁语 plangere, 原义为 "beat," but 尤指 of the breast, 作为 sign of grief. U.S. 口语 for crying out loud is 1924 年, 可能 another euphemism for for Christ's sake.

example.en: The toddler began to cry loudly after dropping her ice cream on the ground.
example.zh: 小孩把冰淇淋掉在地上后，放声大哭起来。

definitionLines: a. 水晶的，晶体的；透明的
entries.definition: n. 水晶，晶体 a. 水晶的，晶体的；透明的
entries.etymology: Old English cristal "clear ice, clear mineral," from Old French cristal (12c., Modern French crystal), from Latin crystallus "crystal, ice," from Greek krystallos, from kryos "frost," from PIE root *kru(s)- "hard, hard outer surface" (see crust). Spelling adopted the Latin form 15c.-17c. The mineral has been so-called since Old English; it was regarded by the ancients as a sort of fossilized ice. As a shortened form of crystal-glass it dates from 1590s. As an adjective, from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cristal "clear ice, clear mineral," 源自 古法语 cristal (12 世纪, 现代法语 crystal), 源自 拉丁语 crystallus "crystal, ice," 源自 希腊语 krystallos, 源自 kryos "frost," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kru(s)- "hard, hard outer surface" （参见 crust). Spelling adopted the 拉丁语 form 15 世纪-17 世纪 The mineral has been so-called 自 古英语; it was regarded by the ancients 作为 sort of fossilized ice. 作为 shortened form of crystal-glass it dates 源自 1590 年代. 作形容词时, 源自 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The chandelier was made of hundreds of tiny crystal pieces that sparkled in the light.
example.zh: 这盏枝形吊灯由数百个在灯光下闪闪发光的小水晶片制成。

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French cube (13c.) and directly from Latin cubus, from Greek kybos "a six-sided die," used metaphorically of dice-like blocks of any sort, also "cake; piece of salted fish; vertebra," of uncertain origin. Beekes points out that "words for dice are often loans" and that "the Lydians claimed to have invented the game" of kybos. The mathematical sense is from 1550s in English (it also was in the ancient Greek word: the Greeks threw with three dice; the highest possible roll was three sixes).
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 cube (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 cubus, 源自 希腊语 kybos "a six-sided die," used metaphorically of dice-like blocks of any sort, also "cake; piece of salted fish; vertebra," 来源存疑. Beekes points out that "words for dice are often loans" and that "the Lydians claimed to have invented the game" of kybos. The mathematical sense 始于 1550 年代 in English (it also was in the ancient 希腊语 word: the Greeks threw with three dice; the highest possible roll was three sixes).

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French cubique (14c.), from Latin cubicus, from Greek kybikos, from kybos "cube" (see cube (n.)). Related: Cubical.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 cubique (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 cubicus, 源自 希腊语 kybikos, 源自 kybos "cube" （参见 cube （名）). 同源词：Cubical.

entries.etymology: 1928, from cue (n.1). Related: Cued, cueing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1928 年, 源自 cue (n.1). 同源词：Cued, cueing.

example.en: The actor missed his cue and entered the stage too early.
example.zh: 那名演员错过了他的提示，提前走上了舞台。

definitionLines: vi. 到绝顶；达到高潮；达到 顶点
vt. 使结束；使达到高潮
entries.definition: vi. 到绝顶；达到高潮；达到 顶点 vt. 使结束；使达到高潮
entries.etymology: 1640s, from Late Latin culminatus past participle of culminare "to top, to crown," from Latin culmen (genitive culminis) "top, peak, summit, roof, gable," also used figuratively, contraction of columen (see column). Related: Culminated; culminating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 culminatus 为 … 的过去分词 culminare "to top, to crown," 源自 拉丁语 culmen (属格 culminis) "top, peak, summit, roof, gable," also used figuratively, contraction of columen （参见 column). 同源词：Culminated; culminating.

entries.etymology: early 17c., from Medieval Latin cultivatus, past participle of cultivare "to cultivate," from Late Latin cultivus "tilled," from Latin cultus (see cult). Figurative sense of "improve by training or education" is from 1680s. Related: Cultivable; cultivated; cultivating.
entries.etymologyZh: 17 世纪初, 源自 中古拉丁语 cultivatus, 为 … 的过去分词 cultivare "to cultivate," 源自 晚期拉丁语 cultivus "tilled," 源自 拉丁语 cultus （参见 cult). Figurative 语义 "improve by training or education" 始于 1680 年代. 同源词：Cultivable; cultivated; cultivating.

example.en: Schools should cultivate critical thinking skills in students from an early age.
example.zh: 学校应该从小培养学生的批判性思维能力。

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., "the tilling of land," from Middle French culture and directly from Latin cultura "a cultivating, agriculture," figuratively "care, culture, an honoring," from past participle stem of colere "tend, guard, cultivate, till" (see colony). The figurative sense of "cultivation through education" is first attested c. 1500. Meaning "the intellectual side of civilization" is from 1805; that of "collective customs and achievements of a people" is from 1867.

Slang culture vulture is from 1947. Culture shock first recorded 1940. Ironic or contemptuous spelling kulchur is attested from 1940 (Pound), and compare kultur.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "the tilling of land," 源自 中古法语 culture and 直接源自 拉丁语 cultura "a cultivating, agriculture," figuratively "care, culture, an honoring," 源自 past participle stem of colere "tend, guard, cultivate, till" （参见 colony). The figurative 语义 "cultivation through education" is 最早见于 约 1500 年. 义为 "the intellectual side of civilization" 始于 1805 年; that of "collective customs and achievements of a people" 始于 1867 年. Slang culture vulture 始于 1947 年. Culture shock 首见于 1940 年. Ironic or contemptuous spelling kulchur 见于 1940 年 (Pound), and 对比 kultur.

example.en: The festival celebrates the rich culture of the local community.
example.zh: 这个节日庆祝当地社区丰富的文化。

entries.etymology:
Old English cuppe, from Late Latin cuppa "cup" (source of Italian coppa, Spanish copa, Old French coupe "cup"), from Latin cupa "tub, cask, tun, barrel," from PIE *keup- "a hollow" (source also of Sanskrit kupah "hollow, pit, cave," Greek kype "a kind of ship," Old Church Slavonic kupu, Lithuanian kaupas).

The Late Latin word was borrowed throughout Germanic: Old Frisian kopp "cup, head," Middle Low German kopp "cup," Middle Dutch coppe, Dutch kopje "cup, head." German cognate Kopf now means exclusively "head" (compare French tête, from Latin testa "potsherd"). Meaning "part of a bra that holds a breast" is from 1938. [One's] cup of tea "what interests one" (1932), earlier used of persons (1908), the sense being "what is invigorating."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 cuppe, 源自 晚期拉丁语 cuppa "cup" (source of 意大利语 coppa, 西班牙语 copa, 古法语 coupe "cup"), 源自 拉丁语 cupa "tub, cask, tun, barrel," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *keup- "a hollow" (source also of 梵语 kupah "hollow, pit, cave," 希腊语 kype "a kind of ship," Old Church Slavonic kupu, Lithuanian kaupas). The 晚期拉丁语 word was borrowed throughout 日耳曼语: 古弗里西语 kopp "cup, head," Middle Low 德语 kopp "cup," Middle 荷兰语 coppe, 荷兰语 kopje "cup, head." 德语 同源 Kopf 现在 means exclusively "head" (对比 法语 tête, 源自 拉丁语 testa "potsherd"). 义为 "part of a bra that holds a breast" 始于 1938 年. [One's] cup of tea "what interests one" (1932 年), earlier used of persons (1908 年), the sense being "what is invigorating."

entries.etymology: late 14c., "a board or table to place cups and like objects," from cup (n.) + board (n.1). As a type of closed cabinet for food, etc., from early 16c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a board or table to place cups and like objects," 源自 cup （名） + board (n.1). 作为 type of closed cabinet for food, etc., 源自 16 世纪初

entries.definition: n. 抑制；勒马绳；路边 vt. 勒住；控制
entries.etymology: late 15c., "strap passing under the jaw of a horse" (used to restrain the animal), from Old French courbe (12c.) "curb on a horse," from Latin curvus, from curvare "to bend" (see curve (v.)). Meaning "enclosed framework" is from 1510s, probably originally with a notion of "curved;" extended to margins of garden beds 1731; to "margin of stone between a sidewalk and road" 1791 (sometimes spelled kerb). Figurative sense of "a check, a restraint" is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "strap passing under the jaw of a horse" (used to restrain the animal), 源自 古法语 courbe (12 世纪) "curb on a horse," 源自 拉丁语 curvus, 源自 curvare "to bend" （参见 curve （动）). 义为 "enclosed framework" 始于 1510 年代, 可能 原义为 with a 概念 "curved;" extended to margins of garden beds 1731 年; to "margin of stone between a sidewalk and road" 1791 年 (有时 spelled kerb). Figurative 语义 "a check, a restraint" 始于 1610 年代.

entries.definition: n./v. （of）治愈，医治 n. 良药，疗法
entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French curer, from Latin curare "take care of," hence, in medical language, "treat medically, cure" (see cure (n.1)). In reference to fish, pork, etc., first recorded 1743. Related: Cured; curing.

Most words for "cure, heal" in European languages originally applied to the person being treated but now can be used with reference to the disease, too. Relatively few show an ancient connection to words for "physician;" typically they are connected instead to words for "make whole" or "tend to" or even "conjurer." French guérir (with Italian guarir, Old Spanish guarir) is from a Germanic verb stem also found in in Gothic warjan, Old English wearian "ward off, prevent, defend" (see warrant (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 curer, 源自 拉丁语 curare "take care of," hence, in medical language, "treat medically, cure" （参见 cure (n.1)). In reference to fish, pork, etc., 首见于 1743 年. 同源词：Cured; curing. Most words for "cure, heal" in European languages 原义为 applied to the person being treated but 现在 can be used with reference to the disease, too. Relatively few show an ancient connection to words for "physician;" typically they are connected instead to words for "make whole" or "tend to" or even "conjurer." 法语 guérir (with 意大利语 guarir, Old 西班牙语 guarir) 始于 a 日耳曼语 动词 stem also found in in Gothic warjan, 古英语 wearian "ward off, prevent, defend" （参见 warrant （名）).

example.en: Scientists are still searching for a cure for the common cold.
example.zh: 科学家们仍在寻找治疗普通感冒的方法。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "evening signal, ringing of a bell at a fixed hour," from Anglo-French coeverfu (late 13c.), from Old French cuevrefeu, literally "cover fire" (Modern French couvre-feu), from cuevre, imperative of covrir "to cover" (see cover (v.)) + feu "fire" (see focus (n.)). The medieval practice of ringing a bell at fixed time in the evening as an order to bank the hearths and prepare for sleep. The original purpose was to prevent conflagrations from untended fires. The modern extended sense of "periodic restriction of movement" had evolved by 1800s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "evening signal, ringing of a bell at a fixed hour," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 coeverfu (13 世纪晚期), 源自 古法语 cuevrefeu, 字面义为 "cover fire" (现代法语 couvre-feu), 源自 cuevre, imperative of covrir "to cover" （参见 cover （动）) + feu "fire" （参见 focus （名）). The medieval practice of ringing a bell at fixed time in the evening 作为 order to bank the hearths and prepare for sleep. The original purpose was to prevent conflagrations 源自 untended fires. The modern extended 语义 "periodic restriction of movement" had evolved by 1800 年代.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "eager to know" (often in a bad sense), from Old French curios "solicitous, anxious, inquisitive; odd, strange" (Modern French curieux) and directly from Latin curiosus "careful, diligent; inquiring eagerly, meddlesome," akin to cura "care" (see cure (n.)). The objective sense of "exciting curiosity" is 1715 in English. In booksellers' catalogues, the word means "erotic, pornographic." Curiouser and curiouser is from "Alice in Wonderland" (1865).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "eager to know" (常 in a bad sense), 源自 古法语 curios "solicitous, anxious, inquisitive; odd, strange" (现代法语 curieux) and 直接源自 拉丁语 curiosus "careful, diligent; inquiring eagerly, meddlesome," akin to cura "care" （参见 cure （名）). The objective 语义 "exciting curiosity" is 1715 年 in English. In booksellers' catalogues, the word means "erotic, pornographic." Curiouser and curiouser 始于 "Alice in Wonderland" (1865 年).

example.en: The child was curious about how the magician made the rabbit disappear.
example.zh: 这个孩子对魔术师如何让兔子消失感到好奇。

entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, metathesis of crulle (约 1300 年), 可能 源自 an unrecorded 古英语 word or 源自 Middle 荷兰语 krul "curly," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *krusl- (source also of East Frisian krull "lock of hair," Middle High 德语 krol, Norwegian krull, Danish krølle "curl"). The 名词 见于 约 1600 年.

entries.definition: n. 流，水流，气流，电流；潮流， 趋势 a. 通用的，流行的，当前的
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "running, flowing," from Old French corant "running, lively, eager, swift," present participle of corre "to run," from Latin currere "to run, move quickly" (of persons or things), from PIE *kers- "to run" (source also of Greek -khouros "running," Lithuanian karsiu "go quickly," Old Norse horskr "swift," Old Irish and Middle Welsh carr "cart, wagon," Breton karr "chariot," Welsh carrog "torrent"). Meaning "prevalent, generally accepted" is from 1560s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "running, flowing," 源自 古法语 corant "running, lively, eager, swift," 为 … 的现在分词 corre "to run," 源自 拉丁语 currere "to run, move quickly" (of persons or things), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kers- "to run" (source also of 希腊语 -khouros "running," Lithuanian karsiu "go quickly," 古北欧语 horskr "swift," Old 爱尔兰语 and Middle Welsh carr "cart, wagon," Breton karr "chariot," Welsh carrog "torrent"). 义为 "prevalent, generally accepted" 始于 1560 年代.

example.en: The current trend shows a steady rise in online shopping.
example.zh: 当前趋势显示网购持续稳步上升。

definitionLines: n.（学校、专业的）全部课程； （取得毕业资格的）必修课程

entries.etymology: 1824, from Modern Latin transferred use of classical Latin curriculum "a running, course, career" (also "a fast chariot, racing car"), from currere (see current (adj.)). Used in English as a Latin word since 1630s at Scottish universities.
entries.etymologyZh: 1824 年, 源自 现代 拉丁语 transferred use of classical 拉丁语 curriculum "a running, course, career" (also "a fast chariot, racing car"), 源自 currere （参见 current （形）). Used in English 作为 拉丁语 word 自 1630 年代 at 苏格兰语 universities.

example.en: The school updated its curriculum to include more science courses.

entries.etymology: late Old English curs "a prayer that evil or harm befall one," of uncertain origin, perhaps from Old French curuz "anger," or Latin cursus "course." Connection with cross is unlikely. No similar word exists in Germanic, Romance, or Celtic. Curses as a histrionic exclamation is from 1885. The curse "menstruation" is from 1930. Curse of Scotland, the 9 of diamonds in cards, is attested from 1791, but the origin is obscure.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 curs "a prayer that evil or harm befall one," 来源存疑, 或源自 古法语 curuz "anger," or 拉丁语 cursus "course." Connection with cross is unlikely. No similar word exists in 日耳曼语, Romance，或Celtic. Curses 作为 histrionic exclamation 始于 1885 年. The curse "menstruation" 始于 1930 年. Curse of Scotland, the 9 of diamonds in cards, 见于 1791 年, but the origin is obscure.

example.en: He let out a loud curse when he stubbed his toe.
example.zh: 他踢到脚趾时大声咒骂了一句。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French cortine "curtain, tapestry, drape, blanket," from Late Latin cortina "curtain," but in classical Latin "round vessel, cauldron," from Latin cortem (older cohortem) "enclosure, courtyard" (see cohort). The confusion apparently begins in using cortina as a loan-translation for Greek aulaia ("curtain") in the Vulgate (to render Hebrew yeriah in Exodus xxvi:1, etc.) because the Greek word was connected to aule "court," perhaps because the "door" of a Greek house that led out to the courtyard was a hung cloth. The figurative sense in curtain call is from 1884. Curtains "the end" is 1912, originally from stage plays. An Old English word for "curtain" was fleonet "fly-net."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 cortine "curtain, tapestry, drape, blanket," 源自 晚期拉丁语 cortina "curtain," but in classical 拉丁语 "round vessel, cauldron," 源自 拉丁语 cortem (older cohortem) "enclosure, courtyard" （参见 cohort). The confusion 似乎 begins in using cortina 作为 loan-translation for 希腊语 aulaia ("curtain") in the Vulgate (to render 希伯来语 yeriah in Exodus xxvi:1, etc.) because the 希腊语 word was connected to aule "court," 或许 because the "door" of a 希腊语 house that led out to the courtyard was a hung cloth. The figurative sense in curtain call 始于 1884 年. Curtains "the end" is 1912 年, 原义为 源自 stage plays. An 古英语 word for "curtain" was fleonet "fly-net."

example.en: She pulled back the curtain to let the morning sunlight in.
example.zh: 她拉开窗帘，让清晨的阳光照进来。

entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (implied in curved), 源自 拉丁语 curvus "crooked, curved, bent," and curvare "to bend," both 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *(s)ker- (2) "to turn, bend" （参见 ring （名）).

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French coissin "seat cushion" (12c., Modern French coussin), probably a variant of Vulgar Latin *coxinum, from Latin coxa "hip, thigh," or from Latin culcita "mattress." Someone has counted more than 400 spellings of the plural of this word in Middle English wills and inventories. Also from the French word are Italian cuscino, Spanish cojin.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 coissin "seat cushion" (12 世纪, 现代法语 coussin), 可能 a 为 … 的变体 通俗拉丁语 *coxinum, 源自 拉丁语 coxa "hip, thigh," or 源自 拉丁语 culcita "mattress." Someone has counted more than 400 spellings of the 为 … 的复数 this word in 中古英语 wills and inventories. Also 源自 法语 word are 意大利语 cuscino, 西班牙语 cojin.

definitionLines: n. 习惯，风俗，惯例； （pL.）海关
entries.definition: n. 习惯，风俗，惯例； （pL.）海关
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "habitual practice," from Old French costume "custom, habit, practice; clothes, dress" (12c., Modern French coutume), from Vulgar Latin *consuetumen, from Latin consuetudinem (nominative consuetudo) "habit, usage, way, practice, tradition, familiarity," from consuetus, past participle of consuescere "accustom," from com-, intensive prefix (see com-), + suescere "become used to, accustom oneself," related to sui, genitive of suus "oneself," from PIE *swe- "oneself" (see idiom). Replaced Old English þeaw. Sense of a "regular" toll or tax on goods is early 14c. The native word here is toll.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "habitual practice," 源自 古法语 costume "custom, habit, practice; clothes, dress" (12 世纪, 现代法语 coutume), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *consuetumen, 源自 拉丁语 consuetudinem (主格 consuetudo) "habit, usage, way, practice, tradition, familiarity," 源自 consuetus, 为 … 的过去分词 consuescere "accustom," 源自 com-, intensive prefix （参见 com-), + suescere "become used to, accustom oneself," related to sui, 属格 of suus "oneself," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *swe- "oneself" （参见 idiom). Replaced 古英语 þeaw. 义为 a "regular" toll or tax on goods is 14 世纪初 The 本族 word here is toll.

example.en: It is an ancient custom in this village to light lanterns on the first day of the new year.
example.zh: 在新年第一天点灯笼是这个村子的古老习俗。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "customs official;" later "buyer" (early 15c.), from Anglo-French custumer, from Medieval Latin custumarius, from Latin consuetudinarius (see custom (n.)). More generalized meaning "a person with whom one has dealings" emerged 1540s; that of "a person to deal with" (usually with an adjective, tough, etc.) is by 1580s. In Shakespeare, the word also can mean "prostitute."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "customs official;" later "buyer" (15 世纪初), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 custumer, 源自 中古拉丁语 custumarius, 源自 拉丁语 consuetudinarius （参见 custom （名）). More generalized 意为 "a person with whom one has dealings" emerged 1540 年代; that of "a person to deal with" (通常 with an 形容词, tough, etc.) is by 1580 年代. example.en: The store manager made sure every customer received polite and helpful service.
example.zh: 店长确保每位顾客都得到礼貌且周到的服务。

entries.definition: n. /v. 切，剪，割，削；删，缩减 n. 伤口
entries.etymology: late 13c., possibly Scandinavian, from North Germanic *kut- (source also of Swedish dialectal kuta "to cut," kuta "knife," Old Norse kuti "knife"), or from Old French couteau "knife." Replaced Old English ceorfan (see carve (v.)), sniþan, and scieran (see shear). Meaning "to be absent without excuse" is British university slang from 1794. To cut a pack of cards is from 1590s. Related: Cutting.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, possibly Scandinavian, 源自 North 日耳曼语 *kut- (source also of Swedish 方言 kuta "to cut," kuta "knife," 古北欧语 kuti "knife")，或源自 古法语 couteau "knife." Replaced 古英语 ceorfan （参见 carve （动）), sniþan, and scieran （参见 shear). 义为 "to be absent without excuse" is British university 俚语 自 1794 年起. To cut a pack of cards 始于 1590 年代. 同源词：Cutting.

example.en: The ministry announced plans to cut funding for rural infrastructure by half.
example.zh: 该部委宣布计划将农村基础设施拨款削减一半。

entries.definition: a. 每日的，日常的 ad.每日，天天 n. 日报

entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "building for making butter and cheese; dairy farm," formed with 盎格鲁-法语 -erie affixed to 中古英语 daie (in daie maid "dairymaid"), 源自 古英语 dæge "kneader of bread, housekeeper, female servant" （参见 dey (n.1)). The purely 本族 word was dey-house.

example.zh: 工程师们在河流上修建了一座大坝以控制洪水。

entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 damage (12 世纪, 现代法语 dommage) "loss caused by injury," 源自 dam "damage," 源自 拉丁语 damnum "loss, hurt, damage" （参见 damn).
