entries.etymology:
late 13c., "to condemn," from Old French damner "damn, condemn; convict, blame; injure," derivative of Latin damnare "to adjudge guilty; to doom; to condemn, blame, reject," from noun damnum "damage, hurt, harm; loss, injury; a fine, penalty," from Proto-Italic *dapno-, possibly from an ancient religious term from PIE *dap- "to apportion in exchange" [see Watkins]. The Latin word evolved a legal meaning of "pronounce judgment upon." Theological sense is first recorded early 14c.; the optative expletive use likely is as old.

Damn and its derivatives generally were avoided in print from 18c. to c. 1930s (the famous line in the film version of "Gone with the Wind" was a breakthrough and required much effort by the studio). The noun is recorded from 1610s; to be not worth a damn is from 1817. The adjective is 1775, short for damned; Damn Yankee, characteristic Southern U.S. term for "Northerner," is attested from 1812. Related: Damning.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "to condemn," 源自 古法语 damner "damn, condemn; convict, blame; injure," 为 … 的派生形式 拉丁语 damnare "to adjudge guilty; to doom; to condemn, blame, reject," 源自 名词 damnum "damage, hurt, harm; loss, injury; a fine, penalty," 源自 Proto-Italic *dapno-, possibly 源自 an ancient religious term 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dap- "to apportion in exchange" [参见 Watkins]. The 拉丁语 word evolved a legal 意为 of "pronounce judgment upon." Theological sense is 首见于 14 世纪初; the optative expletive use likely is as old. Damn and its derivatives generally were avoided in print 源自 18 世纪 to c. 1930 年代 (the famous line in the film version of "Gone with the Wind" was a breakthrough and required much effort by the studio). The 名词 见于 1610 年代; to be not worth a damn 始于 1817 年. The 形容词 is 1775 年, short for damned; Damn Yankee, characteristic Southern U.S. term for "Northerner," 见于 1812 年. 同源词：Damning.

entries.etymology: early 14c., "noxious vapor," perhaps in Old English but there is no record of it. If not, probably from Middle Low German damp; ultimately in either case from Proto-Germanic *dampaz (source also of Old High German damph, German Dampf "vapor;" Old Norse dampi "dust"). Sense of "moisture, humidity" is first certainly attested 1706.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "noxious vapor," 或许 in 古英语 but there is no record of it. If not, 可能 源自 Middle Low 德语 damp; ultimately in either case 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dampaz (source also of 古高地德语 damph, 德语 Dampf "vapor;" 古北欧语 dampi "dust"). 义为 "moisture, humidity" is first certainly attested 1706 年.

example.en: The basement walls felt damp after several days of heavy rain.
example.zh: 连续几天大雨之后，地下室的墙壁摸起来湿漉漉的。

entries.definition: vi.跳舞 n. 舞蹈，舞会
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French dancier (12c., Modern French danser), which is of unknown origin, perhaps from Low Frankish *dintjan and akin to Old Frisian dintje "tremble, quiver." A word of uncertain origin but which, through French influence in arts and society, has become the primary word for this activity from Spain to Russia (Italian danzare, Spanish danzar, Rumanian dansa, Swedish dansa, German tanzen).

Replaced Old English sealtian, itself a borrowing from Latin saltare "to dance," frequentative of salire "to leap" (see salient (adj.); "dance" words frequently are derived from words meaning "jump, leap"). Related: Danced; dancing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 dancier (12 世纪, 现代法语 danser), which is 来源不详, 或源自 Low Frankish *dintjan and akin to 古弗里西语 dintje "tremble, quiver." A word 来源存疑 but which, through 法语 influence in arts and society, has become the primary word for this activity 源自 Spain to Russia (意大利语 danzare, 西班牙语 danzar, Rumanian dansa, Swedish dansa, 德语 tanzen). Replaced 古英语 sealtian, itself a borrowing 源自 拉丁语 saltare "to dance," 为 … 的反复体 salire "to leap" （参见 salient （形）; "dance" words frequently are derived 源自 words 意为 "jump, leap"). 同源词：Danced; dancing.

example.en: The children were excited to dance at the school concert.
example.zh: 孩子们很兴奋，要在学校音乐会上跳舞。

entries.etymology:
mid-13c., "power of a lord or master, jurisdiction," from Anglo-French daunger, Old French dangier "power, power to harm, mastery, authority, control" (12c., Modern French danger), alteration (due to assoc. with damnum) of dongier, from Vulgar Latin *dominarium "power of a lord," from Latin dominus "lord, master" (see domain).

Modern sense of "risk, peril" (from being in the control of someone or something else) evolved first in French and was in English late 14c. Replaced Old English pleoh; in early Middle English this sense is found in peril.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "power of a lord or master, jurisdiction," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 daunger, 古法语 dangier "power, power to harm, mastery, authority, control" (12 世纪, 现代法语 danger), alteration (due to assoc. with damnum) of dongier, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *dominarium "power of a lord," 源自 拉丁语 dominus "lord, master" （参见 domain). 现代 语义 "risk, peril" (源自 being in the control of someone or something else) evolved first in 法语 and was in English 14 世纪晚期 Replaced 古英语 pleoh; in early 中古英语 this sense is found in peril.

example.en: Swimmers must not enter the river due to the danger of being swept away by strong currents.
example.zh: 游泳者不得进入该河流，因为有被强劲水流冲走的危险。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., "difficult, arrogant, severe" (the opposite of affable), from Anglo-French dangerous, Old French dangeros (12c., Modern French dangereux), from danger (see danger).

In Chaucer, it means "hard to please, reluctant to give;" sense of "full of danger, risky" is from late 15c. Other words used in this sense included dangersome (1560s), dangerful (1540s). Related: Dangerously.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "difficult, arrogant, severe" (the opposite of affable), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 dangerous, 古法语 dangeros (12 世纪, 现代法语 dangereux), 源自 danger （参见 danger). In Chaucer, it means "hard to please, reluctant to give;" 语义 "full of danger, risky" 始于 15 世纪晚期 Other words used in this sense included dangersome (1560 年代), dangerful (1540 年代). 同源词：Dangerously.

example.en: It is dangerous to drive at high speed in heavy rain.
example.zh: 在大雨中高速驾驶是危险的。

entries.definition: vt. 敢，竟敢；向……挑战 auz. v. 敢，胆敢
entries.etymology:
from first and third person singular of Old English durran "to brave danger, dare; venture, presume," from Proto-Germanic *ders- (source also of Old Norse dearr, Old High German giturran, Gothic gadaursan), from PIE *dhers- "to dare, be courageous" (source also of Sanskrit dadharsha "to be bold;" Old Persian darš- "to dare;" Greek thrasys "bold;" Old Church Slavonic druzate "to be bold, dare;" Lithuanian dristi "to dare," drasus "courageous").

An Old English irregular preterite-present verb: darr, dearst, dear were first, second and third person singular present indicative; mostly regularized 16c., though past tense dorste survived as durst, but is now dying, persisting mainly in northern English dialect. Meaning "to challenge or defy (someone)" is first recorded 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: 源自 first and third person singular of 古英语 durran "to brave danger, dare; venture, presume," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ders- (source also of 古北欧语 dearr, 古高地德语 giturran, Gothic gadaursan), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhers- "to dare, be courageous" (source also of 梵语 dadharsha "to be bold;" Old 波斯语 darš- "to dare;" 希腊语 thrasys "bold;" Old Church Slavonic druzate "to be bold, dare;" Lithuanian dristi "to dare," drasus "courageous"). An 古英语 irregular preterite-present 动词: darr, dearst, dear were first, second and third person singular present indicative; mostly regularized 16 世纪, though past tense dorste survived as durst, but is 现在 dying, persisting mainly in northern English dialect. 义为 "to challenge or defy (someone)" is 首见于 1570 年代.

example.en: Nobody dared challenge the director's decision openly at the meeting.
example.zh: 会议上没有人敢公开挑战总监的决定。

entries.definition: a.暗，黑暗；深色，黑色 n. 黑暗，暗处
entries.etymology: Old English deorc "dark, obscure, gloomy; sad, cheerless; sinister, wicked," from Proto-Germanic *derkaz (source also of Old High German tarchanjan "to hide, conceal"). "Absence of light" especially at night is the original meaning. Application to colors is 16c. Theater slang for "closed" is from 1916.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deorc "dark, obscure, gloomy; sad, cheerless; sinister, wicked," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *derkaz (source also of 古高地德语 tarchanjan "to hide, conceal"). "Absence of light" 尤指 at night is the original 意为. Application to colors is 16 世纪 Theater 俚语 for "closed" 始于 1916 年.

example.en: The hikers were lost and had to camp in the dark without any flashlight.
example.zh: 徒步者迷路了，不得不在黑暗中没有手电筒地露营。

entries.etymology: Old English deorling "darling, favorite minion," double diminutive of deor "dear" (see dear (adj.)). The vowel shift from -e- to -a- (16c.) is usual for -er- followed by a consonant. "It is better to be An olde mans derlyng, than a yong mans werlyng" (1562).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deorling "darling, favorite minion," double 为 … 的指小形式 deor "dear" （参见 dear （形）). The vowel shift 源自 -e- to -a- (16 世纪) is usual for -er- followed by a consonant. "It is better to be An olde mans derlyng, than a yong mans werlyng" (1562 年).

entries.definition: ^．破折号；冲撞 vt. 使……破灭；猛撞；泼溅 vi. 猛冲；撞击
entries.etymology: c. 1300, probably from a Scandinavian source (compare Swedish daska, Danish daske "to beat, strike"), somehow imitative. The oldest sense is that in dash to pieces and dashed hopes. Intransitive meaning "move quickly" appeared c. 1300, that of "to write hurriedly" is 1726.  Related: Dashed; dashing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 可能 源自 a Scandinavian source (对比 Swedish daska, Danish daske "to beat, strike"), somehow imitative. The oldest sense is that in dash to pieces and dashed hopes. Intransitive 意为 "move quickly" appeared 约 1300 年, that of "to write hurriedly" is 1726 年. 同源词：Dashed; dashing.

example.en: The bad news dashed all hopes of a peaceful settlement.
example.zh: 这个坏消息使所有和平解决的希望都破灭了。

entries.etymology: 1640s, plural of datum, from Latin datum "(thing) given," neuter past participle of dare "to give" (see date (n.1)). Meaning "transmittable and storable computer information" first recorded 1946. Data processing is from 1954.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 为 … 的复数 datum, 源自 拉丁语 datum "(thing) given," neuter 为 … 的过去分词 dare "to give" （参见 date (n.1)). 义为 "transmittable and storable computer information" 首见于 1946 年. Data processing 始于 1954 年.

example.en: The researchers collected data from over a thousand participants.
example.zh: 研究人员从一千多名参与者那里收集了数据。

entries.etymology: "to act as a banker," 1727, from bank (n.1). As "to deposit in a bank" from 1833. Figurative sense of "to rely on" (i.e. "to put money on") is from 1884, U.S. colloquial. Meaning "to ascend," as of an incline, is from 1892. In aeronautics, from 1911. Related: Banked; banking.
entries.etymologyZh: "to act as a banker," 1727 年, 源自 bank (n.1). As "to deposit in a bank" 自 1833 年起. Figurative 语义 "to rely on" (i.e. "to put money on") 始于 1884 年, U.S. 口语. 义为 "to ascend," as of an incline, 始于 1892 年. In aeronautics, 自 1911 年起. 同源词：Banked; banking.

example.en: All patient records are stored in a secure database.
example.zh: 所有患者记录都存储在一个安全的数据库中。

entries.definition: n. 日期，年代；约会 v. 注日期；约会

example.en: Please write the date of birth on the application form.
example.zh: 请在申请表上填写出生日期。

entries.etymology: Old English dohtor, from Proto-Germanic *dokhter, earlier *dhukter (source also of Old Saxon dohtar, Old Norse dottir, Old Frisian and Dutch dochter, German Tochter, Gothic dauhtar), from PIE *dhugheter (source also of Sanskrit duhitar-, Avestan dugeda-, Armenian dustr, Old Church Slavonic dušti, Lithuanian dukte, Greek thygater). The common Indo-European word, lost in Celtic and Latin (Latin filia "daughter" is fem. of filius "son"). The modern spelling evolved 16c. in southern England. Daughter-in-law is attested from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dohtor, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dokhter, earlier *dhukter (source also of 古撒克逊语 dohtar, 古北欧语 dottir, 古弗里西语 and 荷兰语 dochter, 德语 Tochter, Gothic dauhtar), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhugheter (source also of 梵语 duhitar-, Avestan dugeda-, Armenian dustr, Old Church Slavonic dušti, Lithuanian dukte, 希腊语 thygater). The common Indo-European word, lost in Celtic and 拉丁语 (拉丁语 filia "daughter" is fem. of filius "son"). The modern spelling evolved 16 世纪 in southern England. Daughter-in-law 见于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: His daughter just graduated from medical school last month.
example.zh: 他的女儿上个月刚从医学院毕业。

entries.definition: n. 黎明，曙光 vi. 破晓；开始发展
entries.etymology: c. 1200, dauen, "to dawn, grow light," shortened or back-formed from dauinge, dauing "period between darkness and sunrise," (c. 1200), from Old English dagung, from dagian "to become day," from Proto-Germanic *dagaz "day" (source also of German tagen "to dawn;" see day (n.)). Probably influenced by Scandinavian cognates (Danish dagning, Old Norse dagan "a dawning"). Related: Dawned; dawning.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, dauen, "to dawn, grow light," shortened or back-formed 源自 dauinge, dauing "period between darkness and sunrise," (约 1200 年), 源自 古英语 dagung, 源自 dagian "to become day," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dagaz "day" (source also of 德语 tagen "to dawn;" 参见 day （名）). Probably influenced by Scandinavian cognates (Danish dagning, 古北欧语 dagan "a dawning"). 同源词：Dawned; dawning.

example.en: They set out at dawn to avoid the midday heat.
example.zh: 他们在黎明时出发以避开正午的炎热。

entries.etymology:
Old English dæg "day," also "lifetime," from Proto-Germanic *dagaz "day" (source also of Old Saxon, Middle Dutch, Dutch dag, Old Frisian dei, Old High German tag, German Tag, Old Norse dagr, Gothic dags), according to Watkins, from PIE *agh- (2) "a day" considered as a span of time. He adds that the Germanic initial d- is "of obscure origin."

Not considered to be related to Latin dies (see diurnal), but rather to Sanskrit dah "to burn," Lithuanian dagas "hot season," Old Prussian dagis "summer." Meaning originally, in English, "the daylight hours;" expanded to mean "the 24-hour period" in late Anglo-Saxon times. The day formerly began at sunset, hence Old English Wodnesniht was what we would call "Tuesday night." Names of the weekdays were not regularly capitalized in English until 17c. Day off first recorded 1883; day-tripper first recorded 1897. The days in nowadays, etc. is a relic of the Old English and Middle English use of the adverbial genitive.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dæg "day," also "lifetime," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dagaz "day" (source also of 古撒克逊语, Middle 荷兰语, 荷兰语 dag, 古弗里西语 dei, 古高地德语 tag, 德语 Tag, 古北欧语 dagr, Gothic dags), according to Watkins, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *agh- (2) "a day" considered 作为 span of time. He adds that the 日耳曼语 initial d- is "of obscure origin." Not considered to be related to 拉丁语 dies （参见 diurnal), but rather to 梵语 dah "to burn," Lithuanian dagas "hot season," Old Prussian dagis "summer." 义为 原义为, in English, "the daylight hours;" expanded to mean "the 24-hour period" in late 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 times. The day formerly began at sunset, hence 古英语 Wodnesniht was what we would call "Tuesday night." Names of the weekdays were not regularly capitalized in English until 17 世纪 Day off 首见于 1883 年; day-tripper 首见于 1897 年. The days in nowadays, etc. is a relic of the 古英语 and 中古英语 use of the adverbial 属格.

example.en: She spends most of her working day in a small home office, rarely going out.
example.zh: 她大部分工作时间都待在一间小小的家庭办公室里，很少外出。

entries.etymology: c. 1300 (as two words from mid-12c., daies liht), from day + light (n.); its figurative sense of "clearly visible open space between two things" (1820) has been used in references to boats in a race, U.S. football running backs avoiding opposing tackles, a rider and a saddle, and the rim of a glass and the surface of the liquor. The (living) daylights that you beat out of someone were originally slang for "the eyes" (1752), extended figuratively to the vital senses.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年 (as two words 源自 12 世纪中期, daies liht), 源自 day + light （名）; its figurative 语义 "clearly visible open space between two things" (1820 年) has been used in references to boats in a race, U.S. football running backs avoiding opposing tackles, a rider and a saddle, and the rim of a glass and the surface of the liquor. The (living) daylights that you beat out of someone were 原义为 俚语 for "the eyes" (1752 年), extended figuratively to the vital senses.

example.en: The hikers set out at daylight to avoid the midday heat.
example.zh: 徒步者们在天亮时出发，以避开正午的高温。

entries.definition: vt. 使…•…目眩；使……眼花 vi. 炫耀；眼花缭乱
entries.etymology: late 15c., frequentative of Middle English dasen (see daze (v.)). Originally intransitive; the transitive sense is from 1530s. Related: Dazzled; dazzling.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 为 … 的反复体 中古英语 dasen （参见 daze （动）). Originally intransitive; the transitive sense 始于 1530 年代. 同源词：Dazzled; dazzling.

entries.etymology:
Old English dead "dead," also "torpid, dull;" of water, "still, standing," from Proto-Germanic *daudaz (source also of Old Saxon dod, Danish død, Swedish död, Old Frisian dad, Middle Dutch doot, Dutch dood, Old High German tot, German tot, Old Norse dauðr, Gothic dauþs "dead"), from PIE *dhou-toz-, from root *dheu- (3) "to die" (see die (v.)).

Meaning "insensible" is first attested early 13c. Of places, "inactive, dull," from 1580s. Used from 16c. in adjectival sense of "utter, absolute, quite" (as in dead drunk, first attested 1590s; dead heat, 1796). As an adverb, from late 14c. Dead on is 1889, from marksmanship. Dead duck is from 1844. Dead letter is from 1703, used of laws lacking force as well as uncollected mail. Phrase in the dead of the night first recorded 1540s. Dead soldier "emptied liquor bottle" is from 1913 in that form; the image is older.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dead "dead," also "torpid, dull;" of water, "still, standing," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *daudaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 dod, Danish død, Swedish död, 古弗里西语 dad, Middle 荷兰语 doot, 荷兰语 dood, 古高地德语 tot, 德语 tot, 古北欧语 dauðr, Gothic dauþs "dead"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhou-toz-, 源自 root *dheu- (3) "to die" （参见 die （动）). 义为 "insensible" is 最早见于 13 世纪初 Of places, "inactive, dull," 源自 1580 年代. Used 源自 16 世纪 in adjectival 语义 "utter, absolute, quite" (as in dead drunk, 最早见于 1590 年代; dead heat, 1796 年). 作为 副词, 源自 14 世纪晚期 Dead on is 1889 年, 源自 marksmanship. Dead duck 始于 1844 年. Dead letter 始于 1703 年, used of laws lacking force as well as uncollected mail. Phrase in the dead of the night 首见于 1540 年代. Dead soldier "emptied liquor bottle" 始于 1913 年 in that form; the image is older.

example.en: The flowers in the vase had been dead for days, with brown, brittle petals.
example.zh: 花瓶里的花已经死了好几天，花瓣枯褐易碎。

definitionLines: n. 最后期限，截止交稿日期
entries.definition: n. 最后期限，截止交稿日期
entries.etymology: "time limit," 1920, American English newspaper jargon, from dead (adj.) + line (n.). Perhaps influenced by earlier use (1864) to mean the "do-not-cross" line in Civil War prisons, which figured in the Wirz trial.
entries.etymologyZh: "time limit," 1920 年, American English newspaper jargon, 源自 dead （形） + line （名）. Perhaps influenced by earlier use (1864 年) to mean the "do-not-cross" line in Civil War prisons, which figured in the Wirz trial.

example.en: The team worked through the night to meet the project deadline.
example.zh: 团队彻夜工作以赶上项目的截止日期。

definitionLines: a. 致命的，致死的；极有害的
entries.definition: a. 致命的，致死的；极有害的
entries.etymology: Old English deadlic "mortal, subject to death," also "causing death;" see dead + -ly (1). Meaning "having the capacity to kill" is from late 14c. (Old English words for this included deaðbærlic, deaðberende).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deadlic "mortal, subject to death," also "causing death;" 参见 dead + -ly (1). 义为 "having the capacity to kill" 始于 14 世纪晚期 (古英语 words for this included deaðbærlic, deaðberende).

example.en: The climbers faced deadly conditions on the mountain that night.
example.zh: 那天夜里，登山者在山上面临致命的险境。

entries.definition: v.（with） 处理，应付 vt. 给予 n. 交易，买卖；契约
entries.etymology: Old English dælan "to divide, distribute, separate, share, bestow, dispense," from the source of deal (n.). Meaning "to distribute cards before a game" is from 1520s. To deal with "handle" is attested from mid-15c. Related: Dealt; dealing.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dælan "to divide, distribute, separate, share, bestow, dispense," 源自 source of deal （名）. 义为 "to distribute cards before a game" 始于 1520 年代. To deal with "handle" 见于 15 世纪中期 同源词：Dealt; dealing.

example.en: The manager knows how to deal with rude and demanding customers professionally.
example.zh: 这位经理懂得如何专业地应对粗鲁而苛求的顾客。

definitionLines: n. 院长；系主任；教务长
entries.definition: n. 院长；系主任；教务长
entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French deien (12c., Modern French doyen), from Late Latin decanus "head of a group of 10 monks in a monastery," from earlier secular meaning "commander of 10 soldiers" (which was extended to civil administrators in the late empire), from Greek dekanos, from deka "ten" (see ten). Replaced Old English teoðingealdor. College sense is from 1570s (in Latin from late 13c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 deien (12 世纪, 现代法语 doyen), 源自 晚期拉丁语 decanus "head of a group of 10 monks in a monastery," 源自 earlier secular 意为 "commander of 10 soldiers" (which was extended to civil administrators in the late empire), 源自 希腊语 dekanos, 源自 deka "ten" （参见 ten). Replaced 古英语 teoðingealdor. College sense 始于 1570 年代 (in 拉丁语 源自 13 世纪晚期).

definitionLines: a. 贵的；亲爱的，可爱的
entries.definition: a. 贵的；亲爱的，可爱的 int.啊，哎呀
entries.etymology: Old English deore "precious, valuable, costly, loved, beloved," from Proto-Germanic *deurjaz (source also of Old Saxon diuri, Old Norse dyrr, Old Frisian diore, Middle Dutch dure, Dutch duur, Old High German tiuri, German teuer), further etymology unknown. Used interjectorily since 1690s. As a polite introductory word to letters, it is attested from mid-15c. As a noun, from late 14c., perhaps short for dear one, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deore "precious, valuable, costly, loved, beloved," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *deurjaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 diuri, 古北欧语 dyrr, 古弗里西语 diore, Middle 荷兰语 dure, 荷兰语 duur, 古高地德语 tiuri, 德语 teuer), further etymology unknown. Used interjectorily 自 1690 年代. 作为 polite introductory word to letters, it 见于 15 世纪中期 作名词时, 源自 14 世纪晚期, 或许 short for dear one, etc.

entries.etymology:
Old English deað "death, dying, cause of death," in plura, "ghosts," from Proto-Germanic *dauthuz (source also of Old Saxon doth, Old Frisian dath, Dutch dood, Old High German tod, German Tod, Old Norse dauði, Danish død, Swedish död, Gothic dauþus "death"), from verbal stem *dheu- (3) "to die" (see die (v.)) + *-thuz suffix indicating "act, process, condition."

Death's-head, a symbol of mortality, is from 1590s. Death row first recorded 1940s. Death knell is attested from 1814; death penalty from 1875; death rate from 1859. Slang be death on "be very good at" is from 1839. Death wish first recorded 1896. The death-watch beetle (1660s) inhabits houses, makes a ticking noise like a watch, and was superstitiously supposed to portend death.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deað "death, dying, cause of death," in plura, "ghosts," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dauthuz (source also of 古撒克逊语 doth, 古弗里西语 dath, 荷兰语 dood, 古高地德语 tod, 德语 Tod, 古北欧语 dauði, Danish død, Swedish död, Gothic dauþus "death"), 源自 verbal stem *dheu- (3) "to die" （参见 die （动）) + *-thuz suffix indicating "act, process, condition." Death's-head, a symbol of mortality, 始于 1590 年代. Death row 首见于 1940 年代. Death knell 见于 1814 年; death penalty 自 1875 年起; death rate 自 1859 年起. Slang be death on "be very good at" 始于 1839 年. Death wish 首见于 1896 年. The death-watch beetle (1660 年代) inhabits houses, makes a ticking noise like a watch, and was superstitiously supposed to portend death.

example.en: The death of the beloved professor in a road accident shocked the entire campus.
example.zh: 这位深受爱戴的教授在一场交通事故中不幸罹难，震惊了整个校园。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to quarrel, dispute," also "discuss, deliberate upon the pros and cons of," from Old French debatre (13c., Modern French débattre), originally "to fight," from de- "down, completely" (see de-) + batre "to beat" (see battery). Related: Debated; debating.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to quarrel, dispute," also "discuss, deliberate upon the pros and cons of," 源自 古法语 debatre (13 世纪, 现代法语 débattre), 原义为 "to fight," 源自 de- "down, completely" （参见 de-) + batre "to beat" （参见 battery). 同源词：Debated; debating.

example.en: The politicians held a live debate on national television over tax reform.
example.zh: 政客们就税制改革在国家电视台进行了一场现场辩论。

entries.etymology: late 13c., dette, from Old French dete, from Latin debitum "thing owed," neuter past participle of debere "to owe," originally, "keep something away from someone," from de- "away" (see de-) + habere "to have" (see habit (n.)). Restored spelling after c. 1400. In Middle English, debt of the body (mid-14c.) was "that which spouses owe to each other, sexual intercourse."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, dette, 源自 古法语 dete, 源自 拉丁语 debitum "thing owed," neuter 为 … 的过去分词 debere "to owe," 原义为, "keep something away from someone," 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + habere "to have" （参见 habit （名）). Restored spelling after 约 1400 年. In 中古英语, debt of the body (14 世纪中期) was "that which spouses owe to each other, sexual intercourse."

example.en: After years of careful saving, she finally paid off all her credit card debt.
example.zh: 经过多年认真储蓄，她终于还清了所有信用卡债务。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "ten parts" (of anything; originally in reference to the books of Livy), from Middle French décade (14c.), from Late Latin decadem (nominative decas), from Greek dekas (genitive dekados) "group of ten," from deka "ten" (see ten). Meaning "period of ten years" is 1590s in English.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "ten parts" (of anything; 原义为 in reference to the books of Livy), 源自 中古法语 décade (14 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 decadem (主格 decas), 源自 希腊语 dekas (属格 dekados) "group of ten," 源自 deka "ten" （参见 ten). 义为 "period of ten years" is 1590 年代 in English.

example.en: The city has changed dramatically over the past decade.
example.zh: 这座城市在过去十年里发生了巨大变化。

entries.etymology: late 15c., "to decrease," from Anglo-French decair, Old North French decair (Old French decheoir, 12c., Modern French déchoir) "to fall, set (of the sun), weaken, decline, decay," from Vulgar Latin *decadere "to fall off," from de- (see de-) + Latin cadere "to fall" (see case (n.1)). Meaning "decline, deteriorate" is c. 1500; that of "to decompose, rot" is from 1570s. Related: Decayed; decaying.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "to decrease," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 decair, Old North 法语 decair (古法语 decheoir, 12 世纪, 现代法语 déchoir) "to fall, set (of the sun), weaken, decline, decay," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *decadere "to fall off," 源自 de- （参见 de-) + 拉丁语 cadere "to fall" （参见 case (n.1)). 义为 "decline, deteriorate" is 约 1500 年; that of "to decompose, rot" 始于 1570 年代. 同源词：Decayed; decaying.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French decevoir "to deceive" (12c., Modern French décevoir), from Latin decipere "to ensnare, take in, beguile, cheat," from de- "from" or pejorative + capere "to take" (see capable). Related: Deceived; deceiver; deceiving.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 decevoir "to deceive" (12 世纪, 现代法语 décevoir), 源自 拉丁语 decipere "to ensnare, take in, beguile, cheat," 源自 de- "from" or pejorative + capere "to take" （参见 capable). 同源词：Deceived; deceiver; deceiving.

entries.etymology:
c. 1000, from Old French decembre, from Latin December, from decem "ten" (see ten); tenth month of the old Roman calendar, which began with March.

The -ber in four Latin month names is probably from -bris, an adjectival suffix. Tucker thinks that the first five months were named for their positions in the agricultural cycle, and "after the gathering in of the crops, the months were merely numbered."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1000 年, 源自 古法语 decembre, 源自 拉丁语 December, 源自 decem "ten" （参见 ten); tenth month of the old Roman calendar, which began with March. The -ber in four 拉丁语 month names is 可能 源自 -bris, an adjectival suffix. Tucker thinks that the first five months were named for their positions in the agricultural cycle, and "after the gathering in of the crops, the months were merely numbered."

definitionLines: a.体面的，像样的，过得去的； 正派的，得体的
entries.definition: a.体面的，像样的，过得去的； 正派的，得体的
entries.etymology: 1530s, "proper to one's station or rank," also "tasteful," from Middle French décent, or directly from Latin decentem (nominative decens) "becoming, seemly, fitting, proper," present participle of decere "to be fitting or suitable," from PIE *deke-, from root *dek- "to take, accept, to receive, greet, be suitable" (source also of Greek dokein "to appear, seem, think," dekhesthai "to accept;" Sanskrit daśasyati "shows honor, is gracious," dacati "makes offerings, bestows;" Latin docere "to teach," decus "grace, ornament"). Meaning "kind, pleasant" is from 1902. Are you decent? (1949) was originally backstage theater jargon for "are you dressed."
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "proper to one's station or rank," also "tasteful," 源自 中古法语 décent，或直接源自 拉丁语 decentem (主格 decens) "becoming, seemly, fitting, proper," 为 … 的现在分词 decere "to be fitting or suitable," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *deke-, 源自 root *dek- "to take, accept, to receive, greet, be suitable" (source also of 希腊语 dokein "to appear, seem, think," dekhesthai "to accept;" 梵语 daśasyati "shows honor, is gracious," dacati "makes offerings, bestows;" 拉丁语 docere "to teach," decus "grace, ornament"). 义为 "kind, pleasant" 始于 1902 年. Are you decent? (1949 年) was 原义为 backstage theater jargon for "are you dressed."

example.en: He finally found a decent job that paid enough to cover his rent.
example.zh: 他终于找到了一份能够支付房租的体面工作。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French déception (13c., decepcion) or directly from Late Latin deceptionem (nominative deceptio) "a deceiving," from Latin decept-, past participle stem of decipere (see deceive).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 déception (13 世纪, decepcion) or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 deceptionem (主格 deceptio) "a deceiving," 源自 拉丁语 decept-, past participle stem of decipere （参见 deceive).

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to settle a dispute," from Old French decider, from Latin decidere "to decide, determine," literally "to cut off," from de- "off" (see de-) + caedere "to cut" (see -cide). For Latin vowel change, see acquisition. Sense is of resolving difficulties "at a stroke." Meaning "to make up one's mind" is attested from 1830. Related: Decided; deciding.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to settle a dispute," 源自 古法语 decider, 源自 拉丁语 decidere "to decide, determine," 字面义为 "to cut off," 源自 de- "off" （参见 de-) + caedere "to cut" （参见 -cide). For 拉丁语 vowel change, 参见 acquisition. Sense is of resolving difficulties "at a stroke." 义为 "to make up one's mind" 见于 1830 年. 同源词：Decided; deciding.

example.en: The committee had to decide whether to approve the new budget.
example.zh: 委员会必须决定是否批准新预算。

entries.definition: a. 小数的；十进位的 n. 小数
entries.etymology: c. 1600, from Medeival Latin decimalis "of tithes or tenths," from Latin decimus "tenth," from decem "ten" (see ten). Applied to Arabic notation before modern sense of "decimal fractions" emerged. As a noun from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 Medeival 拉丁语 decimalis "of tithes or tenths," 源自 拉丁语 decimus "tenth," 源自 decem "ten" （参见 ten). Applied to 阿拉伯语 notation before modern 语义 "decimal fractions" emerged. 作名词时 源自 1640 年代.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French décision (14c.), from Latin decisionem (nominative decisio) "a decision, settlement, agreement," noun of action from past participle stem of decidere (see decide). Decision making (adjective, also decision-making) is recorded from 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 décision (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 decisionem (主格 decisio) "a decision, settlement, agreement," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of decidere （参见 decide). Decision making (形容词, also decision-making) 见于 1953 年.

example.en: After careful thought, she made the decision to resign.
example.zh: 经过深思熟虑，她做出了辞职的决定。

entries.etymology: 1610s, from Medieval Latin decisivus, from Latin decis-, past participle stem of decidere (see decide). Related: Decisively; decisiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 decisivus, 源自 拉丁语 decis-, past participle stem of decidere （参见 decide). 同源词：Decisively; decisiveness.

entries.etymology:
"covering over part of a ship," mid-15c., perhaps a shortening of Middle Low German verdeck (or a related North Sea Germanic word), a nautical word, from ver- "fore" + decken "to cover, put under roof," from Proto-Germanic *thakjan (related to thatch, q.v.).

Sense extended early in English from "covering" to "platform of a ship." "Pack of cards" is 1590s, perhaps because they were stacked like decks of a ship. Deck chair (1884) so called because they were used on ocean liners. Tape deck (1949) is in reference to the flat surface of old reel-to-reel tape recorders.
entries.etymologyZh: "covering over part of a ship," 15 世纪中期, 或许 a shortening of Middle Low 德语 verdeck (or a related North Sea 日耳曼语 word), a nautical word, 源自 ver- "fore" + decken "to cover, put under roof," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *thakjan (related to thatch, q.v.). Sense extended early in English 源自 "covering" to "platform of a ship." "Pack of cards" is 1590 年代, 或许 because they were stacked like decks of a ship. Deck chair (1884 年) so called because they were used on ocean liners. Tape deck (1949 年) is in reference to the flat surface of old reel-to-reel tape recorders.

example.en: Passengers gathered on the deck to watch the sunset over the sea.
example.zh: 乘客们聚集在甲板上观看海上的日落。

definitionLines: n. 宣布，宣告；声明；申报
entries.definition: n. 宣布，宣告；声明；申报
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "action of stating," from Old French declaration, from Latin declarationem (nominative declaratio), noun of action from past participle stem of declarare (see declare). Meaning "proclamation, public statement" is from 1650s. Declaration of independence is recorded from 1776 (the one by the British American colonies seems to be the first so called; though the phrase is not in the document itself, it was titled that from the first in the press).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "action of stating," 源自 古法语 declaration, 源自 拉丁语 declarationem (主格 declaratio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of declarare （参见 declare). 义为 "proclamation, public statement" 始于 1650 年代. Declaration of independence 见于 1776 年 (the one by the British American colonies seems to be the first so called; though the phrase is not in the document itself, it was titled that 源自 first in the press).

example.en: The government issued a formal declaration of war against the neighboring country.
example.zh: 政府正式宣布对邻国宣战。

definitionLines: vt. 断言，宣称；宣布，宣告，声 明；申报
entries.definition: vt. 断言，宣称；宣布，宣告，声 明；申报
entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French declarer "explain, elucidate," or directly from Latin declarare "make clear, reveal, disclose, announce," from de- intensive prefix (see de-) + clarare "clarify," from clarus "clear" (see clear (adj.)). Related: Declared; declaring.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 declarer "explain, elucidate," or 直接源自 拉丁语 declarare "make clear, reveal, disclose, announce," 源自 de- intensive prefix （参见 de-) + clarare "clarify," 源自 clarus "clear" （参见 clear （形）). 同源词：Declared; declaring.

example.en: The government officially declare a state of emergency following the floods.
example.zh: 洪灾过后，政府正式宣布进入紧急状态。

definitionLines: vi. 减少，下降；衰落；婉言拒绝
entries.definition: vi. 减少，下降；衰落；婉言拒绝
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to turn aside, deviate," from Old French decliner "to sink, decline, degenerate, turn aside," from Latin declinare "to lower; avoid, deviate; bend from, inflect," from de- "from" (see de-) + clinare "to bend," from PIE *klei-n-, suffixed form of *klei- "to lean" (see lean (v.)). Sense has been altered since c. 1400 by interpretation of de- as "downward." Meaning "not to consent, politely refuse," is from 1630s. Related: Declined; declining.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to turn aside, deviate," 源自 古法语 decliner "to sink, decline, degenerate, turn aside," 源自 拉丁语 declinare "to lower; avoid, deviate; bend from, inflect," 源自 de- "from" （参见 de-) + clinare "to bend," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *klei-n-, suffixed form of *klei- "to lean" （参见 lean （动）). Sense has been altered 自 约 1400 年 by interpretation of de- as "downward." 义为 "not to consent, politely refuse," 始于 1630 年代. 同源词：Declined; declining.

example.en: Sales began to decline sharply after the new competitor entered the market.
example.zh: 新竞争者进入市场后，销售额开始急剧下降。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin decoratus, past participle of decorare "to decorate, adorn, embellish, beautify," from decus (genitive decoris) "an ornament," from PIE root *dek- "to receive, be suitable" (see decent). Related: Decorated; decorating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 decoratus, 为 … 的过去分词 decorare "to decorate, adorn, embellish, beautify," 源自 decus (属格 decoris) "an ornament," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dek- "to receive, be suitable" （参见 decent). 同源词：Decorated; decorating.

example.en: They spent the afternoon decorate the living room with lights and garlands.
example.zh: 他们花了整个下午用灯饰和花环装饰客厅。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Anglo-French decreiss-, present participle stem of decreistre, Old French descroistre (12c., Modern French décroître), from Latin decrescere "to grow less, diminish," from de- "away from" (see de-) + crescere "to grow" (see crescent). Related: Decreased; decreasing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 decreiss-, present participle stem of decreistre, 古法语 descroistre (12 世纪, 现代法语 décroître), 源自 拉丁语 decrescere "to grow less, diminish," 源自 de- "away from" （参见 de-) + crescere "to grow" （参见 crescent). 同源词：Decreased; decreasing.

example.en: Sales showed a sharp decrease in the third quarter of last year.
example.zh: 去年第三季度销售额出现了急剧下滑。

entries.definition: n. 法令；判决 vt. 颁布；命令；判决 vi. 发布命令；注定
entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French decre, variant of decret (12c., Modern French décret), from Latin decretum, neuter of decretus, past participle of decernere "to decree, decide, pronounce a decision," from de- (see de-) + cernere "to separate" (see crisis).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 decre, 为 … 的变体 decret (12 世纪, 现代法语 décret), 源自 拉丁语 decretum, neuter of decretus, 为 … 的过去分词 decernere "to decree, decide, pronounce a decision," 源自 de- （参见 de-) + cernere "to separate" （参见 crisis).

entries.etymology: early 15c. (of churches), from Latin dedicatus, past participle of dedicare "consecrate, proclaim, affirm, set apart," from de- "away" (see de-) + dicare "proclaim" (see diction). Dedicated "devoted to one's aims or vocation" is first attested 1944.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (of churches), 源自 拉丁语 dedicatus, 为 … 的过去分词 dedicare "consecrate, proclaim, affirm, set apart," 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + dicare "proclaim" （参见 diction). Dedicated "devoted to one's aims or vocation" is 最早见于 1944 年.

example.en: She chose to dedicate her entire career to cancer research.
example.zh: 她选择将整个职业生涯献给癌症研究。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin deducere "lead down, derive" (in Medieval Latin, "infer logically"), from de- "down" (see de-) + ducere "to lead" (see duke (n.)). Originally literal; sense of "draw a conclusion from something already known" is first recorded 1520s, from Medieval Latin. Related: Deduced; deducing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 deducere "lead down, derive" (in 中古拉丁语, "infer logically"), 源自 de- "down" （参见 de-) + ducere "to lead" （参见 duke （名）). Originally literal; 语义 "draw a conclusion from something already known" is 首见于 1520 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语. 同源词：Deduced; deducing.

definitionLines: n. 行为，行动；功绩，事迹
entries.definition: n. 行为，行动；功绩，事迹
entries.etymology: Old English dæd "a doing, act, action, transaction, event," from Proto-Germanic *dædis (source also of Old Saxon dad, Old Norse dað, Old Frisian dede, Middle Dutch daet, Dutch daad, Old High German tat, German Tat "deed," Gothic gadeþs "a putting, placing"), from PIE *dhetis (source also of Lithuanian detis "load, burden," Greek thesis "a placing, setting"), from *dhe- "place, put" (see do). Sense of "written legal document" is early 14c. As a verb, 1806, American English Related: Deeded; deeding.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dæd "a doing, act, action, transaction, event," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dædis (source also of 古撒克逊语 dad, 古北欧语 dað, 古弗里西语 dede, Middle 荷兰语 daet, 荷兰语 daad, 古高地德语 tat, 德语 Tat "deed," Gothic gadeþs "a putting, placing"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhetis (source also of Lithuanian detis "load, burden," 希腊语 thesis "a placing, setting"), 源自 *dhe- "place, put" （参见 do). 义为 "written legal document" is 14 世纪初 作动词时, 1806 年, American English 同源词：Deeded; deeding.

example.en: He was honored for his heroic deed during the rescue mission.
example.zh: 他因在救援行动中的英勇事迹而受到表彰。

definitionLines: a. 深的，深刻的；深奥的；深 切的
entries.definition: a. 深的，深刻的；深奥的；深 切的 ad. 深深地
entries.etymology:
Old English deop "profound, awful, mysterious; serious, solemn; deepness, depth," deope (adv.), from Proto-Germanic *deupaz (source also of Old Saxon diop, Old Frisian diap, Dutch diep, Old High German tiof, German tief, Old Norse djupr, Danish dyb, Swedish djup, Gothic diups "deep"), from PIE *dheub- "deep, hollow" (source also of Lithuanian dubus "deep, hollow, Old Church Slavonic duno "bottom, foundation," Welsh dwfn "deep," Old Irish domun "world," via sense development from "bottom" to "foundation" to "earth" to "world").

Figurative senses were in Old English; extended 16c. to color, sound. Deep pocket "wealth" is from 1951. To go off the deep end "lose control of oneself" is slang first recorded 1921, probably in reference to the deep end of a swimming pool, where a person on the surface can no longer touch bottom. When 3-D films seemed destined to be the next wave and the biggest thing to hit cinema since talkies, they were known as deepies (1953).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deop "profound, awful, mysterious; serious, solemn; deepness, depth," deope （副）, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *deupaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 diop, 古弗里西语 diap, 荷兰语 diep, 古高地德语 tiof, 德语 tief, 古北欧语 djupr, Danish dyb, Swedish djup, Gothic diups "deep"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dheub- "deep, hollow" (source also of Lithuanian dubus "deep, hollow, Old Church Slavonic duno "bottom, foundation," Welsh dwfn "deep," Old Irish domun "world," via sense development from "bottom" to "foundation" to "earth" to "world"). Figurative senses were in Old English; extended 16c. to color, sound. Deep pocket "wealth" is from 1951. To go off the deep end "lose control of oneself" is 俚语 首见于 1921 年, 可能 in reference to the deep end of a swimming pool, where a person on the surface can no longer touch bottom. When 3-D films seemed destined to be the next wave and the biggest thing to hit cinema 自 talkies, they were known as deepies (1953 年).

example.en: She has a deep understanding of medieval history that few scholars can match.
example.zh: 她对中世纪历史的理解之深刻，鲜有学者能与之媲美。

entries.etymology:
Old English deor "animal, beast," from Proto-Germanic *deuzam, the general Germanic word for "animal" (as opposed to man), but often restricted to "wild animal" (source also of Old Frisian diar, Dutch dier, Old Norse dyr, Old High German tior, German Tier "animal," Gothic dius "wild animal," also see reindeer), from PIE *dheusom "creature that breathes," from root *dheu- (1) "cloud, breath" (source also of Lithuanian dusti "gasp," dvesti "gasp, perish;" Old Church Slavonic dychati "breathe").

For prehistoric sense development, compare Latin animal from anima "breath"). Sense specialization to a specific animal began in Old English (usual Old English for what we now call a deer was heorot; see hart), common by 15c., now complete. Probably via hunting, deer being the favorite animal of the chase (compare Sanskrit mrga- "wild animal," used especially for "deer"). Deer-lick is first attested 1778, in an American context.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deor "animal, beast," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *deuzam, the general 日耳曼语 word for "animal" (as opposed to man), but 常 restricted to "wild animal" (source also of 古弗里西语 diar, 荷兰语 dier, 古北欧语 dyr, 古高地德语 tior, 德语 Tier "animal," Gothic dius "wild animal," also 参见 reindeer), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dheusom "creature that breathes," 源自 root *dheu- (1) "cloud, breath" (source also of Lithuanian dusti "gasp," dvesti "gasp, perish;" Old Church Slavonic dychati "breathe"). For prehistoric sense development, 对比 拉丁语 animal 源自 anima "breath"). Sense specialization to a specific animal began in 古英语 (usual 古英语 for what we 现在 call a deer was heorot; 参见 hart), common by 15 世纪, 现在 complete. Probably 经由 hunting, deer being the favorite animal of the chase (对比 梵语 mrga- "wild animal," used 尤指 for "deer"). Deer-lick is 最早见于 1778 年, in an American context.

example.en: The wildlife photographer spotted a herd of deer crossing the frozen river.
example.zh: 野生动物摄影师发现一群鹿正在穿越冰封的河流。

entries.definition: n. 违约；缺乏；缺席；系统默 认值 vi. 拖欠；不到场；不履行
entries.etymology: early 13c., "offense, crime, sin," later (late 13c.) "failure, failure to act," from Old French defaute (12c.) "fault, defect, failure, culpability, lack, privation," from Vulgar Latin *defallita "a deficiency or failure," past participle of *defallere, from Latin de- "away" (see de-) + fallere "to deceive, to cheat; to put wrong, to lead astray, cause to be mistaken; to escape notice of, be concealed from" (see fail (v.)). The financial sense is first recorded 1858; the computing sense is from 1966.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "offense, crime, sin," later (13 世纪晚期) "failure, failure to act," 源自 古法语 defaute (12 世纪) "fault, defect, failure, culpability, lack, privation," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *defallita "a deficiency or failure," 为 … 的过去分词 *defallere, 源自 拉丁语 de- "away" （参见 de-) + fallere "to deceive, to cheat; to put wrong, to lead astray, cause to be mistaken; to escape notice of, be concealed from" （参见 fail （动）). The financial sense is 首见于 1858 年; the computing sense 始于 1966 年.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French defect and directly from Latin defectus "failure, revolt, falling away," noun use of past participle of deficere "to fail, desert" (see deficient).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 defect and 直接源自 拉丁语 defectus "failure, revolt, falling away," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 deficere "to fail, desert" （参见 deficient).

example.en: The recall was issued due to a manufacturing defect in the brake system.
example.zh: 由于制动系统存在制造缺陷，该产品被召回。

entries.etymology: see defense.
entries.etymologyZh: 参见 defense.

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from Old French defendre (12c.) "defend, resist," and directly from Latin defendere "ward off, protect, guard, allege in defense," from de- "from, away" (see de-) + -fendere "to strike, push," from PIE root *gwhen- "to strike, kill" (see bane). In the Mercian hymns, Latin defendet is glossed by Old English gescildeð. Related: Defended; defending.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 defendre (12 世纪) "defend, resist," and 直接源自 拉丁语 defendere "ward off, protect, guard, allege in defense," 源自 de- "from, away" （参见 de-) + -fendere "to strike, push," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gwhen- "to strike, kill" （参见 bane). In the Mercian hymns, 拉丁语 defendet is glossed by 古英语 gescildeð. 同源词：Defended; defending.

example.en: The lawyer worked hard to defend her client against the serious charges.
example.zh: 律师努力为其当事人辩护，抵抗严重指控。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, in the legal sense, from French défendant, present participle of défendre (see defend). Earliest use in English was as a present participle adjective meaning "defending" (c. 1300).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, in the legal sense, 源自 法语 défendant, 为 … 的现在分词 défendre （参见 defend). Earliest use in English was 作为 present participle 形容词 意为 "defending" (约 1300 年).

example.en: The defendant pleaded not guilty to all charges in the trial.
example.zh: 被告在庭审中对所有指控表示无罪。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French desfiance "challenge, declaration of war," from desfiant, present participle of desfier (see defy).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 desfiance "challenge, declaration of war," 源自 desfiant, 为 … 的现在分词 desfier （参见 defy).

entries.etymology: 1630s, from deficience (mid-15c.) + -cy; or from Late Latin deficientia, from deficientem (see deficient).

example.en: A deficiency of vitamin D can lead to weak bones and fatigue.
example.zh: 维生素D缺乏会导致骨骼脆弱和疲劳。

entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 deficientem (主格 deficiens), 为 … 的现在分词 deficere "to desert, revolt, fail," 源自 de- "down, away" （参见 de-) + facere "to do, perform" （参见 factitious).

entries.etymologyZh: 1782 年, 源自 法语 déficit (17 世纪晚期), 源自 拉丁语 deficit "it is wanting," an introductory word in clauses of inventory, third person singular present indicative of deficere "to be deficient" （参见 deficient).

example.en: The government announced a budget deficit of ten billion dollars.
example.zh: 政府宣布了一百亿美元的财政赤字。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to specify; to end," from Old French defenir, definir "to finish, conclude, come to an end; bring to an end; define, determine with precision," and directly from Latin definire "to limit, determine, explain," from de- "completely" (see de-) + finire "to bound, limit," from finis "boundary, end" (see finish (v.)). Related: Defined; defining.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to specify; to end," 源自 古法语 defenir, definir "to finish, conclude, come to an end; bring to an end; define, determine with precision," and 直接源自 拉丁语 definire "to limit, determine, explain," 源自 de- "completely" （参见 de-) + finire "to bound, limit," 源自 finis "boundary, end" （参见 finish （动）). 同源词：Defined; defining.

example.en: The textbook fails to clearly define the term 「inflation」 for beginners.
example.zh: 这本教科书未能为初学者清楚地定义「通货膨胀」这一术语。

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Latin definitus "defined, bounded, limited," past participle of definire (see define). Definite means "defined, clear, precise, unmistakable;" definitive means "having the character of finality."
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 拉丁语 definitus "defined, bounded, limited," 为 … 的过去分词 definire （参见 define). Definite means "defined, clear, precise, unmistakable;" definitive means "having the character of finality."

entries.etymology: 1580s, from definite + -ly (2). As a colloquial emphatic word, attested by 1931.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 definite + -ly (2). 作为 口语 emphatic word, attested 截至 1931 年.

example.en: I will definitely attend the conference next week.
example.zh: 我下周肯定会参加这次会议。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "decision, setting of boundaries," from Old French definicion, from Latin definitionem (nominative definitio), noun of action from past participle stem of definire (see define).

In logic, meaning "act of stating what something means" is from 1640s; meaning "a statement of the essential nature of something" is from late 14c.; the special focus on words developed after c. 1550. Meaning "degree of distinctness of the details in a picture" is from 1889.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "decision, setting of boundaries," 源自 古法语 definicion, 源自 拉丁语 definitionem (主格 definitio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of definire （参见 define). In logic, 意为 "act of stating what something means" 始于 1640 年代; 意为 "a statement of the essential nature of something" 始于 14 世纪晚期; the special focus on words developed after 约 1550 年. 义为 "degree of distinctness of the details in a picture" 始于 1889 年.

example.en: The definition of success varies greatly from person to person.
example.zh: 对于成功的定义因人而异。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to renounce one's allegiance;" mid-14c., "to challenge, defy," from Old French defier, desfier "to challenge, defy, provoke; renounce (a belief), repudiate (a vow, etc.)," from Vulgar Latin *disfidare "renounce one's faith," from Latin dis- "away" (see dis-) + fidus "faithful," from the same root as fides "faith" (see faith).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to renounce one's allegiance;" 14 世纪中期, "to challenge, defy," 源自 古法语 defier, desfier "to challenge, defy, provoke; renounce (a belief), repudiate (a vow, etc.)," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *disfidare "renounce one's faith," 源自 拉丁语 dis- "away" （参见 dis-) + fidus "faithful," 源自 same root as fides "faith" （参见 faith).

example.en: The young artist chose to defy convention by painting in a completely new style.
example.zh: 这位年轻艺术家选择以全新风格作画来挑战传统。

entries.definition: vt.使退化；恶化 vi. 堕落；退化 a. 退化的；堕落的
entries.etymology: late 15c., from Latin degeneratus, past participle of degenerare "to be inferior to one's ancestors, to become unlike one's race or kind, fall from ancestral quality," used of physical as well as moral qualities, from phrase de genere, from de + genus (genitive generis) "birth, descent" (see genus). The noun is from 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 degeneratus, 为 … 的过去分词 degenerare "to be inferior to one's ancestors, to become unlike one's race or kind, fall from ancestral quality," used of physical as well as moral qualities, 源自 phrase de genere, 源自 de + genus (属格 generis) "birth, descent" （参见 genus). The 名词 始于 1550 年代.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French degrader (12c.) "degrade, deprive (of office, rank, etc.)," from des- "down" (see dis-) + Latin gradus "step" (see grade (n.)). Related: Degraded; degrading.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 degrader (12 世纪) "degrade, deprive (of office, rank, etc.)," 源自 des- "down" （参见 dis-) + 拉丁语 gradus "step" （参见 grade （名）). 同源词：Degraded; degrading.

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Old French degré (12c.) "a step (of a stair), pace, degree (of relationship), academic degree; rank, status, position," said to be from Vulgar Latin *degradus "a step," from Late Latin degredare, from Latin de- "down" (see de-) + gradus "step" (see grade (n.)).

Most modern senses date from Middle English, from notion of a hierarchy of steps. Meaning "a grade of crime" is 1670s; that of "a unit of temperature" is from 1727. The division of the circle into 360 degrees was known in Babylon and Egypt. It is perhaps from the daily motion of the sun through the zodiac in the course of a year.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 degré (12 世纪) "a step (of a stair), pace, degree (of relationship), academic degree; rank, status, position," said to be 源自 通俗拉丁语 *degradus "a step," 源自 晚期拉丁语 degredare, 源自 拉丁语 de- "down" （参见 de-) + gradus "step" （参见 grade （名）). Most modern senses date 源自 中古英语, 源自 概念 a hierarchy of steps. 义为 "a grade of crime" is 1670 年代; that of "a unit of temperature" 始于 1727 年. The division of the circle into 360 degrees was known in Babylon and Egypt. It is 或源自 the daily motion of the sun through the zodiac in the course of a year.

example.en: Doctors measure the degree of pain using a ten-point scale.
example.zh: 医生使用十分制量表来衡量疼痛程度。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French delaiier, from de- "away, from" (see de-) + laier "leave, let," probably a variant of Old French laissier, from Latin laxare "slacken, undo" (see lax). Related: Delayed; delaying.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 delaiier, 源自 de- "away, from" （参见 de-) + laier "leave, let," 可能 a 为 … 的变体 古法语 laissier, 源自 拉丁语 laxare "slacken, undo" （参见 lax). 同源词：Delayed; delaying.

example.en: Bad weather caused a two-hour delay in the flight schedule.
example.zh: 恶劣天气导致航班计划延误两小时。

entries.etymology: late 15c., from Old French delegat or directly from Latin delegatus, past participle of delegare "to send as a representative," from de- "from, away" (see de-) + legare "send with a commission" (see legate).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 delegat or 直接源自 拉丁语 delegatus, 为 … 的过去分词 delegare "to send as a representative," 源自 de- "from, away" （参见 de-) + legare "send with a commission" （参见 legate).

example.en: Each country sent a delegate to represent its interests at the summit.
example.zh: 每个国家派遣了一名代表在峰会上代表本国利益。

entries.etymology: late 15c., "destroy, eradicate," from Latin deletus, past participle of delere "destroy, blot out, efface," from delevi, originally perfective tense of delinere "to daub, erase by smudging" (as of the wax on a writing table), from de- "from, away" (see de-) + linere "to smear, wipe" (see lime (n.1)). In English, specifically of written matter, from c. 1600. Related: Deleted; deleting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "destroy, eradicate," 源自 拉丁语 deletus, 为 … 的过去分词 delere "destroy, blot out, efface," 源自 delevi, 原义为 perfective tense of delinere "to daub, erase by smudging" (as of the wax on a writing table), 源自 de- "from, away" （参见 de-) + linere "to smear, wipe" （参见 lime (n.1)). In English, specifically of written matter, 源自 约 1600 年. 同源词：Deleted; deleting.

definitionLines: a. 故意的；从容的；深思熟虑的
entries.definition: a. 故意的；从容的；深思熟虑的 vt. 仔细考虑；商议
entries.etymology: early 15c., "done with careful consideration," from Latin deliberatus "resolved upon, determined," past participle of deliberare (see deliberation). Meaning "slow, consciously unhurried" is attested by 1590s. Related: Deliberately.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "done with careful consideration," 源自 拉丁语 deliberatus "resolved upon, determined," 为 … 的过去分词 deliberare （参见 deliberation). 义为 "slow, consciously unhurried" is attested by 1590 年代. 同源词：Deliberately.

example.en: The manager made a deliberate effort to include all team members.
example.zh: 这位经理刻意努力地把所有团队成员都纳入其中。

entries.definition: n.细软，娇嫩；精致；脆弱；微妙
entries.etymology: late 14c., "delightfulness; fastidiousness; quality of being addicted to sensuous pleasure," from delicate + -cy. Meaning "fineness, softness, tender loveliness" is from 1580s; that of "weakness of constitution" is from 1630s. Meaning "fine food, a dainty viand" is from early 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "delightfulness; fastidiousness; quality of being addicted to sensuous pleasure," 源自 delicate + -cy. 义为 "fineness, softness, tender loveliness" 始于 1580 年代; that of "weakness of constitution" 始于 1630 年代. 义为 "fine food, a dainty viand" 始于 15 世纪初

entries.etymology: late 14c., "self-indulgent, loving ease; delightful; sensitive, easily hurt; feeble," from Latin delicatus "alluring, delightful, dainty," also "addicted to pleasure, luxurious, effeminate;" which is of uncertain origin; related by folk etymology (and perhaps genuinely) to deliciae "a pet," and delicere "to allure, entice" (see delicious). Meaning "easily broken" is recorded from 1560s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "self-indulgent, loving ease; delightful; sensitive, easily hurt; feeble," 源自 拉丁语 delicatus "alluring, delightful, dainty," also "addicted to pleasure, luxurious, effeminate;" which is 来源存疑; related by folk etymology (and 或许 genuinely) to deliciae "a pet," and delicere "to allure, entice" （参见 delicious). 义为 "easily broken" 见于 1560 年代.

example.en: The craftsman spent hours on the delicate carvings of the wooden box.
example.zh: 工匠在木盒精美的雕刻上花费了数小时。

entries.etymology: c. 1300 (implied in deliciously), from Old French delicios (Modern French délicieux), from Late Latin deliciosus "delicious, delicate," from Latin delicia (plural deliciae) "a delight, allurement, charm," from delicere "to allure, entice," from de- "away" (see de-) + lacere "lure, deceive" (related to laqueus "noose, snare;" see lace). As a name of a type of apple, attested from 1903, first grown by Jesse Hiatt of Iowa, U.S.A. Colloquial shortening delish is attested from 1920.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年 (implied in deliciously), 源自 古法语 delicios (现代法语 délicieux), 源自 晚期拉丁语 deliciosus "delicious, delicate," 源自 拉丁语 delicia (plural deliciae) "a delight, allurement, charm," 源自 delicere "to allure, entice," 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + lacere "lure, deceive" (related to laqueus "noose, snare;" 参见 lace). 作为 name of a type of apple, attested 自 1903 年起, first grown by Jesse Hiatt of Iowa, U.S.A. Colloquial shortening delish 见于 1920 年.

example.en: The pasta smelled so delicious that everyone rushed to the table.
example.zh: 这道意面闻起来太香了，大家都急忙跑向餐桌。

entries.definition: n. 快乐，高兴 vt. 使高兴，使欣喜
entries.etymology: c. 1200, delit, from Old French delit "pleasure, delight, sexual desire," from delitier "please greatly, charm," from Latin delectare "to allure, delight, charm, please," frequentative of delicere "entice" (see delicious). Spelled delite until 16c. when it changed under influence of light, flight, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, delit, 源自 古法语 delit "pleasure, delight, sexual desire," 源自 delitier "please greatly, charm," 源自 拉丁语 delectare "to allure, delight, charm, please," 为 … 的反复体 delicere "entice" （参见 delicious). Spelled delite until 16 世纪 when it changed under influence of light, flight, etc.

example.en: The children's laughter filled the room with delight.
example.zh: 孩子们的笑声让整个房间充满了欢乐。

definitionLines: vt. 交付，递送；释放，解救；发 表，表达
entries.definition: vt. 交付，递送；释放，解救；发 表，表达
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "save, rescue, set free, liberate," from Old French delivrer "to set free; remove; save, preserve; hand over (goods)," also used of childbirth, from Late Latin deliberare, from de- "away" (see de-) + Latin liberare "to free" (see liberal (adj.)).

Childbirth sense in English, "to bring (a woman) to childbirth," is from c. 1300. Sense of "hand over, give, give up, yield" is c. 1300. in English, which brings it in opposition to its root. Meaning "project, throw" is 1590s. Related: Delivered; delivering.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "save, rescue, set free, liberate," 源自 古法语 delivrer "to set free; remove; save, preserve; hand over (goods)," also used of childbirth, 源自 晚期拉丁语 deliberare, 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + 拉丁语 liberare "to free" （参见 liberal （形）). Childbirth sense in English, "to bring (a woman) to childbirth," 始于 约 1300 年. 义为 "hand over, give, give up, yield" is 约 1300 年. in English, which brings it in opposition to its root. 义为 "project, throw" is 1590 年代. 同源词：Delivered; delivering.

example.en: The courier promised to deliver the package before noon the next day.
example.zh: 快递员承诺在第二天中午之前将包裹送达。

definitionLines: n. 传电；传送，交付；分娩
entries.definition: n. 传电；传送，交付；分娩
entries.etymology: early 15c., "action of handing over to another," from Anglo-French delivrée, noun use of fem. past participle of Old French délivrer (see deliver). Childbirth sense is attested from 1570s. Of speech, from 1580s. Of a blow, throw of a ball, etc., from 1702.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "action of handing over to another," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 delivrée, 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 古法语 délivrer （参见 deliver). Childbirth sense 见于 1570 年代. Of speech, 源自 1580 年代. Of a blow, throw of a ball, etc., 自 1702 年起.

example.en: The package arrived via express delivery within two days.
example.zh: 包裹通过快递在两天内送达。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "ask, make inquiry," from Old French demander (12c.) "to request; to demand," from Latin demandare "entrust, charge with a commission" (in Vulgar Latin, "to ask, request, demand"), from de- "completely" (see de-) + mandare "to order" (see mandate). Meaning "to ask for as a right" is early 15c., from Anglo-French legal use. Related: Demanded; demanding.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "ask, make inquiry," 源自 古法语 demander (12 世纪) "to request; to demand," 源自 拉丁语 demandare "entrust, charge with a commission" (in 通俗拉丁语, "to ask, request, demand"), 源自 de- "completely" （参见 de-) + mandare "to order" （参见 mandate). 义为 "to ask for as a right" is 15 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 legal use. 同源词：Demanded; demanding.

example.en: There is a growing demand for skilled engineers in the technology sector.
example.zh: 科技行业对技术工程师的需求日益增长。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "asking, questioning," present participle adjective from demand (v.). Meaning "insistent" is by late 19c. Related: Demandingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "asking, questioning," present participle 形容词 源自 demand （动）. 义为 "insistent" is by 19 世纪晚期 同源词：Demandingly.

definitionLines: n. 民主，民主制；民主国家
entries.definition: n. 民主，民主制；民主国家
entries.etymology: 1570s, from Middle French démocratie (14c.), from Medieval Latin democratia (13c.), from Greek demokratia "popular government," from demos "common people," originally "district" (see demotic), + kratos "rule, strength" (see -cracy).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 源自 中古法语 démocratie (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 democratia (13 世纪), 源自 希腊语 demokratia "popular government," 源自 demos "common people," 原义为 "district" （参见 demotic), + kratos "rule, strength" （参见 -cracy).

example.en: Free elections are considered a cornerstone of democracy in modern societies.
example.zh: 自由选举被认为是现代社会民主制度的基石。

definitionLines: a. 民主的，有民主精神/作风的
entries.definition: a. 民主的，有民主精神/作风的
entries.etymology:
c. 1600, from French démocratique, from Medieval Latin democraticus, from Greek demokratikos "of or for democracy; favoring democracy," from demokratia "popular government" (see democracy). Earlier was democratian (1570s).

As a political faction name, from 1790 in reference to France. U.S. political usage (with a capital D) attested from c. 1800. The party originally was the Anti-Federal party, then the Democratic-Republican (Democratic for short). It formed among those opposed to extensive powers for the U.S. federal government. The name of the party was not formally shortened to Democratic until 1829. Democratic socialism is attested from 1849.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 démocratique, 源自 中古拉丁语 democraticus, 源自 希腊语 demokratikos "of or for democracy; favoring democracy," 源自 demokratia "popular government" （参见 democracy). Earlier was democratian (1570 年代). 作为 political faction name, 自 1790 年起 in reference to France. U.S. political usage (with a capital D) attested 源自 约 1800 年. The party 原义为 was the Anti-Federal party, 之后 the Democratic-Republican (Democratic for short). It formed among those opposed to extensive powers for the U.S. federal government. The name of the party was not formally shortened to Democratic until 1829 年. Democratic socialism 见于 1849 年.

example.en: The country held its first democratic election after years of authoritarian rule.
example.zh: 这个国家在多年威权统治后举行了首次民主选举。

entries.definition: vt. 表明；论证；演示 vi. 示威
entries.etymology: 1550s, "to point out," from Latin demonstratus, past participle of demonstrare "to indicate, describe" (see demonstration). Meaning "to point out by argument or deduction" is from 1570s. Related: Demonstrated; demonstrating. Latin also had commonstrare "point out, reveal," praemonstrare "show beforehand, foretell."
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "to point out," 源自 拉丁语 demonstratus, 为 … 的过去分词 demonstrare "to indicate, describe" （参见 demonstration). 义为 "to point out by argument or deduction" 始于 1570 年代. 同源词：Demonstrated; demonstrating. 拉丁语 also had commonstrare "point out, reveal," praemonstrare "show beforehand, foretell."

example.en: The scientist used charts to demonstrate how the virus mutates across generations.
example.zh: 这位科学家用图表演示了病毒如何跨代变异。

definitionLines: n. 否认；拒绝；节制；背弃
entries.definition: n. 否认；拒绝；节制；背弃
entries.etymology: 1520s; see deny + -al (2). Replaced earlier denyance (mid-15c.). Meaning "unconscious suppression of painful or embarrassing feelings" first attested 1914 in A.A. Brill's translation of Freud's "Psychopathology of Everyday Life"; phrase in denial popularized 1980s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代; 参见 deny + -al (2). Replaced earlier denyance (15 世纪中期). 义为 "unconscious suppression of painful or embarrassing feelings" 最早见于 1914 年 in A.A. Brill's translation of Freud's "Psychopathology of Everyday Life"; phrase in denial popularized 1980 年代.

example.en: His flat denial of the allegations surprised everyone in court.
example.zh: 他对指控的断然否认令法庭上所有人感到惊讶。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Middle French dénoter (14c.), from Latin denotare "denote, mark out," from de- "completely" (see de-) + notare "to mark" (see note (v.)). Related: Denoted; denoting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 dénoter (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 denotare "denote, mark out," 源自 de- "completely" （参见 de-) + notare "to mark" （参见 note （动）). 同源词：Denoted; denoting.

definitionLines: vt. 谴责；告发；公然抨击
entries.definition: vt. 谴责；告发；公然抨击
entries.etymology: early 14c., "announce," from Old French denoncier (12c., Modern French dénoncer), from Latin denuntiare "to announce, proclaim; denounce, menace; command, order," from de- "down" + nuntiare "proclaim, announce," from nuntius "messenger" (see nuncio). Negative sense in English via meaning "to declare or proclaim" something as cursed, excommunicated, forgiven, removed from office. Related: Denounced; denouncing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "announce," 源自 古法语 denoncier (12 世纪, 现代法语 dénoncer), 源自 拉丁语 denuntiare "to announce, proclaim; denounce, menace; command, order," 源自 de- "down" + nuntiare "proclaim, announce," 源自 nuntius "messenger" （参见 nuncio). Negative sense in English 经由 意为 "to declare or proclaim" something as cursed, excommunicated, forgiven, removed 源自 office. 同源词：Denounced; denouncing.

example.en: Human rights groups denounce the government for its treatment of refugees.
example.zh: 人权组织公开谴责该政府对待难民的方式。

definitionLines: a. 密的，稠密的，浓密的
entries.definition: a. 密的，稠密的，浓密的
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French dense and directly from Latin densus "thick, crowded; cloudy," perhaps from PIE root *dens- "dense, thick" (source also of Greek dasus "hairy, shaggy"). Sense of "stupid" is first recorded 1822.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 dense and 直接源自 拉丁语 densus "thick, crowded; cloudy," 或源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dens- "dense, thick" (source also of 希腊语 dasus "hairy, shaggy"). 义为 "stupid" is 首见于 1822 年.

example.en: The city is surrounded by dense forest that blocks sunlight for most of the day.
example.zh: 这座城市被茂密的森林所包围，大部分时间阳光无法照入。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from French densité (16c.), from Old French dempsité (13c.), from Latin densitas "thickness," from densus "thick, dense" (see dense).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 densité (16 世纪), 源自 古法语 dempsité (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 densitas "thickness," 源自 densus "thick, dense" （参见 dense).

example.en: The density of the wood determines whether it sinks or floats in water.
example.zh: 木材的密度决定了它在水中是沉还是浮。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Middle French dental "of teeth" or Medieval Latin dentalis, from Latin dens (genitive dentis) "tooth," from PIE root *dent- (see tooth).
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 dental "of teeth" or 中古拉丁语 dentalis, 源自 拉丁语 dens (属格 dentis) "tooth," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dent- （参见 tooth).

entries.etymology:
1759, from French dentiste, from dent "tooth," from Latin dens (see tooth) + -ist. 
Tooth-drawer is attested from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 1759 年, 源自 法语 dentiste, 源自 dent "tooth," 源自 拉丁语 dens （参见 tooth) + -ist. Tooth-drawer 见于 14 世纪晚期

definitionLines: v. 否定，否认；拒绝，谢绝
entries.definition: v. 否定，否认；拒绝，谢绝
entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French denoiir "deny, repudiate, withhold," from Latin denegare "to deny, reject, refuse" (source of Italian dinegarre, Spanish denegar), from de- "away" (see de-) + negare "refuse, say 'no,' " from Old Latin nec "not," from Italic base *nek- "not," from PIE root *ne- "no, not" (see un-). Related: Denied; denying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 denoiir "deny, repudiate, withhold," 源自 拉丁语 denegare "to deny, reject, refuse" (source of 意大利语 dinegarre, 西班牙语 denegar), 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + negare "refuse, say 'no,' " 源自 Old 拉丁语 nec "not," 源自 Italic base *nek- "not," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ne- "no, not" （参见 un-). 同源词：Denied; denying.

example.en: The website did not deny users access to the report: anyone could download it without signing in.
example.zh: 网站没有拒绝用户访问这份报告，任何人都能在不登录的情况下下载它。

entries.etymology:
mid-13c., "part from each other," from Old French departir (10c.) "to divide, distribute; separate (oneself), depart; die," from Late Latin departire "divide" (transitive), from de- "from" (see de-) + partire "to part, divide," from pars (genitive partis) "a part" (see part (n.)).

As a euphemism for "to die" (to depart this life; compare Old French departir de cest siecle) it is attested from c. 1500, as is the departed for "the dead," singly or collectively. Transitive lingers in some English usages; the wedding service was till death us depart until 1662. Related: Departed; departing.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "part from each other," 源自 古法语 departir (10 世纪) "to divide, distribute; separate (oneself), depart; die," 源自 晚期拉丁语 departire "divide" (transitive), 源自 de- "from" （参见 de-) + partire "to part, divide," 源自 pars (属格 partis) "a part" （参见 part （名）). 作为 euphemism for "to die" (to depart this life; 对比 古法语 departir de cest siecle) it 见于 约 1500 年, as is the departed for "the dead," singly or collectively. Transitive lingers in some English usages; the wedding service was till death us depart until 1662 年. 同源词：Departed; departing.

example.en: The last train will depart from platform three at midnight.
example.zh: 最后一班列车将于午夜从三号站台出发。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "a going away, act of leaving," from Old French departement (12c.) "division, sharing out; divorce, parting," from Late Latin departire (see depart). French department meant "group of people" (as well as "departure"), from which English borrowed the sense of "separate division, separate business assigned to someone in a larger organization" (c. 1735). Meaning "separate division of a government" is from 1769. As an administrative district in France, from 1792.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "a going away, act of leaving," 源自 古法语 departement (12 世纪) "division, sharing out; divorce, parting," 源自 晚期拉丁语 departire （参见 depart). 法语 department meant "group of people" (as well as "departure"), 源自 which English borrowed the 语义 "separate division, separate business assigned to someone in a larger organization" (约 1735 年). 义为 "separate division of a government" 始于 1769 年. 作为 administrative district in France, 自 1792 年起.

example.en: Please send your resume directly to the human resources department.
example.zh: 请将您的简历直接发送至人力资源部门。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Old French deporteure "departure," figuratively, "death," from departir (see depart) + -ure (see -ure).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 deporteure "departure," figuratively, "death," 源自 departir （参见 depart) + -ure （参见 -ure).

example.en: The departure of the last train is scheduled for midnight.
example.zh: 末班列车的出发时间定在午夜。

definitionLines: vi. （on/upon）依靠，依赖；信 任；决定于
entries.definition: vi. （on/upon）依靠，依赖；信 任；决定于
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to be attached to as a condition or cause," a figurative use, from Middle French dependre, literally "to hang from, hang down," from Latin dependere "to hang from, hang down; be dependent on, be derived," from de- "from, down" (see de-) + pendere "to hang, be suspended" (see pendant). Related: Depended; depending.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to be attached to as a condition or cause," a figurative use, 源自 中古法语 dependre, 字面义为 "to hang from, hang down," 源自 拉丁语 dependere "to hang from, hang down; be dependent on, be derived," 源自 de- "from, down" （参见 de-) + pendere "to hang, be suspended" （参见 pendant). 同源词：Depended; depending.

example.en: Whether you pass the exam will depend entirely on how hard you study.
example.zh: 你能否通过考试完全取决于你有多努力学习。

definitionLines: a. （on/upon） 依靠的，依赖的， 从属的
entries.definition: a. （on/upon） 依靠的，依赖的， 从属的
entries.etymology: 15c., variant spelling of dependant, now mostly restricted to adjectival use; see -ance. Dependent variable in mathematics is recorded from 1852.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪, variant spelling of dependant, 现在 mostly restricted to adjectival use; 参见 -ance. Dependent variable in mathematics 见于 1852 年.

example.en: Many rural communities are dependent on agriculture for their income.
example.zh: 许多农村社区依靠农业维持收入。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin depictus, past participle of depingere "to portray, paint, sketch; describe, imagine," from de- "down" (see de-) + pingere "to paint" (see paint (v.)). Related: Depicted; depicting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 depictus, 为 … 的过去分词 depingere "to portray, paint, sketch; describe, imagine," 源自 de- "down" （参见 de-) + pingere "to paint" （参见 paint （动）). 同源词：Depicted; depicting.

example.en: The painting depict a peaceful scene of life in the countryside.
example.zh: 这幅画描绘了一幅乡村生活的宁静场景。

definitionLines: vt. 悲悼；哀叹；谴责；对……深 感遗憾
entries.definition: vt. 悲悼；哀叹；谴责；对……深 感遗憾
entries.etymology: 1550s, "to give up as hopeless," from French déplorer (13c.), from Latin deplorare "deplore, bewail, lament, give up for lost," from de- "entirely" (see de-) + plorare "weep, cry out," which is of unknown origin. Meaning "to regret deeply" is from 1560s. Related: Deplored; deploring.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "to give up as hopeless," 源自 法语 déplorer (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 deplorare "deplore, bewail, lament, give up for lost," 源自 de- "entirely" （参见 de-) + plorare "weep, cry out," which is 来源不详. 义为 "to regret deeply" 始于 1560 年代. 同源词：Deplored; deploring.

entries.definition: vt. 配置；展开；使疏开 vi. 部署；展开 n.部署
entries.etymology: 1786 as a military word, from French déployer "unroll, unfold," from Old French desploiier "unfold," from Latin displicare "unfold, scatter," from dis- (see dis-) + plicare "to fold" see ply (v.1)). "In its AFr. form regularly adopted in ME as desplay" [OED]. Related: Deployed; deploying.
entries.etymologyZh: 1786 年 作为 military word, 源自 法语 déployer "unroll, unfold," 源自 古法语 desploiier "unfold," 源自 拉丁语 displicare "unfold, scatter," 源自 dis- （参见 dis-) + plicare "to fold" 参见 ply (v.1)). "In its AFr. form regularly adopted in ME as desplay" [OED]. 同源词：Deployed; deploying.

example.en: The military decided to deploy additional troops to the conflict zone.
example.zh: 军方决定向冲突地区增派兵力。

definitionLines: vt. 存放，寄存；储蓄；使沉淀
n. 存款；押金，保证金；沉淀物
entries.definition: vt. 存放，寄存；储蓄；使沉淀 n. 存款；押金，保证金；沉淀物
entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin depositus, past participle of deponere "lay aside, put down, deposit," also used of births and bets, from de- "away" (see de-) + ponere "to put, place" (past participle positus; see position (n.)). Related: Deposited; depositing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 depositus, 为 … 的过去分词 deponere "lay aside, put down, deposit," also used of births and bets, 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + ponere "to put, place" (past participle positus; 参见 position （名）). 同源词：Deposited; depositing.

example.en: You must pay a security deposit before moving into the apartment.
example.zh: 入住公寓前您必须支付一笔安全押金。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "put down by force," from Old French depresser, from Late Latin depressare, frequentative of Latin deprimere "press down," from de- "down" (see de-) + premere "to press" (see press (v.1)). Meaning "push down physically" is from early 15c.; that of "deject, make gloomy" is from 1620s; economic sense of "lower in value" is from 1878. Related: Depressed; depressing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "put down by force," 源自 古法语 depresser, 源自 晚期拉丁语 depressare, 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 deprimere "press down," 源自 de- "down" （参见 de-) + premere "to press" （参见 press (v.1)). 义为 "push down physically" 始于 15 世纪初; that of "deject, make gloomy" 始于 1620 年代; economic 语义 "lower in value" 始于 1878 年. 同源词：Depressed; depressing.

definitionLines: n. 不景气，萧条；沮丧，消沉
entries.definition: n. 不景气，萧条；沮丧，消沉
entries.etymology:
late 14c. as a term in astronomy, from Old French depression (14c.) or directly from Latin depressionem (nominative depressio), noun of action from past participle stem of deprimere "to press down, depress" (see depress).

Attested from 1650s in the literal sense; meaning "dejection, depression of spirits" is from early 15c. (as a clinical term in psychology, from 1905); meteorological sense is from 1881 (in reference to barometric pressure); meaning "a lowering or reduction in economic activity" was in use by 1826; given a specific application (with capital D-) by 1934 to the one that began worldwide in 1929. For "melancholy, depression" an Old English word was grevoushede.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 作为 term in astronomy, 源自 古法语 depression (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 depressionem (主格 depressio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of deprimere "to press down, depress" （参见 depress). Attested 源自 1650 年代 in the literal sense; 意为 "dejection, depression of spirits" 始于 15 世纪初 (作为 clinical term in psychology, 自 1905 年起); meteorological sense 始于 1881 年 (in reference to barometric pressure); 意为 "a lowering or reduction in economic activity" was in use 截至 1826 年; given a specific application (with capital D-) 截至 1934 年 to the one that began worldwide 于 1929 年. For "melancholy, depression" an 古英语 word was grevoushede.

example.en: After losing his job, he sank into a deep depression.
example.zh: 失业后，他陷入了深度抑郁。
