entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French depriver, from Medieval Latin deprivare, from Latin de- "entirely" (see de-) + privare "release from" (see private). Replaced Old English bedælan. Related: Deprived; depriving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 depriver, 源自 中古拉丁语 deprivare, 源自 拉丁语 de- "entirely" （参见 de-) + privare "release from" （参见 private). Replaced 古英语 bedælan. 同源词：Deprived; depriving.

example.en: The new law would deprive citizens of their basic right to privacy.
example.zh: 这项新法律将剥夺公民的基本隐私权。

entries.etymology: late 14c., apparently formed in Middle English on model of length, breadth; from Old English deop "deep" (see deep) + -th (2). Replaced older deopnes "deepness." Though the English word is relatively recent, the formation is in Proto-Germanic, *deupitho-, and corresponds to Old Saxon diupitha, Dutch diepte, Old Norse dypð, Gothic diupiþa.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 似乎 formed in 中古英语 on model of length, breadth; 源自 古英语 deop "deep" （参见 deep) + -th (2). Replaced older deopnes "deepness." Though the English word is relatively recent, the formation is in 原始日耳曼语, *deupitho-, and corresponds to 古撒克逊语 diupitha, 荷兰语 diepte, 古北欧语 dypð, Gothic diupiþa.

example.en: The researchers explored the topic in great depth.
example.zh: 研究人员对这一课题进行了深入探讨。

definitionLines: n. 副，副职；代表，代表人
entries.definition: n. 副，副职；代表，代表人
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "one given the full power of an officer without holding the office," from Anglo-French deputé, noun use of past participle of Middle French députer "appoint, assign" (14c.), from Late Latin deputare "to destine, allot," in classical Latin "to esteem, consider, consider as," literally "to cut off, prune," from de- "away" (see de-) + putare "to think, count, consider," literally "to cut, prune" (see pave).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "one given the full power of an officer without holding the office," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 deputé, 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 中古法语 députer "appoint, assign" (14 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 deputare "to destine, allot," in classical 拉丁语 "to esteem, consider, consider as," 字面义为 "to cut off, prune," 源自 de- "away" （参见 de-) + putare "to think, count, consider," 字面义为 "to cut, prune" （参见 pave).

example.en: The deputy director signed the contract in the absence of the director.
example.zh: 副主任在主任缺席的情况下签署了合同。

entries.etymology: 1850, in both transitive and intransitive senses, from French dérailler "to go off the rails," from de- (see de-) + railler (see rail (n.1)). In general use first in U.S. Related: Derailed; derailing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1850 年, in both transitive and intransitive senses, 源自 法语 dérailler "to go off the rails," 源自 de- （参见 de-) + railler （参见 rail (n.1)). In general use first in U.S. 同源词：Derailed; derailing.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French deriver "to flow, pour out; derive, originate," from Latin derivare "to lead or draw off (a stream of water) from its source" (in Late Latin also "to derive"), from phrase de rivo (de "from" + rivus "stream;" see rivulet). Etymological sense is 1550s. Related: Derived; deriving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 deriver "to flow, pour out; derive, originate," 源自 拉丁语 derivare "to lead or draw off (a stream of water) from its source" (in 晚期拉丁语 also "to derive"), 源自 phrase de rivo (de "from" + rivus "stream;" 参见 rivulet). Etymological sense is 1550 年代. 同源词：Derived; deriving.

example.en: The English word 「salary」 derives from the Latin word for salt.
example.zh: 英语单词「salary」源自拉丁语中表示盐的词。

entries.etymology: mid-15c. (adj.), c. 1600 (n.), from French descendant (13c.), present participle of descendre (see descend). Despite a tendency to use descendent for the adjective and descendant for the noun, descendant seems to be prevailing in all uses and appears 5 times more often than its rival in books printed since 1900. Compare dependant.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期 （形）, 约 1600 年 （名）, 源自 法语 descendant (13 世纪), 为 … 的现在分词 descendre （参见 descend). Despite a tendency to use descendent for the 形容词 and descendant for the 名词, descendant seems to be prevailing in all uses and appears 5 times more 常 than its rival in books printed 自 1900 年. 对比 dependant.

example.en: The estate was passed down to the last living descendant of the noble family.
example.zh: 这份遗产传给了这个贵族家庭最后在世的后裔。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French descente "descent, descendance, lineage," formed from descendre (see descend) on analogy of French nouns such as attente from attendre "to expect," vente "sale" from vendre "to sell," pente "slope" from pendre "to hang" (the etymological English word from Latin would be *descence).

Figurative use is from late 14c. Meaning "action of descending," also "a downward slope" is from 1590s. Meaning "act of descending from an ancestor" is from mid-14c. Evolutionary sense is from 1859 in Darwin, though there are uses which suggest essentially the same thing going back to 1630s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 descente "descent, descendance, lineage," formed 源自 descendre （参见 descend) on analogy of 法语 nouns such as attente 源自 attendre "to expect," vente "sale" 源自 vendre "to sell," pente "slope" 源自 pendre "to hang" (the etymological English word 源自 拉丁语 would be *descence). Figurative use 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "action of descending," also "a downward slope" 始于 1590 年代. 义为 "act of descending from an ancestor" 始于 14 世纪中期 Evolutionary sense 始于 1859 年 in Darwin, though there are uses which suggest essentially the same thing going back to 1630 年代.

example.en: She is proud of her French descent and speaks the language fluently.
example.zh: 她为自己的法国血统感到骄傲，法语说得很流利。

entries.etymology: early 13c., descriven, from Old French descrivre, descrire (13c.), from Latin describere "to write down, copy; sketch, represent" (see description). Reconstructed with Latin spelling 16c. Related: Describable; described, describes, describing.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, descriven, 源自 古法语 descrivre, descrire (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 describere "to write down, copy; sketch, represent" （参见 description). Reconstructed with 拉丁语 spelling 16 世纪 同源词：Describable; described, describes, describing.

example.en: The author uses vivid language to describe the main character's troubled childhood.
example.zh: 作者用生动的语言描述主人公动荡的童年。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French description (12c.) and directly from Latin descriptionem (nominative descriptio) "representation, description, copy," noun of action from past participle stem of describere "write down, transcribe, copy, sketch," from de- "down" (see de-) + scribere "write" (see script (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 description (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 descriptionem (主格 descriptio) "representation, description, copy," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of describere "write down, transcribe, copy, sketch," 源自 de- "down" （参见 de-) + scribere "write" （参见 script （名）).

example.en: The witness gave a detailed description of the suspect's clothing and height.
example.zh: 目击者详细描述了嫌疑人的衣着和身高。

definitionLines: vt. 离开，抛弃；从……开小差
entries.definition: n. 沙漠，不毛之地 vt. 离开，抛弃；从……开小差
entries.etymology: "to leave one's duty," late 14c., from Old French deserter (12c.) "leave," literally "undo or sever connection," from Late Latin desertare, frequentative of Latin deserere "to abandon, to leave, forsake, give up, leave in the lurch," from de- "undo" (see de-) + serere "join together, put in a row" (see series). Military sense is first recorded 1640s. Related: Deserted; deserting.
entries.etymologyZh: "to leave one's duty," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 deserter (12 世纪) "leave," 字面义为 "undo or sever connection," 源自 晚期拉丁语 desertare, 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 deserere "to abandon, to leave, forsake, give up, leave in the lurch," 源自 de- "undo" （参见 de-) + serere "join together, put in a row" （参见 series). Military sense is 首见于 1640 年代. 同源词：Deserted; deserting.

example.en: Camels are well adapted to survive in the desert.
example.zh: 骆驼非常适应在沙漠中生存。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French deservir (Modern French desservir) "deserve, be worthy of, earn, merit," from Latin deservire "serve well," from de- "completely" (see de-) + servire "to serve" (see serve). From "be entitled to because of good service" (a sense found in Late Latin), meaning generalized c. 1300 to "be worthy of." Related: Deserved; deserving.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 deservir (现代法语 desservir) "deserve, be worthy of, earn, merit," 源自 拉丁语 deservire "serve well," 源自 de- "completely" （参见 de-) + servire "to serve" （参见 serve). From "be entitled to because of good service" (a sense found in 晚期拉丁语), 意为 generalized 约 1300 年 to "be worthy of." 同源词：Deserved; deserving.

example.en: After years of hard work, she finally got the recognition she truly deserve.
example.zh: 经过多年的努力，她终于获得了她真正应得的认可。

definitionLines: vt. 标出；指定；把……定名； 指派
entries.definition: vt. 标出；指定；把……定名； 指派
entries.etymology: 1640s, from Latin designatus, past participle of designare (see design (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 拉丁语 designatus, 为 … 的过去分词 designare （参见 design （动）).

example.en: The committee will designate a new spokesperson by Friday.
example.zh: 委员会将在周五前指定一位新发言人。

definitionLines: a.合乎需要的，令人满意的
entries.definition: a.合乎需要的，令人满意的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French desirable (12c.), from dasirer (see desire (v.)). Related: Desirably; desirability.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 desirable (12 世纪), 源自 dasirer （参见 desire （动）). 同源词：Desirably; desirability.

example.en: A quiet neighborhood with good schools is a very desirable place to raise children.
example.zh: 一个安静且学校优质的社区是养育孩子的理想之地。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French desirrer (12c.) "wish, desire, long for," from Latin desiderare "long for, wish for; demand, expect," original sense perhaps "await what the stars will bring," from the phrase de sidere "from the stars," from sidus (genitive sideris) "heavenly body, star, constellation" (but see consider). Related: Desired; desiring.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 desirrer (12 世纪) "wish, desire, long for," 源自 拉丁语 desiderare "long for, wish for; demand, expect," original sense 或许 "await what the stars will bring," 源自 phrase de sidere "from the stars," 源自 sidus (属格 sideris) "heavenly body, star, constellation" (but 参见 consider). 同源词：Desired; desiring.

example.en: She felt a strong desire to travel the world after graduation.
example.zh: 毕业后，她强烈渴望游历世界。

definitionLines: n. 书桌，服务台，办公桌
entries.definition: n. 书桌，服务台，办公桌
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Medieval Latin desca "table to write on" (mid-13c.), from Latin discus "quoit, platter, dish," from Greek diskos (see disk (n.)). The Medieval Latin is perhaps via Italian desco. Used figuratively of office or clerical work since 1797; desk job is first attested 1965.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 中古拉丁语 desca "table to write on" (13 世纪中期), 源自 拉丁语 discus "quoit, platter, dish," 源自 希腊语 diskos （参见 disk （名）). The 中古拉丁语 is 或许 经由 意大利语 desco. Used figuratively of office or clerical work 自 1797 年; desk job is 最早见于 1965 年.

example.en: She found the missing file in her desk drawer.
example.zh: 她在书桌抽屉里找到了那份丢失的文件。

entries.etymology: early 14c., from stem of Old French desperer "be dismayed, lose hope, despair," from Latin desperare "to despair, to lose all hope," from de- "without" (see de-) + sperare "to hope," from spes "hope" (see sperate). Related: Despaired; despairing; despairingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 stem of 古法语 desperer "be dismayed, lose hope, despair," 源自 拉丁语 desperare "to despair, to lose all hope," 源自 de- "without" （参见 de-) + sperare "to hope," 源自 spes "hope" （参见 sperate). 同源词：Despaired; despairing; despairingly.

example.en: After years of failed attempts, she began to despair of ever finding a solution.
example.zh: 经过多年的失败尝试，她开始对找到解决方案感到绝望。

definitionLines: a.绝望的，危急的；不顾一切 的，铤而走险的
entries.definition: a.绝望的，危急的；不顾一切 的，铤而走险的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "despairing, hopeless," from Latin desperatus "given up, despaired of," past participle of desperare (see despair (v.)). Sense of "driven to recklessness" is from late 15c.; weakened sense of "having a great desire for" is from 1950s. Related: Desperately.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "despairing, hopeless," 源自 拉丁语 desperatus "given up, despaired of," 为 … 的过去分词 desperare （参见 despair （动）). 义为 "driven to recklessness" 始于 15 世纪晚期; weakened 语义 "having a great desire for" 始于 1950 年代. 同源词：Desperately.

example.en: The survivors were desperate for food and clean water after the flood.
example.zh: 洪水过后，幸存者们极度渴求食物和干净的水。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, originally a noun, from Old French despit (12c., Modern French dépit), from Latin despectus "a looking down on, scorn, contempt," from past participle of despicere (see despise).

The preposition (early 15c.) is short for in despite of (late 13c.), a loan-translation of Old French en despit de "in contempt of." Almost became despight during 16c. spelling reform.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 原义为 a 名词, 源自 古法语 despit (12 世纪, 现代法语 dépit), 源自 拉丁语 despectus "a looking down on, scorn, contempt," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 despicere （参见 despise). The preposition (15 世纪初) is short for in despite of (13 世纪晚期), a loan-translation of 古法语 en despit de "in contempt of." Almost became despight during 16 世纪 spelling reform.

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from Middle French dessert (mid-16c.) "last course," literally "removal of what has been served," from desservir "clear the table," literally "un-serve," from des- "remove, undo" (see dis-) + Old French servir "to serve" (see serve (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 中古法语 dessert (16 世纪中期) "last course," 字面义为 "removal of what has been served," 源自 desservir "clear the table," 字面义为 "un-serve," 源自 des- "remove, undo" （参见 dis-) + 古法语 servir "to serve" （参见 serve （动）).

entries.etymology: 1590s, "act of appointing," from Latin destinationem (nominative destinatio) "purpose, design," from past participle stem of destinare "determine, appoint, choose, make firm or fast," from de- "completely, formally" (see de-) + -stinare (related to stare "to stand") from PIE *ste-no-, from root *sta- "to stand" (see stet). Modern sense (1787) is from place of destination, where one is "destined" to go.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "act of appointing," 源自 拉丁语 destinationem (主格 destinatio) "purpose, design," 源自 past participle stem of destinare "determine, appoint, choose, make firm or fast," 源自 de- "completely, formally" （参见 de-) + -stinare (related to stare "to stand") 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ste-no-, 源自 root *sta- "to stand" （参见 stet). 现代 sense (1787 年) 始于 place of destination, where one is "destined" to go.

example.en: Tokyo was their final destination after a month-long trip across Asia.
example.zh: 在历时一个月的亚洲之旅后，东京是他们的最终目的地。

definitionLines: a.命定的；注定的；（for）去 往……的
entries.definition: a.命定的；注定的；（for）去 往……的

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French destinée (12c.) "purpose, intent, fate, destiny; that which is destined," noun use of fem. past participle of destiner, from Latin destinare "make firm, establish" (see destination). The sense is of "that which has been firmly established," as by fate.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 destinée (12 世纪) "purpose, intent, fate, destiny; that which is destined," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 destiner, 源自 拉丁语 destinare "make firm, establish" （参见 destination). The sense is of "that which has been firmly established," as by fate.

example.en: She believed that meeting him was part of her destiny.
example.zh: 她相信与他相遇是她命运的一部分。

definitionLines: vt. 破坏，摧毁；消灭，扑灭；打 破，粉碎
entries.definition: vt. 破坏，摧毁；消灭，扑灭；打 破，粉碎
entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French destruire (12c., Modern French détruire) "destroy, ravage, lay waste," from Vulgar Latin *destrugere (source of Italian distruggere), refashioned (influenced by destructus), from Latin destruere "tear down, demolish," literally "un-build," from de- "un-, down" (see de-) + struere "to pile, build" (see structure (n.)). Related: Destroyed; destroying.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 destruire (12 世纪, 现代法语 détruire) "destroy, ravage, lay waste," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *destrugere (source of 意大利语 distruggere), refashioned (influenced by destructus), 源自 拉丁语 destruere "tear down, demolish," 字面义为 "un-build," 源自 de- "un-, down" （参见 de-) + struere "to pile, build" （参见 structure （名）). 同源词：Destroyed; destroying.

example.en: The fire completely destroy the old warehouse overnight.
example.zh: 那场大火一夜之间将那座旧仓库彻底摧毁了。

entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French destruction (12c.) and directly from Latin destructionem (nominative destructio) "a pulling down, destruction," from past participle stem of destruere "tear down" (see destroy).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 destruction (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 destructionem (主格 destructio) "a pulling down, destruction," 源自 past participle stem of destruere "tear down" （参见 destroy).

example.en: The earthquake caused widespread destruction to the city's underground pipeline network.
example.zh: 地震对该城市的地下管网造成了大范围的彻底破坏。

entries.etymology: 1680s, from French détacher "to detach, untie," from Old French destachier, from des- "apart" + attachier "attach" (see attach). Related: Detached; detaching.
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, 源自 法语 détacher "to detach, untie," 源自 古法语 destachier, 源自 des- "apart" + attachier "attach" （参见 attach). 同源词：Detached; detaching.

entries.etymology:
c. 1600, from French détail, from Old French detail "small piece or quantity," literally "a cutting in pieces," from detaillier "cut in pieces," from de- "entirely" (see de-) + taillier "to cut in pieces" (see tailor).
Modern sense is from French en détail "piece by piece, item by item" (as opposed to en gros), a commercial term used where we would today use retail. Military sense is 1708, from notion of "distribution in detail of the daily orders first given in general," including assignment of specific duties.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 détail, 源自 古法语 detail "small piece or quantity," 字面义为 "a cutting in pieces," 源自 detaillier "cut in pieces," 源自 de- "entirely" （参见 de-) + taillier "to cut in pieces" （参见 tailor). 现代 sense 始于 法语 en détail "piece by piece, item by item" (as opposed to en gros), a commercial term used where we would today use retail. Military sense is 1708 年, 源自 概念 "distribution in detail of the daily orders first given in general," including assignment of specific duties.

example.en: Please check every detail of the contract before signing it.
example.zh: 签字前请仔细检查合同的每一个细节。

example.en: The manager provided a detailed report on the project's progress.
example.zh: 经理提供了一份关于项目进展的详细报告。

entries.etymology: early 15c., deteynen, from Old French detenir "to hold off, keep back" (12c.), from Latin detinere "hold off, keep back," from de- "from, away" (see de-) + tenere "to hold" (see tenet). Modern spelling is 17c., from influence of contain, retain, etc. Related: Detained; detaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, deteynen, 源自 古法语 detenir "to hold off, keep back" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 detinere "hold off, keep back," 源自 de- "from, away" （参见 de-) + tenere "to hold" （参见 tenet). 现代 spelling is 17 世纪, 源自 influence of contain, retain, etc. 同源词：Detained; detaining.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin detectus, past participle of detegere "uncover, expose," figuratively "discover, reveal, disclose," from de- "un-, off" (see de-) + tegere "to cover" (see stegosaurus). Related: Detected; detecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 detectus, 为 … 的过去分词 detegere "uncover, expose," figuratively "discover, reveal, disclose," 源自 de- "un-, off" （参见 de-) + tegere "to cover" （参见 stegosaurus). 同源词：Detected; detecting.

example.en: The sensor can detect even the slightest change in temperature.
example.zh: 该传感器能够探测到温度最细微的变化。

definitionLines: n. 觉察，发觉；侦察；探测
entries.definition: n. 觉察，发觉；侦察；探测
entries.etymology: early 15c., "exposure, accusation," from Latin detectionem (nominative detectio) "an uncovering," noun of action from past participle stem of detegere (see detect).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "exposure, accusation," 源自 拉丁语 detectionem (主格 detectio) "an uncovering," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of detegere （参见 detect).

entries.etymology: 1850, short for detective police, from detective (adj.), 1843; see detect + -ive.
entries.etymologyZh: 1850 年, short for detective police, 源自 detective （形）, 1843 年; 参见 detect + -ive.

example.en: The detective gathered clues at the crime scene before making an arrest.
example.zh: 侦探在逮捕之前在犯罪现场收集线索。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French détention (13c.), from Late Latin detentionem (nominative detentio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin detinere (see detain). Sense of "confinement" used by 1570s (in reference to Mary Queen of Scots). In reference to school punishment, recorded from 1882.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 détention (13 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 detentionem (主格 detentio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 detinere （参见 detain). 义为 "confinement" used by 1570 年代 (in reference to Mary Queen of Scots). In reference to school punishment, recorded 自 1882 年起.

entries.definition: vi. 恶化，变坏 vt.恶化
entries.etymology: 1640s (as a past participle adjective, 1570s), from Late Latin deterioratus, past participle of deteriorare "get worse, make worse," from Latin deterior "worse, lower, inferior, meaner," contrastive of *deter "bad, lower," from PIE *de-tero-, from demonstrative stem *de- (see de). Originally transitive in English; intransitive sense is from 1758. Related: Deteriorated; deteriorating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代 (作为 past participle 形容词, 1570 年代), 源自 晚期拉丁语 deterioratus, 为 … 的过去分词 deteriorare "get worse, make worse," 源自 拉丁语 deterior "worse, lower, inferior, meaner," contrastive of *deter "bad, lower," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *de-tero-, 源自 demonstrative stem *de- （参见 de). Originally transitive in English; intransitive sense 始于 1758 年. 同源词：Deteriorated; deteriorating.

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "decision, sentence," from Old French déterminacion (14c.) "determination, settlement, definition," from Latin determinationem (nominative determinatio) "conclusion, boundary," noun of action from past participle stem of determinare "to enclose, bound, set limits to" (see determine).

As "a bringing to an end" (especilly of a suit at law), late 15c. As "fixed direction toward a goal," from 1650s, originally in physics or anatomy; metaphoric sense "fixation of will" is from 1680s; that of "quality of being resolute" is from 1822.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "decision, sentence," 源自 古法语 déterminacion (14 世纪) "determination, settlement, definition," 源自 拉丁语 determinationem (主格 determinatio) "conclusion, boundary," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of determinare "to enclose, bound, set limits to" （参见 determine). As "a bringing to an end" (especilly of a suit at law), 15 世纪晚期 As "fixed direction toward a goal," 源自 1650 年代, 原义为 in physics or anatomy; metaphoric sense "fixation of will" 始于 1680 年代; that of "quality of being resolute" 始于 1822 年.

example.en: Her determination to succeed kept her going through the hardships.
example.zh: 她成功的决心支撑着她度过了重重困难。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "to come to an end," also "to settle, decide" (late 14c.), from Old French determiner (12c.) or directly from Latin determinare "to enclose, bound, set limits to," from de- "off" (see de-) + terminare "to mark the end or boundary," from terminus "end, limit" (see terminus). Sense of "coming to a firm decision" (to do something) is from mid-15c. Related: Determined; determining; determiner.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to come to an end," also "to settle, decide" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 古法语 determiner (12 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 determinare "to enclose, bound, set limits to," 源自 de- "off" （参见 de-) + terminare "to mark the end or boundary," 源自 terminus "end, limit" （参见 terminus). 义为 "coming to a firm decision" (to do something) 始于 15 世纪中期 同源词：Determined; determining; determiner.

example.en: She determined to finish her thesis before the spring deadline.
example.zh: 她下定决心在春季截止日期前完成论文。

definitionLines: 发展，进展；开发，研制；显 现，显影；发育，生长；进化
entries.definition: 发展，进展；开发，研制；显 现，显影；发育，生长；进化
entries.etymology: 1650s, "unroll, unfold," from French développer, replacing English disvelop (1590s, from Middle French desveloper), both from Old French desveloper "unwrap, unfurl, unveil; reveal the meaning of, explain," from des- "undo" + veloper "wrap up," which is of uncertain origin, possibly Celtic or Germanic. Modern figurative use is 18c. The photographic sense is from 1845; the real estate sense is from 1890.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "unroll, unfold," 源自 法语 développer, replacing English disvelop (1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 desveloper), both 源自 古法语 desveloper "unwrap, unfurl, unveil; reveal the meaning of, explain," 源自 des- "undo" + veloper "wrap up," which is 来源存疑, possibly Celtic or 日耳曼语. 现代 figurative use is 18 世纪 The photographic sense 始于 1845 年; the real estate sense 始于 1890 年.

example.en: Children develop at different rates depending on their environment.
example.zh: 孩子们根据所处环境以不同的速度发育成长。

definitionLines: n. 发展，进展；开发，研制；新 发展
entries.definition: n. 发展，进展；开发，研制；新 发展
entries.etymology: 1756, "an unfolding;" see develop + -ment. Of property, with the sense "bringing out the latent possibilities," from 1885 (Pickering's glossary of Americanisms, 1816, has betterments "The improvements made on new lands, by cultivation, and the erection of buildings, &c."). Meaning "state of economic advancement" is from 1902. Meaning "advancement through progressive stages" is 1836.
entries.etymologyZh: 1756 年, "an unfolding;" 参见 develop + -ment. Of property, with the sense "bringing out the latent possibilities," 自 1885 年起 (Pickering's glossary of Americanisms, 1816 年, has betterments "The improvements made on new lands, by cultivation, and the erection of buildings, &c."). 义为 "state of economic advancement" 始于 1902 年. 义为 "advancement through progressive stages" is 1836 年.

example.en: Rapid technological development has fundamentally changed how businesses operate globally.
example.zh: 快速的技术发展从根本上改变了企业在全球的运营方式。

definitionLines: n. 设备，装置；方法，设计
entries.definition: n. 设备，装置；方法，设计
entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French devis "division, separation, disposition, wish, desire; coat of arms, emblem; last will," from deviser "to divide, distribute" (see devise). Sense of "method by which something is divided" arose in French and led to modern meaning.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 devis "division, separation, disposition, wish, desire; coat of arms, emblem; last will," 源自 deviser "to divide, distribute" （参见 devise). 义为 "method by which something is divided" arose in 法语 and led to modern 意为.

example.en: This wearable device tracks your sleep patterns and sends data to your phone.
example.zh: 这款可穿戴设备追踪你的睡眠模式并将数据发送到你的手机。

entries.etymology:
Old English deofol "evil spirit, a devil, the devil, false god, diabolical person," from Late Latin diabolus (also the source of Italian diavolo, French diable, Spanish diablo; German Teufel is Old High German tiufal, from Latin via Gothic diabaulus).

The Late Latin word is from Ecclesiastical Greek diabolos, in Jewish and Christian use, "Devil, Satan" (scriptural loan-translation of Hebrew satan), in general use "accuser, slanderer," from diaballein "to slander, attack," literally "throw across," from dia- "across, through" + ballein "to throw" (see ballistics). Jerome re-introduced Satan in Latin bibles, and English translators have used both in different measures.

In Vulgate, as in Greek, diabolus and dæmon (see demon) were distinct, but they have merged in English and other Germanic languages.

Playful use for "clever rogue" is from c. 1600. Meaning "sand spout, dust storm" is from 1835. In U.S. place names, the word often represents a native word such as Algonquian manito, more properly "spirit, god." Phrase a devil way (c. 1300) was originally "Hell-ward, to Hell," but by late 14c. as an expression of irritation.

Devil's books "playing cards" is from 1729, but the cited quote says they've been called that "time out of mind" (the four of clubs is the devil's bedposts); devil's coach-horse is from 1840, the large rove-beetle, which is defiant when disturbed. "Talk of the Devil, and he's presently at your elbow" [1660s].
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 deofol "evil spirit, a devil, the devil, false god, diabolical person," 源自 晚期拉丁语 diabolus (also the source of 意大利语 diavolo, 法语 diable, 西班牙语 diablo; 德语 Teufel is 古高地德语 tiufal, 源自 拉丁语 经由 Gothic diabaulus). The 晚期拉丁语 word 始于 Ecclesiastical 希腊语 diabolos, in Jewish and Christian use, "Devil, Satan" (scriptural loan-translation of 希伯来语 satan), in general use "accuser, slanderer," 源自 diaballein "to slander, attack," 字面义为 "throw across," 源自 dia- "across, through" + ballein "to throw" （参见 ballistics). Jerome re-introduced Satan in 拉丁语 bibles, and English translators have used both in different measures. In Vulgate, as in 希腊语, diabolus and dæmon （参见 demon) were distinct, but they have merged in English and other 日耳曼语 languages. Playful use for "clever rogue" 始于 约 1600 年. 义为 "sand spout, dust storm" 始于 1835 年. In U.S. place names, the word 常 represents a 本族 word such as Algonquian manito, more properly "spirit, god." Phrase a devil way (约 1300 年) was 原义为 "Hell-ward, to Hell," but by 14 世纪晚期 作为 expression of irritation. Devil's books "playing cards" is from 1729, but the cited quote says they've been called that "time out of mind" (the four of clubs is the devil's bedposts); devil's coach-horse 始于 1840 年, the large rove-beetle, which is defiant when disturbed. "Talk of the Devil, and he's presently at your elbow" [1660 年代].

entries.etymology: early 13c., "to form, fashion;" c. 1300, "to plan, contrive," from Old French deviser "dispose in portions, arrange, plan, contrive" (in modern French, "to chat, gossip"), from Vulgar Latin *divisare, frequentative of Latin dividere "to divide" (see divide). Modern sense is from "to arrange a division" (especially via a will), a meaning present in the Old French word. Related: Devised; devising.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "to form, fashion;" 约 1300 年, "to plan, contrive," 源自 古法语 deviser "dispose in portions, arrange, plan, contrive" (in modern 法语, "to chat, gossip"), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *divisare, 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 dividere "to divide" （参见 divide). 现代 sense 始于 "to arrange a division" (尤指 经由 a will), a 意为 present in the 古法语 word. 同源词：Devised; devising.

example.en: Scientists devise a new method to purify drinking water.
example.zh: 科学家们想出了一种净化饮用水的新方法。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Latin devotus, past participle of devovere (see devotion). Second and third meanings in Johnson's Dictionary (1755) are "to addict, to give up to ill" and "to curse, to execrate; to doom to destruction." Related: Devoted; devoting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 devotus, 为 … 的过去分词 devovere （参见 devotion). Second and third meanings in Johnson's Dictionary (1755 年) are "to addict, to give up to ill" and "to curse, to execrate; to doom to destruction." 同源词：Devoted; devoting.

example.en: She has devoted her life to helping children in poverty.
example.zh: 她把一生奉献给了帮助贫困儿童的事业。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Old French devocion "devotion, piety," from Latin devotionem (nominative devotio), noun of action from past participle stem of devovere "dedicate by a vow, sacrifice oneself, promise solemnly," from de- "down, away" (see de-) + vovere "to vow," from votum "vow" (see vow (n.)).

In ancient Latin, "act of consecrating by a vow," also "loyalty, fealty, allegiance;" in Church Latin, "devotion to God, piety." This was the original sense in English; the etymological sense, including secular situations, returned 16c. via Italian and French.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 devocion "devotion, piety," 源自 拉丁语 devotionem (主格 devotio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of devovere "dedicate by a vow, sacrifice oneself, promise solemnly," 源自 de- "down, away" （参见 de-) + vovere "to vow," 源自 votum "vow" （参见 vow （名）). In ancient 拉丁语, "act of consecrating by a vow," also "loyalty, fealty, allegiance;" in 教会拉丁语, "devotion to God, piety." This was the original sense in English; the etymological sense, including secular situations, returned 16 世纪 经由 意大利语 and 法语.

example.en: Her devotion to the cause inspired everyone around her.
example.zh: 她对这项事业的献身精神激励了周围的每一个人。

entries.etymology: 1861, back-formation from diagnosis. Related: Diagnosed; diagnosing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1861 年, back-formation 源自 diagnosis. 同源词：Diagnosed; diagnosing.

example.en: The doctor was able to diagnose the illness after reviewing the scan.
example.zh: 医生在查看扫描结果后诊断出了这种疾病。

entries.etymology: 1680s, medical Latin application of Greek diagnosis "a discerning, distinguishing," from stem of diagignoskein "discern, distinguish," literally "to know thoroughly," from dia- "apart" (see dia-) + gignoskein "to learn" (see gnostic).
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, medical 拉丁语 application of 希腊语 diagnosis "a discerning, distinguishing," 源自 stem of diagignoskein "discern, distinguish," 字面义为 "to know thoroughly," 源自 dia- "apart" （参见 dia-) + gignoskein "to learn" （参见 gnostic).

example.en: The doctor reached a diagnosis after reviewing all the test results.
example.zh: 医生在审阅所有检测结果后作出了诊断。

entries.etymology: 1610s, from French diagramme, from Latin diagramma, from Greek diagramma "geometric figure, that which is marked out by lines," from diagraphein "mark out by lines, delineate," from dia- "across, out" (see dia-) + graphein "write, mark, draw" (see -graphy). The verb is 1840, from the noun.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 法语 diagramme, 源自 拉丁语 diagramma, 源自 希腊语 diagramma "geometric figure, that which is marked out by lines," 源自 diagraphein "mark out by lines, delineate," 源自 dia- "across, out" （参见 dia-) + graphein "write, mark, draw" （参见 -graphy). The 动词 is 1840 年, 源自 名词.

definitionLines: n. 标度盘，钟面，拨号盘
entries.definition: n. 标度盘，钟面，拨号盘 n. 拨号，打电话
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "sundial," earlier "dial of a compass" (mid-14c.), apparently from Medieval Latin dialis "daily," from Latin dies "day" (see diurnal).

The word perhaps was abstracted from a phrase such as Medieval Latin rota dialis "daily wheel," and evolved to mean any round plate over which something rotates. Telephone sense is from 1879, which led to dial tone (1921), "the signal to begin dialing," which term soon might be the sole relic of the rotary phone.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "sundial," earlier "dial of a compass" (14 世纪中期), 似乎 源自 中古拉丁语 dialis "daily," 源自 拉丁语 dies "day" （参见 diurnal). The word 或许 was abstracted 源自 a phrase such as 中古拉丁语 rota dialis "daily wheel," and evolved to mean any round plate over which something rotates. Telephone sense 始于 1879 年, which led to dial tone (1921 年), "the signal to begin dialing," which term soon might be the sole relic of the rotary phone.

example.en: She picked up the phone and began to dial the number slowly.
example.zh: 她拿起电话，慢慢地拨了号码。

entries.definition: n. 方言 dialog（ue） n. 对话，对白
entries.etymology: 1570s, "form of speech of a region or group," from Middle French dialecte, from Latin dialectus "local language, way of speaking, conversation," from Greek dialektos "talk, conversation, speech;" also "the language of a country, dialect," from dialegesthai "converse with each other," from dia- "across, between" (see dia-) + legein "speak" (see lecture (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "form of speech of a region or group," 源自 中古法语 dialecte, 源自 拉丁语 dialectus "local language, way of speaking, conversation," 源自 希腊语 dialektos "talk, conversation, speech;" also "the language of a country, dialect," 源自 dialegesthai "converse with each other," 源自 dia- "across, between" （参见 dia-) + legein "speak" （参见 lecture （名）).

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French diametre, from Latin diametrus, from Greek diametros (gramme) "diagonal of a circle," from dia- "across, through" (see dia-) + metron "a measure" (see meter (n.2)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 diametre, 源自 拉丁语 diametrus, 源自 希腊语 diametros (gramme) "diagonal of a circle," 源自 dia- "across, through" （参见 dia-) + metron "a measure" （参见 meter (n.2)).

entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French diamant, from Medieval Latin diamantem (nominative diamas), from Vulgar Latin *adiamantem (altered by influence of the many Greek words in dia-), from Latin adamantem (nominative adamans) "the hardest metal," later, "diamond" (see adamant). Playing card suit is from 1590s; Sense in baseball is American English, 1875.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 diamant, 源自 中古拉丁语 diamantem (主格 diamas), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *adiamantem (altered by influence of the many 希腊语 words in dia-), 源自 拉丁语 adamantem (主格 adamans) "the hardest metal," later, "diamond" （参见 adamant). Playing card suit 始于 1590 年代; Sense in baseball is American English, 1875 年.

example.en: She wore a necklace with a small diamond pendant at its center.
example.zh: 她戴着一条中间镶有小钻石吊坠的项链。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Latin diarium "daily allowance," later "a journal," neuter of diarius "daily," from dies "day" (see diurnal); also see -ary. Earliest sense was a daily record of events; sense of the book in which such are written is said to be first attested in Ben Jonson's "Volpone" (1605).
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 diarium "daily allowance," later "a journal," neuter of diarius "daily," 源自 dies "day" （参见 diurnal); also 参见 -ary. Earliest sense was a daily record of events; 语义 the book in which such are written is said to be 最早见于 in Ben Jonson's "Volpone" (1605 年).

example.en: She kept a diary where she recorded her thoughts and feelings every night.
example.zh: 她坚持写日记，每晚记录自己的思想和感受。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "to practice dictation, say aloud for another to write down," from Latin dictatus, past participle of dictare "say often, prescribe," frequentative of dicere "to say, speak" (see diction). Sense of "to command" is 1620s. Related: Dictated; dictates; dictating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "to practice dictation, say aloud for another to write down," 源自 拉丁语 dictatus, 为 … 的过去分词 dictare "say often, prescribe," 为 … 的反复体 dicere "to say, speak" （参见 diction). 义为 "to command" is 1620 年代. 同源词：Dictated; dictates; dictating.

example.en: The manager used to dictate letters to his assistant every morning.
example.zh: 这位经理过去每天早晨向助理口述信件内容。

entries.etymology: 1650s, from Late Latin dictationem (nominative dictatio), noun of action from past participle stem of dictare (see dictate (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 dictationem (主格 dictatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of dictare （参见 dictate （动）).

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin dictator, agent noun from dictare (see dictate (v.)). Transferred sense of "one who has absolute power or authority" in any sphere is from c. 1600. In Latin use, a dictator was a judge in the Roman republic temporarily invested with absolute power.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 dictator, agent 名词 源自 dictare （参见 dictate （动）). Transferred 语义 "one who has absolute power or authority" in any sphere 始于 约 1600 年. In 拉丁语 use, a dictator was a judge in the Roman republic temporarily invested with absolute power.

entries.etymology: 1520s, from Medieval Latin dictionarium "collection of words and phrases," from Latin dictionarius "of words," from dictio "word" (see diction). Probably first English use in title of a book was in Sir Thomas Elyot's "Latin Dictionary" (1538) though Latin Dictionarius was so used from early 13c. Grose's 1788 "Dictionary of the Vulgar Tongue" has "RICHARD SNARY. A dictionary."
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 dictionarium "collection of words and phrases," 源自 拉丁语 dictionarius "of words," 源自 dictio "word" （参见 diction). Probably first English use in title of a book was in Sir Thomas Elyot's "Latin Dictionary" (1538) though Latin Dictionarius was so used from early 13c. Grose's 1788 年 "Dictionary of the Vulgar Tongue" has "RICHARD SNARY. A dictionary."

entries.etymology:
mid-12c., possibly from Old Danish døja or Old Norse deyja "to die, pass away," both from Proto-Germanic *dawjan (source also of Old Frisian deja "to kill," Old Saxon doian, Old High German touwen, Gothic diwans "mortal"), from PIE root *dheu- (3) "to pass away, die, become senseless" (source also of Old Irish dith "end, death," Old Church Slavonic daviti, Russian davit' "to choke, suffer").

It has been speculated that Old English had *diegan, from the same source, but it is not in any of the surviving texts and the preferred words were steorfan (see starve), sweltan (see swelter), wesan dead, also forðgan and other euphemisms.

Languages usually don't borrow words from abroad for central life experiences, but "die" words are an exception, because they are often hidden or changed euphemistically out of superstitious dread. A Dutch euphemism translates as "to give the pipe to Maarten." Regularly spelled dege through 15c., and still pronounced "dee" by some in Lancashire and Scotland. Used figuratively (of sounds, etc.) from 1580s. Related: Died; dies.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, possibly 源自 Old Danish døja or 古北欧语 deyja "to die, pass away," both 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dawjan (source also of 古弗里西语 deja "to kill," 古撒克逊语 doian, 古高地德语 touwen, Gothic diwans "mortal"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dheu- (3) "to pass away, die, become senseless" (source also of Old 爱尔兰语 dith "end, death," Old Church Slavonic daviti, 俄语 davit' "to choke, suffer"). It has been speculated that Old English had *diegan, from the same source, but it is not in any of the surviving texts and the preferred words were steorfan (see starve), sweltan (see swelter), wesan dead, also forðgan and other euphemisms. Languages usually don't borrow words 源自 abroad for central life experiences, but "die" words are an exception, because they are 常 hidden or changed euphemistically out of superstitious dread. A 荷兰语 euphemism translates as "to give the pipe to Maarten." Regularly spelled dege through 15 世纪, and still pronounced "dee" by some in Lancashire and Scotland. Used figuratively (of sounds, etc.) 源自 1580 年代. 同源词：Died; dies.

example.en: Without water for two weeks, even the hardiest plants will die completely.
example.zh: 断水两周，即便是最耐旱的植物也会彻底死亡。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to regulate one's diet for the sake of health," from Old French dieter, from diete (see diet (n.1)); meaning "to regulate oneself as to food" (especially against fatness) is from 1650s. Related: Dieted; dieting. An obsolete word for this is banting. The adjective in this sense (Diet Coke, etc.) is from 1963, originally American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to regulate one's diet for the sake of health," 源自 古法语 dieter, 源自 diete （参见 diet (n.1)); 意为 "to regulate oneself as to food" (尤指 against fatness) 始于 1650 年代. 同源词：Dieted; dieting. An 已废 word for this is banting. The 形容词 in this sense (Diet Coke, etc.) 始于 1963 年, 原义为 American English.

example.en: A balanced diet is essential for maintaining good health.
example.zh: 均衡饮食对保持良好健康至关重要。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French differer (14c.) and directly from Latin differre "to set apart, differ," from dis- "away from" (see dis-) + ferre "carry" (see infer).

Two senses that were present in Latin have gone separate ways in English since c. 1500 with defer (transitive) and differ (intransitive). Related: Differed; differing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 differer (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 differre "to set apart, differ," 源自 dis- "away from" （参见 dis-) + ferre "carry" （参见 infer). Two senses that were present in 拉丁语 have gone separate ways in English 自 约 1500 年 with defer (transitive) and differ (intransitive). 同源词：Differed; differing.

example.en: The twins differ greatly in personality despite their identical appearance.
example.zh: 这对双胞胎外貌相同，性格却大相径庭。

definitionLines: n. 差别，差异；分歧，争论
entries.definition: n. 差别，差异；分歧，争论
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French difference (12c.) "difference, distinction; argument, dispute," from Latin differentia "diversity, difference," from differentem (nominative differens), present participle of differre "to set apart" (see differ). Sense of "a quarrel" first attested late 14c. Colloquial phrase what's the diff? first recorded 1896.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 difference (12 世纪) "difference, distinction; argument, dispute," 源自 拉丁语 differentia "diversity, difference," 源自 differentem (主格 differens), 为 … 的现在分词 differre "to set apart" （参见 differ). 义为 "a quarrel" 最早见于 14 世纪晚期 Colloquial phrase what's the diff? 首见于 1896 年.

example.en: There is a clear difference between what he promised and what he delivered.
example.zh: 他承诺的与他实际兑现的之间有明显的差距。

definitionLines: a. 困难，艰难；难应付的，难满 足的
entries.definition: a. 困难，艰难；难应付的，难满 足的
entries.etymology: c. 1400, apparently a back-formation from difficulty. French has difficile, Latin difficilis. Of persons, "hard to please," from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 似乎 a back-formation 源自 difficulty. 法语 has difficile, 拉丁语 difficilis. Of persons, "hard to please," 源自 1580 年代.

example.en: Learning a new language can be difficult, but it is very rewarding.
example.zh: 学习一门新语言可能很困难，但非常有收获。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French difficulté, from Latin difficultatem (nominative difficultas) "difficulty, distress, poverty," from difficilis "hard," from dis- "not, away from" (see dis-) + facilis "easy" (see facile).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 difficulté, 源自 拉丁语 difficultatem (主格 difficultas) "difficulty, distress, poverty," 源自 difficilis "hard," 源自 dis- "not, away from" （参见 dis-) + facilis "easy" （参见 facile).

example.en: The team faced great difficulty completing the project on time.
example.zh: 团队在按时完成项目方面面临很大的困难。

entries.etymology:
early 14c. (diggen), of uncertain origin, perhaps related to dike and ditch, either via Old French diguer (ultimately from a Germanic source), or directly from an unrecorded Old English word. Native words were deolfan (see delve), grafan (see grave (v.)).

Slang sense of "understand" first recorded 1934 in African-American vernacular, probably based on the notion of "excavate." A slightly varied sense of "appreciate" emerged 1939. Strong past participle dug appeared 16c., but is not etymological. Related: Digging.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初 (diggen), 来源存疑, 或许 related to dike and ditch, either 经由 古法语 diguer (最终源自 a 日耳曼语 source)，或直接源自 an unrecorded 古英语 word. Native words were deolfan （参见 delve), grafan （参见 grave （动）). Slang 语义 "understand" 首见于 1934 年 in African-American vernacular, 可能 based on the 概念 "excavate." A slightly varied 语义 "appreciate" emerged 1939 年. Strong past participle dug appeared 16 世纪, but is not etymological. 同源词：Digging.

example.en: The archaeologists had to dig carefully to uncover the ancient coins.
example.zh: 考古学家必须仔细挖掘才能发现那些古钱币。

entries.definition: v. /n. 消化；领悟；摘要 n. 文摘
entries.etymology: "collection of writing," late 14c., from Latin digesta, from neuter plural of digestus, literally "digested thing," noun use of past participle of digerere "to separate, divide, arrange," from dis- "apart" (see dis-) + gerere "to carry" (see gest).
entries.etymologyZh: "collection of writing," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 digesta, 源自 neuter 为 … 的复数 digestus, 字面义为 "digested thing," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 digerere "to separate, divide, arrange," 源自 dis- "apart" （参见 dis-) + gerere "to carry" （参见 gest).

entries.etymology: 1650s, "pertaining to fingers," from Latin digitalis, from digitus (see digit). Meaning "using numerical digits" is from 1938, especially of computers after c. 1945; in reference to recording or broadcasting, from 1960. Related: Digitize.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "pertaining to fingers," 源自 拉丁语 digitalis, 源自 digitus （参见 digit). 义为 "using numerical digits" 始于 1938 年, 尤指 of computers after 约 1945 年; in reference to recording or broadcasting, 自 1960 年起. 同源词：Digitize.

example.en: He prefers to read digital books rather than printed ones.
example.zh: 他更喜欢阅读电子书而不是印刷书。

entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French dignite "dignity, privilege, honor," from Latin dignitatem (nominative dignitas) "worthiness," from dignus "worth (n.), worthy, proper, fitting" from PIE *dek-no-, from root *dek- "to take, accept" (see decent).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 dignite "dignity, privilege, honor," 源自 拉丁语 dignitatem (主格 dignitas) "worthiness," 源自 dignus "worth (n.), worthy, proper, fitting" 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dek-no-, 源自 root *dek- "to take, accept" （参见 decent).

example.en: Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity and respect.
example.zh: 每个人都应该受到有尊严、有尊重的对待。

entries.etymology: 1520s, from Late Latin dilemma, from Greek dilemma "double proposition," a technical term in rhetoric, from di- "two" + lemma "premise, anything received or taken," from root of lambanein "to take" (see analemma). It should be used only of situations where someone is forced to choose between two alternatives, both unfavorable to him. But even logicians disagree on whether certain situations are dilemmas or mere syllogisms.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 dilemma, 源自 希腊语 dilemma "double proposition," a technical term in rhetoric, 源自 di- "two" + lemma "premise, anything received or taken," 源自 root of lambanein "to take" （参见 analemma). It should be used only of situations where someone is forced to choose between two alternatives, both unfavorable to him. But even logicians disagree on whether certain situations are dilemmas or mere syllogisms.

example.en: The manager faced a dilemma between cutting costs and keeping staff.
example.zh: 这位经理面临削减成本与留住员工之间的两难困境。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French diligent (14c.), from Latin diligentem "attentive, assiduous" (see diligence). Related: Diligently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 diligent (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 diligentem "attentive, assiduous" （参见 diligence). 同源词：Diligently.

entries.definition: a.稀释的；淡的 vt. 稀释；冲淡；削弱 vi. 变稀薄；变淡
entries.etymology: 1550s, from Latin dilutus, past participle of diluere "dissolve, wash away, dilute," from dis- "apart" + -luere, comb. form of lavere "to wash" (see lave). Related: Diluted; diluting. As an adjective from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 拉丁语 dilutus, 为 … 的过去分词 diluere "dissolve, wash away, dilute," 源自 dis- "apart" + -luere, comb. form of lavere "to wash" （参见 lave). 同源词：Diluted; diluting. 作形容词时 源自 约 1600 年.

entries.etymology: Old English dimm "dark, gloomy, obscure," from Proto-Germanic *dimbaz (source also of Old Norse dimmr, Old Frisian dim, Old High German timber "dark, black, somber"). Not known outside Germanic. Slang sense of "stupid" is from 1892. Related: Dimly; dimness.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dimm "dark, gloomy, obscure," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dimbaz (source also of 古北欧语 dimmr, 古弗里西语 dim, 古高地德语 timber "dark, black, somber"). Not known outside 日耳曼语. Slang 语义 "stupid" 始于 1892 年. 同源词：Dimly; dimness.

example.en: The hallway was so dim that she could barely see the steps.
example.zh: 走廊太昏暗了，她几乎看不见台阶。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "measurement, size," from Latin dimensionem (nominative dimensio) "a measuring," noun of action from past participle stem of dimetri "to measure out," from dis- (see dis-) + metiri "to measure" (see measure (v.)). Meaning "any component of a situation" is from 1929. Related: Dimensional; dimensions.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "measurement, size," 源自 拉丁语 dimensionem (主格 dimensio) "a measuring," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of dimetri "to measure out," 源自 dis- （参见 dis-) + metiri "to measure" （参见 measure （动）). 义为 "any component of a situation" 始于 1929 年. 同源词：Dimensional; dimensions.

example.en: The sculpture has an interesting third dimension that surprises visitors.
example.zh: 这件雕塑有一个令访客惊喜的有趣第三维度。

entries.definition: vt. 使减少；使变小 vi. 变小；减少，缩小
entries.etymology:
early 15c., from merger of two obsolete verbs, diminue and minish. Diminue is from Old French diminuer "make small," from Latin diminuere "break into small pieces," variant of deminuere "lessen, diminish," from de- "completely" + minuere "make small" (see minus).

Minish is from Old French menuisier, from Latin minuere. Related: Diminished; diminishes; diminishing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 merger of two 已废 verbs, diminue and minish. Diminue 始于 古法语 diminuer "make small," 源自 拉丁语 diminuere "break into small pieces," 为 … 的变体 deminuere "lessen, diminish," 源自 de- "completely" + minuere "make small" （参见 minus). Minish 始于 古法语 menuisier, 源自 拉丁语 minuere. 同源词：Diminished; diminishes; diminishing.

example.en: Constantly criticizing colleagues in public will only diminish you in the eyes of others.
example.zh: 总是当众批评同事只会让你在别人眼中显得低人一等（贬低你的形象）。

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French disner (Modern French dîner) "to dine, eat, have a meal," originally "take the first meal of the day," from stem of Gallo-Roman *desjunare "to break one's fast," from Vulgar Latin *disjejunare, from dis- "undo" (see dis-) + Late Latin jejunare "to fast," from Latin iejunus "fasting, hungry" (see jejune).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 disner (现代法语 dîner) "to dine, eat, have a meal," 原义为 "take the first meal of the day," 源自 stem of Gallo-Roman *desjunare "to break one's fast," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *disjejunare, 源自 dis- "undo" （参见 dis-) + 晚期拉丁语 jejunare "to fast," 源自 拉丁语 iejunus "fasting, hungry" （参见 jejune).

definitionLines: n. 吃饭；正餐，主餐；宴会
entries.definition: n. 吃饭；正餐，主餐；宴会
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French disner (11c.), originally "breakfast," later "lunch," noun use of infinitive disner (see dine). Always used in English for the main meal of the day; shift from midday to evening began with the fashionable classes. Childish reduplication din-din is attested from 1905.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 disner (11 世纪), 原义为 "breakfast," later "lunch," 为 … 的名词用法 infinitive disner （参见 dine). Always used in English for the main meal of the day; shift 源自 midday to evening began with the fashionable classes. Childish reduplication din-din 见于 1905 年.

example.en: The whole family sat down to a traditional dinner of roast turkey on Thanksgiving.
example.zh: 感恩节那天，全家人坐下来享用传统的烤火鸡正餐。

entries.etymology: Old English dyppan "immerse, baptize by immersion," from Proto-Germanic *duppjan (source also of Old Norse deypa "to dip," Danish døbe "to baptize," Old Frisian depa, Dutch dopen, German taufen, Gothic daupjan "to baptize"), related to Old English diepan "immerse, dip," and perhaps ultimately to deep. As a noun, from 1590s. Sense of "downward slope" is 1708. Meaning "sweet sauce for pudding, etc." first recorded 1825.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dyppan "immerse, baptize by immersion," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *duppjan (source also of 古北欧语 deypa "to dip," Danish døbe "to baptize," 古弗里西语 depa, 荷兰语 dopen, 德语 taufen, Gothic daupjan "to baptize"), related to 古英语 diepan "immerse, dip," and 或许 ultimately to deep. 作名词时, 源自 1590 年代. 义为 "downward slope" is 1708 年. 义为 "sweet sauce for pudding, etc." 首见于 1825 年.

example.en: She liked to dip her biscuit in tea before eating it.
example.zh: 她喜欢在吃饼干前先把它浸一下茶。

entries.etymology: 1640s, "state paper, official document," from Latin diploma, from Greek diploma "license, chart," originally "paper folded double," from diploun "to double, fold over," from diploos "double" (see diploid) + -oma. Specific academic sense is 1680s in English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "state paper, official document," 源自 拉丁语 diploma, 源自 希腊语 diploma "license, chart," 原义为 "paper folded double," 源自 diploun "to double, fold over," 源自 diploos "double" （参见 diploid) + -oma. Specific academic sense is 1680 年代 in English.

entries.etymology: 1813, from French diplomate, a back-formation from diplomatique (see diplomatic) on model of aristocrate from aristocratique.
entries.etymologyZh: 1813 年, 源自 法语 diplomate, a back-formation 源自 diplomatique （参见 diplomatic) on model of aristocrate 源自 aristocratique.

example.en: The experienced diplomat negotiated a peace agreement overnight.
example.zh: 这位经验丰富的外交官连夜谈判达成了和平协议。

definitionLines: a. /ad. 径直（的），直接（的）；率 直（的）
vt. （at/against/to） 把•…对 准……；指示；管理，指导
entries.definition: a. /ad. 径直（的），直接（的）；率 直（的） vt. （at/against/to） 把•…对 准……；指示；管理，指导
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to write (to someone), to address," from Latin directus "straight," past participle of dirigere "set straight," from dis- "apart" (see dis-) + regere "to direct, to guide, keep straight" (see regal). Compare dress; address.

Meaning "to govern, regulate" is from c. 1500; "to order, ordain" is from 1650s. Sense of "to write the destination on the outside of a letter" is from 16c. Of plays, films, etc., from 1913. Related: Directed; directing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to write (to someone), to address," 源自 拉丁语 directus "straight," 为 … 的过去分词 dirigere "set straight," 源自 dis- "apart" （参见 dis-) + regere "to direct, to guide, keep straight" （参见 regal). 对比 dress; address. 义为 "to govern, regulate" 始于 约 1500 年; "to order, ordain" 始于 1650 年代. 义为 "to write the destination on the outside of a letter" 始于 16 世纪 Of plays, films, etc., 自 1913 年起. 同源词：Directed; directing.

example.en: The manager gave a direct and blunt assessment of the team's poor performance.
example.zh: 经理对团队糟糕表现给出了直接而坦率的评估。

definitionLines: n. 方向，方位；指导，指令； （pl.用法说明
entries.definition: n. 方向，方位；指导，指令； （pl.用法说明
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "orderly arrangement;" c. 1500 as "action of directing," from Latin directionem (nominative directio), noun of action from past participle stem of dirigere (see direct (v.)). Meaning "course pursued by a moving object" is from 1660s. Related: Directional.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "orderly arrangement;" 约 1500 年 as "action of directing," 源自 拉丁语 directionem (主格 directio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of dirigere （参见 direct （动）). 义为 "course pursued by a moving object" 始于 1660 年代. 同源词：Directional.

example.en: The compass gave us a sense of direction when we got lost in the forest.
example.zh: 当我们在森林中迷路时，指南针给了我们方向感。

definitionLines: ad.直接地，直截了当地；立即， 马上
entries.definition: ad.直接地，直截了当地；立即， 马上
entries.etymology: 1510s, "in a straight line," from direct (adj.) + -ly (2). Figurative use is slightly earlier (c. 1500). Meaning "at once, immediately in time" (c. 1600) is from earlier sense of "without intermediate steps" (1520s).
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "in a straight line," 源自 direct （形） + -ly (2). Figurative use is slightly earlier (约 1500 年). 义为 "at once, immediately in time" (约 1600 年) 始于 earlier 语义 "without intermediate steps" (1520 年代).

example.en: You should contact the manager directly instead of going through his assistant.
example.zh: 你应该直接联系经理，而不是通过他的助手。

definitionLines: n. 主任，处长，局长；主管，董 事；导演
entries.definition: n. 主任，处长，局长；主管，董 事；导演
entries.etymology: late 15c., "a guide," from Anglo-French directour, French directeur, agent noun from Latin dirigere (see direct (v.)). Corporate sense is from 1630s; theatrical sense from 1911.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "a guide," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 directour, 法语 directeur, agent 名词 源自 拉丁语 dirigere （参见 direct （动）). Corporate sense 始于 1630 年代; theatrical sense 自 1911 年起.

example.en: The board appointed a new director to lead the marketing department.
example.zh: 董事会任命了一位新主管来领导市场部门。

entries.etymology: 15c. metathesis of Middle English drit, drytt "mud, dirt, dung" (c. 1300), from Old Norse drit, cognate with Old English dritan "to void excrement," from Proto-Germanic *dritan (source also of Dutch drijten, Old High German trizan). Used abusively of persons from c. 1300. Meaning "gossip" first attested 1926 (in Hemingway); dirt bike is 1960s. Dirt-cheap is from 1821. Dirt road attested by 1852.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪 metathesis of 中古英语 drit, drytt "mud, dirt, dung" (约 1300 年), 源自 古北欧语 drit, 与 … 同源 古英语 dritan "to void excrement," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dritan (source also of 荷兰语 drijten, 古高地德语 trizan). Used abusively of persons 源自 约 1300 年. 义为 "gossip" 最早见于 1926 年 (in Hemingway); dirt bike is 1960 年代. Dirt-cheap 始于 1821 年. Dirt road attested 截至 1852 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1500, from dirt + -y (2). Earlier dritty (late 14c.). Meaning "smutty, morally unclean" is from 1590s. Of colors, from 1690s. Dirty linen "personal or familial secrets" is first recorded 1860s. Dirty work in the figurative sense is from 1764; dirty trick is from 1670s. The dirty look someone gives you is from 1928; dirty old man "superannuated lecher" is from 1932. Related: dirtiness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, 源自 dirt + -y (2). Earlier dritty (14 世纪晚期). 义为 "smutty, morally unclean" 始于 1590 年代. Of colors, 源自 1690 年代. Dirty linen "personal or familial secrets" is 首见于 1860 年代. Dirty work in the figurative sense 始于 1764 年; dirty trick 始于 1670 年代. The dirty look someone gives you 始于 1928 年; dirty old man "superannuated lecher" 始于 1932 年. 同源词：dirtiness.

example.en: The mechanic's uniform was covered in dirty grease stains.
example.zh: 机械师的工作服上布满了污秽的油脂污渍。

entries.etymology: "incapacitated," 1630s, past participle adjective from disable. Earlier it meant "legally disqualified" (mid-15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: "incapacitated," 1630 年代, past participle 形容词 源自 disable. Earlier it meant "legally disqualified" (15 世纪中期).

example.en: The new ramp was built to help disabled visitors access the building.
example.zh: 新建的坡道是为了帮助残障访客进入建筑。

definitionLines: n. 不利，不利条件；损失，损害
entries.definition: n. 不利，不利条件；损失，损害
entries.etymology: late 14c., disavauntage, from Old French desavantage (13c.), from des- (see dis-) + avantage (see advantage).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, disavauntage, 源自 古法语 desavantage (13 世纪), 源自 des- （参见 dis-) + avantage （参见 advantage).

definitionLines: vi.（with ... on/about）不一 致；不适宜；不同意；争执
entries.definition: vi.（with ... on/about）不一 致；不适宜；不同意；争执
entries.etymology: late 15c., "refuse to assent," from Old French desagreer (12c.), from des- (see dis-) + agreer (see agree). Related: Disagreed; disagreeing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "refuse to assent," 源自 古法语 desagreer (12 世纪), 源自 des- （参见 dis-) + agreer （参见 agree). 同源词：Disagreed; disagreeing.

example.en: The two scientists disagree sharply on the interpretation of the lab results.
example.zh: 两位科学家在实验结果的解读上存在明显分歧。

entries.etymology: early 15c., disaperen, from dis- "do the opposite of" + appear. Earlier was disparish (early 15c.), from French disparaiss-, stem of disparaître. Transitive sense. "cause to disappear," is from 1897 in chemistry; by 1948 of inconvenient persons. Related: Disappeared; disappearing; disappears. Slang disappearing act is originally of magic shows; in figurative sense of "getting away" first attested 1913.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, disaperen, 源自 dis- "do the opposite of" + appear. Earlier was disparish (15 世纪初), 源自 法语 disparaiss-, stem of disparaître. Transitive sense. "cause to disappear," 始于 1897 年 in chemistry; 截至 1948 年 of inconvenient persons. 同源词：Disappeared; disappearing; disappears. Slang disappearing act is 原义为 of magic shows; in figurative 语义 "getting away" 最早见于 1913 年.

example.en: The morning fog slowly began to disappear as the sun climbed higher in the sky.
example.zh: 随着太阳升得越来越高，晨雾开始慢慢消散。

entries.etymology:
early 15c., "dispossess of appointed office," from Middle French desappointer (14c.) "undo the appointment, remove from office," from des- (see dis-) + appointer "appoint" (see appoint).

Modern sense of "to frustrate expectations" (late 15c.) is from secondary meaning of "fail to keep an appointment." Related: Disappointed; disappointing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "dispossess of appointed office," 源自 中古法语 desappointer (14 世纪) "undo the appointment, remove from office," 源自 des- （参见 dis-) + appointer "appoint" （参见 appoint). 现代 语义 "to frustrate expectations" (15 世纪晚期) 始于 secondary 意为 of "fail to keep an appointment." 同源词：Disappointed; disappointing.

definitionLines: vt. 解除武装；缓和；裁军
vi. 放下武器；裁减军备
entries.definition: vt. 解除武装；缓和；裁军 vi. 放下武器；裁减军备
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French desarmer (11c.), from des- (see dis-) + armer "to arm" (see arm (v.)). The figurative sense is slightly earlier in English than the literal. Related: Disarmed; disarming.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 desarmer (11 世纪), 源自 des- （参见 dis-) + armer "to arm" （参见 arm （动）). The figurative sense is slightly earlier in English than the literal. 同源词：Disarmed; disarming.

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Middle French désastre (1560s), from Italian disastro "ill-starred," from dis-, here merely pejorative (see dis-) + astro "star, planet," from Latin astrum, from Greek astron (see star (n.)). The sense is astrological, of a calamity blamed on an unfavorable position of a planet.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 désastre (1560 年代), 源自 意大利语 disastro "ill-starred," 源自 dis-, here merely pejorative （参见 dis-) + astro "star, planet," 源自 拉丁语 astrum, 源自 希腊语 astron （参见 star （名）). The sense is astrological, of a calamity blamed on an unfavorable position of a planet.

example.en: The earthquake was one of the worst natural disasters to strike the region in the past fifty years.
example.zh: 这场地震是过去五十年来袭击该地区最严重的自然灾害之一。

entries.etymology: Latinate spelling preferred in British English for most uses of disk (q.v.). American English tends to use it in the musical recording sense; originally of phonograph records, recently of compact discs. Hence, discophile "enthusiast for gramophone recordings" (1940).
entries.etymologyZh: Latinate spelling preferred in British English for most uses of disk (q.v.). American English tends to use it in the musical recording sense; 原义为 of phonograph records, recently of compact discs. Hence, discophile "enthusiast for gramophone recordings" (1940 年).

entries.definition: v. 丢弃；抛弃；放弃 vi. 放弃
entries.etymology: 1590s, literally "to throw a card away," from dis- "away" + card (n.). Figurative use (in a non-gaming sense) is first recorded 1580s. In the card-playing sense, decard is attested by 1550s. Related: Discarded; discarding. As a noun, from 1742.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 字面义为 "to throw a card away," 源自 dis- "away" + card （名）. Figurative use (in a non-gaming sense) is 首见于 1580 年代. In the card-playing sense, decard is attested by 1550 年代. 同源词：Discarded; discarding. 作名词时, 自 1742 年起.

example.en: He chose to discard the old plan and start fresh with a new approach.
example.zh: 他选择放弃旧计划，以新的方式重新开始。

definitionLines: v./n. 卸（货），解除，排出；释 放，允许离开；放电
entries.definition: v./n. 卸（货），解除，排出；释 放，允许离开；放电
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "to exempt, exonerate, release," from Old French deschargier (12c., Modern French décharger) "to unload, discharge," from Late Latin discarricare, from dis- "do the opposite of" (see dis-) + carricare "load" (see charge (v.)).

Meaning "to unload, to free from" is late 14c. Of weapons, from 1550s. The electrical sense is first attested 1748. Meaning "to fulfill, to perform one's duties" is from c. 1400. Related: Discharged; discharging.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to exempt, exonerate, release," 源自 古法语 deschargier (12 世纪, 现代法语 décharger) "to unload, discharge," 源自 晚期拉丁语 discarricare, 源自 dis- "do the opposite of" （参见 dis-) + carricare "load" （参见 charge （动）). 义为 "to unload, to free from" is 14 世纪晚期 Of weapons, 源自 1550 年代. The electrical sense is 最早见于 1748 年. 义为 "to fulfill, to perform one's duties" 始于 约 1400 年. 同源词：Discharged; discharging.

example.en: The hospital will discharge the patient once the test results come back normal.
example.zh: 一旦检测结果正常，医院将允许患者出院。

entries.definition: n.纪律，风纪；学科；训练 vt.训练，训导；惩罚
entries.etymology:
early 13c., "penitential chastisement; punishment," from Old French descepline (11c.) "discipline, physical punishment; teaching; suffering; martyrdom," and directly from Latin disciplina "instruction given, teaching, learning, knowledge," also "object of instruction, knowledge, science, military discipline," from discipulus (see disciple (n.)).

Sense of "treatment that corrects or punishes" is from notion of "order necessary for instruction." The Latin word is glossed in Old English by þeodscipe.
Meaning "branch of instruction or education" is first recorded late 14c. Meaning "military training" is from late 15c.; that of "orderly conduct as a result of training" is from c. 1500.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "penitential chastisement; punishment," 源自 古法语 descepline (11 世纪) "discipline, physical punishment; teaching; suffering; martyrdom," and 直接源自 拉丁语 disciplina "instruction given, teaching, learning, knowledge," also "object of instruction, knowledge, science, military discipline," 源自 discipulus （参见 disciple （名）). 义为 "treatment that corrects or punishes" 始于 概念 "order necessary for instruction." The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by þeodscipe. 义为 "branch of instruction or education" is 首见于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "military training" 始于 15 世纪晚期; that of "orderly conduct as a result of training" 始于 约 1500 年.

example.en: The army values strict discipline above all and expects every soldier to follow orders without question.
example.zh: 军队最重视严格纪律，要求每位士兵毫无疑问地服从命令。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French desclos "open, exposed, plain, explicit," past participle of desclore (Modern French déclore) "open, break open, unlock, reveal," from des- (see dis-) + clore "to close" (see close (v.)). Related: Disclosed; disclosing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 desclos "open, exposed, plain, explicit," 为 … 的过去分词 desclore (现代法语 déclore) "open, break open, unlock, reveal," 源自 des- （参见 dis-) + clore "to close" （参见 close （动）). 同源词：Disclosed; disclosing.

example.en: The journalist refused to disclose her source to the authorities.
example.zh: 这位记者拒绝向当局透露其消息来源。

entries.etymology: 1964, American English shortening of discotheque; sense extended by 1972 to the kind of music played there.
entries.etymologyZh: 1964 年, American English shortening of discotheque; sense extended 截至 1972 年 to the kind of music played there.

entries.definition: n. 折扣；贴现（率） vt. 打折扣
entries.etymology: 1620s, "abatement," alteration of 16c. French descompte, from Medieval Latin discomputus (source of Italian disconto), from discomputare (see discount (v.)). Meaning "deduction for early payment" is from 1680s; meaning "reduction in the price of goods" attested by 1837.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "abatement," alteration of 16 世纪 法语 descompte, 源自 中古拉丁语 discomputus (source of 意大利语 disconto), 源自 discomputare （参见 discount （动）). 义为 "deduction for early payment" 始于 1680 年代; 意为 "reduction in the price of goods" attested 截至 1837 年.

example.en: The store offered a ten percent discount on all winter clothing.
example.zh: 这家店对所有冬季服装提供九折优惠。

definitionLines: vt. 使失去信心，使泄气
entries.definition: vt. 使失去信心，使泄气
entries.etymology: mid-15c., discoragen, from Middle French descourager, from Old French descoragier, from des- "away" (see dis-) + corage (see courage). Related: Discouraged; discouragement; discouraging.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, discoragen, 源自 中古法语 descourager, 源自 古法语 descoragier, 源自 des- "away" （参见 dis-) + corage （参见 courage). 同源词：Discouraged; discouragement; discouraging.

example.en: Repeated failures can discourage even the most ambitious students from pursuing their goals.
example.zh: 反复失败甚至会让最有抱负的学生对追求目标感到沮丧。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "divulge, reveal, disclose," from Old French descovrir "uncover, unroof, unveil, reveal, betray," from Late Latin discooperire, from Latin dis- "opposite of" (see dis-) + cooperire "to cover up" (see cover). At first with a sense of betrayal or malicious exposure (discoverer originally meant "informant"); the meaning "to obtain knowledge or sight of what was not known" is from 1550s. Related: Discovered; discovering.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "divulge, reveal, disclose," 源自 古法语 descovrir "uncover, unroof, unveil, reveal, betray," 源自 晚期拉丁语 discooperire, 源自 拉丁语 dis- "opposite of" （参见 dis-) + cooperire "to cover up" （参见 cover). At first with a 语义 betrayal or malicious exposure (discoverer 原义为 meant "informant"); the 意为 "to obtain knowledge or sight of what was not known" 始于 1550 年代. 同源词：Discovered; discovering.

example.en: Researchers discovered that the ancient ruins were far older than originally thought.
example.zh: 研究人员发现这些古代遗址比最初认为的要古老得多。

entries.etymology: 1550s, "fact of discovering;" see discover + -y (1). Earlier in this sense was discovering (mid-14c.). Meaning "that which is discovered" is from 1630s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "fact of discovering;" 参见 discover + -y (1). Earlier in this sense was discovering (14 世纪中期). 义为 "that which is discovered" 始于 1630 年代.

example.en: The discovery of penicillin changed the course of modern medicine.
example.zh: 青霉素的发现改变了现代医学的进程。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "morally discerning, prudent, circumspect," from Old French discret "discreet, sensible, intelligent, wise," from Latin discretus "separated, distinct," in Medieval Latin "discerning, careful," past participle of discernere "distinguish" (see discern). Meaning "separate, distinct" in English is late 14c.

Spellings discrete and nativized discreet co-existed until after c. 1600, when discreet became the common word for "careful, prudent," and discrete was maintained in philosophy, medicine, music and other disciplines that remembered Latin and made effort to obey it. Related: Discreetly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "morally discerning, prudent, circumspect," 源自 古法语 discret "discreet, sensible, intelligent, wise," 源自 拉丁语 discretus "separated, distinct," in 中古拉丁语 "discerning, careful," 为 … 的过去分词 discernere "distinguish" （参见 discern). 义为 "separate, distinct" in English is 14 世纪晚期 Spellings discrete and nativized discreet co-existed until after 约 1600 年, when discreet became the common word for "careful, prudent," and discrete was maintained in philosophy, medicine, music and other disciplines that remembered 拉丁语 and made effort to obey it. 同源词：Discreetly.

entries.etymology: mid-15c. (discrepance), from Latin discrepantia "discordance, discrepancy," from discrepantem (nominative discrepans), present participle of discrepare "sound differently, differ," from dis- "apart, off" (see dis-) + crepare "to rattle, crack" (see raven). Related: Discrepancies.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期 (discrepance), 源自 拉丁语 discrepantia "discordance, discrepancy," 源自 discrepantem (主格 discrepans), 为 … 的现在分词 discrepare "sound differently, differ," 源自 dis- "apart, off" （参见 dis-) + crepare "to rattle, crack" （参见 raven). 同源词：Discrepancies.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "to examine, investigate," from Latin discuss-, past participle stem of discutere "to dash to pieces, agitate," in Late Latin and Vulgar Latin also "to discuss, investigate" (see discussion). Meaning "examine by argument, debate" is from mid-15c. Related: Discussed; discussing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to examine, investigate," 源自 拉丁语 discuss-, past participle stem of discutere "to dash to pieces, agitate," in 晚期拉丁语 and 通俗拉丁语 also "to discuss, investigate" （参见 discussion). 义为 "examine by argument, debate" 始于 15 世纪中期 同源词：Discussed; discussing.

example.en: The team will discuss the new project plan in tomorrow's meeting.
example.zh: 团队将在明天的会议上讨论新项目计划。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "discomfort, inconvenience," from Old French desaise "lack, want; discomfort, distress; trouble, misfortune; disease, sickness," from des- "without, away" (see dis-) + aise "ease" (see ease). Sense of "sickness, illness" in English first recorded late 14c.; the word still sometimes was used in its literal sense early 17c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "discomfort, inconvenience," 源自 古法语 desaise "lack, want; discomfort, distress; trouble, misfortune; disease, sickness," 源自 des- "without, away" （参见 dis-) + aise "ease" （参见 ease). 义为 "sickness, illness" in English 首见于 14 世纪晚期; the word still 有时 was used in its literal sense 17 世纪初

example.en: Researchers are still looking for a cure for this rare inherited disease.
example.zh: 研究人员仍在寻找这种罕见遗传疾病的治疗方法。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "graceless," opposite of graceful; see dis- + graceful. Meaning "full of disgrace" (1590s) is from disgrace + -ful. Related: Disgracefully.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "graceless," opposite of graceful; 参见 dis- + graceful. 义为 "full of disgrace" (1590 年代) 始于 disgrace + -ful. 同源词：Disgracefully.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French desguiser (11c.) "disguise, change one's appearance," from des- "away, off" (see dis-) + guise "style, appearance" (see guise). Originally primarily "to put out of one's usual manner" (of dress, etc.). Oldest sense preserved in phrase disguised with liquor (1560s).
Related: Disguised; disguising.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 desguiser (11 世纪) "disguise, change one's appearance," 源自 des- "away, off" （参见 dis-) + guise "style, appearance" （参见 guise). Originally primarily "to put out of one's usual manner" (of dress, etc.). Oldest sense preserved in phrase disguised with liquor (1560 年代). 同源词：Disguised; disguising.

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Middle French desgoust "strong dislike, repugnance," literally "distaste" (16c., Modern French dégoût), from desgouster "have a distaste for," from des- "opposite of" (see dis-) + gouster "taste," from Latin gustare "to taste" (see gusto).
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 中古法语 desgoust "strong dislike, repugnance," 字面义为 "distaste" (16 世纪, 现代法语 dégoût), 源自 desgouster "have a distaste for," 源自 des- "opposite of" （参见 dis-) + gouster "taste," 源自 拉丁语 gustare "to taste" （参见 gusto).

entries.etymology: Old English disc "plate, bowl, platter," from Latin discus "dish, platter, quoit," from Greek diskos "disk, platter" (see disk (n.)). A common West Germanic borrowing; Old High German borrowed the word as tisc "plate," but German tisch now means "table," in common with other later Romanic forms (such as Italian desco, French dais). Meaning "particular variety of food served" is first recorded mid-15c. Meaning "what one likes" is c. 1900; that of "attractive woman" is 1920s. Meaning "concave reflector or antenna" attested from 1948.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 disc "plate, bowl, platter," 源自 拉丁语 discus "dish, platter, quoit," 源自 希腊语 diskos "disk, platter" （参见 disk （名）). A common West 日耳曼语 borrowing; 古高地德语 borrowed the word as tisc "plate," but 德语 tisch 现在 means "table," in common with other later Romanic forms (such as 意大利语 desco, 法语 dais). 义为 "particular variety of food served" is 首见于 15 世纪中期 义为 "what one likes" is 约 1900 年; that of "attractive woman" is 1920 年代. 义为 "concave reflector or antenna" attested 自 1948 年起.

example.en: The chef prepared a special dish using fresh seafood and herbs.
example.zh: 厨师用新鲜海鲜和香草烹制了一道特别的菜肴。

entries.definition: vt. 不喜欢，厌恶 n. 嫌恶，反感，不喜爱
entries.etymology: 1540s (implied in disliking), hybrid which ousted native mislike as the opposite of like (v.). Related: Disliked; disliking. English in 16c. also had the excellent dislove "hate, cease to love," but it did not survive.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代 (implied in disliking), hybrid which ousted 本族 mislike as the opposite of like （动）. 同源词：Disliked; disliking. English in 16 世纪 also had the excellent dislove "hate, cease to love," but it did not survive.

entries.definition: n. 沮丧，灰心；惊慌 vt.使惊慌；使沮丧
entries.etymology: late 13c., dismaien, from Old French *desmaier (attested only in past participle dismaye), from Latin de- intensive prefix + Old French esmaier "to trouble, disturb," from Vulgar Latin *exmagare "divest of power or ability" (source of Italian smagare "to weaken, dismay, discourage"), from ex- (see ex-) + Germanic stem *mag- "power, ability" (source also of Old High German magen "to be powerful or able;" see may (v.)). Spanish desmayer "to be dispirited" is a loan word from Old French. Related: Dismayed; dismaying.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, dismaien, 源自 古法语 *desmaier (attested only in past participle dismaye), 源自 拉丁语 de- intensive prefix + 古法语 esmaier "to trouble, disturb," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *exmagare "divest of power or ability" (source of 意大利语 smagare "to weaken, dismay, discourage"), 源自 ex- （参见 ex-) + 日耳曼语 stem *mag- "power, ability" (source also of 古高地德语 magen "to be powerful or able;" 参见 may （动）). 西班牙语 desmayer "to be dispirited" is a loan word 源自 古法语. 同源词：Dismayed; dismaying.

definitionLines: vt. 不再考虑；免职，解雇，开 除；解散
entries.definition: vt. 不再考虑；免职，解雇，开 除；解散
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin dimissus, past participle of dimittere "send away, send different ways; break up, discharge; renounce, abandon," from dis- "apart, away" (see dis-) + mittere "send, let go" (see mission). Prefix altered by analogy with many dis- verbs. Dismit, in the same sense, is attested from late 14c. Related: Dismissed; dismissing.
