entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 dimissus, 为 … 的过去分词 dimittere "send away, send different ways; break up, discharge; renounce, abandon," 源自 dis- "apart, away" （参见 dis-) + mittere "send, let go" （参见 mission). Prefix altered by analogy with many dis- verbs. Dismit, in the same sense, 见于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Dismissed; dismissing.

example.en: The manager was dismissed following the financial scandal.
example.zh: 财务丑闻发生后，这位经理被正式解雇了。

definitionLines: n. 紊乱，混乱；骚动，骚乱；疾 病，失调
entries.definition: n. 紊乱，混乱；骚动，骚乱；疾 病，失调
entries.etymology: late 15c., from dis- "not" (see dis-) + the verb order (v.). Replaced earlier disordeine (mid-14c.), from Old French desordainer, from Medieval Latin disordinare "throw into disorder," from Latin ordinare "to order, regulate" (see ordain). Related: Disordered; disordering.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 dis- "not" （参见 dis-) + the 动词 order （动）. Replaced earlier disordeine (14 世纪中期), 源自 古法语 desordainer, 源自 中古拉丁语 disordinare "throw into disorder," 源自 拉丁语 ordinare "to order, regulate" （参见 ordain). 同源词：Disordered; disordering.

example.en: He was diagnosed with a rare eating disorder at the age of fifteen.
example.zh: 他在十五岒时被诊断出患有一种罕见的饮食失调症。

entries.definition: vt. 派遣，发送 n. 派遣；急件
entries.etymology: 1510s, "to send off in a hurry," from a word in Spanish (despachar "expedite, hasten") or Italian (dispacciare "to dispatch"). For first element, see dis-. The exact source of the second element has been proposed as Vulgar Latin *pactare "to fasten, fix" or *pactiare, or as Latin -pedicare "to entrap" (from Latin pedica "shackle;" see impeach); and the Spanish and Italian words seem to be related to (perhaps opposites of) Old Provençal empachar "impede." See OED for full discussion. Meaning "to get rid of by killing" is attested from 1520s. Related: Dispatched; dispatching. As a noun, from 1540s, originally "dismissal;" sense of "a message sent speedily" is first attested 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "to send off in a hurry," 源自 a word in 西班牙语 (despachar "expedite, hasten") or 意大利语 (dispacciare "to dispatch"). For first element, 参见 dis-. The exact source of the second element has been proposed as 通俗拉丁语 *pactare "to fasten, fix" or *pactiare，或as 拉丁语 -pedicare "to entrap" (源自 拉丁语 pedica "shackle;" 参见 impeach); and the 西班牙语 and 意大利语 words seem to be related to (或许 opposites of) Old Provençal empachar "impede." See OED for full discussion. 义为 "to get rid of by killing" 见于 1520 年代. 同源词：Dispatched; dispatching. 作名词时, 源自 1540 年代, 原义为 "dismissal;" 语义 "a message sent speedily" is 最早见于 1580 年代.

definitionLines: vt. 分配，分发；执行；免除
entries.definition: vt. 分配，分发；执行；免除 vi. 免除，豁免
entries.etymology:
early 14c., from Old French dispenser "give out" (13c.), from Latin dispensare "disburse, administer, distribute (by weight)," frequentative of dispendere "pay out," from dis- "out" (see dis-) + pendere "to pay, weigh" (see pendant).

In Medieval Latin, dispendere was used in the ecclesiastical sense of "grant license to do what is forbidden or omit what is required" (a power of popes, bishops, etc.), and thus acquired a sense of "grant remission from punishment or exemption from law," hence "to do away with" (1570s), "do without" (c. 1600). Older sense is preserved in dispensary. Related: Dispensed; dispensing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 dispenser "give out" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 dispensare "disburse, administer, distribute (by weight)," 为 … 的反复体 dispendere "pay out," 源自 dis- "out" （参见 dis-) + pendere "to pay, weigh" （参见 pendant). In 中古拉丁语, dispendere was used in the ecclesiastical 语义 "grant license to do what is forbidden or omit what is required" (a power of popes, bishops, etc.), and thus acquired a 语义 "grant remission from punishment or exemption from law," hence "to do away with" (1570 年代), "do without" (约 1600 年). Older sense is preserved in dispensary. 同源词：Dispensed; dispensing.

entries.definition: vt. 使散开；分散；传播 vi. 分散
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin dispersus, past participle of dispergere "to scatter," from dis- "apart, in every direction" (see dis-) + spargere "to scatter" (see sparse). The Latin word is glossed in Old English by tostregdan. Related: Dispersed; dispersing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 dispersus, 为 … 的过去分词 dispergere "to scatter," 源自 dis- "apart, in every direction" （参见 dis-) + spargere "to scatter" （参见 sparse). The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by tostregdan. 同源词：Dispersed; dispersing.

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French desplacer (15c.), from des- (see dis-) + placer "to place." Related: Displaced; displacing. Displaced person "refugee" is from 1944.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 desplacer (15 世纪), 源自 des- （参见 dis-) + placer "to place." 同源词：Displaced; displacing. Displaced person "refugee" 始于 1944 年.

entries.etymology:
late 13c., "unfurl" (a banner, etc.), from Old French desploiir (Modern French déployer) "unfold, unfasten, spread out" (of knots, sealed letters, etc.), from Latin displicare "to scatter," from dis- "un-, apart" (see dis-) + plicare "to fold" (see ply (v.1)).

Properly of sails or flags (and unconnected to play); meaning "reveal, exhibit" is late 14c. Related: Displayed; displaying.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "unfurl" (a banner, etc.), 源自 古法语 desploiir (现代法语 déployer) "unfold, unfasten, spread out" (of knots, sealed letters, etc.), 源自 拉丁语 displicare "to scatter," 源自 dis- "un-, apart" （参见 dis-) + plicare "to fold" （参见 ply (v.1)). Properly of sails or flags (and unconnected to play); 意为 "reveal, exhibit" is 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Displayed; displaying.

example.en: The museum will display ancient artifacts from Egypt next spring.
example.zh: 博物馆明年春天将展出来自埃及的古代文物。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French disposer (13c.) "arrange, order, control, regulate" (influenced in form by poser "to place"), from Latin disponere "put in order, arrange, distribute," from dis- "apart" (see dis-) + ponere "to put, place" (past participle positus; see position (n.)). Related: Disposed; disposing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 disposer (13 世纪) "arrange, order, control, regulate" (influenced in form by poser "to place"), 源自 拉丁语 disponere "put in order, arrange, distribute," 源自 dis- "apart" （参见 dis-) + ponere "to put, place" (past participle positus; 参见 position （名）). 同源词：Disposed; disposing.

entries.definition: v. 争论，辩驳，争吵 n. 争论，争端
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French desputer (12c.) "dispute, fight over, contend for, discuss," from Latin disputare "weigh, examine, discuss, argue, explain," from dis- "separately" (see dis-) + putare "to count, consider," originally "to prune" (see pave).

Used in Vulgate in sense of "to argue, contend with words." Related: Disputable; disputed; disputing. The noun is not certainly recorded before 1590s (disputacioun in that sense is from late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 desputer (12 世纪) "dispute, fight over, contend for, discuss," 源自 拉丁语 disputare "weigh, examine, discuss, argue, explain," 源自 dis- "separately" （参见 dis-) + putare "to count, consider," 原义为 "to prune" （参见 pave). Used in Vulgate in 语义 "to argue, contend with words." 同源词：Disputable; disputed; disputing. The 名词 is not certainly recorded before 1590 年代 (disputacioun in that sense 始于 14 世纪晚期).

example.en: The two countries are in a trade dispute over import tariffs.
example.zh: 两国就进口关税问题陷入贸易争端。

definitionLines: vt. 忽视；不理；漠视；不顾
entries.definition: vt. 忽视；不理；漠视；不顾 n. 忽视；不尊重
entries.etymology: 1640s, from dis- + regard. Related: Disregarded; disregarding. As a noun, from 1660s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 dis- + regard. 同源词：Disregarded; disregarding. 作名词时, 源自 1660 年代.

definitionLines: vt. 使分裂；使瓦解；使中断；使 陷于混乱；破坏
entries.definition: vt. 使分裂；使瓦解；使中断；使 陷于混乱；破坏
entries.etymology: 1650s, but rare before c. 1820, from Latin disruptus, past participle of disrumpere (see disruption). Or perhaps a back-formation from disruption. Related: Disrupted; disrupting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, but rare before 约 1820 年, 源自 拉丁语 disruptus, 为 … 的过去分词 disrumpere （参见 disruption). Or 或许 a back-formation 源自 disruption. 同源词：Disrupted; disrupting.

example.en: Heavy snowfall threatened to disrupt train services across the region.
example.zh: 大雪威胁到该地区各地的火车服务中断。

definitionLines: v.溶解，融化；解除，解散，取消
entries.definition: v.溶解，融化；解除，解散，取消
entries.etymology: late 14c. (transitive and intransitive) "to break up" (of material substances), from Latin dissolvere "to loosen up, break apart," from dis- "apart" (see dis-) + solvere "to loose, loosen" (see solve). Meaning "to disband" (an assembly) is early 15c. Related: Dissolved; dissolving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 (transitive and intransitive) "to break up" (of material substances), 源自 拉丁语 dissolvere "to loosen up, break apart," 源自 dis- "apart" （参见 dis-) + solvere "to loose, loosen" （参见 solve). 义为 "to disband" (an assembly) is 15 世纪初 同源词：Dissolved; dissolving.

example.en: Sugar will dissolve quickly in hot water, making it easy to prepare the syrup.
example.zh: 糖在热水中会迅速溶解，使糖浆的制备变得容易。

definitionLines: n. 距离，路程；远方，远处
entries.definition: n. 距离，路程；远方，远处
entries.etymology:
late 13c., "quarrel, estrangement, discord, strife," from Old French destance (13c.), from Latin distantia "a standing apart," from distantem (nominative distans) "standing apart, separate, distant," present participle of distare "stand apart," from dis- "apart, off" (see dis-) + stare "to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand, set down, make or be firm" (see stet).

Meaning "remoteness, space between things or places" is late 14c. The figurative sense of "aloofness" is the same as in stand-offish. Phrase go the distance (1930s) seems to be originally from the prize ring, where the word meant "scheduled length of a bout."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "quarrel, estrangement, discord, strife," 源自 古法语 destance (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 distantia "a standing apart," 源自 distantem (主格 distans) "standing apart, separate, distant," 为 … 的现在分词 distare "stand apart," 源自 dis- "apart, off" （参见 dis-) + stare "to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand, set down, make or be firm" （参见 stet). 义为 "remoteness, space between things or places" is 14 世纪晚期 The figurative 语义 "aloofness" is the same as in stand-offish. Phrase go the distance (1930 年代) seems to be 原义为 源自 prize ring, where the word meant "scheduled length of a bout."

example.en: The two cities are separated by a distance of over three hundred kilometers.
example.zh: 这两座城市相距三百多公里。

definitionLines: vt. 蒸馏；提取……的精华；使 渗出
entries.definition: a.远的，疏远的，冷漠的 distil（1） vi. 蒸馏；提炼；渗出 vt. 蒸馏；提取……的精华；使 渗出
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French distant (14c.), from Latin distantem (nominative distans), present participle of distare "to stand apart, be remote" (see distance (n.)). Related: Distantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 distant (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 distantem (主格 distans), 为 … 的现在分词 distare "to stand apart, be remote" （参见 distance （名）). 同源词：Distantly.

example.en: The thunder grew distant as the storm moved away from the coast.
example.zh: 随着风暴远离海岸，雷声变得越来越遥远。

definitionLines: a. （from） 不同的；清楚的，明显 的，显著的
entries.definition: a. （from） 不同的；清楚的，明显 的，显著的
entries.etymology: late 14c., originally past participle of distincten (c. 1300) "to distinguish," from Old French distincter, from Latin distinctus, past participle of distinguere (see distinguish). Related: Distinctness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 原义为 为 … 的过去分词 distincten (约 1300 年) "to distinguish," 源自 古法语 distincter, 源自 拉丁语 distinctus, 为 … 的过去分词 distinguere （参见 distinguish). 同源词：Distinctness.

example.en: The two proposals were distinct different in their approach.
example.zh: 这两个提案在方法上截然不同。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "one of the parts into which something is divided;" mid-14c. as "action of distinguishing," from Old French distinction and directly from Latin distinctionem (nominative distinctio) "separation, distinction, discrimination," noun of action from past participle stem of distinguere (see distinguish). Meaning "distinctive nature or character" is late 14c. Meaning "excellence or eminence" (what distinguishes from others) is first recorded 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "one of the parts into which something is divided;" 14 世纪中期 as "action of distinguishing," 源自 古法语 distinction and 直接源自 拉丁语 distinctionem (主格 distinctio) "separation, distinction, discrimination," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of distinguere （参见 distinguish). 义为 "distinctive nature or character" is 14 世纪晚期 义为 "excellence or eminence" (what distinguishes 源自 others) is 首见于 1690 年代.

example.en: A legal expert must understand the fine distinction between similar terms.
example.zh: 法律专家必须理解相似术语之间的细微区别。

entries.etymology:
1560s, from Middle French distinguiss-, stem of distinguer, or directly from Latin distinguere "to separate between, keep separate, mark off, distinguish," perhaps literally "separate by pricking," from dis- "apart" (see dis-) + -stinguere "to prick" (compare extinguish and Latin instinguere "to incite, impel").

Watkins says "semantic transmission obscure;" the sense might be from "pricking out" as the old way to make punctuation in parchment or some literal image, but de Vaan derives the second element from a different PIE root meaning "to push, thrust":

The suffix -ish is due to the influence of many verbs in which it is the equivalent of Old French -iss-, ultimately from Latin inchoative suffix -iscere (this is also the case in extinguish, admonish, and astonish). Related: Distinguishing. The earlier form of the verb was distinguen (mid-14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 中古法语 distinguiss-, stem of distinguer，或直接源自 拉丁语 distinguere "to separate between, keep separate, mark off, distinguish," 或许 字面义为 "separate by pricking," 源自 dis- "apart" （参见 dis-) + -stinguere "to prick" (对比 extinguish and 拉丁语 instinguere "to incite, impel"). Watkins says "semantic transmission obscure;" the sense might be 源自 "pricking out" as the old way to make punctuation in parchment or some literal image, but de Vaan derives the second element 源自 a different 原始印欧语 (PIE) root 意为 "to push, thrust": The suffix -ish is due to the influence of many verbs in which it is the equivalent of 古法语 -iss-, 最终源自 拉丁语 inchoative suffix -iscere (this is also the case in extinguish, admonish, and astonish). 同源词：Distinguishing. The earlier form of the 动词 was distinguen (14 世纪中期).

example.en: It can be hard to distinguish between the two nearly identical twins.
example.zh: 要区分这对几乎一模一样的双胞胎可能很难。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Latin distortus, past participle of distorquere "to twist different ways, distort," from dis- "completely" + torquere "to twist" (see torque (n.)). Related: Distorted; distorting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 distortus, 为 … 的过去分词 distorquere "to twist different ways, distort," 源自 dis- "completely" + torquere "to twist" （参见 torque （名）). 同源词：Distorted; distorting.

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "to draw asunder or apart, to turn aside" (literal and figurative), from Latin distractus, past participle of distrahere "draw in different directions," from dis- "away" (see dis-) + trahere "to draw" (see tract (n.1)).

Sense of "to throw into a state of mind in which one knows not how to act" is from 1580s. Related: Distracted; distracting; distractedly; distractedness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to draw asunder or apart, to turn aside" (literal and figurative), 源自 拉丁语 distractus, 为 … 的过去分词 distrahere "draw in different directions," 源自 dis- "away" （参见 dis-) + trahere "to draw" （参见 tract (n.1)). 义为 "to throw into a state of mind in which one knows not how to act" 始于 1580 年代. 同源词：Distracted; distracting; distractedly; distractedness.

example.en: Loud music from next door kept distracting him from his studies.
example.zh: 隔壁传来的嘈杂音乐一直让他无法专心学习。

definitionLines: vt. 分发，分送，配给；分布
entries.definition: vt. 分发，分送，配给；分布
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to deal out or apportion," from Latin distributus, past participle of distribuere "to divide, distribute" (see distribution). Related: Distributable; distributed; distributing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to deal out or apportion," 源自 拉丁语 distributus, 为 … 的过去分词 distribuere "to divide, distribute" （参见 distribution). 同源词：Distributable; distributed; distributing.

example.en: Volunteers worked all night to distribute food to flood victims.
example.zh: 志愿者彻夜工作，向洪灾受害者分发食物。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "territory under the jurisdiction of a lord or officer," from French district (16c.), from Medieval Latin districtus "restraining of offenders, jurisdiction," then under the feudal system "area of jurisdiction," noun use of past participle of Latin distringere "hinder, detain" (see distress). Used vaguely of "any tract of land" from 1712. District attorney attested by 1789, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "territory under the jurisdiction of a lord or officer," 源自 法语 district (16 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 districtus "restraining of offenders, jurisdiction," 之后 under the feudal system "area of jurisdiction," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 distringere "hinder, detain" （参见 distress). Used vaguely of "any tract of land" 自 1712 年起. District attorney attested 截至 1789 年, American English.

example.en: Each district in the city has its own elected council and local budget.
example.zh: 城市中的每个区都有自己的民选议会和地方预算。

definitionLines: vt. 扰乱，妨碍；打扰，使不安
entries.definition: vt. 扰乱，妨碍；打扰，使不安
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to stop or hinder," from Old French destorber (Old North French distourber) and directly from Latin disturbare "throw into disorder," from dis- "completely" (see dis-) + turbare "to disorder, disturb," from turba "turmoil" (see turbid).

Meaning "to frighten" is late 13c.; that of "to stir up, agitate" is c. 1300. Related: Disturbed; disturbing; disturbingly. Middle English also had distourbler (n.) "one who disturbs or incites" (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to stop or hinder," 源自 古法语 destorber (Old North 法语 distourber) and 直接源自 拉丁语 disturbare "throw into disorder," 源自 dis- "completely" （参见 dis-) + turbare "to disorder, disturb," 源自 turba "turmoil" （参见 turbid). 义为 "to frighten" is 13 世纪晚期; that of "to stir up, agitate" is 约 1300 年. 同源词：Disturbed; disturbing; disturbingly. 中古英语 also had distourbler （名） "one who disturbs or incites" (14 世纪晚期).

example.en: Please do not disturb the patients who are resting in their rooms.
example.zh: 请不要打扰正在房间里休息的病人。

definitionLines: n. 动乱；骚扰，干扰；（身心） 失调
entries.definition: n. 动乱；骚扰，干扰；（身心） 失调
entries.etymology: late 13c., "mental distress," from Old French destorbance (12c., Old North French distorbance), from destourber, from Latin disturbare (see disturb). Meaning "public disturbance" is c. 1300; that of "destruction of peace or unity" is late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "mental distress," 源自 古法语 destorbance (12 世纪, Old North 法语 distorbance), 源自 destourber, 源自 拉丁语 disturbare （参见 disturb). 义为 "public disturbance" is 约 1300 年; that of "destruction of peace or unity" is 14 世纪晚期

entries.etymology: Old English dic "ditch, dike," a variant of dike (q.v.). Last ditch (1715) refers to the last line of military defenses.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dic "ditch, dike," a 为 … 的变体 dike (q.v.). Last ditch (1715 年) refers to the last line of military defenses.

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from Old English dufan "to dive, duck, sink" (intransitive, class II strong verb; past tense deaf, past participle dofen) and dyfan "to dip, submerge" (weak, transitive), from Proto-Germanic verb *dubijan, from PIE *dheub- "deep, hollow" (see deep (adj.)). Past tense dove is a later formation, perhaps on analogy of drive/drove. Related: Diving. Dive bomber attested by 1939.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古英语 dufan "to dive, duck, sink" (intransitive, class II strong 动词; past tense deaf, past participle dofen) and dyfan "to dip, submerge" (weak, transitive), 源自 原始日耳曼语 动词 *dubijan, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dheub- "deep, hollow" （参见 deep （形）). Past tense dove is a later formation, 或许 on analogy of drive/drove. 同源词：Diving. Dive bomber attested 截至 1939 年.

example.en: She took a deep breath and dived into the clear blue water.
example.zh: 她深吸一口气，跳入清澈的蓝色水中。

definitionLines: a. 不同的，多种多样的
entries.definition: a. 不同的，多种多样的
entries.etymology: c. 1300, spelling variant of divers (q.v.), perhaps by analogy with converse, traverse, etc. In some cases directly from Latin diversus, and since c. 1700 restricted to the meaning "different in character or quality." Related: Diversely.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, spelling 为 … 的变体 divers (q.v.), 或许 by analogy with converse, traverse, etc. In some cases 直接源自 拉丁语 diversus, and 自 约 1700 年 restricted to the 意为 "different in character or quality." 同源词：Diversely.

example.en: The city is known for its diverse population and rich cultural life.
example.zh: 这座城市以其多元化的人口和丰富的文化生活而闻名。

definitionLines: n. 转移；消遣；分散注意力
entries.definition: n. 转移；消遣；分散注意力
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "diverse condition;" c. 1600 "act of diverting," from Middle French diversion, from Late Latin diversionem (nominative diversio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin divertere (see divert).

Sense of "amusement, entertainment" is first recorded 1640s. Hence, divertimento (1823), from the Italian form; originally "a musical composition designed primarily for entertainment."
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "diverse condition;" 约 1600 年 "act of diverting," 源自 中古法语 diversion, 源自 晚期拉丁语 diversionem (主格 diversio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 divertere （参见 divert). 义为 "amusement, entertainment" is 首见于 1640 年代. Hence, divertimento (1823 年), 源自 意大利语 form; 原义为 "a musical composition designed primarily for entertainment."

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "quality of being diverse," mostly in a neutral sense, from Old French diversité (12c.) "difference, diversity, unique feature, oddness:" also "wickedness, perversity," from Latin diversitatem (nominative diversitas) "contrariety, contradiction, disagreement;" also, as a secondary sense, "difference, diversity," from diversus "turned different ways" (in Late Latin "various"), past participle of divertere (see divert).

Negative meaning, "being contrary to what is agreeable or right; perversity, evil" existed in English from late 15c. but was obsolete from 17c. Diversity as a virtue in a nation is an idea from the rise of modern democracies in the 1790s, where it kept one faction from arrogating all power (but this was not quite the modern sense, as ethnicity, gender, sexual identity, etc. were not the qualities in mind):

Specific focus (in a positive sense) on race, gender, etc. is from 1992.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "quality of being diverse," mostly in a neutral sense, 源自 古法语 diversité (12 世纪) "difference, diversity, unique feature, oddness:" also "wickedness, perversity," 源自 拉丁语 diversitatem (主格 diversitas) "contrariety, contradiction, disagreement;" also, 作为 secondary sense, "difference, diversity," 源自 diversus "turned different ways" (in 晚期拉丁语 "various"), 为 … 的过去分词 divertere （参见 divert). Negative 意为, "being contrary to what is agreeable or right; perversity, evil" existed in English 源自 15 世纪晚期 but was 已废 源自 17 世纪 Diversity 作为 virtue in a nation is an idea 源自 rise of modern democracies in the 1790 年代, where it kept one faction 源自 arrogating all power (but this was not quite the modern sense, as ethnicity, gender, sexual identity, etc. were not the qualities in mind): Specific focus (in a positive sense) on race, gender, etc. 始于 1992 年.

example.en: The university values cultural diversity among its students.
example.zh: 该大学重视学生群体中的文化多样性。

definitionLines: vt. 转移；使……欢娱；使…… 转向
entries.definition: vt. 转移；使……欢娱；使…… 转向 vi. 转移
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French divertir (14c.), from Latin divertere "to turn in different directions," blended with devertere "turn aside," from dis- "aside" and de- "from" + vertere "to turn" (see versus). Related: Diverted; diverting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 divertir (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 divertere "to turn in different directions," blended with devertere "turn aside," 源自 dis- "aside" and de- "from" + vertere "to turn" （参见 versus). 同源词：Diverted; diverting.

definitionLines: （into） 分，划分，隔开；分配， 分享，分担；隔开；除
entries.definition: （into） 分，划分，隔开；分配， 分享，分担；隔开；除
entries.etymology:
early 14c., from Latin dividere "to force apart, cleave, distribute," from dis- "apart" (see dis-) + -videre "to separate," from PIE root *weidh- "to separate" (see widow; also see with).

Mathematical sense is from early 15c. Divide and rule (c. 1600) translates Latin divide et impera, a maxim of Machiavelli. Related: Divided; dividing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 dividere "to force apart, cleave, distribute," 源自 dis- "apart" （参见 dis-) + -videre "to separate," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *weidh- "to separate" （参见 widow; also 参见 with). Mathematical sense 始于 15 世纪初 Divide and rule (约 1600 年) translates 拉丁语 divide et impera, a maxim of Machiavelli. 同源词：Divided; dividing.

example.en: The teacher asked students to divide into groups of four for the project.
example.zh: 老师要求学生们分成四人一组来完成项目。

entries.etymology:
Old English dysig "foolish, stupid," from Proto-Germanic *dusijaz (source also of Low German düsig "dizzy," Dutch duizelen "to be dizzy," Old High German dusig "foolish," German Tor "fool," Old English dwæs, Dutch dwaas "foolish"), perhaps from PIE *dheu- (1) "dust, vapor, smoke; to rise in a cloud" (and related notions of "defective perception or wits").

Meaning "having a whirling sensation" is from mid-14c.; that of "giddy" is from c. 1500 and seems to merge the two earlier meanings. Used of the "foolish virgins" in early translations of Matthew xxv; used especially of blondes since 1870s. Related: Dizzily.

Used of the "foolish virgins" in early translations of Matthew xxv; used 尤指 of blondes 自 1870 年代. 同源词：Dizzily.

entries.etymology:
Middle English do, first person singular of Old English don "make, act, perform, cause; to put, to place," from West Germanic *don (source also of Old Saxon duan, Old Frisian dua, Dutch doen, Old High German tuon, German tun), from PIE root *dhe- "to put, place, do, make" (see factitious).

Use as an auxiliary began in Middle English. Periphrastic form in negative sentences ("They did not think") replaced the Old English negative particles ("Hie ne wendon"). Slang meaning "to do the sex act with or to" is from 1913. Expression do or die is attested from 1620s.
Compare does, did, done.
entries.etymologyZh: 中古英语 do, first person singular of 古英语 don "make, act, perform, cause; to put, to place," 源自 West 日耳曼语 *don (source also of 古撒克逊语 duan, 古弗里西语 dua, 荷兰语 doen, 古高地德语 tuon, 德语 tun), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dhe- "to put, place, do, make" （参见 factitious). Use 作为 auxiliary began in 中古英语. Periphrastic form in negative sentences ("They did not think") replaced the 古英语 negative particles ("Hie ne wendon"). Slang 意为 "to do the sex act with or to" 始于 1913 年. Expression do or die 见于 1620 年代. 对比 does, did, done.

entries.etymology: "cut an animal's tail," late 14c., from dok (n.) Meaning "to reduce (someone's) pay for some infraction" is first recorded 1822. Related: Docked; docking.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "Church father," from Old French doctour, from Medieval Latin doctor "religious teacher, adviser, scholar," in classical Latin "teacher," agent noun from docere "to show, teach, cause to know," originally "make to appear right," causative of decere "be seemly, fitting" (see decent).

Meaning "holder of highest degree in university" is first found late 14c.; as is that of "medical professional" (replacing native leech (n.2)), though this was not common till late 16c. The transitional stage is exemplified in Chaucer's Doctor of phesike (Latin physica came to be used extensively in Medieval Latin for medicina). Similar usage of the equivalent of doctor is colloquial in most European languages: Italian dottore, French docteur, German doktor, Lithuanian daktaras, though these are typically not the main word in those languages for a medical healer. For similar evolution, see Sanskrit vaidya- "medical doctor," literally "one versed in science." German Arzt, Dutch arts are from Late Latin archiater, from Greek arkhiatros "chief healer," hence "court physician." French médecin is a back-formation from médicine, replacing Old French miege, from Latin medicus.

Similar usage of the equivalent of doctor is 口语 in most European languages: 意大利语 dottore, 法语 docteur, 德语 doktor, Lithuanian daktaras, though these are typically not the main word in those languages for a medical healer. For similar evolution, 参见 梵语 vaidya- "medical doctor," 字面义为 "one versed in science." 德语 Arzt, 荷兰语 arts 始于 晚期拉丁语 archiater, 源自 希腊语 arkhiatros "chief healer," hence "court physician." 法语 médecin is a back-formation 源自 médicine, replacing 古法语 miege, 源自 拉丁语 medicus.

entries.etymology:
Old English docga, a late, rare word, used in at least one Middle English source in reference to a powerful breed of canine. The word forced out Old English hund (the general Germanic and Indo-European word; see canine) by 16c. and subsequently was picked up in many continental languages (French dogue (16c.), Danish dogge, German Dogge (16c.)), but the origin remains one of the great mysteries of English etymology.

Many expressions -- a dog's life (c. 1600), go to the dogs (1610s), etc. -- reflect earlier hard use of the animals as hunting accessories, not pampered pets. In ancient times, "the dog" was the worst throw in dice (attested in Greek, Latin, and Sanskrit, where the word for "the lucky player" was literally "the dog-killer"), which plausibly explains the Greek word for "danger," kindynas, which appears to be "play the dog."

Slang meaning "ugly woman" is from 1930s; that of "sexually aggressive man" is from 1950s. Adjectival phrase dog-eat-dog attested by 1850s. Dog tag is from 1918. To dog-ear a book is from 1650s; dog-eared in extended sense of "worn, unkempt" is from 1894. Phrase put on the dog "get dressed up" (1934) may look back to the stiff stand-up shirt collars that in the 1890s were the height of male fashion (and were known as dog-collars at least from 1883), with reference to collars worn by dogs. The common Spanish word for "dog," perro, also is a mystery word of unknown origin, perhaps from Iberian. A group of Slavic "dog" words (Old Church Slavonic pisu, Polish pies, Serbo-Croatian pas) likewise are of unknown origin.

Many expressions -- a dog's life (约 1600 年), go to the dogs (1610 年代), etc. -- reflect earlier hard use of the animals as hunting accessories, not pampered pets. In ancient times, "the dog" was the worst throw in dice (见于 希腊语, 拉丁语, and 梵语, where the word for "the lucky player" was 字面义为 "the dog-killer"), which plausibly explains the 希腊语 word for "danger," kindynas, which appears to be "play the dog." entries.etymology: 1550s, endearing name for a female pet or a mistress; originally a familiar form of fem. proper name Dorothy (q.v.). The -l- for -r- substitution in nicknames is common in English: compare Hal for Harold, Moll for Mary, Sally for Sarah, etc. Attested from 1640s as colloquial for "slattern;" sense of "child's toy baby" is c. 1700. Transferred back to living beings 1778 in sense of "pretty, silly woman."

entries.etymology:
1550s, from Low German daler, from German taler (1530s, later thaler), abbreviation of Joachimstaler, literally "(gulden) of Joachimstal," coin minted 1519 from silver from mine opened 1516 near Joachimstal, town in Erzgebirge Mountains in northwest Bohemia. German Tal is cognate with English dale.

The thaler was a large silver coin of varying value in the German states; from 17c. it was the more-or-less standardized coin of northern Germany (as opposed to the southern gulden). It also served as a currency unit in Denmark and Sweden (and later was a unit of the German monetary union of 1857-73 equal to three marks). English colonists in America used the word in reference to Spanish pieces of eight. Due to extensive trade with the Spanish Indies and the proximity of Spanish colonies along the Gulf Coast, the Spanish "dollar" probably was the coin most familiar in the American colonies and the closest thing to a standard in all of them. It had the added advantage of not being British. It was used in the government's records of public debt and expenditures, and the Continental Congress in 1786 adopted dollar as a unit when it set up the modern U.S. currency system, which was based on the suggestion of Gouverneur Morris (1782) as modified by Thomas Jefferson. None were circulated until 1794.

Phrase dollars to doughnuts attested from 1890; dollar diplomacy is from 1910. The dollar sign ($) is said to derive from the image of the Pillars of Hercules, stamped with a scroll, on the Spanish piece of eight. However, according to the Bureau of Engraving and Printing of the U.S. Department of the Treasury:

Joachimsthal was founded 1604 by Joachim Frederick (1546-1608), Elector of Brandenburg.

entries.etymology:
"round, vaulted roof," 1650s, from French dome (16c.), from Provençal doma, from Greek doma "house, housetop" (especially a style of roof from the east), related to domos "house" (see domestic).

In the Middle Ages, German dom and Italian duomo were used for "cathedral" (on the notion of "God's house"), so English began to use this word in the sense "cupola," an architectural feature characteristic of Italian cathedrals. Used in U.S. also with reference to round summits of mountains.
entries.etymologyZh: "round, vaulted roof," 1650 年代, 源自 法语 dome (16 世纪), 源自 Provençal doma, 源自 希腊语 doma "house, housetop" (尤指 a style of roof 源自 east), related to domos "house" （参见 domestic). In the Middle Ages, 德语 dom and 意大利语 duomo were used for "cathedral" (on the 概念 "God's house"), so English began to use this word in the sense "cupola," an architectural feature characteristic of 意大利语 cathedrals. Used in U.S. also with reference to round summits of mountains.

example.en: The cathedral is crowned with a magnificent dome.

example.en: A single corporation has come to dominate the global search engine market with over 90% share.
example.zh: 一家公司凭借超过90%的市场份额主导了全球搜索引擎市场。

entries.etymology: 1819, back-formation from donation. Related: Donated; donating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1819 年, back-formation 源自 donation. 同源词：Donated; donating.

example.en: Many companies donate a portion of their profits to local charities.
example.zh: 许多公司将部分利润捐赠给当地慈善机构。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French donacion (13c.), from Latin donationem (nominative donatio) "a presenting, giving," noun of action from past participle stem of donare "give as a gift," from donum "gift," from PIE *donum "gift" (source also of Sanskrit danam "offering, present," Old Church Slavonic dani "tribute," Lithuanian duonis "gift," Old Irish dan "gift, endowment, talent," Welsh dawn "gift"), from root *do- "to give" (see date (n.1)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 donacion (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 donationem (主格 donatio) "a presenting, giving," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of donare "give as a gift," 源自 donum "gift," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *donum "gift" (source also of 梵语 danam "offering, present," Old Church Slavonic dani "tribute," Lithuanian duonis "gift," Old 爱尔兰语 dan "gift, endowment, talent," Welsh dawn "gift"), 源自 root *do- "to give" （参见 date (n.1)).

example.en: The hospital received a generous donation from a local business to fund new equipment.
example.zh: 医院收到了当地一家企业的慷慨捐款，用于购置新设备。

entries.etymology: 1785, originally slang, perhaps a diminutive from dun "dull gray-brown," the form perhaps influenced by monkey. Or possibly from a familiar form of Duncan (compare dobbin). The older English word was ass (n.1).
entries.etymologyZh: 1785 年, 原义为 俚语, 或许 a diminutive 源自 dun "dull gray-brown," the form 或许 influenced by monkey. Or possibly 源自 a familiar form of Duncan (对比 dobbin). The older English word was ass (n.1).

definitionLines: n. 供者；捐赠者；赠送人
entries.definition: n. 供者；捐赠者；赠送人
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Anglo-French donour, Old French doneur (Modern French donneur), from Latin donatorem (nominative donator) "giver, donor," agent noun from past participle stem of donare "give as a gift" (see donation). Of blood, from 1910; of organs or tissues, from 1918.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 donour, 古法语 doneur (现代法语 donneur), 源自 拉丁语 donatorem (主格 donator) "giver, donor," agent 名词 源自 past participle stem of donare "give as a gift" （参见 donation). Of blood, 自 1910 年起; of organs or tissues, 自 1918 年起.

example.en: The hospital sent a thank-you letter to every donor.
example.zh: 医院向每一位捐赠者发送了感谢信。

entries.definition: n. 厄运；死亡；判决 vt. 判决；注定；使失败
entries.etymology: Old English dom "law, judgment, condemnation," from Proto-Germanic *domaz (source also of Old Saxon and Old Frisian dom, Old Norse domr, Old High German tuom, Gothic doms "judgment, decree"), from PIE root *dhe- "to set, place, put, do" (source also of Sanskrit dhaman- "law," Greek themis "law," Lithuanian dome "attention;" see factitious). A book of laws in Old English was a dombec. Modern sense of "fate, ruin, destruction" is c. 1600, from the finality of the Christian Judgment Day.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dom "law, judgment, condemnation," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *domaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 and 古弗里西语 dom, 古北欧语 domr, 古高地德语 tuom, Gothic doms "judgment, decree"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dhe- "to set, place, put, do" (source also of 梵语 dhaman- "law," 希腊语 themis "law," Lithuanian dome "attention;" 参见 factitious). A book of laws in 古英语 was a dombec. 现代 语义 "fate, ruin, destruction" is 约 1600 年, 源自 finality of the Christian Judgment Day.

entries.etymology:
Middle English merger of Old English dor (neuter; plural doru) "large door, gate," and Old English duru (fem., plural dura) "door, gate, wicket;" both from Proto-Germanic *dur- (source also of Old Saxon duru, Old Norse dyrr, Danish dør, Old Frisian dure, Old High German turi, German Tür).

The Germanic words are from PIE *dhwer- "a doorway, a door, a gate" (source also of Greek thyra, Latin foris, Gaulish doro "mouth," Gothic dauro "gate," Sanskrit dvárah "door, gate," Old Persian duvara- "door," Old Prussian dwaris "gate," Russian dver' "a door").

The base form is frequently in dual or plural, leading to speculation that houses of the original Indo-Europeans had doors with two swinging halves. Middle English had both dure and dor; form dore predominated by 16c., but was supplanted by door.
entries.etymologyZh: 中古英语 merger of 古英语 dor (neuter; plural doru) "large door, gate," and 古英语 duru (fem., plural dura) "door, gate, wicket;" both 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dur- (source also of 古撒克逊语 duru, 古北欧语 dyrr, Danish dør, 古弗里西语 dure, 古高地德语 turi, 德语 Tür). The 日耳曼语 words 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhwer- "a doorway, a door, a gate" (source also of 希腊语 thyra, 拉丁语 foris, Gaulish doro "mouth," Gothic dauro "gate," 梵语 dvárah "door, gate," Old 波斯语 duvara- "door," Old Prussian dwaris "gate," 俄语 dver' "a door"). The base form is frequently in dual or plural, leading to speculation that houses of the original Indo-Europeans had doors with two swinging halves. 中古英语 had both dure and dor; form dore predominated by 16 世纪, but was supplanted by door.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Latin dormitorium "sleeping place," from dormire "to sleep" (see dormant). Old English had slæpern "dormitory," with ending as in barn.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 dormitorium "sleeping place," 源自 dormire "to sleep" （参见 dormant). 古英语 had slæpern "dormitory," with ending as in barn.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "the giving of medicine (in a specified amount or at a stated time)," from Middle French dose (15c.) or directly from Late Latin dosis, from Greek dosis "a portion prescribed," literally "a giving," used by Galen and other Greek physicians to mean an amount of medicine, from stem of didonai "to give" (see date (n.1)). Slang meaning "venereal disease" is from 1914.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "the giving of medicine (in a specified amount or at a stated time)," 源自 中古法语 dose (15 世纪) or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 dosis, 源自 希腊语 dosis "a portion prescribed," 字面义为 "a giving," used by Galen and other 希腊语 physicians to mean an amount of medicine, 源自 stem of didonai "to give" （参见 date (n.1)). Slang 意为 "venereal disease" 始于 1914 年.

example.en: The doctor prescribed a higher dose of antibiotics to fight the infection.
example.zh: 医生开了更高剂量的抗生素来对抗感染。

entries.etymology:
Old English dott "speck, head of a boil," perhaps related to Norwegian dot "lump, small knot," Dutch dot "knot, small bunch, wisp," Old High German tutta "nipple;" further etymology unclear.

Known from a single source c. 1000; the word reappeared with modern meaning "mark" c. 1530; not common until 18c. Morse telegraph sense is from 1838. On the dot "punctual" is 1909, in reference to a clock dial face. Dot-matrix first attested 1975.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dott "speck, head of a boil," 或许 related to Norwegian dot "lump, small knot," 荷兰语 dot "knot, small bunch, wisp," 古高地德语 tutta "nipple;" further etymology unclear. Known 源自 a single source 约 1000 年; the word reappeared with modern 意为 "mark" 约 1530 年; not common until 18 世纪 Morse telegraph sense 始于 1838 年. On the dot "punctual" is 1909 年, in reference to a clock dial face. Dot-matrix 最早见于 1975 年.

entries.definition: a. 两倍的；双，双重 vt. 使加倍，翻一番
entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French doble (10c.) "double, two-fold; two-faced, deceitful," from Latin duplus "twofold, twich as much" from duo "two" (see two) + -plus "more" (see -plus). Double standard attested by 1951. Military double time (1833) originally was 130 steps per minute.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 doble (10 世纪) "double, two-fold; two-faced, deceitful," 源自 拉丁语 duplus "twofold, twich as much" 源自 duo "two" （参见 two) + -plus "more" （参见 -plus). Double standard attested 截至 1951 年. Military double time (1833 年) 原义为 was 130 steps per minute.

example.en: The company managed to double its profits in just two years.
example.zh: 这家公司在短短两年内成功将利润翻了一番。

entries.definition: n. 怀疑，疑问，疑惑 v. 怀疑，不相信
entries.etymology:
early 13c., "to dread, fear," from Old French doter "doubt, be doubtful; be afraid," from Latin dubitare "to doubt, question, hesitate, waver in opinion" (related to dubius "uncertain;" see dubious); etymologically, "to have to choose between two things."

The sense of "fear" developed in Old French and was passed on to English. Meaning "to be uncertain" is attested in English from c. 1300. The -b- was restored 14c. by scribes in imitation of Latin. Replaced Old English tweogan (noun twynung), from tweon "two," on notion of "of two minds" or the choice of two implied in Latin dubitare (compare German Zweifel "doubt," from zwei "two").
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "to dread, fear," 源自 古法语 doter "doubt, be doubtful; be afraid," 源自 拉丁语 dubitare "to doubt, question, hesitate, waver in opinion" (related to dubius "uncertain;" 参见 dubious); etymologically, "to have to choose between two things." The 语义 "fear" developed in 古法语 and was passed on to English. 义为 "to be uncertain" is 见于 English 源自 约 1300 年. The -b- was restored 14 世纪 by scribes in imitation of 拉丁语. Replaced 古英语 tweogan (名词 twynung), 源自 tweon "two," on 概念 "of two minds" or the choice of two implied in 拉丁语 dubitare (对比 德语 Zweifel "doubt," 源自 zwei "two").

example.en: I doubt whether he will keep his promise, given how many times he has lied to us.
example.zh: 考虑到他骗过我们那么多次，我怀疑他到底会不会信守诺言。

definitionLines: a. 怀疑的，不相信的；可疑；难 料的
entries.definition: a. 怀疑的，不相信的；可疑；难 料的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from doubt (n.) + -ful. Related: Doubtfully; doubtfulness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 doubt （名） + -ful. 同源词：Doubtfully; doubtfulness.

definitionLines: ad. 下，向下；由多到少；往南； 处于低落状态
entries.definition: ad. 下，向下；由多到少；往南； 处于低落状态 prep. 下，顺……而下
entries.etymology:
late Old English shortened form of Old English ofdune "downwards," from dune "from the hill," dative of dun "hill" (see down (n.2)). A sense development peculiar to English.

Used as a preposition since c. 1500. Sense of "depressed mentally" is attested from c. 1600. Slang sense of "aware, wide awake" is attested from 1812. Computer crash sense is from 1965. As a preposition from late 14c.; as an adjective from 1560s. Down-and-out is from 1889, American English, from situation of a beaten prizefighter. Down home (adj.) is 1931, American English; down the hatch as a toast is from 1931; down to the wire is 1901, from horse-racing. Down time is from 1952. Down under "Australia and New Zealand" attested from 1886; Down East "Maine" is from 1825; Down South "in the Southern states of the U.S." is attested by 1834.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 shortened form of 古英语 ofdune "downwards," 源自 dune "from the hill," dative of dun "hill" （参见 down (n.2)). A sense development peculiar to English. Used 作为 preposition 自 约 1500 年. 义为 "depressed mentally" 见于 约 1600 年. Slang 语义 "aware, wide awake" 见于 1812 年. Computer crash sense 始于 1965 年. 作为 preposition 源自 14 世纪晚期; 作形容词时 源自 1560 年代. Down-and-out 始于 1889 年, American English, 源自 situation of a beaten prizefighter. Down home （形） is 1931 年, American English; down the hatch 作为 toast 始于 1931 年; down to the wire is 1901 年, 源自 horse-racing. Down time 始于 1952 年. Down under "Australia and New Zealand" attested 自 1886 年起; Down East "Maine" 始于 1825 年; Down South "in the Southern states of the U.S." is attested 截至 1834 年.

entries.etymology: 1977 (n.), 1980 (v.), from down (adv.) + load (v.). Related: Downloaded; downloading.
entries.etymologyZh: 1977 年 （名）, 1980 年 （动）, 源自 down （副） + load （动）. 同源词：Downloaded; downloading.

entries.definition: ad.在楼下，往楼下 a. 楼下的

example.en: She heard strange noises coming from downstairs and went to check.
example.zh: 她听到从楼下传来奇怪的声音，便下去查看。

definitionLines: ad./a.（在/往）商业区，（在/ 往）闹市区（的）
entries.definition: ad./a.（在/往）商业区，（在/ 往）闹市区（的）
entries.etymology: 1835, from down (adv.) + town. The notion is of suburbs built on heights around a city.
entries.etymologyZh: 1835 年, 源自 down （副） + town. The notion is of suburbs built on heights around a city.

example.en: She works in a busy office downtown and commutes by subway every day.
example.zh: 她在繁忙的市中心办公室工作，每天乘地铁通勤。

entries.definition: ad.（s）向下地，下行地 a.向下的，下行的
entries.etymology: c. 1200, from down (adv.) + -ward. Old English had aduneweard in this sense. Downwards, with adverbial genitive, had a parallel in Old English ofduneweardes.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 down （副） + -ward. 古英语 had aduneweard in this sense. Downwards, with adverbial 属格, had a parallel in 古英语 ofduneweardes.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French dozaine "a dozen," from doze (12c.) "twelve," from Latin duodecim "twelve," from duo "two" + decem "ten" (see ten).

The Old French fem. suffix -aine is characteristically added to cardinals to form collectives in a precise sense ("exactly 12," not "about 12"). The dozens "invective contest" (1928) originated in slave culture, the custom probably African, the word probably from bulldoze (q.v.) in its original sense of "a whipping, a thrashing."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 dozaine "a dozen," 源自 doze (12 世纪) "twelve," 源自 拉丁语 duodecim "twelve," 源自 duo "two" + decem "ten" （参见 ten). The 古法语 fem. suffix -aine is characteristically added to cardinals to form collectives in a precise sense ("exactly 12," not "about 12"). The dozens "invective contest" (1928 年) originated in slave culture, the custom 可能 African, the word 可能 源自 bulldoze (q.v.) in its original 语义 "a whipping, a thrashing."

example.en: She bought a dozen roses for the dinner table centerpiece.
example.zh: 她买了一打玫瑰花作为晚宴桌上的装饰。

entries.definition: n.草稿，草案，草图 vt. 起草，草拟
entries.etymology: c. 1500, spelling variant of draught (q.v.) to reflect change in pronunciation. Among the senses that have gone with this form of the word in American English, the meaning "rough copy of a writing" (something "drawn") is attested from 14c.; that of "preliminary sketch from which a final copy is made" is from 1520s; that of "flow of a current of air" is from c. 1770. Of beer from the 1830s, in reference to the method of "drawing" it from the cask. Sense in bank draft is from 1745. The meaning "a drawing off a group for special duty" is from 1703, in U.S. especially of military service; the verb in this sense first recorded 1714. Related: Drafted; drafting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, spelling 为 … 的变体 draught (q.v.) to reflect change in pronunciation. Among the senses that have gone with this form of the word in American English, the 意为 "rough copy of a writing" (something "drawn") 见于 14 世纪; that of "preliminary sketch from which a final copy is made" 始于 1520 年代; that of "flow of a current of air" 始于 约 1770 年. Of beer 源自 1830 年代, in reference to the method of "drawing" it 源自 cask. Sense in bank draft 始于 1745 年. The 意为 "a drawing off a group for special duty" 始于 1703 年, in U.S. 尤指 of military service; the 动词 in this sense 首见于 1714 年. 同源词：Drafted; drafting.

example.en: The committee submitted a draft proposal pending final approval from the board.
example.zh: 委员会提交了一份草案，等待董事会最终审批。

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., from Old Norse draga, or a dialectal variant of Old English dragan "to draw," both from Proto-Germanic *dragan "to draw, pull," from PIE root *dhragh- "to draw, drag on the ground" (source also of Sanskrit dhrajati "pulls, slides in," Russian drogi "wagon;" but not considered to be directly the source of Latin trahere).

Meaning "to take a puff" (of a cigarette, etc.) is from 1914. Related: Dragged; dragging. Drag-out "violent fight" is from c. 1859. To drag (one's) feet (1946, in figurative sense) supposedly is from logging, from a lazy way to use a two-man saw.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 古北欧语 draga，或a 方言 为 … 的变体 古英语 dragan "to draw," both 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dragan "to draw, pull," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dhragh- "to draw, drag on the ground" (source also of 梵语 dhrajati "pulls, slides in," 俄语 drogi "wagon;" but not considered to be directly the source of 拉丁语 trahere). 义为 "to take a puff" (of a cigarette, etc.) 始于 1914 年. 同源词：Dragged; dragging. Drag-out "violent fight" 始于 约 1859 年. To drag (one's) feet (1946 年, in figurative sense) supposedly 始于 logging, 源自 a lazy way to use a two-man saw.

example.en: He had to drag his heavy suitcase up three flights of stairs.
example.zh: 他不得不把沉重的手提箱拖上三层楼梯。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Old French dragon, from Latin draconem (nominative draco) "huge serpent, dragon," from Greek drakon (genitive drakontos) "serpent, giant seafish," apparently from drak-, strong aorist stem of derkesthai "to see clearly," from PIE *derk- "to see." Perhaps the literal sense is "the one with the (deadly) glance."

The young are dragonets (14c.). Obsolete drake "dragon" is an older borrowing of the same word. Used in the Bible to translate Hebrew tannin "a great sea-monster," and tan, a desert mammal now believed to be the jackal.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 dragon, 源自 拉丁语 draconem (主格 draco) "huge serpent, dragon," 源自 希腊语 drakon (属格 drakontos) "serpent, giant seafish," 似乎 源自 drak-, strong aorist stem of derkesthai "to see clearly," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *derk- "to see." Perhaps the literal sense is "the one with the (deadly) glance." The young are dragonets (14 世纪). Obsolete drake "dragon" is an older borrowing of the same word. Used in the Bible to translate 希伯来语 tannin "a great sea-monster," and tan, a desert mammal 现在 believed to be the jackal.

definitionLines: n. 耗竭，消耗；排水管，水沟，下 水道
entries.definition: n. 耗竭，消耗；排水管，水沟，下 水道 .排（水），放（水）：放千
entries.etymology: Old English dreahnian "to drain, strain out," from Proto-Germanic *dreug-, source of drought, dry, giving the English word originally a sense of "make dry." Figurative meaning of "exhaust" is attested from 1650s. The word is not found in surviving texts between late Old English and the 1500s. Related: Drained; draining.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dreahnian "to drain, strain out," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dreug-, source of drought, dry, giving the English word 原义为 a 语义 "make dry." Figurative 意为 of "exhaust" 见于 1650 年代. The word is not found in surviving texts between late 古英语 and the 1500 年代. 同源词：Drained; draining.

example.en: Long hours at the computer were a serious drain on his energy.
example.zh: 长时间使用电脑严重消耗了他的精力。

entries.etymology: 1510s, from Late Latin drama "play, drama," from Greek drama (genitive dramatos) "play, action, deed," from dran "to do, act, perform" (especially some great deed, whether good or bad), from PIE *dere- "to work." Drama queen attested by 1992.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 drama "play, drama," 源自 希腊语 drama (属格 dramatos) "play, action, deed," 源自 dran "to do, act, perform" (尤指 some great deed, whether good or bad), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dere- "to work." Drama queen attested 截至 1992 年.

example.en: The television drama depicted a complex murder trial over twelve episodes.
example.zh: 这部电视剧用十二集描绘了一场复杂的谋杀案审判。

definitionLines: a.戏剧的，戏剧性的；引人注目 的
entries.definition: a.戏剧的，戏剧性的；引人注目 的 n.（pl.）戏剧，戏曲
entries.etymology: 1580s, from Late Latin dramaticus, from Greek dramatikos "pertaining to plays," from drama (genitive dramatos; see drama). Meaning "full of action and striking display, fit for a drama" is from 1725. Dramatic irony is recorded from 1907. Related: Dramatical; dramatically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 dramaticus, 源自 希腊语 dramatikos "pertaining to plays," 源自 drama (属格 dramatos; 参见 drama). 义为 "full of action and striking display, fit for a drama" 始于 1725 年. Dramatic irony 见于 1907 年. 同源词：Dramatical; dramatically.

example.en: The dramatic rise in temperatures alarmed climate scientists.
example.zh: 气温的骤然上升令气候科学家深感震惊。

entries.etymology: 1690s, originally medical, "forceful, vigorous, especially in effect on bowels," from Greek drastikos "effective, efficacious; active, violent," from drasteon "(thing) to be done," from dran "to do, act, perform." Sense of "extreme, severe" is first recorded 1808. Related: Drastically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1690 年代, 原义为 medical, "forceful, vigorous, especially in effect on bowels," 源自 希腊语 drastikos "effective, efficacious; active, violent," 源自 drasteon "(thing) to be done," 源自 dran "to do, act, perform." 义为 "extreme, severe" is 首见于 1808 年. 同源词：Drastically.

definitionLines: vt. 划，画；拉，拖；拔出，抽出， 引出；吸，汲取，提取；推 断出
entries.definition: vt. 划，画；拉，拖；拔出，抽出， 引出；吸，汲取，提取；推 断出 n. 平局，和局
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, spelling alteration of Old English dragan "to drag, to draw, protract" (class VI strong verb; past tense drog, past participle dragen), from Proto-Germanic *dragan "to draw, pull" (source also of Old Norse draga "to draw," Old Saxon dragan, Old Frisian draga, Middle Dutch draghen, Old High German tragen, German tragen "to carry, bear"), from PIE root *dhragh- (see drag (v.)).

Sense of "make a line or figure" (by "drawing" a pencil across paper) is c. 1200. Meaning "pull out a weapon" is c. 1200. To draw a criminal (drag him from a horse to place of execution) is from early 14c. To draw a blank "come up with nothing" (1825) is an image from lotteries. As a noun, from 1660s; colloquial sense of "anything that can draw a crowd" is from 1881 (the verb in this sense is 1580s).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, spelling alteration of 古英语 dragan "to drag, to draw, protract" (class VI strong 动词; past tense drog, past participle dragen), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dragan "to draw, pull" (source also of 古北欧语 draga "to draw," 古撒克逊语 dragan, 古弗里西语 draga, Middle 荷兰语 draghen, 古高地德语 tragen, 德语 tragen "to carry, bear"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dhragh- （参见 drag （动）). 义为 "make a line or figure" (by "drawing" a pencil across paper) is 约 1200 年. 义为 "pull out a weapon" is 约 1200 年. To draw a criminal (drag him 源自 a horse to place of execution) 始于 14 世纪初 To draw a blank "come up with nothing" (1825 年) is an image 源自 lotteries. 作名词时, 源自 1660 年代; 口语 语义 "anything that can draw a crowd" 始于 1881 年 (the 动词 in this sense is 1580 年代).

example.en: She loves to draw portraits of people she meets on her travels.
example.zh: 她喜欢为旅途中遇到的人画肖像素描。

entries.etymology: "hindrance, disadvantage,"1720, from draw (v.) + back (adv.). The notion is of something that "holds back" success or activity.
entries.etymologyZh: "hindrance, disadvantage,"1720 年, 源自 draw （动） + back （副）. The notion is of something that "holds back" success or activity.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., agent noun from draw (v.). Attested from 1570s in sense of a box that can be "drawn" out of a cabinet.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, agent 名词 源自 draw （动）. Attested 源自 1570 年代 in 语义 a box that can be "drawn" out of a cabinet.

example.en: She kept all her important documents in the top drawer of her desk.
example.zh: 她把所有重要文件都放在书桌最上面的抽屉里。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "a pulling," in various senses, verbal noun from draw (v.). The "picture-making" sense is from 1520s; of the picture itself from 1660s. Drawing board is from 1725; used in figurative expression from mid-20c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "a pulling," in various senses, verbal 名词 源自 draw （动）. The "picture-making" sense 始于 1520 年代; of the picture itself 源自 1660 年代. Drawing board 始于 1725 年; used in figurative expression 源自 20 世纪中期

example.en: She completed a large drawing of the city skyline using charcoal on canvas.
example.zh: 她用炭笔在画布上完成了一幅大型城市天际线素描。

entries.definition: vi. 惧怕；担心 vt. 惧怕；担心
entries.etymology: late 12c., a shortening of Old English adrædan, contraction of ondrædan "counsel or advise against," also "to dread, fear, be afraid," from on- "against" + rædan "to advise" (see read (v.)). Cognate of Old Saxon andradon, Old High German intraten. Related: Dreaded; dreading. As a noun from 12c.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪晚期, a shortening of 古英语 adrædan, contraction of ondrædan "counsel or advise against," also "to dread, fear, be afraid," 源自 on- "against" + rædan "to advise" （参见 read （动）). Cognate of 古撒克逊语 andradon, 古高地德语 intraten. 同源词：Dreaded; dreading. 作名词时 源自 12 世纪

definitionLines: a. 可怕的；糟透的，令人不快的
entries.definition: a. 可怕的；糟透的，令人不快的
entries.etymology: early 13c., "full of dread," from dread (n.) + -ful. Meaning "causing dread" is from mid-13c.; weakened sense of "very bad" is from c. 1700. Related: Dreadfully.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "full of dread," 源自 dread （名） + -ful. 义为 "causing dread" 始于 13 世纪中期; weakened 语义 "very bad" 始于 约 1700 年. 同源词：Dreadfully.

entries.definition: n. 梦，梦想，幻想 n. 做梦，幻想
entries.etymology:
mid-13c. in the sense "sequence of sensations passing through a sleeping person's mind" (also as a verb), probably related to Old Norse draumr, Danish drøm, Swedish dröm, Old Saxon drom "merriment, noise," Old Frisian dram "dream," Dutch droom, Old High German troum, German traum "dream," perhaps from Proto-Germanic *draugmas "deception, illusion, phantasm" (source also of Old Saxon bidriogan, Old High German triogan, German trügen "to deceive, delude," Old Norse draugr "ghost, apparition"). Possible cognates outside Germanic are Sanskrit druh- "seek to harm, injure," Avestan druz- "lie, deceive."

But Old English dream meant only "joy, mirth, noisy merriment," also "music." And much study has failed to prove that Old English dream is the root of the modern word for "sleeping vision," despite being identical in spelling. Either the meaning of the word changed dramatically or "vision" was an unrecorded secondary Old English meaning of dream, or there are two separate words here. OED offers this theory: "It seems as if the presence of dream 'joy, mirth, music,' had caused dream 'dream' to be avoided, at least in literature, and swefn, lit. 'sleep,' to be substituted ...."

Words for "sleeping vision" in Old English were mæting and swefn. Old English swefn originally meant "sleep," as did a great many Indo-European "dream" nouns, such as Lithuanian sapnas, Old Church Slavonic sunu, and the Romanic words (French songe, Spanish sueño, Italian sogno all from Latin somnium (from PIE *swep-no-; cognate with Greek hypnos; see somnolence; Old English swefn is from the same root). Dream in the sense of "ideal or aspiration" is from 1931, from earlier sense of "something of dream-like beauty or charm" (1888).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期 in the sense "sequence of sensations passing through a sleeping person's mind" (also 作动词时), 可能 related to 古北欧语 draumr, Danish drøm, Swedish dröm, 古撒克逊语 drom "merriment, noise," 古弗里西语 dram "dream," 荷兰语 droom, 古高地德语 troum, 德语 traum "dream," 或源自 原始日耳曼语 *draugmas "deception, illusion, phantasm" (source also of 古撒克逊语 bidriogan, 古高地德语 triogan, 德语 trügen "to deceive, delude," 古北欧语 draugr "ghost, apparition"). Possible cognates outside 日耳曼语 are 梵语 druh- "seek to harm, injure," Avestan druz- "lie, deceive." But 古英语 dream meant only "joy, mirth, noisy merriment," also "music." And much study has failed to prove that 古英语 dream is the root of the modern word for "sleeping vision," despite being identical in spelling. Either the 意为 of the word changed dramatically or "vision" was an unrecorded secondary 古英语 意为 of dream，或there are two separate words here. OED offers this theory: "It seems as if the presence of dream 'joy, mirth, music,' had caused dream 'dream' to be avoided, at least in literature, and swefn, lit. 'sleep,' to be substituted ...." Words for "sleeping vision" in 古英语 were mæting and swefn. 古英语 swefn 原义为 meant "sleep," as did a great many Indo-European "dream" nouns, such as Lithuanian sapnas, Old Church Slavonic sunu, and the Romanic words (法语 songe, 西班牙语 sueño, 意大利语 sogno all 源自 拉丁语 somnium (源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *swep-no-; 与 … 同源 希腊语 hypnos; 参见 somnolence; 古英语 swefn 始于 the same root). Dream in the 语义 "ideal or aspiration" 始于 1931 年, 源自 earlier 语义 "something of dream-like beauty or charm" (1888 年).

example.en: His lifelong dream was to perform at Carnegie Hall one day.
example.zh: 他毕生的梦想就是有朝一日能在卡内基音乐厅演出。

definitionLines: a.梦想的；空幻的；轻柔的；恍 惚的
entries.definition: a.梦想的；空幻的；轻柔的；恍 惚的
entries.etymology: 1560s, "full of dreams," from dream + -y (2). Meaning "perfect, ideal," attested from 1941, American English teen slang. Compare dreamboat "romantically desirable person;" dream girl (1903).
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "full of dreams," 源自 dream + -y (2). 义为 "perfect, ideal," attested 自 1941 年起, American English teen 俚语. 对比 dreamboat "romantically desirable person;" dream girl (1903 年).

entries.definition: n. 服装，女装，童装 v. 给……穿衣，打扮
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "make straight; direct, guide, control, prepare for cooking," from Old French dresser, drecier "raise (oneself), address, prepare, lift, raise, hoist, set up, arrange, set (a table), serve (food), straighten, put right, direct," from Vulgar Latin *directiare, from Latin directus "direct, straight" (see direct (v.)).

Sense of "decorate, adorn" is late 14c., as is that of "put on clothing." Original sense survives in military meaning "align columns of troops." Dress up "attire elaborately" is from 1670s; to dress (someone) down (1769) is ironical. Related: Dressed; dressing. Dressing down "wearing clothes less formal than expected" is from 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "make straight; direct, guide, control, prepare for cooking," 源自 古法语 dresser, drecier "raise (oneself), address, prepare, lift, raise, hoist, set up, arrange, set (a table), serve (food), straighten, put right, direct," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *directiare, 源自 拉丁语 directus "direct, straight" （参见 direct （动）). 义为 "decorate, adorn" is 14 世纪晚期, as is that of "put on clothing." Original sense survives in military 意为 "align columns of troops." Dress up "attire elaborately" 始于 1670 年代; to dress (someone) down (1769 年) is ironical. 同源词：Dressed; dressing. Dressing down "wearing clothes less formal than expected" 始于 1960 年.

example.en: Guests are expected to dress formally for the award ceremony.
example.zh: 出席颁奖典礼的嘉宾须着正式服装。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, literally "a being driven" (of snow, etc.); not recorded in Old English; either a suffixed form of drive (v.) (compare thrift/thrive) or borrowed from Old Norse drift "snow drift," or Middle Dutch drift "pasturage, drove, flock," both from Proto-Germanic *driftiz (source also of Danish and Swedish drift, German Trift), from PIE root *dhreibh- "to drive, push" (see drive (v.)). Sense of "what one is getting at" is from 1520s. Meaning "controlled slide of a sports car" attested by 1955.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 字面义为 "a being driven" (of snow, etc.); not recorded in 古英语; either a suffixed form of drive （动） (对比 thrift/thrive) or 借自 古北欧语 drift "snow drift," or Middle 荷兰语 drift "pasturage, drove, flock," both 源自 原始日耳曼语 *driftiz (source also of Danish and Swedish drift, 德语 Trift), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dhreibh- "to drive, push" （参见 drive （动）). 义为 "what one is getting at" 始于 1520 年代. 义为 "controlled slide of a sports car" attested 截至 1955 年.

example.en: Clouds began to drift slowly across the afternoon sky.
example.zh: 云朵开始慢慢地飘过下午的天空。

definitionLines: v./n. 练习，操练，训练；钻孔， 打孔
entries.definition: v./n. 练习，操练，训练；钻孔， 打孔
entries.etymology: c. 1600 (implied in drilling), from Dutch drillen "to bore (a hole), turn around, whirl," from Proto-Germanic *thr- (source also of Middle High German drillen "to turn, round off, bore," Old Engish þyrel "hole"), from PIE *tere- (1) "to turn, rub" (see throw (v.)). Sense of "to instruct in military exercise" is 1620s (also in Dutch drillen and in the Danish and German cognates), probably from the notion of troops "turning" in maneuvers. Extended noun sense of "the agreed-upon procedure" is from 1940. Related: Drilled.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年 (implied in drilling), 源自 荷兰语 drillen "to bore (a hole), turn around, whirl," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *thr- (source also of Middle High 德语 drillen "to turn, round off, bore," Old Engish þyrel "hole"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *tere- (1) "to turn, rub" （参见 throw （动）). 义为 "to instruct in military exercise" is 1620 年代 (also in 荷兰语 drillen and in the Danish and 德语 cognates), 可能 源自 概念 troops "turning" in maneuvers. Extended 名词 语义 "the agreed-upon procedure" 始于 1940 年. 同源词：Drilled.

example.en: The soldiers were put through intensive combat drill every morning.
example.zh: 士兵们每天早晨都要接受高强度的战斗操练。

entries.definition: v.饮，喝，饮酒 n. 饮料，酒
entries.etymology:
Old English drincan "to drink," also "to swallow up, engulf" (class III strong verb; past tense dranc, past participle druncen), from Proto-Germanic *drenkan (source also of Old Saxon drinkan, Old Frisian drinka, Dutch drinken, Old High German trinkan, German trinken, Old Norse drekka, Gothic drigkan "to drink"), which is of uncertain origin or connections, perhaps from a root meaning "to draw."

Most Indo-European words for this trace to PIE *po(i)- (source of Greek pino, Latin biber, Irish ibim, Old Church Slavonic piti, Russian pit'; see imbibe).

The noun meaning "beverage, alcoholic beverage" was in late Old English.

To drink like a fish is first recorded 1747.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 drincan "to drink," also "to swallow up, engulf" (class III strong 动词; past tense dranc, past participle druncen), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *drenkan (source also of 古撒克逊语 drinkan, 古弗里西语 drinka, 荷兰语 drinken, 古高地德语 trinkan, 德语 trinken, 古北欧语 drekka, Gothic drigkan "to drink"), which is 来源存疑 or connections, 或源自 a root 意为 "to draw." Most Indo-European words for this trace to 原始印欧语 (PIE) *po(i)- (source of 希腊语 pino, 拉丁语 biber, 爱尔兰语 ibim, Old Church Slavonic piti, 俄语 pit'; 参见 imbibe). The 名词 意为 "beverage, alcoholic beverage" was in late 古英语. To drink like a fish is 首见于 1747 年.

definitionLines: vt. 驾驶，开动；驱，赶；驱使， 迫使
entries.definition: vt. 驾驶，开动；驱，赶；驱使， 迫使 vi. 驾驶，开车
entries.etymology: Old English drifan "to drive, force, hunt, pursue; rush against" (class I strong verb; past tense draf, past participle drifen), from Proto-Germanic *driban (source also of Old Frisian driva, Old Saxon driban, Dutch drijven, Old High German triban, German treiben, Old Norse drifa, Gothic dreiban "to drive"), from PIE root *dhreibh- "to drive, push." Original sense of "pushing from behind," altered in Modern English by application to automobiles. Related: Driving.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 drifan "to drive, force, hunt, pursue; rush against" (class I strong 动词; past tense draf, past participle drifen), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *driban (source also of 古弗里西语 driva, 古撒克逊语 driban, 荷兰语 drijven, 古高地德语 triban, 德语 treiben, 古北欧语 drifa, Gothic dreiban "to drive"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dhreibh- "to drive, push." Original 语义 "pushing from behind," altered in 现代英语 by application to automobiles. 同源词：Driving.

example.en: She learned to drive a car before she turned eighteen.
example.zh: 她在十八岁之前就学会了开车。

entries.etymology: "one who drives" in various senses, c. 1400; agent noun from drive (v.). Slavery sense is attested by 1796. Driver's seat is attested by 1867; figurative use by 1954.
entries.etymologyZh: "one who drives" in various senses, 约 1400 年; agent 名词 源自 drive （动）. Slavery sense is attested 截至 1796 年. Driver's seat is attested 截至 1867 年; figurative use 截至 1954 年.

entries.definition: n. 下降，滴，水滴 vt.投下，落下；降低 vi.落下，下降
entries.etymology: Old English dropa "a drop of liquid," from Proto-Germanic *drupon (source also of Old Saxon dropo, Old Norse dropi, Dutch drop, Old High German tropfo, German Tropfen (n.)), from PIE *dhreu-. Meaning "an act of dropping" is from 1630s; of immaterial things (prices, temperatures, etc.) from mid-19c. Meaning "lozenge, hard candy" is 1723. Meaning "secret place where things can be left illicitly and picked up later" is from 1931. Drop in the bucket (late 14c.) is from Isa. ix:15 [KJV]. At the drop of a hat "suddenly" is from 1854; drop-in "casual visit" is 1819; drop-kick is 1857. To get the drop on someone originally was Old West gunslinger slang (1869).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dropa "a drop of liquid," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *drupon (source also of 古撒克逊语 dropo, 古北欧语 dropi, 荷兰语 drop, 古高地德语 tropfo, 德语 Tropfen （名）), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhreu-. 义为 "an act of dropping" 始于 1630 年代; of immaterial things (prices, temperatures, etc.) 源自 19 世纪中期 义为 "lozenge, hard candy" is 1723 年. 义为 "secret place where things can be left illicitly and picked up later" 始于 1931 年. Drop in the bucket (14 世纪晚期) 始于 Isa. ix:15 [KJV]. At the drop of a hat "suddenly" 始于 1854 年; drop-in "casual visit" is 1819 年; drop-kick is 1857 年. To get the drop on someone 原义为 was Old West gunslinger 俚语 (1869 年).

example.en: Sales dropped by forty percent after the product recall was announced.
example.zh: 产品召回宣布后，销量下降了百分之四十。

definitionLines: n. 中途退学；辍学学生
entries.definition: n. 中途退学；辍学学生
entries.etymology: "one who 'drops out' of something," 1930, from drop (v.) + out (adv.). As a phrase, drop out "withdraw" is recorded from 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: "one who 'drops out' of something," 1930 年, 源自 drop （动） + out （副）. 作为 phrase, drop out "withdraw" 见于 1550 年代.

entries.etymology: Old English drugað, drugoð "drought, dryness, desert," from Proto-Germanic *drugothaz, from Germanic root *dreug- "dry" (cf high/height) with *-itho, Germanic suffix for forming abstract nouns (see -th (2)). Drouth was a Middle English variant continued in Scottish and northern English dialect and in poetry.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 drugað, drugoð "drought, dryness, desert," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *drugothaz, 源自 日耳曼语 root *dreug- "dry" (cf high/height) with *-itho, 日耳曼语 suffix for forming abstract nouns （参见 -th (2)). Drouth was a 中古英语 variant continued in 苏格兰语 and northern English dialect and in poetry.

example.en: The prolonged drought devastated crops and left farmers in despair.
example.zh: 长期干旱摧毁了庄稼，让农民陷入绝望。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, transitive  and intransitive, perhaps from an unrecorded derivative word of Old English druncnian (Middle English druncnen) "be swallowed up by water" (originally of ships as well as living things), probably from the base of drincan "to drink."

Modern form is from northern England dialect, probably influenced by Old Norse drukna "be drowned." Related: Drowned; drowning.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, transitive and intransitive, 或源自 an unrecorded derivative word of 古英语 druncnian (中古英语 druncnen) "be swallowed up by water" (原义为 of ships as well as living things), 可能 源自 base of drincan "to drink." 现代 form 始于 northern England dialect, 可能 influenced by 古北欧语 drukna "be drowned." 同源词：Drowned; drowning.

example.en: The swimmer struggled not to drown in the strong current.
example.zh: 游泳者在湍急的水流中拼命挣扎以免溺水。

entries.etymology:
late 14c. (early 14c. in Anglo-French), "medicine, chemical ingredients," from Old French droge "supply, stock, provision" (14c.), which is of unknown origin, perhaps from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German droge-vate "dry barrels," or droge waere, literally "dry wares," but specifically drugs and spices, with first element mistaken as word for the contents (see dry goods), or because medicines mostly consisted of dried herbs.

Compare Latin species, in Late Latin "wares," then specialized to "spices" (French épice, English spice). The same source produced Italian and Spanish droga, Swedish drog.

Application to "narcotics and opiates" is late 19c., though association with "poisons" is 1500s. Druggie first recorded 1968. To be a drug on or in the market (mid-17c.) is of doubtful connection and may be a different word, perhaps a play on drag, which was sometimes drug c. 1240-1800.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 (14 世纪初 in 盎格鲁-法语), "medicine, chemical ingredients," 源自 古法语 droge "supply, stock, provision" (14 世纪), which is 来源不详, 或源自 Middle 荷兰语 or Middle Low 德语 droge-vate "dry barrels," or droge waere, 字面义为 "dry wares," but specifically drugs and spices, with first element mistaken as word for the contents （参见 dry goods)，或because medicines mostly consisted of dried herbs. 对比 拉丁语 species, in 晚期拉丁语 "wares," 之后 specialized to "spices" (法语 épice, English spice). The same source produced 意大利语 and 西班牙语 droga, Swedish drog. Application to "narcotics and opiates" is 19 世纪晚期, though association with "poisons" is 1500 年代. Druggie 首见于 1968 年. To be a drug on or in the market (17 世纪中期) is of doubtful connection and may be a different word, 或许 a play on drag, which was 有时 drug 约 1240 年-1800 年.

example.en: The doctor warned that misusing this drug could have serious side effects.
example.zh: 医生警告说滥用这种药物可能会产生严重的副作用。

entries.etymology: 1540s, probably from Middle Dutch tromme "drum," common Germanic (compare German Trommel, Danish tromme, Swedish trumma), probably of imitative origin. Not common before 1570s. Slightly older, and more common at first, was drumslade, apparently from Dutch or Low German trommelslag. Machinery sense attested from 1740, from similarity of shape.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 可能 源自 Middle 荷兰语 tromme "drum," common 日耳曼语 (对比 德语 Trommel, Danish tromme, Swedish trumma), 可能 of imitative origin. Not common before 1570 年代. Slightly older, and more common at first, was drumslade, 似乎 源自 荷兰语 or Low 德语 trommelslag. Machinery sense attested 自 1740 年起, 源自 similarity of shape.

example.en: He played the drum so loudly that the neighbors complained.
example.zh: 他打鼓打得太响，邻居都抱怨了。

entries.etymology: past participle of drink, used as an adjective from mid-14c. in sense "intoxicated." In various expressions, such as "drunk as a lord" (1891); Chaucer has "dronke ... as a Mous" (c. 1386); and, from 1709, "as Drunk as a Wheelbarrow." Medieval folklore distinguished four successive stages of drunkenness, based on the animals they made men resemble: sheep, lion, ape, sow. Drunk driver first recorded 1948. Drunk-tank "jail cell for drunkards" attested by 1912, American English. The noun meaning "drunken person" is from 1852; earlier this would have been a drunkard.
entries.etymologyZh: 为 … 的过去分词 drink, used 作形容词时 源自 14 世纪中期 in sense "intoxicated." Drunk-tank "jail cell for drunkards" attested 截至 1912 年, American English. The 名词 意为 "drunken person" 始于 1852 年; earlier this would have been a drunkard.

entries.etymology:
Old English dryge, from Proto-Germanic *draugiz (source also of Middle Low German dröge, Middle Dutch druge, Dutch droog, Old High German trucchon, German trocken, Old Norse draugr), from Germanic root *dreug- "dry."

Meaning "barren" is mid-14c. Of humor or jests, early 15c. (implied in dryly); as "uninteresting, tedious" from 1620s. Of places prohibiting alcoholic drink, 1870 (but dry feast, one at which no liquor is served, is from late 15c.; colloquial dry (n.) "prohibitionist" is 1888, American English). Dry goods (1708) were those measured out in dry, not liquid, measure. Dry land (that not under the sea) is from early 13c. Dry run is from 1940s.

Of places prohibiting alcoholic drink, 1870 年 (but dry feast, one at which no liquor is served, 始于 15 世纪晚期; 口语 dry （名） "prohibitionist" is 1888 年, American English). Dry goods (1708 年) were those measured out in dry, not liquid, measure. Dry land (that not under the sea) 始于 13 世纪初 Dry run 始于 1940 年代.

entries.etymology: 1540s, from Latin dubiosus "doubtful," from dubium "doubt," neuter of dubius "vacillating, moving two ways, fluctuating;" figuratively "wavering in opinion, doubting, doubtful," from duo "two" (see two), with a sense of "of two minds, undecided between two things." Old English also used tweo "two" to mean "doubt." Compare doubt (v.). Related: Dubiously; dubiousness.

entries.etymology:
early 14c., "customary, regular;" mid-14c., "owing, payable," from Old French deu, past participle of devoir "to owe," from Latin debere "to owe" (see debt).

In reference to points of the compass (as in due east) it is attested from c. 1600, originally nautical, from notion of "fitting, rightful." As an adverb from 1590s; as a noun from early 15c. Prepositional phrase due to (much maligned by grammarians) is from 1897.

In reference to points of the compass (as in due east) it 见于 约 1600 年, 原义为 nautical, 源自 概念 "fitting, rightful." 作为 副词 源自 1590 年代; 作名词时 源自 15 世纪初 Prepositional phrase due to (much maligned by grammarians) 始于 1897 年.

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "stupid;" early 13c., "blunt, not sharp;" rare before mid-14c., apparently from Old English dol "dull-witted, foolish," or an unrecorded parallel word, or from Middle Low German dul "slow-witted," both from Proto-Germanic *dulaz (source also of Old Frisian and Old Saxon dol "foolish," Old High German tol, German toll "mad, wild," Gothic dwals "foolish"), from PIE *dheu- (1) "dust, vapor, smoke" (and related notions of "defective perception or wits"). Of color from early 15c.; of pain or other sensations from 1725. Sense of "boring" first recorded 1580s.

Dullsville, slang for "town where nothing happens," attested from 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "stupid;" 13 世纪初, "blunt, not sharp;" rare before 14 世纪中期, 似乎 源自 古英语 dol "dull-witted, foolish," or an unrecorded parallel word，或源自 Middle Low 德语 dul "slow-witted," both 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dulaz (source also of 古弗里西语 and 古撒克逊语 dol "foolish," 古高地德语 tol, 德语 toll "mad, wild," Gothic dwals "foolish"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dheu- (1) "dust, vapor, smoke" (and related notions of "defective perception or wits"). Of color 源自 15 世纪初; of pain or other sensations 自 1725 年起. 义为 "boring" 首见于 1580 年代. Dullsville, 俚语 for "town where nothing happens," attested 自 1960 年起.
