entries.etymology:
Old English dumb "silent, unable to speak," from PIE *dheubh- "confusion, stupefaction, dizziness," from root *dheu- (1) "dust, mist, vapor, smoke," and related notions of "defective perception or wits."

The Old English, Old Saxon (dumb), Gothic (dumbs), and Old Norse (dumbr) forms of the word meant only "mute, speechless;" in Old High German (thumb) it meant both this and "stupid," and in Modern German this latter became the only sense. Meaning "foolish, ignorant" was occasionally in Middle English, but modern use (1823) comes from influence of German dumm. Related: dumber; dumbest.

Applied to silent contrivances, hence dumbwaiter. As a verb, in late Old English, "to become mute;" c. 1600, "to make mute." To dumb (something) down is from 1933.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dumb "silent, unable to speak," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dheubh- "confusion, stupefaction, dizziness," 源自 root *dheu- (1) "dust, mist, vapor, smoke," and related notions of "defective perception or wits." The 古英语, 古撒克逊语 (dumb), Gothic (dumbs), and 古北欧语 (dumbr) forms of the word meant only "mute, speechless;" in 古高地德语 (thumb) it meant both this and "stupid," and in 现代 德语 this latter became the only sense. 义为 "foolish, ignorant" was occasionally in 中古英语, but modern use (1823 年) comes 源自 influence of 德语 dumm. 同源词：dumber; dumbest. Applied to silent contrivances, hence dumbwaiter. 作动词时, in late 古英语, "to become mute;" 约 1600 年, "to make mute." To dumb (something) down 始于 1933 年.

entries.etymology: late 14c., durand, present participle of obsolete verb duren "to last, endure" (mid-13c.), from Old French durer, from Latin durare "endure" (see endure). During the day really is "while the day endures," and the usage is a transference into English of a Latin ablative absolute (compare durante bello "during (literally 'enduring') the war").

entries.etymology: c. 1200, dosk "obscure, to become dark," perhaps from Old English dox "dark-haired, dark from the absence of light" (cognate with Swedish duska "be misty," Latin fuscus "dark," Sanskrit dhusarah "dust-colored;" also compare Old English dosan "chestnut-brown," Old High German tusin "pale yellow") with transposition of -k- and -s-, perhaps via a Northumbrian variant (compare colloquial ax for ask). But OED notes that "few of our words in -sk are of OE origin." A color word originally; the sense of "twilight" is recorded from 1620s.

Meaning "that to which living matter decays" was in Old English, hence, figuratively, "mortal life."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dust, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dunstaz (source also of 古高地德语 tunst "storm, breath," 德语 Dunst "mist, vapor," Danish dyst "milldust," 荷兰语 duist), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dheu- (1) "dust, smoke, vapor" (source also of 梵语 dhu- "shake," 拉丁语 fumus "smoke"). 义为 "that to which living matter decays" was in 古英语, hence, figuratively, "mortal life."

entries.etymology:
Old English dweorh, dweorg (West Saxon), duerg (Mercian), "very short human being," from Proto-Germanic *dweraz (source also of Old Frisian dwerch, Old Saxon dwerg, Old High German twerg, German Zwerg, Old Norse dvergr), perhaps from PIE *dhwergwhos "something tiny," but with no established cognates outside Germanic. The mythological sense is 1770, from German (it seems never to have developed independently in English).

The shift of the Old English guttural at the end of the word to modern -f is typical (compare enough, draft). Old English plural dweorgas became Middle English dwarrows, later leveled down to dwarfs. The use of dwarves for the legendary race was popularized by J.R.R. Tolkien. As an adjective, from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dweorh, dweorg (West Saxon), duerg (Mercian), "very short human being," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dweraz (source also of 古弗里西语 dwerch, 古撒克逊语 dwerg, 古高地德语 twerg, 德语 Zwerg, 古北欧语 dvergr), 或源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhwergwhos "something tiny," but with no established cognates outside 日耳曼语. The mythological sense is 1770 年, 源自 德语 (it seems never to have developed independently in English). The shift of the 古英语 guttural at the end of the word to modern -f is typical (对比 enough, draft). 古英语 plural dweorgas became 中古英语 dwarrows, later leveled down to dwarfs. The use of dwarves for the legendary race was popularized by J.R.R. Tolkien. 作形容词时, 源自 1590 年代.

entries.etymology:
Old English dwellan "to mislead, deceive," originally "to make a fool of, lead astray," from Proto-Germanic *dwelan "to go or lead astray" (source also of Old Norse dvöl "delay," dvali "sleep;" Middle Dutch dwellen "to stun, make giddy, perplex;" Old High German twellen "to hinder, delay;" Danish dvale "trance, stupor," dvaelbær "narcotic berry," source of Middle English dwale "nightshade"), from PIE *dhwel-, extended form of root *dheu- (1) "dust, cloud, vapor, smoke" (and related notions of "defective perception or wits").

Related to Old English gedweola "error, heresy, madness." Sense shifted in Middle English through "hinder, delay," to "linger" (c. 1200, as still in phrase to dwell upon), to "make a home" (mid-13c.). Related: Dwelled; dwelt; dwells.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 dwellan "to mislead, deceive," 原义为 "to make a fool of, lead astray," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *dwelan "to go or lead astray" (source also of 古北欧语 dvöl "delay," dvali "sleep;" Middle 荷兰语 dwellen "to stun, make giddy, perplex;" 古高地德语 twellen "to hinder, delay;" Danish dvale "trance, stupor," dvaelbær "narcotic berry," source of 中古英语 dwale "nightshade"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dhwel-, extended form of root *dheu- (1) "dust, cloud, vapor, smoke" (and related notions of "defective perception or wits"). Related to 古英语 gedweola "error, heresy, madness." Sense shifted in 中古英语 through "hinder, delay," to "linger" (约 1200 年, as still in phrase to dwell upon), to "make a home" (13 世纪中期). 同源词：Dwelled; dwelt; dwells.

entries.etymology: Old English ælc (n., pron., adj.) "any, all, every, each (one)," short for a-gelic "ever alike," from a "ever" (see aye (2)) + gelic "alike" (see like (adj.)). From a common West Germanic expression *aiwo galika (source also of Dutch elk, Old Frisian ellik, Old High German iogilih, German jeglich "each, every"). Originally used as we now use every (which is a compound of each) or all; modern use is by influence of Latin quisque. Modern spelling appeared late 1500s. Also see ilk, such, which.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ælc (n., pron., adj.) "any, all, every, each (one)," short for a-gelic "ever alike," 源自 a "ever" （参见 aye (2)) + gelic "alike" （参见 like （形）). From a common West 日耳曼语 expression *aiwo galika (source also of 荷兰语 elk, 古弗里西语 ellik, 古高地德语 iogilih, 德语 jeglich "each, every"). Originally used as we 现在 use every (which is a 由 … 复合而成 each) or all; modern use is by influence of 拉丁语 quisque. 现代 spelling appeared late 1500 年代. Also 参见 ilk, such, which.

entries.etymology:
late 13c., "strenuous, ardent, fierce, angry," from Old French aigre "sour, acid; harsh, bitter, rough; eager greedy; lively, active, forceful," from Latin acrem (nominative acer) "keen, sharp, pointed, piercing; acute, ardent, zealous" (see acrid).

Meaning "full of keen desire" (early 14c.) seems to be peculiar to English. The English word kept a secondary meaning of "pungent, sharp-edged" till 19c. (as in Shakespeare's "The bitter clamour of two eager tongues," in "Richard II"). Related: Eagerly; eagerness. Eager beaver "glutton for work" [OED] is from 1943, U.S. armed forces slang.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "strenuous, ardent, fierce, angry," 源自 古法语 aigre "sour, acid; harsh, bitter, rough; eager greedy; lively, active, forceful," 源自 拉丁语 acrem (主格 acer) "keen, sharp, pointed, piercing; acute, ardent, zealous" （参见 acrid). 义为 "full of keen desire" (14 世纪初) seems to be peculiar to English. The English word kept a secondary 意为 of "pungent, sharp-edged" till 19 世纪 (as in Shakespeare's "The bitter clamour of two eager tongues," in "Richard II"). 同源词：Eagerly; eagerness. Eager beaver "glutton for work" [OED] 始于 1943 年, U.S. armed forces 俚语.

example.en: She was eager to learn everything she could about marine biology.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French egle, from Old Provençal aigla, from Latin aquila "black eagle," fem. of aquilus, often explained as "dark colored" (bird); see aquiline. The native term was erne. Golf score sense is by 1908 (according to old golf sources, because it "soars higher" than a birdie). As the name of a U.S. $10 coin minted from 1792 to 1933, established in the 1786 resolution for a new monetary system (but at first only the desperately needed small copper coins were minted). The figurative eagle-eyed is attested from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 egle, 源自 Old Provençal aigla, 源自 拉丁语 aquila "black eagle," fem. of aquilus, 常 explained as "dark colored" (bird); 参见 aquiline. The 本族 term was erne. Golf score sense is 截至 1908 年 (according to old golf sources, because it "soars higher" than a birdie). As the name of a U.S. $10 coin minted 自 1792 年起 to 1933 年, established in the 1786 年 resolution for a new monetary system (but at first only the desperately needed small copper coins were minted). The figurative eagle-eyed 见于 约 1600 年.

entries.etymology: Old English ærlice "early," from ær "soon, ere" (see ere) + -lice, adverbial suffix (see -ly (2)). Compare Old Norse arliga "early." The adjective is Old English ærlic. The early bird of the proverb is from 1670s. Related: Earlier; earliest.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ærlice "early," 源自 ær "soon, ere" （参见 ere) + -lice, adverbial suffix （参见 -ly (2)). 对比 古北欧语 arliga "early." The 形容词 is 古英语 ærlic. The early bird of the proverb 始于 1670 年代. 同源词：Earlier; earliest.

example.en: He arrived early and managed to get a seat near the front.
example.zh: 他来得很早，设法找到了前排的座位。

entries.etymology: Old English earnian "deserve, earn, merit, labor for, win, get a reward for labor," from Proto-Germanic *aznon "do harvest work, serve" (source also of Old Frisian esna "reward, pay"), denominative verb from *azno "labor" especially "field labor" (source of Old Norse önn "work in the field," Old High German arnon "to reap"), from PIE root *es-en- "harvest, fall" (source also of Old High German aren "harvest, crop," German Ernte "harvest," Old English ern "harvest," Gothic asans "harvest, summer," Old Church Slavonic jeseni, Russian osen, Old Prussian assanis "autumn"). Also from the same root are Gothic asneis, Old High German esni "hired laborer, day laborer," Old English esne "serf, laborer, man." Related: Earned; earning.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 earnian "deserve, earn, merit, labor for, win, get a reward for labor," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aznon "do harvest work, serve" (source also of 古弗里西语 esna "reward, pay"), denominative 动词 源自 *azno "labor" 尤指 "field labor" (source of 古北欧语 önn "work in the field," 古高地德语 arnon "to reap"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *es-en- "harvest, fall" (source also of 古高地德语 aren "harvest, crop," 德语 Ernte "harvest," 古英语 ern "harvest," Gothic asans "harvest, summer," Old Church Slavonic jeseni, 俄语 osen, Old Prussian assanis "autumn"). Also 源自 same root are Gothic asneis, 古高地德语 esni "hired laborer, day laborer," 古英语 esne "serf, laborer, man." 同源词：Earned; earning.

example.en: He works two jobs just to earn enough money to support his family.
example.zh: 他打两份工，只为挣到足够的钱养家。

entries.etymology: amount of money one makes (from labor or investment), 1732, from plural of verbal noun earning, from earn (v.). Old English had earnung in sense "fact of deserving; what one deserves; merit, reward, consideration, pay," but the modern word seems to be a new formation.
entries.etymologyZh: amount of money one makes (源自 labor or investment), 1732 年, 源自 为 … 的复数 verbal 名词 earning, 源自 earn （动）. 古英语 had earnung in sense "fact of deserving; what one deserves; merit, reward, consideration, pay," but the modern word seems to be a new formation.

example.en: Her annual earnings doubled after she got promoted to manager.
example.zh: 升任经理后，她的年收入翻了一番。

entries.etymology: Old English eorþe "ground, soil, dirt, dry land; country, district," also used (along with middangeard) for "the (material) world, the abode of man" (as opposed to the heavens or the underworld), from Proto-Germanic *ertho (source also of Old Frisian erthe "earth," Old Saxon ertha, Old Norse jörð, Middle Dutch eerde, Dutch aarde, Old High German erda, German Erde, Gothic airþa), from extended form of PIE root *er- (2) "earth, ground" (source also of Middle Irish -ert "earth"). The earth considered as a planet was so called from c. 1400. Use in old chemistry is from 1728. Earth-mover "large digging machine" is from 1940.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 eorþe "ground, soil, dirt, dry land; country, district," also used (along with middangeard) for "the (material) world, the abode of man" (as opposed to the heavens or the underworld), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ertho (source also of 古弗里西语 erthe "earth," 古撒克逊语 ertha, 古北欧语 jörð, Middle 荷兰语 eerde, 荷兰语 aarde, 古高地德语 erda, 德语 Erde, Gothic airþa), 源自 extended form of 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *er- (2) "earth, ground" (source also of Middle 爱尔兰语 -ert "earth"). The earth considered 作为 planet was so called 源自 约 1400 年. Use in old chemistry 始于 1728 年. Earth-mover "large digging machine" 始于 1940 年.

example.en: Scientists warn that rising temperatures are threatening life on earth.
example.zh: 科学家警告说，气温上升正在威胁地球上的生命。

entries.etymology: late 13c., eorthequakynge, from earth + quake (n.). In this sense Old English had eorðdyn, eorðhrernes, eorðbeofung, eorðstyrung.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, eorthequakynge, 源自 earth + quake （名）. In this sense 古英语 had eorðdyn, eorðhrernes, eorðbeofung, eorðstyrung.

example.en: The earthquake destroyed thousands of homes and left many families homeless.
example.zh: 这场地震摧毁了数千座房屋，使许多家庭无家可归。

definitionLines: n. 容易，轻易；安逸，安心；
entries.definition: n. 容易，轻易；安逸，安心； v. 减轻，放松，缓和
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "physical comfort, undisturbed state of the body; tranquility, peace of mind," from Old French aise "comfort, pleasure, well-being; opportunity," which is of unknown origin, despite attempts to link it to various Latin verbs; perhaps Celtic. According to OED, the earliest senses in French appear to be 1. "elbow-room" (from an 11th century Hebrew-French glossary) and 2. "opportunity." This led Sophus Bugge to suggest an origin in Vulgar Latin asa, a shortened form of Latin ansa "handle," which could be used in the figurative sense of "opportunity, occasion," as well as being a possible synonym for "elbow," because Latin ansatus "furnished with handles" also was used to mean "having the arms akimbo." OED editors add, "This is not very satisfactory, but it does not appear that any equally plausible alternative has yet been proposed."

At ease "at rest, at peace, in comfort" is from late 14c.; as a military order (1802) the word denotes "freedom from stiffness or formality."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "physical comfort, undisturbed state of the body; tranquility, peace of mind," 源自 古法语 aise "comfort, pleasure, well-being; opportunity," which is 来源不详, despite attempts to link it to various 拉丁语 verbs; 或许 Celtic. According to OED, the earliest senses in 法语 appear to be 1. "elbow-room" (源自 an 11th century 希伯来语-法语 glossary) and 2. "opportunity." This led Sophus Bugge to suggest an origin in 通俗拉丁语 asa, a shortened form of 拉丁语 ansa "handle," which could be used in the figurative 语义 "opportunity, occasion," as well as being a possible synonym for "elbow," because 拉丁语 ansatus "furnished with handles" also was used to mean "having the arms akimbo." OED editors add, "This is not very satisfactory, but it does not appear that any equally plausible alternative has yet been proposed." At ease "at rest, at peace, in comfort" 始于 14 世纪晚期; 作为 military order (1802 年) the word denotes "freedom from stiffness or formality."

example.en: The medication helped ease the pain within an hour.
example.zh: 这种药物在一小时内帮助减轻了疼痛。

entries.definition: n. /a. 东方（的），东部（的） ad. 向/自/在东方
entries.etymology:
Old English east, eastan (adj., adv.) "east, easterly, eastward;" easte (n.), from Proto-Germanic *aust- "east," literally "toward the sunrise" (source also of Old Frisian ast "east," aster "eastward," Dutch oost Old Saxon ost, Old High German ostan, German Ost, Old Norse austr "from the east"), from PIE *aus- (1) "to shine," especially of the dawn (source also of Sanskrit ushas "dawn;" Greek aurion "morning;" Old Irish usah, Lithuanian auszra "dawn;" Latin aurora "dawn," auster "south;" see aurora). The east is the direction in which dawn breaks. For theory of shift in the geographical sense in Latin, see Australia.

As one of the four cardinal points of the compass, from c. 1200. Meaning "the eastern part of the world" (from Europe) is from c. 1300. Cold War use of East for "communist states" first recorded 1951. French est, Spanish este are borrowings from Middle English, originally nautical. The east wind in Biblical Palestine was scorching and destructive (as in Ezek. xvii:10); in New England it is bleak, wet, unhealthful. East End of London so called by 1846; East Side of Manhattan so called from 1871; East Indies (India and Southeast Asia) so called 1590s to distinguish them from the West Indies.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 east, eastan (adj., adv.) "east, easterly, eastward;" easte （名）, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aust- "east," 字面义为 "toward the sunrise" (source also of 古弗里西语 ast "east," aster "eastward," 荷兰语 oost 古撒克逊语 ost, 古高地德语 ostan, 德语 Ost, 古北欧语 austr "from the east"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *aus- (1) "to shine," 尤指 of the dawn (source also of 梵语 ushas "dawn;" 希腊语 aurion "morning;" Old 爱尔兰语 usah, Lithuanian auszra "dawn;" 拉丁语 aurora "dawn," auster "south;" 参见 aurora). The east is the direction in which dawn breaks. For theory of shift in the geographical sense in 拉丁语, 参见 Australia. As one of the four cardinal points of the compass, 源自 约 1200 年. 义为 "the eastern part of the world" (源自 Europe) 始于 约 1300 年. Cold War use of East for "communist states" 首见于 1951 年. 法语 est, 西班牙语 este are borrowings 源自 中古英语, 原义为 nautical. The east wind in Biblical Palestine was scorching and destructive (as in Ezek. xvii:10); in New England it is bleak, wet, unhealthful. East End of London so called 截至 1846 年; East Side of Manhattan so called 自 1871 年起; East Indies (India and Southeast Asia) so called 1590 年代 to distinguish them 源自 West Indies.

definitionLines: a. 东方的，东部的，朝东的
entries.definition: a. 东方的，东部的，朝东的
entries.etymology: Old English easterne "of the east, from the east; oriental; of the Eastern Orthodox Church; of the eastern part of the globe," from east + -erne, suffix denoting direction. Cognate with Old Saxon ostroni, Old High German ostroni, Old Norse austroenn. Eastern Shore of Maryland and Virginia so called from 1620s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 easterne "of the east, from the east; oriental; of the Eastern Orthodox Church; of the eastern part of the globe," 源自 east + -erne, suffix denoting direction. Cognate with 古撒克逊语 ostroni, 古高地德语 ostroni, 古北欧语 austroenn. Eastern Shore of Maryland and Virginia so called 源自 1620 年代.

example.en: The eastern coast of the country is known for its dramatic cliffs.
example.zh: 该国东部海岸以其壮观的悬崖而闻名。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "at ease, having ease, free from bodily discomfort and anxiety," from Old French aisie "comfortable, at ease, rich, well-off" (Modern French aisé), past participle of aisier "to put at ease," from aise (see ease (n.)). Sense of "not difficult, requiring no great labor or effort" is from late 13c.; of conditions, "offering comfort, pleasant," early 14c. Of persons, "lenient, kind, calm, gentle," late 14c. Meaning "readily yielding, not difficult of persuasion" is from 1610s. The concept of "not difficult" was expressed in Old English and early Middle English by eaþe (adv.), ieþe (adj.), apparently common West Germanic (compare German öde "empty, desolate," but of disputed origin.

Easy Street is from 1890. Easy money attested by 1889; to take it easy "relax" is from 1804 (be easy in same sense recorded from 1746); easy does it recorded by 1835. Easy rider (1912) was African-American vernacular for "sexually satisfying lover." The easy listening radio format is from 1961, defined by William Safire (in 1986) as, "the music of the 60's played in the 80's with the style of the 40's."  Related: Easier; easiest.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "at ease, having ease, free from bodily discomfort and anxiety," 源自 古法语 aisie "comfortable, at ease, rich, well-off" (现代法语 aisé), 为 … 的过去分词 aisier "to put at ease," 源自 aise （参见 ease （名）). 义为 "not difficult, requiring no great labor or effort" 始于 13 世纪晚期; of conditions, "offering comfort, pleasant," 14 世纪初 Of persons, "lenient, kind, calm, gentle," 14 世纪晚期 义为 "readily yielding, not difficult of persuasion" 始于 1610 年代. The concept of "not difficult" was expressed in 古英语 and early 中古英语 by eaþe （副）, ieþe （形）, 似乎 common West 日耳曼语 (对比 德语 öde "empty, desolate," but of disputed origin. Easy Street 始于 1890 年. Easy money attested 截至 1889 年; to take it easy "relax" 始于 1804 年 (be easy in same sense recorded 自 1746 年起); easy does it recorded 截至 1835 年. Easy rider (1912 年) was African-American vernacular for "sexually satisfying lover." The easy listening radio format 始于 1961 年, defined by William Safire (于 1986 年) as, "the music of the 60's played in the 80's with the style of the 40's." 同源词：Easier; easiest.

definitionLines: a. 随和的，容易相处的
entries.definition: a. 随和的，容易相处的
entries.etymology: also easygoing, "good-natured," 1640s, from easy + going.
entries.etymologyZh: also easygoing, "good-natured," 1640 年代, 源自 easy + going.

entries.etymology:
Old English etan (class V strong verb; past tense æt, past participle eten) "to consume food, devour, consume," from Proto-Germanic *etan (source also of Old Frisian ita, Old Saxon etan, Middle Dutch eten, Dutch eten, Old High German ezzan, German essen, Old Norse eta, Gothic itan), from PIE root *ed- "to eat" (see edible).

Transferred sense of "corrode, wear away, consume, waste" is from 1550s. Meaning "to preoccupy, engross" (as in what's eating you?) first recorded 1893. Slang sexual sense of "do cunnilingus on" is first recorded 1927. The slang phrase eat one's words "retract, take back what one has uttered" is from 1570s; to eat one's heart out is from 1590s; for eat one's hat, see hat. Eat-in (adj.) in reference to kitchens is from 1955. To eat out "dine away from home" is from 1930.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 etan (class V strong 动词; past tense æt, past participle eten) "to consume food, devour, consume," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *etan (source also of 古弗里西语 ita, 古撒克逊语 etan, Middle 荷兰语 eten, 荷兰语 eten, 古高地德语 ezzan, 德语 essen, 古北欧语 eta, Gothic itan), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ed- "to eat" （参见 edible). Transferred 语义 "corrode, wear away, consume, waste" 始于 1550 年代. 义为 "to preoccupy, engross" (as in what's eating you?) first recorded 1893. Slang sexual sense of "do cunnilingus on" is first recorded 1927. The slang phrase eat one's words "retract, take back what one has uttered" 始于 1570 年代; to eat one's heart out is from 1590s; for eat one's hat, 参见 hat. Eat-in （形） in reference to kitchens 始于 1955 年. To eat out "dine away from home" 始于 1930 年.

example.en: Doctors advise patients to eat less salt to reduce blood pressure.
example.zh: 医生建议患者少吃盐以降低血压。

entries.definition: a. 古的，反常的 n. 古怪的人
entries.etymology: early 15c., "eccentric circle or orbit," originally a term in Ptolemaic astronomy, "circle or orbit not having the Earth precisely at its center," from Middle French eccentrique and directly from Medieval Latin eccentricus (noun and adjective), from Greek ekkentros "out of the center" (as opposed to concentric), from ek "out" (see ex-) + kentron "center" (see center (n.)). Meaning "odd or whimsical person" is attested by 1817 (S.W. Ryley, "The Itinerant, or Memoirs of an Actor").
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "eccentric circle or orbit," 原义为 a term in Ptolemaic astronomy, "circle or orbit not having the Earth precisely at its center," 源自 中古法语 eccentrique and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 eccentricus (名词 and 形容词), 源自 希腊语 ekkentros "out of the center" (as opposed to concentric), 源自 ek "out" （参见 ex-) + kentron "center" （参见 center （名）). 义为 "odd or whimsical person" is attested 截至 1817 年 (S.W. Ryley, "The Itinerant, or Memoirs of an Actor").

entries.definition: n. 回声，反响 v. 发出回声，共鸣
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "sound repeated by reflection," from Latin echo, from Greek echo, personified in classical mythology as a mountain nymph who pined away for love of Narcissus until nothing was left of her but her voice, from or related to ekhe "sound," ekhein "to resound," from PIE *wagh-io-, extended form of root *(s)wagh- "to resound" (source also of Sanskrit vagnuh "sound," Latin vagire "to cry," Old English swogan "to resound"). Related: Echoes. Echo chamber attested from 1937.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "sound repeated by reflection," 源自 拉丁语 echo, 源自 希腊语 echo, personified in classical mythology 作为 mountain nymph who pined away for love of Narcissus until nothing was left of her but her voice, 源自 or related to ekhe "sound," ekhein "to resound," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wagh-io-, extended form of root *(s)wagh- "to resound" (source also of 梵语 vagnuh "sound," 拉丁语 vagire "to cry," 古英语 swogan "to resound"). 同源词：Echoes. Echo chamber attested 自 1937 年起.

example.en: The tour guide's voice seemed to echo off the stone walls of the cave.
example.zh: 导游的声音似乎从山洞的石壁上回响了出来。

definitionLines: vt. 形成食；使黯然失色
n. 日食，月食；黯然失色
entries.definition: vt. 形成食；使黯然失色 n. 日食，月食；黯然失色
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French eclipse "eclipse, darkness" (12c.), from Latin eclipsis, from Greek ekleipsis "an eclipse; an abandonment," literally "a failing, forsaking," from ekleipein "to forsake a usual place, fail to appear, be eclipsed," from ek "out" (see ex-) + leipein "to leave" (cognate with Latin linquere; see relinquish).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 eclipse "eclipse, darkness" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 eclipsis, 源自 希腊语 ekleipsis "an eclipse; an abandonment," 字面义为 "a failing, forsaking," 源自 ekleipein "to forsake a usual place, fail to appear, be eclipsed," 源自 ek "out" （参见 ex-) + leipein "to leave" (与 … 同源 拉丁语 linquere; 参见 relinquish).

entries.etymology: 1873, oecology, "branch of science dealing with the relationship of living things to their environments," coined in German by German zoologist Ernst Haeckel (1834-1919) as Ökologie, from Greek oikos "house, dwelling place, habitation" (see villa) + -logia "study of" (see -logy). In use with reference to anti-pollution activities from 1960s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1873 年, oecology, "branch of science dealing with the relationship of living things to their environments," coined in 德语 by 德语 zoologist Ernst Haeckel (1834 年-1919 年) as Ökologie, 源自 希腊语 oikos "house, dwelling place, habitation" （参见 villa) + -logia "study of" （参见 -logy). In use with reference to anti-pollution activities 源自 1960 年代.

example.en: The professor taught a course on urban ecology and green city planning.
example.zh: 这位教授讲授了一门关于城市生态学与绿色城市规划的课程。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "pertaining to management of a household," perhaps shortened from economical, or else from French économique or directly from Latin oeconomicus "of domestic economy," from Greek oikonomikos "practiced in the management of a household or family" (also the name of a treatise by Xenophon on the duties of domestic life), hence, "frugal, thrifty," from oikonomia "household management" (see economy (n.)). Meaning "relating to the science of economics" is from 1835 and now is the main sense, economical retaining the older one of "characterized by thrift."
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "pertaining to management of a household," 或许 shortened 源自 economical，或else 源自 法语 économique or 直接源自 拉丁语 oeconomicus "of domestic economy," 源自 希腊语 oikonomikos "practiced in the management of a household or family" (also the name of a treatise by Xenophon on the duties of domestic life), hence, "frugal, thrifty," 源自 oikonomia "household management" （参见 economy （名）). 义为 "relating to the science of economics" 始于 1835 年 and 现在 is the main sense, economical retaining the older one of "characterized by thrift."

example.en: Rising inflation remains the most pressing economic challenge facing households.
example.zh: 不断上升的通货膨胀仍是家庭面临的最紧迫的经济挑战。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "pertaining to household management;" from economic + -al (1). Sense of "pertaining to political economy" is from 1781, but that sense more commonly goes with economic, and the main modern sense of this spelling is "thrifty" (1780). Related: Economically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "pertaining to household management;" 源自 economic + -al (1). 义为 "pertaining to political economy" 始于 1781 年, but that sense more commonly goes with economic, and the main modern 语义 this spelling is "thrifty" (1780 年). 同源词：Economically.

example.en: Cooking at home rather than eating out is far more economical, saving the family hundreds of dollars each month.
example.zh: 在家做饭而不是下馆子要划算得多，每月能为这个家庭省下数百美元。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "art of managing a household," perhaps from French économique (see economic); also see -ics. Meaning "science of wealth" is from 1792.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "art of managing a household," 或源自 法语 économique （参见 economic); also 参见 -ics. 义为 "science of wealth" 始于 1792 年.

example.en: She studied economics at university and later worked in finance.
example.zh: 她在大学学习经济学，后来进入金融领域工作。

definitionLines: n. 经济，经济制度；节约，节省
entries.definition: n. 经济，经济制度；节约，节省
entries.etymology: 1530s, "household management," from Latin oeconomia (source of French économie, Spanish economia, German Ökonomie, etc.), from Greek oikonomia "household management, thrift," from oikonomos "manager, steward," from oikos "house, abode, dwelling" (cognate with Latin vicus "district," vicinus "near;" Old English wic "dwelling, village;" see villa) + nomos "managing," from nemein "manage" (see numismatic). Meaning "frugality, judicious use of resources" is from 1660s. The sense of "wealth and resources of a country" (short for political economy) is from 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "household management," 源自 拉丁语 oeconomia (source of 法语 économie, 西班牙语 economia, 德语 Ökonomie, etc.), 源自 希腊语 oikonomia "household management, thrift," 源自 oikonomos "manager, steward," 源自 oikos "house, abode, dwelling" (与 … 同源 拉丁语 vicus "district," vicinus "near;" 古英语 wic "dwelling, village;" 参见 villa) + nomos "managing," 源自 nemein "manage" （参见 numismatic). 义为 "frugality, judicious use of resources" 始于 1660 年代. The 语义 "wealth and resources of a country" (short for political economy) 始于 1650 年代.

example.en: The country's economy depends heavily on exports of oil and gas.
example.zh: 该国经济在很大程度上依赖石油和天然气出口。

entries.etymology: 1935; see eco- + system. Perhaps coined by English ecologist Sir Arthur George Tansley (1871-1955).
entries.etymologyZh: 1935 年; 参见 eco- + system. Perhaps coined by English ecologist Sir Arthur George Tansley (1871 年-1955 年).

entries.etymology:
Old English ecg "corner, edge, point," also "sword" (also found in ecgplega, literally "edge play," ecghete, literally "edge hate," both used poetically for "battle"), from Proto-Germanic *agjo (source also of Old Frisian egg "edge;" Old Saxon eggia "point, edge;" Middle Dutch egghe, Dutch eg; Old Norse egg, see egg (v.); Old High German ecka, German Eck "corner"), from PIE root *ak- "sharp, pointed" (source also of Sanskrit asrih "edge," Latin acies, Greek akis "point;" see acrid).

Spelling development of Old English -cg to Middle English -gg to Modern English -dge represents a widespread shift in pronunciation. To get the edge on (someone) is U.S. colloquial, first recorded 1911. Edge city is from Joel Garreau's 1992 book of that name. Razor's edge as a perilous narrow path translates Greek epi xyrou akmes. To be on edge "excited or irritable" is from 1872; to have (one's) teeth on edge is from late 14c., though "It is not quite clear what is the precise notion originally expressed in this phrase" [OED].
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ecg "corner, edge, point," also "sword" (also found in ecgplega, 字面义为 "edge play," ecghete, 字面义为 "edge hate," both used poetically for "battle"), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *agjo (source also of 古弗里西语 egg "edge;" 古撒克逊语 eggia "point, edge;" Middle 荷兰语 egghe, 荷兰语 eg; 古北欧语 egg, 参见 egg （动）; 古高地德语 ecka, 德语 Eck "corner"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ak- "sharp, pointed" (source also of 梵语 asrih "edge," 拉丁语 acies, 希腊语 akis "point;" 参见 acrid). Spelling development of 古英语 -cg to 中古英语 -gg to 现代英语 -dge represents a widespread shift in pronunciation. To get the edge on (someone) is U.S. 口语, 首见于 1911 年. Edge city 始于 Joel Garreau's 1992 book of that name. Razor's edge 作为 perilous narrow path translates 希腊语 epi xyrou akmes. To be on edge "excited or irritable" 始于 1872 年; to have (one's) teeth on edge 始于 14 世纪晚期, though "It is not quite clear what is the precise notion originally expressed in this phrase" [OED].

example.en: She stood at the edge of the cliff and looked down nervously.
example.zh: 她站在悬崖边缘，紧张地向下张望。

entries.etymology: 1791, "to publish," perhaps a back-formation from editor, or from French éditer (itself a back-formation from édition) or from Latin editus, past participle of edere "give out, put out, publish" (see edition). Meaning "to supervise for publication" is from 1793. Meaning "make revisions to a manuscript, etc.," is from 1885. Related: Edited; editing. As a noun, by 1960, "an act of editing."
entries.etymologyZh: 1791 年, "to publish," 或许 a back-formation 源自 editor，或源自 法语 éditer (itself a back-formation 源自 édition) or 源自 拉丁语 editus, 为 … 的过去分词 edere "give out, put out, publish" （参见 edition). 义为 "to supervise for publication" 始于 1793 年. 义为 "make revisions to a manuscript, etc.," 始于 1885 年. 同源词：Edited; editing. 作名词时, 截至 1960 年, "an act of editing."

example.en: She spent the afternoon editing the article before submitting it to the journal.
example.zh: 她花了整个下午编辑这篇文章，然后将其提交给期刊。

entries.etymology: 1640s, "publisher," from Latin editor "one who puts forth," agent noun from editus, past participle of edere "to bring forth, produce" (see edition). By 1712 in sense of "person who prepares written matter for publication;" specific sense in newspapers is from 1803.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "publisher," 源自 拉丁语 editor "one who puts forth," agent 名词 源自 editus, 为 … 的过去分词 edere "to bring forth, produce" （参见 edition). By 1712 年 in 语义 "person who prepares written matter for publication;" specific sense in newspapers 始于 1803 年.

example.en: The editor spent the afternoon correcting grammar errors in the manuscript.
example.zh: 编辑花了一下午时间修改手稿中的语法错误。

entries.etymology: 1741, "pertaining to an editor;" see editor + -al (2). Noun meaning "newspaper article by an editor," is from 1830, American English, from the adjective in reference to such writings (1802). Related: Editorially.
entries.etymologyZh: 1741 年, "pertaining to an editor;" 参见 editor + -al (2). Noun 意为 "newspaper article by an editor," 始于 1830 年, American English, 源自 形容词 in reference to such writings (1802 年). 同源词：Editorially.

example.en: The newspaper published an editorial criticizing the new policy.

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., "bring up (children), to train," from Latin educatus, past participle of educare "bring up, rear, educate" (source also of Italian educare, Spanish educar, French éduquer), which is a frequentative of or otherwise related to educere "bring out, lead forth," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + ducere "to lead" (see duke (n.)). Meaning "provide schooling" is first attested 1580s. Related: Educated; educating.

According to "Century Dictionary," educere, of a child, is "usually with reference to bodily nurture or support, while educare refers more frequently to the mind," and, "There is no authority for the common statement that the primary sense of education is to 'draw out or unfold the powers of the mind.'"
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "bring up (children), to train," 源自 拉丁语 educatus, 为 … 的过去分词 educare "bring up, rear, educate" (source also of 意大利语 educare, 西班牙语 educar, 法语 éduquer), which is a 为 … 的反复体 or otherwise related to educere "bring out, lead forth," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + ducere "to lead" （参见 duke （名）). 义为 "provide schooling" is 最早见于 1580 年代. 同源词：Educated; educating. According to "Century Dictionary," educere, of a child, is "usually with reference to bodily nurture or support, while educare refers more frequently to the mind," and, "There is no authority for the common statement that the primary sense of education is to 'draw out or unfold the powers of the mind.'"

example.en: Parents have a duty to educate their children about environmental responsibility.
example.zh: 父母有责任教育孩子关于环保的重要性。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "childrearing," also "the training of animals," from Middle French education (14c.) and directly from Latin educationem (nominative educatio) "a rearing, training," noun of action from past participle stem of educare (see educate). Originally of instruction in social codes and manners; meaning "systematic schooling and training for work" is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "childrearing," also "the training of animals," 源自 中古法语 education (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 educationem (主格 educatio) "a rearing, training," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of educare （参见 educate). Originally of instruction in social codes and manners; 意为 "systematic schooling and training for work" 始于 1610 年代.

example.en: Access to quality education can transform a child's future opportunities.

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "execution or completion (of an act)," from Old French efet (13c., Modern French effet) "result, execution, completion, ending," from Latin effectus "accomplishment, performance," from past participle stem of efficere "work out, accomplish," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + facere "to do" (see factitious). From French, borrowed into Dutch, German, Scandinavian.

From late 14c. as "power or capacity to produce an intended result; efficacy, effectiveness," and in astrology, "operation or action (of a heavenly body) on human affairs; influence." Also "that which follows from something else; a consequence, a result." From early 15c. as "intended result, purpose, object, intent." Also formerly with a sense of "reality, fact," hence in effect (late 14c.), originally "in fact, actually, really." Meaning "impression produced on the beholder" is from 1736. Sense in stage effect, sound effect, etc. first recorded 1881.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "execution or completion (of an act)," 源自 古法语 efet (13 世纪, 现代法语 effet) "result, execution, completion, ending," 源自 拉丁语 effectus "accomplishment, performance," 源自 past participle stem of efficere "work out, accomplish," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + facere "to do" （参见 factitious). From 法语, borrowed into 荷兰语, 德语, Scandinavian. From 14 世纪晚期 as "power or capacity to produce an intended result; efficacy, effectiveness," and in astrology, "operation or action (of a heavenly body) on human affairs; influence." Also "that which follows from something else; a consequence, a result." From 15 世纪初 as "intended result, purpose, object, intent." Also formerly with a 语义 "reality, fact," hence in effect (14 世纪晚期), 原义为 "in fact, actually, really." 义为 "impression produced on the beholder" 始于 1736 年. Sense in stage effect, sound effect, etc. 首见于 1881 年.

example.en: The new medication is effective, but it may cause an unpleasant side effect such as drowsiness.
example.zh: 这种新药很有效，但可能引起令人不适的副作用，比如嗜睡。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "serving to effect the intended purpose," from Old French effectif, from Latin effectivus "productive, effective," from effect-, stem of efficere (see effect (n.)). Of military forces, meaning "fit for action or duty" is from 1680s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "serving to effect the intended purpose," 源自 古法语 effectif, 源自 拉丁语 effectivus "productive, effective," 源自 effect-, stem of efficere （参见 effect （名）). Of military forces, 意为 "fit for action or duty" 始于 1680 年代.

example.en: The antibiotic proved highly effective against the stubborn bacterial infection, clearing it within days.
example.zh: 这种抗生素对那种顽固的细菌感染非常有效，几天之内就将其清除了。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "power to accomplish something," from Latin efficientia "efficient power; efficiency; influence" (from efficientem; see efficient) + -cy. In mechanics, "ratio of useful work done to energy expended," from 1858. Attested from 1952 as short for efficiency apartment (itself from 1920).
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "power to accomplish something," 源自 拉丁语 efficientia "efficient power; efficiency; influence" (源自 efficientem; 参见 efficient) + -cy. example.en: The new automated system doubled the efficiency of the packaging line.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "making, producing immediate effect, active, effective," from Old French efficient and directly from Latin efficientem (nominative efficiens) "effective, efficient, producing, active," present participle of efficere "work out, accomplish" (see effect). Meaning "productive, skilled" is from 1787. Related: Efficiently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "making, producing immediate effect, active, effective," 源自 古法语 efficient and 直接源自 拉丁语 efficientem (主格 efficiens) "effective, efficient, producing, active," 为 … 的现在分词 efficere "work out, accomplish" （参见 effect). 义为 "productive, skilled" 始于 1787 年. 同源词：Efficiently.

example.en: The new secretary is so efficient that she finishes a whole day's paperwork in just two hours.
example.zh: 这位新秘书效率极高，仅用两个小时就完成了一整天的文书工作。

entries.etymology:
late 15c., "laborious attempt, strenuous exertion," from Middle French effort, from Old French esforz "force, impetuosity, strength, power," verbal noun from esforcier "force out, exert oneself," from Vulgar Latin *exfortiare "to show strength" (source of Italian sforza), from Latin ex- "out" (see ex-) + Latin fortis "strong" (see fort).

Related: Efforts "voluntary exertion," also "result of exertion."
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "laborious attempt, strenuous exertion," 源自 中古法语 effort, 源自 古法语 esforz "force, impetuosity, strength, power," verbal 名词 源自 esforcier "force out, exert oneself," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *exfortiare "to show strength" (source of 意大利语 sforza), 源自 拉丁语 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + 拉丁语 fortis "strong" （参见 fort). 同源词：Efforts "voluntary exertion," also "result of exertion."

example.en: She put in a great deal of effort to finish the project on time.
example.zh: 她付出了大量努力，按时完成了这个项目。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., egge, mostly in northern England dialect, from Old Norse egg, from Proto-Germanic *ajja(m) (source also of Old Saxon, Middle Dutch, Dutch, Old High German, German ei, Gothic ada), probably from PIE *owyo-/*oyyo- "egg" (source also of Old Church Slavonic aja, Russian jajco, Breton ui, Welsh wy, Greek oon, Latin ovum); possibly derived from root *awi- "bird."

This Norse-derived northern word vied in Middle English with native cognates eye, eai, from Old English æg, until finally displacing the others after c. 1500. Caxton (15c.) writes of a merchant (probably a north-country man) in a public house on the Thames who asked for eggs:She did, however, recognize another customer's request for "eyren." Used of persons from c. 1600. Bad egg in the figurative sense is from 1855; bad eggs aren't always obvious to outward view (there was an old proverb, "bad bird, bad egg"). To have egg on (one's) face "look foolish" is attested by 1948.

Eggs Benedict attested by 1898. The figure of speech represented in to have all (one's) eggs in one basket is attested by 1660s. The conundrum of the chicken (or hen) and the egg is attested from 1875.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, egge, mostly in northern England dialect, 源自 古北欧语 egg, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ajja(m) (source also of 古撒克逊语, Middle 荷兰语, 荷兰语, 古高地德语, 德语 ei, Gothic ada), 可能 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *owyo-/*oyyo- "egg" (source also of Old Church Slavonic aja, 俄语 jajco, Breton ui, Welsh wy, 希腊语 oon, 拉丁语 ovum); possibly derived 源自 root *awi- "bird." This Norse-derived northern word vied in 中古英语 with 本族 cognates eye, eai, 源自 古英语 æg, until finally displacing the others after 约 1500 年. Caxton (15 世纪) writes of a merchant (可能 a north-country man) in a public house on the Thames who asked for eggs:She did, however, recognize another customer's request for "eyren." To have egg on (one's) face "look foolish" is attested by 1948. Eggs Benedict attested by 1898. The figure of speech represented in to have all (one's) eggs in one basket is attested by 1660 年代. The conundrum of the chicken (or hen) and the egg 见于 1875 年.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., eighte, earlier ehte (c. 1200), from Old English eahta, æhta, from Proto-Germanic *akhto (source also of Old Saxon ahto, Old Frisian ahta, Old Norse atta, Swedish åtta, Dutch acht, Old High German Ahto, German acht, Gothic ahtau), from PIE *okto(u) "eight" (source also of Sanskrit astau, Avestan ashta, Greek okto, Latin octo, Old Irish ocht-n, Breton eiz, Old Church Slavonic osmi, Lithuanian aštuoni). From the Latin word come Italian otto, Spanish ocho, Old French oit, Modern French huit.

For spelling, see fight (v.). Meaning "eight-man crew of a rowing boat" is from 1847. The Spanish piece of eight (1690s) was so called because it was worth eight reals (see piece (n.)). Figure (of) eight as the shape of a race course, etc., attested from c. 1600. To be behind the eight ball "in trouble" (1932) is a metaphor from shooting pool. Eight hours as the ideal length of a fair working day is recorded by 1845.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, eighte, earlier ehte (约 1200 年), 源自 古英语 eahta, æhta, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *akhto (source also of 古撒克逊语 ahto, 古弗里西语 ahta, 古北欧语 atta, Swedish åtta, 荷兰语 acht, 古高地德语 Ahto, 德语 acht, Gothic ahtau), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *okto(u) "eight" (source also of 梵语 astau, Avestan ashta, 希腊语 okto, 拉丁语 octo, Old 爱尔兰语 ocht-n, Breton eiz, Old Church Slavonic osmi, Lithuanian aštuoni). From the 拉丁语 word come 意大利语 otto, 西班牙语 ocho, 古法语 oit, 现代法语 huit. For spelling, 参见 fight （动）. 义为 "eight-man crew of a rowing boat" 始于 1847 年. The 西班牙语 piece of eight (1690 年代) was so called because it was worth eight reals （参见 piece （名）). Figure (of) eight as the shape of a race course, etc., attested 源自 约 1600 年. To be behind the eight ball "in trouble" (1932 年) is a metaphor 源自 shooting pool. Eight hours as the ideal length of a fair working day is recorded 截至 1845 年.

entries.etymology:
Old English ægðer, contraction of æghwæðer (pron., adv., conj.) "each of two, both," from a "always" (see aye (adv.)) + ge- collective prefix + hwæðer "which of two, whether" (see whether). Cognate with Dutch ieder, Old High German eogiwedar, German jeder "either, each, every").

Modern sense of "one or the other of two" is late 13c. Adverbially, for emphasis, "in any case, at all," especially when expressing negation, by 1828. Use of either-or to suggest an unavoidable choice between alternatives (1931) in some cases reflects Danish enten-eller, title of an 1843 book by Kierkegaard.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ægðer, contraction of æghwæðer (pron., adv., conj.) "each of two, both," 源自 a "always" （参见 aye （副）) + ge- collective prefix + hwæðer "which of two, whether" （参见 whether). Cognate with 荷兰语 ieder, 古高地德语 eogiwedar, 德语 jeder "either, each, every"). 现代 语义 "one or the other of two" is 13 世纪晚期 Adverbially, for emphasis, "in any case, at all," 尤指 when expressing negation, 截至 1828 年. Use of either-or to suggest an unavoidable choice between alternatives (1931 年) in some cases reflects Danish enten-eller, title of an 1843 年 book by Kierkegaard.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Latin eiectus "thrown out," past participle of eicere "throw out, cast out, thrust out; drive into exile, expel, drive away," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + -icere, comb. form of iacere "to throw" (see jet (v.)). Related: Ejected; ejecting. Ejecta "matter thrown out by a volcano" is from 1851.

entries.etymology: 1650s, formerly also elastick, coined in French (1650s) as a scientific term to describe gases, from Modern Latin elasticus, from Greek elastos "ductile, flexible," related to elaunein "to strike, beat out," which is of uncertain origin; according to Watkins from an extended form of the PIE base *ele- "to go." Applied to solids from 1670s. Figurative use by 1859. The noun meaning "piece of elastic material," originally a cord or string woven with rubber, is from 1847, American English.

entries.etymology:
"bend of the arm," c. 1200, elbowe, from a contraction of Old English elnboga "elbow," from Proto-Germanic *elino-bugon, literally "bend of the forearm" (source also of Middle Dutch ellenboghe, Dutch elleboog, Old High German elinbogo, German Ellenboge, Old Norse ölnbogi). For first element, see ell (n.1) "length of the forearm;" second element represented by Old English boga "bow, arch" (see bow (n.1)). 

Second element related to Old English bugan "to bend" (see bow (v.)); first element from *alina "arm," from PIE *el- (1) "elbow, forearm" (see ell (n.1)). To be out at elbows (1620s) was literally to have holes in one's coat. Phrase elbow grease "hard rubbing" is attested from 1670s, from jocular sense of "the best substance for polishing furniture." Elbow-room, "room to extend one's elbows," hence, "ample room for activity," attested 1530s.
entries.etymologyZh: "bend of the arm," 约 1200 年, elbowe, 源自 a contraction of 古英语 elnboga "elbow," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *elino-bugon, 字面义为 "bend of the forearm" (source also of Middle 荷兰语 ellenboghe, 荷兰语 elleboog, 古高地德语 elinbogo, 德语 Ellenboge, 古北欧语 ölnbogi). For first element, 参见 ell (n.1) "length of the forearm;" second element represented by 古英语 boga "bow, arch" （参见 bow (n.1)). Second element related to 古英语 bugan "to bend" （参见 bow （动）); first element 源自 *alina "arm," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *el- (1) "elbow, forearm" （参见 ell (n.1)). To be out at elbows (1620 年代) was 字面义为 to have holes in one's coat. Phrase elbow grease "hard rubbing" is attested from 1670s, from jocular sense of "the best substance for polishing furniture." Elbow-room, "room to extend one's elbows," hence, "ample room for activity," attested 1530 年代.

example.en: He propped his elbow on the armrest and rested his chin in his hand.
example.zh: 他把肘部撑在扶手上，用手托着下巴。

entries.definition: a. 年长的，资格老的 n. 长者，长辈
entries.etymology: "more old," Old English (Mercian) eldra, comparative of eald, ald (see old); only English survival of umlaut in comparison. Superseded by older since 16c. Elder statesman (1921) originally was a translation of Japanese genro (plural).
entries.etymologyZh: "more old," 古英语 (Mercian) eldra, comparative of eald, ald （参见 old); only English survival of umlaut in comparison. Superseded by older 自 16 世纪 Elder statesman (1921 年) 原义为 was a translation of 日语 genro (plural).

example.en: The elder members of the community were asked to share their wisdom.
example.zh: 社区中的长辈被邀请分享他们的智慧。

entries.etymology: "bordering on old age, somewhat old," 1610s, from elder + -ly (1). Now, generally, "old." Old English ealdorlic meant "chief, princely, excellent, authentic." Old English also had related eldernliche "of old time," literally "forefatherly."
entries.etymologyZh: "bordering on old age, somewhat old," 1610 年代, 源自 elder + -ly (1). Now, generally, "old." 古英语 ealdorlic meant "chief, princely, excellent, authentic." 古英语 also had related eldernliche "of old time," 字面义为 "forefatherly."

example.en: The hospital has a special ward dedicated to elderly patients with dementia.
example.zh: 这家医院有一个专门为患有痴呆症的老年患者设置的病房。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to choose for an office, position, or duty," from Latin electus, past participle of eligere "to pick out, choose" (see election). Related: Elected; electing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to choose for an office, position, or duty," 源自 拉丁语 electus, 为 … 的过去分词 eligere "to pick out, choose" （参见 election). 同源词：Elected; electing.

example.en: The citizens went to the polls to elect a new president last week.
example.zh: 上周，公民前往投票站选举新总统。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "act of choosing someone to occupy a position, elevation to office" (whether by one person or a body of electors); also "the holding of a vote by a body of electors; the time and place of such a vote," from Anglo-French eleccioun, Old French elecion "choice, election, selection" (12c.), from Latin electionem (nominative electio), noun of action from past participle stem of eligere "pick out, select," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + -ligere, comb. form of legere "to choose, read" (see lecture (n.)). Theological sense "God's choice of someone" for eternal life is from late 14c. Meaning "act of choosing, choice" is from c. 1400.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "act of choosing someone to occupy a position, elevation to office" (whether by one person or a body of electors); also "the holding of a vote by a body of electors; the time and place of such a vote," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 eleccioun, 古法语 elecion "choice, election, selection" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 electionem (主格 electio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of eligere "pick out, select," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + -ligere, comb. form of legere "to choose, read" （参见 lecture （名）). Theological sense "God's choice of someone" for eternal life 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "act of choosing, choice" 始于 约 1400 年.

example.en: Millions of citizens voted in the presidential election last November.
example.zh: 数百万公民在去年十一月的总统选举中投了票。

entries.etymology:
1640s, first used in English by physician Sir Thomas Browne (1605-1682), apparently coined as Modern Latin electricus (literally "resembling amber") by English physicist William Gilbert (1540-1603) in treatise "De Magnete" (1600), from Latin electrum "amber," from Greek elektron "amber" (Homer, Hesiod, Herodotus), also "pale gold" (a compound of 1 part silver to 4 of gold); which is of unknown origin.

Originally the word described substances which, like amber, attract other substances when rubbed. Meaning "charged with electricity" is from 1670s; the physical force so called because it first was generated by rubbing amber. In many modern instances, the word is short for electrical. Figurative sense is attested by 1793. Electric light is from 1767. Electric toothbrush first recorded 1936; electric blanket in 1930. Electric typewriter is from 1958. Electric guitar is from 1938; electric organ coined as the name of a hypothetical future instrument in 1885.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, first used in English by physician Sir Thomas Browne (1605 年-1682 年), 似乎 coined as 现代 拉丁语 electricus (字面义为 "resembling amber") by English physicist William Gilbert (1540 年-1603 年) in treatise "De Magnete" (1600 年), 源自 拉丁语 electrum "amber," 源自 希腊语 elektron "amber" (Homer, Hesiod, Herodotus), also "pale gold" (a 由 … 复合而成 1 part silver to 4 of gold); which is 来源不详. Originally the word described substances which, like amber, attract other substances when rubbed. 义为 "charged with electricity" 始于 1670 年代; the physical force so called because it first was generated by rubbing amber. In many modern instances, the word is short for electrical. Figurative sense is attested 截至 1793 年. Electric light 始于 1767 年. Electric toothbrush 首见于 1936 年; electric blanket 于 1930 年. Electric typewriter 始于 1958 年. Electric guitar 始于 1938 年; electric organ coined as the name of a hypothetical future instrument 于 1885 年.

example.en: The city plans to replace all buses with electric vehicles by 2030.
example.zh: 该城市计划到2030年将所有公共汽车替换为电动车辆。

entries.etymology: 1630s, "giving off electricity when rubbed," from electric + -al (1). Meaning "relating to electricity, run by electricity" is from 1746. Related: Electrically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "giving off electricity when rubbed," 源自 electric + -al (1). 义为 "relating to electricity, run by electricity" 始于 1746 年. 同源词：Electrically.

example.en: The technician fixed the electrical fault that caused the blackout.
example.zh: 技术人员修复了导致停电的电气故障。

entries.etymology: 1751, "scientist concerned with electricity;" 1869 as "technician concerned with electrical systems and appliances;" see electric + -ian.
entries.etymologyZh: 1751 年, "scientist concerned with electricity;" 1869 年 as "technician concerned with electrical systems and appliances;" 参见 electric + -ian.

entries.etymology: 1640s (Browne, from Gilbert's Modern Latin), from electric (q.v.) + -ity. Originally in reference to friction.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代 (Browne, 源自 Gilbert's 现代 拉丁语), 源自 electric (q.v.) + -ity. Originally in reference to friction.

example.en: The storm knocked out electricity in half the city for several hours.
example.zh: 这场暴风雨导致城市半数地区断电数小时。

entries.etymology: coined 1891 by Irish physicist George J. Stoney (1826-1911) from electric + -on, as in ion (q.v.). Electron microscope (1932) translates German Elektronenmikroskop.
entries.etymologyZh: coined 1891 年 by 爱尔兰语 physicist George J. Stoney (1826 年-1911 年) 源自 electric + -on, as in ion (q.v.). Electron microscope (1932 年) translates 德语 Elektronenmikroskop.

example.en: Each electron carries a negative electric charge and orbits the nucleus.
example.zh: 每个电子都携带负电荷并围绕原子核运转。

entries.etymology: 1901, "pertaining to electrons;" see electron + -ic; 1930 as "pertaining to electronics." Related: Electronically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1901 年, "pertaining to electrons;" 参见 electron + -ic; 1930 年 as "pertaining to electronics." 同源词：Electronically.

example.en: She bought a new electronic dictionary to look up vocabulary offline.
example.zh: 她买了一本新的电子词典，用于离线查词。

entries.etymology: 1910, from electronic; also see -ics. The science of how electrons behave in vacuums, gas, semi-conductors, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 1910 年, 源自 electronic; also 参见 -ics. The science of how electrons behave in vacuums, gas, semi-conductors, etc.

example.en: She studied electronics at university and now designs microchips for a tech firm.
example.zh: 她在大学攻读电子学，现在为一家科技公司设计微芯片。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "earth, air, fire, or water; one of the four things regarded by the ancients as the constituents of all things," from Old French element (10c.), from Latin elementem "rudiment, first principle, matter in its most basic form" (translating Greek stoikheion), origin and original sense unknown. Meaning "simplest component of a complex substance" is late 14c. Modern sense in chemistry is from 1813, but is not essentially different from the ancient one. Meaning "proper or natural environment of anything" is from 1590s, from the old notion that each class of living beings had its natural abode in one of the four elements. Elements "atmospheric force" is 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "earth, air, fire, or water; one of the four things regarded by the ancients as the constituents of all things," 源自 古法语 element (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 elementem "rudiment, first principle, matter in its most basic form" (translating 希腊语 stoikheion), origin and original sense unknown. 义为 "simplest component of a complex substance" is 14 世纪晚期 现代 sense in chemistry 始于 1813 年, but is not essentially different 源自 ancient one. 义为 "proper or natural environment of anything" 始于 1590 年代, 源自 old notion that each class of living beings had its natural abode in one of the four elements. Elements "atmospheric force" is 1550 年代.

example.en: Oxygen is a vital element in the chemical reaction that produces rust.
example.zh: 氧气是产生铁锈的化学反应中的一个关键要素。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "having the nature of one of the four elements," from Middle French elementaire and directly from Latin elementarius "belonging to the elements or rudiments," from elementum (see element). Meaning "rudimentary, involving first principles" is from 1540s; meaning "simple" is from 1620s. In elementary school (1841) it has the "rudimentary" sense.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "having the nature of one of the four elements," 源自 中古法语 elementaire and 直接源自 拉丁语 elementarius "belonging to the elements or rudiments," 源自 elementum （参见 element). 义为 "rudimentary, involving first principles" 始于 1540 年代; 意为 "simple" 始于 1620 年代. In elementary school (1841 年) it has the "rudimentary" sense.

example.en: The program targets children at the elementary school level in rural areas.
example.zh: 该项目面向农村地区小学阶段的儿童。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, olyfaunt, from Old French olifant (12c., Modern French éléphant), from Latin elephantus, from Greek elephas (genitive elephantos) "elephant; ivory," probably from a non-Indo-European language, likely via Phoenician (compare Hamitic elu "elephant," source of the word for it in many Semitic languages, or possibly from Sanskrit ibhah "elephant").

Re-spelled after 1550 on Latin model. Cognate with the common term for the animal in Romanic and Germanic; Slavic words (for example Polish slon', Russian slonu are from a different word. Old English had it as elpend, and compare elpendban, elpentoð "ivory," but a confusion of exotic animals led to olfend "camel."

As an emblem of the Republican Party in U.S. politics, 1860. To see the elephant "be acquainted with life, gain knowledge by experience" is an American English colloquialism from 1835. The elephant joke was popular 1960s-70s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, olyfaunt, 源自 古法语 olifant (12 世纪, 现代法语 éléphant), 源自 拉丁语 elephantus, 源自 希腊语 elephas (属格 elephantos) "elephant; ivory," 可能 源自 a non-Indo-European language, likely 经由 Phoenician (对比 Hamitic elu "elephant," source of the word for it in many Semitic languages，或possibly 源自 梵语 ibhah "elephant"). Re-spelled after 1550 年 on 拉丁语 model. Cognate with the common term for the animal in Romanic and 日耳曼语; Slavic words (for example Polish slon', 俄语 slonu 始于 a different word. 古英语 had it as elpend, and 对比 elpendban, elpentoð "ivory," but a confusion of exotic animals led to olfend "camel." 作为 emblem of the Republican Party in U.S. politics, 1860 年. To 参见 the elephant "be acquainted with life, gain knowledge by experience" is an American English colloquialism 自 1835 年起. The elephant joke was popular 1960 年代-70s.

entries.etymology: late 15c., "to raise above the usual position," from Latin elevatus, past participle of elevare "lift up, raise," figuratively, "to lighten, alleviate," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + levare "lighten, raise," from levis "light" in weight (see lever). Sense of "raise in rank or status" is from c. 1500. Moral or intellectual sense is from 1620s. Related: Elevated (which also was old slang for "drunk"); elevating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "to raise above the usual position," 源自 拉丁语 elevatus, 为 … 的过去分词 elevare "lift up, raise," figuratively, "to lighten, alleviate," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + levare "lighten, raise," 源自 levis "light" in weight （参见 lever). 义为 "raise in rank or status" 始于 约 1500 年. Moral or intellectual sense 始于 1620 年代. 同源词：Elevated (which also was old 俚语 for "drunk"); elevating.

example.en: The new policy aims to elevate the status of teachers in society.
example.zh: 这项新政策旨在提升教师在社会中的地位。

entries.etymology: 1640s, originally of muscles which raise a part of the body, from Latin elevator "one who raises up," agent noun from past participle stem of elevare (see elevate). As a name for a mechanical lift (originally for grain) attested from 1787. Elevator music is attested by 1963. Elevator as a lift for shoes is from 1940.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 原义为 of muscles which raise a part of the body, 源自 拉丁语 elevator "one who raises up," agent 名词 源自 past participle stem of elevare （参见 elevate). 作为 name for a mechanical lift (原义为 for grain) attested 自 1787 年起. Elevator music is attested 截至 1963 年. Elevator 作为 lift for shoes 始于 1940 年.

example.en: We took the elevator to reach the top floor of the building.
example.zh: 我们乘电梯到达了大楼顶层。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, elleovene, from Old English enleofan, endleofan, literally "one left" (over ten), from Proto-Germanic *ainlif- (compare Old Saxon elleban, Old Frisian andlova, Dutch elf, Old High German einlif, German elf, Old Norse ellifu, Gothic ainlif), a compound of *ain "one" (see one) + PIE *leikw- "leave, remain" (source of Greek leipein "to leave behind;" see relinquish).

Viking survivors who escaped an Anglo-Saxon victory were daroþa laf "the leavings of spears," while hamora laf "the leavings of hammers" was an Old English kenning for "swords" (both from "The Battle of Brunanburgh"). Twelve reflects the same formation. Outside Germanic the only instance of this formation is in Lithuanian, which uses -lika "left over" and continues the series to 19 (vienio-lika "eleven," dvy-lika "twelve," try-lika "thirteen," keturio-lika "fourteen," etc.). Meaning "a team or side" in cricket or football is from 1743.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, elleovene, 源自 古英语 enleofan, endleofan, 字面义为 "one left" (over ten), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ainlif- (对比 古撒克逊语 elleban, 古弗里西语 andlova, 荷兰语 elf, 古高地德语 einlif, 德语 elf, 古北欧语 ellifu, Gothic ainlif), a 由 … 复合而成 *ain "one" （参见 one) + 原始印欧语 (PIE) *leikw- "leave, remain" (source of 希腊语 leipein "to leave behind;" 参见 relinquish). Viking survivors who escaped an 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 victory were daroþa laf "the leavings of spears," while hamora laf "the leavings of hammers" was an 古英语 kenning for "swords" (both 源自 "The Battle of Brunanburgh"). Twelve reflects the same formation. Outside 日耳曼语 the only instance of this formation is in Lithuanian, which uses -lika "left over" and continues the series to 19 (vienio-lika "eleven," dvy-lika "twelve," try-lika "thirteen," keturio-lika "fourteen," etc.). 义为 "a team or side" in cricket or football 始于 1743 年.

entries.etymology: late 14c., eleventhe, superseding earlier ellefte (c. 1300), enlefte (early 13c.), from Old English endleofta; see eleven + -th (1). Eleventh hour "last moment, just before it is too late" is in Old English, from the parable of the laborers in the vineyard (Matt. xx:1-16); as an adjective by 1829.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, eleventhe, superseding earlier ellefte (约 1300 年), enlefte (13 世纪初), 源自 古英语 endleofta; 参见 eleven + -th (1). Eleventh hour "last moment, just before it is too late" is in 古英语, 源自 parable of the laborers in the vineyard (Matt. xx:1-16); 作形容词时 截至 1829 年.

entries.etymology: 1640s, from Latin elicitus, past participle of elicere "draw out, draw forth," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + -licere, comb. form of lacere "to entice, lure, deceive" (related to laqueus "noose, snare;" see lace (n.)). Related: Elicited; eliciting; elicits; elicitation.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 拉丁语 elicitus, 为 … 的过去分词 elicere "draw out, draw forth," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + -licere, comb. form of lacere "to entice, lure, deceive" (related to laqueus "noose, snare;" 参见 lace （名）). 同源词：Elicited; eliciting; elicits; elicitation.

definitionLines: a. 合格的，合适的；符合条件 的；有资格当选的
entries.definition: a. 合格的，合适的；符合条件 的；有资格当选的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "fit or proper to be chosen," from Old French eligible "fit to be chosen" (14c.), from Late Latin eligibilis "that may be chosen," from Latin eligere "choose" (see election). Related: Eligibly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "fit or proper to be chosen," 源自 古法语 eligible "fit to be chosen" (14 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 eligibilis "that may be chosen," 源自 拉丁语 eligere "choose" （参见 election). 同源词：Eligibly.

example.en: Only candidates with a valid degree are eligible to apply for this position.
example.zh: 只有拥有有效学位的候选人才有资格申请这个职位。

entries.etymology:
1560s, from Latin eliminatus, past participle of eliminare "thrust out of doors, expel," from ex limine "off the threshold," from ex "off, out" (see ex-) + limine, ablative of limen "threshold" (see limit (n.)).

Used literally at first; sense of "exclude" first attested 1714; sense of "expel waste from the body" is c. 1795. Related: Eliminated; eliminating; eliminative; eliminatory.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 拉丁语 eliminatus, 为 … 的过去分词 eliminare "thrust out of doors, expel," 源自 ex limine "off the threshold," 源自 ex "off, out" （参见 ex-) + limine, ablative of limen "threshold" （参见 limit （名）). Used 字面义为 at first; 语义 "exclude" 最早见于 1714 年; 语义 "expel waste from the body" is 约 1795 年. 同源词：Eliminated; eliminating; eliminative; eliminatory.

example.en: The new law aims to eliminate all forms of racial bias from hiring practices.
example.zh: 新法律旨在从招聘实践中彻底消除所有形式的种族偏见。

entries.etymology: "a choice or select body, the best part," 1823, from French élite "selection, choice," from Old French eslite (12c.), fem. past participle of elire, elisre "pick out, choose," from Latin eligere "choose" (see election). Borrowed in Middle English as "chosen person" (late 14c.), especially a bishop-elect; died out mid-15c.; re-introduced by Byron's "Don Juan." As an adjective by 1852. As a typeface, first recorded 1920.
entries.etymologyZh: "a choice or select body, the best part," 1823 年, 源自 法语 élite "selection, choice," 源自 古法语 eslite (12 世纪), fem. 为 … 的过去分词 elire, elisre "pick out, choose," 源自 拉丁语 eligere "choose" （参见 election). Borrowed in 中古英语 as "chosen person" (14 世纪晚期), 尤指 a bishop-elect; died out 15 世纪中期; re-introduced by Byron's "Don Juan." 作形容词时 截至 1852 年. 作为 typeface, 首见于 1920 年.

example.en: The conference was attended by a small elite of top scientists and policymakers.
example.zh: 这场会议由一小批顶尖科学家和政策制定者参加。

definitionLines: a.雄辩的，有口才的；有说服 力的
entries.definition: a.雄辩的，有口才的；有说服 力的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French eloquent, from Latin eloquentem (nominative eloquens) "speaking, having the faculty of speech; eloquent," present participle of eloqui "to speak out" (see eloquence). Related: Eloquently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 eloquent, 源自 拉丁语 eloquentem (主格 eloquens) "speaking, having the faculty of speech; eloquent," 为 … 的现在分词 eloqui "to speak out" （参见 eloquence). 同源词：Eloquently.

definitionLines: ad. 其他，另外，别的；（与 or 连 用）否则
entries.definition: ad. 其他，另外，别的；（与 or 连 用）否则
entries.etymology:
Old English elles "in another manner, other, otherwise, besides, different," from Proto-Germanic *aljaz (source also of Gothic aljis "other," Old High German eli-lenti, Old English el-lende, both meaning "in a foreign land;" see also Alsace), an adverbial genitive of the neuter of PIE root *al- (1) "beyond" (source also of Greek allos "other," Latin alius; see alias (adv.)). As a quasi-adjective, synonymous with other, from 1660s; the nuances of usage are often arbitrary.

Productive of a number of handy compounds that somehow never got traction or have been suffered to fall from use: elsehow (1660s) "somehow or other;" elsewards (adv.), 1882, "somewhere else;" Old English elsewhat (pron.) " something else, anything else;" elsewhen (adv.), early 15c., "at another time; elsewhence (c. 1600); elsewho (1540s). Among the survivors are elsewhere, elsewise. Menacing or else, with omitted but implied threat, is from 1833.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 elles "in another manner, other, otherwise, besides, different," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aljaz (source also of Gothic aljis "other," 古高地德语 eli-lenti, 古英语 el-lende, both 意为 "in a foreign land;" 亦参见 Alsace), an adverbial 属格 of the neuter of 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *al- (1) "beyond" (source also of 希腊语 allos "other," 拉丁语 alius; 参见 alias （副）). 作为 quasi-形容词, synonymous with other, 源自 1660 年代; the nuances of usage are 常 arbitrary. Productive of a number of handy compounds that somehow never got traction or have been suffered to fall 源自 use: elsehow (1660 年代) "somehow or other;" elsewards （副）, 1882 年, "somewhere else;" 古英语 elsewhat （代） " something else, anything else;" elsewhen （副）, 15 世纪初, "at another time; elsewhence (约 1600 年); elsewho (1540 年代). Among the survivors are elsewhere, elsewise. Menacing or else, with omitted but implied threat, 始于 1833 年.

entries.etymology: "in another place, in other places," c. 1400, elswher, from Old English elles hwær (see else + where). Related: Elsewhither (Old English elleshwider.
entries.etymologyZh: "in another place, in other places," 约 1400 年, elswher, 源自 古英语 elles hwær （参见 else + where). 同源词：Elsewhither (古英语 elleshwider.

example.en: If the item is out of stock here, you may find it elsewhere.
example.zh: 如果这里的商品缺货，您可以在其他地方找到。

entries.etymology:
1982, short for electronic mail (1977; see electronic + mail (n.1)); this led to the contemptuous application of snail mail (1983) to the old system.

Associated Press style guide collapsed it to email 2011.
entries.etymologyZh: 1982 年, short for electronic mail (1977 年; 参见 electronic + mail (n.1)); this led to the contemptuous application of snail mail (1983 年) to the old system. Associated Press style guide collapsed it to email 2011 年.

example.en: Please send me your report by e-mail before noon.
example.zh: 请在中午之前通过电子邮件把报告发给我。

definitionLines: vi. 上船或飞机；从事，着手
entries.definition: vi. 上船或飞机；从事，着手 vt. 使上船；使从事
entries.etymology: 1540s (transitive); 1570s (intransitive), from Middle French embarquer, from assimilated form of en- "in" (see en- (1)) + barque "small ship" (see bark (n.)). Related: Embarked; embarking.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代 (transitive); 1570 年代 (intransitive), 源自 中古法语 embarquer, 源自 为 … 的同化形式 en- "in" （参见 en- (1)) + barque "small ship" （参见 bark （名）). 同源词：Embarked; embarking.

example.en: Next month, she will embark on a year-long journey around the world.
example.zh: 下个月，她将踏上为期一年的环球旅程。

definitionLines: vt. 使窘迫，使困惑，使为难
entries.definition: vt. 使窘迫，使困惑，使为难
entries.etymology:
1670s, "perplex, throw into doubt," from French embarrasser (16c.), literally "to block," from Italian imbarrazzo, from imbarrare "to bar," from assimilated form of in- "into, upon" (see in- (2)) + Vulgar Latin *barra "bar" (see bar (n.1)).

Meaning "to hamper, hinder" is from 1680s. Meaning "make (someone) feel awkward" first recorded 1828. Original sense preserved in embarras de richesse (1751), from French (1726): the condition of having more wealth than one knows what to do with. Related: Embarrassed; embarrassing; embarrassingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1670 年代, "perplex, throw into doubt," 源自 法语 embarrasser (16 世纪), 字面义为 "to block," 源自 意大利语 imbarrazzo, 源自 imbarrare "to bar," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + 通俗拉丁语 *barra "bar" （参见 bar (n.1)). 义为 "to hamper, hinder" 始于 1680 年代. 义为 "make (someone) feel awkward" 首见于 1828 年. Original sense preserved in embarras de richesse (1751 年), 源自 法语 (1726 年): the condition of having more wealth than one knows what to do with. 同源词：Embarrassed; embarrassing; embarrassingly.

entries.etymology:
1570s, "position of an ambassador," from Middle French embassee "mission, charge, office of ambassador," Old French ambassee, from Italian ambasciata, from Old Provençal ambaisada "office of ambassador," from Gaulish *ambactos "dependant, vassal," literally "one going around," from PIE *amb(i)-ag-to, from *ambi- (see ambi-) + *ambi- "around" (see ambi-) + *ag- "to drive, move" (see act (n.)).

Meaning "official residence and retinue of an ambassador" is from 1764. In earlier use were embassade (late 15c.), ambassade (early 15c.), from Old French variant ambassade.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "position of an ambassador," 源自 中古法语 embassee "mission, charge, office of ambassador," 古法语 ambassee, 源自 意大利语 ambasciata, 源自 Old Provençal ambaisada "office of ambassador," 源自 Gaulish *ambactos "dependant, vassal," 字面义为 "one going around," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *amb(i)-ag-to, 源自 *ambi- （参见 ambi-) + *ambi- "around" （参见 ambi-) + *ag- "to drive, move" （参见 act （名）). 义为 "official residence and retinue of an ambassador" 始于 1764 年. In earlier use were embassade (15 世纪晚期), ambassade (15 世纪初), 源自 古法语 variant ambassade.

definitionLines: vt. 栽种；使嵌入，使插入
entries.definition: vt. 栽种；使嵌入，使插入
entries.etymology: 1778, "to lay in a bed (of surrounding matter)," from em- (1) + bed (n.). Originally a geological term, in reference to fossils in rock; figurative sense is by 1835; meaning "place (a journalist) within a military unit at war" is from 2003 and the Iraq war. Related: Embedded; embedding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1778 年, "to lay in a bed (of surrounding matter)," 源自 em- (1) + bed （名）. Originally a geological term, in reference to fossils in rock; figurative sense is 截至 1835 年; 意为 "place (a journalist) within a military unit at war" 始于 2003 年 and the Iraq war. 同源词：Embedded; embedding.

example.en: The journalist managed to embed herself in the local community to gather stories.
example.zh: 这位记者设法融入当地社区以收集报道素材。

definitionLines: vt. 体现，使具体化；具体表达
entries.definition: vt. 体现，使具体化；具体表达
entries.etymology: 1540s, in reference to a soul or spirit invested with a physical form; from 1660s of principles, ideas, etc.; from em- (1) "in" + body (n.). Related: Embodied; embodying.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, in reference to a soul or spirit invested with a physical form; 源自 1660 年代 of principles, ideas, etc.; 源自 em- (1) "in" + body （名）. 同源词：Embodied; embodying.

example.en: This sculpture embodies the spirit of freedom that the artist fought for.
example.zh: 这座雕塑体现了艺术家为之奋斗的自由精神。

definitionLines: vt. 拥，拥抱；包括，包含；包围， 环绕
entries.definition: vt. 拥，拥抱；包括，包含；包围， 环绕
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "clasp in the arms," from Old French embracier (12c., Modern French embrasser) "clasp in the arms, enclose; covet, handle, cope with," from assimilated form of en- "in" (see en- (1)) + brace, braz "the arms," from Latin bracchium (neuter plural brachia); see brace (n.). Related: Embraced; embracing; embraceable. Replaced Old English clyppan (see clip (v.2)), also fæðm (see fathom (v.)). Sexual sense is from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "clasp in the arms," 源自 古法语 embracier (12 世纪, 现代法语 embrasser) "clasp in the arms, enclose; covet, handle, cope with," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 en- "in" （参见 en- (1)) + brace, braz "the arms," 源自 拉丁语 bracchium (neuter plural brachia); 参见 brace （名）. 同源词：Embraced; embracing; embraceable. Replaced 古英语 clyppan （参见 clip (v.2)), also fæðm （参见 fathom （动）). Sexual sense 始于 1590 年代.

example.en: The school was quick to embrace online learning after the pandemic began.
example.zh: 疫情开始后，学校很快就热情接纳了在线学习。

entries.etymology: 1560s, from Middle French émerger and directly from Latin emergere "bring forth, bring to light," intransitively "arise out or up, come forth, come up, come out, rise," from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + mergere "to dip, sink" (see merge). The notion is of rising from a liquid by virtue of buoyancy. Related: Emerged; emerging.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 中古法语 émerger and 直接源自 拉丁语 emergere "bring forth, bring to light," intransitively "arise out or up, come forth, come up, come out, rise," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + mergere "to dip, sink" （参见 merge). The notion is of rising 源自 a liquid by virtue of buoyancy. 同源词：Emerged; emerging.

example.en: A new solution began to emerge from the data after months of analysis.
example.zh: 经过数月分析，数据中开始浮现出一个新的解决方案。

definitionLines: n. 紧急情况，突然事件
entries.definition: n. 紧急情况，突然事件
entries.etymology: "unforeseen occurrence requiring immediate attention," 1630s, from Latin emergens, present participle of emergere "to rise out or up" (see emerge). Or from emerge + -ency. As an adjective by 1881.
entries.etymologyZh: "unforeseen occurrence requiring immediate attention," 1630 年代, 源自 拉丁语 emergens, 为 … 的现在分词 emergere "to rise out or up" （参见 emerge). Or 源自 emerge + -ency. 作形容词时 截至 1881 年.

example.en: The nurse responded quickly and calmly to the medical emergency.
example.zh: 护士迅速而冷静地应对了这次医疗紧急情况。

entries.definition: vi.移居；移居外国 vt.移民
entries.etymology: 1778, a back-formation from emigration, or else from Latin emigratus, past participle of emigrare "move away." In 19c. U.S., "to remove from one state to another state or territory." Related: Emigrated; emigrating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1778 年, a back-formation 源自 emigration，或else 源自 拉丁语 emigratus, 为 … 的过去分词 emigrare "move away." In 19 世纪 U.S., "to remove from one state to another state or territory." 同源词：Emigrated; emigrating.

definitionLines: n. （光、热等的）发射，散发；喷 射
entries.definition: n. （光、热等的）发射，散发；喷 射
entries.etymology: early 15c., "something sent forth," from Middle French émission (14c.) and directly from Latin emissionem (nominative emissio) "a sending out, a projecting, hurling, letting go, releasing," noun of action from past participle stem of emittere "send out" (see emit). Meaning "a giving off or emitting" is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "something sent forth," 源自 中古法语 émission (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 emissionem (主格 emissio) "a sending out, a projecting, hurling, letting go, releasing," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of emittere "send out" （参见 emit). 义为 "a giving off or emitting" 始于 1610 年代.

example.en: The factory must cut its carbon emission to meet new regulations.
example.zh: 这家工厂必须削减碳排放量以符合新规。
