definitionLines: vt. 发出，发射；散发（光、热、气 味等）
entries.definition: vt. 发出，发射；散发（光、热、气 味等）
entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin emittere "send forth," from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + mittere "to send" (see mission). Related: Emitted; emitting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 emittere "send forth," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + mittere "to send" （参见 mission). 同源词：Emitted; emitting.

entries.etymology: 1570s, "a (social) moving, stirring, agitation," from Middle French émotion (16c.), from Old French emouvoir "stir up" (12c.), from Latin emovere "move out, remove, agitate," from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + movere "to move" (see move (v.)). Sense of "strong feeling" is first recorded 1650s; extended to any feeling by 1808.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "a (social) moving, stirring, agitation," 源自 中古法语 émotion (16 世纪), 源自 古法语 emouvoir "stir up" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 emovere "move out, remove, agitate," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + movere "to move" （参见 move （动）). 义为 "strong feeling" is 首见于 1650 年代; extended to any feeling 截至 1808 年.

example.en: He struggled to express the emotion he felt after hearing the news.
example.zh: 听到这个消息后，他难以表达自己内心的情绪。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Old French empereor "emperor, leader, ruler" (11c.; accusative; nominative emperere; Modern French empereur), from Latin imperiatorem (nominative imperiator) "commander, emperor," from past participle stem of imperare "to command" (see empire).

Originally a title conferred by vote of the Roman army on a successful general, later by the Senate on Julius and Augustus Caesar and adopted by their successors except Tiberius and Claudius. In the Middle Ages, applied to rulers of China, Japan, etc.; non-historical European application in English had been only to the Holy Roman Emperors (who in German documents are called kaiser), from late 13c., until in 1804 Napoleon took the title "Emperor of the French."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 empereor "emperor, leader, ruler" (11 世纪; 宾格; 主格 emperere; 现代法语 empereur), 源自 拉丁语 imperiatorem (主格 imperiator) "commander, emperor," 源自 past participle stem of imperare "to command" （参见 empire). Originally a title conferred by vote of the Roman army on a successful general, later by the Senate on Julius and Augustus Caesar and adopted by their successors except Tiberius and Claudius. In the Middle Ages, applied to rulers of China, Japan, etc.; non-historical European application in English had been only to the Holy Roman Emperors (who in 德语 documents are called kaiser), 源自 13 世纪晚期, until 于 1804 年 Napoleon took the title "Emperor of the French."

entries.etymology: 1570s, "intensity of expression," from Latin emphasis, from Greek emphasis "an appearing in, outward appearance;" in rhetoric, "significance, indirect meaning," from emphainein "to present, exhibit, display, let (a thing) be seen; be reflected (in a mirror), become visible," from assimilated form of en "in" (see en- (2)) + phainein "to show" (see phantasm). In Greek and Latin, originally a figure of expression implying more than would ordinarily be meant by the words, it developed a sense of "extra stress" given to a word or phrase in speech as a clue that it implies something more than literal meaning. In pure Latin, significatio.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "intensity of expression," 源自 拉丁语 emphasis, 源自 希腊语 emphasis "an appearing in, outward appearance;" in rhetoric, "significance, indirect meaning," 源自 emphainein "to present, exhibit, display, let (a thing) be seen; be reflected (in a mirror), become visible," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 en "in" （参见 en- (2)) + phainein "to show" （参见 phantasm). In 希腊语 and 拉丁语, 原义为 a figure of expression implying more than would ordinarily be meant by the words, it developed a 语义 "extra stress" given to a word or phrase in speech 作为 clue that it implies something more than literal 意为. In pure 拉丁语, significatio.

example.en: The report places special emphasis on the need for early childhood education.
example.zh: 报告特别强调了早期儿童教育的必要性。

entries.etymology: 1765, from emphasis + -ize. Related: Emphasized; emphasizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1765 年, 源自 emphasis + -ize. 同源词：Emphasized; emphasizing.

example.en: The professor always emphasize the importance of critical thinking in her lectures.
example.zh: 这位教授在讲课中总是强调批判性思维的重要性。

entries.etymology:
early 14c., from Old French empire "rule, authority, kingdom, imperial rule" (11c.), from Latin imperium "a rule, a command; authority, control, power; supreme power, sole dominion; military authority; a dominion, realm," from imperare "to command," from assimilated form of in- "in" (see in- (2)) + parare "to order, prepare" (see pare).

Not etymologically restricted to "territory ruled by an emperor," but used that way. The Empire, meaning "the British Empire," first recorded 1772 (it officially devolved into "The Commonwealth" in 1931); before that it meant the Holy Roman Empire (1670s). Empire as the name of a style (especially in reference to a style of dresses with high waistlines) is by 1869, in reference to the affected classicism prevailing in France during the reign of Napoleon I (1804-15). Second Empire is in reference to the rule of Napoleon III of France (1852-70). New York has been called the Empire State since 1834.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 empire "rule, authority, kingdom, imperial rule" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 imperium "a rule, a command; authority, control, power; supreme power, sole dominion; military authority; a dominion, realm," 源自 imperare "to command," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + parare "to order, prepare" （参见 pare). Not etymologically restricted to "territory ruled by an emperor," but used that way. The Empire, 意为 "the British Empire," 首见于 1772 年 (it officially devolved into "The Commonwealth" 于 1931 年); before that it meant the Holy Roman Empire (1670 年代). Empire as the name of a style (尤指 in reference to a style of dresses with high waistlines) is 截至 1869 年, in reference to the affected classicism prevailing in France during the reign of Napoleon I (1804 年-15). Second Empire is in reference to the rule of Napoleon III of France (1852 年-70). New York has been called the Empire State 自 1834 年.

example.en: At its height, the Roman empire stretched from Britain to the Middle East.
example.zh: 在鼎盛时期，罗马帝国的版图从不列颠延伸至中东。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "apply or devote (something to some purpose); expend or spend," from Old French emploiier (12c.) "make use of, apply; increase; entangle; devote," from Latin implicare "enfold, involve, be connected with, unite, associate," from assimilated form of in- (see in- (2)) + plicare "to fold" (see ply (v.1)). Imply, which is the same word, retains more of the original sense. Sense of "hire, engage" first recorded in English 1580s, from meaning "involve in a particular purpose," which arose in Late Latin. Related: Employed; employing; employable.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "apply or devote (something to some purpose); expend or spend," 源自 古法语 emploiier (12 世纪) "make use of, apply; increase; entangle; devote," 源自 拉丁语 implicare "enfold, involve, be connected with, unite, associate," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- （参见 in- (2)) + plicare "to fold" （参见 ply (v.1)). Imply, which is the same word, retains more of the original sense. 义为 "hire, engage" 首见于 in English 1580 年代, 源自 意为 "involve in a particular purpose," which arose in 晚期拉丁语. 同源词：Employed; employing; employable.

example.en: The company decided to employ more engineers to meet the growing demand.
example.zh: 公司决定雇用更多工程师以满足不断增长的需求。

entries.etymology: "person employed," 1850, mainly in U.S. use, from employ + -ee. Formed on model of French employé.
entries.etymologyZh: "person employed," 1850 年, mainly in U.S. use, 源自 employ + -ee. Formed on model of 法语 employé.

example.en: Every employee is entitled to paid vacation under the new labor law.
example.zh: 根据新劳动法，每位雇员都有权享受带薪假期。

entries.etymology: 1590s, agent noun from employ.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, agent 名词 源自 employ.

example.en: Her employer offered her a promotion after she consistently exceeded her quarterly targets for two years.
example.zh: 在她连续两年超额完成季度目标后，雇主给她提供了晋升机会。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "the spending of money," from Middle English emploien (see employ) + -ment.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "the spending of money," 源自 中古英语 emploien （参见 employ) + -ment.

example.en: The region has seen a sharp rise in employment over the past year.
example.zh: 过去一年该地区就业率大幅上升。

entries.definition: a.空的；空洞的 vt. 倒空，搬空
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, from Old English æmettig "at leisure, not occupied; unmarried," also "containing nothing, unoccupied," from æmetta "leisure," from æ "not" + -metta, from motan "to have" (see might (n.)). The -p- is a euphonic insertion.

Sense evolution from "at leisure" to "containing nothing, unoccupied" is paralleled in several languages, such as Modern Greek adeios "empty," originally "freedom from fear," from deios "fear." "The adj. adeios must have been applied first to persons who enjoyed freedom from duties, leisure, and so were unoccupied, whence it was extended to objects that were unoccupied" [Buck]. Related: Emptier. Figurative sense of empty-nester attested by 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古英语 æmettig "at leisure, not occupied; unmarried," also "containing nothing, unoccupied," 源自 æmetta "leisure," 源自 æ "not" + -metta, 源自 motan "to have" （参见 might （名）). The -p- is a euphonic insertion. Sense evolution 源自 "at leisure" to "containing nothing, unoccupied" is paralleled in several languages, such as 现代 希腊语 adeios "empty," 原义为 "freedom from fear," 源自 deios "fear." "The adj. adeios must have been applied first to persons who enjoyed freedom from duties, leisure, and so were unoccupied, whence it was extended to objects that were unoccupied" [Buck]. 同源词：Emptier. Figurative 语义 empty-nester attested 截至 1960 年.

example.en: The hallway was completely empty when she arrived at the office early.
example.zh: 她一大早到办公室时，走廊完全空无一人。

definitionLines: vt. 仿真；模仿；尽力赶上；同…… 竞争
entries.definition: vt. 仿真；模仿；尽力赶上；同…… 竞争
entries.etymology: 1580s, back-formation from emulation, or else from Latin aemulatus, past participle of aemulari "to rival." Related: Emulated; emulating; emulable; emulative.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, back-formation 源自 emulation，或else 源自 拉丁语 aemulatus, 为 … 的过去分词 aemulari "to rival." 同源词：Emulated; emulating; emulable; emulative.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to make fit;" mid-15c., "to make able to," from en- (1) "make, put in" + able. Related: Enabled; enabling. An enabling act (1684) is so called because it empowers a body or person to take certain action.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to make fit;" 15 世纪中期, "to make able to," 源自 en- (1) "make, put in" + able. 同源词：Enabled; enabling. An enabling act (1684 年) is so called because it empowers a body or person to take certain action.

example.en: The new software will enable users to manage their files more efficiently.
example.zh: 这款新软件将使用户能够更高效地管理文件。

entries.etymology: early 14c., from en- (1) + close, and partially from Old French enclos, past participle of enclore "surround; confine; contain." Specific sense of "to fence in waste or common ground" for the purpose of cultivation or to give it to private owners is from c. 1500. Meaning "place a document with a letter for transmission" is from 1707. Related: Enclosed; enclosing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 en- (1) + close, and partially 源自 古法语 enclos, 为 … 的过去分词 enclore "surround; confine; contain." Specific 语义 "to fence in waste or common ground" for the purpose of cultivation or to give it to private owners 始于 约 1500 年. 义为 "place a document with a letter for transmission" 始于 1707 年. 同源词：Enclosed; enclosing.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "meeting of adversaries, confrontation," from Old French encontre "meeting; fight; opportunity" (12c.), noun use of preposition/adverb encontre "against, counter to" from Late Latin incontra "in front of," from Latin in- "in" (see in- (2)) + contra "against" (see contra). Modern use of the word in psychology is from 1967, from the work of U.S. psychologist Carl Rogers (1902-1987). Encounter group attested from 1967.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "meeting of adversaries, confrontation," 源自 古法语 encontre "meeting; fight; opportunity" (12 世纪), 为 … 的名词用法 preposition/副词 encontre "against, counter to" 源自 晚期拉丁语 incontra "in front of," 源自 拉丁语 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + contra "against" （参见 contra). 现代 use of the word in psychology 始于 1967 年, 源自 work of U.S. psychologist Carl Rogers (1902 年-1987 年). Encounter group attested 自 1967 年起.

example.en: The hikers encountered a bear on the trail and stayed very still.
example.zh: 徒步者在小径上遭遇了一头熊，他们保持一动不动。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French encoragier "make strong, hearten," from en- "make, put in" (see en- (1)) + corage "courage, heart" (see courage). Related: Encouraged; encouraging; encouragingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 encoragier "make strong, hearten," 源自 en- "make, put in" （参见 en- (1)) + corage "courage, heart" （参见 courage). 同源词：Encouraged; encouraging; encouragingly.

example.en: The coach stood by the door to encourage each player before the final match.
example.zh: 教练站在门口，在决赛前给每位球员加油打气。

entries.definition: n. 端，尾；目标，目的 vt. 终止，结束
entries.etymology:
Old English ende "end, conclusion, boundary, district, species, class," from Proto-Germanic *andja (source also of Old Frisian enda, Old Dutch ende, Dutch einde, Old Norse endir "end;" Old High German enti "top, forehead, end," German Ende, Gothic andeis "end"), originally "the opposite side," from PIE *antjo "end, boundary," from root *ant- "opposite, in front of, before" (see ante).

Original sense of "outermost part" is obsolete except in phrase ends of the earth. Sense of "destruction, death" was in Old English. Meaning "division or quarter of a town" was in Old English. The end "the last straw, the limit" (in a disparaging sense) is from 1929. The end-man in minstrel troupes was one of the two at the ends of the semicircle of performers, who told funny stories and cracked jokes with the middle-man. U.S. football end zone is from 1909 (end for "side of the field occupied by one team" is from 1851). The noun phrase end-run is attested from 1893 in U.S. football; extended to military tactics by 1940. End time in reference to the end of the world is from 1917. To end it all "commit suicide" is attested by 1911. Be-all and end-all is from Shakespeare ("Macbeth" I.vii.5).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ende "end, conclusion, boundary, district, species, class," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *andja (source also of 古弗里西语 enda, 古荷兰语 ende, 荷兰语 einde, 古北欧语 endir "end;" 古高地德语 enti "top, forehead, end," 德语 Ende, Gothic andeis "end"), 原义为 "the opposite side," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *antjo "end, boundary," 源自 root *ant- "opposite, in front of, before" （参见 ante). Original 语义 "outermost part" is 已废 except in phrase ends of the earth. 义为 "destruction, death" was in 古英语. 义为 "division or quarter of a town" was in 古英语. The end "the last straw, the limit" (in a disparaging sense) 始于 1929 年. The end-man in minstrel troupes was one of the two at the ends of the semicircle of performers, who told funny stories and cracked jokes with the middle-man. U.S. football end zone 始于 1909 年 (end for "side of the field occupied by one team" 始于 1851 年). The 名词 phrase end-run 见于 1893 年 in U.S. football; extended to military tactics 截至 1940 年. End time in reference to the end of the world 始于 1917 年. To end it all "commit suicide" is attested 截至 1911 年. Be-all and end-all 始于 Shakespeare ("Macbeth" I.vii.5).

example.en: The concert came to an end with a stunning fireworks display.
example.zh: 音乐会以一场精彩的烟火表演落幕。

entries.definition: vt. 危及；使遭到危险 endeavo（u） r n. 努力；尽力 vi. 努力；尽力
entries.etymology: late 15c., from en- (1) "make, put in" + danger. Related: Endangered; endangering. Endangered species recorded by 1958.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 en- (1) "make, put in" + danger. 同源词：Endangered; endangering. Endangered species recorded 截至 1958 年.

entries.etymology: "a coming to an end," early 14c., verbal noun from end (v.). Meaning "the end part (of something)" is from c. 1400. Old English had endunge "ending, end, death."
entries.etymologyZh: "a coming to an end," 14 世纪初, verbal 名词 源自 end （动）. 义为 "the end part (of something)" 始于 约 1400 年. 古英语 had endunge "ending, end, death."

example.en: The movie's ending left audiences debating its meaning for weeks.
example.zh: 这部电影的结局让观众争论了数周其含义。

entries.etymology: Old English endeleas "boundless, eternal;" see end (n.) + -less. Compare Old Saxon endilos, Dutch eindeloos, German endlos. Related: Endlessly; endlessness. Old English used endeleasnes for "infinity, eternity."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 endeleas "boundless, eternal;" 参见 end （名） + -less. 对比 古撒克逊语 endilos, 荷兰语 eindeloos, 德语 endlos. 同源词：Endlessly; endlessness. 古英语 used endeleasnes for "infinity, eternity."

example.en: The researchers faced an endless list of variables to account for in their study.
example.zh: 研究人员在研究中面临着一份无穷无尽的变量清单。

definitionLines: vt. 背书；签署；认可；赞同；在 背面签名
entries.definition: vt. 背书；签署；认可；赞同；在 背面签名
entries.etymology: c. 1400, endosse "confirm or approve" (a charter, bill, etc.), originally by signing or writing on the back of the document, from Old French endosser (12c.), literally "to put on the back," from en- "put on" (see en- (1)) + dos "back," from Latin dossum, variant of dorsum "back" (see dorsal). Assimilated 16c. in form to Medieval Latin indorsare. Figurative sense of "confirm, approve" is recorded in English first in 1847. Related: Endorsed; endorsing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, endosse "confirm or approve" (a charter, bill, etc.), 原义为 by signing or writing on the back of the document, 源自 古法语 endosser (12 世纪), 字面义为 "to put on the back," 源自 en- "put on" （参见 en- (1)) + dos "back," 源自 拉丁语 dossum, 为 … 的变体 dorsum "back" （参见 dorsal). Assimilated 16 世纪 in form to 中古拉丁语 indorsare. Figurative 语义 "confirm, approve" is recorded in English first 于 1847 年. 同源词：Endorsed; endorsing.

example.en: Several celebrities were hired to endorse the new product line.
example.zh: 几位名人受雇为这款新产品系列代言。

definitionLines: vi. 忍受，忍耐；持久，持续
entries.definition: vt. 忍受，容忍 vi. 忍受，忍耐；持久，持续
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to undergo or suffer" (especially without breaking); also "to continue in existence," from Old French endurer (12c.) "make hard, harden; bear, tolerate; keep up, maintain," from Latin indurare "make hard," in Late Latin "harden (the heart) against," from in- (see in- (2)) + durare "to harden," from durus "hard," from PIE *dru-ro-, from root *deru- "be firm, solid, steadfast" (see true).

Replaced the important Old English verb dreogan (past tense dreag, past participle drogen), which survives in dialectal dree. Related: Endured; endures.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to undergo or suffer" (尤指 without breaking); also "to continue in existence," 源自 古法语 endurer (12 世纪) "make hard, harden; bear, tolerate; keep up, maintain," 源自 拉丁语 indurare "make hard," in 晚期拉丁语 "harden (the heart) against," 源自 in- （参见 in- (2)) + durare "to harden," 源自 durus "hard," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *dru-ro-, 源自 root *deru- "be firm, solid, steadfast" （参见 true). Replaced the important 古英语 动词 dreogan (past tense dreag, past participle drogen), which survives in 方言 dree. 同源词：Endured; endures.

example.en: She had to endure years of hardship before achieving success.
example.zh: 她在获得成功之前不得不忍受多年的艰辛。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., "one hateful toward and intent on harming (someone)," from Old French enemi (12c., Modern French ennemi), earlier inimi (9c.) "enemy, adversary, foe; demon, the Devil," from Latin inimicus "an enemy," literally "an unfriend," noun use of adjective meaning "hostile, unfriendly" (source also of Italian nemico, Catalan enamic, Spanish enemigo, Portuguese inimigo), from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + amicus "friend" related to amare "to love" (see Amy). From c. 1300 in English as "adversary of God, unbeliever, heathen, anti-Christian;" late 14c. as "the Devil;" also late 14c. as "member of an armed, hostile body in a war, feud, etc.;" of the opposing military forces as a whole, from c. 1600. From mid-14c. as an adjective.

Most Indo-European words for "personal enemy" cover also "enemy in war," but certain languages have special terms for the latter, such as Greek polemioi (distinct from ekhthroi), Latin hostis, originally "stranger" (distinct from inimicus), Russian neprijatel' (distinct from vrag). Russian vrag (Old Church Slavonic vragu) is cognate with Lithuanian vargas "misery" (see urge (v.)), and probably is related to Proto-Germanic *wargoz, source of Old Norse vargr "outlaw," hence "wolf;" Icelandic vargur "fox;" Old English wearg "criminal, felon;" which likely were the inspirations for J.R.R. Tolkien's warg as the name of a kind of large ferocious wolf in "The Hobbit" (1937) and "Lord of the Rings." Related: Enemies.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "one hateful toward and intent on harming (someone)," 源自 古法语 enemi (12 世纪, 现代法语 ennemi), earlier inimi (9 世纪) "enemy, adversary, foe; demon, the Devil," 源自 拉丁语 inimicus "an enemy," 字面义为 "an unfriend," 为 … 的名词用法 形容词 意为 "hostile, unfriendly" (source also of 意大利语 nemico, Catalan enamic, 西班牙语 enemigo, 葡萄牙语 inimigo), 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + amicus "friend" related to amare "to love" （参见 Amy). From 约 1300 年 in English as "adversary of God, unbeliever, heathen, anti-Christian;" 14 世纪晚期 as "the Devil;" also 14 世纪晚期 as "member of an armed, hostile body in a war, feud, etc.;" of the opposing military forces 作为 whole, 源自 约 1600 年. From 14 世纪中期 作形容词时. Most Indo-European words for "personal enemy" cover also "enemy in war," but certain languages have special terms for the latter, such as 希腊语 polemioi (distinct 源自 ekhthroi), 拉丁语 hostis, 原义为 "stranger" (distinct 源自 inimicus), 俄语 neprijatel' (distinct from vrag). Russian vrag (Old Church Slavonic vragu) is cognate with Lithuanian vargas "misery" (see urge (v.)), and probably is related to Proto-Germanic *wargoz, source of Old Norse vargr "outlaw," hence "wolf;" Icelandic vargur "fox;" Old English wearg "criminal, felon;" which likely were the inspirations for J.R.R. Tolkien's warg as the name of a kind of large ferocious wolf in "The Hobbit" (1937 年) and "Lord of the Rings." 同源词：Enemies.

example.en: Overconfidence can become your greatest enemy when making important decisions.
example.zh: 在做重要决策时，过度自信可能成为你最大的敌人。

definitionLines: a. 精力充沛的；积极的
entries.definition: a. 精力充沛的；积极的
entries.etymology: 1650s, "powerful in operation," from Greek energetikos "active," from energein "to work, be in action, act upon" (see energy). Of persons, "active," in English from 1796 (energetical "operative" is from c. 1600; from 1630s as "full of energy," while energical is attested from 1560s). Related: Energetically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "powerful in operation," 源自 希腊语 energetikos "active," 源自 energein "to work, be in action, act upon" （参见 energy). Of persons, "active," in English 自 1796 年起 (energetical "operative" 始于 约 1600 年; 源自 1630 年代 as "full of energy," while energical 见于 1560 年代). 同源词：Energetically.

definitionLines: n. 精力，气力，活力；能，能量
entries.definition: n. 精力，气力，活力；能，能量
entries.etymology:
1590s, "force of expression," from Middle French énergie (16c.), from Late Latin energia, from Greek energeia "activity, action, operation," from energos "active, working," from en "at" (see en- (2)) + ergon "work, that which is wrought; business; action" (see organ).

Used by Aristotle with a sense of "actuality, reality, existence" (opposed to "potential") but this was misunderstood in Late Latin and afterward as "force of expression," as the power which calls up realistic mental pictures. Broader meaning of "power" in English is first recorded 1660s. Scientific use is from 1807. Energy crisis first attested 1970.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "force of expression," 源自 中古法语 énergie (16 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 energia, 源自 希腊语 energeia "activity, action, operation," 源自 energos "active, working," 源自 en "at" （参见 en- (2)) + ergon "work, that which is wrought; business; action" （参见 organ). Used by Aristotle with a 语义 "actuality, reality, existence" (opposed to "potential") but this was misunderstood in 晚期拉丁语 and afterward as "force of expression," as the power which calls up realistic mental pictures. Broader 意为 of "power" in English is 首见于 1660 年代. Scientific use 始于 1807 年. Energy crisis 最早见于 1970 年.

definitionLines: vt. 实行，执行；强制，强迫
entries.definition: vt. 实行，执行；强制，强迫
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "to drive by physical force; to try, attempt, strive; to fortify, strengthen a place;" late 14c. as "exert force, compel; make stronger, reinforce; strengthen an argument; grow stronger, become violent," from Old French enforcier "strengthen, reinforce; use force (on), offer violence (to); oppress; violate, rape" (12c.) or a native formation from en- (1) "make, put in" + force (n.). Meaning "compel obedience to (a law, etc.) is from 1640s. Related: Enforced; enforcing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to drive by physical force; to try, attempt, strive; to fortify, strengthen a place;" 14 世纪晚期 as "exert force, compel; make stronger, reinforce; strengthen an argument; grow stronger, become violent," 源自 古法语 enforcier "strengthen, reinforce; use force (on), offer violence (to); oppress; violate, rape" (12 世纪) or a 本族 formation 源自 en- (1) "make, put in" + force （名）. 义为 "compel obedience to (a law, etc.) 始于 1640 年代. 同源词：Enforced; enforcing.

example.en: The city hired more officers to enforce the no-parking zones in the school district.
example.zh: 该市雇用了更多警员来执行学区内的禁止停车区规定。

definitionLines: vt. 使从事，使忙于；占用（时间 等）；雇用，聘用；使订婚；
entries.definition: vt. 使从事，使忙于；占用（时间 等）；雇用，聘用；使订婚； vi. （in）从事于，参加
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to pledge" (something, as security for payment), from Old French engagier "bind (by promise or oath), pledge; pawn" (12c.), from phrase en gage "under pledge," from en "in" (see en- (1)) + gage "pledge," through Frankish from Proto-Germanic *wadiare "pledge" (see wed). It shows the common evolution of Germanic -w- to central French -g- (see gu-). Meaning "attract and occupy the attention of" is from 1640s; that of "employ, secure for aid, employment or use" is from 1640s, from notion of "binding as by a pledge;" meaning "enter into combat or contest with" is from 1640s. Specific sense of "promise to marry" is 1610s (implied in engaged). Machinery sense is from 1884. Also from the French word are German engagiren, Dutch engageren, Danish engagere.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to pledge" (something, as security for payment), 源自 古法语 engagier "bind (by promise or oath), pledge; pawn" (12 世纪), 源自 phrase en gage "under pledge," 源自 en "in" （参见 en- (1)) + gage "pledge," through Frankish 源自 原始日耳曼语 *wadiare "pledge" （参见 wed). It shows the common evolution of 日耳曼语 -w- to central 法语 -g- （参见 gu-). 义为 "attract and occupy the attention of" 始于 1640 年代; that of "employ, secure for aid, employment or use" 始于 1640 年代, 源自 概念 "binding as by a pledge;" 意为 "enter into combat or contest with" 始于 1640 年代. Specific 语义 "promise to marry" is 1610 年代 (implied in engaged). Machinery sense 始于 1884 年. Also 源自 法语 word are 德语 engagiren, 荷兰语 engageren, Danish engagere.

example.en: Young people are encouraged to engage deeply in community service projects.
example.zh: 年轻人被鼓励深度参与社区服务项目。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "formal promise," from engage + -ment. Meaning "a battle or fight between armies or fleets" is from 1660s; sense of "state of having entered into a promise of marriage" is from 1742; meaning "appointment" is from 1806. Engagement ring attested by 1863.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "formal promise," 源自 engage + -ment. 义为 "a battle or fight between armies or fleets" 始于 1660 年代; 语义 "state of having entered into a promise of marriage" 始于 1742 年; 意为 "appointment" 始于 1806 年. Engagement ring attested 截至 1863 年.

example.en: He had a prior engagement and could not attend the evening meeting.
example.zh: 他有一个事先的约定，无法参加晚上的会议。

definitionLines: n. 发动机，引擎；火车头，机车
entries.definition: n. 发动机，引擎；火车头，机车
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "mechanical device," especially one used in war; "manner of construction," also "skill, craft, innate ability; deceitfulness, trickery," from Old French engin "skill, wit, cleverness," also "trick, deceit, stratagem; war machine" (12c.), from Latin ingenium "inborn qualities, talent" (see ingenious), in Late Latin "a war engine, battering ram" (Tertullian, Isidore of Seville). Sense of "device that converts energy to mechanical power" is 18c.; in 19c. especially of steam engines. Middle English also had ingeny (n.) "gadget, apparatus, device," directly from Latin ingenium.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "mechanical device," 尤指 one used in war; "manner of construction," also "skill, craft, innate ability; deceitfulness, trickery," 源自 古法语 engin "skill, wit, cleverness," also "trick, deceit, stratagem; war machine" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 ingenium "inborn qualities, talent" （参见 ingenious), in 晚期拉丁语 "a war engine, battering ram" (Tertullian, Isidore of Seville). 义为 "device that converts energy to mechanical power" is 18 世纪; in 19 世纪 尤指 of steam engines. 中古英语 also had ingeny （名） "gadget, apparatus, device," 直接源自 拉丁语 ingenium.

example.en: The engine of the old car makes a rattling noise every time it starts.
example.zh: 那辆旧车的发动机每次启动时都会发出嘎嘎声。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., enginour, "constructor of military engines," from Old French engigneor "engineer, architect, maker of war-engines; schemer" (12c.), from Late Latin ingeniare (see engine); general sense of "inventor, designer" is recorded from early 15c.; civil sense, in reference to public works, is recorded from c. 1600 but not the common meaning of the word until 19c (hence lingering distinction as civil engineer). Meaning "locomotive driver" is first attested 1832, American English. A "maker of engines" in ancient Greece was a mekhanopoios.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, enginour, "constructor of military engines," 源自 古法语 engigneor "engineer, architect, maker of war-engines; schemer" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 ingeniare （参见 engine); general 语义 "inventor, designer" 见于 15 世纪初; civil sense, in reference to public works, 见于 约 1600 年 but not the common 意为 of the word until 19c (hence lingering distinction as civil engineer). 义为 "locomotive driver" is 最早见于 1832 年, American English. A "maker of engines" in ancient Greece was a mekhanopoios.

example.en: The engineer designed a bridge that could withstand strong earthquakes.
example.zh: 这位工程师设计了一座能抵御强烈地震的桥梁。

entries.etymology: 1720, "work done by an engineer," from engineer (n.). As a field of study, attested from 1792. An earlier word was engineership (1640s); engineery was attempted in 1793, but it did not stick.
entries.etymologyZh: 1720 年, "work done by an engineer," 源自 engineer （名）. 作为 field of study, attested 自 1792 年起. An earlier word was engineership (1640 年代); engineery was attempted 于 1793 年, but it did not stick.

entries.etymology: Old English Engla land, literally "the land of the Angles" (see English (n.1)), used alongside Angelcynn "the English race," which, with other forms, shows Anglo-Saxon persistence in thinking in terms of tribes rather than place. By late Old English times both words had come to be used with a clear sense of place, not people; a Dane, Canute, is first to call himself "King of England." By the 14c. the name was being used in reference to the entire island of Great Britain and to the land of the Celtic Britons before the Anglo-Saxon conquest. The loss of one of the duplicate syllables is a case of haplology.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 Engla land, 字面义为 "the land of the Angles" （参见 English (n.1)), used alongside Angelcynn "the English race," which, with other forms, shows 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 persistence in thinking in terms of tribes rather than place. By late 古英语 times both words had come to be used with a clear 语义 place, not people; a Dane, Canute, is first to call himself "King of England." By the 14 世纪 the name was being used in reference to the entire island of Great Britain and to the land of the Celtic Britons before the 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 conquest. The loss of one of the duplicate syllables is a case of haplology.

entries.definition: a.英语的，英国（人）的 n. 英语，英国人
entries.etymology: Old English, "belonging to the English people;" late 13c., "belonging to England," from English (n.1). The adjective in Old English meant "of or pertaining to the Angles." The adverb Englishly (mid-15c.) is rare.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语, "belonging to the English people;" 13 世纪晚期, "belonging to England," 源自 English (n.1). The 形容词 in 古英语 meant "of or pertaining to the Angles." The 副词 Englishly (15 世纪中期) is rare.

entries.etymology:
late 13c., anhaunsen "to raise, make higher," from Anglo-French enhauncer, probably from Old French enhaucier "make greater, make higher or louder; fatten, foster; raise in esteem," from Vulgar Latin *inaltiare, from Late Latin inaltare "raise, exalt,"  from altare "make high," from altus "high" (see old). Meaning "raise in station, wealth, or fame" attested in English from c. 1300. Related: Enhanced; enhancing.

The -h- in Old French supposedly is from influence of Frankish *hoh "high." The -n- perhaps is due to association with Provençal enansar, enanzar "promote, further," from enant "before, rather," from Latin in + ante "before."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, anhaunsen "to raise, make higher," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 enhauncer, 可能 源自 古法语 enhaucier "make greater, make higher or louder; fatten, foster; raise in esteem," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *inaltiare, 源自 晚期拉丁语 inaltare "raise, exalt," 源自 altare "make high," 源自 altus "high" （参见 old). 义为 "raise in station, wealth, or fame" 见于 English 源自 约 1300 年. 同源词：Enhanced; enhancing. The -h- in 古法语 supposedly 始于 influence of Frankish *hoh "high." The -n- 或许 is due to association with Provençal enansar, enanzar "promote, further," 源自 enant "before, rather," 源自 拉丁语 in + ante "before."

example.en: The new lighting was installed to enhance the appearance of the exhibition, making every painting easier to see.
example.zh: 安装这套新照明是为了改善展览的视觉效果，使每幅画都更容易看清。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "grow fat, increase" (intrans.); c. 1400, "make larger" (trans.), from Old French enlargier "to widen, increase, make larger," from en- "make, put in" (see en- (1)) + large (see large). Meaning "expand in words, speak at large" is from 1650s. There was a Middle English verb large "to extend, increase, make bigger," but it did not survive. Related: Enlarged; enlarging.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "grow fat, increase" (intrans.); 约 1400 年, "make larger" (trans.), 源自 古法语 enlargier "to widen, increase, make larger," 源自 en- "make, put in" （参见 en- (1)) + large （参见 large). 义为 "expand in words, speak at large" 始于 1650 年代. There was a 中古英语 动词 large "to extend, increase, make bigger," but it did not survive. 同源词：Enlarged; enlarging.

definitionLines: vt. 启发，启蒙；教导，开导
entries.definition: vt. 启发，启蒙；教导，开导
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to remove the dimness or blindness" (usually figurative, from one's eyes or heart); see en- (1) + lighten. From 1660s as "supply with intellectual light." Literal senses are later and less common in English: "put light in" is from 1580s; "shed light upon" is from 1610s. Related: Enlightened; enlightening. Old English had inlihtan "to illuminate, enlighten."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to remove the dimness or blindness" (通常 figurative, 源自 one's eyes or heart); 参见 en- (1) + lighten. From 1660 年代 as "supply with intellectual light." Literal senses are later and less common in English: "put light in" 始于 1580 年代; "shed light upon" 始于 1610 年代. 同源词：Enlightened; enlightening. 古英语 had inlihtan "to illuminate, enlighten."

definitionLines: vi. 从军；应募；赞助；支持
entries.definition: vi. 从军；应募；赞助；支持 vt. 征募；使入伍
entries.etymology: also inlist, 1690s (trans.), 1753 (intrans.), from en- (1) "make, put in" + list (n.). Possibly suggested by Dutch inlijsten "to write on a list." Related: Enlisted; enlisting.
entries.etymologyZh: also inlist, 1690 年代 (trans.), 1753 年 (intrans.), 源自 en- (1) "make, put in" + list （名）. Possibly suggested by 荷兰语 inlijsten "to write on a list." 同源词：Enlisted; enlisting.

example.en: He decided to enlist in the army right after finishing high school.
example.zh: 他决定高中毕业后立刻参军入伍。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "abnormal" (usually in a bad sense), from Latin enormis "out of rule, irregular, shapeless; extraordinary, very large," from assimilated form of ex- "out of" (see ex-) + norma "rule, norm" (see norm), with English -ous substituted for Latin -is. Meaning "extraordinary in size" is attested from 1540s; original sense of "outrageous" is more clearly preserved in enormity. Earlier was enormyous (mid-15c.) "exceedingly great, monstrous." Related: Enormously; enormousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "abnormal" (通常 in a bad sense), 源自 拉丁语 enormis "out of rule, irregular, shapeless; extraordinary, very large," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out of" （参见 ex-) + norma "rule, norm" （参见 norm), with English -ous substituted for 拉丁语 -is. 义为 "extraordinary in size" 见于 1540 年代; original 语义 "outrageous" is more clearly preserved in enormity. Earlier was enormyous (15 世纪中期) "exceedingly great, monstrous." 同源词：Enormously; enormousness.

example.en: The project required an enormous amount of funding to complete.
example.zh: 这个项目需要巨额资金才能完成。

entries.definition: a./n.足够，充足 ad. 足够地
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old English genog "sufficient in quantity or number," from Proto-Germanic compound *ganoga- "sufficient" (source also of Old Saxon ginog, Old Frisian enoch, Dutch genoeg, Old High German ginuog, German genug, Old Norse gnogr, Gothic ganohs).

First element is Old English ge- "with, together" (also a participial, collective, intensive, or perfective prefix), making this word the most prominent surviving example of the Old English prefix, the equivalent of Latin com- and Modern German ge- (from PIE *kom- "beside, near, by, with;" see com-). Second element is from PIE *nok-, from root *nek- (2) "to reach, attain" (source also of Sanskrit asnoti "reaches," Hittite ninikzi "lifts, raises," Lithuanian nešti "to bear, carry," Latin nancisci "to obtain"). 

As an adverb, "sufficiently for the purpose," in Old English; meaning "moderately, fairly, tolerably" (good enough) was in Middle English. Understated sense, as in have had enough "have had too much" was in Old English (which relied heavily on double negatives and understatement). As a noun in Old English, "a quantity or number sufficient for the purpose." As an interjection, "that is enough," from c. 1600. Colloquial 'nough said is attested from 1839.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古英语 genog "sufficient in quantity or number," 源自 原始日耳曼语 复合词 *ganoga- "sufficient" (source also of 古撒克逊语 ginog, 古弗里西语 enoch, 荷兰语 genoeg, 古高地德语 ginuog, 德语 genug, 古北欧语 gnogr, Gothic ganohs). First element is 古英语 ge- "with, together" (also a participial, collective, intensive，或perfective prefix), making this word the most prominent surviving example of the 古英语 prefix, the equivalent of 拉丁语 com- and 现代 德语 ge- (源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kom- "beside, near, by, with;" 参见 com-). Second element 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) *nok-, 源自 root *nek- (2) "to reach, attain" (source also of 梵语 asnoti "reaches," Hittite ninikzi "lifts, raises," Lithuanian nešti "to bear, carry," 拉丁语 nancisci "to obtain"). 作为 副词, "sufficiently for the purpose," in 古英语; 意为 "moderately, fairly, tolerably" (good enough) was in 中古英语. Understated sense, as in have had enough "have had too much" was in 古英语 (which relied heavily on double negatives and understatement). 作名词时 in 古英语, "a quantity or number sufficient for the purpose." 作为 interjection, "that is enough," 源自 约 1600 年. Colloquial 'nough said 见于 1839 年.

example.en: He didn't sleep enough last night and felt tired all day.
example.zh: 他昨晚睡眠不足，整天都感到疲倦。

definitionLines: vt. 使富足；使肥沃；装饰
entries.definition: vt. 使富足；使肥沃；装饰 enrol（1） vt. 登记，编人，招收
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to make wealthy," from Old French enrichir "enrich, enlarge," from en- "make, put in" (see en- (1)) + riche "rich" (see rich). Figurative sense "supply with abundance of something desirable" is from 1590s. Meaning "to fertilize" is from c. 1600. Scientific sense of "to increase the abundance of a particular isotope in some material" is first attested 1945. Related: Enriched; enriching.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to make wealthy," 源自 古法语 enrichir "enrich, enlarge," 源自 en- "make, put in" （参见 en- (1)) + riche "rich" （参见 rich). Figurative sense "supply with abundance of something desirable" 始于 1590 年代. 义为 "to fertilize" 始于 约 1600 年. Scientific 语义 "to increase the abundance of a particular isotope in some material" is 最早见于 1945 年. 同源词：Enriched; enriching.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Anglo-French enseurer, from en- "make" (see en- (1)) + Old French seur "sure" (see sure); probably influenced by Old French asseurer "assure." Compare insure. Related: Ensured; ensures; ensuring.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 enseurer, 源自 en- "make" （参见 en- (1)) + 古法语 seur "sure" （参见 sure); 可能 influenced by 古法语 asseurer "assure." 对比 insure. 同源词：Ensured; ensures; ensuring.

example.en: The safety guidelines are designed to ensure that no one gets injured.
example.zh: 安全准则的设计是为了确保没有人受伤。

definitionLines: v. 走进，进人；参加，加入；写 入，登录
entries.definition: v. 走进，进人；参加，加入；写 入，登录
entries.etymology: late 13c. entren, "enter into a place or a situation; join a group or society" (trans.); early 14c., "make one's entrance" (intrans.), from Old French entrer "enter, go in; enter upon, assume; initiate," from Latin intrare "to go into, enter" (source of Spanish entrar, Italian entrare), from intra "within," related to inter (prep., adj.) "among, between" (see inter-). Transitive and intransitive in Latin; in French intransitive only. From c. 1300 in English as "join or engage in: (an activity);" late 14c. as "penetrate," also "have sexual intercourse" (with a woman);" also "make an entry in a record or list," also "assume the duties" (of office, etc.). Related: Entered; entering.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期 entren, "enter into a place or a situation; join a group or society" (trans.); 14 世纪初, "make one's entrance" (intrans.), 源自 古法语 entrer "enter, go in; enter upon, assume; initiate," 源自 拉丁语 intrare "to go into, enter" (source of 西班牙语 entrar, 意大利语 entrare), 源自 intra "within," related to inter (prep., adj.) "among, between" （参见 inter-). Transitive and intransitive in 拉丁语; in 法语 intransitive only. From 约 1300 年 in English as "join or engage in: (an activity);" 14 世纪晚期 as "penetrate," also "have sexual intercourse" (with a woman);" also "make an entry in a record or list," also "assume the duties" (of office, etc.). 同源词：Entered; entering.

example.en: You must enter your PIN code before the machine will dispense any cash.
example.zh: 你必须先输入PIN码，机器才会出钞。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "an undertaking," formerly also enterprize, from Old French enterprise "an undertaking," noun use of fem. past participle of entreprendre "undertake, take in hand" (12c.), from entre- "between" (see entre-) + prendre "to take," contraction of prehendere (see prehensile). Abstract sense of "adventurous disposition, readiness to undertake challenges, spirit of daring" is from late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "an undertaking," formerly also enterprize, 源自 古法语 enterprise "an undertaking," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 entreprendre "undertake, take in hand" (12 世纪), 源自 entre- "between" （参见 entre-) + prendre "to take," contraction of prehendere （参见 prehensile). Abstract 语义 "adventurous disposition, readiness to undertake challenges, spirit of daring" 始于 15 世纪晚期

example.en: The young enterprise quickly expanded into three new markets within a year.
example.zh: 这家年轻的企业在一年内迅速扩张到三个新市场。

definitionLines: vt. 使欢乐，使娱乐；招待，款待
entries.definition: vt. 使欢乐，使娱乐；招待，款待
entries.etymology:
late 15c., "to keep up, maintain, to keep (someone) in a certain frame of mind," from Middle French entretenir, from Old French entretenir "hold together, stick together, support" (12c.), from entre- "among" (from Latin inter; see inter-) + tenir "to hold" (from Latin tenere; see tenet).

Sense of "have a guest" is late 15c.; that of "gratify, amuse" is 1620s. Meaning "to allow (something) to consideration, take into the mind" (of opinions, notions, etc.) is 1610s. Related: Entertained; entertaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "to keep up, maintain, to keep (someone) in a certain frame of mind," 源自 中古法语 entretenir, 源自 古法语 entretenir "hold together, stick together, support" (12 世纪), 源自 entre- "among" (源自 拉丁语 inter; 参见 inter-) + tenir "to hold" (源自 拉丁语 tenere; 参见 tenet). 义为 "have a guest" is 15 世纪晚期; that of "gratify, amuse" is 1620 年代. 义为 "to allow (something) to consideration, take into the mind" (of opinions, notions, etc.) is 1610 年代. 同源词：Entertained; entertaining.

example.en: The comedian was hired to entertain guests at the wedding.
example.zh: 这位喜剧演员被雇来在婚礼上招待和娱乐宾客。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "provision for support of a retainer; manner of social behavior," now obsolete, along with other 16c. senses; from entertain + -ment. Meaning "the amusement of someone" is from 1610s; sense of "that which entertains" is from 1650s; that of "public performance or display meant to amuse" is from 1727.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "provision for support of a retainer; manner of social behavior," 今废, along with other 16 世纪 senses; 源自 entertain + -ment. 义为 "the amusement of someone" 始于 1610 年代; 语义 "that which entertains" 始于 1650 年代; that of "public performance or display meant to amuse" 始于 1727 年.

example.en: The resort's nightly entertainment includes live music, dance shows, and comedy acts.
example.zh: 度假村的夜间娱乐包括现场音乐、舞蹈表演和喜剧节目。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from Middle French enthousiasme (16c.) and directly from Late Latin enthusiasmus, from Greek enthousiasmos "divine inspiration, enthusiasm (produced by certain kinds of music, etc.)," from enthousiazein "be inspired or possessed by a god, be rapt, be in ecstasy," from entheos "divinely inspired, possessed by a god," from en "in" (see en- (2)) + theos "god" (see theo-). Acquired a derogatory sense of "excessive religious emotion through the conceit of special revelation from God" (1650s) under the Puritans; generalized meaning "fervor, zeal" (the main modern sense) is first recorded 1716.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 中古法语 enthousiasme (16 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 enthusiasmus, 源自 希腊语 enthousiasmos "divine inspiration, enthusiasm (produced by certain kinds of music, etc.)," 源自 enthousiazein "be inspired or possessed by a god, be rapt, be in ecstasy," 源自 entheos "divinely inspired, possessed by a god," 源自 en "in" （参见 en- (2)) + theos "god" （参见 theo-). Acquired a derogatory 语义 "excessive religious emotion through the conceit of special revelation from God" (1650 年代) under the Puritans; generalized 意为 "fervor, zeal" (the main modern sense) is 首见于 1716 年.

example.en: Her enthusiasm for teaching inspired students to love learning.
example.zh: 她对教学的热情激励学生爱上了学习。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French entier "whole, unbroken, intact, complete," from Latin integrum "completeness" (nominative integer; see integer). Related: Entireness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 entier "whole, unbroken, intact, complete," 源自 拉丁语 integrum "completeness" (主格 integer; 参见 integer). 同源词：Entireness.

example.en: The patient rested for the entire duration of his hospital stay without leaving his room.
example.zh: 病人在整个住院期间都在休息，没有离开过病房。

definitionLines: vt. 给/授予……权利（或资 格），给…•…•题名，给…… 称号
entries.definition: vt. 给/授予……权利（或资 格），给…•…•题名，给…… 称号
entries.etymology:
also intitle, late 14c., "to give a title to a chapter, book, etc.," from Anglo-French entitler, Old French entiteler "entitle, call" (Modern French intituler), from Late Latin intitulare "give a title or name to," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + titulus "title" (see title (n.)).

Meaning "to bestow (on a person) a rank or office" is mid-15c. Sense of "to give (someone) 'title' to an estate or property," hence to give that person a claim to possession or privilege, is mid-15c.; this now is used mostly in reference to circumstances and actions. Related: Entitled; entitling.
entries.etymologyZh: also intitle, 14 世纪晚期, "to give a title to a chapter, book, etc.," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 entitler, 古法语 entiteler "entitle, call" (现代法语 intituler), 源自 晚期拉丁语 intitulare "give a title or name to," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + titulus "title" （参见 title （名）). 义为 "to bestow (on a person) a rank or office" is 15 世纪中期 义为 "to give (someone) 'title' to an estate or property," hence to give that person a claim to possession or privilege, is 15 世纪中期; this 现在 is used mostly in reference to circumstances and actions. 同源词：Entitled; entitling.

example.en: All employees are entitled to two weeks of paid vacation each year.
example.zh: 所有员工每年都有权享受两周带薪假期。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Late Latin entitatem (nominative entitas), from ens (genitive entis) "a thing," proposed by Caesar as present participle of esse "be" (see is), to render Greek philosophical term to on "that which is" (from neuter of present participle of einai "to be;" see essence). Originally abstract; concrete sense in English is from 1620s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 entitatem (主格 entitas), 源自 ens (属格 entis) "a thing," proposed by Caesar as 为 … 的现在分词 esse "be" （参见 is), to render 希腊语 philosophical term to on "that which is" (源自 neuter of 为 … 的现在分词 einai "to be;" 参见 essence). Originally abstract; concrete sense in English 始于 1620 年代.

example.en: The university is a separate legal entity from the hospital it oversees.
example.zh: 这所大学在法律上是独立于其监管医院的实体。

definitionLines: n. 入口，门口；人场，人会，人学
entries.definition: n. 入口，门口；人场，人会，人学
entries.etymology: 1520s, "act of entering," from Middle French entrance, from entrer (see enter). Sense of "door, gate" first recorded in English 1530s. Meaning "a coming of an actor upon the stage" is from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "act of entering," 源自 中古法语 entrance, 源自 entrer （参见 enter). 义为 "door, gate" 首见于 in English 1530 年代. 义为 "a coming of an actor upon the stage" 始于 约 1600 年.

example.en: Visitors must sign in at the main entrance before entering the building.
example.zh: 访客必须在主入口处登记后才能进入大楼。

entries.etymology: 1828, "manager or promoter of a theatrical production," reborrowing of French entrepreneur "one who undertakes or manages," agent noun from Old French entreprendre "undertake" (see enterprise). The word first crossed the Channel late 15c. (Middle English entreprenour) but did not stay. Meaning "business manager" is from 1852. Related: Entrepreneurship.
entries.etymologyZh: 1828 年, "manager or promoter of a theatrical production," reborrowing of 法语 entrepreneur "one who undertakes or manages," agent 名词 源自 古法语 entreprendre "undertake" （参见 enterprise). The word first crossed the Channel 15 世纪晚期 (中古英语 entreprenour) but did not stay. 义为 "business manager" 始于 1852 年. 同源词：Entrepreneurship.

example.en: A successful entrepreneur must be willing to take calculated risks in business.
example.zh: 一个成功的企业家必须愿意在商业中承担有计划的风险。

entries.etymology: also intrust, c. 1600, from en- (1) "make, put in" + trust (n.). Related: Entrusted; entrusting.
entries.etymologyZh: also intrust, 约 1600 年, 源自 en- (1) "make, put in" + trust （名）. 同源词：Entrusted; entrusting.

definitionLines: n. 进入，人场；入口，河口；登 记，登录
entries.definition: n. 进入，人场；入口，河口；登 记，登录
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "act or fact of physically entering; place of entrance, means of entering a building; opportunity or right of entering; initiation or beginning of an action;" from Old French entree "entry, entrance" (12c.), noun use of fem. past participle of entrer "to enter" (see enter). Meaning "that which is entered or set down (in a book, list, etc.)" is from c. 1500.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "act or fact of physically entering; place of entrance, means of entering a building; opportunity or right of entering; initiation or beginning of an action;" 源自 古法语 entree "entry, entrance" (12 世纪), 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 entrer "to enter" （参见 enter). 义为 "that which is entered or set down (in a book, list, etc.)" 始于 约 1500 年.

example.en: Please sign your name in the entry register at the front desk.
example.zh: 请在前台的登记册上签名。

entries.etymology: "a wrapper, an enclosing cover," specifically a prepared wrapper for a letter or other paper, 1705, from French enveloppe (13c.), a back-formation from envelopper "to envelop" (see envelop).
entries.etymologyZh: "a wrapper, an enclosing cover," specifically a prepared wrapper for a letter or other paper, 1705 年, 源自 法语 enveloppe (13 世纪), a back-formation 源自 envelopper "to envelop" （参见 envelop).

example.en: She sealed the letter and placed it in the envelope.
example.zh: 她把信封好，放进了信封里。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Anglo-French envious, Old French envieus (13c.), earlier envidius "envious, jealous" (12c., Modern French envieux), from Latin invidiosus "full of envy" (source of Spanish envidioso, Italian invidioso, Portuguese invejoso), from invidia (see envy). Related: Enviously; enviousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 envious, 古法语 envieus (13 世纪), earlier envidius "envious, jealous" (12 世纪, 现代法语 envieux), 源自 拉丁语 invidiosus "full of envy" (source of 西班牙语 envidioso, 意大利语 invidioso, 葡萄牙语 invejoso), 源自 invidia （参见 envy). 同源词：Enviously; enviousness.

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "state of being environed" (see environ (v.) + -ment); sense of "the aggregate of the conditions in which a person or thing lives" first recorded 1827 (used by Carlyle to render German Umgebung); specialized ecology sense first recorded 1956.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "state of being environed" （参见 environ （动） + -ment); 语义 "the aggregate of the conditions in which a person or thing lives" 首见于 1827 年 (used by Carlyle to render 德语 Umgebung); specialized ecology sense 首见于 1956 年.

example.en: The new factory must not discharge chemicals that harm the local environment.
example.zh: 新工厂不得排放危害当地环境的化学物质。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., from Old French envie "envy, jealousy, rivalry" (10c.), from Latin invidia "envy, jealousy" (source also of Spanish envidia, Portuguese inveja), from invidus "envious, having hatred or ill-will," from invidere "to envy, hate," earlier "look at (with malice), cast an evil eye upon," from in- "upon" (see in- (2)) + videre "to see" (see vision).

Similar formations in Avestan nipashnaka "envious," also "look at;" Old Church Slavonic zavideti "to envy," from videti "to see;" Lithuanian pavydeti "to envy," related to veizdeti "to see, to look at."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 envie "envy, jealousy, rivalry" (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 invidia "envy, jealousy" (source also of 西班牙语 envidia, 葡萄牙语 inveja), 源自 invidus "envious, having hatred or ill-will," 源自 invidere "to envy, hate," earlier "look at (with malice), cast an evil eye upon," 源自 in- "upon" （参见 in- (2)) + videre "to see" （参见 vision). Similar formations in Avestan nipashnaka "envious," also "look at;" Old Church Slavonic zavideti "to envy," 源自 videti "to see;" Lithuanian pavydeti "to envy," related to veizdeti "to see, to look at."

entries.etymology: 1580s, "pertaining to or constituting a lengthy heroic poem," via Middle French épique or directly from Latin epicus, from Greek epikos, from epos "a word; a tale, story; promise, prophecy, proverb; poetry in heroic verse," from PIE *wekw- "to speak" (see voice (n.)). Extended sense of "grand, heroic" first recorded in English 1731. From 1706 as a noun in reference to an epic poem, "A long narrative told on a grand scale of time and place, featuring a larger-than-life protagonist and heroic actions" [Miller Williams, "Patterns of Poetry"]. Earlier as "an epic poet" (1630s).
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "pertaining to or constituting a lengthy heroic poem," 经由 中古法语 épique or 直接源自 拉丁语 epicus, 源自 希腊语 epikos, 源自 epos "a word; a tale, story; promise, prophecy, proverb; poetry in heroic verse," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wekw- "to speak" （参见 voice （名）). Extended 语义 "grand, heroic" 首见于 in English 1731 年. From 1706 年 作名词时 in reference to an epic poem, "A long narrative told on a grand scale of time and place, featuring a larger-than-life protagonist and heroic actions" [Miller Williams, "Patterns of Poetry"]. Earlier as "an epic poet" (1630 年代).

entries.definition: a. 流行的；传染性的 n. 流行病；传染病
entries.etymology: c. 1600, "common to or affecting a whole people," originally and usually, though not etymologically, in reference to diseases, from French épidémique, from épidemié "an epidemic disease," from Medieval Latin epidemia, from Greek epidemia "a stay in a place; prevalence of an epidemic disease" (especially the plague), from epi "among, upon" (see epi-) + demos "people, district" (see demotic).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "common to or affecting a whole people," 原义为 and 通常, though not etymologically, in reference to diseases, 源自 法语 épidémique, 源自 épidemié "an epidemic disease," 源自 中古拉丁语 epidemia, 源自 希腊语 epidemia "a stay in a place; prevalence of an epidemic disease" (尤指 the plague), 源自 epi "among, upon" （参见 epi-) + demos "people, district" （参见 demotic).

example.en: Health officials declared a cholera epidemic in the region.
example.zh: 卫生官员宣布该地区暴发了霍乱疫情。

definitionLines: n. 一段情节；一个事件；插曲
entries.definition: n. 一段情节；一个事件；插曲
entries.etymology: 1670s, "commentary between two choric songs in a Greek tragedy," also "an incidental narrative or digression within a story, poem, etc.," from French épisode or directly from Greek epeisodion "an episode," literally "an addition," noun use of neuter of epeisodios "coming in besides," from epi "in addition" (see epi-) + eisodos "a coming in, entrance" (from eis "into" + hodos "way"). Transferred sense of "outstanding incident, experience" first recorded in English 1773. Transferred by 1930s to individual broadcasts of serial radio programs.
entries.etymologyZh: 1670 年代, "commentary between two choric songs in a Greek tragedy," also "an incidental narrative or digression within a story, poem, etc.," 源自 法语 épisode or 直接源自 希腊语 epeisodion "an episode," 字面义为 "an addition," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of epeisodios "coming in besides," 源自 epi "in addition" （参见 epi-) + eisodos "a coming in, entrance" (源自 eis "into" + hodos "way"). Transferred 语义 "outstanding incident, experience" 首见于 in English 1773 年. Transferred by 1930 年代 to individual broadcasts of serial radio programs.

example.en: The most dramatic episode of the series aired on Friday night.
example.zh: 这部剧最精彩的一集在周五晚上播出。

definitionLines: a.（to）同等的，相等的；平等 的；胜任的
n.（地位等）相同的人，匹敌者
entries.definition: a.（to）同等的，相等的；平等 的；胜任的 n.（地位等）相同的人，匹敌者 vt.等于，比得上
entries.etymology: late 14c., "identical in amount, extent, or portion;" early 15c., "even or smooth of surface," from Latin aequalis "uniform, identical, equal," from aequus "level, even, flat; as tall as, on a level with; friendly, kind, just, fair, equitable, impartial; proportionate; calm, tranquil," which is of unknown origin. Parallel formation egal (from Old French egal) was in use late 14c.-17c. Equal rights is from 1752; by 1854 in American English in reference to men and women. Equal opportunity (adj.) in terms of hiring, etc. is recorded by 1925.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "identical in amount, extent, or portion;" 15 世纪初, "even or smooth of surface," 源自 拉丁语 aequalis "uniform, identical, equal," 源自 aequus "level, even, flat; as tall as, on a level with; friendly, kind, just, fair, equitable, impartial; proportionate; calm, tranquil," which is 来源不详. Parallel formation egal (源自 古法语 egal) was in use 14 世纪晚期-17 世纪 Equal rights 始于 1752 年; 截至 1854 年 in American English in reference to men and women. Equal opportunity （形） in terms of hiring, etc. is recorded 截至 1925 年.

definitionLines: n. 同等，平等，相等，等同性
entries.definition: n. 同等，平等，相等，等同性
entries.etymology: late 14c., "evenness, smoothness, uniformity;" c. 1400, in reference to amount or number, from Old French equalité "equality, parity" (Modern French égalité, which form dates from 17c.), from Latin aequalitatem (nominative aequalitas) "equality, similarity, likeness" (also sometimes with reference to civil rights), from aequalis "uniform, identical, equal" (see equal (adj.)). Early 15c. as "state of being equal." Of privileges, rights, etc., in English from 1520s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "evenness, smoothness, uniformity;" 约 1400 年, in reference to amount or number, 源自 古法语 equalité "equality, parity" (现代法语 égalité, which form dates 源自 17 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 aequalitatem (主格 aequalitas) "equality, similarity, likeness" (also 有时 with reference to civil rights), 源自 aequalis "uniform, identical, equal" （参见 equal （形）). Early 15 世纪 as "state of being equal." Of privileges, rights, etc., in English 源自 1520 年代.

example.en: The constitution guarantees equality before the law for all citizens.
example.zh: 宪法保障所有公民在法律面前一律平等。

entries.etymology: late 14c., a term in astrology (from French équation, 14c.); general sense of "action of making equal" is from 1650s, from Latin aequationem (nominative aequatio) "an equal distribution, a sharing in common," noun of state from past participle stem of aequare (see equal (adj.)). Mathematical sense is from 1560s, on notion of equalizing the expressions;  Chemistry sense is from 1807.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, a term in astrology (源自 法语 équation, 14 世纪); general 语义 "action of making equal" 始于 1650 年代, 源自 拉丁语 aequationem (主格 aequatio) "an equal distribution, a sharing in common," 名词 of state 源自 past participle stem of aequare （参见 equal （形）). Mathematical sense 始于 1560 年代, on 概念 equalizing the expressions; Chemistry sense 始于 1807 年.

example.en: The physics teacher wrote a complex equation on the board.
example.zh: 物理老师在黑板上写了一个复杂的方程式。

entries.etymology: 1520s, from Middle French équiper "to fit out," from Old French esquiper "fit out a ship, load on board" (12c.), probably from Old Norse skipa "arrange, place in order," usually "fit out a ship," but also of warriors manning a hall and trees laden with ripe fruit, from skip "ship" (see ship (n.)). Related: Equipped; equipping. Similar words in  Spanish and Portuguese ultimately are from Germanic.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 中古法语 équiper "to fit out," 源自 古法语 esquiper "fit out a ship, load on board" (12 世纪), 可能 源自 古北欧语 skipa "arrange, place in order," 通常 "fit out a ship," but also of warriors manning a hall and trees laden with ripe fruit, 源自 skip "ship" （参见 ship （名）). 同源词：Equipped; equipping. Similar words in 西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 ultimately 始于 日耳曼语.

example.en: The school will equip every student with a laptop for remote learning.
example.zh: 学校将为每位学生配备一台用于远程学习的笔记本电脑。

entries.etymology: 1717, "things equipped;" 1748, "action of equipping;" from equip + -ment, or from French équipement. Superseding earlier equipage.
entries.etymologyZh: 1717 年, "things equipped;" 1748 年, "action of equipping;" 源自 equip + -ment，或源自 法语 équipement. Superseding earlier equipage.

example.en: The gym donated all its equipment to the community center after closing down.
example.zh: 健身房关闭后将所有设备捐赠给了社区中心。

entries.etymology: 1716, earlier aera (1610s), from Late Latin aera, era "an era or epoch from which time is reckoned" (7c.), probably identical with Latin aera "counters used for calculation," plural of aes (genitive aeris) "brass, copper, money" (see ore, also compare copper). The Latin word's use in chronology said to have begun in 5c. Spain (where the local era, aera Hispanica, began 38 B.C.E.; some say because of a tax levied that year). Other ancient eras included the Chaldean (autumn of 311 B.C.E.), the Era of Actium (31 B.C.E.), of Antioch (49 B.C.E.), of Tyre (126 B.C.E.), the Olympiadic (July 1, 776 B.C.E.) and the Seleucidan (autumn 312 B.C.E.). In English it originally meant "the starting point of an age" (compare epoch); meaning "system of chronological notation" is from 1640s; that of "historical period" is from 1741, as in the U.S. Era of Good Feeling (1817) was anything but.
entries.etymologyZh: 1716 年, earlier aera (1610 年代), 源自 晚期拉丁语 aera, era "an era or epoch from which time is reckoned" (7 世纪), 可能 identical with 拉丁语 aera "counters used for calculation," 为 … 的复数 aes (属格 aeris) "brass, copper, money" （参见 ore, also 对比 copper). The 拉丁语 word's use in chronology said to have begun in 5 世纪 Spain (where the local era, aera Hispanica, began 38 B.C.E.; some say because of a tax levied that year). Other ancient eras included the Chaldean (autumn of 311 B.C.E.), the Era of Actium (31 B.C.E.), of Antioch (49 B.C.E.), of Tyre (126 B.C.E.), the Olympiadic (July 1, 776 B.C.E.) and the Seleucidan (autumn 312 B.C.E.). In English it 原义为 meant "the starting point of an age" (对比 epoch); 意为 "system of chronological notation" 始于 1640 年代; that of "historical period" 始于 1741 年, as in the U.S. Era of Good Feeling (1817 年) was anything but.

example.en: The digital revolution marked the beginning of a new era in communication.
example.zh: 数字革命标志着通信领域新时代的开始。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "destroy utterly," literally "pull up by the roots," from Latin eradicatus, past participle of eradicare "to root out, annihilate" (see eradication). Related: Eradicated; eradicating; eradicable.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "destroy utterly," 字面义为 "pull up by the roots," 源自 拉丁语 eradicatus, 为 … 的过去分词 eradicare "to root out, annihilate" （参见 eradication). 同源词：Eradicated; eradicating; eradicable.

definitionLines: vt. 使竖立，使直立，树立，建立
entries.definition: a.直立的，竖立的，笔直的 vt. 使竖立，使直立，树立，建立
entries.etymology: late 14c., "upright, not bending," from Latin erectus "upright, elevated, lofty; eager, alert, aroused; resolute; arrogant," past participle of erigere "raise or set up," from e- "up, out of" + regere "to direct, keep straight, guide" (see regal).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "upright, not bending," 源自 拉丁语 erectus "upright, elevated, lofty; eager, alert, aroused; resolute; arrogant," 为 … 的过去分词 erigere "raise or set up," 源自 e- "up, out of" + regere "to direct, keep straight, guide" （参见 regal).

example.en: Workers began to erect the steel frame of the new building.
example.zh: 工人们开始竖立新大楼的钢架。

entries.definition: vt. 腐蚀，侵蚀 vi. 侵蚀；受腐蚀
entries.etymology: 1610s, "gnaw or eat away" (transitive), a back-formation from erosion, or else from French éroder, from Latin erodere "to gnaw away, consume," from assimilated form of ex- "away" (see ex-) + rodere "gnaw" (see rodent). Intransitive sense "become worn away" is by 1905. Related: Eroded; eroding. Originally of acids, ulcers, etc.; geological sense is from 1830.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "gnaw or eat away" (transitive), a back-formation 源自 erosion，或else 源自 法语 éroder, 源自 拉丁语 erodere "to gnaw away, consume," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "away" （参见 ex-) + rodere "gnaw" （参见 rodent). Intransitive sense "become worn away" is 截至 1905 年. 同源词：Eroded; eroding. Originally of acids, ulcers, etc.; geological sense 始于 1830 年.

entries.etymology:
also, through 18c., errour; c. 1300, "a deviation from truth made through ignorance or inadvertence, a mistake," also "offense against morality or justice; transgression, wrong-doing, sin;" from Old French error "mistake, flaw, defect, heresy," from Latin errorem (nominative error) "a wandering, straying, a going astray; meandering; doubt, uncertainty;" also "a figurative going astray, mistake," from errare "to wander; to err" (see err). From early 14c. as "state of believing or practicing what is false or heretical; false opinion or belief, heresy." From late 14c. as "deviation from what is normal; abnormality, aberration." From 1726 as "difference between observed value and true value."

Words for "error" in most Indo-European languages originally meant "wander, go astray" (for example Greek plane in the New Testament, Old Norse villa, Lithuanian klaida, Sanskrit bhrama-), but Irish has dearmad "error," from dermat "a forgetting."
entries.etymologyZh: also, through 18 世纪, errour; 约 1300 年, "a deviation from truth made through ignorance or inadvertence, a mistake," also "offense against morality or justice; transgression, wrong-doing, sin;" 源自 古法语 error "mistake, flaw, defect, heresy," 源自 拉丁语 errorem (主格 error) "a wandering, straying, a going astray; meandering; doubt, uncertainty;" also "a figurative going astray, mistake," 源自 errare "to wander; to err" （参见 err). From 14 世纪初 as "state of believing or practicing what is false or heretical; false opinion or belief, heresy." From 14 世纪晚期 as "deviation from what is normal; abnormality, aberration." From 1726 年 as "difference between observed value and true value." Words for "error" in most Indo-European languages 原义为 meant "wander, go astray" (for example 希腊语 plane in the New Testament, 古北欧语 villa, Lithuanian klaida, 梵语 bhrama-), but 爱尔兰语 has dearmad "error," 源自 dermat "a forgetting."

example.en: The report contained a factual error in the statistics section that had to be corrected.
example.zh: 报告统计部分存在一处事实错误，必须予以纠正。

entries.definition: vi.爆发；喷出；发疹；长牙 vt. 爆发；喷出
entries.etymology: 1650s, of diseases, etc., from Latin eruptus, past participle of erumpere "to break out, burst," from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + rumpere "to break, rupture" (see rupture (n.)). Of volcanoes, from 1770 (the Latin word was used in reference to Mount Etna). Related: Erupted; erupting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, of diseases, etc., 源自 拉丁语 eruptus, 为 … 的过去分词 erumpere "to break out, burst," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + rumpere "to break, rupture" （参见 rupture （名）). Of volcanoes, 自 1770 年起 (the 拉丁语 word was used in reference to Mount Etna). 同源词：Erupted; erupting.

example.en: The volcano could erupt at any time without warning.
example.zh: 火山随时可能在没有任何预警的情况下爆发。

definitionLines: vi. 逃跑；逃避，避免；逸出
entries.definition: vi. 逃跑；逃避，避免；逸出
entries.etymology: c. 1300, transitive and intransitive, "free oneself from confinement; extricate oneself from trouble; get away safely by flight (from battle, an enemy, etc.)," from Old North French escaper, Old French eschaper (12c., Modern French échapper), from Vulgar Latin *excappare, literally "get out of one's cape, leave a pursuer with just one's cape," from Latin ex- "out of" (see ex-) + Late Latin cappa "mantle" (see cap (n.)). Mid-14c., of things, "get or keep out of a person's grasp, elude (notice, perception, attention, etc.);" late 14c. as  "avoid experiencing or suffering (something), avoid physical contact with; avoid (a consequence)." Related: Escaped; escaping.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, transitive and intransitive, "free oneself from confinement; extricate oneself from trouble; get away safely by flight (from battle, an enemy, etc.)," 源自 Old North 法语 escaper, 古法语 eschaper (12 世纪, 现代法语 échapper), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *excappare, 字面义为 "get out of one's cape, leave a pursuer with just one's cape," 源自 拉丁语 ex- "out of" （参见 ex-) + 晚期拉丁语 cappa "mantle" （参见 cap （名）). Mid-14 世纪, of things, "get or keep out of a person's grasp, elude (notice, perception, attention, etc.);" 14 世纪晚期 as "avoid experiencing or suffering (something), avoid physical contact with; avoid (a consequence)." 同源词：Escaped; escaping.

example.en: The prisoners managed to escape from the high-security facility.
example.zh: 囚犯们设法从高度安保的设施中逃脱。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, from especial + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 especial + -ly (2).

example.en: Cold weather affects her health, especially when temperatures drop below zero.
example.zh: 寒冷天气影响她的健康，尤其是气温降至零度以下时。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "trial, attempt, endeavor," also "short, discursive literary composition" (first attested in writings of Francis Bacon, probably in imitation of Montaigne), from Middle French essai "trial, attempt, essay" (in Old French from 12c.), from Late Latin exagium "a weighing, a weight," from Latin exigere "drive out; require, exact; examine, try, test," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + agere (see act (n.)) apparently meaning here "to weigh." The suggestion is of unpolished writing. Compare assay, also examine.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "trial, attempt, endeavor," also "short, discursive literary composition" (最早见于 in writings of Francis Bacon, 可能 in imitation of Montaigne), 源自 中古法语 essai "trial, attempt, essay" (in 古法语 源自 12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 exagium "a weighing, a weight," 源自 拉丁语 exigere "drive out; require, exact; examine, try, test," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + agere （参见 act （名）) 似乎 意为 here "to weigh." The suggestion is of unpolished writing. 对比 assay, also examine.

example.en: Students must submit a five-paragraph essay by Friday.
example.zh: 学生们必须在周五前提交一篇五段式论文。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., essencia (respelled late 15c. on French model), from Latin essentia "being, essence," abstract noun formed (to translate Greek ousia "being, essence") from essent-, present participle stem of esse "to be," from PIE *es- "to be" (source also of Sanskrit asmi, Hittite eimi, Old Church Slavonic jesmi, Lithuanian esmi, Gothic imi, Old English eom "I am;" see be).

Originally "substance of the Trinity;" the general sense of "basic element of anything" is first recorded in English 1650s, though this is the underlying notion of the first English use of essential. Meaning "ingredient which gives something its particular character" is from c. 1600, especially of distilled oils from plants (1650s), hence "fragrance, perfume" (17c.). In 19c. U.S., essence-peddler could mean "medical salesman" and "skunk."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, essencia (respelled 15 世纪晚期 on 法语 model), 源自 拉丁语 essentia "being, essence," abstract 名词 formed (to translate 希腊语 ousia "being, essence") 源自 essent-, present participle stem of esse "to be," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *es- "to be" (source also of 梵语 asmi, Hittite eimi, Old Church Slavonic jesmi, Lithuanian esmi, Gothic imi, 古英语 eom "I am;" 参见 be). Originally "substance of the Trinity;" the general 语义 "basic element of anything" is 首见于 in English 1650 年代, though this is the underlying 概念 the first English use of essential. 义为 "ingredient which gives something its particular character" 始于 约 1600 年, 尤指 of distilled oils 源自 plants (1650 年代), hence "fragrance, perfume" (17 世纪). In 19 世纪 U.S., essence-peddler could mean "medical salesman" and "skunk."

example.en: Compassion is the essence of good leadership, without which authority becomes cold and hollow.
example.zh: 同情心是优秀领导力的本质，没有它，权威就会变得冷漠而空洞。

definitionLines: a.必不可少，必要的；本质的， 实质的；基本的
entries.definition: a.必不可少，必要的；本质的， 实质的；基本的
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "that is such by its essence," from Late Latin essentialis, from essentia "essence" (see essence). Meaning "pertaining to essence" is from late 14c., that of "constituting the essence of something" is from 1540s; that of "necessary" is from 1520s. Essentials "indispensable elements" is from early 16c. Related: Essentially.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "that is such by its essence," 源自 晚期拉丁语 essentialis, 源自 essentia "essence" （参见 essence). 义为 "pertaining to essence" 始于 14 世纪晚期, that of "constituting the essence of something" 始于 1540 年代; that of "necessary" 始于 1520 年代. Essentials "indispensable elements" 始于 16 世纪初 同源词：Essentially.

example.en: Sodium and potassium are essential minerals that the human body cannot produce on its own.
example.zh: 钠和钾是人体自身无法合成的必需矿物质。

definitionLines: v. 建立，设立，创办；确立，使确 认
entries.definition: v. 建立，设立，创办；确立，使确 认
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French establiss-, present participle stem of establir "cause to stand still, establish, stipulate, set up, erect, build" (12c., Modern French établir), from Latin stabilire "make stable," from stabilis "stable" (see stable (adj.)). For the excrescent e-, see e-. Related: Established; establishing. An established church or religion is one sanctioned by the state.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 establiss-, present participle stem of establir "cause to stand still, establish, stipulate, set up, erect, build" (12 世纪, 现代法语 établir), 源自 拉丁语 stabilire "make stable," 源自 stabilis "stable" （参见 stable （形）). For the excrescent e-, 参见 e-. 同源词：Established; establishing. An established church or religion is one sanctioned by the state.

example.en: The government signed a treaty to establish diplomatic ties with three new nations.
example.zh: 政府签署了一项条约，与三个新国家建立外交关系。

definitionLines: n. 建立，设立，确立；建立的机|evening
entries.definition: n. 建立，设立，确立；建立的机|evening
entries.etymology: late 15c., "settled arrangement," also "income, property," from establish + -ment. Meaning "established church" is from 1731; Sense of "place of business" is from 1832. Meaning "social matrix of ruling people and institutions" is attested occasionally from 1923, consistently from 1955.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "settled arrangement," also "income, property," 源自 establish + -ment. 义为 "established church" 始于 1731 年; 义为 "place of business" 始于 1832 年. 义为 "social matrix of ruling people and institutions" is attested occasionally 自 1923 年起, consistently 自 1955 年起.

example.en: The establishment of the new hospital took three years and millions in funding.
example.zh: 这所新医院的建立历经三年并耗费了数百万资金。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., "rank, standing, condition," from Anglo-French astat, Old French estat "state, position, condition, health, status, legal estate" (13c., Modern French état), from Latin status "state or condition, position, place; social position of the aristocracy," from PIE root *stā- "to stand" (see stet).

For the excrescent e-, see e-. Sense of "property" is late 14c., from that of "worldly prosperity;" specific application to "landed property" (usually of large extent) is first recorded in American English 1620s. A native word for this was Middle English ethel (Old English æðel) "ancestral land or estate, patrimony." Meaning "collective assets of a dead person or debtor" is from 1830.

The three estates (in Sweden and Aragon, four) conceived as orders in the body politic date from late 14c. In France, they are the clergy, nobles, and townsmen; in England, originally the clergy, barons, and commons, later Lords Spiritual, Lords Temporal, and commons. For Fourth Estate see four.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "rank, standing, condition," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 astat, 古法语 estat "state, position, condition, health, status, legal estate" (13 世纪, 现代法语 état), 源自 拉丁语 status "state or condition, position, place; social position of the aristocracy," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand" （参见 stet). For the excrescent e-, 参见 e-. 义为 "property" is 14 世纪晚期, 源自 that of "worldly prosperity;" specific application to "landed property" (通常 of large extent) is 首见于 in American English 1620 年代. A 本族 word for this was 中古英语 ethel (古英语 æðel) "ancestral land or estate, patrimony." 义为 "collective assets of a dead person or debtor" 始于 1830 年. The three estates (in Sweden and Aragon, four) conceived as orders in the body politic date 源自 14 世纪晚期 In France, they are the clergy, nobles, and townsmen; in England, 原义为 the clergy, barons, and commons, later Lords Spiritual, Lords Temporal, and commons. For Fourth Estate 参见 four.

example.en: The businessman left his entire estate to charity after his death.
example.zh: 这位商人去世后将全部财产留给了慈善机构。

definitionLines: vt. 认为；尊敬；考虑；估价
entries.definition: vt. 认为；尊敬；考虑；估价 n. 尊重；尊敬
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Old French estimer "to estimate, determine" (14c.), from Latin aestimare "to value, determine the value of, appraise," perhaps ultimately from *ais-temos "one who cuts copper," i.e. mints money (but de Vaan finds this "not very credible"). At first used as we would now use estimate; sense of "value, respect" is 1530s. Related: Esteemed; esteeming.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 estimer "to estimate, determine" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 aestimare "to value, determine the value of, appraise," 或许 最终源自 *ais-temos "one who cuts copper," i.e. mints money (but de Vaan finds this "not very credible"). At first used as we would 现在 use estimate; 语义 "value, respect" is 1530 年代. 同源词：Esteemed; esteeming.

entries.etymology: 1560s, "valuation," from Latin aestimatus "determine the value of," figuratively "to value, esteem," verbal noun from aestimare (see esteem (v.)). Earlier in sense "power of the mind" (mid-15c.). Meaning "approximate judgment" is from 1580s. As a builder's statement of projected costs, from 1796.
