entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "valuation," 源自 拉丁语 aestimatus "determine the value of," figuratively "to value, esteem," verbal 名词 源自 aestimare （参见 esteem （动）). Earlier in sense "power of the mind" (15 世纪中期). 义为 "approximate judgment" 始于 1580 年代. 作为 builder's statement of projected costs, 自 1796 年起.

example.en: Experts estimate that the project will cost around two million dollars to complete.
example.zh: 专家估计该项目完工费用约为两百万美元。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French eternel "eternal," or directly from Late Latin aeternalis, from Latin aeternus "of an age, lasting, enduring, permanent, everlasting, endless," contraction of aeviternus "of great age," from aevum "age" (see eon). Used since Middle English both of things or conditions without beginning or end and things with a beginning only but no end. A parallel form, Middle English eterne, is from Old French eterne (cognate with Spanish eterno), directly from Latin aeternus. Related: Eternally. The Eternal (n.) for "God" is attested from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 eternel "eternal," or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 aeternalis, 源自 拉丁语 aeternus "of an age, lasting, enduring, permanent, everlasting, endless," contraction of aeviternus "of great age," 源自 aevum "age" （参见 eon). Used 自 中古英语 both of things or conditions without beginning or end and things with a beginning only but no end. A parallel form, 中古英语 eterne, 始于 古法语 eterne (与 … 同源 西班牙语 eterno), 直接源自 拉丁语 aeternus. 同源词：Eternally. The Eternal （名） for "God" 见于 1580 年代.

example.en: Great works of art often deal with eternal themes such as love, loss, and hope.
example.zh: 伟大的艺术作品往往涉及爱、失去与希望等永恒主题。

entries.etymology:
"figure which stands for naught in the Arabic notation," also "the absence of all quantity considered as quantity," c. 1600, from French zéro or directly from Italian zero, from Medieval Latin zephirum, from Arabic sifr "cipher," translation of Sanskrit sunya-m "empty place, desert, naught" (see cipher (n.)).

A brief history of the invention of "zero" can be found here. Meaning "worthless person" is recorded from 1813. As an adjective from 1810. Zero tolerance first recorded 1972, originally U.S. political language. Zero-sum in game theory is from 1944 (von Neumann), indicating that if one player wins X amount the other or others must lose X amount.
entries.etymologyZh: "figure which stands for naught in the Arabic notation," also "the absence of all quantity considered as quantity," 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 zéro or 直接源自 意大利语 zero, 源自 中古拉丁语 zephirum, 源自 阿拉伯语 sifr "cipher," translation of 梵语 sunya-m "empty place, desert, naught" （参见 cipher （名）). A brief history of the invention of "zero" can be found here. 义为 "worthless person" 见于 1813 年. 作形容词时 自 1810 年起. Zero tolerance 首见于 1972 年, 原义为 U.S. political language. Zero-sum in game theory 始于 1944 年 (von Neumann), indicating that if one player wins X amount the other or others must lose X amount.

entries.etymology:
from Latin Europa "Europe," from Greek Europe, which is of uncertain origin; as a geographic name first recorded in the Homeric hymn to Apollo (522 B.C.E. or earlier):

Often explained as "broad face," from eurys "wide" (see eury-) + ops "face," literally "eye" (see eye (n.)). But also traditionally linked with Europa, Phoenician princess in Greek mythology. Klein (citing Heinrich Lewy) suggests a possible Semitic origin in Akkad. erebu "to go down, set" (in reference to the sun) which would parallel orient. Another suggestion along those lines is Phoenician 'ereb "evening," hence "west."
entries.etymologyZh: 源自 拉丁语 Europa "Europe," 源自 希腊语 Europe, which is 来源存疑; 作为 geographic name 首见于 in the Homeric hymn to Apollo (522 B.C.E. or earlier): Often explained as "broad face," 源自 eurys "wide" （参见 eury-) + ops "face," 字面义为 "eye" （参见 eye （名）). But also traditionally linked with Europa, Phoenician princess in 希腊语 mythology. Klein (citing Heinrich Lewy) suggests a possible Semitic origin in Akkad. erebu "to go down, set" (in reference to the sun) which would parallel orient. Another suggestion along those lines is Phoenician 'ereb "evening," hence "west."

entries.definition: a.欧洲的 n. 欧洲人
entries.etymology: c. 1600 (adj.); 1630s (n.), from French Européen, from Latin Europaeus, from Greek Europaios "European," from Europe (see Europe).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年 （形）; 1630 年代 （名）, 源自 法语 Européen, 源自 拉丁语 Europaeus, 源自 希腊语 Europaios "European," 源自 Europe （参见 Europe).

example.en: The museum held a special exhibition of European art from the Renaissance period.
example.zh: 该博物馆举办了一场文艺复兴时期欧洲艺术的特别展览。

entries.definition: vt. 疏散，撤退 vi.撤退；疏散
entries.etymology:
1520s (trans.), from Latin evacuatus, past participle of evacuare "to empty, make void, nullify," used by Pliny in reference to the bowels, used figuratively in Late Latin for "clear out;" from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + vacuus "empty" (see vacuum).

Earliest sense in English is medical. Military use is by 1710. Meaning "remove inhabitants to safer ground" is from 1934. Intransitive sense is from 1630s; of civilian persons by 1900. Replaced Middle English evacuen "draw off or expel (humors) from the body" (c. 1400). Related: Evacuated; evacuating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代 (trans.), 源自 拉丁语 evacuatus, 为 … 的过去分词 evacuare "to empty, make void, nullify," used by Pliny in reference to the bowels, used figuratively in 晚期拉丁语 for "clear out;" 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + vacuus "empty" （参见 vacuum). Earliest sense in English is medical. Military use is 截至 1710 年. 义为 "remove inhabitants to safer ground" 始于 1934 年. Intransitive sense 始于 1630 年代; of civilian persons 截至 1900 年. Replaced 中古英语 evacuen "draw off or expel (humors) from the body" (约 1400 年). 同源词：Evacuated; evacuating.

entries.definition: vt. 逃避；规避；逃脱 vi. 逃避；规避；逃脱
entries.etymology: 1510s, "escape," from Middle French evader, from Latin evadere "to escape, get away," from assimilated form of ex- "away" (see ex-) + vadere "to go, walk" (see vamoose). Special sense of "escape by trickery" is from 1530s. Related: Evaded; evading.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "escape," 源自 中古法语 evader, 源自 拉丁语 evadere "to escape, get away," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "away" （参见 ex-) + vadere "to go, walk" （参见 vamoose). Special 语义 "escape by trickery" 始于 1530 年代. 同源词：Evaded; evading.

entries.etymology: 1831, back-formation from evaluation, or else from French évaluer, back-formation from évaluation. Originally in mathematics. Related: Evaluated; evaluating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1831 年, back-formation 源自 evaluation，或else 源自 法语 évaluer, back-formation 源自 évaluation. Originally in mathematics. 同源词：Evaluated; evaluating.

example.en: The board will evaluate the CEO's performance against specific financial targets.
example.zh: 董事会将依据具体财务指标评估CEO的绩效。

entries.definition: vt. 使……蒸发；使…•…脫水； 使……消失 vi. 消失，失踪；蒸发，挥发
entries.etymology: early 15c., "draw off (humors or spirits) as vapor," from Late Latin evaporatum, past participle of evaporare "disperse in vapor" (see evaporation). Intransitive sense by 1560s. Figurative use by 1610s. Related: Evaporated; evaporating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "draw off (humors or spirits) as vapor," 源自 晚期拉丁语 evaporatum, 为 … 的过去分词 evaporare "disperse in vapor" （参见 evaporation). Intransitive sense by 1560 年代. Figurative use by 1610 年代. 同源词：Evaporated; evaporating.

entries.etymology: fem. proper name, Biblical first woman, Late Latin, from Hebrew Hawwah, literally "a living being," from base hawa "he lived" (compare Arabic hayya, Aramaic hayyin).
entries.etymologyZh: fem. proper name, Biblical first woman, 晚期拉丁语, 源自 希伯来语 Hawwah, 字面义为 "a living being," 源自 base hawa "he lived" (对比 阿拉伯语 hayya, Aramaic hayyin).

definitionLines: a. 平的，平坦的；均匀的；平等 的，均等的；偶数的
entries.definition: ad. 甚至，连……都 a. 平的，平坦的；均匀的；平等 的，均等的；偶数的
entries.etymology:
Old English efen "level," also "equal, like; calm, harmonious; equally; quite, fully; namely," from Proto-Germanic *ebnaz (source also of Old Saxon eban, Old Frisian even "level, plain, smooth," Dutch even, Old High German eban, German eben, Old Norse jafn, Danish jævn, Gothic ibns). The adverb is Old English efne "exactly, just, likewise." Modern adverbial sense (introducing an extreme case of something more generally implied) seems to have arisen 16c. from use of the word to emphasize identity ("Who, me?" "Even you").

Etymologists are uncertain whether the original sense was "level" or "alike." Used extensively in Old English compounds, with a sense of "fellow, co-" (as in efeneald "of the same age;" Middle English even-sucker "foster-brother"). Of numbers, from 1550s. Sense of "on an equal footing" is from 1630s. Rhyming reduplication phrase even steven is attested from 1866; even break (n.) first recorded 1907. Even-tempered from 1712. To get even with "retaliate upon" is attested by 1833.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 efen "level," also "equal, like; calm, harmonious; equally; quite, fully; namely," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ebnaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 eban, 古弗里西语 even "level, plain, smooth," 荷兰语 even, 古高地德语 eban, 德语 eben, 古北欧语 jafn, Danish jævn, Gothic ibns). The 副词 is 古英语 efne "exactly, just, likewise." 现代 adverbial sense (introducing an extreme case of something more generally implied) seems to have arisen 16 世纪 源自 use of the word to emphasize identity ("Who, me?" "Even you"). Etymologists are uncertain whether the original sense was "level" or "alike." Used extensively in 古英语 compounds, with a 语义 "fellow, co-" (as in efeneald "of the same age;" 中古英语 even-sucker "foster-brother"). Of numbers, 源自 1550 年代. 义为 "on an equal footing" 始于 1630 年代. Rhyming reduplication phrase even steven 见于 1866 年; even break （名） 首见于 1907 年. Even-tempered 自 1712 年起. To get even with "retaliate upon" is attested 截至 1833 年.

example.en: The project finished ahead of schedule, even saving money.
example.zh: 项目提前完成，甚至还节省了一些钱。

definitionLines: n. 事件，事变，大事；比赛项目
entries.definition: n. 事件，事变，大事；比赛项目
entries.etymology: 1570s, "the consequence of anything" (as in in the event that); 1580s, "that which happens;" from Middle French event, from Latin eventus "occurrence, accident, event, fortune, fate, lot, issue," from past participle stem of evenire "to come out, happen, result," from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + venire "to come" (see venue). Meaning "a contest or single proceeding in a public sport" is from 1865. Events as "the course of events" is attested from 1842. Event horizon in astrophysics is from 1969.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "the consequence of anything" (as in in the event that); 1580 年代, "that which happens;" 源自 中古法语 event, 源自 拉丁语 eventus "occurrence, accident, event, fortune, fate, lot, issue," 源自 past participle stem of evenire "to come out, happen, result," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + venire "to come" （参见 venue). 义为 "a contest or single proceeding in a public sport" 始于 1865 年. Events as "the course of events" 见于 1842 年. Event horizon in astrophysics 始于 1969 年.

example.en: The opening ceremony was the most memorable event of the entire festival.
example.zh: 开幕式是整个节日中最令人难忘的事件。

entries.etymology: "ultimately," 1670s, from eventual + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: "ultimately," 1670 年代, 源自 eventual + -ly (2).

example.en: After years of setbacks, she eventually achieved her dream of becoming a doctor.
example.zh: 经历多年挫折后，她最终实现了成为医生的梦想。

entries.etymology:
Old English æfre "ever, at any time, always;" of uncertain origin, no cognates in any other Germanic language; perhaps a contraction of a in feore, literally "ever in life" (the expression a to fore is common in Old English writings). First element is almost certainly related to Old English a "always, ever," from Proto-Germanic *aiwo, from PIE *aiw- "vital force, life, long life, eternity" (see eon). Liberman suggests second element is comparative adjectival suffix -re.

Sometimes contracted to e'er in dialect and poetry. Ever began to be used in late Old English as a way to generalize or intensify when, what, where, etc. The sense evolution was from "at any time at all, in any way" to "at any particular time; at some time or another; under any circumstances." Ever so "to whatever extent" is recorded by 1680s. Expression did you ever? (implying "see/do/hear of such a thing") attested by 1840.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 æfre "ever, at any time, always;" 来源存疑, no cognates in any other 日耳曼语 language; 或许 a contraction of a in feore, 字面义为 "ever in life" (the expression a to fore is common in 古英语 writings). First element is almost certainly related to 古英语 a "always, ever," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aiwo, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *aiw- "vital force, life, long life, eternity" （参见 eon). Liberman suggests second element is comparative adjectival suffix -re. Sometimes contracted to e'er in dialect and poetry. Ever began to be used in late 古英语 作为 way to generalize or intensify when, what, where, etc. The sense evolution was 源自 "at any time at all, in any way" to "at any particular time; at some time or another; under any circumstances." Ever so "to whatever extent" is recorded by 1680 年代. Expression did you ever? (implying "see/do/hear of such a thing") attested 截至 1840 年.

definitionLines: a. 永恒的；接连不断的
entries.definition: a. 永恒的；接连不断的
entries.etymology: early 13c., "eternal" (adj.); "eternally" (adv.); "eternity" (n.); from ever + lasting. Colloquially in mid-19c. U.S., "very, exceedingly." A verb, everlast, "to endure forever," is recorded late 14c. Related: Everlastingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "eternal" （形）; "eternally" （副）; "eternity" （名）; 源自 ever + lasting. Colloquially in 19 世纪中期 U.S., "very, exceedingly." A 动词, everlast, "to endure forever," is recorded 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Everlastingly.

entries.etymology:
early 13c., contraction of Old English æfre ælc "each of a group," literally "ever each" (Chaucer's everich), from each with ever added for emphasis. The word still is felt to want emphasis; as in Modern English every last ..., every single ..., etc.

Also a pronoun to Chaucer, Shakespeare, Spenser. Compare everybody, everything, etc. The word everywhen is attested from 1843 but never caught on; neither did everyhow (1837). Slang phrase every Tom, Dick, and Harry "every man, everyone" dates from at least 1734, from common English given names.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, contraction of 古英语 æfre ælc "each of a group," 字面义为 "ever each" (Chaucer's everich), 源自 each with ever added for emphasis. The word still is felt to want emphasis; as in 现代英语 every last ..., every single ..., etc. Also a pronoun to Chaucer, Shakespeare, Spenser. 对比 everybody, everything, etc. The word everywhen 见于 1843 年 but never caught on; neither did everyhow (1837 年). Slang phrase every Tom, Dick, and Harry "every man, everyone" dates 源自 at least 1734 年, 源自 common English given names.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from every + body (n.) in obsolete sense of "person."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 every + body （名） in 已废 语义 "person."

entries.etymology: 1630s, "worn on ordinary days," as opposed to Sundays or high days, from noun meaning "a week day" (late 14c.), from every (adj.) + day (n.). Extended sense of "to be met with every day, common" is from 1763.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "worn on ordinary days," as opposed to Sundays or high days, 源自 名词 意为 "a week day" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 every （形） + day （名）. Extended 语义 "to be met with every day, common" 始于 1763 年.

example.en: He wore everyday clothes to the casual Friday gathering.
example.zh: 他穿着日常便装去参加周五的休闲聚会。

definitionLines: pron. 事事，凡事，一切东西
entries.definition: pron. 事事，凡事，一切东西
entries.etymology: late 14c., from every + thing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 every + thing.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, eauerihwer, contracted from Old English æfre gehwær; see ever (adv.) + where. Not from every; the -i- in the word apparently was a prefix; compare handiwork.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, eauerihwer, contracted 源自 古英语 æfre gehwær; 参见 ever （副） + where. Not 源自 every; the -i- in the word 似乎 was a prefix; 对比 handiwork.

example.en: Tourists with cameras could be seen everywhere in the city center.
example.zh: 在市中心到处都能看到拿着相机的游客。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "appearance from which inferences may be drawn," from Old French evidence, from Late Latin evidentia "proof," in classical Latin "distinction, vivid presentation, clearness" in rhetoric, from stem of Latin evidens "obvious, apparent" (see evident).

Meaning "ground for belief" is from late 14c.; that of "obviousness" is from 1660s and tacks closely to the sense of evident. Legal senses are from c. 1500, when it began to oust witness. Also "one who furnishes testimony, witness" (1590s); hence turn (State's) evidence.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "appearance from which inferences may be drawn," 源自 古法语 evidence, 源自 晚期拉丁语 evidentia "proof," in classical 拉丁语 "distinction, vivid presentation, clearness" in rhetoric, 源自 stem of 拉丁语 evidens "obvious, apparent" （参见 evident). 义为 "ground for belief" 始于 14 世纪晚期; that of "obviousness" 始于 1660 年代 and tacks closely to the 语义 evident. Legal senses 始于 约 1500 年, when it began to oust witness. Also "one who furnishes testimony, witness" (1590 年代); hence turn (State's) evidence.

example.en: The lawyer presented forensic evidence that proved his client was innocent.
example.zh: 律师出示了法证证据，证明其当事人无罪。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French evident and directly from Latin evidentem (nominative evidens) "perceptible, clear, obvious, apparent" from ex- "fully, out of" (see ex-) + videntem (nominative videns), present participle of videre "to see" (see vision).

entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 evident + -ly (2).

example.en: She had evidently not slept well, given the dark circles under her eyes.

entries.definition: a. 坏的，邪恶的 n. 邪恶，罪恶；祸害
entries.etymology:
Old English yfel (Kentish evel) "bad, vicious, ill, wicked," from Proto-Germanic *ubilaz (source also of Old Saxon ubil, Old Frisian and Middle Dutch evel, Dutch euvel, Old High German ubil, German übel, Gothic ubils), from PIE *upelo-, from root *wap- "bad, evil" (source also of Hittite huwapp- "evil").

In Old English and other older Germanic languages other than Scandinavian, "this word is the most comprehensive adjectival expression of disapproval, dislike or disparagement" [OED]. Evil was the word the Anglo-Saxons used where we would use bad, cruel, unskillful, defective (adj.), or harm (n.), crime, misfortune, disease (n.). In Middle English, bad took the wider range of senses and evil began to focus on moral badness. Both words have good as their opposite. Evil-favored (1520s) meant "ugly." Evilchild is attested as an English surname from 13c.

The adverb is Old English yfele, originally of words or speech. Also as a noun in Old English, "what is bad; sin, wickedness; anything that causes injury, morally or physically." Especially of a malady or disease from c. 1200. The meaning "extreme moral wickedness" was one of the senses of the Old English noun, but it did not become established as the main sense of the modern word until 18c. As a noun, Middle English also had evilty. Related: Evilly. Evil eye (Latin oculus malus) was Old English eage yfel. The jocular notion of an evil twin as an excuse for regrettable deeds is by 1986, American English, from an old motif in mythology.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 yfel (Kentish evel) "bad, vicious, ill, wicked," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ubilaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 ubil, 古弗里西语 and Middle 荷兰语 evel, 荷兰语 euvel, 古高地德语 ubil, 德语 übel, Gothic ubils), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *upelo-, 源自 root *wap- "bad, evil" (source also of Hittite huwapp- "evil"). In 古英语 and other older 日耳曼语 languages other than Scandinavian, "this word is the most comprehensive adjectival expression of disapproval, dislike or disparagement" [OED]. Evil was the word the Anglo-Saxons used where we would use bad, cruel, unskillful, defective （形），或harm （名）, crime, misfortune, disease （名）. In 中古英语, bad took the wider range of senses and evil began to focus on moral badness. Both words have good as their opposite. Evil-favored (1520 年代) meant "ugly." Evilchild is attested 作为 English surname 源自 13 世纪 The 副词 is 古英语 yfele, 原义为 of words or speech. Also 作名词时 in 古英语, "what is bad; sin, wickedness; anything that causes injury, morally or physically." Especially of a malady or disease 源自 约 1200 年. The 意为 "extreme moral wickedness" was one of the senses of the 古英语 名词, but it did not become established as the main 语义 the modern word until 18 世纪 作名词时, 中古英语 also had evilty. 同源词：Evilly. Evil eye (拉丁语 oculus malus) was 古英语 eage yfel. The jocular 概念 an evil twin 作为 excuse for regrettable deeds is 截至 1986 年, American English, 源自 an old motif in mythology.

example.en: The story explores the eternal battle between good and evil in human nature.
example.zh: 这个故事探讨了人性中善与恶之间永恒的较量。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from French évoquer or directly from Latin evocare "call out, rouse, summon" (see evocation). Often more or less with a sense of "calling spirits," or being called by them. Of feelings, memories, etc., by 1856. Related: Evoked; evokes; evoking.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 法语 évoquer or 直接源自 拉丁语 evocare "call out, rouse, summon" （参见 evocation). Often more or less with a 语义 "calling spirits," or being called by them. Of feelings, memories, etc., 截至 1856 年. 同源词：Evoked; evokes; evoking.

example.en: The old photograph evoked memories of their childhood together.
example.zh: 那张旧照片唤起了他们童年共同的回忆。

definitionLines: n. 渐进，发展；进化，演化
entries.definition: n. 渐进，发展；进化，演化
entries.etymology:
1620s, "an opening of what was rolled up," from Latin evolutionem (nominative evolutio) "unrolling (of a book)," noun of action from past participle stem of evolvere "to unroll" (see evolve).

Used in medicine, mathematics, and general writing in various senses including "growth to maturity and development of an individual living thing" (1660s). Modern use in biology, of species, first attested 1832 in works of Scottish geologist Charles Lyell. Charles Darwin used the word in print once only, in the closing paragraph of "The Origin of Species" (1859), and preferred descent with modification, in part because evolution already had been used in the discarded 18c. homunculus theory of embryological development (first proposed under this name by Bonnet, 1762) and in part because it carried a sense of "progress" not present in Darwin's idea. But Victorian belief in progress prevailed (and the advantages of brevity), and Herbert Spencer and other biologists after Darwin popularized evolution.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "an opening of what was rolled up," 源自 拉丁语 evolutionem (主格 evolutio) "unrolling (of a book)," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of evolvere "to unroll" （参见 evolve). Used in medicine, mathematics, and general writing in various senses including "growth to maturity and development of an individual living thing" (1660 年代). 现代 use in biology, of species, 最早见于 1832 年 in works of 苏格兰语 geologist Charles Lyell. Charles Darwin used the word in print once only, in the closing paragraph of "The Origin of Species" (1859 年), and preferred descent with modification, in part because evolution already had been used in the discarded 18 世纪 homunculus theory of embryological development (first proposed under this name by Bonnet, 1762 年) and in part because it carried a 语义 "progress" not present in Darwin's idea. But Victorian belief in progress prevailed (and the advantages of brevity), and Herbert Spencer and other biologists after Darwin popularized evolution.

example.en: Darwin's theory of evolution changed how humans understand life on Earth.
example.zh: 达尔文的进化论改变了人类对地球生命的理解。

definitionLines: v.（使）进化，（使）演化；（使） 发展，（使）演变
entries.definition: v.（使）进化，（使）演化；（使） 发展，（使）演变
entries.etymology: 1640s, "to unfold, open out, expand," from Latin evolvere "to unroll, roll out, roll forth, unfold," especially of books; figuratively "to make clear, disclose; to produce, develop," from assimilated form of ex- "out" (see ex-) + volvere "to roll" (see volvox). Meaning "to develop by natural processes to a higher state" is from 1832. Related: Evolved; evolving.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "to unfold, open out, expand," 源自 拉丁语 evolvere "to unroll, roll out, roll forth, unfold," 尤指 of books; figuratively "to make clear, disclose; to produce, develop," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + volvere "to roll" （参见 volvox). 义为 "to develop by natural processes to a higher state" 始于 1832 年. 同源词：Evolved; evolving.

example.en: Birds are believed to have evolved from small dinosaurs over millions of years.
example.zh: 鸟类被认为是在数百万年间从小型恐龙进化而来的。

entries.etymology: "precise, rigorous, accurate," 1530s, from Latin exactus "precise, accurate, highly finished," past participle adjective from exigere "demand, require, enforce," literally "to drive or force out," also "finish, measure," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + agere "drive, lead, act" (see act (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: "precise, rigorous, accurate," 1530 年代, 源自 拉丁语 exactus "precise, accurate, highly finished," past participle 形容词 源自 exigere "demand, require, enforce," 字面义为 "to drive or force out," also "finish, measure," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + agere "drive, lead, act" （参见 act （名）).

example.en: Can you tell me the exact time the meeting is scheduled to start?
example.zh: 你能告诉我会议确切的开始时间吗？

entries.etymology: 1530s, "to pile up, accumulate," from Latin exaggeratus, past participle of exaggerare "heighten, amplify, magnify," literally "to heap, pile, load, fill," from ex- "thoroughly" (see ex-) + aggerare "heap up, accumulate," figuratively "amplify, magnify," from agger (genitive aggeris) "heap," from aggerere "bring together, carry toward," from assimilated form of ad- "to, toward" (see ad-) + gerere "carry" (see gest). Sense of "overstate" first recorded in English 1560s. Related: Exaggerated; exaggerating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "to pile up, accumulate," 源自 拉丁语 exaggeratus, 为 … 的过去分词 exaggerare "heighten, amplify, magnify," 字面义为 "to heap, pile, load, fill," 源自 ex- "thoroughly" （参见 ex-) + aggerare "heap up, accumulate," figuratively "amplify, magnify," 源自 agger (属格 aggeris) "heap," 源自 aggerere "bring together, carry toward," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 ad- "to, toward" （参见 ad-) + gerere "carry" （参见 gest). 义为 "overstate" 首见于 in English 1560 年代. 同源词：Exaggerated; exaggerating.

definitionLines: n. 考试，测验；检验，检查， 审查
entries.definition: n. 考试，测验；检验，检查， 审查
entries.etymology: late 14c., "action of testing or judging; judicial inquiry," from Old French examinacion, from Latin examinationem (nominative examinatio), noun of action from past participle stem of examinare "to weigh; to ponder, consider" (see examine). Sense of "test of knowledge" is attested from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "action of testing or judging; judicial inquiry," 源自 古法语 examinacion, 源自 拉丁语 examinationem (主格 examinatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of examinare "to weigh; to ponder, consider" （参见 examine). 义为 "test of knowledge" 见于 1610 年代.

example.en: The doctor ordered a thorough examination to find the cause of the pain.
example.zh: 医生下令进行彻底检查以找出疼痛原因。

definitionLines: vt. 检验，审查，调查；考试
entries.definition: vt. 检验，审查，调查；考试
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French examiner "interrogate, question, torture," from Latin examinare "to test or try; consider, ponder," literally "to weigh," from examen "a means of weighing or testing," probably ultimately from exigere "weigh accurately" (see exact (adj.)). Related: Examined; examining.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 examiner "interrogate, question, torture," 源自 拉丁语 examinare "to test or try; consider, ponder," 字面义为 "to weigh," 源自 examen "a means of weighing or testing," 可能 最终源自 exigere "weigh accurately" （参见 exact （形）). 同源词：Examined; examining.

example.en: The doctor examined the patient carefully before making a diagnosis.
example.zh: 医生在作出诊断前仔细检查了这位患者。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "an instance typical of a class; a model, either good or bad, action or conduct as an object of imitation; an example to be avoided; punishment as a warning," partial re-Latinization of earlier essample, asaumple (mid-13c.), from Old French essemple "sample, model, example, precedent, cautionary tale," from Latin exemplum "a sample, specimen; image, portrait; pattern, model, precedent; a warning example, one that serves as a warning," literally "that which is taken out," from eximere "take out, remove" (see exempt (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "an instance typical of a class; a model, either good or bad, action or conduct as an object of imitation; an example to be avoided; punishment as a warning," partial re-Latinization of earlier essample, asaumple (13 世纪中期), 源自 古法语 essemple "sample, model, example, precedent, cautionary tale," 源自 拉丁语 exemplum "a sample, specimen; image, portrait; pattern, model, precedent; a warning example, one that serves as a warning," 字面义为 "that which is taken out," 源自 eximere "take out, remove" （参见 exempt （形）).

example.en: Can you give a concrete example of how this policy has benefited students?
example.zh: 你能举一个具体的例子说明这项政策如何使学生受益吗？

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French exceder (14c.) "exceed, surpass, go too far," from Latin excedere "depart, go beyond, be in excess, surpass," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + cedere "go, yield" (see cede). Related: Exceeded; exceeding. Exceedingly (late 15c.) means "very greatly or very much;" excessively (mid-15c.) means "too greatly or too much."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 exceder (14 世纪) "exceed, surpass, go too far," 源自 拉丁语 excedere "depart, go beyond, be in excess, surpass," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + cedere "go, yield" （参见 cede). 同源词：Exceeded; exceeding. Exceedingly (15 世纪晚期) means "very greatly or very much;" excessively (15 世纪中期) means "too greatly or too much."

example.en: His salary now exceed what he earned five years ago by far.
example.zh: 他现在的薪水远远超过了五年前的收入。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French excellent "outstanding, excellent," from Latin excellentem (nominative excellens) "towering, prominent, distinguished, superior, surpassing," present participle of excellere "surpass, be superior; to rise, be eminent" (see excel). Related: Excellently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 excellent "outstanding, excellent," 源自 拉丁语 excellentem (主格 excellens) "towering, prominent, distinguished, superior, surpassing," 为 … 的现在分词 excellere "surpass, be superior; to rise, be eminent" （参见 excel). 同源词：Excellently.

example.en: Her excellent score on the exam earned her a full scholarship.
example.zh: 她在考试中的优秀成绩为她赢得了全额奖学金。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to receive," from Middle French excepter (12c.), from Latin exceptus, past participle of excipere "to take out, withdraw; make an exception, reserve," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + capere "to take" (see capable). Meaning "to leave out" is from 1510s. Related: Excepted; excepting. Adjectival function led to use as a preposition, conjunction (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to receive," 源自 中古法语 excepter (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 exceptus, 为 … 的过去分词 excipere "to take out, withdraw; make an exception, reserve," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + capere "to take" （参见 capable). 义为 "to leave out" 始于 1510 年代. 同源词：Excepted; excepting. Adjectival function led to use 作为 preposition, conjunction (14 世纪晚期).

entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Anglo-French excepcioun, Old French excepcion, from Latin exceptionem (nominative exceptio) "an exception, restriction, limitation; an objection," noun of action from past participle stem of excipere "to take out" (see except).

The exception that proves the rule is from law: exceptio probat regulam in casibus non exceptis, "the exception proves the rule in cases not excepted;" exception here being "action of excepting" someone or something from the rule in question, not the person or thing that is excepted. The figure of speech in to take exception is from excipere being used in Roman law as a modern attorney would say objection.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 excepcioun, 古法语 excepcion, 源自 拉丁语 exceptionem (主格 exceptio) "an exception, restriction, limitation; an objection," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of excipere "to take out" （参见 except). The exception that proves the rule 始于 law: exceptio probat regulam in casibus non exceptis, "the exception proves the rule in cases not excepted;" exception here being "action of excepting" someone or something 源自 rule in question, not the person or thing that is excepted. The figure of speech in to take exception 始于 excipere being used in Roman law 作为 modern attorney would say objection.

example.en: Every rule has at least one exception.
example.zh: 每条规则至少有一个例外。

entries.etymology: 1828, from exception + -al (1). Related: Exceptionally. Exceptionalism attested from 1864; phrase American exceptionalism by 1960. Other noun forms include exceptionalness (1868), exceptionality (1851).
entries.etymologyZh: 1828 年, 源自 exception + -al (1). 同源词：Exceptionally. Exceptionalism attested 自 1864 年起; phrase American exceptionalism 截至 1960 年. Other 名词 forms include exceptionalness (1868 年), exceptionality (1851 年).

example.en: Her performance in the competition was truly exceptional, earning a standing ovation.
example.zh: 她在比赛中的表现真的出类拔萃，赢得了全场起立鼓掌。

entries.etymology: early 15c. (implied in excerpte), from Latin excerptus, past participle of excerpere "pluck out, pick out, extract," figuratively "choose, select, gather," also "to leave out, omit," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + carpere "pluck, gather," from PIE *kerp- "to gather, pluck, harvest" (see harvest (n.)). Related: Excerpted; excerpting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (implied in excerpte), 源自 拉丁语 excerptus, 为 … 的过去分词 excerpere "pluck out, pick out, extract," figuratively "choose, select, gather," also "to leave out, omit," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + carpere "pluck, gather," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *kerp- "to gather, pluck, harvest" （参见 harvest （名）). 同源词：Excerpted; excerpting.

example.en: The professor read a brief excerpt from the novel to illustrate the writing style.
example.zh: 教授朗读了小说中的一段摘录，以说明其写作风格。

entries.definition: n. 超过；过分，过量 a. 过度的，额外的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French exces (14c.) "excess, extravagance, outrage," from Latin excessus "departure, a going beyond the bounds of reason or beyond the subject," from stem of excedere "to depart, go beyond" (see exceed). As an adjective from late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 exces (14 世纪) "excess, extravagance, outrage," 源自 拉丁语 excessus "departure, a going beyond the bounds of reason or beyond the subject," 源自 stem of excedere "to depart, go beyond" （参见 exceed). 作形容词时 源自 15 世纪晚期

example.en: Travelers are charged a fee for carrying excess baggage on the flight.
example.zh: 旅客携带超额行李乘机需缴纳费用。

definitionLines: a. 过度的，过分的，极度的
entries.definition: a. 过度的，过分的，极度的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French excessif "excessive, oppressive," from Latin excess-, past participle stem of excedere "to depart, go beyond" (see exceed). Related: Excessively; excessiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 excessif "excessive, oppressive," 源自 拉丁语 excess-, past participle stem of excedere "to depart, go beyond" （参见 exceed). 同源词：Excessively; excessiveness.

example.en: The doctor warned him against excessive alcohol consumption.
example.zh: 医生警告他不要过度饮酒。

definitionLines: vt. /n. 交换，交流；调换，兑换；
entries.definition: vt. /n. 交换，交流；调换，兑换； n. 交换台，交易所
entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of reciprocal giving and receiving," from Anglo-French eschaunge, Old French eschange (Modern French échange), from Late Latin excambium, from excambiare, from Latin ex- "out" (see ex-) + cambire "barter" (see change (v.)). Practice of merchants or lenders meeting to exchange bills of debt led to meaning "building for mercantile business" (1580s).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of reciprocal giving and receiving," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 eschaunge, 古法语 eschange (现代法语 échange), 源自 晚期拉丁语 excambium, 源自 excambiare, 源自 拉丁语 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + cambire "barter" （参见 change （动）). Practice of merchants or lenders meeting to exchange bills of debt led to 意为 "building for mercantile business" (1580 年代).

example.en: The two universities agreed to exchange students for a semester-long cultural program.
example.zh: 两所大学同意为一个为期一学期的文化项目互换学生。

definitionLines: vt. 激动，使兴奋；激发，刺激， 唤起
entries.definition: vt. 激动，使兴奋；激发，刺激， 唤起
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "to move, stir up, instigate," from Old French esciter (12c.) or directly from Latin excitare "rouse, call out, summon forth, produce," frequentative of exciere "call forth, instigate," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + ciere "set in motion, call" (see cite). Of feelings, from late 14c. Of bodily organs or tissues, from 1831. Main modern sense of "emotionally agitate" is first attested 1821.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to move, stir up, instigate," 源自 古法语 esciter (12 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 excitare "rouse, call out, summon forth, produce," 为 … 的反复体 exciere "call forth, instigate," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + ciere "set in motion, call" （参见 cite). Of feelings, 源自 14 世纪晚期 Of bodily organs or tissues, 自 1831 年起. Main modern 语义 "emotionally agitate" is 最早见于 1821 年.

example.en: The surprise announcement excited the audience more than anyone had expected.
example.zh: 这个突如其来的公告让观众比任何人预期的都更加兴奋。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "encouragement;" c. 1600, "something that tends to excite," from excite + -ment. Meaning "condition of mental and emotional agitation" is from 1846.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "encouragement;" 约 1600 年, "something that tends to excite," 源自 excite + -ment. 义为 "condition of mental and emotional agitation" 始于 1846 年.

example.en: There was a great sense of excitement as the results were announced.
example.zh: 结果宣布时，现场充满了强烈的兴奋感。

entries.etymology: 1560s, back-formation from exclamation or else from Middle French exclamer (16c.), from Latin exclamare "cry out loud, call out," from ex- "out," or else here as an intensive prefix (see ex-) + clamare "cry, shout, call" (see claim (v.)). Spelling influenced by claim. Related: Exclaimed; exclaiming.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, back-formation 源自 exclamation or else 源自 中古法语 exclamer (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 exclamare "cry out loud, call out," 源自 ex- "out," or else here 作为 intensive prefix （参见 ex-) + clamare "cry, shout, call" （参见 claim （动）). Spelling influenced by claim. 同源词：Exclaimed; exclaiming.

definitionLines: v. 拒绝接纳，把……排除在 外，排斥
entries.definition: v. 拒绝接纳，把……排除在 外，排斥
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Latin excludere "keep out, shut out, hinder," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + claudere "to close, shut" (see close (v.)). Related: Excluded; excluding.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 excludere "keep out, shut out, hinder," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + claudere "to close, shut" （参见 close （动）). 同源词：Excluded; excluding.

example.en: Women were historically excluded from voting rights in most countries.
example.zh: 历史上，女性在大多数国家被剥夺了投票权。

entries.definition: vt.原谅 n. 借口，理由
entries.etymology:
mid-13c., "attempt to clear (someone) from blame, find excuses for," from Old French escuser (12c., Modern French excuser) "apologize, make excuses; pardon, exonerate," from Latin excusare "excuse, apologize, make an excuse for, plead as an excuse; release from a charge; decline, refuse, excuse the refusal of" (source also of Spanish excusar, Italian scusare), from ex- "out, away" (see ex-) + causa "accusation, legal action" (see cause (n.)).

Sense of "forgive, pardon, accept another's plea of excuse" is from early 14c. Meaning "to obtain exemption or release from an obligation or duty; beg to be excused" is from mid-14c. in English, as is the sense "defend (someone or something) as right." Sense of "serve as justification for" is from 1530s.  Related: Excused; excusing. Excuse me as a mild apology or statement of polite disagreement is from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "attempt to clear (someone) from blame, find excuses for," 源自 古法语 escuser (12 世纪, 现代法语 excuser) "apologize, make excuses; pardon, exonerate," 源自 拉丁语 excusare "excuse, apologize, make an excuse for, plead as an excuse; release from a charge; decline, refuse, excuse the refusal of" (source also of 西班牙语 excusar, 意大利语 scusare), 源自 ex- "out, away" （参见 ex-) + causa "accusation, legal action" （参见 cause （名）). 义为 "forgive, pardon, accept another's plea of excuse" 始于 14 世纪初 义为 "to obtain exemption or release from an obligation or duty; beg to be excused" 始于 14 世纪中期 in English, as is the sense "defend (someone or something) as right." 义为 "serve as justification for" 始于 1530 年代. 同源词：Excused; excusing. Excuse me 作为 mild apology or statement of polite disagreement 始于 约 1600 年.

example.en: There is no excuse for being rude to customers under any circumstance.
example.zh: 在任何情况下，对顾客粗鲁都没有借口。

definitionLines: vt.实行，执行，实施；处死，处 决
entries.definition: vt.实行，执行，实施；处死，处 决
entries.etymology: late 14c. "to carry into effect" (transitive, mostly in law with reference to warrants, sentences, etc.), also "carry out or accomplish a course of action" (intransitive), from Old French executer (14c.), from Medieval Latin executare, from Latin execut-/exsecut-, past participle stem of exequi/exsequi "to follow out, to follow to the grave," figuratively "to follow, follow after, accompany, follow up, prosecute, carry out, enforce; execute, accomplish; punish, avenge," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + sequi "follow" (see sequel). Meaning "to inflict capital punishment" is from late 15c., from earlier legal sense "perform judgment or sentence on" (early 15c.). Related: Executed; executing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 "to carry into effect" (transitive, mostly in law with reference to warrants, sentences, etc.), also "carry out or accomplish a course of action" (intransitive), 源自 古法语 executer (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 executare, 源自 拉丁语 execut-/exsecut-, past participle stem of exequi/exsequi "to follow out, to follow to the grave," figuratively "to follow, follow after, accompany, follow up, prosecute, carry out, enforce; execute, accomplish; punish, avenge," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + sequi "follow" （参见 sequel). 义为 "to inflict capital punishment" 始于 15 世纪晚期, 源自 earlier legal sense "perform judgment or sentence on" (15 世纪初). 同源词：Executed; executing.

example.en: The manager was asked to execute the new company policy immediately.
example.zh: 经理被要求立即执行新的公司政策。

definitionLines: n. 执行，实行；完成；死刑
entries.definition: n. 执行，实行；完成；死刑
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "a carrying out, a putting into effect; enforcement; performance (of a law, statute, etc.), the carrying out (of a plan, etc.)," from Anglo-French execucioun (late 13c.), Old French execucion "a carrying out" (of an order, etc.), from Latin executionem (nominative executio) "an accomplishing," noun of action from past participle stem of exequi/exsequi "to follow out" (see execute).

Specific sense of "act of putting to death" (mid-14c.) is from Middle English legal phrases such as don execution of deth "carry out a sentence of death." Literal meaning "action of carrying something into effect" is from late 14c. John McKay, coach of the woeful Tampa Bay Buccaneers (U.S. football team), when asked by a reporter what he thought of his team's execution, replied, "I think it would be a good idea." Executor and executioner were formerly used indifferently, because both are carrying out legal orders.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a carrying out, a putting into effect; enforcement; performance (of a law, statute, etc.), the carrying out (of a plan, etc.)," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 execucioun (13 世纪晚期), 古法语 execucion "a carrying out" (of an order, etc.), 源自 拉丁语 executionem (主格 executio) "an accomplishing," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of exequi/exsequi "to follow out" （参见 execute). Specific 语义 "act of putting to death" (14 世纪中期) 始于 中古英语 legal phrases such as don execution of deth "carry out a sentence of death." Literal 意为 "action of carrying something into effect" 始于 14 世纪晚期 John McKay, coach of the woeful Tampa Bay Buccaneers (U.S. football team), when asked by a reporter what he thought of his team's execution, replied, "I think it would be a good idea." Executor and executioner were formerly used indifferently, because both are carrying out legal orders.

example.en: The team completed the execution of the new software update ahead of schedule.
example.zh: 团队提前完成了新软件更新的执行工作。

definitionLines: n. 执行者，行政官；高级官员
entries.definition: a. 执行的，实施的 n. 执行者，行政官；高级官员
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "performed, carried out;" 1640s, "of the branch of government that carries out the laws," from Middle French executif, from Latin executivus, from past participle stem of exequi "follow after; carry out, accomplish" (see execution). The noun in this sense is from 1776, as a branch of government charged with the execution and enforcement of the laws. Meaning "high-ranking businessman" is 1902 in American English; hence the adjectival sense "stylish, luxurious, costly" (1970s). Executive privilege is attested by 1805, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "performed, carried out;" 1640 年代, "of the branch of government that carries out the laws," 源自 中古法语 executif, 源自 拉丁语 executivus, 源自 past participle stem of exequi "follow after; carry out, accomplish" （参见 execution). The 名词 in this sense 始于 1776 年, 作为 branch of government charged with the execution and enforcement of the laws. 义为 "high-ranking businessman" is 1902 年 in American English; hence the adjectival sense "stylish, luxurious, costly" (1970 年代). Executive privilege is attested 截至 1805 年, American English.

example.en: As executive director, she oversees three departments and reports directly to the CEO.
example.zh: 作为执行董事，她监管三个部门并直接向首席执行官汇报。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to illustrate by examples, to instruct by (good) example," from Medieval Latin exemplificare "to illustrate," from Latin exemplum "example, pattern, model" (see example). Meaning "to serve as an example" is recorded from 1793. Related: Exemplified; exemplifies; exemplifying.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to illustrate by examples, to instruct by (good) example," 源自 中古拉丁语 exemplificare "to illustrate," 源自 拉丁语 exemplum "example, pattern, model" （参见 example). 义为 "to serve as an example" 见于 1793 年. 同源词：Exemplified; exemplifies; exemplifying.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French exempt (13c.) and directly from Latin exemptus, past participle of eximere "remove, take out, take away; free, release, deliver, make an exception of," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + emere "buy," originally "take," from PIE root *em- "to take, distribute" (source also of Latin sumere "to take, obtain, buy," Old Church Slavonic imo "to take," Lithuanian imui, Sanskrit yamati "holds, subdues"). For sense shift from "take" to "buy," compare Old English sellan "to give," source of Modern English sell "to give in exchange for money;" Hebrew laqah "he bought," originally "he took;" and colloquial English I'll take it for "I'll buy it."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 exempt (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 exemptus, 为 … 的过去分词 eximere "remove, take out, take away; free, release, deliver, make an exception of," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + emere "buy," 原义为 "take," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *em- "to take, distribute" (source also of 拉丁语 sumere "to take, obtain, buy," Old Church Slavonic imo "to take," Lithuanian imui, 梵语 yamati "holds, subdues"). For sense shift 源自 "take" to "buy," 对比 古英语 sellan "to give," source of 现代英语 sell "to give in exchange for money;" 希伯来语 laqah "he bought," 原义为 "he took;" and 口语 English I'll take it for "I'll buy it."

entries.definition: n. 练习，习题 vt. 运用，行使，实行 v./n.锻炼，训练
entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "condition of being in active operation; practice for the sake of training," from Old French exercice (13c.) "exercise, execution of power; physical or spiritual exercise," from Latin exercitium "training, exercise" (of soldiers, horsemen, etc.); "play;" in Medieval Latin also of arts, from exercitare, frequentative of exercere "keep busy, keep at work, oversee, engage busily; train, exercise; practice, follow; carry into effect; disturb, disquiet," literally "remove restraint," from ex- "off" (see ex-) + arcere "keep away, prevent, enclose," from PIE *ark- "to hold, contain, guard" (see arcane).

Original sense may have been driving farm animals to the field to plow. Meaning "physical activity for fitness, etc." first recorded in English late 14c. Also from late 14c. as "a carrying out of an action; a doing or practicing; a disciplinary task." In reference to written schoolwork from early 17c. The ending was abstracted for formations such as dancercise (1967); jazzercise (1977); and boxercise (1985).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "condition of being in active operation; practice for the sake of training," 源自 古法语 exercice (13 世纪) "exercise, execution of power; physical or spiritual exercise," 源自 拉丁语 exercitium "training, exercise" (of soldiers, horsemen, etc.); "play;" in 中古拉丁语 also of arts, 源自 exercitare, 为 … 的反复体 exercere "keep busy, keep at work, oversee, engage busily; train, exercise; practice, follow; carry into effect; disturb, disquiet," 字面义为 "remove restraint," 源自 ex- "off" （参见 ex-) + arcere "keep away, prevent, enclose," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ark- "to hold, contain, guard" （参见 arcane). Original sense may have been driving farm animals to the field to plow. 义为 "physical activity for fitness, etc." 首见于 in English 14 世纪晚期 Also 源自 14 世纪晚期 as "a carrying out of an action; a doing or practicing; a disciplinary task." In reference to written schoolwork 源自 17 世纪初 The ending was abstracted for formations such as dancercise (1967 年); jazzercise (1977 年); and boxercise (1985 年).

example.en: The physiotherapist recommended gentle exercise to strengthen the injured knee.
example.zh: 物理治疗师建议做轻柔的锻炼来强化受伤的膝盖。

definitionLines: vt. 用尽，耗尽，竭力；使衰竭， 使精疲力竭
entries.definition: vt. 用尽，耗尽，竭力；使衰竭， 使精疲力竭 n. 排气装置，废气
entries.etymology: 1530s, "to draw off or out, to use up completely," from Latin exhaustus, past participle of exhaurire "draw off, take away, use up, empty," from ex- "off" (see ex-) + haurire "to draw up" (as water), from PIE *aus- (3) "to draw water." Meaning "make weak or helpless, as by fatigue" is from 1630s. Related: Exhausted; exhausting; exhaustible.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "to draw off or out, to use up completely," 源自 拉丁语 exhaustus, 为 … 的过去分词 exhaurire "draw off, take away, use up, empty," 源自 ex- "off" （参见 ex-) + haurire "to draw up" (as water), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *aus- (3) "to draw water." 义为 "make weak or helpless, as by fatigue" 始于 1630 年代. 同源词：Exhausted; exhausting; exhaustible.

example.en: After the twelve-hour shift, the nurses were completely exhausted and could barely speak.
example.zh: 十二小时轮班结束后，护士们筋疲力尽，几乎说不出话来。

entries.definition: vt. 展览，陈列；显示 n. 展览，展品
entries.etymology: "offer or present to view," mid-15c., from Latin exhibitus, past participle of exhibere "to hold out, display, show, present, deliver" (see exhibition). Related: Exhibited; exhibiting.
entries.etymologyZh: "offer or present to view," 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 exhibitus, 为 … 的过去分词 exhibere "to hold out, display, show, present, deliver" （参见 exhibition). 同源词：Exhibited; exhibiting.

example.en: The museum will exhibit a collection of ancient Chinese paintings next month.
example.zh: 博物馆下个月将展览一批中国古代绘画作品。

definitionLines: n. 流放，充军；流犯；放逐
entries.definition: n. 流放，充军；流犯；放逐
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French essillier "exile, banish, expel, drive off" (12c.), from Late Latin exilare/exsilare, from Latin exilium/exsilium "banishment, exile; place of exile," from exul "banished person," from ex- "away" (see ex-) + PIE root *al- (2) "to wander" (source also of Greek alaomai "to wander, stray, or roam about"). In ancient times folk etymology derived the second element from Latin solum "soil." Related: Exiled; exiling.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 essillier "exile, banish, expel, drive off" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 exilare/exsilare, 源自 拉丁语 exilium/exsilium "banishment, exile; place of exile," 源自 exul "banished person," 源自 ex- "away" （参见 ex-) + 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *al- (2) "to wander" (source also of 希腊语 alaomai "to wander, stray, or roam about"). In ancient times folk etymology derived the second element 源自 拉丁语 solum "soil." 同源词：Exiled; exiling.

example.en: The dissident writer spent twenty years in exile abroad.
example.zh: 这位异见作家在海外流亡了二十年。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from French exister (17c.), from Latin existere/exsistere "to step out, stand forth, emerge, appear; exist, be" (see existence). "The late appearance of the word is remarkable" [OED]. Related: Existed; existing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 exister (17 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 existere/exsistere "to step out, stand forth, emerge, appear; exist, be" （参见 existence). "The late appearance of the word is remarkable" [OED]. 同源词：Existed; existing.

example.en: Hundreds of plant species exist only in this remote valley.
example.zh: 数百种植物物种只存在于这片偏远的山谷中。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "reality," from Old French existence, from Medieval Latin existentia/exsistentia, from existentem/exsistentem (nominative existens/exsistens) "existent," present participle of Latin existere/exsistere "stand forth, come out, emerge; appear, be visible, come to light; arise, be produced; turn into," and, as a secondary meaning, "exist, be;" from ex- "forth" (see ex-) + sistere "cause to stand" (see assist).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "reality," 源自 古法语 existence, 源自 中古拉丁语 existentia/exsistentia, 源自 existentem/exsistentem (主格 existens/exsistens) "existent," 为 … 的现在分词 拉丁语 existere/exsistere "stand forth, come out, emerge; appear, be visible, come to light; arise, be produced; turn into," and, 作为 secondary 意为, "exist, be;" 源自 ex- "forth" （参见 ex-) + sistere "cause to stand" （参见 assist).

example.en: Scientists debated the existence of life on other planets.
example.zh: 科学家们争论其他星球上是否存在生命。

entries.definition: n. 出口；太平门 vi. / n. 退出，退场
entries.etymology:
1530s (late 15c. as a Latin word in English), originally a stage direction, from Latin exit "he or she goes out," third person singular present indicative of exire "go out, go forth, depart," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + ire "to go" (see ion). Also from Latin exitus "a leaving, a going out," noun of action from exire. Meaning "a departure" (originally from the stage) is from 1580s.  Meaning "a way of departure" is from 1690s; specific meaning "door for leaving" is from 1786. The verb is c. 1600, from the noun; it ought to be left to stage directions and the clunky jargon of police reports. Related: Exited; exiting.

Exit poll attested by 1980.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代 (15 世纪晚期 作为 拉丁语 word in English), 原义为 a stage direction, 源自 拉丁语 exit "he or she goes out," third person singular present indicative of exire "go out, go forth, depart," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + ire "to go" （参见 ion). Also 源自 拉丁语 exitus "a leaving, a going out," 名词 of action 源自 exire. 义为 "a departure" (原义为 源自 stage) 始于 1580 年代. 义为 "a way of departure" 始于 1690 年代; specific 意为 "door for leaving" 始于 1786 年. The 动词 is 约 1600 年, 源自 名词; it ought to be left to stage directions and the clunky jargon of police reports. 同源词：Exited; exiting. Exit poll attested 截至 1980 年.

example.en: Passengers were directed to the nearest exit during the fire drill.
example.zh: 消防演习期间，乘客被引导到最近的出口。

definitionLines: a.外来的；异国的；异国情调的
entries.definition: a.外来的；异国的；异国情调的
entries.etymology:
1590s, "belonging to another country," from Middle French exotique (16c.) and directly from Latin exoticus, from Greek exotikos "foreign," literally "from the outside," from exo "outside" (see exo-). Sense of "unusual, strange" in English first recorded 1620s, from notion of "alien, outlandish." In reference to strip-teasers and dancing girls, it is attested by 1942, American English.

As a noun from 1640s, "anything of foreign origin," originally plants.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "belonging to another country," 源自 中古法语 exotique (16 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 exoticus, 源自 希腊语 exotikos "foreign," 字面义为 "from the outside," 源自 exo "outside" （参见 exo-). 义为 "unusual, strange" in English 首见于 1620 年代, 源自 概念 "alien, outlandish." In reference to strip-teasers and dancing girls, it is attested 截至 1942 年, American English. 作名词时 源自 1640 年代, "anything of foreign origin," 原义为 plants.

example.en: The market was filled with exotic spices and fabrics from distant lands.
example.zh: 市场里摆满了来自遥远地方的异域香料和布料。

example.en: The company plans to expand its operations into three new overseas markets next year.
example.zh: 该公司计划明年将业务扩展到三个新的海外市场。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "anything spread out;" 1640s, "act of expanding," from French expansion, from Late Latin expansionem (nominative expansio) "a spreading out," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin expandere "to spread out" (see expand).
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "anything spread out;" 1640 年代, "act of expanding," 源自 法语 expansion, 源自 晚期拉丁语 expansionem (主格 expansio) "a spreading out," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 expandere "to spread out" （参见 expand).

example.en: The rapid overseas expansion of the company required hiring hundreds of new staff abroad.
example.zh: 公司的快速海外扩张需要在海外招聘数百名新员工。

definitionLines: vt. 期待，盼望；料想，预期
entries.definition: vt. 期待，盼望；料想，预期
entries.etymology:
1550s, "wait, defer action," from Latin expectare/exspectare "await, look out for; desire, hope, long for, anticipate; look for with anticipation," from ex- "thoroughly" (see ex-) + spectare "to look," frequentative of specere "to look at" (see scope (n.1)).

Figurative sense of "anticipate, look forward to" developed in Latin and is attested in English from c. 1600. Also from c. 1600 as "regard as about to happen." Meaning "count upon (to do something), trust or rely on" is from 1630s. Used since 1817 as a euphemism for "be pregnant." In the sense "suppose, reckon, suspect," it is attested from 1640s but was regarded as a New England provincialism. Related: Expected; expecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "wait, defer action," 源自 拉丁语 expectare/exspectare "await, look out for; desire, hope, long for, anticipate; look for with anticipation," 源自 ex- "thoroughly" （参见 ex-) + spectare "to look," 为 … 的反复体 specere "to look at" （参见 scope (n.1)). Figurative 语义 "anticipate, look forward to" developed in 拉丁语 and is 见于 English 源自 约 1600 年. Also 源自 约 1600 年 as "regard as about to happen." 义为 "count upon (to do something), trust or rely on" 始于 1630 年代. Used 自 1817 年 作为 euphemism for "be pregnant." In the sense "suppose, reckon, suspect," it 见于 1640 年代 but was regarded 作为 New England provincialism. 同源词：Expected; expecting.

example.en: Organizers did not expect such a massive turnout at the charity run.
example.zh: 主办方没有预料到慈善跑步活动会有如此大规模的到场人数。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "military campaign; the act of rapidly setting forth," from Old French expedicion "an expediting, implementation; expedition, mission" (13c.) and directly from Latin expeditionem (nominative expeditio) "an enterprise against an enemy, a military campaign," noun of action from past participle stem of expedire "make ready, prepare" (see expedite). Meaning "journey for some purpose" is from 1590s. Sense by 1690s also included the body of persons on such a journey.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "military campaign; the act of rapidly setting forth," 源自 古法语 expedicion "an expediting, implementation; expedition, mission" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 expeditionem (主格 expeditio) "an enterprise against an enemy, a military campaign," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of expedire "make ready, prepare" （参见 expedite). 义为 "journey for some purpose" 始于 1590 年代. Sense by 1690 年代 also included the body of persons on such a journey.

example.en: The team prepared for months before setting off on the polar expedition.
example.zh: 团队在出发前往极地探险之前准备了数月。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "cast out," from Latin expellere "drive out, drive away," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + pellere "to drive" (see pulse (n.1)). Specific meaning "to eject from a school" is first recorded 1640s. Related: Expelled; expelling.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "cast out," 源自 拉丁语 expellere "drive out, drive away," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + pellere "to drive" （参见 pulse (n.1)). Specific 意为 "to eject from a school" is 首见于 1640 年代. 同源词：Expelled; expelling.

definitionLines: n. 支出，花费；经费，消费额
entries.definition: n. 支出，花费；经费，消费额
entries.etymology: 1769, "act of expending," from Medieval Latin expenditus, irregular past participle of Latin expendere "to weigh out; to pay out" (see expend) + -ure. Meaning "that which is expended" is from 1791. Related: Expenditures.
entries.etymologyZh: 1769 年, "act of expending," 源自 中古拉丁语 expenditus, irregular 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 expendere "to weigh out; to pay out" （参见 expend) + -ure. 义为 "that which is expended" 始于 1791 年. 同源词：Expenditures.

example.en: The government cut military expenditure to redirect funds toward education.
example.zh: 政府削减军事支出，将资金重新导向教育领域。

entries.etymology:
also formerly expence, late 14c., "action of spending or giving away, a laying out or expending," also "funds provided for expenses, expense money; damage or loss from any cause," from Anglo-French expense, Old French espense "money provided for expenses," from Late Latin expensa "disbursement, outlay, expense," noun use of neuter plural past participle of Latin expendere "to weigh out money, to pay down" (see expend).

Latin spensa also yielded Medieval Latin spe(n)sa, the sense of which specialized to "outlay for provisions," then "provisions, food" before it was borrowed into Old High German as spisa and became the root of German Speise "food," now mostly meaning prepared food, and speisen "to eat." Expense account is from 1872.
entries.etymologyZh: also formerly expence, 14 世纪晚期, "action of spending or giving away, a laying out or expending," also "funds provided for expenses, expense money; damage or loss from any cause," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 expense, 古法语 espense "money provided for expenses," 源自 晚期拉丁语 expensa "disbursement, outlay, expense," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter plural 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 expendere "to weigh out money, to pay down" （参见 expend). 拉丁语 spensa also yielded 中古拉丁语 spe(n)sa, the 语义 which specialized to "outlay for provisions," 之后 "provisions, food" before it was borrowed into 古高地德语 as spisa and became the root of 德语 Speise "food," 现在 mostly 意为 prepared food, and speisen "to eat." Expense account 始于 1872 年.

example.en: Travel expense for the conference will be reimbursed by the company.
example.zh: 参加会议的差旅费用将由公司报销。

definitionLines: a.花钱多的，高价的，昂贵的
entries.definition: a.花钱多的，高价的，昂贵的
entries.etymology: 1620s, "given to profuse expenditure," from expense (n.) + -ive. Meaning "costly, requiring profuse expenditure" is from 1630s. Earlier was expenseful (c. 1600). Expenseless was in use mid-17c.-18c., but there seems now nothing notable to which it applies, and the dictionaries label it "obsolete." Related: Expensively; expensiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "given to profuse expenditure," 源自 expense （名） + -ive. 义为 "costly, requiring profuse expenditure" 始于 1630 年代. Earlier was expenseful (约 1600 年). Expenseless was in use 17 世纪中期-18 世纪, but there seems 现在 nothing notable to which it applies, and the dictionaries label it "obsolete." 同源词：Expensively; expensiveness.

example.en: Dining at that restaurant is too expensive for students.
example.zh: 在那家餐厅用餐对学生来说太昂贵了。

definitionLines: n. 经验，感受，体验；经历
entries.definition: n. 经验，感受，体验；经历 vt. 体验，经历
entries.etymology: late 14c., "observation as the source of knowledge; actual observation; an event which has affected one," from Old French esperience "experiment, proof, experience" (13c.), from Latin experientia "a trial, proof, experiment; knowledge gained by repeated trials," from experientem (nominative experiens) "experienced, enterprising, active, industrious," present participle of experiri "to try, test," from ex- "out of" (see ex-) + peritus "experienced, tested," from PIE *per-yo-, suffixed form of root *per- (3) "to try, risk" (see peril). Meaning "state of having done something and gotten handy at it" is from late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "observation as the source of knowledge; actual observation; an event which has affected one," 源自 古法语 esperience "experiment, proof, experience" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 experientia "a trial, proof, experiment; knowledge gained by repeated trials," 源自 experientem (主格 experiens) "experienced, enterprising, active, industrious," 为 … 的现在分词 experiri "to try, test," 源自 ex- "out of" （参见 ex-) + peritus "experienced, tested," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *per-yo-, suffixed form of root *per- (3) "to try, risk" （参见 peril). 义为 "state of having done something and gotten handy at it" 始于 15 世纪晚期

example.en: Living abroad gave her the experience of navigating daily life in an unfamiliar language.
example.zh: 海外生活让她有了用陌生语言应对日常生活的亲身体验。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "action of observing or testing; an observation, test, or trial;" also "piece of evidence or empirical proof; feat of magic or sorcery," from Old French esperment "practical knowledge, cunning; enchantment, magic spell; trial, proof, example; lesson, sign, indication," from Latin experimentum "a trial, test, proof, experiment," noun of action from experiri "to test, try" (see experience (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "action of observing or testing; an observation, test, or trial;" also "piece of evidence or empirical proof; feat of magic or sorcery," 源自 古法语 esperment "practical knowledge, cunning; enchantment, magic spell; trial, proof, example; lesson, sign, indication," 源自 拉丁语 experimentum "a trial, test, proof, experiment," 名词 of action 源自 experiri "to test, try" （参见 experience （名）).

example.en: Scientists decided to experiment with a new method to improve crop yields.
example.zh: 科学家们决定用一种新方法进行试验，以提高作物产量。

entries.etymology: mid 15c., "having experience," from experiment (n.) + -al (1). Meaning "based on experiment" is from 1560s. Meaning "for the sake of experiment" is from 1792.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "having experience," 源自 experiment （名） + -al (1). 义为 "based on experiment" 始于 1560 年代. 义为 "for the sake of experiment" 始于 1792 年.

example.en: The hospital is using an experimental drug that has not yet been approved.
example.zh: 这家医院正在使用一种尚未获批的试验性药物。

definitionLines: n. 专门技术；专门知识；专家的 意见
entries.definition: n. 专门技术；专门知识；专家的 意见
entries.etymology: "quality or state of being an expert," 1868, from French expertise (16c.) "expert appraisal, expert's report," from expert (see expert). Earlier and more English was expertness (c. 1600).
entries.etymologyZh: "quality or state of being an expert," 1868 年, 源自 法语 expertise (16 世纪) "expert appraisal, expert's report," 源自 expert （参见 expert). Earlier and more English was expertness (约 1600 年).

example.en: The company hired a consultant with expertise in cybersecurity.
example.zh: 公司聘请了一位网络安全领域的专家顾问。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "to die," from Old French expirer "expire, elapse" (12c.), from Latin expirare/exspirare "breathe out, blow out, exhale; breathe one's last, die," hence, figuratively, "expire, come to an end, cease," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + spirare "to breathe" (see spirit (n.)). "Die" is the older sense in English; that of "breathe out" is first attested 1580s. Of laws, patents, treaties, etc., mid-15c. In 17c. also transitive. Related: Expired; expiring.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "to die," 源自 古法语 expirer "expire, elapse" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 expirare/exspirare "breathe out, blow out, exhale; breathe one's last, die," hence, figuratively, "expire, come to an end, cease," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + spirare "to breathe" （参见 spirit （名）). "Die" is the older sense in English; that of "breathe out" is 最早见于 1580 年代. Of laws, patents, treaties, etc., 15 世纪中期 In 17 世纪 also transitive. 同源词：Expired; expiring.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin explanare "to explain, make clear, make plain" (see explanation). Originally explane, spelling altered by influence of plain. Also see plane (v.2). In 17c., occasionally used more literally, of the unfolding of material things: Evelyn has buds that "explain into leaves" ["Sylva, or, A discourse of forest-trees, and the propagation of timber in His Majesties dominions," 1664]. Related: Explained; explaining; explains. To explain (something) away is from 1709.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 explanare "to explain, make clear, make plain" （参见 explanation). Originally explane, spelling altered by influence of plain. Also 参见 plane (v.2). In 17 世纪, occasionally used more 字面义为, of the unfolding of material things: Evelyn has buds that "explain into leaves" ["Sylva, or, A discourse of forest-trees, and the propagation of timber in His Majesties dominions," 1664 年]. 同源词：Explained; explaining; explains. To explain (something) away 始于 1709 年.

example.en: Can you explain why the experiment produced unexpected results?
example.zh: 你能解释为什么实验产生了意外结果吗？

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin explanationem (nominative explanatio) "an explanation, interpretation," noun of action from past participle stem of explanare "to make plain or clear, explain," literally "make level, flatten," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + planus "flat" (see plane (n.1)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 explanationem (主格 explanatio) "an explanation, interpretation," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of explanare "to make plain or clear, explain," 字面义为 "make level, flatten," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + planus "flat" （参见 plane (n.1)).

example.en: She gave a step-by-step explanation of how the software works.
example.zh: 她对这款软件的工作原理做了逐步的解释。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "open to the understanding, not obscure or ambiguous," from French explicite, from Latin explicitus "unobstructed," variant past participle of explicare "unfold, unravel, explain," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + plicare "to fold" (see ply (v.1)). As a euphemism for "pornographic" it dates from 1971. Related: Explicitness. "Explicitus" was written at the end of medieval books, originally short for explicitus est liber "the book is unrolled."
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "open to the understanding, not obscure or ambiguous," 源自 法语 explicite, 源自 拉丁语 explicitus "unobstructed," variant 为 … 的过去分词 explicare "unfold, unravel, explain," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + plicare "to fold" （参见 ply (v.1)). 作为 euphemism for "pornographic" it dates 自 1971 年起. 同源词：Explicitness. "Explicitus" was written at the end of medieval books, 原义为 short for explicitus est liber "the book is unrolled."

example.en: The contract must include explicit terms about payment deadlines.
example.zh: 合同必须包含关于付款期限的明确条款。

entries.etymology:
1530s (transitive), "to reject with scorn," from Latin explodere "drive out or off by clapping, hiss off, hoot off," originally theatrical, "to drive an actor off the stage by making noise," hence "drive out, reject, destroy the repute of" (a sense surviving in an exploded theory), from ex- "out" (see ex-) + plaudere "to clap the hands, applaud," which is of uncertain origin. Athenian audiences were highly demonstrative. clapping and shouting approval, stamping, hissing, and hooting for disapproval. The Romans seem to have done likewise.

English used it to mean "drive out with violence and sudden noise" (1650s), later "cause to burst suddenly and noisily" (1794). Intransitive sense of "go off with a loud noise" is from 1790, American English; figurative sense of "to burst with destructive force" is by 1882; that of "burst into sudden activity" is from 1817; of population by 1959. Related: Exploded; exploding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代 (transitive), "to reject with scorn," 源自 拉丁语 explodere "drive out or off by clapping, hiss off, hoot off," 原义为 theatrical, "to drive an actor off the stage by making noise," hence "drive out, reject, destroy the repute of" (a sense surviving in an exploded theory), 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + plaudere "to clap the hands, applaud," which is 来源存疑. Athenian audiences were highly demonstrative. clapping and shouting approval, stamping, hissing, and hooting for disapproval. The Romans seem to have done likewise. English used it to mean "drive out with violence and sudden noise" (1650 年代), later "cause to burst suddenly and noisily" (1794 年). Intransitive 语义 "go off with a loud noise" 始于 1790 年, American English; figurative 语义 "to burst with destructive force" is 截至 1882 年; that of "burst into sudden activity" 始于 1817 年; of population 截至 1959 年. 同源词：Exploded; exploding.

example.en: The gas leak caused the building to explode with a deafening sound.
example.zh: 煤气泄漏导致整栋楼发生了震耳欲聋的爆炸。

definitionLines: vt. 使用，利用；开采，开发
entries.definition: vt. 使用，利用；开采，开发
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "outcome of an action," from Old French esploit "a carrying out; achievement, result; gain, advantage" (12c., Modern French exploit), a very common word, used in senses of "action, deed, profit, achievement," from Latin explicitum "a thing settled, ended, or displayed," noun use of neuter of explicitus, past participle of explicare "unfold, unroll, disentangle" (see explicit).

Meaning "feat, achievement" is c. 1400. Sense evolution is from "unfolding" to "bringing out" to "having advantage" to "achievement." Related: Exploits.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "outcome of an action," 源自 古法语 esploit "a carrying out; achievement, result; gain, advantage" (12 世纪, 现代法语 exploit), a very common word, used in senses of "action, deed, profit, achievement," 源自 拉丁语 explicitum "a thing settled, ended, or displayed," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of explicitus, 为 … 的过去分词 explicare "unfold, unroll, disentangle" （参见 explicit). 义为 "feat, achievement" is 约 1400 年. Sense evolution 始于 "unfolding" to "bringing out" to "having advantage" to "achievement." 同源词：Exploits.

example.en: The company was accused of trying to exploit cheap labor in developing countries.
example.zh: 该公司被指控试图剥削发展中国家的廉价劳动力。

definitionLines: vt. 探险；探索，探究；勘探
entries.definition: vt. 探险；探索，探究；勘探
entries.etymology: 1580s, "to investigate, examine," a back-formation from exploration, or else from Middle French explorer (16c.), from Latin explorare "investigate, search out, examine, explore," said to be originally a hunters' term meaning "set up a loud cry," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + plorare "to weep, cry." Compare deplore. However, de Vaan notes that "the ancient explanation, ... that the verb explorare originally meant 'to scout the hunting area for game by means of shouting'" is now considered "unlikely." Second element also is explained as "to make to flow," from pluere "to flow." Meaning "to go to a country or place in quest of discoveries" is first attested 1610s. Related: Explored; exploring.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "to investigate, examine," a back-formation 源自 exploration，或else 源自 中古法语 explorer (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 explorare "investigate, search out, examine, explore," said to be 原义为 a hunters' term meaning "set up a loud cry," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + plorare "to weep, cry." Compare deplore. However, de Vaan notes that "the ancient explanation, ... that the verb explorare originally meant 'to scout the hunting area for game by means of shouting'" is now considered "unlikely." Second element also is explained as "to make to flow," from pluere "to flow." Meaning "to go to a country or place in quest of discoveries" is 最早见于 1610 年代. 同源词：Explored; exploring.

example.en: Scientists continue to explore the deep ocean, uncovering species never seen before.
example.zh: 科学家们持续探索深海，发现了前所未见的物种。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "action of driving out with violence and noise," from French explosion, from Latin explosionem (nominative explosio) "a driving off by clapping," noun of action from past participle stem of explodere "drive out by clapping" (see explode for origin and sense evolution). Meaning "a going off with violence and noise" is from 1660s. Sense of "a rapid increase or development" is first attested 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "action of driving out with violence and noise," 源自 法语 explosion, 源自 拉丁语 explosionem (主格 explosio) "a driving off by clapping," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of explodere "drive out by clapping" （参见 explode for origin and sense evolution). 义为 "a going off with violence and noise" 始于 1660 年代. 义为 "a rapid increase or development" is 最早见于 1953 年.

example.en: The explosion in the factory was heard several kilometers away.
example.zh: 工厂里的爆炸声在数公里外都能听到。

entries.definition: a. 爆炸（性）的 n. 炸药
entries.etymology: 1660s, "tending to explode," from Latin explos-, past participle stem of explodere "drive out, reject" (see explosion) + -ive. As a noun, from 1874. Related: Explosives (n.); explosively; explosiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, "tending to explode," 源自 拉丁语 explos-, past participle stem of explodere "drive out, reject" （参见 explosion) + -ive. 作名词时, 自 1874 年起. 同源词：Explosives （名）; explosively; explosiveness.

example.en: Investigators found traces of explosive material at the scene of the blast.
example.zh: 调查人员在爆炸现场发现了炸药物质的痕迹。

entries.definition: n./v. 出口，输出 n. 出口商品
entries.etymology: by 1610s, "carrying out of a place;" perhaps from late 15c., from Latin exportare "to carry out, bring out; send away, export," from ex- "away" (see ex-) + portare "carry" (see port (n.1)). The sense of "send out (commodities) from one country to another" is first recorded in English 1660s. Related: Exported; exporting; exporter.
entries.etymologyZh: by 1610 年代, "carrying out of a place;" 或源自 15 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 exportare "to carry out, bring out; send away, export," 源自 ex- "away" （参见 ex-) + portare "carry" （参见 port (n.1)). The 语义 "send out (commodities) from one country to another" is 首见于 in English 1660 年代. 同源词：Exported; exporting; exporter.

example.en: The country relies heavily on oil exports to fund its government.
example.zh: 该国严重依赖石油出口来为政府提供资金。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to leave without shelter or defense," from Old French esposer, exposer "lay open, set forth, speak one's mind, explain" (13c.), from Latin exponere "set forth, lay open, exhibit, reveal, publish" (see expound), altered by confusion with poser "to place, lay down" (see pose (v.1)). Meaning "to exhibit openly" is from 1620s; that of "to unmask" is from 1690s. Photographic sense is from 1839. Related: Exposed; exposes; exposing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to leave without shelter or defense," 源自 古法语 esposer, exposer "lay open, set forth, speak one's mind, explain" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 exponere "set forth, lay open, exhibit, reveal, publish" （参见 expound), altered by confusion with poser "to place, lay down" （参见 pose (v.1)). 义为 "to exhibit openly" 始于 1620 年代; that of "to unmask" 始于 1690 年代. Photographic sense 始于 1839 年. 同源词：Exposed; exposes; exposing.

example.en: The documentary aimed to expose the harsh conditions in the factory.
example.zh: 这部纪录片旨在揭露工厂中的恶劣条件。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "public exhibition," from expose (v.) + -ure. Sense of "situation with regard to sun or weather" is from 1660s. Photographic sense "act of exposing to light" is from 1839. Indecent exposure attested by 1825.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "public exhibition," 源自 expose （动） + -ure. 义为 "situation with regard to sun or weather" 始于 1660 年代. Photographic sense "act of exposing to light" 始于 1839 年. Indecent exposure attested 截至 1825 年.

example.en: Long-term exposure to sunlight can increase the risk of skin cancer.
example.zh: 长期暴露在阳光下会增加患皮肤癌的风险。

entries.definition: vt. 表示，表达 a.特快的，快速的 n.快车，快运
entries.etymology: late 14c., "stated explicitly, not implied, clearly made known" from Old French espres, expres (13c.), from Latin expressus "clearly presented, distinct, articulated precisely," past participle of exprimere (see express (v.)). Also late 14c. as an adverb, "specially, on purpose;" it also doubled as an adverb in Old French. An express train (1841) originally was one that ran to a certain station.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "stated explicitly, not implied, clearly made known" 源自 古法语 espres, expres (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 expressus "clearly presented, distinct, articulated precisely," 为 … 的过去分词 exprimere （参见 express （动）). Also 14 世纪晚期 作为 副词, "specially, on purpose;" it also doubled 作为 副词 in 古法语. An express train (1841 年) 原义为 was one that ran to a certain station.

example.en: She struggled to express how grateful she was for their support.
example.zh: 她努力表达自己对他们支持的感激之情。

entries.etymology: by 1945, American English, from express (adj.) + way (n.). Express highway is recorded by 1938.
