In reference to driving under the influence of alcohol, first recorded 1951 in Canadian English. Related: Impaired; impairing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, a re-Latinizing of earlier ampayre, apeyre "make worse, cause to deteriorate" (约 1300 年), 源自 古法语 empeirier "make worse" (现代法语 empirer), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *impeiorare "make worse," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in" （参见 in- (2)) + 晚期拉丁语 peiorare "make worse" （参见 pejorative). In reference to driving under the influence of alcohol, 首见于 1951 年 in Canadian English. 同源词：Impaired; impairing.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French impacient "impatient" (Modern French impatient), from Latin impatientem (nominative impatiens) "that cannot bear, intolerant, impatient," from assimilated form of in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + patiens "bearing, enduring" (see patience). Related: Impatiently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 impacient "impatient" (现代法语 impatient), 源自 拉丁语 impatientem (主格 impatiens) "that cannot bear, intolerant, impatient," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + patiens "bearing, enduring" （参见 patience). 同源词：Impatiently.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "having a commanding quality," from Old French imperial, emperial "imperial; princely, splendid; strong, powerful" (12c.), from Latin imperialis "of the empire or emperor," from imperium "empire" (see empire). Meaning "pertaining to an empire" (especially Rome's) is from late 14c.; by 1774 of Britain's. Meaning "of imposing size or excellence" is from 1731. Imperial presidency in a U.S. context traces to Arthur Schlesinger Jr.'s book on the Nixon administration (1974). Related: Imperially. The noun is from 1520s as "member of the emperor's party;" 1670s as the name of gold coins issued by various imperial authorities.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "having a commanding quality," 源自 古法语 imperial, emperial "imperial; princely, splendid; strong, powerful" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 imperialis "of the empire or emperor," 源自 imperium "empire" （参见 empire). 义为 "pertaining to an empire" (尤指 Rome's) is from late 14c.; by 1774 of Britain's. 义为 "of imposing size or excellence" 始于 1731 年. Imperial presidency in a U.S. context traces to Arthur Schlesinger Jr.'s book on the Nixon administration (1974). Related: Imperially. The noun is from 1520s as "member of the emperor's party;" 1670 年代 as the name of gold coins issued by various imperial authorities.

example.en: The imperial palace is now open to tourists from around the world.
example.zh: 这座皇家宫殿现已向世界各地的游客开放。

entries.etymology: 1826, "advocacy of empire, devotion to imperial interests," originally in a Napoleonic context, also of Rome and of British foreign policy; from imperial + -ism. At times in British usage (and briefly in U.S.) with a neutral or positive sense relating to national interests or the spread of the benefits of Western civilization, but from the begining usually more or less a term of reproach. General sense of "one country's rule over another," first recorded 1878. Picked up disparagingly in Communist jargon by 1918.
entries.etymologyZh: 1826 年, "advocacy of empire, devotion to imperial interests," 原义为 in a Napoleonic context, also of Rome and of British foreign policy; 源自 imperial + -ism. At times in British usage (and briefly in U.S.) with a neutral or positive sense relating to national interests or the spread of the benefits of Western civilization, but 源自 begining 通常 more or less a term of reproach. General 语义 "one country's rule over another," 首见于 1878 年. Picked up disparagingly in Communist jargon 截至 1918 年.

entries.definition: n. 帝国主义者 a. 帝国主义的
entries.etymology: c. 1600, "an adherent of an emperor or the imperial cause," such as the emperor of Germany (in the Thirty Years War), France, China, etc., probably modeled on French impérialiste (early 16c.); from imperial + -ist. The shift in meaning to "advocate of imperialism" (1893) came via the British Empire, which involved a worldwide colonial system. See imperialism. As a term of abuse in communist circles, attested by 1918. As an adjective by 1816.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "an adherent of an emperor or the imperial cause," such as the emperor of Germany (in the Thirty Years War), France, China, etc., 可能 modeled on 法语 impérialiste (16 世纪初); 源自 imperial + -ist. The shift in 意为 to "advocate of imperialism" (1893 年) came 经由 the British Empire, which involved a worldwide colonial system. See imperialism. 作为 term of abuse in communist circles, attested 截至 1918 年. 作形容词时 截至 1816 年.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "supplementary payment, amount needed to complete repayment," from Late Latin implementem "a filling up" (as with provisions), from Latin implere "to fill, fill up, make full; fatten; fulfill, satisfy," from assimilated form of in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + plere "to fill" (see pleio-). Sense of "workman's tool, utensil of a trade, things necessary to do work" is 1530s. The underlying connection of the senses is "whatever may supply a want, that which fills up a need." Related: Implemental; implements.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "supplementary payment, amount needed to complete repayment," 源自 晚期拉丁语 implementem "a filling up" (as with provisions), 源自 拉丁语 implere "to fill, fill up, make full; fatten; fulfill, satisfy," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + plere "to fill" （参见 pleio-). 义为 "workman's tool, utensil of a trade, things necessary to do work" is 1530 年代. The underlying connection of the senses is "whatever may supply a want, that which fills up a need." 同源词：Implemental; implements.

example.en: The city council voted to implement stricter recycling regulations starting next January.
example.zh: 市议会投票决定从明年一月起实施更严格的垃圾回收法规。

definitionLines: n. 暗示，暗指，含义；牵连
entries.definition: n. 暗示，暗指，含义；牵连
entries.etymology: early 15c., "action of entangling," from Latin implicationem (nominative implicatio) "an interweaving, an entanglement," noun of state from past participle stem of implicare "involve, entangle; embrace; connect closely, associate," from assimilated form of in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + plicare "to fold" (see ply (v.1)). Meaning "that which is implied (but not expressed), inference drawn from what is observed" is from 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "action of entangling," 源自 拉丁语 implicationem (主格 implicatio) "an interweaving, an entanglement," 名词 of state 源自 past participle stem of implicare "involve, entangle; embrace; connect closely, associate," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + plicare "to fold" （参见 ply (v.1)). 义为 "that which is implied (but not expressed), inference drawn from what is observed" 始于 1550 年代.

example.en: The implication of her silence was that she disagreed.
example.zh: 她沉默的言外之意是她不同意。

definitionLines: a. 暗示的；盲从的；含蓄的
entries.definition: a. 暗示的；盲从的；含蓄的
entries.etymology: 1590s, "implied, resting on inference," from Middle French implicite and directly from Latin implicitus, later variant of implicatus "entangled, confused, involved," past participle of implicare "entangle, involve" (see implication). From c. 1600 as "resulting from perfect confidence (in authority), unquestioning" (especially of faith).
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "implied, resting on inference," 源自 中古法语 implicite and 直接源自 拉丁语 implicitus, later 为 … 的变体 implicatus "entangled, confused, involved," 为 … 的过去分词 implicare "entangle, involve" （参见 implication). From 约 1600 年 as "resulting from perfect confidence (in authority), unquestioning" (尤指 of faith).

entries.etymology: late 14c., implien, emplien "to enfold, enwrap, entangle" (the classical Latin sense), from Old French emplier, from Latin implicare "involve, enfold, entangle" (see implication). Meaning "to involve something unstated as a logical consequence" first recorded c. 1400; that of "to hint at" is from 1580s. Related: Implied; implying. The distinction between imply and infer is in "What do you imply by that remark?" but, "What am I to infer from that remark?" Or, as Century Dictionary puts it, "An action implies ability or preparation, but involves consequences."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, implien, emplien "to enfold, enwrap, entangle" (the classical 拉丁语 sense), 源自 古法语 emplier, 源自 拉丁语 implicare "involve, enfold, entangle" （参见 implication). 义为 "to involve something unstated as a logical consequence" 首见于 约 1400 年; that of "to hint at" 始于 1580 年代. 同源词：Implied; implying. The distinction between imply and infer is in "What do you imply by that remark?" but, "What am I to infer from that remark?" Or, as Century Dictionary puts it, "An action implies ability or preparation, but involves consequences."

example.en: Her silence seemed to imply that she disagreed with the plan.
example.zh: 她的沉默似乎暗示她不同意这个计划。

entries.definition: vt./n.输人，进口 n. （pl.）进口商品，进口物质
entries.etymology: early 15c., "signify, show, bear or convey in meaning," from Latin importare "bring in, convey, bring in from abroad," from assimilated form of in- "into, in" (see in- (2)) + portare "to carry" (see port (n.1)). In English, the sense of "bring from another state or land," especially "bring in goods from abroad" first recorded 1540s. As "be important" from 1580s. Related: Imported; importing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "signify, show, bear or convey in meaning," 源自 拉丁语 importare "bring in, convey, bring in from abroad," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in" （参见 in- (2)) + portare "to carry" （参见 port (n.1)). In English, the 语义 "bring from another state or land," 尤指 "bring in goods from abroad" 首见于 1540 年代. As "be important" 源自 1580 年代. 同源词：Imported; importing.

example.en: The country plans to import more oil from the Middle East next year.
example.zh: 该国计划明年从中东进口更多石油。

entries.etymology: "the quality of having consequence," c. 1500, from Middle French importance or directly from Medieval Latin importantia "importance," from importantem "important" (see important).
entries.etymologyZh: "the quality of having consequence," 约 1500 年, 源自 中古法语 importance or 直接源自 中古拉丁语 importantia "importance," 源自 importantem "important" （参见 important).

example.en: The report stressed the importance of daily exercise for preventing chronic disease.
example.zh: 报告强调了每日锻炼对预防慢性病的重要性。

definitionLines: a.重要的，重大的；有地位的， 显要的
entries.definition: a.重要的，重大的；有地位的， 显要的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French important and directly from Medieval Latin importantem (nominative importans) "important, momentous," present-participle adjective from importare "be significant in," from Latin importare "bring in" (see import (v.)). Meaning "pretentious, pompous" is from 1713. Related: Importantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 important and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 importantem (主格 importans) "important, momentous," present-participle 形容词 源自 importare "be significant in," 源自 拉丁语 importare "bring in" （参见 import （动）). 义为 "pretentious, pompous" 始于 1713 年. 同源词：Importantly.

example.en: It is important to read the safety instructions before operating heavy machinery.
example.zh: 在操作重型机械之前阅读安全说明是很重要的。

definitionLines: vt.（on）征税，强加；以……欺 骗；利用，施影响
entries.definition: vt.（on）征税，强加；以……欺 骗；利用，施影响
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to lay (a crime, duty, obligation, etc.) to the account of," from Old French imposer "put, place; impute, charge, accuse" (c. 1300), from assimilated form of in- "into, in" (see in- (2)) + poser "put, place" (see pose (v.1)). From c. 1500 as "apply authoritatively." Sense of "lay on as a burden, inflict by force or authority" first recorded 1580s. Related: Imposed; imposer; imposing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to lay (a crime, duty, obligation, etc.) to the account of," 源自 古法语 imposer "put, place; impute, charge, accuse" (约 1300 年), 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in" （参见 in- (2)) + poser "put, place" （参见 pose (v.1)). From 约 1500 年 as "apply authoritatively." 义为 "lay on as a burden, inflict by force or authority" 首见于 1580 年代. 同源词：Imposed; imposer; imposing.

example.en: The new law will impose heavy duties on all imported electronics.
example.zh: 新法律将对所有进口电子产品征收重税。

definitionLines: a. 不可能的，做不到的
entries.definition: a. 不可能的，做不到的
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French impossible (14c.), from Latin impossibilis "not possible," from assimilated form of in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + possibilis (see possible). Weakened sense of "unable to be accomplished or tolerated" is from mid-19c. Related: Impossibly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 impossible (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 impossibilis "not possible," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + possibilis （参见 possible). Weakened 语义 "unable to be accomplished or tolerated" 始于 19 世纪中期 同源词：Impossibly.

example.en: It seemed impossible to finish the entire project within a single week.
example.zh: 在一周内完成整个项目似乎是不可能的。

definitionLines: a. 不切实际的，不现实的；不能 实行的
entries.definition: a. 不切实际的，不现实的；不能 实行的
entries.etymology: 1823, from assimilated form of in- (1) "not, opposite of" + practical (adj.). Impracticable in the same sense dates from 1670s; unpractical is rare. Related: Impractically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1823 年, 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- (1) "not, opposite of" + practical （形）. Impracticable in the same sense dates 源自 1670 年代; unpractical is rare. 同源词：Impractically.

entries.etymology: "act of impressing" (1590s), also "characteristic mark" (1580s), from impress (v.1). From 1620s as "badge worn by nobility or their retainers," from Italian impresa; earlier in English in this sense as impreso, imprese (1580s).
entries.etymologyZh: "act of impressing" (1590 年代), also "characteristic mark" (1580 年代), 源自 impress (v.1). From 1620 年代 as "badge worn by nobility or their retainers," 源自 意大利语 impresa; earlier in English in this sense as impreso, imprese (1580 年代).

example.en: Her confident speech managed to impress the entire audience.
example.zh: 她自信的演讲成功地给全场观众留下了深刻印象。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "mark produced by pressure," also "image produced in the mind or emotions by something external," from Old French impression "print, stamp; a pressing on the mind" (13c.), from Latin impressionem (nominative impressio) "a pressing into, onset, attack," figuratively "a perception, mental impression," literally "a pressing into," from imprimere "press into or upon" (see impress (v.1)).

Meaning "act or process of making a mark upon the surface by pressing" is from early 15c.. Meaning "copy made by pressure from type or an engraving" is from 1550s; that of "printing of a number of copies, aggregate of copies printed at one time" is from 1570s. Meaning "belief, vague notion" (as in under the impression) is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "mark produced by pressure," also "image produced in the mind or emotions by something external," 源自 古法语 impression "print, stamp; a pressing on the mind" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 impressionem (主格 impressio) "a pressing into, onset, attack," figuratively "a perception, mental impression," 字面义为 "a pressing into," 源自 imprimere "press into or upon" （参见 impress (v.1)). 义为 "act or process of making a mark upon the surface by pressing" 始于 15 世纪初. 义为 "copy made by pressure from type or an engraving" 始于 1550 年代; that of "printing of a number of copies, aggregate of copies printed at one time" 始于 1570 年代. 义为 "belief, vague notion" (as in under the impression) 始于 1610 年代.

example.en: The new employee made a strong impression on her first day.
example.zh: 这位新员工在第一天就留下了深刻的印象。

definitionLines: a.给人印象深刻的，感人的
entries.definition: a.给人印象深刻的，感人的
entries.etymology: 1590s, "capable of being easily impressed" (a sense now rare or obsolete), from impress (v.1) + -ive. Meaning "capable of making an impression on the mind or senses, tending to excite attention and feeling" is from 1775. Related: Impressively; impressiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "capable of being easily impressed" (a sense 今罕用 or 已废), 源自 impress (v.1) + -ive. 义为 "capable of making an impression on the mind or senses, tending to excite attention and feeling" 始于 1775 年. 同源词：Impressively; impressiveness.

example.en: Her performance at the concert was truly impressive.
example.zh: 她在音乐会上的表演真的令人印象深刻。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French emprisoner "imprison; be in prison" (12c.), from assimilated form of in- "in" (see in- (2)) + prison (see prison). Formerly also emprison. Related: Imprisoned; imprisoning.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 emprisoner "imprison; be in prison" (12 世纪), 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + prison （参见 prison). Formerly also emprison. 同源词：Imprisoned; imprisoning.

entries.definition: ad. 即席地 a. 即席的
entries.etymology: 1660s, from French impromptu (1650s), from Latin in promptu "in readiness," from assimilated form of in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + promptu, ablative of promptus "ready, prepared; set forth, brought forward," from past participle of promere "to bring out," from pro- "before, forward, for" (see pro-) + emere "to obtain" (see exempt (adj.)). From 1764 as an adjective; as a noun from 1680s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 法语 impromptu (1650 年代), 源自 拉丁语 in promptu "in readiness," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + promptu, ablative of promptus "ready, prepared; set forth, brought forward," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 promere "to bring out," 源自 pro- "before, forward, for" （参见 pro-) + emere "to obtain" （参见 exempt （形）). From 1764 年 作形容词时; 作名词时 源自 1680 年代.

definitionLines: n. 改进，改良，增进；改进措施
entries.definition: n. 改进，改良，增进；改进措施
entries.etymology: mid-15c., enprowment "profitable use, management of something for profit," from Anglo-French emprowement, from emprouwer "turn to profit" (see improve). Meaning "betterment; act of making better, amelioration" is from 1640s. Meaning "production of something better, something better (than something else)" is from 1712. Meaning "buildings, etc. on a piece of property" is from 1773. Related: Improvements.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, enprowment "profitable use, management of something for profit," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 emprowement, 源自 emprouwer "turn to profit" （参见 improve). 义为 "betterment; act of making better, amelioration" 始于 1640 年代. 义为 "production of something better, something better (than something else)" 始于 1712 年. 义为 "buildings, etc. on a piece of property" 始于 1773 年. 同源词：Improvements.

example.en: There has been a noticeable improvement in her writing skills this semester.
example.zh: 这学期她的写作能力有了明显的提高。

definitionLines: n. 冲动；脉冲；刺激；推动力
entries.definition: n. 冲动；脉冲；刺激；推动力
entries.etymology: early 15c., "an act of impelling, a thrust, push," from Latin impulsus "a push against, pressure, shock," figuratively "incitement, instigation," past participle of impellere "to strike against, push against" (see impel). Meaning "a stimulus in the mind to action, arising from some state or feeling" is first recorded 1640s. As an adjective, in reference to purchases made on impulse, 1955 (in impulse buyer).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "an act of impelling, a thrust, push," 源自 拉丁语 impulsus "a push against, pressure, shock," figuratively "incitement, instigation," 为 … 的过去分词 impellere "to strike against, push against" （参见 impel). 义为 "a stimulus in the mind to action, arising from some state or feeling" is 首见于 1640 年代. 作形容词时, in reference to purchases made on impulse, 1955 年 (in impulse buyer).

example.en: He bought the expensive jacket on impulse and regretted it later.
example.zh: 他一时冲动买下了那件昂贵的夹克，事后后悔不已。

definitionLines: prep.［表示地点、场所、位置］ 在……里，在……中；［表 示时间］在…••期间， 在…•••以后；［表示工具、 方式］以…•…方式；［表示 状态、情况］在…••…•中，处 于；［表示范围、领域、方 向］在……之内，在…… 方面
ad. 向里，向内；在家里，屋里
entries.definition: prep.［表示地点、场所、位置］ 在……里，在……中；［表 示时间］在…••期间， 在…•••以后；［表示工具、 方式］以…•…方式；［表示 状态、情况］在…••…•中，处 于；［表示范围、领域、方 向］在……之内，在…… 方面 ad. 向里，向内；在家里，屋里
entries.etymology: "that is within, internal," 1590s, from in (adv.). Sense of "holding power" (the in party) first recorded c. 1600; that of "exclusive" (the in-crowd, an in-joke) is from 1907 (in-group); that of "stylish, fashionable" (the in thing) is from 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: "that is within, internal," 1590 年代, 源自 in （副）. 义为 "holding power" (the in party) 首见于 约 1600 年; that of "exclusive" (the in-crowd, an in-joke) 始于 1907 年 (in-group); that of "stylish, fashionable" (the in thing) 始于 1960 年.

definitionLines: vt. 举行开幕典礼；举行就职 典礼
entries.definition: vt. 举行开幕典礼；举行就职 典礼
entries.etymology: "induct into office by formal ceremony," c. 1600, a back-formation from inauguration (q.v.) and also from Latin inauguratus, past participle of inaugurare. The etymological sense is "make a formal beginning or induction into office with suitable ceremonies" (which in ancient Rome included especially the taking of auguries). Related: Inaugurated; inaugurating; inaugurator.
entries.etymologyZh: "induct into office by formal ceremony," 约 1600 年, a back-formation 源自 inauguration (q.v.) and 亦源自 拉丁语 inauguratus, 为 … 的过去分词 inaugurare. The etymological sense is "make a formal beginning or induction into office with suitable ceremonies" (which in ancient Rome included 尤指 the taking of auguries). 同源词：Inaugurated; inaugurating; inaugurator.

entries.etymology: Old English inboren "native to a place, indigenous, aboriginal," from in (prep.) "within" + boren "brought forth" (see born). Of personal qualities, "innate, implanted by nature," 1510s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 inboren "native to a place, indigenous, aboriginal," 源自 in （介） "within" + boren "brought forth" （参见 born). Of personal qualities, "innate, implanted by nature," 1510 年代.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "that which moves the mind or stirs the passion," from Late Latin incentivum, noun use of neuter of Latin adjective incentivus "setting the tune" (in Late Latin "inciting"), from past participle stem of incinere "strike up," from in- "in, into" (see in- (2)) + canere "to sing" (see chant (v.)). The sense apparently was influenced in Late Latin by association with incendere "to kindle." (Milton uses the adjective to mean "setting fire, incendiary.") Meaning "rewards meant to encourage harder work" is from 1948, short for incentive payment, etc. (see incentive (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "that which moves the mind or stirs the passion," 源自 晚期拉丁语 incentivum, 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of 拉丁语 形容词 incentivus "setting the tune" (in 晚期拉丁语 "inciting"), 源自 past participle stem of incinere "strike up," 源自 in- "in, into" （参见 in- (2)) + canere "to sing" （参见 chant （动）). The sense 似乎 was influenced in 晚期拉丁语 by association with incendere "to kindle." (Milton uses the 形容词 to mean "setting fire, incendiary.") 义为 "rewards meant to encourage harder work" 始于 1948 年, short for incentive payment, etc. （参见 incentive （形）).

example.en: The cash bonus acted as a powerful incentive for the sales team to exceed their targets.
example.zh: 现金奖励对销售团队超额完成指标是一种强有力的激励。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "move little by little" (intrans.), from inch (n.1). Meaning "drive or force by small degrees" (trans.) is from 1660s. Related: Inched; inching.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "move little by little" (intrans.), 源自 inch (n.1). 义为 "drive or force by small degrees" (trans.) 始于 1660 年代. 同源词：Inched; inching.

definitionLines: n. 事件，政治事件，事变
entries.definition: n. 事件，政治事件，事变
entries.etymology: early 15c., "something which occurs casually in connection with something else," from Old French incident (13c.), and directly from Latin incidentem (nominative incidens), present participle of incidere "to fall in, fall, find the way; light upon, fall in with; fall upon, occur; happen, befall," from in- "on" (see in- (2)) + -cidere, comb. form of cadere "to fall" (see case (n.1)). Broader sense of "an occurrence viewed as a separate circumstance" is from mid-15c. Euphemistic meaning "event that might trigger a crisis or political unrest" first attested 1913.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "something which occurs casually in connection with something else," 源自 古法语 incident (13 世纪), and 直接源自 拉丁语 incidentem (主格 incidens), 为 … 的现在分词 incidere "to fall in, fall, find the way; light upon, fall in with; fall upon, occur; happen, befall," 源自 in- "on" （参见 in- (2)) + -cidere, comb. form of cadere "to fall" （参见 case (n.1)). Broader 语义 "an occurrence viewed as a separate circumstance" 始于 15 世纪中期 Euphemistic 意为 "event that might trigger a crisis or political unrest" 最早见于 1913 年.

example.en: The police investigated the violent incident that occurred near the train station.
example.zh: 警方对火车站附近发生的暴力事件展开了调查。

definitionLines: v.使认，使倾向；使倾斜，使 偏向
entries.definition: v.使认，使倾向；使倾斜，使 偏向 n. 斜坡，斜面
entries.etymology: in early use also encline, c. 1300, "to bend or bow toward," from Old French encliner "to lean, bend, bow down," from Latin inclinare "to cause to lean; bend, incline, turn, divert," from in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + clinare "to bend," from PIE *klei-n-, suffixed form of *klei- "to lean" (see lean (v.)). Metaphoric sense of "have a mental disposition toward" is early 15c. in English (but existed in classical Latin). Related: Inclined; inclining.
entries.etymologyZh: in early use also encline, 约 1300 年, "to bend or bow toward," 源自 古法语 encliner "to lean, bend, bow down," 源自 拉丁语 inclinare "to cause to lean; bend, incline, turn, divert," 源自 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + clinare "to bend," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *klei-n-, suffixed form of *klei- "to lean" （参见 lean （动）). Metaphoric 语义 "have a mental disposition toward" is 15 世纪初 in English (but existed in classical 拉丁语). 同源词：Inclined; inclining.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to shut (someone or something) in materially, enclose, imprison, confine," also "to have (something) as a constituent part," from Latin includere "to shut in, enclose, imprison, insert," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + claudere "to shut" (see close (v.)). The alleged Sam Goldwyn-ism "Include me out" is attested from 1937. Related: Included; including.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to shut (someone or something) in materially, enclose, imprison, confine," also "to have (something) as a constituent part," 源自 拉丁语 includere "to shut in, enclose, imprison, insert," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + claudere "to shut" （参见 close （动）). The alleged Sam Goldwyn-ism "Include me out" 见于 1937 年. 同源词：Included; including.

example.en: Please note that the price does not include the cost of insurance.
example.zh: 请注意，此价格不包含保险费用。

entries.etymology: "including the stated limits in the number or sum," mid-15c., from Medieval Latin inclusivus, from Latin inclus-, past participle stem of includere "to shut in, enclose" (see include).
entries.etymologyZh: "including the stated limits in the number or sum," 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古拉丁语 inclusivus, 源自 拉丁语 inclus-, past participle stem of includere "to shut in, enclose" （参见 include).

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "entrance, arrival," literally "a coming in;" see in (adv.) + come (v.). Perhaps a noun use of the late Old English verb incuman "come in, enter." Meaning "money made through business or labor" (i.e., "that which 'comes in' as payment for work or business") first recorded c. 1600. Compare German einkommen "income," Swedish inkomst. Income tax is from 1790, introduced in Britain during the Napoleonic wars, re-introduced 1842; in U.S. levied by the federal government 1861-72, authorized on a national level in 1913.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "entrance, arrival," 字面义为 "a coming in;" 参见 in （副） + come （动）. Perhaps a 为 … 的名词用法 the late 古英语 动词 incuman "come in, enter." 义为 "money made through business or labor" (i.e., "that which 'comes in' as payment for work or business") 首见于 约 1600 年. 对比 德语 einkommen "income," Swedish inkomst. Income tax 始于 1790 年, introduced in Britain during the Napoleonic wars, re-introduced 1842 年; in U.S. levied by the federal government 1861 年-72, authorized on a national level 于 1913 年.

example.en: The family relies on a single income to cover all their monthly expenses.
example.zh: 这家人靠单一收入来源支付所有每月开支。

entries.etymology: "that cannot coexist or be conjoined," mid-15c., from Medieval Latin incompatibilis, from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + compatibilis (see compatible). Originally of benefices, "incapable of being held together;" sense of "mutually intolerant" is from 1590s. Related: Incompatibly.
entries.etymologyZh: "that cannot coexist or be conjoined," 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古拉丁语 incompatibilis, 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + compatibilis （参见 compatible). Originally of benefices, "incapable of being held together;" 语义 "mutually intolerant" 始于 1590 年代. 同源词：Incompatibly.

entries.definition: vt. 包含，吸收；体现 vi. 合并；组成一体
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to put (something) into the body or substance of (something else), blend; absorb, eat," also "solidify, harden," often in medical writing, from Late Latin incorporatus, past participle of incorporare "unite into one body, embody, include," from Latin in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + verb from corpus (genitive corporis) "body" (see corporeal).

Meaning "to legally form a body politic with perpetual succession and power to act as one person, establish as a legal corporation" is from mid-15c. Intransitive sense of "unite with another body so as to become part of it" is from 1590s. Related: Incorporated; incorporating.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to put (something) into the body or substance of (something else), blend; absorb, eat," also "solidify, harden," 常 in medical writing, 源自 晚期拉丁语 incorporatus, 为 … 的过去分词 incorporare "unite into one body, embody, include," 源自 拉丁语 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + 动词 源自 corpus (属格 corporis) "body" （参见 corporeal). 义为 "to legally form a body politic with perpetual succession and power to act as one person, establish as a legal corporation" 始于 15 世纪中期 Intransitive 语义 "unite with another body so as to become part of it" 始于 1590 年代. 同源词：Incorporated; incorporating.

example.en: The new policy will incorporate environmental standards into all building codes.
example.zh: 新政策将把环境标准纳入所有建筑法规之中。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., encresen, "become greater in size or number" (intransitive); late 14c., "cause to grow, enlarge" (transitive), from Anglo-French encress-, Old French encreiss-, present participle stem of encreistre, from Latin increscere "to increase, to grow upon, grow over, swell, grow into," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + crescere "to grow" (see crescent). Modern English restored the Latin spelling 16c. Related: Increased; increasing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, encresen, "become greater in size or number" (intransitive); 14 世纪晚期, "cause to grow, enlarge" (transitive), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 encress-, 古法语 encreiss-, present participle stem of encreistre, 源自 拉丁语 increscere "to increase, to grow upon, grow over, swell, grow into," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + crescere "to grow" （参见 crescent). 现代英语 restored the 拉丁语 spelling 16 世纪 同源词：Increased; increasing.

example.en: The number of electric vehicles on the road continues to increase each year.
example.zh: 道路上的电动车数量每年持续增加。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from increasing (see increase (v.)) + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 increasing （参见 increase （动）) + -ly (2).

example.en: Young people are increasingly choosing to work remotely rather than commute daily.
example.zh: 年轻人越来越多地选择远程工作而非每天通勤。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "unbelievable, surpassing belief as to what is possible," from Latin incredibilis "not to be believed, extraordinary," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + credibilis "worthy of belief" (see credible). Used c. 1400 in a now-extinct sense of "unbelieving, incredulous." Related: Incredibly; incredibility.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "unbelievable, surpassing belief as to what is possible," 源自 拉丁语 incredibilis "not to be believed, extraordinary," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + credibilis "worthy of belief" （参见 credible). Used 约 1400 年 in a 现在-extinct 语义 "unbelieving, incredulous." 同源词：Incredibly; incredibility.

example.en: It is incredible how quickly technology has changed our daily lives.
example.zh: 技术改变我们日常生活的速度快得令人难以置信。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "bring (an undesirable consequence) upon oneself;" mid-15c. as "become liable for (payment or expenses)," from Anglo-French encurir, Old French encorir "to run, flee; commit, contract, incur" (Modern French encourir), from Latin incurrere "run into or against, rush at, make an attack;" figuratively, "to befall, happen, occur to," from in- "upon" (see in- (2)) + currere "to run" (see current (adj.)). Related: Incurred; incurring.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "bring (an undesirable consequence) upon oneself;" 15 世纪中期 as "become liable for (payment or expenses)," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 encurir, 古法语 encorir "to run, flee; commit, contract, incur" (现代法语 encourir), 源自 拉丁语 incurrere "run into or against, rush at, make an attack;" figuratively, "to befall, happen, occur to," 源自 in- "upon" （参见 in- (2)) + currere "to run" （参见 current （形）). 同源词：Incurred; incurring.

entries.etymology: c. 1600, a contraction into one word of the prepositional phrase in dede "in fact, in truth" (early 14c.), from Old English dæd "a doing, act, action, event"  (see deed (n.)). As an interjection, 1590s; as an expression of surprise or disgust, 1834. Emphatic form yes (or no) indeedy attested from 1856, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, a contraction into one word of the prepositional phrase in dede "in fact, in truth" (14 世纪初), 源自 古英语 dæd "a doing, act, action, event" （参见 deed （名）). 作为 interjection, 1590 年代; 作为 expression of surprise or disgust, 1834 年. Emphatic form yes (or no) indeedy attested 自 1856 年起, American English.

entries.etymology:
1630s, "fact of not depending on others or another, self-support and self-government;" see independent + -ence. Earlier in same sense was independency (1610s). U.S. Independence Day (July 4, commemorating events of 1776) is recorded under that name by 1791.

An Old English word for it was selfdom, with self + dom "law," but in form this is closer to privilege (n.). The two concepts are not always distinguishable.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "fact of not depending on others or another, self-support and self-government;" 参见 independent + -ence. Earlier in same sense was independency (1610 年代). U.S. Independence Day (July 4, commemorating events of 1776 年) is recorded under that name 截至 1791 年. An 古英语 word for it was selfdom, with self + dom "law," but in form this is closer to privilege （名）. The two concepts are not always distinguishable.

example.en: The country celebrated the anniversary of its independence with a grand parade and fireworks display.
example.zh: 该国以盛大的游行和烟火表演庆祝独立周年。

definitionLines: a. 独立的，自立的，自主的
entries.definition: a. 独立的，自立的，自主的
entries.etymology:
1610s, "not dependent on something else," from in- (1) "not, opposite of" + dependent. French independant is attested from c. 1600; Italian independente from 1590s. In English originally of churches, nations; in reference to persons from 1660s. Meaning "able to live well without labor" is from 1732. Meaning "unbiased, set up so as to be unaffected by outside influence" is from 1790. Related: Independently.

As a noun, from 1640s as "member of an independent congregational church, English Congregationalist." It is attested from 1670s as "one who acts according to his own will" and 1808 in the specific sense "person not acting as part of a political party."
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "not dependent on something else," 源自 in- (1) "not, opposite of" + dependent. 法语 independant 见于 约 1600 年; 意大利语 independente 源自 1590 年代. In English 原义为 of churches, nations; in reference to persons 源自 1660 年代. 义为 "able to live well without labor" 始于 1732 年. 义为 "unbiased, set up so as to be unaffected by outside influence" 始于 1790 年. 同源词：Independently. 作名词时, 源自 1640 年代 as "member of an independent congregational church, English Congregationalist." It 见于 1670 年代 as "one who acts according to his own will" and 1808 年 in the specific sense "person not acting as part of a political party."

example.en: After moving abroad alone, she learned to be fully independent and manage her own finances.
example.zh: 只身移居海外后，她学会了完全独立，自己打理个人财务。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "the forefinger," from Latin index (genitive indicis) "one who points out, discloser, discoverer, informer; forefinger (because used in pointing); pointer, sign; title, inscription, list," literally "anything which points out," from indicare "to point out" (see indication). Related: Indexical.

Obsolete in English in its original sense (index finger is recorded from 1768). Meaning "alphabetical list of a book's contents with directions where in the text to find them" is from late 16c., from Latin phrases such as Index Nominum "Index of Names."

Meaning "object serving as a pointer on an instrument, hand of a clock or watch" is from 1590s. Scientific sense (refractive index, etc.) is from 1829, from notion of "an indicator." Economic sense (cost-of-living index, etc.) is from 1870, from the scientific usage. 

The Church sense of "forbidden books" is from index librorum prohibitorum, first published 1564 by authority of Pius IV. The Index Expurgatorius was the catalogue of books that Catholics were forbidden to read unless certain passages were deleted, first printed 1571.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "the forefinger," 源自 拉丁语 index (属格 indicis) "one who points out, discloser, discoverer, informer; forefinger (because used in pointing); pointer, sign; title, inscription, list," 字面义为 "anything which points out," 源自 indicare "to point out" （参见 indication). 同源词：Indexical. Obsolete in English in its original sense (index finger 见于 1768 年). 义为 "alphabetical list of a book's contents with directions where in the text to find them" 始于 16 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 phrases such as Index Nominum "Index of Names." 义为 "object serving as a pointer on an instrument, hand of a clock or watch" 始于 1590 年代. Scientific sense (refractive index, etc.) 始于 1829 年, 源自 概念 "an indicator." Economic sense (cost-of-living index, etc.) 始于 1870 年, 源自 scientific usage. The Church 语义 "forbidden books" 始于 index librorum prohibitorum, first published 1564 年 by authority of Pius IV. The Index Expurgatorius was the catalogue of books that Catholics were forbidden to read unless certain passages were deleted, first printed 1571 年.

example.en: The body mass index is a common measure used to assess healthy weight.
example.zh: 体重指数是评估健康体重的常用指标。

entries.etymology:
"the Indian subcontinent, central Asia south of the Himalayas," formerly sometimes used generally for "Asia;" since 1947 specifically in reference to the Republic of India, Old English India, Indea, from Latin India, from Greek India "region of the Indus River," later used of the region beyond it, from Indos "Indus River," also "an Indian," from Old Persian Hindu, the name for the province of Sind, from Sanskrit sindhu "river."

The more common Middle English form was Ynde or Inde, from Old French (hence Indies). The form India began to prevail again in English from 16c., perhaps under Spanish or Portuguese influence.
entries.etymologyZh: "the Indian subcontinent, central Asia south of the Himalayas," formerly 有时 used generally for "Asia;" 自 1947 年 specifically in reference to the Republic of India, 古英语 India, Indea, 源自 拉丁语 India, 源自 希腊语 India "region of the Indus River," later used of the region beyond it, 源自 Indos "Indus River," also "an Indian," 源自 Old 波斯语 Hindu, the name for the province of Sind, 源自 梵语 sindhu "river." The more common 中古英语 form was Ynde or Inde, 源自 古法语 (hence Indies). The form India began to prevail again in English 源自 16 世纪, 或许 under 西班牙语 or 葡萄牙语 influence.

definitionLines: a. 印度（人）的，印第安人的
entries.definition: a. 印度（人）的，印第安人的 n. 印度人，印第安人

entries.etymology: 1650s, "to point out," back-formation from indication (q.v.) or else from Latin indicatus, past participle of indicare "to point out, show, indicate." Especially "to give suggestion of, be reason for inferring" (1706). Related: Indicated; indicating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "to point out," back-formation 源自 indication (q.v.) or else 源自 拉丁语 indicatus, 为 … 的过去分词 indicare "to point out, show, indicate." Especially "to give suggestion of, be reason for inferring" (1706 年). 同源词：Indicated; indicating.

example.en: The steady drop in birth rates indicates a long-term demographic change.
example.zh: 出生率的持续下降表明正在发生长期的人口结构变化。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "a sign, that which indicates," from Latin indicationem (nominative indicatio) "an indicating; valuation," noun of action from past participle stem of indicare "point out, show," from in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + dicare "proclaim" (see diction).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "a sign, that which indicates," 源自 拉丁语 indicationem (主格 indicatio) "an indicating; valuation," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of indicare "point out, show," 源自 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + dicare "proclaim" （参见 diction).

example.en: There was no indication that the storm would arrive so quickly.
example.zh: 没有任何迹象表明风暴会来得这么快。

definitionLines: a. 漠不关心的，冷漠的
entries.definition: a. 漠不关心的，冷漠的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "unbiased, impartial, not preferring one to the other" (of persons), "alike, equal" (of things), from Old French indifferent "impartial" or directly from Latin indifferentem (nominative indifferens) "not differing, not particular, of no consequence, neither good nor evil," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + differens, present participle of differre "set apart" (see differ). Extended sense of "apathetic, no more inclined to one thing than to another" first recorded early 15c.; that of "neither good nor bad" is from 1530s, on notion of "neither more nor less advantageous," but since 17c. it has tended toward "rather bad."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "unbiased, impartial, not preferring one to the other" (of persons), "alike, equal" (of things), 源自 古法语 indifferent "impartial" or 直接源自 拉丁语 indifferentem (主格 indifferens) "not differing, not particular, of no consequence, neither good nor evil," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + differens, 为 … 的现在分词 differre "set apart" （参见 differ). Extended 语义 "apathetic, no more inclined to one thing than to another" 首见于 15 世纪初; that of "neither good nor bad" 始于 1530 年代, on 概念 "neither more nor less advantageous," but 自 17 世纪 it has tended toward "rather bad."

definitionLines: a.不关心的；不在乎的；中立
entries.definition: a.不关心的；不在乎的；中立
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "quality of being neither good nor bad, neutral quality," from Latin indifferentia "want of difference, similarity," noun of quality from indifferentem (see indifferent). From late 15c. as "lack of prejudice, impartiality;" from 1650s as "state of being apathetic." Meaning "comparative mediocrity, inexcellence"" is from 1864.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "quality of being neither good nor bad, neutral quality," 源自 拉丁语 indifferentia "want of difference, similarity," 名词 of quality 源自 indifferentem （参见 indifferent). From 15 世纪晚期 as "lack of prejudice, impartiality;" 源自 1650 年代 as "state of being apathetic." 义为 "comparative mediocrity, inexcellence"" 始于 1864 年.

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Latin indignantem (nominative indignans) "impatient, reluctant, indignant," present participle of indignari "to be displeased at, be offended, resent, deem unworthy" (see indignation). Related: Indignantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 indignantem (主格 indignans) "impatient, reluctant, indignant," 为 … 的现在分词 indignari "to be displeased at, be offended, resent, deem unworthy" （参见 indignation). 同源词：Indignantly.

definitionLines: a. 不可缺少的；绝对必要的
entries.definition: a. 不可缺少的；绝对必要的
entries.etymology:
1530s, "not subject to dispensation," from Medieval Latin *indispensabilis, from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + dispensabilis, from Latin dispensare "disburse, administer, distribute (by weight)" (see dispense). Meaning "necessary" is from 1690s. From 17c. into 19c. often spelled indispensible, but modern dictionaries considered this improper.

As a noun, "indispensable thing," from 1794; c. 1800-1810, after French use, it was the name of a type of pocket bag worn by women. indispensables (1820) also was one of the many 1820s jocular euphemisms for "trousers" (see inexpressible). Related: Indispensably.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "not subject to dispensation," 源自 中古拉丁语 *indispensabilis, 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + dispensabilis, 源自 拉丁语 dispensare "disburse, administer, distribute (by weight)" （参见 dispense). 义为 "necessary" 始于 1690 年代. From 17 世纪 into 19 世纪 常 spelled indispensible, but modern dictionaries considered this improper. 作名词时, "indispensable thing," 自 1794 年起; 约 1800 年-1810 年, after 法语 use, it was the name of a type of pocket bag worn by women. indispensables (1820 年) also was one of the many 1820 年代 jocular euphemisms for "trousers" （参见 inexpressible). 同源词：Indispensably.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French indirect (14c.) or directly from Late Latin indirectus "not direct," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + directus (see direct (adj.)). Related: Indirectness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 indirect (14 世纪) or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 indirectus "not direct," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + directus （参见 direct （形）). 同源词：Indirectness.

example.en: The politician gave an indirect answer to avoid controversy.
example.zh: 这位政客给出了一个间接的回答以避免争议。

definitionLines: a. 个别，单独的；独特的
entries.definition: n. 个人，个体 a. 个别，单独的；独特的 indoor（s） a./ad.室内（的），户内（的）
entries.etymology: early 15c., "one and indivisible, inseparable" (with reference to the Trinity), from Medieval Latin individualis, from Latin individuus "indivisible," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + dividuus "divisible," from dividere "divide" (see divide). Original sense now obsolete; the word was not common before c. 1600 and the 15c. example might be an outlier. Sense of "single, separate, of but one person or thing" is from 1610s; meaning "intended for one person" is from 1889.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "one and indivisible, inseparable" (with reference to the Trinity), 源自 中古拉丁语 individualis, 源自 拉丁语 individuus "indivisible," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + dividuus "divisible," 源自 dividere "divide" （参见 divide). Original sense 今废; the word was not common before 约 1600 年 and the 15 世纪 example might be an outlier. 义为 "single, separate, of but one person or thing" 始于 1610 年代; 意为 "intended for one person" 始于 1889 年.

example.en: Every individual has the right to express their opinion freely.
example.zh: 每个人都有自由表达意见的权利。

entries.etymology: formerly also enduce, late 14c., "to lead by persuasions or other influences," from Latin inducere "lead into, bring in, introduce, conduct; persuade; suppose, imagine," from in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + ducere "to lead" (see duke (n.)). Meaning "to bring about" in any way (in reference to a trance, a fever, etc.) is from early 15c.; sense of "to infer by reasoning" is from 1560s. Electro-magnetic sense first recorded 1777. Related: Induced; inducing.
entries.etymologyZh: formerly also enduce, 14 世纪晚期, "to lead by persuasions or other influences," 源自 拉丁语 inducere "lead into, bring in, introduce, conduct; persuade; suppose, imagine," 源自 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + ducere "to lead" （参见 duke （名）). 义为 "to bring about" in any way (in reference to a trance, a fever, etc.) 始于 15 世纪初; 语义 "to infer by reasoning" 始于 1560 年代. Electro-magnetic sense 首见于 1777 年. 同源词：Induced; inducing.

example.en: Stress can induce physical symptoms such as headaches and fatigue.
example.zh: 压力可以引发头痛和疲劳等身体症状。

definitionLines: vt. 满足；使沉迷于……；使高 兴；纵容
entries.definition: vt. 满足；使沉迷于……；使高 兴；纵容 vi. （in）满足；沉溺；放任
entries.etymology: formerly also endulge, 1630s, "to grant as a favor;" 1650s, "to treat with unearned favor" (in reference both to persons and desires), a back-formation from indulgence (q.v.), or else from Latin indulgere "be complaisant, be indulgent, yield; give oneself up to;" probably a compound verb with first element in- "in," but the second element is obscure. Related: Indulged; indulging; indulgingly.
entries.etymologyZh: formerly also endulge, 1630 年代, "to grant as a favor;" 1650 年代, "to treat with unearned favor" (in reference both to persons and desires), a back-formation 源自 indulgence (q.v.)，或else 源自 拉丁语 indulgere "be complaisant, be indulgent, yield; give oneself up to;" 可能 a 复合词 动词 with first element in- "in," but the second element is obscure. 同源词：Indulged; indulging; indulgingly.

entries.etymology:
1774, "resulting from labor," from French industriel, from Medieval Latin industrialis, from Latin industria "diligence, activity" (see industry). There is an isolated earlier used in the same sense from 1580s, from Latin industria.

The main modern meaning "pertaining to the manufacture of commodities, connected with the application of industry to manufactures" is from 1830, from a sense in French.

Meaning "suitable for industrial use" is from 1904. As a style of dance music, attested from 1988. Industrial revolution was in use by 1840 to refer to what were then recent developments and changes in England and elsewhere.
entries.etymologyZh: 1774 年, "resulting from labor," 源自 法语 industriel, 源自 中古拉丁语 industrialis, 源自 拉丁语 industria "diligence, activity" （参见 industry). There is an isolated earlier used in the same sense 源自 1580 年代, 源自 拉丁语 industria. The main modern 意为 "pertaining to the manufacture of commodities, connected with the application of industry to manufactures" 始于 1830 年, 源自 a sense in 法语. 义为 "suitable for industrial use" 始于 1904 年. 作为 style of dance music, attested 自 1988 年起. Industrial revolution was in use 截至 1840 年 to refer to what were 之后 recent developments and changes in England and elsewhere.

example.en: The city grew rapidly during the industrial revolution of the 19th century.
example.zh: 这座城市在19世纪工业革命期间迅速发展。

entries.etymology: 1883, noun of action from industrialize (q.v.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1883 年, 名词 of action 源自 industrialize (q.v.).

entries.etymology: late 15c., "cleverness, skill," from Old French industrie "activity; aptitude, experience" (14c.) or directly from Latin industria "diligence, activity, zeal," noun use of fem. of industrius "active, diligent," from early Latin indostruus "diligent," from indu "in, within" (see indigenous) + stem of struere "to build" (see structure (n.)). The meaning "habitual diligence, effort" is from 1530s; that of "systematic work" is from 1610s. The sense "a particular trade or manufacture" is first recorded 1560s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "cleverness, skill," 源自 古法语 industrie "activity; aptitude, experience" (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 industria "diligence, activity, zeal," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. of industrius "active, diligent," 源自 early 拉丁语 indostruus "diligent," 源自 indu "in, within" （参见 indigenous) + stem of struere "to build" （参见 structure （名）). The 意为 "habitual diligence, effort" 始于 1530 年代; that of "systematic work" 始于 1610 年代. The sense "a particular trade or manufacture" is 首见于 1560 年代.

example.en: The automotive industry has undergone major changes over the past decade.
example.zh: 过去十年间，汽车工业经历了重大变革。

entries.etymology: 1713, "that property of matter by virtue of which it retains its state of rest or of uniform rectilinear motion so long as no foreign cause changes that state" [Century Dictionary], introduced as a term in physics 17c. by German astronomer and physician Johann Kepler (1571-1630) as a special sense of Latin inertia "unskillfulness, ignorance; inactivity, idleness," from iners (genitive inertis) "unskilled; inactive" (see inert). Also sometimes vis inertia "force of inertia." Used in 1687 by Newton, writing in Modern Latin. The classical Latin sense of "apathy, passiveness, inactivity" is attested in English from 1822.
entries.etymologyZh: 1713 年, "that property of matter by virtue of which it retains its state of rest or of uniform rectilinear motion so long as no foreign cause changes that state" [Century Dictionary], introduced 作为 term in physics 17 世纪 by 德语 astronomer and physician Johann Kepler (1571 年-1630 年) 作为 special 语义 拉丁语 inertia "unskillfulness, ignorance; inactivity, idleness," 源自 iners (属格 inertis) "unskilled; inactive" （参见 inert). Also 有时 vis inertia "force of inertia." Used 于 1687 年 by Newton, writing in 现代 拉丁语. The classical 拉丁语 语义 "apathy, passiveness, inactivity" is 见于 English 自 1822 年起.

entries.etymology: "unavoidable," mid-15c., from Latin inevitabilis "unavoidable," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + evitabilis "avoidable," from evitare "to avoid," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + vitare "shun," originally "go out of the way." As a noun from 1850. Related: Inevitableness.
entries.etymologyZh: "unavoidable," 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 inevitabilis "unavoidable," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + evitabilis "avoidable," 源自 evitare "to avoid," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + vitare "shun," 原义为 "go out of the way." 作名词时 自 1850 年起. 同源词：Inevitableness.

example.en: Given the pace of automation, some degree of workforce displacement seems inevitable.
example.zh: 考虑到自动化的速度，一定程度的劳动力替代似乎不可避免。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., infant, infaunt, "a child," also especially "child during earliest period of life, a newborn" (sometimes meaning a fetus), from Latin infantem (nominative infans) "young child, babe in arms," noun use of adjective meaning "not able to speak," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + fans, present participle of fari "to speak," from PIE root *bha- (2) "to speak, tell, say" (see fame (n.)). As an adjective in English, 1580s, from the noun.

The Romans extended the sense of Latin infans to include older children, hence French enfant "child," Italian fanicullo, faniculla. In English the word formerly also had the wider sense of "child" (commonly reckoned as up to age 7). The common Germanic words for "child" (represented in English by bairn and child) also are sense extensions of words that originally must have meant "newborn."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, infant, infaunt, "a child," also 尤指 "child during earliest period of life, a newborn" (有时 意为 a fetus), 源自 拉丁语 infantem (主格 infans) "young child, babe in arms," 为 … 的名词用法 形容词 意为 "not able to speak," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + fans, 为 … 的现在分词 fari "to speak," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *bha- (2) "to speak, tell, say" （参见 fame （名）). 作形容词时 in English, 1580 年代, 源自 名词. The Romans extended the 语义 拉丁语 infans to include older children, hence 法语 enfant "child," 意大利语 fanicullo, faniculla. In English the word formerly also had the wider 语义 "child" (commonly reckoned as up to age 7). The common 日耳曼语 words for "child" (represented in English by bairn and child) also are sense extensions of words that 原义为 must have meant "newborn."

example.en: The infant fell asleep within minutes of being placed in the crib.
example.zh: 那名婴儿被放进婴儿床后几分钟就睡着了。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "fill with disease, render pestilential; pollute, contaminate; to corrupt morally," from Latin infectus, past participle of inficere "to stain, tinge, dye," also "to corrupt, stain, spoil," literally "to put in to, dip into," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + facere "to make, do, perform" (see factitious). In Middle English occasionally in a neutral sense "tinge, darken," but typically used of things indifferent or bad, and especially of disease. Related: Infected; infecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "fill with disease, render pestilential; pollute, contaminate; to corrupt morally," 源自 拉丁语 infectus, 为 … 的过去分词 inficere "to stain, tinge, dye," also "to corrupt, stain, spoil," 字面义为 "to put in to, dip into," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + facere "to make, do, perform" （参见 factitious). In 中古英语 occasionally in a neutral sense "tinge, darken," but typically used of things indifferent or bad, and 尤指 of disease. 同源词：Infected; infecting.

example.en: The virus can infect others through direct contact with the patient.
example.zh: 该病毒可以通过与患者的直接接触感染他人。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "infectious disease; contaminated condition;" from Old French infeccion "contamination, poisoning" (13c.) and directly from Late Latin infectionem (nominative infectio) "infection, contagion," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin inficere "to spoil, to stain" (see infect). Meaning "communication of disease by agency of air or water" (distinguished from contagion, which is body-to-body communication), is from 1540s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "infectious disease; contaminated condition;" 源自 古法语 infeccion "contamination, poisoning" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 infectionem (主格 infectio) "infection, contagion," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 inficere "to spoil, to stain" （参见 infect). 义为 "communication of disease by agency of air or water" (distinguished 源自 contagion, which is body-to-body communication), 始于 1540 年代.

example.en: Washing your hands regularly can prevent the infection of bacteria.
example.zh: 经常洗手可以预防细菌感染。

entries.etymology: "catching, having the quality of spreading from person to person, communicable by infection," 1540s of diseases, 1610s of emotions, actions, etc.; see infection + -ous. Earlier in the same sense were infectuous (late 15c.), infective (late 14c.). Related: Infectiously; infectiousness.
entries.etymologyZh: "catching, having the quality of spreading from person to person, communicable by infection," 1540 年代 of diseases, 1610 年代 of emotions, actions, etc.; 参见 infection + -ous. Earlier in the same sense were infectuous (15 世纪晚期), infective (14 世纪晚期). 同源词：Infectiously; infectiousness.

entries.etymology:
in logic, "to 'bring in' as a conclusion of a process of reasoning," 1520s, from Latin inferre "bring into, carry in; deduce, infer, conclude, draw an inference; bring against," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + ferre "carry, bear," from PIE *bher- (1) "to bear, to carry, to take" (source also of Sanskrit bharati "carries;" Avestan baraiti "carries;" Old Persian barantiy "they carry;" Armenian berem "I carry;" Greek pherein "to carry;" Old Irish beru/berim "I catch, I bring forth;" Gothic bairan "to carry;" Old English and Old High German beran, Old Norse bera "barrow;" Old Church Slavonic birati "to take;" Russian brat' "to take," bremya "a burden").

General sense of "draw a conclusion" is first attested 1520s; intransitive sense is from 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: in logic, "to 'bring in' as a conclusion of a process of reasoning," 1520 年代, 源自 拉丁语 inferre "bring into, carry in; deduce, infer, conclude, draw an inference; bring against," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + ferre "carry, bear," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *bher- (1) "to bear, to carry, to take" (source also of 梵语 bharati "carries;" Avestan baraiti "carries;" Old 波斯语 barantiy "they carry;" Armenian berem "I carry;" 希腊语 pherein "to carry;" Old 爱尔兰语 beru/berim "I catch, I bring forth;" Gothic bairan "to carry;" 古英语 and 古高地德语 beran, 古北欧语 bera "barrow;" Old Church Slavonic birati "to take;" 俄语 brat' "to take," bremya "a burden"). General 语义 "draw a conclusion" is 最早见于 1520 年代; intransitive sense 始于 1570 年代.

entries.etymology: 1590s, "action of inferring;" 1610s, "that which is inferred;" from Medieval Latin inferentia, from Latin inferentem (nominative inferens), present participle of inferre "bring into; conclude, deduce" (see infer).
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "action of inferring;" 1610 年代, "that which is inferred;" 源自 中古拉丁语 inferentia, 源自 拉丁语 inferentem (主格 inferens), 为 … 的现在分词 inferre "bring into; conclude, deduce" （参见 infer).

definitionLines: a.（to）次的，低劣的；下级的， 低等的
entries.definition: a.（to）次的，低劣的；下级的， 低等的
entries.etymology: early 15c., of land, "low, lower down, lower in position," from Latin inferior "lower, further down" (also used figuratively), comparative of inferus (adj.) "that is below or beneath," from infra "below" (see infra-). Meaning "lower in degree, rank, grade, or importance" is from 1530s; absolutely, "of low quality or rank," also from 1530s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, of land, "low, lower down, lower in position," 源自 拉丁语 inferior "lower, further down" (also used figuratively), comparative of inferus （形） "that is below or beneath," 源自 infra "below" （参见 infra-). 义为 "lower in degree, rank, grade, or importance" 始于 1530 年代; absolutely, "of low quality or rank," 亦源自 1530 年代.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "eternal, limitless," also "extremely great in number," from Old French infinit "endless, boundless" and directly from Latin infinitus "unbounded, unlimited, countless, numberless," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + finitus "defining, definite," from finis "end" (see finish (v.)). The noun meaning "that which is infinite" is from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "eternal, limitless," also "extremely great in number," 源自 古法语 infinit "endless, boundless" and 直接源自 拉丁语 infinitus "unbounded, unlimited, countless, numberless," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + finitus "defining, definite," 源自 finis "end" （参见 finish （动）). The 名词 意为 "that which is infinite" 始于 1580 年代.

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "swelling caused by gathering of 'wind' in the body; flatulence," also, figuratively, "outbursts of pride," from Latin inflationem (nominative inflatio) "a puffing up, a blowing into; flatulence," noun of action from past participle stem of inflare "blow into, puff up," figuratively "inspire, encourage," from in- "into" (see in- (2)) + flare "to blow" (see blow (v.1)).

Meaning "action of inflating with air or gas" is from c. 1600. Monetary sense of "enlargement of prices" (originally by an increase in the amount of money in circulation) first recorded 1838 in American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "swelling caused by gathering of 'wind' in the body; flatulence," also, figuratively, "outbursts of pride," 源自 拉丁语 inflationem (主格 inflatio) "a puffing up, a blowing into; flatulence," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of inflare "blow into, puff up," figuratively "inspire, encourage," 源自 in- "into" （参见 in- (2)) + flare "to blow" （参见 blow (v.1)). 义为 "action of inflating with air or gas" 始于 约 1600 年. Monetary 语义 "enlargement of prices" (原义为 by an increase in the amount of money in circulation) 首见于 1838 年 in American English.

example.en: Rising inflation has made everyday groceries much more expensive.
example.zh: 通货膨胀上升使日常杂货的价格大幅提高。

entries.definition: vt. /n.（on）影响，感化 n. 势力，权势
entries.etymology:
late 14c., an astrological term, "streaming ethereal power from the stars when in certain positions, acting upon character or destiny of men," from Old French influence "emanation from the stars that acts upon one's character and destiny" (13c.), also "a flow of water, a flowing in," from Medieval Latin influentia "a flowing in" (also used in the astrological sense), from Latin influentem (nominative influens), present participle of influere "to flow into, stream in, pour in," from in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + fluere "to flow" (see fluent).

The range of senses in Middle English were non-personal, in reference to any outflowing of energy that produces effect, of fluid or vaporous substance as well as immaterial or unobservable forces. Meaning "exertion of unseen influence by persons" is from 1580s (a sense already in Medieval Latin, for instance Aquinas); meaning "capacity for producing effects by insensible or invisible means" is from 1650s. Under the influence (of alcohol, etc.) "drunk" first attested 1866.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, an astrological term, "streaming ethereal power from the stars when in certain positions, acting upon character or destiny of men," 源自 古法语 influence "emanation from the stars that acts upon one's character and destiny" (13 世纪), also "a flow of water, a flowing in," 源自 中古拉丁语 influentia "a flowing in" (also used in the astrological sense), 源自 拉丁语 influentem (主格 influens), 为 … 的现在分词 influere "to flow into, stream in, pour in," 源自 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + fluere "to flow" （参见 fluent). The range of senses in 中古英语 were non-personal, in reference to any outflowing of energy that produces effect, of fluid or vaporous substance as well as immaterial or unobservable forces. 义为 "exertion of unseen influence by persons" 始于 1580 年代 (a sense already in 中古拉丁语, for instance Aquinas); 意为 "capacity for producing effects by insensible or invisible means" 始于 1650 年代. Under the influence (of alcohol, etc.) "drunk" 最早见于 1866 年.

example.en: Good teachers have a lasting influence on their students' confidence and curiosity.
example.zh: 好老师对学生的自信心和求知欲有着持久的影响。

definitionLines: a. 有影响的，有势力的
entries.definition: a. 有影响的，有势力的
entries.etymology: "powerful, having influence," 1650s, from Medieval Latin influentialis, from influentia (see influence (n.)). Earlier in an astrological sense (1560s). Related: Influentially.
entries.etymologyZh: "powerful, having influence," 1650 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 influentialis, 源自 influentia （参见 influence （名）). Earlier in an astrological sense (1560 年代). 同源词：Influentially.

example.en: She is one of the most influential voices in modern environmental policy.
example.zh: 她是现代环境政策中最具影响力的声音之一。

entries.etymology:
1743, borrowed (during an outbreak of the disease in Europe), from Italian influenza "influenza, epidemic," originally "visitation, influence (of the stars)," from Medieval Latin influentia in the astrological sense (see influence).

Used in Italian for diseases since at least 1504 (as in influenza di febbre scarlattina "scarlet fever") on notion of astral,  occult, or atmospheric influence. The 1743 outbreak began in Italy. Often applied since mid-19c. to severe colds.
entries.etymologyZh: 1743 年, borrowed (during an outbreak of the disease in Europe), 源自 意大利语 influenza "influenza, epidemic," 原义为 "visitation, influence (of the stars)," 源自 中古拉丁语 influentia in the astrological sense （参见 influence). Used in 意大利语 for diseases 自 at least 1504 年 (as in influenza di febbre scarlattina "scarlet fever") on 概念 astral, occult，或atmospheric influence. The 1743 年 outbreak began in Italy. Often applied 自 19 世纪中期 to severe colds.

definitionLines: vt. （of）通知，告诉，报告；告发， 告密
entries.definition: vt. （of）通知，告诉，报告；告发， 告密
entries.etymology: early 14c., "to train or instruct in some specific subject," from Old French informer, enformer "instruct, teach" (13c.) and directly from Latin informare "to shape, give form to, delineate," figuratively "train, instruct, educate," from in- "into" (see in- (2)) + formare "to form, shape," from forma "form" (see form (n.)). In early use also enform until c. 1600. Sense of "report facts or news, communicate information to" first recorded late 14c. Related: Informed; informing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to train or instruct in some specific subject," 源自 古法语 informer, enformer "instruct, teach" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 informare "to shape, give form to, delineate," figuratively "train, instruct, educate," 源自 in- "into" （参见 in- (2)) + formare "to form, shape," 源自 forma "form" （参见 form （名）). In early use also enform until 约 1600 年. 义为 "report facts or news, communicate information to" 首见于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Informed; informing.

example.en: Please inform us of any changes to your flight arrival time.
example.zh: 如果您的航班到达时间有任何变化，请告知我们。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., informacion, "act of informing, communication of news," from Old French informacion, enformacion "advice, instruction," from Latin informationem (nominative informatio) "outline, concept, idea," noun of action from past participle stem of informare "to train, instruct, educate; shape, give form to" (see inform). The restored Latin spelling is from 16c.

Meaning "knowledge communicated concerning a particular topic" is from mid-15c. The word was used in reference to television broadcast signals from 1937; to punch-card operating systems from 1944; to DNA from 1953. Information theory is from 1950; information technology is from 1958 (coined in "Harvard Business Review"); information revolution, to be brought about by advances in computing, is from 1966. Information overload is by 1967.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, informacion, "act of informing, communication of news," 源自 古法语 informacion, enformacion "advice, instruction," 源自 拉丁语 informationem (主格 informatio) "outline, concept, idea," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of informare "to train, instruct, educate; shape, give form to" （参见 inform). The restored 拉丁语 spelling 始于 16 世纪 义为 "knowledge communicated concerning a particular topic" 始于 15 世纪中期 The word was used in reference to television broadcast signals 自 1937 年起; to punch-card operating systems 自 1944 年起; to DNA 自 1953 年起. Information theory 始于 1950 年; information technology 始于 1958 年 (coined in "Harvard Business Review"); information revolution, to be brought about by advances in computing, 始于 1966 年. Information overload is 截至 1967 年.

example.en: The website provides free information about visa application procedures.
example.zh: 该网站提供有关签证申请程序的免费信息。

entries.etymology: in early use also engredient, early 15c., "something forming part of a mixture," from Latin ingredientem (nominative ingrediens) "that which enters into" (a compound, recipe, etc.), present participle of ingredi "go in, enter," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + gradi "to step, go" (see grade (n.)). Also from early 15c. as an adjective, "forming part of a mixture."
entries.etymologyZh: in early use also engredient, 15 世纪初, "something forming part of a mixture," 源自 拉丁语 ingredientem (主格 ingrediens) "that which enters into" (a 复合词, recipe, etc.), 为 … 的现在分词 ingredi "go in, enter," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + gradi "to step, go" （参见 grade （名）). Also 源自 15 世纪初 作形容词时, "forming part of a mixture."

example.en: Sugar is the main ingredient that makes this cake so sweet.
example.zh: 糖是使这个蛋糕如此甜的主要成分。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French enhabiter, enabiter "dwell in, live in, reside" (12c.), from Latin inhabitare "to dwell in," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + habitare "to dwell," frequentative of habere "hold, have" (see habit (n.)). Formerly also enhabit. Related: Inhabited; inhabiting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 enhabiter, enabiter "dwell in, live in, reside" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 inhabitare "to dwell in," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + habitare "to dwell," 为 … 的反复体 habere "hold, have" （参见 habit （名）). Formerly also enhabit. 同源词：Inhabited; inhabiting.

example.en: Thousands of species inhabit the dense rainforest of the Amazon.
example.zh: 数千个物种栖息在亚马逊茂密的雨林中。

entries.etymology: "one who dwells in a place" (as distinguished from a visitor or transient), early 15c., from Anglo-French inhabitant, from Latin inhabitantem (nominative inhabitans), present participle of inhabitare "to dwell in" (see inhabit). Related: Inhabitants. As an adjective, also from early 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: "one who dwells in a place" (as distinguished 源自 a visitor or transient), 15 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 inhabitant, 源自 拉丁语 inhabitantem (主格 inhabitans), 为 … 的现在分词 inhabitare "to dwell in" （参见 inhabit). 同源词：Inhabitants. 作形容词时, 亦源自 15 世纪初

example.en: The local inhabitants were asked to vote on the new development plan.
example.zh: 当地居民被要求就新的发展计划进行投票。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to make (someone) an heir" (a sense now obsolete), from Old French enheriter "make heir, attribute the right of inheretance to, appoint as heir," from Late Latin inhereditare "to appoint as heir," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + Latin hereditare "to inherit," from heres (genitive heredis) "heir" (see heredity).

Sense of "receive inheritance, get by succession as representative of the former possessor" is attested from mid-14c.; in Medieval Latin inhereditare also had taken on a sense "put in possession." Original sense is retained in disinherit. Related: Inherited; inheriting; inheritable.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to make (someone) an heir" (a sense 今废), 源自 古法语 enheriter "make heir, attribute the right of inheretance to, appoint as heir," 源自 晚期拉丁语 inhereditare "to appoint as heir," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + 拉丁语 hereditare "to inherit," 源自 heres (属格 heredis) "heir" （参见 heredity). 义为 "receive inheritance, get by succession as representative of the former possessor" 见于 14 世纪中期; in 中古拉丁语 inhereditare also had taken on a sense "put in possession." Original sense is retained in disinherit. 同源词：Inherited; inheriting; inheritable.

example.en: She was surprised to inherit her grandfather's vast estate after his passing.
example.zh: 她惊讶地发现自己在祖父去世后继承了他的大笔遗产。

entries.definition: a.最初的，开头的 n. 首字母
entries.etymology: 1520s, "of or pertaining to a beginning," from Middle French initial or directly from Latin initialis "initial, incipient, of the beginning," from initium "a beginning, a commencement; an entrance, a going in," noun use of neuter past participle of inire "to go into, enter upon, begin," from in- "into, in" (see in- (2)) + ire "to go" (see ion). Related: Initially.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "of or pertaining to a beginning," 源自 中古法语 initial or 直接源自 拉丁语 initialis "initial, incipient, of the beginning," 源自 initium "a beginning, a commencement; an entrance, a going in," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的过去分词 inire "to go into, enter upon, begin," 源自 in- "into, in" （参见 in- (2)) + ire "to go" （参见 ion). 同源词：Initially.

example.en: The initial results of the experiment were very promising.
example.zh: 实验的初步结果非常令人期待。

entries.etymology: "one who has been initiated" (in secret doctrines, etc.), 1732, from obsolete or archaic past participle adjective initiate "initiated, instructed in secret knowledge" (c. 1600), from Latin initiatus (see initiate (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: "one who has been initiated" (in secret doctrines, etc.), 1732 年, 源自 已废 or 古旧 past participle 形容词 initiate "initiated, instructed in secret knowledge" (约 1600 年), 源自 拉丁语 initiatus （参见 initiate （动）).

example.en: The committee voted to initiate a formal inquiry by appointing an independent auditor.
example.zh: 委员会投票通过任命独立审计员来正式启动调查。

entries.definition: n. 主动权；首创精神 a.起始的；主动的；自发的
entries.etymology: "power of initiating," 1775, from French initiative (16c.), from Latin initiatus, past participle of initiare "to begin," from initium "a beginning" (see initial (adj.)). From 1793 as "disposition to take the lead." Phrase take the initiative recorded by 1815.
entries.etymologyZh: "power of initiating," 1775 年, 源自 法语 initiative (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 initiatus, 为 … 的过去分词 initiare "to begin," 源自 initium "a beginning" （参见 initial （形）). From 1793 年 as "disposition to take the lead." Phrase take the initiative recorded 截至 1815 年.

example.en: She took the initiative to redesign the company website on her own.
example.zh: 她主动承担了重新设计公司网站的任务。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, in medicine, from specialized sense of Latin iniectus "a casting on, a throwing over," past participle of inicere "to throw in or on; insert, bring into," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + -icere, comb. form of iacere "to throw" (see jet (v.)). Related: Injectable; injected; injecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, in medicine, 源自 specialized 语义 拉丁语 iniectus "a casting on, a throwing over," 为 … 的过去分词 inicere "to throw in or on; insert, bring into," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + -icere, comb. form of iacere "to throw" （参见 jet （动）). 同源词：Injectable; injected; injecting.

example.en: The nurse had to inject a painkiller directly into the patient's arm.
example.zh: 护士不得不直接向患者的手臂注射止痛药。

entries.etymology: "a forcing of a fluid into a body" (with a syringe, etc.), early 15c., from Old French iniection (14c.) or directly from Latin iniectionem (nominative iniectio) "a throwing in," noun of action from past participle stem of inicere "to throw in or on" (see inject).
entries.etymologyZh: "a forcing of a fluid into a body" (with a syringe, etc.), 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 iniection (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 iniectionem (主格 iniectio) "a throwing in," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of inicere "to throw in or on" （参见 inject).

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "do an injustice to, dishonor," probably a back-formation from injury, or else from Old French injuriier "to damage; offend," from Latin iniuriari "do an injury," from iniuria. Injury itself also served as a verb meaning "to injure, hurt, harm" (late 15c.). Related: Injured; injuring.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "do an injustice to, dishonor," 可能 a back-formation 源自 injury，或else 源自 古法语 injuriier "to damage; offend," 源自 拉丁语 iniuriari "do an injury," 源自 iniuria. Injury itself also served 作动词时 意为 "to injure, hurt, harm" (15 世纪晚期). 同源词：Injured; injuring.

example.en: The player was forced to withdraw after he injured his knee during training.
example.zh: 这名球员在训练中膝盖受伤，被迫退出比赛。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "harm, damage, loss; a specific injury," from Anglo-French injurie "wrongful action" (Old French injure, 13c.), from Latin iniuria "wrong, an injustice, insult, unlawful violence, assault, damage, harm," noun use of fem. of iniurius "wrongful, unjust, unlawful," from in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + ius (genitive iuris) "right, law" (see jurist).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "harm, damage, loss; a specific injury," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 injurie "wrongful action" (古法语 injure, 13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 iniuria "wrong, an injustice, insult, unlawful violence, assault, damage, harm," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. of iniurius "wrongful, unjust, unlawful," 源自 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + ius (属格 iuris) "right, law" （参见 jurist).

example.en: The athlete suffered a knee injury during the final game.
example.zh: 那名运动员在决赛中膝盖受了伤。

entries.etymology:
"the black liquor with which men write" [Johnson], mid-13c., from Old French enche, encre "dark writing fluid" (12c.), earlier enque (11c.), originally enca, from Late Latin encaustum, from Late Greek enkauston. This is the neuter of the past-participle adjective enkaustos "burned in," from the stem of enkaiein "to burn in," from en- "in" (see en- (1)) + kaiein "to burn" (see caustic).

In Pliny the word is the name of a kind of painting executed by fire or heat. Later it was the name of the purple-red ink, the sacrum encaustum, used by the Roman emperors to sign their documents; this was said to have been obtained from the ground remains of certain shellfish, formed into writing fluid by the application of fire or heat, which explained the name. In the Code of Justinian, the making of it for common uses, or by common persons, was prohibited under penalty of death and confiscation of goods.

The usual words for "ink" in Latin was atramentum (source of Old French arrement), literally "anything that serves to dye black," from ater "black;" the Greek word was melan, neuter of melas "black." The Old English word for it was blæc, literally "black," and compare Swedish bläk, Danish blæk "ink." Spanish and Portuguese (tinta) and German (tinte) get their "ink" words from Latin tinctus "a dyeing."

Donkin credits a Greek pronunciation, with the accent at the front of the word, for the French evolution; the same Latin word, behaving regularly,  became inchiostro (with excrescent -r-) in Italian, encausto in Spanish. As an adjective, inken (c. 1600) occasionally has been used. Ink-slinger, contemptuous for "journalist," is from 1870. The psychologist's ink-blot test attested from 1915.

This is the neuter of the past-participle 形容词 enkaustos "burned in," 源自 stem of enkaiein "to burn in," 源自 en- "in" （参见 en- (1)) + kaiein "to burn" （参见 caustic). In Pliny the word is the name of a kind of painting executed by fire or heat. Later it was the name of the purple-red ink, the sacrum encaustum, used by the Roman emperors to sign their documents; this was said to have been obtained 源自 ground remains of certain shellfish, formed into writing fluid by the application of fire or heat, which explained the name. In the Code of Justinian, the making of it for common uses，或by common persons, was prohibited under penalty of death and confiscation of goods. The usual words for "ink" in 拉丁语 was atramentum (source of 古法语 arrement), 字面义为 "anything that serves to dye black," 源自 ater "black;" the 希腊语 word was melan, neuter of melas "black." The 古英语 word for it was blæc, 字面义为 "black," and 对比 Swedish bläk, Danish blæk "ink." 西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 (tinta) and 德语 (tinte) get their "ink" words 源自 拉丁语 tinctus "a dyeing." Donkin credits a 希腊语 pronunciation, with the accent at the front of the word, for the 法语 evolution; the same 拉丁语 word, behaving regularly, became inchiostro (with excrescent -r-) in 意大利语, encausto in 西班牙语. 作形容词时, inken (约 1600 年) occasionally has been used.
