example.en: The old letter was written in faded ink that was hard to read.
example.zh: 这封旧信用已褪色的墨水书写，很难辨认。

definitionLines: ad.向内地；在内地；向内陆；在 内陆
entries.definition: a.内陆的；国内的；内地的 ad.向内地；在内地；向内陆；在 内陆
entries.etymology: "of or pertaining to interior parts of a country," 1550s, from in + land (n.). The noun meaning "interior parts of a country (remote from the sea or borders)" is attested from 1570s. Meaning "confined to a country" (as opposed to foreign) is from 1540s. In Middle English and Old English the same compound meant "land immediately around the mansion of an estate, land in the lord's own occupation (as opposed to land occupied by tenants)." Related: Inlander.
entries.etymologyZh: "of or pertaining to interior parts of a country," 1550 年代, 源自 in + land （名）. The 名词 意为 "interior parts of a country (remote from the sea or borders)" 见于 1570 年代. 义为 "confined to a country" (as opposed to foreign) 始于 1540 年代. In 中古英语 and 古英语 the same 复合词 meant "land immediately around the mansion of an estate, land in the lord's own occupation (as opposed to land occupied by tenants)." 同源词：Inlander.

entries.etymology: Old English inn "lodging, dwelling, house," probably from inne (adv.) "inside, within" (see in). Meaning "public house with lodging" is perhaps by c. 1200, certainly by c. 1400. Meaning "lodging house or residence for students" is attested from early 13c. in Anglo-Latin, now obsolete except in names of buildings that were so used (such as Inns of Court, mid-15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 inn "lodging, dwelling, house," 可能 源自 inne （副） "inside, within" （参见 in). 义为 "public house with lodging" is 或许 by 约 1200 年, certainly by 约 1400 年. 义为 "lodging house or residence for students" 见于 13 世纪初 in Anglo-拉丁语, 今废 except in names of buildings that were so used (such as Inns of Court, 15 世纪中期).

entries.etymology:
c. 1400, from Old English inra, comparative of inne (adv.) "inside" (see in (adv.)). Similar formation in Old High German innaro, German inner. The original order of comparison was in/inner/inmost; the evolution has been unusual for a comparative, and inner has not been used with than since Middle English.

Inner man "the soul" is from late Old English. The Quaker inner light is attested by that name from 1833. Inner tube in the pneumatic tire sense is from 1894. Inner city is attested from 1690s; as a euphemism for "urban poverty and crime," from 1963.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 古英语 inra, comparative of inne （副） "inside" （参见 in （副）). Similar formation in 古高地德语 innaro, 德语 inner. The original order of comparison was in/inner/inmost; the evolution has been unusual for a comparative, and inner has not been used with than 自 中古英语. Inner man "the soul" 始于 late 古英语. The Quaker inner light is attested by that name 自 1833 年起. Inner tube in the pneumatic tire sense 始于 1894 年. Inner city 见于 1690 年代; 作为 euphemism for "urban poverty and crime," 自 1963 年起.

example.en: She found the strength from her inner self to keep going.
example.zh: 她从内心深处找到了继续前行的力量。

definitionLines: n. 清白，无罪；天真无邪
entries.definition: n. 清白，无罪；天真无邪
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "freedom from guilt or moral wrong," from Old French inocence "innocence; purity, chastity" (12c., Modern French innocence), from Latin innocentia "blamelessness, uprightness, integrity," from innocens "harmless; blameless; disinterested" (see innocent). Meaning "lacking in guile or artifice," as of childhood, is from late 14c. Meaning "freedom from legal wrong" is from 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "freedom from guilt or moral wrong," 源自 古法语 inocence "innocence; purity, chastity" (12 世纪, 现代法语 innocence), 源自 拉丁语 innocentia "blamelessness, uprightness, integrity," 源自 innocens "harmless; blameless; disinterested" （参见 innocent). 义为 "lacking in guile or artifice," as of childhood, 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "freedom from legal wrong" 始于 1550 年代.

example.en: The lawyer argued passionately for the defendant's innocence throughout the trial.
example.zh: 律师在整个审判过程中激情澎湃地为被告的清白辩护。

definitionLines: a.无罪的，清白的；无害的；天 真的，单纯的
entries.definition: a.无罪的，清白的；无害的；天 真的，单纯的
entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "doing no evil; free from sin, guilt, or moral wrong," from Old French inocent "harmless; not guilty; pure" (12c.), from Latin innocentem (nominative innocens) "not guilty, blameless; harmless; disinterested," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + nocentem (nominative nocens), present participle of nocere "to harm," from *nok-s-, suffixed form of PIE root *nek- (1) "death" (see necro-).

Meaning "free from guilt of a specific crime or charge" is from late 14c., as is the meaning "with childlike simplicity or artlessness." Humorous sense "free, devoid of" is from 1706. The noun meaning "person who is innocent of sin or evil, artless or simple person" is from c. 1200, especially a young child (who presumably has not yet sinned actively). The Holy Innocents (early 14c.) were the young children slain by Herod after the birth of Jesus (Matt. ii:16), hence Innocents day (Dec. 28).

Indo-European words for "innocent" are generally negative compound of the word for "guilty." An exception is the Germanic group represented by Gothic swikns (also "pure, chaste"), Old Norse sykn "free from guilt, innocent" (especially as a law term), Old English swicn "clearance from a charge," also "cleansing," but these are of uncertain origin.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "doing no evil; free from sin, guilt, or moral wrong," 源自 古法语 inocent "harmless; not guilty; pure" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 innocentem (主格 innocens) "not guilty, blameless; harmless; disinterested," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + nocentem (主格 nocens), 为 … 的现在分词 nocere "to harm," 源自 *nok-s-, suffixed form of 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *nek- (1) "death" （参见 necro-). 义为 "free from guilt of a specific crime or charge" 始于 14 世纪晚期, as is the 意为 "with childlike simplicity or artlessness." Humorous sense "free, devoid of" 始于 1706 年. The 名词 意为 "person who is innocent of sin or evil, artless or simple person" 始于 约 1200 年, 尤指 a young child (who presumably has not yet sinned actively). The Holy Innocents (14 世纪初) were the young children slain by Herod after the birth of Jesus (Matt. ii:16), hence Innocents day (Dec. 28). Indo-European words for "innocent" are generally negative 由 … 复合而成 the word for "guilty." An exception is the 日耳曼语 group represented by Gothic swikns (also "pure, chaste"), 古北欧语 sykn "free from guilt, innocent" (尤指 作为 law term), 古英语 swicn "clearance from a charge," also "cleansing," but these are 来源存疑.

example.en: The jury declared the defendant innocent of all charges.
example.zh: 陪审团宣判被告所有指控均无罪。

entries.etymology: 1540s, "introduce as new" (trans.), from Latin innovatus, past participle of innovare "to renew, restore;" also "to change," from in- "into" (see in- (2)) + novus "new" (see new). Intransitive meaning "bring in new things, alter established practices" is from 1590s. Related: Innovated; innovating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "introduce as new" (trans.), 源自 拉丁语 innovatus, 为 … 的过去分词 innovare "to renew, restore;" also "to change," 源自 in- "into" （参见 in- (2)) + novus "new" （参见 new). Intransitive 意为 "bring in new things, alter established practices" 始于 1590 年代. 同源词：Innovated; innovating.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "restoration, renewal," from Late Latin innovationem (nominative innovatio), noun of action from past participle stem of innovare "to change; to renew" (see innovate). Meaning "a novel change, experimental variation, new thing introduced in an established arrangement" is from 1540s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "restoration, renewal," 源自 晚期拉丁语 innovationem (主格 innovatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of innovare "to change; to renew" （参见 innovate). 义为 "a novel change, experimental variation, new thing introduced in an established arrangement" 始于 1540 年代.

example.en: The company's success was driven by continuous innovation in design.
example.zh: 该公司的成功源于设计上的持续创新。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Latin innumerabilis "countless, immeasurable," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + numerabilis "able to be numbered," from numerare "to count, number," from numerus "a number" (see number (n.)). Related: Innumerability.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 innumerabilis "countless, immeasurable," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + numerabilis "able to be numbered," 源自 numerare "to count, number," 源自 numerus "a number" （参见 number （名）). 同源词：Innumerability.

entries.etymology: 1753, "a sum (of cash) put in, a sharing, contribution," from verbal phrase; see in (adv.) + put (v.). Meaning "energy supplied to a device or machine" is from 1902, later of electronic devices; computing sense of "data fed into a machine" is from 1948, though this is perhaps from the verb in the computing sense.
entries.etymologyZh: 1753 年, "a sum (of cash) put in, a sharing, contribution," 源自 verbal phrase; 参见 in （副） + put （动）. 义为 "energy supplied to a device or machine" 始于 1902 年, later of electronic devices; computing 语义 "data fed into a machine" 始于 1948 年, though this is 或源自 the 动词 in the computing sense.

example.en: Please check your input carefully before submitting the form.
example.zh: 提交表格前请仔细检查您的输入内容。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, enqueren, anqueren, "to ask (a question), ask about, ask for (specific information); learn or find out by asking, seek information or knowledge; to conduct a legal or official investigation (into an alleged offense)," from Old French enquerre "ask, inquire about" (Modern French enquérir) and directly from Medieval Latin inquerere, from in- "into" (see in- (2)) + Latin quaerere "ask, seek" (see query (v.)), in place of classical Latin inquirere "seek after, search for, examine, scrutinize." The English word was respelled 14c. on the Latin model, but half-Latinized enquire persists. Related: Inquired; inquiring.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, enqueren, anqueren, "to ask (a question), ask about, ask for (specific information); learn or find out by asking, seek information or knowledge; to conduct a legal or official investigation (into an alleged offense)," 源自 古法语 enquerre "ask, inquire about" (现代法语 enquérir) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 inquerere, 源自 in- "into" （参见 in- (2)) + 拉丁语 quaerere "ask, seek" （参见 query （动）), in place of classical 拉丁语 inquirere "seek after, search for, examine, scrutinize." The English word was respelled 14 世纪 on the 拉丁语 model, but half-Latinized enquire persists. 同源词：Inquired; inquiring.

entries.etymology: early 15c., enquery, "a judicial examination of facts to determine truth;" mid-15c. in general sense "attempt to learn something, act or fact of inquiring," probably an Anglo-French noun developed from enqueren "to inquire" (see inquire). Respelled from mid-16c. to conform to Latin.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, enquery, "a judicial examination of facts to determine truth;" 15 世纪中期 in general sense "attempt to learn something, act or fact of inquiring," 可能 an 盎格鲁-法语 名词 developed 源自 enqueren "to inquire" （参见 inquire). Respelled 源自 16 世纪中期 to conform to 拉丁语.

example.en: The manager launched an inquiry into the missing funds.
example.zh: 经理就资金失踪一事展开了调查。

definitionLines: a. 精神病的；极愚蠢的；疯狂的
entries.definition: a. 精神病的；极愚蠢的；疯狂的
entries.etymology: 1550s, of persons, "mentally damaged," from Latin insanus "mad, insane, of unsound mind; outrageous, excessive, extravagant," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + sanus "well, healthy, sane" (see sane). In reference to actions, "irrational, evidencing madness," from 1842 in English. The noun meaning "insane person" is attested from 1786. For the notion of insanity as sickness, compare lunatic; and Italian pazzo "insane," originally a euphemism, from Latin patiens "suffering." German verrückt, literally past participle of verrücken "to displace," "applied to the brain as to a clock that is 'out of order' " [Buck].
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, of persons, "mentally damaged," 源自 拉丁语 insanus "mad, insane, of unsound mind; outrageous, excessive, extravagant," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + sanus "well, healthy, sane" （参见 sane). In reference to actions, "irrational, evidencing madness," 自 1842 年起 in English. The 名词 意为 "insane person" 见于 1786 年. For the 概念 insanity as sickness, 对比 lunatic; and 意大利语 pazzo "insane," 原义为 a euphemism, 源自 拉丁语 patiens "suffering." 德语 verrückt, 字面义为 为 … 的过去分词 verrücken "to displace," "applied to the brain as to a clock that is 'out of order' " [Buck].

example.en: It would be insane to attempt that climb without proper equipment.
example.zh: 在没有适当装备的情况下尝试那次攀登简直是疯狂的。

entries.etymology:
c. 1600, from Latin (animal) insectum "(animal) with a notched or divided body," literally "cut into," noun use of neuter past participle of insectare "to cut into, to cut up," from in- "into" (see in- (2)) + secare "to cut" (see section (n.)).

The Latin word is Pliny's loan-translation of Greek entomon "insect" (see entomology), which was Aristotle's term for this class of life, in reference to their "notched" bodies. First in English in 1601 in Holland's translation of Pliny. In zoology, in reference to a class of animals, 1753. Translations of Aristotle's term also form the usual word for "insect" in Welsh (trychfil, from trychu "cut" + mil "animal"), Serbo-Croatian (zareznik, from rezati "cut"), Russian (nasekomoe, from sekat "cut"), etc. Insectarian "one who eats insects" is attested from 1893.

Among the adjectival forms that have been tried in English (and mostly rejected by disuse) are insectile (1620s), insectic (1767), insective (1834), insectual (1849), insectine (1853), insecty (1859), insectan (1888).

example.en: Scientists studied how the insect survived the extreme cold of winter.
example.zh: 科学家研究了这种昆虫如何在极寒冬天中存活。

entries.etymology: "to set in, put or place in," 1520s, from Latin insertus, past participle of inserere "to graft, implant," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + serere "attach, join; arrange, line up," from PIE *ser- (3) "to line up" (see series). Middle English had inseren "to set in place, to graft, to introduce (into the mind)" (late 14c.), directly from the Latin verb. Related: Inserted; inserting.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., ynneside "interior part (of the body)," compound of in (prep.) + side (n.). General sense "inner side or part (of anything)" is from c. 1500.

The adjective sense "being on the inside" is from 1610s, from the noun. It began to be used in slang c. 1900 in reference to the supposed real facts or situation that only an insider would know. Inside man is from 1911 (originally in reference to workers used by management to sniff out union activity); inside job "robbery, espionage, etc., committed by or with the help of a resident or servant of a place" is attested by 1887, American English (also, late 19c., early 20c., "indoors work"). The figurative inside track "advantage" (1854) however is a metaphor from horse racing (1830); inside lanes are shorter than the outer ones on a curved track. Adverbial use in American English inside of (in reference to time) is from 1839.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, ynneside "interior part (of the body)," 由 … 复合而成 in （介） + side （名）. General sense "inner side or part (of anything)" 始于 约 1500 年. The 形容词 sense "being on the inside" 始于 1610 年代, 源自 名词. It began to be used in 俚语 约 1900 年 in reference to the supposed real facts or situation that only an insider would know. Inside man 始于 1911 年 (原义为 in reference to workers used by management to sniff out union activity); inside job "robbery, espionage, etc., committed by or with the help of a resident or servant of a place" is attested 截至 1887 年, American English (also, 19 世纪晚期, 20 世纪初, "indoors work"). The figurative inside track "advantage" (1854 年) however is a metaphor 源自 horse racing (1830 年); inside lanes are shorter than the outer ones on a curved track. Adverbial use in American English inside of (in reference to time) 始于 1839 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, innsihht, "sight with the 'eyes' of the mind, mental vision, understanding from within," from in (prep.) + sight (n.). But the meaning often seems to be felt as "sight into" (something else), and so the sense shifted to "penetrating understanding into character or hidden nature" (1580s). Similar formation in Dutch inzigt, German einsicht, Danish indsigt.

example.en: His years of experience gave him a deep insight into human behavior.
example.zh: 多年的经验使他对人类行为有了深刻的洞察。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from French insister (14c.) or directly from Latin insistere "take a stand, stand on, stand still; follow, pursue; insist, press vigorously, urge, dwell upon," from in- "upon" (see in- (2)) + sistere "take a stand" (see assist (v.)). Perhaps in some cases a back-formation from insistence. Related: Insisted; insisting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 法语 insister (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 insistere "take a stand, stand on, stand still; follow, pursue; insist, press vigorously, urge, dwell upon," 源自 in- "upon" （参见 in- (2)) + sistere "take a stand" （参见 assist （动）). Perhaps in some cases a back-formation 源自 insistence. 同源词：Insisted; insisting.

example.en: She continued to insist on her innocence even as the jury read the verdict.
example.zh: 即使陪审团宣读裁决，她仍坚持声称自己是无辜的。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin inspectus, past participle of inspicere "look at, observe, view; look into, inspect, examine," from in- "into" (see in- (2)) + specere "to look" (see scope (n.1)). Related: Inspected; inspecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 inspectus, 为 … 的过去分词 inspicere "look at, observe, view; look into, inspect, examine," 源自 in- "into" （参见 in- (2)) + specere "to look" （参见 scope (n.1)). 同源词：Inspected; inspecting.

example.en: The health officer came to inspect the kitchen of the restaurant.
example.zh: 卫生官员来检查这家餐厅的厨房。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "immediate influence of God or a god," especially that under which the holy books were written, from Old French inspiracion "inhaling, breathing in; inspiration" (13c.), from Late Latin inspirationem (nominative inspiratio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin inspirare "blow into, breathe upon," figuratively "inspire, excite, inflame," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + spirare "to breathe" (see spirit (n.)).

The sense evolution seems to be from "breathe into" to "infuse animation or influence," thus "affect, rouse, guide or control," especially by divine influence. Inspire (v.) in Middle English also was used to mean "breath or put life or spirit into the human body; impart reason to a human soul." Literal sense "act of inhaling" attested in English from 1560s. Meaning "one who inspires others" is attested by 1867.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "immediate influence of God or a god," 尤指 that under which the holy books were written, 源自 古法语 inspiracion "inhaling, breathing in; inspiration" (13 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 inspirationem (主格 inspiratio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 inspirare "blow into, breathe upon," figuratively "inspire, excite, inflame," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + spirare "to breathe" （参见 spirit （名）). The sense evolution seems to be 源自 "breathe into" to "infuse animation or influence," thus "affect, rouse, guide or control," 尤指 by divine influence. Inspire （动） in 中古英语 also was used to mean "breath or put life or spirit into the human body; impart reason to a human soul." Literal sense "act of inhaling" 见于 English 源自 1560 年代. 义为 "one who inspires others" is attested 截至 1867 年.

example.en: The mountain landscape served as the inspiration for her new poem.
example.zh: 这片山地风光成为了她新诗的灵感源泉。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., enspiren, "to fill (the mind, heart, etc., with grace, etc.);" also "to prompt or induce (someone to do something)," from Old French enspirer (13c.), from Latin inspirare "blow into, breathe upon," figuratively "inspire, excite, inflame," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + spirare "to breathe" (see spirit (n.)).

The Latin word was used as a loan-translation of Greek pnein in the Bible. General sense of "influence or animate with an idea or purpose" is from late 14c. Also sometimes used in literal sense in Middle English. Related: Inspires; inspiring.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, enspiren, "to fill (the mind, heart, etc., with grace, etc.);" also "to prompt or induce (someone to do something)," 源自 古法语 enspirer (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 inspirare "blow into, breathe upon," figuratively "inspire, excite, inflame," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + spirare "to breathe" （参见 spirit （名）). The 拉丁语 word was used 作为 loan-translation of 希腊语 pnein in the Bible. General 语义 "influence or animate with an idea or purpose" 始于 14 世纪晚期 Also 有时 used in literal sense in 中古英语. 同源词：Inspires; inspiring.

example.en: Her courage under intense pressure continues to inspire the younger members of the team.
example.zh: 她在巨大压力下表现出的勇气持续激励着团队中的年轻成员。

entries.etymology: also instal, formerly also enstall, early 15c., "place in (ecclesiastical) office by seating in an official stall," from Old French installer (14c.) or directly from Medieval Latin installare, from Latin in- "in" (see in- (2)) + Medieval Latin stallum "stall," from a Germanic source (compare Old High German stal "standing place;" see stall (n.1)). Related: Installed; installing.
entries.etymologyZh: also instal, formerly also enstall, 15 世纪初, "place in (ecclesiastical) office by seating in an official stall," 源自 古法语 installer (14 世纪) or 直接源自 中古拉丁语 installare, 源自 拉丁语 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + 中古拉丁语 stallum "stall," 源自 a 日耳曼语 source (对比 古高地德语 stal "standing place;" 参见 stall (n.1)). 同源词：Installed; installing.

example.en: The technician came to install a new security system in our office.
example.zh: 技术人员来到我们办公室安装新的安保系统。

Of machinery, etc., "act of setting up, a placing in  position for use," from 1882.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "action of installing," in reference to church offices or other positions, 源自 中古拉丁语 installationem (主格 installatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of installare （参见 install). Of machinery, etc., "act of setting up, a placing in position for use," 自 1882 年起.

example.en: The installation of the new security system took the entire afternoon.
example.zh: 新安防系统的安装花了整整一个下午。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "urgency, insistence" (a sense now archaic), from Old French instance "effort, application; urgency, eagerness, anxiety" (13c.), from Latin instantia "presence, effort, intention; earnestness, urgency," literally "a standing near," from instans (see instant).

In logic, "a fact, a case, an example" (a sense in English from early 15c.), from Medieval Latin instantia, which translated Greek enstasis. This led to for instance "as an example" (1650s), and the noun phrase give (someone) a for instance (1953, American English). The general sense "anything that illustrates a general type" was in use by 19c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "urgency, insistence" (a sense 现在 古旧), 源自 古法语 instance "effort, application; urgency, eagerness, anxiety" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 instantia "presence, effort, intention; earnestness, urgency," 字面义为 "a standing near," 源自 instans （参见 instant). In logic, "a fact, a case, an example" (a sense in English 源自 15 世纪初), 源自 中古拉丁语 instantia, which translated 希腊语 enstasis. This led to for instance "as an example" (1650 年代), and the 名词 phrase give (someone) a for instance (1953 年, American English). The general sense "anything that illustrates a general type" was in use by 19 世纪

entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "moment in time, infinitely short space of time," 源自 为 … 的名词用法 古法语 instant "near, immediate, at hand; assiduous, urgent" （参见 instant （形）). 同源词：Instanted; instanting.

entries.etymology: 1590s, contraction of Middle English prepositional phrase ine stede (early 13c.; see stead), itself a loan-translation of Latin in loco (French en lieu de). Typically written as two words until mid-17c.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, contraction of 中古英语 prepositional phrase ine stede (13 世纪初; 参见 stead), itself a loan-translation of 拉丁语 in loco (法语 en lieu de). Typically written as two words until 17 世纪中期

example.en: He decided to walk instead of taking the bus.

entries.etymology:
early 15c., "a prompting" (a sense now obsolete), from Old French instinct (14c.) or directly from Latin instinctus "instigation, impulse, inspiration," noun use of past participle of instinguere "to incite, impel," from in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + stinguere "prick, goad," from PIE *steig- "to prick, stick, pierce" (see stick (v.)).

Meaning "animal faculty of intuitive perception" is from mid-15c., from notion of "natural prompting." General sense of "natural tendency" is first recorded 1560s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "a prompting" (a sense 今废), 源自 古法语 instinct (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 instinctus "instigation, impulse, inspiration," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 instinguere "to incite, impel," 源自 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + stinguere "prick, goad," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *steig- "to prick, stick, pierce" （参见 stick （动）). 义为 "animal faculty of intuitive perception" 始于 15 世纪中期, 源自 概念 "natural prompting." General 语义 "natural tendency" is 首见于 1560 年代.

example.en: The mother bird acted on instinct to protect her chicks from danger.
example.zh: 那只母鸟凭借本能保护她的雏鸟免受危险。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "to establish in office, appoint," from Latin institutus, past participle of instituere "to set up, put in place; arrange; found, establish; appoint, designate; govern, administer; teach, instruct," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + statuere "establish, to cause to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand," with derivatives meaning "place or thing that is standing" (see stet). General sense of "set up, found, introduce" first attested late 15c. Related: Instituted; instituting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to establish in office, appoint," 源自 拉丁语 institutus, 为 … 的过去分词 instituere "to set up, put in place; arrange; found, establish; appoint, designate; govern, administer; teach, instruct," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + statuere "establish, to cause to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand," with derivatives 意为 "place or thing that is standing" （参见 stet). General 语义 "set up, found, introduce" 最早见于 15 世纪晚期 同源词：Instituted; instituting.

example.en: She was awarded a fellowship at a prestigious research institute.
example.zh: 她获得了一所知名研究所的奖学金。

entries.etymology:
c. 1400, "action of establishing or founding (a system of government, a religious order, etc.)," from Old French institucion "foundation; thing established" (12c.), from Latin institutionem (nominative institutio) "a disposition, arrangement; instruction, education," noun of state from institutus (see institute (v.)).

Meaning "established law or practice" is from 1550s. Meaning "establishment or organization for the promotion of some charity" is from 1707. Jocular or colloquial use for "anything that's been around a long time" is from 1837.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "action of establishing or founding (a system of government, a religious order, etc.)," 源自 古法语 institucion "foundation; thing established" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 institutionem (主格 institutio) "a disposition, arrangement; instruction, education," 名词 of state 源自 institutus （参见 institute （动）). 义为 "established law or practice" 始于 1550 年代. 义为 "establishment or organization for the promotion of some charity" 始于 1707 年. Jocular or 口语 use for "anything that's been around a long time" 始于 1837 年.

example.en: The research was funded by a well-known academic institution.
example.zh: 这项研究由一所知名学术机构资助。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "of or pertaining to an institution," from institution + -al (1). Related: Institutionally.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "of or pertaining to an institution," 源自 institution + -al (1). 同源词：Institutionally.

example.en: The reform aimed to address deep institutional barriers to equality.
example.zh: 这项改革旨在解决深层的制度性平等壁垒。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to tell, inform, impart knowledge or information," also "furnish with authoritative directions," from Latin instructus, past participle of instruere "arrange, prepare, set in order; inform, teach," literally "to build, erect," from in- "on" (see in- (2)) + struere "to pile, build" (see structure (n.)). Related: Instructed; instructing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to tell, inform, impart knowledge or information," also "furnish with authoritative directions," 源自 拉丁语 instructus, 为 … 的过去分词 instruere "arrange, prepare, set in order; inform, teach," 字面义为 "to build, erect," 源自 in- "on" （参见 in- (2)) + struere "to pile, build" （参见 structure （名）). 同源词：Instructed; instructing.

example.en: The supervisor instruct the new employees to follow all safety procedures.
