definitionLines: n..（p.）指令，指示，说明； 教学，教导
entries.definition: n..（p.）指令，指示，说明； 教学，教导
entries.etymology:
c. 1400, instruccioun, "action or process of teaching," from Old French instruccion (14c., Modern French instruction), from Latin instructionem (nominative instructio) "an array, arrangement," in Late Latin "teaching," from past participle stem of instruere "arrange, prepare, set in order; inform, teach," from in- "on" (see in- (2)) + struere "to pile, build" (see structure (n.)).

Meaning "an authoritative direction telling someone what to do; a document giving such directions," is early 15c. Related: Instructions.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, instruccioun, "action or process of teaching," 源自 古法语 instruccion (14 世纪, 现代法语 instruction), 源自 拉丁语 instructionem (主格 instructio) "an array, arrangement," in 晚期拉丁语 "teaching," 源自 past participle stem of instruere "arrange, prepare, set in order; inform, teach," 源自 in- "on" （参见 in- (2)) + struere "to pile, build" （参见 structure （名）). 义为 "an authoritative direction telling someone what to do; a document giving such directions," is 15 世纪初 同源词：Instructions.

example.en: Read the instruction on the label carefully before taking this medication.
example.zh: 服用此药之前，请仔细阅读标签上的说明。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., "musical instrument, mechanical apparatus for producing musical sounds," from Old French instrument, enstrument "means, device; musical instrument" (14c., earlier estrument, 13c.) and directly from Latin instrumentum "a tool, an implement; means, furtherance; apparatus, furniture; ornament, dress, embellishment; a commission, authorization; a document," from instruere "arrange, furnish" (see instruct (v.)).  The word in other Germanic languages also is from French.

In English the meaning "a means, an agency" is from mid-14c. The sense of "hand-tool, implement, utensil, something used to produce a mechanical effect" is from early 14c. "Now usually distinguished from a tool, as being used for more delicate work or for artistic or scientific purposes" [OED]. The legal meaning "written document by which formal expression is given to a legal act" is from early 15c. Formerly also used of body parts or organs with special functions.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "musical instrument, mechanical apparatus for producing musical sounds," 源自 古法语 instrument, enstrument "means, device; musical instrument" (14 世纪, earlier estrument, 13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 instrumentum "a tool, an implement; means, furtherance; apparatus, furniture; ornament, dress, embellishment; a commission, authorization; a document," 源自 instruere "arrange, furnish" （参见 instruct （动）). The word in other 日耳曼语 languages also 始于 法语. In English the 意为 "a means, an agency" 始于 14 世纪中期 The 语义 "hand-tool, implement, utensil, something used to produce a mechanical effect" 始于 14 世纪初 "Now usually distinguished from a tool, as being used for more delicate work or for artistic or scientific purposes" [OED]. The legal 意为 "written document by which formal expression is given to a legal act" 始于 15 世纪初 Formerly also used of body parts or organs with special functions.

example.en: The surgeon selected a sterile instrument from the tray before making the incision.
example.zh: 外科医生在切开之前从托盘上选了一件消毒器械。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "make into an island," from Late Latin insulatus "made like an island," from insula "island" (see isle). Sense of "place in an isolated situation, cause (someone or something) to be detached from surroundings" is from 1785. Electrical/chemical sense of "block from electricity or heat" (by interposition of a non-conductor) is from 1742. Related: Insulated; insulating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "make into an island," 源自 晚期拉丁语 insulatus "made like an island," 源自 insula "island" （参见 isle). 义为 "place in an isolated situation, cause (someone or something) to be detached from surroundings" 始于 1785 年. Electrical/chemical 语义 "block from electricity or heat" (by interposition of a non-conductor) 始于 1742 年. 同源词：Insulated; insulating.

entries.etymology:
1560s, "triumph over in an arrogant way" (obsolete), from Middle French insulter "to wrong; reproach; triumph arrogantly over," earlier "to leap upon" (14c.) and directly from Latin insultare "to assail, to make a sudden leap upon," which was used by the time of Cicero in sense of "to insult, scoff at, revile," frequentative of insilire "leap at or upon," from in- "on, at" (see in- (2)) + salire "to leap" (see salient (adj.)).

Sense of "verbally abuse, affront, assail with disrespect, offer an indignity to" is from 1610s. Related: Insulted; insulting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "triumph over in an arrogant way" (已废), 源自 中古法语 insulter "to wrong; reproach; triumph arrogantly over," earlier "to leap upon" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 insultare "to assail, to make a sudden leap upon," which was used by the time of Cicero in 语义 "to insult, scoff at, revile," 为 … 的反复体 insilire "leap at or upon," 源自 in- "on, at" （参见 in- (2)) + salire "to leap" （参见 salient （形）). 义为 "verbally abuse, affront, assail with disrespect, offer an indignity to" 始于 1610 年代. 同源词：Insulted; insulting.

example.en: His remark was meant to insult her in front of the whole class.
example.zh: 他的话是故意在全班同学面前羞辱她。

entries.etymology:
1550s, "engagement to marry," a variant of ensurance "an assurance, pledge, guarantee," from Old French enseurance "assurance," from ensurer, from en- "make" (see en- (1)) + sur "safe, secure, undoubted" (see sure (adj.)).

Commercial sense of "security against loss or death in exchange for payment" is from 1650s. Assurance was the older word for this specific sense (late 16c.). Compare insure.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "engagement to marry," a 为 … 的变体 ensurance "an assurance, pledge, guarantee," 源自 古法语 enseurance "assurance," 源自 ensurer, 源自 en- "make" （参见 en- (1)) + sur "safe, secure, undoubted" （参见 sure （形）). Commercial 语义 "security against loss or death in exchange for payment" 始于 1650 年代. Assurance was the older word for this specific sense (16 世纪晚期). 对比 insure.

example.en: All employees are required to have health insurance before starting work.
example.zh: 所有员工在入职前都必须购买健康保险。

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., insuren, spelling variant of ensuren "to assure, give formal assurance" (late 14c.), also "make secure, make safe" (c. 1400), from Anglo-French enseurer, Old French ensurer, from en- "make" (see en- (1)) + seur, sur "safe, secure, undoubted" (see sure (adj.)).

The particular commercial senses of "make safe against loss by payment of premiums; undertake to ensure against loss, etc." are from mid-17c. (replacing assure in that meaning). Related: Insured; insuring.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, insuren, spelling 为 … 的变体 ensuren "to assure, give formal assurance" (14 世纪晚期), also "make secure, make safe" (约 1400 年), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 enseurer, 古法语 ensurer, 源自 en- "make" （参见 en- (1)) + seur, sur "safe, secure, undoubted" （参见 sure （形）). The particular commercial senses of "make safe against loss by payment of premiums; undertake to ensure against loss, etc." 始于 17 世纪中期 (replacing assure in that 意为). 同源词：Insured; insuring.

example.en: It is wise to insure your home against fire and natural disasters.
example.zh: 为房屋投保，以防火灾和自然灾害，是明智之举。

entries.definition: a.起义的；叛乱的 n. 叛乱者；起义者
entries.etymology:
"one who rises in revolt" against a government or its laws, 1745, from Latin insurgentem (nominative insurgens), present participle of insurgere "rise up, lift oneself; rise against; stand high, gather force," from in- "against," or here perhaps merely intensive, + surgere "to rise" (see surge (n.)).

An obsolete verb insurge (from French insurger) "to rise in opposition or insurrection" was common 16c. For verb forms 19c. writers sometimes turned to insurrectionize or insurrect.
entries.etymologyZh: "one who rises in revolt" against a government or its laws, 1745 年, 源自 拉丁语 insurgentem (主格 insurgens), 为 … 的现在分词 insurgere "rise up, lift oneself; rise against; stand high, gather force," 源自 in- "against," or here 或许 merely intensive, + surgere "to rise" （参见 surge （名）). An 已废 动词 insurge (源自 法语 insurger) "to rise in opposition or insurrection" was common 16 世纪 For 动词 forms 19 世纪 writers 有时 turned to insurrectionize or insurrect.

definitionLines: a.完整的；原封不动的；未受损 伤的
entries.definition: a.完整的；原封不动的；未受损 伤的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Latin intactus "untouched, uninjured; undefiled, chaste; unsubdued," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + tactus, past participle of tangere "to touch" (see tangent (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 intactus "untouched, uninjured; undefiled, chaste; unsubdued," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + tactus, 为 … 的过去分词 tangere "to touch" （参见 tangent （形）).

example.en: The ancient manuscript was found intact despite centuries of neglect.
example.zh: 那份古老的手稿尽管被忽视了数百年，仍被发现保存完好。

entries.etymology: late 15c., "of or pertaining to a whole; intrinsic, belonging as a part to a whole," from Middle French intégral (14c.), from Medieval Latin integralis "forming a whole," from Latin integer "whole" (see integer). Related: Integrally. As a noun, 1610s, from the adjective.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "of or pertaining to a whole; intrinsic, belonging as a part to a whole," 源自 中古法语 intégral (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 integralis "forming a whole," 源自 拉丁语 integer "whole" （参见 integer). 同源词：Integrally. 作名词时, 1610 年代, 源自 形容词.

example.en: Regular feedback is an integral part of any effective training program.
example.zh: 定期反馈是任何有效培训计划不可或缺的组成部分。

definitionLines: n. 正直，诚实；完整，完全，完 整性
entries.definition: n. 正直，诚实；完整，完全，完 整性
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "innocence, blamelessness; chastity, purity," from Old French integrité or directly from Latin integritatem (nominative integritas) "soundness, wholeness, completeness," figuratively "purity, correctness, blamelessness," from integer "whole" (see integer). Sense of "wholeness, perfect condition" is mid-15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "innocence, blamelessness; chastity, purity," 源自 古法语 integrité or 直接源自 拉丁语 integritatem (主格 integritas) "soundness, wholeness, completeness," figuratively "purity, correctness, blamelessness," 源自 integer "whole" （参见 integer). 义为 "wholeness, perfect condition" is 15 世纪中期

example.en: A judge must maintain absolute integrity and refuse all gifts from parties in a case.
example.zh: 法官必须保持绝对的廉洁，拒绝案件当事方的一切馈赠。

definitionLines: n. 智力；有才智的人；知识分子
entries.definition: n. 智力；有才智的人；知识分子
entries.etymology: "the sum of the cognitive facilities (except sense or sense and imagination), the capacity for reasoning truth," late 14c. (but little used before 16c.), from Old French intellect "intellectual capacity" (13c.), and directly from Latin intellectus "discernment, a perception, understanding," noun use of past participle of intelligere "to understand, discern" (see intelligence). The Latin word was used to translate Greek nous "mind, thought, intellect" in Aristotle.
entries.etymologyZh: "the sum of the cognitive facilities (except sense or sense and imagination), the capacity for reasoning truth," 14 世纪晚期 (but little used before 16 世纪), 源自 古法语 intellect "intellectual capacity" (13 世纪), and 直接源自 拉丁语 intellectus "discernment, a perception, understanding," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 intelligere "to understand, discern" （参见 intelligence). The 拉丁语 word was used to translate 希腊语 nous "mind, thought, intellect" in Aristotle.

definitionLines: a. 智力的；聪明的；理智的
entries.definition: a. 智力的；聪明的；理智的 n. 知识分子
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "grasped by the understanding" (rather than by the senses), from Old French intellectuel (13c.) and directly from Latin intellectualis "relating to the understanding," from intellectus "discernment, understanding," noun use of past participle of intelligere "to understand, discern" (see intelligence).

Sense of "characterized by a high degree of intellect" is from 1819. Meaning "appealing to or engaging the mental powers" is from 1834. Intellectual property "products of the intellect" is attested from 1845. Adjective formations in the sense "of or pertaining to the intellect" included intellective (early 15c.), intellectile (1670s).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "grasped by the understanding" (rather than by the senses), 源自 古法语 intellectuel (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 intellectualis "relating to the understanding," 源自 intellectus "discernment, understanding," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 intelligere "to understand, discern" （参见 intelligence). 义为 "characterized by a high degree of intellect" 始于 1819 年. 义为 "appealing to or engaging the mental powers" 始于 1834 年. Intellectual property "products of the intellect" 见于 1845 年. Adjective formations in the sense "of or pertaining to the intellect" included intellective (15 世纪初), intellectile (1670 年代).

example.en: The professor was known for his intellectual curiosity and wide reading.
example.zh: 这位教授以其学术好奇心和广泛阅读而著称。

definitionLines: n. 智力，理解力；情报，消息， 报导
entries.definition: n. 智力，理解力；情报，消息， 报导
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "the highest faculty of the mind, capacity for comprehending general truths;" c. 1400, "faculty of understanding, comprehension," from Old French intelligence (12c.) and directly from Latin intelligentia, intellegentia "understanding, knowledge, power of discerning; art, skill, taste," from intelligentem (nominative intelligens) "discerning, appreciative," present participle of intelligere "to understand, comprehend, come to know," from inter- "between" (see inter-) + legere "choose, pick out, read" (see lecture (n.)).

Meaning "superior understanding, sagacity, quality of being intelligent" is from early 15c. Sense of "information received or imparted, news" first recorded mid-15c., especially "secret information from spies" (1580s). Meaning "a being endowed with understanding or intelligence" is late 14c. Intelligence quotient first recorded 1921 (see I.Q.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "the highest faculty of the mind, capacity for comprehending general truths;" 约 1400 年, "faculty of understanding, comprehension," 源自 古法语 intelligence (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 intelligentia, intellegentia "understanding, knowledge, power of discerning; art, skill, taste," 源自 intelligentem (主格 intelligens) "discerning, appreciative," 为 … 的现在分词 intelligere "to understand, comprehend, come to know," 源自 inter- "between" （参见 inter-) + legere "choose, pick out, read" （参见 lecture （名）). 义为 "superior understanding, sagacity, quality of being intelligent" 始于 15 世纪初 义为 "information received or imparted, news" 首见于 15 世纪中期, 尤指 "secret information from spies" (1580 年代). 义为 "a being endowed with understanding or intelligence" is 14 世纪晚期 Intelligence quotient 首见于 1921 年 （参见 I.Q.).

example.en: Emotional intelligence is just as important as IQ in the workplace.
example.zh: 在职场中，情商和智商同样重要。

entries.etymology: c. 1500, a back-formation from intelligence or else from Latin intelligentem (nominative intelligens), present participle of intelligere. Intelligent design, as a name for an alternative to atheistic cosmology and the theory of evolution, is from 1999. Related: Intelligently.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, a back-formation 源自 intelligence or else 源自 拉丁语 intelligentem (主格 intelligens), 为 … 的现在分词 intelligere. Intelligent design, 作为 name for an alternative to atheistic cosmology and the theory of evolution, 始于 1999 年. 同源词：Intelligently.

example.en: Dolphins are among the most intelligent species on earth, with brains capable of abstract reasoning.
example.zh: 海豚是地球上最聪明的物种之一,其大脑能够进行抽象推理。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "able to understand, intelligent," from Latin intelligibilis, intellegibilis "that can understand; that can be understood," from intellegere "to understand, come to know" (see intelligence). In Middle English also "to be grasped by the intellect" (rather than the senses). In English, sense of "capable of being understood, that can be understood" first recorded c. 1600. Related: Intelligibly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "able to understand, intelligent," 源自 拉丁语 intelligibilis, intellegibilis "that can understand; that can be understood," 源自 intellegere "to understand, come to know" （参见 intelligence). In 中古英语 also "to be grasped by the intellect" (rather than the senses). In English, 语义 "capable of being understood, that can be understood" 首见于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Intelligibly.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, entenden, "direct one's attention to, pay attention, give heed," from Old French entendre, intendre "to direct one's attention" (in Modern French principally "to hear"), from Latin intendere "turn one's attention, strain (in quest of something), be zealous," literally "stretch out, extend," from in- "toward" (see in- (2)) + tendere "to stretch" (see tenet).

Sense of "have as a plan, have in mind or purpose" (late 14c.) was present in Latin. A Germanic word for this was ettle, from Old Norse ætla "to think, conjecture, propose," from Proto-Germanic *ahta "consideration, attention" (source also of Old English eaht, German acht). Related: Intended; intending.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, entenden, "direct one's attention to, pay attention, give heed," 源自 古法语 entendre, intendre "to direct one's attention" (in 现代法语 principally "to hear"), 源自 拉丁语 intendere "turn one's attention, strain (in quest of something), be zealous," 字面义为 "stretch out, extend," 源自 in- "toward" （参见 in- (2)) + tendere "to stretch" （参见 tenet). 义为 "have as a plan, have in mind or purpose" (14 世纪晚期) was present in 拉丁语. A 日耳曼语 word for this was ettle, 源自 古北欧语 ætla "to think, conjecture, propose," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ahta "consideration, attention" (source also of 古英语 eaht, 德语 acht). 同源词：Intended; intending.

example.en: The company intend to launch its new product line next spring.
example.zh: 该公司打算在明年春天推出新产品线。

entries.etymology: early 15c., of situations or qualities, "great, extreme," from Old French intense (13c.), from Latin intensus "stretched, strained, high-strung, tight," originally past participle of intendere in its literal sense of "stretch out, strain" (see intend). From 1630s of persons, "high-strung." Related: Intensely; intenseness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, of situations or qualities, "great, extreme," 源自 古法语 intense (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 intensus "stretched, strained, high-strung, tight," 原义为 为 … 的过去分词 intendere in its literal 语义 "stretch out, strain" （参见 intend). From 1630 年代 of persons, "high-strung." 同源词：Intensely; intenseness.

example.en: The final debate between the two candidates was so intense that it trended online for days.
example.zh: 两位候选人之间的最终辩论如此激烈，以至于在网上热议了好几天。

definitionLines: vt. 使加强，使强化；使变激烈
entries.definition: vi.增强，强化；变激烈 vt. 使加强，使强化；使变激烈
entries.etymology: 1817 (transitive), from intense + -ify, first attested in Coleridge, in place of intend, which he said no longer was felt as connected with intense. Intransitive sense is from 1845. Middle English used intensen (v.) "to increase (something), strengthen, intensify," early 15c. Related: Intensified; intensifying.
entries.etymologyZh: 1817 年 (transitive), 源自 intense + -ify, 最早见于 in Coleridge, in place of intend, which he said no longer was felt as connected with intense. Intransitive sense 始于 1845 年. 中古英语 used intensen （动） "to increase (something), strengthen, intensify," 15 世纪初 同源词：Intensified; intensifying.

example.en: The dispute began to intensify into a full-blown international crisis.
example.zh: 这场争端开始升级为一场全面的国际危机。

definitionLines: n. 强烈，剧烈，强度，亮度
entries.definition: n. 强烈，剧烈，强度，亮度
entries.etymology: 1660s, from intense + -ity. Earlier was intenseness (1610s). A scientific term originally; sense of "extreme depth of feeling" attested by 1830.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 intense + -ity. Earlier was intenseness (1610 年代). A scientific term 原义为; 语义 "extreme depth of feeling" attested 截至 1830 年.

example.en: The intensity of her grief was evident in her voice.
example.zh: 她声音中流露出明显的悲痛强度。

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., "intense, fervent, great," from Old French intensif (14c.) and Medieval Latin intensivus, from Latin intens-, past participle stem of intendere "turn one's attention; strain, stretch" (see intend).

Grammatical meaning "expressing intensity" is from c. 1600; as a noun, "something expressing intensity," 1813, from the adjective. Alternative intensitive is a malformation. Intensive care attested from 1958. Related: Intensively; intensiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "intense, fervent, great," 源自 古法语 intensif (14 世纪) and 中古拉丁语 intensivus, 源自 拉丁语 intens-, past participle stem of intendere "turn one's attention; strain, stretch" （参见 intend). Grammatical 意为 "expressing intensity" 始于 约 1600 年; 作名词时, "something expressing intensity," 1813 年, 源自 形容词. Alternative intensitive is a malformation. Intensive care attested 自 1958 年起. 同源词：Intensively; intensiveness.

example.en: The athletes underwent intensive training for the upcoming championship.
example.zh: 运动员们为即将到来的锦标赛进行了密集训练。

entries.etymology: late 14c., entencioun, "purpose, design, aim or object; will, wish, desire, that which is intended," from Old French entencion "intent, purpose, aspiration; will; thought" (12c.), from Latin intentionem (nominative intentio) "a stretching out, straining, exertion, effort; attention," noun of action from intendere "to turn one's attention," literally "to stretch out" (see intend). Also in Middle English "emotion, feelings; heart, mind, mental faculties, understanding."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, entencioun, "purpose, design, aim or object; will, wish, desire, that which is intended," 源自 古法语 entencion "intent, purpose, aspiration; will; thought" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 intentionem (主格 intentio) "a stretching out, straining, exertion, effort; attention," 名词 of action 源自 intendere "to turn one's attention," 字面义为 "to stretch out" （参见 intend). Also in 中古英语 "emotion, feelings; heart, mind, mental faculties, understanding."

example.en: She had no intention of giving up despite the many setbacks.
example.zh: 尽管遭遇了很多挫折，她没有任何放弃的打算。

entries.etymology: "act on each other, act reciprocally," 1805, from inter- + act (v.). Related: Interacted; interacting.
entries.etymologyZh: "act on each other, act reciprocally," 1805 年, 源自 inter- + act （动）. 同源词：Interacted; interacting.

example.en: Students are encouraged to interact with their classmates during group projects.
example.zh: 学生在小组项目中被鼓励与同学互动交流。

entries.etymology: 1812, from inter- + action.
entries.etymologyZh: 1812 年, 源自 inter- + action.

example.en: Regular face-to-face interaction with classmates builds social skills.
example.zh: 与同学定期面对面互动有助于培养社交技能。

entries.etymology: 1711, "that concerns, important" (archaic), present-participle adjective from interest (v.). Meaning "engaging the attention, so as to excite interest" is from 1751. Related: Interestingly. Euphemistic phrase interesting condition, etc., "pregnant" is from 1748.
entries.etymologyZh: 1711 年, "that concerns, important" (古旧), present-participle 形容词 源自 interest （动）. 义为 "engaging the attention, so as to excite interest" 始于 1751 年. 同源词：Interestingly. Euphemistic phrase interesting condition, etc., "pregnant" 始于 1748 年.

example.en: The documentary about deep-sea creatures was truly interesting.
example.zh: 这部关于深海生物的纪录片真的很有趣。

entries.etymology:
formerly also enterfere, mid-15c., "to strike against," from Middle French enterferir "exchange blows, strike each other," from entre- "between" (see entre-) + ferir "to strike," from Latin ferire "to knock, strike," related to Latin forare "to bore, pierce" (see bore (v.), and compare punch (v.), which has both the senses "to hit" and "to make a hole in").

Figurative sense of "to meddle with, oppose unrightfully" is from 1630s. Related: Interfered; interfering. Modern French interférer is from English.
entries.etymologyZh: formerly also enterfere, 15 世纪中期, "to strike against," 源自 中古法语 enterferir "exchange blows, strike each other," 源自 entre- "between" （参见 entre-) + ferir "to strike," 源自 拉丁语 ferire "to knock, strike," related to 拉丁语 forare "to bore, pierce" （参见 bore （动）, and 对比 punch （动）, which has both the senses "to hit" and "to make a hole in"). Figurative 语义 "to meddle with, oppose unrightfully" 始于 1630 年代. 同源词：Interfered; interfering. 现代法语 interférer 始于 English.

example.en: Please do not interfere with the experiment while it is running.
example.zh: 实验进行期间，请不要干扰实验。

entries.etymology: 1783, "intermeddling," from interfere on model of difference, etc. In physics, in reference to the mutual action of waves on each other, from 1802, coined in this sense by English scientist Dr. Thomas Young (1773-1829). Telephoning (later broadcasting) sense is from 1887. In chess from 1913; in U.S. football from 1894.
entries.etymologyZh: 1783 年, "intermeddling," 源自 interfere on model of difference, etc. In physics, in reference to the mutual action of waves on each other, 自 1802 年起, coined in this sense by English scientist Dr. Thomas Young (1773 年-1829 年). Telephoning (later broadcasting) sense 始于 1887 年. In chess 自 1913 年起; in U.S. football 自 1894 年起.

example.en: The neighbors complained about the constant interference in their private affairs.
example.zh: 邻居们抱怨对他们私事的不断干涉。

definitionLines: a.临时的，暂时的；中间的； 间歇的
n. 过渡时期，中间时期
entries.definition: a.临时的，暂时的；中间的； 间歇的 n. 过渡时期，中间时期
entries.etymology: "time intervening," 1560s, from Latin interim (adv.) "in the meantime, meanwhile," originally "in the midst of that," from inter- "between" (see inter-) + im, ancient adverb from stem of pronoun is "this, that." As an adjective from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: "time intervening," 1560 年代, 源自 拉丁语 interim （副） "in the meantime, meanwhile," 原义为 "in the midst of that," 源自 inter- "between" （参见 inter-) + im, ancient 副词 源自 stem of pronoun is "this, that." 作形容词时 源自 约 1600 年.

entries.definition: n. 内部，内地 a.内部的，里面的；内地的
entries.etymology: late 15c., from Latin interior "inner, interior, middle," comparative adjective of inter "within" (see inter-). Specific meaning "away from the coast, of the interior parts of a country" is from 1777. Interior decoration first attested 1769; interior decorator is from 1830. Interior design from 1927.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 interior "inner, interior, middle," comparative 形容词 of inter "within" （参见 inter-). Specific 意为 "away from the coast, of the interior parts of a country" 始于 1777 年. Interior decoration 最早见于 1769 年; interior decorator 始于 1830 年. Interior design 自 1927 年起.

example.en: The interior of the cathedral was decorated with stunning gold mosaics.
example.zh: 大教堂的内部装饰着令人叹为观止的金色马赛克。

entries.definition: a.中间的，居中的 n.中间体，媒介物
entries.etymology: "being or occurring between" (two things), early 15c., from Medieval Latin intermediatus "lying between," from Latin intermedius "that which is between," from inter- "between" (see inter-) + medius "in the middle" (see medial (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: "being or occurring between" (two things), 15 世纪初, 源自 中古拉丁语 intermediatus "lying between," 源自 拉丁语 intermedius "that which is between," 源自 inter- "between" （参见 inter-) + medius "in the middle" （参见 medial （形）).

definitionLines: a.内的，内部的；国内的，内政 的
entries.definition: a.内的，内部的；国内的，内政 的
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "extending toward the interior," from Medieval Latin internalis, from Latin internus "within, inward, internal," figuratively "domestic," expanded from pre-Latin *interos, *interus "on the inside, inward," from PIE *en-ter- (source also of Old Church Slavonic anter, Sanskrit antar "within, between," Old High German unter "between," and the "down" sense of Old English under); suffixed (comparative) form of *en "in" (see in (adv.)).

Meaning "situated within" is from 1590s. Meaning "of or pertaining to the domestic affairs of a country (as in internal revenue) is from 1795; the notion is "pertaining to the subject itself; independent of others." Internal-combustion in reference to an engine in which fuel is burned inside it, is from 1884. Related: Internally.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "extending toward the interior," 源自 中古拉丁语 internalis, 源自 拉丁语 internus "within, inward, internal," figuratively "domestic," expanded 源自 pre-拉丁语 *interos, *interus "on the inside, inward," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *en-ter- (source also of Old Church Slavonic anter, 梵语 antar "within, between," 古高地德语 unter "between," and the "down" 语义 古英语 under); suffixed (comparative) form of *en "in" （参见 in （副）). 义为 "situated within" 始于 1590 年代. 义为 "of or pertaining to the domestic affairs of a country (as in internal revenue) is from 1795; the notion is "pertaining to the subject itself; independent of others." Internal-combustion in reference to an engine in which fuel is burned inside it, 始于 1884 年. 同源词：Internally.

example.en: The committee conducted an internal review of its financial procedures.
example.zh: 委员会对其财务程序进行了内部审查。

entries.etymology:
1780, coined by Jeremy Bentham from inter- "between" + national (adj.). In the phrase international jurisprudence. He footnotes the word with:

As a noun and with a capital -i-, it is short for International Working Men's Association, a socialistic worker's movement with global aims, the first chapter of which was founded in London by Marx in 1864. The group lends its name to "The Internationale" (from fem. of French international, which is from English), the socialist hymn, written 1871 by Eugène Pottier. International Dateline is from 1882. Related: Internationally (1821).
entries.etymologyZh: 1780 年, coined by Jeremy Bentham 源自 inter- "between" + national （形）. In the phrase international jurisprudence. He footnotes the word with: 作名词时 and with a capital -i-, it is short for International Working Men's Association, a socialistic worker's movement with global aims, the first chapter of which was founded in London by Marx 于 1864 年. The group lends its name to "The Internationale" (源自 fem. of 法语 international, which 始于 English), the socialist hymn, written 1871 年 by Eugène Pottier. International Dateline 始于 1882 年. 同源词：Internationally (1821 年).

example.en: The two countries signed an international trade agreement last week.
example.zh: 两国上周签署了一项国际贸易协定。

entries.etymology: 1984, "the linked computer networks of the U.S. Defense Department," shortened from internetwork, inter-network, which was used from 1972 in reference to (then-hypothetical) networks involving many separate computers. From inter- "between" + network (n.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1984 年, "the linked computer networks of the U.S. Defense Department," shortened 源自 internetwork, inter-network, which was used 自 1972 年起 in reference to (之后-hypothetical) networks involving many separate computers. From inter- "between" + network （名）.

example.en: Millions of people use the internet to shop and bank every day.
example.zh: 每天有数百万人通过互联网购物和进行银行业务。

definitionLines: vt. 口译，翻译；解释，说明
entries.definition: vt. 口译，翻译；解释，说明
entries.etymology: late 14c., "expound the meaning of, render clear or explicit," from Old French interpreter "explain; translate" (13c.) and directly from Latin interpretari "explain, expound, understand," from interpres "agent, translator," from inter- "between" (see inter-) + second element of uncertain origin, perhaps related to Sanskrit prath- "to spread abroad," PIE *per- (5) "to traffic in, sell" (see pornography). Related: Interpreted; interpreting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "expound the meaning of, render clear or explicit," 源自 古法语 interpreter "explain; translate" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 interpretari "explain, expound, understand," 源自 interpres "agent, translator," 源自 inter- "between" （参见 inter-) + second element 来源存疑, 或许 related to 梵语 prath- "to spread abroad," 原始印欧语 (PIE) *per- (5) "to traffic in, sell" （参见 pornography). 同源词：Interpreted; interpreting.

example.en: Different critics tend to interpret the poem in very different ways.
example.zh: 不同的评论家往往以截然不同的方式解读这首诗。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c. "a translated text, a translation" (late 13c. in Anglo-French), from Old French interpretacion, entrepretatiun "explanation, translation" (12c.) and directly from Latin interpretationem (nominative interpretatio) "explanation, exposition," noun of action from past participle stem of interpretari "explain, expound; understand" (see interpret).

From late 14c. as "act or process of explaining or interpreting; an explanation; construction placed upon an action." Meaning "dramatic or musical representation" is from 1880.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期 "a translated text, a translation" (13 世纪晚期 in 盎格鲁-法语), 源自 古法语 interpretacion, entrepretatiun "explanation, translation" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 interpretationem (主格 interpretatio) "explanation, exposition," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of interpretari "explain, expound; understand" （参见 interpret). From 14 世纪晚期 as "act or process of explaining or interpreting; an explanation; construction placed upon an action." 义为 "dramatic or musical representation" 始于 1880 年.

example.en: Different scholars offer different interpretations of this ancient poem.
example.zh: 不同学者对这首古诗给出了不同的解读。

entries.etymology: "one who translates spoken languages; a translator of written texts," late 14c., from Old French interpreteor, entrepreteur, from Late Latin interpretator "an explainer," agent noun from interpretari "explain, expound" (see interpret).
entries.etymologyZh: "one who translates spoken languages; a translator of written texts," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 interpreteor, entrepreteur, 源自 晚期拉丁语 interpretator "an explainer," agent 名词 源自 interpretari "explain, expound" （参见 interpret).

example.en: The conference hired a skilled interpreter to translate the speeches into three languages.
example.zh: 会议聘请了一名技术熟练的口译员，将演讲翻译成三种语言。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "a question;" c. 1500, "a questioning; a set of questions," from Old French interrogacion "a questioning" (13c.) or directly from Latin interrogationem (nominative interrogatio) "a question; questioning; judicial inquiry," noun of action from past participle stem of interrogare "to ask, question, inquire; interrogate judicially, cross-examine," from inter- "between" (see inter-) + rogare "to ask, to question" (see rogation).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a question;" 约 1500 年, "a questioning; a set of questions," 源自 古法语 interrogacion "a questioning" (13 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 interrogationem (主格 interrogatio) "a question; questioning; judicial inquiry," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of interrogare "to ask, question, inquire; interrogate judicially, cross-examine," 源自 inter- "between" （参见 inter-) + rogare "to ask, to question" （参见 rogation).

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "to interfere with a legal right," from Latin interruptus, past participle of interrumpere "break apart, break off, break through," from inter- "between" (see inter-) + rumpere "to break" (see rupture (n.), and compare corrupt (adj.)). Meaning "to break into, break in upon, disturb the action of" (especially of speech) is from early 15c. in English (it is also in Latin). Related: Interrupted; interrupting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "to interfere with a legal right," 源自 拉丁语 interruptus, 为 … 的过去分词 interrumpere "break apart, break off, break through," 源自 inter- "between" （参见 inter-) + rumpere "to break" （参见 rupture （名）, and 对比 corrupt （形）). 义为 "to break into, break in upon, disturb the action of" (尤指 of speech) 始于 15 世纪初 in English (it is also in 拉丁语). 同源词：Interrupted; interrupting.

example.en: It is rude to interrupt someone while they are speaking in a meeting.
example.zh: 在会议上打断正在发言的人是不礼貌的。

entries.etymology:
early 14c., "time elapsed between two actions or events," from Old French intervalle "interval, interim" (14c.), earlier entreval (13c.) and directly from Late Latin intervallum "a space between, an interval of time, a distance," originally "space between palisades or ramparts" [OED], from inter "between" (see inter-) + vallum "rampart, palisade, wall," which is apparently a collective form of vallus "stake," from PIE *walso- "a post" (see wall (n.)).

Metaphoric sense of "gap in time" also was in Latin. From c. 1400 in English as "a pause, an interruption in a state or activity." Musical sense "difference in pitch between two tones" is from c. 1600. Related: Intervallic.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "time elapsed between two actions or events," 源自 古法语 intervalle "interval, interim" (14 世纪), earlier entreval (13 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 intervallum "a space between, an interval of time, a distance," 原义为 "space between palisades or ramparts" [OED], 源自 inter "between" （参见 inter-) + vallum "rampart, palisade, wall," which is 似乎 a collective form of vallus "stake," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *walso- "a post" （参见 wall （名）). Metaphoric 语义 "gap in time" also was in 拉丁语. From 约 1400 年 in English as "a pause, an interruption in a state or activity." Musical sense "difference in pitch between two tones" 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Intervallic.

example.en: Trains on this line depart at regular interval of twenty minutes.
example.zh: 这条线路的列车每隔二十分钟定时发车。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "intercept" (obsolete), a back-formation from intervention, or else from Latin intervenire "to come between, intervene; interrupt; stand in the way, oppose, hinder," from inter "between" (see inter-) + venire "to come" (see venue). Sense of "come between, fall or happen between" (of events) is from c. 1600; that of "interfere, interpose oneself between, act mediatorially" is from 1640s. Related: Intervened; intervener; intervening.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "intercept" (已废), a back-formation 源自 intervention，或else 源自 拉丁语 intervenire "to come between, intervene; interrupt; stand in the way, oppose, hinder," 源自 inter "between" （参见 inter-) + venire "to come" （参见 venue). 义为 "come between, fall or happen between" (of events) 始于 约 1600 年; that of "interfere, interpose oneself between, act mediatorially" 始于 1640 年代. 同源词：Intervened; intervener; intervening.

example.en: The United Nations decided to intervene in the border dispute between the two countries.
example.zh: 联合国决定介入两国之间的边境争端。

entries.definition: n. 接见，会见，面试 vt. 接见，会见
entries.etymology:
1510s, "face-to-face meeting, formal conference," from Middle French entrevue, verbal noun from s'entrevoir "to see each other, visit each other briefly, have a glimpse of," from entre- "between" (see inter-) + Old French voir "to see" (from Latin videre; see vision). Modern French interview is from English. Journalistic sense "conversation with someone to obtain statements for publication" is from 1869 in American English.
Meaning "personal meeting to discuss hiring or employment" is by 1921; earlier it was used in military recruiting (1918).
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "face-to-face meeting, formal conference," 源自 中古法语 entrevue, verbal 名词 源自 s'entrevoir "to see each other, visit each other briefly, have a glimpse of," 源自 entre- "between" （参见 inter-) + 古法语 voir "to see" (源自 拉丁语 videre; 参见 vision). 现代法语 interview 始于 English. Journalistic sense "conversation with someone to obtain statements for publication" 始于 1869 年 in American English. 义为 "personal meeting to discuss hiring or employment" is 截至 1921 年; earlier it was used in military recruiting (1918 年).

example.en: She practiced her answers before the job interview at the tech company.
example.zh: 她在科技公司求职面试前练习了自己的回答。

entries.etymology: 1630s, "closely acquainted, very familiar," also "inmost, intrinsic," from Late Latin intimatus, past participle of intimare "make known, announce, impress," from Latin intimus "inmost, innermost, deepest" (adj.), also used figuratively, of affections, feelings, as a noun, "close friend;" superlative of in "in" (see in- (2)). Intimate (adj.) used euphemistically in reference to women's underwear from 1904. Related: Intimately.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "closely acquainted, very familiar," also "inmost, intrinsic," 源自 晚期拉丁语 intimatus, 为 … 的过去分词 intimare "make known, announce, impress," 源自 拉丁语 intimus "inmost, innermost, deepest" （形）, also used figuratively, of affections, feelings, 作名词时, "close friend;" superlative of in "in" （参见 in- (2)). Intimate （形） used euphemistically in reference to women's underwear 自 1904 年起. 同源词：Intimately.

example.en: They had been friends for decades and shared an intimate understanding of each other.
example.zh: 他们相识数十年，对彼此有着亲密而深刻的了解。

entries.etymology: 1640s, from Medieval Latin intimidatus, past participle of intimidare "to frighten, make afraid," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + Latin timidus "fearful" (see timid). Related: Intimidated; intimidating. The French verb was intimider (16c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 intimidatus, 为 … 的过去分词 intimidare "to frighten, make afraid," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + 拉丁语 timidus "fearful" （参见 timid). 同源词：Intimidated; intimidating. The 法语 动词 was intimider (16 世纪).

entries.etymology: Old English into "into, to, against, in," originally in to. It emerged in late Old English to do the work of the dative case inflections, then fading, that formerly distinguished, for instance, the notion of "in the house" from that of "into the house." Compare onto, unto. To be into (something) "be intensely involved in or devoted to" recorded by 1967 in American English youth slang.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 into "into, to, against, in," 原义为 in to. It emerged in late 古英语 to do the work of the dative case inflections, 之后 fading, that formerly distinguished, for instance, the 概念 "in the house" 源自 that of "into the house." 对比 onto, unto. To be into (something) "be intensely involved in or devoted to" recorded 截至 1967 年 in American English youth 俚语.

entries.etymology:
1735, "unable or unwilling to endure" (a condition, etc.), from Latin intolerantem (nominative intolerans) "not enduring, impatient, intolerant; intolerable," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + tolerans, present participle of tolerare "to bear, endure" (see toleration).

Meaning "not disposed to endure contrary opinions or beliefs, impatient of dissent or opposition" is from 1765. Of plants, with reference to deep shade, from 1898. The noun meaning "person or persons who do not favor toleration" is from 1765. Related: Intolerantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1735 年, "unable or unwilling to endure" (a condition, etc.), 源自 拉丁语 intolerantem (主格 intolerans) "not enduring, impatient, intolerant; intolerable," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + tolerans, 为 … 的现在分词 tolerare "to bear, endure" （参见 toleration). 义为 "not disposed to endure contrary opinions or beliefs, impatient of dissent or opposition" 始于 1765 年. Of plants, with reference to deep shade, 自 1898 年起. The 名词 意为 "person or persons who do not favor toleration" 始于 1765 年. 同源词：Intolerantly.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin intricatus "entangled," past participle of intricare "to entangle, perplex, embarrass," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + tricae (plural) "perplexities, hindrances, toys, tricks," a word of uncertain origin (compare extricate). Related: Intricately; intricateness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 intricatus "entangled," 为 … 的过去分词 intricare "to entangle, perplex, embarrass," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + tricae (plural) "perplexities, hindrances, toys, tricks," a word 来源存疑 (对比 extricate). 同源词：Intricately; intricateness.

entries.etymology:
late 15c., "interior, inward, internal," from Middle French intrinsèque "inner" (14c.), from Medieval Latin intrinsecus "interior, internal," from Latin intrinsecus (adv.) "inwardly, on the inside," from intra "within" (see intra-) + secus "along, alongside," from PIE *sekw-os- "following," suffixed form of root *sekw- (1) "to follow" (see sequel).

The form in English was conformed to words in -ic by 18c. Meaning "belonging to the nature of a thing" is from 1640s. Related: Intrinsical; intrinsically.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "interior, inward, internal," 源自 中古法语 intrinsèque "inner" (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 intrinsecus "interior, internal," 源自 拉丁语 intrinsecus （副） "inwardly, on the inside," 源自 intra "within" （参见 intra-) + secus "along, alongside," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *sekw-os- "following," suffixed form of root *sekw- (1) "to follow" （参见 sequel). The form in English was conformed to words in -ic by 18 世纪 义为 "belonging to the nature of a thing" 始于 1640 年代. 同源词：Intrinsical; intrinsically.

definitionLines: vt. 介绍；引进，传入；提出
entries.definition: vt. 介绍；引进，传入；提出
entries.etymology: early 15c., "convey or bring (something) in or into," a back-formation from introduction or else from Latin introducere "to lead in, bring in." Meaning "to bring forward, open to notice" (of a subject, etc.) is from 1550s. Sense of "bring into personal acquaintance, make known" (as of one person to another) is from 1650s. Related: Introduced; introducing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "convey or bring (something) in or into," a back-formation 源自 introduction or else 源自 拉丁语 introducere "to lead in, bring in." 义为 "to bring forward, open to notice" (of a subject, etc.) 始于 1550 年代. 义为 "bring into personal acquaintance, make known" (as of one person to another) 始于 1650 年代. 同源词：Introduced; introducing.

example.en: The professor will introduce a brand-new grading system at the start of next term.
example.zh: 教授将在下学期开始时推出一套全新的评分体系。

definitionLines: n.介绍，引进，传入；引论， 导言，绪论；入门
entries.definition: n.介绍，引进，传入；引论， 导言，绪论；入门
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "act of bringing into existence," from Old French introduccion (14c.) and directly from Latin introductionem (nominative introductio) "a leading in," noun of action from past participle stem of introducere "to lead in, bring in; introduce; found, establish; bring forward (as an assertion)," from intro- "inward, to the inside" (see intro-) + ducere "to lead" (see duke (n.)).

Meanings "initial instruction in a subject" and "an introductory statement" are from mid-15c.; meaning "elementary treatise on some subject" is from 1520s. The sense of "formal presentation of one person to another" is from 1711.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of bringing into existence," 源自 古法语 introduccion (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 introductionem (主格 introductio) "a leading in," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of introducere "to lead in, bring in; introduce; found, establish; bring forward (as an assertion)," 源自 intro- "inward, to the inside" （参见 intro-) + ducere "to lead" （参见 duke （名）). Meanings "initial instruction in a subject" and "an introductory statement" 始于 15 世纪中期; 意为 "elementary treatise on some subject" 始于 1520 年代. The 语义 "formal presentation of one person to another" 始于 1711 年.

example.en: The introduction of compulsory education changed the country's literacy rates dramatically.
example.zh: 义务教育的引入使该国识字率发生了显著变化。

definitionLines: n. 直觉；直觉的知识；直觉力
entries.definition: n. 直觉；直觉的知识；直觉力
entries.etymology: mid-15c., intuicioun, "insight, direct or immediate cognition, spiritual perception," originally theological, from Late Latin intuitionem (nominative intuitio) "a looking at, consideration," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin intueri "look at, consider," from in- "at, on" (see in- (2)) + tueri "to look at, watch over" (see tutor (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, intuicioun, "insight, direct or immediate cognition, spiritual perception," 原义为 theological, 源自 晚期拉丁语 intuitionem (主格 intuitio) "a looking at, consideration," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 intueri "look at, consider," 源自 in- "at, on" （参见 in- (2)) + tueri "to look at, watch over" （参见 tutor （名）).

entries.etymology: "enter in a hostile manner," late 15c., from Latin invadere "to go, come, or get into; enter violently, penetrate into as an enemy, assail, assault, make an attack on," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + vadere "go, walk" (see vamoose). Compare evade. Related: invaded; invading.
entries.etymologyZh: "enter in a hostile manner," 15 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 invadere "to go, come, or get into; enter violently, penetrate into as an enemy, assail, assault, make an attack on," 源自 in- "in" （参见 in- (2)) + vadere "go, walk" （参见 vamoose). 对比 evade. 同源词：invaded; invading.

example.en: Enemy forces attempted to invade the coastal town at dawn.
example.zh: 敌军试图在黎明时分入侵这座沿海城镇。

entries.definition: a.无效的；有病的；残废的 n. 病人；残废者
entries.etymology: "infirm or sickly person," 1709, originally of disabled military men, from invalid (adj.1). In Paris, Invalides is short for Hôtel des Invalides, home for old and disabled soldiers in the 7th arrondissement of Paris.
entries.etymologyZh: "infirm or sickly person," 1709 年, 原义为 of disabled military men, 源自 invalid (adj.1). In Paris, Invalides is short for Hôtel des Invalides, home for old and disabled soldiers in the 7th arrondissement of Paris.

definitionLines: a. 无价的；非常贵重的
entries.definition: a. 无价的；非常贵重的
entries.etymology: 1570s, "above value, too valuable for exact estimate," from in- (1) "not" + value (v.) "estimate the worth of" + -able. It also has been used in a sense "without value, worthless" (1630s, from in- + valuable). Related: Invaluably.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "above value, too valuable for exact estimate," 源自 in- (1) "not" + value （动） "estimate the worth of" + -able. It also has been used in a sense "without value, worthless" (1630 年代, 源自 in- + valuable). 同源词：Invaluably.

definitionLines: vt. 发明，创造；捏造，虚构
entries.definition: vt. 发明，创造；捏造，虚构
entries.etymology: c. 1500, "to find, discover" (obsolete), a back-formation from invention or else from Latin inventus, past participle of invenire "to come upon; devise, discover." General sense of "make up, fabricate, concoct, devise" (a plot, excuse, etc.) is from 1530s, as is that of "produce by original thought, find out by original study or contrivance." Related: Invented; inventing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "to find, discover" (已废), a back-formation 源自 invention or else 源自 拉丁语 inventus, 为 … 的过去分词 invenire "to come upon; devise, discover." General 语义 "make up, fabricate, concoct, devise" (a plot, excuse, etc.) 始于 1530 年代, as is that of "produce by original thought, find out by original study or contrivance." 同源词：Invented; inventing.

example.en: Alexander Graham Bell was the first to invent a practical telephone.
example.zh: 亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔是第一个发明实用电话的人。

entries.etymology:
early 15c., "finding or discovering of something," from Old French invencion (13c.) and directly from Latin inventionem (nominative inventio) "faculty of invention," noun of action from past participle stem of invenire "to come upon, find; find out; invent, discover, devise; ascertain; acquire, get earn," from in- "in, on" (see in- (2)) + venire "to come" (see venue). Sense of "thing invented" is first recorded 1510s; that of "act or process of finding out how to make or do" is from 1530s.

Earliest sense of the word in Middle English was "devised method of organization" (c. 1400), now obsolete. Meaning "finding or discovery of something" is preserved in Invention of the Cross, Church festival (May 3) celebrating the reputed finding of the Cross of the Crucifixion by Helena, mother of Constantine, in 326 C.E. The related classical Latin word for "a device, contrivance" was inventum.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "finding or discovering of something," 源自 古法语 invencion (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 inventionem (主格 inventio) "faculty of invention," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of invenire "to come upon, find; find out; invent, discover, devise; ascertain; acquire, get earn," 源自 in- "in, on" （参见 in- (2)) + venire "to come" （参见 venue). 义为 "thing invented" is 首见于 1510 年代; that of "act or process of finding out how to make or do" 始于 1530 年代. Earliest 语义 the word in 中古英语 was "devised method of organization" (约 1400 年), 今废. 义为 "finding or discovery of something" is preserved in Invention of the Cross, Church festival (May 3) celebrating the reputed finding of the Cross of the Crucifixion by Helena, mother of Constantine, in 326 C.E. The related classical 拉丁语 word for "a device, contrivance" was inventum.

example.en: The printing press was one of the greatest inventions in human history.
example.zh: 印刷机是人类历史上最伟大的发明之一。

definitionLines: a. 发明的，有发明才能的
entries.definition: a. 发明的，有发明才能的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "skilled in invention," from Old French inventif (15c.), from Latin invent-, past participle stem of invenire "devise, discover, find" (see invention). Related: Inventively; inventiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "skilled in invention," 源自 古法语 inventif (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 invent-, past participle stem of invenire "devise, discover, find" （参见 invention). 同源词：Inventively; inventiveness.

definitionLines: n. 存货，库存量；财产等的清单
entries.definition: n. 存货，库存量；财产等的清单
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French inventoire "detailed list of goods, a catalogue" (15c.), from Medieval Latin inventorium, alteration of Late Latin inventarium "list of what is found," from Latin inventus, past participle of invenire "to find, discover, ascertain" (see invention). Altered in Medieval Latin by influence of words in -orium; it properly belongs with words in -ary. Related: Inventorial; inventorially.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 inventoire "detailed list of goods, a catalogue" (15 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 inventorium, alteration of 晚期拉丁语 inventarium "list of what is found," 源自 拉丁语 inventus, 为 … 的过去分词 invenire "to find, discover, ascertain" （参见 invention). Altered in 中古拉丁语 by influence of words in -orium; it properly belongs with words in -ary. 同源词：Inventorial; inventorially.

example.en: The manager asked the staff to do a full inventory check before the holidays.
example.zh: 经理要求员工在假期前进行全面的库存盘点。

entries.etymology: "to turn (something) in an opposite direction; reverse the position, order, or sequence of," 1530s, from Middle French invertir or directly from Latin invertere "turn upside down, turn about; upset, reverse, transpose," figuratively "pervert, corrupt, misrepresent," of words, "to use ironically," from in- "in, on" (see in- (2)) + vertere "to turn" (see versus). Related: Inverted; inverting; invertedly.
entries.etymologyZh: "to turn (something) in an opposite direction; reverse the position, order, or sequence of," 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 invertir or 直接源自 拉丁语 invertere "turn upside down, turn about; upset, reverse, transpose," figuratively "pervert, corrupt, misrepresent," of words, "to use ironically," 源自 in- "in, on" （参见 in- (2)) + vertere "to turn" （参见 versus). 同源词：Inverted; inverting; invertedly.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to clothe in the official robes of an office," from Latin investire "to clothe in, cover, surround," from in "in, into" (see in- (2)) + vestire "to dress, clothe," from PIE *wes-ti-, suffixed form of root *wes- (4) "to clothe" (see wear (v.)).

The meaning "use money to produce profit" first attested 1610s in connection with the East Indies trade, and is probably a borrowing of a special use of Italian investire (13c.) from the same Latin root, via the notion of giving one's capital a new form. Figurative sense of "to clothe (with attributes)" is from c. 1600. The military meaning "to besiege, surround with hostile intent" also is from c. 1600. Related: Invested; investing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to clothe in the official robes of an office," 源自 拉丁语 investire "to clothe in, cover, surround," 源自 in "in, into" （参见 in- (2)) + vestire "to dress, clothe," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wes-ti-, suffixed form of root *wes- (4) "to clothe" （参见 wear （动）). The 意为 "use money to produce profit" 最早见于 1610 年代 in connection with the East Indies trade, and is 可能 a borrowing of a special use of 意大利语 investire (13 世纪) 源自 same 拉丁语 root, 经由 the 概念 giving one's capital a new form. Figurative 语义 "to clothe (with attributes)" 始于 约 1600 年. The military 意为 "to besiege, surround with hostile intent" also 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Invested; investing.

example.en: The government plans to invest heavily in renewable energy projects.
example.zh: 政府计划在可再生能源项目上大力投资。

entries.etymology: c. 1500, back-formation from investigation or else from Latin investigatus, past participle of investigare "to trace out, search after," figuratively "search into, investigate," from in- "in, into" (see in- (2)) + vestigare "to track, trace," from vestigium "footprint, track" (see vestige). Related: Investigated; investigating.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, back-formation 源自 investigation or else 源自 拉丁语 investigatus, 为 … 的过去分词 investigare "to trace out, search after," figuratively "search into, investigate," 源自 in- "in, into" （参见 in- (2)) + vestigare "to track, trace," 源自 vestigium "footprint, track" （参见 vestige). 同源词：Investigated; investigating.

example.en: Authorities were sent to investigate the cause of the factory explosion.
example.zh: 当局派人调查工厂爆炸的原因。

entries.etymology:
1590s, "act of putting on vestments" (a sense now found in investiture); later "act of being invested with an office, right, endowment, etc." (1640s); and "surrounding and besieging" of a military target (1811); from invest + -ment.

Commercial sense of "an investing of money or capital" is from 1610s, originally in reference to the East India Company; general use is from 1740 in the sense of "conversion of money to property in hopes of profit," and by 1837 in the sense "amount of money invested." For evolution of the commercial senses, see invest.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "act of putting on vestments" (a sense 现在 found in investiture); later "act of being invested with an office, right, endowment, etc." (1640 年代); and "surrounding and besieging" of a military target (1811 年); 源自 invest + -ment. Commercial 语义 "an investing of money or capital" 始于 1610 年代, 原义为 in reference to the East India Company; general use 始于 1740 年 in the 语义 "conversion of money to property in hopes of profit," and 截至 1837 年 in the sense "amount of money invested." For evolution of the commercial senses, 参见 invest.

example.en: The government announced a major investment in renewable energy infrastructure.
example.zh: 政府宣布对可再生能源基础设施进行重大投资。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "not perceptible to sight, incapable of being seen," from Old French invisible (13c.), from Latin invisibilis "unseen, not visible," from in- "not" (see in- (1)) + visibilis (see visible). Meaning "kept out of sight" is from 1640s. As a noun, "things invisible," from 1640s. Invisible Man is from H.G. Wells's novel (1897); invisible ink is from 1680s. Related: Invisibly.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "not perceptible to sight, incapable of being seen," 源自 古法语 invisible (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 invisibilis "unseen, not visible," 源自 in- "not" （参见 in- (1)) + visibilis （参见 visible). 义为 "kept out of sight" 始于 1640 年代. 作名词时, "things invisible," 源自 1640 年代. Invisible Man 始于 H.G. Wells's novel (1897 年); invisible ink 始于 1680 年代. 同源词：Invisibly.

example.en: The spy used invisible ink that only appeared under ultraviolet light.
example.zh: 间谍使用了只有在紫外线下才能显现的隐形墨水。

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., "act of inviting, solicitation," from Latin invitationem (nominative invitatio) "an invitation, incitement, challenge," noun of action from past participle stem of invitare "invite, treat, entertain," originally "be pleasant toward," from in- "toward" (see in- (2)).

The second element is obscure. Watkins suggests a suffixed form of the PIE root *weie- "to go after something, pursue with vigor" (see gain (v.)); de Vaan also traces it to a PIE form meaning "pursued." Meaning "the spoken or written form in which a person is invited" is from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "act of inviting, solicitation," 源自 拉丁语 invitationem (主格 invitatio) "an invitation, incitement, challenge," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of invitare "invite, treat, entertain," 原义为 "be pleasant toward," 源自 in- "toward" （参见 in- (2)). The second element is obscure. Watkins suggests a suffixed form of the 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *weie- "to go after something, pursue with vigor" （参见 gain （动）); de Vaan also traces it to a 原始印欧语 (PIE) form 意为 "pursued." 义为 "the spoken or written form in which a person is invited" 始于 1610 年代.

example.en: She received an invitation to speak at the international conference.
example.zh: 她收到了在国际会议上发言的邀请。

entries.etymology: "solicit to come," 1530s, a back-formation from invitation, or else from Middle French inviter (15c.), from Latin invitare "to invite," also "to summon, challenge; to feast, to entertain," a word of uncertain origin. Related: Invited; inviting.
entries.etymologyZh: "solicit to come," 1530 年代, a back-formation 源自 invitation，或else 源自 中古法语 inviter (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 invitare "to invite," also "to summon, challenge; to feast, to entertain," a word 来源存疑. 同源词：Invited; inviting.

example.en: She decided to invite her colleagues to the company's annual dinner.
example.zh: 她决定邀请同事们参加公司的年度晚宴。

entries.etymology: "written account of the particulars and prices of merchandise shipped or sent," 1550s, apparently from Middle French envois, plural of envoi "dispatch (of goods)," literally "a sending," from envoyer "to send" (see envoy). As a verb, 1690s, from the noun.
entries.etymologyZh: "written account of the particulars and prices of merchandise shipped or sent," 1550 年代, 似乎 源自 中古法语 envois, 为 … 的复数 envoi "dispatch (of goods)," 字面义为 "a sending," 源自 envoyer "to send" （参见 envoy). 作动词时, 1690 年代, 源自 名词.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "envelop, surround; make cloudy or obscure," from Old French involver and directly from Latin involvere "envelop, surround, overwhelm," literally "roll into," from in- "in" (see in- (2)) + volvere "to roll" (see volvox). Mid-15c. as "concern oneself." Sense of "take in, include" first recorded c. 1600. Related: Involved; Involving.

entries.etymology:
Middle English iron, iren, yron, from Old English iren, variant (with rhotacism of -s-) of isen, later form of isern, isærn  "the metal iron; an iron weapon or instrument," from Proto-Germanic *isarnan (source also of Old Saxon isarn, Old Frisian isern, Old Norse isarn, Middle Dutch iser, Old High German isarn, German Eisen).

This probably is an early borrowing of Celtic *isarnon (compare Old Irish iarn, Welsh haiarn), which Watkins suggests is from PIE *is-(e)ro- "powerful, holy," from PIE *eis "strong" (source also of Sanskrit isirah "vigorous, strong," Greek ieros "strong"), on the notion of  "holy metal" or "strong metal" (in contrast to softer bronze).

It was both an adjective and a noun in Old English, but in form it is an adjective. The alternative isen survived into early Middle English as izen. In southern England the Middle English word tended to be ire, yre, with loss of -n, perhaps regarded as an inflection; in the north and Scotland, however, the word tended to be contracted to irn, yrn, still detectable in dialect.

Chemical symbol Fe is from the Latin word for the metal, ferrum (see ferro-). Meaning "metal device used to press or smooth clothes" is from 1610s. Meaning "golf club with an iron head, 1842. To have (too) many irons in the fire "to be doing too much at once" is from 1540s. Iron lung "artificial respiration tank" is from 1932. The iron crown was that of the ancient kings of Lombardy, with a thin band of iron in the gold, said to have been forged from a nail of Christ's Cross. Iron horse "railroad locomotive" is from an 1839 poem. Iron maiden, instrument of torture, is from 1837 (probably translating German eiserne jungfrau). The unidentified French political prisoner known as the man in the iron mask died in the Bastille in 1703. In British history, Wellington was called the Iron Duke by 1832.
entries.etymologyZh: 中古英语 iron, iren, yron, 源自 古英语 iren, variant (with rhotacism of -s-) of isen, later form of isern, isærn "the metal iron; an iron weapon or instrument," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *isarnan (source also of 古撒克逊语 isarn, 古弗里西语 isern, 古北欧语 isarn, Middle 荷兰语 iser, 古高地德语 isarn, 德语 Eisen). This 可能 is an early borrowing of Celtic *isarnon (对比 Old 爱尔兰语 iarn, Welsh haiarn), which Watkins suggests 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) *is-(e)ro- "powerful, holy," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *eis "strong" (source also of 梵语 isirah "vigorous, strong," 希腊语 ieros "strong"), on the 概念 "holy metal" or "strong metal" (in contrast to softer bronze). It was both an 形容词 and a 名词 in 古英语, but in form it is an 形容词. The alternative isen survived into early 中古英语 as izen. In southern England the 中古英语 word tended to be ire, yre, with loss of -n, 或许 regarded 作为 inflection; in the north and Scotland, however, the word tended to be contracted to irn, yrn, still detectable in dialect. Chemical symbol Fe 始于 the 拉丁语 word for the metal, ferrum （参见 ferro-). 义为 "metal device used to press or smooth clothes" 始于 1610 年代. 义为 "golf club with an iron head, 1842. To have (too) many irons in the fire "to be doing too much at once" is from 1540s. Iron lung "artificial respiration tank" is from 1932. The iron crown was that of the ancient kings of Lombardy, with a thin band of iron in the gold, said to have been forged from a nail of Christ's Cross. Iron horse "railroad locomotive" 始于 an 1839 年 poem. Iron maiden, instrument of torture, 始于 1837 年 (可能 translating 德语 eiserne jungfrau). The unidentified 法语 political prisoner known as the man in the iron mask died in the Bastille 于 1703 年. In British history, Wellington was called the Iron Duke 截至 1832 年.

entries.etymology:
"figure of speech in which the intended meaning is the opposite of the literal meaning" (usually covert sarcasm under a serious or friendly pretense), c. 1500, from Latin ironia, from Greek eironeia "dissimulation, assumed ignorance," from eiron "dissembler," perhaps related to eirein "to speak," from PIE *wer-yo-, suffixed form of root *were- (3) "to speak" (see verb). Used in Greek of affected ignorance, especially that of Socrates, as a method of exposing an antagonist's ignorance by pretending to modestly seek information or instruction from him. Thus sometimes in English in the sense "simulated ignorance."

For nuances of usage, see humor (n.). In early use often ironia. Figurative use for "condition opposite to what might be expected; contradictory circumstances; apparent mockery of natural or expected consequences" is from 1640s, sometimes distinguished as irony of fate or irony of circumstances. Related: Ironist. A verb ironize "speak ironically" is recorded from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: "figure of speech in which the intended meaning is the opposite of the literal meaning" (通常 covert sarcasm under a serious or friendly pretense), 约 1500 年, 源自 拉丁语 ironia, 源自 希腊语 eironeia "dissimulation, assumed ignorance," 源自 eiron "dissembler," 或许 related to eirein "to speak," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wer-yo-, suffixed form of root *were- (3) "to speak" （参见 动词). Used in 希腊语 of affected ignorance, 尤指 that of Socrates, 作为 method of exposing an antagonist's ignorance by pretending to modestly seek information or instruction 源自 him. Thus 有时 in English in the sense "simulated ignorance." For nuances of usage, 参见 humor （名）. In early use 常 ironia. Figurative use for "condition opposite to what might be expected; contradictory circumstances; apparent mockery of natural or expected consequences" 始于 1640 年代, 有时 distinguished as irony of fate or irony of circumstances. 同源词：Ironist. A 动词 ironize "speak ironically" 见于 约 1600 年.

example.en: There was a bitter irony in the fact that he failed the driving test on his tenth attempt.
example.zh: 他第十次驾照考试仍然失败，这其中有一种辛辣的讽刺意味。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "not in conformity with Church rules," from Old French irreguler "irregular, incapable, incompetent" (13c., Modern French irrégulier), from Medieval Latin irregularis "not regular," from assimilated form of in- "not, opposite of" (see in- (1)) + Latin regularis "having rules" (see regular (adj.)). General sense of "not conforming to regular rules or principles" is from late 15c. "It expresses the fact of being out of conformity with rule, but implies nothing more with certainty. Yet the word is sometimes used in a sinister sense, as though it were a euphemism for something worse." [Century Dictionary] Meaning "unsymmetrical" is from 1580s. In reference to variable stars, from 1797.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "not in conformity with Church rules," 源自 古法语 irreguler "irregular, incapable, incompetent" (13 世纪, 现代法语 irrégulier), 源自 中古拉丁语 irregularis "not regular," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "not, opposite of" （参见 in- (1)) + 拉丁语 regularis "having rules" （参见 regular （形）). General 语义 "not conforming to regular rules or principles" 始于 15 世纪晚期 "It expresses the fact of being out of conformity with rule, but implies nothing more with certainty. Yet the word is sometimes used in a sinister sense, as though it were a euphemism for something worse." [Century Dictionary] 义为 "unsymmetrical" 始于 1580 年代. In reference to variable stars, 自 1797 年起.

entries.definition: vt.灌溉，修水利 vi. 进行灌溉
entries.etymology:
"supply land with water," 1610s, from Latin irrigatus, past participle of irrigare "lead water to, refresh, irrigate, flood," from assimilated form of in- "into, in, on, upon" (see in- (2)) + rigare "to water, to moisten," of uncertain origin. Perhaps [Watkins] from PIE *reg- (2) "moist" (see rain (n.)). De Vaan offers as possibilities the root of regere "to direct, lead," on the notion of leading water onto the fields, or to the root of rigere "be stiff," literally "stretch." The first better suits the sense, but has phonetic problems.

Related: Irrigated; irrigating. In Middle English it was an adjective, "watered, flooded" (mid-15c.). Other adjectival forms have been irriguous (1650s), irrigative (1842), irrigatorial (1867).
entries.etymologyZh: "supply land with water," 1610 年代, 源自 拉丁语 irrigatus, 为 … 的过去分词 irrigare "lead water to, refresh, irrigate, flood," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 in- "into, in, on, upon" （参见 in- (2)) + rigare "to water, to moisten," 来源存疑. Perhaps [Watkins] 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *reg- (2) "moist" （参见 rain （名）). De Vaan offers as possibilities the root of regere "to direct, lead," on the 概念 leading water onto the fields，或to the root of rigere "be stiff," 字面义为 "stretch." The first better suits the sense, but has phonetic problems. 同源词：Irrigated; irrigating. In 中古英语 it was an 形容词, "watered, flooded" (15 世纪中期). Other adjectival forms have been irriguous (1650 年代), irrigative (1842 年), irrigatorial (1867 年).

definitionLines: vi. 引起恼怒，引起不愉快
entries.definition: vt. 激怒；刺激，使兴奋 vi. 引起恼怒，引起不愉快
entries.etymology: 1530s, "stimulate to action, rouse, incite," from Latin irritatus, past participle of irritare "excite, provoke, annoy;" according to de Vaan, probably a verb from Proto-Italic *rito- "stirred," from the same PIE root that produced English run (v.). Meaning "annoy, make impatient" in English is from 1590s. The earlier verb in English was irrite (mid-15c.), from Old French irriter. Related: Irritated; irritating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "stimulate to action, rouse, incite," 源自 拉丁语 irritatus, 为 … 的过去分词 irritare "excite, provoke, annoy;" according to de Vaan, 可能 a 动词 源自 Proto-Italic *rito- "stirred," 源自 same 原始印欧语 (PIE) root that produced English run （动）. 义为 "annoy, make impatient" in English 始于 1590 年代. The earlier 动词 in English was irrite (15 世纪中期), 源自 古法语 irriter. 同源词：Irritated; irritating.

entries.etymology:
"religious system revealed by Muhammad," 1816, from Arabic islam, literally "submission" (to the will of God), from root of aslama "he resigned, he surrendered, he submitted," causative conjunction of salima "he was safe," and related to salam "peace."

Earlier English names for the faith include Mahometry (late 15c.), Muhammadism (1610s), Islamism (1747), and Ismaelism (c. 1600; see Ismailite). The Ismailites were not numerous in Islam, but among them were the powerful Fatimid dynasty in Egypt and the Assassins, both of which loomed large in European imagination. This use also is in part from Ishmaelite, a name formerly given (especially by Jews) to Arabs, as descendants of Ishmael (q.v.).
entries.etymologyZh: "religious system revealed by Muhammad," 1816 年, 源自 阿拉伯语 islam, 字面义为 "submission" (to the will of God), 源自 root of aslama "he resigned, he surrendered, he submitted," causative conjunction of salima "he was safe," and related to salam "peace." Earlier English names for the faith include Mahometry (15 世纪晚期), Muhammadism (1610 年代), Islamism (1747 年), and Ismaelism (约 1600 年; 参见 Ismailite). The Ismailites were not numerous in Islam, but among them were the powerful Fatimid dynasty in Egypt and the Assassins, both of which loomed large in European imagination. example.en: Islam is one of the world's largest religions with over a billion followers.

entries.etymology:
1590s, earlier yland (c. 1300), from Old English igland, iegland "an island," from ieg "island" (from Proto-Germanic *aujo "thing on the water," from PIE *akwa- "water;" see aqua-) + land (n.). As an adjective from 1620s.

Spelling modified 15c.-16c. by association with similar but unrelated isle. Similar formation in Old Frisian eiland, Middle Dutch eyland, German Eiland, Danish öland, etc. In place names, Old English ieg is often used of "slightly raised dry ground offering settlement sites in areas surrounded by marsh or subject to flooding" [Cambridge Dictionary of English Place-Names]. Island universe "solar system" (1846) translates German Weltinsel (von Humboldt, 1845). An Old English cognate was ealand "river-land, watered place, meadow by a river." Related: Islander.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, earlier yland (约 1300 年), 源自 古英语 igland, iegland "an island," 源自 ieg "island" (源自 原始日耳曼语 *aujo "thing on the water," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *akwa- "water;" 参见 aqua-) + land （名）. 作形容词时 源自 1620 年代. Spelling modified 15 世纪-16 世纪 by association with similar but unrelated isle. Similar formation in 古弗里西语 eiland, Middle 荷兰语 eyland, 德语 Eiland, Danish öland, etc. In place names, 古英语 ieg is 常 used of "slightly raised dry ground offering settlement sites in areas surrounded by marsh or subject to flooding" [Cambridge Dictionary of English Place-Names]. Island universe "solar system" (1846 年) translates 德语 Weltinsel (von Humboldt, 1845 年). An 古英语 同源 was ealand "river-land, watered place, meadow by a river." 同源词：Islander.

example.en: The tropical island attracted thousands of tourists every summer.
example.zh: 这座热带岛屿每年夏天吸引数千名游客。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., ile, from Old French ile, earlier isle, from Latin insula "island," a word of uncertain origin.

Perhaps (as the Ancients guessed) from in salo "(that which is) in the (salty) sea," from ablative of salum "the open sea," related to sal "salt" (see salt (n.)). De Vaan finds this "theoretically possible as far as the phonetics go, but being 'in the sea' is not a very precise description of what an island is; furthermore, the Indo-Europeans seem to have indicated with 'island' mainly 'river islands.' ... Since no other etymology is obvious, it may well be a loanword from an unknown language." He proposes the same lost word as the source of Old Irish inis, Welsh ynys "island" and Greek nesos "island." The -s- was restored first in French, then in English in the late 1500s.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, ile, 源自 古法语 ile, earlier isle, 源自 拉丁语 insula "island," a word 来源存疑. Perhaps (as the Ancients guessed) 源自 in salo "(that which is) in the (salty) sea," 源自 ablative of salum "the open sea," related to sal "salt" （参见 salt （名）). De Vaan finds this "theoretically possible as far as the phonetics go, but being 'in the sea' is not a very precise description of what an island is; furthermore, the Indo-Europeans seem to have indicated with 'island' mainly 'river islands.' ... Since no other etymology is obvious, it may well be a loanword from an unknown language." He proposes the same lost word as the source of Old 爱尔兰语 inis, Welsh ynys "island" and 希腊语 nesos "island." The -s- was restored first in 法语, 之后 in English in the late 1500 年代.

entries.etymology:
"to set or place apart, to detach so as to make alone," by 1786, a back-formation from isolated (q.v.).

As a noun, "something isolated," 1890; from earlier adjectival use (1819), which is from Italian isolato or Medieval Latin insulatus.
entries.etymologyZh: "to set or place apart, to detach so as to make alone," 截至 1786 年, a back-formation 源自 isolated (q.v.). 作名词时, "something isolated," 1890 年; 源自 earlier adjectival use (1819 年), which 始于 意大利语 isolato or 中古拉丁语 insulatus.

example.en: The infected patients were isolated to prevent the virus from spreading.

definitionLines: n. 问题，论点，争端；发行，发 行物
entries.definition: n. 问题，论点，争端；发行，发 行物 vt. 发行，发布
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "an exit," from Old French issue "a way out, a going out, exit; final event," from fem. past participle of issir "to go out," from Latin exire "go out, go forth; become public; flow, gush, pour forth" (source also of Italian uscire, Catalan exir), from ex- "out" (see ex-) + ire "to go," from PIE root *ei- (1) "to go" (see ion).

Meaning "discharge of blood or other fluid from the body" is from 1520s; sense of "offspring, children" is from late 14c. Meaning "outcome of an action, consequence, result" is attested from late 14c., probably from this sense in French. Meaning "action of sending into publication or circulation" is from 1833.

Legal sense developed from the notion of "end or result of pleadings in a suit (by presentation of the point to be determined by trial)," hence "the controversy over facts in a trial" (early 14c., Anglo-French) and transferred sense "point of contention between two parties" (early 15c.) and the general sense "an important point to be decided" (1836). Hence also the verbal phrase take issue with (1797, earlier join issue, 1690s) "take up an affirmative or negative position in a dispute with another." To have issues "have unresolved conflicts" is by 1990.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "an exit," 源自 古法语 issue "a way out, a going out, exit; final event," 源自 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 issir "to go out," 源自 拉丁语 exire "go out, go forth; become public; flow, gush, pour forth" (source also of 意大利语 uscire, Catalan exir), 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + ire "to go," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ei- (1) "to go" （参见 ion). 义为 "discharge of blood or other fluid from the body" 始于 1520 年代; 语义 "offspring, children" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "outcome of an action, consequence, result" 见于 14 世纪晚期, 可能 源自 this sense in 法语. 义为 "action of sending into publication or circulation" 始于 1833 年. Legal sense developed 源自 概念 "end or result of pleadings in a suit (by presentation of the point to be determined by trial)," hence "the controversy over facts in a trial" (14 世纪初, 盎格鲁-法语) and transferred sense "point of contention between two parties" (15 世纪初) and the general sense "an important point to be decided" (1836 年). Hence also the verbal phrase take issue with (1797 年, earlier join issue, 1690 年代) "take up an affirmative or negative position in a dispute with another." To have issues "have unresolved conflicts" is 截至 1990 年.

entries.etymology:
Old English hit, neuter nominative and accusative of third person singular pronoun, from Proto-Germanic demonstrative base *khi- (source also of Old Frisian hit, Dutch het, Gothic hita "it"), from PIE *ko- "this" (see he). Used in place of any neuter noun, hence, as gender faded in Middle English, it took on the meaning "thing or animal spoken about before."

The h- was lost due to being in an unemphasized position, as in modern speech the h- in "give it to him," "ask her," is heard only "in the careful speech of the partially educated" [Weekley]. It "the sex act" is from 1610s; meaning "sex appeal (especially in a woman)" first attested 1904 in works of Rudyard Kipling, popularized 1927 as title of a book by Elinor Glyn, and by application of It Girl to silent-film star Clara Bow (1905-1965). In children's games, the meaning "the one who must tag or catch the others" is attested from 1842.

From Old English as nominative of an impersonal verb or statement when the thing for which it stands is implied (it rains, it pleases me). After an intransitive verb, used transitively for the action denoted, from 1540s (originally in fight it out). That's it "there is no more" is from 1966; this is it "the anticipated or dreaded moment has arrived" is from 1942.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 hit, neuter 主格 and 宾格 of third person singular pronoun, 源自 原始日耳曼语 demonstrative base *khi- (source also of 古弗里西语 hit, 荷兰语 het, Gothic hita "it"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ko- "this" （参见 he). Used in place of any neuter 名词, hence, as gender faded in 中古英语, it took on the 意为 "thing or animal spoken about before." The h- was lost due to being in an unemphasized position, as in modern speech the h- in "give it to him," "ask her," is heard only "in the careful speech of the partially educated" [Weekley].
