entries.etymology:
Old English hlot "object (anything from dice to straw, but often a chip of wood with a name inscribed on it) used to determine someone's share," also "what falls to a person by lot," from Proto-Germanic *khlutom (source also of Old Norse hlutr "lot, share," Old Frisian hlot "lot," Old Saxon hlot, Middle Dutch, Dutch lot, Old High German hluz "share of land," German Los; Old English hleotan "to cast lots, to foretell"), of unknown origin. The object was placed with others in a receptacle, which was shaken, the winner being the one that fell out first. Hence, to cast lots. In some cases the lots were drawn by hand. The word was adopted from Germanic into the Romanic languages (compare lottery, lotto). Meaning "choice resulting from the casting of lots" first attested c. 1200.

Sense of "plot of land" is first recorded 1630s (distribution of the best property in new settlements often determined by casting lots), that of "group, collection" is 1725, from notion of auction lots. The generalized sense of "great many" is first attested in 1812. To cast (one's) lot with another is to agree to share winnings.

The word was adopted 源自 日耳曼语 into the Romanic languages (对比 lottery, lotto). 义为 "choice resulting from the casting of lots" 最早见于 约 1200 年. 义为 "plot of land" is 首见于 1630 年代 (distribution of the best property in new settlements 常 determined by casting lots), that of "group, collection" is 1725 年, 源自 概念 auction lots. The generalized 语义 "great many" is 最早见于 于 1812 年. To cast (one's) lot with another is to agree to share winnings.

example.en: We received a lot of complaints from customers about the delayed shipments.
example.zh: 我们收到了很多客户关于货物延误的投诉。

definitionLines: a. 响亮的，大声的；吵闹的， 喧嚣的
entries.definition: a. 响亮的，大声的；吵闹的， 喧嚣的 ad. 响亮，大声地
entries.etymology:
Old English hlud "noisy, making noise, sonorous," from West Germanic *khluthaz "heard" (source also of Old Frisian and Old Saxon hlud, Middle Dutch luut, Dutch luid, Old High German hlut, German laut "loud"), from PIE past participle *klutos- (source also of Sanskrit srutah, Greek klytos "heard of, celebrated," Armenian lu "known," Welsh clod "praise"), from root *kleu- "to hear" (see listen).

Application to colors first recorded 1849. The adverb is from Old English hlude, from Proto-Germanic *khludai (source also of Dutch luid, German laut). Paired with clear since at least c. 1650.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 hlud "noisy, making noise, sonorous," 源自 West 日耳曼语 *khluthaz "heard" (source also of 古弗里西语 and 古撒克逊语 hlud, Middle 荷兰语 luut, 荷兰语 luid, 古高地德语 hlut, 德语 laut "loud"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) past participle *klutos- (source also of 梵语 srutah, 希腊语 klytos "heard of, celebrated," Armenian lu "known," Welsh clod "praise"), 源自 root *kleu- "to hear" （参见 listen). Application to colors 首见于 1849 年. The 副词 始于 古英语 hlude, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *khludai (source also of 荷兰语 luid, 德语 laut). Paired with clear 自 at least 约 1650 年.

example.en: The music next door was so loud that she could not concentrate on her work.
example.zh: 隔壁的音乐声太响了，她根本无法专心工作。

definitionLines: vi. 闲逛；懒洋洋地躺卧
entries.definition: n. 休息室；闲逛；躺椅 vi. 闲逛；懒洋洋地躺卧
entries.etymology: "to loll idly," c. 1500, Scottish, of uncertain origin, perhaps [Barnhart] from French s'allonger (paresseusement) "to lounge about, lie at full length," from Old French alongier "lengthen," from Latin longus "long" (see long (adj.)). Another etymology traces it through obsolete lungis (n.) "slow, lazy person" (c. 1560), from Middle French longis, a generic application of Longinus, supposed to be the name of the centurion who pierced Christ's side with a spear in John xix:34. Popular etymology associated the name directly with long (adj.). Related: Lounged; lounging.

example.en: We waited for our flight in the airport lounge, reading and relaxing.
example.zh: 我们在机场休息室等待航班，阅读放松。

definitionLines: n. /vt. 爱，热爱，爱戴；喜欢， 爱好
entries.definition: n. /vt. 爱，热爱，爱戴；喜欢， 爱好
entries.etymology:
Old English lufu "love, affection, friendliness," from Proto-Germanic *lubo (source also of Old High German liubi "joy," German Liebe "love;" Old Norse, Old Frisian, Dutch lof; German Lob "praise;" Old Saxon liof, Old Frisian liaf, Dutch lief, Old High German liob, German lieb, Gothic liufs "dear, beloved").

The Germanic words are from PIE *leubh- "to care, desire, love" (source also of Latin lubet, later libet "pleases;" Sanskrit lubhyati "desires;" Old Church Slavonic l'ubu "dear, beloved;" Lithuanian liaupse "song of praise").

Meaning "a beloved person" is from early 13c. The sense "no score" (in tennis, etc.) is 1742, from the notion of "playing for love," i.e. "for nothing" (1670s). Phrase for love or money "for anything" is attested from 1580s. Love seat is from 1904. Love-letter is attested from mid-13c.; love-song from early 14c. To fall in love is attested from early 15c. To be in love with (someone) is from c. 1500. To make love is from 1570s in the sense "pay amorous attention to;" as a euphemism for "have sex," it is attested from c. 1950. Love life "one's collective amorous activities" is from 1919, originally a term in psychological jargon. Love affair is from 1590s. The phrase no love lost (between two people) is ambiguous and was used 17c. in reference to two who love each other well (c. 1640) as well as two who have no love for each other (1620s).

The 日耳曼语 words 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) *leubh- "to care, desire, love" (source also of 拉丁语 lubet, later libet "pleases;" 梵语 lubhyati "desires;" Old Church Slavonic l'ubu "dear, beloved;" Lithuanian liaupse "song of praise"). Meaning "a beloved person" is from early 13c. The sense "no score" (in tennis, etc.) is 1742, from the notion of "playing for love," i.e. "for nothing" (1670s). Phrase for love or money "for anything" is attested from 1580s. Love seat is from 1904. Love-letter is attested from mid-13c.; love-song from early 14c. To fall in love is attested from early 15c. To be in love with (someone) is from c. 1500. To make love is from 1570s in the sense "pay amorous attention to;" as a euphemism for "have sex," it is attested from c. 1950. Love life "one's collective amorous activities" 始于 1919 年, 原义为 a term in psychological jargon. Love affair 始于 1590 年代. The phrase no love lost (between two people) is ambiguous and was used 17 世纪 in reference to two who love each other well (约 1640 年) as well as two who have no love for each other (1620 年代).

example.en: She has always had a deep love for her hometown and its traditions.
example.zh: 她一直对故乡及其传统怀有深厚的热爱。

definitionLines: a. 可爱的，秀丽的；令人愉快 的，美好的
entries.definition: a. 可爱的，秀丽的；令人愉快 的，美好的
entries.etymology: Old English luflic "affectionate, loveable;" see love (n.) + -ly (1). The modern sense of "lovable on account of beauty, attractive" is from c. 1300, "applied indiscriminately to all pleasing material objects, from a piece of plum-cake to a Gothic cathedral" [George P. Marsh, "The Origin and History of the English Language," 1862].
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 luflic "affectionate, loveable;" 参见 love （名） + -ly (1). The modern 语义 "lovable on account of beauty, attractive" 始于 约 1300 年, "applied indiscriminately to all pleasing material objects, from a piece of plum-cake to a Gothic cathedral" [George P. Marsh, "The Origin and History of the English Language," 1862 年].

example.en: What a lovely little cottage surrounded by flowers!
example.zh: 多可爱的小屋，四周都是鲜花！

entries.etymology: early 13c., agent noun from love (v.). Old English had lufend for male lovers, lufestre for women. Meaning "one who has a predilection for" (a thing, concept, pursuit, etc.) is mid-14c. As a form of address to a lover, from 1911. Related: Loverly.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, agent 名词 源自 love （动）. 古英语 had lufend for male lovers, lufestre for women. 义为 "one who has a predilection for" (a thing, concept, pursuit, etc.) is 14 世纪中期 作为 form of address to a lover, 自 1911 年起. 同源词：Loverly.

example.en: He is an outdoor lover who hikes every weekend.
example.zh: 他是一位户外爱好者，每个周末都去徒步。

definitionLines: a. 低，矮；低级的，下层的，卑贱 的；低声的
entries.definition: a. 低，矮；低级的，下层的，卑贱 的；低声的
entries.etymology:
"not high," late 13c., from lah (late 12c.), "not rising much, being near the base or ground" (of objects or persons); "lying on the ground or in a deep place" (late 13c.), from Old Norse lagr "low," or a similar Scandinavian source (compare Swedish låg, Danish lav), from Proto-Germanic *lega- "lying flat, low" (source also of Old Frisian lech, Middle Dutch lage, Dutch laag "low," dialectal German läge "flat"), from PIE *legh- "to lie" (see lie (v.2)).

Meaning "humble in rank" is from c. 1200; "undignified" is from 1550s; sense of "dejected, dispirited" is attested from 1737; meaning "coarse, vulgar" is from 1759. In reference to sounds, "not loud," also "having a deep pitch," it is attested from c. 1300. Of prices, from c. 1400. In geographical usage, low refers to the part of a country near the sea-shore (c. 1300, as in Low Countries "Holland, Belgium, Luxemburg," 1540s). As an adverb c. 1200, from the adjective.
entries.etymologyZh: "not high," 13 世纪晚期, 源自 lah (12 世纪晚期), "not rising much, being near the base or ground" (of objects or persons); "lying on the ground or in a deep place" (13 世纪晚期), 源自 古北欧语 lagr "low," or a similar Scandinavian source (对比 Swedish låg, Danish lav), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *lega- "lying flat, low" (source also of 古弗里西语 lech, Middle 荷兰语 lage, 荷兰语 laag "low," 方言 德语 läge "flat"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *legh- "to lie" （参见 lie (v.2)). 义为 "humble in rank" 始于 约 1200 年; "undignified" 始于 1550 年代; 语义 "dejected, dispirited" 见于 1737 年; 意为 "coarse, vulgar" 始于 1759 年. In reference to sounds, "not loud," also "having a deep pitch," it 见于 约 1300 年. Of prices, 源自 约 1400 年. In geographical usage, low refers to the part of a country near the sea-shore (约 1300 年, as in Low Countries "Holland, Belgium, Luxemburg," 1540 年代). 作为 副词 约 1200 年, 源自 形容词.

example.en: The temperature dropped so low overnight that the pipes froze solid.
example.zh: 气温在夜间骤降至极低，水管完全结冰。

entries.definition: a.较低的；下级的；下游的 vt. 放低，降低
entries.etymology: c. 1200, lahre, comparative of lah (see low (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, lahre, comparative of lah （参见 low （形）).

example.en: The airline decided to lower fares on domestic routes to boost demand.
example.zh: 航空公司决定降低国内航线票价以刺激需求。

entries.etymology: 1530s, in reference to subjects of sovereigns or governments, from Middle French loyal, from Old French loial, leal "of good quality; faithful; honorable; law-abiding; legitimate, born in wedlock," from Latin legalem, from lex "law." In most cases it has displaced Middle English leal, which is from the same French source. Sense development in English is feudal, via notion of "faithful in carrying out legal obligations." In a general sense (of dogs, lovers, etc.), from c. 1600. As a noun meaning "those who are loyal" from 1530s (originally often in plural).
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, in reference to subjects of sovereigns or governments, 源自 中古法语 loyal, 源自 古法语 loial, leal "of good quality; faithful; honorable; law-abiding; legitimate, born in wedlock," 源自 拉丁语 legalem, 源自 lex "law." In most cases it has displaced 中古英语 leal, which 始于 the same 法语 source. Sense development in English is feudal, 经由 概念 "faithful in carrying out legal obligations." In a general sense (of dogs, lovers, etc.), 源自 约 1600 年. 作名词时 意为 "those who are loyal" 源自 1530 年代 (原义为 常 in plural).

example.en: She remained loyal to her principles even under pressure.
example.zh: 即使承受压力，她仍然忠于自己的原则。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, from Old French loialté, leauté "loyalty, fidelity; legitimacy; honesty; good quality" (Modern French loyauté), from loial (see loyal). Earlier leaute (mid-13c.), from the older French form. Loyalty oath first attested 1852.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 古法语 loialté, leauté "loyalty, fidelity; legitimacy; honesty; good quality" (现代法语 loyauté), 源自 loial （参见 loyal). Earlier leaute (13 世纪中期), 源自 older 法语 form. Loyalty oath 最早见于 1852 年.

example.en: Employees expect loyalty to be rewarded with job security.
example.zh: 员工期望忠诚能换来工作保障。

definitionLines: vt. 使…•…润滑；给…•加润 滑油
entries.definition: vt. 使…•…润滑；给…•加润 滑油
entries.etymology: 1620s, "to make slippery or smooth" (especially by the application of an oil), from Latin lubricatus, past participle of lubricare "to make slippery or smooth," from lubricus "slippery" (see lubricant (adj.)). Related: Lubricated; lubricating. Earlier verb was lubrify (1610s), from Medieval Latin lubrificare.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "to make slippery or smooth" (尤指 by the application of an oil), 源自 拉丁语 lubricatus, 为 … 的过去分词 lubricare "to make slippery or smooth," 源自 lubricus "slippery" （参见 lubricant （形）). 同源词：Lubricated; lubricating. Earlier 动词 was lubrify (1610 年代), 源自 中古拉丁语 lubrificare.

entries.etymology: late 15c. from early Middle Dutch luc, shortening of gheluc "happiness, good fortune," of unknown origin. It has cognates in Dutch geluk, Middle High German g(e)lücke, German Glück "fortune, good luck." Perhaps first borrowed in English as a gambling term. To be down on (one's) luck is from 1832; to be in luck is from 1900; to push (one's) luck is from 1911. Good luck as a salutation to one setting off to do something is from 1805. Expression better luck next time attested from 1802.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期 源自 early Middle 荷兰语 luc, shortening of gheluc "happiness, good fortune," 来源不详. It has cognates in 荷兰语 geluk, Middle High 德语 g(e)lücke, 德语 Glück "fortune, good luck." Perhaps first borrowed in English 作为 gambling term. To be down on (one's) luck is from 1832; to be in luck is from 1900; to push (one's) luck 始于 1911 年. Good luck 作为 salutation to one setting off to do something 始于 1805 年. Expression better luck next time attested 自 1802 年起.

example.en: With a bit of luck, we will finish the project before the deadline.
example.zh: 只要有一点运气，我们就能在截止日期前完成项目。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., of persons; 1540s, of actions or objects, "likely to bring luck;" from luck + -y (2). Meaning "occurring by chance" is 1590s. Related: Luckier; luckiest; luckiness. Lucky break is attested from 1884 in billiards; 1872 as "failure or break-down which turns out to be fortunate." Lucky Strike as the name of a brand of cigarettes (originally chewing tobacco) popular mid-20c. is said to date from 1871; popular from 1935 when the brand's maker picked up sponsorship of "Your Hit Parade" on radio.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, of persons; 1540 年代, of actions or objects, "likely to bring luck;" 源自 luck + -y (2). 义为 "occurring by chance" is 1590 年代. 同源词：Luckier; luckiest; luckiness. Lucky break 见于 1884 年 in billiards; 1872 年 as "failure or break-down which turns out to be fortunate." Lucky Strike as the name of a brand of cigarettes (原义为 chewing tobacco) popular 20 世纪中期 is said to date 自 1871 年起; popular 自 1935 年起 when the brand's maker picked up sponsorship of "Your Hit Parade" on radio.

example.en: We were lucky to grab the last two tickets before they sold out.
example.zh: 我们很幸运，在票卖完之前抢到了最后两张。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from lug (v.) "to drag" + -age; so, literally "what has to be lugged about" (or, in Johnson's definition, "any thing of more weight than value"). In 20c., the usual word for "baggage belonging to passengers."
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 lug （动） "to drag" + -age; so, 字面义为 "what has to be lugged about" (or, in Johnson's definition, "any thing of more weight than value"). In 20 世纪, the usual word for "baggage belonging to passengers."

entries.etymology: early 15c., "full of light," from Latin luminosus "shining, full of light," from lumen (genitive luminis) "light," related to lucere "to shine" (see light (n.)). Related: Luminously.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "full of light," 源自 拉丁语 luminosus "shining, full of light," 源自 lumen (属格 luminis) "light," related to lucere "to shine" （参见 light （名）). 同源词：Luminously.

entries.etymology: early 14c., lumpe (1224 as surname), probably in Old English, perhaps from a Scandinavian source (compare Danish lumpe, 16c.), of unknown origin. Compare also Middle High German lumpe, early modern Dutch lompe. Phrase lump in (one's) throat "feeling of tightness brought on by emotion" is from 1803. Lumps "hard knocks, a beating" is colloquial, from 1934. Lump sum, one covering a number of items, is from 1867.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, lumpe (1224 年 as surname), 可能 in 古英语, 或源自 a Scandinavian source (对比 Danish lumpe, 16 世纪), 来源不详. 对比 also Middle High 德语 lumpe, early modern 荷兰语 lompe. Phrase lump in (one's) throat "feeling of tightness brought on by emotion" 始于 1803 年. Lumps "hard knocks, a beating" is 口语, 自 1934 年起. Lump sum, one covering a number of items, 始于 1867 年.

example.en: The doctor found a small lump under his skin during the routine examination.
example.zh: 医生在例行检查中发现他皮肤下有一个小肿块。

entries.etymology: "crescent-shaped," early 15c.; "pertaining to the moon," 1620s, from Old French lunaire (15c.), from Latin lunaris "of the moon," from luna "moon" (with capital L- "moon goddess"); see Luna.
entries.etymologyZh: "crescent-shaped," 15 世纪初; "pertaining to the moon," 1620 年代, 源自 古法语 lunaire (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 lunaris "of the moon," 源自 luna "moon" (with capital L- "moon goddess"); 参见 Luna.

entries.etymology:
"mid-day repast," 1786, shortened form of luncheon (q.v.). The verb meaning "to take to lunch" (said to be from the noun) also is attested from 1786:

But as late as 1817 the only definition of lunch in Webster's is "a large piece of food." OED says in 1820s the word "was regarded either as a vulgarism, or as a fashionable affectation." Related: Lunched; lunching. Lunch money is attested from 1868; lunch-time (n.) is from 1821; lunch hour is from 1840. Slang phrase out to lunch "insane, stupid, clueless" first recorded 1955, on notion of being "not there." Old English had nonmete "afternoon meal," literally "noon-meat."
entries.etymologyZh: "mid-day repast," 1786 年, shortened form of luncheon (q.v.). The 动词 意为 "to take to lunch" (said to be 源自 名词) also 见于 1786 年: But as late as 1817 年 the only definition of lunch in Webster's is "a large piece of food." OED says in 1820 年代 the word "was regarded either as a vulgarism, or as a fashionable affectation." 同源词：Lunched; lunching. Lunch money 见于 1868 年; lunch-time （名） 始于 1821 年; lunch hour 始于 1840 年. Slang phrase out to lunch "insane, stupid, clueless" 首见于 1955 年, on 概念 being "not there." 古英语 had nonmete "afternoon meal," 字面义为 "noon-meat."

example.en: We grabbed a quick lunch at the café before the afternoon conference.
example.zh: 我们在下午会议前在咖啡馆快速吃了午饭。

definitionLines: n. 午宴；正式的午餐会
entries.definition: n. 午宴；正式的午餐会
entries.etymology:
"light repast between mealtimes," 1650s (lunching; spelling luncheon by 1706); earlier "thick piece, hunk," 1570s (luncheon), of uncertain origin. Perhaps northern English dialectal lunch "hunk of bread or cheese" (1580s; probably from Spanish lonja "a slice," literally "loin"), blended with or influenced by nuncheon (Middle English nonechenche, mid-14c.) "light mid-day meal," from none "noon" (see noon) + schench "drink," from Old English scenc, from scencan "pour out." 

Despite the form lunching in the 1650s source OED discounts that it possibly could be from lunch (v.), which is much later. It suggests perhaps an analogy with truncheon, etc. Especially in reference to an early afternoon meal eaten by those who have a noontime dinner.
entries.etymologyZh: "light repast between mealtimes," 1650 年代 (lunching; spelling luncheon 截至 1706 年); earlier "thick piece, hunk," 1570 年代 (luncheon), 来源存疑. Perhaps northern English 方言 lunch "hunk of bread or cheese" (1580 年代; 可能 源自 西班牙语 lonja "a slice," 字面义为 "loin"), blended with or influenced by nuncheon (中古英语 nonechenche, 14 世纪中期) "light mid-day meal," 源自 none "noon" （参见 noon) + schench "drink," 源自 古英语 scenc, 源自 scencan "pour out." Despite the form lunching in the 1650 年代 source OED discounts that it possibly could be 源自 lunch （动）, which is much later. It suggests 或许 an analogy with truncheon, etc. Especially in reference to an early afternoon meal eaten by those who have a noontime dinner.

entries.etymology:
late 12c., wenge, from Old Norse vængr "wing of a bird, aisle, etc." (cognate with Danish and Swedish vinge "wing"), of unknown origin, perhaps from a Proto-Germanic *we-ingjaz, suffixed form of PIE root *we- "blow" (source of Old English wawan "to blow;" see wind (n.)). Replaced Old English feðra (plural) "wings" (see feather). The meaning "either of two divisions of a political party, army, etc." is first recorded c. 1400; theatrical sense is from 1790.

The slang sense of earn (one's) wings is 1940s, from the wing-shaped badges awarded to air cadets on graduation. To be under (someone's) wing "protected by (someone)" is recorded from early 13c. Phrase on a wing and a prayer is title of a 1943 song about landing a damaged aircraft.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪晚期, wenge, 源自 古北欧语 vængr "wing of a bird, aisle, etc." (与 … 同源 Danish and Swedish vinge "wing"), 来源不详, 或源自 a 原始日耳曼语 *we-ingjaz, suffixed form of 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *we- "blow" (source of 古英语 wawan "to blow;" 参见 wind （名）). Replaced 古英语 feðra (plural) "wings" （参见 feather). The 意为 "either of two divisions of a political party, army, etc." is 首见于 约 1400 年; theatrical sense 始于 1790 年. The 俚语 语义 earn (one's) wings is 1940s, from the wing-shaped badges awarded to air cadets on graduation. To be under (someone's) wing "protected by (someone)" 见于 13 世纪初 Phrase on a wing and a prayer is title of a 1943 年 song about landing a damaged aircraft.

example.en: The eagle spread its wing and soared into the sky.
example.zh: 那只鹰展开翅膀，翱翔天际。

entries.definition: n. 诱惑物；诱惑；饵 vt. 引诱；诱惑
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "something which allures or entices, an attraction" (a figurative use), also "bait for recalling hawks," from Anglo-French lure, Old French loirre "device used to recall hawks, lure," from Frankish *loþr or some other Germanic source, from Proto-Germanic *lothran "to call" (source also of Middle High German luoder, Middle Low German loder "lure, bait," German Luder "lure, deceit, bait;" also Old English laþian "to call, invite," German laden).

Originally a bunch of feathers on a long cord, from which the hawk is fed during its training. Used of means of alluring other animals (especially fish) from c. 1700. Technically, bait is something the animal can eat; lure is a more general term. Also in 15c. a collective word for a group of young women.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "something which allures or entices, an attraction" (a figurative use), also "bait for recalling hawks," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 lure, 古法语 loirre "device used to recall hawks, lure," 源自 Frankish *loþr or some other 日耳曼语 source, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *lothran "to call" (source also of Middle High 德语 luoder, Middle Low 德语 loder "lure, bait," 德语 Luder "lure, deceit, bait;" also 古英语 laþian "to call, invite," 德语 laden). Originally a bunch of feathers on a long cord, 源自 which the hawk is fed during its training. Used of means of alluring other animals (尤指 fish) 源自 约 1700 年. Technically, bait is something the animal can eat; lure is a more general term. Also in 15 世纪 a collective word for a group of young women.

example.en: The advertisement was designed to lure shoppers into the store.
example.zh: 这则广告旨在把购物者引诱进店里。

entries.definition: v.潜伏；埋伏；潜藏 n. 埋伏；潜伏
entries.etymology: c. 1300, lurken "to hide, lie hidden," probably from Scandinavian (compare dialectal Norwegian lurka "to sneak away," dialectal Swedish lurka "to be slow in one's work"), perhaps ultimately related to Middle English luren "to frown, lurk" (see lower (v.2)). Related: Lurked; lurking.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, lurken "to hide, lie hidden," 可能 源自 Scandinavian (对比 方言 Norwegian lurka "to sneak away," 方言 Swedish lurka "to be slow in one's work"), 或许 ultimately related to 中古英语 luren "to frown, lurk" （参见 lower (v.2)). 同源词：Lurked; lurking.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "sexual intercourse;" mid-14c., "lasciviousness, sinful self-indulgence," from Old French luxurie "debauchery, dissoluteness, lust" (Modern French luxure), from Latin luxuria "excess, luxury, extravagance, profusion; delicacy" (source also of Spanish lujuria, Italian lussuria), from luxus "excess, extravagance, magnificence," probably a figurative use of luxus (adj.) "dislocated," which is related to luctari "wrestle, strain" (see reluctance).

Meaning "sensual pleasure" is late 14c. Lost its pejorative taint 17c. Meaning "habit of indulgence in what is choice or costly" is from 1630s; that of "sumptuous surroundings" is from 1704; that of "something enjoyable or comfortable beyond life's necessities" is from 1780. Used as an adjective from 1916.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "sexual intercourse;" 14 世纪中期, "lasciviousness, sinful self-indulgence," 源自 古法语 luxurie "debauchery, dissoluteness, lust" (现代法语 luxure), 源自 拉丁语 luxuria "excess, luxury, extravagance, profusion; delicacy" (source also of 西班牙语 lujuria, 意大利语 lussuria), 源自 luxus "excess, extravagance, magnificence," 可能 a figurative use of luxus （形） "dislocated," which is related to luctari "wrestle, strain" （参见 reluctance). 义为 "sensual pleasure" is 14 世纪晚期 Lost its pejorative taint 17 世纪 义为 "habit of indulgence in what is choice or costly" 始于 1630 年代; that of "sumptuous surroundings" 始于 1704 年; that of "something enjoyable or comfortable beyond life's necessities" 始于 1780 年. Used 作形容词时 自 1916 年起.

example.en: Taking a private jet to work is an unaffordable luxury for most people.
example.zh: 对大多数人来说，乘坐私人飞机上班是一种负担不起的奢侈。

entries.etymology:
1540s, "structure of any kind," from Middle French machine "device, contrivance," from Latin machina "machine, engine, military machine; device, trick; instrument" (source also of Spanish maquina, Italian macchina), from Greek makhana, Doric variant of mekhane "device, means," related to mekhos "means, expedient, contrivance," from PIE *maghana- "that which enables," from root *magh- (1) "to be able, have power" (source also of Old Church Slavonic mogo "be able," Old English mæg "I can;" see may (v.)).

Main modern sense of "device made of moving parts for applying mechanical power" (1670s) probably grew out of mid-17c. senses of "apparatus, appliance" and "military siege-tower." In late 19c. slang the word was used for both "penis" and "vagina," one of the few so honored. Political sense is U.S. slang, first recorded 1876. Machine age is attested by 1851:

Machine for living (in) "house" translates Le Corbusier's machine à habiter (1923).
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "structure of any kind," 源自 中古法语 machine "device, contrivance," 源自 拉丁语 machina "machine, engine, military machine; device, trick; instrument" (source also of 西班牙语 maquina, 意大利语 macchina), 源自 希腊语 makhana, Doric 为 … 的变体 mekhane "device, means," related to mekhos "means, expedient, contrivance," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *maghana- "that which enables," 源自 root *magh- (1) "to be able, have power" (source also of Old Church Slavonic mogo "be able," 古英语 mæg "I can;" 参见 may （动）). Main modern 语义 "device made of moving parts for applying mechanical power" (1670 年代) 可能 grew out of 17 世纪中期 senses of "apparatus, appliance" and "military siege-tower." In 19 世纪晚期 俚语 the word was used for both "penis" and "vagina," one of the few so honored. Political sense is U.S. 俚语, 首见于 1876 年. Machine age is attested 截至 1851 年: Machine for living (in) "house" translates Le Corbusier's machine à habiter (1923 年).

example.en: The factory installed a new machine to speed up the packaging process.
example.zh: 工厂安装了一台新机器来加快包装流程。

entries.etymology: 1680s; from machine (n.) + -ery. Originally theatrical, "devices for creating stage effects" (which also was a sense of Greek mekhane); meaning "machines collectively" is attested from 1731. Middle English had machinament "a contrivance" (early 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代; 源自 machine （名） + -ery. Originally theatrical, "devices for creating stage effects" (which also was a 语义 希腊语 mekhane); 意为 "machines collectively" 见于 1731 年. 中古英语 had machinament "a contrivance" (15 世纪初).

example.en: The factory upgraded its old machinery to improve production efficiency.
example.zh: 工厂升级了旧机械设备以提高生产效率。

definitionLines: a. 疯，神经错乱；恼火的，狂怒 的；狂热的，着迷的
entries.definition: a. 疯，神经错乱；恼火的，狂怒 的；狂热的，着迷的
entries.etymology:
late 13c., from Old English gemædde (plural) "out of one's mind" (usually implying also violent excitement), also "foolish, extremely stupid," earlier gemæded "rendered insane," past participle of a lost verb *gemædan "to make insane or foolish," from Proto-Germanic *ga-maid-jan, demonstrative form of *ga-maid-az "changed (for the worse), abnormal" (source also of Old Saxon gimed "foolish," Old High German gimeit "foolish, vain, boastful," Gothic gamaiþs "crippled, wounded," Old Norse meiða "to hurt, maim"), from intensive prefix *ga- + PIE *moito-, past participle of root *mei- (1) "to change" (source also of Latin mutare "to change," mutuus "done in exchange," migrare "to change one's place of residence;" see mutable).

Emerged in Middle English to replace the more usual Old English word, wod (see wood (adj.)). Sense of "beside oneself with excitement or enthusiasm" is from early 14c. Meaning "beside oneself with anger" is attested from early 14c., but deplored by Rev. John Witherspoon (1781) as an Americanism. It now competes in American English with angry for this sense. Of animals, "affected with rabies," from late 13c. Phrase mad as a March hare is attested from 1520s, via notion of breeding season; mad as a hatter is from 1829 as "demented," 1837 as "enraged," according to a modern theory supposedly from erratic behavior caused by prolonged exposure to poison mercuric nitrate, used in making felt hats. For mad as a wet hen see hen. Mad money is attested from 1922; mad scientist is from 1891.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古英语 gemædde (plural) "out of one's mind" (通常 implying also violent excitement), also "foolish, extremely stupid," earlier gemæded "rendered insane," 为 … 的过去分词 a lost 动词 *gemædan "to make insane or foolish," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ga-maid-jan, demonstrative form of *ga-maid-az "changed (for the worse), abnormal" (source also of 古撒克逊语 gimed "foolish," 古高地德语 gimeit "foolish, vain, boastful," Gothic gamaiþs "crippled, wounded," 古北欧语 meiða "to hurt, maim"), 源自 intensive prefix *ga- + 原始印欧语 (PIE) *moito-, 为 … 的过去分词 root *mei- (1) "to change" (source also of 拉丁语 mutare "to change," mutuus "done in exchange," migrare "to change one's place of residence;" 参见 mutable). Emerged in 中古英语 to replace the more usual 古英语 word, wod （参见 wood （形）). 义为 "beside oneself with excitement or enthusiasm" 始于 14 世纪初 义为 "beside oneself with anger" 见于 14 世纪初, but deplored by Rev. John Witherspoon (1781 年) 作为 Americanism. It 现在 competes in American English with angry for this sense. Of animals, "affected with rabies," 源自 13 世纪晚期 Phrase mad 作为 March hare 见于 1520 年代, 经由 概念 breeding season; mad 作为 hatter 始于 1829 年 as "demented," 1837 年 as "enraged," according to a modern theory supposedly 源自 erratic behavior caused by prolonged exposure to poison mercuric nitrate, used in making felt hats. For mad 作为 wet hen 参见 hen. Mad money 见于 1922 年; mad scientist 始于 1891 年.

example.en: She was mad at her brother for breaking her favourite mug.
example.zh: 她因弟弟打碎了她最喜欢的杯子而十分恼火。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French ma dame, literally "my lady," from Latin mea domina (compare madonna). Meaning "female owner or manager of a brothel" is first attested 1871.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 ma dame, 字面义为 "my lady," 源自 拉丁语 mea domina (对比 madonna). 义为 "female owner or manager of a brothel" is 最早见于 1871 年.

entries.etymology: 1580s, "place for storing goods, especially military ammunition," from Middle French magasin "warehouse, depot, store" (15c.), from Italian magazzino, from Arabic makhazin, plural of makhzan "storehouse" (source of Spanish almacén "warehouse, magazine"), from khazana "to store up." The original sense is almost obsolete; meaning "periodical journal" dates from the publication of the first one, "Gentleman's Magazine," in 1731, which was so called from earlier use of the word for a printed list of military stores and information, or in a figurative sense, from the publication being a "storehouse" of information.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "place for storing goods, especially military ammunition," 源自 中古法语 magasin "warehouse, depot, store" (15 世纪), 源自 意大利语 magazzino, 源自 阿拉伯语 makhazin, 为 … 的复数 makhzan "storehouse" (source of 西班牙语 almacén "warehouse, magazine"), 源自 khazana "to store up." The original sense is almost 已废; 意为 "periodical journal" dates 源自 publication of the first one, "Gentleman's Magazine," 于 1731 年, which was so called 源自 earlier use of the word for a printed list of military stores and information，或in a figurative sense, 源自 publication being a "storehouse" of information.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "art of influencing events and producing marvels using hidden natural forces," from Old French magique "magic, magical," from Late Latin magice "sorcery, magic," from Greek magike (presumably with tekhne "art"), fem. of magikos "magical," from magos "one of the members of the learned and priestly class," from Old Persian magush, possibly from PIE *magh- (1) "to be able, to have power" (see machine).  Transferred sense of "legerdemain, optical illusion, etc." is from 1811. Displaced Old English wiccecræft (see witch); also drycræft, from dry "magician," from Irish drui "priest, magician" (see druid).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "art of influencing events and producing marvels using hidden natural forces," 源自 古法语 magique "magic, magical," 源自 晚期拉丁语 magice "sorcery, magic," 源自 希腊语 magike (presumably with tekhne "art"), fem. of magikos "magical," 源自 magos "one of the members of the learned and priestly class," 源自 Old 波斯语 magush, possibly 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *magh- (1) "to be able, to have power" （参见 machine). Transferred 语义 "legerdemain, optical illusion, etc." 始于 1811 年. Displaced 古英语 wiccecræft （参见 witch); also drycræft, 源自 dry "magician," 源自 爱尔兰语 drui "priest, magician" （参见 druid).

example.en: The children watched in delight as the magician performed his magic on stage.
example.zh: 孩子们高兴地观看魔术师在台上表演魔法。

definitionLines: a. 有魔力的，不可思议的
entries.definition: a. 有魔力的，不可思议的
entries.etymology: 1550s, from magic (n.) + -al (1). Related: Magically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 magic （名） + -al (1). 同源词：Magically.

example.en: There was something magical about the way the northern lights danced across the sky.
example.zh: 极光在天空中舞动的方式有某种不可思议的魔力。

definitionLines: n. 地方法官；文职官员；治安 推事
entries.definition: n. 地方法官；文职官员；治安 推事
entries.etymology: late 14c., "civil officer in charge of administering laws," from Old French magistrat, from Latin magistratus "a magistrate, public functionary," originally "magisterial rank or office," from magistrare "serve as a magistrate," from magister "chief, director" (see master). Related: Magistracy.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "civil officer in charge of administering laws," 源自 古法语 magistrat, 源自 拉丁语 magistratus "a magistrate, public functionary," 原义为 "magisterial rank or office," 源自 magistrare "serve as a magistrate," 源自 magister "chief, director" （参见 master). 同源词：Magistracy.

entries.etymology: mid-15c. (earlier magnes, late 14c.), from Old French magnete "magnetite, magnet, lodestone," and directly from Latin magnetum (nominative magnes) "lodestone," from Greek ho Magnes lithos "the Magnesian stone," from Magnesia, region in Thessaly where magnetized ore was obtained. Figurative use from 1650s. It has spread from Latin to most Western European languages (German and Danish magnet, Dutch magneet, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese magnete), but it was superseded in French by aimant. Also see magnesia. Chick magnet attested from 1989.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期 (earlier magnes, 14 世纪晚期), 源自 古法语 magnete "magnetite, magnet, lodestone," and 直接源自 拉丁语 magnetum (主格 magnes) "lodestone," 源自 希腊语 ho Magnes lithos "the Magnesian stone," 源自 Magnesia, region in Thessaly where magnetized ore was obtained. Figurative use 源自 1650 年代. It has spread 源自 拉丁语 to most Western European languages (德语 and Danish magnet, 荷兰语 magneet, 意大利语, 西班牙语, 葡萄牙语 magnete), but it was superseded in 法语 by aimant. Also 参见 magnesia. Chick magnet attested 自 1989 年起.

definitionLines: a. 磁性的；有吸引力的
entries.definition: a. 磁性的；有吸引力的
entries.etymology: 1610s, literal; 1630s, figurative, from Modern Latin magneticus, from Latin magnes (see magnet).
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, literal; 1630 年代, figurative, 源自 现代 拉丁语 magneticus, 源自 拉丁语 magnes （参见 magnet).

example.en: The crane uses magnetic force to lift heavy steel beams at the construction site.
example.zh: 起重机利用磁力在建筑工地吊起沉重的钢梁。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Old French magnificent, a back-formation from Latin magnificentior, comparative of magnificus "great, elevated, noble, distinguished," literally "doing great deeds" (see magnificence).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 magnificent, a back-formation 源自 拉丁语 magnificentior, comparative of magnificus "great, elevated, noble, distinguished," 字面义为 "doing great deeds" （参见 magnificence).

example.en: The tourists were speechless when they first saw the magnificent view of the Grand Canyon.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to speak or act for the glory or honor (of someone or something)," from Old French magnefiier "glorify, magnify," from Latin magnificare "esteem greatly, extol, make much of," from magnificus "great, elevated, noble" (see magnificence). Meaning "use a telescope or microscope" is first attested 1660s, said to be a unique development in English. Related: Magnified; magnifying.

entries.etymology: late 12c., "a virgin, a young unmarried woman," shortening of maiden (n.). Like that word, used in Middle English of unmarried men as well as women (as in maiden-man, c. 1200, used of both sexes, reflecting also the generic use of man). Domestic help sense is from c. 1300. In reference to Joan of Arc, attested from 1540s (French la Pucelle). Maid Marian, one of Robin Hood's companions, first recorded 1520s, perhaps from French, where Robin et Marian have been stock names for country lovers since 13c. Maid of Honor (1580s) originally was "unmarried lady of noble birth who attends a queen or princess;" meaning "principal bridesmaid" is attested from 1895. Maydelond (translating Latin terra feminarum) was "the land of the Amazons."

entries.etymology: Old English mægen (n.) "power, bodily strength, force, efficacy," from Proto-Germanic *maginam "power," suffixed form of PIE root *magh- (1) "be able, have power" (see may (v.)). Original sense preserved in phrase with might and main. Meaning "principal channel in a utility system" is first recorded 1727 in main drain. Used since 1540s for "continuous stretch of land or water;" in nautical jargon used loosely for "the ocean," but in Spanish Main the word is short for mainland and refers to the coast between Panama and Orinoco (as contrasted to the islands of the West Indies).

entries.etymology:
Old English macian "to make, form, construct, do; prepare, arrange, cause; behave, fare, transform," from West Germanic *makon "to fashion, fit" (source also of Old Saxon makon, Old Frisian makia "to build, make," Middle Dutch and Dutch maken, Old High German mahhon "to construct, make," German machen "to make"), from PIE *mag- "to knead, mix; to fashion, fit" (see macerate). If so, sense evolution perhaps is via prehistoric houses built of mud. Gradually replaced the main Old English word, gewyrcan (see work (v.)).

Meaning "to arrive at" (a place), first attested 1620s, originally was nautical. Formerly used in many places where specific verbs now are used, such as to make Latin (c. 1500) "to write Latin compositions." This broader usage survives in some phrases, such as to make water "to urinate," to make a book "arrange a series of bets" (1828), make hay "to turn over mown grass to expose it to sun." Make the grade is 1912, perhaps from the notion of railway engines going up an incline.

But the phrase also was in use in a schoolwork context at the time. Make do "manage with what is available" is attested from 1867. Make time "go fast" is 1849; make tracks in this sense is from 1834. To make a federal case out of (something) popularized in 1959 movie "Anatomy of a Murder;" to make an offer (one) can't refuse is from Mario Puzo's 1969 novel "The Godfather." To make (one's) day is from 1909; menacing make my day is from 1971, popularized by Clint Eastwood in film "Sudden Impact" (1983). Related: Made; making.

If so, sense evolution 或许 is 经由 prehistoric houses built of mud. Gradually replaced the main 古英语 word, gewyrcan （参见 work （动）). 义为 "to arrive at" (a place), 最早见于 1620 年代, 原义为 was nautical. Formerly used in many places where specific verbs 现在 are used, such as to make 拉丁语 (约 1500 年) "to write Latin compositions." This broader usage survives in some phrases, such as to make water "to urinate," to make a book "arrange a series of bets" (1828 年), make hay "to turn over mown grass to expose it to sun." Make time "go fast" is 1849 年; make tracks in this sense 始于 1834 年. To make a federal case out of (something) popularized 于 1959 年 movie "Anatomy of a Murder;" to make an offer (one) can't refuse is from Mario Puzo's 1969 年 novel "The Godfather." entries.etymology: 1737, "shaded walk serving as a promenade," generalized from The Mall, name of a broad, tree-lined promenade in St. James's Park, London (so called from 1670s, earlier Maill, 1640s), which was so called because it formerly was an open alley that was used to play pall-mall, a croquet-like game involving hitting a ball with a mallet through a ring, from French pallemaille, from Italian pallamaglio, from palla "ball" (see balloon) + maglio "mallet" (see mallet). Modern sense of "enclosed shopping gallery" is from 1962 (from 1951 in reference to city streets set aside for pedestrians only). Mall rat is from 1985.

entries.etymology:
Old English man, mann "human being, person (male or female); brave man, hero; servant, vassal," from Proto-Germanic *manwaz (source also of Old Saxon, Swedish, Dutch, Old High German man, German Mann, Old Norse maðr, Danish mand, Gothic manna "man"), from PIE root *man- (1) "man" (source also of Sanskrit manuh, Avestan manu-, Old Church Slavonic mozi, Russian muzh "man, male").

Plural men (German Männer) shows effects of i-mutation. Sometimes connected to root *men- "to think" (see mind), which would make the ground sense of man "one who has intelligence," but not all linguists accept this. Liberman, for instance, writes, "Most probably man 'human being' is a secularized divine name" from Mannus [Tacitus, "Germania," chap. 2], "believed to be the progenitor of the human race."

Sense of "adult male" is late (c. 1000); Old English used wer and wif to distinguish the sexes, but wer began to disappear late 13c. and was replaced by man. Universal sense of the word remains in mankind and manslaughter. Similarly, Latin had homo "human being" and vir "adult male human being," but they merged in Vulgar Latin, with homo extended to both senses. A like evolution took place in Slavic languages, and in some of them the word has narrowed to mean "husband." PIE had two stems: *uiHro "freeman" (source of Sanskrit vira-, Lithuanian vyras, Latin vir, Old Irish fer, Gothic wair) and *hner "man," a title more of honor than *uiHro (source of Sanskrit nar-, Armenian ayr, Welsh ner, Greek aner).

Man also was in Old English as an indefinite pronoun, "one, people, they." The chess pieces so called from c. 1400. As an interjection of surprise or emphasis, first recorded c. 1400, but especially popular from early 20c. Man-about-town is from 1734; the Man "the boss" is from 1918. To be man or mouse "be brave or be timid" is from 1540s. Men's Liberation first attested 1970.

Plural men (德语 Männer) shows effects of i-mutation. Sometimes connected to root *men- "to think" （参见 mind), which would make the ground 语义 man "one who has intelligence," but not all linguists accept this. Liberman, for instance, writes, "Most probably man 'human being' is a secularized divine name" 源自 Mannus [Tacitus, "Germania," chap. 2], "believed to be the progenitor of the human race." 义为 "adult male" is late (约 1000 年); 古英语 used wer and wif to distinguish the sexes, but wer began to disappear 13 世纪晚期 and was replaced by man. Universal 语义 the word remains in mankind and manslaughter. Similarly, 拉丁语 had homo "human being" and vir "adult male human being," but they merged in 通俗拉丁语, with homo extended to both senses. A like evolution took place in Slavic languages, and in some of them the word has narrowed to mean "husband." 原始印欧语 (PIE) had two stems: *uiHro "freeman" (source of 梵语 vira-, Lithuanian vyras, 拉丁语 vir, Old 爱尔兰语 fer, Gothic wair) and *hner "man," a title more of honor than *uiHro (source of 梵语 nar-, Armenian ayr, Welsh ner, 希腊语 aner). Man also was in 古英语 作为 indefinite pronoun, "one, people, they." The chess pieces so called 源自 约 1400 年. 作为 interjection of surprise or emphasis, 首见于 约 1400 年, but 尤指 popular 源自 20 世纪初 Man-about-town 始于 1734 年; the Man "the boss" 始于 1918 年. entries.definition: v. 管理，经营，处理；设法，对付
entries.etymology: 1560s, probably from Italian maneggiare "to handle," especially "to control a horse," ultimately from Latin noun manus "hand" (see manual (adj.)). Influenced by French manège "horsemanship" (earliest English sense was of handling horses), which also was from Italian. Extended to other objects or business from 1570s. Slang sense of "get by" first recorded 1650s. Related: Managed; managing. Managed economy was used by 1933.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 可能 源自 意大利语 maneggiare "to handle," 尤指 "to control a horse," 最终源自 拉丁语 名词 manus "hand" （参见 manual （形）). Influenced by 法语 manège "horsemanship" (earliest English sense was of handling horses), which also was 源自 意大利语. Extended to other objects or business 源自 1570 年代. Slang 语义 "get by" 首见于 1650 年代. 同源词：Managed; managing. Managed economy was used 截至 1933 年.

example.en: She had to manage the company's overseas operations from the London headquarters.

entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "act of managing," 源自 manage + -ment. 义为 "governing body" (原义为 of a theater) 始于 1739 年.

example.en: Poor management of company finances led to the firm's bankruptcy last year.
example.zh: 对公司财务的管理不善导致了该公司去年破产。

entries.definition: n.经理，管理人 managerla_ a. 管理的；经理的
entries.etymology: 1580s, "one who manages," agent noun from manage. Specific sense of "one who conducts a house of business or public institution" is from 1705.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "one who manages," agent 名词 源自 manage. Specific 语义 "one who conducts a house of business or public institution" 始于 1705 年.

example.en: The store manager thanked each employee personally for their hard work.
example.zh: 门店经理亲自感谢了每位员工的辛勤付出。

definitionLines: n. 命令，指令；委托管理；授权
entries.definition: n. 命令，指令；委托管理；授权 vt. 托管；授权
entries.etymology: "judicial or legal order," c. 1500, from Middle French mandat (15c.) and directly from Latin mandatum "commission, command, order," noun use of neuter past participle of mandare "to order, commit to one's charge," literally "to give into one's hand," probably from manus "hand" (see manual) + dare "to give" (see date (n.1)). Political sense of "approval supposedly conferred by voters to the policies or slogans advocated by winners of an election" is from 1796. League of Nations sense is from 1919.
entries.etymologyZh: "judicial or legal order," 约 1500 年, 源自 中古法语 mandat (15 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 mandatum "commission, command, order," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的过去分词 mandare "to order, commit to one's charge," 字面义为 "to give into one's hand," 可能 源自 manus "hand" （参见 manual) + dare "to give" （参见 date (n.1)). Political 语义 "approval supposedly conferred by voters to the policies or slogans advocated by winners of an election" 始于 1796 年. League of Nations sense 始于 1919 年.

example.en: The government issued a mandate requiring all vehicles to pass annual safety checks.
example.zh: 政府发布了一项命令，要求所有车辆通过年度安全检查。

entries.definition: vt. 证明，表明；显示 vi. 显示，出现 a. 明白的；显然的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "clearly revealed," from Old French manifest "evident, palpable," (12c.), or directly from Latin manifestus "plainly apprehensible, clear, apparent, evident;" of offenses, "proved by direct evidence;" of offenders, "caught in the act," probably from manus "hand" (see manual) + -festus "struck" (compare second element of infest).

The phrase apparently is O'Sullivan's coinage; the notion is as old as the republic.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "clearly revealed," 源自 古法语 manifest "evident, palpable," (12 世纪)，或直接源自 拉丁语 manifestus "plainly apprehensible, clear, apparent, evident;" of offenses, "proved by direct evidence;" of offenders, "caught in the act," 可能 源自 manus "hand" （参见 manual) + -festus "struck" (对比 second element of infest). The phrase 似乎 is O'Sullivan's coinage; the notion is as old as the republic.

example.en: His calm tone failed to manifest the anxiety he felt inside.
example.zh: 他平静的语气未能掩盖他内心的焦虑。

entries.etymology: 1827, "to handle skillfully by hand," a back-formation from manipulation. Of mental influence, from 1864. Financial sense is from 1870. In mid-20c., it served as a euphemism for "masturbation." Related: Manipulated; manipulating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1827 年, "to handle skillfully by hand," a back-formation 源自 manipulation. Of mental influence, 自 1864 年起. Financial sense 始于 1870 年. In 20 世纪中期, it served 作为 euphemism for "masturbation." 同源词：Manipulated; manipulating.

example.en: Critics accused the company of trying to manipulate public opinion through social media.
example.zh: 批评人士指责该公司试图通过社交媒体操纵舆论。

entries.etymology: "the human race," c. 1300, earlier man-kende (early 13c.), from man (n.) + kind (n.). Replaced Old English mancynn "human race." Also used occasionally in Middle English for "male persons" (late 14c.), but otherwise preserving the original gender neutrality of man (n.). For "menfolk, the male sex," menkind (late 14c.) and menskind (1590s) have been used.
entries.etymologyZh: "the human race," 约 1300 年, earlier man-kende (13 世纪初), 源自 man （名） + kind （名）. Replaced 古英语 mancynn "human race." Also used occasionally in 中古英语 for "male persons" (14 世纪晚期), but otherwise preserving the original gender neutrality of man （名）. For "menfolk, the male sex," menkind (14 世纪晚期) and menskind (1590 年代) have been used.

definitionLines: 一 1. 方式，方法；态度，举止； （pL.）礼貌，规矩
entries.definition: 一 1. 方式，方法；态度，举止； （pL.）礼貌，规矩
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "kind, sort, variety," from Anglo-French manere, Old French maniere "fashion, method, manner, way; appearance, bearing; custom" (12c., Modern French manière), from Vulgar Latin *manaria (source of Spanish manera, Portuguese maneira, Italian maniera), from fem. of Latin manuarius "belonging to the hand," from manus "hand" (see manual (adj.)). The French word also was borrowed by Dutch (manier), German (manier), Swedish (maner).

Meaning "customary practice" is from c. 1300. Senses of "way of doing something; a personal habit or way of doing; way of conducting oneself toward others" are from c. 1300. Meaning "specific nature, form, way something happens" is mid-14c. Of literature from 1660s. Most figurative meanings derive from the original sense "method of handling" which was extended when the word was used to translate Latin modus "method." Phrase manner of speaking is recorded from 1530s. To the manner born ("Hamlet" I iv.15) generally is used incorrectly and means "destined by birth to be subject to the custom."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "kind, sort, variety," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 manere, 古法语 maniere "fashion, method, manner, way; appearance, bearing; custom" (12 世纪, 现代法语 manière), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *manaria (source of 西班牙语 manera, 葡萄牙语 maneira, 意大利语 maniera), 源自 fem. of 拉丁语 manuarius "belonging to the hand," 源自 manus "hand" （参见 manual （形）). The 法语 word also was borrowed by 荷兰语 (manier), 德语 (manier), Swedish (maner). 义为 "customary practice" 始于 约 1300 年. Senses of "way of doing something; a personal habit or way of doing; way of conducting oneself toward others" 始于 约 1300 年. 义为 "specific nature, form, way something happens" is 14 世纪中期 Of literature 源自 1660 年代. Most figurative meanings derive 源自 original sense "method of handling" which was extended when the word was used to translate 拉丁语 modus "method." Phrase manner of speaking 见于 1530 年代. To the manner born ("Hamlet" I iv.15) generally is used incorrectly and means "destined by birth to be subject to the custom."

example.en: He spoke to his elders in a respectful manner that impressed everyone present.
example.zh: 他以一种恭敬的方式和长辈交谈，给在场所有人留下了深刻印象。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "chief residence of a lord," from Old French mansion "stay, permanent abode, house, habitation, home; mansion; state, situation" (13c.), from Latin mansionem (nominative mansio) "a staying, a remaining, night quarters, station," noun of action from past participle stem of manere "to stay, abide," from PIE *men- "to remain, wait for" (source also of Greek menein "to remain," Persian mandan "to remain"). Sense of "any large and stately house" is from 1510s. The word also was used in Middle English as "a stop or stage of a journey," hence probably astrological sense "temporary home" (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "chief residence of a lord," 源自 古法语 mansion "stay, permanent abode, house, habitation, home; mansion; state, situation" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 mansionem (主格 mansio) "a staying, a remaining, night quarters, station," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of manere "to stay, abide," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *men- "to remain, wait for" (source also of 希腊语 menein "to remain," 波斯语 mandan "to remain"). 义为 "any large and stately house" 始于 1510 年代. The word also was used in 中古英语 as "a stop or stage of a journey," hence 可能 astrological sense "temporary home" (14 世纪晚期).

example.en: The billionaire owns a mansion on the outskirts of the city.
example.zh: 这位亿万富翁在城市郊区拥有一座豪宅。

definitionLines: a. 用手的，手工的；体力的
entries.definition: a. 用手的，手工的；体力的 n. 手册，指南
entries.etymology: c. 1400, from Latin manualis "of or belonging to the hand; that can be thrown by hand," from manus "hand, strength, power over; armed force; handwriting," from PIE *man- (2) "hand" (source also of Old Norse mund "hand," Old English mund "hand, protection, guardian," German Vormund "guardian," Greek mane "hand").
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 拉丁语 manualis "of or belonging to the hand; that can be thrown by hand," 源自 manus "hand, strength, power over; armed force; handwriting," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *man- (2) "hand" (source also of 古北欧语 mund "hand," 古英语 mund "hand, protection, guardian," 德语 Vormund "guardian," 希腊语 mane "hand").

example.en: Read the manual carefully before assembling the furniture.
example.zh: 组装家具前请仔细阅读说明手册。

entries.definition: vt. 制造，加工 n. 制造（业），产品
entries.etymology: 1560s, "something made by hand," from Middle French manufacture, from Medieval Latin *manufactura (source of Italian manifattura, Spanish manufactura), from Latin manu, ablative of manus "hand" (see manual (adj.)) + factura "a working," from past participle stem of facere "to perform" (see factitious). Sense of "process of manufacturing" first recorded c. 1600. Related: Manufactures.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "something made by hand," 源自 中古法语 manufacture, 源自 中古拉丁语 *manufactura (source of 意大利语 manifattura, 西班牙语 manufactura), 源自 拉丁语 manu, ablative of manus "hand" （参见 manual （形）) + factura "a working," 源自 past participle stem of facere "to perform" （参见 factitious). 义为 "process of manufacturing" 首见于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Manufactures.

example.en: The factory was set up to manufacture electronic components for export.
example.zh: 这家工厂专门生产用于出口的电子元件。

definitionLines: n. 制造者，制造商，制造厂
entries.definition: n. 制造者，制造商，制造厂
entries.etymology: 1719, "worker in a manufacturing establishment," agent noun from manufacture (v.). Meaning "one who employs workers in manufacturing" is from 1752.
entries.etymologyZh: 1719 年, "worker in a manufacturing establishment," agent 名词 源自 manufacture （动）. 义为 "one who employs workers in manufacturing" 始于 1752 年.

example.en: The manufacturer recalled thousands of cars due to a safety defect.
example.zh: 该制造商因安全缺陷召回了数千辆汽车。

entries.etymology: "document or book written by hand," 1590s (adj.), c. 1600 (n.), from Medieval Latin manuscriptum "document written by hand," from Latin manu scriptus "written by hand," from manu, ablative of manus "hand" (see manual (adj.)) + scriptus (neuter scriptum), past participle of scribere "to write" (see script (n.)). Abbreviation is MS, plural MSS.
entries.etymologyZh: "document or book written by hand," 1590 年代 （形）, 约 1600 年 （名）, 源自 中古拉丁语 manuscriptum "document written by hand," 源自 拉丁语 manu scriptus "written by hand," 源自 manu, ablative of manus "hand" （参见 manual （形）) + scriptus (neuter scriptum), 为 … 的过去分词 scribere "to write" （参见 script （名）). Abbreviation is MS, plural MSS.

example.en: The historian discovered an original manuscript written by the famous philosopher.
example.zh: 这位历史学家发现了一份由这位著名哲学家撰写的原始手稿。

entries.definition: a.许多的 n. 许多（人）
entries.etymology: Old English monig, manig "many, many a, much," from Proto-Germanic *managaz (source also of Old Saxon manag, Swedish mången, Old Frisian manich, Dutch menig, Old High German manag, German manch, Gothic manags), from PIE *menegh- "copious" (source also of Old Church Slavonic munogu "much, many," Old Irish menicc, Welsh mynych "frequent," Old Irish magham "gift"). Pronunciation altered by influence of any (see manifold).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 monig, manig "many, many a, much," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *managaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 manag, Swedish mången, 古弗里西语 manich, 荷兰语 menig, 古高地德语 manag, 德语 manch, Gothic manags), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *menegh- "copious" (source also of Old Church Slavonic munogu "much, many," Old 爱尔兰语 menicc, Welsh mynych "frequent," Old 爱尔兰语 magham "gift"). Pronunciation altered by influence of any （参见 manifold).

example.en: There are many reasons why regular exercise is good for health.
example.zh: 定期锻炼有益健康，原因有很多。

entries.etymology: 1520s, shortening of Middle English mapemounde "map of the world" (late 14c.), and in part from Middle French mappe, shortening of Old French mapemonde, both English and French words from Medieval Latin mappa mundi "map of the world;" first element from Latin mappa "napkin, cloth" (on which maps were drawn), "tablecloth, signal-cloth, flag," said by Quintilian to be of Punic origin (compare Talmudic Hebrew mappa, contraction of Mishnaic menaphah "a fluttering banner, streaming cloth") + Latin mundi "of the world," from mundus "universe, world" (see mundane). Commonly used 17c. in a figurative sense of "epitome; detailed representation." To put (something) on the map "bring it to wide attention" is from 1913.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, shortening of 中古英语 mapemounde "map of the world" (14 世纪晚期), and in part 源自 中古法语 mappe, shortening of 古法语 mapemonde, both English and 法语 words 源自 中古拉丁语 mappa mundi "map of the world;" first element 源自 拉丁语 mappa "napkin, cloth" (on which maps were drawn), "tablecloth, signal-cloth, flag," said by Quintilian to be of Punic origin (对比 Talmudic 希伯来语 mappa, contraction of Mishnaic menaphah "a fluttering banner, streaming cloth") + 拉丁语 mundi "of the world," 源自 mundus "universe, world" （参见 mundane). Commonly used 17 世纪 in a figurative 语义 "epitome; detailed representation." To put (something) on the map "bring it to wide attention" 始于 1913 年.

example.en: She spread the map on the table and traced the hiking route.
example.zh: 她把地图摊开在桌上，描出了徒步路线。

entries.etymology: type of stone much used in sculpture, monuments, etc., early 14c., by dissimilation from marbra (mid-12c.), from Old French marbre (which itself underwent dissimilation of 2nd -r- to -l- in 14c.; marbre persisted in English into early 15c.), from Latin marmor, from or cognate with Greek marmaros "marble, gleaming stone," of unknown origin, perhaps originally an adjective meaning "sparkling," which would connect it with marmairein "to shine." The Latin word was taken directly into Old English as marma. German Marmor is restored Latin from Old High German marmul. Meaning "little balls of marble used in a children's game" is attested from 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: type of stone much used in sculpture, monuments, etc., 14 世纪初, by dissimilation 源自 marbra (12 世纪中期), 源自 古法语 marbre (which itself underwent dissimilation of 2nd -r- to -l- in 14 世纪; marbre persisted in English into 15 世纪初), 源自 拉丁语 marmor, 源自 or 与 … 同源 希腊语 marmaros "marble, gleaming stone," 来源不详, 或许 原义为 an 形容词 意为 "sparkling," which would connect it with marmairein "to shine." The 拉丁语 word was taken directly into 古英语 as marma. 德语 Marmor is restored 拉丁语 源自 古高地德语 marmul. 义为 "little balls of marble used in a children's game" 见于 1690 年代.

example.en: The floor of the museum entrance was laid with polished marble.
example.zh: 博物馆入口的地板铺了抛光大理石。

entries.etymology: third month, c. 1200, from Anglo-French marche, Old French marz, from Latin Martius (mensis) "(month) of Mars," from Mars (genitive Martis). Replaced Old English hreðmonaþ, the first part of which is of uncertain meaning, perhaps from hræd "quick, nimble, ready, active, alert, prompt." For March hare, proverbial type of madness, see mad.
entries.etymologyZh: third month, 约 1200 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 marche, 古法语 marz, 源自 拉丁语 Martius (mensis) "(month) of Mars," 源自 Mars (属格 Martis). Replaced 古英语 hreðmonaþ, the first part of which is of uncertain 意为, 或源自 hræd "quick, nimble, ready, active, alert, prompt." For March hare, proverbial type of madness, 参见 mad.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "edge of a sea or lake;" late 14c., "space between a block of text and the edge of a page," from Latin marginem (nominative margo) "edge, brink, border, margin," from PIE *merg- "edge, border, boundary" (see mark (n.1)). General sense of "boundary space; rim or edge of anything" is from late 14c. Meaning "comfort allowance, cushion" is from 1851; margin of safety first recorded 1888. Stock market sense of "sum deposited with a broker to cover risk of loss" is from 1848. Related: Margins.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "edge of a sea or lake;" 14 世纪晚期, "space between a block of text and the edge of a page," 源自 拉丁语 marginem (主格 margo) "edge, brink, border, margin," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *merg- "edge, border, boundary" （参见 mark (n.1)). General 语义 "boundary space; rim or edge of anything" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "comfort allowance, cushion" 始于 1851 年; margin of safety 首见于 1888 年. Stock market 语义 "sum deposited with a broker to cover risk of loss" 始于 1848 年. 同源词：Margins.

example.en: He wrote notes in the margin of the textbook while studying.
example.zh: 他学习时在教科书的页边空白处写笔记。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "written on the margin," from Medieval Latin marginalis, from Latin margo "edge, brink, border, margin" (see margin (n.)). Sense of "of little effect or importance" first recorded 1887. Related: Marginally.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "written on the margin," 源自 中古拉丁语 marginalis, 源自 拉丁语 margo "edge, brink, border, margin" （参见 margin （名）). 义为 "of little effect or importance" 首见于 1887 年. 同源词：Marginally.

example.en: The extra funding made only a marginal difference to the overall project budget.
example.zh: 额外的资金对整个项目预算只产生了微乎其微的影响。

definitionLines: a. 海的，海产的，航海的，船舶 的，海运的
entries.definition: a. 海的，海产的，航海的，船舶 的，海运的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "pertaining to the sea," from Middle French marin, from Old French marin "of the sea, maritime," from Latin marinus "of the sea," from mare "sea, the sea, seawater," from PIE *mori- "body of water, lake" (see mere (n.)). The Old English word was sælic.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "pertaining to the sea," 源自 中古法语 marin, 源自 古法语 marin "of the sea, maritime," 源自 拉丁语 marinus "of the sea," 源自 mare "sea, the sea, seawater," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mori- "body of water, lake" （参见 mere （名）). The 古英语 word was sælic.

example.en: The marine biologist studied coral reefs for twenty years.
example.zh: 这位海洋生物学家研究珊瑚礁二十年。

entries.definition: 记号，标记，痕迹；分数 vt.记分，打分；作标记，标志
entries.etymology: masc. proper name, variant of Marcus (q.v.). Among the top 10 names given to boy babies born in the U.S. between 1955 and 1970.
entries.etymologyZh: masc. proper name, 为 … 的变体 Marcus (q.v.). Among the top 10 names given to boy babies born in the U.S. between 1955 年 and 1970 年.

definitionLines: n. 集市，市场；销路，需求
entries.definition: n. 集市，市场；销路，需求 vt.销售
entries.etymology: early 12c., "a meeting at a fixed time for buying and selling livestock and provisions," from Old North French market "marketplace, trade, commerce" (Old French marchiet, Modern French marché), from Latin mercatus "trading, buying and selling, trade, market" (source of Italian mercato, Spanish mercado, Dutch markt, German Markt), from past participle of mercari "to trade, deal in, buy," from merx (genitive mercis) "wares, merchandise," from Italic root *merk-, possibly from Etruscan, referring to various aspects of economics. Meaning "public building or space where markets are held" first attested mid-13c. Sense of "sales, as controlled by supply and demand" is from 1680s. Market value (1690s) first attested in writings of John Locke. Market economy is from 1948; market research is from 1921.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, "a meeting at a fixed time for buying and selling livestock and provisions," 源自 Old North 法语 market "marketplace, trade, commerce" (古法语 marchiet, 现代法语 marché), 源自 拉丁语 mercatus "trading, buying and selling, trade, market" (source of 意大利语 mercato, 西班牙语 mercado, 荷兰语 markt, 德语 Markt), 源自 为 … 的过去分词 mercari "to trade, deal in, buy," 源自 merx (属格 mercis) "wares, merchandise," 源自 Italic root *merk-, possibly 源自 Etruscan, referring to various aspects of economics. 义为 "public building or space where markets are held" 最早见于 13 世纪中期 义为 "sales, as controlled by supply and demand" 始于 1680 年代. Market value (1690 年代) 最早见于 in writings of John Locke. Market economy 始于 1948 年; market research 始于 1921 年.

example.en: The startup hired an expert to market its new software to enterprise clients.
example.zh: 这家初创公司聘请了一位专家，向企业客户推销其新软件。

entries.etymology: 1560s, "buying and selling," verbal noun from market (v.). Meaning "produce bought at a market" is from 1701. The business sense, "process of moving goods from producer to consumer with emphasis on advertising and sales," is attested by 1897.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "buying and selling," verbal 名词 源自 market （动）. 义为 "produce bought at a market" 始于 1701 年. The business sense, "process of moving goods from producer to consumer with emphasis on advertising and sales," is attested 截至 1897 年.

example.en: The startup invested heavily in digital marketing to build brand awareness among younger consumers.
example.zh: 这家初创公司大力投资数字营销，以在年轻消费者中建立品牌知名度。

definitionLines: n. 结婚，婚姻；结婚仪式
entries.definition: n. 结婚，婚姻；结婚仪式
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "action of marrying, entry into wedlock;" also "state or condition of being husband and wife, matrimony, wedlock;" from Old French mariage "marriage; dowry" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *maritaticum (11c.), from Latin maritatus, past participle of maritatre "to wed, marry, give in marriage" (see marry (v.)). The Vulgar Latin word also is the source of Italian maritaggio, Spanish maridaje.

Meaning "a union of a man and woman for life by marriage, a particular matrimonial union" is early 14c. Meanings "the marriage vow, formal declaration or contract by which two join in wedlock;" also "a wedding, celebration of a marriage; the marriage ceremony" are from late 14c. Figurative use (non-theological) "intimate union, a joining as if by marriage" is from early 15c.Marriage counseling recorded by 1939. Marriage bed, figurative of marital intercourse generally, is attested from 1580s (bed of marriage is from early 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "action of marrying, entry into wedlock;" also "state or condition of being husband and wife, matrimony, wedlock;" 源自 古法语 mariage "marriage; dowry" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *maritaticum (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 maritatus, 为 … 的过去分词 maritatre "to wed, marry, give in marriage" （参见 marry （动）). The 通俗拉丁语 word also is the source of 意大利语 maritaggio, 西班牙语 maridaje. 义为 "a union of a man and woman for life by marriage, a particular matrimonial union" is 14 世纪初 Meanings "the marriage vow, formal declaration or contract by which two join in wedlock;" also "a wedding, celebration of a marriage; the marriage ceremony" 始于 14 世纪晚期 Figurative use (non-theological) "intimate union, a joining as if by marriage" 始于 15 世纪初Marriage counseling recorded 截至 1939 年. Marriage bed, figurative of marital intercourse generally, 见于 1580 年代 (bed of marriage 始于 15 世纪初).

example.en: Their marriage lasted over fifty years and was full of love.
example.zh: 他们的婚姻延续了五十多年，充满了爱。

entries.etymology: "formally wedded," late 14c., from past participle of marry (v.).
entries.etymologyZh: "formally wedded," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 为 … 的过去分词 marry （动）.

example.en: They have been married for over twenty years and are still deeply in love.
example.zh: 他们结婚已超过二十年，依然深爱着彼此。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to give (offspring) in marriage," from Old French marier "to get married; to marry off, give in marriage; to bring together in marriage," from Latin maritare "to wed, marry, give in marriage" (source of Italian maritare, Spanish and Portuguese maridar), from maritus (n.) "married man, husband," of uncertain origin, originally a past participle, perhaps ultimately from "provided with a *mari," a young woman, from PIE root *mari- "young wife, young woman," akin to *meryo- "young man" (source of Sanskrit marya- "young man, suitor").

Meaning "to get married, join (with someone) in matrimony" is early 14c. in English, as is that of "to take in marriage." Said from 1520s of the priest, etc., who performs the rite. Figurative use from early 15c. Related: Married; marrying. Phrase the marrying kind, describing one inclined toward marriage and almost always used with a negative, is attested by 1824, probably short for marrying kind of men, which is from a popular 1756 essay by Chesterfield.

In some Indo-European languages there were distinct "marry" verbs for men and women, though some of these have become generalized. Compare Latin ducere uxorem (of men), literally "to lead a wife;" nubere (of women), perhaps originally "to veil" [Buck]. Also compare Old Norse kvangask (of men) from kvan "wife" (see quean), so, "take a wife;" giptask (of women), from gipta, a specialized use of "to give" (see gift (n.)), so, "to be given."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to give (offspring) in marriage," 源自 古法语 marier "to get married; to marry off, give in marriage; to bring together in marriage," 源自 拉丁语 maritare "to wed, marry, give in marriage" (source of 意大利语 maritare, 西班牙语 and 葡萄牙语 maridar), 源自 maritus （名） "married man, husband," 来源存疑, 原义为 a past participle, 或许 最终源自 "provided with a *mari," a young woman, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *mari- "young wife, young woman," akin to *meryo- "young man" (source of 梵语 marya- "young man, suitor"). 义为 "to get married, join (with someone) in matrimony" is 14 世纪初 in English, as is that of "to take in marriage." Said 源自 1520 年代 of the priest, etc., who performs the rite. Figurative use 源自 15 世纪初 同源词：Married; marrying. Phrase the marrying kind, describing one inclined toward marriage and almost always used with a negative, is attested 截至 1824 年, 可能 short for marrying kind of men, which 始于 a popular 1756 年 essay by Chesterfield. In some Indo-European languages there were distinct "marry" verbs for men and women, though some of these have become generalized. 对比 拉丁语 ducere uxorem (of men), 字面义为 "to lead a wife;" nubere (of women), 或许 原义为 "to veil" [Buck]. Also 对比 古北欧语 kvangask (of men) 源自 kvan "wife" （参见 quean), so, "take a wife;" giptask (of women), 源自 gipta, a specialized use of "to give" （参见 gift （名）), so, "to be given."

example.en: They decided to marry after dating for three years.
example.zh: 他们交往了三年后决定结婚。

entries.etymology: Roman god of war, also the name of the bright red planet, late 14c., from Latin Mars (stem *Mawort-), the Roman god of war, of unknown origin, apparently from earlier Mavors, related to Oscan Mamers. According to Watkins the Latin word is from *Mawort- "name of an Italic deity who became the god of war at Rome ...." He also had agricultural attributes, and might ultimately have been a Spring-Dionysus. The planet was so named by the Romans, no doubt for its blood-like color. The Greeks also called the planet Pyroeis "the fiery."
entries.etymologyZh: Roman god of war, also the name of the bright red planet, 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 Mars (stem *Mawort-), the Roman god of war, 来源不详, 似乎 源自 earlier Mavors, related to Oscan Mamers. According to Watkins the 拉丁语 word 始于 *Mawort- "name of an Italic deity who became the god of war at Rome ...." He also had agricultural attributes, and might ultimately have been a Spring-Dionysus. The planet was so named by the Romans, no doubt for its blood-like color. The Greeks also called the planet Pyroeis "the fiery."

entries.etymology: Old English mersc, merisc "marsh, swamp," from Proto-Germanic *marisko (source also of Old Frisian and Old Saxon marsk "marsh," Middle Dutch mersch, Dutch mars, German Marsch, Danish marsk), probably from Proto-Germanic *mari- "sea" (see mere (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 mersc, merisc "marsh, swamp," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *marisko (source also of 古弗里西语 and 古撒克逊语 marsk "marsh," Middle 荷兰语 mersch, 荷兰语 mars, 德语 Marsch, Danish marsk), 可能 源自 原始日耳曼语 *mari- "sea" （参见 mere （名）).

entries.etymology:
early 13c. as a surname; mid-13c. as "high officer of the royal court;" from Old French mareschal "commanding officer of an army; officer in charge of a household" (Modern French maréchal), originally "stable officer, horse tender, groom" (Frankish Latin mariscaluis) from Frankish *marhskalk or a similar Germanic word, literally "horse-servant" (compare Old High German marahscalc "groom," Middle Dutch maerschalc), from Proto-Germanic *markhaz "horse" (see mare (n.1)) + *skalkaz "servant" (source of Old English scealc "servant, retainer, member of a crew," Dutch schalk "rogue, wag," Gothic skalks "servant").

Cognate with Old English horsþegn. From c. 1300 as "stable officer;" early 14c. as "military commander, general in the army." For development history, compare constable. Also from Germanic are Italian scalco "steward," Spanish mariscal "marshal."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初 作为 surname; 13 世纪中期 as "high officer of the royal court;" 源自 古法语 mareschal "commanding officer of an army; officer in charge of a household" (现代法语 maréchal), 原义为 "stable officer, horse tender, groom" (Frankish 拉丁语 mariscaluis) 源自 Frankish *marhskalk or a similar 日耳曼语 word, 字面义为 "horse-servant" (对比 古高地德语 marahscalc "groom," Middle 荷兰语 maerschalc), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *markhaz "horse" （参见 mare (n.1)) + *skalkaz "servant" (source of 古英语 scealc "servant, retainer, member of a crew," 荷兰语 schalk "rogue, wag," Gothic skalks "servant"). Cognate with 古英语 horsþegn. From 约 1300 年 as "stable officer;" 14 世纪初 as "military commander, general in the army." For development history, 对比 constable. Also 源自 日耳曼语 are 意大利语 scalco "steward," 西班牙语 mariscal "marshal."

entries.etymology:
Old English martyr, from Late Latin martyr, from Doric Greek martyr, earlier martys (genitive martyros), in Christian use "martyr," literally "witness," probably related to mermera "care, trouble," from mermairein "be anxious or thoughtful," from PIE *(s)mrtu- (source also of Sanskrit smarati "remember," Latin memor "mindful;" see memory).

Adopted directly into most Germanic languages, but Norse substituted native formation pislarvattr, literally "torture-witness." General sense of "constant sufferer" is from 1550s. Martyr complex "exaggerated desire for self-sacrifice" is attested from 1920.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 martyr, 源自 晚期拉丁语 martyr, 源自 Doric 希腊语 martyr, earlier martys (属格 martyros), in Christian use "martyr," 字面义为 "witness," 可能 related to mermera "care, trouble," 源自 mermairein "be anxious or thoughtful," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *(s)mrtu- (source also of 梵语 smarati "remember," 拉丁语 memor "mindful;" 参见 memory). Adopted directly into most 日耳曼语 languages, but Norse substituted 本族 formation pislarvattr, 字面义为 "torture-witness." General 语义 "constant sufferer" 始于 1550 年代. Martyr complex "exaggerated desire for self-sacrifice" 见于 1920 年.

Meaning "having the appropriate qualities of the male sex, manly, virile, powerful" is first attested 1620s. As a noun from mid-15c.

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French masque "covering to hide or guard the face" (16c.), from Italian maschera, from Medieval Latin masca "mask, specter, nightmare," of uncertain origin, perhaps from Arabic maskharah "buffoon, mockery," from sakhira "be mocked, ridiculed." Or via Provençal mascarar, Catalan mascarar, Old French mascurer "to black (the face)," perhaps from a Germanic source akin to English mesh (q.v.). But compare Occitan mascara "to blacken, darken," derived from mask- "black," which is held to be from a pre-Indo-European language, and Old Occitan masco "witch," surviving in dialects; in Beziers it means "dark cloud before the rain comes." [See Walther von Wartburg, "Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch: Eine Darstellung galloromanischen sprachschatzes"]. Figurative use by 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 masque "covering to hide or guard the face" (16 世纪), 源自 意大利语 maschera, 源自 中古拉丁语 masca "mask, specter, nightmare," 来源存疑, 或源自 阿拉伯语 maskharah "buffoon, mockery," 源自 sakhira "be mocked, ridiculed." Or 经由 Provençal mascarar, Catalan mascarar, 古法语 mascurer "to black (the face)," 或源自 a 日耳曼语 source akin to English mesh (q.v.). But 对比 Occitan mascara "to blacken, darken," derived 源自 mask- "black," which is held to be 源自 a pre-Indo-European language, and Old Occitan masco "witch," surviving in dialects; in Beziers it means "dark cloud before the rain comes." [See Walther von Wartburg, "Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch: Eine Darstellung galloromanischen sprachschatzes"]. Figurative use by 1570 年代.

entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 中古法语 massif "bulky, solid," 源自 古法语 masse "lump" （参见 mass (n.1)). 同源词：Massively; massiveness. U.S. Cold War strategy of massive retaliation was introduced by J.F. Dulles in early 1954 年.

entries.etymology: late Old English mægester "one having control or authority," from Latin magister (n.) "chief, head, director, teacher" (source of Old French maistre, French maître, Spanish and Italian maestro, Portuguese mestre, Dutch meester, German Meister), contrastive adjective ("he who is greater") from magis (adv.) "more," from PIE *mag-yos-, comparative of root *meg- "great" (see mickle). Form influenced in Middle English by Old French cognate maistre. Meaning "original of a recording" is from 1904. In academic senses (from Medieval Latin magister) it is attested from late 14c., originally a degree conveying authority to teach in the universities. As an adjective from late 12c.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 mægester "one having control or authority," 源自 拉丁语 magister （名） "chief, head, director, teacher" (source of 古法语 maistre, 法语 maître, 西班牙语 and 意大利语 maestro, 葡萄牙语 mestre, 荷兰语 meester, 德语 Meister), contrastive 形容词 ("he who is greater") 源自 magis （副） "more," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mag-yos-, comparative of root *meg- "great" （参见 mickle). Form influenced in 中古英语 by 古法语 同源 maistre. 义为 "original of a recording" 始于 1904 年. In academic senses (源自 中古拉丁语 magister) it 见于 14 世纪晚期, 原义为 a degree conveying authority to teach in the universities. 作形容词时 源自 12 世纪晚期
