entries.etymology:
c. 1200, materie, "subject of thought, speech, or expression," from Anglo-French matere, Old French matere "subject, theme, topic; substance, content, material; character, education" (12c., Modern French matière), from Latin materia "substance from which something is made," also "hard inner wood of a tree" (source also of Portuguese madeira "wood"), from mater "origin, source, mother" (see mother (n.1)). Or, on another theory, it represents *dmateria, from PIE root *dem-/*dom- (source of Latin domus "house," English timber). With sense development in Latin influenced by Greek hyle (see hylo-), of which it was the equivalent in philosophy.

Meaning "physical substance generally, matter, material" is early 14c.; that of "substance of which some specific object is made or consists of" is attested from late 14c. That of "piece of business, affair, activity, situation, circumstance" is from late 14c. From mid-14c. as "subject of a literary work, content of what is written, main theme." Also in Middle English as "cause, reasons, ground; essential character; field of investigation."

Matter of course "something expected" attested from 1739. For that matter attested from 1670s. What is the matter "what concerns (someone), the cause of the difficulty" is attested from mid-15c. To make no matter "be no difference to" also is mid-15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, materie, "subject of thought, speech, or expression," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 matere, 古法语 matere "subject, theme, topic; substance, content, material; character, education" (12 世纪, 现代法语 matière), 源自 拉丁语 materia "substance from which something is made," also "hard inner wood of a tree" (source also of 葡萄牙语 madeira "wood"), 源自 mater "origin, source, mother" （参见 mother (n.1)). Or, on another theory, it represents *dmateria, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *dem-/*dom- (source of 拉丁语 domus "house," English timber). With sense development in 拉丁语 influenced by 希腊语 hyle （参见 hylo-), of which it was the equivalent in philosophy. 义为 "physical substance generally, matter, material" is 14 世纪初; that of "substance of which some specific object is made or consists of" 见于 14 世纪晚期 That of "piece of business, affair, activity, situation, circumstance" 始于 14 世纪晚期 From 14 世纪中期 as "subject of a literary work, content of what is written, main theme." Also in 中古英语 as "cause, reasons, ground; essential character; field of investigation." Matter of course "something expected" attested 自 1739 年起. For that matter attested 源自 1670 年代. What is the matter "what concerns (someone), the cause of the difficulty" 见于 15 世纪中期 To make no matter "be no difference to" also is 15 世纪中期

"bring to maturity," from Latin maturare "to ripen, bring to maturity," from maturus "ripe, timely, early," related to manus "good" and mane "early, of the morning," from PIE root *ma- (1) "good," with derivatives meaning "occurring at a good moment, timely, seasonable, early." Meaning "come or bring to maturity" is from 1620s. The financial sense of "reach the time for payment" is from 1861. Related: Matured; maturing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "encourage suppuration;" 15 世纪中期 "bring to maturity," 源自 拉丁语 maturare "to ripen, bring to maturity," 源自 maturus "ripe, timely, early," related to manus "good" and mane "early, of the morning," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ma- (1) "good," with derivatives 意为 "occurring at a good moment, timely, seasonable, early." 义为 "come or bring to maturity" 始于 1620 年代. The financial 语义 "reach the time for payment" 始于 1861 年. 同源词：Matured; maturing.

example.en: She made a mature decision after carefully weighing all the risks.
example.zh: 她在仔细权衡所有风险后做出了一个成熟的决定。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "maturity of character;" mid-15c., "ripeness," from Middle French maturité and directly from Latin maturitatem (nominative maturitas) "ripeness," from maturus "ripe" (see mature (v.)). Financial sense "state of being due for payment" is from 1815.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "maturity of character;" 15 世纪中期, "ripeness," 源自 中古法语 maturité and 直接源自 拉丁语 maturitatem (主格 maturitas) "ripeness," 源自 maturus "ripe" （参见 mature （动）). Financial sense "state of being due for payment" 始于 1815 年.

example.en: Emotional maturity takes time and varied life experiences to develop.
example.zh: 情绪成熟需要时间和多样的人生经历来培养。

entries.etymology: 1802, formed in English from maximum + -ize; first attested in Bentham, who used it often. Related: Maximized; maximizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1802 年, formed in English 源自 maximum + -ize; 最早见于 in Bentham, who used it 常. 同源词：Maximized; maximizing.

example.en: The new schedule was designed to maximize productivity during peak hours.
example.zh: 新的时间表旨在高峰时段最大化生产效率。

entries.definition: n. 最大量，最高值 a，最大的，最高的
entries.etymology: 1740, from French maximum and directly from Latin maximum (plural maxima), neuter of maximus "greatest," which is superlative of magnus "great, large" (see magnum).
entries.etymologyZh: 1740 年, 源自 法语 maximum and 直接源自 拉丁语 maximum (plural maxima), neuter of maximus "greatest," which is superlative of magnus "great, large" （参见 magnum).

example.en: The temperature reached its maximum of 42 degrees that summer.
example.zh: 那个夏天气温达到了42度的最高值。

definitionLines: auz.v. 可能，或许；可以， 不妨；祝，愿
entries.definition: auz.v. 可能，或许；可以， 不妨；祝，愿
entries.etymology: fifth month, early 12c., from Old French mai and directly from Latin Majus, Maius mensis "month of May," possibly from Maja, Maia, a Roman earth goddess (wife of Vulcan) whose name is of unknown origin; possibly from PIE *mag-ya "she who is great," fem. suffixed form of root *meg- "great" (cognate with Latin magnus). Replaced Old English þrimilce, month in which cows can be milked three times a day. May marriages have been considered unlucky at least since Ovid's day. May-apple attested from 1733, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: fifth month, 12 世纪初, 源自 古法语 mai and 直接源自 拉丁语 Majus, Maius mensis "month of May," possibly 源自 Maja, Maia, a Roman earth goddess (wife of Vulcan) whose name is 来源不详; possibly 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mag-ya "she who is great," fem. suffixed form of root *meg- "great" (与 … 同源 拉丁语 magnus). Replaced 古英语 þrimilce, month in which cows can be milked three times a day. May marriages have been considered unlucky at least 自 Ovid's day. May-apple attested 自 1733 年起, American English.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from (it) may be; see may (v.1) + be (v.). Still sometimes written as two words early 19c.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 (it) may be; 参见 may (v.1) + be （动）. Still 有时 written as two words 19 世纪初

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French maire "head of a city or town government" (13c.), originally "greater, superior" (adj.), from Latin maior, major, comparative of magnus "great" (see magnum).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 maire "head of a city or town government" (13 世纪), 原义为 "greater, superior" （形）, 源自 拉丁语 maior, major, comparative of magnus "great" （参见 magnum).

example.en: The mayor gave a speech at the opening of the new library.
example.zh: 市长在新图书馆的开幕式上发表了讲话。

entries.etymology:
Old English me (dative), me, mec (accusative); oblique cases of I, from Proto-Germanic *meke (accusative), *mes (dative), source also of Old Frisian mi/mir, Old Saxon mi, Middle Dutch mi, Dutch mij, Old High German mih/mir, German mich/mir, Old Norse mik/mer, Gothic mik/mis; from PIE root *me-, oblique form of the personal pronoun of the first person singular (nominative *eg; see I); source also of Sanskrit, Avestan mam, Greek eme, Latin me, mihi, Old Irish me, Welsh mi "me," Old Church Slavonic me, Hittite ammuk.

Erroneous or vulgar use for nominative (such as it is me) attested from c. 1500. Dative preserved in obsolete meseems, methinks and expressions such as sing me a song ("dative of interest"). Reflexively, "myself, for myself, to myself" from late Old English.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 me (dative), me, mec (宾格); oblique cases of I, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *meke (宾格), *mes (dative), source also of 古弗里西语 mi/mir, 古撒克逊语 mi, Middle 荷兰语 mi, 荷兰语 mij, 古高地德语 mih/mir, 德语 mich/mir, 古北欧语 mik/mer, Gothic mik/mis; 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *me-, oblique form of the personal pronoun of the first person singular (主格 *eg; 参见 I); source also of 梵语, Avestan mam, 希腊语 eme, 拉丁语 me, mihi, Old 爱尔兰语 me, Welsh mi "me," Old Church Slavonic me, Hittite ammuk. Erroneous or vulgar use for 主格 (such as it is me) attested 源自 约 1500 年. Dative preserved in 已废 meseems, methinks and expressions such as sing me a song ("dative of interest"). Reflexively, "myself, for myself, to myself" 源自 late 古英语.

entries.etymology: Old English mædwe "meadow, pasture," originally "land covered in grass which is mown for hay;" oblique case of mæd (see mead (n.2)).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 mædwe "meadow, pasture," 原义为 "land covered in grass which is mown for hay;" oblique case of mæd （参见 mead (n.2)).

example.en: The horses grazed peacefully in the wide green meadow by the river.
example.zh: 马儿在河边宽阔的绿色草地上安静地吃草。

example.en: We had a delicious meal at the Italian restaurant downtown.
example.zh: 我们在市中心那家意大利餐厅吃了一顿美味的饭。

definitionLines: vt. 意指，意味着；意欲，打算
a. 低劣的，平庸的；卑鄙的， 吝啬的；平均的
entries.definition: vt. 意指，意味着；意欲，打算 a. 低劣的，平庸的；卑鄙的， 吝啬的；平均的 n. 平均值
entries.etymology: "that which is halfway between extremes," early 14c., from Old French meien "middle, means, intermediary," noun use of adjective from Latin medianus "of or that is in the middle" (see mean (adj.2)). Oldest sense is musical; mathematical sense is from c. 1500. Some senses reflect confusion with mean (adj.1). This is the mean in by no means (late 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: "that which is halfway between extremes," 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 meien "middle, means, intermediary," 为 … 的名词用法 形容词 源自 拉丁语 medianus "of or that is in the middle" （参见 mean (adj.2)). Oldest sense is musical; mathematical sense 始于 约 1500 年. Some senses reflect confusion with mean (adj.1). This is the mean in by no means (15 世纪晚期).

entries.etymology: "course of action," late 14c., from mean (n.); sense of "wealth" is first recorded c. 1600. Compare French moyens, German Mittel. Phrase by no means attested from late 15c.; means-test is from 1930.
entries.etymologyZh: "course of action," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 mean （名）; 语义 "wealth" is 首见于 约 1600 年. 对比 法语 moyens, 德语 Mittel. Phrase by no means attested 源自 15 世纪晚期; means-test 始于 1930 年.

example.en: A flashing red light means that you must stop and give way.
example.zh: 闪烁的红灯意味着你必须停车让行。

entries.definition: n. 其间，其时 ad.其间
entries.etymology: late 13c., "at one time or another" (adv.); as an adjective, late 15c. Meaning "at some future time" is late 14c. From some + time (n.).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "at one time or another" （副）; 作形容词时, 15 世纪晚期 义为 "at some future time" is 14 世纪晚期 From some + time （名）.

entries.definition: n. 其时，其间 ad. 同时，当时
entries.etymology: also mean while, mid-14c., from mean (adj.2) "middle, intermediate" + while (n.). Late 14c. as an adverb.
entries.etymologyZh: also mean while, 14 世纪中期, 源自 mean (adj.2) "middle, intermediate" + while （名）. Late 14 世纪 作为 副词.

example.en: The surgery lasted six hours; meanwhile, the family waited anxiously outside.
example.zh: 手术持续了六个小时；与此同时，家人在外面焦急地等待。

definitionLines: n. 度量，测量；（pL.）措施，办 法

entries.definition: n. 度量，测量；（pL.）措施，办 法 ct. 量，测量；有……长（宽/高 等）
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to deal out by measure," from Old French mesurer "measure; moderate, curb" (12c.), from Late Latin mensurare "to measure," from Latin mensura "a measuring, a measurement; thing to measure by," from mensus, past participle of metiri "to measure," from PIE *me- (2) "to measure" (see meter (n.2)).

Replaced Old English cognate mæð "measure." Meaning "to ascertain spatial dimensions of" is mid-14c. To measure up "have the necessary abilities" is 1910, American English. Related: Measured; measuring.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to deal out by measure," 源自 古法语 mesurer "measure; moderate, curb" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 mensurare "to measure," 源自 拉丁语 mensura "a measuring, a measurement; thing to measure by," 源自 mensus, 为 … 的过去分词 metiri "to measure," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *me- (2) "to measure" （参见 meter (n.2)). Replaced 古英语 同源 mæð "measure." 义为 "to ascertain spatial dimensions of" is 14 世纪中期 To measure up "have the necessary abilities" is 1910 年, American English. 同源词：Measured; measuring.

example.en: The city took strong measures to reduce air pollution last year.
example.zh: 该市去年采取了强有力的措施来减少空气污染。

definitionLines: n. 测量，度量；尺寸，大小
entries.definition: n. 测量，度量；尺寸，大小
entries.etymology: 1751, "act of measuring," from measure (v.) + -ment. Related: Measurements. Meaning "dimension obtained by measuring" is from 1756.
entries.etymologyZh: 1751 年, "act of measuring," 源自 measure （动） + -ment. 同源词：Measurements. 义为 "dimension obtained by measuring" 始于 1756 年.

example.en: Accurate measurement of the room is needed before buying furniture.
example.zh: 购买家具前需要对房间进行精确测量。

entries.etymology:
Old English mete "food, item of food" (paired with drink), from Proto-Germanic *mati (source also of Old Frisian mete, Old Saxon meti, Old Norse matr, Old High German maz, Gothic mats "food," Middle Dutch, Dutch metworst, German Mettwurst "type of sausage"), from PIE *mad-i-, from root *mad- "moist, wet," also with reference to food qualities, (source also of Sanskrit medas- "fat" (n.), Old Irish mat "pig;" see mast (n.2)).
Narrower sense of "flesh used as food" is first attested c. 1300; similar sense evolution in French viande "meat," originally "food." In Middle English, vegetables still could be called grene-mete (15c.). Figurative sense of "essential part" is from 1901. Dark meat, white meat popularized 19c., supposedly as euphemisms for leg and breast, but earliest sources use both terms without apparent embarrassment.

First record of meat loaf is from 1876. Meat-market "place where one looks for sex partners" is from 1896 (meat in various sexual senses of "penis, vagina, body regarded as a sex object, prostitute" are attested from 1590s; Old English for "meat-market" was flæsccyping ('flesh-cheaping')); meat wagon "ambulance" is from 1920, American English slang, said to date from World War I (in a literal sense by 1857). Meat-grinder in the figurative sense attested by 1951. Meat-hook in colloquial transferred sense "arm" attested by 1919.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 mete "food, item of food" (paired with drink), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *mati (source also of 古弗里西语 mete, 古撒克逊语 meti, 古北欧语 matr, 古高地德语 maz, Gothic mats "food," Middle 荷兰语, 荷兰语 metworst, 德语 Mettwurst "type of sausage"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mad-i-, 源自 root *mad- "moist, wet," also with reference to food qualities, (source also of 梵语 medas- "fat" （名）, Old 爱尔兰语 mat "pig;" 参见 mast (n.2)). Narrower 语义 "flesh used as food" is 最早见于 约 1300 年; similar sense evolution in 法语 viande "meat," 原义为 "food." In 中古英语, vegetables still could be called grene-mete (15 世纪). Figurative 语义 "essential part" 始于 1901 年. Dark meat, white meat popularized 19 世纪, supposedly as euphemisms for leg and breast, but earliest sources use both terms without apparent embarrassment. First record of meat loaf 始于 1876 年. Meat-market "place where one looks for sex partners" 始于 1896 年 (meat in various sexual senses of "penis, vagina, body regarded as a sex object, prostitute" are attested 源自 1590 年代; 古英语 for "meat-market" was flæsccyping ('flesh-cheaping')); meat wagon "ambulance" 始于 1920 年, American English 俚语, said to date 源自 World War I (in a literal sense 截至 1857 年). Meat-grinder in the figurative sense attested 截至 1951 年. Meat-hook in 口语 transferred sense "arm" attested 截至 1919 年.

example.en: Many nutritionists recommend reducing red meat consumption to protect heart health.
example.zh: 许多营养学家建议减少红肉摄入以保护心脏健康。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "pertaining to or involving mechanical labor" (now usually mechanical), also "having to do with tools," from Latin mechanicus, from Greek mekhanikos "full of resources, inventive, ingenious," literally "mechanical, pertaining to machines," from mekhane (see machine (n.)). Meaning "of the nature of or pertaining to machines" is from 1620s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "pertaining to or involving mechanical labor" (现在 通常 mechanical), also "having to do with tools," 源自 拉丁语 mechanicus, 源自 希腊语 mekhanikos "full of resources, inventive, ingenious," 字面义为 "mechanical, pertaining to machines," 源自 mekhane （参见 machine （名）). 义为 "of the nature of or pertaining to machines" 始于 1620 年代.

example.en: The mechanic quickly diagnosed the problem with the car engine.
example.zh: 那位技工迅速诊断出了汽车发动机的问题。

definitionLines: 一 Q.机械的；机械学的，力学的； 机械似的，呆板的
entries.definition: 一 Q.机械的；机械学的，力学的； 机械似的，呆板的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "of or pertaining to machines," from mechanic (adj.) + -al (1); of persons or human actions, "resembling machines, automatic" it is from c. 1600. Related: Mechanically. Mechanical-minded is recorded from 1820.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "of or pertaining to machines," 源自 mechanic （形） + -al (1); of persons or human actions, "resembling machines, automatic" it 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Mechanically. Mechanical-minded 见于 1820 年.

example.en: The assembly line performs mechanical tasks that do not require human judgment.
example.zh: 流水线执行的是不需要人类判断的机械性任务。

entries.etymology: 1640s, based on Late Latin mechanica, from Greek mekhanike, mekhanika (see mechanic (adj.)); also see -ics.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, based on 晚期拉丁语 mechanica, 源自 希腊语 mekhanike, mekhanika （参见 mechanic （形）); also 参见 -ics.

definitionLines: n. 机械装置；机构；机制
entries.definition: n. 机械装置；机构；机制
entries.etymology: 1660s, from Modern Latin mechanismus, from Greek mekhane "machine, instrument" (see machine (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 现代 拉丁语 mechanismus, 源自 希腊语 mekhane "machine, instrument" （参见 machine （名）).

example.en: Scientists are still studying the mechanism by which the virus spreads.
example.zh: 科学家们仍在研究该病毒传播的机制。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from Middle French médaille (15c.), from Italian medaglia "a medal," according to OED from Vulgar Latin *metallea (moneta) "metal (coin)," from Latin metallum (see metal). The other theory [Klein, Barnhart, Watkins] is that medaglia originally meant "coin worth half a denarius," and is from Vulgar Latin *medalia, from Late Latin medialia "little halves," neuter plural of medialis "of the middle" (see medial (adj.)). Originally a trinket or charm; as a reward for merit, proficiency, etc., attested from 1751.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 中古法语 médaille (15 世纪), 源自 意大利语 medaglia "a medal," according to OED 源自 通俗拉丁语 *metallea (moneta) "metal (coin)," 源自 拉丁语 metallum （参见 metal). The other theory [Klein, Barnhart, Watkins] is that medaglia 原义为 meant "coin worth half a denarius," and 始于 通俗拉丁语 *medalia, 源自 晚期拉丁语 medialia "little halves," neuter 为 … 的复数 medialis "of the middle" （参见 medial （形）). Originally a trinket or charm; 作为 reward for merit, proficiency, etc., attested 自 1751 年起.

example.en: The soldier was awarded a gold medal for his bravery in battle.
example.zh: 这名士兵因在战场上的英勇表现而被授予金质奖章。

definitionLines: n. 媒体；媒介，媒介物，传导体
entries.definition: n. 媒体；媒介，媒介物，传导体
entries.etymology: "newspapers, radio, TV, etc." 1927, perhaps abstracted from mass media (1923, a technical term in advertising), plural of medium, on notion of "intermediate agency," a sense found in that word in English from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: "newspapers, radio, TV, etc." 1927 年, 或许 abstracted 源自 mass media (1923 年, a technical term in advertising), 为 … 的复数 medium, on 概念 "intermediate agency," a sense found in that word in English 源自 约 1600 年.

example.en: The story spread quickly through online media channels overnight.
example.zh: 这则报道通过网络媒体渠道一夜之间迅速传播开来。

entries.definition: vi. 调解；斡旋；居中 vt.调停；传达
entries.etymology: 1540s, "divide in two equal parts," probably a back-formation from mediation or mediator, or else from Latin mediatus, past participle of mediare "to halve," later, "be in the middle," from Latin medius "middle" (see medial (adj.)). Meaning "act as a mediator" is from 1610s; that of "settle by mediation" is from 1560s. Related: Mediated, mediates, mediating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "divide in two equal parts," 可能 a back-formation 源自 mediation or mediator，或else 源自 拉丁语 mediatus, 为 … 的过去分词 mediare "to halve," later, "be in the middle," 源自 拉丁语 medius "middle" （参见 medial （形）). 义为 "act as a mediator" 始于 1610 年代; that of "settle by mediation" 始于 1560 年代. 同源词：Mediated, mediates, mediating.

entries.etymology: 1640s, from French médical, from Late Latin medicalis "of a physician," from Latin medicus "physician, surgeon, medical man" (n.); "healing, madicinal" (adj.), from mederi "to heal, give medical attention to, cure," originally "know the best course for," from an early specialization of the PIE root *med- "to measure, limit, consider, advise, take appropriate measures" (source also of Greek medomai "be mindful of," medein "to rule;"  Avestan vi-mad- "physician;" Latin meditari "think or reflect on, consider;" Irish miduir "judge;" Old English metan "to measure out"); also see meditation. The earlier adjective in English in this sense was medicinal. Related: Medically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 法语 médical, 源自 晚期拉丁语 medicalis "of a physician," 源自 拉丁语 medicus "physician, surgeon, medical man" （名）; "healing, madicinal" （形）, 源自 mederi "to heal, give medical attention to, cure," 原义为 "know the best course for," 源自 an early specialization of the 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *med- "to measure, limit, consider, advise, take appropriate measures" (source also of 希腊语 medomai "be mindful of," medein "to rule;" Avestan vi-mad- "physician;" 拉丁语 meditari "think or reflect on, consider;" 爱尔兰语 miduir "judge;" 古英语 metan "to measure out"); also 参见 meditation. The earlier 形容词 in English in this sense was medicinal. 同源词：Medically.

definitionLines: n. 内服药，医药；医学，医术
entries.definition: n. 内服药，医药；医学，医术
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "medical treatment, cure, remedy," also used figuratively, of spiritual remedies, from Old French medecine (Modern French médicine) "medicine, art of healing, cure, treatment, potion," from Latin medicina "the healing art, medicine; a remedy," also used figuratively, perhaps originally ars medicina "the medical art," from fem. of medicinus (adj.) "of a doctor," from medicus "a physician" (see medical); though OED finds evidence for this is wanting. Meaning "a medicinal potion or plaster" in English is mid-14c.

To take (one's) medicine "submit to something disagreeable" is first recorded 1865. North American Indian medicine-man "shaman" is first attested 1801, from American Indian adoption of the word medicine in sense of "magical influence." The U.S.-Canadian boundary they called Medicine Line (first attested 1910), because it conferred a kind of magic protection: punishment for crimes committed on one side of it could be avoided by crossing over to the other. Medicine show "traveling show meant to attract a crowd so patent medicine can be sold to them" is American English, 1938. Medicine ball "stuffed leather ball used for exercise" is from 1889.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "medical treatment, cure, remedy," also used figuratively, of spiritual remedies, 源自 古法语 medecine (现代法语 médicine) "medicine, art of healing, cure, treatment, potion," 源自 拉丁语 medicina "the healing art, medicine; a remedy," also used figuratively, 或许 原义为 ars medicina "the medical art," 源自 fem. of medicinus （形） "of a doctor," 源自 medicus "a physician" （参见 medical); though OED finds evidence for this is wanting. 义为 "a medicinal potion or plaster" in English is 14 世纪中期 To take (one's) medicine "submit to something disagreeable" is 首见于 1865 年. North American Indian medicine-man "shaman" is 最早见于 1801 年, 源自 American Indian adoption of the word medicine in 语义 "magical influence." The U.S.-Canadian boundary they called Medicine Line (最早见于 1910 年), because it conferred a kind of magic protection: punishment for crimes committed on one side of it could be avoided by crossing over to the other. Medicine show "traveling show meant to attract a crowd so patent medicine can be sold to them" is American English, 1938 年. Medicine ball "stuffed leather ball used for exercise" 始于 1889 年.

example.en: She took her medicine on time every day as the doctor prescribed.
example.zh: 她每天按时按医嘱服药。

entries.etymology: 1827, "pertaining to or suggestive of the Middle Ages," coined in English from Latin medium "the middle" (see medium (n.)) + aevum "age" (see eon).
entries.etymologyZh: 1827 年, "pertaining to or suggestive of the Middle Ages," coined in English 源自 拉丁语 medium "the middle" （参见 medium （名）) + aevum "age" （参见 eon).

example.en: The castle was built during the medieval period and still stands today.
example.zh: 这座城堡建于中世纪，至今仍然矗立。

entries.etymology: "the sea between southern Europe and northern Africa," c. 1400, from Late Latin Mediterraneum mare "Mediterranean Sea" (7c.), from Latin mediterraneus "midland;" the original sense being of "sea in the middle of the earth," from medius "middle" (see medial (adj.)) + terra "land, earth" (see terrain). The Old English name was Wendel-sæ, so called for the Vandals, Germanic tribe that settled on the southwest coast of it after the fall of Rome. The noun meaning "a person of Mediterranean race" is from 1888.
entries.etymologyZh: "the sea between southern Europe and northern Africa," 约 1400 年, 源自 晚期拉丁语 Mediterraneum mare "Mediterranean Sea" (7 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 mediterraneus "midland;" the original sense being of "sea in the middle of the earth," 源自 medius "middle" （参见 medial （形）) + terra "land, earth" （参见 terrain). The 古英语 name was Wendel-sæ, so called for the Vandals, 日耳曼语 tribe that settled on the southwest coast of it after the fall of Rome. The 名词 意为 "a person of Mediterranean race" 始于 1888 年.

entries.definition: a. 中等的，适中的 n. 中间，适中；
entries.etymology: 1580s, "a middle ground, quality, or degree," from Latin medium "the middle, midst, center; interval," noun use of neuter of adjective medius (see medial (adj.)). Meaning "intermediate agency, channel of communication" is from c. 1600. That of "person who conveys spiritual messages" first recorded 1853, from notion of "substance through which something is conveyed." Artistic sense (oil, watercolors, etc.) is from 1854. Happy medium is the "golden mean," Horace's aurea mediocritas.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "a middle ground, quality, or degree," 源自 拉丁语 medium "the middle, midst, center; interval," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of 形容词 medius （参见 medial （形）). 义为 "intermediate agency, channel of communication" 始于 约 1600 年. That of "person who conveys spiritual messages" 首见于 1853 年, 源自 概念 "substance through which something is conveyed." Artistic sense (oil, watercolors, etc.) 始于 1854 年. Happy medium is the "golden mean," Horace's aurea mediocritas.

example.en: The restaurant offered meals at a medium price range.
example.zh: 这家餐厅提供中等价位的餐食。

definitionLines: v. 遇见，碰上；会见，迎接；会 合，开会；遭到，经历；满足， 符合
entries.definition: v. 遇见，碰上；会见，迎接；会 合，开会；遭到，经历；满足， 符合 n. 聚会，运动会
entries.etymology: Old English metan "to find, find out; fall in with, encounter; obtain," from Proto-Germanic *motjan (source also of Old Norse mæta, Old Frisian meta, Old Saxon motian "to meet," Gothic gamotijan), from PIE root *mod- "to meet, assemble." Related to Old English gemot "meeting." Meaning "to assemble" is from 1520s. Of things, "to come into contact," c. 1300. Related: Met; meeting. To meet (someone) halfway in the figurative sense is from 1620s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 metan "to find, find out; fall in with, encounter; obtain," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *motjan (source also of 古北欧语 mæta, 古弗里西语 meta, 古撒克逊语 motian "to meet," Gothic gamotijan), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *mod- "to meet, assemble." Related to 古英语 gemot "meeting." 义为 "to assemble" 始于 1520 年代. Of things, "to come into contact," 约 1300 年. 同源词：Met; meeting. To meet (someone) halfway in the figurative sense 始于 1620 年代.

example.en: Let us meet at the coffee shop near the library at noon.
example.zh: 我们中午在图书馆附近的咖啡店见面吧。

entries.etymology: "action of coming together," Old English gemeting, verbal noun from meet (v.). Meaning "gathering of people for discussion, etc." is from 1510s. In 17c., it was applied generally to worship assemblies of nonconformists, but this now is retained mostly by Quakers.
entries.etymologyZh: "action of coming together," 古英语 gemeting, verbal 名词 源自 meet （动）. 义为 "gathering of people for discussion, etc." 始于 1510 年代. In 17 世纪, it was applied generally to worship assemblies of nonconformists, but this 现在 is retained mostly by Quakers.

example.en: The weekly meeting was postponed due to the manager's absence.
example.zh: 由于经理缺席，每周例会被推迟了。

definitionLines: n. 旋律；歌曲；美妙的音乐
entries.definition: n. 旋律；歌曲；美妙的音乐
entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French melodie "music, song, tune" (12c.), from Late Latin melodia, from Greek meloidia "a singing, a chanting, choral song, a tune for lyric poetry," from melos "song, part of song" (see melisma) + oide "song, ode" (see ode).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 melodie "music, song, tune" (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 melodia, 源自 希腊语 meloidia "a singing, a chanting, choral song, a tune for lyric poetry," 源自 melos "song, part of song" （参见 melisma) + oide "song, ode" （参见 ode).

example.en: She hummed a soft melody while washing the dishes after dinner.
example.zh: 她洗完晚饭的碗碟时，轻声哼着一段柔和的旋律。

entries.etymology:
Old English meltan "become liquid, consume by fire, burn up" (class III strong verb; past tense mealt, past participle molten), from Proto-Germanic *meltanan; fused with Old English gemæltan (Anglian), gemyltan (West Saxon) "make liquid," from Proto-Germanic *gamaltijan (source also of Old Norse melta "to digest"), both from PIE *meldh-, (source also of Sanskrit mrduh "soft, mild," Greek meldein "to melt, make liquid," Latin mollis "soft, mild"), from root *mel- "soft," with derivatives referring to soft or softened (especially ground) materials (see mild). Figurative use by c. 1200. Related: Melted; melting.

Of food, to melt in (one's) mouth is from 1690s. Melting pot is from 1540s; figurative use from 1855; popularized with reference to America by play "The Melting Pot" by Israel Zangwill (1908).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 meltan "become liquid, consume by fire, burn up" (class III strong 动词; past tense mealt, past participle molten), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *meltanan; fused with 古英语 gemæltan (Anglian), gemyltan (West Saxon) "make liquid," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *gamaltijan (source also of 古北欧语 melta "to digest"), both 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *meldh-, (source also of 梵语 mrduh "soft, mild," 希腊语 meldein "to melt, make liquid," 拉丁语 mollis "soft, mild"), 源自 root *mel- "soft," with derivatives referring to soft or softened (尤指 ground) materials （参见 mild). Figurative use by 约 1200 年. 同源词：Melted; melting. Of food, to melt in (one's) mouth 始于 1690 年代. Melting pot 始于 1540 年代; figurative use 自 1855 年起; popularized with reference to America by play "The Melting Pot" by Israel Zangwill (1908 年).

example.en: The ice sculpture slowly began to melt under the hot studio lights.
example.zh: 冰雕在炽热的摄影棚灯光下开始慢慢融化。

entries.etymology: late 13c., "sex organ" (compare Latin membrum virile, but in English originally of women as well as men), also, "body part or organ" (in plural, "the body"), from Old French membre "part, portion; topic, subject; limb, member of the body; member" (of a group, etc.)," 11c., from Latin membrum "limb, member of the body, part," probably from PIE *mems-ro, from root *mems- "flesh, meat" (source also of Sanskrit mamsam "flesh;" Greek meninx "membrane," meros "thigh" (the "fleshy part"); Gothic mimz "flesh"). In English, sense of "person belonging to a group" is first attested early 14c., from notion of "constituent part of a complex structure." Meaning "one who has been elected to parliament" is from early 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "sex organ" (对比 拉丁语 membrum virile, but in English 原义为 of women as well as men), also, "body part or organ" (in plural, "the body"), 源自 古法语 membre "part, portion; topic, subject; limb, member of the body; member" (of a group, etc.)," 11c., from Latin membrum "limb, member of the body, part," probably from PIE *mems-ro, from root *mems- "flesh, meat" (source also of Sanskrit mamsam "flesh;" Greek meninx "membrane," meros "thigh" (the "fleshy part"); Gothic mimz "flesh"). In English, sense of "person belonging to a group" is first attested early 14c., from notion of "constituent part of a complex structure." Meaning "one who has been elected to parliament" 始于 15 世纪初

example.en: Only a paid member of the club can vote at the annual general meeting.
example.zh: 只有缴费的俱乐部成员才能在年度大会上投票。

definitionLines: n. 成员资格，会员资格
entries.definition: n. 成员资格，会员资格
entries.etymology: 1640s, "state of being a member," from member + -ship. Meaning "number of members" is from 1850.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "state of being a member," 源自 member + -ship. 义为 "number of members" 始于 1850 年.

example.en: Annual membership to the gym includes unlimited access to all fitness classes.
example.zh: 健身房的年度会员资格包含所有健身课程的无限次参与权。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin memorandum "(thing) to be remembered," neuter singular of memorandus "worthy of remembrance, noteworthy," gerundive of memorare "to call to mind," from memor "mindful of" (see memory). Originally a word written at the top of a note, by 1540s it came to stand for the note itself. The Latin plural is memoranda. Compare also agenda.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 memorandum "(thing) to be remembered," neuter singular of memorandus "worthy of remembrance, noteworthy," gerundive of memorare "to call to mind," 源自 memor "mindful of" （参见 memory). Originally a word written at the top of a note, by 1540 年代 it came to stand for the note itself. The 拉丁语 plural is memoranda. 对比 also agenda.

entries.definition: a.记忆的，纪念的 n.纪念物，纪念碑，纪念馆
entries.etymology: late 14c., "memorable, excellent; remembered, committed to memory," from Old French memorial "mindful of, remembering," from Latin memorialis (adj.) "of or belonging to memory," from memoria "memory" (see memory).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "memorable, excellent; remembered, committed to memory," 源自 古法语 memorial "mindful of, remembering," 源自 拉丁语 memorialis （形） "of or belonging to memory," 源自 memoria "memory" （参见 memory).

example.en: A memorial was built in the town square to honor the fallen soldiers.
example.zh: 在城镇广场建造了一座纪念碑，以纪念牺牲的士兵。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "commit to writing;" see memory + -ize. The meaning "commit to memory" is from 1838. Related: Memorized; memorizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "commit to writing;" 参见 memory + -ize. The 意为 "commit to memory" 始于 1838 年. 同源词：Memorized; memorizing.

definitionLines: n. 记忆力，记忆；回忆；内存
entries.definition: n. 记忆力，记忆；回忆；内存
entries.etymology:
mid-13c., "recollection (of someone or something); awareness, consciousness," also "fame, renown, reputation," from Anglo-French memorie (Old French memoire, 11c., "mind, memory, remembrance; memorial, record") and directly from Latin memoria "memory, remembrance, faculty of remembering," noun of quality from memor "mindful, remembering," from PIE root *(s)mer- (1) "to remember" (Sanskrit smarati "remembers," Avestan mimara "mindful;" Greek merimna "care, thought," mermeros "causing anxiety, mischievous, baneful;" Serbo-Croatian mariti "to care for;" Welsh marth "sadness, anxiety;" Old Norse Mimir, name of the giant who guards the Well of Wisdom; Old English gemimor "known," murnan "mourn, remember sorrowfully;" Dutch mijmeren "to ponder"). Meaning "faculty of remembering" is late 14c. in English.

Computer sense, "device which stores information," is from 1946. Related: Memories.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "recollection (of someone or something); awareness, consciousness," also "fame, renown, reputation," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 memorie (古法语 memoire, 11 世纪, "mind, memory, remembrance; memorial, record") and 直接源自 拉丁语 memoria "memory, remembrance, faculty of remembering," 名词 of quality 源自 memor "mindful, remembering," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *(s)mer- (1) "to remember" (梵语 smarati "remembers," Avestan mimara "mindful;" 希腊语 merimna "care, thought," mermeros "causing anxiety, mischievous, baneful;" Serbo-Croatian mariti "to care for;" Welsh marth "sadness, anxiety;" 古北欧语 Mimir, name of the giant who guards the Well of Wisdom; 古英语 gemimor "known," murnan "mourn, remember sorrowfully;" 荷兰语 mijmeren "to ponder"). 义为 "faculty of remembering" is 14 世纪晚期 in English. Computer sense, "device which stores information," 始于 1946 年. 同源词：Memories.

example.en: She has an excellent memory for names and faces.
example.zh: 她对姓名和面孔有极强的记忆力。

entries.etymology: plural of man (n.). To separate the men from the boys in a figurative sense is from 1943; earliest uses tend to credit it to U.S. aviators in World War II.
entries.etymologyZh: 为 … 的复数 man （名）. To separate the men 源自 boys in a figurative sense 始于 1943 年; earliest uses tend to credit it to U.S. aviators in World War II.

entries.definition: n. 威胁；恐吓 vi. 恐吓；进行威胁 vt. 威胁；恐吓
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "declaration of hostile intent," also "act of threatening," from Old French menace "menace, threat" (9c.), from Vulgar Latin minacia "threat, menace" (also source of Spanish amenaza, Italian minaccia), singular of Latin minaciæ "threatening things," from minax (genitive minacis) "threatening," from minari "threaten, jut, project," from minæ "threats, projecting points," from PIE root *men- (2) "to project" (see mount (n.1)). Applied to persons from 1936.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "declaration of hostile intent," also "act of threatening," 源自 古法语 menace "menace, threat" (9 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 minacia "threat, menace" (also source of 西班牙语 amenaza, 意大利语 minaccia), singular of 拉丁语 minaciæ "threatening things," 源自 minax (属格 minacis) "threatening," 源自 minari "threaten, jut, project," 源自 minæ "threats, projecting points," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *men- (2) "to project" （参见 mount (n.1)). Applied to persons 自 1936 年起.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "to repair," from a shortened form of Old French amender (see amend). Meaning "to put right, atone for, amend (one's life), repent" is from c. 1300; that of "to regain health" is from early 15c. Related: Mended; mending.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "to repair," 源自 a shortened form of 古法语 amender （参见 amend). 义为 "to put right, atone for, amend (one's life), repent" 始于 约 1300 年; that of "to regain health" 始于 15 世纪初 同源词：Mended; mending.

definitionLines: a. 思想的，精神的；智力的， 脑力的
entries.definition: a. 思想的，精神的；智力的， 脑力的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "pertaining to the mind," from Middle French mental, from Late Latin mentalis "of the mind," from Latin mens (genitive mentis) "mind," from PIE root *men- "to think" (source also of Sanskrit matih "thought, mind," Gothic gamunds, Old English gemynd "memory, remembrance;" see mind (n.)). Meaning "crazy, deranged" is from 1927, probably from combinations such as mental hospital.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "pertaining to the mind," 源自 中古法语 mental, 源自 晚期拉丁语 mentalis "of the mind," 源自 拉丁语 mens (属格 mentis) "mind," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *men- "to think" (source also of 梵语 matih "thought, mind," Gothic gamunds, 古英语 gemynd "memory, remembrance;" 参见 mind （名）). 义为 "crazy, deranged" 始于 1927 年, 可能 源自 combinations such as mental hospital.

example.en: Therapy and meditation both contribute to mental health and emotional stability.
example.zh: 心理治疗和冥想都有助于心理健康和情绪稳定。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "a note, reference," from Old French mencion "mention, memory, speech," from Latin mentionem (nominative mentio) "a calling to mind, a speaking of, a making mention," from root of Old Latin minisci "to think," related to mens (genitive mentis) "mind," from PIE root *men- (1) "think" (see mind (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "a note, reference," 源自 古法语 mencion "mention, memory, speech," 源自 拉丁语 mentionem (主格 mentio) "a calling to mind, a speaking of, a making mention," 源自 root of Old 拉丁语 minisci "to think," related to mens (属格 mentis) "mind," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *men- (1) "think" （参见 mind （名）).

example.en: She briefly mentioned the incident but refused to give any details.
example.zh: 她简短地提了一下那件事，但拒绝透露任何细节。

entries.etymology: 1837, from French menu de repas "list of what is served at a meal," from Middle French menu (adj.) "small, detailed" (11c.), from Latin minutus "small," literally "made smaller," past participle of minuere "to diminish," from root of minus "to diminish" (see minus). Computer usage is from 1967, from expanded sense of "any detailed list," first attested 1889.
entries.etymologyZh: 1837 年, 源自 法语 menu de repas "list of what is served at a meal," 源自 中古法语 menu （形） "small, detailed" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 minutus "small," 字面义为 "made smaller," 为 … 的过去分词 minuere "to diminish," 源自 root of minus "to diminish" （参见 minus). Computer usage 始于 1967 年, 源自 expanded 语义 "any detailed list," 最早见于 1889 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Anglo-French marchaunt "merchant, shopkeeper" (Old French marcheant, Modern French marchand), from Vulgar Latin *mercatantem (nominative *mercatans) "a buyer," present participle of *mercatare, frequentative of Latin mercari "to trade, traffic, deal in" (see market). Meaning "fellow, chap" is from 1540s; with a specific qualifier, and suggesting someone who deals in it (such as speed merchant "one who enjoys fast driving"), from 1914.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 marchaunt "merchant, shopkeeper" (古法语 marcheant, 现代法语 marchand), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *mercatantem (主格 *mercatans) "a buyer," 为 … 的现在分词 *mercatare, 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 mercari "to trade, traffic, deal in" （参见 market). 义为 "fellow, chap" 始于 1540 年代; with a specific qualifier, and suggesting someone who deals in it (such as speed merchant "one who enjoys fast driving"), 自 1914 年起.

example.en: The silk merchant traveled thousands of miles to reach Europe.
example.zh: 这位丝绸商人跋山涉水数千英里才抵达欧洲。

entries.etymology: "the Roman god Mercury," mid-12c., from Latin Mercurius "Mercury," originally a god of tradesmen and thieves, from merx "merchandise" (see market (n.)); or perhaps [Klein, Tucker] from Etruscan and influenced by merx. Later he was associated with Greek Hermes. The planet closest to the sun so called in classical Latin (late 14c. in English). A hypothetical inhabitant of the planet was a Mercurean (1855) or a Mercurian (1868). For the metallic element, see mercury.
entries.etymologyZh: "the Roman god Mercury," 12 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 Mercurius "Mercury," 原义为 a god of tradesmen and thieves, 源自 merx "merchandise" （参见 market （名）); or 或许 [Klein, Tucker] 源自 Etruscan and influenced by merx. Later he was associated with 希腊语 Hermes. The planet closest to the sun so called in classical 拉丁语 (14 世纪晚期 in English). A hypothetical inhabitant of the planet was a Mercurean (1855 年) or a Mercurian (1868 年). For the metallic element, 参见 mercury.

entries.etymology:
late 12c., "God's forgiveness of his creatures' offenses," from Old French mercit, merci (9c.) "reward, gift; kindness, grace, pity," from Latin mercedem (nominative merces) "reward, wages, pay hire" (in Vulgar Latin "favor, pity"), from merx (genitive mercis) "wares, merchandise" (see market (n.)). In Church Latin (6c.) applied to the heavenly reward of those who show kindness to the helpless.

Meaning "disposition to forgive or show compassion" is attested from early 13c. As an interjection, attested from mid-13c. In French largely superseded by miséricorde except as a word of thanks. Seat of mercy "golden covering of the Ark of the Covenant" (1530) is Tyndale's loan-translation of Luther's gnadenstuhl, an inexact rendering of Hebrew kapporeth, literally "propitiatory."
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪晚期, "God's forgiveness of his creatures' offenses," 源自 古法语 mercit, merci (9 世纪) "reward, gift; kindness, grace, pity," 源自 拉丁语 mercedem (主格 merces) "reward, wages, pay hire" (in 通俗拉丁语 "favor, pity"), 源自 merx (属格 mercis) "wares, merchandise" （参见 market （名）). In 教会拉丁语 (6 世纪) applied to the heavenly reward of those who show kindness to the helpless. 义为 "disposition to forgive or show compassion" 见于 13 世纪初 作为 interjection, attested 源自 13 世纪中期 In 法语 largely superseded by miséricorde except 作为 word of thanks. Seat of mercy "golden covering of the Ark of the Covenant" (1530 年) is Tyndale's loan-translation of Luther's gnadenstuhl, an inexact rendering of 希伯来语 kapporeth, 字面义为 "propitiatory."

example.en: The judge showed mercy and reduced the prisoner's sentence.
example.zh: 法官发了慈悲，减轻了囚犯的刑期。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "unmixed, pure," from Old French mier "pure" (of gold), "entire, total, complete," and directly from Latin merus "unmixed" (of wine), "pure; bare, naked;" figuratively "true, real, genuine," probably originally "clear, bright," from PIE *mer- "to gleam, glimmer, sparkle" (source also of Old English amerian "to purify," Old Irish emer "not clear," Sanskrit maricih "ray, beam," Greek marmarein "to gleam, glimmer"). Original sense of "nothing less than, absolute" (mid-15c., now only in vestiges such as mere folly) existed for centuries alongside opposite sense of "nothing more than" (1580s, as in a mere dream).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "unmixed, pure," 源自 古法语 mier "pure" (of gold), "entire, total, complete," and 直接源自 拉丁语 merus "unmixed" (of wine), "pure; bare, naked;" figuratively "true, real, genuine," 可能 原义为 "clear, bright," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mer- "to gleam, glimmer, sparkle" (source also of 古英语 amerian "to purify," Old 爱尔兰语 emer "not clear," 梵语 maricih "ray, beam," 希腊语 marmarein "to gleam, glimmer"). Original 语义 "nothing less than, absolute" (15 世纪中期, 现在 only in vestiges such as mere folly) existed for centuries alongside opposite 语义 "nothing more than" (1580 年代, as in a mere dream).

entries.definition: vt. 合并；吞没；使合并 vi. 合并；融合
entries.etymology: 1630s, "to plunge or sink in," from Latin mergere "to dip, dip in, immerse, plunge," probably rhotacized from *mezgo, from PIE *mezg- "to dip, plunge" (source also of Sanskrit majjati "dives under," Lithuanian mazgoju "to wash"). Legal sense of "absorb an estate, contract, etc. into another" is from 1726. Related: Merged; merging. As a noun, from 1805.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "to plunge or sink in," 源自 拉丁语 mergere "to dip, dip in, immerse, plunge," 可能 rhotacized 源自 *mezgo, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mezg- "to dip, plunge" (source also of 梵语 majjati "dives under," Lithuanian mazgoju "to wash"). Legal 语义 "absorb an estate, contract, etc. into another" 始于 1726 年. 同源词：Merged; merging. 作名词时, 自 1805 年起.

example.en: The two banks agreed to merge and form the largest financial institution in the country.

entries.etymology: 1728 in legal sense, "extinguishment by absorption,"  from merge (v.), on analogy of French infinitives used as nouns (see waiver). From 1889 in the business sense; not common until c. 1926. General meaning "any act of merging" is from 1881.
entries.etymologyZh: 1728 年 in legal sense, "extinguishment by absorption," 源自 merge （动）, on analogy of 法语 infinitives used as nouns （参见 waiver). From 1889 年 in the business sense; not common until 约 1926 年. General 意为 "any act of merging" 始于 1881 年.

example.en: The merger between the two banks created the largest financial group in the country.

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "spiritual credit" (for good works, etc.); c. 1300, "spiritual reward," from Old French merite "wages, pay, reward; thanks; merit, moral worth, that which assures divine pity," and directly from Latin meritum "a merit, service, kindness, benefit, favor; worth, value, importance," neuter of meritus, past participle of merere, meriri "to earn, deserve, acquire, gain," from PIE root *(s)mer- (2) "to allot, assign" (source also of Greek meros "part, lot," moira "share, fate," moros "fate, destiny, doom," Hittite mark "to divide" a sacrifice).

Sense of "worthiness, excellence" is from early 14c.; from late 14c. as "condition or conduct that deserves either reward or punishment;" also "a reward, benefit." Related: Merits. Merit system attested from 1880. Merit-monger was in common use 16c.-17c. in a sense roughly of "do-gooder."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "spiritual credit" (for good works, etc.); 约 1300 年, "spiritual reward," 源自 古法语 merite "wages, pay, reward; thanks; merit, moral worth, that which assures divine pity," and 直接源自 拉丁语 meritum "a merit, service, kindness, benefit, favor; worth, value, importance," neuter of meritus, 为 … 的过去分词 merere, meriri "to earn, deserve, acquire, gain," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *(s)mer- (2) "to allot, assign" (source also of 希腊语 meros "part, lot," moira "share, fate," moros "fate, destiny, doom," Hittite mark "to divide" a sacrifice). 义为 "worthiness, excellence" 始于 14 世纪初; 源自 14 世纪晚期 as "condition or conduct that deserves either reward or punishment;" also "a reward, benefit." 同源词：Merits. Merit system attested 自 1880 年起. Merit-monger was in common use 16 世纪-17 世纪 in a sense roughly of "do-gooder."

example.en: The main merit of this approach is its simplicity and low cost.

entries.etymology:
Old English myrge "pleasing, agreeable, pleasant, sweet; pleasantly, melodiously," from Proto-Germanic *murgijaz, which probably originally meant "short-lasting," (compare Old High German murg "short," Gothic gamaurgjan "to shorten"), from PIE *mreghu- "short" (see brief (adj.)). The only exact cognate for meaning outside English was Middle Dutch mergelijc "joyful."

Connection to "pleasure" is likely via notion of "making time fly, that which makes the time seem to pass quickly" (compare German Kurzweil "pastime," literally "a short time;" Old Norse skemta "to amuse, entertain, amuse oneself," from skamt, neuter of skammr "short"). There also was a verbal form in Old English, myrgan "be merry, rejoice." For vowel evolution, see bury (v.).The word had much wider senses in Middle English, such as "pleasant-sounding" (of animal voices), "fine" (of weather), "handsome" (of dress), "pleasant-tasting" (of herbs). Merry-bout "an incident of sexual intercourse" was low slang from 1780. Merry-begot "illegitimate" (adj.), "bastard" (n.) is from 1785. Merrie England (now frequently satirical or ironic) is 14c. meri ingland, originally in a broader sense of "bountiful, prosperous." Merry Monday was a 16c. term for "the Monday before Shrove Tuesday" (Mardi Gras).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 myrge "pleasing, agreeable, pleasant, sweet; pleasantly, melodiously," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *murgijaz, which 可能 原义为 meant "short-lasting," (对比 古高地德语 murg "short," Gothic gamaurgjan "to shorten"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mreghu- "short" （参见 brief （形）). The only exact 同源 for 意为 outside English was Middle 荷兰语 mergelijc "joyful." Connection to "pleasure" is likely 经由 概念 "making time fly, that which makes the time seem to pass quickly" (对比 德语 Kurzweil "pastime," 字面义为 "a short time;" 古北欧语 skemta "to amuse, entertain, amuse oneself," 源自 skamt, neuter of skammr "short"). There also was a verbal form in 古英语, myrgan "be merry, rejoice." For vowel evolution, 参见 bury （动）.The word had much wider senses in 中古英语, such as "pleasant-sounding" (of animal voices), "fine" (of weather), "handsome" (of dress), "pleasant-tasting" (of herbs). Merry-bout "an incident of sexual intercourse" was low 俚语 自 1780 年起. Merry-begot "illegitimate" （形）, "bastard" （名） 始于 1785 年. Merrie England (现在 frequently satirical or ironic) is 14 世纪 meri ingland, 原义为 in a broader 语义 "bountiful, prosperous." Merry Monday was a 16 世纪 term for "the Monday before Shrove Tuesday" (Mardi Gras).

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "food for one meal, pottage," from Old French mes "portion of food, course at dinner," from Late Latin missus "course at dinner," literally "a placing, a putting (on a table, etc.)," from past participle of mittere "to put, place," in classical Latin "to send, let go" (see mission).

Meaning "communal eating place" (especially a military one) is first attested 1530s, from earlier sense of "company of persons eating together" (early 15c.), originally a group of four. Sense of "mixed food," especially for animals, (1738) led to contemptuous use for "jumble, mixed mass" (1828) and figurative sense of "state of confusion" (1834), as well as "condition of untidiness" (1851). General use for "a quantity" of anything is attested by 1830. Meaning "excrement" (of animals) is from 1903.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "food for one meal, pottage," 源自 古法语 mes "portion of food, course at dinner," 源自 晚期拉丁语 missus "course at dinner," 字面义为 "a placing, a putting (on a table, etc.)," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 mittere "to put, place," in classical 拉丁语 "to send, let go" （参见 mission). 义为 "communal eating place" (尤指 a military one) is 最早见于 1530 年代, 源自 earlier 语义 "company of persons eating together" (15 世纪初), 原义为 a group of four. 义为 "mixed food," 尤指 for animals, (1738 年) led to contemptuous use for "jumble, mixed mass" (1828 年) and figurative 语义 "state of confusion" (1834 年), as well as "condition of untidiness" (1851 年). General use for "a quantity" of anything is attested 截至 1830 年. 义为 "excrement" (of animals) 始于 1903 年.

example.en: The kitchen was in a complete mess after the kids had cooked.

definitionLines: n. 消息，音信，文电，口信，
entries.definition: n. 消息，音信，文电，口信，
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "communication transmitted via a messenger," from Old French message "message, news, tidings, embassy" (11c.), from Medieval Latin missaticum, from Latin missus "a sending away, sending, despatching; a throwing, hurling," noun use of past participle of mittere "to send" (see mission). The Latin word is glossed in Old English by ærende. Specific religious sense of "divinely inspired communication via a prophet" (1540s) led to transferred sense of "the broad meaning (of something)," first attested 1828. To get the message "understand" is from 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "communication transmitted via a messenger," 源自 古法语 message "message, news, tidings, embassy" (11 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 missaticum, 源自 拉丁语 missus "a sending away, sending, despatching; a throwing, hurling," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 mittere "to send" （参见 mission). The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by ærende. Specific religious 语义 "divinely inspired communication via a prophet" (1540 年代) led to transferred 语义 "the broad meaning (of something)," 最早见于 1828 年. To get the message "understand" 始于 1960 年.

example.en: Please leave a message if I am not available when you call.

definitionLines: n. 送行者，使者，传令兵
entries.definition: n. 送行者，使者，传令兵
entries.etymology: c. 1200, messager, from Old French messagier "messenger, envoy, ambassador," from message (see message (n.)). With parasitic -n- inserted by c. 1300 for no apparent reason except that people liked to say it that way (compare passenger, harbinger, scavenger).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, messager, 源自 古法语 messagier "messenger, envoy, ambassador," 源自 message （参见 message （名）). With parasitic -n- inserted by 约 1300 年 for no apparent reason except that people liked to say it that way (对比 passenger, harbinger, scavenger).

example.en: A messenger arrived at the castle with urgent news from the king.
example.zh: 一名信使带着国王的紧急消息抵达了城堡。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from Old French metal "metal; material, substance, stuff" (12c.), from Latin metallum "metal; mine, quarry, mineral, what is got by mining," from Greek metallon "metal, ore" (senses only in post-classical texts; originally "mine, quarry, pit"), probably from metalleuein "to mine, to quarry," of unknown origin, but related somehow to metallan "to seek after." Compare Greek metalleutes "a miner," metalleia "a searching for metals, mining."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 metal "metal; material, substance, stuff" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 metallum "metal; mine, quarry, mineral, what is got by mining," 源自 希腊语 metallon "metal, ore" (senses only in post-classical texts; 原义为 "mine, quarry, pit"), 可能 源自 metalleuein "to mine, to quarry," 来源不详, but related somehow to metallan "to seek after." 对比 希腊语 metalleutes "a miner," metalleia "a searching for metals, mining."

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "open air place in ancient times for viewing spectacles and plays," from Old French theatre (12c., Modern French théâtre, improperly accented) and directly from Latin theatrum "play-house, theater; stage; spectators in a theater" (source also of Spanish, Italian teatro), from Greek theatron "theater; the people in the theater; a show, a spectacle," literally "place for viewing," from theasthai "to behold" (related to thea "a view, a seeing; a seat in the theater," theates "spectator") + -tron, suffix denoting place.

Meaning "building where plays are shown" is from 1570s in English. Transferred sense of "plays, writing, production, the stage" is from 1660s. Generic sense of "place of action" is from 1580s; especially "region where war is being fought" (1914). Spelling with -re arose late 17c. and prevailed in Britain after c. 1700 by French influence, but American English retained or revived the older spelling in -er.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "open air place in ancient times for viewing spectacles and plays," 源自 古法语 theatre (12 世纪, 现代法语 théâtre, improperly accented) and 直接源自 拉丁语 theatrum "play-house, theater; stage; spectators in a theater" (source also of 西班牙语, 意大利语 teatro), 源自 希腊语 theatron "theater; the people in the theater; a show, a spectacle," 字面义为 "place for viewing," 源自 theasthai "to behold" (related to thea "a view, a seeing; a seat in the theater," theates "spectator") + -tron, suffix denoting place. 义为 "building where plays are shown" 始于 1570 年代 in English. Transferred 语义 "plays, writing, production, the stage" 始于 1660 年代. Generic 语义 "place of action" 始于 1580 年代; 尤指 "region where war is being fought" (1914 年). Spelling with -re arose 17 世纪晚期 and prevailed in Britain after 约 1700 年 by 法语 influence, but American English retained or revived the older spelling in -er.

example.en: We bought tickets to see a play at the theater downtown.
example.zh: 我们买票去市中心的剧院看了一场话剧。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "regular, systematic treatment of disease," from Latin methodus "way of teaching or going," from Greek methodos "scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation," originally "pursuit, a following after," from meta- "after" (see meta-) + hodos "a traveling, way" (see cede). Meaning "way of doing anything" is from 1580s; that of "orderliness, regularity" is from 1610s. In reference to a theory of acting associated with Russian director Konstantin Stanislavsky, it is attested from 1923.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "regular, systematic treatment of disease," 源自 拉丁语 methodus "way of teaching or going," 源自 希腊语 methodos "scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation," 原义为 "pursuit, a following after," 源自 meta- "after" （参见 meta-) + hodos "a traveling, way" （参见 cede). 义为 "way of doing anything" 始于 1580 年代; that of "orderliness, regularity" 始于 1610 年代. In reference to a theory of acting associated with 俄语 director Konstantin Stanislavsky, it 见于 1923 年.

example.en: Scientists developed a new method for detecting the virus in blood samples.
example.zh: 科学家开发了一种在血液样本中检测该病毒的新方法。

entries.etymology: "pertaining to the system of measures based on the meter," 1855, from French métrique, from mèter (see meter (n.2)). In this sense, metrical is attested from 1797.
entries.etymologyZh: "pertaining to the system of measures based on the meter," 1855 年, 源自 法语 métrique, 源自 mèter （参见 meter (n.2)). In this sense, metrical 见于 1797 年.

entries.definition: a. 大都市的 n. 大城市人
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "bishop having oversight of other bishops," from Late Latin metropolitanus, from Greek metropolis "mother city" (from which others have been colonized), also "capital city," from meter "mother" (see mother (n.1)) + polis "city" (see polis).

In Greek, "parent state of a colony;" later, "see of a metropolitan bishop." In the West, the position now roughly corresponds to archbishop, but in the Greek church it ranks above it.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "bishop having oversight of other bishops," 源自 晚期拉丁语 metropolitanus, 源自 希腊语 metropolis "mother city" (源自 which others have been colonized), also "capital city," 源自 meter "mother" （参见 mother (n.1)) + polis "city" （参见 polis). In 希腊语, "parent state of a colony;" later, "see of a metropolitan bishop." In the West, the position 现在 roughly corresponds to archbishop, but in the 希腊语 church it ranks above it.

example.en: She grew up in a metropolitan area and loved the energy of city life.
example.zh: 她在大都市地区长大，热爱城市生活的活力。

entries.definition: n./a. 墨西哥（的） n. 墨西哥（人）
entries.etymology: c. 1600 (n.); by 1640s (adj.), from Mexico + -an.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年 （名）; by 1640 年代 （形）, 源自 Mexico + -an.

entries.etymology: popular name for a bacterium, 1878, from French microbe, "badly coined ... by Sédillot" [Weekley] in 1878 from Greek mikros "small" (see mica) + bios "life" (see bio-). It is an incorrect use of bios; in Greek the word would mean literally "short-lived."
entries.etymologyZh: popular name for a bacterium, 1878 年, 源自 法语 microbe, "badly coined ... by Sédillot" [Weekley] 于 1878 年 源自 希腊语 mikros "small" （参见 mica) + bios "life" （参见 bio-). It is an incorrect use of bios; in 希腊语 the word would mean 字面义为 "short-lived."

entries.etymology: 1680s, "ear trumpet for the hard-of-hearing," coined from Greek mikros "small" (see mica) + phone "sound," from PIE root *bha- (2) "to speak, tell, say" (see fame (n.)). Modern meaning dates from 1929, from use in radio broadcasting and movie recording. Earlier, "amplifying telephone transmitter" (1878). Of the two spellings of the short form of the word, mike (1927) is older than mic (1961).
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, "ear trumpet for the hard-of-hearing," coined 源自 希腊语 mikros "small" （参见 mica) + phone "sound," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *bha- (2) "to speak, tell, say" （参见 fame （名）). 现代 意为 dates 自 1929 年起, 源自 use in radio broadcasting and movie recording. Earlier, "amplifying telephone transmitter" (1878 年). Of the two spellings of the short form of the word, mike (1927 年) is older than mic (1961 年).

example.en: Please speak clearly into the microphone so everyone in the hall can hear you.
example.zh: 请对着麦克风清晰地说话，这样大厅里的每个人都能听到你。

entries.etymology: 1650s, from Modern Latin microscopium, literally "an instrument for viewing what is small," from Greek micro- (see micro-) + -skopion, from skopein "to look, see" (see -scope).
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, 源自 现代 拉丁语 microscopium, 字面义为 "an instrument for viewing what is small," 源自 希腊语 micro- （参见 micro-) + -skopion, 源自 skopein "to look, see" （参见 -scope).

entries.etymology: type of electromagnetic wave, 1931, coined in English from micro- + wave (n.). First record of microwave oven is from 1961; microwave as short for this is attested from 1974; as a verb, from 1976.
entries.etymologyZh: type of electromagnetic wave, 1931 年, coined in English 源自 micro- + wave （名）. First record of microwave oven 始于 1961 年; microwave as short for this 见于 1974 年; 作动词时, 自 1976 年起.

example.en: She heated the leftovers quickly in the microwave.
example.zh: 她用微波炉很快地加热了剩菜。

entries.definition: n. 正午，中午 a.正午的
entries.etymology: Old English middæg "midday, noon," contracted from midne dæg; see mid + day. Similar formation in Old High German mittitag, German mittag, Old Norse miðdagr.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 middæg "midday, noon," contracted 源自 midne dæg; 参见 mid + day. Similar formation in 古高地德语 mittitag, 德语 mittag, 古北欧语 miðdagr.

entries.definition: n. 中间，当中 a.中间的，中部的
entries.etymology:
Old English middel, from West Germanic *middila (source also of Old Frisian middel, Old Saxon middil, Middle Low German, Dutch middel, Old High German mittil, German mittel), from Proto-Germanic *medjaz (see mid). Middle name attested from 1815; as "one's outstanding characteristic," colloquial, from 1911, American English.

Middle school attested from 1838, originally "middle-class school, school for middle-class children;" the sense in reference to a school for grades between elementary and high school is from 1960. Middle management is 1957. Middle-of-the-road in the figurative sense is attested from 1894; edges of a dirt road can be washed out and thus less safe. Middle finger so called from c. 1000.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 middel, 源自 West 日耳曼语 *middila (source also of 古弗里西语 middel, 古撒克逊语 middil, Middle Low 德语, 荷兰语 middel, 古高地德语 mittil, 德语 mittel), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *medjaz （参见 mid). Middle name attested 自 1815 年起; as "one's outstanding characteristic," 口语, 自 1911 年起, American English. Middle school attested 自 1838 年起, 原义为 "middle-class school, school for middle-class children;" the sense in reference to a school for grades between elementary and high school 始于 1960 年. Middle management is 1957 年. Middle-of-the-road in the figurative sense 见于 1894 年; edges of a dirt road can be washed out and thus less safe. Middle finger so called 源自 约 1000 年.

example.en: The wedding cake was placed right in the middle of the banquet table.
example.zh: 婚礼蛋糕被摆放在宴席桌子的正中间。

entries.etymology: Old English mid-niht, or middre niht (with dative). See mid + night. Midnight oil symbolizing "late night work" is attested from 1630s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 mid-niht，或middre niht (with dative). See mid + night. Midnight oil symbolizing "late night work" 见于 1630 年代.

example.en: The phone rang at midnight, waking everyone in the house.

entries.definition: auz. v.［may 的过去式］ n. 力量，威力
entries.etymology: Old English mihte, meahte, originally the past tense of may (Old English magen "to be able"), thus "*may-ed." See may (v.). The first record of might-have-been is from 1848.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 mihte, meahte, 原义为 the 为 … 的过去时 may (古英语 magen "to be able"), thus "*may-ed." See may （动）. The first record of might-have-been 始于 1848 年.

entries.etymology: 1690s, from Latin migratus, past participle of migrare "to move from one place to another" (see migration). Related: Migrated; migrating.

example.en: Every autumn, millions of birds migrate south to warmer regions.
example.zh: 每年秋天，数以百万计的鸟类向南迁徙到更温暖的地区。

entries.etymology: Old English milde "gentle, merciful," from Proto-Germanic *milthjaz- (source also of Old Norse mildr, Old Saxon mildi, Old Frisian milde, Middle Dutch milde, Dutch mild, Old High German milti, German milde "mild," Gothic mildiþa "kindness"), from PIE *meldh-, from root *mel- "soft," with derivatives referring to soft or softened materials (source also of Greek malthon "weakling," myle "mill;" Latin molere "to grind;" Old Irish meldach "tender;" Sanskrit mrdh "to neglect," also "to be moist"). Originally of persons and powers; of the weather from c. 1400, of disease from 1744. Also in Old English as an adverb, "mercifully, graciously."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 milde "gentle, merciful," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *milthjaz- (source also of 古北欧语 mildr, 古撒克逊语 mildi, 古弗里西语 milde, Middle 荷兰语 milde, 荷兰语 mild, 古高地德语 milti, 德语 milde "mild," Gothic mildiþa "kindness"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *meldh-, 源自 root *mel- "soft," with derivatives referring to soft or softened materials (source also of 希腊语 malthon "weakling," myle "mill;" 拉丁语 molere "to grind;" Old 爱尔兰语 meldach "tender;" 梵语 mrdh "to neglect," also "to be moist"). Originally of persons and powers; of the weather 源自 约 1400 年, of disease 自 1744 年起. Also in 古英语 作为 副词, "mercifully, graciously."

example.en: The coastal city is known for its mild winters with little frost.
example.zh: 这座沿海城市以其少霜冻的温和冬季而闻名。

entries.etymology:
Old English mil, from West Germanic *milja (source also of Middle Dutch mile, Dutch mijl, Old High German mila, German meile), from Latin milia "thousands," plural of mille "a thousand" (neuter plural was mistaken in Germanic as a fem. singular), of unknown origin.

The Latin word also is the source of French mille, Italian miglio, Spanish milla. The Scandinavian words (Old Norse mila, etc.) are from English. An ancient Roman mile was 1,000 double paces (one step with each foot), for about 4,860 feet, but there were many local variants and a modern statute mile is about 400 feet longer. In Germany, Holland, and Scandinavia in the Middle Ages, the Latin word was applied arbitrarily to the ancient Germanic rasta, a measure of from 3.25 to 6 English miles. Mile-a-minute (adj.) "very fast" is attested from 1957.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 mil, 源自 West 日耳曼语 *milja (source also of Middle 荷兰语 mile, 荷兰语 mijl, 古高地德语 mila, 德语 meile), 源自 拉丁语 milia "thousands," 为 … 的复数 mille "a thousand" (neuter plural was mistaken in 日耳曼语 作为 fem. singular), 来源不详. The 拉丁语 word also is the source of 法语 mille, 意大利语 miglio, 西班牙语 milla. The Scandinavian words (古北欧语 mila, etc.) 始于 English. An ancient Roman mile was 1,000 double paces (one step with each foot), for about 4,860 feet, but there were many local variants and a modern statute mile is about 400 feet longer. In Germany, Holland, and Scandinavia in the Middle Ages, the 拉丁语 word was applied arbitrarily to the ancient 日耳曼语 rasta, a measure of 源自 3.25 to 6 English miles. Mile-a-minute （形） "very fast" 见于 1957 年.

definitionLines: a. 军队的，军事的，军用的
entries.definition: a. 军队的，军事的，军用的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French militaire (14c.), from Latin militaris "of soldiers or war, of military service, warlike," from miles (genitive militis) "soldier," of unknown origin, perhaps ultimately from Etruscan, or else meaning "one who marches in a troop," and thus connected to Sanskrit melah "assembly," Greek homilos "assembled crowd, throng." Related: Militarily. Old English had militisc, from Latin. Military-industrial complex coined 1961 in farewell speech of U.S. president Dwight D. Eisenhower.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 militaire (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 militaris "of soldiers or war, of military service, warlike," 源自 miles (属格 militis) "soldier," 来源不详, 或许 最终源自 Etruscan，或else 意为 "one who marches in a troop," and thus connected to 梵语 melah "assembly," 希腊语 homilos "assembled crowd, throng." 同源词：Militarily. 古英语 had militisc, 源自 拉丁语. entries.etymology: 1580s, "system of military discipline," from Latin militia "military service, warfare," from miles "soldier" (see military). Sense of "citizen army" (as distinct from professional soldiers) is first recorded 1690s, perhaps from a sense in French cognate milice. In U.S. history, "the whole body of men declared by law amenable to military service, without enlistment, whether armed and drilled or not" (1777).

In U.S. history, "the whole body of men declared by law amenable to military service, without enlistment, whether armed and drilled or not" (1777 年).

entries.etymology:
Old English meoluc (West Saxon), milc (Anglian), from Proto-Germanic *meluks "milk" (source also of Old Norse mjolk, Old Frisian melok, Old Saxon miluk, Dutch melk, Old High German miluh, German Milch, Gothic miluks), from *melk- "to milk," from PIE root *melg- "to wipe, to rub off," also "to stroke; to milk," in reference to the hand motion involved in milking an animal (source also of Greek amelgein, Latin mulgere, Old Church Slavonic mlesti, Lithuanian melžu "to milk," Old Irish melg "milk," Sanskrit marjati "wipes off"). Old Church Slavonic noun meleko (Russian moloko, Czech mleko) is considered to be adopted from Germanic.

Of milk-like plant juices from late 14c. Milk chocolate is first recorded 1723; milk shake is first recorded 1889, for a variety of creations, but the modern version is only from the 1930s. Milk tooth (1727) uses the word in its figurative sense "period of infancy," attested from 17c. To cry over spilt milk is first attested 1836 in writing of Canadian humorist Thomas C. Haliburton. Milk and honey is from the Old Testament phrase describing the richness of the Promised Land (Num. xvi:13, Old English meolc and hunie). Milk of human kindness is from "Macbeth" (1605).

Old Church Slavonic 名词 meleko (俄语 moloko, Czech mleko) is considered to be adopted 源自 日耳曼语. Milk and honey 始于 the Old Testament phrase describing the richness of the Promised Land (Num. xvi:13, 古英语 meolc and hunie). Milk of human kindness 始于 "Macbeth" (1605 年).

entries.etymology: also millimetre, 1802, from French millimetre; see milli- + meter (n.2).

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French million (late 13c.), from Italian millione (now milione), literally "a great thousand," augmentative of mille "thousand," from Latin mille, which is of uncertain origin. Used mainly by mathematicians until 16c. India, with its love of large numbers, had names before 3c. for numbers well beyond a billion. The ancient Greeks had no name for a number greater than ten thousand, the Romans for none higher than a hundred thousand. "A million" in Latin would have been decies centena milia, literally "ten hundred thousand." Million to one as a type of "long odds" is attested from 1761. Related: Millions.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 million (13 世纪晚期), 源自 意大利语 millione (现在 milione), 字面义为 "a great thousand," 为 … 的扩大形式 mille "thousand," 源自 拉丁语 mille, which is 来源存疑. example.en: The charity raised over a million dollars for disaster relief.
example.zh: 该慈善机构为赈灾筹集了超过一百万美元。

entries.etymology: 1821, from French millionnaire (1762); see million. The first in America is said to have been John Jacob Astor (1763-1848).

definitionLines: n. 头脑，精神；理智，智能；想
entries.definition: n. 头脑，精神；理智，智能；想
entries.etymology:
late 12c., from Old English gemynd "memory, remembrance, state of being remembered; thought, purpose; conscious mind, intellect, intention," Proto-Germanic *ga-mundiz (source also of Gothic muns "thought," munan "to think;" Old Norse minni "mind;" German Minne (archaic) "love," originally "memory, loving memory"), from PIE root *men- (1) "think, remember, have one's mind aroused," with derivatives referring to qualities of mind or states of thought (source also of Sanskrit matih "thought," munih "sage, seer;" Greek memona "I yearn," mania "madness," mantis "one who divines, prophet, seer;" Latin mens "mind, understanding, reason," memini "I remember," mentio "remembrance;" Lithuanian mintis "thought, idea," Old Church Slavonic mineti "to believe, think," Russian pamjat "memory").

Meaning "mental faculty" is mid-14c. "Memory," one of the oldest senses, now is almost obsolete except in old expressions such as bear in mind, call to mind. Mind's eye "remembrance" is early 15c. Phrase time out of mind is attested from early 15c. To pay no mind "disregard" is recorded from 1916, American English dialect. To have half a mind to "to have one's mind half made up to (do something)" is recorded from 1726. Mind-reading is from 1882.

Mind's eye "remembrance" is early 15c. Phrase time out of mind is attested from early 15c. To pay no mind "disregard" is recorded from 1916, American English dialect. To have half a mind to "to have one's mind half made up to (do something)" 见于 1726 年. Mind-reading 始于 1882 年.

example.en: A calm mind helps you make better decisions under pressure.
example.zh: 冷静的头脑帮助你在压力下做出更好的决定。

entries.definition: pron. ［所有格］我的 n. 矿，矿山，矿井 vt.采掘，开矿
entries.etymology: Old English min "mine, my," (pronoun and adjective), from Proto-Germanic *minaz (source also of Old Frisian, Old Saxon Old High German min, Middle Dutch, Dutch mijn, German mein, Old Norse minn, Gothic meins "my, mine"), from the base of me. Superseded as adjective beginning 13c. by my.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 min "mine, my," (pronoun and 形容词), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *minaz (source also of 古弗里西语, 古撒克逊语 古高地德语 min, Middle 荷兰语, 荷兰语 mijn, 德语 mein, 古北欧语 minn, Gothic meins "my, mine"), 源自 base of me. Superseded as 形容词 beginning 13 世纪 by my.

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French minour (13c.), from miner "to mine" (see mine (n.1)).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 minour (13 世纪), 源自 miner "to mine" （参见 mine (n.1)).

entries.definition: n. 矿物，矿石 a.矿物的，矿质的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "substance obtained by mining," from Medieval Latin minerale "something mined," noun use of neuter of mineralis "pertaining to mines," from minera "mine." Meaning "material substance that is neither animal nor vegetable" is first recorded c. 1600. Modern scientific sense is from 1813.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "substance obtained by mining," 源自 中古拉丁语 minerale "something mined," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of mineralis "pertaining to mines," 源自 minera "mine." 义为 "material substance that is neither animal nor vegetable" is 首见于 约 1600 年. 现代 scientific sense 始于 1813 年.

example.en: The region is rich in mineral deposits, including iron and copper.
example.zh: 该地区矿物储量丰富，包括铁矿和铜矿。

entries.definition: vi. 混合；交往 vt. 使相混；使混合
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "to bring together," frequentative of Middle English myngen "to mix," from Old English mengan (related to second element in among), from Proto-Germanic *mangjan "to knead together" (source also of Old Saxon mengian, Old Norse menga, Old Frisian mendza, German mengen), from PIE *mag- "to knead, fashion, fit" (see macerate). The formation may have been suggested by cognate Middle Dutch mengelen. Of persons, "to join with others, be sociable" (intransitive), from c. 1600. Related: Mingled; mingling.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "to bring together," 为 … 的反复体 中古英语 myngen "to mix," 源自 古英语 mengan (related to second element in among), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *mangjan "to knead together" (source also of 古撒克逊语 mengian, 古北欧语 menga, 古弗里西语 mendza, 德语 mengen), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *mag- "to knead, fashion, fit" （参见 macerate). The formation may have been suggested by 同源 Middle 荷兰语 mengelen. Of persons, "to join with others, be sociable" (intransitive), 源自 约 1600 年. 同源词：Mingled; mingling.

entries.definition: a. 微型的，小规模的 n.缩图；微型画
entries.etymology: 1580s, "a reduced image," from Italian miniatura "manuscript illumination or small picture," from past participle of miniare "to illuminate a manuscript," from Latin miniare "to paint red," from minium "red lead," used in ancient times to make red ink, a word said to be of Iberian origin. Sense development is because pictures in medieval manuscripts were small, but no doubt there was influence as well from the similar-sounding Latin words that express smallness: minor, minimus, minutus, etc.

entries.etymologyZh: 1802 年, 首见于 in Bentham; 参见 minimum + -ize.

example.en: We should minimize unnecessary risks before launching the product.

entries.definition: n. 最小量，最低限度 a.最低的，最小的
entries.etymology: 1660s, "smallest portion into which matter is divisible," from Latin minimum "smallest" (thing), neuter of minimus "smallest, least," superlative of minor "smaller" (see minor). Meaning "least amount attainable" is from 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, "smallest portion into which matter is divisible," 源自 拉丁语 minimum "smallest" (thing), neuter of minimus "smallest, least," superlative of minor "smaller" （参见 minor). 义为 "least amount attainable" 始于 1670 年代.

example.en: Keep the noise to a minimum during library hours.
example.zh: 在图书馆开放时间内，请将噪音降到最低。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "one who acts upon the authority of another," from Old French menistre "servant, valet, member of a household staff, administrator, musician, minstrel" (12c.), from Latin minister (genitive ministri) "inferior, servant, priest's assistant" (in Medieval Latin, "priest"), from minus, minor "less," hence "subordinate," (see minus) + comparative suffix *-teros. Formed on model of magister. Meaning "priest" is attested in English from early 14c. Political sense of "high officer of the state" is attested from 1620s, from notion of "service to the crown."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "one who acts upon the authority of another," 源自 古法语 menistre "servant, valet, member of a household staff, administrator, musician, minstrel" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 minister (属格 ministri) "inferior, servant, priest's assistant" (in 中古拉丁语, "priest"), 源自 minus, minor "less," hence "subordinate," （参见 minus) + comparative suffix *-teros. example.en: The prime minister gave a speech about the new economic policy.
example.zh: 总理就新经济政策发表了讲话。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "function of a priest," from Old French menistere "service, ministry; position, post, employment," and directly from Latin ministerium "office, service, attendance, ministry," from minister (see minister (n.)). example.en: The ministry of Education announced new policies for rural schools.
