Application to five-cent piece (原义为 one part nickel, three parts copper) 始于 1883 年, American English; in earlier circulation there were silver half-dimes. To nickel-and-dime (someone) 始于 1964 年 (nickels and dimes "very small amounts of money" 见于 1893 年).

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French niece "niece, granddaughter" (12c., Modern French nièce), earlier niepce, from Latin neptia (also source of Portuguese neta, Spanish nieta), a more decidedly feminine form of neptis "granddaughter," in Late Latin "niece," fem. of nepos "grandson, nephew" (see nephew). Replaced Old English nift, from Proto-Germanic *neftiz, from the same PIE root (Old English also used broðordohter and nefene).

Until c. 1600, it also commonly meant "a granddaughter" or any remote female descendant. Cognate with Spanish nieta, Old Lithuanian nepte, Sanskrit naptih "granddaughter;" Czech net, Old Irish necht, Welsh nith, German Nichte "niece."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 niece "niece, granddaughter" (12 世纪, 现代法语 nièce), earlier niepce, 源自 拉丁语 neptia (also source of 葡萄牙语 neta, 西班牙语 nieta), a more decidedly feminine form of neptis "granddaughter," in 晚期拉丁语 "niece," fem. of nepos "grandson, nephew" （参见 nephew). Replaced 古英语 nift, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *neftiz, 源自 same 原始印欧语 (PIE) root (古英语 also used broðordohter and nefene). Until 约 1600 年, it also commonly meant "a granddaughter" or any remote female descendant. Cognate with 西班牙语 nieta, Old Lithuanian nepte, 梵语 naptih "granddaughter;" Czech net, Old 爱尔兰语 necht, Welsh nith, 德语 Nichte "niece."

entries.etymology:
Old English niht (West Saxon neaht, Anglian næht, neht) "night, darkness;" the vowel indicating that the modern word derives from oblique cases (genitive nihte, dative niht), from Proto-Germanic *nakht- (source also of Old Saxon and Old High German naht, Old Frisian and Dutch nacht, German Nacht, Old Norse natt, Gothic nahts).

The Germanic words are from PIE *nekwt- "night" (source also of Greek nuks "a night," Latin nox, Old Irish nochd, Sanskrit naktam "at night," Lithuanian naktis "night," Old Church Slavonic nosti, Russian noch', Welsh henoid "tonight"), according to Watkins, probably from a verbal root *neg- "to be dark, be night." For spelling with -gh- see fight.Compare German Weihnachten "Christmas." In early times, the day was held to begin at sunset, so Old English monanniht "Monday night" was the night before Monday, or what we would call Sunday night. The Greeks, by contrast, counted their days by mornings.

To work nights preserves the Old English genitive of time. Night shift is attested from 1710 in the sense of "garment worn by a woman at night" (see shift (n.1)); meaning "gang of workers employed after dark" is from 1839. Night soil "excrement" (1770) is so called because it was removed (from cesspools, etc.) after dark. Night train attested from 1838. Night life "habitual nocturnal carousing" attested from 1852.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 niht (West Saxon neaht, Anglian næht, neht) "night, darkness;" the vowel indicating that the modern word derives 源自 oblique cases (属格 nihte, dative niht), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *nakht- (source also of 古撒克逊语 and 古高地德语 naht, 古弗里西语 and 荷兰语 nacht, 德语 Nacht, 古北欧语 natt, Gothic nahts). The 日耳曼语 words 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) *nekwt- "night" (source also of 希腊语 nuks "a night," 拉丁语 nox, Old 爱尔兰语 nochd, 梵语 naktam "at night," Lithuanian naktis "night," Old Church Slavonic nosti, 俄语 noch', Welsh henoid "tonight"), according to Watkins, 可能 源自 a verbal root *neg- "to be dark, be night." For spelling with -gh- 参见 fight.对比 德语 Weihnachten "Christmas." In early times, the day was held to begin at sunset, so 古英语 monanniht "Monday night" was the night before Monday，或what we would call Sunday night. The Greeks, by contrast, counted their days by mornings. To work nights preserves the 古英语 属格 of time. Night shift 见于 1710 年 in the 语义 "garment worn by a woman at night" （参见 shift (n.1)); 意为 "gang of workers employed after dark" 始于 1839 年. Night soil "excrement" (1770 年) is so called because it was removed (源自 cesspools, etc.) after dark. Night train attested 自 1838 年起. Night life "habitual nocturnal carousing" attested 自 1852 年起.

example.en: He studied late into the night to prepare for the final exam.
example.zh: 为了准备期末考试，他学习到深夜。

definitionLines: n. 梦魇，恶梦；可怕的事物
entries.definition: n. 梦魇，恶梦；可怕的事物
entries.etymology: late 13c., "an evil female spirit afflicting sleepers with a feeling of suffocation," compounded from night + mare (3) "goblin that causes nightmares, incubus." Meaning shifted mid-16c. from the incubus to the suffocating sensation it causes. Sense of "any bad dream" first recorded 1829; that of "very distressing experience" is from 1831. Cognate with Middle Dutch nachtmare, German Nachtmahr.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "an evil female spirit afflicting sleepers with a feeling of suffocation," compounded 源自 night + mare (3) "goblin that causes nightmares, incubus." 义为 shifted 16 世纪中期 源自 incubus to the suffocating sensation it causes. 义为 "any bad dream" 首见于 1829 年; that of "very distressing experience" 始于 1831 年. Cognate with Middle 荷兰语 nachtmare, 德语 Nachtmahr.

example.en: Sitting in traffic for three hours every day is a commuter's nightmare.
example.zh: 每天堵车三小时是通勤者的噩梦。

entries.etymology:
Old English nigen, from Proto-Germanic *niwun (source also of Old Saxon nigun, Old Frisian niugun, Old Norse niu, Swedish nio, Middle Dutch neghen, Dutch negen, Old High German niun, German neun, Gothic niun "nine"), from PIE *newn "nine" (source also of Sanskrit nava, Avestan nava, Greek ennea, Albanian nende, Latin novem (with change of -n- to -m- by analogy of septem, decem), Lithuanian devnyi, Old Church Slavonic deveti (the Balto-Slavic forms by dissimilation of -n- to -d-), Old Irish noin, Welsh naw).

Nine to five "the average workday" is attested from 1935. Nine days has been proverbial since 14c. for the time which a wonder or novelty holds attention.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 nigen, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *niwun (source also of 古撒克逊语 nigun, 古弗里西语 niugun, 古北欧语 niu, Swedish nio, Middle 荷兰语 neghen, 荷兰语 negen, 古高地德语 niun, 德语 neun, Gothic niun "nine"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *newn "nine" (source also of 梵语 nava, Avestan nava, 希腊语 ennea, Albanian nende, 拉丁语 novem (with change of -n- to -m- by analogy of septem, decem), Lithuanian devnyi, Old Church Slavonic deveti (the Balto-Slavic forms by dissimilation of -n- to -d-), Old 爱尔兰语 noin, Welsh naw). Nine to five "the average workday" 见于 1935 年. Nine days has been proverbial 自 14 世纪 for the time which a wonder or novelty holds attention.

entries.etymology: late Old English nigontene (Anglian), nigontyne (West Saxon); see nine + -teen.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 nigontene (Anglian), nigontyne (West Saxon); 参见 nine + -teen.

entries.etymology: Old English nigontig, from nine + -tig "group of ten" (see -ty (1)). Cognate with Old Frisian niontich, Middle Dutch negentich, Dutch negentig, German neunzig.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 nigontig, 源自 nine + -tig "group of ten" （参见 -ty (1)). Cognate with 古弗里西语 niontich, Middle 荷兰语 negentich, 荷兰语 negentig, 德语 neunzig.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, modification (by influence of nine) of nigonðe, from Old English nigoða, nigend.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, modification (by influence of nine) of nigonðe, 源自 古英语 nigoða, nigend.

definitionLines: a. 没有；并非；不许；完全不是
entries.definition: n. 氮 a. 没有；并非；不许；完全不是 ad. 不，不是，没有，毫不
entries.etymology: 1794, from French nitrogène, coined 1790 by French chemist Jean Antoine Chaptal (1756-1832), from comb. form of Greek nitron "sodium carbonate" (see nitro-) + French gène "producing," from Greek -gen "giving birth to" (see -gen). The gas was identified in part by analysis of nitre. Earlier name (1772) was mephitic air, and Lavoisier called it azote (see azo-).
entries.etymologyZh: 1794 年, 源自 法语 nitrogène, coined 1790 年 by 法语 chemist Jean Antoine Chaptal (1756 年-1832 年), 源自 comb. form of 希腊语 nitron "sodium carbonate" （参见 nitro-) + 法语 gène "producing," 源自 希腊语 -gen "giving birth to" （参见 -gen). The gas was identified in part by analysis of nitre. Earlier name (1772 年) was mephitic air, and Lavoisier called it azote （参见 azo-).

example.en: Plants absorb carbon dioxide and release nitrogen as a byproduct.
example.zh: 植物吸收二氧化碳，并释放氮气作为副产品。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "illustrious, distinguished; worthy of honor or respect," from Old French noble "of noble bearing or birth," from Latin nobilis "well-known, famous, renowned; excellent, superior, splendid; high-born, of superior birth," earlier *gnobilis, literally "knowable," from gnoscere "to come to know," from PIE root *gno- "to know" (see know). The prominent Roman families, which were "well known," provided most of the Republic's public officials.

Meaning "distinguished by rank, title, or birth" is first recorded late 13c. Sense of "having lofty character, having high moral qualities" is from c. 1600. A noble gas (1902) is so called for its inactivity or intertness; a use of the word that had been applied in Middle English to precious stones, metals, etc., of similar quality (late 14c.), from the sense of "having admirable properties" (c. 1300).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "illustrious, distinguished; worthy of honor or respect," 源自 古法语 noble "of noble bearing or birth," 源自 拉丁语 nobilis "well-known, famous, renowned; excellent, superior, splendid; high-born, of superior birth," earlier *gnobilis, 字面义为 "knowable," 源自 gnoscere "to come to know," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *gno- "to know" （参见 know). The prominent Roman families, which were "well known," provided most of the Republic's public officials. 义为 "distinguished by rank, title, or birth" is 首见于 13 世纪晚期 义为 "having lofty character, having high moral qualities" 始于 约 1600 年. A noble gas (1902 年) is so called for its inactivity or intertness; a use of the word that had been applied in 中古英语 to precious stones, metals, etc., of similar quality (14 世纪晚期), 源自 语义 "having admirable properties" (约 1300 年).

entries.etymology: mid-14c., no body "no person noone," from Middle English no (adj.) "not any" + bodi (see body (n.)). Written as two words 14c.-18c.; hyphenated 17c.-18c. Incorrect use with their is attested from 1540s. Meaning "person of no importance" is from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, no body "no person noone," 源自 中古英语 no （形） "not any" + bodi （参见 body （名）). Written as two words 14 世纪-18 世纪; hyphenated 17 世纪-18 世纪 Incorrect use with their 见于 1540 年代. 义为 "person of no importance" 始于 1580 年代.

definitionLines: v./n. 点头；表示同意；打盹， 瞌睡
entries.definition: v./n. 点头；表示同意；打盹， 瞌睡
entries.etymology: "to quickly bow the head," late 14c., of unknown origin, probably an Old English word, but not recorded; perhaps related to Old High German hnoton "to shake," from Proto-Germanic *hnudan. Meaning "to drift in and out of consciousness while on drugs" is attested from 1968. Related: Nodded; nodding. A nodding acquaintance (1711) is one you know just well enough to greet with a nod.
entries.etymologyZh: "to quickly bow the head," 14 世纪晚期, 来源不详, 可能 an 古英语 word, but not recorded; 或许 related to 古高地德语 hnoton "to shake," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *hnudan. 义为 "to drift in and out of consciousness while on drugs" 见于 1968 年. 同源词：Nodded; nodding. A nodding acquaintance (1711 年) is one you know just well enough to greet with a nod.

example.en: He gave a slow nod to show that he understood what was being asked.
example.zh: 他缓慢地点了点头，表示他明白被问到的问题。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., "loud outcry, clamor, shouting," from Old French noise "din, disturbance, uproar, brawl" (11c., in modern French only in phrase chercher noise "to pick a quarrel"), also "rumor, report, news," apparently from Latin nausea "disgust, annoyance, discomfort," literally "seasickness" (see nausea).

Another theory traces the Old French word to Latin noxia "hurting, injury, damage." OED considers that "the sense of the word is against both suggestions," but nausea could have developed a sense in Vulgar Latin of "unpleasant situation, noise, quarrel" (compare Old Provençal nauza "noise, quarrel"). Meaning "loud or unpleasant sound" is from c. 1300. Replaced native gedyn (see din).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "loud outcry, clamor, shouting," 源自 古法语 noise "din, disturbance, uproar, brawl" (11 世纪, in modern 法语 only in phrase chercher noise "to pick a quarrel"), also "rumor, report, news," 似乎 源自 拉丁语 nausea "disgust, annoyance, discomfort," 字面义为 "seasickness" （参见 nausea). Another theory traces the 古法语 word to 拉丁语 noxia "hurting, injury, damage." OED considers that "the sense of the word is against both suggestions," but nausea could have developed a sense in 通俗拉丁语 of "unpleasant situation, noise, quarrel" (对比 Old Provençal nauza "noise, quarrel"). 义为 "loud or unpleasant sound" 始于 约 1300 年. Replaced 本族 gedyn （参见 din).

example.en: The construction noise made it difficult to concentrate in the office.
example.zh: 施工噪音使得在办公室集中注意力十分困难。

entries.etymology: 1690s, "making noise," also "full of noise," from noise + -y (2). Earlier was noiseful (late 14c.). Related: Noisily; noisiness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1690 年代, "making noise," also "full of noise," 源自 noise + -y (2). Earlier was noiseful (14 世纪晚期). 同源词：Noisily; noisiness.

example.en: The café was too noisy for us to have a proper conversation.
example.zh: 咖啡馆太吵了，我们无法好好交谈。

entries.etymology: 1540s, "to call by name," back-formation from nomination or else from Latin nominatus, past participle of nominare "to name, call by name, give a name to," also "name for office,"" from nomen "name" (see name (n.)). Later "to appoint to some office or duty" (1560s); "to formally enter (someone) as a candidate for election" (c. 1600). It also occasionally was used from c. 1600 with a sense "give a name to." Related: Nominated; nominating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "to call by name," back-formation 源自 nomination or else 源自 拉丁语 nominatus, 为 … 的过去分词 nominare "to name, call by name, give a name to," also "name for office,"" from nomen "name" (see name (n.)). Later "to appoint to some office or duty" (1560s); "to formally enter (someone) 作为 candidate for election" (c. 1600). It also occasionally was used from c. 1600 with a sense "give a name to." 同源词：Nominated; nominating.

example.en: She was nominated for the best director award at the ceremony.
example.zh: 她在颁奖典礼上获得了最佳导演奖提名。

entries.etymology: Old English nan (pron.) "not one, not any," from ne "not" (see no) + an "one" (see one). Cognate with Old Saxon, Middle Low German nen, Old Norse neinn, Middle Dutch, Dutch neen, Old High German, German nein "no," and analogous to Latin non- (see non-). As an adverb from c. 1200. As an adjective, since c. 1600 reduced to no except in a few archaic phrases, especially before vowels, such as none other, none the worse.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 nan （代） "not one, not any," 源自 ne "not" （参见 no) + an "one" （参见 one). Cognate with 古撒克逊语, Middle Low 德语 nen, 古北欧语 neinn, Middle 荷兰语, 荷兰语 neen, 古高地德语, 德语 nein "no," and analogous to 拉丁语 non- （参见 non-). 作为 副词 源自 约 1200 年. 作形容词时, 自 约 1600 年 reduced to no except in a few 古旧 phrases, 尤指 before vowels, such as none other, none the worse.

example.en: The hospital operates as a nonprofit organization funded by donations.
example.zh: 该医院作为一家靠捐款运营的非营利组织。

entries.etymology: 1610s, from non- + sense; perhaps influenced by French nonsens.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 non- + sense; 或许 influenced by 法语 nonsens.

example.en: Stop talking nonsense; what you said makes absolutely no sense.
example.zh: 别说废话了；你说的根本没有任何意义。

entries.etymology: "narrow strip of dried dough," 1779, from German Nudel, which is of unknown origin. West Flemish noedel and French nouille are German loan-words. The older noun meaning "simpleton, stupid person" (1753) probably is an unrelated word, as is the slang word for "head" (attested from 1914).
entries.etymologyZh: "narrow strip of dried dough," 1779 年, 源自 德语 Nudel, which is 来源不详. West Flemish noedel and 法语 nouille are 德语 loan-words. The older 名词 意为 "simpleton, stupid person" (1753 年) 可能 is an unrelated word, as is the 俚语 word for "head" (attested 自 1914 年起).

entries.etymology: mid-12c., non "midday, 12 o'clock p.m., midday meal," from Old English non "3 o'clock p.m., the ninth hour," also "the canonical hour of nones," from Latin nona hora "ninth hour" of daylight, by Roman reckoning about 3 p.m., from nona, fem. singular of nonus "ninth" (see nones). Sense shift from "3 p.m." to "12 p.m." began during 12c., when time of Church prayers shifted from ninth hour to sixth hour, or perhaps because the customary time of the midday meal shifted, or both. The shift was complete by 14c. (same evolution in Dutch noen).
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪中期, non "midday, 12 o'clock p.m., midday meal," 源自 古英语 non "3 o'clock p.m., the ninth hour," also "the canonical hour of nones," 源自 拉丁语 nona hora "ninth hour" of daylight, by Roman reckoning about 3 p.m., 源自 nona, fem. singular of nonus "ninth" （参见 nones). Sense shift 源自 "3 p.m." to "12 p.m." began during 12 世纪, when time of Church prayers shifted 源自 ninth hour to sixth hour，或或许 because the customary time of the midday meal shifted，或both. The shift was complete by 14 世纪 (same evolution in 荷兰语 noen).

example.en: The sun is at its strongest around noon in summer.
example.zh: 夏天正午前后太阳最强烈。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, contraction of Middle English nauther (see neither). Influenced in form by or.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, contraction of 中古英语 nauther （参见 neither). Influenced in form by or.

entries.etymology: "standard, pattern, model," 1821, from French norme, from Latin norma "carpenter's square, rule, pattern," of unknown origin. Klein suggests a borrowing (via Etruscan) of Greek gnomon "carpenter's square." The Latin form of the word, norma, was used in English in the sense of "carpenter's square" from 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: "standard, pattern, model," 1821 年, 源自 法语 norme, 源自 拉丁语 norma "carpenter's square, rule, pattern," 来源不详. Klein suggests a borrowing (经由 Etruscan) of 希腊语 gnomon "carpenter's square." The 拉丁语 form of the word, norma, was used in English in the 语义 "carpenter's square" 源自 1670 年代.

example.en: Arriving late without notice has become an unfortunate norm in this office.
example.zh: 在这间办公室里，不打招呼就迟到已成为一种令人遗憾的规范。

definitionLines: a.正常的，标准的；正规的；精 神健全的
entries.definition: a.正常的，标准的；正规的；精 神健全的
entries.etymology:
c. 1500, "typical, common;" 1640s, "standing at a right angle," from Late Latin normalis "in conformity with rule, normal," from Latin normalis "made according to a carpenter's square," from norma "rule, pattern," literally "carpenter's square" (see norm). Meaning "conforming to common standards, usual" is from 1828, but probably older than the record [Barnhart].

As a noun meaning "usual state or condition," from 1890. Sense of "normal person or thing" is from 1894. Normal school (1834) is from French école normale (1794), a republican foundation. The city of Normal, Illinois, U.S., was named 1857 for the normal school established there.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "typical, common;" 1640 年代, "standing at a right angle," 源自 晚期拉丁语 normalis "in conformity with rule, normal," 源自 拉丁语 normalis "made according to a carpenter's square," 源自 norma "rule, pattern," 字面义为 "carpenter's square" （参见 norm). 义为 "conforming to common standards, usual" 始于 1828 年, but 可能 older than the record [Barnhart]. 作名词时 意为 "usual state or condition," 自 1890 年起. 义为 "normal person or thing" 始于 1894 年. Normal school (1834 年) 始于 法语 école normale (1794 年), a republican foundation. The city of Normal, Illinois, U.S., was named 1857 年 for the normal school established there.

example.en: It is normal for children to feel nervous on their first day of school.
example.zh: 孩子在第一天上学时感到紧张是很正常的。

definitionLines: vt. 使规格化，使标准化；使正 常化
entries.definition: vt. 使规格化，使标准化；使正 常化
entries.etymology: 1865, from normal + -ize. Related: Normalized; normalizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1865 年, 源自 normal + -ize. 同源词：Normalized; normalizing.

entries.etymology: 1590s, "regularly," from normal + -ly (2). Meaning "under ordinary conditions" is from 1853.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "regularly," 源自 normal + -ly (2). 义为 "under ordinary conditions" 始于 1853 年.

example.en: She normally arrives at the office before nine in the morning.
example.zh: 她通常早上九点前就到办公室了。

entries.definition: a. /n.北，北方 ad. 向/自/在北方
entries.etymology:
Old English norð "northern" (adj.), "northwards" (adv.), from Proto-Germanic *nurtha- (source also of Old Norse norðr, Old Saxon north, Old Frisian north, Middle Dutch nort, Dutch noord, German nord), possibly ultimately from PIE *ner- (1) "left," also "below," as north is to the left when one faces the rising sun (source also of Sanskrit narakah "hell," Greek enerthen "from beneath," Oscan-Umbrian nertrak "left"). The same notion underlies Old Irish tuath "left; northern;" Arabic shamal "left hand; north." The usual word for "north" in the Romance languages ultimately is from English, for example Old French north (Modern French nord), borrowed from Old English norð; Italian, Spanish norte are borrowed from French.

As a noun, c. 1200, from the adverb. North Pole attested from mid-15c. (earlier the Arctic pole, late 14c.). North American (n.) first used 1766, by Franklin; as an adjective, from 1770.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 norð "northern" （形）, "northwards" （副）, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *nurtha- (source also of 古北欧语 norðr, 古撒克逊语 north, 古弗里西语 north, Middle 荷兰语 nort, 荷兰语 noord, 德语 nord), possibly 最终源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *ner- (1) "left," also "below," as north is to the left when one faces the rising sun (source also of 梵语 narakah "hell," 希腊语 enerthen "from beneath," Oscan-Umbrian nertrak "left"). The same notion underlies Old 爱尔兰语 tuath "left; northern;" 阿拉伯语 shamal "left hand; north." The usual word for "north" in the Romance languages ultimately 始于 English, for example 古法语 north (现代法语 nord), 借自 古英语 norð; 意大利语, 西班牙语 norte are 借自 法语. 作名词时, 约 1200 年, 源自 副词. North Pole attested 源自 15 世纪中期 (earlier the Arctic pole, 14 世纪晚期). North American （名） first used 1766 年, by Franklin; 作形容词时, 自 1770 年起.

entries.definition: a. /n. 东北，东北部 ad. 向东北，在东北
entries.etymology: Old English norð east; see north + east. Related: Northeasterly (1743).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 norð east; 参见 north + east. 同源词：Northeasterly (1743 年).

example.en: The storm moved northeast and hit the coast by midnight.
example.zh: 暴风雨向东北方向移动，在午夜前袭击了海岸。

entries.etymology: Old English norþerna, norðerne "northern, Northumbrian, Scandinavian," cognate with Old High German nordroni, Old Norse norroenn (see north). With -erne, suffix denoting direction. Related: Northernmost. Northerner in U.S. geo-political sense is attested from 1831. Northern lights "aurora borealis" first recorded by that name 1721 (earlier north-light, 1706).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 norþerna, norðerne "northern, Northumbrian, Scandinavian," 与 … 同源 古高地德语 nordroni, 古北欧语 norroenn （参见 north). With -erne, suffix denoting direction. 同源词：Northernmost. Northerner in U.S. geo-political sense 见于 1831 年. Northern lights "aurora borealis" 首见于 by that name 1721 年 (earlier north-light, 1706 年).

example.en: The northern coast of the island is known for its dramatic cliffs.
example.zh: 该岛的北部海岸以壮观的悬崖闻名。

entries.definition: a./n. 西北，西北部 ad. 向西北，在西北
entries.etymology:
Old English norðwest (adv.); 
from north + west. As a noun from late 14c. Related: Northwestern; northwesterly; northwestward. Northwest Passage first attested c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 norðwest （副）; 源自 north + west. 作名词时 源自 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Northwestern; northwesterly; northwestward. Northwest Passage 最早见于 约 1600 年.

entries.definition: a.挪威（人）的 n. 挪威人/语
entries.etymology: c. 1600 (n. and adj.), sometimes in early use Norvegian, from Medieval Latin Norvegia "Norway," from Old Norse Norvegr (see Norway) + -ian.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年 (n. and adj.), 有时 in early use Norvegian, 源自 中古拉丁语 Norvegia "Norway," 源自 古北欧语 Norvegr （参见 Norway) + -ian.

entries.etymology: negative particle, mid-13c., unstressed variant of noht, naht "in no way" (see naught). As an interjection to negate what was said before or reveal it as sarcasm, it is first attested 1900; popularized 1989 by "Wayne's World" sketches on "Saturday Night Live" TV show. To not know X from Y (one's ass from one's elbow, shit from Shinola, etc.) was a construction first attested c. 1930. Double negative construction not un- was derided by Orwell, but is persistent and ancient in English, popular with Milton and the Anglo-Saxon poets.
entries.etymologyZh: negative particle, 13 世纪中期, unstressed 为 … 的变体 noht, naht "in no way" （参见 naught). 作为 interjection to negate what was said before or reveal it as sarcasm, it is 最早见于 1900 年; popularized 1989 年 by "Wayne's World" sketches on "Saturday Night Live" TV show. To not know X 源自 Y (one's ass from one's elbow, shit 源自 Shinola, etc.) was a construction 最早见于 约 1930 年. Double negative construction not un- was derided by Orwell, but is persistent and ancient in English, popular with Milton and the 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 poets.

definitionLines: a. 值得注意的，显著的
entries.definition: a. 值得注意的，显著的
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French notable "well-known, notable, remarkable" (13c.) and directly from Latin notabilis "noteworthy, extraordinary," from notare "to note" (see note (v.)). The noun meaning "a person of distinction" is first recorded 1815. Related: Notably; notableness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 notable "well-known, notable, remarkable" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 notabilis "noteworthy, extraordinary," 源自 notare "to note" （参见 note （动）). The 名词 意为 "a person of distinction" is 首见于 1815 年. 同源词：Notably; notableness.

example.en: One notable exception to the rule is the case of rare earth elements.
example.zh: 该规则的一个值得关注的例外是稀土元素的情况。

definitionLines: n. 笔记，记录；便条；名望；注 意，注释，评论；钞票，纸币
entries.definition: n. 笔记，记录；便条；名望；注 意，注释，评论；钞票，纸币 vt. 记下，记录；注意
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "observe, take mental note of, mark carefully," from Old French noter "indicate, designate; take note of, write down," from Latin notare "to mark, to note, to make a note," from nota "mark, sign, note, character, letter" (see note (n.)). Meaning "to set in writing" is from early 14c. Related: Noted; noting.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "observe, take mental note of, mark carefully," 源自 古法语 noter "indicate, designate; take note of, write down," 源自 拉丁语 notare "to mark, to note, to make a note," 源自 nota "mark, sign, note, character, letter" （参见 note （名）). 义为 "to set in writing" 始于 14 世纪初 同源词：Noted; noting.

example.en: Please note down only the key terms, not every word the professor says.
example.zh: 请只记下关键术语，而不是教授说的每一个字。

definitionLines: n. 笔记本；笔记本电脑
entries.definition: n. 笔记本；笔记本电脑
entries.etymology: 1570s, from note + book (n.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 源自 note + book （名）.

example.en: She wrote all the key points in her notebook during the lecture.
example.zh: 她在讲座期间把所有要点都写在笔记本上。

definitionLines: a. 显著的；值得注意的
entries.definition: a. 显著的；值得注意的
entries.etymology: 1550s, from note (v.) + worthy. Related: Noteworthiness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 note （动） + worthy. 同源词：Noteworthiness.

definitionLines: pron.没有东西，什么也没有； 无，小事
n. 微不足道的人或事
entries.definition: pron.没有东西，什么也没有； 无，小事 n. 微不足道的人或事
entries.etymology: Old English naþing, naðinc, from nan "not one" (see none) + þing "thing" (see thing). Meaning "insignificant thing" is from c. 1600. As an adverb from c. 1200. As an adjective from 1961.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 naþing, naðinc, 源自 nan "not one" （参见 none) + þing "thing" （参见 thing). 义为 "insignificant thing" 始于 约 1600 年. 作为 副词 源自 约 1200 年. 作形容词时 自 1961 年起.

definitionLines: n. 注意，认识；通知，通告，布告
entries.definition: n. 注意，认识；通知，通告，布告 vt. 看到，注意到
entries.etymology: early 15c., "information, intelligence," from Middle French notice (14c.), and directly from Latin notitia "a being known, celebrity, fame, knowledge," from notus "known," past participle of (g)noscere "come to know, to get to know, get acquainted (with)," from PIE *gno-sko-, a suffixed form of root *gno- (see know). Sense of "formal warning" is attested from 1590s. Meaning "a sign giving information" is from 1805.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "information, intelligence," 源自 中古法语 notice (14 世纪), and 直接源自 拉丁语 notitia "a being known, celebrity, fame, knowledge," 源自 notus "known," 为 … 的过去分词 (g)noscere "come to know, to get to know, get acquainted (with)," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *gno-sko-, a suffixed form of root *gno- （参见 know). 义为 "formal warning" 见于 1590 年代. 义为 "a sign giving information" 始于 1805 年.

example.en: I happened to notice that she had been crying when she came into the office.
example.zh: 她走进办公室时，我碰巧注意到她刚刚哭过。

definitionLines: a.显而易见的，显著的，值得注 意的
entries.definition: a.显而易见的，显著的，值得注 意的
entries.etymology: 1796, "worthy of notice," from notice (n.) + -able. Meaning "capable of being noticed" is from 1809. Related: Noticeably.
entries.etymologyZh: 1796 年, "worthy of notice," 源自 notice （名） + -able. 义为 "capable of being noticed" 始于 1809 年. 同源词：Noticeably.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French notefiier "make known, inform, apprise" (13c.), from Latin notificare "to make known, notify," from Latin notus "known" (see notice (n.)) + root of facere "make, do" (see factitious). Related: Notified; notifying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 notefiier "make known, inform, apprise" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 notificare "to make known, notify," 源自 拉丁语 notus "known" （参见 notice （名）) + root of facere "make, do" （参见 factitious). 同源词：Notified; notifying.

example.en: Please notify the relevant departments of any changes to the schedule immediately.
example.zh: 请立即将日程的任何变动通知相关部门。

definitionLines: n. 概念，意念；想法，见解
entries.definition: n. 概念，意念；想法，见解
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin notionem (nominative notio) "concept, conception, idea, notice," noun of action from past participle stem of noscere "come to know" (see know). Coined by Cicero as a loan-translation of Greek ennoia "act of thinking, notion, conception," or prolepsis "previous notion, previous conception."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 notionem (主格 notio) "concept, conception, idea, notice," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of noscere "come to know" （参见 know). Coined by Cicero 作为 loan-translation of 希腊语 ennoia "act of thinking, notion, conception," or prolepsis "previous notion, previous conception."

example.en: He rejected the notion that hard work alone guarantees success.
example.zh: 他否定了仅靠努力就能保证成功的这一想法。

definitionLines: a.声名狼藉的，臭名昭著的
entries.definition: a.声名狼藉的，臭名昭著的
entries.etymology: 1540s, "publicly known," from Medieval Latin notorius "well-known, commonly known," from Latin notus "known," past participle of noscere "come to know" (see know). Negative connotation arose 17c. from frequent association with derogatory nouns. Related: Notoriously.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "publicly known," 源自 中古拉丁语 notorius "well-known, commonly known," 源自 拉丁语 notus "known," 为 … 的过去分词 noscere "come to know" （参见 know). Negative connotation arose 17 世纪 源自 frequent association with derogatory nouns. 同源词：Notoriously.

example.en: The gang leader was notorious throughout the country for a series of brutal robberies and murders.
example.zh: 这个团伙头目因一连串残忍的抢劫和谋杀而在全国臭名昭著。

entries.definition: adv. 尽管，仍然 prep. 尽管，虽然
entries.etymology: late 14c., notwiþstondynge, from not + present participle of the verb withstand. A loan-translation of Medieval Latin non obstante "being no hindrance," from ablative of obstans, present participle of obstare "stand opposite to" (see obstacle). As an adverb and as a conjunction from early 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, notwiþstondynge, 源自 not + 为 … 的现在分词 the 动词 withstand. A loan-translation of 中古拉丁语 non obstante "being no hindrance," 源自 ablative of obstans, 为 … 的现在分词 obstare "stand opposite to" （参见 obstacle). 作为 副词 and 作为 conjunction 源自 15 世纪初

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Anglo-French noun "name, noun," from Old French nom, non (Modern French nom), from Latin nomen "name, noun" (see name (n.)). Old English used name to mean "noun." Related: Nounal.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 名词 "name, noun," 源自 古法语 nom, non (现代法语 nom), 源自 拉丁语 nomen "name, noun" （参见 name （名）). 古英语 used name to mean "noun." 同源词：Nounal.

entries.etymology: late 13c., "to bring up, nurture" (a child, a feeling, etc.), from Old French norriss-, stem of norrir "raise, bring up, nurture, foster; maintain, provide for" (12c., Modern French nourrir), from Latin nutrire "to feed, nurse, foster, support, preserve," from *nutri (older form of nutrix "nurse"), literally "she who gives suck," from PIE *nu- (from root *(s)nau- "to swim, flow, let flow," hence "to suckle;" see nutriment) + fem. agent suffix. Related: Nourished; nourishing.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "to bring up, nurture" (a child, a feeling, etc.), 源自 古法语 norriss-, stem of norrir "raise, bring up, nurture, foster; maintain, provide for" (12 世纪, 现代法语 nourrir), 源自 拉丁语 nutrire "to feed, nurse, foster, support, preserve," 源自 *nutri (older form of nutrix "nurse"), 字面义为 "she who gives suck," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *nu- (源自 root *(s)nau- "to swim, flow, let flow," hence "to suckle;" 参见 nutriment) + fem. agent suffix. 同源词：Nourished; nourishing.

entries.etymology: "new, strange, unusual," early 15c., but little used before 1600, from Old French novel, nouvel "new, young, fresh, recent; additional; early, soon" (Modern French nouveau, fem. nouvelle), from Latin novellus "new, young, recent," diminutive of novus "new" (see new).
entries.etymologyZh: "new, strange, unusual," 15 世纪初, but little used 1600 年之前, 源自 古法语 novel, nouvel "new, young, fresh, recent; additional; early, soon" (现代法语 nouveau, fem. nouvelle), 源自 拉丁语 novellus "new, young, recent," 为 … 的指小形式 novus "new" （参见 new).

example.en: She spent three years writing her debut novel.
example.zh: 她花了三年时间写她的处女作长篇小说。

entries.etymology: "writer of novels," 1728, hybrid from novel (n.) + -ist. Influenced by Italian novellista. Earlier in English, it meant "an innovator" (1580s).
entries.etymologyZh: "writer of novels," 1728 年, hybrid 源自 novel （名） + -ist. Influenced by 意大利语 novellista. Earlier in English, it meant "an innovator" (1580 年代).

example.en: The award-winning novelist spent ten years writing her debut book.
example.zh: 这位获奖小说家花了十年时间写她的处女作。

definitionLines: n. 新奇；新奇的事物；新颖小巧 而廉价的物品
entries.definition: n. 新奇；新奇的事物；新颖小巧 而廉价的物品
entries.etymology: late 14c., "quality of being new," also "a new manner or fashion, an innovation; something new or unusual," from Old French noveleté "newness, innovation, change; news, new fashion" (Modern French nouveauté), from novel "new" (see novel (adj.)). Meaning "newness" is attested from late 14c.; sense of "useless but amusing object" is attested from 1901 (as in novelty shop, 1973).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "quality of being new," also "a new manner or fashion, an innovation; something new or unusual," 源自 古法语 noveleté "newness, innovation, change; news, new fashion" (现代法语 nouveauté), 源自 novel "new" （参见 novel （形）). 义为 "newness" 见于 14 世纪晚期; 语义 "useless but amusing object" 见于 1901 年 (as in novelty shop, 1973 年).

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old French novembre and directly from Latin November (also Novembris (mensis)), from novem "nine" (see nine). The ninth month of the Roman calendar, which began in March. For -ber see December. In Old English, it was Blotmonað "month of sacrifice," literally "blood-month," the time when the early Saxons prepared for winter by sacrificing animals, which they then butchered and stored for food.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 novembre and 直接源自 拉丁语 November (also Novembris (mensis)), 源自 novem "nine" （参见 nine). The ninth month of the Roman calendar, which began in March. For -ber 参见 December. In 古英语, it was Blotmonað "month of sacrifice," 字面义为 "blood-month," the time when the early Saxons prepared for winter by sacrificing animals, which they 之后 butchered and stored for food.

definitionLines: ad. 现在，当前，如今；这时候； 现在就，马上；［用以改变口 气，加强语气］
entries.definition: ad. 现在，当前，如今；这时候； 现在就，马上；［用以改变口 气，加强语气］
entries.etymology:
Old English nu "now, at present, immediately; now that," also used as an interjection and as an introductory word; common Germanic (Old Norse nu, Dutch nu, Old Frisian nu, German nun, Gothic nu "now"), from PIE *nu "now" (source also of Sanskrit and Avestan nu, Old Persian nuram, Hittite nuwa, Greek nu, nun, Latin nunc, Old Church Slavonic nyne, Lithuanian nu, Old Irish nu-). Perhaps originally "newly, recently," and related to the root of new.

Often merely emphatic; non-temporal usage (as in Now, then) was in Old English. The adjective meaning "up to date" first recorded 1967, but the word was used also as an adjective in Middle English with the sense "current" from late 14c. Now and then "occasionally" is from 1530s; now or never attested from 1550s.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 nu "now, at present, immediately; now that," also used 作为 interjection and 作为 introductory word; common 日耳曼语 (古北欧语 nu, 荷兰语 nu, 古弗里西语 nu, 德语 nun, Gothic nu "now"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *nu "now" (source also of 梵语 and Avestan nu, Old 波斯语 nuram, Hittite nuwa, 希腊语 nu, nun, 拉丁语 nunc, Old Church Slavonic nyne, Lithuanian nu, Old 爱尔兰语 nu-). Perhaps 原义为 "newly, recently," and related to the root of new. Often merely emphatic; non-temporal usage (as in Now, 之后) was in 古英语. The 形容词 意为 "up to date" 首见于 1967 年, but the word was used also 作形容词时 in 中古英语 with the sense "current" 源自 14 世纪晚期 Now and 之后 "occasionally" 始于 1530 年代; 现在 or never attested 源自 1550 年代.

example.en: We must act now before the deadline passes and the chance is gone.
example.zh: 我们必须立刻行动，否则截止日期一过机会就没了。

entries.etymology: late 14c., contracted from Middle English nou adayes (mid-14c.), from now + adayes "during the day," with adverbial genitive (see day).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, contracted 源自 中古英语 nou adayes (14 世纪中期), 源自 现在 + adayes "during the day," with adverbial 属格 （参见 day).

definitionLines: ad. 哪儿也不，什么地方都没有
entries.definition: ad. 哪儿也不，什么地方都没有
entries.etymology: Old English nahwær "nowhere, not at all;" see no + where. Similar constructions were attempted with nowhat (1520s) and nowhen (1764), but they failed to take hold and remain nonce words.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 nahwær "nowhere, not at all;" 参见 no + where. Similar constructions were attempted with nowhat (1520 年代) and nowhen (1764 年), but they failed to take hold and remain nonce words.

example.en: After wandering for hours, they found themselves nowhere near familiar.
example.zh: 漫游数小时后，他们发现自己到了一个完全不熟悉的地方。

entries.etymology: 1841, "of or like the nucleus of a cell," from nucleus + -ar, probably by influence of French nucléaire. Use in atomic physics is from 1914; of weapons, from 1945. Hence nuclear physics (1933), nuclear energy (1941), nuclear war (1954). Nuclear winter coined by Richard Turco, but first attested in article by Carl Sagan in "Parade" magazine, Oct. 30, 1983. General sense of "central" is from 1912. Nuclear family, originally a sociologists' term, is first attested 1949 in "Social Structure," by American anthropologist G.P. Murdock (1897-1985). Alternative adjective nucleal is recorded from 1840.
entries.etymologyZh: 1841 年, "of or like the nucleus of a cell," 源自 nucleus + -ar, 可能 by influence of 法语 nucléaire. Use in atomic physics 始于 1914 年; of weapons, 自 1945 年起. Hence nuclear physics (1933 年), nuclear energy (1941 年), nuclear war (1954 年). Nuclear winter coined by Richard Turco, but 最早见于 in article by Carl Sagan in "Parade" magazine, Oct. 30, 1983 年. General 语义 "central" 始于 1912 年. Nuclear family, 原义为 a sociologists' term, is 最早见于 1949 年 in "Social Structure," by American anthropologist G.P. Murdock (1897 年-1985 年). Alternative 形容词 nucleal 见于 1840 年.

example.en: Several countries are debating whether to phase out nuclear power plants entirely.
example.zh: 几个国家正在讨论是否要彻底淘汰核电站。

definitionLines: n. 麻烦事，讨厌的人/事
entries.definition: n. 麻烦事，讨厌的人/事
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "injury, hurt, harm," from Anglo-French nusaunce, Old French nuisance "harm, wrong, damage," from past participle stem of nuire "to harm," from Latin nocere "to hurt" (see noxious). Sense has softened over time, to "anything obnoxious to a community" (bad smells, pests, eyesores), 1660s, then "source of annoyance, something personally disagreeable" (1831). Applied to persons from 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "injury, hurt, harm," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 nusaunce, 古法语 nuisance "harm, wrong, damage," 源自 past participle stem of nuire "to harm," 源自 拉丁语 nocere "to hurt" （参见 noxious). Sense has softened over time, to "anything obnoxious to a community" (bad smells, pests, eyesores), 1660 年代, 之后 "source of annoyance, something personally disagreeable" (1831 年). Applied to persons 源自 1690 年代.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "sum, aggregate of a collection," from Anglo-French noumbre, Old French nombre and directly from Latin numerus "a number, quantity," from PIE root *nem- "to divide, distribute, allot" (related to Greek nemein "to deal out;" see nemesis). Meaning "symbol or figure of arithmetic value" is from late 14c. Meaning "single (numbered) issue of a magazine" is from 1795. Meaning "dialing combination to reach a particular telephone receiver" is from 1879; hence wrong number (1886). The modern meaning "musical selection" (1885) is from vaudeville theater programs, where acts were marked by a number. Earlier numbers meant "Harmony; proportion calculated by number," and "Verses, poetry" [Johnson].

Number one "oneself" is from 1704 (mock-Italian form numero uno attested from 1973); the biblical Book of Numbers (c. 1400, Latin Numeri, Greek Arithmoi) so called because it begins with a census of the Israelites. Slang number one and number two for "urination" and "defecation" attested from 1902. Number cruncher is 1966, of machines; 1971, of persons. To get or have (someone's) number "have someone figured out" is attested from 1853. The numbers "illegal lottery" is from 1897, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "sum, aggregate of a collection," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 noumbre, 古法语 nombre and 直接源自 拉丁语 numerus "a number, quantity," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *nem- "to divide, distribute, allot" (related to 希腊语 nemein "to deal out;" 参见 nemesis). 义为 "symbol or figure of arithmetic value" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "single (numbered) issue of a magazine" 始于 1795 年. 义为 "dialing combination to reach a particular telephone receiver" 始于 1879 年; hence wrong number (1886 年). The modern 意为 "musical selection" (1885 年) 始于 vaudeville theater programs, where acts were marked by a number. Earlier numbers meant "Harmony; proportion calculated by number," and "Verses, poetry" [Johnson]. Number one "oneself" 始于 1704 年 (mock-意大利语 form numero uno attested 自 1973 年起); the biblical Book of Numbers (约 1400 年, 拉丁语 Numeri, 希腊语 Arithmoi) so called because it begins with a census of the Israelites. Slang number one and number two for "urination" and "defecation" attested 自 1902 年起. Number cruncher is 1966 年, of machines; 1971 年, of persons. To get or have (someone's) number "have someone figured out" 见于 1853 年. The numbers "illegal lottery" 始于 1897 年, American English.

example.en: A growing number of students now choose to study abroad after graduation.

entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin numerus "a number" (see number (n.)) + suffix -ical. Perhaps by influence of French numérique "of a number or numbers." Related: Numerically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 numerus "a number" （参见 number （名）) + suffix -ical. Perhaps by influence of 法语 numérique "of a number or numbers." 同源词：Numerically.

definitionLines: a. 众多的，大批的，无数的
entries.definition: a. 众多的，大批的，无数的
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin numerosus "numerous," from numerus "a number" (see number (n.)). Related: Numerosity.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 numerosus "numerous," 源自 numerus "a number" （参见 number （名）). 同源词：Numerosity.

example.en: Numerous studies spanning thirty years have confirmed the link between smoking and lung cancer.

entries.etymology: 1530s, "to suckle (an infant);" 1520s in the passive sense, "to bring up" (a child); alteration of Middle English nurshen (13c.; see nourish), Sense of "take care of (a sick person)" is first recorded 1736. Related: Nursed; nursing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "to suckle (an infant);" 1520 年代 in the passive sense, "to bring up" (a child); alteration of 中古英语 nurshen (13 世纪; 参见 nourish), 义为 "take care of (a sick person)" is 首见于 1736 年. 同源词：Nursed; nursing.

Meaning "place or room for infants and young children and their nurse" is from c. 1300. As a type of school, 1580s. Horticultural sense is from 1560s. Nursery rhyme is from 1832.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "breeding, nursing," 源自 古法语 norture, norreture "food, nourishment; education, training," 源自 晚期拉丁语 nutritia "a nursing, suckling," 源自 拉丁语 nutrire "to nourish, suckle" （参见 nourish). 义为 "place or room for infants and young children and their nurse" 始于 约 1300 年. 作为 type of school, 1580 年代. Horticultural sense 始于 1560 年代. Nursery rhyme 始于 1832 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "breeding, upbringing," from Old French norture, nourreture "food, nourishment; education, training," from Late Latin nutritia (see nursery).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "breeding, upbringing," 源自 古法语 norture, nourreture "food, nourishment; education, training," 源自 晚期拉丁语 nutritia （参见 nursery).

example.en: Good teachers not only educate but also nurture the potential of every student.
example.zh: 优秀的老师不仅传授知识，还能培育每位学生的潜能。

entries.etymologyZh: "a nutritious substance," 1828 年, 为 … 的名词用法 形容词 (1640 年代) 意为 "providing nourishment," 源自 拉丁语 nutrientem (主格 nutriens), 为 … 的现在分词 nutrire "to nourish, suckle, feed, foster" （参见 nourish).

example.en: Leafy vegetables are rich in vitamins and essential nutrient for the body.
example.zh: 绿叶蔬菜富含维生素和对身体有益的必需营养物质。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French nutrition (14c.) and directly from Latin nutritionem (nominative nutritio) "a nourishing," noun of action from past participle stem of nutrire "to nourish, suckle" (see nourish).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 nutrition (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 nutritionem (主格 nutritio) "a nourishing," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of nutrire "to nourish, suckle" （参见 nourish).

example.en: A balanced diet provides all the nutrition your body needs to function well.
example.zh: 均衡的饮食能为你的身体提供正常运转所需的全部营养。

entries.etymologyZh: 1938 年, coined, according to DuPont, 源自 random generic syllable nyl- + -on, common ending in fiber names (对比 rayon), said to be 最终源自 cotton. Use (in plural) for "nylon stockings" 始于 1940 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1720, abbreviation of of the clock (1640s), from Middle English of the clokke (late 14c.). Use of clock hand positions to describe vector directions or angles is from late 18c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1720 年, abbreviation of of the clock (1640 年代), 源自 中古英语 of the clokke (14 世纪晚期). Use of clock hand positions to describe vector directions or angles 始于 18 世纪晚期

entries.definition: n. 栎树，橡树，橡木 a. 橡木制的
entries.etymology:
Old English ac "oak tree," from Proto-Germanic *aiks (source also of Old Norse eik, Old Saxon and Old Frisian ek, Middle Dutch eike, Dutch eik, Old High German eih, German Eiche), of uncertain origin with no certain cognates outside Germanic.

The usual Indo-European base for "oak" (*deru-) has become Modern English tree (n.); likewise in Greek and Celtic words for "oak" are from the Indo-European root for "tree," probably reflecting the importance of the oak to ancient Indo-Europeans. The Old Norse form was eik, but as there were no oaks in Iceland the word came to be used there for "tree" in general. Used in Biblical translations to render Hebrew elah (probably usually "terebinth tree") and four other words.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ac "oak tree," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aiks (source also of 古北欧语 eik, 古撒克逊语 and 古弗里西语 ek, Middle 荷兰语 eike, 荷兰语 eik, 古高地德语 eih, 德语 Eiche), 来源存疑 with no certain cognates outside 日耳曼语. The usual Indo-European base for "oak" (*deru-) has become 现代英语 tree （名）; likewise in 希腊语 and Celtic words for "oak" 始于 the Indo-European root for "tree," 可能 reflecting the importance of the oak to ancient Indo-Europeans. The 古北欧语 form was eik, but as there were no oaks in Iceland the word came to be used there for "tree" in general. Used in Biblical translations to render 希伯来语 elah (可能 通常 "terebinth tree") and four other words.

example.en: The old table was carved from a single piece of oak.
example.zh: 这张旧桌子是用一整块橡木雕刻而成的。

definitionLines: n. 誓言，誓约；诅咒，咒骂
entries.definition: n. 誓言，誓约；诅咒，咒骂
entries.etymology: Old English að "oath, judicial swearing, solemn appeal to deity in witness of truth or a promise," from Proto-Germanic *aithaz (source also of Old Norse eiðr, Swedish ed, Old Saxon, Old Frisian eth, Middle Dutch eet, Dutch eed, German eid, Gothic aiþs "oath"), from PIE *oi-to- "an oath" (source also of Old Irish oeth "oath"). Common to Celtic and Germanic, possibly a loan-word from one to the other, but the history is obscure. In reference to careless invocations of divinity, from late 12c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 að "oath, judicial swearing, solemn appeal to deity in witness of truth or a promise," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *aithaz (source also of 古北欧语 eiðr, Swedish ed, 古撒克逊语, 古弗里西语 eth, Middle 荷兰语 eet, 荷兰语 eed, 德语 eid, Gothic aiþs "oath"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *oi-to- "an oath" (source also of Old 爱尔兰语 oeth "oath"). Common to Celtic and 日耳曼语, possibly a loan-word 源自 one to the other, but the history is obscure. In reference to careless invocations of divinity, 源自 12 世纪晚期

example.en: The new president took an oath to defend the constitution.
example.zh: 新总统宣誓捍卫宪法。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "submission to a higher power or authority," from Old French obedience "obedience, submission" (12c.) and directly from Latin oboedientia "obedience," noun of quality from oboedientem (nominative oboediens); see obedient. In reference to dog training from 1930.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "submission to a higher power or authority," 源自 古法语 obedience "obedience, submission" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 oboedientia "obedience," 名词 of quality 源自 oboedientem (主格 oboediens); 参见 obedient. In reference to dog training 自 1930 年起.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old French obedient "obedient" (11c.), from Latin oboedientem (nominative oboediens), present participle of oboedire "to obey" (see obey). Related: Obediently.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 obedient "obedient" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 oboedientem (主格 oboediens), 为 … 的现在分词 oboedire "to obey" （参见 obey). 同源词：Obediently.

entries.etymology: 1610s, from French obésité and directly from Latin obesitas "fatness, corpulence," from obesus "that has eaten itself fat," past participle of obdere "to eat all over, devour," from ob "over" (see ob-) + edere "eat" (see edible).
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 法语 obésité and 直接源自 拉丁语 obesitas "fatness, corpulence," 源自 obesus "that has eaten itself fat," 为 … 的过去分词 obdere "to eat all over, devour," 源自 ob "over" （参见 ob-) + edere "eat" （参见 edible).

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French obeir "obey, be obedient, do one's duty" (12c.), from Latin obedire, oboedire "obey, be subject, serve; pay attention to, give ear," literally "listen to," from ob "to" (see ob-) + audire "listen, hear" (see audience). Same sense development is in cognate Old English hiersumnian. Related: Obeyed; obeying.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 obeir "obey, be obedient, do one's duty" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 obedire, oboedire "obey, be subject, serve; pay attention to, give ear," 字面义为 "listen to," 源自 ob "to" （参见 ob-) + audire "listen, hear" （参见 audience). Same sense development is in 同源 古英语 hiersumnian. 同源词：Obeyed; obeying.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "tangible thing, something perceived or presented to the senses," from Medieval Latin objectum "thing put before" (the mind or sight), noun use of neuter of Latin obiectus "lying before, opposite" (as a noun in classical Latin, "charges, accusations"), past participle of obicere "to present, oppose, cast in the way of," from ob "against" (see ob-) + iacere "to throw" (see jet (v.)). Sense of "thing aimed at" is late 14c. No object "not a thing regarded as important" is from 1782. As an adjective, "presented to the senses," from late 14c. Object lesson "instruction conveyed by examination of a material object" is from 1831.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "tangible thing, something perceived or presented to the senses," 源自 中古拉丁语 objectum "thing put before" (the mind or sight), 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of 拉丁语 obiectus "lying before, opposite" (作名词时 in classical 拉丁语, "charges, accusations"), 为 … 的过去分词 obicere "to present, oppose, cast in the way of," 源自 ob "against" （参见 ob-) + iacere "to throw" （参见 jet （动）). 义为 "thing aimed at" is 14 世纪晚期 No object "not a thing regarded as important" 始于 1782 年. 作形容词时, "presented to the senses," 源自 14 世纪晚期 Object lesson "instruction conveyed by examination of a material object" 始于 1831 年.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French objeccion "reply, retort" (12c.) and directly from Late Latin obiectionem (nominative obiectio), "a throwing or putting before," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin obicere "to oppose" (see object (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 objeccion "reply, retort" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 obiectionem (主格 obiectio), "a throwing or putting before," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 obicere "to oppose" （参见 object （名）).

example.en: No one raised any objection to the proposed schedule changes.
example.zh: 没有人对拟议的日程变更提出任何异议。

entries.definition: n. 目标，目的 a.客观的
entries.etymology: 1610s, originally in the philosophical sense of "considered in relation to its object" (opposite of subjective), formed on pattern of Medieval Latin objectivus, from objectum "object" (see object (n.)) + -ive. Meaning "impersonal, unbiased" is first found 1855, influenced by German objektiv. Related: Objectively.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 原义为 in the philosophical 语义 "considered in relation to its object" (opposite of subjective), formed on pattern of 中古拉丁语 objectivus, 源自 objectum "object" （参见 object （名）) + -ive. 义为 "impersonal, unbiased" is first found 1855 年, influenced by 德语 objektiv. 同源词：Objectively.

example.en: The team set a clear objective for the next quarter.
example.zh: 团队为下一季度设定了明确的目标。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French obligacion "obligation, duty, responsibility" (early 13c.) and directly from Latin obligationem (nominative obligatio) "an engaging or pledging," literally "a binding" (but rarely used in this sense), noun of action from past participle stem of obligare (see oblige). The notion is of binding with promises or by law or duty.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 obligacion "obligation, duty, responsibility" (13 世纪初) and 直接源自 拉丁语 obligationem (主格 obligatio) "an engaging or pledging," 字面义为 "a binding" (but rarely used in this sense), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of obligare （参见 oblige). The notion is of binding with promises or by law or duty.

example.en: Under this contract, you have a legal obligation to deliver the goods on time.
example.zh: 根据此合同，你有按时交货的法律义务。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to bind by oath," from Old French obligier "engage one's faith, commit (oneself), pledge" (13c.), from Latin obligare "to bind, bind up, bandage," figuratively "put under obligation," from ob "to" (see ob-) + ligare "to bind," from PIE root *leig- "to bind" (see ligament). Main modern meaning "to make (someone) indebted by conferring a benefit or kindness" is from 1560s. Related: obliged; obliging.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to bind by oath," 源自 古法语 obligier "engage one's faith, commit (oneself), pledge" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 obligare "to bind, bind up, bandage," figuratively "put under obligation," 源自 ob "to" （参见 ob-) + ligare "to bind," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *leig- "to bind" （参见 ligament). Main modern 意为 "to make (someone) indebted by conferring a benefit or kindness" 始于 1560 年代. 同源词：obliged; obliging.

entries.definition: a.模糊的；晦涩的 vt. 遮掩；使难理解
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "dark," figuratively "morally unenlightened; gloomy," from Old French obscur, oscur "dark, clouded, gloomy; dim, not clear" (12c.) and directly from Latin obscurus "dark, dusky, shady," figuratively "unknown; unintelligible; hard to discern; from insignificant ancestors," from ob "over" (see ob-) + -scurus "covered," from PIE *(s)keu- "to cover, conceal" (see sky). Related: Obscurely.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "dark," figuratively "morally unenlightened; gloomy," 源自 古法语 obscur, oscur "dark, clouded, gloomy; dim, not clear" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 obscurus "dark, dusky, shady," figuratively "unknown; unintelligible; hard to discern; from insignificant ancestors," 源自 ob "over" （参见 ob-) + -scurus "covered," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *(s)keu- "to cover, conceal" （参见 sky). 同源词：Obscurely.

example.en: The meaning of that ancient text remains obscure to most scholars.
example.zh: 那段古代文献的含义对大多数学者来说仍然晦涩难懂。

definitionLines: n. 观察，监视；观察力；评论， 意见
entries.definition: n. 观察，监视；观察力；评论， 意见
entries.etymology: late 14c., "performance of a religious rite," from Latin observationem (nominative observatio) "a watching over, observance, investigation," noun of action from past participle stem of observare (see observe). Sense of "act or fact of paying attention" is from 1550s. Meaning "a remark in reference to something observed" first recorded 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "performance of a religious rite," 源自 拉丁语 observationem (主格 observatio) "a watching over, observance, investigation," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of observare （参见 observe). 义为 "act or fact of paying attention" 始于 1550 年代. 义为 "a remark in reference to something observed" 首见于 1590 年代.

example.en: The scientist recorded her observation in a detailed notebook.
example.zh: 这位科学家把她的观察记录在一个详细的笔记本里。

definitionLines: vt. 观察，注意到，看到；遵守， 奉行；说，评论
entries.definition: vt. 观察，注意到，看到；遵守， 奉行；说，评论
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to hold to" (a manner of life or course of conduct), from Old French observer, osserver "to observe, watch over, follow" (10c.), from Latin observare "watch over, note, heed, look to, attend to, guard, regard, comply with," from ob "over" (see ob-) + servare "to watch, keep safe," from PIE root *ser- (1) "to protect." Meaning "to attend to in practice, to keep, follow" is attested from late 14c. Sense of "watch, perceive, notice" is 1560s, via notion of "see and note omens." Meaning "to say by way of remark" is from c. 1600. Related: Observed; observing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to hold to" (a manner of life or course of conduct), 源自 古法语 observer, osserver "to observe, watch over, follow" (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 observare "watch over, note, heed, look to, attend to, guard, regard, comply with," 源自 ob "over" （参见 ob-) + servare "to watch, keep safe," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ser- (1) "to protect." 义为 "to attend to in practice, to keep, follow" 见于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "watch, perceive, notice" is 1560 年代, 经由 概念 "see and note omens." 义为 "to say by way of remark" 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Observed; observing.

example.en: Scientists carefully observe the migration patterns of monarch butterflies each year.
example.zh: 科学家们每年仔细观察帝王蝶的迁徙规律。

entries.etymology: 1550s, "one who keeps a rule, custom, etc.," agent noun from observe. Meaning "one who watches and takes notice" is from 1580s; this is the sense of the word in many newspaper names.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "one who keeps a rule, custom, etc.," agent 名词 源自 observe. 义为 "one who watches and takes notice" 始于 1580 年代; this is the 语义 the word in many newspaper names.

example.en: Every independent observer noted that the election was conducted fairly.
example.zh: 每一位独立观察员都指出此次选举是公正进行的。

entries.etymology: 1510s, "action of besieging," from French obsession and directly from Latin obsessionem (nominative obsessio) "siege, blockade, a blocking up," noun of action from past participle stem of obsidere "to besiege" (see obsess). Later (c. 1600), "hostile action of an evil spirit" (like possession but without the spirit actually inhabiting the body). Transferred sense of "action of anything which engrosses the mind" is from 1670s. Psychological sense is from 1901.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "action of besieging," 源自 法语 obsession and 直接源自 拉丁语 obsessionem (主格 obsessio) "siege, blockade, a blocking up," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of obsidere "to besiege" （参见 obsess). Later (约 1600 年), "hostile action of an evil spirit" (like possession but without the spirit actually inhabiting the body). Transferred 语义 "action of anything which engrosses the mind" 始于 1670 年代. Psychological sense 始于 1901 年.

example.en: His obsession with cleanliness made it impossible for him to relax at home.
example.zh: 他对洁净的痴迷使他在家里根本无法放松。

entries.etymology:
mid-14c., from Old French obstacle, ostacle "opposition, obstruction, hindrance" (13c.) or directly from Latin obstaculum "a hindrance, obstacle," with instrumental suffix *-tlom + obstare "stand before, stand opposite to, block, hinder, thwart," from ob "against" (see ob-) + stare "to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand" (see stet).
Obstacle course is attested from 1891.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 obstacle, ostacle "opposition, obstruction, hindrance" (13 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 obstaculum "a hindrance, obstacle," with instrumental suffix *-tlom + obstare "stand before, stand opposite to, block, hinder, thwart," 源自 ob "against" （参见 ob-) + stare "to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand" （参见 stet). Obstacle course 见于 1891 年.

example.en: Lack of funding remains the biggest obstacle to the project's completion.
example.zh: 资金不足仍是项目完成的最大障碍。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French obtenir "acquire, obtain" (14c.), from Latin obtinere "hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire," from ob "to" (though perhaps intensive in this case; see ob-) + tenere "to hold" (see tenet). Related: Obtained; obtaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 obtenir "acquire, obtain" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 obtinere "hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire," 源自 ob "to" (though 或许 intensive in this case; 参见 ob-) + tenere "to hold" （参见 tenet). 同源词：Obtained; obtaining.

example.en: You must obtain written permission from the landlord before subletting the flat.
example.zh: 转租这套公寓之前，你必须从房东那里取得书面许可。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "frequently met with," from Latin obvius "that is in the way, presenting itself readily, open, exposed, commonplace," from obviam (adv.) "in the way," from ob "against" (see ob-) + viam, accusative of via "way" (see via). Meaning "plain to see, evident" is first recorded 1630s. Related: Obviously; obviousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "frequently met with," 源自 拉丁语 obvius "that is in the way, presenting itself readily, open, exposed, commonplace," 源自 obviam （副） "in the way," 源自 ob "against" （参见 ob-) + viam, 宾格 of 经由 "way" （参见 经由). 义为 "plain to see, evident" is 首见于 1630 年代. 同源词：Obviously; obviousness.

example.en: It was obvious that she had not slept at all the previous night.
example.zh: 很明显，她前一晚根本没有睡觉。

example.en: The answer was obviously wrong, and everyone in the room could see it.
example.zh: 答案显然是错的，房间里的每个人都看得出来。

definitionLines: n. 场合；大事，节日；时机，机会
entries.definition: n. 场合；大事，节日；时机，机会
entries.etymology: late 14c., "opportunity; grounds for action, state of affairs that makes something else possible; a happening, occurrence," from Old French ochaison, ocasion "cause, reason, excuse, pretext; opportunity" (13c.) or directly from Latin occasionem (nominative occasio) "opportunity, appropriate time," in Late Latin "cause," from occasum, occasus, past participle of occidere "fall down, go down," from ob "down, away" (see ob-) + cadere "to fall" (see case (n.1)). The notion is of a "falling together," or juncture, of circumstances.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "opportunity; grounds for action, state of affairs that makes something else possible; a happening, occurrence," 源自 古法语 ochaison, ocasion "cause, reason, excuse, pretext; opportunity" (13 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 occasionem (主格 occasio) "opportunity, appropriate time," in 晚期拉丁语 "cause," 源自 occasum, occasus, 为 … 的过去分词 occidere "fall down, go down," 源自 ob "down, away" （参见 ob-) + cadere "to fall" （参见 case (n.1)). The notion is of a "falling together," or juncture, of circumstances.

example.en: A wedding is a very special occasion that most people remember all their lives.
example.zh: 婚礼是一个非常特别的场合，大多数人终身难忘。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "occurring now and then," from occasion (n.) + -al (1). Meaning "casual" is 1560s. Meaning "happening on or pertaining to a particular occasion" is from 1630s. Of furniture, etc., from 1749.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "occurring now and then," 源自 occasion （名） + -al (1). 义为 "casual" is 1560 年代. 义为 "happening on or pertaining to a particular occasion" 始于 1630 年代. Of furniture, etc., 自 1749 年起.

example.en: He made occasional visits to the office but mostly worked from home.
example.zh: 他偶尔去办公室，但大多数时候在家工作。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "fact of holding or possessing;" mid-14c., "a being employed in something," also "a particular action," from Old French occupacion "pursuit, work, employment; occupancy, occupation" (12c.), from Latin occupationem (nominative occupatio) "a taking possession; business, employment," noun of action from past participle stem of occupare (see occupy). Meaning "employment, business in which one engages" is late 14c. That of "condition of being held and ruled by troops of another country" is from 1940.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "fact of holding or possessing;" 14 世纪中期, "a being employed in something," also "a particular action," 源自 古法语 occupacion "pursuit, work, employment; occupancy, occupation" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 occupationem (主格 occupatio) "a taking possession; business, employment," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of occupare （参见 occupy). 义为 "employment, business in which one engages" is 14 世纪晚期 That of "condition of being held and ruled by troops of another country" 始于 1940 年.

example.en: Please write your name, age and occupation in the blanks on this form.
example.zh: 请在表格的空白处填写你的姓名、年龄和职业。

definitionLines: vt. 占，占领，占据；使忙碌， 使从事
entries.definition: vt. 占，占领，占据；使忙碌， 使从事
entries.etymology:
mid-14c., "to take possession of," also "to take up space or time, employ (someone)," irregularly borrowed from Old French occuper "occupy (a person or place), hold, seize" (13c.) or directly from Latin occupare "take over, seize, take into possession, possess, occupy," from ob "over" (see ob-) + intensive form of capere "to grasp, seize" (see capable). The final syllable of the English word is difficult to explain, but it is as old as the record; perhaps from a modification made in Anglo-French. During 16c.-17c. a common euphemism for "have sexual intercourse with" (sense attested from early 15c.), which caused it to fall from polite usage.
Related: Occupied; occupying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "to take possession of," also "to take up space or time, employ (someone)," irregularly 借自 古法语 occuper "occupy (a person or place), hold, seize" (13 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 occupare "take over, seize, take into possession, possess, occupy," 源自 ob "over" （参见 ob-) + intensive form of capere "to grasp, seize" （参见 capable). The final syllable of the English word is difficult to explain, but it is as old as the record; 或源自 a modification made in 盎格鲁-法语. During 16 世纪-17 世纪 a common euphemism for "have sexual intercourse with" (sense attested 源自 15 世纪初), which caused it to fall 源自 polite usage. 同源词：Occupied; occupying.

example.en: Protesters began to occupy the central square by nightfall.
example.zh: 抗议者在夜幕降临时开始占据中心广场。

definitionLines: vi. 发生，出现；（to）想起，想到
entries.definition: vi. 发生，出现；（to）想起，想到
entries.etymology: 1520s, "meet, meet in argument," from Middle French occurrer "happen unexpectedly" or directly from Latin occurrere "run to meet, run against, befall, present itself," from ob "against, toward" (see ob-) + currere "to run" (see current (adj.)). Sense development is from "meet" to "present itself" to "appear" to "happen" ("present itself in the course of events"). Meaning "to come into one's mind" is from 1620s. Related: Occurred; occurring.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "meet, meet in argument," 源自 中古法语 occurrer "happen unexpectedly" or 直接源自 拉丁语 occurrere "run to meet, run against, befall, present itself," 源自 ob "against, toward" （参见 ob-) + currere "to run" （参见 current （形）). Sense development 始于 "meet" to "present itself" to "appear" to "happen" ("present itself in the course of events"). 义为 "to come into one's mind" 始于 1620 年代. 同源词：Occurred; occurring.

example.en: Accidents are more likely to occur when drivers use their phones.
example.zh: 当司机使用手机时，事故更容易发生。

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French occurrence "unexpected happening" or directly from Medieval Latin occurrentia, from Latin occurentem (nominative occurens), present participle of occurrere (see occur).
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 occurrence "unexpected happening" or 直接源自 中古拉丁语 occurrentia, 源自 拉丁语 occurentem (主格 occurens), 为 … 的现在分词 occurrere （参见 occur).

entries.etymology: late 13c., from Old French occean "ocean" (12c., Modern French océan), from Latin oceanus, from Greek okeanos, the great river or sea surrounding the disk of the Earth (as opposed to the Mediterranean), of unknown origin. Personified as Oceanus, son of Uranus and Gaia and husband of Tethys. In early times, when the only known land masses were Eurasia and Africa, the ocean was an endless river that flowed around them. Until c. 1650, commonly ocean sea, translating Latin mare oceanum. Application to individual bodies of water began 14c.; there are usually reckoned to be five of them, but this is arbitrary; also occasionally applied to smaller subdivisions, such as German Ocean "North Sea."
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 occean "ocean" (12 世纪, 现代法语 océan), 源自 拉丁语 oceanus, 源自 希腊语 okeanos, the great river or sea surrounding the disk of the Earth (as opposed to the Mediterranean), 来源不详. Personified as Oceanus, son of Uranus and Gaia and husband of Tethys. In early times, when the only known land masses were Eurasia and Africa, the ocean was an endless river that flowed around them. Until 约 1650 年, commonly ocean sea, translating 拉丁语 mare oceanum. Application to individual bodies of water began 14 世纪; there are 通常 reckoned to be five of them, but this is arbitrary; also occasionally applied to smaller subdivisions, such as 德语 Ocean "North Sea."

example.en: Plastic waste poses a growing threat to life in the deep ocean.
example.zh: 塑料垃圾对深海生命构成日益严重的威胁。

entries.etymology: "southern Pacific island and Australia, conceived as a continent," 1849, Modern Latin, from French Océanie (c. 1812). Apparently coined by Danish geographer Conrad Malte-Brun (1755-1826). Earlier in English as Oceanica (1832). Oceania was the name of one of the superstates in Orwell's "Nineteen Eighty-Four." Oceanea, name of James Harrington's 17c. ideal state, later was applied to the British empire.
entries.etymologyZh: "southern Pacific island and Australia, conceived as a continent," 1849 年, 现代 拉丁语, 源自 法语 Océanie (约 1812 年). Apparently coined by Danish geographer Conrad Malte-Brun (1755 年-1826 年). Earlier in English as Oceanica (1832 年). Oceania was the name of one of the superstates in Orwell's "Nineteen Eighty-Four." Oceanea, name of James Harrington's 17 世纪 ideal state, later was applied to the British empire.

entries.etymology: c. 1050, from Latin October (mensis), from octo "eight," from PIE root *octo(u)- "eight" (see eight). Eighth month of the old Roman calendar (pre-46 B.C.E.), which began the year in March. For -ber see December. Replaced Old English winterfylleð. In Russian history, October Revolution (in which the Bolsheviks overthrew the Provisional Government) happened Nov. 7, but because Russia had not at that time adpoted the Gregorian calendar reform, this date was reckoned there (Old Style) as Oct. 25.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1050 年, 源自 拉丁语 October (mensis), 源自 octo "eight," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *octo(u)- "eight" （参见 eight). Eighth month of the old Roman calendar (pre-46 B.C.E.), which began the year in March. For -ber 参见 December. Replaced 古英语 winterfylleð. In 俄语 history, October Revolution (in which the Bolsheviks overthrew the Provisional Government) happened Nov. 7, but because Russia had not at that time adpoted the Gregorian calendar reform, this date was reckoned there (Old Style) as Oct. 25.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "constituting a unit in excess of an even number," from Old Norse oddi "third or additional number," as in odda-maðr "third man, odd man (who gives the casting vote)," odda-tala "odd number." The literal meaning of Old Norse oddi is "point of land, angle" (related via notion of "triangle" to oddr "point of a weapon"); from Proto-Germanic *uzdaz "pointed upward" (source also of Old English ord "point of a weapon, spear, source, beginning," Old Frisian ord "point, place," Dutch oord "place, region," Old High German ort "point, angle," German Ort "place"), from PIE *uzdho- (source also of Lithuanian us-nis "thistle"). None of the other languages, however, shows the Old Norse development from "point" to "third number." Used from late 14c. to indicate a surplus over any given sum.

Sense of "strange, peculiar" first attested 1580s from notion of "odd one out, unpaired one of three" (attested earlier, c. 1400, as "singular" in a positive sense of "renowned, rare, choice"). Odd job (c. 1770) is so called from notion of "not regular." Odd lot "incomplete or random set" is from 1897. The international order of Odd Fellows began as local social clubs in England, late 18c., with Masonic-type trappings; formally organized 1813 in Manchester.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "constituting a unit in excess of an even number," 源自 古北欧语 oddi "third or additional number," as in odda-maðr "third man, odd man (who gives the casting vote)," odda-tala "odd number." The literal 意为 of 古北欧语 oddi is "point of land, angle" (related 经由 概念 "triangle" to oddr "point of a weapon"); 源自 原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz "pointed upward" (source also of 古英语 ord "point of a weapon, spear, source, beginning," 古弗里西语 ord "point, place," 荷兰语 oord "place, region," 古高地德语 ort "point, angle," 德语 Ort "place"), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *uzdho- (source also of Lithuanian us-nis "thistle"). None of the other languages, however, shows the 古北欧语 development 源自 "point" to "third number." Used 源自 14 世纪晚期 to indicate a surplus over any given sum. 义为 "strange, peculiar" 最早见于 1580 年代 源自 概念 "odd one out, unpaired one of three" (attested earlier, 约 1400 年, as "singular" in a positive 语义 "renowned, rare, choice"). Odd job (约 1770 年) is so called 源自 概念 "not regular." Odd lot "incomplete or random set" 始于 1897 年. The international order of Odd Fellows began as local social clubs in England, 18 世纪晚期, with Masonic-type trappings; formally organized 1813 年 in Manchester.

example.en: There was something odd about his behavior that made everyone uneasy.
example.zh: 他的行为有些奇怪，让所有人都感到不安。

entries.definition: ad.离，距，（离开）；切断，停止， 中止；完，光；减掉，扣掉， 消除 prep. 从……离开，离 •••••• 偏离
entries.etymology: by c. 1200 as an emphatic form of Old English of (see of), employed in the adverbial use of that word. The prepositional meaning "away from" and the adjectival sense of "farther" were not firmly fixed in this variant until 17c., but once they were they left the original of with the transferred and weakened senses of the word. Meaning "not working" is from 1861. Off the cuff (1938) is from the notion of speaking from notes written in haste on one's shirt cuffs. Off the rack (adj.) is from 1963; off the record is from 1933; off the wall "crazy" is 1968, probably from the notion of a lunatic "bouncing off the walls" or else in reference to carom shots in squash, handball, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: by 约 1200 年 作为 emphatic form of 古英语 of （参见 of), employed in the adverbial use of that word. The prepositional 意为 "away from" and the adjectival 语义 "farther" were not firmly fixed in this variant until 17 世纪, but once they were they left the original of with the transferred and weakened senses of the word. 义为 "not working" 始于 1861 年. Off the cuff (1938 年) 始于 the 概念 speaking 源自 notes written in haste on one's shirt cuffs. Off the rack （形） 始于 1963 年; off the record 始于 1933 年; off the wall "crazy" is 1968 年, 可能 源自 概念 a lunatic "bouncing off the walls" or else in reference to carom shots in squash, handball, etc.

definitionLines: n. 犯罪，犯规，过错；冒犯，触怒
entries.definition: n. 犯罪，犯规，过错；冒犯，触怒
entries.etymology: see offense.
entries.etymologyZh: 参见 offense.

definitionLines: vt. 冒犯，触犯，得罪；使不快， 使恼火
entries.definition: vt. 冒犯，触犯，得罪；使不快， 使恼火
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "to sin against (someone)," from Old French ofendre "transgress, antagonize," and directly from Latin offendere "to hit, strike against," figuratively "to stumble, commit a fault, displease, trespass against, provoke," from ob "against" (see ob-) + -fendere "to strike" (found only in compounds; see defend).

Meaning "to violate (a law), to make a moral false step, to commit a crime" is from late 14c. Meaning "to wound the feelings" is from late 14c. The literal sense of "to attack, assail" is attested from late 14c.; this has been lost in Modern English, but is preserved in offense and offensive. Related: Offended; offending.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to sin against (someone)," 源自 古法语 ofendre "transgress, antagonize," and 直接源自 拉丁语 offendere "to hit, strike against," figuratively "to stumble, commit a fault, displease, trespass against, provoke," 源自 ob "against" （参见 ob-) + -fendere "to strike" (found only in compounds; 参见 defend). 义为 "to violate (a law), to make a moral false step, to commit a crime" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "to wound the feelings" 始于 14 世纪晚期 The literal 语义 "to attack, assail" 见于 14 世纪晚期; this has been lost in 现代英语, but is preserved in offense and offensive. 同源词：Offended; offending.

example.en: His blunt remarks offended several colleagues at the meeting.
example.zh: 他直率的言辞在会议上冒犯了几位同事。

definitionLines: a.讨厌的；无礼的；攻击性的
entries.definition: a.讨厌的；无礼的；攻击性的 n. 进攻；攻势
entries.etymology: "attacking" (1540s), "insulting" (1570s), both  from Middle French offensif (16c.) and directly from Medieval Latin offensivus, from Latin offens-, past participle stem of offendere "offend" (see offend). Related: Offensively; offensiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: "attacking" (1540 年代), "insulting" (1570 年代), both 源自 中古法语 offensif (16 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 offensivus, 源自 拉丁语 offens-, past participle stem of offendere "offend" （参见 offend). 同源词：Offensively; offensiveness.

example.en: Some viewers found the comedian's jokes about race to be deeply offensive.
example.zh: 一些观众认为这位喜剧演员关于种族的笑话极为冒犯。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin omittere "let go, let fall," figuratively "lay aside, disregard," from assimilated form of ob (here perhaps intensive) + mittere "let go, send" (see mission). Related: Omitted; omitting.
