entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 源自 拉丁语 participantem (主格 participans), 为 … 的现在分词 participare "to share in, partake of," 源自 particeps "sharing, partaking" （参见 participation).

example.en: All participants in the workshop were asked to sign a consent form before starting.
example.zh: 研讨会的所有参与者被要求在开始前签署一份同意书。

entries.etymology: 1530s, back-formation from participation, or else from Latin participatus, past participle of participare "to share, share in, participate in; to impart," from particeps "partaking, sharing," from parti, past participle of partir "to divide" (see part (n.)) + -cip-, weak form of stem of capere "to take" (see capable). Related: Participated; participating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, back-formation 源自 participation，或else 源自 拉丁语 participatus, 为 … 的过去分词 participare "to share, share in, participate in; to impart," 源自 particeps "partaking, sharing," 源自 parti, 为 … 的过去分词 partir "to divide" （参见 part （名）) + -cip-, weak form of stem of capere "to take" （参见 capable). 同源词：Participated; participating.

example.en: All students must participate in the mandatory fire drill scheduled for Friday.
example.zh: 所有学生必须参加周五安排的必修消防演习。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "small part or division of a whole, minute portion of matter," from Latin particula "little bit or part, grain, jot," diminutive of pars (genitive partis) "part;" see part (n.). Particle physics attested from 1969. In construction, particle board (1957) is so called because it is made from chips and shavings of wood.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "small part or division of a whole, minute portion of matter," 源自 拉丁语 particula "little bit or part, grain, jot," 为 … 的指小形式 pars (属格 partis) "part;" 参见 part （名）. Particle physics attested 自 1969 年起. In construction, particle board (1957 年) is so called because it is made 源自 chips and shavings of wood.

example.en: Dust particles in the air can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.
example.zh: 空气中的尘埃颗粒会引发敏感人群的过敏反应。

definitionLines: a.特别的，特殊的；特定的， 个别的；（过分）讲究，挑剔 的
entries.definition: a.特别的，特殊的；特定的， 个别的；（过分）讲究，挑剔 的 n. （pl.）细节，详情
entries.etymology: late 14c., "pertaining to a single thing or person," from Old French particuler (14c., Modern French particulier) and directly from Late Latin particularis "of a part, concerning a small part," from Latin particula "particle" (see particle). Sense of "precise, exacting" first recorded 1814.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "pertaining to a single thing or person," 源自 古法语 particuler (14 世纪, 现代法语 particulier) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 particularis "of a part, concerning a small part," 源自 拉丁语 particula "particle" （参见 particle). 义为 "precise, exacting" 首见于 1814 年.

example.en: The doctor paid particular attention to the patient's unusual reaction to the drug.
example.zh: 医生特别注意到患者对该药物的异常反应。

entries.etymology: "in a special degree, more than others," 1670s, from particular (adj.) + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: "in a special degree, more than others," 1670 年代, 源自 particular （形） + -ly (2).

definitionLines: ad.在一定程度上，部分地， 不完全地
entries.definition: ad.在一定程度上，部分地， 不完全地
entries.etymology: 1520s, from part (n.) + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 part （名） + -ly (2).

definitionLines: n. 伙伴，合伙人，舞伴；配偶， 搭档
entries.definition: n. 伙伴，合伙人，舞伴；配偶， 搭档
entries.etymology: 1610s, transitive, "to make a partner," from partner (n.). Intransitive sense from 1961. Related: Partnered; partnering.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, transitive, "to make a partner," 源自 partner （名）. Intransitive sense 自 1961 年起. 同源词：Partnered; partnering.

example.en: She found the perfect business partner to help expand her startup.
example.zh: 她找到了完美的商业伙伴来帮助扩展她的初创公司。

definitionLines: 党，政党；聚会；一方，当事人
entries.definition: 党，政党；聚会；一方，当事人
entries.etymology: late 13c., "part, portion, side," from Old French partie "side, part; portion, share; separation, division" (12c.), literally "that which is divided," noun use of fem. past participle of partir "to divide" (see part (v.)). Political sense of "side in a contest or dispute" evolved by 1300; meaning "a person" is from mid-15c. Sense of "gathering for social pleasure" is first found 1716, from general sense of persons gathered together (originally for some specific purpose, such as dinner party, hunting party). Phrase the party is over is from 1937; party line is first recorded 1834 in the sense of "policy adopted by a political party," 1893 in the sense of "telephone line shared by two or more subscribers." Party pooper is from 1951, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "part, portion, side," 源自 古法语 partie "side, part; portion, share; separation, division" (12 世纪), 字面义为 "that which is divided," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 partir "to divide" （参见 part （动）). Political 语义 "side in a contest or dispute" evolved 截至 1300 年; 意为 "a person" 始于 15 世纪中期 义为 "gathering for social pleasure" is first found 1716 年, 源自 general 语义 persons gathered together (原义为 for some specific purpose, such as dinner party, hunting party). Phrase the party is over 始于 1937 年; party line is 首见于 1834 年 in the 语义 "policy adopted by a political party," 1893 年 in the 语义 "telephone line shared by two or more subscribers." Party pooper 始于 1951 年, American English.

example.en: They threw a surprise party for her birthday and invited all her friends.
example.zh: 他们为她举办了一场生日惊喜派对，邀请了她所有的朋友。

definitionLines: v. 经过，走过；通过，穿过；传， 传递；度；通过（考试等）
n. 通行证，护照；关隘；考试
entries.definition: v. 经过，走过；通过，穿过；传， 传递；度；通过（考试等） n. 通行证，护照；关隘；考试
entries.etymology:
late 13c. (transitive) "to go by (something)," also "to cross over," from Old French passer (11c.), from Vulgar Latin *passare "to step, walk, pass" (source also of Spanish pasar, Italian passare), from Latin passus "step, pace" (see pace (n.)). Intransitive sense of "to go on, to move forward, make one's way" is attested from c. 1300. Figurative sense of "to experience, undergo" (as in pass the time) is first recorded late 14c. Sense of "to go through an examination successfully" is from early 15c. Meaning "decline to do something" is attested from 1869, originally in cards (euchre). In football, hockey, soccer, etc., the meaning "to transfer the ball or puck to another player" is from c. 1865. Related: Passed; passing.

The meaning "to be thought to be something one is not" (especially in racial sense) is from 1935, from pass oneself off (as), first found 1809. The general verb sense of "to be accepted as equivalent" is from 1590s. Pass up "decline, refuse" is attested from 1896. Pass the buck is from 1865, said to be poker slang reference to the buck horn-handled knife that was passed around to signify whose turn it was to deal. Pass the hat "seek contributions" is from 1762. Pass-fail as a grading method is attested from 1955, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期 (transitive) "to go by (something)," also "to cross over," 源自 古法语 passer (11 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *passare "to step, walk, pass" (source also of 西班牙语 pasar, 意大利语 passare), 源自 拉丁语 passus "step, pace" （参见 pace （名）). Intransitive 语义 "to go on, to move forward, make one's way" 见于 约 1300 年. Figurative 语义 "to experience, undergo" (as in pass the time) is 首见于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "to go through an examination successfully" 始于 15 世纪初 义为 "decline to do something" 见于 1869 年, 原义为 in cards (euchre). In football, hockey, soccer, etc., the 意为 "to transfer the ball or puck to another player" 始于 约 1865 年. 同源词：Passed; passing. The 意为 "to be thought to be something one is not" (尤指 in racial sense) 始于 1935 年, 源自 pass oneself off (as), first found 1809 年. The general 动词 语义 "to be accepted as equivalent" 始于 1590 年代. Pass up "decline, refuse" 见于 1896 年. Pass the buck 始于 1865 年, said to be poker 俚语 reference to the buck horn-handled knife that was passed around to signify whose turn it was to deal. Pass the hat "seek contributions" 始于 1762 年. Pass-fail 作为 grading method 见于 1955 年, American English.

example.en: Only two of the ten applicants managed to pass the rigorous background check.
example.zh: 十位申请人中只有两位成功通过了严格的背景调查。

definitionLines: n. 通过，经过；通路，走廊； 段，节
entries.definition: n. 通过，经过；通路，走廊； 段，节
entries.etymology: early 13c., "a road, passage;" late 13c., "action of passing," from Old French passage "mountain pass, passage" (11c.), from passer "to go by" (see pass (v.)). Meaning "corridor in a building" first recorded 1610s. Meaning "a portion of writing" is from 1610s, of music, from 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "a road, passage;" 13 世纪晚期, "action of passing," 源自 古法语 passage "mountain pass, passage" (11 世纪), 源自 passer "to go by" （参见 pass （动）). 义为 "corridor in a building" 首见于 1610 年代. 义为 "a portion of writing" 始于 1610 年代, of music, 源自 1670 年代.

example.en: A narrow underground passage linked the two buildings beneath the busy street.
example.zh: 一条狭窄的地下通道在繁忙街道下方连接着两栋建筑。

entries.etymology:
early 14c., passager "passer-by," from Old French passagier "traveler, passer-by" (Modern French passager), noun use of passagier (adj.) "passing, fleeting, traveling," from passage (see passage).

The -n- was added early 15c. (compare messenger, harbinger, scavenger, porringer). Meaning "one traveling in a vehicle or vessel" first attested 1510s. Passenger-pigeon of North America so called from 1802; extinct since 1914.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, passager "passer-by," 源自 古法语 passagier "traveler, passer-by" (现代法语 passager), 为 … 的名词用法 passagier （形） "passing, fleeting, traveling," 源自 passage （参见 passage). The -n- was added 15 世纪初 (对比 messenger, harbinger, scavenger, porringer). 义为 "one traveling in a vehicle or vessel" 最早见于 1510 年代. Passenger-pigeon of North America so called 自 1802 年起; extinct 自 1914 年.

example.en: The passenger fell asleep during the long train ride.
example.zh: 这位乘客在漫长的火车旅途中睡着了。

entries.etymology:
late 12c., "sufferings of Christ on the Cross," from Old French passion "Christ's passion, physical suffering" (10c.), from Late Latin passionem (nominative passio) "suffering, enduring," from past participle stem of Latin pati "to suffer, endure," possibly from PIE root *pe(i)- "to hurt" (see fiend).

Sense extended to sufferings of martyrs, and suffering generally, by early 13c.; meaning "strong emotion, desire" is attested from late 14c., from Late Latin use of passio to render Greek pathos. Replaced Old English þolung (used in glosses to render Latin passio), literally "suffering," from þolian (v.) "to endure." Sense of "sexual love" first attested 1580s; that of "strong liking, enthusiasm, predilection" is from 1630s. The passion-flower so called from 1630s.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪晚期, "sufferings of Christ on the Cross," 源自 古法语 passion "Christ's passion, physical suffering" (10 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 passionem (主格 passio) "suffering, enduring," 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 pati "to suffer, endure," possibly 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *pe(i)- "to hurt" （参见 fiend). Sense extended to sufferings of martyrs, and suffering generally, by 13 世纪初; 意为 "strong emotion, desire" 见于 14 世纪晚期, 源自 晚期拉丁语 use of passio to render 希腊语 pathos. Replaced 古英语 þolung (used in glosses to render 拉丁语 passio), 字面义为 "suffering," 源自 þolian （动） "to endure." 义为 "sexual love" 最早见于 1580 年代; that of "strong liking, enthusiasm, predilection" 始于 1630 年代. The passion-flower so called 源自 1630 年代.

example.en: Her passion for classical music drove her to practice piano six hours a day throughout her childhood.
example.zh: 她对古典音乐的热情驱使她在整个童年期间每天练习钢琴六小时。

entries.etymology: late 14c., in grammatical sense (opposed to active), Old French passif "suffering, undergoing hardship" (14c.) and directly from Latin passivus "capable of feeling or suffering," from pass-, past participle stem of pati "to suffer" (see passion). Meaning "not active" is first recorded late 15c.; sense of "enduring suffering without resistance" is from 1620s. Related: Passively. Passive resistance first attested 1819 in Scott's "Ivanhoe," used throughout 19c.; re-coined by Gandhi c. 1906 in South Africa. Passive-aggressive with reference to behavior is attested by 1971.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in grammatical sense (opposed to active), 古法语 passif "suffering, undergoing hardship" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 passivus "capable of feeling or suffering," 源自 pass-, past participle stem of pati "to suffer" （参见 passion). 义为 "not active" is 首见于 15 世纪晚期; 语义 "enduring suffering without resistance" 始于 1620 年代. 同源词：Passively. Passive resistance 最早见于 1819 年 in Scott's "Ivanhoe," used throughout 19 世纪; re-coined by Gandhi 约 1906 年 in South Africa. Passive-aggressive with reference to behavior is attested 截至 1971 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1500, from Middle French passeport "authorization to pass through a port" to enter or leave a country (15c.), from passe, imperative of Old French passer "to pass" (see pass (v.)) + port "port" (see port (n.1)).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, 源自 中古法语 passeport "authorization to pass through a port" to enter or leave a country (15 世纪), 源自 passe, imperative of 古法语 passer "to pass" （参见 pass （动）) + port "port" （参见 port (n.1)).

entries.etymology: "word appointed as a sign to distinguish friend from foe," 1798, from pass (v.) + word (n.).
entries.etymologyZh: "word appointed as a sign to distinguish friend from foe," 1798 年, 源自 pass （动） + word （名）.

entries.definition: a.过去的 n. 过去，昔时，往事 prep. 过，经过
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "done with, over," from past participle of passen "go by" (see pass (v.)). Past participle is recorded from 1798; past tense from 1813.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "done with, over," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 passen "go by" （参见 pass （动）). Past participle 见于 1798 年; past tense 自 1813 年起.

example.en: In the past, people traveled mainly by horse and cart.
example.zh: 在过去，人们主要靠马车出行。

entries.etymology: c. 1300 (mid-12c. as a surname), "dough," from Old French paste "dough, pastry" (13c., Modern French pâte), from Late Latin pasta "dough, pastry cake, paste" (see pasta). Meaning "glue mixture" is first attested mid-15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年 (12 世纪中期 作为 surname), "dough," 源自 古法语 paste "dough, pastry" (13 世纪, 现代法语 pâte), 源自 晚期拉丁语 pasta "dough, pastry cake, paste" （参见 pasta). 义为 "glue mixture" is 最早见于 15 世纪中期

entries.etymology: late 15c., passe tyme "recreation, diversion, amusement, sport," from pass (v.) + time (n.). Formed on model of Middle French passe-temps (15c.), from passe, imperative of passer "to pass" + temps "time."
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, passe tyme "recreation, diversion, amusement, sport," 源自 pass （动） + time （名）. Formed on model of 中古法语 passe-temps (15 世纪), 源自 passe, imperative of passer "to pass" + temps "time."

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "grass eaten by cattle," from Old French pasture "fodder, grass eaten by cattle" (12c., Modern French pâture), from Late Latin pastura "a feeding, grazing," from Latin pastus, past participle of pascere "to feed, graze" (see pastor). Meaning "land covered with vegetation suitable for grazing" is from early 14c. To be out to pasture "retired" is from 1945, from what was done (ideally) to horses after the active working life.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "grass eaten by cattle," 源自 古法语 pasture "fodder, grass eaten by cattle" (12 世纪, 现代法语 pâture), 源自 晚期拉丁语 pastura "a feeding, grazing," 源自 拉丁语 pastus, 为 … 的过去分词 pascere "to feed, graze" （参见 pastor). 义为 "land covered with vegetation suitable for grazing" 始于 14 世纪初 To be out to pasture "retired" 始于 1945 年, 源自 what was done (ideally) to horses after the active working life.

entries.etymology: as a fem. proper name, short for Patricia. As a masc. proper name, short for  Patrick; hence a nickname for any Irishman.
entries.etymologyZh: 作为 fem. proper name, short for Patricia. 作为 masc. proper name, short for Patrick; hence a nickname for any Irishman.

example.en: The coach gave the nervous player an encouraging pat on the shoulder.
example.zh: 教练鼓励地拍了拍那名紧张球员的肩膀。

entries.definition: n. 小片，小块，补丁 vt. 补，修补
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from patch (n.1). Electronics sense of "to connect temporarily" is attested from 1923. Related: Patched; patching.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 patch (n.1). Electronics 语义 "to connect temporarily" 见于 1923 年. 同源词：Patched; patching.

example.en: She sewed a patch onto the torn jeans to cover the hole.
example.zh: 她在破牛仔裤上缝了一块补丁来遮住洞。

definitionLines: vt. 取得……的专利权，请准 专利
entries.definition: n. 专利权，专利品； a.特许的，专利的 vt. 取得……的专利权，请准 专利
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "open letter or document from some authority," shortened form of Anglo-French lettre patent (also in Medieval Latin (litteræ) patentes), literally "open letter" (late 13c.), from Old French patente (see patent (adj.).

Meaning "a license covering an invention" is from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "open letter or document from some authority," shortened form of 盎格鲁-法语 lettre patent (also in 中古拉丁语 (litteræ) patentes), 字面义为 "open letter" (13 世纪晚期), 源自 古法语 patente （参见 patent （形）. 义为 "a license covering an invention" 始于 1580 年代.

example.en: The inventor filed a patent to protect her new device from being copied.
example.zh: 这位发明家申请了专利，以保护她的新设备不被仿制。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "affecting the emotions, exciting the passions," from Middle French pathétique "moving, stirring, affecting" (16c.), from Late Latin patheticus, from Greek pathetikos "subject to feeling, sensitive, capable of emotion," from pathetos "liable to suffer," verbal adjective of pathein "to suffer" (see pathos). Meaning "arousing pity, pitiful" is first recorded 1737. Colloquial sense of "so miserable as to be ridiculous" is attested from 1937.  Related: Pathetical (1570s); pathetically. Pathetic fallacy (1856, first used by Ruskin) is the attribution of human qualities to inanimate objects.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "affecting the emotions, exciting the passions," 源自 中古法语 pathétique "moving, stirring, affecting" (16 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 patheticus, 源自 希腊语 pathetikos "subject to feeling, sensitive, capable of emotion," 源自 pathetos "liable to suffer," verbal 形容词 of pathein "to suffer" （参见 pathos). 义为 "arousing pity, pitiful" is 首见于 1737 年. Colloquial 语义 "so miserable as to be ridiculous" 见于 1937 年. 同源词：Pathetical (1570 年代); pathetically. Pathetic fallacy (1856 年, first used by Ruskin) is the attribution of human qualities to inanimate objects.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "quality of being willing to bear adversities, calm endurance of misfortune, suffering, etc.," from Old French pacience "patience; sufferance, permission" (12c.) and directly from Latin patientia "patience, endurance, submission," also "indulgence, leniency; humility; submissiveness; submission to lust;" literally "quality of suffering." It is an abstract noun formed from the adjective patientem (nominative patiens) "bearing, supporting; suffering, enduring, permitting; tolerant," but also "firm, unyielding, hard," used of persons as well as of navigable rivers, present participle of pati "to suffer, endure," from PIE root *pe(i)- "to damage, injure, hurt" (see passion).Meaning "constancy in effort" is attested from 1510s. Meaning "card game for one person" is from 1816.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "quality of being willing to bear adversities, calm endurance of misfortune, suffering, etc.," 源自 古法语 pacience "patience; sufferance, permission" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 patientia "patience, endurance, submission," also "indulgence, leniency; humility; submissiveness; submission to lust;" 字面义为 "quality of suffering." It is an abstract 名词 formed 源自 形容词 patientem (主格 patiens) "bearing, supporting; suffering, enduring, permitting; tolerant," but also "firm, unyielding, hard," used of persons as well as of navigable rivers, 为 … 的现在分词 pati "to suffer, endure," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *pe(i)- "to damage, injure, hurt" （参见 passion).义为 "constancy in effort" 见于 1510 年代. 义为 "card game for one person" 始于 1816 年.

example.en: Teaching young children requires a great deal of patience and creativity.
example.zh: 教导幼童需要极大的耐心和创造力。

definitionLines: a. 有耐心的，能忍耐的
entries.definition: a. 有耐心的，能忍耐的 n. 病人，患者
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "enduring without complaint," from Old French pacient and directly from Latin patientem "bearing, supporting, suffering, enduring, permitting" (see patience). Meaning "pertaining to a medical patient" is late 14c., from the noun. Related: Patiently.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "enduring without complaint," 源自 古法语 pacient and 直接源自 拉丁语 patientem "bearing, supporting, suffering, enduring, permitting" （参见 patience). 义为 "pertaining to a medical patient" is 14 世纪晚期, 源自 名词. 同源词：Patiently.

example.en: The nurse reminded everyone to be patient while waiting for the test results to come back.
example.zh: 护士提醒大家在等待检测结果时要有耐心。

entries.etymology: 1650s, "of one's own country," from French patriotique or directly from Late Latin patrioticus, from Greek patriotikos, from patriotes (see patriot). Meaning "loyal, supporting one's own country" is from 1757. Related: Patriotical.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "of one's own country," 源自 法语 patriotique or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 patrioticus, 源自 希腊语 patriotikos, 源自 patriotes （参见 patriot). 义为 "loyal, supporting one's own country" 始于 1757 年. 同源词：Patriotical.

definitionLines: n. 爱国心，爱国精神；爱国主义
entries.definition: n. 爱国心，爱国精神；爱国主义
entries.etymology: 1726, from patriot + -ism.
entries.etymologyZh: 1726 年, 源自 patriot + -ism.

entries.definition: n.巡逻；巡逻队 vt./ vi. 巡逻；巡查
entries.etymology: 1660s, "action of going the rounds" (of a military camp, etc.), from French patrouille "a night watch" (1530s), from patrouiller "go the rounds to watch or guard," originally "tramp through the mud," probably soldiers' slang, from Old French patouiller "paddle in water," probably from pate "paw, foot" (see patten). Compare paddlefoot, World War II U.S. Army slang for "infantry soldier." Meaning "those who go on a patrol" is from 1660s. Sense of "detachment of soldiers sent out to scout the countryside, the enemy, etc." is attested from 1702.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, "action of going the rounds" (of a military camp, etc.), 源自 法语 patrouille "a night watch" (1530 年代), 源自 patrouiller "go the rounds to watch or guard," 原义为 "tramp through the mud," 可能 soldiers' 俚语, 源自 古法语 patouiller "paddle in water," 可能 源自 pate "paw, foot" （参见 patten). 对比 paddlefoot, World War II U.S. Army 俚语 for "infantry soldier." 义为 "those who go on a patrol" 始于 1660 年代. 义为 "detachment of soldiers sent out to scout the countryside, the enemy, etc." 见于 1702 年.

example.en: Security guards patrol the perimeter of the building every two hours.
example.zh: 保安每两小时巡逻一次建筑物周围区域。

entries.etymology: "a lord-master, a protector," c. 1300, from Old French patron "patron, protector, patron saint" (12c.) and directly from Medieval Latin patronus "patron saint, bestower of a benefice, lord, master, model, pattern," from Latin patronus "defender, protector, former master (of a freed slave); advocate," from pater (genitive patris) "father" (see father (n.)). Meaning "one who advances the cause" (of an artist, institution, etc.), usually by the person's wealth and power, is attested from late 14c.; "commonly a wretch who supports with insolence, and is paid with flattery" [Johnson]. Commercial sense of "regular customer" first recorded c. 1600. Patron saint (1717) originally was simply patron (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: "a lord-master, a protector," 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 patron "patron, protector, patron saint" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 patronus "patron saint, bestower of a benefice, lord, master, model, pattern," 源自 拉丁语 patronus "defender, protector, former master (of a freed slave); advocate," 源自 pater (属格 patris) "father" （参见 father （名）). 义为 "one who advances the cause" (of an artist, institution, etc.), 通常 by the person's wealth and power, 见于 14 世纪晚期; "commonly a wretch who supports with insolence, and is paid with flattery" [Johnson]. Commercial 语义 "regular customer" 首见于 约 1600 年. Patron saint (1717 年) 原义为 was simply patron (14 世纪晚期).

example.en: The art gallery relies heavily on patron donations to fund its exhibitions.
example.zh: 这家画廊在很大程度上依靠赞助人捐款来资助展览。

definitionLines: n. 模式，样式；图案，花样
entries.definition: n. 模式，样式；图案，花样
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "outline, plan, model, pattern;" early 15c. as "model of behavior, exemplar," from Old French patron and directly from Medieval Latin patronus (see patron).

Extended sense of "decorative design" first recorded 1580s, from earlier sense of a "patron" as a model to be imitated. The difference in form and sense between patron and pattern wasn't firm till 1700s. Meaning "model or design in dressmaking" (especially one of paper) is first recorded 1792, in Jane Austen.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "outline, plan, model, pattern;" 15 世纪初 as "model of behavior, exemplar," 源自 古法语 patron and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 patronus （参见 patron). Extended 语义 "decorative design" 首见于 1580 年代, 源自 earlier 语义 a "patron" 作为 model to be imitated. The difference in form and sense between patron and pattern wasn't firm till 1700 年代. 义为 "model or design in dressmaking" (尤指 one of paper) is 首见于 1792 年, in Jane Austen.

example.en: Researchers noticed a clear pattern in how teenagers use social media.
example.zh: 研究人员注意到青少年使用社交媒体的方式有一种清晰的模式。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French pausee "a pause, interruption" (14c.) and directly from Latin pausa "a halt, stop, cessation," from Greek pausis "stopping, ceasing," from pauein "to stop, to cause to cease," from PIE root *paus- "to leave, desert, cease, stop."
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 pausee "a pause, interruption" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 pausa "a halt, stop, cessation," 源自 希腊语 pausis "stopping, ceasing," 源自 pauein "to stop, to cause to cease," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *paus- "to leave, desert, cease, stop."

example.en: The speaker took a brief pause before answering the difficult question.
example.zh: 演讲者在回答这个难题之前短暂地停顿了一下。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "to cover (a street) with stones or other material," from Old French paver "to pave" (12c.), perhaps a back-formation from Old French pavement or else from Vulgar Latin *pavare, from Latin pavire "to beat, ram, tread down," from PIE *pau- "to cut, strike, stamp" (source also of Latin putare "to prune;" Greek paiein "to strike;" Lithuanian piauju "to cut," piuklas "saw"). Related: Paved; paving. The figurative sense of "make smooth" (as in pave the way) is attested from 1580s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to cover (a street) with stones or other material," 源自 古法语 paver "to pave" (12 世纪), 或许 a back-formation 源自 古法语 pavement or else 源自 通俗拉丁语 *pavare, 源自 拉丁语 pavire "to beat, ram, tread down," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *pau- "to cut, strike, stamp" (source also of 拉丁语 putare "to prune;" 希腊语 paiein "to strike;" Lithuanian piauju "to cut," piuklas "saw"). 同源词：Paved; paving. The figurative 语义 "make smooth" (as in pave the way) 见于 1580 年代.

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from Old French pavement "roadway, pathway; paving stone" (12c.) and directly from Latin pavimentum "hard floor, level surface beaten firm," from pavire (see pave).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 pavement "roadway, pathway; paving stone" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 pavimentum "hard floor, level surface beaten firm," 源自 pavire （参见 pave).

example.en: A cyclist lost control and rode onto the pavement narrowly missing pedestrians.
example.zh: 一名骑自行车的人失控后骑上人行道，险些撞上行人。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French powe, poe "paw, fist," of uncertain origin. Evidence points to a Gallo-Roman root form *pauta which probably is related to the source of patten.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 powe, poe "paw, fist," 来源存疑. Evidence points to a Gallo-Roman root form *pauta which 可能 is related to the source of patten.

definitionLines: v. 付款，缴纳；付清；给予，致以 （问候），进行（访问）
entries.definition: v. 付款，缴纳；付清；给予，致以 （问候），进行（访问） n.工资，薪钠；报酬
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "to appease, pacify, satisfy," from Old French paier "to pay, pay up" (12c., Modern French payer), from Latin pacare "to please, pacify, satisfy" (in Medieval Latin especially "satisfy a creditor"), literally "make peaceful," from pax (genitive pacis) "peace" (see peace). Meaning "to give what is due for goods or services" arose in Medieval Latin and was attested in English by early 13c.; sense of "please, pacify" died out in English by 1500. Sense of "suffer, endure" (a punishment, etc.) is first recorded late 14c. Related: Paid; paying.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "to appease, pacify, satisfy," 源自 古法语 paier "to pay, pay up" (12 世纪, 现代法语 payer), 源自 拉丁语 pacare "to please, pacify, satisfy" (in 中古拉丁语 尤指 "satisfy a creditor"), 字面义为 "make peaceful," 源自 pax (属格 pacis) "peace" （参见 peace). 义为 "to give what is due for goods or services" arose in 中古拉丁语 and was 见于 English by 13 世纪初; 语义 "please, pacify" died out in English 截至 1500 年. 义为 "suffer, endure" (a punishment, etc.) is 首见于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Paid; paying.

example.en: You should pay more attention to the safety instructions before the experiment.
example.zh: 在实验之前你应该多留意安全须知。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French paiement (13c.), from paiier (see pay (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 paiement (13 世纪), 源自 paiier （参见 pay （动）).

example.en: The final payment for the house is due next month.
example.zh: 购房的最后一笔款项下个月到期。

entries.etymology:
early or mid-17c., false singular from Middle English pease (plural pesen), which was both single and collective (as with wheat, corn) but the "s" sound was mistaken for the plural inflection. From Old English pise (West Saxon), piose (Mercian) "pea," from Late Latin pisa, variant of Latin pisum "pea," from Greek pison "the pea," perhaps of Thracian or Phrygian origin [Klein].

In Southern U.S. and the Caribbean, used of other legumes as well. Pea soup is first recorded 1711 (pease-soup); applied to London fogs since at least 1849. Pea-shooter attested from 1803.
entries.etymologyZh: early or 17 世纪中期, false singular 源自 中古英语 pease (plural pesen), which was both single and collective (as with wheat, corn) but the "s" sound was mistaken for the plural inflection. From 古英语 pise (West Saxon), piose (Mercian) "pea," 源自 晚期拉丁语 pisa, 为 … 的变体 拉丁语 pisum "pea," 源自 希腊语 pison "the pea," 或许 of Thracian or Phrygian origin [Klein]. In Southern U.S. and the Caribbean, used of other legumes as well. Pea soup is 首见于 1711 年 (pease-soup); applied to London fogs 自 at least 1849 年. Pea-shooter attested 自 1803 年起.

entries.etymology: early 14c., "inclined to peace, friendly, pacific," from peace + -ful. Meaning "tranquil, calm, full of peace" is from mid-14c. In reference to nonviolent methods of effecting social change, it is attested from 1876. Related: Peacefully; peacefulness. Peaceful coexistence (1920) originally was in regard to Soviet policy toward the capitalist West.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "inclined to peace, friendly, pacific," 源自 peace + -ful. 义为 "tranquil, calm, full of peace" 始于 14 世纪中期 In reference to nonviolent methods of effecting social change, it 见于 1876 年. 同源词：Peacefully; peacefulness. Peaceful coexistence (1920 年) 原义为 was in regard to Soviet policy toward the capitalist West.

example.en: The village was peaceful at dawn, with no one on the streets.
example.zh: 黎明时分，村子里一片平静，街上没有人。

entries.etymology:
c. 1400 (late 12c. as a surname), from Old French pesche "peach, peach tree" (Old North French peske, Modern French pêche), and directly from Medieval Latin pesca, from Late Latin pessica, variant of persica "peach, peach tree," from Latin malum Persicum, literally "Persian apple," translating Greek Persikon malon, from Persis "Persia" (see Persian).

In ancient Greek Persikos could mean "Persian" or "the peach." The tree is native to China, but reached Europe via Persia. By 1663 William Penn observed peaches in cultivation on American plantations. Meaning "attractive woman" is attested from 1754; that of "good person" is from 1904. Peaches and cream in reference to a type of complexion is from 1901. Peach blossom as a color is from 1702. Georgia has been the Peach State since 1939.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年 (12 世纪晚期 作为 surname), 源自 古法语 pesche "peach, peach tree" (Old North 法语 peske, 现代法语 pêche), and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 pesca, 源自 晚期拉丁语 pessica, 为 … 的变体 persica "peach, peach tree," 源自 拉丁语 malum Persicum, 字面义为 "Persian apple," translating 希腊语 Persikon malon, 源自 Persis "Persia" （参见 波斯语). In ancient 希腊语 Persikos could mean "Persian" or "the peach." The tree is 本族 to China, but reached Europe 经由 Persia. By 1663 年 William Penn observed peaches in cultivation on American plantations. 义为 "attractive woman" 见于 1754 年; that of "good person" 始于 1904 年. Peaches and cream in reference to a type of complexion 始于 1901 年. Peach blossom 作为 color 始于 1702 年. Georgia has been the Peach State 自 1939 年.

definitionLines: n. 峰，山峰；尖端，突出物
entries.definition: n. 峰，山峰；尖端，突出物
entries.etymology: "pointed top," 1520s, variant of pike (n.4) "sharp point." Meaning "top of a mountain" first recorded 1630s, though pike was used in this sense c. 1400. Figurative sense is 1784. Meaning "point formed by hair on the forehead" is from 1833. According to OED, The Peak in Derbyshire is older than the word for "mountaintop;" compare Old English Peaclond, for the district, Pecsaetan, for the people who settled there, Peaces ærs for Peak Cavern; sometimes said to be a reference to an elf-denizen Peac "Puck."
entries.etymologyZh: "pointed top," 1520 年代, 为 … 的变体 pike (n.4) "sharp point." 义为 "top of a mountain" 首见于 1630 年代, though pike was used in this sense 约 1400 年. Figurative sense is 1784 年. 义为 "point formed by hair on the forehead" 始于 1833 年. According to OED, The Peak in Derbyshire is older than the word for "mountaintop;" 对比 古英语 Peaclond, for the district, Pecsaetan, for the people who settled there, Peaces ærs for Peak Cavern; 有时 said to be a reference to an elf-denizen Peac "Puck."

example.en: Conditions on the peak of Everest can be life-threatening even in summer.
example.zh: 即使在夏天，珠峰顶部的条件也可能危及生命。

entries.etymology: 1807; see pea + nut. Earlier ground nut, ground pea (1769). The plant is native to South America; Portuguese traders took peanuts from Brazil and Peru to Africa by 1502 and it is known to have been cultivated in Chekiang Province in China by 1573, probably arriving with Portuguese sailors who made stops in Brazil en route to the Orient. Peanut butter attested by 1892; peanut brittle is from 1894. Peanut gallery "topmost rows of a theater" is from 1874, American English; peanuts "trivial sum" is from 1934.
entries.etymologyZh: 1807 年; 参见 pea + nut. Earlier ground nut, ground pea (1769 年). The plant is 本族 to South America; 葡萄牙语 traders took peanuts 源自 Brazil and Peru to Africa 截至 1502 年 and it is known to have been cultivated in Chekiang Province in China 截至 1573 年, 可能 arriving with 葡萄牙语 sailors who made stops in Brazil en route to the Orient. Peanut butter attested 截至 1892 年; peanut brittle 始于 1894 年. Peanut gallery "topmost rows of a theater" 始于 1874 年, American English; peanuts "trivial sum" 始于 1934 年.

entries.etymology: Old English pere, peru "pear," common West Germanic (Middle Dutch, Middle Low German pere, Old High German pira, bira, Dutch peer), from Vulgar Latin *pera, variant of Latin pira, plural (taken for fem. singular) of pirum "pear," a loan word from an unknown source. It likely shares an origin with Greek apion "pear," apios "pear tree."
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 pere, peru "pear," common West 日耳曼语 (Middle 荷兰语, Middle Low 德语 pere, 古高地德语 pira, bira, 荷兰语 peer), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *pera, 为 … 的变体 拉丁语 pira, plural (taken for fem. singular) of pirum "pear," a loan word 源自 an unknown source. It likely shares an origin with 希腊语 apion "pear," apios "pear tree."

entries.etymology:
mid-13c., from Old French perle (13c.) and directly from Medieval Latin perla (mid-13c.), of unknown origin. Perhaps from Vulgar Latin *pernula, diminutive of Latin perna, which in Sicily meant "pearl," earlier "sea-mussel," literally "ham, haunch, gammon," so called for the shape of the mollusk shells.

Other theories connect it with the root of pear, also somehow based on shape, or Latin pilula "globule," with dissimilation. The usual Latin word for "pearl" was margarita (see margarite).

For pearls before swine, see swine. Pearl Harbor translates Hawaiian Wai Momi, literally "pearl waters," so named for the pearl oysters found there; transferred sense of "effective sudden attack" is attested from 1942 (in reference to Dec. 7, 1941).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 perle (13 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 perla (13 世纪中期), 来源不详. Perhaps 源自 通俗拉丁语 *pernula, 为 … 的指小形式 拉丁语 perna, which in Sicily meant "pearl," earlier "sea-mussel," 字面义为 "ham, haunch, gammon," so called for the shape of the mollusk shells. Other theories connect it with the root of pear, also somehow based on shape，或拉丁语 pilula "globule," with dissimilation. The usual 拉丁语 word for "pearl" was margarita （参见 margarite). For pearls before swine, 参见 swine. Pearl Harbor translates Hawaiian Wai Momi, 字面义为 "pearl waters," so named for the pearl oysters found there; transferred 语义 "effective sudden attack" 见于 1942 年 (in reference to Dec. 7, 1941 年).

entries.etymology:
early 15c., from Anglo-French paisant (mid-14c.), Old French paisent "local inhabitant" (12c., Modern French paysan), earlier paisenc, from pais "country, region" + Frankish suffix -enc "-ing."

Pais is from Late Latin pagensis "(inhabitant) of the district," from Latin pagus "country or rural district" (see pagan). As a style of garment in fashion (such as peasant blouse) from 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 paisant (14 世纪中期), 古法语 paisent "local inhabitant" (12 世纪, 现代法语 paysan), earlier paisenc, 源自 pais "country, region" + Frankish suffix -enc "-ing." Pais 始于 晚期拉丁语 pagensis "(inhabitant) of the district," 源自 拉丁语 pagus "country or rural district" （参见 pagan). 作为 style of garment in fashion (such as peasant blouse) 自 1953 年起.

example.en: The peasant worked long hours in the field under the blazing sun.
example.zh: 农民在烈日下在田间辛苦劳作了很长时间。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "belonging exclusively to one person," from Latin peculiaris "of one's own (property)," from peculium "private property," literally "property in cattle" (in ancient times the most important form of property), from pecu "cattle, flock," related to pecus "cattle" (see pecuniary). Meaning "unusual" is first attested c. 1600 (earlier "distinguished, special," 1580s; for sense development, compare idiom). Related: Peculiarly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "belonging exclusively to one person," 源自 拉丁语 peculiaris "of one's own (property)," 源自 peculium "private property," 字面义为 "property in cattle" (in ancient times the most important form of property), 源自 pecu "cattle, flock," related to pecus "cattle" （参见 pecuniary). 义为 "unusual" is 最早见于 约 1600 年 (earlier "distinguished, special," 1580 年代; for sense development, 对比 idiom). 同源词：Peculiarly.

example.en: There was something peculiar about the way the old man stared at the wall without blinking.
example.zh: 那个老人一动不动地盯着墙的样子有些古怪。

entries.etymology:
1610s, "lever (on an organ) worked by foot," from French pédale "feet, trick with the feet," from Italian pedale "treadle, pedal," from Late Latin pedale "(thing) of the foot," neuter of Latin pedalis "of the foot," from pes (genitive pedis) "foot," from PIE root *ped- (1) "a foot" (see foot (n.)).

Extended to various mechanical contrivances by 1789. Pedal steel guitar is from 1969. Pedal-pushers "type of women's trousers suitable for bicycling" is from 1944.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "lever (on an organ) worked by foot," 源自 法语 pédale "feet, trick with the feet," 源自 意大利语 pedale "treadle, pedal," 源自 晚期拉丁语 pedale "(thing) of the foot," neuter of 拉丁语 pedalis "of the foot," 源自 pes (属格 pedis) "foot," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ped- (1) "a foot" （参见 foot （名）). Extended to various mechanical contrivances 截至 1789 年. Pedal steel guitar 始于 1969 年. Pedal-pushers "type of women's trousers suitable for bicycling" 始于 1944 年.

entries.etymology: 1716, "prosaic, dull" (of writing), from Latin pedester (genitive pedestris) "plain, not versified, prosaic," literally "on foot" (sense contrasted with equester "on horseback"), from pedes "one who goes on foot," from pes (genitive pedis) "foot," from PIE root *ped- (1) "a foot" (see foot (n.)). Meaning "going on foot" is first attested 1791 in English (it also was a sense of Latin pedester). The earlier adjective in English was pedestrial (1610s).
entries.etymologyZh: 1716 年, "prosaic, dull" (of writing), 源自 拉丁语 pedester (属格 pedestris) "plain, not versified, prosaic," 字面义为 "on foot" (sense contrasted with equester "on horseback"), 源自 pedes "one who goes on foot," 源自 pes (属格 pedis) "foot," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ped- (1) "a foot" （参见 foot （名）). 义为 "going on foot" is 最早见于 1791 年 in English (it also was a 语义 拉丁语 pedester). The earlier 形容词 in English was pedestrial (1610 年代).

entries.etymology: "to strip off," developed from Old English pilian "to peel, skin, decorticate, strip the skin or ring," and Old French pillier, both from Latin pilare "to strip of hair," from pilus "hair" (see pile (n.3)). Probably also influenced by Latin pellis "skin, hide." Related: Peeled; peeling. Figurative expression keep (one's) eyes peeled be observant, be on the alert" is from 1853, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: "to strip off," developed 源自 古英语 pilian "to peel, skin, decorticate, strip the skin or ring," and 古法语 pillier, both 源自 拉丁语 pilare "to strip of hair," 源自 pilus "hair" （参见 pile (n.3)). Probably also influenced by 拉丁语 pellis "skin, hide." 同源词：Peeled; peeling. Figurative expression keep (one's) eyes peeled be observant, be on the alert" 始于 1853 年, American English.

example.en: Please peel the potatoes before boiling them.
example.zh: 煮土豆之前请先削皮。

entries.definition: n. 同等的人，贵族 vi. 凝视，窥视
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "an equal in rank or status" (early 13c. in Anglo-Latin), from Anglo-French peir, Old French per (10c.), from Latin par "equal" (see par (n.)). Sense of "a noble" (late 14c.) is from Charlemagne's Twelve Peers in the old romances, who, like the Arthurian knights of the Round Table, originally were so called because all were equal. Sociological sense of "one of the same age group or social set" is from 1944. Peer review attested by 1970. Peer pressure is first recorded 1971.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "an equal in rank or status" (13 世纪初 in Anglo-拉丁语), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 peir, 古法语 per (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 par "equal" （参见 par （名）). 义为 "a noble" (14 世纪晚期) 始于 Charlemagne's Twelve Peers in the old romances, who, like the Arthurian knights of the Round Table, 原义为 were so called because all were equal. Sociological 语义 "one of the same age group or social set" 始于 1944 年. Peer review attested 截至 1970 年. Peer pressure is 首见于 1971 年.

example.en: Teenagers often care deeply about the opinions of their peer.
example.zh: 青少年往往非常在意同龄人的看法。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French penalité and directly from Medieval Latin poenalitatem (nominative poenalitas), from Latin poenalis (see penal). The sporting sense is first recorded 1885. Ice hockey penalty box attested by 1931.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 penalité and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 poenalitatem (主格 poenalitas), 源自 拉丁语 poenalis （参见 penal). The sporting sense is 首见于 1885 年. Ice hockey penalty box attested 截至 1931 年.

example.en: The court imposed a heavy penalty on the company for polluting the river.
example.zh: 法院就该公司污染河流一事对其处以重罚。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "an artist's fine brush of camel hair," from Old French pincel "artist's paintbrush" (13c., Modern French pinceau), from Latin penicillus "painter's brush, hair-pencil," literally "little tail," diminutive of peniculus "brush," itself a diminutive of penis "tail" (see penis). Small brushes formerly were used for writing before modern lead or chalk pencils; meaning "graphite writing implement" apparently evolved late 16c. Derogatory slang pencil-pusher "office worker" is from 1881; pencil neck "weak person" first recorded 1973.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "an artist's fine brush of camel hair," 源自 古法语 pincel "artist's paintbrush" (13 世纪, 现代法语 pinceau), 源自 拉丁语 penicillus "painter's brush, hair-pencil," 字面义为 "little tail," 为 … 的指小形式 peniculus "brush," itself a 为 … 的指小形式 penis "tail" （参见 penis). Small brushes formerly were used for writing before modern lead or chalk pencils; 意为 "graphite writing implement" 似乎 evolved 16 世纪晚期 Derogatory 俚语 pencil-pusher "office worker" 始于 1881 年; pencil neck "weak person" 首见于 1973 年.

example.en: She sketched the outline of the building with a pencil.
example.zh: 她用铅笔勾勒出建筑的轮廓。

entries.etymology: 1660, from Modern Latin pendulum (1643), noun use of neuter of Latin adjective pendulus "hanging down," from pendere "to hang" (see pendant). The Modern Latin word is perhaps a Latinization of Italian pendolo.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年, 源自 现代 拉丁语 pendulum (1643 年), 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of 拉丁语 形容词 pendulus "hanging down," 源自 pendere "to hang" （参见 pendant). The 现代 拉丁语 word is 或许 a Latinization of 意大利语 pendolo.

entries.etymology: 1520s, from Latin penetratus, past participle of penetrare "to put or get into, enter into," related to penitus "within, inmost," penus "innermost part of a temple, store of food," penates "household gods." Related: Penetrated; penetrating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 拉丁语 penetratus, 为 … 的过去分词 penetrare "to put or get into, enter into," related to penitus "within, inmost," penus "innermost part of a temple, store of food," penates "household gods." 同源词：Penetrated; penetrating.

example.en: The cold wind seemed to penetrate every layer of her clothing.
example.zh: 寒风似乎穿透了她衣服的每一层。

entries.etymology: 1570s, originally used of the great auk of Newfoundland (now extinct), shift in meaning to the Antarctic bird (which looks something like it, found by Drake in Magellan's Straits in 1578) is from 1580s. Of unknown origin, though often asserted to be from Welsh pen "head" (see pen-) + gwyn "white" (see Gwendolyn), but Barnhart says the proposed formation is not proper Welsh. The great auk had a large white patch between its bill and eye. The French and Breton versions of the word ultimately are from English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 原义为 used of the great auk of Newfoundland (现在 extinct), shift in 意为 to the Antarctic bird (which looks something like it, found by Drake in Magellan's Straits 于 1578 年) 始于 1580 年代. Of unknown origin, though 常 asserted to be 源自 Welsh pen "head" （参见 pen-) + gwyn "white" （参见 Gwendolyn), but Barnhart says the proposed formation is not proper Welsh. The great auk had a large white patch between its bill and eye. The 法语 and Breton versions of the word ultimately 始于 English.

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Latin pæninsula "a peninsula," literally "almost an island," from pæne "almost" + insula "island" (see isle). Earlier translated as demie island.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 拉丁语 pæninsula "a peninsula," 字面义为 "almost an island," 源自 pæne "almost" + insula "island" （参见 isle). Earlier translated as demie island.

entries.etymology:
Old English pening, penig, Northumbrian penning "penny," from Proto-Germanic *panninggaz (source also of Old Norse penningr, Swedish pänning, Danish penge, Old Frisian panning, Old Saxon pending, Middle Dutch pennic, Dutch penning, Old High German pfenning, German Pfennig, not recorded in Gothic, where skatts is used instead), of unknown origin.

The English coin was originally set at one-twelfth of a shilling and was of silver, later copper, then bronze. There are two plural forms: pennies of individual coins, pence collectively. In translations it rendered various foreign coins of small denomination, especially Latin denarius, whence comes its abbreviation d.

As American English colloquial for cent, it is recorded from 1889. Penny-a-liner "writer for a journal or newspaper" is attested from 1834. Penny dreadful "cheap and gory fiction" dates from c. 1870. Phrase penny-wise and pound-foolish is recorded from c. 1600. Penny-pincher "miserly person" is recorded from 1906 (as an adjective penny-pinching is recorded from 1858, American English). Penny loafers attested from 1960.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 pening, penig, Northumbrian penning "penny," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *panninggaz (source also of 古北欧语 penningr, Swedish pänning, Danish penge, 古弗里西语 panning, 古撒克逊语 pending, Middle 荷兰语 pennic, 荷兰语 penning, 古高地德语 pfenning, 德语 Pfennig, not recorded in Gothic, where skatts is used instead), 来源不详. The English coin was 原义为 set at one-twelfth of a shilling and was of silver, later copper, 之后 bronze. There are two plural forms: pennies of individual coins, pence collectively. In translations it rendered various foreign coins of small denomination, 尤指 拉丁语 denarius, whence comes its abbreviation d. As American English 口语 for cent, it 见于 1889 年. Penny-a-liner "writer for a journal or newspaper" 见于 1834 年. Penny dreadful "cheap and gory fiction" dates 源自 约 1870 年. Phrase penny-wise and pound-foolish 见于 约 1600 年. Penny-pincher "miserly person" 见于 1906 年 (作形容词时 penny-pinching 见于 1858 年, American English). Penny loafers attested 自 1960 年起.

definitionLines: n. 抚恤金，养老金，年金
entries.definition: n. 抚恤金，养老金，年金
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "payment for services," especially "reward, payment out of a benefice" (early 14c., in Anglo-Latin), from Old French pension "payment, rent" (13c.) and directly from Latin pensionem (nominative pensio) "a payment, installment, rent," from past participle stem of pendere "pay, weigh" (see pendant). Meaning "regular payment in consideration of past service" first recorded 1520s. Meaning "boarding house, boarding school" first attested 1640s, from French, and usually in reference to places in France or elsewhere on the Continent.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "payment for services," 尤指 "reward, payment out of a benefice" (14 世纪初, in Anglo-拉丁语), 源自 古法语 pension "payment, rent" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 pensionem (主格 pensio) "a payment, installment, rent," 源自 past participle stem of pendere "pay, weigh" （参见 pendant). 义为 "regular payment in consideration of past service" 首见于 1520 年代. 义为 "boarding house, boarding school" 最早见于 1640 年代, 源自 法语, and 通常 in reference to places in France or elsewhere on the Continent.

example.en: After 30 years of service, she receives a generous monthly pension.
example.zh: 服务30年后，她每月领取一笔丰厚的养老金。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., "humans, persons in general," from Anglo-French people, Old French peupel "people, population, crowd; mankind, humanity," from Latin populus "a people, nation; body of citizens; a multitude, crowd, throng," of unknown origin, possibly from Etruscan. The Latin word also is the source of Spanish pueblo, Italian popolo. In English, it displaced native folk. 

Meaning "body of persons comprising a community" first recorded late 13c. in Anglo-French; meaning "common people, masses" (as distinguished from the nobility) first recorded c. 1300 in Anglo-French. Meaning "one's own tribe, group, etc." is from late 14c. The word was adopted after c. 1920 by Communist totalitarian states to give a spurious sense of populism to their governments. Legal phrase The People vs., in U.S. cases of prosecution under certain laws, dates from 1801. People of the Book "those whose religion entails adherence to a book of divine revelation (1834) translates Arabic Ahl al-Kitab.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "humans, persons in general," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 people, 古法语 peupel "people, population, crowd; mankind, humanity," 源自 拉丁语 populus "a people, nation; body of citizens; a multitude, crowd, throng," 来源不详, possibly 源自 Etruscan. The 拉丁语 word also is the source of 西班牙语 pueblo, 意大利语 popolo. In English, it displaced 本族 folk. 义为 "body of persons comprising a community" 首见于 13 世纪晚期 in 盎格鲁-法语; 意为 "common people, masses" (as distinguished 源自 nobility) 首见于 约 1300 年 in 盎格鲁-法语. 义为 "one's own tribe, group, etc." 始于 14 世纪晚期 The word was adopted after 约 1920 年 by Communist totalitarian states to give a spurious 语义 populism to their governments. Legal phrase The People vs., in U.S. cases of prosecution under certain laws, dates 自 1801 年起. People of the Book "those whose religion entails adherence to a book of divine revelation (1834 年) translates 阿拉伯语 Ahl al-Kitab.

example.en: Many people gathered in the square to watch the fireworks display.
example.zh: 许多人聚集在广场上观看烟火表演。

entries.etymology: Old English pipor, from an early West Germanic borrowing of Latin piper "pepper," from Greek piperi, probably (via Persian) from Middle Indic pippari, from Sanskrit pippali "long pepper." The Latin word is the source of German Pfeffer, Italian pepe, French poivre, Old Church Slavonic pipru, Lithuanian pipiras, Old Irish piobhar, Welsh pybyr, etc. Application to fruits of the capsicum family (unrelated, originally native of tropical America) is 16c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 pipor, 源自 an early West 日耳曼语 borrowing of 拉丁语 piper "pepper," 源自 希腊语 piperi, 可能 (经由 波斯语) 源自 Middle Indic pippari, 源自 梵语 pippali "long pepper." The 拉丁语 word is the source of 德语 Pfeffer, 意大利语 pepe, 法语 poivre, Old Church Slavonic pipru, Lithuanian pipiras, Old 爱尔兰语 piobhar, Welsh pybyr, etc. Application to fruits of the capsicum family (unrelated, 原义为 本族 of tropical America) is 16 世纪

example.en: She added a pinch of pepper to give the bland soup a spicy kick.
example.zh: 她加了一小撮胡椒粉，给这道淡而无味的汤增添了辛辣感。

entries.etymology: 1580s (earlier in various Latin and French phrases), from Latin per "through, during, by means of, on account of, as in," from PIE root *per- (1) "Base of prepositions and preverbs with the basic meanings of 'forward,' 'through,' and a wide range of extended senses such as 'in front of,' 'before,' 'early,' 'first,' 'chief,' 'toward,' 'against,' 'near,' 'at,' 'around'" [Watkins]. Cognates: Sanskrit pari- "around, about, through," pura "before, formerly;" Avestan pairi- "around," paro "before;" Old Persian pariy; Hittite para- "on, forth;" Greek peri "around, about, near, beyond," paros "before," para "from beside, beyond," pro "before;" Latin pro "before, for, on behalf of, instead of," porro "forward," prae "before;" Old English fore (prep.) "before, in front of;" (adv.) "before, previously;" German vor "for;" Old Church Slavonic pra-dedu "great-grandfather;" Russian pere- "through;" Lithuanian per "through;" Old Irish air- Gothic fair-, German ver-, Old English fer-, intensive prefixes.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代 (earlier in various 拉丁语 and 法语 phrases), 源自 拉丁语 per "through, during, by means of, on account of, as in," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *per- (1) "Base of prepositions and preverbs with the basic meanings of 'forward,' 'through,' and a wide range of extended senses such as 'in front of,' 'before,' 'early,' 'first,' 'chief,' 'toward,' 'against,' 'near,' 'at,' 'around'" [Watkins]. Cognates: 梵语 pari- "around, about, through," pura "before, formerly;" Avestan pairi- "around," paro "before;" Old 波斯语 pariy; Hittite para- "on, forth;" 希腊语 peri "around, about, near, beyond," paros "before," para "from beside, beyond," pro "before;" 拉丁语 pro "before, for, on behalf of, instead of," porro "forward," prae "before;" 古英语 fore （介） "before, in front of;" （副） "before, previously;" 德语 vor "for;" Old Church Slavonic pra-dedu "great-grandfather;" 俄语 pere- "through;" Lithuanian per "through;" Old 爱尔兰语 air- Gothic fair-, 德语 ver-, 古英语 fer-, intensive prefixes.

definitionLines: vt. 察觉，感知；理解，领悟
entries.definition: vt. 察觉，感知；理解，领悟
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, via Anglo-French parceif, Old North French *perceivre (Old French perçoivre) "perceive, notice, see; recognize, understand," from Latin percipere "obtain, gather, seize entirely, take possession of," also, figuratively, "to grasp with the mind, learn, comprehend," literally "to take entirely," from per "thoroughly" (see per) + capere "to grasp, take" (see capable).

Replaced Old English ongietan. Both the Latin senses were in Old French, though the primary sense of Modern French percevoir is literal, "to receive, collect" (rents, taxes, etc.), while English uses the word almost always in the metaphorical sense. Related: Perceived; perceiving.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 经由 盎格鲁-法语 parceif, Old North 法语 *perceivre (古法语 perçoivre) "perceive, notice, see; recognize, understand," 源自 拉丁语 percipere "obtain, gather, seize entirely, take possession of," also, figuratively, "to grasp with the mind, learn, comprehend," 字面义为 "to take entirely," 源自 per "thoroughly" （参见 per) + capere "to grasp, take" （参见 capable). Replaced 古英语 ongietan. Both the 拉丁语 senses were in 古法语, though the primary 语义 现代法语 percevoir is literal, "to receive, collect" (rents, taxes, etc.), while English uses the word almost always in the metaphorical sense. 同源词：Perceived; perceiving.

example.en: Children often perceive sounds and colors more vividly than adults do.
example.zh: 孩子们往往比成人更生动地感知声音和颜色。

entries.etymology: 1560s, per cent, from Modern Latin per centum "by the hundred" (see per and see hundred). Until early 20c. often treated as an abbreviation and punctuated accordingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, per cent, 源自 现代 拉丁语 per centum "by the hundred" （参见 per and 参见 hundred). Until 20 世纪初 常 treated 作为 abbreviation and punctuated accordingly.

entries.etymology: 1789, from percent + -age. Sense of "profit, advantage" is from 1862.
entries.etymologyZh: 1789 年, 源自 percent + -age. 义为 "profit, advantage" 始于 1862 年.

example.en: A large percentage of students said they preferred studying in the library.
example.zh: 很大比例的学生表示更喜欢在图书馆学习。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "receiving, collection," from Latin perceptionem (nominative perceptio) "perception, apprehension, a taking," from percipere "perceive" (see perceive). First used in the more literal sense of the Latin word; in secondary sense, "the taking cognizance of," it is recorded in English from 1610s. Meaning "intuitive or direct recognition of some innate quality" is from 1827.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "receiving, collection," 源自 拉丁语 perceptionem (主格 perceptio) "perception, apprehension, a taking," 源自 percipere "perceive" （参见 perceive). First used in the more literal 语义 the 拉丁语 word; in secondary sense, "the taking cognizance of," it is recorded in English 源自 1610 年代. 义为 "intuitive or direct recognition of some innate quality" 始于 1827 年.

example.en: Public perception of the company changed dramatically after the financial scandal.
example.zh: 财务丑闻曝光后，公众对该公司的认知发生了巨大改变。

definitionLines: a. 完善的，完美的；完全的， 十足的
entries.definition: a. 完善的，完美的；完全的， 十足的 vt. 使完美，改进
entries.etymology: early 15c. alteration of Middle English parfit (c. 1300), from Old French parfit "finished, completed, ready" (11c.), from Latin perfectus "completed, excellent, accomplished, exquisite," past participle of perficere "accomplish, finish, complete," from per- "completely" (see per) + facere "to make, do, perform" (see factitious). Often used in English as an intensive (perfect stranger, etc.). Grammatical sense, in reference to verb tense, is from c. 1500. As a noun, late 14c. ("perfection"), from the adjective.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 alteration of 中古英语 parfit (约 1300 年), 源自 古法语 parfit "finished, completed, ready" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 perfectus "completed, excellent, accomplished, exquisite," 为 … 的过去分词 perficere "accomplish, finish, complete," 源自 per- "completely" （参见 per) + facere "to make, do, perform" （参见 factitious). Often used in English 作为 intensive (perfect stranger, etc.). Grammatical sense, in reference to 动词 tense, 始于 约 1500 年. 作名词时, 14 世纪晚期 ("perfection"), 源自 形容词.

definitionLines: n. 完全，完美；完成，改善
entries.definition: n. 完全，完美；完成，改善
entries.etymology: early 13c., from Old French perfection "perfection, completeness" (12c.), from Latin perfectionem (nominative perfectio) "a finishing, compling, perfection," noun of action from past participle stem of perficere (see perfect (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 perfection "perfection, completeness" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 perfectionem (主格 perfectio) "a finishing, compling, perfection," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of perficere （参见 perfect （形）).

example.en: She practiced the piano daily in pursuit of perfection.
example.zh: 她每天练习钢琴，追求完美。

definitionLines: v. 做，施行，完成；表演，演出
entries.definition: v. 做，施行，完成；表演，演出
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "carry into effect, fulfill, discharge," via Anglo-French performer, altered (by influence of Old French forme "form") from Old French parfornir "to do, carry out, finish, accomplish," from par- "completely" (see per-) + fornir "to provide" (see furnish).

Theatrical/musical sense is from c. 1600. The verb was used with wider senses in Middle English than now, including "to make, construct; produce, bring about;" also "come true" (of dreams), and to performen muche time was "to live long." Related: Performed; performing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "carry into effect, fulfill, discharge," 经由 盎格鲁-法语 performer, altered (by influence of 古法语 forme "form") 源自 古法语 parfornir "to do, carry out, finish, accomplish," 源自 par- "completely" （参见 per-) + fornir "to provide" （参见 furnish). Theatrical/musical sense 始于 约 1600 年. The 动词 was used with wider senses in 中古英语 than 现在, including "to make, construct; produce, bring about;" also "come true" (of dreams), and to performen muche time was "to live long." 同源词：Performed; performing.

example.en: The pianist was invited to perform at the Royal Concert Hall next month.
example.zh: 这位钢琴家受邀下个月在皇家音乐厅演出。

definitionLines: n. 表演，演出；执行，完成；工作 情况，表现情况
entries.definition: n. 表演，演出；执行，完成；工作 情况，表现情况
entries.etymology: late a5c., "accomplishment" (of something), from perform + -ance. Meaning "a thing performed" is from 1590s; that of "action of performing a play, etc." is from 1610s; that of "a public entertainment" is from 1709. Performance art is attested from 1971.
entries.etymologyZh: late a5c., "accomplishment" (of something), 源自 perform + -ance. 义为 "a thing performed" 始于 1590 年代; that of "action of performing a play, etc." 始于 1610 年代; that of "a public entertainment" 始于 1709 年. Performance art 见于 1971 年.

example.en: The audience gave a standing ovation after the opening night performance.
example.zh: 首演夜的演出结束后，观众起立鼓掌喝彩。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "fumes from a burning substance," from Middle French parfum (16c.), from parfumer "to scent," from Old Provençal perfumar or cognate words in dialectal Italian (perfumare) or Spanish (perfumar), from Latin per- "through" (see per) + fumare "to smoke" (see fume (n.)). Meaning "fluid containing agreeable essences of flowers, etc.," is attested from 1540s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "fumes from a burning substance," 源自 中古法语 parfum (16 世纪), 源自 parfumer "to scent," 源自 Old Provençal perfumar or 同源 words in 方言 意大利语 (perfumare) or 西班牙语 (perfumar), 源自 拉丁语 per- "through" （参见 per) + fumare "to smoke" （参见 fume （名）). 义为 "fluid containing agreeable essences of flowers, etc.," 见于 1540 年代.

example.en: She put a little perfume on her wrists for its pleasant fragrance before leaving home.
example.zh: 出门前，她在手腕上抹了一点香水，让自己带着怡人的香气。

definitionLines: n. 期间，一段时间；时期，时代
entries.definition: n. 期间，一段时间；时期，时代
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "course or extent of time," from Middle French periode (14c.) and directly from Medieval Latin periodus "recurring portion, cycle," from Latin periodus "a complete sentence," also "cycle of the Greek games," from Greek periodos "cycle, circuit, period of time," literally "a going around," from peri- "around" (see peri-) + hodos "a going, way, journey" (see cede).

Sense of "repeated cycle of events" led to that of "interval of time." Meaning "dot marking end of a sentence" first recorded c. 1600, from similar use in Medieval Latin (in late 16c. English it meant "full pause at the end of a sentence"). Sense of "menstruation" dates from 1822. Educational sense of "portion of time set apart for a lesson" is from 1876. Sporting sense attested from 1898. As an adjective from 1905; period piece attested from 1911.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "course or extent of time," 源自 中古法语 periode (14 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 periodus "recurring portion, cycle," 源自 拉丁语 periodus "a complete sentence," also "cycle of the Greek games," 源自 希腊语 periodos "cycle, circuit, period of time," 字面义为 "a going around," 源自 peri- "around" （参见 peri-) + hodos "a going, way, journey" （参见 cede). 义为 "repeated cycle of events" led to that of "interval of time." 义为 "dot marking end of a sentence" 首见于 约 1600 年, 源自 similar use in 中古拉丁语 (in 16 世纪晚期 English it meant "full pause at the end of a sentence"). 义为 "menstruation" dates 自 1822 年起. Educational 语义 "portion of time set apart for a lesson" 始于 1876 年. Sporting sense attested 自 1898 年起. 作形容词时 自 1905 年起; period piece attested 自 1911 年起.

example.en: Historians often divide the past into distinct periods such as ancient and modern.
example.zh: 历史学家常将过去划分为不同的时期，如古代和近代。

entries.etymology:
1640s, from French périodique (14c.), from Latin periodicus, from periodus (see period).

Periodic table in chemistry (1889) is from notion of the arrangement, in which similar properties recur at intervals in elements in the same area as you read down the rows of the table. This sense of the word is attested from 1872 (periodic law).
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 法语 périodique (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 periodicus, 源自 periodus （参见 period). Periodic table in chemistry (1889 年) 始于 概念 the arrangement, in which similar properties recur at intervals in elements in the same area as you read down the rows of the table. This 语义 the word 见于 1872 年 (periodic law).

entries.definition: a.周期的，定期的 n. 期刊，杂志
entries.etymology: c. 1600, from periodic + -al (1). As a noun meaning "magazine published at regular intervals," attested from 1798. Related: Periodically.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 periodic + -al (1). 作名词时 意为 "magazine published at regular intervals," attested 自 1798 年起. 同源词：Periodically.

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from periss- present participle stem of Old French perir "perish, be lost, be shipwrecked" (12c.), from Latin perire "to be lost, perish," literally "to go through," from per- "through, completely, to destruction" (see per) + ire "to go" (see ion). Related: Perished; perishing.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 periss- present participle stem of 古法语 perir "perish, be lost, be shipwrecked" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 perire "to be lost, perish," 字面义为 "to go through," 源自 per- "through, completely, to destruction" （参见 per) + ire "to go" （参见 ion). 同源词：Perished; perishing.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French permanent (14c.) or directly from Latin permanentem (nominative permanens) "remaining," present participle of permanere "endure, hold out, continue, stay to the end," from per- "through"  (see per) + manere "stay" (see mansion). As a noun meaning "permanent wave," by 1909. Of clothing, permanent press attested from 1964.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 permanent (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 permanentem (主格 permanens) "remaining," 为 … 的现在分词 permanere "endure, hold out, continue, stay to the end," 源自 per- "through" （参见 per) + manere "stay" （参见 mansion). 作名词时 意为 "permanent wave," 截至 1909 年. Of clothing, permanent press attested 自 1964 年起.

example.en: After three years as a contractor, she finally got a permanent position at the firm.
example.zh: 做了三年合同工后，她终于在公司获得了一个长期职位。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin permissionem (nominative permissio), noun of action from past participle stem of permittere (see permit (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 permissionem (主格 permissio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of permittere （参见 permit （动）).

example.en: You need permission from the manager before leaving early.
example.zh: 你需要经理的许可才能提前离开。

entries.definition: v.允许，许可 n. 执照，许可证
entries.etymology: late 15c., from Middle French permetre and directly from Latin permittere "let pass, let go, let loose; give up, hand over; let, allow, grant, permit," from per- "through" (see per) + mittere "let go, send" (see mission). Related: Permitted; permitting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 中古法语 permetre and 直接源自 拉丁语 permittere "let pass, let go, let loose; give up, hand over; let, allow, grant, permit," 源自 per- "through" （参见 per) + mittere "let go, send" （参见 mission). 同源词：Permitted; permitting.

example.en: According to the regulations, the museum does not permit visitors to touch any of the exhibits.
example.zh: 根据规定，博物馆不允许参观者触摸任何展品。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French perpetuel "without end" (12c.) and directly from Latin perpetualis "universal," in Medieval Latin "permanent," from perpetuus "continuous, universal," from perpetis, genitive of Old Latin perpes "lasting," probably from per- "through" + root of petere "to seek, go to, aim at" (see petition (n.)). Related: Perpetually. Perpetual motion is attested from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 perpetuel "without end" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 perpetualis "universal," in 中古拉丁语 "permanent," 源自 perpetuus "continuous, universal," 源自 perpetis, 属格 of Old 拉丁语 perpes "lasting," 可能 源自 per- "through" + root of petere "to seek, go to, aim at" （参见 petition （名）). 同源词：Perpetually. Perpetual motion 见于 1590 年代.

entries.etymology:
late 14c. as an adjective, "perplexed, puzzled, bewildered," from Latin perplexus "involved, confused, intricate;" but Latin had no corresponding verb *perplectere. The Latin compound would be per "through" (see per) + plexus "entangled," past participle of plectere "to twine, braid, fold" (see complex (adj.)).

The form of the English adjective shifted to perplexed by late 15c., probably to conform to other past participle adjectives. The verb is latest attested of the group, in 1590s, evidently a back-formation from the adjective. Related: Perplexing, which well describes the history of the word.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 作形容词时, "perplexed, puzzled, bewildered," 源自 拉丁语 perplexus "involved, confused, intricate;" but 拉丁语 had no corresponding 动词 *perplectere. The 拉丁语 复合词 would be per "through" （参见 per) + plexus "entangled," 为 … 的过去分词 plectere "to twine, braid, fold" （参见 complex （形）). The form of the English 形容词 shifted to perplexed by 15 世纪晚期, 可能 to conform to other past participle adjectives. The 动词 is latest attested of the group, in 1590 年代, 显然 a back-formation 源自 形容词. 同源词：Perplexing, which well describes the history of the word.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "oppression for the holding of a belief or opinion," from Old French persecucion "persecution, damage, affliction, suffering" (12c.) and directly from Latin persecutionem (nominative persecutio), noun of action from past participle stem of persequi "follow, pursue, hunt down; proceed against, prosecute, start a legal action," from per- "through" (see per) + sequi "follow" (see sequel). Psychological persecution complex is recorded from 1961; earlier persecution mania (1892).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "oppression for the holding of a belief or opinion," 源自 古法语 persecucion "persecution, damage, affliction, suffering" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 persecutionem (主格 persecutio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of persequi "follow, pursue, hunt down; proceed against, prosecute, start a legal action," 源自 per- "through" （参见 per) + sequi "follow" （参见 sequel). Psychological persecution complex 见于 1961 年; earlier persecution mania (1892 年).

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Middle French persister (14c.), from Latin persistere "abide, continue steadfastly," from per- "thoroughly" (see per) + sistere "come to stand, cause to stand still" (see assist (v.)). Related: Persisted; persisting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 中古法语 persister (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 persistere "abide, continue steadfastly," 源自 per- "thoroughly" （参见 per) + sistere "come to stand, cause to stand still" （参见 assist （动）). 同源词：Persisted; persisting.

example.en: Despite repeated failures, she continued to persist with her research.
example.zh: 尽管屡次失败，她仍坚持进行研究。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Old French persone "human being, anyone, person" (12c., Modern French personne) and directly from Latin persona "human being, person, personage; a part in a drama, assumed character," originally "mask, false face," such as those of wood or clay worn by the actors in later Roman theater. OED offers the general 19c. explanation of persona as "related to" Latin personare "to sound through" (i.e. the mask as something spoken through and perhaps amplifying the voice), "but the long o makes a difficulty ...." Klein and Barnhart say it is possibly borrowed from Etruscan phersu "mask." Klein goes on to say this is ultimately of Greek origin and compares Persephone.

Of corporate entities from mid-15c. The use of -person to replace -man in compounds and avoid alleged sexist connotations is first recorded 1971 (in chairperson). In person "by bodily presence" is from 1560s. Person-to-person first recorded 1919, originally of telephone calls.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, 源自 古法语 persone "human being, anyone, person" (12 世纪, 现代法语 personne) and 直接源自 拉丁语 persona "human being, person, personage; a part in a drama, assumed character," 原义为 "mask, false face," such as those of wood or clay worn by the actors in later Roman theater. OED offers the general 19 世纪 explanation of persona as "related to" 拉丁语 personare "to sound through" (i.e. the mask as something spoken through and 或许 amplifying the voice), "but the long o makes a difficulty ...." Klein and Barnhart say it is possibly 借自 Etruscan phersu "mask." Klein goes on to say this is ultimately of 希腊语 origin and compares Persephone. Of corporate entities 源自 15 世纪中期 The use of -person to replace -man in compounds and avoid alleged sexist connotations is 首见于 1971 年 (in chairperson). In person "by bodily presence" 始于 1560 年代. Person-to-person 首见于 1919 年, 原义为 of telephone calls.

definitionLines: a.个人的，私人的；本人的， 亲白的
entries.definition: a.个人的，私人的；本人的， 亲白的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "pertaining to the self," from Old French personal (12c., Modern French personnel), from Late Latin personalis "pertaining to a person," from Latin persona (see person). Meaning "aimed at some particular person" (usually in a hostile manner) first attested 1610s. The noun sense of "newspaper item about private matters" is attested from 1888. As "a classified ad addressed to an individual," it is recorded from 1861. Personal computer is from 1976.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "pertaining to the self," 源自 古法语 personal (12 世纪, 现代法语 personnel), 源自 晚期拉丁语 personalis "pertaining to a person," 源自 拉丁语 persona （参见 person). 义为 "aimed at some particular person" (通常 in a hostile manner) 最早见于 1610 年代. The 名词 语义 "newspaper item about private matters" 见于 1888 年. As "a classified ad addressed to an individual," it 见于 1861 年. Personal computer 始于 1976 年.

example.en: Please keep this matter personal and do not share it with others.
example.zh: 请将此事视为私事，不要与他人分享。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "quality or fact of being a person," from Medieval Latin personalitatem (nominative personalitas), from Late Latin personalis (see personal). Sense of "a distinctive character" is first recorded 1795, from French personnalité.Meaning "person whose character stands out from that of others" is from 1889. Personality cult is attested from 1956.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "quality or fact of being a person," 源自 中古拉丁语 personalitatem (主格 personalitas), 源自 晚期拉丁语 personalis （参见 personal). 义为 "a distinctive character" is 首见于 1795 年, 源自 法语 personnalité.义为 "person whose character stands out from that of others" 始于 1889 年. Personality cult 见于 1956 年.

example.en: Her warm and outgoing personality makes her easy to get along with.
example.zh: 她温暖外向的个性使她很容易相处。

definitionLines: n. 全体人员，全体职工；人事 部门
entries.definition: n. 全体人员，全体职工；人事 部门
entries.etymology: 1837, from French personnel (a contrastive term to matériel), noun use of personnel (adj.) "personal," from Old French personel (see personal).
entries.etymologyZh: 1837 年, 源自 法语 personnel (a contrastive term to matériel), 为 … 的名词用法 personnel （形） "personal," 源自 古法语 personel （参见 personal).

example.en: All personnel are required to attend the mandatory safety training.
example.zh: 所有员工都必须参加强制性安全培训。

entries.etymology: 1510s, from Middle French persuader (14c.), from Latin persuadere "to bring over by talking," (see persuasion). Related: Persuaded; persuading.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, 源自 中古法语 persuader (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 persuadere "to bring over by talking," （参见 persuasion). 同源词：Persuaded; persuading.

example.en: It took hours to persuade him to see a doctor.
example.zh: 花了好几个小时才说服他去看医生。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "action of inducing (someone) to believe (something); argument to persuade, inducement," from Old French persuasion (14c.) and directly from Latin persuasionem (nominative persuasio) "a convincing, persuading," noun of action from past participle stem of persuadere "persuade, convince," from per- "thoroughly, strongly" (see per) + suadere "to urge, persuade," from PIE *swad- "sweet, pleasant" (see sweet (adj.)). Meaning "religious belief, creed" is from 1620s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "action of inducing (someone) to believe (something); argument to persuade, inducement," 源自 古法语 persuasion (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 persuasionem (主格 persuasio) "a convincing, persuading," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of persuadere "persuade, convince," 源自 per- "thoroughly, strongly" （参见 per) + suadere "to urge, persuade," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *swad- "sweet, pleasant" （参见 sweet （形）). 义为 "religious belief, creed" 始于 1620 年代.

definitionLines: a.劝诱的，劝说的；有说服力的
entries.definition: a.劝诱的，劝说的；有说服力的
entries.etymology: 1580s, from Middle French persuasif, from Medieval Latin persuasivus, from Latin persuas-, past participle stem of persuadere "persuade, convince" (see persuasion). Related: Persuasively; persuasiveness. Replaced earlier persuasible in this sense (see persuadable).
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 中古法语 persuasif, 源自 中古拉丁语 persuasivus, 源自 拉丁语 persuas-, past participle stem of persuadere "persuade, convince" （参见 persuasion). 同源词：Persuasively; persuasiveness. Replaced earlier persuasible in this sense （参见 persuadable).

definitionLines: a. 普遍的；到处渗透的
entries.definition: a. 普遍的；到处渗透的
entries.etymology: 1750, from Latin pervas-, past participle stem of pervadere (see pervade) + -ive.
entries.etymologyZh: 1750 年, 源自 拉丁语 pervas-, past participle stem of pervadere （参见 pervade) + -ive.

entries.etymology: 1866, from pessimist + -ic.
entries.etymologyZh: 1866 年, 源自 pessimist + -ic.

entries.etymology: 1550s (in imprecations, "a pest upon ____," etc.), "plague, pestilence," from Middle French peste (1530s), from Latin pestis "deadly contagious disease; a curse, bane," of uncertain origin. Meaning "noxious or troublesome person or thing" first recorded c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代 (in imprecations, "a pest upon ____," etc.), "plague, pestilence," 源自 中古法语 peste (1530 年代), 源自 拉丁语 pestis "deadly contagious disease; a curse, bane," 来源存疑. 义为 "noxious or troublesome person or thing" 首见于 约 1600 年.

entries.definition: n. 爱畜，宠儿 a. 宠爱，表示亲昵的
entries.etymology: 1620s, "treat as a pet," from pet (n.1). Sense of "to stroke" is first found 1818. Slang sense of "kiss and caress" is from 1920 (implied in petting). Related: Petted.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "treat as a pet," 源自 pet (n.1). 义为 "to stroke" is first found 1818 年. Slang 语义 "kiss and caress" 始于 1920 年 (implied in petting). 同源词：Petted.

entries.etymology: early 14c., "a supplication or prayer, especially to a deity," from Old French peticion "request, petition" (12c., Modern French pétition) and directly from Latin petitionem (nominative petitio) "a blow, thrust, attack, aim; a seeking, searching," in law "a claim, suit," noun of action from past participle stem of petere "to make for, go to; attack, assail; seek, strive after; ask for, beg, beseech, request; fetch; derive; demand, require," from PIE root *pet-, also *pete- "to rush; to fly" (source also of Sanskrit pattram "wing, feather, leaf," patara- "flying, fleeting;" Hittite pittar "wing;" Greek piptein "to fall," potamos "rushing water," pteryx "wing;" Old English feðer "feather;" Latin penna "feather, wing;" Old Church Slavonic pero "feather;" Old Welsh eterin "bird"). Meaning "formal written request to a superior (earthly)" is attested from early 15c.
