example.en: He spent an hour trying to polish his old shoes before the interview.
example.zh: 面试前他花了一个小时努力擦亮他的旧皮鞋。

definitionLines: a.有礼貌的，客气的；斯文的， 的有教养的
entries.definition: a.有礼貌的，客气的；斯文的， 的有教养的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "polished, burnished" (mid-13c. as a surname), from Latin politus "refined, elegant, accomplished," literally "polished," past participle of polire "to polish, to make smooth" (see polish (v.)). Used literally at first in English; sense of "elegant, cultured" is first recorded c. 1500, that of "behaving courteously" is 1748 (implied in politely). Related: Politeness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "polished, burnished" (13 世纪中期 作为 surname), 源自 拉丁语 politus "refined, elegant, accomplished," 字面义为 "polished," 为 … 的过去分词 polire "to polish, to make smooth" （参见 polish （动）). Used 字面义为 at first in English; 语义 "elegant, cultured" is 首见于 约 1500 年, that of "behaving courteously" is 1748 年 (implied in politely). 同源词：Politeness.

example.en: It is polite to hold the door open for the person behind you.
example.zh: 为身后的人扶住门是有礼貌的行为。

entries.etymology: 1550s, "pertaining to a polity, civil affairs, or government;" from Latin politicus "of citizens or the state" (see politic (adj.)) + -al (1). Meaning "taking sides in party politics" (usually pejorative) is from 1749. Political prisoner first recorded 1860; political science is from 1779 (first attested in Hume). Political animal translates Greek politikon zoon (Aristotle, "Politics," I.ii.9) "an animal intended to live in a city; a social animal."
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "pertaining to a polity, civil affairs, or government;" 源自 拉丁语 politicus "of citizens or the state" （参见 politic （形）) + -al (1). 义为 "taking sides in party politics" (通常 pejorative) 始于 1749 年. Political prisoner 首见于 1860 年; political science 始于 1779 年 (最早见于 in Hume). Political animal translates 希腊语 politikon zoon (Aristotle, "Politics," I.ii.9) "an animal intended to live in a city; a social animal."

example.en: The candidates debated several political issues, including campaign finance and voting rights.
example.zh: 候选人辩论了几个政治议题，包括竞选资金和投票权。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "person skilled in politics," from politics + -ian. It quickly took on overtones, not typically good ones. Johnson defines it as "A man of artifice; one of deep contrivance."
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "person skilled in politics," 源自 politics + -ian. It quickly took on overtones, not typically good ones. Johnson defines it as "A man of artifice; one of deep contrivance."

example.en: The veteran politician spent decades crafting legislation and navigating party politics.
example.zh: 这位资深政客花了数十年时间起草法案并周旋于党派政治之间。

entries.definition: n. 政治；政见，政纲 pOl！ n. 民意测验；（pL.）大选
entries.etymology: 1520s, "science of government," from politic (adj.), modeled on Aristotle's ta politika "affairs of state," the name of his book on governing and governments, which was in English mid-15c. as "Polettiques." Also see -ics.Meaning "a person's political allegiances or opinions" is from 1769.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "science of government," 源自 politic （形）, modeled on Aristotle's ta politika "affairs of state," the name of his book on governing and governments, which was in English mid-15c. as "Polettiques." Also see -ics.Meaning "a person's political allegiances or opinions" 始于 1769 年.

example.en: Young voters showed little interest in politics at the last election.
example.zh: 年轻选民在上次选举中对政治表现出兴趣不大。

entries.etymology: 1888, from pollute + -ant. Related: Pollutants.
entries.etymologyZh: 1888 年, 源自 pollute + -ant. 同源词：Pollutants.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to defile," a back formation from pollution, or else from Latin pollutus, past participle of polluere "to defile, pollute, contaminate." Related: Polluted; polluting. Meaning "make physically foul" is from 1540s; specific sense "contaminate the environment" emerged from late 19c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to defile," a back formation 源自 pollution，或else 源自 拉丁语 pollutus, 为 … 的过去分词 polluere "to defile, pollute, contaminate." 同源词：Polluted; polluting. 义为 "make physically foul" 始于 1540 年代; specific sense "contaminate the environment" emerged 源自 19 世纪晚期

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "discharge of semen other than during sex," later, "desecration, defilement" (late 14c.), from Late Latin pollutionem (nominative pollutio) "defilement," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin polluere "to soil, defile, contaminate," from por- "before" + -luere "smear," from PIE root *leu- "dirt; make dirty" (source also of Latin lutum "mud, mire, clay," lues "filth;" Greek lyma "filth, dirt, disgrace," lymax "rubbish, refuse;" Old Irish loth "mud, dirt;" Lithuanian lutynas "pool, puddle"). Sense of "contamination of the environment" first recorded c. 1860, but not common until c. 1955.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "discharge of semen other than during sex," later, "desecration, defilement" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 晚期拉丁语 pollutionem (主格 pollutio) "defilement," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 polluere "to soil, defile, contaminate," 源自 por- "before" + -luere "smear," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *leu- "dirt; make dirty" (source also of 拉丁语 lutum "mud, mire, clay," lues "filth;" 希腊语 lyma "filth, dirt, disgrace," lymax "rubbish, refuse;" Old 爱尔兰语 loth "mud, dirt;" Lithuanian lutynas "pool, puddle"). 义为 "contamination of the environment" 首见于 约 1860 年, but not common until 约 1955 年.

example.en: The river's pollution levels were so high that fish could no longer survive.
example.zh: 河流的污染程度已高到鱼类无法存活的地步。

definitionLines: n.工艺学校；理工专科学校
entries.definition: n.工艺学校；理工专科学校 pond 一 n. 池塘
entries.etymology: 1805, "pertaining to instruction in many (technical) subjects," from French École Polytechnique, engineering school founded 1794 (as École des Travaux publics) in Paris; from Greek polytekhnos "skilled in many arts," from polys "many" (see poly-) + tekhne "art" (see techno-). As a noun (short for polytechnic institution) from 1836.
entries.etymologyZh: 1805 年, "pertaining to instruction in many (technical) subjects," 源自 法语 École Polytechnique, engineering school founded 1794 年 (as École des Travaux publics) in Paris; 源自 希腊语 polytekhnos "skilled in many arts," 源自 polys "many" （参见 poly-) + tekhne "art" （参见 techno-). 作名词时 (short for polytechnic institution) 自 1836 年起.

entries.definition: vt. 仔细考虑；衡量 vi. 沉思；考虑
entries.etymology: early 14c., "to estimate the worth of, to appraise," from Old French ponderer "to weigh, poise" (14c., Modern French pondérer) and directly from Latin ponderare "ponder, consider, reflect," literally "to weigh," from pondus (genitive ponderis) "weight" (see pound (n.1)). Meaning "to weigh a matter mentally" is attested from late 14c. Related: Pondered; pondering; ponderation.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to estimate the worth of, to appraise," 源自 古法语 ponderer "to weigh, poise" (14 世纪, 现代法语 pondérer) and 直接源自 拉丁语 ponderare "ponder, consider, reflect," 字面义为 "to weigh," 源自 pondus (属格 ponderis) "weight" （参见 pound (n.1)). 义为 "to weigh a matter mentally" 见于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Pondered; pondering; ponderation.

example.en: He sat quietly by the window and began to ponder his next move.
example.zh: 他静静地坐在窗边，开始思考下一步该怎么做。

example.en: The children splashed around in the shallow pool all afternoon.
example.zh: 孩子们整个下午都在浅水池里嬉水玩耍。

definitionLines: a.穷；可怜的；低劣的，不好的
entries.definition: a.穷；可怜的；低劣的，不好的
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "lacking money or resources, destitute; needy, indigent; small, scanty," from Old French povre "poor, wretched, dispossessed; inadequate; weak, thin" (Modern French pauvre), from Latin pauper "poor, not wealthy," from pre-Latin *pau-paros "producing little; getting little," a compound from the roots of paucus "little" (see paucity) and parare "to produce, bring forth" (see pare).

Replaced Old English earm. Figuratively from early 14c. Meaning "of inferior quality" is from c. 1300. Of inhabited places from c. 1300; of soil, etc., from late 14c. The poor boy sandwich, made of simple but filling ingredients, was invented and named in New Orleans in 1921. To poor mouth "deny one's advantages" is from 1965 (to make a poor mouth "whine" is Scottish dialect from 1822). Slang poor man's ________ "the cheaper alternative to _______," is from 1854.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "lacking money or resources, destitute; needy, indigent; small, scanty," 源自 古法语 povre "poor, wretched, dispossessed; inadequate; weak, thin" (现代法语 pauvre), 源自 拉丁语 pauper "poor, not wealthy," 源自 pre-拉丁语 *pau-paros "producing little; getting little," a 复合词 源自 roots of paucus "little" （参见 paucity) and parare "to produce, bring forth" （参见 pare). Replaced 古英语 earm. Figuratively 源自 14 世纪初 义为 "of inferior quality" 始于 约 1300 年. Of inhabited places 源自 约 1300 年; of soil, etc., 源自 14 世纪晚期 The poor boy sandwich, made of simple but filling ingredients, was invented and named in New Orleans 于 1921 年. To poor mouth "deny one's advantages" 始于 1965 年 (to make a poor mouth "whine" is 苏格兰语 dialect 自 1822 年起). Slang poor man's ________ "the cheaper alternative to _______," 始于 1854 年.

example.en: Many families in the drought-stricken region remain poor despite government aid.
example.zh: 尽管有政府援助，这个受旱灾影响的地区许多家庭仍然贫困。

entries.definition: n.流行音乐 v.突然出现，发生 a.流行的，通俗的
entries.etymology: "having popular appeal," 1926, of individual songs from many genres; 1954 as a noun, as genre of its own; abbreviation of popular; earlier as a shortened form of popular concert (1862), and often in the plural form pops. Pop art first recorded 1957, said to have been in use conversationally among Independent group of artists from late 1954. Pop culture attested from 1959, short for popular culture (attested by 1846).
entries.etymologyZh: "having popular appeal," 1926 年, of individual songs 源自 many genres; 1954 年 作名词时, as genre of its own; abbreviation of popular; earlier 作为 shortened form of popular concert (1862 年), and 常 in the plural form pops. Pop art 首见于 1957 年, said to have been in use conversationally among Independent group of artists 源自 late 1954 年. Pop culture attested 自 1959 年起, short for popular culture (attested 截至 1846 年).

example.en: The band released a new pop album that topped the charts.
example.zh: 这支乐队发布了一张登上排行榜榜首的流行音乐专辑。

entries.etymology: 1819, from pop (v.) + corn (n.1).
entries.etymologyZh: 1819 年, 源自 pop （动） + corn (n.1).

entries.etymology: Old English papa (9c.), from Church Latin papa "bishop, pope" (in classical Latin, "tutor"), from Greek papas "patriarch, bishop," originally "father." Applied to bishops of Asia Minor and taken as a title by the Bishop of Alexandria c.250. In Western Church, applied especially to the Bishop of Rome since the time of Leo the Great (440-461) and claimed exclusively by them from 1073 (usually in English with a capital P-). Popemobile, his car, is from 1979. Papal, papacy, later acquisitions in English, preserve the original vowel.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 papa (9 世纪), 源自 教会拉丁语 papa "bishop, pope" (in classical 拉丁语, "tutor"), 源自 希腊语 papas "patriarch, bishop," 原义为 "father." Applied to bishops of Asia Minor and taken 作为 title by the Bishop of Alexandria 约 250 年. In Western Church, applied 尤指 to the Bishop of Rome 自 the time of Leo the Great (440-461) and claimed exclusively by them 自 1073 年起 (通常 in English with a capital P-). Popemobile, his car, 始于 1979 年. Papal, papacy, later acquisitions in English, preserve the original vowel.

example.en: The pope addressed thousands of faithful pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square.
example.zh: 教皇向聚集在圣彼得广场的数千名虔诚朝圣者发表讲话。

definitionLines: a. 广受欢迎的，有名的；通俗
entries.definition: a. 广受欢迎的，有名的；通俗
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "public," from Middle French populier (Modern French populaire) and directly from Latin popularis "belonging to the people, general, common; devoted to or accepted by the people; democratic," from populus "people" (see people (n.)).

Meaning "suited to ordinary people" is from 1570s in English; hence, of prices, "low, affordable to average persons" (1859). Meaning "well-liked, admired by the people" is attested from c. 1600. Of art, entertainment, etc., "favored by people generally" from 1819 (popular song). Related: Popularly. Popular Front "coalition of Communists, Socialists, and radicals" is from 1936, first in a French context.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "public," 源自 中古法语 populier (现代法语 populaire) and 直接源自 拉丁语 popularis "belonging to the people, general, common; devoted to or accepted by the people; democratic," 源自 populus "people" （参见 people （名）). 义为 "suited to ordinary people" 始于 1570 年代 in English; hence, of prices, "low, affordable to average persons" (1859 年). 义为 "well-liked, admired by the people" 见于 约 1600 年. Of art, entertainment, etc., "favored by people generally" 自 1819 年起 (popular song). 同源词：Popularly. Popular Front "coalition of Communists, Socialists, and radicals" 始于 1936 年, first in a 法语 context.

example.en: Jazz became popular worldwide during the 1920s and 1930s.
example.zh: 爵士乐在20世纪20至30年代风靡全球。

entries.etymology: "fact or condition of being beloved by the people," c. 1600, from French popularité (15c.), from popular + -ity. Classical Latin popularitas meant "fellow-citizenship." Popularity contest is from 1880.
entries.etymologyZh: "fact or condition of being beloved by the people," 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 popularité (15 世纪), 源自 popular + -ity. Classical 拉丁语 popularitas meant "fellow-citizenship." Popularity contest 始于 1880 年.

example.en: The app gained popularity quickly after a celebrity endorsed it online.
example.zh: 这款应用在一位名人在网上为其代言后迅速走红。

entries.etymology: 1610s, from Medieval Latin populatus, past participle of populare "inhabit, to people," from Latin populus "inhabitants, people, nation" (see people (n.)). Related: Populated; populating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 中古拉丁语 populatus, 为 … 的过去分词 populare "inhabit, to people," 源自 拉丁语 populus "inhabitants, people, nation" （参见 people （名）). 同源词：Populated; populating.

entries.etymology: 1610s, from Late Latin populationem (nominative populatio) "a people; a multitude," as if from Latin populus "a people" (see people (n.)). Population explosion is first attested 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 晚期拉丁语 populationem (主格 populatio) "a people; a multitude," as if 源自 拉丁语 populus "a people" （参见 people （名）). Population explosion is 最早见于 1953 年.

example.en: The city's population has grown rapidly over the past decade.
example.zh: 过去十年间，这座城市的人口快速增长。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "covered entrance," from Old French porche "porch, vestibule," from Latin porticus "covered gallery, covered walk between columns, arcade, portico, porch," from porta "city gate, gate; door, entrance," from PIE root *per- (2) "to lead, pass over" (see port (n.1)). The Latin word was borrowed directly into Old English as portic.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "covered entrance," 源自 古法语 porche "porch, vestibule," 源自 拉丁语 porticus "covered gallery, covered walk between columns, arcade, portico, porch," 源自 porta "city gate, gate; door, entrance," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *per- (2) "to lead, pass over" （参见 port (n.1)). The 拉丁语 word was borrowed directly into 古英语 as portic.

example.en: The family gathered on the front porch to watch the sunset.
example.zh: 一家人聚在前廊观看日落。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300 (early 13c. in surname Porkuiller), "flesh of a pig as food," from Old French porc "pig, swine, boar," and directly from Latin porcus "pig, tame swine," from PIE *porko- "young swine" (source also of Umbrian purka; Old Church Slavonic prase "young pig;" Lithuanian parsas "pig;" and Old English fearh, Middle Dutch varken, both from Proto-Germanic *farhaz).

Pork barrel in the literal sense is from 1801, American English; meaning "state's financial resources (available for distribution)" is attested from 1907 (in full, national pork barrel); it was noted as an expression of U.S. President President William Howard Taft:

The magazine article that includes the quote opens with:

Pork in this sense is attested from 1862 (compare figurative use of bacon). Pork chop is attested from 1858. Pork pie is from 1732; pork-pie hat (1855) originally described a woman's style popular c. 1855-65, so called for its shape.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年 (13 世纪初 in surname Porkuiller), "flesh of a pig as food," 源自 古法语 porc "pig, swine, boar," and 直接源自 拉丁语 porcus "pig, tame swine," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *porko- "young swine" (source also of Umbrian purka; Old Church Slavonic prase "young pig;" Lithuanian parsas "pig;" and 古英语 fearh, Middle 荷兰语 varken, both 源自 原始日耳曼语 *farhaz). Pork barrel in the literal sense 始于 1801 年, American English; 意为 "state's financial resources (available for distribution)" 见于 1907 年 (in full, national pork barrel); it was noted 作为 expression of U.S. President President William Howard Taft: The magazine article that includes the quote opens with: Pork in this sense 见于 1862 年 (对比 figurative use of bacon). Pork chop 见于 1858 年. Pork pie 始于 1732 年; pork-pie hat (1855 年) 原义为 described a woman's style popular 约 1855 年-65, so called for its shape.

entries.etymology: 1530s, porage "soup of meat and vegetables," alteration of pottage, perhaps from influence of Middle English porray, porreie "leek broth," from Old French poree "leek soup," from Vulgar Latin *porrata, from Latin porrum "leek." Spelling with -idge attested from c. 1600. Association with oatmeal is 1640s, first in Scottish.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, porage "soup of meat and vegetables," alteration of pottage, 或源自 influence of 中古英语 porray, porreie "leek broth," 源自 古法语 poree "leek soup," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *porrata, 源自 拉丁语 porrum "leek." Spelling with -idge attested 源自 约 1600 年. Association with oatmeal is 1640 年代, first in 苏格兰语.

entries.etymology: "to carry," from Middle French porter, from Latin portare "to carry" (see port (n.1)). Related: Ported; porting.
entries.etymologyZh: "to carry," 源自 中古法语 porter, 源自 拉丁语 portare "to carry" （参见 port (n.1)). 同源词：Ported; porting.

example.en: The cargo ship docked at the commercial port to unload its containers.
example.zh: 货轮停靠在商业港口卸下集装箱。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from French portable "that can be carried," from Late Latin portabilis "that can be carried," from Latin portare "to carry" (see port (n.1)). Related: Portability.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 法语 portable "that can be carried," 源自 晚期拉丁语 portabilis "that can be carried," 源自 拉丁语 portare "to carry" （参见 port (n.1)). 同源词：Portability.

example.en: She bought a portable speaker that she could easily carry to the beach.
example.zh: 她买了一个便携式扬声器，可以轻松带去海滩。

definitionLines: n. 守门人，门房；行李搬运工
entries.definition: n. 守门人，门房；行李搬运工

entries.etymology: early 14c., "allotted part, share," from Old French porcion "part, portion" (12c., Modern French portion) and directly from Latin portionem (nominative portio) "share, part," accusative of the noun in the phrase pro portione "according to the relation (of parts to each other)" (see proportion). From late 14c. in general sense of "section into which something is divided."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "allotted part, share," 源自 古法语 porcion "part, portion" (12 世纪, 现代法语 portion) and 直接源自 拉丁语 portionem (主格 portio) "share, part," 宾格 of the 名词 in the phrase pro portione "according to the relation (of parts to each other)" （参见 proportion). From 14 世纪晚期 in general 语义 "section into which something is divided."

example.en: She donated a large portion of her salary to charity every month.
example.zh: 她每个月把工资的很大一部分捐给慈善机构。

entries.etymology: 1560s, "a figure, drawn or painted," a back formation from portraiture or directly from Middle French portrait, from Old French portret (13c.), noun use of past participle of portraire "to paint, depict" (see portray). Especially of the head and face of a person.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "a figure, drawn or painted," a back formation 源自 portraiture or 直接源自 中古法语 portrait, 源自 古法语 portret (13 世纪), 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 portraire "to paint, depict" （参见 portray). Especially of the head and face of a person.

example.en: The museum displayed a stunning portrait of the queen painted in 1650.
example.zh: 博物馆展出了一幅绘于1650年的精美女王肖像画。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., "to draw, paint" (something), from Anglo-French purtraire, Old French portraire "to draw, to paint, portray" (12c.), literally "trace, draw forth," from por- "forth" (from Latin pro-; see pro-) + traire "trace, draw," from Latin trahere "to drag, draw" (see tract (n.1)). Meaning "depict in words, describe" is from late 14c. Related: Portrayed; portraying.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "to draw, paint" (something), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 purtraire, 古法语 portraire "to draw, to paint, portray" (12 世纪), 字面义为 "trace, draw forth," 源自 por- "forth" (源自 拉丁语 pro-; 参见 pro-) + traire "trace, draw," 源自 拉丁语 trahere "to drag, draw" （参见 tract (n.1)). 义为 "depict in words, describe" 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Portrayed; portraying.

example.en: The artist chose to portray rural life in vivid colors.
example.zh: 这位艺术家选择用鲜艳的色彩描绘农村生活。

definitionLines: v.（使）摆好姿势；形成，引起， 造成

entries.etymology:
late 14c., as a term in logic and philosophy, from Old French posicion "position, supposition" (Modern French position), from Latin positionem (nominative positio) "act or fact of placing, situation, position, affirmation," noun of state from past participle stem of ponere "put, place," from PIE *po-s(i)nere, from *apo- "off, away" (see apo-) + *sinere "to leave, let" (see site).

Meaning "proper place occupied by a person or thing" is from 1540s. Meaning "manner in which some physical thing is arranged or posed" first recorded 1703; specifically in reference to dance steps, 1778, sexual intercourse, 1883. Meaning "official station, employment" is from 1890.

entries.etymology:
early 14c., originally a legal term meaning "formally laid down," from Old French positif (13c.) and directly from Latin positivus "settled by agreement, positive" (opposed to naturalis "natural"), from positus, past participle of ponere "put, place" (see position (n.)).

Sense of "absolute" is from mid-15c. Meaning in philosophy of "dealing only with facts" is from 1590s. Sense broadened to "expressed without qualification" (1590s), then "confident in opinion" (1660s); mathematical use is from 1704; in electricity, 1755. Psychological sense of "concentrating on what is constructive and good" is recorded from 1916.

Sense broadened to "expressed without qualification" (1590 年代), 之后 "confident in opinion" (1660 年代); mathematical use 始于 1704 年; in electricity, 1755 年. Psychological 语义 "concentrating on what is constructive and good" 见于 1916 年.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to hold, occupy, reside in" (without regard to ownership), a back formation from possession and in part from Old French possesser "to have and hold, take, be in possession of" (mid-13c.), from Latin possess-, past participle stem of possidere "to have and hold, possess, be master of, own," from posse "to be able," from potis "able, powerful" (see potent) + esse "to be" (see be). entries.etymology:
1560s, from Spanish patata, from a Carib language of Haiti batata "sweet potato." Sweet potatoes were first to be introduced to Europe; in cultivation in Spain by mid-16c.; in Virginia by 1648. Early 16c. Portuguese traders carried the crop to all their shipping ports and the sweet potato was quickly adopted from Africa to India and Java.

The name later (1590s) was extended to the common white potato, from Peru, which was at first (mistakenly) called Virginia potato, or, because at first it was of minor importance compared to the sweet potato, bastard potato. Spanish invaders in Peru began to use white potatoes as cheap food for sailors 1530s. The first potato from South America reached Pope Paul III in 1540; grown in France at first as an ornamental plant. According to popular tradition, introduced to Ireland 1565 by John Hawkins. Brought to England from Colombia by Sir Thomas Herriot, 1586.
German kartoffel (17c.) is a dissimilation from tartoffel, ultimately from Italian tartufolo (Vulgar Latin *territuberem), originally "truffle." Frederick II forced its cultivation on Prussian peasants in 1743. The French is pomme de terre, literally "earth-apple;" a Swedish dialectal word for "potato" is jordpäron, literally "earth-pear."

Colloquial pronunciation tater is attested in print from 1759. Potato chip (n.) attested from 1879. To drop (something) like a hot potato is from 1824. Children's counting-out rhyme that begins one potato, two potato first recorded 1885 in Canada. Slang potato trap "mouth" attested from 1785.

The noun, meaning "that which is possible," is first attested 1817, from the adjective.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "ash, cinders; dust of the earth;" early 14c., "pulverized substance;" mid-14c., "medicinal powder;" late 14c. as "gunpowder," from Old French poudre "dust, powder; ashes; powdered substance" (13c.), earlier pouldre (11c.), from Latin pulverem (nominative pulvis) "dust" (see pollen). Specialized sense "gunpowder" is from late 14c. In the sense "powdered cosmetic," it is recorded from 1570s.

In figurative sense, powder keg is first attested 1855. Powder room, euphemistic for "women's lavatory," is attested from 1936. Earlier it meant "place where gunpowder is loaded on a warship" (1620s). Powder horn attested by 1530s. Powder puff first recorded 1704; as a symbol of femaleness or effeminacy, in use from at least 1930s.

Phrase take a powder "scram, vanish," is from 1920; it was a common phrase as a doctor's instruction, so perhaps from the notion of taking a laxative medicine or a sleeping powder, with the result that one has to leave in a hurry (or, on another guess, from a magician's magical powder, which made things disappear). Powder blue (1650s) was smelt used in laundering; as a color name from 1894.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "ability; ability to act or do; strength, vigor, might," especially in battle; "efficacy; control, mastery, lordship, dominion; legal power or authority; authorization; military force, an army," from Anglo-French pouair, Old French povoir, noun use of the infinitive, "to be able," earlier podir (9c.), from Vulgar Latin *potere, from Latin potis "powerful" (see potent).

Meaning "one who has power" is late 14c. Meaning "specific ability or capacity" is from early 15c. Meaning "a state or nation with regard to international authority or influence" [OED] is from 1726. Used for "a large number of" from 1660s. Meaning "energy available for work is from 1727. Sense of "electrical supply" is from 1896.

Phrase the powers that be is from Rom. xiii:1. As a statement wishing good luck, more power to (someone) is recorded from 1842. A power play in ice hockey so called by 1940. Power failure is from 1911; power steering from 1921.

entries.etymology: c. 1400, from power (n.) + -ful. Meaning "of great quality or number" is from 1811; colloquial sense of "exceedingly" (adv.) is from 1822. Related: Powerfully. example.zh: 新款发动机比上一型号强劲得多，且更省油。

entries.etymology:
early 15c., practicale "of or pertaining to matters of practice; applied," with -al (1) + earlier practic (adj.) "dealing with practical matters, applied, not merely theoretical" (early 15c.), or practic (n.) "method, practice, use" (late 14c.). In some cases directly from Old French practique (adj.) "fit for action," earlier pratique (13c.) and Medieval Latin practicalis, from Late Latin practicus "practical, active," from Greek praktikos "fit for action, fit for business; business-like, practical; active, effective, vigorous," from praktos "done; to be done," verbal adjective of prassein, prattein "to do, act, effect, accomplish."

Practical joke "trick played on someone for the sake of a laugh at his expense" is from 1771 (earlier handicraft joke, 1741).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, practicale "of or pertaining to matters of practice; applied," with -al (1) + earlier practic （形） "dealing with practical matters, applied, not merely theoretical" (15 世纪初)，或practic （名） "method, practice, use" (14 世纪晚期). In some cases 直接源自 古法语 practique （形） "fit for action," earlier pratique (13 世纪) and 中古拉丁语 practicalis, 源自 晚期拉丁语 practicus "practical, active," 源自 希腊语 praktikos "fit for action, fit for business; business-like, practical; active, effective, vigorous," 源自 praktos "done; to be done," verbal 形容词 of prassein, prattein "to do, act, effect, accomplish." Practical joke "trick played on someone for the sake of a laugh at his expense" 始于 1771 年 (earlier handicraft joke, 1741 年).

example.en: The course focuses on practical skills that students can apply directly in the workplace from day one.
example.zh: 该课程侧重于学生从第一天起就能直接用于职场的实用技能。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "in a practical manner," from practical + -ly (2). Meaning "for practical purposes, as good as" is from 1748; loosened sense of "almost" is from 1869.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "in a practical manner," 源自 practical + -ly (2). 义为 "for practical purposes, as good as" 始于 1748 年; loosened 语义 "almost" 始于 1869 年.

example.en: The exam was practically impossible without proper preparation.
example.zh: 没有充分准备，这场考试几乎是不可能通过的。

definitionLines: n. 实践，实施；练习，实习； 业务，开业
v. 实践，实行；练习，实习； 开业，从事
entries.definition: n. 实践，实施；练习，实习； 业务，开业 v. 实践，实行；练习，实习； 开业，从事
entries.etymology:
c. 1400, "to do, act;" early 15c., "to follow or employ; to carry on a profession," especially medicine, from Old French pratiser, practiser "to practice," alteration of practiquer, from Medieval Latin practicare "to do, perform, practice," from Late Latin practicus "practical," from Greek praktikos "practical" (see practical).

From early 15c. as "to perform repeatedly to acquire skill, to learn by repeated performance;" mid-15c. as "to perform, to work at, exercise." Related: Practiced; practicing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "to do, act;" 15 世纪初, "to follow or employ; to carry on a profession," 尤指 medicine, 源自 古法语 pratiser, practiser "to practice," alteration of practiquer, 源自 中古拉丁语 practicare "to do, perform, practice," 源自 晚期拉丁语 practicus "practical," 源自 希腊语 praktikos "practical" （参见 practical). From 15 世纪初 as "to perform repeatedly to acquire skill, to learn by repeated performance;" 15 世纪中期 as "to perform, to work at, exercise." 同源词：Practiced; practicing.

example.en: Piano teachers often say that daily practice builds muscle memory over time.
example.zh: 钢琴老师常说，每天的练习会随着时间建立肌肉记忆。

entries.definition: v. 称赞，表扬 n. 称赞，赞美
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to laud, commend, flatter," from Old French preisier, variant of prisier "to praise, value," from Late Latin preciare, earlier pretiare (see price (n.)). Replaced Old English lof, hreþ.

Specifically with God as an object from late 14c. Related: Praised; praising. Now a verb in most Germanic languages (German preis, Danish pris, etc.), but only in English is it differentiated in form from cognate price.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to laud, commend, flatter," 源自 古法语 preisier, 为 … 的变体 prisier "to praise, value," 源自 晚期拉丁语 preciare, earlier pretiare （参见 price （名）). Replaced 古英语 lof, hreþ. Specifically with God 作为 object 源自 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Praised; praising. Now a 动词 in most 日耳曼语 languages (德语 preis, Danish pris, etc.), but only in English is it differentiated in form 源自 同源 price.

example.en: The coach publicly praised the team for their outstanding performance in the final.
example.zh: 教练公开表扬了球队在决赛中的出色表现。

definitionLines: n. 祈祷，祈求；请求，恳求
entries.definition: n. 祈祷，祈求；请求，恳求
entries.etymology:
early 13c., "ask earnestly, beg," also (c. 1300) "pray to a god or saint," from Old French preier "to pray" (c.900, Modern French prier), from Vulgar Latin *precare (also source of Italian pregare), from Latin precari "ask earnestly, beg, entreat," from *prex (plural preces, genitive precis) "prayer, request, entreaty," from PIE root *prek- "to ask, request, entreat" (source also of Sanskrit prasna-, Avestan frashna- "question;" Old Church Slavonic prositi, Lithuanian prasyti "to ask, beg;" Old High German frahen, German fragen, Old English fricgan "to ask" a question).

Parenthetical expression I pray you, "please, if you will," attested from 1510s, contracted to pray 16c. Related: Prayed; praying. Praying mantis attested from 1809. The "Gardener's Monthly" of July 1861 lists other names for it as camel cricket, soothsayer, and rear horse.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "ask earnestly, beg," also (约 1300 年) "pray to a god or saint," 源自 古法语 preier "to pray" (约 900 年, 现代法语 prier), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *precare (also source of 意大利语 pregare), 源自 拉丁语 precari "ask earnestly, beg, entreat," 源自 *prex (plural preces, 属格 precis) "prayer, request, entreaty," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *prek- "to ask, request, entreat" (source also of 梵语 prasna-, Avestan frashna- "question;" Old Church Slavonic prositi, Lithuanian prasyti "to ask, beg;" 古高地德语 frahen, 德语 fragen, 古英语 fricgan "to ask" a question). Parenthetical expression I pray you, "please, if you will," attested 源自 1510 年代, contracted to pray 16 世纪 同源词：Prayed; praying. Praying mantis attested 自 1809 年起. The "Gardener's Monthly" of July 1861 年 lists other names for it as camel cricket, soothsayer, and rear horse.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, from Old French prier "prayer, petition, request" (12c., Modern French prière), from Medieval Latin precaria "petition, prayer," noun use of Latin adjective precaria, fem. of precarius "obtained by prayer, given as a favor," from precari "to ask, beg, pray" (see pray). Related: Prayers.

Prayer-book attested from 1590s; prayer-meeting from 1780. To not have a prayer "have no chance" is from 1941.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 prier "prayer, petition, request" (12 世纪, 现代法语 prière), 源自 中古拉丁语 precaria "petition, prayer," 为 … 的名词用法 拉丁语 形容词 precaria, fem. of precarius "obtained by prayer, given as a favor," 源自 precari "to ask, beg, pray" （参见 pray). 同源词：Prayers. Prayer-book attested 源自 1590 年代; prayer-meeting 自 1780 年起. To not have a prayer "have no chance" 始于 1941 年.

example.en: She said a quiet prayer before going to bed each night.
example.zh: 她每晚睡前都会默默祈祷一番。

definitionLines: n. 预防，警惕；预防措施
entries.definition: n. 预防，警惕；预防措施 vt. 预先警告；警惕
entries.etymology: c. 1600, from French précaution (16c.) and directly from Late Latin praecautionem (nominative praecautio) "a safeguarding," from past participle stem of Latin praecavere "to guard against beforehand," from prae "before" (see pre-) + cavere "to be one's own guard" (see caution (n.)). The verb meaning "to warn (someone) in advance" is from c. 1700.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 précaution (16 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 praecautionem (主格 praecautio) "a safeguarding," 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 praecavere "to guard against beforehand," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + cavere "to be one's own guard" （参见 caution （名）). The 动词 意为 "to warn (someone) in advance" 始于 约 1700 年.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "lead the way; occur before," from Middle French preceder and directly from Latin praecedere "to go before," from prae "before" (see pre-) + cedere "to go" (see cede). Meaning "to walk in front of" is late 15c.; that of "to go before in rank or importance" is attested from mid-15c. Related: Preceded; preceding.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "lead the way; occur before," 源自 中古法语 preceder and 直接源自 拉丁语 praecedere "to go before," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + cedere "to go" （参见 cede). 义为 "to walk in front of" is 15 世纪晚期; that of "to go before in rank or importance" 见于 15 世纪中期 同源词：Preceded; preceding.

example.en: A short introduction preceded the main presentation at the conference.
example.zh: 一段简短的介绍先于大会的主报告进行。

entries.definition: n. 先例；前例 a. 在前的；在先的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "case which may be taken as a rule in similar cases," from Middle French precedent, noun use of an adjective, from Latin praecedentum (nominative praecedens), present participle of praecedere "go before" (see precede). Meaning "thing or person that goes before another" is attested from mid-15c. As an adjective in English from c. 1400. As a verb meaning "to furnish with a precedent" from 1610s, now only in past participle precedented.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "case which may be taken as a rule in similar cases," 源自 中古法语 precedent, 为 … 的名词用法 an 形容词, 源自 拉丁语 praecedentum (主格 praecedens), 为 … 的现在分词 praecedere "go before" （参见 precede). 义为 "thing or person that goes before another" 见于 15 世纪中期 作形容词时 in English 源自 约 1400 年. 作动词时 意为 "to furnish with a precedent" 源自 1610 年代, 现在 only in past participle precedented.

example.en: The court ruling set a precedent that would influence future cases for years.
example.zh: 这项法院裁决树立了一个先例，将对未来多年的案件产生影响。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from Old French precios "precious, costly, honorable, of great worth" (11c., Modern French précieux), from Latin pretiosus "costly, valuable," from pretium "value, worth, price" (see price (n.)). Meaning "over-refined" in English first recorded late 14c. In Johnson's day, it also had a secondary inverted sense of "worthless." Related: Preciously; preciousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 precios "precious, costly, honorable, of great worth" (11 世纪, 现代法语 précieux), 源自 拉丁语 pretiosus "costly, valuable," 源自 pretium "value, worth, price" （参见 price （名）). 义为 "over-refined" in English 首见于 14 世纪晚期 In Johnson's day, it also had a secondary inverted 语义 "worthless." 同源词：Preciously; preciousness.

example.en: Time is our most precious resource, so we must use it wisely.
example.zh: 时间是我们最宝贵的资源，因此我们必须明智地使用它。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French précis "condensed, cut short" (14c.) and directly from Medieval Latin precisus, from Latin praecisus "abrupt, abridged, cut off," past participle of praecidere "to cut off, shorten," from prae "before" (see pre-) + caedere "to cut" (see -cide; for Latin vowel change, see acquisition). Related: Precisely (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 précis "condensed, cut short" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 precisus, 源自 拉丁语 praecisus "abrupt, abridged, cut off," 为 … 的过去分词 praecidere "to cut off, shorten," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + caedere "to cut" （参见 -cide; for 拉丁语 vowel change, 参见 acquisition). 同源词：Precisely (14 世纪晚期).

example.en: The engineer gave a precise measurement of each component.
example.zh: 工程师给出了每个零件的精确测量值。

entries.etymology: 1630s, "a cutting off (mentally), abstraction," from French précision (16c.) and directly from Latin praecisionem (nominative praecisio) "a cutting off," noun of action from past participle stem of praecidere (see precise). Meaning "preciseness" is from 1740.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "a cutting off (mentally), abstraction," 源自 法语 précision (16 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 praecisionem (主格 praecisio) "a cutting off," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praecidere （参见 precise). 义为 "preciseness" 始于 1740 年.

example.en: The surgeon performed the operation with remarkable precision, leaving no room for error.
example.zh: 外科医生以出色的精确度完成了手术，没有任何失误的余地。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "one who has held an office or position before the present holder," from Old French predecesseor "forebear" and directly from Late Latin praedecessorem (nominative praedecessor), from Latin prae "before" (see pre-) + decessor "retiring official," from decess-, past participle stem of decedere "go away," also "die" (see decease (n.)). Meaning "ancestor, forefather" is recorded from c. 1400.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "one who has held an office or position before the present holder," 源自 古法语 predecesseor "forebear" and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 praedecessorem (主格 praedecessor), 源自 拉丁语 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + decessor "retiring official," 源自 decess-, past participle stem of decedere "go away," also "die" （参见 decease （名）). 义为 "ancestor, forefather" 见于 约 1400 年.

example.en: Her predecessor had served as director for over two decades.
example.zh: 她的前任担任主任一职已超过二十年。

entries.etymology: 1620s (implied in predicted), "foretell, prophesy," a back formation from prediction or else from Latin praedicatus, past participle of praedicere "foretell, advise, give notice," from prae "before" (see pre-) + dicere "to say" (see diction). Related: Predicted; predicting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代 (implied in predicted), "foretell, prophesy," a back formation 源自 prediction or else 源自 拉丁语 praedicatus, 为 … 的过去分词 praedicere "foretell, advise, give notice," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + dicere "to say" （参见 diction). 同源词：Predicted; predicting.

example.en: Meteorologists use advanced models to predict rainfall patterns weeks in advance.
example.zh: 气象学家使用先进模型提前数周预测降雨模式。

definitionLines: a. 卓越的；有力的；支配的
entries.definition: a. 卓越的；有力的；支配的
entries.etymology: 1570s, from Middle French prédominant (14c.), from Medieval Latin *praedominantem (nominative praedominans), present participle of *praedominare, from Latin prae- "before" (see pre-) + dominari "to rule" (see dominate). Related: Predominantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 源自 中古法语 prédominant (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 *praedominantem (主格 praedominans), 为 … 的现在分词 *praedominare, 源自 拉丁语 prae- "before" （参见 pre-) + dominari "to rule" （参见 dominate). 同源词：Predominantly.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French preface "opening part of sung devotions" (14c.) and directly from Medieval Latin prefatia, from Latin praefationem (nominative praefatio) "fore-speaking, introduction," in Medieval Latin "prologue," noun of action from past participle stem of praefari "to say beforehand," from prae "before" (see pre-) + fari "speak" (see fame (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 preface "opening part of sung devotions" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 prefatia, 源自 拉丁语 praefationem (主格 praefatio) "fore-speaking, introduction," in 中古拉丁语 "prologue," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praefari "to say beforehand," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + fari "speak" （参见 fame （名）).

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to put forward or advance in rank or fortune, to promote," from Old French preferer (14c.) and directly from Latin praeferre "place or set before, carry in front," from prae "before" (see pre-) + ferre "to carry, to place" (see infer). Meaning "to esteem (something) more than others" also is recorded from late 14c. Original sense in English is preserved in preferment.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to put forward or advance in rank or fortune, to promote," 源自 古法语 preferer (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 praeferre "place or set before, carry in front," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + ferre "to carry, to place" （参见 infer). 义为 "to esteem (something) more than others" also 见于 14 世纪晚期 Original sense in English is preserved in preferment.

example.en: Most students prefer to study in a quiet library rather than a noisy café.
example.zh: 大多数学生宁愿在安静的图书馆学习，而不是在嘈杂的咖啡馆。

definitionLines: a. 更好的，更可取的；更合意的
entries.definition: a. 更好的，更可取的；更合意的
entries.etymology: 1640s, from or on model of French préférable, from préfér (see prefer). OED notes preferrable is better English but has not prevailed. Related: Preferably.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 or on model of 法语 préférable, 源自 préfér （参见 prefer). OED notes preferrable is better English but has not prevailed. 同源词：Preferably.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "advancement in position or status;" 1650s as "act of prefering," from Middle French preference (14c., Modern French préférence), from Medieval Latin preferentia, from past participle stem of Latin praeferrere (see prefer). Sense of "that which one prefers" is from 1852.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "advancement in position or status;" 1650 年代 as "act of prefering," 源自 中古法语 preference (14 世纪, 现代法语 préférence), 源自 中古拉丁语 preferentia, 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 praeferrere （参见 prefer). 义为 "that which one prefers" 始于 1852 年.

example.en: She has a strong preference for classical music over pop songs.
example.zh: 她明显更偏爱古典音乐而非流行歌曲。

definitionLines: a. 怀孕的；重要的，富有意义 的；孕育的
entries.definition: a. 怀孕的；重要的，富有意义 的；孕育的

example.en: The doctor confirmed that she was three months pregnant.
example.zh: 医生确认她已经怀孕三个月了。

definitionLines: n. 偏见，成见；损害，侵害
entries.definition: n. 偏见，成见；损害，侵害
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "despite, contempt," from Old French prejudice "prejudice, damage" (13c.), from Medieval Latin prejudicium "injustice," from Latin praeiudicium "prior judgment," from prae- "before" (see pre-) + iudicium "judgment," from iudex (genitive iudicis) "a judge" (see judge (v.)). Meaning "injury, physical harm" is mid-14c., as is legal sense "detriment or damage caused by the violation of a legal right." Meaning "preconceived opinion" (especially but not necessarily unfavorable) is from late 14c. in English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "despite, contempt," 源自 古法语 prejudice "prejudice, damage" (13 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 prejudicium "injustice," 源自 拉丁语 praeiudicium "prior judgment," 源自 prae- "before" （参见 pre-) + iudicium "judgment," 源自 iudex (属格 iudicis) "a judge" （参见 judge （动）). 义为 "injury, physical harm" is 14 世纪中期, as is legal sense "detriment or damage caused by the violation of a legal right." 义为 "preconceived opinion" (尤指 but not necessarily unfavorable) 始于 14 世纪晚期 in English.

example.en: She challenged the prejudice that women are less capable in engineering.
example.zh: 她挑战了女性在工程领域能力不足的偏见。

entries.etymology: 1660s, from French préliminaire and directly from Medieval Latin praeliminaris, from Latin prae- "before" (see pre-) + limen (genitive liminis) "threshold" (see limit (n.)). A word that arose in reference to negotiations to end the Thirty Years' War. Earliest attested form in English is preliminaries (n.), 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, 源自 法语 préliminaire and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 praeliminaris, 源自 拉丁语 prae- "before" （参见 pre-) + limen (属格 liminis) "threshold" （参见 limit （名）). A word that arose in reference to negotiations to end the Thirty Years' War. Earliest attested form in English is preliminaries （名）, 1650 年代.

example.en: A preliminary investigation revealed several flaws in the design.
example.zh: 初步调查发现了设计中的几处缺陷。

definitionLines: a. 比预期早的；不成熟的；早|preservation
entries.definition: a. 比预期早的；不成熟的；早|preservation
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Latin praematurus "early ripe" (as fruit), "too early, untimely," from prae "before" (see pre-) + maturus "ripe, timely" (see mature (v.)). Related: Prematurely; prematurity; prematuration. Premature ejaculation is attested from 1848; Latin euphemism ejaculatio praecox dates to 1891 in English but was used earlier in German and appears to have been, at first at least, the psychologist's term for it.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 praematurus "early ripe" (as fruit), "too early, untimely," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + maturus "ripe, timely" （参见 mature （动）). 同源词：Prematurely; prematurity; prematuration. Premature ejaculation 见于 1848 年; 拉丁语 euphemism ejaculatio praecox dates to 1891 年 in English but was used earlier in 德语 and appears to have been, at first at least, the psychologist's term for it.

entries.definition: n2. 首相，总理 a. 第一的；最初的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "first in time;" late 15c. as "first in rank," from Middle French premier "first, chief," from Latin primarius "of the first rank, chief" (see primary (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "first in time;" 15 世纪晚期 as "first in rank," 源自 中古法语 premier "first, chief," 源自 拉丁语 primarius "of the first rank, chief" （参见 primary （形）).

entries.etymology: late 14c., in logic, "a previous proposition from which another follows," from Old French premisse (14c.), from Medieval Latin premissa (propositio or sententia) "(the proposition) set before," noun use of fem. past participle of Latin praemittere "send forward, put before," from prae "before" (see pre-) + mittere "to send" (see mission). In legal documents it meant "matter previously stated" (early 15c.), which in deeds or wills often was a house or building, hence the extended meaning "house or building, with grounds" (1730).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in logic, "a previous proposition from which another follows," 源自 古法语 premisse (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 premissa (propositio or sententia) "(the proposition) set before," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 拉丁语 praemittere "send forward, put before," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + mittere "to send" （参见 mission). In legal documents it meant "matter previously stated" (15 世纪初), which in deeds or wills 常 was a house or building, hence the extended 意为 "house or building, with grounds" (1730 年).

example.en: The entire argument rests on the premise that people act rationally.
example.zh: 整个论点建立在人们理性行动这一前提上。

definitionLines: n. 奖赏，奖金/品，佣金；（利 息、工资等以外的）酬金；额 外的费用
entries.definition: n. 奖赏，奖金/品，佣金；（利 息、工资等以外的）酬金；额 外的费用
entries.etymology: c. 1600, "reward given for a specific act," from Latin praemium "reward, profit derived from booty," from prae- "before" (see pre-) + emere "to buy," originally "to take" (see exempt (adj.)). Insurance sense is 1660s, from Italian premio. Adjectival sense of "superior in quality" is first attested 1925, originally in reference to butter.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "reward given for a specific act," 源自 拉丁语 praemium "reward, profit derived from booty," 源自 prae- "before" （参见 pre-) + emere "to buy," 原义为 "to take" （参见 exempt （形）). Insurance sense is 1660 年代, 源自 意大利语 premio. Adjectival 语义 "superior in quality" is 最早见于 1925 年, 原义为 in reference to butter.

example.en: Customers pay a premium for next-day delivery of their orders.
example.zh: 顾客为次日送达的订单支付额外费用。

definitionLines: n. 准备，预备；制剂，制备品
entries.definition: n. 准备，预备；制剂，制备品
entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of preparing," from Latin praeparationem (nominative praeparatio) "a making ready," noun of action from past participle stem of praeparare "prepare," from prae "before" (see pre-) + parare "make ready" (see pare). Meaning "a substance especially prepared" is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of preparing," 源自 拉丁语 praeparationem (主格 praeparatio) "a making ready," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praeparare "prepare," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + parare "make ready" （参见 pare). 义为 "a substance especially prepared" 始于 1640 年代.

example.en: Careful preparation is the key to a successful scientific experiment.
example.zh: 仔细的准备是成功进行科学实验的关键。

definitionLines: v. 准备，预备；制作，制备
entries.definition: v. 准备，预备；制作，制备
entries.etymology: mid-15c., a back formation from preparation and in part from Middle French preparer (14c.), from Latin praeparare "make ready beforehand" (see preparation). Related: Prepared; preparing. Be prepared as the Boy Scouts' motto is attested from 1911.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, a back formation 源自 preparation and in part 源自 中古法语 preparer (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 praeparare "make ready beforehand" （参见 preparation). 同源词：Prepared; preparing. Be prepared as the Boy Scouts' motto 见于 1911 年.

example.en: Teachers need extra time to prepare engaging lessons for their students.
example.zh: 教师需要额外时间来为学生准备有吸引力的课程。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin praepositionem (nominative praepositio) "a putting before, a prefixing," noun of action from past participle stem of praeponere "put before," from prae "before" (see pre-) + ponere "put, set, place" (past participle positus; see position (n.)). In grammatical use, a loan-translation of Greek prothesis, literally "a setting before."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 praepositionem (主格 praepositio) "a putting before, a prefixing," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praeponere "put before," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + ponere "put, set, place" (past participle positus; 参见 position （名）). definitionLines: v. 开处方，开药；规定，指示
entries.definition: v. 开处方，开药；规定，指示
entries.etymology: "to write down as a direction," mid-15c., from Latin praescribere "write beforehand" (see prescription). Related: Prescribed; prescribing. Medical sense is from 1580s, probably a back formation from prescription.
entries.etymologyZh: "to write down as a direction," 15 世纪中期, 源自 拉丁语 praescribere "write beforehand" （参见 prescription). 同源词：Prescribed; prescribing. Medical sense 始于 1580 年代, 可能 a back formation 源自 prescription.

example.en: The doctor decided to prescribe a stronger antibiotic for the infection.
example.zh: 医生决定为这次感染开一种更强效的抗生素。

entries.etymology: late 14c., in law, "the right to something through long use," from Old French prescription (13c.) and directly from Latin praescriptionem (nominative praescriptio) "a writing before, order, direction," noun of action from past participle stem of praescribere "write before, prefix in writing; ordain, determine in advance," from prae "before" (see pre-) + scribere "to write" (see script (n.)). Medical sense of "written directions from a doctor" first recorded 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in law, "the right to something through long use," 源自 古法语 prescription (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 praescriptionem (主格 praescriptio) "a writing before, order, direction," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praescribere "write before, prefix in writing; ordain, determine in advance," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + scribere "to write" （参见 script （名）). Medical 语义 "written directions from a doctor" 首见于 1570 年代.

example.en: The doctor wrote a prescription for antibiotics after examining the patient.
example.zh: 医生检查病人后开了一张抗生素处方。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "fact of being present," from Old French presence (12c., Modern French présence), from Latin praesentia "a being present," from praesentem (see present (n.)). Meaning "carriage, demeanor, aspect" (especially if impressive) is from 1570s; that of "divine, spiritual, or incorporeal being felt as present" is from 1660s. Presence of mind (1660s) is a loan-translation of French présence d'esprit, Latin praesentia animi.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "fact of being present," 源自 古法语 presence (12 世纪, 现代法语 présence), 源自 拉丁语 praesentia "a being present," 源自 praesentem （参见 present （名）). 义为 "carriage, demeanor, aspect" (尤指 if impressive) 始于 1570 年代; that of "divine, spiritual, or incorporeal being felt as present" 始于 1660 年代. Presence of mind (1660 年代) is a loan-translation of 法语 présence d'esprit, 拉丁语 praesentia animi.

example.en: His calm presence in the room made everyone feel more comfortable.
example.zh: 他在房间里沉稳的存在让每个人都感到更加放松。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "existing at the time," from Old French present "evident, at hand, within reach;" as a noun, "the present time" (11c., Modern French présent) and directly from Latin praesentem (nominative praesens) "present, at hand, in sight; immediate; prompt, instant; contemporary," from present participle of præesse "be before (someone or something), be at hand," from prae- "before" (see pre-) + esse "to be" (see essence). Meaning "being there" is from mid-14c. in English. As a grammatical tense, recorded from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "existing at the time," 源自 古法语 present "evident, at hand, within reach;" 作名词时, "the present time" (11 世纪, 现代法语 présent) and 直接源自 拉丁语 praesentem (主格 praesens) "present, at hand, in sight; immediate; prompt, instant; contemporary," 源自 为 … 的现在分词 præesse "be before (someone or something), be at hand," 源自 prae- "before" （参见 pre-) + esse "to be" （参见 essence). 义为 "being there" 始于 14 世纪中期 in English. 作为 grammatical tense, recorded 源自 14 世纪晚期

entries.definition: n. 介绍，陈述；表现形式
entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of presenting," from Old French presentacion (13c.), from Latin praesentationem (nominative praesentatio) "a placing before," noun of action from  past participle stem of praesentare (see present (v.)). Meaning "that which is offered or presented" is mid-15c.; that of "a theatrical or other representation" is recorded from c. 1600. Related: Presentational.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of presenting," 源自 古法语 presentacion (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 praesentationem (主格 praesentatio) "a placing before," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praesentare （参见 present （动）). 义为 "that which is offered or presented" is 15 世纪中期; that of "a theatrical or other representation" 见于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Presentational.

example.en: The manager delivered a presentation on the quarterly sales results.
example.zh: 经理就季度销售业绩进行了一次正式汇报。
