entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "immediately, at this time," 源自 present （形） + -ly (2). By 1560 年代 it had relaxed into "sooner or later."

definitionLines: vt. 保护，保存；保藏，腌制； 维持，保持
entries.definition: vt. 保护，保存；保藏，腌制； 维持，保持
entries.etymology: late 14c., "keep safe," from Anglo-French preservare, Old French preserver, from Medieval Latin preservare "keep, preserve," from Late Latin praeservare "guard beforehand," from Latin prae "before" (see pre-) + servare "to keep safe" (see observe). As a treatment of fruit, etc., 1570s; of organic bodies from 1610s. Related: Preserved; preserving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "keep safe," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 preservare, 古法语 preserver, 源自 中古拉丁语 preservare "keep, preserve," 源自 晚期拉丁语 praeservare "guard beforehand," 源自 拉丁语 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + servare "to keep safe" （参见 observe). 作为 treatment of fruit, etc., 1570 年代; of organic bodies 源自 1610 年代. 同源词：Preserved; preserving.

example.en: The government took measures to preserve the ancient temple from further damage.
example.zh: 政府采取措施保护这座古寺免遭进一步破坏。

definitionLines: n. 主席，总统，校长，会长； 总裁；董事长
entries.definition: n. 主席，总统，校长，会长； 总裁；董事长
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "appointed governor of a province; chosen leader of a body of persons," from Old French president and directly from Latin praesidentum (nominative praesidens) "president, governor," noun use of present participle of praesidere "to act as head or chief" (see preside).

In Middle English of heads of religious houses, hospitals, colleges and universities. First use for "chief executive officer of a republic" is in U.S. Constitution (1787), from earlier American use for "officer in charge of the Continental Congress" (1774), a sense derived from that of "chosen head of a meeting or group of persons," which is from Middle English. It had been used of chief officers of banks from 1781, of individual colonies since 1608 (originally Virginia) and heads of colleges since mid-15c. Slang shortening prez is recorded from 1883. Fem. form presidentess is attested from 1763.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "appointed governor of a province; chosen leader of a body of persons," 源自 古法语 president and 直接源自 拉丁语 praesidentum (主格 praesidens) "president, governor," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的现在分词 praesidere "to act as head or chief" （参见 preside). In 中古英语 of heads of religious houses, hospitals, colleges and universities. First use for "chief executive officer of a republic" is in U.S. Constitution (1787 年), 源自 earlier American use for "officer in charge of the Continental Congress" (1774 年), a sense derived 源自 that of "chosen head of a meeting or group of persons," which 始于 中古英语. It had been used of chief officers of banks 自 1781 年起, of individual colonies 自 1608 年 (原义为 Virginia) and heads of colleges 自 15 世纪中期 Slang shortening prez 见于 1883 年. Fem. form presidentess 见于 1763 年.

example.en: The president signed the new trade agreement at the White House.
example.zh: 总统在白宫签署了新的贸易协定。

definitionLines: n.压，挤，按：报刊，出版界/社； 压机，压榨机，印刷机
entries.definition: vt. 压，挤，按；催促 n.压，挤，按：报刊，出版界/社； 压机，压榨机，印刷机
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, presse, "crowd, throng, company; crowding and jostling of a throng; a massing together," from Old French presse (n.) "throng, crush, crowd; wine or cheese press" (11c.), from Latin pressare (see press (v.1)). Late Old English had press "clothes press."

Meaning "device for pressing cloth" is from late 14c., as is also the sense "device to squeeze juice from grapes, oil from olives, cider from apples, etc.," from Middle French presse. Specific sense "machine for printing" is from 1530s; this was extended to publishing houses by 1570s and to publishing generally (in phrases like freedom of the press) from c. 1680. This gradually shifted c. 1800-1820 to "periodical publishing, journalism." The press, meaning "journalists collectively" is attested from 1921 (though superseded by media since the rise of television, etc.).

Press agent is from 1873; press conference is attested from 1931, though the thing itself dates to at least World War I. Press secretary is recorded from 1940. Via the sense "crowd, throng," Middle English in press meant "in public," a coincidental parallel to the modern phrase in the press. Weightlifting sense is from 1908. The basketball defense so called from 1959 (in full-court press).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, presse, "crowd, throng, company; crowding and jostling of a throng; a massing together," 源自 古法语 presse （名） "throng, crush, crowd; wine or cheese press" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 pressare （参见 press (v.1)). Late 古英语 had press "clothes press." 义为 "device for pressing cloth" 始于 14 世纪晚期, as is also the sense "device to squeeze juice from grapes, oil from olives, cider from apples, etc.," 源自 中古法语 presse. Specific sense "machine for printing" 始于 1530 年代; this was extended to publishing houses by 1570 年代 and to publishing generally (in phrases like freedom of the press) 源自 约 1680 年. This gradually shifted 约 1800 年-1820 年 to "periodical publishing, journalism." The press, 意为 "journalists collectively" 见于 1921 年 (though superseded by media 自 the rise of television, etc.). Press agent 始于 1873 年; press conference 见于 1931 年, though the thing itself dates to at least World War I. Press secretary 见于 1940 年. Via the sense "crowd, throng," 中古英语 in press meant "in public," a coincidental parallel to the modern phrase in the press. Weightlifting sense 始于 1908 年. The basketball defense so called 自 1959 年起 (in full-court press).

example.en: Reporters gathered outside the courthouse, waiting for the press to make a statement.
example.zh: 记者们聚集在法院外，等待媒体发表声明。

definitionLines: n. 压力，紧张；强制；压强
entries.definition: n. 压力，紧张；强制；压强 vt. 迫使
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "suffering, anguish; act or fact of pressing on the mind or heart," from Old French presseure "oppression; torture; anguish; press" (for wine or cheeses), "instrument of torture" (12c.) and directly from Latin pressura "action of pressing," from pressus, past participle of premere "to press" (see press (v.1)).

Literal meaning "act or fact of pressing" in a physical sense is attested from early 15c. Meaning "moral or mental coercing force" is from 1620s; meaning "urgency" is from 1812. Scientific sense in physics is from 1650s. Pressure cooker is attested from 1915; figurative sense is from 1958. Pressure point is attested from 1876. Pressure-treated, of woods, is from 1911.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "suffering, anguish; act or fact of pressing on the mind or heart," 源自 古法语 presseure "oppression; torture; anguish; press" (for wine or cheeses), "instrument of torture" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 pressura "action of pressing," 源自 pressus, 为 … 的过去分词 premere "to press" （参见 press (v.1)). Literal 意为 "act or fact of pressing" in a physical sense 见于 15 世纪初 义为 "moral or mental coercing force" 始于 1620 年代; 意为 "urgency" 始于 1812 年. Scientific sense in physics 始于 1650 年代. Pressure cooker 见于 1915 年; figurative sense 始于 1958 年. Pressure point 见于 1876 年. Pressure-treated, of woods, 始于 1911 年.

example.en: Young professionals often struggle with the pressure of meeting deadlines.
example.zh: 年轻职场人常常为赶截止日期的压力而苦恼。

entries.etymology: 1650s, "trick," from French prestige (16c.) "deceit, imposture, illusion" (in Modern French, "illusion, magic, glamour"), from Latin praestigium "delusion, illusion" (see prestigious). Derogatory until 19c.; sense of "dazzling influence" first applied 1815, to Napoleon.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "trick," 源自 法语 prestige (16 世纪) "deceit, imposture, illusion" (in 现代法语, "illusion, magic, glamour"), 源自 拉丁语 praestigium "delusion, illusion" （参见 prestigious). Derogatory until 19 世纪; 语义 "dazzling influence" first applied 1815 年, to Napoleon.

entries.definition: vt. 假定；推测 vi. 相信
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to take upon oneself, to take liberty," also "to take for granted, presuppose," especially overconfidently, from Old French presumer (12c.) and directly from Latin praesumere "anticipate," in Late Latin, "assume" (see presumption). Related: Presumed; presumedly; presuming.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to take upon oneself, to take liberty," also "to take for granted, presuppose," 尤指 overconfidently, 源自 古法语 presumer (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 praesumere "anticipate," in 晚期拉丁语, "assume" （参见 presumption). 同源词：Presumed; presumedly; presuming.

example.en: I presume you have already read the report before this meeting.
example.zh: 我推测你在这次会议前已经读过那份报告了。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to profess, assert, maintain" (a claim, etc.), "to direct (one's) efforts," from Old French pretendre "to lay claim," from Latin praetendere "stretch in front, put forward, allege," from prae "before" (see pre-) + tendere "to stretch," from PIE root *ten- "to stretch" (see tend).

Main modern sense of "feign, put forward a false claim" is recorded from c. 1400; the older sense of simply "to claim" is behind the string of royal pretenders (1690s) in English history. Meaning "to play, make believe" is recorded from 1865. In 17c. pretend also could mean "make a suit of marriage for," from a sense in French. Related: Pretended; pretending.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to profess, assert, maintain" (a claim, etc.), "to direct (one's) efforts," 源自 古法语 pretendre "to lay claim," 源自 拉丁语 praetendere "stretch in front, put forward, allege," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + tendere "to stretch," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ten- "to stretch" （参见 tend). Main modern 语义 "feign, put forward a false claim" 见于 约 1400 年; the older 语义 simply "to claim" is behind the string of royal pretenders (1690 年代) in English history. 义为 "to play, make believe" 见于 1865 年. In 17 世纪 pretend also could mean "make a suit of marriage for," 源自 a sense in 法语. 同源词：Pretended; pretending.

example.en: She pretended not to hear him, but her eyes gave her away.
example.zh: 她假装没听见他说话，但她的眼神出卖了她。

entries.definition: a.漂亮，俊俏 ad. 相当地
entries.etymology:
Old English prættig (West Saxon), pretti (Kentish), *prettig (Mercian) "cunning, skillful, artful, wily, astute," from prætt, *prett "a trick, wile, craft," from Proto-Germanic *pratt- (source also of Old Norse prettr "a trick," prettugr "tricky;" Frisian pret, Middle Dutch perte, Dutch pret "trick, joke," Dutch prettig "sportive, funny," Flemish pertig "brisk, clever"), of unknown origin.

Connection between Old English and Middle English words is uncertain, but if they are the same, meaning had shifted by c. 1400 to "manly, gallant," and later moved via "attractive, skillfully made," to "fine," to "beautiful in a slight way" (mid-15c.). Ironical use from 1530s. For sense evolution, compare nice, silly. Also used of bees (c. 1400). "After the OE. period the word is unknown till the 15th c., when it becomes all at once frequent in various senses, none identical with the OE., though derivable from it" [OED]. 

Meaning "not a few, considerable" is from late 15c. With a sense of "moderately," qualifying adjectives and adverbs, since 1560s. Pretty please as an emphatic plea is attested from 1902. A pretty penny "lot of money" is first recorded 1768.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 prættig (West Saxon), pretti (Kentish), *prettig (Mercian) "cunning, skillful, artful, wily, astute," 源自 prætt, *prett "a trick, wile, craft," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *pratt- (source also of 古北欧语 prettr "a trick," prettugr "tricky;" Frisian pret, Middle 荷兰语 perte, 荷兰语 pret "trick, joke," 荷兰语 prettig "sportive, funny," Flemish pertig "brisk, clever"), 来源不详. Connection between 古英语 and 中古英语 words is uncertain, but if they are the same, 意为 had shifted by 约 1400 年 to "manly, gallant," and later moved 经由 "attractive, skillfully made," to "fine," to "beautiful in a slight way" (15 世纪中期). Ironical use 源自 1530 年代. For sense evolution, 对比 nice, silly. Also used of bees (约 1400 年). "After the OE. period the word is unknown till the 15th c., when it becomes all at once frequent in various senses, none identical with the OE., though derivable from it" [OED]. 义为 "not a few, considerable" 始于 15 世纪晚期 With a 语义 "moderately," qualifying adjectives and adverbs, 自 1560 年代. Pretty please 作为 emphatic plea 见于 1902 年. A pretty penny "lot of money" is 首见于 1768 年.

definitionLines: vi. 取胜，占优势；流行，盛行
entries.definition: vi. 取胜，占优势；流行，盛行
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "be successful; be efficacious," from Old French prevaleir (Modern French prévaloir) and directly from Latin praevalere "be stronger, have greater power," from prae "before" (see pre-) + valere "have power, be strong" (see valiant). Spelling in English perhaps influenced by avail. Related: Prevailed; prevailing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "be successful; be efficacious," 源自 古法语 prevaleir (现代法语 prévaloir) and 直接源自 拉丁语 praevalere "be stronger, have greater power," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + valere "have power, be strong" （参见 valiant). Spelling in English 或许 influenced by avail. 同源词：Prevailed; prevailing.

example.en: A pessimistic mood seemed to prevail among the investors.
example.zh: 悲观情绪似乎在投资者中间普遍蔓延。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "having great power or force," from Latin praevalentem (nominative praevalens) "of superior strength; mighty," present participle of praevalere "to be more able" (see prevail). Meaning "extensively existing, in general use" is from 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "having great power or force," 源自 拉丁语 praevalentem (主格 praevalens) "of superior strength; mighty," 为 … 的现在分词 praevalere "to be more able" （参见 prevail). 义为 "extensively existing, in general use" 始于 1650 年代.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "act in anticipation of," from Latin praeventus, past participle of praevenire "come before, anticipate, hinder," in Late Latin also "to prevent," from prae "before" (see pre-) + venire "to come" (see venue). Originally literal; sense of "anticipate to hinder" was in Latin, but not recorded in English until 1540s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "act in anticipation of," 源自 拉丁语 praeventus, 为 … 的过去分词 praevenire "come before, anticipate, hinder," in 晚期拉丁语 also "to prevent," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + venire "to come" （参见 venue). Originally literal; 语义 "anticipate to hinder" was in 拉丁语, but not recorded in English until 1540 年代.

example.en: Wearing sunscreen daily can help prevent skin cancer caused by UV exposure.
example.zh: 每天涂防晒霜有助于预防紫外线照射引起的皮肤癌。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "action of stopping an event or practice," from Middle French prévention and directly from Late Latin praeventionem (nominative praeventio) "action of anticipating," noun of action from past participle stem of praevenire (see prevent).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "action of stopping an event or practice," 源自 中古法语 prévention and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 praeventionem (主格 praeventio) "action of anticipating," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of praevenire （参见 prevent).

example.en: Regular exercise is key to the prevention of many chronic diseases.
example.zh: 定期锻炼是预防许多慢性疾病的关键。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin praevius "going before," from prae "before" (see pre-) + via "road" (see via). Related: Previously.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 praevius "going before," 源自 prae "before" （参见 pre-) + 经由 "road" （参见 经由). 同源词：Previously.

example.en: The previous owner of the building had renovated it extensively in the 1980s.
example.zh: 该建筑的前任业主曾在20世纪80年代对其进行大规模翻新。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, pris "value, worth; praise," later "cost, recompense, prize" (mid-13c.), from Old French pris "price, value, wages, reward," also "honor, fame, praise, prize" (Modern French prix), from Late Latin precium, from Latin pretium "reward, prize, value, worth," from PIE *pret-yo-, 
from root *per- (5) "to traffic in, to sell" (source also of Sanskrit aprata "without recompense, gratuitously;" Greek porne "prostitute," originally "bought, purchased," pernanai "to sell;" Lithuanian perku "I buy").

Praise, price, and prize began to diverge in Old French, with praise emerging in Middle English by early 14c. and prize being evident by late 1500s with the rise of the -z- spelling. Having shed the extra Old French and Middle English senses, the word now again has the base sense of the Latin original. To set (or put) a price on someone, "offer a reward for capture" is from 1766.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, pris "value, worth; praise," later "cost, recompense, prize" (13 世纪中期), 源自 古法语 pris "price, value, wages, reward," also "honor, fame, praise, prize" (现代法语 prix), 源自 晚期拉丁语 precium, 源自 拉丁语 pretium "reward, prize, value, worth," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *pret-yo-, 源自 root *per- (5) "to traffic in, to sell" (source also of 梵语 aprata "without recompense, gratuitously;" 希腊语 porne "prostitute," 原义为 "bought, purchased," pernanai "to sell;" Lithuanian perku "I buy"). Praise, price, and prize began to diverge in 古法语, with praise emerging in 中古英语 by 14 世纪初 and prize being evident by late 1500 年代 with the rise of the -z- spelling. Having shed the extra 古法语 and 中古英语 senses, the word 现在 again has the base 语义 the 拉丁语 original. To set (or put) a price on someone, "offer a reward for capture" 始于 1766 年.

example.en: The price of imported goods rose sharply due to new tariffs.
example.zh: 由于新关税，进口商品的价格急剧上涨。

definitionLines: n. 骄傲，自豪，白满；自尊心； 引以 豪的东西
entries.definition: n. 骄傲，自豪，白满；自尊心； 引以 豪的东西 vt. 使自豪，使自夸
entries.etymology: late Old English pryto, Kentish prede, Mercian pride "pride, haughtiness, pomp," from prud (see proud). There is debate whether Scandinavian cognates (Old Norse pryði, Old Swedish prydhe , Danish pryd, etc.) are borrowed from Old French (from Germanic) or from Old English. Meaning "that which makes a person or people most proud" is from c. 1300. First applied to groups of lions late 15c., but not commonly so used until c. 1930. Paired with prejudice from 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 pryto, Kentish prede, Mercian pride "pride, haughtiness, pomp," 源自 prud （参见 proud). There is debate whether Scandinavian cognates (古北欧语 pryði, Old Swedish prydhe , Danish pryd, etc.) are 借自 古法语 (源自 日耳曼语) or 源自 古英语. 义为 "that which makes a person or people most proud" 始于 约 1300 年. First applied to groups of lions 15 世纪晚期, but not commonly so used until 约 1930 年. Paired with prejudice 源自 1610 年代.

example.en: She took pride in her children's achievements at school.
example.zh: 她为孩子们在学校取得的成就感到自豪。

entries.etymology:
Old English preost probably shortened from the older Germanic form represented by Old Saxon and Old High German prestar, Old Frisian prestere, all from Vulgar Latin *prester "priest," from Late Latin presbyter "presbyter, elder," from Greek presbyteros (see Presbyterian).

An alternative theory (to account for the -eo- of the Old English word) makes it cognate with Old High German priast, prest, from Vulgar Latin *prevost "one put over others," from Latin praepositus "person placed in charge," from past participle of praeponere (see provost). In Old Testament sense, a translation of Hebrew kohen, Greek hiereus, Latin sacerdos.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 preost 可能 shortened 源自 older 日耳曼语 form represented by 古撒克逊语 and 古高地德语 prestar, 古弗里西语 prestere, all 源自 通俗拉丁语 *prester "priest," 源自 晚期拉丁语 presbyter "presbyter, elder," 源自 希腊语 presbyteros （参见 Presbyterian). An alternative theory (to account for the -eo- of the 古英语 word) makes it 与 … 同源 古高地德语 priast, prest, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *prevost "one put over others," 源自 拉丁语 praepositus "person placed in charge," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 praeponere （参见 provost). In Old Testament sense, a translation of 希伯来语 kohen, 希腊语 hiereus, 拉丁语 sacerdos.

example.en: The Catholic priest heard confession every Saturday morning at the small stone chapel.
example.zh: 这位天主教神父每周六上午在小石教堂为教徒听忏悔。

definitionLines: ad. 首先，起初；主要地；根本上
entries.definition: ad. 首先，起初；主要地；根本上

example.en: The report is primarily aimed at improving public health.
example.zh: 该报告主要旨在改善公众健康。

definitionLines: a.首要的，主要的，基本的； 最初的，初级的
entries.definition: a.首要的，主要的，基本的； 最初的，初级的
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "of the first order," from Latin primarius "of the first rank, chief, principal, excellent," from primus "first" (see prime (adj.)). Meaning "first in order" is from 1802. Primary color is first recorded 1610s (at first the seven of the spectrum, later the three from which others can be made); primary school is 1802, from French école primaire.
Related: Primarily.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "of the first order," 源自 拉丁语 primarius "of the first rank, chief, principal, excellent," 源自 primus "first" （参见 prime （形）). 义为 "first in order" 始于 1802 年. Primary color is 首见于 1610 年代 (at first the seven of the spectrum, later the three 源自 which others can be made); primary school is 1802 年, 源自 法语 école primaire. 同源词：Primarily.

example.en: Reducing carbon emissions is the primary objective of this international agreement.
example.zh: 减少碳排放是这项国际协议的首要目标。

definitionLines: n. 全盛时期；初期；青年
entries.definition: a.基本的；最好的；主要的 n. 全盛时期；初期；青年
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "first in order," from Latin primus "first, the first, first part," figuratively "chief, principal; excellent, distinguished, noble" (source also of Italian and Spanish primo), from pre-Italic *prismos, superlative of PIE *preis- "before," from root *per- (1) "beyond, forward, through" (see per).

Meaning "first in importance" is from 1610s in English; that of "first-rate" is from 1620s. Arithmetical sense (as in prime number) is from 1560s; prime meridian is from 1878. Prime time originally (c. 1500) meant "spring time;" broadcasting sense of "peak tuning-in period" is attested from 1961.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "first in order," 源自 拉丁语 primus "first, the first, first part," figuratively "chief, principal; excellent, distinguished, noble" (source also of 意大利语 and 西班牙语 primo), 源自 pre-Italic *prismos, superlative of 原始印欧语 (PIE) *preis- "before," 源自 root *per- (1) "beyond, forward, through" （参见 per). 义为 "first in importance" 始于 1610 年代 in English; that of "first-rate" 始于 1620 年代. Arithmetical sense (as in prime number) 始于 1560 年代; prime meridian 始于 1878 年. Prime time 原义为 (约 1500 年) meant "spring time;" broadcasting 语义 "peak tuning-in period" 见于 1961 年.

example.en: He retired when he was still in the prime of his career.
example.zh: 他在事业仍处于巅峰时期就退休了。

definitionLines: a. 原始的，远古的；粗糙的， 简单的
entries.definition: a. 原始的，远古的；粗糙的， 简单的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "of an original cause; of a thing from which something is derived; not secondary" (a sense now associated with primary), from Old French primitif "very first, original" (14c.) and directly from Latin primitivus "first or earliest of its kind," from primitus "at first," from primus "first" (see prime (adj.)).

Meaning "of or belonging to the first age" is from early 15c. Meaning "having the style of an early or ancient time" is from 1680s. In Christian sense of "adhering to the qualities of the early Church" it is recorded from 1680s. Of untrained artists from 1942. Related: Primitively.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "of an original cause; of a thing from which something is derived; not secondary" (a sense 现在 associated with primary), 源自 古法语 primitif "very first, original" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 primitivus "first or earliest of its kind," 源自 primitus "at first," 源自 primus "first" （参见 prime （形）). 义为 "of or belonging to the first age" 始于 15 世纪初 义为 "having the style of an early or ancient time" 始于 1680 年代. In Christian 语义 "adhering to the qualities of the early Church" it 见于 1680 年代. Of untrained artists 自 1942 年起. 同源词：Primitively.

example.en: The tribe lived in primitive shelters made of wood and leaves.
example.zh: 这个部落住在用木头和树叶搭建的原始棚屋里。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "ruler of a principality" (mid-12c. as a surname), from Old French prince "prince, noble lord" (12c.), from Latin princeps (genitive principis) "first man, chief leader; ruler, sovereign," noun use of adjective meaning "that takes first," from primus "first" (see prime (adj.)) + root of capere "to take" (see capable). German cognate fürst, from Old High German furist "first," is apparently an imitation of the Latin formation. Colloquial meaning "admirable or generous person" is from 1911, American English. Prince Regent was the title of George, Prince of Wales (later George VI) during the mental incapacity of George III (1811-1820).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "ruler of a principality" (12 世纪中期 作为 surname), 源自 古法语 prince "prince, noble lord" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 princeps (属格 principis) "first man, chief leader; ruler, sovereign," 为 … 的名词用法 形容词 意为 "that takes first," 源自 primus "first" （参见 prime （形）) + root of capere "to take" （参见 capable). 德语 同源 fürst, 源自 古高地德语 furist "first," is 似乎 an imitation of the 拉丁语 formation. Colloquial 意为 "admirable or generous person" 始于 1911 年, American English. Prince Regent was the title of George, Prince of Wales (later George VI) during the mental incapacity of George III (1811 年-1820 年).

entries.etymology: late 14c., "woman of royal or noble birth; daughter or wife of a ruler or prince; female ruler," a native formation, or else from Old French princesse, fem. of prince (see prince). Compare Medieval Latin principissa, Italian principessa. As a colloquial form of address to a woman or girl, it is recorded from 1924 (as a term of address to a lover, early 15c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "woman of royal or noble birth; daughter or wife of a ruler or prince; female ruler," a 本族 formation，或else 源自 古法语 princesse, fem. of prince （参见 prince). 对比 中古拉丁语 principissa, 意大利语 principessa. 作为 口语 form of address to a woman or girl, it 见于 1924 年 (作为 term of address to a lover, 15 世纪初).

definitionLines: a. 最重要的，主要的，首要的
n. 负责人，校长；资本，本金
entries.definition: a. 最重要的，主要的，首要的 n. 负责人，校长；资本，本金
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "main, principal, chief, dominant, most important;" also "great, large," from Old French principal "main, most important," of persons, "princely, high-ranking" (11c.), from Latin principalis "first in importance; original, primitive," from princeps "first man, chief, leader" (see prince).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "main, principal, chief, dominant, most important;" also "great, large," 源自 古法语 principal "main, most important," of persons, "princely, high-ranking" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 principalis "first in importance; original, primitive," 源自 princeps "first man, chief, leader" （参见 prince).

example.en: The principal challenge facing the company is reducing its carbon footprint.
example.zh: 该公司面临的主要挑战是减少碳足迹。

definitionLines: n. 原理，原则；主义，信念
entries.definition: n. 原理，原则；主义，信念
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "origin, source, beginning; rule of conduct; axiom, basic assumption; elemental aspect of a craft or discipline," from Anglo-French principle, Old French principe "origin, cause, principle," from Latin principium (plural principia) "a beginning, commencement, origin, first part," in plural "foundation, elements," from princeps (see prince). Used absolutely for (good or moral) principle from 1650s.
Scientific sense of "general law of nature" is recorded from 1802. The English -l- apparently is by analogy of participle, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "origin, source, beginning; rule of conduct; axiom, basic assumption; elemental aspect of a craft or discipline," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 principle, 古法语 principe "origin, cause, principle," 源自 拉丁语 principium (plural principia) "a beginning, commencement, origin, first part," in plural "foundation, elements," 源自 princeps （参见 prince). Used absolutely for (good or moral) principle 源自 1650 年代. Scientific 语义 "general law of nature" 见于 1802 年. The English -l- 似乎 is by analogy of participle, etc.

example.en: He refused to compromise on his core principles even under great pressure.
example.zh: 即使承受巨大压力，他也拒绝在核心原则上妥协。

definitionLines: v. 打印；印刷；出版；用印刷 体写
entries.definition: v. 打印；印刷；出版；用印刷 体写 n. 印刷品，字体
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "impression, mark" (as by a stamp or seal), from Old French preinte "impression," noun use of fem. past participle of preindre "to press, crush," altered from prembre, from Latin premere "to press" (see press (v.1)). The Old French word also was borrowed into Middle Dutch (prente, Dutch prent) and other Germanic languages.

Meaning "printed lettering" is from 1620s; print-hand "print-like handwriting" is from 1658. Sense of "picture or design from a block or plate" is first attested 1660s. Meaning "piece of printed cloth" is from 1756. In Middle English, stigmata were called precious prentes of crist; to perceiven the print of sight was "to feel (someone's) gaze." Out of print "no longer to be had from the publisher" is from 1670s (to be in print is recorded from late 15c.). Print journalism attested from 1962.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "impression, mark" (as by a stamp or seal), 源自 古法语 preinte "impression," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 preindre "to press, crush," altered 源自 prembre, 源自 拉丁语 premere "to press" （参见 press (v.1)). The 古法语 word also was borrowed into Middle 荷兰语 (prente, 荷兰语 prent) and other 日耳曼语 languages. 义为 "printed lettering" 始于 1620 年代; print-hand "print-like handwriting" 始于 1658 年. 义为 "picture or design from a block or plate" is 最早见于 1660 年代. 义为 "piece of printed cloth" 始于 1756 年. In 中古英语, stigmata were called precious prentes of crist; to perceiven the print of sight was "to feel (someone's) gaze." Out of print "no longer to be had from the publisher" 始于 1670 年代 (to be in print 见于 15 世纪晚期). Print journalism attested 自 1962 年起.

example.en: The magazine decided to print the recipe on the back cover for easy reference.
example.zh: 杂志决定把食谱印在封底，方便读者参考。

example.en: The printer ran out of ink right before the meeting.
example.zh: 打印机在会议前夕没墨了。

entries.etymology: "earlier," 1714, from Latin prior "former, previous, first;" figuratively "superior, better;" as a noun "forefather; superior rank;" comparative of Old Latin pri "before," from PIE *prai-, *prei-, from root *per- (1) "forward, through" (see per).
entries.etymologyZh: "earlier," 1714 年, 源自 拉丁语 prior "former, previous, first;" figuratively "superior, better;" 作名词时 "forefather; superior rank;" comparative of Old 拉丁语 pri "before," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *prai-, *prei-, 源自 root *per- (1) "forward, through" （参见 per).

example.en: You must get approval prior to starting construction.
example.zh: 在开始施工之前，你必须获得批准。

entries.etymology: early 12c., from Old French prisoun "captivity, imprisonment; prison; prisoner, captive" (11c., Modern French prison), altered (by influence of pris "taken;" see prize (n.2)) from earlier preson, from Vulgar Latin *presionem, from Latin prensionem (nominative prensio), shortening of prehensionem (nominative *prehensio) "a taking," noun of action from past participle stem of prehendere "to take" (see prehensile). "Captivity," hence by extension "a place for captives," the main modern sense.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, 源自 古法语 prisoun "captivity, imprisonment; prison; prisoner, captive" (11 世纪, 现代法语 prison), altered (by influence of pris "taken;" 参见 prize (n.2)) 源自 earlier preson, 源自 通俗拉丁语 *presionem, 源自 拉丁语 prensionem (主格 prensio), shortening of prehensionem (主格 *prehensio) "a taking," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of prehendere "to take" （参见 prehensile). "Captivity," hence by extension "a place for captives," the main modern sense.

example.en: He was sentenced to three years in prison for the theft.
example.zh: 他因盗窃罪被判处三年监禁。

entries.etymology: "person in prison, captive person," late 14c. (earlier "a jailer," mid-13c., but this did not survive Middle English), from Old French prisonier "captive, hostage" (12c., Modern French prisonnier), from prisoun (see prison (n.)). Captives taken in war have been called prisoners since mid-14c.; phrase prisoner of war dates from 1670s (see also POW). Prisoner's dilemma attested from 1957.
entries.etymologyZh: "person in prison, captive person," 14 世纪晚期 (earlier "a jailer," 13 世纪中期, but this did not survive 中古英语), 源自 古法语 prisonier "captive, hostage" (12 世纪, 现代法语 prisonnier), 源自 prisoun （参见 prison （名）). Captives taken in war have been called prisoners 自 14 世纪中期; phrase prisoner of war dates 源自 1670 年代 （亦参见 POW). Prisoner's dilemma attested 自 1957 年起.

example.en: The prisoner was released after serving ten years in jail.
example.zh: 这名囚犯服刑十年后获释。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "a private matter, a secret;" c. 1600 as "seclusion," from private (adj.) + -cy. Meaning "state of freedom from intrusion" is from 1814. Earlier was privatie (late 14c. as "secret, mystery;" c. 1400 as "a secret, secret deed; solitude, privacy"), from Old French privauté.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "a private matter, a secret;" 约 1600 年 as "seclusion," 源自 private （形） + -cy. 义为 "state of freedom from intrusion" 始于 1814 年. Earlier was privatie (14 世纪晚期 as "secret, mystery;" 约 1400 年 as "a secret, secret deed; solitude, privacy"), 源自 古法语 privauté.

example.en: Sharing someone's medical records without consent is a serious invasion of privacy.
example.zh: 未经同意分享他人医疗记录是对隐私的严重侵犯。

definitionLines: a.私人的，私有的，私立的； 秘密的，私下的
entries.definition: a.私人的，私有的，私立的； 秘密的，私下的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "pertaining or belonging to oneself, not shared, individual; not open to the public;" of a religious rule, "not shared by Christians generally, distinctive; from Latin privatus "set apart, belonging to oneself (not to the state), peculiar, personal," used in contrast to publicus, communis; past participle of privare "to separate, deprive," from privus "one's own, individual," from PIE *prei-wo-, from PIE *prai-, *prei-, from root *per- (1) "forward, through" (see per).

Old English in this sense had syndrig. Private grew popular 17c. as an alternative to common (adj.), which had overtones of condescension. Of persons, "not holding public office," recorded from early 15c. In private "privily" is from 1580s. Related: Privately. Private school is from 1650s. Private parts "the pudenda" is from 1785. Private enterprise first recorded 1797; private property by 1680s; private sector is from 1948. Private eye "private detective" is recorded from 1938, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "pertaining or belonging to oneself, not shared, individual; not open to the public;" of a religious rule, "not shared by Christians generally, distinctive; from Latin privatus "set apart, belonging to oneself (not to the state), peculiar, personal," used in contrast to publicus, communis; past participle of privare "to separate, deprive," from privus "one's own, individual," from PIE *prei-wo-, from PIE *prai-, *prei-, from root *per- (1) "forward, through" (see per). Old English in this sense had syndrig. Private grew popular 17c. as an alternative to common (adj.), which had overtones of condescension. Of persons, "not holding public office," recorded from early 15c. In private "privily" is from 1580s. Related: Privately. Private school is from 1650s. Private parts "the pudenda" is from 1785. Private enterprise first recorded 1797; private property by 1680s; private sector is from 1948. Private eye "private detective" 见于 1938 年, American English.

example.en: She kept her diary in a private drawer that no one else could open.
example.zh: 她把日记锁在一个别人无法打开的私密抽屉里。

definitionLines: vt. 给予优惠，给予特权
entries.definition: n. 优惠，特许，特权 vt. 给予优惠，给予特权
entries.etymology: early 14c., privilegen, "to invest with a privilege," from privilege (n.) and from Old French privilegier (13c.), from Medieval Latin privilegare, from Latin privilegium. Related: Privileged; priviledging.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, privilegen, "to invest with a privilege," 源自 privilege （名） and 源自 古法语 privilegier (13 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 privilegare, 源自 拉丁语 privilegium. 同源词：Privileged; priviledging.

example.en: Access to clean water should be a right, not a privilege.
example.zh: 获得清洁水源应该是一项权利，而不是特权。

definitionLines: a.有特别恩典的；享有特权的
entries.definition: a.有特别恩典的；享有特权的
entries.etymology: late 14c. of things; mid-15c. of persons, past participle adjective from privilege (v.).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 of things; 15 世纪中期 of persons, past participle 形容词 源自 privilege （动）.

example.en: Growing up with access to good schools, she felt privileged compared to others.
example.zh: 她在能接受优质教育的环境中长大，与他人相比，她感到自己是有特权的。

entries.definition: n. 奖，奖金，奖品 vt.珍视，珍惜
entries.etymology: "to estimate," 1580s, alteration of Middle English prisen "to prize, value" (late 14c.), from stem of Old French preisier "to praise" (see praise (v.)). Related: Prized; prizing.
entries.etymologyZh: "to estimate," 1580 年代, alteration of 中古英语 prisen "to prize, value" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 stem of 古法语 preisier "to praise" （参见 praise （动）). 同源词：Prized; prizing.

example.en: She won first prize at the international piano competition last year.
example.zh: 她去年在国际钢琴比赛中获得了一等奖。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "quality of being probable," from Old French probabilite (14c.) and directly from Latin probabilitatem (nominative probabilitas) "credibility, probability," from probabilis (see probable). Meaning "something likely to be true" is from 1570s; mathematical sense is from 1718.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "quality of being probable," 源自 古法语 probabilite (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 probabilitatem (主格 probabilitas) "credibility, probability," 源自 probabilis （参见 probable). 义为 "something likely to be true" 始于 1570 年代; mathematical sense 始于 1718 年.

example.en: There is a high probability that it will rain tomorrow, so bring an umbrella.
example.zh: 明天很可能会下雨，所以带把伞吧。

definitionLines: a.有希望的，可能的；也许， 大概
entries.definition: a.有希望的，可能的；也许， 大概
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French probable "provable, demonstrable" (14c.), from Latin probabilis "worthy of approval, pleasing, agreeable, acceptable; provable, that may be assumed to be believed, credible," from probare "to try, to test" (see prove). Probable cause as a legal term is attested from 1670s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 probable "provable, demonstrable" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 probabilis "worthy of approval, pleasing, agreeable, acceptable; provable, that may be assumed to be believed, credible," 源自 probare "to try, to test" （参见 prove). Probable cause 作为 legal term 见于 1670 年代.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "plausibly," from probable + -ly (2). As a general purpose qualifier, 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "plausibly," 源自 probable + -ly (2). 作为 general purpose qualifier, 1610 年代.

example.en: She probably missed the bus, which would explain why she's late.
example.zh: 她很可能错过了公交车，这可以解释为什么她迟到了。

definitionLines: vt. 穿刺；探查，查究，调查
entries.definition: n. 探针，探测器 vt. 穿刺；探查，查究，调查
entries.etymology: early 15c., "instrument for exploring wounds, etc.," also "an examination," from Medieval Latin proba "examination," in Late Latin "a test, proof," from Latin probare (see prove). Meaning "act of probing" is 1890, from the verb; figurative sense of "penetrating investigation" is from 1903. Meaning "small, unmanned exploratory craft" is attested from 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "instrument for exploring wounds, etc.," also "an examination," 源自 中古拉丁语 proba "examination," in 晚期拉丁语 "a test, proof," 源自 拉丁语 probare （参见 prove). 义为 "act of probing" is 1890 年, 源自 动词; figurative 语义 "penetrating investigation" 始于 1903 年. 义为 "small, unmanned exploratory craft" 见于 1953 年.

example.en: Investigators used an underwater camera to probe the wreck.
example.zh: 调查人员用水下摄像机探查这艘沉船。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "a difficult question proposed for solution," from Old French problème (14c.) and directly from Latin problema, from Greek problema "a task, that which is proposed, a question;" also "anything projecting, headland, promontory; fence, barrier;" also "a problem in geometry," literally "thing put forward," from proballein "propose," from pro "forward" (see pro-) + ballein "to throw" (see ballistics).

Meaning "a difficulty" is mid-15c. Mathematical sense is from 1560s in English. Problem child first recorded 1920. Phrase _______ problem in reference to a persistent and seemingly insoluble difficulty is attested at least from 1882, in Jewish problem. Response no problem "that is acceptable; that can be done without difficulty" is recorded from 1968.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a difficult question proposed for solution," 源自 古法语 problème (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 problema, 源自 希腊语 problema "a task, that which is proposed, a question;" also "anything projecting, headland, promontory; fence, barrier;" also "a problem in geometry," 字面义为 "thing put forward," 源自 proballein "propose," 源自 pro "forward" （参见 pro-) + ballein "to throw" （参见 ballistics). 义为 "a difficulty" is 15 世纪中期 Mathematical sense 始于 1560 年代 in English. Problem child 首见于 1920 年. Phrase _______ problem in reference to a persistent and seemingly insoluble difficulty is attested at least 自 1882 年起, in Jewish problem. Response no problem "that is acceptable; that can be done without difficulty" 见于 1968 年.

entries.etymology: 1610s, "fact or manner of proceeding," from French procédure "manner of proceeding" (c. 1200), from Old French proceder "to proceed" (see proceed). Meaning "method of conducting business in Parliament" is from 1839.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "fact or manner of proceeding," 源自 法语 procédure "manner of proceeding" (约 1200 年), 源自 古法语 proceder "to proceed" （参见 proceed). 义为 "method of conducting business in Parliament" 始于 1839 年.

example.en: Please follow the standard procedure when filing a formal complaint with HR.
example.zh: 向人力资源部门提交正式投诉时，请遵循标准程序。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to go on," also "to emanate from, result from," from Old French proceder (13c., Modern French procéder) and directly from Latin procedere (past participle processus) "go before, go forward, advance, make progress; come forward," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + cedere "to go" (see cede). Related: Proceeded; proceeding.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to go on," also "to emanate from, result from," 源自 古法语 proceder (13 世纪, 现代法语 procéder) and 直接源自 拉丁语 procedere (past participle processus) "go before, go forward, advance, make progress; come forward," 源自 pro- "forward" （参见 pro-) + cedere "to go" （参见 cede). 同源词：Proceeded; proceeding.

example.en: After the fire alarm was cleared, the surgery was allowed to proceed.
example.zh: 火警解除后，手术获准继续进行。

definitionLines: n. 进行；程序；事项；诉讼
entries.definition: n. 进行；程序；事项；诉讼
entries.etymology: 1510s, "action of going forward," verbal noun from proceed (v.). From 1550s as "what is done, conduct." Proceedings "records of the doings of a society" is attested by 1824.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "action of going forward," verbal 名词 源自 proceed （动）. From 1550 年代 as "what is done, conduct." Proceedings "records of the doings of a society" is attested 截至 1824 年.

definitionLines: n. 过程，历程；工序，工艺
entries.definition: n. 过程，历程；工序，工艺 vt. 加工，处理
entries.etymology:
early 14c., "fact of being carried on" (as in in process), from Old French proces "a journey; continuation, development; legal trial" (13c.) and directly from Latin processus "a going forward, advance, progress," from past participle stem of procedere "go forward" (see proceed).

Meaning "course or method of action" is from mid-14c.; sense of "continuous series of actions meant to accomplish some result" (the main modern sense) is from 1620s. Legal sense of "course of action of a suit at law" is attested from early 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "fact of being carried on" (as in in process), 源自 古法语 proces "a journey; continuation, development; legal trial" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 processus "a going forward, advance, progress," 源自 past participle stem of procedere "go forward" （参见 proceed). 义为 "course or method of action" 始于 14 世纪中期; 语义 "continuous series of actions meant to accomplish some result" (the main modern sense) 始于 1620 年代. Legal 语义 "course of action of a suit at law" 见于 14 世纪初

example.en: The process of making wine involves fermentation and careful temperature control.
example.zh: 酿酒的过程涉及发酵和细致的温度控制。

entries.etymology: late 14c., proclamen, from Latin proclamare "cry or call out," from pro- "forth" (see pro-) + clamare "to cry out" (see claim (v.)). Spelling altered by influence of claim. Related: Proclaimed; proclaiming; proclaimer.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, proclamen, 源自 拉丁语 proclamare "cry or call out," 源自 pro- "forth" （参见 pro-) + clamare "to cry out" （参见 claim （动）). Spelling altered by influence of claim. 同源词：Proclaimed; proclaiming; proclaimer.

example.en: The president proclaimed a national emergency after the earthquake.
example.zh: 地震后，总统宣告进入全国紧急状态。

definitionLines: vt. 生产，制造，产生；显示， 出示；上演，演出
entries.definition: vt. 生产，制造，产生；显示， 出示；上演，演出 n. 农产品
entries.etymology: early 15c., "develop, proceed, extend," from Latin producere "lead or bring forth, draw out," figuratively "to promote, empower; stretch out, extend," from pro- "forth" (see pro-) + ducere "to bring, lead" (see duke). Sense of "bring into being" is first recorded 1510s; that of "put (a play) on stage" is from 1580s. Related: Produced; producing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "develop, proceed, extend," 源自 拉丁语 producere "lead or bring forth, draw out," figuratively "to promote, empower; stretch out, extend," 源自 pro- "forth" （参见 pro-) + ducere "to bring, lead" （参见 duke). 义为 "bring into being" is 首见于 1510 年代; that of "put (a play) on stage" 始于 1580 年代. 同源词：Produced; producing.

example.en: This factory can produce up to 5,000 units of the product each day.
example.zh: 这家工厂每天最多能生产5,000件产品。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "mathematical quantity obtained by multiplication," from Medieval Latin productum, in classical Latin "something produced," noun use of neuter past participle of producere "bring forth" (see produce (v.)). General sense of "anything produced" is attested in English from 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "mathematical quantity obtained by multiplication," 源自 中古拉丁语 productum, in classical 拉丁语 "something produced," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的过去分词 producere "bring forth" （参见 produce （动）). General 语义 "anything produced" is 见于 English 源自 1570 年代.

example.en: This company launched a new product that quickly became a bestseller.
example.zh: 这家公司推出了一款新产品，迅速成为畅销品。

definitionLines: n. 生产，产量；产品，作品
entries.definition: n. 生产，产量；产品，作品
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "a coming into being," from Old French production "production, exhibition" (13c.) and directly from Medieval Latin productionem (nominative productio), from past participle stem of Latin producere "bring forth" (see produce (v.)). Meaning "that which is produced" is mid-15c. Colloquial sense of "fuss, commotion" is from 1941, transferred from meaning "theatrical performance" (1894).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "a coming into being," 源自 古法语 production "production, exhibition" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 productionem (主格 productio), 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 producere "bring forth" （参见 produce （动）). 义为 "that which is produced" is 15 世纪中期 Colloquial 语义 "fuss, commotion" 始于 1941 年, transferred 源自 意为 "theatrical performance" (1894 年).

example.en: The factory doubled its production of steel within two years.
example.zh: 该工厂在两年内将钢铁产量翻了一番。

definitionLines: a.生产性的，生产的；能产的， 多产的
entries.definition: a.生产性的，生产的；能产的， 多产的
entries.etymology: 1610s, from French productif (16c.) and directly from Medieval Latin productivus "fit for production," from Latin product-, past participle stem of producere (see produce (v.)). Related: Productively; productiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 法语 productif (16 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 productivus "fit for production," 源自 拉丁语 product-, past participle stem of producere （参见 produce （动）). 同源词：Productively; productiveness.

example.en: Working from home made her more productive than she had expected.
example.zh: 居家办公让她的工作效率比预期的更高。

entries.etymology: 1809, "quality of being productive," from productive + -ity. An earlier word for this was productiveness (1727). Economic sense of "rate of output per unit" is from 1899.
entries.etymologyZh: 1809 年, "quality of being productive," 源自 productive + -ity. An earlier word for this was productiveness (1727 年). Economic 语义 "rate of output per unit" 始于 1899 年.

example.en: Automation has significantly boosted factory productivity over the past decade.
example.zh: 过去十年间，自动化大幅提升了工厂的生产率。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "vows taken upon entering a religious order," from Old French profession (12c.), from Latin professionem (nominative professio) "public declaration," from past participle stem of profiteri "declare openly" (see profess). Meaning "any solemn declaration" is from mid-14c. Meaning "occupation one professes to be skilled in" is from early 15c.; meaning "body of persons engaged in some occupation" is from 1610; as a euphemism for "prostitution" (compare oldest profession) it is recorded from 1888.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "vows taken upon entering a religious order," 源自 古法语 profession (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 professionem (主格 professio) "public declaration," 源自 past participle stem of profiteri "declare openly" （参见 profess). 义为 "any solemn declaration" 始于 14 世纪中期 义为 "occupation one professes to be skilled in" 始于 15 世纪初; 意为 "body of persons engaged in some occupation" 始于 1610 年; 作为 euphemism for "prostitution" (对比 oldest profession) it 见于 1888 年.

example.en: Medicine is a highly respected profession that requires years of training.
example.zh: 医学是一门需要多年培训、备受尊敬的专业职业。

entries.definition: a.职业的，专门的 n. 专业人员
entries.etymology: early 15c., of religious orders; 1747 of careers (especially of the skilled or learned trades from c. 1793); see profession. In sports, opposed to amateur, from 1846. Related: Professionally.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, of religious orders; 1747 年 of careers (尤指 of the skilled or learned trades 源自 约 1793 年); 参见 profession. In sports, opposed to amateur, 自 1846 年起. 同源词：Professionally.

example.en: They hired a professional chef trained in France to run the hotel kitchen.
example.zh: 他们聘请了一位在法国受过培训的专业厨师来掌管酒店厨房。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "one who teaches a branch of knowledge," from Old French professeur (14c.) and directly from Latin professor "person who professes to be an expert in some art or science; teacher of highest rank," agent noun from profiteri "lay claim to, declare openly" (see profess). As a title prefixed to a name, it dates from 1706. Short form prof is recorded from 1838.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "one who teaches a branch of knowledge," 源自 古法语 professeur (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 professor "person who professes to be an expert in some art or science; teacher of highest rank," agent 名词 源自 profiteri "lay claim to, declare openly" （参见 profess). 作为 title prefixed to a name, it dates 自 1706 年起. Short form prof 见于 1838 年.

entries.etymology: 1540s, probably from -cy + Latin proficientem (nominative proficiens), present participle of proficere "accomplish, make progress; be useful, do good; have success, profit," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + root of facere "to make, do" (see factitious).
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 可能 源自 -cy + 拉丁语 proficientem (主格 proficiens), 为 … 的现在分词 proficere "accomplish, make progress; be useful, do good; have success, profit," 源自 pro- "forward" （参见 pro-) + root of facere "to make, do" （参见 factitious).

entries.definition: n. 收益，利润，益处 v. 得利，获益
entries.etymology: mid-13c., "income;" c. 1300, "benefit, advantage;"from Old French prufit, porfit "profit, gain" (mid-12c.), from Latin profectus "profit, advance, increase, success, progress," noun use of past participle of proficere (see proficiency). As the opposite of loss, it replaced Old English gewinn. Profit margin attested from 1853.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "income;" 约 1300 年, "benefit, advantage;"源自 古法语 prufit, porfit "profit, gain" (12 世纪中期), 源自 拉丁语 profectus "profit, advance, increase, success, progress," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 proficere （参见 proficiency). As the opposite of loss, it replaced 古英语 gewinn. Profit margin attested 自 1853 年起.

example.en: The new product line helped the company profit significantly last quarter.
example.zh: 新产品线帮助公司上季度显著获利。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "yielding benefit, useful," from profit (v.) + -able or from Old French profitable, porfitable. Specific sense of "money-making" is attested from 1758. Related: Profitably.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "yielding benefit, useful," 源自 profit （动） + -able or 源自 古法语 profitable, porfitable. Specific 语义 "money-making" 见于 1758 年. 同源词：Profitably.

example.en: The new product line proved highly profitable within its first quarter.
example.zh: 新产品线在第一个季度就证明了其高度盈利性。

definitionLines: a. 深厚的；意义深远的
n. 计划，规划，大纲；节目，节目
entries.definition: a. 深厚的；意义深远的 program（me） n. 计划，规划，大纲；节目，节目
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "characterized by intellectual depth," from Old French profund (12c., Modern French profond), from Latin profundus "deep, bottomless, vast," also "obscure; profound; immoderate," from pro- "forth" (see pro-) + fundus "bottom" (see fund (n.)). The literal and figurative senses both were in Latin, but English, having already deep, employed this word primarily in its figurative sense. Related: Profoundly.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "characterized by intellectual depth," 源自 古法语 profund (12 世纪, 现代法语 profond), 源自 拉丁语 profundus "deep, bottomless, vast," also "obscure; profound; immoderate," 源自 pro- "forth" （参见 pro-) + fundus "bottom" （参见 fund （名）). The literal and figurative senses both were in 拉丁语, but English, having already deep, employed this word primarily in its figurative sense. 同源词：Profoundly.

example.en: Reading that novel had a profound effect on how she viewed the world.
example.zh: 阅读那部小说对她看待世界的方式产生了深远的影响。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "a going on, action of walking forward," from Old French progres (Modern French progrès), from Latin progressus "a going forward," from past participle of progredi (see progression).

In early use in English especially "a state journey by royalty." Figurative sense of "growth, development, advancement to higher stages" is from c. 1600. To be in progress "underway" is attested by 1849. Progress report attested by 1865.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a going on, action of walking forward," 源自 古法语 progres (现代法语 progrès), 源自 拉丁语 progressus "a going forward," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 progredi （参见 progression). In early use in English 尤指 "a state journey by royalty." Figurative 语义 "growth, development, advancement to higher stages" 始于 约 1600 年. To be in progress "underway" is attested 截至 1849 年. Progress report attested 截至 1865 年.

example.en: The team has made significant progress in developing the new software.
example.zh: 该团队在开发新软件方面取得了显著进展。

entries.etymology:
c. 1600, "characterized by advancement" (in action, character, etc.), from progress (n.) + -ive, or else from French progressif, from past participle stem of Latin progredi. Of taxation, from 1889; of jazz, from 1947. Meaning "characterized by striving for change and innovation, avant-garde, liberal" is from 1908.

In the socio-political sense "favoring reform; radically liberal," it emerged in various British contexts from the 1880s; in the U.S. it was active as a movement in the 1890s and a generation thereafter, the name being taken again from time to time, most recently by some more liberal Democrats and other social activists, by c. 2000. The noun in the sense "one who favors social and political change in the name of progress" is first attested 1865 (originally in Christianity). Earlier in a like sense were progressionist (1849, adjective; 1884, noun), progressist (1848). Related: Progressively; progressiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "characterized by advancement" (in action, character, etc.), 源自 progress （名） + -ive，或else 源自 法语 progressif, 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 progredi. Of taxation, 自 1889 年起; of jazz, 自 1947 年起. 义为 "characterized by striving for change and innovation, avant-garde, liberal" 始于 1908 年. In the socio-political sense "favoring reform; radically liberal," it emerged in various British contexts 源自 1880 年代; in the U.S. it was active 作为 movement in the 1890 年代 and a generation thereafter, the name being taken again 源自 time to time, most recently by some more liberal Democrats and other social activists, by 约 2000 年. The 名词 in the sense "one who favors social and political change in the name of progress" is 最早见于 1865 年 (原义为 in Christianity). Earlier in a like sense were progressionist (1849 年, 形容词; 1884 年, 名词), progressist (1848 年). 同源词：Progressively; progressiveness.

example.en: The school adopted a progressive approach to teaching that emphasized creativity.
example.zh: 这所学校采用了一种强调创造力的进步教学方法。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin prohibitus, past participle of prohibere "to hold back, restrain" (see prohibition). Related: Prohibited; prohibiting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 prohibitus, 为 … 的过去分词 prohibere "to hold back, restrain" （参见 prohibition). 同源词：Prohibited; prohibiting.

example.en: The school rules prohibit students from using phones during class.
example.zh: 学校规定禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。

definitionLines: vt.设计，规划；投射；放映；使 突出
entries.definition: n.计划，方案；工程，项目 vt.设计，规划；投射；放映；使 突出
entries.etymology:
c. 1400, "a plan, draft, scheme," from Latin proiectum "something thrown forth," noun use of neuter of proiectus, past participle of proicere "stretch out, throw forth," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + combining form of iacere (past participle iactus) "to throw" (see jet (v.)).

Meaning "scheme, proposal, mental plan" is from c. 1600. Meaning "group of low-rent apartment buildings" first recorded 1935, American English, short for housing project (1932). Related: Projects. Project manager attested from 1913.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "a plan, draft, scheme," 源自 拉丁语 proiectum "something thrown forth," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of proiectus, 为 … 的过去分词 proicere "stretch out, throw forth," 源自 pro- "forward" （参见 pro-) + 构词形式 of iacere (past participle iactus) "to throw" （参见 jet （动）). 义为 "scheme, proposal, mental plan" 始于 约 1600 年. 义为 "group of low-rent apartment buildings" 首见于 1935 年, American English, short for housing project (1932 年). 同源词：Projects. Project manager attested 自 1913 年起.

example.en: The engineering team spent months planning the new bridge project.
example.zh: 工程团队花了数月时间规划新桥梁项目。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "one who forms a project," agent noun in Latin form from project (v.). In the optical, camera sense it is from 1884.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "one who forms a project," agent 名词 in 拉丁语 form 源自 project （动）. In the optical, camera sense it 始于 1884 年.

entries.etymology: early 15c., back-formation from prolongation or else from Old French prolonguer, porloignier (13c.), from Late Latin prolongare "to prolong, extend," from Latin pro- "forth" (see pro-) + longus "long" (adj.); see long (adj.). Related: Prolonged; prolonging; prolongable.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, back-formation 源自 prolongation or else 源自 古法语 prolonguer, porloignier (13 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 prolongare "to prolong, extend," 源自 拉丁语 pro- "forth" （参见 pro-) + longus "long" （形）; 参见 long （形）. 同源词：Prolonged; prolonging; prolongable.

definitionLines: a.突出的，显著的；杰出的； 卓越的
entries.definition: a.突出的，显著的；杰出的； 卓越的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "projecting, jutting out," from Latin prominentem (nominative prominens) "prominent," present participle of prominere "jut or stand out, be prominent, overhang," from pro- "before, forward" (see pro-) + -minere "project, jut out," which is related to mons "hill" (see mount (n.1)). Meaning "conspicuous" is from 1759; that of "notable, leading" is from 1849. Related: Prominently.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "projecting, jutting out," 源自 拉丁语 prominentem (主格 prominens) "prominent," 为 … 的现在分词 prominere "jut or stand out, be prominent, overhang," 源自 pro- "before, forward" （参见 pro-) + -minere "project, jut out," which is related to mons "hill" （参见 mount (n.1)). 义为 "conspicuous" 始于 1759 年; that of "notable, leading" 始于 1849 年. 同源词：Prominently.

example.en: The scientist's work on cancer research made her a prominent figure in medicine.
example.zh: 这位科学家在癌症研究方面的工作使她成为医学界的杰出人物。

definitionLines: vt. 答应，允诺；有……可能，有 希望
n. 承诺，诺言；希望，出息
entries.definition: vt. 答应，允诺；有……可能，有 希望 n. 承诺，诺言；希望，出息
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "a pledge, vow," from Old French promesse "promise, guarantee, assurance" (13c.) and directly from Latin promissum "a promise," noun use of neuter past participle of promittere "send forth; let go; foretell; assure beforehand, promise," from pro- "before" (see pro-) + mittere "to put, send" (see mission). The ground sense is "declaration made about the future, about some act to be done or not done."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "a pledge, vow," 源自 古法语 promesse "promise, guarantee, assurance" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 promissum "a promise," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的过去分词 promittere "send forth; let go; foretell; assure beforehand, promise," 源自 pro- "before" （参见 pro-) + mittere "to put, send" （参见 mission). The ground sense is "declaration made about the future, about some act to be done or not done."

example.en: He made a promise to call his parents every Sunday.
example.zh: 他承诺每个星期天都给父母打电话。

entries.etymology: "showing signs of future excellence," c. 1600, present participle adjective from promise (v.). Related: Promisingly.
entries.etymologyZh: "showing signs of future excellence," 约 1600 年, present participle 形容词 源自 promise （动）. 同源词：Promisingly.

example.en: She has a promising career ahead of her in medicine.
example.zh: 她在医学领域有着光明的前途。

definitionLines: w.提升，晋升；促进，增进， 助长
entries.definition: w.提升，晋升；促进，增进， 助长
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to advance (someone) to a higher grade or office," from Old French promoter and directly from Latin promotus, past participle of promovere "move forward, advance; cause to advance, push onward; bring to light, reveal," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + movere "to move" (see move (v.)). General sense of "to further the growth or progress of (anything)" is from 1510s. Related: Promoted; promoting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to advance (someone) to a higher grade or office," 源自 古法语 promoter and 直接源自 拉丁语 promotus, 为 … 的过去分词 promovere "move forward, advance; cause to advance, push onward; bring to light, reveal," 源自 pro- "forward" （参见 pro-) + movere "to move" （参见 move （动）). General 语义 "to further the growth or progress of (anything)" 始于 1510 年代. 同源词：Promoted; promoting.

example.en: Regular exercise helps promote both physical and mental well-being.
example.zh: 定期锻炼有助于促进身心健康。

definitionLines: n. 升级，晋级；宣传，推广
entries.definition: n. 升级，晋级；宣传，推广
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "advancement in rank or position," from Old French promocion "election, promotion" (14c., Modern French promotion) and directly from Latin promotionem (nominative promotio) "a moving forward," noun of action from past participle stem of promovere (see promote). Meaning "advertising, publicity" first recorded 1925.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "advancement in rank or position," 源自 古法语 promocion "election, promotion" (14 世纪, 现代法语 promotion) and 直接源自 拉丁语 promotionem (主格 promotio) "a moving forward," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of promovere （参见 promote). 义为 "advertising, publicity" 首见于 1925 年.

example.en: Hard work and dedication finally earned her a well-deserved promotion.
example.zh: 勤奋和专注终于为她赢得了当之无愧的晋升。

entries.definition: a.敏捷的，迅速的，即刻的 vt. 促使，推动
entries.etymology: mid-14c., prompten, from Latin promptus, past participle of promere "to bring forth," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + emere "to take" (see exempt (adj.)). Theatrical sense of "to assist a speaker with lines" is first recorded early 15c. Related: Prompted; prompting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, prompten, 源自 拉丁语 promptus, 为 … 的过去分词 promere "to bring forth," 源自 pro- "forward" （参见 pro-) + emere "to take" （参见 exempt （形）). Theatrical 语义 "to assist a speaker with lines" is 首见于 15 世纪初 同源词：Prompted; prompting.

example.en: The rising prices prompt consumers to seek cheaper alternatives.
example.zh: 价格上涨促使消费者寻找更便宜的替代品。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "naturally inclined to something, apt, liable," from Latin pronus "bent forward, leaning forward, bent over," figuratively "inclined to, disposed," perhaps from adverbial form of pro- "before, for, instead of" (see pro-) + ending as in infernus, externus. Meaning "lying face-down" is first recorded 1570s. Literal and figurative senses both were in Latin; figurative is older in English. Related: Proneness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "naturally inclined to something, apt, liable," 源自 拉丁语 pronus "bent forward, leaning forward, bent over," figuratively "inclined to, disposed," 或源自 adverbial form of pro- "before, for, instead of" （参见 pro-) + ending as in infernus, externus. 义为 "lying face-down" is 首见于 1570 年代. Literal and figurative senses both were in 拉丁语; figurative is older in English. 同源词：Proneness.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from pro- and noun; modeled on Middle French pronom, from Latin pronomen, from pro- "in place of" + nomen "name, noun" (see name (n.)). A loan-translation of Greek antonymia.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 pro- and 名词; modeled on 中古法语 pronom, 源自 拉丁语 pronomen, 源自 pro- "in place of" + nomen "name, noun" （参见 name （名）). A loan-translation of 希腊语 antonymia.

entries.etymology: early 14c., "to declare officially;" late 14c., "to speak, utter," from Old French prononcier "declare, speak out, pronounce" (late 13c., Modern French prononcer), from Late Latin pronunciare, from Latin pronuntiare "to proclaim, announce; pronounce, utter," from pro- "forth, out, in public" (see pro-) + nuntiare "announce," from nuntius "messenger" (see nuncio). With reference to the mode of sounding words or languages, it is attested from 1620s (but see pronunciation in this sense from early 15c.). Related: Pronounced; pronouncing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to declare officially;" 14 世纪晚期, "to speak, utter," 源自 古法语 prononcier "declare, speak out, pronounce" (13 世纪晚期, 现代法语 prononcer), 源自 晚期拉丁语 pronunciare, 源自 拉丁语 pronuntiare "to proclaim, announce; pronounce, utter," 源自 pro- "forth, out, in public" （参见 pro-) + nuntiare "announce," 源自 nuntius "messenger" （参见 nuncio). With reference to the mode of sounding words or languages, it 见于 1620 年代 (but 参见 pronunciation in this sense 源自 15 世纪初). 同源词：Pronounced; pronouncing.

example.en: She could not pronounce his last name correctly on the first try.
example.zh: 她第一次无法正确发出他的姓氏。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "mode in which a word is pronounced," from Middle French prononciation and directly from Latin pronuntiationem (nominative pronuntiatio) "act of speaking, utterance, delivery," also "proclamation, public declaration," noun of action from past participle stem of pronuntiare "announce" (see pronounce).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "mode in which a word is pronounced," 源自 中古法语 prononciation and 直接源自 拉丁语 pronuntiationem (主格 pronuntiatio) "act of speaking, utterance, delivery," also "proclamation, public declaration," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of pronuntiare "announce" （参见 pronounce).

entries.etymology:
early 13c., preove "evidence to establish the fact of (something)," from Anglo-French preove, Old French prueve "proof, test, experience" (13c., Modern French preuve), from Late Latin proba "a proof," a back-formation from Latin probare "to prove" (see prove). "The devocalization of v to f ensued upon the loss of final e; cf. the relation of v and f in believe, belief, relieve, relief, behove, behoof, etc. [OED].

Meaning "act of proving" is early 14c. Meaning "act of testing or making trial of anything" is from late 14c., from influence of prove. Meaning "standard of strength of distilled liquor" is from 1705. In photography from 1855. Typographical sense of "trial impression to test type" is from c. 1600. Numismatic sense of "coin struck to test a die" is from 1762; now mostly in reference to coins struck from highly polished dies, mainly for collectors.

Adjectival sense (proof against) is recorded from 1590s, from the noun in expressions such as proof of (mid-15c.), hence extended senses involving "tested power" in compounds such as fireproof (1630s), waterproof (1725), foolproof (1902), etc. Shakespeare has shame-proof. Expression the proof is in the pudding (1915) is a curious perversion of earlier proof of the pudding is in the eating (1708), with proof in the sense "quality of proving good or turning out well" (17c.); perhaps an advertiser's condensed form of the original.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, preove "evidence to establish the fact of (something)," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 preove, 古法语 prueve "proof, test, experience" (13 世纪, 现代法语 preuve), 源自 晚期拉丁语 proba "a proof," a back-formation 源自 拉丁语 probare "to prove" （参见 prove). "The devocalization of v to f ensued upon the loss of final e; cf. the relation of v and f in believe, belief, relieve, relief, behove, behoof, etc. [OED]. Meaning "act of proving" is early 14c. Meaning "act of testing or making trial of anything" is from late 14c., from influence of prove. Meaning "standard of strength of distilled liquor" is from 1705. In photography from 1855. Typographical sense of "trial impression to test type" is from c. 1600. Numismatic sense of "coin struck to test a die" is from 1762; now mostly in reference to coins struck from highly polished dies, mainly for collectors. Adjectival sense (proof against) is recorded from 1590s, from the noun in expressions such as proof of (mid-15c.), hence extended senses involving "tested power" in compounds such as fireproof (1630s), waterproof (1725), foolproof (1902), etc. Shakespeare has shame-proof. Expression the proof is in the pudding (1915) is a curious perversion of earlier proof of the pudding is in the eating (1708), with proof in the sense "quality of proving good or turning out well" (17 世纪); 或许 an advertiser's condensed form of the original.

example.en: The DNA test provided conclusive proof of his innocence.
example.zh: DNA检测提供了其清白的确凿证明。

entries.etymology: 1718, "committee of cardinals in charge of Catholic missionary work," short for Congregatio de Propaganda Fide "congregation for propagating the faith," a committee of cardinals established 1622 by Gregory XV to supervise foreign missions. The word is properly the ablative fem. gerundive of Latin propagare (see propagation). Hence, "any movement to propagate some practice or ideology" (1790). Modern political sense dates from World War I, not originally pejorative. Meaning "material or information propagated to advance a cause, etc." is from 1929.
entries.etymologyZh: 1718 年, "committee of cardinals in charge of Catholic missionary work," short for Congregatio de Propaganda Fide "congregation for propagating the faith," a committee of cardinals established 1622 年 by Gregory XV to supervise foreign missions. The word is properly the ablative fem. gerundive of 拉丁语 propagare （参见 propagation). Hence, "any movement to propagate some practice or ideology" (1790 年). 现代 political sense dates 源自 World War I, not 原义为 pejorative. 义为 "material or information propagated to advance a cause, etc." 始于 1929 年.

example.en: The regime relied on state propaganda to control public opinion.
example.zh: 该政权依靠国家宣传来控制舆论。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "to drive away, expel," from Latin propellere "push forward, drive forward, drive forth; move, impel," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + pellere "to push, drive" (see pulse (n.1)). Meaning "to drive onward, cause to move forward" is from 1650s. Related: Propelled; propelling.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "to drive away, expel," 源自 拉丁语 propellere "push forward, drive forward, drive forth; move, impel," 源自 pro- "forward" （参见 pro-) + pellere "to push, drive" （参见 pulse (n.1)). 义为 "to drive onward, cause to move forward" 始于 1650 年代. 同源词：Propelled; propelling.

definitionLines: a. 适当，恰当；特有的，固有的
entries.definition: a. 适当，恰当；特有的，固有的
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "adapted to some purpose, fit, apt; commendable, excellent" (sometimes ironic), from Old French propre "own, particular; exact, neat, fitting, appropriate" (11c.), from Latin proprius "one's own, particular to itself," from pro privo "for the individual, in particular," from ablative of privus "one's own, individual" (see private (adj.)) + pro "for" (see pro-). Related: Properly.

From early 14c. as "belonging or pertaining to oneself; individual; intrinsic;" from mid-14c. as "pertaining to a person or thing in particular, special, specific; distinctive, characteristic;" also "what is by the rules, correct, appropriate, acceptable." From early 15c. as "separate, distinct; itself." Meaning "socially appropriate, decent, respectable" is first recorded 1704. Proper name "name belonging to or relating to the person or thing in question," is from late 13c., a sense also preserved in astronomical proper motion (c. 1300). Proper noun is from c. 1500.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "adapted to some purpose, fit, apt; commendable, excellent" (有时 ironic), 源自 古法语 propre "own, particular; exact, neat, fitting, appropriate" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 proprius "one's own, particular to itself," 源自 pro privo "for the individual, in particular," 源自 ablative of privus "one's own, individual" （参见 private （形）) + pro "for" （参见 pro-). 同源词：Properly. From 14 世纪初 as "belonging or pertaining to oneself; individual; intrinsic;" 源自 14 世纪中期 as "pertaining to a person or thing in particular, special, specific; distinctive, characteristic;" also "what is by the rules, correct, appropriate, acceptable." From 15 世纪初 as "separate, distinct; itself." 义为 "socially appropriate, decent, respectable" is 首见于 1704 年. Proper name "name belonging to or relating to the person or thing in question," 始于 13 世纪晚期, a sense also preserved in astronomical proper motion (约 1300 年). Proper 名词 始于 约 1500 年.

example.en: Please wear proper clothing to the job interview tomorrow.
example.zh: 请明天参加工作面试时穿着得体的服装。

definitionLines: n. 财产，所有物；性质，特性
entries.definition: n. 财产，所有物；性质，特性
entries.etymology: c. 1300, properte, "nature, quality," later "possession, thing owned" (early 14c., a sense rare before 17c.), from an Anglo-French modification of Old French propriete "individuality, peculiarity; property" (12c., Modern French propreté; see propriety), from Latin proprietatem (nominative proprietas) "ownership, a property, propriety, quality," literally "special character" (a loan-translation of Greek idioma), noun of quality from proprius "one's own, special" (see proper). For "possessions, private property" Middle English sometimes used proper goods. Hot property "sensation, a success" is from 1947 in "Billboard" stories.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, properte, "nature, quality," later "possession, thing owned" (14 世纪初, a sense rare before 17 世纪), 源自 an 盎格鲁-法语 modification of 古法语 propriete "individuality, peculiarity; property" (12 世纪, 现代法语 propreté; 参见 propriety), 源自 拉丁语 proprietatem (主格 proprietas) "ownership, a property, propriety, quality," 字面义为 "special character" (a loan-translation of 希腊语 idioma), 名词 of quality 源自 proprius "one's own, special" （参见 proper). For "possessions, private property" 中古英语 有时 used proper goods. Hot property "sensation, a success" 始于 1947 年 in "Billboard" stories.

example.en: The company owns considerable property in the city center.
example.zh: 该公司在市中心拥有大量房产。

entries.etymology:
late 12c., "person who speaks for God; one who foretells, inspired preacher," from Old French prophete, profete "prophet, soothsayer" (11c., Modern French prophète) and directly from Latin propheta, from Greek prophetes (Doric prophatas) "an interpreter, spokesman," especially of the gods, "inspired preacher or teacher," from pro- "before" (see pro-) + root of phanai "to speak," from PIE *bha- (2) "speak" (see fame (n.)).

The Greek word was used in Septuagint for Hebrew nabj "soothsayer." Early Latin writers translated Greek prophetes with Latin vates, but the Latinized form propheta predominated in post-Classical times, chiefly due to Christian writers, probably because of pagan associations of vates. In English, meaning "prophetic writer of the Old Testament" is from late 14c. Non-religious sense is from 1848; used of Muhammad from 1610s (translating Arabic al-nabiy, and sometimes also al-rasul, properly "the messenger"). The Latin word is glossed in Old English by witga.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪晚期, "person who speaks for God; one who foretells, inspired preacher," 源自 古法语 prophete, profete "prophet, soothsayer" (11 世纪, 现代法语 prophète) and 直接源自 拉丁语 propheta, 源自 希腊语 prophetes (Doric prophatas) "an interpreter, spokesman," 尤指 of the gods, "inspired preacher or teacher," 源自 pro- "before" （参见 pro-) + root of phanai "to speak," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *bha- (2) "speak" （参见 fame （名）). The 希腊语 word was used in Septuagint for 希伯来语 nabj "soothsayer." Early 拉丁语 writers translated 希腊语 prophetes with 拉丁语 vates, but the Latinized form propheta predominated in post-Classical times, chiefly due to Christian writers, 可能 because of pagan associations of vates. In English, 意为 "prophetic writer of the Old Testament" 始于 14 世纪晚期 Non-religious sense 始于 1848 年; used of Muhammad 源自 1610 年代 (translating 阿拉伯语 al-nabiy, and 有时 also al-rasul, properly "the messenger"). The 拉丁语 word is glossed in 古英语 by witga.

definitionLines: n. 部分，份儿；比例，比重； 均衡，相称
entries.definition: n. 部分，份儿；比例，比重； 均衡，相称
entries.etymology: late 14c., "due relation of one part to another," also "size, extent; compartative relation in size, degree, number, etc.," from Old French proporcion "measure, proportion" (13c.), from Latin proportionem (nominative proportio) "comparative relation, analogy," from phrase pro portione "according to the relation" (of parts to each other), from pro "for" (see pro-) + ablative of *partio "division," related to pars (see part (n.)). Phrase out of proportion attested by 1670s.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French proposer "propose, advance, suggest" (12c.), from pro- "forth" (see pro-) + poser "put, place" (see pose (v.1)). entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "story, narration," from Old French prose (13c.), from Latin prosa oratio "straightforward or direct speech" (without the ornaments of verse), from prosa, fem. of prosus, earlier prorsus "straightforward, direct," from Old Latin provorsus "(moving) straight ahead," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + vorsus "turned," past participle of vertere "to turn" (see verse).

Meaning "prose writing; non-poetry" is from mid-14c. The sense of "dull or commonplace expression" is from 1680s, out of earlier sense "plain expression" (1560s). Those who lament the want of an English agent noun to correspond to poet might try prosaist (1776), proser (1620s), or Frenchified prosateur (1880), though the first two in their day also acquired in English the secondary sense "dull writer."

entries.etymology: early 15c., "follow up, pursue" (some course or action), from Latin prosecutus, past participle of prosequi "follow after, accompany; chase, pursue; attack, assail, abuse" (see pursue). Meaning "bring to a court of law" is first recorded 1570s. Meaning "go into detail" is from 1530s.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "act of looking into the distance," from Latin prospectus "distant view, look out; sight, faculty of sight," noun use of past participle of prospicere "look out on, look forward," from pro- "forward" (see pro-) + specere "look at" (see scope (n.1)). Meaning "extensive view of the landscape" is from 1530s; transferred sense of "mental view or survey" is from 1620s. Sense of "person or thing considered promising" is from 1922. Prospects "expectations, things looked forward to" is from 1660s.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from Old French prosprete (12c., Modern French prospérité) and directly from Latin prosperitatem (nominative prosperitas) "good fortune," from prosperus (see prosper).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 古法语 prosprete (12 世纪, 现代法语 prospérité) and 直接源自 拉丁语 prosperitatem (主格 prosperitas) "good fortune," 源自 prosperus （参见 prosper).

entries.etymology: early 15c., "tending to bring success," from prosper + -ous, or else from obsolete Middle French prospereus (15c.), from prosperer. The sense of "flourishing" is first recorded late 15c.

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Latin protectus, past participle of protegere "to protect, cover in front" (see protection). International economics sense from 1789. Related: Protected; protecting.
