example.zh: 请保留好您的收据，以备退货之用。

definitionLines: vt. 收到，接到；接待，接见；受 到，蒙受
entries.definition: vt. 收到，接到；接待，接见；受 到，蒙受
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old North French receivre (Old French recoivre) "seize, take hold of, pick up; welcome, accept," from Latin recipere "regain, take back, bring back, carry back, recover; take to oneself, take in, admit," from re- "back," though the exact sense here is obscure (see re-) + -cipere, comb. form of capere "to take" (see capable). Radio and (later) television sense is attested from 1908. Related: Received; receiving.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 Old North 法语 receivre (古法语 recoivre) "seize, take hold of, pick up; welcome, accept," 源自 拉丁语 recipere "regain, take back, bring back, carry back, recover; take to oneself, take in, admit," 源自 re- "back," though the exact sense here is obscure （参见 re-) + -cipere, comb. form of capere "to take" （参见 capable). Radio and (later) television sense 见于 1908 年. 同源词：Received; receiving.

example.en: The charity received thousands of donations after the disaster struck.
example.zh: 灾难发生后，该慈善机构收到了数千笔捐款。

definitionLines: n. 话筒，受话器；接待者，接受 者，收信人
entries.definition: n. 话筒，受话器；接待者，接受 者，收信人
entries.etymology: mid-14c. (mid-13c. as a surname), agent noun from receive, or from Old French recevere (Modern French receveur), agent noun from recievere. As a telephone apparatus, from 1877; in reference to a radio unit, from 1891; in U.S. football sense, from 1897.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期 (13 世纪中期 作为 surname), agent 名词 源自 receive，或源自 古法语 recevere (现代法语 receveur), agent 名词 源自 recievere. 作为 telephone apparatus, 自 1877 年起; in reference to a radio unit, 自 1891 年起; in U.S. football sense, 自 1897 年起.

example.en: She picked up the receiver and waited for the caller to speak.
example.zh: 她拿起话筒，等待来电者开口说话。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin recentem (nominative recens) "lately done or made, new, fresh, young," from re- (see re-) + PIE root *ken- (2) "fresh, new, young" (source also of Greek kainos "new;" Sanskrit kanina- "young;" Old Irish cetu- "first;" Old Church Slavonic načino "to begin," koni "beginning"). Related: Recently; recentness (1670s, but OED reports recency (1610s) was "Common in 19th c.").
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 recentem (主格 recens) "lately done or made, new, fresh, young," 源自 re- （参见 re-) + 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *ken- (2) "fresh, new, young" (source also of 希腊语 kainos "new;" 梵语 kanina- "young;" Old 爱尔兰语 cetu- "first;" Old Church Slavonic načino "to begin," koni "beginning"). 同源词：Recently; recentness (1670 年代, but OED reports recency (1610 年代) was "Common in 19th c.").

example.en: Scientists published recent findings on how sleep affects memory consolidation.
example.zh: 科学家们发表了关于睡眠如何影响记忆巩固的最新研究成果。

example.en: She recently returned from a six-month research trip and submitted her report yesterday.
example.zh: 她最近刚从为期六个月的研究之旅归来，昨天提交了报告。

definitionLines: n. 接见，接待，招待会；接受， 接收，接收效果
entries.definition: n. 接见，接待，招待会；接受， 接收，接收效果
entries.etymology: late 14c., in astrology, "effect of two planets on each other;" sense of "act of receiving" is recorded from late 15c., from Latin receptionem (nominative receptio) "a receiving," noun of action from past participle stem of recipere (see receive). Sense of "ceremonial gathering" is 1882, from French.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in astrology, "effect of two planets on each other;" 语义 "act of receiving" 见于 15 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 receptionem (主格 receptio) "a receiving," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of recipere （参见 receive). 义为 "ceremonial gathering" is 1882 年, 源自 法语.

example.en: The new policy received a warm reception from the business community.
example.zh: 新政策受到了商界的热烈欢迎。

entries.etymology:
"person hired to receive clients in an office," 1900, from reception + -ist.
Originally in photography studios.

Earlier as an adjective in theology and law (1867).
entries.etymologyZh: "person hired to receive clients in an office," 1900 年, 源自 reception + -ist. Originally in photography studios. Earlier 作形容词时 in theology and law (1867 年).

definitionLines: n. 退回，后退；（经济）衰退， 不景气
entries.definition: n. 退回，后退；（经济）衰退， 不景气
entries.etymology:
1640s, "act of receding, a going back," from French récession "a going backward, a withdrawing," and directly from Latin  recessionem (nominative recessio) "a going back," noun of action from past participle stem of recedere (see recede).

Sense of "temporary decline in economic activity," 1929, noun of action from recess (q.v.): Ayto notes, "There was more than a hint of euphemism in the coining of this term."
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "act of receding, a going back," 源自 法语 récession "a going backward, a withdrawing," and 直接源自 拉丁语 recessionem (主格 recessio) "a going back," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of recedere （参见 recede). 义为 "temporary decline in economic activity," 1929 年, 名词 of action 源自 recess (q.v.): Ayto notes, "There was more than a hint of euphemism in the coining of this term."

example.en: The country fell into a deep recession following the financial crisis.
example.zh: 金融危机后，该国陷入了严重的经济衰退。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "medical prescription," from Middle French récipé (15c.), from Latin recipe "take!," second person imperative singular of recipere "to take" (see receive); word written by physicians at the head of prescriptions. Figurative use from 1640s. Meaning "instructions for preparing food" first recorded 1743. The original sense survives only in the pharmacist's abbreviation Rx.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "medical prescription," 源自 中古法语 récipé (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 recipe "take!," second person imperative singular of recipere "to take" （参见 receive); word written by physicians at the head of prescriptions. Figurative use 源自 1640 年代. 义为 "instructions for preparing food" 首见于 1743 年. The original sense survives only in the pharmacist's abbreviation Rx.

example.en: She found a simple recipe for banana bread in an old cookbook.
example.zh: 她在一本旧食谱书里找到了一个简单的香蕉面包食谱。

entries.etymology: 1560s, with -al (1) + stem of Latin reciprocus "returning the same way, alternating," from pre-Latin *reco-proco-, from *recus (from re- "back;" see re-, + -cus, adjective formation) + *procus (from pro- "forward;" see pro-, + -cus. Related: Reciprocally. The noun meaning "that which is reciprocal" (to another) is from 1560s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, with -al (1) + stem of 拉丁语 reciprocus "returning the same way, alternating," 源自 pre-拉丁语 *reco-proco-, 源自 *recus (源自 re- "back;" 参见 re-, + -cus, 形容词 formation) + *procus (源自 pro- "forward;" 参见 pro-, + -cus. 同源词：Reciprocally. The 名词 意为 "that which is reciprocal" (to another) 始于 1560 年代.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French reciter (12c.) and directly from Latin recitare "read aloud, read out, repeat from memory, declaim," from re- "back, again" (see re-) + citare "to summon" (see cite). Related: Recited; reciting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 reciter (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 recitare "read aloud, read out, repeat from memory, declaim," 源自 re- "back, again" （参见 re-) + citare "to summon" （参见 cite). 同源词：Recited; reciting.

example.en: Students were asked to recite a short poem in front of the class.
example.zh: 学生们被要求在全班同学面前背诵一首短诗。

definitionLines: a. 鲁莽的，不顾后果的；粗心大 意的
entries.definition: a. 鲁莽的，不顾后果的；粗心大 意的
entries.etymology: Old English receleas "careless, thoughtless, heedless," earlier reccileas, from *rece, recce "care, heed," from reccan "to care" (see reck (v.)) + -less. The same affixed form is in German ruchlos, Dutch roekeloos "wicked." Root verb reck (Old English reccan) is passing into obscurity.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 receleas "careless, thoughtless, heedless," earlier reccileas, 源自 *rece, recce "care, heed," 源自 reccan "to care" （参见 reck （动）) + -less. The same affixed form is in 德语 ruchlos, 荷兰语 roekeloos "wicked." Root 动词 reck (古英语 reccan) is passing into obscurity.

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, recenen, from Old English gerecenian "to explain, relate, recount," from Proto-Germanic *(ga)rekenojan (source also of Old Frisian rekenia, Middle Dutch and Dutch rekenen, Old High German rehhanon, German rechnen, Gothic rahnjan "to count, reckon"), from Proto-Germanic *rakina- "ready, straightforward," from PIE *reg- "to move in a straight line," with derivatives meaning "direct in a straight line, rule" (see regal).

Intransitive sense "make a computation" is from c. 1300. In I reckon, the sense is "hold an impression or opinion," and the expression, used parenthetically, dates from c. 1600 and formerly was in literary use (Richardson, etc.), but came to be associated with U.S. Southern dialect and was regarded as provincial or vulgar. Related: Reckoned; reckoning.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, recenen, 源自 古英语 gerecenian "to explain, relate, recount," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *(ga)rekenojan (source also of 古弗里西语 rekenia, Middle 荷兰语 and 荷兰语 rekenen, 古高地德语 rehhanon, 德语 rechnen, Gothic rahnjan "to count, reckon"), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *rakina- "ready, straightforward," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *reg- "to move in a straight line," with derivatives 意为 "direct in a straight line, rule" （参见 regal). Intransitive sense "make a computation" 始于 约 1300 年. In I reckon, the sense is "hold an impression or opinion," and the expression, used parenthetically, dates 源自 约 1600 年 and formerly was in literary use (Richardson, etc.), but came to be associated with U.S. Southern dialect and was regarded as provincial or vulgar. 同源词：Reckoned; reckoning.

entries.etymology:
mid-15c., "knowledge of an event or incident; understanding," from Middle French recognition (15c.) and directly from Latin recognitionem (nominative recognitio) "a reviewing, investigation, examination," noun of action from past participle stem of recognoscere "to acknowledge, know again; examine" (see recognize).

Sense of "formal avowal of knowledge and approval" is from 1590s; especially acknowledgement of the independence of a country by a state formerly exercising sovereignty (1824). Meaning "a knowing again" is from 1798.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "knowledge of an event or incident; understanding," 源自 中古法语 recognition (15 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 recognitionem (主格 recognitio) "a reviewing, investigation, examination," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of recognoscere "to acknowledge, know again; examine" （参见 recognize). 义为 "formal avowal of knowledge and approval" 始于 1590 年代; 尤指 acknowledgement of the independence of a country by a state formerly exercising sovereignty (1824 年). 义为 "a knowing again" 始于 1798 年.

example.en: The award was given in recognition of her outstanding contributions.
example.zh: 这个奖项是为了表彰她杰出的贡献而授予的。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "resume possession of land," back-formation from recognizance, or else from Old French reconoiss-, stem of reconoistre "to know again, identify, recognize," from Latin recognoscere "acknowledge, recall to mind, know again; examine; certify," from re- "again" (see re-) + cognoscere "to get to know, recognize" (see cognizance). Meaning "know again, recall or recover the knowledge of, perceive an identity with something formerly known or felt" first recorded 1530s. Related: Recognized; recognizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "resume possession of land," back-formation 源自 recognizance，或else 源自 古法语 reconoiss-, stem of reconoistre "to know again, identify, recognize," 源自 拉丁语 recognoscere "acknowledge, recall to mind, know again; examine; certify," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + cognoscere "to get to know, recognize" （参见 cognizance). 义为 "know again, recall or recover the knowledge of, perceive an identity with something formerly known or felt" 首见于 1530 年代. 同源词：Recognized; recognizing.

example.en: She could not recognize her childhood friend after thirty years apart.
example.zh: 分别三十年后，她无法认出她的童年朋友。

definitionLines: vt. 劝告，建议；介绍，推荐
entries.definition: vt. 劝告，建议；介绍，推荐
entries.etymology: late 14c., "praise, present as worthy," from Medieval Latin recommendare, from Latin re-, here probably an intensive prefix, or else from a sense now obscure (see re-), + commendare "commit to one's care, commend" (see commend). Meaning "advise as to action, urge (that something be done)" is from 1746. Related: Recommended; recommending.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "praise, present as worthy," 源自 中古拉丁语 recommendare, 源自 拉丁语 re-, here 可能 an intensive prefix，或else 源自 a sense 现在 obscure （参见 re-), + commendare "commit to one's care, commend" （参见 commend). 义为 "advise as to action, urge (that something be done)" 始于 1746 年. 同源词：Recommended; recommending.

example.en: Can you recommend a good hotel near the train station?
example.zh: 你能推荐一家火车站附近的好酒店吗？

definitionLines: n.劝告，建议；推荐；最高纪录， 最佳成绩；履历，历史
entries.definition: n.劝告，建议；推荐；最高纪录， 最佳成绩；履历，历史
entries.etymology: early 15c., "action of commending oneself to another," from Old French recommendation (Modern French recommandation), from Medieval Latin recommendationem (nominative recommendatio), noun of action from past participle stem of recommendare (see recommend). Meaning "act of recommending (someone or something) as worthy" is from 1570s. Letter of recommendation is from late 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "action of commending oneself to another," 源自 古法语 recommendation (现代法语 recommandation), 源自 中古拉丁语 recommendationem (主格 recommendatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of recommendare （参见 recommend). 义为 "act of recommending (someone or something) as worthy" 始于 1570 年代. Letter of recommendation 始于 15 世纪晚期

example.en: The professor wrote a glowing recommendation for her graduate school application.
example.zh: 教授为她的研究生申请写了一封热情洋溢的推荐信。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., of persons, from Old French reconcilier (12c.) and directly from Latin reconcilare "to bring together again; regain; win over again, conciliate," from re- "again" (see re-) + concilare "make friendly" (see conciliate). Reflexive sense is recorded from 1530s. Meaning "to make (discordant facts or statements) consistent" is from late 14c. Intransitive sense of "become reconciled" is from 1660s. Related: Reconciled; reconciling.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, of persons, 源自 古法语 reconcilier (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 reconcilare "to bring together again; regain; win over again, conciliate," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + concilare "make friendly" （参见 conciliate). Reflexive sense 见于 1530 年代. 义为 "to make (discordant facts or statements) consistent" 始于 14 世纪晚期 Intransitive 语义 "become reconciled" 始于 1660 年代. 同源词：Reconciled; reconciling.

example.en: It is difficult to reconcile personal ambition with family responsibilities.
example.zh: 很难将个人抱负与家庭责任协调统一。

definitionLines: vt. 记录，记载；将（声音等） 录下
entries.definition: n.唱片；记录，记载 vt. 记录，记载；将（声音等） 录下
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "to repeat, reiterate, recite; rehearse, get by heart," from Old French recorder "tell, relate, repeat, recite, report, make known" (12c.) and directly from Latin recordari "remember, call to mind, think over, be mindful of," from re- "restore" (see re-) + cor (genitive cordis) "heart" (as the metaphoric seat of memory, as in learn by heart), from PIE root *kerd- (1) "heart" (see heart (n.)). Meaning "set down in writing" first attested mid-14c.; that of "put sound or pictures on disks, tape, etc." is from 1892. Related: Recorded; recording.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "to repeat, reiterate, recite; rehearse, get by heart," 源自 古法语 recorder "tell, relate, repeat, recite, report, make known" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 recordari "remember, call to mind, think over, be mindful of," 源自 re- "restore" （参见 re-) + cor (属格 cordis) "heart" (as the metaphoric seat of memory, as in learn by heart), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *kerd- (1) "heart" （参见 heart （名）). 义为 "set down in writing" 最早见于 14 世纪中期; that of "put sound or pictures on disks, tape, etc." 始于 1892 年. 同源词：Recorded; recording.

example.en: The scientist kept a daily record of temperature changes in the lab.
example.zh: 这位科学家每天记录实验室的温度变化。

entries.etymology:
"chief legal officer of a city," early 15c., from Anglo-French recordour (early 14c.), Old French recordeor "witness; storyteller; minstrel," from Medieval Latin recordator, from Latin recordari "remember" (see record (v.)).

Meaning "registering apparatus" is from 1873. The musical instrument is attested by this name from early 15c., from record (v.) in the obsolete sense of "practice a tune." Used by Shakespeare and Milton ("of flutes and soft recorders," "Paradise Lost"). The name, and the device, were rarely heard by mid-1800s, ousted by the flute, but enjoyed a revival after 1911 as an easy-to-play instrument for musical beginners.
entries.etymologyZh: "chief legal officer of a city," 15 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 recordour (14 世纪初), 古法语 recordeor "witness; storyteller; minstrel," 源自 中古拉丁语 recordator, 源自 拉丁语 recordari "remember" （参见 record （动）). 义为 "registering apparatus" 始于 1873 年. The musical instrument is attested by this name 源自 15 世纪初, 源自 record （动） in the 已废 语义 "practice a tune." Used by Shakespeare and Milton ("of flutes and soft recorders," "Paradise Lost"). The name, and the device, were rarely heard by mid-1800 年代, ousted by the flute, but enjoyed a revival after 1911 年 作为 easy-to-play instrument for musical beginners.

example.en: The journalist held up a recorder to capture every word of the press conference.
example.zh: 记者举起录音机，记录新闻发布会上的每一句话。

definitionLines: vt. 收回，挽回；重新获得，重新 找回
entries.definition: vt. 收回，挽回；重新获得，重新 找回 vi. 恢复，痊愈
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to regain consciousness," from Anglo-French rekeverer (13c.), Old French recovrer "come back, return; regain health; procure, get again" (11c.), from Medieval Latin recuperare "to recover" (source of Spanish recobrar, Italian ricoverare; see recuperation). Meaning "to regain health or strength" is from early 14c.; sense of "to get (anything) back" is first attested mid-14c. Related: Recovered; recovering.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to regain consciousness," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 rekeverer (13 世纪), 古法语 recovrer "come back, return; regain health; procure, get again" (11 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 recuperare "to recover" (source of 西班牙语 recobrar, 意大利语 ricoverare; 参见 recuperation). 义为 "to regain health or strength" 始于 14 世纪初; 语义 "to get (anything) back" is 最早见于 14 世纪中期 同源词：Recovered; recovering.

example.en: It took her months to recover from the knee surgery.
example.zh: 她花了几个月时间才从膝盖手术中康复。

definitionLines: n. 复原，痊愈；收回，复得
entries.definition: n. 复原，痊愈；收回，复得
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "return to health," from Anglo-French recoverie (c. 1300), Old French recovree "remedy, cure, recovery," from past participle stem of recovrer (see recover). Meaning "a gaining possession by legal action" is from early 15c. That of "act of righting oneself after a blunder, mishap, etc." is from 1520s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "return to health," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 recoverie (约 1300 年), 古法语 recovree "remedy, cure, recovery," 源自 past participle stem of recovrer （参见 recover). 义为 "a gaining possession by legal action" 始于 15 世纪初 That of "act of righting oneself after a blunder, mishap, etc." 始于 1520 年代.

example.en: The patient made a full recovery after the surgery.
example.zh: 患者术后完全康复。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "refreshment or curing of a person, refreshment by eating," from Old French recreacion (13c.), from Latin recreationem (nominative recreatio) "recovery from illness," noun of action from past participle stem of recreare "to refresh, restore, make anew, revive, invigorate," from re- "again" (see re-) + creare (see create). Meaning "refresh oneself by some amusement" is first recorded c. 1400.

A verb recreate "to refresh by physical influence after exertion" is attested from early 15c. and was used by Lyly, Pope, Steele, and Harriet Martineau, but it did not take, probably to avoid confusion with recreate.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "refreshment or curing of a person, refreshment by eating," 源自 古法语 recreacion (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 recreationem (主格 recreatio) "recovery from illness," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of recreare "to refresh, restore, make anew, revive, invigorate," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + creare （参见 create). 义为 "refresh oneself by some amusement" is 首见于 约 1400 年. A 动词 recreate "to refresh by physical influence after exertion" 见于 15 世纪初 and was used by Lyly, Pope, Steele, and Harriet Martineau, but it did not take, 可能 to avoid confusion with recreate.

example.en: Hiking and swimming are popular forms of outdoor recreation.
example.zh: 徒步和游泳是受欢迎的户外娱乐活动形式。

entries.etymology: 1630s, "to strengthen, reinforce," from French recruter (17c.), from recrute "a levy, a recruit" (see recruit (n.)). Sense of "to enlist new soldiers" is attested from 1650s; of student athletes, from 1913. Related: Recruited; recruiting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "to strengthen, reinforce," 源自 法语 recruter (17 世纪), 源自 recrute "a levy, a recruit" （参见 recruit （名）). 义为 "to enlist new soldiers" 见于 1650 年代; of student athletes, 自 1913 年起. 同源词：Recruited; recruiting.

example.en: The company hired fifty new recruit to support the expansion.
example.zh: 公司招募了五十名新员工来支持扩张计划。

entries.etymology: 1620s, from Middle French rectangulaire (16c.) or formed in English from Latin stem of rectangle + -ar. Related: Rectangularity.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 中古法语 rectangulaire (16 世纪) or formed in English 源自 拉丁语 stem of rectangle + -ar. 同源词：Rectangularity.

entries.etymology: c. 1400, from Old French rectifier, literally "to make straight" (14c.), from Late Latin rectificare "make right," from Latin rectus "straight" (see right (adj.1)) + root of facere "to make" (see factitious). Related: Rectified; rectifying.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, 源自 古法语 rectifier, 字面义为 "to make straight" (14 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 rectificare "make right," 源自 拉丁语 rectus "straight" （参见 right (adj.1)) + root of facere "to make" （参见 factitious). 同源词：Rectified; rectifying.

definitionLines: v. 使再循环，反复利用
entries.definition: v. 使再循环，反复利用
entries.etymology: 1922, originally of industrial processes; see re- + cycle (v.). Specifically of waste material from 1960. Related: Recycled; recycling.
entries.etymologyZh: 1922 年, 原义为 of industrial processes; 参见 re- + cycle （动）. Specifically of waste material 自 1960 年起. 同源词：Recycled; recycling.

example.en: The school encourages students to recycle paper and plastic bottles.
example.zh: 学校鼓励学生对纸张和塑料瓶进行回收利用。

entries.definition: a. 红色的 n. 红色

definitionLines: vt. 缩小，减小，减低；使成； 简化；还原
entries.definition: vt. 缩小，减小，减低；使成； 简化；还原
entries.etymology: late 14c., "bring back," from Old French reducer (14c.), from Latin reducere "lead back, bring back," figuratively "restore, replace," from re- "back" (see re-) + ducere "bring, lead" (see duke (n.)). Meaning "bring to an inferior condition" is 1570s; that of "bring to a lower rank" is 1640s (military reduce to ranks is from 1802); that of "subdue by force of arms" is 1610s. Sense of "to lower, diminish, lessen" is from 1787. Related: Reduced; reducing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "bring back," 源自 古法语 reducer (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 reducere "lead back, bring back," figuratively "restore, replace," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + ducere "bring, lead" （参见 duke （名）). 义为 "bring to an inferior condition" is 1570 年代; that of "bring to a lower rank" is 1640 年代 (military reduce to ranks 始于 1802 年); that of "subdue by force of arms" is 1610 年代. 义为 "to lower, diminish, lessen" 始于 1787 年. 同源词：Reduced; reducing.

example.en: The company offered to reduce the price from fifty dollars to forty dollars for returning customers.
example.zh: 公司愿意将回头客的价格从五十美元降到四十美元。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "a restoring to a former state; a subjugation" (of a people, etc.), from Middle French reducion (13c., Modern French réduction) and directly from Latin reductionem (nominative reductio) "a leading back, restoration," noun of action from past participle stem of reducere (see reduce). Meaning "diminution, a lessening" is from 1670s; chemical sense of "reversion to a simpler form" is from 1660s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "a restoring to a former state; a subjugation" (of a people, etc.), 源自 中古法语 reducion (13 世纪, 现代法语 réduction) and 直接源自 拉丁语 reductionem (主格 reductio) "a leading back, restoration," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of reducere （参见 reduce). 义为 "diminution, a lessening" 始于 1670 年代; chemical 语义 "reversion to a simpler form" 始于 1660 年代.

example.en: The factory achieved a 30% reduction in production costs by automating key assembly lines.
example.zh: 工厂通过自动化关键装配线，实现了生产成本降低30%。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from Latin redundantem (nominative redundans), present participle of redundare, literally "overflow, pour over; be over-full;" figuratively "be in excess," from re- "again" (see re-) + undare "rise in waves," from unda "a wave," from PIE *unda-, nasalized form of root *wed- (1) "water, wet" (see water (n.1)). Of persons, in employment situations, from 1928, chiefly British. Related: Redundantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 拉丁语 redundantem (主格 redundans), 为 … 的现在分词 redundare, 字面义为 "overflow, pour over; be over-full;" figuratively "be in excess," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + undare "rise in waves," 源自 unda "a wave," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *unda-, nasalized form of root *wed- (1) "water, wet" （参见 water (n.1)). Of persons, in employment situations, 自 1928 年起, chiefly British. 同源词：Redundantly.

definitionLines: vi. （to）参考，查阅，查询；（to） 提到，引用，指
vt. 叫（人）去……（以便得到消 息、援助等）；把…•…归因于
entries.definition: vi. （to）参考，查阅，查询；（to） 提到，引用，指 vt. 叫（人）去……（以便得到消 息、援助等）；把…•…归因于
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to trace back (to a first cause), attribute, assign," from Old French referer (14c.) and directly from Latin referre "to relate, refer," literally "to carry back," from re- "back" (see re-) + ferre "carry" (see infer). Meaning "to commit to some authority for a decision" is from mid-15c.; sense of "to direct (someone) to a book, etc." is from c. 1600. Related: Referred; referring.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to trace back (to a first cause), attribute, assign," 源自 古法语 referer (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 referre "to relate, refer," 字面义为 "to carry back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + ferre "carry" （参见 infer). 义为 "to commit to some authority for a decision" 始于 15 世纪中期; 语义 "to direct (someone) to a book, etc." 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Referred; referring.

example.en: Please refer to the manual if you need instructions on setup.
example.zh: 如果需要安装说明，请查阅手册。

entries.etymology: 1620s, "person who examines patent applications" (see refer). Sporting use recorded by 1820 (specifically of baseball from 1856).
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, "person who examines patent applications" （参见 refer). Sporting use recorded 截至 1820 年 (specifically of baseball 自 1856 年起).

definitionLines: n. 提及，涉及；参考，查阅；参考 文献，参考书目；介绍人/ 信，证明人/信
entries.definition: n. 提及，涉及；参考，查阅；参考 文献，参考书目；介绍人/ 信，证明人/信
entries.etymology: 1580s, "act of referring," from refer + -ance, or else from French référence, from Medieval Latin *referentia, from Latin referentem (nominative referens), present participle of referre (see refer). Meaning "direction to a book or passage" is recorded from 1610s. Meaning "testimonial" is from 1895. Reference book dates from 1808. Phrase in reference to is attested from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "act of referring," 源自 refer + -ance，或else 源自 法语 référence, 源自 中古拉丁语 *referentia, 源自 拉丁语 referentem (主格 referens), 为 … 的现在分词 referre （参见 refer). 义为 "direction to a book or passage" 见于 1610 年代. 义为 "testimonial" 始于 1895 年. Reference book dates 自 1808 年起. Phrase in reference to 见于 1590 年代.

example.en: Please use the library database as your main reference for the research paper.
example.zh: 请以图书馆数据库作为你研究论文的主要参考资料。

definitionLines: vt. 精练，精制，提纯；改善， 改进
entries.definition: vt. 精练，精制，提纯；改善， 改进
entries.etymology: 1580s, of metals, c. 1590 of manners, from re-, intensive prefix, + obsolete fine (v.) "make fine," from fine (adj.) "delicate." Compare French raffiner, Italian raffinare, Spanish refinar. General and figurative sense is recorded from 1590s; of sugar, from 1610s. Related: Refined; refining.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, of metals, 约 1590 年 of manners, 源自 re-, intensive prefix, + 已废 fine （动） "make fine," 源自 fine （形） "delicate." 对比 法语 raffiner, 意大利语 raffinare, 西班牙语 refinar. General and figurative sense 见于 1590 年代; of sugar, 源自 1610 年代. 同源词：Refined; refining.

example.en: The company uses a special process to refine crude oil by separating it into useful products.
example.zh: 这家公司用一种专门工艺炼制原油，将其分离成有用的产品。

definitionLines: vi. 反射，映出；思考，仔细考虑
entries.definition: vt. 反射；反映，表现 vi. 反射，映出；思考，仔细考虑
entries.etymology: late 14c., "turn or bend back;" early 15c., "to divert, to turn aside, deflect," from Old French reflecter (14c.), from Latin reflectere "bend back, turn back" (see reflection). Of mirrors or polished surfaces, to shine back light rays or images, early 15c.; meaning "to turn one's thoughts back on" is c. 1600. Related: Reflected; reflecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "turn or bend back;" 15 世纪初, "to divert, to turn aside, deflect," 源自 古法语 reflecter (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 reflectere "bend back, turn back" （参见 reflection). Of mirrors or polished surfaces, to shine back light rays or images, 15 世纪初; 意为 "to turn one's thoughts back on" is 约 1600 年. 同源词：Reflected; reflecting.

example.en: His final score clearly reflects the effort he had put into revision.
example.zh: 他的最终成绩清楚地反映了他在复习上所付出的努力。

definitionLines: n. 映像，倒影，反射；沉思，熟虑
entries.definition: n. 映像，倒影，反射；沉思，熟虑
entries.etymology: late 14c., reflexion, in reference to surfaces throwing back light or heat, from Late Latin reflexionem (nominative reflexio) "a reflection," literally "a bending back," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin reflectere "to bend back, bend backwards, turn away," from re- "back" (see re-) + flectere "to bend" (see flexible). Of the mind, from 1670s. Meaning "remark made after turning back one's thought on some subject" is from 1640s. Spelling with -ct- recorded from late 14c., established 18c., by influence of the verb.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, reflexion, in reference to surfaces throwing back light or heat, 源自 晚期拉丁语 reflexionem (主格 reflexio) "a reflection," 字面义为 "a bending back," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 reflectere "to bend back, bend backwards, turn away," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + flectere "to bend" （参见 flexible). Of the mind, 源自 1670 年代. 义为 "remark made after turning back one's thought on some subject" 始于 1640 年代. Spelling with -ct- recorded 源自 14 世纪晚期, established 18 世纪, by influence of the 动词.

example.en: After some quiet reflection, she decided to change her career path.
example.zh: 经过一番静静的沉思，她决定改变职业方向。

definitionLines: vt.改革，改良；改造；重新组成
n. 改革，改良；改过，自新
entries.definition: vt.改革，改良；改造；重新组成 n. 改革，改良；改过，自新
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to convert into another and better form," from Old French reformer "rebuild, reconstruct, recreate" (12c.), from Latin reformare "to form again, change, transform, alter," from re- "again" (see re-) + formare "to form" (see form (n.)). Intransitive sense from 1580s.

Meaning "to bring (a person) away from an evil course of life" is recorded from early 15c.; of governments, institutions, etc., from early 15c. Related: Reformed; reforming. Reformed churches (1580s) usually are Calvinist as opposed to Lutheran. Reformed Judaism (1843) is a movement initiated in Germany by Moses Mendelssohn (1729-1786). Reform school is attested from 1859.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to convert into another and better form," 源自 古法语 reformer "rebuild, reconstruct, recreate" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 reformare "to form again, change, transform, alter," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + formare "to form" （参见 form （名）). Intransitive sense 源自 1580 年代. 义为 "to bring (a person) away from an evil course of life" 见于 15 世纪初; of governments, institutions, etc., 源自 15 世纪初 同源词：Reformed; reforming. Reformed churches (1580 年代) 通常 are Calvinist as opposed to Lutheran. Reformed Judaism (1843 年) is a movement initiated in Germany by Moses Mendelssohn (1729 年-1786 年). Reform school 见于 1859 年.

example.en: The government announced plans to reform the education system to improve student outcomes.
example.zh: 政府宣布计划改革教育体系以提升学生的学习成果。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French refreschier "refresh, renew" (12c.; Modern French rafraîchir), from re- "again" (see re-) + fresche "fresh" (Modern French frais), from a Germanic source (such as Old High German frisc "fresh," see fresh (adj.)). Related: Refreshed; refreshing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 refreschier "refresh, renew" (12 世纪; 现代法语 rafraîchir), 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + fresche "fresh" (现代法语 frais), 源自 a 日耳曼语 source (such as 古高地德语 frisc "fresh," 参见 fresh （形）). 同源词：Refreshed; refreshing.

definitionLines: n. 点心；起提神作用的东西； 精力恢复
entries.definition: n. 点心；起提神作用的东西； 精力恢复
entries.etymology: late 14c., "act or fact of refreshing," originally mental and spiritual, from Old French refreschement (Modern French rafraîchissement, from refreschier (see refresh). Refreshments, of food and drink only, from 1660s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act or fact of refreshing," 原义为 mental and spiritual, 源自 古法语 refreschement (现代法语 rafraîchissement, 源自 refreschier （参见 refresh). Refreshments, of food and drink only, 源自 1660 年代.

definitionLines: n. 冰箱，冷冻机，冷藏库
entries.definition: n. 冰箱，冷冻机，冷藏库
entries.etymology: 1610s, "something that cools," agent noun from refrigerate. As "cabinet for keeping food cool," 1824, originally in the brewery trade, in place of earlier refrigeratory (c. 1600). The electric-powered household device was available from c. 1918.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "something that cools," agent 名词 源自 refrigerate. As "cabinet for keeping food cool," 1824 年, 原义为 in the brewery trade, in place of earlier refrigeratory (约 1600 年). The electric-powered household device was available 源自 约 1918 年.

example.en: Please put the leftover food in the refrigerator to keep it fresh.
example.zh: 请把剩下的食物放进冰箱保鲜。

entries.etymology: 1680s, from French refugié, noun use of past participle of refugier "to take shelter, protect," from Old French refuge (see refuge). First applied to French Huguenots who migrated after the revocation (1685) of the Edict of Nantes. The word meant "one seeking asylum," till 1914, when it evolved to mean "one fleeing home" (first applied in this sense to civilians in Flanders heading west to escape fighting in World War I). In Australian slang from World War II, reffo.
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, 源自 法语 refugié, 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 refugier "to take shelter, protect," 源自 古法语 refuge （参见 refuge). First applied to 法语 Huguenots who migrated after the revocation (1685 年) of the Edict of Nantes. The word meant "one seeking asylum," till 1914 年, when it evolved to mean "one fleeing home" (first applied in this sense to civilians in Flanders heading west to escape fighting in World War I). In Australian 俚语 源自 World War II, reffo.

example.en: The camp provided shelter for thousands of refugees fleeing the conflict.
example.zh: 该营地为数千名逃离冲突的难民提供了庇护所。

entries.etymology: "to give back, restore," early 15c. (earlier "to pour back," late 14c.), from Old French refunder "restore" and directly from Latin refundere "give back, restore, return," literally "pour back, flow back," from re- "back" (see re-) + fundere "to pour" (see found (v.2)). Specifically of money from 1550s. Related: Refunded; refunding.
entries.etymologyZh: "to give back, restore," 15 世纪初 (earlier "to pour back," 14 世纪晚期), 源自 古法语 refunder "restore" and 直接源自 拉丁语 refundere "give back, restore, return," 字面义为 "pour back, flow back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + fundere "to pour" （参见 found (v.2)). Specifically of money 源自 1550 年代. 同源词：Refunded; refunding.

entries.etymology: late 15c., from refuse + -al (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 refuse + -al (2).

example.en: Her refusal to sign the contract surprised the entire legal team.
example.zh: 她拒绝签署合同让整个法律团队大为惊讶。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French refuser "reject, disregard, avoid" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *refusare, frequentative form from past participle stem of Latin refundere "pour back, give back" (see refund (v.)). Related: Refused; refusing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 refuser "reject, disregard, avoid" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *refusare, frequentative form 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 refundere "pour back, give back" （参见 refund （动）). 同源词：Refused; refusing.

example.en: The invitation asked for a reply by Friday, but he refused to give any answer at all.
example.zh: 邀请函要求在星期五前回复，但他拒绝作出任何答复。

entries.etymology:
1510s, "refuse, reject," from Middle French réfuter (16c.) and directly from Latin refutare "drive back; rebut, disprove; repress, repel, resist, oppose," from re- "back" (see re-) + -futare "to beat," probably from PIE root *bhau- "to strike down" (see bat (n.1)).

Meaning "prove wrong" dates from 1540s. Since c. 1964 linguists have frowned on the subtle shift in meaning towards "to deny," as it is used in connection with allegation. Related: Refuted; refuting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "refuse, reject," 源自 中古法语 réfuter (16 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 refutare "drive back; rebut, disprove; repress, repel, resist, oppose," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + -futare "to beat," 可能 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *bhau- "to strike down" （参见 bat (n.1)). 义为 "prove wrong" dates 源自 1540 年代. 自 约 1964 年 linguists have frowned on the subtle shift in 意为 towards "to deny," as it is used in connection with allegation. 同源词：Refuted; refuting.

definitionLines: vt. 看作，对待；考虑，认；尊 重；（pl.）敬重，敬意，问候
entries.definition: vt. 看作，对待；考虑，认；尊 重；（pl.）敬重，敬意，问候
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "a consideration; a judgment," from Old French regard, from regarder "take notice of," from re-, intensive prefix + garder "look, heed," from Germanic (see guard (n.)). Meanings "a look, appearance; respect, esteem, favor, kindly feeling which springs from a consideration of estimable qualities" all recorded late 14c. Phrase in regard to is from mid-15c. (Chaucer uses at regard of).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "a consideration; a judgment," 源自 古法语 regard, 源自 regarder "take notice of," 源自 re-, intensive prefix + garder "look, heed," 源自 日耳曼语 （参见 guard （名）). Meanings "a look, appearance; respect, esteem, favor, kindly feeling which springs from a consideration of estimable qualities" all recorded 14 世纪晚期 Phrase in regard to 始于 15 世纪中期 (Chaucer uses at regard of).

example.en: Most people regard him as an honest and reliable man.
example.zh: 大多数人把他视为一个诚实可靠的人。

entries.etymology: "indifferent," 1590s, from regard (n.) + -less. Elliptical for "regardless of consequences, expenses, etc.," from 1872.
entries.etymologyZh: "indifferent," 1590 年代, 源自 regard （名） + -less. Elliptical for "regardless of consequences, expenses, etc.," 自 1872 年起.

example.en: She continued training regardless of the bad weather.
example.zh: 她不顾恶劣天气，继续训练。

entries.etymology: "system of government or rule," 1792, from French régime, from Old French regimen (14c.), from Latin regimen "rule, guidance, government, means of guidance, rudder," from regere (see regal). Earlier "course of diet, exercise," late 15c. In French, l'ancien régime refers to the system of government before the revolution of 1789.
entries.etymologyZh: "system of government or rule," 1792 年, 源自 法语 régime, 源自 古法语 regimen (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 regimen "rule, guidance, government, means of guidance, rudder," 源自 regere （参见 regal). Earlier "course of diet, exercise," 15 世纪晚期 In 法语, l'ancien régime refers to the system of government before the revolution of 1789 年.

example.en: The authoritarian regime controlled the media and brutally suppressed all opposition.
example.zh: 这个威权政权控制了媒体，并残酷地压制一切反对声音。

entries.definition: n. （军队）团 vt.把…••…•编成团；严格地管制
entries.etymology: late 14c., "government, rule, control," from Old French regiment "government, rule" (14c.), from Late Latin regimentum "rule, direction," from Latin regere "to rule, to direct, keep straight, guide" (see regal). Meaning "unit of an army" first recorded 1570s (originally the reference was to permanent organization and discipline), from French. The exact number in the unit varies over time and place.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "government, rule, control," 源自 古法语 regiment "government, rule" (14 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 regimentum "rule, direction," 源自 拉丁语 regere "to rule, to direct, keep straight, guide" （参见 regal). 义为 "unit of an army" 首见于 1570 年代 (原义为 the reference was to permanent organization and discipline), 源自 法语. The exact number in the unit varies over time and place.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "tract of land of a considerable but indefinite extent," from Anglo-French regioun, Old French region "land, region, province" (12c.), from Latin regionem (nominative regio) "a district, portion of a country, territory, district; a direction, line; boundary line, limit," noun of state from past participle stem of regere "to direct, rule" (see regal). Phrase in the region of "about" (of numbers, etc.) is recorded from 1961.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "tract of land of a considerable but indefinite extent," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 regioun, 古法语 region "land, region, province" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 regionem (主格 regio) "a district, portion of a country, territory, district; a direction, line; boundary line, limit," 名词 of state 源自 past participle stem of regere "to direct, rule" （参见 regal). Phrase in the region of "about" (of numbers, etc.) 见于 1961 年.

example.en: This mountainous region receives very little rainfall throughout the year.
example.zh: 这个多山的地区全年降水量很少。

entries.etymology: late 14c. (transitive), "enter in a listing," from Old French registrer "note down, include" (13c.) and directly from Medieval Latin registrare, from registrum (see register (n.)). Intransitive sense, of instruments, from 1797; of persons and feelings, "make an impression," from 1901. Meaning "to enter one's name in a list" for some purpose is from 1940. Related: Registered; registering. Registered nurse attested from 1879.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 (transitive), "enter in a listing," 源自 古法语 registrer "note down, include" (13 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 registrare, 源自 registrum （参见 register （名）). Intransitive sense, of instruments, 自 1797 年起; of persons and feelings, "make an impression," 自 1901 年起. 义为 "to enter one's name in a list" for some purpose 始于 1940 年. 同源词：Registered; registering. Registered nurse attested 自 1879 年起.

example.en: All new students must register for classes before the semester begins.
example.zh: 所有新生必须在学期开始前登记注册课程。

entries.etymology:
"to look back with distress or sorrowful longing; to grieve for on remembering," late 14c., from Old French regreter "long after, bewail, lament someone's death; ask the help of" (Modern French regretter), from re-, intensive prefix (see re-), + -greter, possibly from Frankish or some other Germanic source (compare Old English grætan "to weep;" Old Norse grata "to weep, groan"), from Proto-Germanic *gretan "weep." "Not found in other Romance languages, and variously explained" [Century Dictionary].

Related: Regretted; regretting. Replaced Old English ofþyncan, from of- "off, away," here denoting opposition, + þyncan "seem, seem fit" (as in methinks).
entries.etymologyZh: "to look back with distress or sorrowful longing; to grieve for on remembering," 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 regreter "long after, bewail, lament someone's death; ask the help of" (现代法语 regretter), 源自 re-, intensive prefix （参见 re-), + -greter, possibly 源自 Frankish or some other 日耳曼语 source (对比 古英语 grætan "to weep;" 古北欧语 grata "to weep, groan"), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *gretan "weep." "Not found in other Romance languages, and variously explained" [Century Dictionary]. 同源词：Regretted; regretting. Replaced 古英语 ofþyncan, 源自 of- "off, away," here denoting opposition, + þyncan "seem, seem fit" (as in methinks).

example.en: He deeply regretted missing his daughter's graduation ceremony.
example.zh: 他对错过女儿的毕业典礼深感遗憾。

definitionLines: a.有规律的；规则的，规矩的； 定时的，定期的；正规的，正 式的；匀称的，整齐的
entries.definition: a.有规律的；规则的，规矩的； 定时的，定期的；正规的，正 式的；匀称的，整齐的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., from Old French reguler "ecclesiastical" (Modern French régulier), from Late Latin regularis "containing rules for guidance," from Latin regula "rule," from PIE *reg- "move in a straight line" (see regal).

Earliest sense was of religious orders (the opposite of secular). Extended from late 16c. to shapes, etc., that followed predictable or uniform patterns; sense of "normal" is from 1630s; meaning "real, genuine" is from 1821. Old English borrowed Latin regula and nativized it as regol "rule, regulation, canon, law, standard, pattern;" hence regolsticca "ruler" (instrument); regollic (adj.) "canonical, regular."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 reguler "ecclesiastical" (现代法语 régulier), 源自 晚期拉丁语 regularis "containing rules for guidance," 源自 拉丁语 regula "rule," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *reg- "move in a straight line" （参见 regal). Earliest sense was of religious orders (the opposite of secular). Extended 源自 16 世纪晚期 to shapes, etc., that followed predictable or uniform patterns; 语义 "normal" 始于 1630 年代; 意为 "real, genuine" 始于 1821 年. 古英语 borrowed 拉丁语 regula and nativized it as regol "rule, regulation, canon, law, standard, pattern;" hence regolsticca "ruler" (instrument); regollic （形） "canonical, regular."

example.en: The clinic sends patients a regular reminder every six months for a check-up.
example.zh: 诊所每六个月定期向患者发送一次复查提醒。

definitionLines: vt. 管理，控制；调整，调节， 校准
entries.definition: vt. 管理，控制；调整，调节， 校准
entries.etymology: early 15c., "adjust by rule, control," from Late Latin regulatus, past participle of regulare "to control by rule, direct," from Latin regula "rule" (see regular). Meaning "to govern by restriction" is from 1620s. Related: Regulated; regulating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "adjust by rule, control," 源自 晚期拉丁语 regulatus, 为 … 的过去分词 regulare "to control by rule, direct," 源自 拉丁语 regula "rule" （参见 regular). 义为 "to govern by restriction" 始于 1620 年代. 同源词：Regulated; regulating.

example.en: The government needs to regulate the use of social media by minors.
example.zh: 政府需要对未成年人使用社交媒体进行规范管理。

definitionLines: n. 管理，控制；规章，规则
entries.definition: n. 管理，控制；规章，规则
entries.etymology: 1670s, "act of regulating; state of being reduced to order," noun of action from regulate. Meaning "rule for management" is from 1715. Related: Regulations.
entries.etymologyZh: 1670 年代, "act of regulating; state of being reduced to order," 名词 of action 源自 regulate. 义为 "rule for management" 始于 1715 年. 同源词：Regulations.

example.en: New safety regulations were introduced after the accident.
example.zh: 事故发生后出台了新的安全规定。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "restatement, repetition of the words of another," from rehearse + -al (2), or from Old French rehearsal "a repeating." Sense in theater and music, "act of rehearsing," is from 1570s. Pre-wedding rehearsal dinner attested by 1953.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "restatement, repetition of the words of another," 源自 rehearse + -al (2)，或源自 古法语 rehearsal "a repeating." Sense in theater and music, "act of rehearsing," 始于 1570 年代. Pre-wedding rehearsal dinner attested 截至 1953 年.

example.en: The director insisted on one final rehearsal before the opening night.
example.zh: 导演坚持在首演之夜前进行最后一次排练。

entries.etymology: early 13c., "kingdom," from Old French reigne "kingdom, land, country" (Modern French règne), from Latin regnum "kingship, dominion, rule, realm," related to regere "to rule, to direct, keep straight, guide" (see regal). Meaning "period of rule" first recorded mid-14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "kingdom," 源自 古法语 reigne "kingdom, land, country" (现代法语 règne), 源自 拉丁语 regnum "kingship, dominion, rule, realm," related to regere "to rule, to direct, keep straight, guide" （参见 regal). 义为 "period of rule" 首见于 14 世纪中期

entries.definition: n. 缰绳；驾驭；统治 vt.勒住；驾驭；控制
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "strap fastened to a bridle," from Old French rene, resne "reins, bridle strap, laces" (Modern French rêne), probably from Vulgar Latin *retina "a bond, check," back-formation from Latin retinere "hold back" (see retain). To give something free rein is originally of horses.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "strap fastened to a bridle," 源自 古法语 rene, resne "reins, bridle strap, laces" (现代法语 rêne), 可能 源自 通俗拉丁语 *retina "a bond, check," back-formation 源自 拉丁语 retinere "hold back" （参见 retain). To give something free rein is 原义为 of horses.

entries.etymology: c. 1600, originally in military sense, from re- "again" + enforce (compare re-enforce). Related: Reinforced; reinforcing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 原义为 in military sense, 源自 re- "again" + enforce (对比 re-enforce). 同源词：Reinforced; reinforcing.

example.en: These exercises are designed to reinforce the key grammar rules.
example.zh: 这些练习旨在巩固关键语法规则。

definitionLines: vt.拒绝，谢绝，驳回；舍弃，排 斥，退掉
entries.definition: vt.拒绝，谢绝，驳回；舍弃，排 斥，退掉
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Old French rejecter and directly from Latin reiectus, past participle of reiectare "throw away, cast away, vomit," frequentative of reicere "to throw back," from re- "back" (see re-) + -icere, comb. form of iacere "to throw" (see jet (v.)). Related: Rejected; rejecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 古法语 rejecter and 直接源自 拉丁语 reiectus, 为 … 的过去分词 reiectare "throw away, cast away, vomit," 为 … 的反复体 reicere "to throw back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + -icere, comb. form of iacere "to throw" （参见 jet （动）). 同源词：Rejected; rejecting.

example.en: The factory had to reject several batches of components that failed the quality check.
example.zh: 工厂不得不把几批没通过质量检验的零件剔除退回。

entries.definition: vi.（to）联系，关联 vt. 叙述，讲述
entries.etymology:
1520s, "to recount, tell," from Middle French relater "refer, report" (14c.) and directly from Latin relatus, used as past participle of referre "bring back, bear back" (see refer), from re- "back, again" + latus (see oblate (n.)).

Meaning "stand in some relation; have reference or respect" is from 1640s; transitive sense of "bring (something) into relation with (something else)" is from 1690s. Meaning "to establish a relation between" is from 1771. Sense of "to feel connected or sympathetic to" is attested from 1950, originally in psychology jargon. Related: Related; relating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "to recount, tell," 源自 中古法语 relater "refer, report" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 relatus, used as 为 … 的过去分词 referre "bring back, bear back" （参见 refer), 源自 re- "back, again" + latus （参见 oblate （名）). 义为 "stand in some relation; have reference or respect" 始于 1640 年代; transitive 语义 "bring (something) into relation with (something else)" 始于 1690 年代. 义为 "to establish a relation between" 始于 1771 年. 义为 "to feel connected or sympathetic to" 见于 1950 年, 原义为 in psychology jargon. 同源词：Related; relating.

example.en: Can you explain how this new policy relates to the budget cuts announced last month?
example.zh: 你能解释一下这项新政策与上个月宣布的预算削减有什么关联吗？

definitionLines: n. 亲属，亲戚；关系，联系
entries.definition: n. 亲属，亲戚；关系，联系
entries.etymology: late 14c., "connection, correspondence;" also "act of telling," from Anglo-French relacioun, Old French relacion "report, connection" (14c.), from Latin relationem (nominative relatio) "a bringing back, restoring; a report, proposition," from relatus (see relate). Meaning "person related by blood or marriage" first attested c. 1500. Stand-alone phrase no relation "not in the same family" is attested by 1930.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "connection, correspondence;" also "act of telling," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 relacioun, 古法语 relacion "report, connection" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 relationem (主格 relatio) "a bringing back, restoring; a report, proposition," 源自 relatus （参见 relate). 义为 "person related by blood or marriage" 最早见于 约 1500 年. Stand-alone phrase no relation "not in the same family" is attested 截至 1930 年.

example.en: She has no close relation still living in this city.
example.zh: 她在这座城市里没有关系亲近的亲属了。

entries.etymology: 1640s, "sense or state of being related," from relation + -ship. Specifically of romantic or sexual relationships by 1944.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "sense or state of being related," 源自 relation + -ship. Specifically of romantic or sexual relationships 截至 1944 年.

example.en: Building trust is essential for a healthy working relationship.
example.zh: 建立信任对于健康的工作关系至关重要。

entries.definition: a. 相对的，比较的 n. 亲属，亲戚
entries.etymology: late 14c., "a relative pronoun," from Old French relatif (13c.), from Late Latin relativus "having reference or relation," from Latin relatus, past participle of referre "to refer" (see refer). Meaning "person in the same family" first recorded 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a relative pronoun," 源自 古法语 relatif (13 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 relativus "having reference or relation," 源自 拉丁语 relatus, 为 … 的过去分词 referre "to refer" （参见 refer). 义为 "person in the same family" 首见于 1650 年代.

example.en: The cost of living here is relative low compared to major cities.
example.zh: 与各大城市相比，这里的生活成本相对较低。

definitionLines: vt. 使放松，使休息；缓和，放宽
vi. 放松，休息；松弛，放松
entries.definition: vt. 使放松，使休息；缓和，放宽 vi. 放松，休息；松弛，放松
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to make (something) less compact or dense," from Old French relaschier "set free; soften; reduce" (14c.), from Latin relaxare "relax, loosen, open, stretch out, widen again; make loose," from re- "back" (see re-) + laxare "loosen," from laxus "loose" (see lax). Of persons, "to become less formal," from 1837. Meaning "decrease tension" is from early 15c.; intransitive sense of "to become less tense" is recorded from 1935. Related: Relaxed; relaxing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to make (something) less compact or dense," 源自 古法语 relaschier "set free; soften; reduce" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 relaxare "relax, loosen, open, stretch out, widen again; make loose," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + laxare "loosen," 源自 laxus "loose" （参见 lax). Of persons, "to become less formal," 自 1837 年起. 义为 "decrease tension" 始于 15 世纪初; intransitive 语义 "to become less tense" 见于 1935 年. 同源词：Relaxed; relaxing.

example.en: Doctors advised him to relax completely for two weeks after surgery.
example.zh: 医生建议他术后完全放松两周。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "hounds placed along a line of chase," from Middle French relai "reserve pack of hounds or other animals" (13c.), from Old French relaier "to exchange tired animals for fresh," literally "leave behind," from re- "back" (see re-) + laier "to leave" (see delay (v.)). The etymological sense is "to leave (dogs) behind (in order to take fresh ones)." Of horses, 1650s. Electromagnetic sense first recorded 1860. As a type of foot-race, it is attested from 1898.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "hounds placed along a line of chase," 源自 中古法语 relai "reserve pack of hounds or other animals" (13 世纪), 源自 古法语 relaier "to exchange tired animals for fresh," 字面义为 "leave behind," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + laier "to leave" （参见 delay （动）). The etymological sense is "to leave (dogs) behind (in order to take fresh ones)." Of horses, 1650 年代. Electromagnetic sense 首见于 1860 年. 作为 type of foot-race, it 见于 1898 年.

definitionLines: vt. 释放，放出；发布，发行；放 开，松开
entries.definition: vt. 释放，放出；发布，发行；放 开，松开
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "to withdraw, revoke (a decree, etc.), cancel, lift; remit," from Old French relaissier, relesser "to relinquish, quit, let go, leave behind, abandon, acquit," variant of relacher "release, relax," from Latin relaxare "loosen, stretch out" (see relax), source also of Spanish relajar, Italian relassare.

Meaning "alleviate, ease" is mid-14c., as is sense of "free from (duty, etc.); exonerate." From late 14c. as "grant remission, forgive; set free from imprisonment, military service, etc." Also "give up, relinquish, surrender." In law, c. 1400, "to grant a release of property." Of press reports, attested from 1904; of motion pictures, from 1912; of music recordings, from 1962. As a euphemism for "to dismiss, fire from a job" it is attested in American English since 1904. Related: Released; releasing.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to withdraw, revoke (a decree, etc.), cancel, lift; remit," 源自 古法语 relaissier, relesser "to relinquish, quit, let go, leave behind, abandon, acquit," 为 … 的变体 relacher "release, relax," 源自 拉丁语 relaxare "loosen, stretch out" （参见 relax), source also of 西班牙语 relajar, 意大利语 relassare. 义为 "alleviate, ease" is 14 世纪中期, as is 语义 "free from (duty, etc.); exonerate." From 14 世纪晚期 as "grant remission, forgive; set free from imprisonment, military service, etc." Also "give up, relinquish, surrender." In law, 约 1400 年, "to grant a release of property." Of press reports, attested 自 1904 年起; of motion pictures, 自 1912 年起; of music recordings, 自 1962 年起. 作为 euphemism for "to dismiss, fire from a job" it is 见于 American English 自 1904 年. 同源词：Released; releasing.

example.en: The company will release its annual earnings report to the public next Monday.
example.zh: 该公司将于下周一向公众正式发布年度收益报告。

definitionLines: a. 无情的，残酷的；持续的，坚 韧的
entries.definition: a. 无情的，残酷的；持续的，坚 韧的
entries.etymology: 1590s, from relent + -less. Related: Relentlessly; relentlessness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 relent + -less. 同源词：Relentlessly; relentlessness.

definitionLines: a. （to）相关的，切题的；适当 的，中肯的
entries.definition: a. （to）相关的，切题的；适当 的，中肯的
entries.etymology: "pertinent to the matter at hand," 1550s, from Middle French relevant "depending upon," originally "helpful," from Medieval Latin relevantem (nominative relevans), from stem of Latin relevare "to lessen, lighten" (see relieve). Not generally used until after 1800.
entries.etymologyZh: "pertinent to the matter at hand," 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 relevant "depending upon," 原义为 "helpful," 源自 中古拉丁语 relevantem (主格 relevans), 源自 stem of 拉丁语 relevare "to lessen, lighten" （参见 relieve). Not generally used until after 1800 年.

example.en: Please include only information relevant to the research question.
example.zh: 请只包含与研究问题相关的信息。

entries.etymology: 1560s, raliabill, Scottish; see rely + -able. Not common before 1850; and sometimes execrated thereafter in Britain as an Americanism because it involves a use of -able different from its use in provable, etc., but defended (by OED, Century Dictionary, etc.) on grounds of use of the suffix in available, laughable, etc.. Related: Reliably.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, raliabill, 苏格兰语; 参见 rely + -able. Not common 1850 年之前; and 有时 execrated thereafter in Britain 作为 Americanism because it involves a use of -able different 源自 its use in provable, etc., but defended (by OED, Century Dictionary, etc.) on grounds of use of the suffix in available, laughable, etc.. 同源词：Reliably.

example.en: You need a reliable source to back up your claims in the essay.
example.zh: 你需要一个可靠的信息来源来支撑你在文章中的论点。

definitionLines: n. 依靠，信赖；受信赖的人或物
entries.definition: n. 依靠，信赖；受信赖的人或物
entries.etymology: c. 1600, from rely + -ance.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 rely + -ance.

example.en: Taking a hot bath brought some relief to her sore and aching muscles.
example.zh: 洗热水澡使她酸痛的肌肉得到了一些缓解。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "alleviate (pain, etc.), mitigate; afford comfort; allow respite; diminish the pressure of," also "give alms to, provide for;" also figuratively, "take heart, cheer up;" from Old French relever "to raise, relieve" (11c.) and directly from Latin relevare "to raise, alleviate, lift up, free from a burden," from re-, intensive prefix (see re-), + levare "to lift up, lighten," from levis "not heavy" (see lever).

The notion is "to raise (someone) out of trouble." From c. 1400 as "advance to the rescue in battle;" also "return from battle; recall (troops)." Meaning "release from duty" is from early 15c. Related: relieved; relieving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "alleviate (pain, etc.), mitigate; afford comfort; allow respite; diminish the pressure of," also "give alms to, provide for;" also figuratively, "take heart, cheer up;" 源自 古法语 relever "to raise, relieve" (11 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 relevare "to raise, alleviate, lift up, free from a burden," 源自 re-, intensive prefix （参见 re-), + levare "to lift up, lighten," 源自 levis "not heavy" （参见 lever). The notion is "to raise (someone) out of trouble." From 约 1400 年 as "advance to the rescue in battle;" also "return from battle; recall (troops)." 义为 "release from duty" 始于 15 世纪初 同源词：relieved; relieving.

example.en: The painkiller took effect and began to relieve her severe headache.
example.zh: 止痛药开始发挥作用，缓解了她严重的头痛。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "state of life bound by monastic vows," also "conduct indicating a belief in a divine power," from Anglo-French religiun (11c.), Old French religion "piety, devotion; religious community," and directly from Latin religionem (nominative religio) "respect for what is sacred, reverence for the gods; conscientiousness, sense of right, moral obligation; fear of the gods; divine service, religious observance; a religion, a faith, a mode of worship, cult; sanctity, holiness," in Late Latin "monastic life" (5c.).

According to Cicero derived from relegere "go through again" (in reading or in thought), from re- "again" (see re-) + legere "read" (see lecture (n.)). However, popular etymology among the later ancients (Servius, Lactantius, Augustine) and the interpretation of many modern writers connects it with religare "to bind fast" (see rely), via notion of "place an obligation on," or "bond between humans and gods." In that case, the re- would be intensive. Another possible origin is religiens "careful," opposite of negligens. In English, meaning "particular system of faith" is recorded from c. 1300; sense of "recognition of and allegiance in manner of life (perceived as justly due) to a higher, unseen power or powers" is from 1530s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "state of life bound by monastic vows," also "conduct indicating a belief in a divine power," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 religiun (11 世纪), 古法语 religion "piety, devotion; religious community," and 直接源自 拉丁语 religionem (主格 religio) "respect for what is sacred, reverence for the gods; conscientiousness, sense of right, moral obligation; fear of the gods; divine service, religious observance; a religion, a faith, a mode of worship, cult; sanctity, holiness," in 晚期拉丁语 "monastic life" (5 世纪). According to Cicero derived 源自 relegere "go through again" (in reading or in thought), 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + legere "read" （参见 lecture （名）). However, popular etymology among the later ancients (Servius, Lactantius, Augustine) and the interpretation of many modern writers connects it with religare "to bind fast" （参见 rely), 经由 概念 "place an obligation on," or "bond between humans and gods." In that case, the re- would be intensive. Another possible origin is religiens "careful," opposite of negligens. In English, 意为 "particular system of faith" 见于 约 1300 年; 语义 "recognition of and allegiance in manner of life (perceived as justly due) to a higher, unseen power or powers" 始于 1530 年代.

example.en: Students study texts from every major world religion in the comparative course.
example.zh: 学生在这门比较课程中学习各主要世界宗教的文本。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "devout, pious, imbued with or expressive of religious devotion," from Anglo-French religius, Old French religious (12c., Modern French religieux) and directly from Latin religiosus, from religio (see religion). Meaning "pertaining to religion" is from 1530s. Transferred sense of "scrupulous, exact" is recorded from 1590s. Related: Religiousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "devout, pious, imbued with or expressive of religious devotion," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 religius, 古法语 religious (12 世纪, 现代法语 religieux) and 直接源自 拉丁语 religiosus, 源自 religio （参见 religion). 义为 "pertaining to religion" 始于 1530 年代. Transferred 语义 "scrupulous, exact" 见于 1590 年代. 同源词：Religiousness.

example.en: Pilgrims travel thousands of miles each year to visit this religious site in the desert.
example.zh: 朝圣者每年不远千里来到沙漠中的这处宗教圣地参拜。

entries.etymology: "unwilling," 1660s, from Latin reluctantem (nominative reluctans), present participle of reluctari (see reluctance). Related: Reluctantly. The Latin word is also the source of Spanish reluchante, Italian riluttante.
entries.etymologyZh: "unwilling," 1660 年代, 源自 拉丁语 reluctantem (主格 reluctans), 为 … 的现在分词 reluctari （参见 reluctance). 同源词：Reluctantly. The 拉丁语 word is also the source of 西班牙语 reluchante, 意大利语 riluttante.

example.en: He was reluctant to admit that he had made a mistake.
example.zh: 他不愿意承认自己犯了错误。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "to gather, assemble" (transitive and intransitive), from Old French relier "assemble, put together; fasten, attach, rally, oblige," from Latin religare "fasten, bind fast," from re-, intensive prefix (see re-), + ligare "to bind" (see ligament). Sense of "depend, trust" is from 1570s, perhaps via notion of "rally to, fall back on." Typically used with on, perhaps by influence of lie (v.2). Related: Relied; relying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to gather, assemble" (transitive and intransitive), 源自 古法语 relier "assemble, put together; fasten, attach, rally, oblige," 源自 拉丁语 religare "fasten, bind fast," 源自 re-, intensive prefix （参见 re-), + ligare "to bind" （参见 ligament). 义为 "depend, trust" 始于 1570 年代, 或许 经由 概念 "rally to, fall back on." Typically used with on, 或许 by influence of lie (v.2). 同源词：Relied; relying.

example.en: Farmers in this arid region rely on seasonal rainfall to water their crops.
example.zh: 这个干旱地区的农民依靠季节性降雨灌溉庄稼。

definitionLines: vi.留下，余留；留待，尚需；仍 然是，依旧是
entries.definition: vi.留下，余留；留待，尚需；仍 然是，依旧是 n. （pl.）余，残余，遗迹；遗体
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Anglo-French remayn-, Old French remain-, stressed stem of remanoir "stay, dwell, remain; be left; hold out," from Latin remanere "to remain, to stay behind; be left behind; endure, abide, last" (source also of Spanish remaner, Italian rimanere), from re- "back" (see re-) + manere "to stay, remain" (see mansion). Related: Remained; remaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 remayn-, 古法语 remain-, stressed stem of remanoir "stay, dwell, remain; be left; hold out," 源自 拉丁语 remanere "to remain, to stay behind; be left behind; endure, abide, last" (source also of 西班牙语 remaner, 意大利语 rimanere), 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + manere "to stay, remain" （参见 mansion). 同源词：Remained; remaining.

example.en: Only a few ancient folk customs remain in those isolated highland communities.
example.zh: 只有少数古老民俗在那些与世隔绝的高地社区中得以留存。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Anglo-French remainder, Old French remaindre, noun use of infinitive, a variant of Old French remanoir (see remain (v.)). The verb meaning "dispose of (books) at a reduced price" is from 1904. Related: Remaindered.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 remainder, 古法语 remaindre, 为 … 的名词用法 infinitive, a 为 … 的变体 古法语 remanoir （参见 remain （动）). The 动词 意为 "dispose of (books) at a reduced price" 始于 1904 年. 同源词：Remaindered.

entries.definition: n. 评语，意见 vt. 说，评论 vi. （on）议论，评论
entries.etymology:
1630s, "to mark out, distinguish" modeled on French remarquer "to mark, note, heed," formed in Middle French from re-, intensive prefix (see re-), + marquer "to mark," probably from a Germanic source such as Old High German marchon "to delimit" (see mark (n.1)).

Meaning "take notice of" is from 1670s; that of "make a comment" is first attested 1690s, from notion of "make a verbal observation" or "call attention to specific points." Related: Remarked; remarking.
entries.etymologyZh: 1630 年代, "to mark out, distinguish" modeled on 法语 remarquer "to mark, note, heed," formed in 中古法语 源自 re-, intensive prefix （参见 re-), + marquer "to mark," 可能 源自 a 日耳曼语 source such as 古高地德语 marchon "to delimit" （参见 mark (n.1)). 义为 "take notice of" 始于 1670 年代; that of "make a comment" is 最早见于 1690 年代, 源自 概念 "make a verbal observation" or "call attention to specific points." 同源词：Remarked; remarking.

example.en: The professor made a sharp remark about the student's grammatical errors.
example.zh: 教授对该学生的语法错误作出了尖锐的评论。

definitionLines: a. 值得注意的；显著的，异常 的，了不起的
entries.definition: a. 值得注意的；显著的，异常 的，了不起的
entries.etymology: c. 1600, from remark (v.) + -able, or from or based on French remarquable (16c.), from remarquer. "Observable, worthy of notice," hence "extraordinary, exceptional, conspicuous." Related: Remarkably.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 remark （动） + -able，或源自 or based on 法语 remarquable (16 世纪), 源自 remarquer. "Observable, worthy of notice," hence "extraordinary, exceptional, conspicuous." 同源词：Remarkably.

example.en: Her remarkable memory allowed her to recall every detail of the case.
example.zh: 她卓越的记忆力使她能回忆起案件的每一个细节。

definitionLines: n. 药品；治疗措施，补救办法
vt. 纠正，补救；医疗，治疗
entries.definition: n. 药品；治疗措施，补救办法 vt. 纠正，补救；医疗，治疗
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "cure for a disease or disorder; means of counteracting an evil," from Anglo-French remedie, Old French remede "remedy, cure" (12c., Modern French remède) and directly from Latin remedium "a cure, remedy, medicine, antidote, that which restores health," from re-, intensive prefix (or perhaps literally, "again;" see re-), + mederi "to heal" (see medical (adj.)). Figurative use from c. 1300.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "cure for a disease or disorder; means of counteracting an evil," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 remedie, 古法语 remede "remedy, cure" (12 世纪, 现代法语 remède) and 直接源自 拉丁语 remedium "a cure, remedy, medicine, antidote, that which restores health," 源自 re-, intensive prefix (or 或许 字面义为, "again;" 参见 re-), + mederi "to heal" （参见 medical （形）). Figurative use 源自 约 1300 年.

example.en: Rest and fluids are the best remedy for a common cold.
example.zh: 休息和补充水分是治疗普通感冒的最佳方法。

definitionLines: vt. 记住，记得；（to）转达问候
entries.definition: vt. 记住，记得；（to）转达问候 vi. 记得，记住
entries.etymology: early 14c., "keep in mind, retain in the memory," from Old French remembrer "remember, recall, bring to mind" (11c.), from Latin rememorari "recall to mind, remember," from re- "again" (see re-) + memorari "be mindful of," from memor "mindful" (see memory). Meaning "recall to mind" is late 14c.; sense of "to mention" is from 1550s. Also in Middle English "to remind" (someone). An Anglo-Saxon verb for it was gemunan.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "keep in mind, retain in the memory," 源自 古法语 remembrer "remember, recall, bring to mind" (11 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 rememorari "recall to mind, remember," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + memorari "be mindful of," 源自 memor "mindful" （参见 memory). 义为 "recall to mind" is 14 世纪晚期; 语义 "to mention" 始于 1550 年代. Also in 中古英语 "to remind" (someone). An 盎格鲁-撒克逊语 动词 for it was gemunan.

example.en: Please remember to submit your report before the end of the week.
example.zh: 请记得在本周末之前提交你的报告。

entries.etymology: 1640s, "to remember," from re- "again" + mind (v.). Meaning "to put (someone) in mind of (something)" is first recorded 1650s. Related: Reminded; reminding.
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, "to remember," 源自 re- "again" + mind （动）. 义为 "to put (someone) in mind of (something)" is 首见于 1650 年代. 同源词：Reminded; reminding.

example.en: The smell of coffee always remind me of mornings at home.
example.zh: 咖啡的香味总是让我想起在家的早晨。

definitionLines: a.遥远的，偏僻的；疏远的，远 缘的
entries.definition: a.遥远的，偏僻的；疏远的，远 缘的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French remot or directly from Latin remotus "afar off, remote, distant in place," past participle of removere "move back or away" (see remove (v.)). Related: Remotely; remoteness. Remote control "fact of controlling from a distance" is recorded from 1904; as a device which allows this from 1920.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 remot or 直接源自 拉丁语 remotus "afar off, remote, distant in place," 为 … 的过去分词 removere "move back or away" （参见 remove （动）). 同源词：Remotely; remoteness. Remote control "fact of controlling from a distance" 见于 1904 年; 作为 device which allows this 自 1920 年起.

example.en: The research station was so remote that supplies could only be delivered by helicopter.
example.zh: 这个研究站如此偏远，物资只能靠直升机运送。

entries.etymology: 1590s; see remove (v.) + -al (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代; 参见 remove （动） + -al (2).

example.en: The removal of hazardous waste must follow strict safety protocols.
example.zh: 危险废物的清除必须遵循严格的安全规程。

definitionLines: vt. 排除，消除，去掉；搬迁，移 动，运走
entries.definition: vt. 排除，消除，去掉；搬迁，移 动，运走
entries.etymology: early 14c., "move, take away, dismiss," from Old French removoir "move, stir; leave, depart; take away," from Latin removere "move back or away, take away, put out of view, subtract," from re- "back, away" (see re-) + movere "to move" (see move (v.)). Related: Removed; removing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "move, take away, dismiss," 源自 古法语 removoir "move, stir; leave, depart; take away," 源自 拉丁语 removere "move back or away, take away, put out of view, subtract," 源自 re- "back, away" （参见 re-) + movere "to move" （参见 move （动）). 同源词：Removed; removing.

example.en: The surgeon used a laser to remove the scar tissue from the patient's skin.
example.zh: 外科医生用激光去除了患者皮肤上的瘢痕组织。

entries.etymology:
"great period of revival of classical-based art and learning in Europe that began in the fourteenth century," 1840, from French renaissance des lettres, from Old French renaissance, literally "rebirth," usually in a spiritual sense, from renastre "grow anew" (of plants), "be reborn" (Modern French renaître), from Vulgar Latin *renascere, from Latin renasci "be born again, rise again, reappear, be renewed," from re- "again" (see re-) + nasci "be born" (Old Latin gnasci; see genus).

An earlier term for it was revival of learning (1785). In general usage, with a lower-case r-, "a revival" of anything that has long been in decay or disuse (especially of learning, literature, art), it is attested from 1872. Renaissance man is first recorded 1906.
entries.etymologyZh: "great period of revival of classical-based art and learning in Europe that began in the fourteenth century," 1840 年, 源自 法语 renaissance des lettres, 源自 古法语 renaissance, 字面义为 "rebirth," 通常 in a spiritual sense, 源自 renastre "grow anew" (of plants), "be reborn" (现代法语 renaître), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *renascere, 源自 拉丁语 renasci "be born again, rise again, reappear, be renewed," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + nasci "be born" (Old 拉丁语 gnasci; 参见 genus). An earlier term for it was revival of learning (1785 年). In general usage, with a lower-case r-, "a revival" of anything that has long been in decay or disuse (尤指 of learning, literature, art), it 见于 1872 年. Renaissance man is 首见于 1906 年.

definitionLines: vt. 使得，致使；给予，提供； 翻译
entries.definition: vt. 使得，致使；给予，提供； 翻译
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "repeat, say again," from Old French rendre "give back, present, yield" (10c.), from Vulgar Latin *rendere (formed by dissimilation or on analogy of its antonym, prendre "to take"), from Latin reddere "give back, return, restore," from red- "back" (see re-) + comb. form of dare "to give" (see date (n.1)).

Meaning "hand over, deliver" is recorded from late 14c.; "to return" (thanks, a verdict, etc.) is attested from late 15c.; meaning "represent, depict" is first attested 1590s. Irregular retention of -er in a French verb in English is perhaps to avoid confusion with native rend (v.) or by influence of a Middle English legalese noun render "a payment of rent," from French noun use of the infinitive. Related: Rendered; rendering.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "repeat, say again," 源自 古法语 rendre "give back, present, yield" (10 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *rendere (formed by dissimilation or on analogy of its antonym, prendre "to take"), 源自 拉丁语 reddere "give back, return, restore," 源自 red- "back" （参见 re-) + comb. form of dare "to give" （参见 date (n.1)). 义为 "hand over, deliver" 见于 14 世纪晚期; "to return" (thanks, a verdict, etc.) 见于 15 世纪晚期; 意为 "represent, depict" is 最早见于 1590 年代. Irregular retention of -er in a 法语 动词 in English is 或许 to avoid confusion with 本族 rend （动） or by influence of a 中古英语 legalese 名词 render "a payment of rent," 源自 法语 为 … 的名词用法 the infinitive. 同源词：Rendered; rendering.

example.en: The new technology could render the old system obsolete within a decade.
example.zh: 这项新技术可能在十年内使旧系统过时。

definitionLines: n. 重新开始，继续；使更新， 更换
entries.definition: n. 重新开始，继续；使更新， 更换
entries.etymology: late 14c., from re- "again" + Middle English newen "resume, revive, renew" (see new); formed on analogy of Latin renovare. Related: Renewed; renewing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 re- "again" + 中古英语 newen "resume, revive, renew" （参见 new); formed on analogy of 拉丁语 renovare. 同源词：Renewed; renewing.

example.en: You need to renew your library card every year to keep borrowing books.
example.zh: 你需要每年续办图书馆借书证，才能继续借书。

entries.etymology: "celebrated, famous," late 14c., past participle adjective from renown.
entries.etymologyZh: "celebrated, famous," 14 世纪晚期, past participle 形容词 源自 renown.

example.en: The surgeon is internationally renowned for her pioneering work in heart transplants and has received many top awards.
example.zh: 这位外科医生因在心脏移植领域的开创性工作而享誉国际，并获得了许多顶级奖项。

entries.definition: vt./n. 修理，修复 vt. 补救，纠正
entries.etymology: 1590s, "act of restoring, restoration after decay," from repair (v.1). Meaning "state or condition in respect to reparation" is from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "act of restoring, restoration after decay," 源自 repair (v.1). 义为 "state or condition in respect to reparation" 始于 约 1600 年.

example.en: The mechanic will repair the engine before the road trip.
example.zh: 机械师会在公路旅行前修好这台发动机。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Old French repaier "pay back, give in return," from re- "back" (see re-) + payer "to pay" (see pay (v.)). Related: Repaid; repaying.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 repaier "pay back, give in return," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + payer "to pay" （参见 pay （动）). 同源词：Repaid; repaying.

definitionLines: v. 重复，重说，重做；背，背诵
entries.definition: v. 重复，重说，重做；背，背诵 n. 重复
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to say what one has already said," from Old French repeter "say or do again, get back, demand the return of" (13c., Modern French répéeter), from Latin repetere "do or say again; attack again," from re- "again" (see re-) + petere "to go to; attack; strive after; ask for, beseech" (see petition (n.)).

Meaning "say what another has said" is from 1590s. As an emphatic word in radio broadcasts, 1938. Meaning "do over again" is from 1550s; specific meaning "to take a course of education over again" is recorded from 1945, American English. Related: Repeated; repeating.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to say what one has already said," 源自 古法语 repeter "say or do again, get back, demand the return of" (13 世纪, 现代法语 répéeter), 源自 拉丁语 repetere "do or say again; attack again," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + petere "to go to; attack; strive after; ask for, beseech" （参见 petition （名）). 义为 "say what another has said" 始于 1590 年代. 作为 emphatic word in radio broadcasts, 1938 年. 义为 "do over again" 始于 1550 年代; specific 意为 "to take a course of education over again" 见于 1945 年, American English. 同源词：Repeated; repeating.

example.en: The teacher asked students to repeat the key phrases aloud until they knew them by heart.
example.zh: 老师要求学生大声反复复诵关键短语，直到熟记于心。

example.en: She repeatedly warned him not to ignore the safety guidelines.
example.zh: 她一再警告他不要忽视安全规定。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to drive away, remove," from Old French repeller or directly from Latin repellere "to drive back," from re- "back" (see re-) + pellere "to drive, strike" (see pulse (n.1)). Meaning "to affect (a person) with distaste or aversion" is from 1817. Related: Repelled; repelling.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to drive away, remove," 源自 古法语 repeller or 直接源自 拉丁语 repellere "to drive back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + pellere "to drive, strike" （参见 pulse (n.1)). 义为 "to affect (a person) with distaste or aversion" 始于 1817 年. 同源词：Repelled; repelling.

entries.etymology: early 15c., "act of saying over again," from Old French repetition and directly from Latin repetitionem (nominative repetitio) "a repeating," noun of action from past participle stem of repetere "do or say again" (see repeat (v.)). Of actions, attested from 1590s; specifically in physical fitness from 1958.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "act of saying over again," 源自 古法语 repetition and 直接源自 拉丁语 repetitionem (主格 repetitio) "a repeating," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of repetere "do or say again" （参见 repeat （动）). Of actions, attested 源自 1590 年代; specifically in physical fitness 自 1958 年起.

example.en: Language learning requires repetition of new vocabulary until it becomes automatic.
example.zh: 语言学习需要反复练习新词汇，直到形成自动反应。
