entries.etymology: 1590s, "to restore to a previous place or position," from re- "back, again" + place (v.). Meaning "to take the place of" is recorded from 1753; that of "to fill the place of (with something else)" is from 1765. Related: Replaced; replacing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "to restore to a previous place or position," 源自 re- "back, again" + place （动）. 义为 "to take the place of" 见于 1753 年; that of "to fill the place of (with something else)" 始于 1765 年. 同源词：Replaced; replacing.

example.en: The company decided to replace its outdated software with a modern system.
example.zh: 该公司决定用现代系统取代其过时的软件。

definitionLines: n. 取代，替换，交换；替代品， 代用品
entries.definition: n. 取代，替换，交换；替代品， 代用品
entries.etymology: "act or fact of being replaced," 1790, from replace (v.) + -ment. Meaning "something that replaces another" is attested from 1894.
entries.etymologyZh: "act or fact of being replaced," 1790 年, 源自 replace （动） + -ment. 义为 "something that replaces another" 见于 1894 年.

example.en: The broken part requires immediate replacement to avoid further damage.
example.zh: 损坏的零件需要立即更换，以避免进一步损坏。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "to make an answer," from Old French replier "to reply, turn back," from Late Latin replicare "to reply, repeat," in classical Latin "fold back, fold over, bend back," from re- "back, again" (see re-) + plicare "to fold" (see ply (v.1)). Latin literal sense of "to fold back" is attested from mid-15c. in English but is not now used. Modern French répliquer (Middle French replier) is directly from Late Latin. Related: Replied; replying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to make an answer," 源自 古法语 replier "to reply, turn back," 源自 晚期拉丁语 replicare "to reply, repeat," in classical 拉丁语 "fold back, fold over, bend back," 源自 re- "back, again" （参见 re-) + plicare "to fold" （参见 ply (v.1)). 拉丁语 literal 语义 "to fold back" 见于 15 世纪中期 in English but is not 现在 used. 现代法语 répliquer (中古法语 replier) is 直接源自 晚期拉丁语. 同源词：Replied; replying.

example.en: She sent a brief email to reply to the job offer she had received.
example.zh: 她发了一封简短的邮件回复收到的工作邀请。

entries.definition: vt./n. 报告，报道，报导 n.传说，传闻 vi. 报到；报告
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "an account brought by one person to another, rumor," from Old French report "pronouncement, judgment" (Modern French rapport), from reporter "to tell, relate" (see report (v.)).

Meaning "resounding noise, sound of an explosion" is from 1580s. Meaning "formal statement of results of an investigation" first attested 1660s; sense of "teacher's official statement of a pupil's work and behavior" is from 1873 (report card in the school sense first attested 1919).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "an account brought by one person to another, rumor," 源自 古法语 report "pronouncement, judgment" (现代法语 rapport), 源自 reporter "to tell, relate" （参见 report （动）). 义为 "resounding noise, sound of an explosion" 始于 1580 年代. 义为 "formal statement of results of an investigation" 最早见于 1660 年代; 语义 "teacher's official statement of a pupil's work and behavior" 始于 1873 年 (report card in the school sense 最早见于 1919 年).

example.en: The journalist was assigned to report on the humanitarian crisis at the border.
example.zh: 这名记者被指派报道边境的人道主义危机。

definitionLines: n. 记者，报导者，通讯员
entries.definition: n. 记者，报导者，通讯员
entries.etymology: late 14c., reportour, "one who gives an account," agent noun from report (v.), or from Old French reporteur (Modern French rapporteur). In the newspaper sense, from 1798. French reporter in this sense is a 19c. borrowing from English.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, reportour, "one who gives an account," agent 名词 源自 report （动），或源自 古法语 reporteur (现代法语 rapporteur). In the newspaper sense, 自 1798 年起. 法语 reporter in this sense is a 19 世纪 borrowing 源自 English.

example.en: The reporter asked the politician several tough questions about the scandal.
example.zh: 记者就丑闻向那位政客提出了几个尖锐的问题。

definitionLines: vt. 表示，阐明，说明；描写， 表现，象征；代理，代表
entries.definition: vt. 表示，阐明，说明；描写， 表现，象征；代理，代表
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to bring to mind by description," also "to symbolize, serve as a sign or symbol of; serve as the type or embodiment of;" from Old French representer "present, show, portray" (12c.), from Latin repraesentare "make present, set in view, show, exhibit, display," from re-, intensive prefix (see re-), + praesentare "to present," literally "to place before" (see present (v.)). Legislative sense is attested from 1650s. Related: Represented; representing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to bring to mind by description," also "to symbolize, serve as a sign or symbol of; serve as the type or embodiment of;" 源自 古法语 representer "present, show, portray" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 repraesentare "make present, set in view, show, exhibit, display," 源自 re-, intensive prefix （参见 re-), + praesentare "to present," 字面义为 "to place before" （参见 present （动）). Legislative sense 见于 1650 年代. 同源词：Represented; representing.

example.en: In China, the dragon represents imperial power and good fortune, not danger.
example.zh: 在中国，龙象征皇权和好运，而非危险。

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "image, likeness," from Old French representacion (14c.) and directly from Latin representationem (nominative representatio), noun of action from past participle stem of repraesentare (see represent). Meaning "statement made in regard to some matter" is from 1670s. Legislative sense first attested 1769.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "image, likeness," 源自 古法语 representacion (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 representationem (主格 representatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of repraesentare （参见 represent). 义为 "statement made in regard to some matter" 始于 1670 年代. Legislative sense 最早见于 1769 年.

example.en: The election results showed an imbalance in women's political representation.
example.zh: 选举结果显示女性政治代表性存在失衡。

definitionLines: a. 抑制的；镇压的；压抑的
entries.definition: a. 抑制的；镇压的；压抑的
entries.etymology: early 15c., from Middle French repressif, from Latin repress-, past participle stem of reprimere (see repress). Related: Repressively.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古法语 repressif, 源自 拉丁语 repress-, past participle stem of reprimere （参见 repress). 同源词：Repressively.

definitionLines: v. 繁殖，生殖；复制，仿造
entries.definition: v. 繁殖，生殖；复制，仿造
entries.etymology: 1610s, "to produce again," from re- "again" + produce (v.), probably on model of French reproduire (16c.). Sense of "make a copy" is first recorded 1850; that of "produce offspring" is from 1894. Related: Reproduced; reproducing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "to produce again," 源自 re- "again" + produce （动）, 可能 on model of 法语 reproduire (16 世纪). 义为 "make a copy" is 首见于 1850 年; that of "produce offspring" 始于 1894 年. 同源词：Reproduced; reproducing.

example.en: Bacteria can reproduce rapidly under warm and moist conditions.
example.zh: 细菌在温暖潮湿的环境下能迅速繁殖。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "state in which supreme power rests in the people via elected representatives," from Middle French république (15c.), from Latin respublica (ablative republica) "the common weal, a commonwealth, state, republic," literally res publica "public interest, the state," from res "affair, matter, thing" + publica, fem. of publicus "public" (see public (adj.)). Republic of letters attested from 1702.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "state in which supreme power rests in the people via elected representatives," 源自 中古法语 république (15 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 respublica (ablative republica) "the common weal, a commonwealth, state, republic," 字面义为 res publica "public interest, the state," 源自 res "affair, matter, thing" + publica, fem. of publicus "public" （参见 public （形）). Republic of letters attested 自 1702 年起.

example.en: France became a republic after its revolution in the eighteenth century.
example.zh: 法国在十八世纪革命后成为一个共和国。

entries.definition: a. 共和政体的 n. 共和党人
entries.etymology: 1712, "belonging to a republic, of the nature of a republic, consonant to the principles of a republic," from republic + -an. The French republican calendar was in use from Nov. 26, 1793 to Dec. 31, 1805.
entries.etymologyZh: 1712 年, "belonging to a republic, of the nature of a republic, consonant to the principles of a republic," 源自 republic + -an. The 法语 republican calendar was in use 源自 Nov. 26, 1793 年 to Dec. 31, 1805 年.

entries.etymology: mid-14c., "credit, good reputation," from Latin reputationem (nominative reputatio) "consideration, a thinking over," noun of action from past participle stem of reputare "reflect upon, reckon, count over," from re- "repeatedly" (see re-) + putare "to reckon, consider" (see putative).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "credit, good reputation," 源自 拉丁语 reputationem (主格 reputatio) "consideration, a thinking over," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of reputare "reflect upon, reckon, count over," 源自 re- "repeatedly" （参见 re-) + putare "to reckon, consider" （参见 putative).

example.en: The scientist built a solid reputation for accuracy and careful research.
example.zh: 这位科学家凭借严谨的研究树立了扎实的声誉。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French requeste (Modern French requête) "a request," from Vulgar Latin *requaesita, from Latin requisita "a thing asked for," fem. of requisitus "requested, demanded," from past participle stem of requirere (see require).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 requeste (现代法语 requête) "a request," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *requaesita, 源自 拉丁语 requisita "a thing asked for," fem. of requisitus "requested, demanded," 源自 past participle stem of requirere （参见 require).

example.en: She made a formal request for more time to finish the project.
example.zh: 她正式申请了更多时间来完成这个项目。

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "to ask a question, inquire," from Old French requerre "seek, procure; beg, ask, petition; demand," from Vulgar Latin *requaerere, from Latin requirere "seek to know, ask," from re-, here perhaps meaning "repeatedly" (see re-), + quaerere "ask, seek" (see query (v.)).

The original sense of this word has been taken over by request (v.). Sense of "demand (someone) to do (something)" is from 1751, via the notion of "to ask for imperatively, or as a right" (late 14c.). Related: Required; requiring.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to ask a question, inquire," 源自 古法语 requerre "seek, procure; beg, ask, petition; demand," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *requaerere, 源自 拉丁语 requirere "seek to know, ask," 源自 re-, here 或许 意为 "repeatedly" （参见 re-), + quaerere "ask, seek" （参见 query （动）). The original 语义 this word has been taken over by request （动）. 义为 "demand (someone) to do (something)" 始于 1751 年, 经由 the 概念 "to ask for imperatively, or as a right" (14 世纪晚期). 同源词：Required; requiring.

example.en: The professor required students to cite all sources in their research papers.
example.zh: 教授要求学生在研究论文中引用所有来源。

entries.etymology: 1520s, "request, requisition," from require + -ment. Meaning "things required, a need" is from 1660s. Meaning "that which must be accomplished, necessary condition" is from 1841. Related: Requirements.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "request, requisition," 源自 require + -ment. 义为 "things required, a need" 始于 1660 年代. 义为 "that which must be accomplished, necessary condition" 始于 1841 年. 同源词：Requirements.

example.en: Meeting the entry requirement of this program requires at least three years of experience.
example.zh: 满足该项目的入学要求至少需要三年的工作经验。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from rescue (v.). Earlier noun was rescous (early 14c.), from Old French rescous.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 rescue （动）. Earlier 名词 was rescous (14 世纪初), 源自 古法语 rescous.

example.en: The firefighters managed to rescue the family trapped in the burning building.
example.zh: 消防员设法救出了被困在燃烧建筑中的家庭。

entries.etymology: 1570s, "act of searching closely," from Middle French recerche (1530s, Modern French recherche), back-formation from Old French recercher (see research (v.)). Meaning "scientific inquiry" is first attested 1630s. Phrase research and development is recorded from 1923.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "act of searching closely," 源自 中古法语 recerche (1530 年代, 现代法语 recherche), back-formation 源自 古法语 recercher （参见 research （动）). 义为 "scientific inquiry" is 最早见于 1630 年代. Phrase research and development 见于 1923 年.

example.en: Scientists conducted extensive research to understand how the virus spreads.
example.zh: 科学家们进行了大量研究，以了解病毒的传播方式。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French resembler "belike" (12c., Modern French ressemble), from re-, intensive prefix, + sembler "to appear, to seem, be like," from Latin simulare "to copy" (see similar (adj.)). Related: Resembled; resembling.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 resembler "belike" (12 世纪, 现代法语 ressemble), 源自 re-, intensive prefix, + sembler "to appear, to seem, be like," 源自 拉丁语 simulare "to copy" （参见 similar （形）). 同源词：Resembled; resembling.

example.en: The twins resemble each other so closely that even their parents were confused.
example.zh: 这对双胞胎彼此太相像了，连他们的父母都搞不清。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of reserving," from Old French reservation (14c.) and directly from Late Latin reservationem (nominative reservatio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin reservare (see reserve (n.)). Mental sense is from c. 1600. U.S. sense "tract of public land set aside for some special use" is recorded from 1789, originally in reference to the Six Nations in New York State. Meaning "act or fact of engaging a room, a seat, etc." is from 1904, originally American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of reserving," 源自 古法语 reservation (14 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 reservationem (主格 reservatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 reservare （参见 reserve （名）). Mental sense 始于 约 1600 年. U.S. sense "tract of public land set aside for some special use" 见于 1789 年, 原义为 in reference to the Six Nations in New York State. 义为 "act or fact of engaging a room, a seat, etc." 始于 1904 年, 原义为 American English.

example.en: Please call ahead to make a reservation before your arrival at the resort.
example.zh: 请提前致电，在抵达度假村前进行预订。

entries.etymology: "take (something) ill; be in some degree angry or provoked at," c. 1600, from French ressentir "feel pain, regret," from Old French resentir "feel again, feel in turn" (13c.), from re-, intensive prefix, + sentir "to feel," from Latin sentire (see sense (n.)). Related: Resented; resenting.
entries.etymologyZh: "take (something) ill; be in some degree angry or provoked at," 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 ressentir "feel pain, regret," 源自 古法语 resentir "feel again, feel in turn" (13 世纪), 源自 re-, intensive prefix, + sentir "to feel," 源自 拉丁语 sentire （参见 sense （名）). 同源词：Resented; resenting.

example.en: She began to resent her coworkers for getting the credit she deserved.
example.zh: 她开始怨恨同事们抢走了本该属于她的功劳。

definitionLines: n. 储备品，储备金，储备；保留 地；节制，谨慎
entries.definition: vt. 保留；储备；预定 n. 储备品，储备金，储备；保留 地；节制，谨慎
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French reserver "set aside, withhold" (12c.) and directly from Latin reservare "keep back, save up; retain, preserve," from re- "back" (see re-) + servare "to keep, save, preserve, protect" (see observe). Meaning "to book" is from 1935. Related: Reserved; reserving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 reserver "set aside, withhold" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 reservare "keep back, save up; retain, preserve," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + servare "to keep, save, preserve, protect" （参见 observe). 义为 "to book" 始于 1935 年. 同源词：Reserved; reserving.

example.en: The hotel asked us to reserve a table two weeks in advance for the holiday dinner.
example.zh: 酒店要求我们提前两周预订节日晚餐的座位。

entries.etymology: 1680s, "a place where something tends to collect," originally figurative, from French réservoir "storehouse," from Old French reserver "to reserve" (see reserve (n.)). Specific meaning "artificial basin to collect and store a large body of water" is from 1705.
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, "a place where something tends to collect," 原义为 figurative, 源自 法语 réservoir "storehouse," 源自 古法语 reserver "to reserve" （参见 reserve （名）). Specific 意为 "artificial basin to collect and store a large body of water" 始于 1705 年.

example.en: The drought caused water levels in the reservoir to drop dramatically.
example.zh: 干旱导致水库水位急剧下降。

entries.definition: n. 居民，常住者 a.居住的，住校的，住院的
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "an inhabitant, one who resides," from resident (adj.). Meaning "medical graduate in practice in a hospital as training" first attested 1892, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "an inhabitant, one who resides," 源自 resident （形）. 义为 "medical graduate in practice in a hospital as training" 最早见于 1892 年, American English.

example.en: Local residents gathered at the town hall to discuss the new housing plan.
example.zh: 当地居民聚集在市政厅，讨论新的住房规划。

entries.etymology: 1650s, "serving as a residence," from resident (n.) + -ial. Meaning "having to do with housing" is from 1856.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "serving as a residence," 源自 resident （名） + -ial. 义为 "having to do with housing" 始于 1856 年.

example.en: The city council approved new residential buildings in the suburbs.
example.zh: 市议会批准在郊区修建新的住宅楼。

entries.definition: vt. 辞去，辞职，放弃 vi.辞职
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "give up, surrender, abandon, submit; relinquish," from Old French resigner "renounce, relinquish" (13c.), from Latin resignare "to check off, annul, cancel, give back, give up," from re- "opposite" (see re-) + signare "to make an entry in an account book," literally "to mark" (see sign (v.)).

The sense is of making an entry (signum) "opposite" -- on the credit side -- balancing the former mark and thus canceling the claim it represents. The specific meaning of "give up a position" is first recorded late 14c. Sense of "to give (oneself) up to some emotion or situation" is from 1718. Related: Resigned; resigning.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "give up, surrender, abandon, submit; relinquish," 源自 古法语 resigner "renounce, relinquish" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 resignare "to check off, annul, cancel, give back, give up," 源自 re- "opposite" （参见 re-) + signare "to make an entry in an account book," 字面义为 "to mark" （参见 sign （动）). The sense is of making an entry (signum) "opposite" -- on the credit side -- balancing the former mark and thus canceling the claim it represents. The specific 意为 of "give up a position" is 首见于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "to give (oneself) up to some emotion or situation" 始于 1718 年. 同源词：Resigned; resigning.

example.en: After years of disagreement with management, she decided to resign from her position.
example.zh: 在与管理层争执多年之后，她决定辞去职务。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "act of resigning" (an office, etc.), from Old French resignation (14c.) and directly from Medieval Latin resignationem (nominative resignatio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin resignare (see resign). Meaning "submission, acquiescence" is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of resigning" (an office, etc.), 源自 古法语 resignation (14 世纪) and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 resignationem (主格 resignatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 resignare （参见 resign). 义为 "submission, acquiescence" 始于 1640 年代.

example.en: The CEO submitted his resignation after the company's worst financial quarter.
example.zh: 在公司最糟糕的财季之后，首席执行官提交了辞呈。

definitionLines: vt. 抵抗，反抗；忍住，抵制
entries.definition: vt. 抵抗，反抗；忍住，抵制
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French resister "hold out against" (14c.), from Latin resistere "to make a stand against, oppose; to stand back; withstand," from re- "against" (see re-) + sistere "take a stand, stand firm" (see assist). Related: Resisted; resisting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 resister "hold out against" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 resistere "to make a stand against, oppose; to stand back; withstand," 源自 re- "against" （参见 re-) + sistere "take a stand, stand firm" （参见 assist). 同源词：Resisted; resisting.

example.en: It was hard to resist the urge to check his phone during the meeting.
example.zh: 在会议期间忍住查看手机的冲动实在很难。

definitionLines: n. （to）抵抗，反抗；抵抗力， 阻力；电阻
entries.definition: n. （to）抵抗，反抗；抵抗力， 阻力；电阻
entries.etymology: mid-14c., from Old French resistance, earlier resistence, from Late Latin resistentia, from present participle stem of Latin resistere "make a stand against, oppose" (see resist). Meaning "organized covert opposition to an occupying or ruling power" [OED] is from 1939. Electromagnetic sense is from 1860. Path of least resistance is from 1825, originally a term in science and engineering.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 resistance, earlier resistence, 源自 晚期拉丁语 resistentia, 源自 present participle stem of 拉丁语 resistere "make a stand against, oppose" （参见 resist). 义为 "organized covert opposition to an occupying or ruling power" [OED] 始于 1939 年. Electromagnetic sense 始于 1860 年. Path of least resistance 始于 1825 年, 原义为 a term in science and engineering.

example.en: The bacteria developed resistance to the antibiotic after repeated exposure.
example.zh: 细菌在反复接触后对该抗生素产生了耐药性。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, from French résistant, present participle of résister (see resist). In reference to diseases or drugs from 1897.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 法语 résistant, 为 … 的现在分词 résister （参见 resist). In reference to diseases or drugs 自 1897 年起.

definitionLines: n. 决心，坚决；决定，决议（案）
entries.definition: n. 决心，坚决；决定，决议（案）
entries.etymology: late 14c., "a breaking into parts," from Old French resolution (14c.) or directly from Latin resolutionem (nominative resolutio) "process of reducing things into simpler forms," from past participle stem of resolvere "loosen" (see resolve). Sense of "a solving" (as of mathematical problems) first recorded 1540s, as is that of "power of holding firmly" (compare resolute). Sense of "decision or expression of a meeting" is from c. 1600. Meaning "effect of an optical instrument" is from 1860. New Year's resolution in reference to a specific intention to better oneself is from at least the 1780s, and through 19c. they generally were of a pious nature.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a breaking into parts," 源自 古法语 resolution (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 resolutionem (主格 resolutio) "process of reducing things into simpler forms," 源自 past participle stem of resolvere "loosen" （参见 resolve). 义为 "a solving" (as of mathematical problems) 首见于 1540 年代, as is that of "power of holding firmly" (对比 resolute). 义为 "decision or expression of a meeting" 始于 约 1600 年. 义为 "effect of an optical instrument" 始于 1860 年. New Year's resolution in reference to a specific intention to better oneself 始于 at least the 1780 年代, and through 19 世纪 they generally were of a pious nature.

example.en: The committee passed a resolution to cut carbon emissions by fifty percent.
example.zh: 委员会通过了一项将碳排放量削减百分之五十的决议。

definitionLines: vt.解决（问题等）；决定，下决 心；决议；分解
entries.definition: vt.解决（问题等）；决定，下决 心；决议；分解 n. 决心，决意
entries.etymology: late 14c., "melt, dissolve, reduce to liquid;" intransitive sense from c. 1400; from Old French resolver or directly from Latin resolvere "to loosen, loose, unyoke, undo; explain; relax; set free; make void, dispel," from re-, perhaps intensive, or "back" (see re-), + solvere "loosen" (see solve). Early 15c. as "separate into components," hence the use in optics (1785). Meaning "determine, decide upon" is from 1520s, hence "pass a resolution" (1580s). For sense evolution, compare resolute (adj.). Related: Resolved; resolving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "melt, dissolve, reduce to liquid;" intransitive sense 源自 约 1400 年; 源自 古法语 resolver or 直接源自 拉丁语 resolvere "to loosen, loose, unyoke, undo; explain; relax; set free; make void, dispel," 源自 re-, 或许 intensive，或"back" （参见 re-), + solvere "loosen" （参见 solve). Early 15 世纪 as "separate into components," hence the use in optics (1785 年). 义为 "determine, decide upon" 始于 1520 年代, hence "pass a resolution" (1580 年代). For sense evolution, 对比 resolute （形）. 同源词：Resolved; resolving.

example.en: The two sides finally agreed to resolve their long-standing differences through negotiation.
example.zh: 双方最终同意通过谈判解决长期以来的分歧。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "that to which one has recourse for aid or assistance," from Old French resort "resource, a help, an aid, a remedy," back-formation from resortir "to resort," literally "to go out again," from re- "again" (see re-) + sortir "go out" (see sortie). Meaning "place people go for recreation" is first recorded 1754. Phrase in the last resort (1670s) translates French en dernier ressort, originally of legal appeals.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "that to which one has recourse for aid or assistance," 源自 古法语 resort "resource, a help, an aid, a remedy," back-formation 源自 resortir "to resort," 字面义为 "to go out again," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + sortir "go out" （参见 sortie). 义为 "place people go for recreation" is 首见于 1754 年. Phrase in the last resort (1670 年代) translates 法语 en dernier ressort, 原义为 of legal appeals.

example.en: As a last resort, they called the emergency services.
example.zh: 作为最后手段，他们拨打了急救电话。

definitionLines: n..（p.）资源，财力；谋略， 应付办法
entries.definition: n..（p.）资源，财力；谋略， 应付办法
entries.etymology: 1610s, "means of supplying a want or deficiency," from French resourse "a source, spring," noun use of fem. past participle of Old French resourdre "to rally, raise again," from Latin resurgere "rise again" (see resurgent). Resources "a country's wealth" first recorded 1779.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "means of supplying a want or deficiency," 源自 法语 resourse "a source, spring," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 古法语 resourdre "to rally, raise again," 源自 拉丁语 resurgere "rise again" （参见 resurgent). Resources "a country's wealth" 首见于 1779 年.

example.en: The country must manage its water resource more carefully to avoid a crisis.
example.zh: 这个国家必须更谨慎地管理水资源以避免危机。

entries.definition: vt./n. 尊敬，尊重 n. （pl.）敬意，问候
entries.etymology: late 14c., "relationship, relation; regard, consideration," from Old French respect and directly from Latin respectus "regard, a looking at," literally "act of looking back (or often) at one," noun use of past participle of respicere "look back at, regard, consider," from re- "back" (see re-) + specere "look at" (see scope (n.1)). Meanings "feeling of esteem excited by actions or attributes of someone or something; courteous or considerate treatment due to personal worth or power" are from 1580s, as is sense of "point, particular feature."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "relationship, relation; regard, consideration," 源自 古法语 respect and 直接源自 拉丁语 respectus "regard, a looking at," 字面义为 "act of looking back (or often) at one," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 respicere "look back at, regard, consider," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + specere "look at" （参见 scope (n.1)). Meanings "feeling of esteem excited by actions or attributes of someone or something; courteous or considerate treatment due to personal worth or power" 始于 1580 年代, as is 语义 "point, particular feature."

example.en: Students are expected to respect their teachers and follow classroom rules.
example.zh: 学生应该尊重老师并遵守课堂规则。

definitionLines: a. 尊敬的，尊重的，恭敬的
entries.definition: a. 尊敬的，尊重的，恭敬的
entries.etymology: 1580s, "characterized by respect" (implied in respectfully), from respect (n.) + -ful. Meaning "full of outward civility" attested from 1680s. Related: Respectfulness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "characterized by respect" (implied in respectfully), 源自 respect （名） + -ful. 义为 "full of outward civility" attested 源自 1680 年代. 同源词：Respectfulness.

example.en: Students should always be respectful to their teachers and listen carefully in class.
example.zh: 学生在课堂上应当始终对老师恭敬有礼，认真听讲。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., "regardful, observing or noting with attention," from Medieval Latin respectivus "having regard for," from Latin respect- past participle stem of respicere (see respect (n.)). Meaning "relating or pertaining severally each to each" is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "regardful, observing or noting with attention," 源自 中古拉丁语 respectivus "having regard for," 源自 拉丁语 respect- past participle stem of respicere （参见 respect （名）). 义为 "relating or pertaining severally each to each" 始于 1640 年代.

example.en: When the meeting ended, the three managers each went back to their respective offices.
example.zh: 会议一结束，三位经理便各自回到了自己的办公室。

definitionLines: ad. 各自地，独自地，个别地， 分别地
entries.definition: ad. 各自地，独自地，个别地， 分别地
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "relatively;" 1620s, "relatively to each singly," from respective + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "relatively;" 1620 年代, "relatively to each singly," 源自 respective + -ly (2).

example.en: The two runners finished the race in eight and nine minutes respectively.
example.zh: 两名跑者分别用了八分钟和九分钟完成比赛。

definitionLines: vi. （to） 回答，答复；响应，起 反应
entries.definition: vi. （to） 回答，答复；响应，起 反应
entries.etymology: c. 1300, respound, from Old French respondere "respond, correspond," from Latin respondere "respond, answer to, promise in return," from re- "back" (see re-) + spondere "to pledge" (see spondee). Modern spelling and pronunciation is from c. 1600. Related: Responded; responding.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, respound, 源自 古法语 respondere "respond, correspond," 源自 拉丁语 respondere "respond, answer to, promise in return," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + spondere "to pledge" （参见 spondee). 现代 spelling and pronunciation 始于 约 1600 年. 同源词：Responded; responding.

example.en: The company failed to respond to customers' complaints in a timely manner.
example.zh: 该公司未能及时回应顾客的投诉。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French respons (Modern French réponse) and directly from Latin responsum "an answer," noun use of neuter past participle of respondere "to respond" (see respond).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 respons (现代法语 réponse) and 直接源自 拉丁语 responsum "an answer," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter 为 … 的过去分词 respondere "to respond" （参见 respond).

example.en: The company issued a formal written response to the regulatory body's findings.
example.zh: 公司就监管机构的调查结果发表了正式书面回应。

entries.etymology: "condition of being responsible," 1787, from responsible + -ity. Meaning "that for which one is responsible" is from 1796. Related: Responsibilities.
entries.etymologyZh: "condition of being responsible," 1787 年, 源自 responsible + -ity. 义为 "that for which one is responsible" 始于 1796 年. 同源词：Responsibilities.

example.en: Taking responsibility for one's mistakes is a sign of maturity and integrity.
example.zh: 为自己的错误承担责任是成熟和诚信的表现。

definitionLines: a. （for）应负责的，有责任的； 可靠的，认真的，负责的；责 任重大的，重要的
entries.definition: a. （for）应负责的，有责任的； 可靠的，认真的，负责的；责 任重大的，重要的
entries.etymology: 1590s, "answerable" (to another, for something), from obsolete French responsible (13c., Modern French responsable, as if from Latin *responsabilis), from Latin respons-, past participle stem of respondere "to respond" (see respond). Meaning "accountable for one's actions" is attested from 1640s; that of "reliable, trustworthy" is from 1690s. Retains the sense of "obligation" in the Latin root word. Related: Responsibly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "answerable" (to another, for something), 源自 已废 法语 responsible (13 世纪, 现代法语 responsable, as if 源自 拉丁语 *responsabilis), 源自 拉丁语 respons-, past participle stem of respondere "to respond" （参见 respond). 义为 "accountable for one's actions" 见于 1640 年代; that of "reliable, trustworthy" 始于 1690 年代. Retains the 语义 "obligation" in the 拉丁语 root word. 同源词：Responsibly.

example.en: Each manager is responsible for submitting quarterly budget reports on time.
example.zh: 每位经理负责按时提交季度预算报告。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "making answer," from Middle French responsif and directly from Late Latin responsivus "answering," from Latin respons-, past participle stem of respondere (see respond). Meaning "responding to influence or action" is from 1762. Related: Responsively; responsiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "making answer," 源自 中古法语 responsif and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 responsivus "answering," 源自 拉丁语 respons-, past participle stem of respondere （参见 respond). 义为 "responding to influence or action" 始于 1762 年. 同源词：Responsively; responsiveness.

definitionLines: n./v. 休息，静止；信赖，依赖， 依据
entries.definition: n./v. 休息，静止；信赖，依赖， 依据 n.（the）其余的人/物

example.en: After the long hike, we stopped to rest our tired legs by the river.
example.zh: 长途徒步后，我们在河边停下来让疲惫的双腿休息。

entries.etymology:
1821, from French restaurant "a restaurant," originally "food that restores," noun use of present participle of restaurer "to restore or refresh," from Old French restorer (see restore).

Italian spelling ristorante attested in English by 1925.
entries.etymologyZh: 1821 年, 源自 法语 restaurant "a restaurant," 原义为 "food that restores," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的现在分词 restaurer "to restore or refresh," 源自 古法语 restorer （参见 restore). 意大利语 spelling ristorante 见于 English 截至 1925 年.

example.en: They decided to celebrate the promotion at a fancy restaurant downtown.
example.zh: 他们决定在市区一家高档餐厅庆祝晋升。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from rest (n.1) + -less. A general Germanic compound (Frisian restleas, Dutch rusteloos, German rastlos, Danish rastlös). Meaning "stirring constantly, desirous of action" is attested from late 15c. Related: Restlessly; restlessness. Old English had restleas "deprived of sleep."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 rest (n.1) + -less. A general 日耳曼语 复合词 (Frisian restleas, 荷兰语 rusteloos, 德语 rastlos, Danish rastlös). 义为 "stirring constantly, desirous of action" 见于 15 世纪晚期 同源词：Restlessly; restlessness. 古英语 had restleas "deprived of sleep."

entries.etymology:
late 14c., "a means of healing or restoring health; renewing of something lost," from Old French restoration (Modern French restauration) and directly from Late Latin restorationem (nominative restoratio), noun of action from past participle stem of Latin restaurare (see restore).

Mid-15c. as "the repairing of a building;" c. 1500 as "a restoring to a former state." With a capital R-, in reference to the reestablishment of the English monarchy under Charles II in 1660, from 1718. As a period in English theater, attested from 1898. In French history, it refers to 1814. An earlier word in this sense was restauration (late 14c.), from French.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "a means of healing or restoring health; renewing of something lost," 源自 古法语 restoration (现代法语 restauration) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 restorationem (主格 restoratio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 restaurare （参见 restore). Mid-15 世纪 as "the repairing of a building;" 约 1500 年 as "a restoring to a former state." With a capital R-, in reference to the reestablishment of the English monarchy under Charles II 于 1660 年, 自 1718 年起. 作为 period in English theater, attested 自 1898 年起. In 法语 history, it refers to 1814 年. An earlier word in this sense was restauration (14 世纪晚期), 源自 法语.

example.en: The restoration of the ancient temple took over a decade to complete.
example.zh: 这座古庙的修复工作历时十余年才得以完成。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to give back," also, "to build up again, repair," from Old French restorer, from Latin restaurare "repair, rebuild, renew," from re- "back, again" (see re-) + -staurare, as in instaurare "restore," from PIE *stau-ro-, from root *stā- "to stand, set down, make or be firm," with derivatives meaning "place or thing that is standing" (see stet). Related: Restored; restoring.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to give back," also, "to build up again, repair," 源自 古法语 restorer, 源自 拉丁语 restaurare "repair, rebuild, renew," 源自 re- "back, again" （参见 re-) + -staurare, as in instaurare "restore," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *stau-ro-, 源自 root *stā- "to stand, set down, make or be firm," with derivatives 意为 "place or thing that is standing" （参见 stet). 同源词：Restored; restoring.

example.en: The team worked hard to restore the damaged painting to its original state.
example.zh: 团队努力将这幅受损的画作修复至原来的状态。

entries.etymology: mid-14c., from stem of Old French restreindre "press, push together; curb, bridle; bandage" (12c.), from Latin restringere "draw back tightly, confine, check" (see restriction). Related: Restrained; restraining.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, 源自 stem of 古法语 restreindre "press, push together; curb, bridle; bandage" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 restringere "draw back tightly, confine, check" （参见 restriction). 同源词：Restrained; restraining.

entries.etymology: 1530s, from Latin restrictus, past participle of restringere (see restriction). Regarded 18c. as a Scottishism. Related: Restricted; restricting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 拉丁语 restrictus, 为 … 的过去分词 restringere （参见 restriction). Regarded 18 世纪 作为 Scottishism. 同源词：Restricted; restricting.

example.en: Budget cuts will restrict the number of staff the department can hire.
example.zh: 预算削减将限制该部门可以招聘的员工人数。

definitionLines: vi. 产生于，来自；结果；导致
entries.definition: n. 结果，成果，成绩 vi. 产生于，来自；结果；导致
entries.etymology: early 15c., "occur as a result, arise as a consequence," from Medieval Latin resultare "to result," in classical Latin "to spring forward, rebound," frequentative of past participle of resilire "to rebound" (see resilience). Related: Resulted; resulting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "occur as a result, arise as a consequence," 源自 中古拉丁语 resultare "to result," in classical 拉丁语 "to spring forward, rebound," 为 … 的反复体 为 … 的过去分词 resilire "to rebound" （参见 resilience). 同源词：Resulted; resulting.

example.en: The heavy rain resulted in several roads being flooded overnight.
example.zh: 这场大雨导致数条道路当晚被淹。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to regain, take back;" mid-15c., "recommence, continue, begin again after interruption," from Middle French resumer (14c.) and directly from Latin resumere "take again, take up again, assume again," from re- "again" (see re-) + sumere "take up" (compare assume). Meaning "begin again" is mid-15c. Intransitive sense "proceed after interruption" is from 1802. Related: Resumed; resuming.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to regain, take back;" 15 世纪中期, "recommence, continue, begin again after interruption," 源自 中古法语 resumer (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 resumere "take again, take up again, assume again," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + sumere "take up" (对比 assume). 义为 "begin again" is 15 世纪中期 Intransitive sense "proceed after interruption" 始于 1802 年. 同源词：Resumed; resuming.

example.en: She updated her resume before applying for the new position.
example.zh: 她在申请新职位之前更新了她的简历。

entries.etymology: mid-14c. "sell in small quantities or parcels," from Old French retaillier "cut back, cut off, pare, clip, reduce, circumcise," from re- "back" (see re-) + taillier "to cut, trim" (see tailor (n.)). Sometimes also "to deal out (information, etc.) in small quantities; hand down by report; recount, tell over again" (1590s). Related: Retailed; retailing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期 "sell in small quantities or parcels," 源自 古法语 retaillier "cut back, cut off, pare, clip, reduce, circumcise," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + taillier "to cut, trim" （参见 tailor （名）). Sometimes also "to deal out (information, etc.) in small quantities; hand down by report; recount, tell over again" (1590 年代). 同源词：Retailed; retailing.

example.en: The company sells its products through retail stores across the country.
example.zh: 该公司通过全国各地的零售门店销售产品。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., agent noun from retail (v.).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, agent 名词 源自 retail （动）.

example.en: The clothing brand partnered with a major online retailer to expand its reach.
example.zh: 这个服装品牌与一家主要的网络零售商合作以扩大市场覆盖。

entries.etymology: late 14c., "hold back, restrain;" c. 1400, "continue keeping, keep possession of," from Old French retenir "keep, retain; take into feudal service; hold back; remember" (12c.), from Latin retinere "hold back, keep back, detain, restrain," from re- "back" (see re-) + tenere "to hold" (see tenet). Meaning "keep (another) attached to one's person, keep in service" is from mid-15c.; specifically of lawyers from 1540s. Meaning "keep in the mind" is from c. 1500. Related: Retained; retaining.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "hold back, restrain;" 约 1400 年, "continue keeping, keep possession of," 源自 古法语 retenir "keep, retain; take into feudal service; hold back; remember" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 retinere "hold back, keep back, detain, restrain," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + tenere "to hold" （参见 tenet). 义为 "keep (another) attached to one's person, keep in service" 始于 15 世纪中期; specifically of lawyers 源自 1540 年代. 义为 "keep in the mind" 始于 约 1500 年. 同源词：Retained; retaining.

example.en: The company managed to retain most of its loyal customers despite the sudden price hike.
example.zh: 尽管突然提价，公司仍设法留住了大多数忠实客户。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from re- "back, again" + tell (v.). Related: Retold; retelling.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 re- "back, again" + tell （动）. 同源词：Retold; retelling.

definitionLines: vi. 退下，离开；退休，引退；隐退
entries.definition: vi. 退下，离开；退休，引退；隐退
entries.etymology:
1530s, of armies, "to retreat," from Middle French retirer "to withdraw (something)," from re- "back" (see re-) + Old French tirer "to draw" (see tirade). Related: Retired; retiring.

Meaning "to withdraw" to some place, especially for the sake of privacy, is recorded from 1530s; sense of "leave an occupation" first attested 1640s (implied in retirement). Meaning "to leave company and go to bed" is from 1660s. Transitive sense is from 1540s, originally "withdraw, lead back" (troops, etc.); meaning "to remove from active service" is from 1680s. Baseball sense of "to put out" is recorded from 1874.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, of armies, "to retreat," 源自 中古法语 retirer "to withdraw (something)," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + 古法语 tirer "to draw" （参见 tirade). 同源词：Retired; retiring. 义为 "to withdraw" to some place, 尤指 for the sake of privacy, 见于 1530 年代; 语义 "leave an occupation" 最早见于 1640 年代 (implied in retirement). 义为 "to leave company and go to bed" 始于 1660 年代. Transitive sense 始于 1540 年代, 原义为 "withdraw, lead back" (troops, etc.); 意为 "to remove from active service" 始于 1680 年代. Baseball 语义 "to put out" 见于 1874 年.

example.en: She plans to retire at sixty and move to the countryside to grow vegetables.
example.zh: 她计划六十岁退休，搬到乡下种蔬菜。

entries.etymology: 1550s, "make return in kind" (especially of an injury), from Old French retort and directly from Latin retortus, past participle of retorquere "turn back, twist back, throw back," from re- "back" (see re-) + torquere "to twist" (see torque (n.)). Applied to exchanges of jest or sarcasm by c. 1600, hence "say or utter sharply and aggressively in reply" (1620s). Related: Retorted; retorting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "make return in kind" (尤指 of an injury), 源自 古法语 retort and 直接源自 拉丁语 retortus, 为 … 的过去分词 retorquere "turn back, twist back, throw back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + torquere "to twist" （参见 torque （名）). Applied to exchanges of jest or sarcasm by 约 1600 年, hence "say or utter sharply and aggressively in reply" (1620 年代). 同源词：Retorted; retorting.

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "a step backward;" late 14c., "act of retiring or withdrawing; military signal for retiring from action or exercise," from Old French retret, noun use of past participle of retrere "draw back," from Latin retrahere "draw back, withdraw, call back," from re- "back" (see re-) + trahere "to draw" (see tract (n.1)). Meaning "place of seclusion" is from early 15c.; sense of "establishment for mentally ill persons" is from 1797. Meaning "period of retirement for religious self-examination" is from 1756.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "a step backward;" 14 世纪晚期, "act of retiring or withdrawing; military signal for retiring from action or exercise," 源自 古法语 retret, 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 retrere "draw back," 源自 拉丁语 retrahere "draw back, withdraw, call back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + trahere "to draw" （参见 tract (n.1)). 义为 "place of seclusion" 始于 15 世纪初; 语义 "establishment for mentally ill persons" 始于 1797 年. 义为 "period of retirement for religious self-examination" 始于 1756 年.

example.en: The army was forced to retreat after suffering heavy losses.
example.zh: 军队在遭受重大伤亡后被迫撤退。

entries.etymology: early 15c., retreve, originally in reference to dogs finding lost game, from Middle French retruev-, stem of Old French retreuver (Modern French retrouver) "find again, recover, meet again, recognize," from re- "again" (see re-) + trouver "to find," probably from Vulgar Latin *tropare "to compose" (see trove). Altered 16c. to retrive; modern form is from mid-17c.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, retreve, 原义为 in reference to dogs finding lost game, 源自 中古法语 retruev-, stem of 古法语 retreuver (现代法语 retrouver) "find again, recover, meet again, recognize," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + trouver "to find," 可能 源自 通俗拉丁语 *tropare "to compose" （参见 trove). Altered 16 世纪 to retrive; modern form 始于 17 世纪中期

example.en: The dog was trained to retrieve the ball each time it was thrown.
example.zh: 这只狗被训练成每次球被扔出后都能将球取回。

definitionLines: vt. 归还，送回；回报，报答
entries.definition: vi. /n.归，回；归还 vt. 归还，送回；回报，报答 a.回程的；回报的
entries.etymology: early 14c., "to come back, come or go back to a former position" (intransitive), from Old French retorner "turn back, turn round, return" (Modern French retourner), from re- "back" (see re-) + torner "to turn" (see turn (v.)). Transitive sense of "report officially" is early 15c.; "to send back" is mid-15c.; that of "to turn back" is from c. 1500. Meaning "to give in repayment" is 1590s; that of "give back, restore" c. 1600. Related: Returned; returning.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to come back, come or go back to a former position" (intransitive), 源自 古法语 retorner "turn back, turn round, return" (现代法语 retourner), 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + torner "to turn" （参见 turn （动）). Transitive 语义 "report officially" is 15 世纪初; "to send back" is 15 世纪中期; that of "to turn back" 始于 约 1500 年. 义为 "to give in repayment" is 1590 年代; that of "give back, restore" 约 1600 年. 同源词：Returned; returning.

example.en: He decided to return to his hometown after years abroad.
example.zh: 在海外多年后，他决定回到家乡。

entries.etymology:
c. 1600, "act or fact of coming together again," from re- "back, again" + union; or from French réunion (1540s). Meaning "meeting of persons of previous connection" is from 1820.

The island of Reunion, formerly known as Bourbon, was renamed during the French Revolution (1793) in commemoration of the 1792 union of revolutionaries from Marseille with the National Guard in Paris, renamed back to Bourbon after 1815, then back to the Revolutionary name after 1848.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "act or fact of coming together again," 源自 re- "back, again" + union; or 源自 法语 réunion (1540 年代). 义为 "meeting of persons of previous connection" 始于 1820 年. The island of Reunion, formerly known as Bourbon, was renamed during the 法语 Revolution (1793 年) in commemoration of the 1792 年 union of revolutionaries 源自 Marseille with the National Guard in Paris, renamed back to Bourbon after 1815 年, 之后 back to the Revolutionary name after 1848 年.

example.en: The whole family gathered for a reunion dinner after years of living apart.
example.zh: 分离多年后，全家人聚在一起共进团聚晚餐。

definitionLines: vt. 揭示，揭露，展现；告诉， 泄露
entries.definition: vt. 揭示，揭露，展现；告诉， 泄露
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French reveler "reveal" (14c.), from Latin revelare "reveal, uncover, disclose," literally "unveil," from re- "opposite of" (see re-) + velare "to cover, veil," from velum "a veil" (see veil (n.)). Related: Revealed; revealing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 reveler "reveal" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 revelare "reveal, uncover, disclose," 字面义为 "unveil," 源自 re- "opposite of" （参见 re-) + velare "to cover, veil," 源自 velum "a veil" （参见 veil （名）). 同源词：Revealed; revealing.

example.en: The audit revealed that millions of dollars had been secretly transferred overseas.
example.zh: 审计揭露了数百万美元被秘密转移到海外。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "disclosure of information to man by a divine or supernatural agency," from Old French revelacion and directly from Latin revelationem (nominative revelatio), noun of action from past participle stem of revelare "unveil, uncover, lay bare" (see reveal). General meaning "disclosure of facts" is attested from late 14c.; meaning "striking disclosure" is from 1862. As the name of the last book of the New Testament (Revelation of St. John), it is first attested late 14c. (see apocalypse); as simply Revelations, it is first recorded 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "disclosure of information to man by a divine or supernatural agency," 源自 古法语 revelacion and 直接源自 拉丁语 revelationem (主格 revelatio), 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of revelare "unveil, uncover, lay bare" （参见 reveal). General 意为 "disclosure of facts" 见于 14 世纪晚期; 意为 "striking disclosure" 始于 1862 年. As the name of the last book of the New Testament (Revelation of St. John), it is 最早见于 14 世纪晚期 （参见 apocalypse); as simply Revelations, it is 首见于 1690 年代.

example.en: The documentary was a revelation about the true cost of fast fashion.
example.zh: 这部纪录片揭示了快时尚真实代价，令人震惊。

entries.definition: n. 复仇；报复 vt. 报复；替……报仇
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French revengier, variant of revenchier "take revenge, avenge" (13c., Modern French revancher), from re-, intensive prefix (see re-), + vengier "take revenge," from Latin vindicare "to lay claim to, avenge, punish" (see vindicate).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 revengier, 为 … 的变体 revenchier "take revenge, avenge" (13 世纪, 现代法语 revancher), 源自 re-, intensive prefix （参见 re-), + vengier "take revenge," 源自 拉丁语 vindicare "to lay claim to, avenge, punish" （参见 vindicate).

example.en: She swore revenge against those who had destroyed her family.
example.zh: 她发誓要向那些毁了她家庭的人复仇。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "income from property or possessions," from Middle French revenue, in Old French, "a return," noun use of fem. past participle of revenir "come back" (10c.), from Latin revenire "return, come back," from re- "back" (see re-) + venire "come" (see venue). Meaning "public income" is first recorded 1680s; revenue sharing popularized from 1971. Revenuer "U.S. Department of Revenue agent," the bane of Appalachian moonshiners, first attested 1880.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "income from property or possessions," 源自 中古法语 revenue, in 古法语, "a return," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 revenir "come back" (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 revenire "return, come back," 源自 re- "back" （参见 re-) + venire "come" （参见 venue). 义为 "public income" is 首见于 1680 年代; revenue sharing popularized 自 1971 年起. Revenuer "U.S. Department of Revenue agent," the bane of Appalachian moonshiners, 最早见于 1880 年.

example.en: Tourism is a major source of revenue for the island government.
example.zh: 旅游业是该岛屿政府的主要财政收入来源。

definitionLines: v. 颠倒，反转；倒退，后退
n/a. 反面（的），颠倒（的），相 反（的）
entries.definition: v. 颠倒，反转；倒退，后退 n/a. 反面（的），颠倒（的），相 反（的）
entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French revers "reverse, cross, opposite" (13c.), from Latin reversus, past participle of revertere "turn back, turn about, come back, return" (see revert). Reverse angle in film-making is from 1934. Reverse discrimination is attested from 1962, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 revers "reverse, cross, opposite" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 reversus, 为 … 的过去分词 revertere "turn back, turn about, come back, return" （参见 revert). Reverse angle in film-making 始于 1934 年. Reverse discrimination 见于 1962 年, American English.

example.en: The appeals court voted to reverse the conviction, citing insufficient evidence.
example.zh: 上诉法院以证据不足为由，投票推翻了定罪判决。

definitionLines: vt. /n. 复习；复查，审核；回顾； 评论
entries.definition: vt. /n. 复习；复查，审核；回顾； 评论
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "an inspection of military forces," from Middle French reveue "a reviewing, review," noun use of fem. past participle of reveeir "to see again, go to see again," from Latin revidere, from re- "again" (see re-) + videre "to see" (see vision). Sense of "process of going over again" is from 1560s; that of "a view of the past, a retrospective survey" is from c. 1600. Meaning "general examination or criticism of a recent work" is first attested 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "an inspection of military forces," 源自 中古法语 reveue "a reviewing, review," 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 reveeir "to see again, go to see again," 源自 拉丁语 revidere, 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + videre "to see" （参见 vision). 义为 "process of going over again" 始于 1560 年代; that of "a view of the past, a retrospective survey" 始于 约 1600 年. 义为 "general examination or criticism of a recent work" is 最早见于 1640 年代.

example.en: Students are advised to review their class notes before the final examination.
example.zh: 建议学生在期末考试前复习课堂笔记。

entries.etymology: 1560s, "to look at again," from Middle French reviser (13c.), from Latin revisere "look at again, visit again, look back on," frequentative of revidere (past participle revisus), from re- "again" (see re-) + videre "to see" (see vision). Meaning "to look over again with intent to improve or amend" is recorded from 1590s. Related: Revised; revising.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, "to look at again," 源自 中古法语 reviser (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 revisere "look at again, visit again, look back on," 为 … 的反复体 revidere (past participle revisus), 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + videre "to see" （参见 vision). 义为 "to look over again with intent to improve or amend" 见于 1590 年代. 同源词：Revised; revising.

example.en: The editor asked the author to revise the final chapter before publication.
example.zh: 编辑要求作者在出版前修改最后一章。

entries.etymology: 1650s, "act of reviving;" 1660s, "the bringing of an old play back to the stage," from revive + -al (2). First in sense "general religious awakening in a community" by Cotton Mather, 1702; revivalist is first attested 1812.
entries.etymologyZh: 1650 年代, "act of reviving;" 1660 年代, "the bringing of an old play back to the stage," 源自 revive + -al (2). First in sense "general religious awakening in a community" by Cotton Mather, 1702 年; revivalist is 最早见于 1812 年.

example.en: The revival of interest in vinyl records surprised many music industry experts.
example.zh: 人们对黑胶唱片重燃兴趣让许多音乐业内人士感到惊讶。

definitionLines: vt. 使苏醒；使复兴；回想起
entries.definition: vi. 苏醒；复兴；复活 vt. 使苏醒；使复兴；回想起
entries.etymology: early 15c., "return to consciousness; restore to health," from Middle French revivre (10c.), from Latin revivere "to live again," from re- "again" (see re-) + vivere "to live" (see vital). Meaning "bring back to notice or fashion" is from mid-15c. Related: Revived; reviving.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "return to consciousness; restore to health," 源自 中古法语 revivre (10 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 revivere "to live again," 源自 re- "again" （参见 re-) + vivere "to live" （参见 vital). 义为 "bring back to notice or fashion" 始于 15 世纪中期 同源词：Revived; reviving.

example.en: The government launched a plan to revive the struggling economy.
example.zh: 政府推出了一项计划，以振兴陷入困境的经济。

entries.etymology: 1540s, from Middle French revolter (15c.), from Italian rivoltare "to overthrow, overturn," from Vulgar Latin *revolvitare "to overturn, overthrow," frequentative of Latin revolvere (past participle revolutus) "turn, roll back" (see revolve). Related: Revolted; revolting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 源自 中古法语 revolter (15 世纪), 源自 意大利语 rivoltare "to overthrow, overturn," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *revolvitare "to overturn, overthrow," 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 revolvere (past participle revolutus) "turn, roll back" （参见 revolve). 同源词：Revolted; revolting.

entries.etymology:
late 14c., originally of celestial bodies, from Old French revolucion "course, revolution (of celestial bodies)" (13c.), or directly from Late Latin revolutionem (nominative revolutio) "a revolving," noun of action from past participle stem of Latin revolvere "turn, roll back" (see revolve).

General sense of "instance of great change in affairs" is recorded from mid-15c. Political meaning "overthrow of an established political system" first recorded c. 1600, derived from French, and was especially applied to the expulsion of the Stuart dynasty under James II in 1688 and transfer of sovereignty to William and Mary.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 原义为 of celestial bodies, 源自 古法语 revolucion "course, revolution (of celestial bodies)" (13 世纪)，或直接源自 晚期拉丁语 revolutionem (主格 revolutio) "a revolving," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 revolvere "turn, roll back" （参见 revolve). General 语义 "instance of great change in affairs" 见于 15 世纪中期 Political 意为 "overthrow of an established political system" 首见于 约 1600 年, derived 源自 法语, and was 尤指 applied to the expulsion of the Stuart dynasty under James II 于 1688 年 and transfer of sovereignty to William and Mary.

example.en: The industrial revolution transformed how goods were produced and distributed.
example.zh: 工业革命改变了商品的生产和分配方式。

entries.definition: a. 革命的，革新的 n.革命者
entries.etymology: 1774; see revolution + -ary. As a noun, from 1850 (cf revolutionist).
entries.etymologyZh: 1774 年; 参见 revolution + -ary. 作名词时, 自 1850 年起 (cf revolutionist).

example.en: This revolutionary technology could change the way we communicate forever.
example.zh: 这项革命性的技术可能永远改变我们的沟通方式。

entries.definition: vi. 旋转；循环出现 vt. 使……旋转；使…•…循环
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to change direction, bend around, turn (the eyes) back," from Old French revolver and directly from Latin revolvere "roll back, unroll, unwind; happen again, return; go over, repeat," from re- "back, again" (see re-) + volvere "to roll" (see volvox). In 15c., "to turn over (in the mind or heart), meditate." Meaning "travel around a central point" first recorded 1660s (earlier "cause to travel in an orbit around a central point," mid-15c.). Related: Revolved; revolving.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to change direction, bend around, turn (the eyes) back," 源自 古法语 revolver and 直接源自 拉丁语 revolvere "roll back, unroll, unwind; happen again, return; go over, repeat," 源自 re- "back, again" （参见 re-) + volvere "to roll" （参见 volvox). In 15 世纪, "to turn over (in the mind or heart), meditate." 义为 "travel around a central point" 首见于 1660 年代 (earlier "cause to travel in an orbit around a central point," 15 世纪中期). 同源词：Revolved; revolving.

entries.definition: n. 酬谢，报酬，奖金 vt. 酬谢，报答，奖酬
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "a regarding, heeding, observation," from Anglo-French and Old North French reward, back-formation from rewarder (see reward (v.)). Meaning "repayment for some service" is from late 14c. Sense of "sum of money in exchange for capture" is from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "a regarding, heeding, observation," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 and Old North 法语 reward, back-formation 源自 rewarder （参见 reward （动）). 义为 "repayment for some service" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "sum of money in exchange for capture" 始于 1590 年代.

example.en: The company plans to reward employees who consistently exceed their annual targets.
example.zh: 公司计划对持续超额完成年度目标的员工给予奖励。

entries.etymology: 1550s, "rhymed verse, metrical movement," from Latin rhythmus "movement in time," from Greek rhythmos "measured flow or movement, rhythm; proportion, symmetry; arrangement, order; form, shape, wise, manner; soul, disposition," related to rhein "to flow," from PIE root *sreu- "to flow" (see rheum). Rhythm method of birth control attested from 1936. Rhythm and blues, U.S. music style, is from 1949 (first in "Billboard").
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "rhymed verse, metrical movement," 源自 拉丁语 rhythmus "movement in time," 源自 希腊语 rhythmos "measured flow or movement, rhythm; proportion, symmetry; arrangement, order; form, shape, wise, manner; soul, disposition," related to rhein "to flow," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *sreu- "to flow" （参见 rheum). Rhythm method of birth control attested 自 1936 年起. Rhythm and blues, U.S. music style, 始于 1949 年 (first in "Billboard").

example.en: The dancer moved perfectly in time with the rhythm of the music.
example.zh: 舞者完美地随着音乐的节奏起舞。

entries.etymology: Old English ribb "rib," from Proto-Germanic *rebja- (source also of Old Norse rif, Old Saxon ribbi, Old Frisian ribb, Middle Dutch, Dutch ribbe, Old High German ribba, German Rippe), literally "a covering" (of the cavity of the chest), from PIE *rebh- "to roof, cover" (source also of Greek ereptein "to roof," Old Church Slavonic rebro "rib, reef"). As an item of food from early 15c. Rib joint "brothel" is slang from 1943, probably in reference to Adam's rib (compare rib "woman, wife," attested from 1580s).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ribb "rib," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *rebja- (source also of 古北欧语 rif, 古撒克逊语 ribbi, 古弗里西语 ribb, Middle 荷兰语, 荷兰语 ribbe, 古高地德语 ribba, 德语 Rippe), 字面义为 "a covering" (of the cavity of the chest), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *rebh- "to roof, cover" (source also of 希腊语 ereptein "to roof," Old Church Slavonic rebro "rib, reef"). 作为 item of food 源自 15 世纪初 Rib joint "brothel" is 俚语 自 1943 年起, 可能 in reference to Adam's rib (对比 rib "woman, wife," attested 源自 1580 年代).

entries.etymology: early 14c., ribane, from Old French riban "a ribbon," variant of ruban (13c.), of unknown origin, possibly from a Germanic compound whose second element is related to band (n.1); compare Middle Dutch ringhband "necklace." Modern spelling is from mid-16c. Originally a stripe in a material. Custom of colored ribbon loops worn on lapels to declare support for some group perceived as suffering or oppressed began in 1991 with AIDS red ribbons.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, ribane, 源自 古法语 riban "a ribbon," 为 … 的变体 ruban (13 世纪), 来源不详, possibly 源自 a 日耳曼语 复合词 whose second element is related to band (n.1); 对比 Middle 荷兰语 ringhband "necklace." 现代 spelling 始于 16 世纪中期 Originally a stripe in a material. Custom of colored ribbon loops worn on lapels to declare support for some group perceived as suffering or oppressed began 于 1991 年 with AIDS red ribbons.

example.en: The children tied a colorful ribbon around each gift box.
example.zh: 孩子们在每个礼品盒上系了一条彩色缎带。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from Old French ris, from Italian riso, from Latin oriza, from Greek oryza "rice," via an Indo-Iranian language (compare Pashto vriže, Old Persian brizi), ultimately from Sanskrit vrihi-s "rice." The Greek word is the ultimate source of all European words (Welsh reis, German reis, Lithuanian rysai, Serbo-Croatian riza, Polish ryż, etc.). Introduced 1647 in the Carolinas. Rice paper (1822), originally used in China, Japan, etc., is made from straw of rice.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 古法语 ris, 源自 意大利语 riso, 源自 拉丁语 oriza, 源自 希腊语 oryza "rice," 经由 an Indo-Iranian language (对比 Pashto vriže, Old 波斯语 brizi), 最终源自 梵语 vrihi-s "rice." The 希腊语 word is the ultimate source of all European words (Welsh reis, 德语 reis, Lithuanian rysai, Serbo-Croatian riza, Polish ryż, etc.). Introduced 1647 年 in the Carolinas. Rice paper (1822 年), 原义为 used in China, Japan, etc., is made 源自 straw of rice.

example.en: Farmers in the region grow rice as their main crop.
example.zh: 该地区的农民以水稻为主要农作物。

definitionLines: vt. （of）免除，使获自由，使 摆脱
entries.definition: vt. （of）免除，使获自由，使 摆脱
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "clear (a space); set free, save," from a Scandinavian source akin to Old Norse ryðja (past tense ruddi, past participle ruddr) "to clear (land) of obstructions," from Proto-Germanic *reudijan (source also of Old High German riuten, German reuten "to clear land," Old Frisian rothia "to clear," Old English -royd "clearing," common in northern place names), from PIE root *reudh- "to clear land." The general sense of "to make (something) free (of something else)" emerged by 1560s. Senses merged somewhat with Northern English, Scottish, and U.S. dialectal redd. To get rid of (something or someone) is from 1660s. Related: Ridden; ridding.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "clear (a space); set free, save," 源自 a Scandinavian source akin to 古北欧语 ryðja (past tense ruddi, past participle ruddr) "to clear (land) of obstructions," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *reudijan (source also of 古高地德语 riuten, 德语 reuten "to clear land," 古弗里西语 rothia "to clear," 古英语 -royd "clearing," common in northern place names), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *reudh- "to clear land." The general 语义 "to make (something) free (of something else)" emerged by 1560 年代. Senses merged somewhat with Northern English, 苏格兰语, and U.S. 方言 redd. To get rid of (something or someone) 始于 1660 年代. 同源词：Ridden; ridding.

example.en: He finally managed to get rid of his old debt.
example.zh: 他终于设法摆脱了旧债务的困扰。

definitionLines: n. 谜，谜语；难解的问题，难理 解的人、物或情况
entries.definition: n. 谜，谜语；难解的问题，难理 解的人、物或情况

entries.etymology:
Old English ridan "sit or be carried on" (as on horseback), "move forward; rock; float, sail" (class I strong verb; past tense rad, past participle riden), from Proto-Germanic *ridan (source also of Old Norse riða, Old Saxon ridan, Old Frisian rida "to ride," Middle Dutch riden, Dutch rijden, Old High Germn ritan, German reiten), from PIE *reidh- "to ride" (source also of Old Irish riadaim "I travel," Old Gaulish reda "chariot"). Common to Celtic and Germanic, perhaps a loan word from one to the other.

Meaning "heckle" is from 1912; that of "have sex with (a woman)" is from mid-13c.; that of "dominate cruelly" is from 1580s. To ride out "endure (a storm, etc.) without great damage" is from 1520s. To ride shotgun is 1963, from custom of having an armed man beside the driver on the stagecoach in Old West movies to ward off trouble. To ride shank's mare "walk" is from 1846 (see shank (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ridan "sit or be carried on" (as on horseback), "move forward; rock; float, sail" (class I strong 动词; past tense rad, past participle riden), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *ridan (source also of 古北欧语 riða, 古撒克逊语 ridan, 古弗里西语 rida "to ride," Middle 荷兰语 riden, 荷兰语 rijden, Old High Germn ritan, 德语 reiten), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *reidh- "to ride" (source also of Old 爱尔兰语 riadaim "I travel," Old Gaulish reda "chariot"). Common to Celtic and 日耳曼语, 或许 a loan word 源自 one to the other. 义为 "heckle" 始于 1912 年; that of "have sex with (a woman)" 始于 13 世纪中期; that of "dominate cruelly" 始于 1580 年代. To ride out "endure (a storm, etc.) without great damage" 始于 1520 年代. To ride shotgun is 1963 年, 源自 custom of having an armed man beside the driver on the stagecoach in Old West movies to ward off trouble. To ride shank's mare "walk" 始于 1846 年 （参见 shank （名）).

example.en: They decided to ride their bikes to the park instead of taking the bus.
example.zh: 他们决定骑自行车去公园，而不是坐公共汽车。

entries.etymology: Old English hrycg "back of a man or beast," probably reinforced by Old Norse hryggr "back, ridge," from Proto-Germanic *khrugjaz (source also of Old Frisian hregg, Old Saxon hruggi, Dutch rug, Old High German hrukki, German Rücken "the back"), of uncertain origin. Also in Old English, "the top or crest of anything," especially when long and narrow. The connecting notion is of the "ridge" of the backbone. Spelling with -dg- is from late 15c. Ridge-runner "Southern Appalachian person" first recorded 1917.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 hrycg "back of a man or beast," 可能 reinforced by 古北欧语 hryggr "back, ridge," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *khrugjaz (source also of 古弗里西语 hregg, 古撒克逊语 hruggi, 荷兰语 rug, 古高地德语 hrukki, 德语 Rücken "the back"), 来源存疑. Also in 古英语, "the top or crest of anything," 尤指 when long and narrow. The connecting notion is of the "ridge" of the backbone. Spelling with -dg- 始于 15 世纪晚期 Ridge-runner "Southern Appalachian person" 首见于 1917 年.

example.en: Hikers followed the narrow path along the ridge of the mountain.
example.zh: 徒步者沿着山脊上的狭窄小路行走。

entries.etymology: 1540s, ridyculouse, from Latin ridiculus "laughable, funny, absurd," from ridere "to laugh" (see risible). Shakespeare and other 17c. writers sometimes spelled it rediculous. Slang extensions to "outrageous" (1839); "excellent" (1959, jazz slang). Related: Ridiculously; ridiculousness. In the sense "concerned with jokes," Latin had ridicularius.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, ridyculouse, 源自 拉丁语 ridiculus "laughable, funny, absurd," 源自 ridere "to laugh" （参见 risible). Shakespeare and other 17 世纪 writers 有时 spelled it rediculous. Slang extensions to "outrageous" (1839 年); "excellent" (1959 年, jazz 俚语). 同源词：Ridiculously; ridiculousness. In the sense "concerned with jokes," 拉丁语 had ridicularius.

example.en: It seems ridiculous to spend that much money on a single pair of shoes.
example.zh: 花那么多钱买一双鞋，这似乎荒谬可笑。

entries.etymology: 1775, "portable firearm having a spirally grooved bore," used earlier of the grooves themselves (1751), noun use of rifled (pistol), 1680s, from verb meaning "to cut spiral grooves in" (a gun barrel); see rifle (v.2).
entries.etymologyZh: 1775 年, "portable firearm having a spirally grooved bore," used earlier of the grooves themselves (1751 年), 为 … 的名词用法 rifled (pistol), 1680 年代, 源自 动词 意为 "to cut spiral grooves in" (a gun barrel); 参见 rifle (v.2).

definitionLines: a.正确的；合适的，恰当的；右边 的；直角的
ad.正确地，笔直地；完全，正 好；直接，马上
entries.definition: a.正确的；合适的，恰当的；右边 的；直角的 n. 权利；右面 ad.正确地，笔直地；完全，正 好；直接，马上
entries.etymology: Old English rihtan "to straighten, rule, set up, set right, amend; guide, govern; restore, replace," from riht (adj.); see right (adj.1). Compare Old Norse retta "to straighten," Old Saxon rihtian, Old Frisian riuchta, German richten, Gothic garaihtjan. Related: Righted; righting.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 rihtan "to straighten, rule, set up, set right, amend; guide, govern; restore, replace," 源自 riht （形）; 参见 right (adj.1). 对比 古北欧语 retta "to straighten," 古撒克逊语 rihtian, 古弗里西语 riuchta, 德语 richten, Gothic garaihtjan. 同源词：Righted; righting.

example.en: Every citizen has the right to vote in national elections.
example.zh: 每位公民都有权在全国选举中投票。

definitionLines: a.正当的；合法的；正直的；公 正的
entries.definition: a.正当的；合法的；正直的；公 正的
entries.etymology: Old English rihtful; see right (adj.1) + -ful. Related: Rightfully; rightfulness.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 rihtful; 参见 right (adj.1) + -ful. 同源词：Rightfully; rightfulness.

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Latin rigidus "hard, stiff, rough, severe," from rigere "be stiff," from PIE *reig- "stretch (tight), bind tightly, make fast" (source also of Old Irish riag "torture," Middle High German ric "band, string"). Related: Rigidly.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 拉丁语 rigidus "hard, stiff, rough, severe," 源自 rigere "be stiff," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *reig- "stretch (tight), bind tightly, make fast" (source also of Old 爱尔兰语 riag "torture," Middle High 德语 ric "band, string"). 同源词：Rigidly.

example.en: The company has rigid rules about punctuality that no one dares to break.
example.zh: 公司对守时有严格的规定，没有人敢违反。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French rigorous (13c., Modern French rigoureux), from Medieval Latin rigorosus, from Latin rigor (see rigor). Related: Rigorously.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 rigorous (13 世纪, 现代法语 rigoureux), 源自 中古拉丁语 rigorosus, 源自 拉丁语 rigor （参见 rigor). 同源词：Rigorously.

example.en: The course requires every claim to be checked against evidence and is known for its rigorous approach to research.
example.zh: 这门课要求用证据核对每一项论断，以严谨的研究方法著称。

definitionLines: n. 戒指；圆圈，环；铃声，钟声； 打电话
entries.definition: n. 戒指；圆圈，环；铃声，钟声； 打电话 vt.敲钟，打铃

example.en: The phone started to ring just as she walked out the door.
example.zh: 就在她走出门的时候，电话开始响了。

entries.etymology:
c. 1200, "debauchery, extravagance, wanton living," from Old French riote (12c.) "dispute, quarrel, (tedious) talk, chattering, argument, domestic strife," also a euphemism for "sexual intercourse," of uncertain origin. Compare Medieval Latin riota "quarrel, dispute, uproar, riot." Perhaps from Latin rugire "to roar."  Meaning "public disturbance" is first recorded late 14c. Meaning "something spectacularly successful" first recorded 1909 in theater slang.

Run riot is first recorded 1520s, a metaphoric extension from Middle English meaning in reference to hounds following the wrong scent. The Riot Act, part of which must be read to a mob before active measures can be taken, was passed 1714 (1 Geo. I, st.2, c.5). Riot girl and alternative form riot grrl first recorded 1992.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "debauchery, extravagance, wanton living," 源自 古法语 riote (12 世纪) "dispute, quarrel, (tedious) talk, chattering, argument, domestic strife," also a euphemism for "sexual intercourse," 来源存疑. 对比 中古拉丁语 riota "quarrel, dispute, uproar, riot." Perhaps 源自 拉丁语 rugire "to roar." 义为 "public disturbance" is 首见于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "something spectacularly successful" 首见于 1909 年 in theater 俚语. Run riot is 首见于 1520 年代, a metaphoric extension 源自 中古英语 意为 in reference to hounds following the wrong scent. The Riot Act, part of which must be read to a mob before active measures can be taken, was passed 1714 年 (1 Geo. I, st.2, c.5). Riot girl and alternative form riot grrl 首见于 1992 年.

example.en: The police struggled to control the riot that broke out after the verdict.
example.zh: 警察竭力控制判决后爆发的骚乱。

definitionLines: v. 撕，剥，劈，锯；裂开，撕裂
entries.definition: v. 撕，剥，劈，锯；裂开，撕裂
entries.etymology:
"tear apart," c. 1400, probably of North Sea Germanic origin (compare Flemish rippen "strip off roughly," Frisian rippe "to tear, rip") or else from a Scandinavian source (compare Swedish reppa, Danish rippe "to tear, rip"). In either case, from Proto-Germanic *rupjan-, from PIE root *reup-, *reub- "to snatch." Meaning "to slash open" is from 1570s. Related: Ripped; ripping.

Meaning "to move with slashing force" (1798) is the sense in let her rip, American English colloquial phrase attested from 1853. The noun is attested from 1711. The parachutist's rip cord (1911) originally was a device in ballooning to open a panel and release air.
entries.etymologyZh: "tear apart," 约 1400 年, 可能 of North Sea 日耳曼语 origin (对比 Flemish rippen "strip off roughly," Frisian rippe "to tear, rip") or else 源自 a Scandinavian source (对比 Swedish reppa, Danish rippe "to tear, rip"). In either case, 源自 原始日耳曼语 *rupjan-, 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *reup-, *reub- "to snatch." 义为 "to slash open" 始于 1570 年代. 同源词：Ripped; ripping. 义为 "to move with slashing force" (1798 年) is the sense in let her rip, American English 口语 phrase attested 自 1853 年起. The 名词 见于 1711 年. The parachutist's rip cord (1911 年) 原义为 was a device in ballooning to open a panel and release air.

example.en: He accidentally rip his jacket sleeve on a rusty nail sticking out from the fence.
example.zh: 他不小心把夹克袖子挂在围栏上伸出的锈钉上扯破了。

entries.etymology: Old English ripe "ready for reaping, fit for eating, mature," from West Germanic *ripijaz (source also of Old Saxon ripi, Middle Dutch ripe, Dutch rijp, Old High German rifi, German reif); related to Old English repan "to reap" (see reap). Meaning "ready for some action or effect" is from 1590s. Related: Ripely; ripeness.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 ripe "ready for reaping, fit for eating, mature," 源自 West 日耳曼语 *ripijaz (source also of 古撒克逊语 ripi, Middle 荷兰语 ripe, 荷兰语 rijp, 古高地德语 rifi, 德语 reif); related to 古英语 repan "to reap" （参见 reap). 义为 "ready for some action or effect" 始于 1590 年代. 同源词：Ripely; ripeness.

example.en: The fruit must be ripe before it can be picked and sold at the market.
example.zh: 水果必须成熟后才能被采摘并在市场上出售。

definitionLines: 一 vi. 上升，上涨；升起；起床，起立；
n. 增加，升高；起源，发生；高地
entries.definition: 一 vi. 上升，上涨；升起；起床，起立； n. 增加，升高；起源，发生；高地
entries.etymology:
Old English risan "to rise, rise from sleep, get out of bed; stand up, rise to one's feet; get up from table; rise together; be fit, be proper" (usually arisan; class I strong verb; past tense ras, past participle risen), from Proto-Germanic *us-risanan "to go up" (source also of Old Norse risa, Old Saxon risan, Gothic urreisan "to rise," Old High German risan "to rise, flow," German reisen "to travel," originally "to rise for a journey").

From c. 1200 as "move from a lower to a higher position, move upward; increase in number or amount; rise in fortune, prosper; become prominent;" also "rise from the dead." Meaning "come into existence, originate; result (from)" is mid-13c. From early 14c. as "rebel, revolt;" also "occur, happen, come to pass; take place." Related to raise (v.). Related: Rose; risen.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 risan "to rise, rise from sleep, get out of bed; stand up, rise to one's feet; get up from table; rise together; be fit, be proper" (通常 arisan; class I strong 动词; past tense ras, past participle risen), 源自 原始日耳曼语 *us-risanan "to go up" (source also of 古北欧语 risa, 古撒克逊语 risan, Gothic urreisan "to rise," 古高地德语 risan "to rise, flow," 德语 reisen "to travel," 原义为 "to rise for a journey"). From 约 1200 年 as "move from a lower to a higher position, move upward; increase in number or amount; rise in fortune, prosper; become prominent;" also "rise from the dead." 义为 "come into existence, originate; result (from)" is 13 世纪中期 From 14 世纪初 as "rebel, revolt;" also "occur, happen, come to pass; take place." Related to raise （动）. 同源词：Rose; risen.

example.en: Food prices continue to rise sharply during the winter months.
example.zh: 食品价格在冬季持续急剧上涨。

entries.definition: n. 风险 vt. 冒风险
entries.etymology: 1660s, risque, from French risque (16c.), from Italian risco, riscio (modern rischio), from riscare "run into danger," of uncertain origin. The Englished spelling first recorded 1728. Spanish riesgo and German Risiko are Italian loan-words. With run (v.) from 1660s. Risk aversion is recorded from 1942; risk factor from 1906; risk management from 1963; risk taker from 1892.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, risque, 源自 法语 risque (16 世纪), 源自 意大利语 risco, riscio (modern rischio), 源自 riscare "run into danger," 来源存疑. The Englished spelling 首见于 1728 年. 西班牙语 riesgo and 德语 Risiko are 意大利语 loan-words. With run （动） 源自 1660 年代. Risk aversion 见于 1942 年; risk factor 自 1906 年起; risk management 自 1963 年起; risk taker 自 1892 年起.

example.en: Driving without a seatbelt is a serious risk you should never take.
example.zh: 不系安全带开车是你永远不应该冒的严重风险。

entries.etymology: 1825, from risk (n.) + -y (2). Riskful in same sense is from 1793. Related: Riskiness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1825 年, 源自 risk （名） + -y (2). Riskful in same sense 始于 1793 年. 同源词：Riskiness.

example.en: Investing all your savings in one stock is an extremely risky move.
example.zh: 把所有积蓄都投入一只股票是极其冒险的举动。

definitionLines: n. 典礼，（宗教）仪式，礼节
a. 典礼的，（宗教）仪式的
entries.definition: n. 典礼，（宗教）仪式，礼节 a. 典礼的，（宗教）仪式的
entries.etymology: 1560s, from Middle French ritual or directly from Latin ritualis "relating to (religious) rites," from ritus "rite" (see rite). Related: Ritually.
entries.etymologyZh: 1560 年代, 源自 中古法语 ritual or 直接源自 拉丁语 ritualis "relating to (religious) rites," 源自 ritus "rite" （参见 rite). 同源词：Ritually.

example.en: The tribe performed an ancient ritual to mark the beginning of the harvest season.
example.zh: 部落举行了一场古老的仪式，以标志收获季节的开始。

entries.definition: vt. 竞争，与……抗衡 a.竞争的 n. 竞争对手
entries.etymology: 1570s, from Latin rivalis "a rival, adversary in love; neighbor," originally, "of the same brook," from rivus "brook" (see rivulet). "One who is in pursuit of the same object as another." The sense evolution seems to be based on the competitiveness of neighbors: "one who uses the same stream," or "one on the opposite side of the stream" A secondary sense in Latin and sometimes in English was "associate, companion in duty," from the notion of "one having a common right or privilege with another." As an adjective 1580s from the noun.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, 源自 拉丁语 rivalis "a rival, adversary in love; neighbor," 原义为, "of the same brook," 源自 rivus "brook" （参见 rivulet). "One who is in pursuit of the same object as another." The sense evolution seems to be based on the competitiveness of neighbors: "one who uses the same stream," or "one on the opposite side of the stream" A secondary sense in 拉丁语 and 有时 in English was "associate, companion in duty," 源自 概念 "one having a common right or privilege with another." 作形容词时 1580 年代 源自 名词.

example.en: The two companies have been fierce rivals in the smartphone market for years.
example.zh: 这两家公司多年来一直是智能手机市场上的强劲竞争对手。

entries.etymology: 1590s; from rival + -ry. Shakespeare has rivality ("Antony and Cleopatra"), but from the secondary sense of the root word and meaning "partnership, equality in rank."
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代; 源自 rival + -ry. Shakespeare has rivality ("Antony and Cleopatra"), but 源自 secondary 语义 the root word and 意为 "partnership, equality in rank."

example.en: The long-standing rivalry between the two companies meant that each tried to win customers away from the other.
example.zh: 这两家公司长期存在竞争关系，每家都试图从对方那里争取客户。

entries.etymology:
early 13c., from Anglo-French rivere, Old French riviere "river, riverside, river bank" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *riparia "riverbank, seashore, river" (source also of Spanish ribera, Italian riviera), noun use of fem. of Latin riparius "of a riverbank" (see riparian). Generalized sense of "a copious flow" of anything is from late 14c. The Old English word was ea "river," cognate with Gothic ahwa, Latin aqua (see aqua-). Romanic cognate words tend to retain the sense "river bank" as the main one, or else the secondary Latin sense "coast of the sea" (compare Riviera).
