Sense of "solidly built, strong and hardy" first recorded late 14c. Related: Sturdily; sturdiness. Sturdy-boots "obstinate person" is from 1762; a sturdy beggar in old language was one capable of work (c. 1400).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "hard to manage, reckless, violent," 源自 古法语 estordi (11 世纪, 现代法语 étourdi) "violent," 原义为 "dazed," 为 … 的过去分词 estordiir "to daze, stun, stupefy," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *exturdire, which some presume to be 源自 拉丁语 intensive prefix ex- + turdus "thrush." Barnhart suggests the notion is of thrushes eating grape remnants at wineries and behaving as if drunk (意大利语 tordo "thrush" also means "simpleton," and 法语 has the expression soûl comme une grive "drunk as a thrush"). OED, however, regards all this as "open to grave objection." Century Dictionary compares 拉丁语 torpidus "dull." 义为 "solidly built, strong and hardy" 首见于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Sturdily; sturdiness. Sturdy-boots "obstinate person" 始于 1762 年; a sturdy beggar in old language was one capable of work (约 1400 年).

definitionLines: 风格，文体；时尚，时髦； 种类，类型
entries.definition: 风格，文体；时尚，时髦； 种类，类型
entries.etymology: c. 1500, "address with a title;" 1560s, "to give a name to," from style (n.). Meaning "to arrange in (fashionable) style" (especially of hair) is attested from 1934. Slang sense of "act or play in a showy way" is by 1974, African-American vernacular. Related: Styled; styling.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "address with a title;" 1560 年代, "to give a name to," 源自 style （名）. 义为 "to arrange in (fashionable) style" (尤指 of hair) 见于 1934 年. Slang 语义 "act or play in a showy way" is 截至 1974 年, African-American vernacular. 同源词：Styled; styling.

example.en: Her writing style blends formal grammar with vivid storytelling.
example.zh: 她的写作风格将规范语法与生动叙事融为一体。

entries.definition: vi. 细分，再分 vt. 把……再分，把……细分
entries.etymology: early 15c. (transitive), from Late Latin subdividere from sub in the sense of "resulting from further division" (see sub-) + Latin dividere (see division). Intransitive sense is from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (transitive), 源自 晚期拉丁语 subdividere 源自 sub in the 语义 "resulting from further division" （参见 sub-) + 拉丁语 dividere （参见 division). Intransitive sense 始于 1590 年代.

definitionLines: n. 主题，题目；学科，科目；实验 对象
entries.definition: n. 主题，题目；学科，科目；实验 对象 a.（to）易遭……的，受……支 配的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to make (a person or nation) subject to another by force," also "to render submissive or dependent," from Medieval Latin subiectare "place beneath," frequentative of Latin subicere "to make subject, subordinate" (see subject (n.)). Meaning "to lay open or expose to (some force or occurrence)" is recorded from early 15c. (implied in subjected). Related: Subjecting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to make (a person or nation) subject to another by force," also "to render submissive or dependent," 源自 中古拉丁语 subiectare "place beneath," 为 … 的反复体 拉丁语 subicere "to make subject, subordinate" （参见 subject （名）). 义为 "to lay open or expose to (some force or occurrence)" 见于 15 世纪初 (implied in subjected). 同源词：Subjecting.

example.en: Her favorite subject at school is history, not PE.
example.zh: 她在学校最喜欢的科目是历史，不是体育。

entries.etymology: c. 1500, "characteristic of one who is submissive or obedient," from Late Latin subiectivus "of the subject, subjective," from subiectus "lying under, below, near bordering on," figuratively "subjected, subdued"(see subject (n.)). In early Modern English as "existing, real;" more restricted meaning "existing in the mind" (the mind as "the thinking subject") is from 1707, popularized by Kant and his contemporaries; thus, in art and literature, "personal, idiosyncratic" (1767). Related: Subjectively; subjectiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "characteristic of one who is submissive or obedient," 源自 晚期拉丁语 subiectivus "of the subject, subjective," 源自 subiectus "lying under, below, near bordering on," figuratively "subjected, subdued"（参见 subject （名）). In early 现代英语 as "existing, real;" more restricted 意为 "existing in the mind" (the mind as "the thinking subject") 始于 1707 年, popularized by Kant and his contemporaries; thus, in art and literature, "personal, idiosyncratic" (1767 年). 同源词：Subjectively; subjectiveness.

example.en: Beauty is largely subjective and varies from person to person.
example.zh: 美很大程度上是主观的，因人而异。

entries.definition: n. 潜水艇；海底生物 a. 水下的；海底的
entries.etymology: 1640s, from sub- + marine (adj.).
entries.etymologyZh: 1640 年代, 源自 sub- + marine （形）.

entries.etymology: c. 1600 (transitive), from French submerger (14c.) or directly from Latin submergere "to plunge under, sink, overwhelm," from sub "under" (see sub-) + mergere "to plunge, immerse" (see merge). Intransitive meaning "sink under water, sink out of sight" is from 1650s, made common 20c. in connection with submarines. Related: Submerged; submerging.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年 (transitive), 源自 法语 submerger (14 世纪) or 直接源自 拉丁语 submergere "to plunge under, sink, overwhelm," 源自 sub "under" （参见 sub-) + mergere "to plunge, immerse" （参见 merge). Intransitive 意为 "sink under water, sink out of sight" 始于 1650 年代, made common 20 世纪 in connection with submarines. 同源词：Submerged; submerging.

definitionLines: n. 服从；提交（物）；投降；谦恭
entries.definition: n. 服从；提交（物）；投降；谦恭
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "act of referring to a third party for judgment or decision," from Old French submission or directly from Latin submissionem (nominative submissio) "a lowering, letting down; sinking," noun of action from past participle stem of submittere "to let down, put down, lower, reduce, yield" (see submit).

Sense of "humble obedience" is first recorded mid-15c. Modern French submission has been replaced by doublet soumission. English in 16c.-17c. also had an adjective submiss "humble, submissive."  Submissionist in various political historical contexts is from 1828.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "act of referring to a third party for judgment or decision," 源自 古法语 submission or 直接源自 拉丁语 submissionem (主格 submissio) "a lowering, letting down; sinking," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of submittere "to let down, put down, lower, reduce, yield" （参见 submit). 义为 "humble obedience" is 首见于 15 世纪中期 现代法语 submission has been replaced by doublet soumission. English in 16 世纪-17 世纪 also had an 形容词 submiss "humble, submissive." Submissionist in various political historical contexts 始于 1828 年.

definitionLines: n. 下属，下级；部属，属下
entries.definition: a. 次要的；从属的 vt. 使…••居下位；使……服从 n. 下属，下级；部属，属下
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "having an inferior rank," from Medieval Latin subordinatus "placed in a lower order, made subject," past participle of subordinare "place in a lower order," from Latin sub "under" (see sub-) + ordinare "arrange, set in order" (see ordain). Related: Subordinance; subordinant; subordinately. For "of or pertaining to the classificatory rank of a suborder," subordinal (1842) is used.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "having an inferior rank," 源自 中古拉丁语 subordinatus "placed in a lower order, made subject," 为 … 的过去分词 subordinare "place in a lower order," 源自 拉丁语 sub "under" （参见 sub-) + ordinare "arrange, set in order" （参见 ordain). 同源词：Subordinance; subordinant; subordinately. For "of or pertaining to the classificatory rank of a suborder," subordinal (1842 年) is used.

entries.etymology: c. 1400, "piece of writing at the end of a document," from Middle French subscription (Modern French souscription) and directly from Latin subscriptionem (nominative subscriptio) "anything written underneath, a signature," noun of action from past participle stem of subscribere (see subscribe). Meaning "act of subscribing money" is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "piece of writing at the end of a document," 源自 中古法语 subscription (现代法语 souscription) and 直接源自 拉丁语 subscriptionem (主格 subscriptio) "anything written underneath, a signature," 名词 of action 源自 past participle stem of subscribere （参见 subscribe). 义为 "act of subscribing money" 始于 1640 年代.

entries.etymology: "following in time, later," mid-15c., from Middle French subsequent (14c.) and directly from Latin subsequentem (nominative subsequens), present participle of subsequi "come after in time, follow closely," figuratively "imitate, conform to," from sub "closely, up to" (see sub-) + sequi "follow" (see suit (n.)). Related: Subsequently; subsequential.
entries.etymologyZh: "following in time, later," 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 subsequent (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 subsequentem (主格 subsequens), 为 … 的现在分词 subsequi "come after in time, follow closely," figuratively "imitate, conform to," 源自 sub "closely, up to" （参见 sub-) + sequi "follow" （参见 suit （名）). 同源词：Subsequently; subsequential.

example.en: The subsequent investigation revealed more evidence of fraud.
example.zh: 随后的调查揭示了更多欺诈证据。

entries.etymology: 1540s, from Latin subsidiarius "belonging to a reserve, of a reserve, reserved; serving to assist or supplement," from subsidium "a help, aid, relief, troops in reserve" (see subsidy). As a noun, c. 1600, "subsidiary thing." In Latin the word was used as a noun meaning "the reserve."
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 源自 拉丁语 subsidiarius "belonging to a reserve, of a reserve, reserved; serving to assist or supplement," 源自 subsidium "a help, aid, relief, troops in reserve" （参见 subsidy). 作名词时, 约 1600 年, "subsidiary thing." In 拉丁语 the word was used 作名词时 意为 "the reserve."

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Anglo-French subsidie, Old French subside "help, aid, assistance, contribution," from Latin subsidium "a help, aid, assistance, (military) reinforcements, troops in reserve," from subsidere "to settle down, stay, remain" (see subside).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 subsidie, 古法语 subside "help, aid, assistance, contribution," 源自 拉丁语 subsidium "a help, aid, assistance, (military) reinforcements, troops in reserve," 源自 subsidere "to settle down, stay, remain" （参见 subside).

example.en: The government provides a monthly subsidy to support small family farms.
example.zh: 政府每月提供补贴以支持小型家庭农场。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "existence, independence," from Late Latin subsistentia "substance, reality," in Medieval Latin also "stability," from Latin subsistens, present participle of subsistere "stand still or firm" (see subsist). Latin subsistentia is a loan-translation of Greek hypostasis "foundation, substance, real nature, subject matter; that which settles at the bottom, sediment," literally "anything set under." In the English word, meaning "act or process of support for physical life" is from 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "existence, independence," 源自 晚期拉丁语 subsistentia "substance, reality," in 中古拉丁语 also "stability," 源自 拉丁语 subsistens, 为 … 的现在分词 subsistere "stand still or firm" （参见 subsist). 拉丁语 subsistentia is a loan-translation of 希腊语 hypostasis "foundation, substance, real nature, subject matter; that which settles at the bottom, sediment," 字面义为 "anything set under." In the English word, 意为 "act or process of support for physical life" 始于 1640 年代.

definitionLines: n. 物质；实质，本质；要旨，大意
entries.definition: n. 物质；实质，本质；要旨，大意
entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "essential nature, real or essential part," from Old French sustance, substance "goods, possessions; nature, composition" (12c.), from Latin substantia "being, essence, material," from substans, present participle of substare "stand firm, stand or be under, be present," from sub "up to, under" (see sub-) + stare "to stand," from PIE root *stā- "to stand" (see stet).

Latin substantia translates Greek ousia "that which is one's own, one's substance or property; the being, essence, or nature of anything." Meaning "any kind of corporeal matter" is first attested mid-14c. Sense of "the matter of a study, discourse, etc." first recorded late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "essential nature, real or essential part," 源自 古法语 sustance, substance "goods, possessions; nature, composition" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 substantia "being, essence, material," 源自 substans, 为 … 的现在分词 substare "stand firm, stand or be under, be present," 源自 sub "up to, under" （参见 sub-) + stare "to stand," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *stā- "to stand" （参见 stet). 拉丁语 substantia translates 希腊语 ousia "that which is one's own, one's substance or property; the being, essence, or nature of anything." 义为 "any kind of corporeal matter" is 最早见于 14 世纪中期 义为 "the matter of a study, discourse, etc." 首见于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The lab tested the water sample for any harmful chemical substance.
example.zh: 实验室检测了水样中是否含有任何有害化学物质。

definitionLines: a.大量的；实质的；牢固的， 坚实的；内容充实的
entries.definition: a.大量的；实质的；牢固的， 坚实的；内容充实的
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "ample, sizeable," from Old French substantiel (13c.) and directly from Latin substantialis "having substance or reality, material," in Late Latin "pertaining to the substance or essence," from substantia "being, essence, material" (see substance). Meaning "existing, having real existence" is from late 14c. Meaning "involving an essential part or point" is early 15c. Related: Substantially.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "ample, sizeable," 源自 古法语 substantiel (13 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 substantialis "having substance or reality, material," in 晚期拉丁语 "pertaining to the substance or essence," 源自 substantia "being, essence, material" （参见 substance). 义为 "existing, having real existence" 始于 14 世纪晚期 义为 "involving an essential part or point" is 15 世纪初 同源词：Substantially.

example.en: The new policy led to a substantial improvement in public health outcomes.
example.zh: 新政策使公众健康状况得到了大幅改善。

entries.definition: n. （for）代用品，代替者 vt.（for）代，代替
entries.etymology: early 15c. (transitive), from Latin substitutus, past participle of substituere "put in place of another" (see substitution). Transitive use is from 1888. Related: Substituted; substituting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (transitive), 源自 拉丁语 substitutus, 为 … 的过去分词 substituere "put in place of another" （参见 substitution). Transitive use 始于 1888 年. 同源词：Substituted; substituting.

example.en: You can use honey as a substitute for sugar in most baking recipes.
example.zh: 在大多数烘焙食谱中，你可以用蜂蜜代替糖。

definitionLines: a.微妙的，细微的；敏感的； 精细的；精巧的
entries.definition: a.微妙的，细微的；敏感的； 精细的；精巧的
entries.etymology:
c. 1300 (mid-13c. as a surname), sotil, "penetrating; ingenious; refined" (of the mind); "sophisticated, intricate, abstruse" (of arguments), from Old French sotil, soutil, subtil "adept, adroit; cunning, wise; detailed; well-crafted" (12c., Modern French subtil), from Latin subtilis "fine, thin, delicate, finely woven;" figuratively "precise, exact, accurate," in taste or judgment, "fine, keen," of style, "plain, simple, direct," from sub "under" (see sub-) + -tilis, from tela "web, net, warp of a fabric" (see texture (n.)). 

From early 14c. in reference to things, "of thin consistency;" in reference to craftsmen, "cunning, skilled, clever;" Depreciative sense "insidious, treacherously cunning; deceitful" is from mid-14c. Material senses of "not dense or viscous, light; pure; delicate, thin, slender; fine, consisting of small particles" are from late 14c. sotil wares were goods sold in powdered form or finely ground. Partially re-Latinized in spelling, and also by confusion with subtile.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年 (13 世纪中期 作为 surname), sotil, "penetrating; ingenious; refined" (of the mind); "sophisticated, intricate, abstruse" (of arguments), 源自 古法语 sotil, soutil, subtil "adept, adroit; cunning, wise; detailed; well-crafted" (12 世纪, 现代法语 subtil), 源自 拉丁语 subtilis "fine, thin, delicate, finely woven;" figuratively "precise, exact, accurate," in taste or judgment, "fine, keen," of style, "plain, simple, direct," 源自 sub "under" （参见 sub-) + -tilis, 源自 tela "web, net, warp of a fabric" （参见 texture （名）). From 14 世纪初 in reference to things, "of thin consistency;" in reference to craftsmen, "cunning, skilled, clever;" Depreciative sense "insidious, treacherously cunning; deceitful" 始于 14 世纪中期 Material senses of "not dense or viscous, light; pure; delicate, thin, slender; fine, consisting of small particles" 始于 14 世纪晚期 sotil wares were goods sold in powdered form or finely ground. Partially re-Latinized in spelling, and also by confusion with subtile.

example.en: There is a subtle difference between the two shades of blue in the design.
example.zh: 设计中两种蓝色色调之间存在一种微妙的差异。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "withdraw, withhold, take away, deduct," a back-formation from subtraction (q.v.), or else from Latin subtractus, past participle of subtrahere "take away, draw off." Related: Subtracted; subtracting. Mathematical calculation sense is from 1550s. Earlier verb form was subtraien (early 15c. in the mathematical sense), which is directly from the Latin verb.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "withdraw, withhold, take away, deduct," a back-formation 源自 subtraction (q.v.)，或else 源自 拉丁语 subtractus, 为 … 的过去分词 subtrahere "take away, draw off." 同源词：Subtracted; subtracting. Mathematical calculation sense 始于 1550 年代. Earlier 动词 form was subtraien (15 世纪初 in the mathematical sense), which is 直接源自 the 拉丁语 动词.

entries.etymology: early 14c., "area outside a town or city," whether agricultural or residential but most frequently residential, from Old French suburbe "suburb of a town," from Latin suburbium "an outlying part of a city" (especially Rome), from sub "below, near" (see sub-) + urbs (genitive urbis) "city" (see urban). Glossed in Old English as underburg. Just beyond the reach of municipal jurisdiction, suburbs had a bad reputation in 17c. England, especially those of London, and suburban had a sense of "inferior, debased, licentious" (as in suburban sinner, slang for "loose woman, prostitute"). By 1817, the tinge had shifted to "of inferior manners and narrow views." Compare also French equivalent faubourg.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "area outside a town or city," whether agricultural or residential but most frequently residential, 源自 古法语 suburbe "suburb of a town," 源自 拉丁语 suburbium "an outlying part of a city" (尤指 Rome), 源自 sub "below, near" （参见 sub-) + urbs (属格 urbis) "city" （参见 urban). Glossed in 古英语 as underburg. Just beyond the reach of municipal jurisdiction, suburbs had a bad reputation in 17 世纪 England, 尤指 those of London, and suburban had a 语义 "inferior, debased, licentious" (as in suburban sinner, 俚语 for "loose woman, prostitute"). By 1817 年, the tinge had shifted to "of inferior manners and narrow views." 对比 also 法语 equivalent faubourg.

example.en: The new train line made it easier for families to commute from the suburb into downtown.
example.zh: 新的轨道交通线路让家庭从郊区通勤到市中心更加便利。

entries.etymology: 1825, "underground passage" (for water pipes or pedestrians, later for electrical wires), from sub- + way (n.). The sense of "underground railway in a city" is first recorded 1892, in reference to London.
entries.etymologyZh: 1825 年, "underground passage" (for water pipes or pedestrians, later for electrical wires), 源自 sub- + way （名）. The 语义 "underground railway in a city" is 首见于 1892 年, in reference to London.

example.en: Taking the subway is faster than driving during rush hour in the city.
example.zh: 在城市高峰时段，乘坐地铁比开车更快。

entries.definition: vi. 成功；继承，接替 vt. 接替，接……之后
entries.etymology:
late 14c., intransitive and transitive, "come next after, follow after another; take the place of another, be elected or chosen for" a position, from Old French succeder "to follow on" (14c.) and directly from Latin succedere "come after, follow after; go near to; come under; take the place of," also "go from under, mount up, ascend," hence "get on well, prosper, be victorious," from sub "next to, after" (see sub-) + cedere "go, move" (see cede).

Meaning "to continue, endure" is from early 15c. The sense of "turn out well, have a favorable result" in English is first recorded late 15c., with ellipsis of adverb (succeed well). Of persons, "to be successful," from c. 1500. Related: Succeeded; succeeding.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, intransitive and transitive, "come next after, follow after another; take the place of another, be elected or chosen for" a position, 源自 古法语 succeder "to follow on" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 succedere "come after, follow after; go near to; come under; take the place of," also "go from under, mount up, ascend," hence "get on well, prosper, be victorious," 源自 sub "next to, after" （参见 sub-) + cedere "go, move" （参见 cede). 义为 "to continue, endure" 始于 15 世纪初 The 语义 "turn out well, have a favorable result" in English is 首见于 15 世纪晚期, with ellipsis of 副词 (succeed well). Of persons, "to be successful," 源自 约 1500 年. 同源词：Succeeded; succeeding.

example.en: She worked hard and finally managed to succeed in her career.
example.zh: 她努力工作，最终在事业上取得了成功。

entries.etymology:
1530s, "result, outcome," from Latin successus "an advance, a coming up; a good result, happy outcome," noun use of past participle of succedere "come after" (see succeed). Meaning "accomplishment of desired end" (good success) first recorded 1580s. Meaning "a thing or person which succeeds," especially in public, is from 1882.

Success story is attested from 1902. Among the French phrases reported by OED as in use in English late 19c. were succès d'estime "cordial reception given to a literary work out of respect rather than admiration" and succès de scandale "success (especially of a work of art) dependent upon its scandalous character."
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "result, outcome," 源自 拉丁语 successus "an advance, a coming up; a good result, happy outcome," 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 succedere "come after" （参见 succeed). 义为 "accomplishment of desired end" (good success) 首见于 1580 年代. 义为 "a thing or person which succeeds," 尤指 in public, 始于 1882 年. Success story 见于 1902 年. Among the 法语 phrases reported by OED as in use in English 19 世纪晚期 were succès d'estime "cordial reception given to a literary work out of respect rather than admiration" and succès de scandale "success (especially of a work of art) dependent upon its scandalous character."

example.en: Hard work and persistence are the keys to success in any career.
example.zh: 努力和坚持是任何职业成功的关键。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from success + -ful. Originally "having or resulting in any kind of success;" since late 19c. it has tended to mean "wealthy, resulting in financial prosperity" unless otherwise indicated. Related: Successfully.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 success + -ful. Originally "having or resulting in any kind of success;" 自 19 世纪晚期 it has tended to mean "wealthy, resulting in financial prosperity" unless otherwise indicated. 同源词：Successfully.

example.en: The startup became extremely successful after launching its innovative product last year.
example.zh: 这家初创公司去年推出创新产品后变得非常成功。

definitionLines: n. 连续，系列；继任，继承
entries.definition: n. 连续，系列；继任，继承
entries.etymology: early 14c., "fact or right of succeeding someone by inheritance," from Old French succession "inheritance; a following on" (13c.), from Latin successionem (nominative successio) "a following after, a coming into another's place, result," noun of action from successus, past participle of succedere (see succeed). Meaning "fact of being later in time" is late 14c. Meaning "a regular sequence" is from mid-15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "fact or right of succeeding someone by inheritance," 源自 古法语 succession "inheritance; a following on" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 successionem (主格 successio) "a following after, a coming into another's place, result," 名词 of action 源自 successus, 为 … 的过去分词 succedere （参见 succeed). 义为 "fact of being later in time" is 14 世纪晚期 义为 "a regular sequence" 始于 15 世纪中期

example.en: The team suffered a succession of defeats before finally winning.
example.zh: 这支队伍在最终获胜之前经历了一连串的失败。

entries.etymology: early 15c., from Medieval Latin successivus "successive," from success-, stem of Latin succedere "to come after" (see succeed). Related: Successively.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, 源自 中古拉丁语 successivus "successive," 源自 success-, stem of 拉丁语 succedere "to come after" （参见 succeed). 同源词：Successively.

definitionLines: n. 继承者；后续的事物
entries.definition: n. 继承者；后续的事物
entries.etymology: "one who comes after," late 13c., from Anglo-French successor and Old French successour "successor, heir" (12c., Modern French successeur), from Latin successor "follower, successor," agent noun from past participle stem of succedere "to come after" (see succeed).
entries.etymologyZh: "one who comes after," 13 世纪晚期, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 successor and 古法语 successour "successor, heir" (12 世纪, 现代法语 successeur), 源自 拉丁语 successor "follower, successor," agent 名词 源自 past participle stem of succedere "to come after" （参见 succeed).

example.en: The board appointed her as the CEO's successor after his sudden resignation.
example.zh: 董事会在首席执行官突然辞职后任命她为继任者。

entries.definition: a. 如此的；这种的 pron. 这样的人/事物
entries.etymology: c. 1200, Old English swylc, swilc "just as, as, in like manner; as if, as though; such a one, he" (pronoun and adjective), from a Proto-Germanic compound *swalikaz "so formed" (source also of Old Saxon sulik, Old Norse slikr, Old Frisian selik, Middle Dutch selc, Dutch zulk, Old High German sulih, German solch, Gothic swaleiks), from swa "so" (see so) + *likan "form," source of Old English gelic "similar" (see like (adj.)). Colloquial suchlike (early 15c.) is pleonastic.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 古英语 swylc, swilc "just as, as, in like manner; as if, as though; such a one, he" (pronoun and 形容词), 源自 a 原始日耳曼语 复合词 *swalikaz "so formed" (source also of 古撒克逊语 sulik, 古北欧语 slikr, 古弗里西语 selik, Middle 荷兰语 selc, 荷兰语 zulk, 古高地德语 sulih, 德语 solch, Gothic swaleiks), 源自 swa "so" （参见 so) + *likan "form," source of 古英语 gelic "similar" （参见 like （形）). Colloquial suchlike (15 世纪初) is pleonastic.

entries.etymology:
Old English sucan "to suck," from a Proto-Germanic word of imitative origin (cognates: Old Saxon, Old High German sugan, Old Norse suga, Danish suge, Swedish suga, Middle Dutch sughen, Dutch zuigen, German saugen "to suck"), possibly from the same source as Latin sugere "to suck," succus "juice, sap;" Old Irish sugim, Welsh sugno "to suck;" see sup (v.2). As a noun from c. 1300.

Meaning "do fellatio" is first recorded 1928. Slang sense of "be contemptible" first attested 1971 (the underlying notion is of fellatio). Related: Sucked; sucking. Suck eggs is from 1906. Suck hind tit "be inferior" is American English slang first recorded 1940.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 sucan "to suck," 源自 a 原始日耳曼语 word of imitative origin (cognates: 古撒克逊语, 古高地德语 sugan, 古北欧语 suga, Danish suge, Swedish suga, Middle 荷兰语 sughen, 荷兰语 zuigen, 德语 saugen "to suck"), possibly 源自 same source as 拉丁语 sugere "to suck," succus "juice, sap;" Old 爱尔兰语 sugim, Welsh sugno "to suck;" 参见 sup (v.2). 作名词时 源自 约 1300 年. 义为 "do fellatio" is 首见于 1928 年. Slang 语义 "be contemptible" 最早见于 1971 年 (the underlying notion is of fellatio). 同源词：Sucked; sucking. Suck eggs 始于 1906 年. Suck hind tit "be inferior" is American English 俚语 首见于 1940 年.

entries.etymology:
early 14c., sodaine, from Anglo-French sodein or directly from Old French sodain, subdain "immediate, sudden" (Modern French soudain), from Vulgar Latin *subitanus, variant of Latin subitaneus "sudden," from subitus past participle of subire "go under; occur secretly, come or go up stealthily," from sub "up to" (see sub-) + ire "come, go" (see ion). "The present spelling was not finally established till after 1700" [OED].

Noun meaning "that which is sudden, a sudden need or emergency" is from 1550s, obsolete except in phrase all of a sudden first attested 1680s, also of a sudayn (1590s), upon the soden (1550s). Sudden death, tie-breakers in sports, first recorded 1927; earlier in reference to coin tosses (1834). Related: Suddenness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, sodaine, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 sodein or 直接源自 古法语 sodain, subdain "immediate, sudden" (现代法语 soudain), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *subitanus, 为 … 的变体 拉丁语 subitaneus "sudden," 源自 subitus 为 … 的过去分词 subire "go under; occur secretly, come or go up stealthily," 源自 sub "up to" （参见 sub-) + ire "come, go" （参见 ion). "The present spelling was not finally established till after 1700" [OED]. Noun 意为 "that which is sudden, a sudden need or emergency" 始于 1550 年代, 已废 except in phrase all of a sudden 最早见于 1680 年代, also of a sudayn (1590 年代), upon the soden (1550 年代). Sudden death, tie-breakers in sports, 首见于 1927 年; earlier in reference to coin tosses (1834 年). 同源词：Suddenness.

example.en: The car came to a sudden stop at the red light.
example.zh: 汽车在红灯前突然停了下来。

entries.etymology: late 13c., sodeinli; see sudden + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, sodeinli; 参见 sudden + -ly (2).

example.en: The connection dropped suddenly, cutting off our video call at a crucial moment.
example.zh: 连接突然断开，在关键时刻切断了我们的视频通话。

entries.etymology: fem. proper name, a shortened or familiar form of Susan.
entries.etymologyZh: fem. proper name, a shortened or familiar form of Susan.

example.en: The customer decided to sue the company for selling a defective product.
example.zh: 该顾客决定就销售有缺陷产品一事起诉这家公司。

entries.definition: vt.受苦，受难，受罪 vi. （from）忍受痛苦；受损失
entries.etymology:
mid-13c., "allow to occur or continue, permit, tolerate, fail to prevent or suppress," also "to be made to undergo, endure, be subjected to" (pain, death, punishment, judgment, grief), from Anglo-French suffrir, Old French sofrir "bear, endure, resist; permit, tolerate, allow" (Modern French souffrir), from Vulgar Latin *sufferire, variant of Latin sufferre "to bear, undergo, endure, carry or put under," from sub "up, under" (see sub-) + ferre "to carry" (see infer).

Replaced Old English þolian, þrowian. Meaning "submit meekly to" is from early 14c. Meaning "undergo, be subject to, be affected by, experience; be acted on by an agent" is from late 14c. Related: Suffered; sufferer; suffering. Suffering ______! as an exclamation is attested from 1859.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, "allow to occur or continue, permit, tolerate, fail to prevent or suppress," also "to be made to undergo, endure, be subjected to" (pain, death, punishment, judgment, grief), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 suffrir, 古法语 sofrir "bear, endure, resist; permit, tolerate, allow" (现代法语 souffrir), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *sufferire, 为 … 的变体 拉丁语 sufferre "to bear, undergo, endure, carry or put under," 源自 sub "up, under" （参见 sub-) + ferre "to carry" （参见 infer). Replaced 古英语 þolian, þrowian. 义为 "submit meekly to" 始于 14 世纪初 义为 "undergo, be subject to, be affected by, experience; be acted on by an agent" 始于 14 世纪晚期 同源词：Suffered; sufferer; suffering. Suffering ______! 作为 exclamation 见于 1859 年.

example.en: Many residents suffered from severe flooding after the heavy rains last week.
example.zh: 上周大雨过后，许多居民遭受了严重洪灾之苦。

entries.definition: n. 受难；苦楚 a.受苦的；患病的
entries.etymology: "patient enduring of pain, inconvenience, loss, etc.," mid-14c.; "undergoing of punishment, affliction, etc.," late 14c., verbal noun from suffer (v.). Meaning "a painful condition, pain felt" is from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: "patient enduring of pain, inconvenience, loss, etc.," 14 世纪中期; "undergoing of punishment, affliction, etc.," 14 世纪晚期, verbal 名词 源自 suffer （动）. 义为 "a painful condition, pain felt" 始于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The novel portrays the suffering of refugees forced to flee their homes.
example.zh: 这部小说描绘了被迫逃离家园的难民所承受的苦楚。

entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French soficient "satisfactory," or directly from Latin sufficientem (nominative sufficiens) "adequate," present participle of sufficere "to supply as a substitute" (see suffice).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 soficient "satisfactory," or 直接源自 拉丁语 sufficientem (主格 sufficiens) "adequate," 为 … 的现在分词 sufficere "to supply as a substitute" （参见 suffice).

example.en: The evidence presented was not sufficient to prove the defendant's guilt beyond doubt.
example.zh: 所呈示的证据不足以毫无疑问地证明被告有罪。

entries.etymology:
late 13c., sugre, from Old French sucre "sugar" (12c.), from Medieval Latin succarum, from Arabic sukkar, from Persian shakar, from Sanskrit sharkara "ground or candied sugar," originally "grit, gravel" (cognate with Greek kroke "pebble"). The Arabic word also was borrowed in Italian (zucchero), Spanish (azucar, with the Arabic article), and German (Old High German zucura, German Zucker), and its forms are represented in most European languages (such as Serbian cukar, Polish cukier, Russian sakhar).

Its Old World home was India (Alexander the Great's companions marveled at the "honey without bees") and it remained exotic in Europe until the Arabs began to cultivate it in Sicily and Spain; not until after the Crusades did it begin to rival honey as the West's sweetener. The Spaniards in the West Indies began raising sugar cane in 1506; first grown in Cuba 1523; first cultivated in Brazil 1532. The reason for the -g- in the English word is obscure (OED compares flagon, from French flacon). The pronunciation shift from s- to sh- is probably from the initial long vowel sound syu- (as in sure).

As a type of chemical compound from 1826. Slang "euphemistic substitute for an imprecation" [OED] is attested from 1891. As a term of endearment, first recorded 1930. Sugar-cane is from 1560s. Sugar-maple is from 1731. Sugar loaf was originally a moulded conical mass of refined sugar (early 15c.); now obsolete, but sense extended 17c. to hills, hats, etc. of that shape.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, sugre, 源自 古法语 sucre "sugar" (12 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 succarum, 源自 阿拉伯语 sukkar, 源自 波斯语 shakar, 源自 梵语 sharkara "ground or candied sugar," 原义为 "grit, gravel" (与 … 同源 希腊语 kroke "pebble"). The 阿拉伯语 word also was borrowed in 意大利语 (zucchero), 西班牙语 (azucar, with the 阿拉伯语 article), and 德语 (古高地德语 zucura, 德语 Zucker), and its forms are represented in most European languages (such as Serbian cukar, Polish cukier, 俄语 sakhar). Its Old World home was India (Alexander the Great's companions marveled at the "honey without bees") and it remained exotic in Europe until the Arabs began to cultivate it in Sicily and Spain; not until after the Crusades did it begin to rival honey as the West's sweetener. The Spaniards in the West Indies began raising sugar cane 于 1506 年; first grown in Cuba 1523 年; first cultivated in Brazil 1532 年. The reason for the -g- in the English word is obscure (OED compares flagon, 源自 法语 flacon). The pronunciation shift 源自 s- to sh- is 可能 源自 initial long vowel sound syu- (as in sure). 作为 type of chemical 复合词 自 1826 年起. Slang "euphemistic substitute for an imprecation" [OED] 见于 1891 年. 作为 term of endearment, 首见于 1930 年. Sugar-cane 始于 1560 年代. Sugar-maple 始于 1731 年. Sugar loaf was 原义为 a moulded conical mass of refined sugar (15 世纪初); 今废, but sense extended 17 世纪 to hills, hats, etc. of that shape.

example.en: The doctor told him to cut down on sugar to protect his teeth and prevent diabetes.
example.zh: 医生告诉他减少糖的摄入，以保护牙齿并预防糖尿病。

definitionLines: vt. 建议，提出；使想起，暗示
entries.definition: vt. 建议，提出；使想起，暗示
entries.etymology: 1520s, "place before another's mind; put forward a proposition," from Latin suggestus, past participle of suggerere "bring up, bring under, lay beneath; furnish, afford, supply; prompt" (see suggestion). Meaning "to act so as to call up the idea of (something else)" is from 1709. Related: Suggested; suggesting.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, "place before another's mind; put forward a proposition," 源自 拉丁语 suggestus, 为 … 的过去分词 suggerere "bring up, bring under, lay beneath; furnish, afford, supply; prompt" （参见 suggestion). 义为 "to act so as to call up the idea of (something else)" 始于 1709 年. 同源词：Suggested; suggesting.

example.en: The safety committee suggested installing smoke detectors on every floor of the building.
example.zh: 安全委员会建议在大楼每一层安装烟雾探测器。

definitionLines: n. 建议，提议；暗示，示意
entries.definition: n. 建议，提议；暗示，示意
entries.etymology: mid-14c., "a prompting to evil," from Anglo-French and Old French suggestioun "hint, temptation," from Latin suggestionem (nominative suggestio) "an addition, intimation, suggestion," noun of action from suggestus, past participle of suggerere "bring up, bring under, lay beneath; furnish, afford, supply; prompt," from sub "up" (see sub-) + gerere "bring, carry" (see gest). Sense evolution in Latin is from "heap up, build" to "bring forward an idea." Meaning "proposal, statement, declaration" appeared by late 14c., but original English notion of "evil prompting" remains in suggestive. Hypnotism sense is from 1887.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期, "a prompting to evil," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 and 古法语 suggestioun "hint, temptation," 源自 拉丁语 suggestionem (主格 suggestio) "an addition, intimation, suggestion," 名词 of action 源自 suggestus, 为 … 的过去分词 suggerere "bring up, bring under, lay beneath; furnish, afford, supply; prompt," 源自 sub "up" （参见 sub-) + gerere "bring, carry" （参见 gest). Sense evolution in 拉丁语 始于 "heap up, build" to "bring forward an idea." 义为 "proposal, statement, declaration" appeared by 14 世纪晚期, but original English 概念 "evil prompting" remains in suggestive. Hypnotism sense 始于 1887 年.

example.en: The teacher welcomed any suggestion for improving the class schedule.
example.zh: 老师欢迎任何关于改善课程安排的建议。

definitionLines: vt. 适合，合适；满足，中……的 意
entries.definition: vt. 适合，合适；满足，中……的 意 n.一套衣服/西服；诉讼
entries.etymology: "be agreeable or convenient, fall in with the views of," 1570s, from suit (n.), perhaps from the notion of "join a retinue clad in like clothes." Earlier "seek out" (mid-15c.); "be becoming" (mid-14c.). Meaning "make agreeable or convenient" is from 1590s. Meaning "provide with clothes" is from 1570s; that of "dress oneself" is from 1590s; with up (adv.) from 1945. Expression suit yourself attested by 1851. Related: Suited; suiting.
entries.etymologyZh: "be agreeable or convenient, fall in with the views of," 1570 年代, 源自 suit （名）, 或源自 the 概念 "join a retinue clad in like clothes." Earlier "seek out" (15 世纪中期); "be becoming" (14 世纪中期). 义为 "make agreeable or convenient" 始于 1590 年代. 义为 "provide with clothes" 始于 1570 年代; that of "dress oneself" 始于 1590 年代; with up （副） 自 1945 年起. Expression suit yourself attested 截至 1851 年. 同源词：Suited; suiting.

example.en: This schedule does not suit everyone on the team.
example.zh: 这个时间安排并不适合团队中的每个人。

entries.etymology: 1580s, from suit (v.) + -able. Earlier suit-like (1560s); suitly (mid-15c.). Related: Suitably; suitableness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, 源自 suit （动） + -able. Earlier suit-like (1560 年代); suitly (15 世纪中期). 同源词：Suitably; suitableness.

example.en: This movie is not suitable for young children.
example.zh: 这部电影不适合幼儿观看。

entries.etymology: 1898, from suit (n.) + case (n.2). Originally a case for holding a suit of clothes. In reference to small nuclear weapons, 1954.
entries.etymologyZh: 1898 年, 源自 suit （名） + case (n.2). Originally a case for holding a suit of clothes. In reference to small nuclear weapons, 1954 年.

example.en: She packed her clothes neatly into a small suitcase for the weekend trip.
example.zh: 她把衣服整齐地装进一个小行李箱，准备周末旅行。

definitionLines: n.套房；（一批）随员，随从；（一 套）家具
entries.definition: n.套房；（一批）随员，随从；（一 套）家具
entries.etymology: 1670s, "train of followers or attendants," from French suite, from Old French suite, sieute "act of following, attendance" (see suit (n.), which is an earlier borrowing of the same French word). The meanings "set of instrumental compositions" (1680s), "connected set of rooms" (1716), and "set of furniture" (1805) were imported from French usages or re-spelled on the French model from suit in its sense of "a number of things taken collectively and constituting a sequence; collection of things of like kind."
entries.etymologyZh: 1670 年代, "train of followers or attendants," 源自 法语 suite, 源自 古法语 suite, sieute "act of following, attendance" （参见 suit （名）, which is an earlier borrowing of the same 法语 word). The meanings "set of instrumental compositions" (1680 年代), "connected set of rooms" (1716 年), and "set of furniture" (1805 年) were imported 源自 法语 usages or re-spelled on the 法语 model 源自 suit in its 语义 "a number of things taken collectively and constituting a sequence; collection of things of like kind."

example.en: The couple booked a presidential suite for their anniversary.
example.zh: 这对夫妇为纪念日预订了一间总统套房。

entries.etymology: also sulphur, c. 1300, from Anglo-French sulfere, Old French soufre "sulfur, fire and brimstone, hellfire" (13c.), later also sulphur, from Late Latin sulfur, from Latin sulphur, probably from a root meaning "to burn." Ousted native brimstone and cognate Old English swefl, German schwefel, Swedish swafel, Dutch zwavel. The spelling with -ph- is standard in Britain, but its suggestion of a Greek origin is misleading.
entries.etymologyZh: also sulphur, 约 1300 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 sulfere, 古法语 soufre "sulfur, fire and brimstone, hellfire" (13 世纪), later also sulphur, 源自 晚期拉丁语 sulfur, 源自 拉丁语 sulphur, 可能 源自 a root 意为 "to burn." Ousted 本族 brimstone and 同源 古英语 swefl, 德语 schwefel, Swedish swafel, 荷兰语 zwavel. The spelling with -ph- is standard in Britain, but its suggestion of a 希腊语 origin is misleading.

entries.etymology: 1837, American English, from summary + -ize. Related: Summarized; summarizing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1837 年, American English, 源自 summary + -ize. 同源词：Summarized; summarizing.

example.en: Could you summarize the main points of the lecture in a few sentences?
example.zh: 你能用几句话概括这次讲座的要点吗？

entries.etymology: early 15c., "brief, abbreviated; containing the sum or substance only," from Medieval Latin summarius "of or pertaining to the sum or substance," from Latin summa "whole, totality, gist" (see sum (n.)). Compare Latin phrase ad summam "on the whole, generally, in short." Sense of "done promptly, performed without hesitation or formality" is from 1713.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "brief, abbreviated; containing the sum or substance only," 源自 中古拉丁语 summarius "of or pertaining to the sum or substance," 源自 拉丁语 summa "whole, totality, gist" （参见 sum （名）). 对比 拉丁语 phrase ad summam "on the whole, generally, in short." 义为 "done promptly, performed without hesitation or formality" 始于 1713 年.

example.en: Please write a brief summary of the report for the board.
example.zh: 请为董事会写一份报告的简短摘要。

entries.etymology: "to pass the summer," mid-15c., from summer (n.1). Related: Summered; summering.
entries.etymologyZh: "to pass the summer," 15 世纪中期, 源自 summer (n.1). 同源词：Summered; summering.

example.en: We usually go to the beach in summer to escape the heat.
example.zh: 我们通常在夏天去海边避暑。

definitionLines: n. 顶，最高点；巅峰，高峰；最高 级会议
entries.definition: n. 顶，最高点；巅峰，高峰；最高 级会议
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "highest point, peak," from Middle French somete, from Old French somete "summit, top," diminutive of som, sum "highest part, top of a hill," from Latin summum, neuter of noun use of summus "highest," related to super "over" (see sum (n.)). The meaning "meeting of heads of state" (1950) is from Winston Churchill's metaphor of "a parley at the summit."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "highest point, peak," 源自 中古法语 somete, 源自 古法语 somete "summit, top," 为 … 的指小形式 som, sum "highest part, top of a hill," 源自 拉丁语 summum, neuter of 为 … 的名词用法 summus "highest," related to super "over" （参见 sum （名）). The 意为 "meeting of heads of state" (1950 年) 始于 Winston Churchill's metaphor of "a parley at the summit."

example.en: World leaders gathered for the annual summit on climate change.
example.zh: 世界各国领导人齐聚一堂，参加年度气候变化峰会。

entries.etymology: 1510s, "to set something in the sun," from sun (n.). Intransitive meaning "expose oneself to the sun" is recorded from c. 1600. Sun-bathing is attested from c. 1600.
entries.etymologyZh: 1510 年代, "to set something in the sun," 源自 sun （名）. Intransitive 意为 "expose oneself to the sun" 见于 约 1600 年. Sun-bathing 见于 约 1600 年.

entries.etymology:
first day of the week, Old English sunnandæg (Northumbrian sunnadæg), literally "day of the sun," from sunnan, oblique case of sunne "sun" (see sun (n.)) + dæg "day" (see day). A Germanic loan-translation of Latin dies solis "day of the sun," which is itself a loan-translation of Greek hemera heliou. Compare Old Saxon sunnun dag, Old Frisian sunnandei, Old Norse sunnundagr, Dutch zondag, German Sonntag "Sunday."

In European Christian cultures outside Germanic often with a name meaning "the Lord's Day" (Latin Dominica). Sunday-school dates from 1783 (originally for secular instruction); Sunday clothes is from 1640s. Sunday driver is from 1925.
entries.etymologyZh: first day of the week, 古英语 sunnandæg (Northumbrian sunnadæg), 字面义为 "day of the sun," 源自 sunnan, oblique case of sunne "sun" （参见 sun （名）) + dæg "day" （参见 day). A 日耳曼语 loan-translation of 拉丁语 dies solis "day of the sun," which is itself a loan-translation of 希腊语 hemera heliou. 对比 古撒克逊语 sunnun dag, 古弗里西语 sunnandei, 古北欧语 sunnundagr, 荷兰语 zondag, 德语 Sonntag "Sunday." In European Christian cultures outside 日耳曼语 常 with a name 意为 "the Lord's Day" (拉丁语 Dominica). Sunday-school dates 自 1783 年起 (原义为 for secular instruction); Sunday clothes 始于 1640 年代. Sunday driver 始于 1925 年.

entries.etymology: c. 1200, from sun (n.) + light (n.). Compare Dutch zonlicht, German sonnenlicht.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 sun （名） + light （名）. 对比 荷兰语 zonlicht, 德语 sonnenlicht.

example.en: The room was filled with warm sunlight in the early morning.
example.zh: 清晨，房间里充满了温暖的阳光。

entries.etymology:
"full of sun," early 14c., from sun (n.) + -y (2). Compare Dutch zonnig, German sonnig. Figurative sense of "cheerful" is attested from 1540s. Sunny side in reference to optimistic outlook is from 1831. Eggs served sunny side up first attested 1887, in lunch counter slang, in reference to appearance when served.

Related: Sunnily; sunniness. As a noun meaning "sunfish" from 1835.
entries.etymologyZh: "full of sun," 14 世纪初, 源自 sun （名） + -y (2). 对比 荷兰语 zonnig, 德语 sonnig. Figurative 语义 "cheerful" 见于 1540 年代. Sunny side in reference to optimistic outlook 始于 1831 年. Eggs served sunny side up 最早见于 1887 年, in lunch counter 俚语, in reference to appearance when served. 同源词：Sunnily; sunniness. 作名词时 意为 "sunfish" 自 1835 年起.

example.en: It was a sunny afternoon, perfect for a walk in the park.
example.zh: 那是一个阳光明媚的下午，非常适合在公园散步。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., from sun (n.) + rise (v.); perhaps it evolved from a Middle English subjunctive, such as before the sun rise. Earlier in same sense were sunrist (mid-14c.); sunrising (mid-13c.). Compare sunset.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 sun （名） + rise （动）; 或许 it evolved 源自 a 中古英语 subjunctive, such as before the sun rise. Earlier in same sense were sunrist (14 世纪中期); sunrising (13 世纪中期). 对比 sunset.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from sun (n.) + set (v.). Perhaps from a Middle English subjunctive such as before the sun set. Old English had sunnansetlgong "sunset," while sunset meant "west." Figurative use from c. 1600. To ride off into the sunset (1963) is from the stereotypical ending of cowboy movies.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 sun （名） + set （动）. Perhaps 源自 a 中古英语 subjunctive such as before the sun set. 古英语 had sunnansetlgong "sunset," while sunset meant "west." Figurative use 源自 约 1600 年. To ride off into the sunset (1963 年) 始于 the stereotypical ending of cowboy movies.

example.en: They sat on the beach and watched the beautiful sunset.
example.zh: 他们坐在沙滩上，欣赏美丽的日落。

entries.etymology: mid-13c., from sun (n.) + shine (n.). Old English had sunnanscima "sunshine;" while sunscin meant "a mirror, speculum." Meaning "happy person who brightens the lives of others" is from 1942. Sunshine law in reference to U.S. open-meeting legislation is recorded from 1972, from the notion of shining the light of public access on deliberations formerly held behind closed doors. Related: Sunshiny.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, 源自 sun （名） + shine （名）. 古英语 had sunnanscima "sunshine;" while sunscin meant "a mirror, speculum." 义为 "happy person who brightens the lives of others" 始于 1942 年. Sunshine law in reference to U.S. open-meeting legislation 见于 1972 年, 源自 概念 shining the light of public access on deliberations formerly held behind closed doors. 同源词：Sunshiny.

entries.etymology: "first-rate, excellent," 1837, from prefix in superfine (1680s), denoting "highest grade of goods," from Latin super "above, over, beyond" (see super-). Extended usage as a general term of approval is 1895 slang, revived by 1967. Rhyming reduplication form super-duper first attested 1940. Super Bowl attested from 1966; Super Glue from 1975; as a verb by 1983.
entries.etymologyZh: "first-rate, excellent," 1837 年, 源自 prefix in superfine (1680 年代), denoting "highest grade of goods," 源自 拉丁语 super "above, over, beyond" （参见 super-). Extended usage 作为 general term of approval is 1895 年 俚语, revived 截至 1967 年. Rhyming reduplication form super-duper 最早见于 1940 年. Super Bowl attested 自 1966 年起; Super Glue 自 1975 年起; 作动词时 截至 1983 年.

entries.etymology: 1540s, "noble, magnificent" (of buildings, etc.), from Latin superbus "grand, proud, splendid; haughty, vain, insolent," from super "above, over" (see super-). The second element perhaps is from PIE root *bhe- "to be." General sense of "very fine" developed by 1729. Related: Superbious (c. 1500); superbly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "noble, magnificent" (of buildings, etc.), 源自 拉丁语 superbus "grand, proud, splendid; haughty, vain, insolent," 源自 super "above, over" （参见 super-). The second element 或许 始于 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *bhe- "to be." General 语义 "very fine" developed 截至 1729 年. 同源词：Superbious (约 1500 年); superbly.

entries.etymology: late 14c., in anatomical and mathematical uses, "of or relating to a surface," from Late Latin superficialis "of or pertaining to the surface," from superficies "surface, upper side, top," from super "above, over" (see super-) + facies "form, face" (see face (n.)). Meaning "not deep, without thorough understanding, cursory, comprehending only what is apparent or obvious" (of perceptions, thoughts, etc.) first recorded early 15c. (implied in superficially "not thoroughly").
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, in anatomical and mathematical uses, "of or relating to a surface," 源自 晚期拉丁语 superficialis "of or pertaining to the surface," 源自 superficies "surface, upper side, top," 源自 super "above, over" （参见 super-) + facies "form, face" （参见 face （名）). 义为 "not deep, without thorough understanding, cursory, comprehending only what is apparent or obvious" (of perceptions, thoughts, etc.) 首见于 15 世纪初 (implied in superficially "not thoroughly").

definitionLines: n. 负责人；主管；监督人
entries.definition: n. 负责人；主管；监督人
entries.etymology:
1550s, originally an ecclesiastical word meaning "bishop" or "minister who supervises churches within a district" (ultimately a loan-translation of Greek episkopos "overseer"), from Medieval Latin superintendentem (nominative superintendens), present participle of Late Latin superintendere "oversee," from Latin super "above" (see super-) + intendere "turn one's attention to, direct" (see intend). Famously used by 16c. radical Protestants in place of bishop, which to them was tainted by Papacy.

The general sense of "a person who has charge of some business" is first recorded 1580s. Meaning "janitor, custodian" is from c. 1935. Shortened form super first attested 1857, especially at first of overseers of sheep ranches in Australia. As an adjective meaning "superintending," from 1590s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 原义为 an ecclesiastical word 意为 "bishop" or "minister who supervises churches within a district" (ultimately a loan-translation of 希腊语 episkopos "overseer"), 源自 中古拉丁语 superintendentem (主格 superintendens), 为 … 的现在分词 晚期拉丁语 superintendere "oversee," 源自 拉丁语 super "above" （参见 super-) + intendere "turn one's attention to, direct" （参见 intend). Famously used by 16 世纪 radical Protestants in place of bishop, which to them was tainted by Papacy. The general 语义 "a person who has charge of some business" is 首见于 1580 年代. 义为 "janitor, custodian" 始于 约 1935 年. Shortened form super 最早见于 1857 年, 尤指 at first of overseers of sheep ranches in Australia. 作形容词时 意为 "superintending," 源自 1590 年代.

example.en: The building superintendent was responsible for managing all maintenance and repairs.
example.zh: 这栋楼的主管负责管理所有的维修和保养工作。

definitionLines: a.（to）更好的，较好的；有优越 感的，高傲的
entries.definition: n. /a. 上级 a.（to）更好的，较好的；有优越 感的，高傲的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "higher in position," from Old French superior "higher, upper" (Modern French superieur), from Latin superiorem (nominative superior) "higher," comparative of superus "situated above, upper," from super "above, over" (see super-).

Meaning "higher in rank or dignity" is attested from late 15c.; sense of "of a higher nature or character" is attested from 1530s. Original sense was preserved more strongly in French (as in les étages supérieur "the upper stories"), and in Lake Superior, a loan-translation of French Lac Supérieur, literally "upper lake" (at 600 feet above sea-level it has the highest surface elevation of the five Great Lakes and is the furthest north).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "higher in position," 源自 古法语 superior "higher, upper" (现代法语 superieur), 源自 拉丁语 superiorem (主格 superior) "higher," comparative of superus "situated above, upper," 源自 super "above, over" （参见 super-). 义为 "higher in rank or dignity" 见于 15 世纪晚期; 语义 "of a higher nature or character" 见于 1530 年代. Original sense was preserved more strongly in 法语 (as in les étages supérieur "the upper stories"), and in Lake Superior, a loan-translation of 法语 Lac Supérieur, 字面义为 "upper lake" (at 600 feet above sea-level it has the highest surface elevation of the five Great Lakes and is the furthest north).

example.en: His performance was superior to that of all other candidates in the competition.
example.zh: 他在比赛中的表现优于所有其他候选人。

entries.etymology: 1903, coined by George Bernard Shaw to translate German Übermensch, "highly evolved human being that transcends good and evil," from "Thus Spake Zarathustra" (1883-91), by Friedrich Nietzsche (1844-1900). First used in German by Hermann Rab (1520s), and also used by Herder and Goethe. Translated as overman (1895) and beyond-man (1896) before Shaw got it right in his play title "Man and Superman" (1903). Application to comic strip hero is from 1938.
entries.etymologyZh: 1903 年, coined by George Bernard Shaw to translate 德语 Übermensch, "highly evolved human being that transcends good and evil," 源自 "Thus Spake Zarathustra" (1883 年-91), by Friedrich Nietzsche (1844 年-1900 年). First used in 德语 by Hermann Rab (1520 年代), and also used by Herder and Goethe. Translated as overman (1895 年) and beyond-man (1896 年) before Shaw got it right in his play title "Man and Superman" (1903 年). Application to comic strip hero 始于 1938 年.

entries.etymology: 1933, American English, from super- + market (n.). The 1933 reference is in an article that says the stores themselves began to open around 1931. An early word for a "superstore" was hypermarket (1967).
entries.etymologyZh: 1933 年, American English, 源自 super- + market （名）. The 1933 年 reference is in an article that says the stores themselves began to open around 1931 年. An early word for a "superstore" was hypermarket (1967 年).

entries.etymology: 1919, "of or having to do with sound waves beyond the limit of human hearing," from super- + sonic. Attested from 1934 in sense of "exceeding the speed of sound" (especially as a measure of aircraft speed), leaving the original sense to ultrasonic (1923).
entries.etymologyZh: 1919 年, "of or having to do with sound waves beyond the limit of human hearing," 源自 super- + sonic. Attested 自 1934 年起 in 语义 "exceeding the speed of sound" (尤指 作为 measure of aircraft speed), leaving the original sense to ultrasonic (1923 年).

entries.etymology: late 15c., "to look over" (implied in supervising), from Medieval Latin supervisus, past participle of supervidere "oversee, inspect," from Latin super "over" (see super-) + videre "see" (see vision). Meaning "to oversee and superintend the work or performance of others" is attested from 1640s. Related: Supervised.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "to look over" (implied in supervising), 源自 中古拉丁语 supervisus, 为 … 的过去分词 supervidere "oversee, inspect," 源自 拉丁语 super "over" （参见 super-) + videre "see" （参见 vision). 义为 "to oversee and superintend the work or performance of others" 见于 1640 年代. 同源词：Supervised.

example.en: A senior engineer was assigned to supervise the construction of the new bridge.
example.zh: 一名高级工程师被指派监督新桥的建设工作。

definitionLines: n. 监督人，管理人，导师
entries.definition: n. 监督人，管理人，导师
entries.etymology: "one who inspects and directs the work of others," mid-15c., from Medieval Latin supervisor, agent noun from supervidere "oversee, inspect" (see supervise).
entries.etymologyZh: "one who inspects and directs the work of others," 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古拉丁语 supervisor, agent 名词 源自 supervidere "oversee, inspect" （参见 supervise).

example.en: Please report any safety concerns directly to your line supervisor.
example.zh: 请直接将任何安全方面的顾虑报告给你的直属主管。

entries.etymology:
mid-13c., soper, "the last meal of the day," from Old French soper "evening meal," noun use of infinitive soper "to eat the evening meal," which is of Germanic origin (see sup (v.1)).

Applied since c. 1300 to the last meal of Christ.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪中期, soper, "the last meal of the day," 源自 古法语 soper "evening meal," 为 … 的名词用法 infinitive soper "to eat the evening meal," which is of 日耳曼语 origin （参见 sup (v.1)). Applied 自 约 1300 年 to the last meal of Christ.

example.en: The family gathered around the table for supper after a long day of work.
example.zh: 一天辛苦工作后，一家人围坐在桌边吃晚饭。

definitionLines: n1. 补遗，补充；附录；增刊
entries.definition: n1. 补遗，补充；附录；增刊 v.补充
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Latin supplementum "that which fills up, that with which anything is made full or whole, something added to supply a deficiency," from supplere "to fill up" (see supply (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 拉丁语 supplementum "that which fills up, that with which anything is made full or whole, something added to supply a deficiency," 源自 supplere "to fill up" （参见 supply （动）).

example.en: Many athletes supplement their diet with protein shakes after training.
example.zh: 许多运动员在训练后用蛋白粉补充饮食营养。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "assistance, relief, act of supplying," from supply (v.). Meaning "that which is provided, quantity or amount of something provided" is attested from c. 1600. Meaning "person who temporarily takes the place of another" (especially a minister or preacher) is from 1580s. In the political economy sense (corollary of demand (n.)) it dates from 1776; supply-side (adj.) in reference to economic policy is attested from 1976; as a noun by 1922. Supplies "necessary provisions held for distribution and use" is from c. 1650.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "assistance, relief, act of supplying," 源自 supply （动）. 义为 "that which is provided, quantity or amount of something provided" 见于 约 1600 年. 义为 "person who temporarily takes the place of another" (尤指 a minister or preacher) 始于 1580 年代. In the political economy sense (corollary of demand （名）) it dates 自 1776 年起; supply-side （形） in reference to economic policy 见于 1976 年; 作名词时 截至 1922 年. Supplies "necessary provisions held for distribution and use" 始于 约 1650 年.

example.en: The aid organization promised to supply food and tents to flood victims.
example.zh: 救援组织承诺向洪水受害者提供食物和帐篷。

definitionLines: vt. 支持，支撑；支持，鼓励； 拥护；供养，资助
entries.definition: vt. 支持，支撑；支持，鼓励； 拥护；供养，资助
entries.etymology: late 14c., "to aid," also "to hold up, prop up, put up with, tolerate," from Old French suporter "to bear, endure, sustain, support" (14c.), from Latin supportare "convey, carry, bring up, bring forward," from sub "up from under" (see sub-) + portare "to carry" (see port (n.1)). Related: Supported; supporting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "to aid," also "to hold up, prop up, put up with, tolerate," 源自 古法语 suporter "to bear, endure, sustain, support" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 supportare "convey, carry, bring up, bring forward," 源自 sub "up from under" （参见 sub-) + portare "to carry" （参见 port (n.1)). 同源词：Supported; supporting.

example.en: Thousands of fans came out to support the local football team.
example.zh: 数千名球迷出来支持当地的足球队。

definitionLines: a. 支持的；支援的；赞助的
entries.definition: a. 支持的；支援的；赞助的
entries.etymology: 1590s, from support (v.) + -ive. Called "rare" in OED 1st edition and Century Dictionary. Related: Supportively; supportiveness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 support （动） + -ive. Called "rare" in OED 1st edition and Century Dictionary. 同源词：Supportively; supportiveness.

example.en: Her family was very supportive when she decided to change careers.
example.zh: 当她决定转行时，她的家人给予了充分的支持。

entries.etymology: early 14c., "to assume as the basis of argument," from Old French suposer "to assume" (13c.), probably a replacement (influenced by Old French poser "put, place") of *suppondre, from Latin supponere "put or place under; to subordinate, make subject," from sub "under" (see sub-) + ponere "put, place" (past participle positus; see position (n.)). Meaning "to admit as possible, to believe to be true" is from 1520s.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "to assume as the basis of argument," 源自 古法语 suposer "to assume" (13 世纪), 可能 a replacement (influenced by 古法语 poser "put, place") of *suppondre, 源自 拉丁语 supponere "put or place under; to subordinate, make subject," 源自 sub "under" （参见 sub-) + ponere "put, place" (past participle positus; 参见 position （名）). 义为 "to admit as possible, to believe to be true" 始于 1520 年代.

example.en: I suppose you already know the meeting has been moved to Thursday.
example.zh: 我猜你已经知道会议改到周四了。

definitionLines: vt. 镇压，压制；抑制，查禁
entries.definition: vt. 镇压，压制；抑制，查禁
entries.etymology: late 14c. (implied in suppressing) "be burdensome;" 1520s as "put down by force or authority," from Latin suppressus, past participle of supprimere "press down, stop, hold back, check, stifle," from sub "down, under" (see sub-) + premere "push against" (see press (v.1)). Sense of "prevent or prohibit the circulation of" is from 1550s of publications; medical use from 1620s. Related: Suppressed; suppressing.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期 (implied in suppressing) "be burdensome;" 1520 年代 as "put down by force or authority," 源自 拉丁语 suppressus, 为 … 的过去分词 supprimere "press down, stop, hold back, check, stifle," 源自 sub "down, under" （参见 sub-) + premere "push against" （参见 press (v.1)). 义为 "prevent or prohibit the circulation of" 始于 1550 年代 of publications; medical use 源自 1620 年代. 同源词：Suppressed; suppressing.

example.en: The government tried to suppress all forms of political dissent.
example.zh: 政府试图压制一切形式的政治异见。

definitionLines: a.最高的；极度的，最重要的
entries.definition: a.最高的；极度的，最重要的
entries.etymology: 1520s, from Middle French suprême (15c.) and directly from Latin supremus "highest," superlative of superus "situated above," from super "above" (see super-). Supreme Being "God" first attested 1690s; Supreme Court is from 1689.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, 源自 中古法语 suprême (15 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 supremus "highest," superlative of superus "situated above," 源自 super "above" （参见 super-). Supreme Being "God" 最早见于 1690 年代; Supreme Court 始于 1689 年.

example.en: The Supreme Court has the final authority to interpret the constitution.
example.zh: 最高法院拥有解释宪法的最终权力。

definitionLines: a.一定的，必然的；确信的； 有把握的；稳当的，可靠的
entries.definition: a.一定的，必然的；确信的； 有把握的；稳当的，可靠的
entries.etymology:
early 13c., "safe against attack, secure," later "firm, reliable" (c. 1300); "mentally certain, confident" (mid-14c.); "firm, strong, resolute" (c. 1400), from Old French seur, sur "safe, secure; undoubted, dependable, trustworthy" (12c.), from Latin securus "free from care, untroubled, heedless, safe" (see secure (adj.)). Pronunciation development is that of sugar (n.).

As an affirmative meaning "yes, certainly" it dates from 1803, from Middle English meanings "firmly established; having no doubt," and phrases like to be sure (1650s), sure enough (1540s), and for sure (1580s). The use as an adverb meaning "assuredly" goes back to early 14c. Sure-footed is from 1630s, literal and figurative; sure thing dates from 1836. In 16c.-17c., Suresby was an appellation for a person to be depended upon.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪初, "safe against attack, secure," later "firm, reliable" (约 1300 年); "mentally certain, confident" (14 世纪中期); "firm, strong, resolute" (约 1400 年), 源自 古法语 seur, sur "safe, secure; undoubted, dependable, trustworthy" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 securus "free from care, untroubled, heedless, safe" （参见 secure （形）). Pronunciation development is that of sugar （名）. 作为 affirmative 意为 "yes, certainly" it dates 自 1803 年起, 源自 中古英语 meanings "firmly established; having no doubt," and phrases like to be sure (1650 年代), sure enough (1540 年代), and for sure (1580 年代). The use 作为 副词 意为 "assuredly" goes back to 14 世纪初 Sure-footed 始于 1630 年代, literal and figurative; sure thing dates 自 1836 年起. In 16 世纪-17 世纪, Suresby was an appellation for a person to be depended upon.

example.en: Are you sure you locked the door? I heard it might still be open.
example.zh: 你确定锁门了吗？我听说门可能还开着。

entries.definition: n. 浪花 vi. 冲浪；网上浏览
entries.etymology: 1680s, probably from earlier suffe (1590s), of uncertain origin. Originally used in reference to the coast of India, hence perhaps of Indic origin. Or perhaps a phonetic respelling of sough, which meant "a rushing sound."
entries.etymologyZh: 1680 年代, 可能 源自 earlier suffe (1590 年代), 来源存疑. Originally used in reference to the coast of India, hence 或许 of Indic origin. Or 或许 a phonetic respelling of sough, which meant "a rushing sound."

entries.etymology: 1610s, from French surface "an outermost boundary, outside part" (16c.), from Old French sur- "above" (see sur-) + face (see face (n.)). Patterned on Latin superficies "surface, upper side, top" (see superficial). As an adjective from 1660s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, 源自 法语 surface "an outermost boundary, outside part" (16 世纪), 源自 古法语 sur- "above" （参见 sur-) + face （参见 face （名）). Patterned on 拉丁语 superficies "surface, upper side, top" （参见 superficial). 作形容词时 源自 1660 年代.

example.en: The surface of the lake was completely still in the early morning light.
example.zh: 早晨的阳光下，湖面完全平静无波。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, sorgien, cirurgian "person who heals by manual operation on the patient," from Anglo-French surgien (13c.), from Old French surgien, cirurgien (13c.), from cirurgie "surgery," from Latin chirurgia "surgery," from Greek kheirourgia, from kheirourgos "working or done by hand," from kheir "hand" (see chiro-) + ergon "work" (see organ).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, sorgien, cirurgian "person who heals by manual operation on the patient," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 surgien (13 世纪), 源自 古法语 surgien, cirurgien (13 世纪), 源自 cirurgie "surgery," 源自 拉丁语 chirurgia "surgery," 源自 希腊语 kheirourgia, 源自 kheirourgos "working or done by hand," 源自 kheir "hand" （参见 chiro-) + ergon "work" （参见 organ).

example.en: The surgeon successfully removed the tumor during a six-hour operation.
example.zh: 外科医生在六小时的手术中成功切除了肿瘤。

entries.etymology: late 15c., "fountain, stream," of uncertain origin, probably from Middle French sourge-, stem of sourdre "to rise, swell," from Latin surgere "to rise, arise, get up, mount up, ascend; attack," contraction of surrigere, from assimilated form of sub "up from below" (see sub-) + regere "to keep straight, guide" (see regal). Meaning "high, rolling swell of water" is from 1520s; figurative sense of "excited rising up" (as of feelings) is from 1510s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "fountain, stream," 来源存疑, 可能 源自 中古法语 sourge-, stem of sourdre "to rise, swell," 源自 拉丁语 surgere "to rise, arise, get up, mount up, ascend; attack," contraction of surrigere, 源自 为 … 的同化形式 sub "up from below" （参见 sub-) + regere "to keep straight, guide" （参见 regal). 义为 "high, rolling swell of water" 始于 1520 年代; figurative 语义 "excited rising up" (as of feelings) 始于 1510 年代.

example.en: There was a sudden surge in demand for masks during the outbreak.
example.zh: 疫情暴发期间，口罩需求量突然激增。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, sirgirie, "medical treatment of an operative nature, such as cutting-operations, setting of fractures, etc.," from Old French surgerie, surgeure, contraction of serurgerie, from Late Latin chirurgia (see surgeon).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, sirgirie, "medical treatment of an operative nature, such as cutting-operations, setting of fractures, etc.," 源自 古法语 surgerie, surgeure, contraction of serurgerie, 源自 晚期拉丁语 chirurgia （参见 surgeon).

example.en: The patient underwent a six-hour surgery to remove the tumor from his spine.
example.zh: 患者接受了长达六小时的手术以切除脊椎肿瘤。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "name, title, or epithet added to a person's name," from sur "above" (from Latin super-; see sur- (1)) + name (n.); modeled on Anglo-French surnoun "surname" (early 14c.), variant of Old French sornom, from sur "over" + nom "name." As "family name" from late 14c.

An Old English word for this was freonama, literally "free name." Meaning "family name" is first found late 14c. Hereditary surnames existed among Norman nobility in England in early 12c., among the common people they began to be used 13c., increasingly frequent until near universal by end of 14c. The process was later in the north of England than the south. The verb is attested from 1510s. Related: Surnamed.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "name, title, or epithet added to a person's name," 源自 sur "above" (源自 拉丁语 super-; 参见 sur- (1)) + name （名）; modeled on 盎格鲁-法语 surnoun "surname" (14 世纪初), 为 … 的变体 古法语 sornom, 源自 sur "over" + nom "name." As "family name" 源自 14 世纪晚期 An 古英语 word for this was freonama, 字面义为 "free name." 义为 "family name" is first found 14 世纪晚期 Hereditary surnames existed among Norman nobility in England in 12 世纪初, among the common people they began to be used 13 世纪, increasingly frequent until near universal by end of 14 世纪 The process was later in the north of England than the south. The 动词 见于 1510 年代. 同源词：Surnamed.

entries.etymology: 1550s, from Middle French surpasser "go beyond, exceed, excel" (16c.), from sur- "beyond" (see sur- (1)) + passer "to go by" (see pass (v.)). Related: Surpassed; surpassing.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 中古法语 surpasser "go beyond, exceed, excel" (16 世纪), 源自 sur- "beyond" （参见 sur- (1)) + passer "to go by" （参见 pass （动）). 同源词：Surpassed; surpassing.

definitionLines: n. 过剩；盈余；剩余；顺差
entries.definition: n. 过剩；盈余；剩余；顺差
entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French sorplus "remainder, extra" (12c., Modern French surplus), from Medieval Latin superplus "excess, surplus," from Latin super "over" (see super-) + plus "more" (see plus). As an adjective from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 sorplus "remainder, extra" (12 世纪, 现代法语 surplus), 源自 中古拉丁语 superplus "excess, surplus," 源自 拉丁语 super "over" （参见 super-) + plus "more" （参见 plus). 作形容词时 源自 14 世纪晚期

definitionLines: vt. 使诧异，使惊奇；突然袭击
entries.definition: n. 诧异，惊奇 vt. 使诧异，使惊奇；突然袭击
entries.etymology:
also formerly surprize, late 14c., "unexpected attack or capture," from Old French surprise "a taking unawares" (13c.), from noun use of past participle of Old French sorprendre "to overtake, seize, invade" (12c.), from sur- "over" (see sur- (1)) + prendre "to take," from Latin prendere, contracted from prehendere "to grasp, seize" (see prehensile). Meaning "something unexpected" first recorded 1590s, that of "feeling of astonishment caused by something unexpected" is c. 1600. Meaning "fancy dish" is attested from 1708.

Surprise party originally was a stealth military detachment (1826); festive sense is attested by 1857; according to Thornton's "American Glossary," originally a gathering of members of a congregation at the house of their preacher "with the ostensible purpose of contributing provisions, &c., for his support," and sometimes called a donation party. Phrase taken by surprise is attested from 1690s.
entries.etymologyZh: also formerly surprize, 14 世纪晚期, "unexpected attack or capture," 源自 古法语 surprise "a taking unawares" (13 世纪), 源自 为 … 的名词用法 为 … 的过去分词 古法语 sorprendre "to overtake, seize, invade" (12 世纪), 源自 sur- "over" （参见 sur- (1)) + prendre "to take," 源自 拉丁语 prendere, contracted 源自 prehendere "to grasp, seize" （参见 prehensile). 义为 "something unexpected" 首见于 1590 年代, that of "feeling of astonishment caused by something unexpected" is 约 1600 年. 义为 "fancy dish" 见于 1708 年. Surprise party 原义为 was a stealth military detachment (1826 年); festive sense is attested 截至 1857 年; according to Thornton's "American Glossary," 原义为 a gathering of members of a congregation at the house of their preacher "with the ostensible purpose of contributing provisions, &c., for his support," and 有时 called a donation party. Phrase taken by surprise 见于 1690 年代.

example.en: The news of her promotion came as a complete surprise to everyone in the office.
example.zh: 她晋升的消息对办公室里的每个人来说都是一个完全的惊喜。

entries.etymology: 1660s, present participle adjective from surprise (v.). Related: Surprisingly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1660 年代, present participle 形容词 源自 surprise （动）. 同源词：Surprisingly.

example.en: The team's victory was surprising given how poorly they had started.
example.zh: 考虑到他们开局很糟糕，这支队伍的胜利令人惊讶。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "to flood, overflow," from Anglo-French surounder, Middle French soronder "to overflow, abound; surpass, dominate," from Late Latin superundare "overflow," from Latin super "over" (see super-) + undare "to flow in waves," from unda "wave" (see water (n.1); and compare abound). Sense of "to shut in on all sides" first recorded 1610s, influenced by figurative meaning in French of "dominate," and by sound association with round, which also influenced the spelling of the English word from 17c. Related: Surrounded; surrounding.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to flood, overflow," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 surounder, 中古法语 soronder "to overflow, abound; surpass, dominate," 源自 晚期拉丁语 superundare "overflow," 源自 拉丁语 super "over" （参见 super-) + undare "to flow in waves," 源自 unda "wave" （参见 water (n.1); and 对比 abound). 义为 "to shut in on all sides" 首见于 1610 年代, influenced by figurative 意为 in 法语 of "dominate," and by sound association with round, which also influenced the spelling of the English word 源自 17 世纪 同源词：Surrounded; surrounding.

example.en: The ancient castle is surrounded by thick forests on three sides, with a river to the south.
example.zh: 这座古老的城堡三面被茂密的森林所包围，南侧临河。

entries.definition: n. （pl.）周围事物，环境 a.周围的

example.en: The cottage blended perfectly into its natural surroundings.
example.zh: 这座小屋完美地融入了周围的自然环境。

definitionLines: vt./n. 俯瞰，眺望；测量，勘察； 全面审查，调查
entries.definition: vt./n. 俯瞰，眺望；测量，勘察； 全面审查，调查
entries.etymology: c. 1400, "to consider, contemplate," from Anglo-French surveier, Old French sorveoir "look (down) at, look upon, notice; guard, watch," from Medieval Latin supervidere "oversee" (see supervise). Meaning "examine the condition of" is from mid-15c. That of "to take linear measurements of a tract of ground" is recorded from 1540s. Related: Surveyed; surveying; surveyance (late 14c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1400 年, "to consider, contemplate," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 surveier, 古法语 sorveoir "look (down) at, look upon, notice; guard, watch," 源自 中古拉丁语 supervidere "oversee" （参见 supervise). 义为 "examine the condition of" 始于 15 世纪中期 That of "to take linear measurements of a tract of ground" 见于 1540 年代. 同源词：Surveyed; surveying; surveyance (14 世纪晚期).

example.en: The company conducted a survey to understand what customers really wanted.
example.zh: 该公司开展了一项调查，以了解顾客的真实需求。

entries.etymology: 1590s, "act of surviving; continuation after some event," from survive + -al (2). Phrase survival of the fittest (1864) was used by Spencer in place of Darwin's natural selection.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, "act of surviving; continuation after some event," 源自 survive + -al (2). Phrase survival of the fittest (1864 年) was used by Spencer in place of Darwin's natural selection.

example.en: Their survival in the wilderness depended on finding clean water.
example.zh: 他们在荒野中的生存取决于能否找到干净的水源。

entries.definition: vi. 幸免于，幸存 vt. 从……逃出
entries.etymology: mid-15c. (implied in surviving), "to outlive, continue in existence after the death of another," originally in the legal (inheritance) sense, from Anglo-French survivre, Old French souvivre (12c., Modern French survivre), from Latin supervivere "live beyond, live longer than," from super "over, beyond" (see super-) + vivere "to live" (see vivid). Intransitive sense "to live on" is from late 15c. Related: Survived; surviving.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期 (implied in surviving), "to outlive, continue in existence after the death of another," 原义为 in the legal (inheritance) sense, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 survivre, 古法语 souvivre (12 世纪, 现代法语 survivre), 源自 拉丁语 supervivere "live beyond, live longer than," 源自 super "over, beyond" （参见 super-) + vivere "to live" （参见 vivid). Intransitive sense "to live on" 始于 15 世纪晚期 同源词：Survived; surviving.

example.en: Only a few species managed to survive the harsh winter conditions that year.
example.zh: 那年只有少数几种物种设法熬过了严酷的冬季条件。

entries.etymology: early 15c. in the legal sense of "one who outlives another," agent noun from survive. Meaning "one who has a knack for pulling through adversity" is attested from 1971. Survivor syndrome is first recorded 1968.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 in the legal 语义 "one who outlives another," agent 名词 源自 survive. 义为 "one who has a knack for pulling through adversity" 见于 1971 年. Survivor syndrome is 首见于 1968 年.

example.en: The only survivor of the shipwreck was rescued after three days at sea.
example.zh: 这场海难唯一的幸存者在海上漂流三天后获救。

entries.definition: n. 可疑分子；嫌疑犯 a. 可疑的 vt. 猜想，怀疑
entries.etymology: early 14c., "suspected of wrongdoing, under suspicion;" mid-14c., "regarded with mistrust, liable to arouse suspicion," from Old French suspect (14c.), from Latin suspectus "suspected, regarded with suspicion or mistrust," past participle of suspicere "look up at, look upward," figuratively "look up to, admire, respect;" also "look at secretly, look askance at," hence, figuratively, "mistrust, regard with suspicion," from assimilated form of sub "up to" (see sub-) + specere "to look at" (see scope (n.1)). The notion behind the word is "look at secretly," hence, "look at distrustfully."
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, "suspected of wrongdoing, under suspicion;" 14 世纪中期, "regarded with mistrust, liable to arouse suspicion," 源自 古法语 suspect (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 suspectus "suspected, regarded with suspicion or mistrust," 为 … 的过去分词 suspicere "look up at, look upward," figuratively "look up to, admire, respect;" also "look at secretly, look askance at," hence, figuratively, "mistrust, regard with suspicion," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 sub "up to" （参见 sub-) + specere "to look at" （参见 scope (n.1)). The notion behind the word is "look at secretly," hence, "look at distrustfully."

example.en: The police strongly suspect that the manager stole the missing funds.
example.zh: 警方强烈怀疑是经理偷走了那笔不见的钱。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "to bar or exclude temporarily from some function or privilege;" also "to set aside (a law, etc.), to cause to cease for a time," from Old French sospendre "remove from office; hang up" (12c.), or directly from Latin suspendere "to hang up, kill by hanging; make uncertain, render doubtful; stay, stop, interrupt, set aside temporarily," from assimilated form of sub "up from under" (see sub-) + pendere "cause to hang, weigh" (see pendant). In English, the literal sense of "to cause to hang by a support from above" is recorded from mid-15c. Related: Suspended; suspending.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "to bar or exclude temporarily from some function or privilege;" also "to set aside (a law, etc.), to cause to cease for a time," 源自 古法语 sospendre "remove from office; hang up" (12 世纪)，或直接源自 拉丁语 suspendere "to hang up, kill by hanging; make uncertain, render doubtful; stay, stop, interrupt, set aside temporarily," 源自 为 … 的同化形式 sub "up from under" （参见 sub-) + pendere "cause to hang, weigh" （参见 pendant). In English, the literal 语义 "to cause to hang by a support from above" 见于 15 世纪中期 同源词：Suspended; suspending.

example.en: The judge decided to suspend the sentence pending a new trial.
example.zh: 法官决定在新审判期间暂缓执行判决。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "act of suspecting; unverified conjecture of wrongdoing; mistrust, distrust," from Anglo-French suspecioun, corresponding to Old French suspicion, sospeçon "mistrust, suspicion" (Modern French soupçon), from Late Latin suspectionem (nominative suspectio) "mistrust, suspicion, fear, awe," noun of state from past participle stem of Latin suspicere "look up at" (see suspect (adj.)).
