entries.etymology: mid-15c., "unlucky," from un- (1) "not" + fortunate (adj.). Infortunate in same sense is older. In late 18c.-early 19c., unfortunate woman was a polite way to say "prostitute." The noun meaning "one who is not fortunate" is recorded from 1630s.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "unlucky," 源自 un- (1) "not" + fortunate （形）. Infortunate in same sense is older. In 18 世纪晚期-19 世纪初, unfortunate woman was a polite way to say "prostitute." The 名词 意为 "one who is not fortunate" 见于 1630 年代.

example.en: It was unfortunate that the concert was cancelled due to rain.
example.zh: 音乐会因雨取消，真是令人遗憾。

entries.etymology: 1540s, "in an unfortunate manner, by ill-fortune," from unfortunate + -ly (2). The original meaning is now rare; the main modern sense of "sad to say, unhappily, unluckily," in parenthetical use, is recorded from 1770s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "in an unfortunate manner, by ill-fortune," 源自 unfortunate + -ly (2). The original 意为 is 今罕用; the main modern 语义 "sad to say, unhappily, unluckily," in parenthetical use, 见于 1770 年代.

example.zh: 很遗憾，音乐会因恶劣天气被取消了。

entries.etymology: 1530s, "of one form," from Middle French uniforme (14c.), from Latin uniformis "having only one form or shape," from uni- "one" (see uni-) + forma "form" (see form (n.)). Related: Uniformly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "of one form," 源自 中古法语 uniforme (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 uniformis "having only one form or shape," 源自 uni- "one" （参见 uni-) + forma "form" （参见 form （名）). 同源词：Uniformly.

example.zh: 该校所有学生均须穿着制服。

entries.etymology: c. 1500, "to make into one," from Middle French unifier (14c.) or directly from Late Latin unificare "make one," from Latin uni- "one" (see uni-) + root of facere "to make" (see factitious). Related: Unified; unifying. Unified (field) theory in physics is recorded from 1935.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "to make into one," 源自 中古法语 unifier (14 世纪) or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 unificare "make one," 源自 拉丁语 uni- "one" （参见 uni-) + root of facere "to make" （参见 factitious). 同源词：Unified; unifying. Unified (field) theory in physics 见于 1935 年.

entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "incapable of being understood," 源自 un- (1) "not" + intelligible. 同源词：Unintelligibly.

definitionLines: n. 结合，组合，联合；协会， 工会，联盟
entries.definition: n. 结合，组合，联合；协会， 工会，联盟
entries.etymology:
early 15c., "action of joining one thing to another," also "agreement, accord," also "state of matrimony," from Anglo-French unioun, Old French union (12c.), from Late Latin unionem (nominative unio) "oneness, unity, a uniting," also in Latin meaning "a single pearl or onion," from unus "one," from PIE *oi-no- "one, unique" (see one).

Sense of "action of uniting into one political body" is attested from 1540s. Meaning "group of people or states" is from 1650s. Short for trade union, it is recorded from 1833. U.S. political sense is attested from 1775; used especially during the Civil War, in reference to the remainder of the United States after the Southern secession.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "action of joining one thing to another," also "agreement, accord," also "state of matrimony," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 unioun, 古法语 union (12 世纪), 源自 晚期拉丁语 unionem (主格 unio) "oneness, unity, a uniting," also in 拉丁语 意为 "a single pearl or onion," 源自 unus "one," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *oi-no- "one, unique" （参见 one). 义为 "action of uniting into one political body" 见于 1540 年代. 义为 "group of people or states" 始于 1650 年代. Short for trade union, it 见于 1833 年. U.S. political sense 见于 1775 年; used 尤指 during the Civil War, in reference to the remainder of the United States after the Southern secession.

example.en: The workers voted to join the trade union.
example.zh: 工人们投票决定加入工会。

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "single, solitary," from Middle French unique (16c.), from Latin unicus "only, single, sole, alone of its kind," from unus "one" (see one). Meaning "forming the only one of its kind" is attested from 1610s; erroneous sense of "remarkable, uncommon" is attested from mid-19c. Related: Uniquely; uniqueness.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "single, solitary," 源自 中古法语 unique (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 unicus "only, single, sole, alone of its kind," 源自 unus "one" （参见 one). 义为 "forming the only one of its kind" 见于 1610 年代; erroneous 语义 "remarkable, uncommon" 见于 19 世纪中期 同源词：Uniquely; uniqueness.

example.en: Each artist has a unique style that no other painter has ever replicated.
example.zh: 每位艺术家都有一种独一无二的风格，从未被其他画家复制过。

definitionLines: v. 统一，结合，合并；联合，团结
entries.definition: v. 统一，结合，合并；联合，团结
entries.etymology: early 15c. (transitive), from Late Latin unitus, past participle of unire "to unite, make into one" (transitive), from Latin unus "one" (see one). Intransitive sense from 1610s. Related: United; uniting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初 (transitive), 源自 晚期拉丁语 unitus, 为 … 的过去分词 unire "to unite, make into one" (transitive), 源自 拉丁语 unus "one" （参见 one). Intransitive sense 源自 1610 年代. 同源词：United; uniting.

example.en: The two clubs decided to unite in order to survive financially.
example.zh: 这两个俱乐部决定合并以在财务上得以生存。

definitionLines: n. 统一，整体；一致，团结，协调
entries.definition: n. 统一，整体；一致，团结，协调
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "state or property of being one," from Anglo-French unite, Old French unite "uniqueness, oneness" (c. 1200), from Latin unitatem (nominative unitas) "oneness, sameness, agreement," from unus "one" (see one).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "state or property of being one," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 unite, 古法语 unite "uniqueness, oneness" (约 1200 年), 源自 拉丁语 unitatem (主格 unitas) "oneness, sameness, agreement," 源自 unus "one" （参见 one).

example.en: The community's unity in the face of crisis helped them recover quickly.
example.zh: 社区在危机面前的团结帮助他们迅速恢复。

definitionLines: a. 宇宙的，全世界的；普通， 一般；通用的，万能的
entries.definition: a. 宇宙的，全世界的；普通， 一般；通用的，万能的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "pertaining to the whole of something specified; occurring everywhere," from Old French universel "general, universal" (12c.), from Latin universalis "of or belonging to all," from universus "all together, whole, entire" (see universe). In mechanics, a universal joint (1670s) is one which allows free movement in any direction. Universal product code is recorded from 1974.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "pertaining to the whole of something specified; occurring everywhere," 源自 古法语 universel "general, universal" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 universalis "of or belonging to all," 源自 universus "all together, whole, entire" （参见 universe). In mechanics, a universal joint (1670 年代) is one which allows free movement in any direction. Universal product code 见于 1974 年.

example.en: The desire to belong is a universal human need across all cultures.
example.zh: 归属感的渴望是跨越所有文化的人类普遍需求。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "the whole world, cosmos, the totality of existing things," from Old French univers (12c.), from Latin universum "all things, everybody, all people, the whole world," noun use of neuter of adjective universus "all together, all in one, whole, entire, relating to all," literally "turned into one," from unus "one" (see one) + versus, past participle of vertere "to turn" (see versus).
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "the whole world, cosmos, the totality of existing things," 源自 古法语 univers (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 universum "all things, everybody, all people, the whole world," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of 形容词 universus "all together, all in one, whole, entire, relating to all," 字面义为 "turned into one," 源自 unus "one" （参见 one) + versus, 为 … 的过去分词 vertere "to turn" （参见 versus).

example.en: Astronomers believe the universe is still expanding after the Big Bang.
example.zh: 天文学家认为，大爆炸之后宇宙仍在不断膨胀。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "institution of higher learning," also "body of persons constituting a university," from Anglo-French université, Old French universite "universality; academic community" (13c.), from Medieval Latin universitatem (nominative universitas), "the whole, aggregate," in Late Latin "corporation, society," from universus "whole, entire" (see universe). In the academic sense, a shortening of universitas magistrorum et scholarium "community of masters and scholars;" superseded studium as the word for this. The Latin word also is the source of Spanish universidad, German universität, Russian universitetŭ, etc.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "institution of higher learning," also "body of persons constituting a university," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 université, 古法语 universite "universality; academic community" (13 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 universitatem (主格 universitas), "the whole, aggregate," in 晚期拉丁语 "corporation, society," 源自 universus "whole, entire" （参见 universe). In the academic sense, a shortening of universitas magistrorum et scholarium "community of masters and scholars;" superseded studium as the word for this. The 拉丁语 word also is the source of 西班牙语 universidad, 德语 universität, 俄语 universitetŭ, etc.

example.en: She was accepted to a prestigious university to study medicine.
example.zh: 她被一所享有盛誉的大学录取，攻读医学专业。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, "strange, unfamiliar" (of persons, places), from un- (1) "not" + past participle of know (v.). Compare Old English ungecnawen. In reference to facts, "not discovered or found out," it attested from early 14c. The noun meaning "unknown person" is recorded from 1590s; the unknown "that which is unknown" is from 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "strange, unfamiliar" (of persons, places), 源自 un- (1) "not" + 为 … 的过去分词 know （动）. 对比 古英语 ungecnawen. In reference to facts, "not discovered or found out," it attested 源自 14 世纪初 The 名词 意为 "unknown person" 见于 1590 年代; the unknown "that which is unknown" 始于 1650 年代.

example.en: The author of the ancient manuscript remains unknown to this day.
example.zh: 这份古代手稿的作者至今仍不为人知。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., earlier onlesse, from (not) on lesse (than) "(not) on a less compelling condition (than);" see less. The first syllable originally on, but the negative connotation and the lack of stress changed it to un-. "Except could once be used as a synonym for unless, but the words have now drawn entirely apart" [Century Dictionary].
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, earlier onlesse, 源自 (not) on lesse (than) "(not) on a less compelling condition (than);" 参见 less. The first syllable 原义为 on, but the negative connotation and the lack of stress changed it to un-. "Except could once be used as a synonym for unless, but the words have now drawn entirely apart" [Century Dictionary].

example.en: You will fail the exam unless you start studying right now.
example.zh: 你如果现在不开始学习，就会不及格。

entries.definition: a.不同的，不相似的 prep. 不像…….和……不同
entries.etymology: c. 1200, "not resembling," from un- (1) "not" + like (adj.). Similar formation in Old English ungelic, Old Frisian unlik, Old Norse ulikr, Middle Danish ulige, German ungleich.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "not resembling," 源自 un- (1) "not" + like （形）. Similar formation in 古英语 ungelic, 古弗里西语 unlik, 古北欧语 ulikr, Middle Danish ulige, 德语 ungleich.

definitionLines: a. 不太可能的；没希望的
entries.definition: a. 不太可能的；没希望的
entries.etymology: late 14c., "not likely to occur," from un- (1) "not" + likely (adj.). Similar formation in Old Norse ulikligr, Middle Danish uligelig. Meaning "not likely to be true" is recorded from 1590s. Related: Unlikeliness; unlikelihood.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "not likely to occur," 源自 un- (1) "not" + likely （形）. Similar formation in 古北欧语 ulikligr, Middle Danish uligelig. 义为 "not likely to be true" 见于 1590 年代. 同源词：Unlikeliness; unlikelihood.

example.en: It is unlikely that she will change her mind given how firmly she stated her position.
example.zh: 鉴于她如此坚定地表明了立场，她改变主意的可能性不大。

definitionLines: a. 不必要的；多余的，无用的
entries.definition: a. 不必要的；多余的，无用的
entries.etymology: 1540s, from un- (1) "not" + necessary (adj.). Related: Unnecessarily.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 源自 un- (1) "not" + necessary （形）. 同源词：Unnecessarily.

definitionLines: a. 使人不愉快的；讨厌的
entries.definition: a. 使人不愉快的；讨厌的
entries.etymology: 1530s, from un- (1) "not" + pleasant (adj.). Related: Unpleasantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 源自 un- (1) "not" + pleasant （形）. 同源词：Unpleasantly.

example.en: The smell from the factory was extremely unpleasant.
example.zh: 工厂里散发出的气味令人极度不适。

entries.etymology: 1520s, in reference to cargo, from un- (2) + load (v.). Figurative sense (in reference to feelings, etc.) is recorded from 1590s. Used in reference to sales of stocks by 1870, hence U.S. colloquial sense "dispose of property the holding of which is risky" (1881). Related: Unloaded; unloading.
entries.etymologyZh: 1520 年代, in reference to cargo, 源自 un- (2) + load （动）. Figurative sense (in reference to feelings, etc.) 见于 1590 年代. Used in reference to sales of stocks 截至 1870 年, hence U.S. 口语 sense "dispose of property the holding of which is risky" (1881 年). 同源词：Unloaded; unloading.

entries.etymology: 1620s, from un- (1) "not" + precedented. In common use from c. 1760.
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 un- (1) "not" + precedented. In common use 源自 约 1760 年.

example.en: The storm caused unprecedented damage to the coastal city.
example.zh: 这场风暴对沿海城市造成了前所未有的破坏。

definitionLines: a. 确实的；毫无疑问的
entries.definition: a. 确实的；毫无疑问的
entries.etymology: c. 1600, from un- (1) "not" + questionable (adj.). Related: Unquestionably.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, 源自 un- (1) "not" + questionable （形）. 同源词：Unquestionably.

definitionLines: prep. /conj. 到••••••为止，在…… 以前；直到……
entries.definition: prep. /conj. 到••••••为止，在…… 以前；直到……
entries.etymology:
c. 1200, from till (prep.). The first element is un- "as far as, up to" (also in  unto), from Old Norse *und "as far as, up to," from Proto-Germanic *und- (source also of Old English oð "up to, as far as," Old Frisian, Old Saxon, Gothic und), from PIE *nti-, from root *ant- "front, forehead" (see ante).

The two syllables have the same meaning. Originally also used of persons and places. As a conjunction from c. 1300. Similar formation in Swedish intill, Danish indtil (northern English and Scottish formerly also had intill/intil "into, in"). The Modern German equivalent, bis (Old High German biaz), is a similar compound, of Old High German bi "by, at, to" and zu "to."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, 源自 till （介）. The first element is un- "as far as, up to" (also in unto), 源自 古北欧语 *und "as far as, up to," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *und- (source also of 古英语 oð "up to, as far as," 古弗里西语, 古撒克逊语, Gothic und), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *nti-, 源自 root *ant- "front, forehead" （参见 ante). The two syllables have the same 意为. Originally also used of persons and places. 作为 conjunction 源自 约 1300 年. Similar formation in Swedish intill, Danish indtil (northern English and 苏格兰语 formerly also had intill/intil "into, in"). The 现代 德语 equivalent, bis (古高地德语 biaz), is a similar 复合词, of 古高地德语 bi "by, at, to" and zu "to."

vi. 除去面纱；显露 业P
ad. 向上；往北；起床，起来；高 昂起来，激动起来；［指从活 动到结束］……完，……光

entries.definition: vt. 揭幕；使公之于众，揭开 vi. 除去面纱；显露 业P ad. 向上；往北；起床，起来；高 昂起来，激动起来；［指从活 动到结束］……完，……光 prep. 向上，向/在高处；沿着， 在…• 那边 a. 向上的
entries.etymology: 1590s, in reference to sight, "to make clear," from un- (2) "opposite of" + veil (v.). Sense of "to display or reveal" (something) is from 1650s. Related: Unveiled; unveiling.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, in reference to sight, "to make clear," 源自 un- (2) "opposite of" + veil （动）. 义为 "to display or reveal" (something) 始于 1650 年代. 同源词：Unveiled; unveiling.

entries.etymology: 1848, "rising;" 1949, "forthcoming," from up (adv.) + coming (see come (v.)). It was a noun in Middle English, meaning "action of ascending" (mid-14c.), also "attack, onslaught" (c. 1300).
entries.etymologyZh: 1848 年, "rising;" 1949 年, "forthcoming," 源自 up （副） + coming （参见 come （动）). It was a 名词 in 中古英语, 意为 "action of ascending" (14 世纪中期), also "attack, onslaught" (约 1300 年).

example.en: Students received an email about the upcoming campus fair next Friday.
example.zh: 学生们收到了一封关于下周五即将举行的校园集市的邮件。

entries.definition: v. 更新，使最新 n. 最新资料，最新版
entries.etymology: 1944, in reference to information, 1952 in reference to persons, from up (adv.) + date (v.1). Related: Updated; updating. The noun is attested from 1967.
entries.etymologyZh: 1944 年, in reference to information, 1952 年 in reference to persons, 源自 up （副） + date (v.1). 同源词：Updated; updating. The 名词 见于 1967 年.

example.en: The software will automatically update itself whenever a new version is available.
example.zh: 只要有新版本，该软件就会自动更新自身。

entries.etymology: also up-grade, 1847, "upward slope," from up (adj.) + grade (n.). The meaning "upgraded version" is recorded from 1980.
entries.etymologyZh: also up-grade, 1847 年, "upward slope," 源自 up （形） + grade （名）. The 意为 "upgraded version" 见于 1980 年.

example.en: The IT team will upgrade all computers to the latest operating system.
example.zh: IT团队将把所有电脑升级到最新操作系统。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "support, sustain," from up (adv.) + hold (v.). Similar formation in Old Frisian upholda, Middle Dutch ophouden, German aufhalten. Meaning "maintain in good condition or repair" is from 1570s. Related: Upheld; upholding.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "support, sustain," 源自 up （副） + hold （动）. Similar formation in 古弗里西语 upholda, Middle 荷兰语 ophouden, 德语 aufhalten. 义为 "maintain in good condition or repair" 始于 1570 年代. 同源词：Upheld; upholding.

example.en: The court ruled to uphold the decision made by the lower court.
example.zh: 法院裁定维持下级法院的裁决。

entries.etymology: early 12c., from Old English uppan (prep.) "on, upon, up to, against," from up (adv.) + on (prep.); probably influenced by Scandinavian sources such as Old Norse upp a.
entries.etymologyZh: 12 世纪初, 源自 古英语 uppan （介） "on, upon, up to, against," 源自 up （副） + on （介）; 可能 influenced by Scandinavian sources such as 古北欧语 upp a.

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, originally comparative of up (adj.). Similar formation in Middle Dutch upper, Dutch opper, Low German upper, Norwegian yppare. Upper hand "advantage" is late 15c., perhaps from wrestling (get the over-hand in the same sense is from early 14c.). Upperclassman is recorded from 1871.

Upper crust is attested from mid-15c. in reference to the top crust of a loaf of bread, 1836 in reference to society. Upper middle class (adj.) is recorded from 1835. Upper ten thousand (1844) was common mid-19c. for "wealthier and more aristocratic part of a large community;" hence uppertendom.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 原义为 comparative of up （形）. Similar formation in Middle 荷兰语 upper, 荷兰语 opper, Low 德语 upper, Norwegian yppare. Upper hand "advantage" is 15 世纪晚期, 或源自 wrestling (get the over-hand in the same sense 始于 14 世纪初). Upperclassman 见于 1871 年. Upper crust 见于 15 世纪中期 in reference to the top crust of a loaf of bread, 1836 年 in reference to society. Upper middle class （形） 见于 1835 年. Upper ten thousand (1844 年) was common 19 世纪中期 for "wealthier and more aristocratic part of a large community;" hence uppertendom.

example.en: The books on the upper shelves are harder to reach.
example.zh: 上层书架上的书更难够到。

definitionLines: a. 直立的，竖立的；正直的， 诚实的
entries.definition: a. 直立的，竖立的；正直的， 诚实的
entries.etymology:
Old English upriht "erect, face-upward;" see up (adv.) + right (adj.1). Similar compounds are found in other Germanic languages (Old Frisian upriucht, Middle Dutch oprecht, Old High German ufreht, German aufrecht, Old Norse uprettr). Figurative sense of "good, honest, adhering to rectitude" is first attested 1520s.

As an adverb, Old English uprihte. As a noun, 1560s in the sense "a vertical front;" c. 1700 as "a vertical timber in framing;" 1742 in the sense "something standing erect." Meaning "an upright piano" is from 1860.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 upriht "erect, face-upward;" 参见 up （副） + right (adj.1). Similar compounds are found in other 日耳曼语 languages (古弗里西语 upriucht, Middle 荷兰语 oprecht, 古高地德语 ufreht, 德语 aufrecht, 古北欧语 uprettr). Figurative 语义 "good, honest, adhering to rectitude" is 最早见于 1520 年代. 作为 副词, 古英语 uprihte. 作名词时, 1560 年代 in the sense "a vertical front;" 约 1700 年 as "a vertical timber in framing;" 1742 年 in the sense "something standing erect." 义为 "an upright piano" 始于 1860 年.

definitionLines: vt.弄翻，打翻；扰乱，打乱， 使不安
entries.definition: vt.弄翻，打翻；扰乱，打乱， 使不安 vi.倾覆
entries.etymology: mid-15c., "to set up, fix," from up (adv.) + set (v.). Similar formation in Middle Dutch opsetten "set up, propose," German aufsetzen. Modern sense of "overturn, capsize" (1803) is that of obsolete overset. In reference to the stomach, from 1834. Meaning "to throw into mental discomposure" is from 1805. Related: Upsetting.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, "to set up, fix," 源自 up （副） + set （动）. Similar formation in Middle 荷兰语 opsetten "set up, propose," 德语 aufsetzen. 现代 语义 "overturn, capsize" (1803 年) is that of 已废 overset. In reference to the stomach, 自 1834 年起. 义为 "to throw into mental discomposure" 始于 1805 年. 同源词：Upsetting.

example.en: The sudden cancellation really upset her carefully arranged weekend plans.
example.zh: 突如其来的取消彻底打乱了她精心安排的周末计划。

definitionLines: a./ad. 颠倒的（地），倒置的 （地）
entries.definition: a./ad. 颠倒的（地），倒置的 （地）
entries.etymology: late 15c., earlier upsadoun (late 14c.), up so down (c. 1300); the so perhaps meaning "as if." As an adjective from 1866.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, earlier upsadoun (14 世纪晚期), up so down (约 1300 年); the so 或许 意为 "as if." 作形容词时 自 1866 年起.

definitionLines: a.时新的，新式的；跟上时代的
entries.definition: a.时新的，新式的；跟上时代的 upward（s） ad. 向上，上升•……以上
entries.etymology: 1840, "right to the present time," from phrase up to date, probably originally from bookkeeping. As an adjective from 1865. Meaning "having the latest facts" is recorded from 1889; that of "having current styles and tastes" is from 1891.
entries.etymologyZh: 1840 年, "right to the present time," 源自 phrase up to date, 可能 原义为 源自 bookkeeping. 作形容词时 自 1865 年起. 义为 "having the latest facts" 见于 1889 年; that of "having current styles and tastes" 始于 1891 年.

entries.etymology:
first planet discovered that was not known in ancient times, named for the god of Heaven, husband of Gaia, the Earth, from Latin Uranus, from Greek Ouranos literally "heaven, the sky;" in Greek cosmology, the god who personifies the heavens, father of the titans.

The planet was discovered and identified as such in 1781 by Sir William Herschel (it had been observed before, but mistaken for a star; in 1690 John Flamsteed cataloged it as 34 Tauri); Herschel proposed calling it Georgium Sidus, literally "George's Star," in honour of his patron, King George III of England.

The planet was known in English in 1780s as the Georgian Planet; French astronomers began calling Herschel, and ultimately German astronomer Johann Bode proposed Uranus as in conformity with other planet names. However, the name didn't come into common usage until c. 1850.
entries.etymologyZh: first planet discovered that was not known in ancient times, named for the god of Heaven, husband of Gaia, the Earth, 源自 拉丁语 Uranus, 源自 希腊语 Ouranos 字面义为 "heaven, the sky;" in 希腊语 cosmology, the god who personifies the heavens, father of the titans. The planet was discovered and identified as such 于 1781 年 by Sir William Herschel (it had been observed before, but mistaken for a star; 于 1690 年 John Flamsteed cataloged it as 34 Tauri); Herschel proposed calling it Georgium Sidus, 字面义为 "George's Star," in honour of his patron, King George III of England. The planet was known in English in 1780 年代 as the Georgian Planet; 法语 astronomers began calling Herschel, and ultimately 德语 astronomer Johann Bode proposed Uranus as in conformity with other planet names. However, the name didn't come into common usage until 约 1850 年.

entries.etymology: masc. proper name, from Latin urbanus "refined, courteous," literally "of a city" (see urban (adj.)).
entries.etymologyZh: masc. proper name, 源自 拉丁语 urbanus "refined, courteous," 字面义为 "of a city" （参见 urban （形）).

example.en: Many urban areas face serious traffic congestion during peak hours.
example.zh: 许多城市地区在高峰期面临严重的交通拥堵。

definitionLines: v./n.强烈希望，竭力主张/鼓 励，促进
entries.definition: v./n.强烈希望，竭力主张/鼓 励，促进
entries.etymology: 1550s, from Latin urgere "to press hard, push forward, force, drive, compel, stimulate," from PIE root *wreg- "to push, shove, drive" (source also of Lithuanian verziu "tie, fasten, squeeze," vargas "need, distress," vergas "slave;" Old Church Slavonic vragu "enemy;" Gothic wrikan "persecute," Old English wrecan "drive, hunt, pursue"). Related: Urged; urging.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, 源自 拉丁语 urgere "to press hard, push forward, force, drive, compel, stimulate," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *wreg- "to push, shove, drive" (source also of Lithuanian verziu "tie, fasten, squeeze," vargas "need, distress," vergas "slave;" Old Church Slavonic vragu "enemy;" Gothic wrikan "persecute," 古英语 wrecan "drive, hunt, pursue"). 同源词：Urged; urging.

example.en: Health officials strongly urge the public to get vaccinated before the flu season.
example.zh: 卫生官员强烈敦促公众在流感季节前接种疫苗。

definitionLines: n. 催促；紧急；紧急的事
entries.definition: n. 催促；紧急；紧急的事
entries.etymology: 1530s, probably from urgent + -cy.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, 可能 源自 urgent + -cy.

example.en: The doctor conveyed a sense of urgency when asking for the test results.
example.zh: 医生在索要检验结果时传达出一种紧迫感。

entries.definition: a. 紧迫的；催促的 uS 一 pron.［宾格］我们
entries.etymology: mid-15c., from Middle French urgent "pressing, impelling" (14c.), from Latin urgentem (nominative urgens), present participle of urgere "to press hard, urge" (see urge (v.)). Related: Urgently.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, 源自 中古法语 urgent "pressing, impelling" (14 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 urgentem (主格 urgens), 为 … 的现在分词 urgere "to press hard, urge" （参见 urge （动）). 同源词：Urgently.

example.en: There is an urgent need for medical supplies in the disaster zone.
example.zh: 灾区急需医疗物资。

definitionLines: n. 用法；使用；惯用法，习语
entries.definition: n. 用法；使用；惯用法，习语
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "established practice, custom," from Anglo-French and Old French usage "custom, habit, experience; taxes levied," from us, from Latin usus "use, custom" (see use (v.)). From late 14c. as "service, use, act of using something."
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "established practice, custom," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 and 古法语 usage "custom, habit, experience; taxes levied," 源自 us, 源自 拉丁语 usus "use, custom" （参见 use （动）). From 14 世纪晚期 as "service, use, act of using something."

example.en: The dictionary explains both the meaning and the usage of each word.
example.zh: 这本词典解释了每个词的含义和用法。

definitionLines: n. 使用，应用；用法，用途； 益处，用处
entries.definition: vt. 用，使用，运用；消耗 n. 使用，应用；用法，用途； 益处，用处
entries.etymology:
Old English wis "learned, sagacious, cunning; sane; prudent, discreet; experienced; having the power of discerning and judging rightly," from Proto-Germanic *wissaz (source also of Old Saxon, Old Frisian wis, Old Norse viss, Dutch wijs, German weise "wise"), from past participle adjective *wittos of PIE root *weid- "to see," hence "to know" (see vision). Modern slang meaning "aware, cunning" first attested 1896. Related to the source of Old English witan "to know, wit."

Wise man was in Old English. Wise guy is attested from 1896, American English; wise-ass (n.) by 1966, American English (probably a literal sense is intended by the phrase in the 1607 comedy "Westward Hoe" by Dekker and Webster). Wisenheimer, with mock German or Yiddish surname suffix, first recorded 1904.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 wis "learned, sagacious, cunning; sane; prudent, discreet; experienced; having the power of discerning and judging rightly," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *wissaz (source also of 古撒克逊语, 古弗里西语 wis, 古北欧语 viss, 荷兰语 wijs, 德语 weise "wise"), 源自 past participle 形容词 *wittos of 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *weid- "to see," hence "to know" （参见 vision). 现代 俚语 意为 "aware, cunning" 最早见于 1896 年. Related to the source of 古英语 witan "to know, wit." Wise man was in 古英语. Wise guy 见于 1896 年, American English; wise-ass （名） 截至 1966 年, American English (可能 a literal sense is intended by the phrase in the 1607 年 comedy "Westward Hoe" by Dekker and Webster). Wisenheimer, with mock 德语 or Yiddish surname suffix, 首见于 1904 年.

example.en: Years later he realized how wise his grandmother had been to invest patiently rather than chase quick profits.
example.zh: 多年以后他才意识到,祖母当年耐心投资、而不去追逐快钱,是多么明智。

definitionLines: a.旧的，用旧了的；（to）习惯 于……；过去惯常，过去经常
entries.definition: a.旧的，用旧了的；（to）习惯 于……；过去惯常，过去经常
entries.etymology: "second-hand," 1590s, past participle adjective from use (v.). To be used to "accustomed, familiar" is recorded by late 14c. Verbal phrase used to "formerly did or was" (as in I used to love her) represents a construction attested from c. 1300, and common from c. 1400, from use (intransitive) "be accustomed, practice customarily," but now surviving only in past tense form. The pronunciation is affected by the t- of to. Used-to-be (n.) "one who has outlived his fame" is from 1853.
entries.etymologyZh: "second-hand," 1590 年代, past participle 形容词 源自 use （动）. To be used to "accustomed, familiar" is recorded by 14 世纪晚期 Verbal phrase used to "formerly did or was" (as in I used to love her) represents a construction attested 源自 约 1300 年, and common 源自 约 1400 年, 源自 use (intransitive) "be accustomed, practice customarily," but 现在 surviving only in past tense form. The pronunciation is affected by the t- of to. Used-to-be （名） "one who has outlived his fame" 始于 1853 年.

definitionLines: a. 有用的，实用的；有益的， 有帮助的
entries.definition: a. 有用的，实用的；有益的， 有帮助的
entries.etymology: 1590s, from use (n.) + -full. Related: Usefully; usefulness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 use （名） + -full. 同源词：Usefully; usefulness.

example.en: This ointment is useful for treating minor cuts and burns.
example.zh: 这种软膏对治疗轻微割伤和烫伤非常有用。

entries.etymology: 1590s, from use (n.) + -less. Related: Uselessly; uselessness.
entries.etymologyZh: 1590 年代, 源自 use （名） + -less. 同源词：Uselessly; uselessness.

definitionLines: vi.（in） 引导，招待；迎接；开辟
entries.definition: vi.（in） 引导，招待；迎接；开辟 n. 引座员，带位员
entries.etymology: late 13c., "servant who has charge of doors and admits people to a chamber, hall, etc.," from Anglo-French usser (12c.), Old French ussier, uissier "porter, doorman," from Vulgar Latin *ustiarius "doorkeeper," variant of Latin ostiarius "door-keeper," from ostium "door, entrance," from os "mouth," from PIE *os- "mouth" (see oral). Fem. form usherette is attested from 1913, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, "servant who has charge of doors and admits people to a chamber, hall, etc.," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 usser (12 世纪), 古法语 ussier, uissier "porter, doorman," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *ustiarius "doorkeeper," 为 … 的变体 拉丁语 ostiarius "door-keeper," 源自 ostium "door, entrance," 源自 os "mouth," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *os- "mouth" （参见 oral). Fem. form usherette 见于 1913 年, American English.

example.en: A staff member ushered the guests into the main hall.
example.zh: 一名工作人员引导客人进入主厅。

entries.etymology: late 15c., from usual + -ly (2).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, 源自 usual + -ly (2).

example.en: She usually takes a short walk right after dinner to help digestion.
example.zh: 她通常在晚饭后立刻散一小段步以促进消化。

definitionLines: n. 效用；实用；功用；公共设施
entries.definition: n. 效用；实用；功用；公共设施
entries.etymology: late 14c., "fact of being useful," from Old French utilite "usefulness" (13c., Modern French + utilité), earlier utilitet (12c.), from Latin utilitatem (nominative utilitas) "usefulness, serviceableness, profit," from utilis "usable," from uti "make use of, profit by, take advantage of" (see use (v.)). Meaning "a useful thing" is from late 15c. As a shortened form of public utility it is recorded from 1930.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "fact of being useful," 源自 古法语 utilite "usefulness" (13 世纪, 现代法语 + utilité), earlier utilitet (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 utilitatem (主格 utilitas) "usefulness, serviceableness, profit," 源自 utilis "usable," 源自 uti "make use of, profit by, take advantage of" （参见 use （动）). 义为 "a useful thing" 始于 15 世纪晚期 作为 shortened form of public utility it 见于 1930 年.

example.en: The utility of this multipurpose tool is evident in how little space it takes up.
example.zh: 这款多用途工具的实用价值体现在它占用空间极小。

entries.etymology: 1794, from French utiliser, from Italian utilizzare, from utile "usable," from Latin utilis "usable," from uti "make use of, profit by, take advantage of" (see use (v.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 1794 年, 源自 法语 utiliser, 源自 意大利语 utilizzare, 源自 utile "usable," 源自 拉丁语 utilis "usable," 源自 uti "make use of, profit by, take advantage of" （参见 use （动）).

example.en: Schools should utilize technology to make lessons more engaging for students.
example.zh: 学校应该充分利用技术使课程对学生更具吸引力。

entries.definition: n. 极限；最大可能 a.极度的
entries.etymology: Old English utmest (Anglian) "outermost," double superlative of ut "out" (see out (adv.)) + -most. Meaning "being of the greatest or highest degree" is from early 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 utmest (Anglian) "outermost," double superlative of ut "out" （参见 out （副）) + -most. 义为 "being of the greatest or highest degree" 始于 14 世纪初

definitionLines: n. 乌托邦（理想中最美好的社 会）；理想国
entries.definition: n. 乌托邦（理想中最美好的社 会）；理想国
entries.etymology: 1551, from Modern Latin Utopia, literally "nowhere," coined by Thomas More (and used as title of his book, 1516, about an imaginary island enjoying the utmost perfection in legal, social, and political systems), from Greek ou "not" + topos "place" (see topos). Extended to any perfect place by 1610s. Commonly, but incorrectly, taken as from Greek eu- "good" (see eu-) an error reinforced by the introduction of dystopia.
entries.etymologyZh: 1551 年, 源自 现代 拉丁语 Utopia, 字面义为 "nowhere," coined by Thomas More (and used as title of his book, 1516 年, about an imaginary island enjoying the utmost perfection in legal, social, and political systems), 源自 希腊语 ou "not" + topos "place" （参见 topos). Extended to any perfect place by 1610 年代. Commonly, but incorrectly, taken as 源自 希腊语 eu- "good" （参见 eu-) an error reinforced by the introduction of dystopia.

definitionLines: vt. 说，发出（声音）；说出， 说明，表达
entries.definition: a.完全的，彻底的，绝对的 vt. 说，发出（声音）；说出， 说明，表达 V
entries.etymology: Old English utera, uterra, "outer, exterior, external,"  from Proto-Germanic *utizon (source also of Old Norse utar, Old Frisian uttra, Middle Dutch utere, Dutch uiter-, Old High German uzar, German äußer "outer"), comparative adjective from ut (see out (adv.)). Meaning "complete, total" (i.e. "going to the utmost point") is from early 15c.
entries.etymologyZh: 古英语 utera, uterra, "outer, exterior, external," 源自 原始日耳曼语 *utizon (source also of 古北欧语 utar, 古弗里西语 uttra, Middle 荷兰语 utere, 荷兰语 uiter-, 古高地德语 uzar, 德语 äußer "outer"), comparative 形容词 源自 ut （参见 out （副）). 义为 "complete, total" (i.e. "going to the utmost point") 始于 15 世纪初

entries.etymology: 1570s, "a vacating;" c. 1600, "state of being vacant," from Late Latin vacantia, from Latin vacans "empty, unoccupied," present participle of vacare "be empty" (see vain). From 1690s as "a vacant office or post;" meaning "available room at a hotel" is recorded from 1953. Related: Vacance (1530s); vacancies.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "a vacating;" 约 1600 年, "state of being vacant," 源自 晚期拉丁语 vacantia, 源自 拉丁语 vacans "empty, unoccupied," 为 … 的现在分词 vacare "be empty" （参见 vain). From 1690 年代 as "a vacant office or post;" 意为 "available room at a hotel" 见于 1953 年. 同源词：Vacance (1530 年代); vacancies.

definitionLines: a. 空的；（职位）空缺的；茫然的
entries.definition: a. 空的；（职位）空缺的；茫然的
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "not filled, held, or occupied," from Old French vacant "idle, unoccupied" (of an office, etc.), from Latin vacantem (nominative vacans), "empty, unoccupied," present participle of vacare "to be empty" (see vain). Meaning "characterized by absence of mental occupation" is from 1570s. Related: Vacantly.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "not filled, held, or occupied," 源自 古法语 vacant "idle, unoccupied" (of an office, etc.), 源自 拉丁语 vacantem (主格 vacans), "empty, unoccupied," 为 … 的现在分词 vacare "to be empty" （参见 vain). 义为 "characterized by absence of mental occupation" 始于 1570 年代. 同源词：Vacantly.

definitionLines: n. 休假，假期；空出，腾出
entries.definition: n. 休假，假期；空出，腾出
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "freedom from obligations, leisure, release" (from some activity or occupation), from Old French vacacion "vacancy, vacant position" (14c.) and directly from Latin vacationem (nominative vacatio) "leisure, freedom, exemption, a being free from duty, immunity earned by service," noun of state from past participle stem of vacare "be empty, free, or at leisure" (see vain).

Meanings "state of being unoccupied," "process of vacating" in English are early 15c. Meaning "formal suspension of activity, time in which there is an intermission of usual employment" (in reference to schools, courts, etc.) is recorded from mid-15c. As the U.S. equivalent of what in Britain is called a holiday, it is attested from 1878.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "freedom from obligations, leisure, release" (源自 some activity or occupation), 源自 古法语 vacacion "vacancy, vacant position" (14 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 vacationem (主格 vacatio) "leisure, freedom, exemption, a being free from duty, immunity earned by service," 名词 of state 源自 past participle stem of vacare "be empty, free, or at leisure" （参见 vain). Meanings "state of being unoccupied," "process of vacating" in English are 15 世纪初 义为 "formal suspension of activity, time in which there is an intermission of usual employment" (in reference to schools, courts, etc.) 见于 15 世纪中期 As the U.S. equivalent of what in Britain is called a holiday, it 见于 1878 年.

example.en: She spent her annual vacation volunteering at an orphanage in Nepal.
example.zh: 她把年假用于在尼泊尔一家孤儿院做志愿者。

entries.etymology: 1800, used by British physician Edward Jenner (1749-1823) for the technique he devised of preventing smallpox by injecting people with the cowpox virus (variolae vaccinae), from vaccine (adj.) "pertaining to cows, from cows" (1798), from Latin vaccinus "from cows," from vacca "cow" (Latin bos "cow" being originally "ox," "a loan word from a rural dialect" according to Buck, who cites Umbrian bue). "The use of the term for diseases other than smallpox is due to Pasteur" [OED].
entries.etymologyZh: 1800 年, used by British physician Edward Jenner (1749 年-1823 年) for the technique he devised of preventing smallpox by injecting people with the cowpox virus (variolae vaccinae), 源自 vaccine （形） "pertaining to cows, from cows" (1798 年), 源自 拉丁语 vaccinus "from cows," 源自 vacca "cow" (拉丁语 bos "cow" being 原义为 "ox," "a loan word from a rural dialect" according to Buck, who cites Umbrian bue). "The use of the term for diseases other than smallpox is due to Pasteur" [OED].

entries.definition: n. 疫苗；牛痘苗 a. 疫苗的；牛痘的
entries.etymology: "matter used in vaccination," 1846, from French vaccin, noun use of adjective, from Latin vaccina, fem. of vaccinus "pertaining to a cow" (see vaccination). Related: Vaccinal; vaccinic.
entries.etymologyZh: "matter used in vaccination," 1846 年, 源自 法语 vaccin, 为 … 的名词用法 形容词, 源自 拉丁语 vaccina, fem. of vaccinus "pertaining to a cow" （参见 vaccination). 同源词：Vaccinal; vaccinic.

example.en: Health officials urged everyone to get the vaccine before the flu season began.
example.zh: 卫生官员敦促所有人在流感季节开始前接种疫苗。

entries.etymology: 1540s, "emptiness of space," from Latin vacuum "an empty space, vacant place, a void," noun use of neuter of vacuus "empty, unoccupied, devoid of," figuratively "free, unoccupied," related to vacare "be empty" (see vain). Properly a loan-translation of Greek kenon, literally "that which is empty." Meaning "a space emptied of air" is attested from 1650s. Vacuum tube "glass thermionic device" is attested from 1859. Vacuum cleaner is from 1903; shortened form vacuum (n.) first recorded 1910.
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, "emptiness of space," 源自 拉丁语 vacuum "an empty space, vacant place, a void," 为 … 的名词用法 neuter of vacuus "empty, unoccupied, devoid of," figuratively "free, unoccupied," related to vacare "be empty" （参见 vain). Properly a loan-translation of 希腊语 kenon, 字面义为 "that which is empty." 义为 "a space emptied of air" 见于 1650 年代. Vacuum tube "glass thermionic device" 见于 1859 年. Vacuum cleaner 始于 1903 年; shortened form vacuum （名） 首见于 1910 年.

example.en: The engineers created a vacuum inside the sealed chamber.
example.zh: 工程师在密封腔内制造了真空状态。

entries.etymology: "uncertain as to specifics," 1540s, from Middle French vague "empty, vacant; wild, uncultivated; wandering" (13c.), from Latin vagus "strolling, wandering, rambling," figuratively "vacillating, uncertain," of unknown origin. Related: Vagueness.
entries.etymologyZh: "uncertain as to specifics," 1540 年代, 源自 中古法语 vague "empty, vacant; wild, uncultivated; wandering" (13 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 vagus "strolling, wandering, rambling," figuratively "vacillating, uncertain," 来源不详. 同源词：Vagueness.

example.en: His answer was so vague that no one understood what he meant.
example.zh: 他的回答如此含糊，以至于没有人明白他的意思。

entries.etymology:
c. 1300, "devoid of real value, idle, unprofitable," from Old French vain, vein "worthless, void, invalid, feeble; conceited" (12c.), from Latin vanus "empty, void," figuratively "idle, fruitless," from PIE *wa-no-, from root *eue- "to leave, abandon, give out" (source also of Old English wanian "to lessen," wan "deficient;" Old Norse vanta "to lack;" Latin vacare "to be empty," vastus "empty, waste;" Avestan va- "lack," Persian vang "empty, poor;" Sanskrit una- "deficient," Armenian unain "empty").

Meaning "conceited, elated with a high opinion of oneself" first recorded 1690s in English; earlier "silly, idle, foolish" (late 14c.). Phrase in vain "to no effect" (c. 1300, after Latin in vanum) preserves the original sense. Related: Vainly; vainness. Compare also vainglory.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "devoid of real value, idle, unprofitable," 源自 古法语 vain, vein "worthless, void, invalid, feeble; conceited" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 vanus "empty, void," figuratively "idle, fruitless," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wa-no-, 源自 root *eue- "to leave, abandon, give out" (source also of 古英语 wanian "to lessen," wan "deficient;" 古北欧语 vanta "to lack;" 拉丁语 vacare "to be empty," vastus "empty, waste;" Avestan va- "lack," 波斯语 vang "empty, poor;" 梵语 una- "deficient," Armenian unain "empty"). 义为 "conceited, elated with a high opinion of oneself" 首见于 1690 年代 in English; earlier "silly, idle, foolish" (14 世纪晚期). Phrase in vain "to no effect" (约 1300 年, after 拉丁语 in vanum) preserves the original sense. 同源词：Vainly; vainness. 对比 also vainglory.

definitionLines: a. 有效的；有根据的；正当的； 正确的
entries.definition: a. 有效的；有根据的；正当的； 正确的
entries.etymology: 1570s, "having force in law, legally binding," from Middle French valide (16c.), from Latin validus "strong, effective, powerful, active," from valere "be strong" (see valiant). The meaning "sufficiently supported by facts or authority, well-grounded" is first recorded 1640s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "having force in law, legally binding," 源自 中古法语 valide (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 validus "strong, effective, powerful, active," 源自 valere "be strong" （参见 valiant). The 意为 "sufficiently supported by facts or authority, well-grounded" is 首见于 1640 年代.

example.en: Your passport must be valid for at least six months before you can apply for the visa.
example.zh: 在申请签证之前，您的护照必须至少有六个月的有效期。

entries.etymology: 1540s, from Middle French validité or directly from Late Latin validitatem (nominative validitas) "strength," from Latin validus (see valid).
entries.etymologyZh: 1540 年代, 源自 中古法语 validité or 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 validitatem (主格 validitas) "strength," 源自 拉丁语 validus （参见 valid).

example.en: Critics questioned the validity of the experiment due to its small sample size.
example.zh: 批评者因样本量太小而质疑该实验的有效性。

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Anglo-French valey, Old French valee "a valley" (12c.), from Vulgar Latin *vallata, from Latin vallis "valley," of unknown origin. Valley Girl (in reference to San Fernando Valley of California) was popularized 1982 in song by Frank Zappa and his daughter. Valley of Death (Psalm xxiii:4) was rendered in Middle English as Helldale (mid-13c.).
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 盎格鲁-法语 valey, 古法语 valee "a valley" (12 世纪), 源自 通俗拉丁语 *vallata, 源自 拉丁语 vallis "valley," 来源不详. Valley Girl (in reference to San Fernando Valley of California) was popularized 1982 年 in song by Frank Zappa and his daughter. Valley of Death (Psalm xxiii:4) was rendered in 中古英语 as Helldale (13 世纪中期).

example.en: The river flows quietly through a narrow valley surrounded by steep cliffs.
example.zh: 这条河静静地流经一个被陡峭悬崖环绕的狭窄山谷。

entries.definition: a. 有价值的，贵重的 n.（pl.）贵重物品，财宝
entries.etymology: "of great value or price," 1580s, from value (v.) + -able. As a noun, "a valuable thing," from 1775 (in modern use often in plural). Related: Valuably.
entries.etymologyZh: "of great value or price," 1580 年代, 源自 value （动） + -able. 作名词时, "a valuable thing," 自 1775 年起 (in modern use 常 in plural). 同源词：Valuably.

example.en: Her nursing expertise proved valuable in stabilizing the injured climber.
example.zh: 她的护理专业知识在稳定受伤登山者状态方面被证明极为宝贵。

definitionLines: n. 价值，实用性，重要性
vt. 评价，估计；尊重，重视
entries.definition: n. 价值，实用性，重要性 vt. 评价，估计；尊重，重视
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "price equal to the intrinsic worth of a thing;" late 14c., "degree to which something is useful or estimable," from Old French value "worth, price, moral worth; standing, reputation" (13c.), noun use of fem. past participle of valoir "be worth," from Latin valere "be strong, be well; be of value, be worth" (see valiant). The meaning "social principle" is attested from 1918, supposedly borrowed from the language of painting. Value judgment (1889) is a loan-translation of German Werturteil.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "price equal to the intrinsic worth of a thing;" 14 世纪晚期, "degree to which something is useful or estimable," 源自 古法语 value "worth, price, moral worth; standing, reputation" (13 世纪), 为 … 的名词用法 fem. 为 … 的过去分词 valoir "be worth," 源自 拉丁语 valere "be strong, be well; be of value, be worth" （参见 valiant). The 意为 "social principle" 见于 1918 年, supposedly 借自 the language of painting. Value judgment (1889 年) is a loan-translation of 德语 Werturteil.

example.en: The antique dealer valued the old painting at over ten thousand dollars.
example.zh: 古董商将这幅旧画估值超过一万美元。

example.en: They rented a van large enough to carry all the bedroom furniture in one trip.
example.zh: 他们租了一辆足够大的厢式货车，一次就能运完所有卧室家具。

definitionLines: vi. 消失，消散；消逝，灭绝
entries.definition: vi. 消失，消散；消逝，灭绝 vapo（u）r n. 蒸汽，雾气
entries.etymology: "disappear quickly," c. 1300, from shortened form of esvaniss-, stem of Old French esvanir "disappear; cause to disappear," from Vulgar Latin *exvanire, from Latin evanescere "disappear, pass away, die out," from ex- "out" (see ex-) + vanescere "vanish," inchoative verb from vanus "empty" (see vain). Related: Vanished; vanishing; vanishingly. Vanishing point in perspective drawing is recorded from 1797.
entries.etymologyZh: "disappear quickly," 约 1300 年, 源自 shortened form of esvaniss-, stem of 古法语 esvanir "disappear; cause to disappear," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *exvanire, 源自 拉丁语 evanescere "disappear, pass away, die out," 源自 ex- "out" （参见 ex-) + vanescere "vanish," inchoative 动词 源自 vanus "empty" （参见 vain). 同源词：Vanished; vanishing; vanishingly. Vanishing point in perspective drawing 见于 1797 年.

example.en: The morning fog began to vanish as the sun rose higher.
example.zh: 随着太阳升高，早晨的雾气开始消散。

definitionLines: a. 可变的，不定的，易变的
entries.definition: a. 可变的，不定的，易变的
entries.etymology: late 14c., of persons, "apt to change, fickle," from Old French variable "various, changeable, fickle," from Late Latin variabilis "changeable," from variare "to change" (see vary). Of weather, seasons, etc., attested from late 15c.; of stars, from 1788.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, of persons, "apt to change, fickle," 源自 古法语 variable "various, changeable, fickle," 源自 晚期拉丁语 variabilis "changeable," 源自 variare "to change" （参见 vary). Of weather, seasons, etc., attested 源自 15 世纪晚期; of stars, 自 1788 年起.

example.en: Weather conditions in the mountains can be extremely variable in spring.
example.zh: 山区春季的天气状况可能极为多变。

definitionLines: n. 变化，变动；变种，变异
entries.definition: n. 变化，变动；变种，变异
entries.etymology: late 14c., "difference, divergence," from Old French variacion "variety, diversity" and directly from Latin variationem (nominative variatio) "a difference, variation, change," from past participle stem of variare "to change" (see vary). The musical sense is attested from 1801. Related: Variational.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "difference, divergence," 源自 古法语 variacion "variety, diversity" and 直接源自 拉丁语 variationem (主格 variatio) "a difference, variation, change," 源自 past participle stem of variare "to change" （参见 vary). The musical sense 见于 1801 年. 同源词：Variational.

example.en: Scientists recorded significant variation in Arctic ice thickness over decades.
example.zh: 科学家记录了数十年间北极冰层厚度的显著变化。

definitionLines: n. 多样性，变化；变种，品种； 种类，种种
entries.definition: n. 多样性，变化；变种，品种； 种类，种种
entries.etymology: 1530s, "change of fortunes," from Middle French variété and directly from Latin varietatem (nominative varietas) "difference, diversity; a kind, variety, species, sort," from varius "various" (see vary). Meaning diversity, absence of monotony" is from 1540s; that of "collection of different things" is from 1550s; sense of "something different from others" is from 1610s. In reference to music hall or theatrical performances of a mixed nature, first recorded 1868, American English.
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, "change of fortunes," 源自 中古法语 variété and 直接源自 拉丁语 varietatem (主格 varietas) "difference, diversity; a kind, variety, species, sort," 源自 varius "various" （参见 vary). 义为 diversity, absence of monotony" is from 1540s; that of "collection of different things" is from 1550s; sense of "something different 源自 others" 始于 1610 年代. In reference to music hall or theatrical performances of a mixed nature, 首见于 1868 年, American English.

example.en: The restaurant offers a wide variety of dishes from around the world.
example.zh: 这家餐厅提供来自世界各地的各种各样菜肴。

definitionLines: a. 各种各样的，不同的；多方面 的，多种的
entries.definition: a. 各种各样的，不同的；多方面 的，多种的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "characterized by variety," from Middle French varieux and directly from Latin varius "changing, different, diverse" (see vary). Meaning "different from one another, having a diversity of features" is recorded from 1630s. Related: Variously.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "characterized by variety," 源自 中古法语 varieux and 直接源自 拉丁语 varius "changing, different, diverse" （参见 vary). 义为 "different from one another, having a diversity of features" 见于 1630 年代. 同源词：Variously.

example.en: The charity accepts donations in various forms, such as cash, food, and clothing.
example.zh: 该慈善机构接受现金、食品和衣物等各种形式的捐赠。

entries.etymology: mid-14c. (transitive); late 14c. (intransitive), from Old French variier "be changed, go astray; change, alter, transform" and directly from Latin variare "change, alter, make different," from varius "varied, different, spotted;" perhaps related to varus "bent, crooked, knock-kneed," and varix "varicose vein," from a PIE root *wer- (1) "high raised spot or other bodily infirmity" (source also of Old English wearte "wart," Swedish varbulde "pus swelling," Latin verruca "wart"). Related: Varied; varying.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪中期 (transitive); 14 世纪晚期 (intransitive), 源自 古法语 variier "be changed, go astray; change, alter, transform" and 直接源自 拉丁语 variare "change, alter, make different," 源自 varius "varied, different, spotted;" 或许 related to varus "bent, crooked, knock-kneed," and varix "varicose vein," 源自 a 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *wer- (1) "high raised spot or other bodily infirmity" (source also of 古英语 wearte "wart," Swedish varbulde "pus swelling," 拉丁语 verruca "wart"). 同源词：Varied; varying.

example.en: Prices of vegetables vary greatly depending on the season.
example.zh: 蔬菜价格因季节不同而变化很大。

definitionLines: a. 巨大的，广阔的；大量的， 巨大的；非常的
entries.definition: a. 巨大的，广阔的；大量的， 巨大的；非常的
entries.etymology: 1570s, "being of great extent or size," from Middle French vaste, from Latin vastus "immense, extensive, huge," also "desolate, unoccupied, empty." The two meanings probably originally attached to two separate words, one with a long -a- one with a short -a-, that merged in early Latin (see waste (v.)). Meaning "very great in quantity or number" is from 1630s; that of "very great in degree" is from 1670s. Very popular early 18c. as an intensifier. Related: Vastly; vastness; vasty.
entries.etymologyZh: 1570 年代, "being of great extent or size," 源自 中古法语 vaste, 源自 拉丁语 vastus "immense, extensive, huge," also "desolate, unoccupied, empty." The two meanings 可能 原义为 attached to two separate words, one with a long -a- one with a short -a-, that merged in early 拉丁语 （参见 waste （动）). 义为 "very great in quantity or number" 始于 1630 年代; that of "very great in degree" 始于 1670 年代. Very popular 18 世纪初 作为 intensifier. 同源词：Vastly; vastness; vasty.

example.en: The explorer stood before a vast desert that stretched endlessly to the horizon.
example.zh: 探险家站在一片无边无际延伸至地平线的广阔沙漠前。

entries.etymology: early 15c., "capable of life or growth; growing, vigorous;" also "neither animal nor mineral, of the plant kingdom, living and growing as a plant," from Old French vegetable "living, fit to live," and directly from Medieval Latin vegetabilis "growing, flourishing," from Late Latin vegetabilis "animating, enlivening," from Latin vegetare "to enliven," from vegetus "vigorous, enlivened, active, sprightly," from vegere "to be alive, active, to quicken," from PIE *weg- (2) "be strong, lively," source of watch (v.), vigor, velocity, and possibly witch (see wake (v.)). The meaning "resembling that of a vegetable, dull, uneventful; having life such as a plant has" is attested from 1854 (see vegetable (n.)).
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "capable of life or growth; growing, vigorous;" also "neither animal nor mineral, of the plant kingdom, living and growing as a plant," 源自 古法语 vegetable "living, fit to live," and 直接源自 中古拉丁语 vegetabilis "growing, flourishing," 源自 晚期拉丁语 vegetabilis "animating, enlivening," 源自 拉丁语 vegetare "to enliven," 源自 vegetus "vigorous, enlivened, active, sprightly," 源自 vegere "to be alive, active, to quicken," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *weg- (2) "be strong, lively," source of watch （动）, vigor, velocity, and possibly witch （参见 wake （动）). The 意为 "resembling that of a vegetable, dull, uneventful; having life such as a plant has" 见于 1854 年 （参见 vegetable （名）).

example.en: The doctor advised him to eat more vegetable and less red meat.
example.zh: 医生建议他多吃蔬菜，少吃红肉。

entries.etymology: 1610s, "a medium through which a drug or medicine is administered," also "any means of conveying or transmitting," from French véhicule (16c.), from Latin vehiculum "means of transport, vehicle, carriage, conveyance," from vehere "to bear, carry, convey," from PIE *wegh- "to go, transport in a vehicle" (source also of Old English wegan "to carry;" Old Norse vegr, Old High German weg "way;" Middle Dutch wagen "wagon;" see wagon). Sense of "cart or other conveyance" in English first recorded 1650s.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代, "a medium through which a drug or medicine is administered," also "any means of conveying or transmitting," 源自 法语 véhicule (16 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 vehiculum "means of transport, vehicle, carriage, conveyance," 源自 vehere "to bear, carry, convey," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wegh- "to go, transport in a vehicle" (source also of 古英语 wegan "to carry;" 古北欧语 vegr, 古高地德语 weg "way;" Middle 荷兰语 wagen "wagon;" 参见 wagon). 义为 "cart or other conveyance" in English 首见于 1650 年代.

example.en: The vehicle broke down on the highway, blocking traffic for hours.
example.zh: 那辆车在高速公路上抛锚，堵了好几个小时的车。

entries.etymology: c. 1200, "nun's head covering," from Anglo-French and Old North French veil (12c., Modern French voile) "a head-covering," also "a sail, a curtain," from Latin vela, plural of velum "sail, curtain, covering," from PIE root *weg- (1) "to weave a web." Vela was mistaken in Vulgar Latin for a feminine singular noun. To take the veil "become a nun" is attested from early 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1200 年, "nun's head covering," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 and Old North 法语 veil (12 世纪, 现代法语 voile) "a head-covering," also "a sail, a curtain," 源自 拉丁语 vela, 为 … 的复数 velum "sail, curtain, covering," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *weg- (1) "to weave a web." Vela was mistaken in 通俗拉丁语 for a feminine singular 名词. To take the veil "become a nun" 见于 14 世纪初

entries.etymology: c. 1300, from Old French veine "vein, artery, pulse" (12c.), from Latin vena "a blood vessel," also "a water course, a vein of metal, a person's natural ability or interest," of unknown origin. The mining sense is attested in English from late 14c. (Greek phleps "vein" had the same secondary sense). Figurative sense of "strain or intermixture" (of some quality) is recorded from 1560s; that of "a humor or mood, natural tendency" is first recorded 1570s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, 源自 古法语 veine "vein, artery, pulse" (12 世纪), 源自 拉丁语 vena "a blood vessel," also "a water course, a vein of metal, a person's natural ability or interest," 来源不详. The mining sense is 见于 English 源自 14 世纪晚期 (希腊语 phleps "vein" had the same secondary sense). Figurative 语义 "strain or intermixture" (of some quality) 见于 1560 年代; that of "a humor or mood, natural tendency" is 首见于 1570 年代.

entries.etymology: late 14c., "emit from a confined space," probably a shortening of aventer "expose oneself to the air" (c. 1300), from Old French eventer "let out, expose to air," from Vulgar Latin *exventare, from Latin ex- "out" + ventus "wind" (see wind (n.1)). Sense of "express freely" first recorded 1590s. Sense of "divulge, publish" (1590s) is behind phrase vent one's spleen (see spleen). Related: Vented; venting.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "emit from a confined space," 可能 a shortening of aventer "expose oneself to the air" (约 1300 年), 源自 古法语 eventer "let out, expose to air," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *exventare, 源自 拉丁语 ex- "out" + ventus "wind" （参见 wind (n.1)). 义为 "express freely" 首见于 1590 年代. 义为 "divulge, publish" (1590 年代) is behind phrase vent one's spleen （参见 spleen). 同源词：Vented; venting.

definitionLines: vt. 使通风；给…••装通风设备
entries.definition: vt. 使通风；给…••装通风设备
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to scatter, disperse (as the wind does)," from Latin ventilatus, past participle of ventilare "to brandish, toss in the air, winnow, fan, agitate, set in motion," from ventulus "a breeze," diminutive of ventus "wind" (see wind (n.1)). Original notion is of cleaning grain by tossing it in the air and letting the wind blow away the chaff. Meaning "supply a room with fresh air" first recorded 1743, a verbal derivative of ventilation. Formerly with diverse slang senses, including "shoot" (someone), recorded from 1875, on the notion of "make holes in." Related: Ventilated; ventilating.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to scatter, disperse (as the wind does)," 源自 拉丁语 ventilatus, 为 … 的过去分词 ventilare "to brandish, toss in the air, winnow, fan, agitate, set in motion," 源自 ventulus "a breeze," 为 … 的指小形式 ventus "wind" （参见 wind (n.1)). Original notion is of cleaning grain by tossing it in the air and letting the wind blow away the chaff. 义为 "supply a room with fresh air" 首见于 1743 年, a verbal 为 … 的派生形式 ventilation. Formerly with diverse 俚语 senses, including "shoot" (someone), recorded 自 1875 年起, on the 概念 "make holes in." 同源词：Ventilated; ventilating.

entries.definition: v./n.冒险，拼，闯 v. 敢于，大胆表示 n. 冒险（事业）
entries.etymology: early 15c., "to risk the loss" (of something), shortened form of aventure, itself a form of adventure. General sense of "to dare, to presume" is recorded from 1550s. Related: Ventured; venturing.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "to risk the loss" (of something), shortened form of aventure, itself a form of adventure. General 语义 "to dare, to presume" 见于 1550 年代. 同源词：Ventured; venturing.

example.en: They decided to venture into the startup world despite the risks.
example.zh: 尽管存在风险，他们还是决定闯入创业领域。

entries.etymology:
late Old English, from Latin Venus (plural veneres), in ancient Roman mythology, the goddess of beauty and love, especially sensual love, from venus "love, sexual desire; loveliness, beauty, charm; a beloved object," from PIE root *wen- (1) "to strive after, wish, desire."

This root is the source of Sanskrit veti "follows after," vanas- "desire," vanati "desires, loves, wins;" Avestan vanaiti "he wishes, is victorious;" Latin venerari "to worship;" Old English wynn "joy," wunian "to dwell," wenian "to accustom, train, wean," wyscan "to wish."

 Applied by the Romans to Greek Aphrodite, Egyptian Hathor, etc. Applied in English to any beautiful, attractive woman by 1570s. As the name of the most brilliant planet from late 13c., from this sense in Latin (Old English called it morgensteorra and æfensteorra). The venus fly-trap (Dionæa muscipula) was discovered 1760 by Gov. Arthur Dobbs in North Carolina and description sent to Collinson in England. The Central Atlantic Coast Algonquian name for the plant, /titipiwitshik/, yielded regional American English tippity wichity.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语, 源自 拉丁语 Venus (plural veneres), in ancient Roman mythology, the goddess of beauty and love, 尤指 sensual love, 源自 venus "love, sexual desire; loveliness, beauty, charm; a beloved object," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *wen- (1) "to strive after, wish, desire." This root is the source of 梵语 veti "follows after," vanas- "desire," vanati "desires, loves, wins;" Avestan vanaiti "he wishes, is victorious;" 拉丁语 venerari "to worship;" 古英语 wynn "joy," wunian "to dwell," wenian "to accustom, train, wean," wyscan "to wish." Applied by the Romans to 希腊语 Aphrodite, Egyptian Hathor, etc. Applied in English to any beautiful, attractive woman by 1570 年代. As the name of the most brilliant planet 源自 13 世纪晚期, 源自 this sense in 拉丁语 (古英语 called it morgensteorra and æfensteorra). The venus fly-trap (Dionæa muscipula) was discovered 1760 年 by Gov. Arthur Dobbs in North Carolina and description sent to Collinson in England. The Central Atlantic Coast Algonquian name for the plant, /titipiwitshik/, yielded regional American English tippity wichity.

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Old French verbe "word; word of God; saying; part of speech that expresses action or being" (12c.) and directly from Latin verbum "verb," originally "a word," from PIE root *were- (3) "to speak" (source also of Avestan urvata- "command;" Sanskrit vrata- "command, vow;" Greek rhetor "public speaker," rhetra "agreement, covenant," eirein "to speak, say;" Hittite weriga- "call, summon;" Lithuanian vardas "name;" Gothic waurd, Old English word "word").
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, 源自 古法语 verbe "word; word of God; saying; part of speech that expresses action or being" (12 世纪) and 直接源自 拉丁语 verbum "verb," 原义为 "a word," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *were- (3) "to speak" (source also of Avestan urvata- "command;" 梵语 vrata- "command, vow;" 希腊语 rhetor "public speaker," rhetra "agreement, covenant," eirein "to speak, say;" Hittite weriga- "call, summon;" Lithuanian vardas "name;" Gothic waurd, 古英语 word "word").

definitionLines: a.口头的；言语的；照字面的； 动词的
entries.definition: a.口头的；言语的；照字面的； 动词的
entries.etymology: early 15c., "dealing with words" (especially in contrast to things or realities), from Old French verbal (14c.) and directly from Late Latin verbalis "consisting of words, relating to verbs," from Latin verbum "word" (see verb). Related: Verbally. Verbal conditioning is recorded from 1954. Colloquial verbal diarrhea is recorded from 1823. A verbal noun is a noun derived from a verb and sharing in its senses and constructions.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪初, "dealing with words" (尤指 in contrast to things or realities), 源自 古法语 verbal (14 世纪) and 直接源自 晚期拉丁语 verbalis "consisting of words, relating to verbs," 源自 拉丁语 verbum "word" （参见 动词). 同源词：Verbally. Verbal conditioning 见于 1954 年. Colloquial verbal diarrhea 见于 1823 年. A verbal 名词 is a 名词 derived 源自 a 动词 and sharing in its senses and constructions.

example.en: The contract requires verbal agreement before any written document is signed.
example.zh: 合同要求在签署任何书面文件之前先达成口头协议。

entries.etymology: 1530s, alteration of Middle English verdit (c. 1300), "a jury's decision in a case," from Anglo-French verdit (Old French voirdit) "sworn testimony, affidavit; judgment, written record of a verdict," literally "a true saying or report," from ver, veir "true" (see very) + dit, past participle of dire "to say" (see diction). Spelling influenced by Medieval Latin verdictum "a verdict."
entries.etymologyZh: 1530 年代, alteration of 中古英语 verdit (约 1300 年), "a jury's decision in a case," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 verdit (古法语 voirdit) "sworn testimony, affidavit; judgment, written record of a verdict," 字面义为 "a true saying or report," 源自 ver, veir "true" （参见 very) + dit, 为 … 的过去分词 dire "to say" （参见 diction). Spelling influenced by 中古拉丁语 verdictum "a verdict."

example.en: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty after reviewing all the evidence.
example.zh: 陪审团审查所有证据后作出了无罪裁决。

definitionLines: vt. 核实，证实；查清，查证
entries.definition: vt. 核实，证实；查清，查证
entries.etymology: early 14c., from Old French verifier "substantiate, find out the truth about" (14c.), from Medieval Latin verificare "make true," from Latin verus "true" (see very) + root of facere "to make" (see factitious).
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪初, 源自 古法语 verifier "substantiate, find out the truth about" (14 世纪), 源自 中古拉丁语 verificare "make true," 源自 拉丁语 verus "true" （参见 very) + root of facere "to make" （参见 factitious).

entries.etymology: c. 1600, "inconstant," from Latin versatilis "turning, revolving, moving, capable of turning with ease to varied subjects or tasks," from past participle stem of versare "keep turning, be engaged in something, turn over in the mind," frequentative of vertere "to turn" (see versus). Meaning "able to do many things well" is from 1762 in English.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1600 年, "inconstant," 源自 拉丁语 versatilis "turning, revolving, moving, capable of turning with ease to varied subjects or tasks," 源自 past participle stem of versare "keep turning, be engaged in something, turn over in the mind," 为 … 的反复体 vertere "to turn" （参见 versus). 义为 "able to do many things well" 始于 1762 年 in English.

entries.etymology:
late Old English (replacing Old English fers, an early West Germanic borrowing directly from Latin), "line or section of a psalm or canticle," later "line of poetry" (late 14c.), from Anglo-French and Old French vers "line of verse; rhyme, song," from Latin versus "a line, row, line of verse, line of writing," from PIE root *wer- (3) "to turn, bend" (see versus). The metaphor is of plowing, of "turning" from one line to another (vertere = "to turn") as a plowman does.

The English New Testament first was divided fully into verses in the Geneva version (1550s). Meaning "metrical composition" is recorded from c. 1300; as the non-repeating part of a modern song (between repetitions of the chorus) by 1918.
entries.etymologyZh: late 古英语 (replacing 古英语 fers, an early West 日耳曼语 borrowing 直接源自 拉丁语), "line or section of a psalm or canticle," later "line of poetry" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 and 古法语 vers "line of verse; rhyme, song," 源自 拉丁语 versus "a line, row, line of verse, line of writing," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *wer- (3) "to turn, bend" （参见 versus). The metaphor is of plowing, of "turning" 源自 one line to another (vertere = "to turn") 作为 plowman does. The English New Testament first was divided fully into verses in the Geneva version (1550 年代). 义为 "metrical composition" 见于 约 1300 年; as the non-repeating part of a modern song (between repetitions of the chorus) 截至 1918 年.

example.en: The poet recited a moving verse about loss and the passage of time.
example.zh: 诗人朗诵了一首关于失去与时光流逝的动人诗篇。

entries.etymology: 1580s, "a translation," from Middle French version, from Medieval Latin versionem (nominative versio) "a turning, a translation," from past participle stem of Latin vertere "to turn, change, alter, translate" (see versus). Also with a Middle English sense of "destruction;" the meaning "particular form of a description" is first attested 1788.
entries.etymologyZh: 1580 年代, "a translation," 源自 中古法语 version, 源自 中古拉丁语 versionem (主格 versio) "a turning, a translation," 源自 past participle stem of 拉丁语 vertere "to turn, change, alter, translate" （参见 versus). Also with a 中古英语 语义 "destruction;" the 意为 "particular form of a description" is 最早见于 1788 年.

example.en: Please download the latest version of the software from the official website.
example.zh: 请从官方网站下载该软件的最新版本。

entries.etymology: mid-15c., in legal case names, denoting action of one party against another, from Latin versus "turned toward or against," from past participle of vertere (frequentative versare) "to turn, turn back, be turned, convert, transform, translate, be changed," from PIE *wert- "to turn, wind," from root *wer- (3) "to turn, bend" (source also of Old English -weard "toward," originally "turned toward," weorthan "to befall," wyrd "fate, destiny," literally "what befalls one;" Sanskrit vartate "turns round, rolls;" Avestan varet- "to turn;" Old Church Slavonic vrŭteti "to turn, roll," Russian vreteno "spindle, distaff;" Lithuanian ver čiu "to turn;" Greek rhatane "stirrer, ladle;" German werden, Old English weorðan "to become" (for sense, compare turn into); Welsh gwerthyd "spindle, distaff;" Old Irish frith "against").
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪中期, in legal case names, denoting action of one party against another, 源自 拉丁语 versus "turned toward or against," 源自 为 … 的过去分词 vertere (frequentative versare) "to turn, turn back, be turned, convert, transform, translate, be changed," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wert- "to turn, wind," 源自 root *wer- (3) "to turn, bend" (source also of 古英语 -weard "toward," 原义为 "turned toward," weorthan "to befall," wyrd "fate, destiny," 字面义为 "what befalls one;" 梵语 vartate "turns round, rolls;" Avestan varet- "to turn;" Old Church Slavonic vrŭteti "to turn, roll," 俄语 vreteno "spindle, distaff;" Lithuanian ver čiu "to turn;" 希腊语 rhatane "stirrer, ladle;" 德语 werden, 古英语 weorðan "to become" (for sense, 对比 turn into); Welsh gwerthyd "spindle, distaff;" Old 爱尔兰语 frith "against").

entries.etymology: 1550s, "of or at the vertex, directly overhead," from Middle French vertical (1540s), from Late Latin verticalis "overhead," from Latin vertex (genitive verticis) "highest point" (see vertex). Meaning "straight up and down" is first recorded 1704. As a noun meaning "the vertical position or line" from 1834. Related: Vertically.
entries.etymologyZh: 1550 年代, "of or at the vertex, directly overhead," 源自 中古法语 vertical (1540 年代), 源自 晚期拉丁语 verticalis "overhead," 源自 拉丁语 vertex (属格 verticis) "highest point" （参见 vertex). 义为 "straight up and down" is 首见于 1704 年. 作名词时 意为 "the vertical position or line" 自 1834 年起. 同源词：Vertically.

example.en: The architect designed vertical lines to make the building appear taller.
example.zh: 建筑师设计了垂直线条，让建筑看起来更高。

definitionLines: ad. 很，非常；真正地，完全
a.［加强名词的语气］正是的， 恰好的；真正，真实的
entries.definition: ad. 很，非常；真正地，完全 a.［加强名词的语气］正是的， 恰好的；真正，真实的
entries.etymology: late 13c., verray "true, real, genuine," later "actual, sheer" (late 14c.), from Anglo-French verrai, Old French verai "true, truthful, sincere; right, just, legal," from Vulgar Latin *veracus, from Latin verax (genitive veracis) "truthful," from verus "true" (source also of Italian vero), from PIE root *were-o- "true, trustworthy" (source also of Old English wær "a compact," Old Dutch, Old High German war, Dutch waar, German wahr "true;" Welsh gwyr, Old Irish fir "true;" Old Church Slavonic vera "faith," Russian viera "faith, belief"). Meaning "greatly, extremely" is first recorded mid-15c. Used as a pure intensive since Middle English.
entries.etymologyZh: 13 世纪晚期, verray "true, real, genuine," later "actual, sheer" (14 世纪晚期), 源自 盎格鲁-法语 verrai, 古法语 verai "true, truthful, sincere; right, just, legal," 源自 通俗拉丁语 *veracus, 源自 拉丁语 verax (属格 veracis) "truthful," 源自 verus "true" (source also of 意大利语 vero), 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) root *were-o- "true, trustworthy" (source also of 古英语 wær "a compact," 古荷兰语, 古高地德语 war, 荷兰语 waar, 德语 wahr "true;" Welsh gwyr, Old 爱尔兰语 fir "true;" Old Church Slavonic vera "faith," 俄语 viera "faith, belief"). 义为 "greatly, extremely" is 首见于 15 世纪中期 Used 作为 pure intensive 自 中古英语.

example.en: The new safety rules were very strict and required additional training for all staff.
example.zh: 新的安全规定非常严格，要求所有员工接受额外培训。

definitionLines: n. 船舶；容器，器皿；管，导管， 血管
entries.definition: n. 船舶；容器，器皿；管，导管， 血管
entries.etymology: c. 1300, "container," from Old French vessel "container, receptacle, barrel; ship" (12c., Modern French vaisseau) from Late Latin vascellum "small vase or urn," also "a ship," alteration of Latin vasculum, diminutive of vas "vessel." Sense of "ship, boat" is found in English from early 14c. "The association between hollow utensils and boats appears in all languages" [Weekley]. Meaning "canal or duct of the body" (especially for carrying blood) is attested from late 14c.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1300 年, "container," 源自 古法语 vessel "container, receptacle, barrel; ship" (12 世纪, 现代法语 vaisseau) 源自 晚期拉丁语 vascellum "small vase or urn," also "a ship," alteration of 拉丁语 vasculum, 为 … 的指小形式 vas "vessel." 义为 "ship, boat" is found in English 源自 14 世纪初 "The association between hollow utensils and boats appears in all languages" [Weekley]. 义为 "canal or duct of the body" (尤指 for carrying blood) 见于 14 世纪晚期

example.en: The cargo vessel was loaded with goods bound for Southeast Asia.
example.zh: 这艘货船装载着运往东南亚的货物。

entries.definition: n. 老手，老兵 a. 老练的
entries.etymology: c. 1500, "old experienced soldier," from French vétéran, from Latin veteranus "old, aged, that has been long in use," especially of soldiers; as a plural noun, "old soldiers," from vetus (genitive veteris) "old, aged, advanced in years; of a former time," as a plural noun, vetores, "men of old, forefathers," from PIE *wet-es-, from root *wet- (2) "year" (source also of Sanskrit vatsa- "year," Greek etos "year," Hittite witish "year," Old Church Slavonic vetuchu "old," Old Lithuanian vetušas "old, aged;" and compare wether). Latin vetus also is the ultimate source of Italian vecchio, French vieux, Spanish viejo. General sense of "one who has seen long service in any office or position" is attested from 1590s. The adjective first recorded 1610s.
entries.etymologyZh: 约 1500 年, "old experienced soldier," 源自 法语 vétéran, 源自 拉丁语 veteranus "old, aged, that has been long in use," 尤指 of soldiers; 作为 plural 名词, "old soldiers," 源自 vetus (属格 veteris) "old, aged, advanced in years; of a former time," 作为 plural 名词, vetores, "men of old, forefathers," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wet-es-, 源自 root *wet- (2) "year" (source also of 梵语 vatsa- "year," 希腊语 etos "year," Hittite witish "year," Old Church Slavonic vetuchu "old," Old Lithuanian vetušas "old, aged;" and 对比 wether). 拉丁语 vetus also is the ultimate source of 意大利语 vecchio, 法语 vieux, 西班牙语 viejo. General 语义 "one who has seen long service in any office or position" 见于 1590 年代. The 形容词 首见于 1610 年代.

example.en: The coach is a veteran who has trained champions for over twenty years.
example.zh: 这位教练是一位经验丰富的老手，执教冠军已逾二十年。

definitionLines: vi. 反对，不赞成；否决，禁止
entries.definition: n. （to）否决权 vt. 使用否决权 vi. 反对，不赞成；否决，禁止
entries.etymology: 1620s, from Latin veto, literally "I forbid," first person singular present indicative of vetare "forbid, prohibit, oppose, hinder," of unknown origin. In ancient Rome, the "technical term for protest interposed by a tribune of the people against any measure of the Senate or of the magistrates" [Lewis].
entries.etymologyZh: 1620 年代, 源自 拉丁语 veto, 字面义为 "I forbid," first person singular present indicative of vetare "forbid, prohibit, oppose, hinder," 来源不详. In ancient Rome, the "technical term for protest interposed by a tribune of the people against any measure of the Senate or of the magistrates" [Lewis].

entries.etymology: 1779, from Latin via "by way of," ablative form of via "way, road, path, highway, channel, course," from PIE *wegh- "to go, convey" (see weigh).
entries.etymologyZh: 1779 年, 源自 拉丁语 经由 "by way of," ablative form of 经由 "way, road, path, highway, channel, course," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wegh- "to go, convey" （参见 weigh).

entries.etymology: 1610s (intransitive) "move to and fro;" 1660s, "swing to and fro;" from Latin vibratus, past participle of vibrare "set in tremulous motion, move quickly to and fro, quiver, tremble, shake," from PIE *wib-ro-, from root *weip- "to turn, vacillate, tremble ecstatically, move quickly to and fro" (source also of Lithuanian wyburiu "to wag" (the tail), Danish vippe, Dutch wippen "to swing," Old English wipan "to wipe"). Transitive sense "cause to vibrate" is from c. 1700. Related: Vibrated; vibrating.
entries.etymologyZh: 1610 年代 (intransitive) "move to and fro;" 1660 年代, "swing to and fro;" 源自 拉丁语 vibratus, 为 … 的过去分词 vibrare "set in tremulous motion, move quickly to and fro, quiver, tremble, shake," 源自 原始印欧语 (PIE) *wib-ro-, 源自 root *weip- "to turn, vacillate, tremble ecstatically, move quickly to and fro" (source also of Lithuanian wyburiu "to wag" (the tail), Danish vippe, 荷兰语 wippen "to swing," 古英语 wipan "to wipe"). Transitive sense "cause to vibrate" 始于 约 1700 年. 同源词：Vibrated; vibrating.

definitionLines: n. 罪恶，恶习；缺点，毛病
entries.definition: n. 罪恶，恶习；缺点，毛病

definitionLines: a. 堕落的；恶毒的；恶意的
entries.definition: a. 堕落的；恶毒的；恶意的
entries.etymology:
late 14c., "unwholesome, impure, of the nature of vice, wicked, corrupting, pernicious, harmful;" of a text, "erroneous, corrupt," from Anglo-French vicious, Old French vicios "wicked, cunning, underhand; defective, illegal" (Modern French vicieux), from Latin vitiosus (Medieval Latin vicious) "faulty, full of faults, defective, corrupt; wicked, depraved," from vitium "fault" (see vice (n.1)).

Meaning "inclined to be savage or dangerous" is first recorded 1711 (originally of animals, especially horses); that of "full of spite, bitter, severe" is from 1825. In law, "marred by some inherent fault" (late 14c.), hence also this sense in logic (c. 1600), as in vicious circle in reasoning (c. 1792, Latin circulus vitiosus), which was given a general sense of "a situation in which action and reaction intensify one another" by 1839. Related: Viciously (mid-14c., "sinfully"); viciousness.
entries.etymologyZh: 14 世纪晚期, "unwholesome, impure, of the nature of vice, wicked, corrupting, pernicious, harmful;" of a text, "erroneous, corrupt," 源自 盎格鲁-法语 vicious, 古法语 vicios "wicked, cunning, underhand; defective, illegal" (现代法语 vicieux), 源自 拉丁语 vitiosus (中古拉丁语 vicious) "faulty, full of faults, defective, corrupt; wicked, depraved," 源自 vitium "fault" （参见 vice (n.1)). 义为 "inclined to be savage or dangerous" is 首见于 1711 年 (原义为 of animals, 尤指 horses); that of "full of spite, bitter, severe" 始于 1825 年. In law, "marred by some inherent fault" (14 世纪晚期), hence also this sense in logic (约 1600 年), as in vicious circle in reasoning (约 1792 年, 拉丁语 circulus vitiosus), which was given a general 语义 "a situation in which action and reaction intensify one another" 截至 1839 年. 同源词：Viciously (14 世纪中期, "sinfully"); viciousness.

entries.etymology: late 15c., "living creature killed and offered as a sacrifice to a deity or supernatural power," from Latin victima "person or animal killed as a sacrifice." Perhaps distantly connected to Old English wig "idol," Gothic weihs "holy," German weihen "consecrate" (compare Weihnachten "Christmas") on notion of "a consecrated animal." Sense of "person who is hurt, tortured, or killed by another" is recorded from 1650s; meaning "person oppressed by some power or situation" is from 1718. Weaker sense of "person taken advantage of" is recorded from 1781.
entries.etymologyZh: 15 世纪晚期, "living creature killed and offered as a sacrifice to a deity or supernatural power," 源自 拉丁语 victima "person or animal killed as a sacrifice." Perhaps distantly connected to 古英语 wig "idol," Gothic weihs "holy," 德语 weihen "consecrate" (对比 Weihnachten "Christmas") on 概念 "a consecrated animal." 义为 "person who is hurt, tortured, or killed by another" 见于 1650 年代; 意为 "person oppressed by some power or situation" 始于 1718 年. Weaker 语义 "person taken advantage of" 见于 1781 年.

example.en: The charity provides legal support for victims of domestic abuse.
example.zh: 该慈善机构为家庭暴力受害者提供法律援助。

entries.etymology: late 14c., from Anglo-French victorious and directly from Late Latin victoriosus "having many victories," from victoria "victory" (see victory). Related: Victoriously; victoriousness.
